Chapter 423: Olivine Gym and Jasmine

As Raikou stared in confusion, water suddenly exploded behind it. Before it could react, a tremendous force slammed directly into it!

The impact sent Raikou flying until it finally struck a rock.

Bang!

A circular web of cracks spread across the stone. As Raikou slid to the ground, it looked toward the lake in alarm and saw an enormous head emerging from the water.

Water streamed from that massive head. Through the flow, a pair of fierce red eyes glared fixedly at Raikou, presenting a savage and intensely oppressive sight!

It was that Steelix!

Raikou could not understand why Steelix did not fear the water!

And with its immense weight and the mud covering the lakebed, how had it climbed out!?

Raikou tried to struggle to its feet, but a sudden wave of dizziness swept over it.

It had already suffered severe injuries when Team Rocket attacked the previous afternoon. A night of treatment had healed the visible wounds, but Raikou had yet to recover fully in either mind or body.

More crucially, it had eaten nothing and taken only a few drinks of water. Its reserves had been dangerously low all along!

On top of that, it had been trapped in the barrier for a second time moments ago. The repeated electric shocks had added many fresh injuries. Enduring this long had already demanded tremendous effort. Now, after taking a direct blow from Crystal Steelix, Raikou's head spun and darkness clouded its vision. It stood weakly in place.

Crystal Steelix naturally gave Raikou no time to recover. Its enormous body climbed from the water and charged straight toward it.

"It's over," Ethan said softly.

Just as he declared, Crystal Steelix raised its massive tail and used Iron Tail again, lashing it viciously into Raikou.

Smack!

Raikou was in no condition to evade. The instant Iron Tail struck, the blow knocked it unconscious!

Seeing Raikou collapse, Ethan took out the Ultra Ball he had prepared and hurled it with all his strength.

The Ultra Ball traced a perfect arc through the air. As it reached Raikou, red light burst from within and enveloped the Legendary Pokemon.

Like an enormous net, the light drew Raikou into the Ultra Ball. The ball shook violently several times, but each movement grew smaller. Finally, with a soft click, it fell completely still!

"Yes!"

Erika was delighted for Ethan from the bottom of her heart when she saw that he had captured Raikou.

Ethan could not suppress his own smile.

After Raikou slipped from his grasp at Greenfield, he had abandoned all hope of capturing it. He never imagined they would meet again!

He felt extraordinarily lucky, but he also had to acknowledge that this capture marked enormous progress for him.

At the abandoned power plant, he had taken advantage of the terrain and surrounded Zapdos with his entire team. Later, he captured Articuno using only a handful of Pokemon. After that, he battled Moltres with the two Legendary Pokemon Zapdos and Articuno. At almost every step along the way, he had relied on superior numbers.

Now he had finally captured a Legendary Pokemon in a one-on-one battle. How could that not count as growth?

Of course, Raikou had entered the battle in poor condition, and Ethan had exploited a favorable type matchup. Even so, he believed that as his Pokemon continued to grow stronger, the day would eventually come when he could capture such Pokemon with far greater ease!

Despite everything, the result still felt rather dreamlike.

Only a few days had passed since he sent away the three Legendary birds and freed several places on his belt. Yet he had already captured Raikou.

Capturing Raikou was wonderful news, but his belt had only one open place left. Space was tight again...

...

Olivine City.

A port city filled with the scent of the sea breeze.

Located in west-central Johto near Ecruteak City and Cianwood City, Olivine faced the ocean and was one of the region's most important tourist destinations.

A cruise ship called the S.S. Aqua docked at its port. Once a month, the ship made a round trip to Vermilion City in Kanto. Compared with other routes, it offered passengers a leisurely vacation at sea. Besides airplanes and the magnetic levitation train, the S.S. Aqua was therefore a popular third choice for travelers heading to Kanto.

For some reason, whenever Olivine City came to mind, Ethan always thought of Farfetch'd. The two had nothing in common except that their Chinese names shared the character for scallion, yet his thoughts invariably linked them.

At that moment, Ethan and Erika were walking along Olivine City's coastal boulevard toward the Olivine Gym.

They had arrived the previous evening. After spending the night at the Pokemon Center and eating breakfast, they had skipped any sightseeing and headed directly to their main objective.

The Olivine Gym was the city's official Gym. It stood in the northwest of the city and was led by Jasmine, a specialist in Steel-type Pokemon. Defeating her would earn the challenger a Mineral Badge.

Olivine's docks lay beside the road. Even with tall buildings blocking parts of the view, the pair still caught periodic glimpses of the city's landmark: the Glitter Lighthouse.

According to local stories, an Ampharos lived at the top of the lighthouse. Every night, its electric light guided passing ships. The Ampharos had become part of the city itself and was protected by Olivine's residents.

Ethan and Erika stopped beside the railing to admire the lighthouse from a distance, then continued toward the Gym.

After crossing nearly half the city, they finally reached their destination.

From the outside, the Olivine Gym stood four stories tall. It had a flat-roofed trapezoidal structure, rather like a pyramid with its peak removed. Its walls consisted of enormous unbroken panes of glass, giving the building a distinctly modern appearance.

Inside, Ethan explained his purpose to a staff member and was led to the battlefield.

Compared with the exterior, the battlefield was far more austere. It resembled an enormous warehouse, with no mechanisms or special features. Even the ground was an ordinary field of packed earth.

Ethan and Erika waited in the empty arena for several minutes before Jasmine finally appeared.

Jasmine was quite young, only seventeen or eighteen. She was petite and fairly pretty, with long flaxen hair falling behind her. A bun had been tied on either side of her head, making them resemble a pair of little wings.

She wore a pale blue dress with a huge bow at her chest, giving her an almost childlike appearance.

It was difficult to imagine that such a pure-looking young woman favored Steel-type Pokemon!

What does she see in them? Is it because she likes pole dancing?

Jasmine smiled when she saw them. "Welcome to the Olivine Gym."

Ethan stepped forward. "Hello, Miss Jasmine. I've come to challenge the Olivine Gym."

"I know who you are." Jasmine approached him and extended a friendly hand. "You're the Indigo League Champion. I watched your matches!"

Chapter 424: A Shift in Their Relationship and Metagross

Ethan was not especially surprised that Jasmine recognized him.

Although he had competed in another region's tournament, Kanto and Johto occupied the same landmass and shared a border. Apart from Gym Leaders like Morty of Ecruteak City, who only followed competitions within his own region, most Gym Leaders kept a keen eye on major tournaments.

They often watched matches to broaden their own perspectives. They could not possibly view every battle, but they generally would not miss the most important contests, such as the semifinals and final.

Still...

No matter how Ethan looked at her, Jasmine seemed like a delicate young woman better suited to quiet pastimes. It was difficult to imagine her sitting in front of a television, emotions rising and falling with every turn in the match!

Then again, that was only to be expected from a woman who liked steel poles... No, Steel-type Pokemon. Beneath that fragile exterior, she clearly possessed a passionate heart!

Those thoughts flashed through Ethan's mind.

After their handshake ended, Jasmine turned toward Erika.

She studied Erika for a moment, looking thoughtful, before sudden recognition crossed her face. "You're Miss Erika of the Celadon Gym, aren't you?"

"Huh?" This time, it was Erika's turn to be surprised. "You know me?"

Jasmine nodded. "When I was little, my parents took me to Kanto, and we attended one of your family's tea gatherings. I spoke with you then. I still remember tripping and falling, and you personally tended my injury. Of course, it was a long time ago, so you may have forgotten."

Erika truly had no memory of it. Embarrassed, she said, "I'm sorry. I don't remember."

"It doesn't matter." Jasmine waved it off without concern. "We were both very young then, so forgetting is perfectly normal. Besides, haven't we just met again now?"

In his mind, Ethan gave Jasmine a thumbs-up.

What an artful response!

Meeting someone again after forgetting them could have been deeply awkward. Yet with only a few words, Jasmine had both spared Erika embarrassment and strengthened the connection between them. Impressive!

Jasmine's gaze moved between Ethan and Erika. Covering her mouth, she asked softly, "Why are the two of you traveling together? Could you be a couple?"

There it was. Another person had misunderstood their relationship.

Ethan had lost count of how many people had made the same mistake!

He sighed helplessly. This was an unavoidable problem whenever an unattached man and woman traveled together.

Erika, however, had far more to think about after hearing the question.

In the past, she had always responded calmly to such remarks. Perhaps too many people had said the same thing along the way, however, because a strange feeling had begun to stir inside her. The many small moments she had shared with Ethan were hardly dramatic, yet they had quietly and imperceptibly changed her state of mind.

Erika stole a glance at Ethan. For some reason, the tips of her ears turned faintly red, and a trace of panic fluttered in her heart.

Fortunately, she quickly regained her composure and gently shook her head at Jasmine. "You've misunderstood. We're merely traveling companions."

"I see."

Jasmine gave her a peculiar smile. Mature beyond her years, how could she fail to notice Erika's embarrassment? She was certain that even if the pair were not a couple, there was at least some ambiguity between them!

Erika could not tell from Jasmine's mysterious expression whether she believed the explanation. Fortunately, Jasmine did not pursue the subject, allowing Erika's tense heart to relax.

The three chatted a little longer. Once the time seemed right, they finally turned to the matter at hand.

Jasmine walked slowly to the command area on the opposite side of the field and faced Ethan from afar. Erika took a seat in the spectator stands.

The staff member who had escorted Ethan inside assumed the role of referee.

Once Ethan was ready, the referee announced the rules according to custom.

"The match between Jasmine on the red side and challenger Ethan on the green side is about to begin! This will be an elimination match in which both Trainers may use two Pokemon. The battle will end when either Trainer has no Pokemon able to continue!"

As the referee finished, Jasmine reached for a Poke Ball, but Ethan suddenly stopped her.

"Miss Jasmine, if possible, could you use your strongest Pokemon?"

Jasmine looked startled for only a second before understanding his intention. She smiled and nodded.

"I see. Weaker Pokemon can no longer offer you meaningful training, can they? Very well. I'll send out my most powerful Pokemon!"

She turned and approached a platform at the side of the arena. After placing the Poke Balls she had brought onto it, she selected two different ones.

By the time she returned to her command area, Ethan had also chosen his first Pokemon.

At the referee's signal, both Trainers threw a Poke Ball. Two flashes of blue light filled the arena, and a pair of Pokemon appeared on the field.

Jasmine's Pokemon drew attention first. Its body was blue-green, with four powerful limbs. A silver metallic cross formed an X across its face. Its entire body resembled an enormous iron disk and gleamed with a metallic luster!

Ethan recognized it instantly.

Metagross...

This Pokemon was powerfulextraordinarily so.

Under the games' classification, it belonged to the same pseudo-legendary tier as Dragonite from the first generation. It could not be underestimated.

Since this was Ethan's first time encountering one, he took out his Pokedex and aimed it at Metagross.

The Pokedex beeped. "Metagross, the Iron Leg Pokemon. A Steel and Psychic type. Metagross is formed from the combination of two Metang. It possesses tremendous psychic power and also prides itself on extraordinary physical strength. Its four brains are said to connect into a complex neural network, making it more intelligent than a supercomputer. It can perform calculations to analyze and defeat its opponent, calmly driving the target into a corner. Metagross can also retract its four legs to hover in the air and fly with its limbs folded."

Ethan put away his Pokedex and studied Metagross once more.

In terms of type matchups, most types could gain no advantage against Steel, apart from a select few.

Of the eighteen known types, Steel took only half damage from ten and was entirely immune to Poison-type moves. Among the seven remaining types, only Fighting-, Ground-, and Fire-type moves inflicted double damage.

That alone was terrifying!

No type other than Steel could claim anything comparable!

Chapter 425: Blastoise Returns

Now it was time to look at Ethan's Pokemon. Since he had known what type his opponent would use, he made no changes in response to Metagross. Instead, he followed the strategy he had prepared the previous night and sent out Blastoise!

That's right. Blastoise!

Ethan had contacted Chloe from the Pokemon Center the previous night and asked her to transfer Blastoise to him. He wanted it for this Gym battle and to keep a Pokemon that had gone so long without fighting from growing rusty!

The Pokemon that had rendered distinguished service during the Indigo League would fight for Ethan once more today, pouring its heart into battle for its Trainer!

The two Pokemon stared each other down, fierce fighting spirit blazing in their eyes.

Within Ethan's roster, Blastoise ranked above average in strength. It could not compare with first-team Pokemon such as Gyarados and Gardevoir, so it was difficult to say which side would win against this Metagross.

Even so, the outcome was hardly certain.

Water-type moves held no advantage against Steel or Psychic types, but Steel-type attacks inflicted only half damage against a Water-type Pokemon.

That undoubtedly relieved much of the pressure on Blastoise.

Of course, that did not mean Blastoise was guaranteed to win. The result would depend on how the two Pokemon performed in the arena.

The referee waved his flags, signaling the start of the match. Metagross immediately charged toward Blastoise.

"Blastoise, use Hydro Pump!" Ethan commanded calmly in the face of the onrushing Metagross.

At his instruction, Blastoise lowered its body as the two cannons on its back began gathering energy. The next instant, once the energy reached its peak, both cannons fired at once!

Fwoosh! Fwoosh!

Two thick streams of water erupted from the cannons and shot directly toward Metagross!

A powerful Water-type move like Hydro Pump could inflict tremendous damage. Even without a type advantage, Jasmine did not dare let Metagross take the attack lightly.

She shouted, "Use Agility!"

Just before Hydro Pump struck, Metagross's speed rose sharply. It accelerated to one side and evaded the attack.

Hydro Pump missed, but Ethan was unconcerned.

Unlike an ordinary cannon shell, Hydro Pump did not become useless after a single shot. The move consisted of a continuous stream of water. As long as the water kept flowing, the attack would not end!

If the opponent evaded, Blastoise merely needed to aim again!

Blastoise rotated its body, and the two cannons on its back turned with it.

The thick streams drew an arc through the air and closed on Metagross once more. This time, Metagross had moved too close to the edge of the battlefield to evade comfortably. Hydro Pump struck it directly.

The rushing water pinned Metagross in place, leaving it unable to move.

However, the attack had already expended much of its energy. Hydro Pump stopped after only a few seconds and did not inflict significant damage.

Ethan was about to order Blastoise to repeat the attack when Metagross's eyes suddenly began to glow. A burst of Confusion followed and struck Blastoise.

Blastoise flew high into the air before crashing heavily back down.

Thud!

Its thick body struck the ground with a muffled impact, and the entire field seemed to tremble.

Metagross had already rushed in front of it by the time Blastoise climbed back to its feet.

Metagross raised its two forelimbs. Its steel-hard claws swung at Blastoise like a stream of comets, one strike following another without pause!

It was the Steel-type move Meteor Mash!

Ethan recognized the move but remained completely unmoved.

"Use Iron Defense!"

Blastoise possessed a thick hide and excellent defenses on both the physical and special sides. Steel-type moves also dealt only half damage. Ethan had no fear of the attack. Once Iron Defense took effect, Blastoise neither dodged nor retreated, withstanding the entire barrage of Meteor Mash head-on!

As Meteor Mash began to weaken, Ethan keenly spotted an opening and immediately launched a counterattack.

"Use Aqua Tail!"

Blastoise turned its body and lashed Metagross with a tail wrapped in flowing water.

Smack!

Metagross had yet to lower its forelimbs. The hit caught it off balance and forced it several steps backward.

It quickly recovered and steadied itself.

Although Metagross had taken damage, Jasmine did not relent from her command area. She shouted, "Use Psychic!"

Ethan issued an order of his own.

"Use Protect!"

A powerful, invisible shock wave formed from psychic energy and arrived in an instant. As it struck Blastoise, a faint light appeared before the Pokemon and blocked the Psychic attack!

In the spectator stands, Erika watched the battle with complete concentration while marveling at its intensity.

She had never expected Jasmine's Metagross to be this strong. It was fighting evenly with Ethan's Blastoise!

Fortunately, Blastoise was formidable as well. It deserved its place on the team that had helped Ethan win the championship. Even after going so long without battling other Pokemon, it had maintained an impressive standard.

And as for Ethan...

Her gaze drifted involuntarily toward the man.

When he commanded a Pokemon in battle, a light seemed to shine in his eyes. His entire presence took on a different brilliance, making him increasingly handsome and deeply compelling.

By the time Erika came to herself, she realized that she had been staring at Ethan for quite a while!

She was startled by the change in herself. Remembering what Jasmine had said before the battle, she could not help sighing.

Pressing a hand against her pounding heart, she marveled at her own transformation.

This is bad...

Could everyone really have been right?

In appearance, Ethan was undeniably outstanding. Spending time with him had also shown her his wit and humor. If she were choosing a boyfriend, he truly suited both her tastes and her temperament.

But...

She thought of Sabrina, and her heart suddenly tightened.

What a shame... If only I'd met him sooner...

Erika shook her head, dismissed the distracting thoughts, and focused on the battlefield again.

The two Pokemon were still fighting. Several injuries of varying severity now marked their bodies. Evidently, while Erika's attention had wandered, the Pokemon had exchanged another fierce series of attacks under their Trainers' commands.

The deadlock soon broke.

Metagross closed in again and used Zen Headbutt. This time, Blastoise immediately used Withdraw. After avoiding the damage, it flowed directly into Rapid Spin and launched a counterattack.

The spinning impact left Metagross frozen in place. Blastoise retained its momentum and struck the Pokemon's hard body, bouncing high into the air. It continued accelerating its rotation overhead, then came crashing straight down toward Metagross.

Boom!

The sound of a heavy object striking the ground echoed throughout the battlefield...

Chapter 426: Battling Lucario

Jasmine showed no surprise when she saw Metagross collapse.

Winning against a Champion would have been ideal, but losing was hardly unacceptable.

Jasmine had watched Ethan's matches and understood just how frighteningly strong the man before her was. He had won the Indigo League without suffering a single defeat.

Besides, Metagross had not been helpless. It had driven Blastoise into desperate situations several times during the battle. Ethan had simply proven the more skillful Trainer, and her Metagross truly was not as strong as Blastoise.

What Jasmine did not know was that Ethan's Blastoise had gone a very long time without battling. If she had known, she probably could not have remained as calm as she was now.

For Ethan, the victory had not come easily either.

Jasmine's Metagross was genuinely powerful. The injuries covering Blastoise made that obvious. If Blastoise had not taken half damage from Steel-type moves, it might have been the one to fall.

Of course, Pokemon battles were like that. They were fair and unfair at the same time, and there was no room for so many hypotheticals.

Regardless of the outcome, both Trainers had acknowledged each other's strength.

Jasmine recalled Metagross and took out her second Poke Ball.

"This one is next!"

She threw the Poke Ball across the arena. Blue light flashed, and a slender, gray-blue Pokemon about 1.2 meters tall appeared on the field.

The Pokemon resembled a real-world dog, though it stood upright. A spike protruded from the back of each forepaw, with another on its chest. Its upper body was lean, giving it an imposing bearing.

Ethan recognized it immediately.

Lucario!

He had never expected Jasmine's second Pokemon to be Lucario!

This species was extraordinarily popular and widely loved. Given the opportunity, Ethan would have liked to capture one himself.

After all, who would not want to become a hero of Aura?

Ethan took out his Pokedex and aimed it at Lucario.

The Pokedex beeped. "Lucario, the Aura Pokemon. A Fighting and Steel type. Lucario possesses the ability to sense Aura. Through Aura, it can read thoughts and actions and understand human language. It can even sense the emotions of an opponent more than one kilometer away. By detecting Aura, Lucario can perceive opponents that would otherwise remain invisible. Because it understands human thoughts, it only becomes close to Trainers with righteous hearts."

Ethan recalled Blastoise while considering which Pokemon to send out next.

Lucario's combination of Fighting and Steel made it exceptionally powerful in close combat, forcing him to choose with care.

His fingers moved slowly across his Poke Balls before settling on Charizard's.

If Jasmine had saved Lucario until the final round, it had to be her ace. Ethan needed to answer with an appropriate level of strength.

Among his other Pokemon, apart from Gengar, only Charizard could face Lucario without suffering any disadvantage.

Blue light flashed, and Charizard appeared on the field. It beat its wings, rose into the air, and studied its opponent with a commanding gaze. Lucario refused to yield and glared straight back from the ground!

Once both Pokemon were ready, the referee waved his flags, and the battle began again.

The intensity reached its peak from the very start.

Ethan attacked first. At his command, Charizard used Flamethrower from the air, launching a ranged assault. Lucario responded without hesitation and met it with Aura Sphere.

A blue-green sphere of energy formed between Lucario's paws and flew skyward, colliding with the sea of flames.

The two attacks detonated in a violent explosion. The shock wave from Aura Sphere extinguished most of the fire.

With its first attack unsuccessful, Charizard searched for another opportunity.

This time, it changed tactics.

Charizard spread its wings and accelerated continuously through the air. Once it had built enough speed, it dived toward Lucario.

This was the Flying-type move Wing Attack. It closed on the target at tremendous speed and struck with devastating force. Because the attack descended from above, hitting a small or midsized Pokemon like Lucario would not only cause damage but also knock it to the ground and leave it exposed!

Jasmine hurriedly shouted, "Quick, use Detect!"

Light flashed in Lucario's eyes as it watched Charizard's every movement. In that instant, Charizard seemed to slow before its gaze like a film shown in slow motion, every detail becoming perfectly clear!

To everyone else, Charizard moved almost too quickly to see. In a single breath, it had already reached Lucario!

Lucario leaped aside and evaded the attack. As the two Pokemon passed one another, it seized Charizard's wing, put all its strength into both arms, and hurled Charizard away!

But Lucario had underestimated its opponent.

Charizard had barely been thrown any distance before it beat its wings violently and forced itself to change direction in midair. It closed on Lucario again!

At the same time, flames erupted across Charizard's entire body. It accelerated once more and slammed heavily into Lucario.

It was the powerful Fire-type move Flare Blitz. Although Charizard would also take some damage, a successful hit inflicted tremendous harm and carried a strong chance of burning the target!

Lucario clearly had not expected Charizard to counterattack after being thrown!

Unable to evade, it could only watch as Flare Blitz struck head-on. With a tremendous bang, Lucario flew backward like a kite with its string cut!

"Lucario!" Jasmine cried out anxiously.

She had every reason to worry. Lucario possessed outstanding offensive power, but its comparatively small frame was too fragile to withstand many attacks like that!

Thud!

Lucario crashed heavily to the ground and rolled several more times. As it struggled to rise, two crescent-shaped blades of air swept across half the battlefield straight toward it!

"Quick, dodge!"

At Jasmine's urgent cry, Lucario tried to leap aside. Before it could move, however, its body suddenly stiffened. Burning pain swept through it and left it unable to move!

Looking down, Lucario realized it had been burned!

Fwoosh! Fwoosh!

At that moment, the two Air Slash blades reached it. Twin impacts hurled Lucario backward once again!

Chapter 427: The Mineral Badge

Lucario struggled to its feet. Burn marks covered its body, and the burn itself made it tremble faintly beyond its control.

Its condition was clearly dire. It was suffering tremendous pain and had already reached the brink.

After taking two heavy attacks in succession, Lucario's stamina was nearly exhausted. Fortunately, its will remained strong. Even now, it refused to abandon the battle.

"Lucario, quickly use Close Combat!"

Jasmine clenched a fist and gave another command. In truth, she was deeply worried about Lucario and had considered stopping the match several times. But if her own Pokemon refused to surrender, how could she give up?

Ethan knew this was Lucario's final stand, so he naturally did not dare lower his guard.

Close Combat was one of the most damaging Fighting-type moves, capable of unleashing tremendous force in an instant. Relaxing now would result in a severe loss!

"Charizard, dodge it!"

Charizard leaped backward and opened the distance, avoiding the punches Lucario threw toward it.

Seeing this, Lucario drew a deep breath. Red light suddenly erupted across its body, as though all the blood within it had begun to burn. With no thought for its own survival, it charged toward Charizard!

Final Gambit!

Ethan narrowed his eyes.

This move poured everything into an attack against the opponent. The user would be left on the verge of collapse afterward, but the target would suffer damage equal to the user's remaining strength.

The worse the user's condition, the more viciously it would fight!

It seemed Lucario intended to trade injury for injury, force Charizard into the same desperate condition, and take it down as well!

Fighting-type Pokemon were often like this. The more severely injured they became, the fiercer their attacks grew, and the more willing they were to risk everything in an exchange.

But now that Ethan understood Lucario's intention, he naturally would not allow it to succeed.

At his command, Charizard flew high into the air. Facing an opponent far above it, Lucario no longer had enough strength to attack with Aura.

Weakened by both exhaustion and its burn, Lucario could not even lift its legs. It could only raise its head slightly and stare up at Charizard with unwillingness written across its face!

High above, Charizard's abdomen expanded as flames gathered inside its mouth. It opened its jaws and unleashed a stream of searing fire that crossed the distance in an instant and struck Lucario directly.

This time, Lucario did not even have the strength to evade. The flames swallowed it whole.

Fire blazed across the field. Through the glow, Lucario's body could just be seen slowly collapsing...

Several seconds later, the flames quickly faded.

When the final spark died, Lucario lay unconscious on the ground, its body blackened and scorched.

The referee stepped forward. After confirming that Lucario had completely lost consciousness, he raised the green flag and announced the result.

"Lucario is unable to battle! The winner is the challenger, Ethan!"

Jasmine recalled Lucario to its Poke Ball and approached Ethan with her expression unchanged.

"What breathtaking pacing. I accept this loss wholeheartedly!"

Charizard landed beside Ethan. He stroked its neck, then turned toward Jasmine.

"Your Metagross and Lucario are both powerful. Of all the Gym opponents I've faced, they rank among the best."

Ethan was not merely consoling Jasmine. Her two Pokemon truly were formidable, and Metagross in particular had been trained exceptionally well!

Jasmine smiled faintly. Receiving praise from a Champion was undoubtedly something to celebrate.

She reached into her pocket, took out a badge gleaming with metallic light, and offered it to Ethan.

"This is my Mineral Badge. Please keep it safe."

Ethan thanked her and accepted the badge. Looking down, he found an octagonal badge with a smooth gray mirrored surface, as though it had been fashioned by polishing an ordinary piece of steel.

Compared with other Gym Badges, the Mineral Badge was exceptionally plain.

He had barely placed it inside his badge case when Erika approached from the spectator stands.

"That was an excellent match." She looked at Ethan and smiled gently. "Especially the first round. For a while, I thought your Blastoise might lose."

Knowing she was joking, Ethan played along and teased her in return. "Then I must have disappointed you. Clearly, my skill carried the day~"

His smug, self-satisfied expression made both women cover their mouths and laugh. The atmosphere was relaxed and friendly.

After chatting a little longer, Ethan announced that they should leave.

Jasmine wanted them to remain a while, but Ethan declined.

She clearly wished to spend more time with Erika. Yet when Ethan remained firm, she could only accept the decision reluctantly.

Jasmine turned to Erika and said sincerely, "Miss Erika, I hope you'll visit me again after your journey ends!"

"Don't worry." Erika nodded. "When I have time, I'll definitely come back to see you. And this time, I promise I won't forget you again!"

...

After leaving the Olivine Gym, Ethan first returned to the Pokemon Center and had both Pokemon that had fought treated. Once their treatment was complete, he did not transfer Blastoise back. He intended to keep it beside him for a while longer.

After eating lunch at the Pokemon Center, the pair lingered no longer. They prepared to continue toward the next city with a Gym.

Two possible routes once again lay before them.

They could travel by sea, pass through the Whirl Islands, reach Cianwood City, and challenge the Cianwood Gym.

Or they could head directly south, first reach Goldenrod City and challenge the Goldenrod Gym, then continue southeast to Azalea Town and challenge the Azalea Gym.

Another choice...

Only those three Gyms remained. Once Ethan earned three more badges, he could enter the Silver Conference. Regardless of which direction they chose, he would need to challenge all three. The only question was their order.

Rather than waste time thinking about it, Ethan handed the decision to Erika and let her choose their route.

Erika hesitated briefly before settling on Cianwood City.

"Let's go to Cianwood." She gazed toward the distant blue sea and sighed. "We've spent so many days flying through the sky or traveling overland. It would be nice to change our surroundings and relax aboard a ship for once."

"A ship..."

Ethan had no objection. He walked with her toward Olivine's docks. Yet he could not tell whether it was his imagination, because since leaving the Olivine Gym, something about Erika seemed to have changed.

The change was difficult to define.

The clearest sign was that whenever their eyes met, she lowered her head and looked away, unable to hold his gaze!

Chapter 428: The Whirl Cup

Olivine City and Cianwood City were both coastal cities, and they were not particularly far apart, so many ships traveled between them every day.

At the docks, Ethan and Erika easily found a medium-sized passenger ferry bound for Cianwood City.

The ferry did not travel there directly, however. It would first pass through the Whirl Islands and make a brief stop before continuing toward Cianwood City.

The route would undoubtedly take much longer, but it was still their best option at present.

They bought their tickets, boarded the ferry, and found seats on the deck.

The damp, salty sea breeze swept over them. Before long, a tremor ran through the hull, and the ferry slowly pulled out of the harbor.

Ethan took out a Poke Ball and released the Eevee that Naoko had given him in Ecruteak City.

It was clearly Eevee's first time aboard a ship. Bursting with excitement, it found everything novel. One moment it ran to the railing to gaze across the sea; the next, it scampered all over the deck, brimming with energy. Perhaps the motion made it seasick, however, because it had not been running for long before it curled up at Ethan's feet and refused to move again.

The little fellow was obviously seasick!

Ethan shook his head in amusement. Leaving Eevee alone, he turned his gaze toward the sea.

Traveling across the ocean truly was pleasant. After growing accustomed to rushing from place to place, relaxing once in a while felt wonderful. It refreshed the mind and even seemed to slow the passage of time.

He ordered two cocktails from the bar on deck, then drank and chatted with Erika as they enjoyed this rare leisurely journey.

The ferry cut through the sea, leaving two even wakes behind it. But after seeing the same scenery for so long, their interest soon faded.

After more than half an hour at sea, Ethan lounged comfortably in a deck chair and was nearly dozing off from boredom when an elderly man suddenly sat beside them.

At first, the man merely sat there in silence. As the voyage grew dull, however, he appeared to feel lonely and struck up a conversation with them.

The old man spoke with uncommon insight and had his own perspective on many subjects. As a native of the Whirl Islands, he also knew at least a little about every place and event in the area.

For example, he told them about a flock of enormous Pidgey living on the islands. More than three times the size of ordinary Pidgey, they were giants among their kind. Yet precisely because they had grown so large, they had lost the ability to fly.

Pidgey that could not fly?

Had their ability deteriorated?

The strange story surprised them both. Their interest piqued, they began asking the old man more questions.

Through his explanation, Ethan learned that the Whirl Islands did not refer to a single island, but to an entire archipelago.

It consisted of four large islandsBlue Point Isle, Red Rock Isle, Yellow Rock Isle, and Silver Rock Islealong with numerous smaller islands. Together, they formed a spiral. Powerful whirlpools surrounded the archipelago, and the dangerous waters had once made it extremely difficult to approach. Only with the advent of modern ships had people escaped the currents' constraints and allowed the Whirl Islands to flourish.

According to legend, the Whirl Islands had been one enormous island in ancient times. Changes in the earth's crust had split it into the four main islands.

Beneath the surface, a series of dark, maze-like caverns therefore connected the islands. Exploring downward from any island was exceptionally difficult, and rumors even claimed that Lugia could be encountered in the deepest reaches of those tangled caves!

Hearing the old man mention Lugia reminded Ethan of the one known as the God of the Sea that he had encountered in the Orange Islands.

The Lugia here in Johto were clearly different from that one. If Ethan remembered correctly, these were a mother and her childtwo Lugia in total.

Glancing at the Eevee by Ethan's feet, the old man smiled. "Are you two also going to enter the Water-type Pokemon tournament?"

"A Water-type Pokemon tournament?"

Ethan and Erika looked at each other, then shook their heads in confusion. They had never planned to stop at the Whirl Islands, so they had done no research on the area.

"This is the first I've heard of it. What kind of tournament is it?"

"Then you've arrived at exactly the right time!" the old man said eagerly. "It's held in Inland City on Blue Point Isle once every three years, specifically for Trainers who use Water-type Pokemon. The winner receives a generous cash prize and becomes famous overnight! As Trainers, you simply can't miss an event like this!"

Ethan did not care about becoming famous, but that generous cash prize the man mentioned...

His funds still felt far too meager. If there was money to be made, this tournament suddenly became much more appealing!

At the thought, he glanced at Erika.

She saw the eagerness in his eyes.

"Then you should enter." She smiled softly. "A tournament like this is certain to draw many skilled competitors. It will be excellent training for your Pokemon too!"

Ethan nodded and asked, "Will you enter?"

"I'm a Grass-type Trainer!" Erika shook her head gently. "I don't have any Water-type Pokemon with me for a tournament like this!"

At three that afternoon, the ferry arrived at the port of Inland City on Blue Point Isle. It was the most prosperous city in the Whirl Islands and the archipelago's capital.

Under their original plan, the pair would have remained aboard and continued to Cianwood City. Now that Ethan had made the Water-type tournament his new objective, however, they disembarked here instead.

Only after leaving the docks and entering the city did they realize just how lively it was!

The tournament had drawn vast numbers of Trainers and spectators from far away. All that activity brought them considerable trouble as well.

Ethan first went to the local Pokemon Center and registered for the preliminary round. Just as he was about to arrange a room there, Nurse Joy informed him that every room was already occupied by Trainers.

With no other choice, they left the Pokemon Center and tried several nearby hotels and inns, only to find every one completely full.

With so many visitors pouring in, the entire city was probably the same.

In the end, Ethan simply booked an expensive, upscale suite at the hotel closest to the tournament venue.

Perhaps because the rate was so high, one such room was still available. But that meant the unmarried man and woman would inevitably be spending the night alone together!

A peculiar atmosphere settled between them.

Since beginning their journey, the two had never even shared a tent in the wilderness. If they had, this might have felt less awkward. Instead, they had skipped straight to this step, and it felt uncomfortably like a couple checking into a hotel together!

Chapter 429: The Preliminary Round

Since it was still early, the pair did not rest at the hotel. Instead, they decided to visit the venue, familiarize themselves with the surroundings, and learn more about the tournament in advance.

The Whirl Cup was divided into preliminary and main rounds. The entrants would first compete in three preliminary matches tomorrow, narrowing the field to sixty-four Trainers. Those sixty-four would then proceed through several elimination rounds until a final winner emerged.

Hmm. The format did not sound any different from the Indigo League Conference.

However, because no Badges were required to enter, the number of participants was surprisingly large despite this being a local tournament held solely by the Whirl Islands!

When Ethan had lined up to register, fifty or sixty Trainers had already been waiting ahead of him. Not only had local Trainers from the Whirl Islands entered enthusiastically, but people from farther away had also come after hearing the news. It was easy to see how popular the event was.

But because anyone could register without needing Badges, the competitors' skill levels varied wildly. They included everyone from men in their sixties and seventies to children only seven or eight years old!

For these people, how well they performed was beside the point. Participation was what mattered!

And what if they somehow won?

Wouldn't they become famous overnight!?

The pair followed the street toward the tournament grounds.

The preliminary round would take place simultaneously across sixteen battlefields. After registering, Ethan had been informed that he was assigned to Field F.

He had also received a map to keep Trainers from getting lost. It clearly marked the location of every battlefield, a very thoughtful arrangement.

They had barely reached the area containing the venues, before Ethan could even find his own battlefield, when someone suddenly called their names.

"Ethan! Miss Erika!"

Turning around, they found Ash and his friends standing at the entrance to one of the battlefields!

Ash, Misty, and Brock were eating popsicles as they waved to Ethan and Erika.

Those three certainly had sharp eyes. Almost every time their groups met, they were the ones who spotted Ethan first!

Walking over, Ethan laughed. "I knew you wouldn't miss a tournament like this! Of course you'd enter!"

Even so, he felt somewhat emotional.

When the group had parted last time, they had all sensed that they would meet again before long. Ethan simply had not expected it to happen this quickly!

Ash truly was like the chosen child of this world. Perhaps it was ordained by fate: wherever something exciting happened, Ash was sure to appear.

After everyone exchanged greetings, Ethan turned toward Misty.

"Did you enter too?"

"Of course!" Misty puffed out her modest chest. "I'm a Water-type Pokemon Trainer! How could I miss something like this?"

Misty suddenly remembered something and hurriedly asked, "Oh, right, Ethan! Which battlefield were you assigned to?"

"Field F."

"Great! I avoided you!" Misty patted her chest, looking delighted.

Although she was a Gym Leader and aspired to become an outstanding Water-type Pokemon Trainer, she knew her own limits. She understood that she definitely could not defeat Ethan.

Before seeing him, Misty had even wanted to compete with Ash and find out which of them could win the championship. Now that Ethan had appeared, she changed her goal almost immediately.

Hmm... Second place would be pretty good too!

Seeing how relieved she looked, Ethan chuckled. "Don't worry. So many people entered the Whirl Cup that the chances of meeting during the preliminary round are very low."

As Ethan had said, if each entrant needed to win three matches before only sixty-four remained, then more than five hundred people had clearly registered!

That was an enormous number, almost equal to the scale of the Indigo League Conference!

With so many competitors, the chances of encountering one another in the preliminary round were extremely small.

Ash had a different opinion. He gave Misty a disdainful glance. "Misty, don't you have any ambition? How can you admit defeat so easily?"

Then he turned toward Ethan and clenched his fist, his fighting spirit seeming to blaze around him.

"Ethan! Whether we meet in the preliminaries or the main tournament, my goal is to defeat you and become the champion!!"

"Oh? That's the spirit!" Ethan laughed at Ash's display. "Then I'll look forward to it!"

...

That afternoon, Ethan treated everyone to a delicious seafood feast at a nearby restaurant.

He had to admit that Ash and Misty had been quite lucky to secure beds at the Pokemon Center. The place might be crowded and chaotic, but they could gather all kinds of information there, learn the latest developments immediately, and adjust their teams as circumstances changed.

Compared with them, Ethan's accommodations were more comfortable, yet they left him feeling less involved in the tournament.

After they had eaten and drunk their fill, Ethan and Erika said goodbye to Ash's group. When they returned to the hotel that evening, the atmosphere between them once again grew strange.

The suite had two bedrooms and a living room, all luxuriously decorated, so privacy was not a concern. But there was only one bathroom, which meant they had to bathe one after the other. That indistinctly intimate feeling was almost like living with someone of the opposite sex!

Ever the gentleman, Ethan gave Erika the main bedroom. After trying several times and failing to change his mind, she could only accept it.

Perhaps realizing that the atmosphere had become too intimate, Erika's face flushed faintly. She said nothing for the rest of the evening, took the first bath, and retired to her room early.

The bathroom was still filled with steam when Ethan entered, and he almost seemed able to sense Erika's lingering presence.

He, too, felt that something in their relationship had changed, but now was not the time to dwell on it.

After bathing, he lay on his bed with his thoughts entirely occupied by tomorrow's tournament. Before he knew it, he had fallen asleep.

The night passed quietly, without any midnight visit.

At eight the next morning, after breakfast, Ethan and Erika arrived at the preliminary venue early and met up with Ash and the others.

The spectators had already taken their seats, filling the stands on all sides. Although this was only the preliminary round, the tournament took place just once every three years, so the scene remained extraordinarily lively.

Erika and Brock sat together in the stands. One specialized in Grass types and the other in Rock and Ground types, leaving neither with any connection to this tournament. All they could do was serve as the cheering section.

Ceremonial cannons burst repeatedly in the sky, creating an atmosphere that was both festive and chaotic.

Ethan, Ash, and Misty entered the waiting room through the competitors' passage. On the television screens inside, they could watch the Whirl Cup's opening ceremony.

Time passed little by little. As nine o'clock approached, so did the official start of the preliminary round.

When the announcement summoning the competitors sounded through the waiting room, Ethan, Ash, and Misty stacked their hands together, then raised them high.

"Let's do this!"

They lowered their arms and shared a laugh before heading toward their respective battlefields.

Chapter 430: Advancing with Ease

After emerging from the competitors' passage, Ethan headed directly to Field F.

The preliminary battlefields had been set up across a pool inside the Whirl Stadium. The organizers had divided the water into sixteen small squares, where the competitors would battle for the sixty-four places in the main tournament.

Since all sixteen fields shared the same pool, however, the water beneath them was connected. If one match became too intense, the resulting waves could easily affect the competitors nearby.

Fortunately, Ethan and the others had explored the venue yesterday. They understood the conditions on the water and were mentally prepared.

Ethan entered the waiting area and quietly waited for his turn. Two matches were still ahead of his on Field F, so he used the time to glance toward Ash and Misty.

Ash had been assigned to Field A, while Misty was at Field B. Through the layers of competitors, Ethan could just make out Ash waiting for his turn as well. Misty had already begun her match.

The angle prevented him from seeing Misty's opponent, but with her strength, she would certainly be fine as long as she did not encounter anyone too troublesome.

Turning back, Ethan focused on his own battlefield and searched for potential opponents.

The first two matches on Field F ended quickly. After watching them, Ethan could only describe the battles as weaklings flailing at one another.

From his perspective, these people were simply too weak. It was not that none of the competitors showed promise, but the great majority performed below the usual standard.

It appeared this was the greatest drawback of removing the Badge requirement!

A little over ten minutes later, the first two matches were over. At the referee's signal, it was finally Ethan's turn to compete.

He stepped out of the crowd and onto the battlefield. For a moment, every competitor around Field F focused on him.

It was not because there was anything unusual about him. Almost every entrant received the same attention.

After all the experience he had accumulated, Ethan remained perfectly calm beneath so many gazes. He did not grow nervous and uneasy like the first-time competitors beside him.

For Trainers with social anxiety or who simply struggled to interact with others, dozens of eyes staring at them made their hands and feet turn cold and sent nervous sweat trickling down their backs.

The preliminary round used one-on-one rules. Each competitor sent out a single Pokemon, and one match decided the winner. There was no room whatsoever for error.

Ethan's opponent in this match was a boy only seven or eight years old. The child still looked very young, yet showed no stage fright at all. Eagerness filled his face, and he was clearly looking forward to the battle!

They took their positions on opposite sides and faced each other across the water.

Studying his opponent, Ethan stroked his chin.

Which Pokemon should he send out?

At present, he had only three Water-type Pokemon: Blastoise, the enormous red Gyarados, and Suicune.

Hmm...

He considered his options for a moment.

Suicune certainly could not be revealed on an occasion like this. It was not that Ethan refused to use Legendary Pokemon in battle. He simply had not encountered the right opportunity, and bringing Suicune out now would be absurdly excessive. If he ever faced an opponent like that Trainer who used Legendary Pokemon, he could answer in kind, but it would clearly be a long time before he met such a person.

As for his enormous red Gyarados...

Forget it. For one thing, it was far away at Professor Cerise's laboratory, and it was too late to change his team now. For another, Gyarados was simply too ferocious. Whenever possible, Ethan preferred to keep it out of battle. He had no desire to leave the other competitors psychologically scarred.

Having reached his decision, Ethan closed his hand around Blastoise's Poke Ball.

There was no other choice. He would have to rely on Blastoise!

Ethan threw the Poke Ball forward. At the same time, the young boy sent out his own Pokemon.

Blue light flashed, and a Poliwag appeared before Ethan.

Blastoise towered over Poliwag. With one Water-type Pokemon enormous and the other tiny, Blastoise looked down at its opponent and found it difficult to muster any interest, even though Ethan had warned it before the match not to grow careless.

Ethan would have liked to use Dragonair, but the organizers imposed a strict requirement on every Pokemon entering the tournament: each one had to possess the Water type. Dragonair might be capable of living in water, but it did not qualify under the rules.

As soon as the match began, both Trainers ordered their Pokemon to attack.

Poliwag used Water Gun. Blastoise simply endured the minor damage, charged straight up to Poliwag, and finished it with an ordinary Tackle followed by Bite.

The victory was swift and decisive, without the slightest complication.

Blastoise had once helped Ethan win the Indigo League Conference. Bringing a Pokemon like this to a small tournament amounted to a complete massacre.

"How could this happen?"

The young boy watched his Pokemon's eyes turn into spirals as it sank beneath the water. He collapsed onto the ground, unable to believe what he was seeing!

Seeing Poliwag defeated so easily shattered his confidence. All his enthusiasm from before the match vanished, and the loss dealt him an especially heavy blow!

After eliminating his first opponent, Ethan won his second and third matches just as easily.

Because every participating Pokemon shared the Water type, the Water-type moves they ordinarily relied upon were greatly weakened. They had to depend on attacks of other types instead, giving a tremendous advantage to tough Pokemon with thick hides and defensive options.

When all three matches ended, Ethan had secured his place in the main tournament. Upon returning to the waiting room, he found Ash and Misty arriving together.

They looked relaxed and chatted cheerfully along the way, clearly having advanced as well.

"How did it go? Everything went smoothly?" Ethan asked.

Ash flashed him an okay sign. "It was way too easy. There wasn't even a decent opponent!"

Misty nodded in complete agreement. "It really was easy. It wasn't what I imagined at all. I thought we'd meet stronger competitors!"

All three had performed normally, and none had suffered an unexpected upset. They had taken a successful first step, leaving everyone delighted. Now all they had to do was wait for tomorrow's main tournament.

After leaving the stadium, they met up with Erika and Brock. The two had watched every one of their matches from the stands and naturally knew the results perfectly well. When the competitors returned, another round of congratulations inevitably followed.

To reward everyone for their excellent performances, Ethan took them to another restaurant and treated them to a feast of grilled meat!

Chapter 431: The Sea Priestess

The venue for the Whirl Cup's main tournament was different from the preliminary grounds. It was a vast, circular aquatic colosseum built in a distinctly ancient Greek style. No one knew how many years its every brick and stone had endured, giving the entire structure a profound sense of history.

The colosseum could hold twenty thousand spectators. Flowing seawater filled its center, and more than a dozen stone pillars of varying heights and sizes rose above the surface, providing places for both Trainers and Pokemon to stand.

Compared with the perfunctory preliminaries, the opening ceremony for the main tournament was undoubtedly grander. Fireworks and ceremonial cannons sounded in unison, while an elegant and beautiful priestess holding a scepter presided over the event!

By nine in the morning, not a single seat remained empty. Countless spectators had arrived early and were waiting in eager anticipation.

Ethan, Ash, Misty, and the other sixty-one competitors entered the colosseum across the sea aboard more than a dozen long, narrow wooden boats. As the surrounding crowd cheered and encouraged them, the competitors stood straight and did their best to present themselves with energy and confidence.

The audience greeted them with thunderous applause and cheers.

Amid that atmosphere, the male announcer's deep, clear voice began echoing over the colosseum, signaling the official beginning of the opening ceremony!

"Ladies and gentlemen, look! These are the competitors who survived the preliminary round of this triennial tournament and now strive to become a Sea Hero! Since ancient times, the Whirl Islands have possessed their own distinct culture and civilization. We revere Water-type Pokemon and have lived alongside them to this very day! That culture has never disappeared, and Maya, the Sea Priestess who has protected these traditions since antiquity, continues to pass it on!"

Ethan had only learned after becoming an official competitor last night that the Whirl Cup was more than a Pokemon tournament. In keeping with an ancient tradition, it would also choose a Sea Hero to participate in this ceremony!

As he listened to the introduction, Ethan turned once more toward the ceremonial platform in the distance.

It was not very far away, so he could see the priestess clearly. She wore a long blue dress and carried a golden scepter. Her long purple hair drifted gently in the wind. Even without considering her features, her bearing alone was already noble and elegant.

Ethan had already experienced a ceremony like this once on Shamouti Island in the Orange Islands, where he had also met the local festival maiden. This spectacle therefore did not feel particularly unfamiliar.

It's only a formality, he thought.

When Ash and Misty beside him noticed Ethan turn his head, they followed his gaze and also saw the Sea Priestess.

Misty pressed both hands to her cheeks, filled with envy. "She's so beautiful!"

Ethan could not tell whether she envied the priestess's elegance, the attention of the enormous crowd, or something else entirely.

The Sea Priestess truly was beautiful, but Misty had always considered herself the world's most beautiful girl. She was certainly no ugly duckling. She was simply still young and had not yet fully grown into her looks. When she reached the priestess's age, Ethan believed she would be every bit as striking.

At that moment, the announcer spoke again. "And now, please welcome Sea Priestess Maya for the tournament declaration!"

As his voice faded, Maya stepped forward. She raised her scepter and declared loudly, "Everyone, the triennial celebration of Water-type Pokemon has begun. On behalf of the Whirl Islands, I welcome you all! Here, we live in harmony with Water-type Pokemon and understand their hearts. Since ancient times, those who mastered the sea alongside their Pokemon have been celebrated as Sea Heroes, and every Sea Hero receives the blessing of the Sea Spirit, granting them the ability to understand the hearts of all Water-type Pokemon!"

The Sea Spirit? Understanding their hearts?

Ethan's gaze shifted to the scepter in Maya's hand.

The scepter was made of pure gold and gleamed beneath the sunlight. At its tip sat a round blue gemstone the size of a fist. The gem radiated blue light and was clearly no ordinary object.

"And so, I wish every competitor success and the chance to receive the blessing of the Sea Spirit!"

As Maya raised the scepter high, the Sea Spirit erupted with dazzling light. The glow was gentle rather than blinding, and it enveloped the entire colosseum!

Ethan and all the others seeing such a phenomenon for the first time stared in surprise.

So this was the Sea Spirit...

The light fell across Ethan and painted everyone pale blue. It produced no other visible effect, but even Ethan could not tell whether it was merely stagecraft or the blue gemstone truly possessed some wondrous power!

This world was far from ordinary, after all. It would hardly be strange if blessings like this genuinely existed.

At the very least, judging from the audience's increasingly excited and fervent reaction, they seemed to believe the competitors in the colosseum had already become somehow extraordinary!

Behind Ethan, Ash raised both hands and stared at the blue light upon them. "Did we really receive a blessing?" he murmured.

"Are you an idiot?" Misty rolled her eyes at him. "Didn't the priestess just say that only the final Sea Hero receives the blessing? This light is only a demonstration of that gemstone's power!"

"Huh? Is that how it works?" Only then did Ash fully understand the rules. He sighed in disappointment. "Aw, man. I like the title of Sea Hero, but it's only an empty title. If you win the tournament, don't you get anything else?"

Misty sighed helplessly. "Come on! Did you even read the tournament schedule beforehand? After the final, the winner receives a generous cash prize along with the titleand even a Mystic Water pendant! That's the real reward. But... hmph! None of it has anything to do with you. Ethan is definitely going to win!"

Misty was Ethan's most devoted supporter. Whenever he entered a tournament or battle, she backed him blindly and without hesitation!

Faced with Misty's extravagant praise and her relentless temptation of fate on his behalf, Ethan could only smile and shake his head.

He did not stop her, however. Winning was his goal as well. Now that he had entered, he intended to become the champion. What kind of Trainer competed without wanting to win?

Ash also knew how powerful Ethan was, but he naturally refused to accept Misty belittling him. Fuming, he began arguing with her.

As Ethan listened to the two bickering behind him, his thoughts returned to the Mystic Water.

Just as Misty had said, the winner would receive a Mystic Water in addition to the prize money. It was a wondrous stone that strengthened a Pokemon's Water-type moves when worn, making it a genuinely valuable reward!

Chapter 432: Ash's Iconic Moment

After the opening ceremony ended, the competitors were given a brief rest to make their final preparations. With the spectators waiting eagerly, the tournament soon began in earnest.

Today's matches formed an elimination tournament, but they would not immediately determine the champion. The sixty-four competitors would first pass through one round after another until only four remained. Tomorrow morning, those four would be reduced to two finalists, who would then battle for the Whirl Cup championship.

Erika and Brock once again sat in the stands, unable to cheer for the others from nearby. Since they had bought their tickets so late, they were forced to sit in the farthest section.

As in the preliminaries, each Trainer could use only one Pokemon during an elimination match. This forced the competitors to bring out their strongest Pokemon in peak condition. Although the format could not reveal the full extent of a Trainer's abilities, it greatly accelerated the tournament. A winner could be crowned in only two days.

That might be unfavorable for local tourism, but it suited Ethan and his friends perfectly. The tournament would not delay their journey.

Of the three, Ash was the first to battle. His opponent was a boy even younger than him who carried a fishing rod. For his opening match, Ash sent out Totodile. The other boy flicked his fishing rod, casting a Poke Ball over the water. When it opened, a Kingdra appeared above the surface.

Since their own matches had not yet begun, Ethan and Misty watched from the competitors' waiting area and focused their attention on Ash's battle.

In terms of typing, Totodile was purely Water type, while Kingdra was both Water and Dragon type. Kingdra had a fourfold resistance to Water, rendering Totodile's Water-type moves all but useless. Kingdra's Dragon-type attacks, by contrast, remained completely effective.

The matchup appeared extremely unfavorable for Ash, but as a master of battling at a type disadvantage, he had long since grown accustomed to such situations and paid it no mind.

As soon as the match began, Totodile dove into the water. Kingdra immediately used Twister beneath the surface. As its body spun faster and faster, it created an enormous vortex reaching between sea and sky, sweeping Totodile inside!

Totodile's body whirled around in midair with the current, unable to break free. Fortunately, the younger boy eventually ordered Kingdra to stop Twister, finally allowing Totodile to escape.

Kingdra's assault was not over. As Totodile fell, Kingdra fired a Water Gun directly at it.

Totodile twisted its body in midair and narrowly avoided the attack.

Totodile had been suppressed from their very first exchange. The sight poured cold water over Ash's confidence and made him abandon any thought of underestimating his opponent!

He had expected to sweep through the tournament just as he had in the preliminaries and charge all the way to the final. He had never imagined his first opponent would already be this strong!

The battle continued. The two Pokemon fought from the stone pillars into the water, where Kingdra expelled a thick cloud of ink. The ink polluted the seawater and blocked Totodile's vision. Unable to tell what Kingdra was planning, Totodile could only climb back onto a pillar and wait for it to reappear.

The black ink spread through the water, staining a vast area and making it impossible to see below the surface. Hidden from view, Kingdra waited like a hunter for Totodile to expose an opening.

Misty immediately frowned at the situation.

"Are all the opponents in the elimination rounds this powerful? They're on a completely different level from the preliminary competitors!"

Ethan shook his head noncommittally. "I wouldn't put it that way. Ash was simply unlucky to meet an opponent like this in his first match. LookKingdra is in its final evolutionary stage, so its physical abilities already surpass Totodile's by a considerable margin. It's also been raised quite well, and its tactics are sound. There's a reason Ash is struggling."

Misty fell quiet as she looked at the boy several years younger than Ash.

Seeing Ash unexpectedly drawn into a difficult battle gave her a sense of danger as well. She no longer dared to be careless in the slightest.

The battle had now reached a stalemate. The boy seemed intent on wearing down Ash's patience and waiting for him to expose an opening. Fortunately, Ash's Totodile was too carefree to worry about any of that. With its simple, happy nature, it began dancing for its own amusement!

Its mischievous, adorable behavior swept away the tense atmosphere and sent the audience into peals of laughter!

The other boy was still young, after all. Now he was the one who lost patience. Feeling that Totodile was looking down on him, he hurriedly ordered Kingdra to surface and attack with Hydro Pump.

Kingdra's belly swelled larger and larger. Totodile realized what was happening, leaped toward it, and created an instantly iconic scene!

Totodile opened its enormous mouth and bit down on Kingdra's long snout. In an instant, the Hydro Pump building inside Kingdra was trapped in its mouth!

The water Kingdra was about to unleash continued to swell its belly, inflating it like a water balloon!

The sudden turn of events left the boy frozen in place. With so little experience, how could he ever have encountered an opponent who refused to follow common sense?

He was not alone. Even the audience stared in astonishment at such a bizarre maneuver!

Kingdra continued to swell until Ash finally ordered Totodile to release its mouth. The water inside Kingdra found an outlet and erupted in a high-pressure jet. Like a punctured water balloon, Kingdra spun through the air and shot high above the battlefield!

Pfft, pfft, pfft...

Perhaps the water pressure was too powerful, or perhaps there was simply too much water. Kingdra left a blue afterimage in the sky, moving too quickly for the human eye to follow!

It spun more than a dozen times high overhead. Only after expelling the last mouthful of water did it plummet headfirst into the pool!

Splash!

Kingdra struck the water and threw up an enormous spray. Several seconds later, it floated back to the surface, unconscious and with its eyes rolled back!

It had clearly fainted completely!

The referee needed only one glance before announcing the result.

To be honest, Ethan had expected Ash to win before the match began, but he had never imagined victory would come this way.

Ethan knew perfectly well that Ash was the sort of person who won through the unexpected, yet he still managed to find fresh ways to surprise him!

The entertaining spectacle sent the audience into roaring laughter and completely reshaped their understanding of what could happen in a battle.

Of course, one person's joy was not another's. The younger boy watched himself lose in such a ridiculous fashion and felt as though his entire understanding of the world had collapsed!

In the waiting area, Ethan and Misty applauded along with the crowd.

Looking back over the match, Totodile had not actually inflicted any damage on Kingdra aside from biting its snout. Ultimately, Kingdra had been defeated by its own Hydro Pump!

Chapter 433: An Overwhelming Victory

After Ash's match ended, it was Ethan's turn to take the field.

His expression remained unchanged. Having already competed in two major tournaments, he could face a scene like this without the slightest disturbance. He emerged from the competitors' passage at a calm pace. At the opposite end of the field, his opponent was clearly attending such an event for the first time and looked far more constrained. The Trainer could only stare at the path ahead, too nervous even to raise his head and look around.

As usual, the announcer gave a brief introduction when the two competitors entered, allowing the spectators to learn a little about them.

The introduction of Ethan's opponent proceeded normally, but when the announcer turned to Ethan, there was a noticeable pause.

Two seconds later, the announcer continued in a slightly startled voice. "Oh? I've just received word that our competitor Ethan is no ordinary Trainer. He's the champion of this year's Indigo League Conference and an Honorable Trainer of the Orange League! Who would have thought our Whirl Cup could attract a competitor of such distinction?"

The Indigo League Conference champion?

An Honorable Trainer of the Orange League?

The spectators immediately became restless.

The Orange League title was one thing. Although the Orange Islands surpassed the Whirl Islands in their number of islands, economy, and population, their competition still belonged to a minor League. Its title did not carry enough weight, and its international standing was only slightly above that of a local tournament like the Whirl Cup.

But the Indigo League Conference champion was entirely different!

That was a true League Conference, almost equal to the Silver Conference in both scale and level of competition. It demanded their attention!

Every spectator craned their neck to look at Ethan. Even Maya, the Sea Priestess seated in the ceremonial section, turned toward him in surprise.

They could hardly believe that a League Conference champion had come to compete in a local cup tournament!

With a smile on his face, Ethan waved to the spectators and walked unhurriedly into the Trainer's command area. His opponent had already been timid, and when he heard that he would be battling a champion, his eyelids began twitching involuntarily!

He swallowed and forced himself to look up at Ethan. The other Trainer was not only handsome, but calm and assured in every gesture. What little confidence the boy possessed immediately evaporated.

How am I supposed to fight someone like this...?

At the same time, Ethan studied his opponent.

The boy was plump and appeared to be fifteen or sixteen. Tension and awkwardness were plainly visible on his face. Judging from his condition, he was even less composed than the six- or seven-year-old boy who had battled Ash!

Ethan did not underestimate him because of that. With a few lucky exceptions, anyone who had emerged from the preliminary round had to possess at least some ability.

Once both Trainers were ready, the referee gave the signal, and they sent out their Pokemon simultaneously.

With no other choice available, Ethan used Blastoise. The other boy sent out a Corsola.

Corsola was primarily pink, with four branching horns growing from its back. It was a common Pokemon along seashores.

The two Pokemon stood atop their respective stone pillars and stared at one another.

The announcer was clearly paying close attention to Ethan. When Blastoise appeared, the rapid rustling of papers could even be heard over the loudspeakers.

After several seconds, the announcer explained, "According to our records, Ethan's Blastoise was among the Pokemon he caught early in his journey. It accompanied him all the way to the Indigo League Conference final and is one of his ace Pokemon! I never expected him to send it out already. Is he determined to eliminate every possible risk and ensure his advancement?"

Although records about Ethan were available, the announcer clearly did not know him well enough. Blastoise currently ranked only among Ethan's second-string Pokemon, yet the man had mistaken it for one of his aces.

By ordinary reasoning, however, the assumption was understandable. The earlier a Pokemon joined a Trainer, the longer they spent together and the more battles it experienced. Such Pokemon often grew quickly, earned the Trainer's trust, and were consequently trained as aces.

The battlefield used for this tournament was spacious: a perfectly circular pool four times the size of an ordinary field. High walls surrounded it, removing any concern about leaving the boundaries and giving Water-type Pokemon ample room to display their abilities.

At that moment, the referee gave the command, and the match officially began.

Every spectator focused on the battlefield. They all wanted to see what this champion was capable of.

Unfortunately, although Corsola appeared far more steadfast and reliable than its Trainer, it was clearly no match for Blastoise and could not force it to use its full strength.

The battle was completely one-sided and presented Ethan with no difficulty whatsoever.

Corsola barely endured several exchanges before Blastoise hoisted it high into the air and slammed it heavily onto a stone pillar, knocking it completely unconscious.

The spectators were somewhat disappointed by the result, but it only made them anticipate Ethan's later matches even more.

Amid their cheers, Ethan calmly left the battlefield and headed toward the competitors' passage. His expression was as relaxed as it had been when he entered.

After successfully advancing to the round of thirty-two, he would battle again at three that afternoon. Another victory would place him in the round of sixteen and allow him to continue his championship run tomorrow. Until then, he could rest in the waiting room and await the result of Misty's match.

Misty was scheduled immediately after him in the ninth match of the morning. The timetable was so tight that Ethan had not even reached the waiting room to wish her luck before she entered the battlefield.

Inside, Ethan joined Ash, and the two began watching Misty's match together.

Her battle had already begun.

Her opponent was a middle-aged man in a straw hat named Harrison.

Harrison's clothing made him look rather like a pirate. As for their Pokemon, Harrison sent out a Qwilfish, while Misty, for reasons of her own, surprisingly chose a Corsola as well!

However...

The spectators did not think much of Corsola.

One of the species had just been defeated with ease by Ethan. Although this was a different Corsola, the audience still had a poor impression of it.

Fortunately, compared with the somewhat unkempt middle-aged Harrison, Misty's image as a beautiful young girl still inspired many spectators to cheer for her.

After watching Ash and Ethan's matches, Misty's fighting spirit was burning brightly, so she launched the first attack.

Perhaps because his opponent was a cute young girl, Harrison wore a dismissive expression. He clearly did not take Misty seriously and believed he would advance with ease!

Chapter 434: A Battle Full of Surprises

Harrison would naturally pay a heavy price for looking down on Misty.

Under Harrison's command, Qwilfish first dodged Corsola's attack, then countered with Water Gun. Misty immediately used Mirror Coat, reflecting the Water Gun straight back!

The attack retraced its path and struck Qwilfish, causing damage to the Pokemon that had fired it.

Misty's timing with Mirror Coat could only be called perfect. She used it at the very instant the attack landed, leaving Harrison no time to react.

The reversal took Harrison completely by surprise, and he hurriedly checked his Pokemon's condition. Fortunately, because Water Gun shared Qwilfish's type, it had not inflicted any serious injuries.

Although Harrison was somewhat startled, he still did not take Misty seriously. He assumed she had merely succeeded through luck and promptly launched a second attack.

Qwilfish opened its mouth and began frantically drawing in seawater. Its body continuously expanded until it resembled a spiny ball.

Ethan recognized the technique at a glance. This was a method of strengthening Pin Missile, a charged attack.

Using the water inside its body to increase the pressure would launch the needles faster and with greater force, preventing the opponent from defending effectively.

This was Ethan's first time seeing such a technique. It broadened his horizons and allowed him to learn something from Harrison.

He had to admit that middle age brought experience. Someone like Harrison might not be especially powerful, but after so many years as a Trainer, he had certainly not wasted his time. People like him generally possessed one or two special techniques.

Facing such an attack, Misty rapidly considered her options.

Mirror Coat could not reflect Pin Missile, so she neither repeated the same tactic nor sent Corsola into the water to evade it. Instead, she chose to meet it head-on with Spike Cannon.

The choice was extremely appropriate. Spike Cannon attacked in much the same fashion as Pin Missile, and its unbroken stream of projectiles could offset Pin Missile's advantage in speed.

White light shone from both Pokemon simultaneously. A moment later, the two similar moves launched at nearly the same time.

Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!

Countless needles and spikes of energy streaked toward one another. The strengthened Pin Missile was clearly faster, crossing the air in an instant. It finally collided with Spike Cannon above a point closer to Misty, producing a chain of explosions!

The resulting shock wave knocked Corsola over. Harrison had anticipated this outcome and ordered Qwilfish to dive beneath the water beforehand, allowing it to avoid the blast.

The lingering force and smoke slowly dissipated.

Before Corsola could rise, Harrison decisively ordered Qwilfish to use Tackle, intending to press his advantage and finish Corsola in one stroke.

Even through the screen, Ethan could see a trace of a triumphant smile on Harrison's face!
