Then, to everyone's astonishment, Corsola happened to rise just as Qwilfish leaped in front of it, turning its body toward the oncoming Pokemon. In the next instant, Qwilfish became wedged between the four horns on Corsola's back!

The force of the impact lodged it firmly in place, leaving it completely unable to move!

The sudden turn of events brought stunned expressions to every spectator's face and froze Harrison's smile where it was!

On the battlefield, Corsola was naturally uncomfortable with another Pokemon embedded in its back. Top-heavy, it paced awkwardly in place and tried to shake Qwilfish loose, but Qwilfish's spines were tangled between its horns and would not come free.

Qwilfish struggled desperately as well, but it could not exert any strength!

The two Pokemon remained locked in place!

Everyone stared at the scene in amazement!

After Totodile had bitten down on Kingdra's snout only a short while ago, they never imagined they would witness another moment this dramatic!

Misty remained dazed for a moment before realizing this was an opportunity that might never come again. She ordered Corsola to use Spike Cannon once more.

White light flared around Corsola. Unable to counterattack or evade, Qwilfish took the attack at full force!

The impact of Spike Cannon finally tore Qwilfish free and launched it into the air. After enduring the attack directly, it flew for several seconds before slamming heavily onto a stone pillar and falling unconscious!

The moment Qwilfish lost the ability to battle, the referee announced the result.

Misty jumped for joy, while Harrison's face fell. He had never imagined he would lose the match in such a fashion!

The spectators applauded, and Misty waved to them with a radiant smile.

In the waiting room, seeing Misty win this way left Ethan lost in thought.

Just like Ash's match, he had never expected both of their battles to end with such dramatic accidents!

It felt as though neither had displayed much of their true strength. Both had won through sheer happenstance.

As the foremost Trainer of unpredictability, Ash maintaining this style was nothing unusual. But now even Misty was fighting this way. She seemed to be growing more and more like Ash.

Regardless of the circumstances, all three had advanced to the round of thirty-two, which was certainly cause for celebration. As for the process... Well... It did not really matter.

After each of them completed one match, none had any more battles that morning. Once Misty returned, the three left the waiting room and headed into the concourse to meet Erika and Brock.

Erika and Brock naturally showered them with praise. Ash and Misty's matches had been especially entertaining, so the pair discussed them with great enthusiasm. Their vivid descriptions of the crowd's excited reactions left both Trainers rather embarrassed.

The group ate lunch at a restaurant inside the colosseum, then rested for a while. Once every morning match had ended, the field of thirty-two was complete. Following an announcement over the loudspeakers, Ethan, Ash, and Misty hurried back to the battlefield for the round of thirty-two.

Once again, luck kept the three from being paired against one another. This time, Ash and Misty displayed the strength expected of them, defeating their opponents through ability and successfully advancing.

The two were delighted, but the spectators were somewhat disappointed.

Compared with ordinary battles, the audience actually preferred seeing something more "exciting"!

As for Ethan, there were no surprises.

He continued using Blastoise, which performed as steadily as ever. With a substantial advantage, it defeated a female Trainer and carried Ethan into the round of sixteen.

Thus, Ethan, Ash, and Misty all successfully reached the final sixteen. From this point onward, with the weaker competitors eliminated, none of their remaining opponents would be easy. The difficulty would undoubtedly rise sharply!

Chapter 435: Psyduck: Let Me Show Everyone My Special Trick!

After a night's rest, the third morning of the tournament arrived in the blink of an eye.

Today's waiting room was no longer crowded like it had been during the previous two days. With most of the competitors eliminated, the entire room felt empty. Aside from Ethan's group, everyone who remained seemed preoccupied. Even their voices had unconsciously grown much quieter.

Advancing this far brought both pressure and anticipation for the future.

They had already reached the final sixteen. With just a little more effort, any one of them might become the Sea Hero and obtain both fame and fortune. How could they avoid feeling excited and anxious?

All the remaining competitors had one thing in common: ever since learning that Ethan was the Indigo League Conference champion, they kept their distance. No one attempted to speak with him. Instead, they merely sent cold looks his way from time to time!

Their hostility was almost visible. They had clearly identified Ethan as their greatest rival!

Ethan did not care in the slightest and continued laughing and chatting with Ash and Misty.

Ash and Misty's good mood disappeared the instant the pairings were announced.

When the Whirl Cup staff posted the bracket on the wall, the three went to look and discovered that Ash and Misty would face each other in the very next match!

Their expressions immediately froze!

What terrible luck.

If given a choice, both would have preferred to battle their friend after achieving a better result, rather than eliminating one another as early as the round of sixteen.

It could only be called a trick of fate, one that had played an enormous joke on them.

Their feelings were complicated. This meant one of them was certain to be eliminated.

Statistically, however, there was no avoiding it. Even if Ash and Misty had not been paired together, either one still had a chance of facing Ethan. A meeting between them was almost inevitable.

Ethan stepped in to smooth things over.

Fortunately, after a brief moment of shock, the two quickly adjusted and became filled with fighting spirit.

Once they returned to normal, Ethan turned his attention to his own opponent. During the break, he looked up recordings of the Trainer's previous two matches online and gained a general understanding of what to expect.

His opponent had used two different Pokemon in those battles, but neither was particularly strong. This was the sort of competitor who had advanced only with great difficulty.

Even so, Ethan's personality would never allow him to grow careless.

Ash and Misty's battle was the second match of the morning. Once the two Trainers in the opening match determined a winner, their turn soon arrived.

After wishing them both luck, Ethan sat on a sofa in the waiting room and watched the live broadcast on the large screen.

The rules changed for the round of sixteen. Each Trainer could now use two Pokemon. This not only provided room to recover from a mistake, but also allowed the Trainers to display their abilities more fully.

Amid the crowd's cheers, the match officially began.

The atmosphere inside the colosseum made it obvious that the spectators were even more enthusiastic today.

As the field continued to shrink, the remaining competitors naturally became more skilled, making the battles increasingly exciting and professional. That was why the audience was so supportive.

Drawing back from his thoughts, Ethan focused on the battlefield again.

Although neither wanted to face a friend, Ash and Misty became completely serious once the match began. Neither showed the slightest intention of holding back.

When the time came to strike, they would show no mercy!

For the first battle, Ash sent out Totodile, while Misty chose her Poliwhirl.

Both Pokemon had defeated their opponents through unexpected accidents in yesterday's opening matches. Their condition had improved greatly in their second matches, where they eliminated their opponents through genuine strength.

Sending them out again today showed that both Trainers had considerable confidence in them!

The first battle lived up to their expectations. The two Pokemon fought fiercely and injured each other as the struggle continued. After a long exchange, Poliwhirl finally dove underwater, approached Totodile, and used Double Slap to knock it unconscious, putting Misty at match point.

It was not that Totodile had performed poorly. Poliwhirl had simply fought even better!

Now behind in the match, Ash confidently sent out Kingler.

Ethan remembered this Pokemon vividly. It had performed brilliantly during the Indigo League Conference, single-handedly sweeping three opponents and helping Ash win several matches in a row!

Misty also knew Kingler could not be underestimated, but she did not change Pokemon. Instead, she kept Poliwhirl in to face it.

When the battle began, Kingler immediately struck the surface with Crabhammer. Incredibly, the attack churned the water across the entire battlefield and created four enormous whirlpools!

The four vortices violently stirred the surface. Caught by the current, Poliwhirl could only drift helplessly across the water at high speed!

Seeing that single attack, Ethan had only one thought: what ridiculous strength!

Creating whirlpools that powerful with one blow defied all reason!

Kingler rarely traveled with Ash. He remembered it only when entering tournaments, while it normally remained with Professor Oak. For it to possess such strength despite that arrangement meant it had grown exceptionally well!

Ethan remembered that back on Earth, faced with all the unreasonable things Kingler could do, many viewers had jokingly credited Professor Oak. They claimed the professor had secretly given Ash's Pokemon private training and raised Kingler and the others to such an extraordinary level.

Of course, anyone who thought about it knew that was only a joke.

As a highly respected Pokemon Professor, Professor Oak had countless matters to handle every day. How could he possibly have time to train Pokemon?

On the battlefield, Kingler easily defeated Poliwhirl with that technique, tying the score at one to one.

For the third battle, Misty took out a Poke Ball and intended to use Corsola. Somehow, Psyduck once againand again, and yet againcame out on its own instead!

No one knew how many times it had ignored Misty's instructions and decided to battle without permission!

The funniest part was that the moment Psyduck appeared, it immediately performed a special trick for everyone!

After falling into the water, it flailed as though it were drowning and even swallowed several mouthfuls of seawater!

The sight delighted the audience. Who could have imagined that a Water-type Pokemon would not know how to swim?!

Fortunately, after thrashing around for quite some time, Psyduck finally managed to climb onto a stone pillar. At least it had avoided drowning itself.

Most crucially, the broadcast director chose that exact moment to switch the camera to Misty.

Every spectator received a clear view of her face, flushed bright red with embarrassment because of Psyduck's behavior!

Chapter 436: Ash Suffers an Upset

Ash's face lit up when Psyduck entered the battle. Delighted, and seemingly afraid that Misty might change her mind, he hurriedly ordered Kingler to attack.

Kingler moved sideways across the water and charged rapidly toward Psyduck.

Perhaps Psyduck had struggled in the water for too long, or perhaps Kingler's momentum was simply too frightening. Whatever the reason, Psyduck appeared to have lost its will to fight. It crouched trembling on the stone pillar with its head bowed, leaving its enormous head completely exposed to Kingler.

Ash naturally would not let such an opportunity pass.

When Kingler reached Psyduck, Ash did not hesitate. He ordered it to raise its oversized pincer, clamp down on Psyduck's vacant-looking head, and lift the duck's entire body high into the air!

As the pincer continued squeezing, Psyduck writhed in unbearable pain, its plump body twisting back and forth. The spectators felt sorry for it, yet could not help finding the sight a little amusing.

Everyone was thinking the same thing. Psyduck could not swim and showed no desire to battle. Had Misty truly sent it out for any reason other than comic relief?

The spectators knew nothing about Psyduck's circumstances. Only Ethan, along with Brock in the stands, shook his head helplessly at the sight.

Of all the places Kingler could have squeezed, why did it have to choose Psyduck's head...?

Ash truly had let his success go to his head...

Had he still not remembered that the worse Psyduck's headache became, the more overwhelming its power would grow?

Sure enough, once the pain became intolerable, faint blue light suddenly shone around Psyduck's body.

Only then did Ash belatedly realize what was happening. As unpleasant memories surfaced, his expression changed dramatically, and he hurriedly ordered Kingler to release its grip.

But it was already far too late to do anything.

In an instant, a shock wave of psychic force erupted with Psyduck at its center. Before Kingler could react, the blast engulfed it and sent it hurtling away!

Kingler continued flying backward until it crashed into Ash.

The impact sent Ash and Kingler tumbling together. When Ash finally climbed to his feet and looked down, he found spirals in Kingler's eyes. It had fainted outright!

The referee raised a colored flag and announced the result. The spectators stared in shock. They had never imagined that the Psyduck which had just embarrassed itself could possess such tremendous power!

Had it been concealing its strength all along?

In the waiting room, Ethan also looked slightly surprised to see that Misty had won.

To be honest, before the match began, he had believed Ash would ultimately emerge victorious, no matter how many twists and turns the battle took. Even after Psyduck entered the field, he still thought Ash would have the last laugh.

He truly had not expected Misty to win!

Psyduck's ability was simply too overpowered. By coming out without permission, it completely changed the course of the match and accidentally handed Misty the victory.

After losing to Misty, Ash looked utterly dejected and deeply frustrated. He formed a stark contrast with Misty, who clutched Psyduck and bounced around in excitement.

Ethan looked away from the screen and rose to his feet. Leaving the two of them behind, he prepared for his own match.

His battle would begin immediately after Ash and Misty's. Although he trusted that his Pokemon would never lose, he did not dare become careless.

Fortunately, because the permitted team size had changed, he had arranged last night for his enormous red Gyarados to be transferred from Cerise Park.

With that great terror in reserve, Ethan would dare battle even Lugia or Kyogre using Gyarados alone! In a local cup tournament like this, it could practically crush entire teams singlehandedly!

As he walked through the competitors' passage, Ethan recalled his video call with Chloe the previous evening, when he had asked her to return Gyarados.

When Chloe learned that he might use Gyarados in the tournament, her mouth dropped open in shock!

The enormous red Gyarados projected an overwhelming presence inside Cerise Park. Even when it lay motionless in the water, its intimidating aura kept Professor Cerise and the others from daring to take a single step closer!

Even the two assistants, Ren and Parker, could feel its predatory gaze when they watched from far away!

Of everyone at the laboratory, only Chloe firmly believed that none of Ethan's Pokemon would hurt her. That faith allowed her to approach Gyarados without fear.

Even without seeing it fight in person, the dominating presence Gyarados radiated was enough for Chloe to imagine how savage it would become in battle.

Thus, while shocked that Ethan was taking Gyarados back, she also observed a moment of silence for his opponents.

Of course, as far as Ethan was concerned, Blastoise alone was sufficient for ordinary circumstances. Gyarados probably would not need to appear anytime soon.

When Ethan entered the colosseum, the audience greeted him with enormous cheers. Even Maya in the ceremonial seating focused her gaze on him.

His swift, decisive victories over the previous two days had already won over a large group of spectators, so quite a few people now supported him.

Ethan could not tell whether it was his imagination, but there seemed to be more security around Maya today. Officer Jenny stood beside her, and more than a dozen guards surrounded the area.

Had something happened?

Before he could think further, Ethan reached the Trainer's command area and stood across the water from his opponent.

This time, his opponent was an elderly man with white hair. He leaned on a cane and could not even straighten his back.

But a sharp light gleamed in the old man's eyes. He was clearly no simple opponent.

Once both Trainers were ready, the referee gave the signal, and they released their Pokemon simultaneously. Ethan sent out the same Blastoise as before, while the old man chose a Tentacruel.

From the recordings he had reviewed, Ethan knew that this Tentacruel was probably the strongest Pokemon the old man had revealed.

Sending it out in the opening round suggested that he intended to seize the momentum and defeat Blastoise immediately.

The strategy was undoubtedly correct. The old man had clearly watched Ethan's previous matches and studied Blastoise's characteristics. Once the battle began, Tentacruel met Blastoise attack for attack, and for a time they fought on equal footing!

But the struggle was ultimately futile. Although Tentacruel caused Ethan some difficulty, Blastoise was still stronger. Under Ethan's direction, it found an opening and finished the opponent with a single decisive strike!

Chapter 437: An Opponent Comes Calling

After Tentacruel was defeated, the old man shook his head helplessly.

That had been his strongest Pokemon. He had never expected it to cause Ethan so little difficulty. The rest of the match would be troublesome...

Before the battle, he had deliberately researched Ethan's team and learned about his even stronger Gyarados. Yet if he could not defeat Blastoise, it appeared his journey through the Whirl Cup would end here.

He was deeply unwilling to accept that. He was already advanced in years and did not know whether he would still be able to compete in the next Whirl Cup. Reaching the final sixteen this time had been his best result across several attempts.

But the gap in strength truly left him in despair. That sense of powerlessness made him understand that Ethan genuinely was different from the other competitors. He was extraordinarily strong!

Really, why would a young man with this much strength enter a tournament like this?

The old man sighed softly. Urged on by the referee, he released his second Pokemon.

Blue light flashed, and a Pokemon resembling an octopus appeared before Ethan.

It was Octillery, a pure Water-type Pokemon. It looked much like an octopus from Earth, with an entirely red body and two suction cups on each tentacle that gave it a slick, slippery appearance.

Octillery generally lived among rocks and caves on the seabed. They had a habit of squeezing into holes and liked remaining in rocky crevices or jars. Sometimes they would suddenly spray ink to escape a powerful enemy or create an opportunity for an ambush.

Despite its soft, squirming appearance, Octillery possessed a hard head. It would bind prey with its tentacles to prevent escape, then ram the victim repeatedly and deliver a final blow once all resistance had ceased.

Facing the old man's second Pokemon, Ethan neither needed nor intended to switch Blastoise. He kept it in the battle.

Given Octillery's size, its tentacles could not wrap around Blastoise's enormous body, rendering that advantage useless.

Fortunately, Octillery knew several Ice-type moves, so it was not completely helpless against Blastoise.

As soon as the battle began, Octillery used Aurora Beam, attempting to exploit Ice-type power against Blastoise from a distance.

Blastoise easily evaded the attack by leaping from its stone pillar into the water. Octillery lacked the power to freeze the enormous battlefield solid, leaving it with no effective answer.

Aurora Beam froze only a small patch of the surface, turning the spray from Blastoise's dive into ice crystals without striking its target.

Once Blastoise approached through the water, Octillery could no longer even use its Ice-type moves.

With no better option, the old man ordered Octillery into the water as well. He hoped it could continually swim away, maintaining distance while searching for an opening in Blastoise's defenses.

Ethan answered the strategy by using overwhelming force to crush every trick. He ordered Blastoise to pursue Octillery relentlessly and gave it no opportunity to escape!

Underwater cameras relayed the action to the large screens, allowing the spectators to clearly watch the two Pokemonone large and one smallchasing each other below the surface.

The old man silently cursed Ethan for having no respect for his elders. How could he use such a shameless tactic against an old man?

Whether on land or in the water, Blastoise was considerably faster than Octillery. The two Pokemon swam in pursuit beneath the surface, but Octillery could never shake Blastoise.

Out of options, the old man ordered Octillery to release ink. Its long mouth sprayed continuously, instantly staining a vast section of the water black. Octillery intended to hide within the ink and gain a brief chance to catch its breath.

Ethan considered the darkened water for a moment, then decided to borrow from Ash's earlier battle.

At his command, Blastoise withdrew into its shell and began spinning at high speed. As it rotated through the water, it created an expanding vortex!

The force of the vortex pushed the ink farther away and successfully diluted it!

The polluted pool could not return to normal in a short time, but it became much clearer. Without the ink's protection, Octillery could no longer conceal itself!

Seeing this, the old man could only make one final attempt. He ordered Octillery to bind Blastoise tightly with its tentacles. But Blastoise possessed tremendous strength and relied on its heavy body. It broke free after only a few movements.

Ethan seized the opportunity while the two Pokemon were at close range and ordered Blastoise to unleash several moves in succession. It finally defeated Octillery in one stroke with Skull Bash.

The referee immediately announced the result.

When the spectators saw Ethan use Blastoise alone to defeat both of his opponent's Pokemon with ease, they erupted into enthusiastic cheers.

At this point in the tournament, his popularity, strength, and handsome appearance had made him the undisputed favorite in their eyes. More people focused on him each day and looked forward to seeing him win the championship!

Ethan waved to the audience and returned to the waiting room.

Ash and Misty both rose to congratulate him. Misty was sincerely delighted, while traces of dejection remained in Ash's expression.

His traveling companion and the rival he admired had both advanced, while he alone had been eliminated. How could he feel entirely at peace?

Fortunately, Ash had a carefree personality. After feeling down for a while, he quickly cast aside his troubles. In fact, he had already returned to normal before Ethan's match ended.

Ethan left with the two of them to meet Erika and the others.

Although he and Misty had successfully advanced to the quarterfinals, today's competition was not over. The remaining eight competitors would battle again that afternoon to determine the semifinalists.

The probability that Ethan and Misty would face each other had also increased considerably.

The tournament schedule truly was packed. But there was no other choice. The Whirl Cup was only a local competition. If it dragged on for too long and wasted too much time, it could easily miss the Trainers who traveled constantly while preparing for the Silver Conference.

Without those elite Trainers, only the island's less capable residents would remain. The number of entrants might stay the same, but the average strength of the competitors would fall considerably. Even if they forced themselves to choose the best of a weak field and named that person Sea Hero, the title would carry no authority. It might even damage the Whirl Cup's reputation further.

With only sixteen competitors remaining, the round took merely two or three hours to complete.

Ethan's group had not even finished lunch at the restaurant when the quarterfinal pairings were released.

Before Ethan and Misty could check who they would face, a beautiful young woman approached them.

She appeared to be twenty-four or twenty-five. Light makeup covered her face, and her long red hair was tied into a side ponytail. She wore two large bead-like earrings, a red T-shirt, and a long pink skirt.

Upon reaching the group, she first looked Ethan up and down with curiosity for quite some time. Only then did she turn toward Misty.

"You're Misty, right?"

Misty looked up at her in confusion. She clearly did not recognize the woman.

"That's right. Who are you?"

Misty had barely finished speaking when Brock leaped to his feet as though struck by one of Cupid's arrows and hurried in front of the woman before she could answer.

"I know! I know!" Brock's eyes seemed to transform into hearts. "You're the beautiful lady who won every one of her previous matches with ease!"

Brock could fall for every beautiful woman he met and remember each one's distinctive qualities perfectly. It had to be acknowledged as an impressive talent.

The woman looked at him in surprise. "Oh? You know me?"

"Of course!" Brock seized her hand and dropped to one knee like a knight proposing marriage. "Apart from my friends' matches, I've watched every one of yours! A beautiful lady like you shines brilliantly wherever she goes!"

The woman was clearly overwhelmed by Brock's sudden enthusiasm. She yanked her hand free, retreated a large step, and stared warily at the narrow-eyed man.

Seeing Brock behave this way, Misty raised a fist and struck him hard on the head. Without allowing any argument, she dragged him back.

"Sorry. Please ignore him. There's something very wrong with his head!"

Beside them, Ethan, Erika, and Ash exchanged glances and smiled wryly.

To themeven to Erika, who did not know Brock particularly wellthis was his normal behavior. Sometimes he even took notes! If a day ever came when he did not hound a beautiful woman like a lovesick fool, that would be the truly abnormal sight!

Ignoring Brock, the woman turned her attention back to Misty.

"Allow me to introduce myself. My name is Trinity, and I'm your opponent in the next match!"

Her opponent in the next match?

Misty froze. She had never expected her opponent to seek her out, and her expression immediately became serious.

Trinity clearly had not come with hostile intentions, however. She smiled at Misty. "I've watched your matches too. You and your Pokemon work together seamlessly, and your instincts in battle are excellent. I can see that you're a genuinely powerful Water-type Pokemon Trainer. Your Psyduck in particular was fascinating. It left a very deep impression on me!"

Hearing Trinity offer such an assessment immediately softened Misty's expression.

"Thank you for saying that!"

Trinity extended her hand and smiled as Misty shook it.

"I'm truly looking forward to our battle. Let's both give it our very best!"

Only after saying this did she turn her burning gaze toward Ethan once more.

Chapter 438: The Scent of Perfume in the Waiting Room

"Mr. Ethan, I watched several of your matches during the Indigo League Conference. Your Pokemon were all incredibly powerful. Even after so much time, their performances remain vivid in my memory. If the opportunity arises, I would very much like to face you during this Whirl Cup!"

Trinity could speak and laugh freely with Misty while remaining calm and composed. That was because she believed she could defeat Misty, allowing her expression and tone to stay so relaxed.

When facing Ethan, however, she showed ample deference. It represented both respect and the anticipation and unease that came from confronting a powerful competitor!

"I'd like to battle you too, but she's your opponent right now." Ethan smiled softly and pointed at Misty beside him. "If you want to face me, you'll have to defeat this young lady first! A word of advice: don't underestimate her. She's very strong!"

This was Ethan's response, but it also showed that he was standing behind Misty and warning Trinity not to overlook her.

Receiving Ethan's acknowledgment made Misty's face instantly light up!

Nothing could make her happier than praise from the person she liked!

As an adult, Trinity naturally understood Ethan's meaning. She looked at Misty again and nodded solemnly.

"I won't. And if I'm unfortunate enough to lose when the time comes, I hope you'll still agree to a private battle with me, Mr. Ethan!"

The woman clearly did want to face him. She must have possessed considerable confidence in her own strength.

Of course, Ethan had absolute confidence in his Pokemon. Faced with a challenge, he agreed without the slightest hesitation.

"Of course. If you want to challenge me, I'll be ready anytime!"

After receiving his answer, Trinity shook hands with the group and departed.

Watching her leave, Misty felt her fighting spirit surge. She had resolved to give everything she had in the afternoon match and never disappoint Ethan!

More than anything, however, his trust and support left a small spark of happiness in her heart.

Still...

Being called a young lady was rather frustrating.

When will Ethan finally see me as a woman?

If she had her way, she wished he would address her differently. Perhaps as "darling"... or "baby"...

At the thought, her face flushed. She turned toward Ethan and found him looking at her too.

Her blush deepened. Believing he had discovered her secret thoughts, she was about to say something heartfelt when Ethan spoke seriously. "Be careful. That woman is extremely confident, so she must truly be strong. Otherwise, she wouldn't have sought us out herself!"

"Huh?" Misty froze, then nodded as even her ears turned redder. "Oh. Don't worry. I'll definitely take this seriously!"

After Trinity left, the group had no reason to remain in the restaurant, so they went to the waiting room to examine the pairings.

Almost no one remained there. Ethan and the others stopped before the bracket and found that Trinity had spoken the truth: she had been paired against Misty. Their match was second that afternoon. Ethan would battle immediately afterward against a mature-looking, middle-aged man who appeared successful in his career.

Perhaps Trinity's visit had placed her under genuine pressure, or perhaps the match simply felt too close. Misty took Ash and Brock to a nearby practice room to adjust her condition.

Once the three left, only Ethan and Erika remained. The entire waiting room fell silent.

Erika glanced around. Although the room was spacious, aside from several large screens, it contained only hundreds of chairs and rows of sofas. There was not even a single green plant. Disappointed, she looked away.

It was entirely different from what she had imagined.

She had expected every competitors' lounge to be quiet, comfortable, and fully equipped like the one at the Indigo League Conference!

When she turned around, she found Ethan reclining on a sofa and could not help laughing softly. "What is this? You have a match this afternoon too. Don't you need to make some adjustments?"

"Adjustments?" Ethan stretched widely. After a satisfying meal, drowsiness slowly crept over him and made his eyelids increasingly heavy. "How am I supposed to adjust? Blastoise is the only Pokemon I can lead with right now. Its strength is extremely consistent, it's in excellent condition, and its fighting spirit is high. I honestly don't know what there is to change."

Erika nodded. He had a point. With Blastoise maintaining such excellent form, there truly was no need for adjustments. As long as it displayed its usual strength, an upset would be very unlikely.

"Even so, if your opponents see you battle with only one Pokemon, they'll easily identify Blastoise's characteristics and devise tactics specifically against it."

"That would be perfect." Ethan smiled. "If things reach the point where Blastoise loses and Gyarados has to enter, I simply won't interfere. I'll let it fight however it wants."

This was not arrogance on Ethan's part. His enormous red Gyarados was simply so powerful that making it lose would be difficult.

Erika looked surprised. "I've heard you mention it many times. Is your Gyarados truly that strong?"

Ethan thought carefully and realized Erika had indeed never seen Gyarados after its evolution, so she had no understanding of its current strength.

"Do you remember that Team Rocket scientist we caught, Professor Sebastian?" Ethan explained the story in detail. "Back when I was traveling with Sabuh... while I was traveling, I passed the Lake of Rage and met him for the first time. He struck my Gyarados with the waves from something called Project R, causing it to mutate. Now Gyarados isn't only exceptionally enormous; its color has turned red and its temperament has become even more brutal. Of course, its strength increased further in exchange."

"I see."

"To be honest..." Ethan suddenly sighed. "If it weren't my own Pokemon, even I might feel a chill down my back whenever I met those enormous red eyes. And its fighting style is so savage that it can hardly be called a battle anymore..."

This surprised Erika. For someone with Ethan's personality to describe his own Pokemon this way meant the Gyarados truly was dangerous.

That only made her want to see it for herself and learn what kind of power the red Gyarados possessed.

Erika suddenly remembered something and pointed toward the bracket. "By the way, you should pay some attention to this person."

Following her finger, Ethan saw the name "Zhe."

"What about him?"

"He's very strong too. You could call him the second favorite in this year's Whirl Cup, behind you." Erika considered for a moment. "I paid attention to his previous match. The strength of his Pokemon can't be underestimated. Speaking of rankings, Miss Trinity should probably be considered the third favorite. If we set Misty aside, the rest of the field is merely decent. No unexpected dark horse has distinguished themselves."

Erika's judgment was very accurate. If she considered the others merely decent, then a clear gap truly separated those Trainers from Trinity and Zhe.

Ethan nodded and examined the bracket once more. Zhe was in the same half, meaning he should become Ethan's next opponent if both successfully advanced.

The second favorite... He should be able to take a beating, shouldn't he?

Ethan was genuinely looking forward to it.

They waited in the lounge for a long time, but Misty and the others still did not return. Bored, Ethan released several of his smaller Pokemon and let them play nearby.

Listening to their cheerful cries and running footsteps, his eyelids grew heavier. Before he knew it, he had fallen asleep.

Some unknown amount of time later, he awoke and found his own jacket draped over him. A faint floral fragrance lingered on it, clearly left behind by Erika.

He slowly sat up and looked toward the other side of the waiting room. Erika had released her Pokemon as well and was using a brush to groom both hers and Ethan's.

From the side, her expression appeared focused and serious. Her sleeves were rolled up, revealing two smooth, pale arms.

Sensing that Ethan had awakened, Erika turned toward him.

"Awake now?"

Rubbing his eyes, Ethan sat upright. "How long did I sleep?"

He did not need to sniff carefully to notice the faint scent of Erika's perfume on his jacket.

Besides being a Gym Leader, Erika owned a perfume shop and had refined taste in fragrances. He could even detect a different scent on her each day. The one left on his jacket now carried the fragrance of daisies, delicate rather than overpowering, yet able to linger for a long time.

"Not long. Only a little over ten minutes. There's still time before the match. Wouldn't you like to sleep a little more?"

Ethan patted his cheeks to wake himself. By the time he lowered his hands, the last trace of drowsiness had disappeared.

"Misty and the others still aren't back?"

"They probably went directly to the battlefield." Erika shook her head. "Miss Trinity clearly placed her under considerable pressure. And your expectations have made her more determined than ever!"

They chatted for a while. When the rest period ended and the match gradually approached, the other competitors began returning to the waiting room. Ethan and Erika recalled their respective Pokemon, and Erika left alone to return to the stands.

Even then, Misty had not returned. Ethan had no idea how well her preparations had gone.

With Ash and Brock accompanying her, however, there should not be any problems. Ethan shifted into a more comfortable position on the sofa and turned his attention to the large screen once again.

After the announcer warmed up the crowd, the quarterfinals officially began on-screen!

Chapter 439: She Crawled Into a Gyarados's Mouth as a Child!

As far as Ethan was concerned, the first match offered nothing worth watching. He would have difficulty learning anything from it. Both competitors performed reasonably well, but that was all. Nothing especially exciting happened.

The spectators clearly felt the same way, judging by their lackluster cheers.

Once the first match ended and Misty and Trinity entered the battlefield, Ethan finally perked up and sat straight.

The real show was finally beginning!

On the screen, Misty's expression was solemn, while Trinity looked equally serious. Both clearly placed exceptional importance on this match. Victory would carry one of them into the semifinals, but more than that, each had a reason she could not afford to lose!

Once they were ready, the referee gave the signal, and both Trainers released their Pokemon simultaneously.

Two flashes of blue light appeared. Misty sent out Poliwhirl, while Trinity chose a Gyarados!

The instant she saw the ferocious Gyarados, Misty's expression changed. In her panic, she unconsciously stepped backward!

Her heart pounded wildly. Merely meeting Gyarados's eyes nearly robbed her of all courage.

Seeing this, Ethan shook his head helplessly. Even after so long, Misty had not overcome her fear of facing Gyarados.

The source of that fear could be traced back to her childhood. Once, while playing outside, she encountered a Gyarados living near the Gym. It was sleeping with its enormous mouth open. Misty was so young that she could barely walk, and her curiosity drove her to crawl directly into its mouth!

Sensing something unusual, Gyarados instinctively closed its jaws. At that moment, Misty thought she was about to be eaten. Fortunately, Gyarados noticed the problem and immediately spat her back out. Even so, the experience frightened Misty into wailing. From that day onward, Gyarados left an indelible shadow in her heart!

The incident had been terrifying and dealt her an enormous psychological blow, one that still haunted her now. But she could not continue this way...

How could the future Gym Leader of a Water-type Gym fear a Water-type Pokemon?

Only after overcoming this obstacle and learning to command Gyarados would she truly become a qualified Water-type Pokemon Trainer. For now, it appeared she still needed much more time to temper herself...

As both her friend and the object of her affection, Ethan sincerely wanted to help. After thinking for a moment, he concluded that the fastest way to solve the problem was to fight poison with poison!

When an opportunity arose, he might as well let Misty spend more time with his enormous red Gyarados.

Despite its terrifying appearance, the red Gyarados was extremely gentle toward people it trusted and would never harm Misty. Hmm... He could only wonder whether that would erase the shadow in her heart.

On the battlefield, Misty understood that she could not retreat. She forced down her fear and adjusted her state of mind. The moment the referee announced the start of the match, she took the initiative and attacked Gyarados.

At her command, Poliwhirl used Bubble Beam. Dozens of bubbles large and small burst from the spiral on its belly and flew toward Gyarados.

Trinity answered the move directly with Hyper Beam!

Gyarados opened its enormous mouth, and a powerful beam of light gathered inside before shooting straight toward Poliwhirl!

Hyper Beam's tremendous power became evident the moment it met Bubble Beam. The searing heat instantly dissolved every bubble, and the beam continued forward until it struck Poliwhirl!

Boom!

The attack sent Poliwhirl flying across the battlefield and crashing into another stone pillar. By the time it slid to the ground, it had already fallen unconscious!

It had been knocked out in one hit!

The referee needed only one glance before decisively announcing the result.

The battle had barely begun. Gyarados defeated Poliwhirl in their first exchange, leaving the spectators in heated discussion as cries of disbelief sounded everywhere.

This was not their first time seeing a one-hit knockout. In several of Ethan's previous matches, Blastoise had defeated its opponent with a single attack.

But this was a quarterfinal. Every weak competitor had already been eliminated. Seeing a Pokemon lose in one blow at this stage was extraordinarily rare!

The difference in strength between these two Pokemon could only be described as enormous!

Misty's expression darkened when Poliwhirl fell. Her match had begun in the worst possible way. She had prepared extensively beforehand, but even after accounting for every possibility, she had never imagined Poliwhirl would fail to withstand a single move!

It also demonstrated how well Trinity's Pokemon had been trained. Otherwise, she would never have approached the group during lunch and spoken with such confidence!

Misty glanced at the camera aimed toward her. She knew Ethan was watching through the screen at that very moment, and the thought gave her tremendous courage.

Ethan is watching me right now. How can I disappoint him?

Only one Pokemon has fallen. The match isn't over, and I haven't lost yet!

Taking a deep breath, she solemnly drew her second Poke Ball.

Blue light flashed as Misty sent out Corsola once again. Gyarados had enjoyed a brief chance to recover, and the aftereffects of using Hyper Beam had faded. It could move normally again.

The two Pokemon now seemed to be starting on equal footing.

This time, Trinity launched the first attack. At her command, Gyarados used Hydro Pump, sending a thick stream of water toward Corsola. Misty answered with Mirror Coat once again!

Strange light flashed over Corsola's body. Hydro Pump struck it, then rebounded with even greater force!

Facing its own attack, Trinity ordered Gyarados to use Hyper Beam again. The powerful blast instantly scattered the returning water and continued toward Corsola.

Fortunately, Corsola jumped into the pool in time and avoided the Hyper Beam.

The attack shattered the stone pillar where Corsola had stood, scattering fragments in every direction without touching the Pokemon itself.

Watching from the waiting room, Ethan had learned enough from Gyarados's attacks to recognize its tremendous power. That last strike had not only destroyed a stone pillar, but vaporized a large volume of seawater in an instant!

Yet its failure to defeat Corsola immediately changed the situation.

Just as Ethan anticipated, Gyarados could not move temporarily after using Hyper Beam, giving Corsola an opening.

The water churned, and countless spikes of energy suddenly erupted from beneath the surface. They broke through the water and shot toward Gyarados at astonishing speed.

Anyone with a discerning eye could identify the Normal-type move: Spike Cannon!

Unable to evade, Gyarados was struck repeatedly by Spike Cannon. The pain sent its body toppling uncontrollably into another pillar. The impact was so powerful that the pillar itself tilted to one side!

Trinity's heart tightened, but Gyarados had not yet regained the ability to move. No matter how anxious she became, she could do nothing.

A moment later, Corsola suddenly leaped from the water and rammed all four horns on its back viciously into Gyarados!

Bang!

Corsola's body might have been small, but it contained tremendous strength.

The impact made Gyarados cry out before collapsing outright!

Ethan shook his head at the sight.

It was genuinely baffling. Just as Gyarados had knocked out Poliwhirl in one blow, Ethan would never have believed a Gyarados could fall after only two or three attacks if he had not witnessed it himself!

Had Corsola struck a vital point?

Trinity's Gyarados clearly emphasized offense at the expense of defense. Something had undoubtedly gone wrong with the direction of its training.

Such an approach worked perfectly while maintaining the initiative. Its tremendous offensive power could defeat opponents easily. But once the opponent counterattacked, Gyarados could withstand very few hits.

After defeating Gyarados, Misty danced with joy. Even through the screen, Ethan could feel her delight.

Trinity, by contrast, did not appear particularly disappointed. She calmly recalled Gyarados, then smiled as she threw her second Poke Ball!

Blue light flashed, and a Chinchou floated on the water.

Compared with the enormous Gyarados, the small Chinchou created a striking contrast. The spectators had never expected Trinity's final Pokemon to be so diminutive.

Yet no one dared underestimate it. Chinchou had fought brilliantly several times during Trinity's earlier matches and had already left a deep impression on the crowd!

Chinchou was both Water and Electric type. Its Electric-type moves were undoubtedly devastating on a battlefield like this. Any opponent daring to enter the water would be shocked mercilessly!

Misty swallowed. She also knew the real challenge had arrived!

Sure enough, when the third battle began, Chinchou immediately fired electricity into the sky. Dark clouds gathered overhead under the current's influence, and only seconds later, a thick bolt of lightning descended!

Chinchou had opened with Thunder!

Even among Electric-type moves, Thunder possessed exceptional power.

Faced with enough force to knock out Corsola in one blow, Misty's expression changed dramatically. She hurriedly ordered Corsola to protect itself with Mirror Coat!

In a flash, the lightning struck Corsola. Fortunately, it reacted in time and successfully used Mirror Coat at the final possible instant. Once reflected, the bolt shot toward Chinchou with even greater power!

Crackle!

Chinchou did not dodge and took the lightning directly. Yet when the smoke and electricity disappeared, it remained floating there entirely unharmed!

Ethan shook his head helplessly.

Clearly, this Chinchou possessed the Volt Absorb Ability. Electric attacks caused it no harm and restored its stamina instead!

Now the situation was truly dire.

On this battlefield, Chinchou's Electric-type moves dealt super-effective damage to Corsola, while the electricity reflected by Corsola could not harm Chinchou at all. How was Misty supposed to fight?

Misty also realized how unfavorable the situation had become. When she saw Corsola's current condition, worry filled her face.

Mirror Coat could reflect an opponent's move with greater force, but its user still suffered some damage. Corsola had used it several times within a short period, placing an enormous burden on its body!

Before Misty could devise a solution, Chinchou attacked again.

This time, it used Confuse Ray. With no other choice, Misty ordered Corsola into the water to evade.

But that accomplished nothing. Chinchou immediately extended its two long, lantern-like antennae into the pool and indiscriminately used Confuse Ray beneath the surface!

Intense pink light suddenly spread through the water. Refracted and reflected by the sea, it made the entire battlefield look extraordinarily eerie!

In the end, Confuse Ray completely enveloped Corsola underwater. With nowhere left to flee, Corsola could only climb back onto a stone pillar. Its eyes had turned entirely pink under the move's influence, and its body swayed unsteadily. Its awareness had clearly fallen into complete confusion!

No matter how Misty called out and encouraged it, Corsola could not regain clarity. Even her command to use Recover could no longer reach its ears.

Trinity gave Corsola no opportunity to recover. At her command, Chinchou used Thunder Shock and defeated Corsola completely!

As soon as Corsola fainted, the referee announced the result. Misty had lost to Trinity and was eliminated from the tournament in the quarterfinals!

In the waiting room, Ethan sighed and rose to leave.

He did not watch Misty's helpless expression on the screen or wait for her return so he could console her. His own match was about to begin.

He still met Misty walking the opposite way inside the competitors' passage. When she saw him, her body trembled. She lowered her head, unable to meet his eyes.

After losing, the person she felt she had disappointed most was Ethan. He had supported her so strongly, yet she had failed to win and betrayed his trust!

Ethan must be disappointed in me now, right?

Ethan approached Misty and smiled gently at her guilty expression.

"What's wrong? Are you upset because you lost?"

"Of course not..." Misty shook her head, but her voice grew quieter. "Miss Trinity's Pokemon really were powerful. I couldn't defeat her this time because I wasn't strong enough. It's just... It's just..."

She repeated herself twice, but no matter how she tried, she could not say what came next.

Ethan extended a finger and gently lifted her chin. His brilliant smile instantly filled her vision.

"It's true that you aren't strong enough yet, but you don't need to lose heart, and you certainly don't need to feel that you've disappointed anyone. When you fall, you should get back up in the same place. Your Pokemon really do need to improve. After the Silver Conference ends, why don't you travel with me through the next region?"

Misty's body jolted. She could hardly believe her ears!

Ethan had actually invited her to travel with him?

She had not misheard him, had she?!

Once she confirmed that Ethan was not joking, she wiped the tears from the corners of her eyes and nodded rapidly. At that moment, she felt as though brilliant, warm sunlight had surrounded her heart!

Chapter 440: Does This Man Own Businesses in Kalos or Something?

When Ethan emerged from the competitors' passage, enormous applause and cheers welcomed him. The sound was far more enthusiastic than during Misty and Trinity's battle, demonstrating that Ethan was unquestionably the most popular competitor in this year's Whirl Cup!

He had been delayed in the passage for a moment, so his opponent was already standing calmly in the command area at the far end, waiting for him.

Ethan walked unhurriedly to his position and studied the other man.

The middle-aged man wore a tasteful casual suit. Judging from its material and cut, it had probably been custom tailored and was clearly expensive. His hair was combed straight back with wax, while a neatly trimmed beard extending to his chin gave him a distinctly masculine appearance.

His style would not attract spectators who cared only about youthful good looks, but it still held considerable appeal for those with more particular tastes.

In Ethan's opinion, a man like this belonged in an office, watching the sunset while holding a glass of red wine and smoking a cigar, rather than standing here.

Pokemon battles truly had become something everyone loved in this world. People of every identity and profession wanted to take part.

Viewed another way, someone like him probably would never have entered if the Whirl Cup had imposed any entry requirements.

Separated by the broad pool, the two did not exchange greetings. At the referee's signal, they immediately released their Pokemon.

The middle-aged man's first Pokemon was a Clawitzer. Its species was common in the Kalos region, but differences in climate and waterways meant it had no natural habitat in Johto or Kanto.

Ethan had already watched recordings of the man's previous battles and knew something about his Pokemon, so the choice did not surprise him.

Clawitzer also supported the impression that this man was successful in business and traveled around the world frequently. Otherwise, he would hardly possess a Pokemon so closely associated with Kalos!

Most local Trainers had never seen Clawitzer and knew nothing about its traits or abilities. That ignorance had helped the middle-aged man win match after match and advance this far.

Clawitzer's own strength certainly contributed, but many of those Trainers had also paid the price for their lack of knowledge.

As always, Ethan sent out Blastoise.

The spectators could not help feeling disappointed when they saw it.

They supported Ethan, certainly, but he had used this one Pokemon from beginning to end, leaving them tired of the same sight. Blastoise might be extremely powerful and stronger than most Pokemon in the tournament, but they wanted to see a fresh face!

They truly could not understand why Ethan insisted on using only Blastoise when he clearly possessed other Pokemon!

When the middle-aged man saw Blastoise, the corner of his mouth rose slightly.

In his view, using only one Pokemon displayed Ethan's confidence, but it was also a way of flaunting his strength and presenting himself as exceptional!

As a successful businessman, the man ought to possess a broad perspective and avoid envying others. Clearly, he was not that sort of person.

He might appear suave and upright, but he was actually extraordinarily petty!

This fellow is nothing more than a brat who got lucky and won a championship. What's so impressive about him?

He even made me wait more than ten seconds for his grand entrance. Doesn't he just want to experience having every eye on him?

Judging Ethan by his own motives made the man dislike him more with every glance. Ethan's young, handsome face gave him an especially sharp sense of defeat.

Listening to the audience cheer for Ethan, the middle-aged man imagined the expression Ethan would wear once he defeated him.

Would the boy regret his arrogance?

Despite criticizing Ethan inwardly, he revealed none of it. In front of the cameras, he maintained a smile he considered irresistibly charming.

At another signal from the referee, the match officially began.

The people here might be unfamiliar with this Pokemon, but Ethan knew Clawitzer reasonably well through games, the animated series, and all the knowledge he had crammed since arriving in this world.

Clawitzer was a pure Water-type Pokemon whose shape resembled a crayfish from Earth. Most of its curled body was blue, while its right arm formed an enormous claw three or four times larger than the rest of it.

That claw was Clawitzer's primary weapon. Its feelers could sense prey, while the claw itself functioned like a cannon, firing many Water-type, pulse, and aura moves. A tube at the rear could even discharge water like a thruster, allowing Clawitzer to move rapidly underwater.

Its Ability, Mega Launcher, was also formidable. Apart from Heal Pulse, Mega Launcher greatly increased the power of pulse and aura attacks.

Even more interestingly, outside Clawitzer and its unevolved form, Clauncher, the only other Pokemon capable of possessing this Ability was Mega Blastoise!

That shared trait could have been one of the match's highlights.

Unfortunately, Clawitzer was not native to this region, and the local spectators knew very little about it. Among everyone present, only Ethan recognized this connection. Even the match commentator was unaware of it.

As the battle began, Clawitzer immediately took the initiative with Dragon Pulse.

The two Pokemon fought fiercely. Clawitzer attacked like a spear, launching assault after assault at Blastoise, while Blastoise stood like a heavy shield and blocked every strike!

Multicolored moves erupted from Clawitzer's enormous claw and streaked toward Blastoise. Blastoise answered with moves of equal power and did not yield in the slightest.

The dazzling exchange captivated the spectators. Huge explosions, torrents of water, and grand spectacles had always been what they loved most!

After a long struggle, the battle appeared deadlocked.

One side specialized in attacking and the other in defending. Now the only question was whether the spear would pierce the shield first or the shield would snap the spear.

As time passed, however, the more knowledgeable spectators recognized the truth. Clawitzer's assault might look astonishing, but it was all thunder and no rain, achieving almost nothing!

For Ethan, battling Clawitzer presented little difficulty as long as Blastoise remained wary of its enormous claw.

Just as Erika had said in the waiting room, apart from Ash, Misty, Trinity, and the still-unseen Zhe, the other competitors in this Whirl Cup were thoroughly ordinary.

While defending, Blastoise continually found openings and counterattacked successfully. Clawitzer, by contrast, never broke through its defenses!

Seeing Clawitzer gradually fall behind made the middle-aged man anxious.

Finally, he staked everything on one move. He ordered Clawitzer to approach Blastoise and use Crabhammer, hoping to defeat it at close range.

This was Clawitzer's strongest attack. Amplified by its enormous claw, the middle-aged man believed that Blastoise could never withstand a direct hit!

Yet Blastoise blocked the Crabhammer in which he placed such confidence with a single Withdraw!

The enormous claw shone with dangerous light and hammered heavily against the shell, only managing to send it spinning!

As soon as Crabhammer ended, the shell suddenly bounced toward Clawitzer. Blastoise's large head shot out, and a Skull Bash defeated its opponent instead!

The referee immediately announced the result.

Amid the spectators' cheers, the middle-aged man's expression involuntarily darkened.

He had spent considerable time studying Ethan's Blastoise before the match. Only now did he discover that its abilities were exceptionally balanced and that it possessed almost no weaknesses.

Like many other competitors, he preferred to send out his ace in the opening battle. A victory would allow him to press the advantage and defeat his opponent in one continuous push.

Now that he had lost, however, the situation immediately became troublesome.

Blastoise had defended for a long time, but remained in excellent condition and had suffered almost no damage. Judging by the strength it displayed, defeating it with his second Pokemon would be extremely difficult.

He was already considering retreat.

If even his second Pokemon failed to defeat this Blastoise, the humiliation would be tremendous and would undoubtedly damage the flawless image he always presented!

But with matters already at this point, he could not flee before the battle ended. Urged on by the referee, he gritted his teeth and drew his second Poke Ball!

Blue light flashed, and a Binacle appeared atop a stone pillar.

Seeing it made Ethan raise an eyebrow!

Another Pokemon common to the Kalos region!?

Did this man own businesses in Kalos or something?

As a Water/Rock-type Pokemon, Binacle looked like two claws protruding from a stone, with a face on each claw. It appeared both ugly and fantastical!

Those two claws were actually the Pokemon themselves. The reason they could be called "they" was that, like Dugtrio, they existed in a cooperative group!

To be honest, Ethan knew little about this Pokemon, primarily because it was far too ugly and did not suit his tastes at all!

Even after it evolved into Barbaracle, Ethan always politely declined any thought of approaching one because of its appearance!

Now that he faced one and knew so little about it, he had no choice but to take out his Pokedex and point it toward the Pokemon.

The Pokedex chimed. "Binacle, the Two-Handed Pokemon. A Rock and Water type. Two Binacle find a rock of suitable size along the coast and live together. They stretch their bodies and use the resulting force to carry the rock beneath them as they move. When waves wash over the shore, they rush forward to eat seaweed. If the two quarrel, one will move to another rock."

Ethan put away the Pokedex and pursed his lips.

Why did that description make them sound strangely adorable?

The realization suddenly horrified him. He hurriedly shook his head and flung the unbelievable thought away!

I refuse to let my tastes become strange!

Across the water, the middle-aged man finally breathed an inward sigh of relief when he saw Ethan use his Pokedex.

Judging from the first battle, Ethan was clearly very familiar with Clawitzer. He had continually avoided its attacks, which was why he won so easily.

The man had begun to believe Ethan possessed extraordinary breadth of knowledge. But now, at last, here was a Pokemon he did not understand!

Perfect. People always feared and hesitated before the unknown! As long as doubt entered Ethan's heart, the middle-aged man would have an excellent chance of winning!

His earlier dejection vanished, and some confidence returned!

Yet the moment the battle began, he realized things did not seem to be unfolding that way.

Why had this man changed strategies and begun attacking immediately?

Shouldn't he proceed cautiously against a Pokemon he had never seen before?!

On the battlefield, Blastoise abandoned the defensive strategy of the previous match and actively launched an offensive.

Ethan might not know much about this species, but Binacle was unevolved, its overall abilities lagged far behind Blastoise's, and it possessed the Rock type. What was there to fear?

If Blastoise had displayed elite defense in the previous battle, it now demonstrated fearless offense!

It first exchanged several Water-type moves with Binacle from a distance, then closed the gap and used close-range attacks to finish the Pokemon swiftly and cleanly.

Seeing his Pokemon defeated so easily made the middle-aged man's face alternate between pale and red!

He had believed this would be his chance to reverse the match and at least take one round. Instead, he lost even faster than before!

Binacle's own lack of strength was partly responsible, but ultimately, Blastoise's uninterrupted combination of attacks had brought it down.

The man stared deeply at Ethan.

They had not exchanged a single word from beginning to end, yet he had long since regarded Ethan as his greatest rival. Now that both of his Pokemon had failed to defeat Blastoise, he felt humiliated and viciously insulted!

Ethan's calm expression throughout the entire match irritated him even more!

A loss was still a loss, and there was nothing he could do. He was about to say something magnanimous for appearances when Ethan recalled Blastoise, turned his back, and simply walked away!

He! Just! Left! Like! That!

The middle-aged man's chest heaved violently. But Ethan was gone and his Pokemon had lost. What could he possibly do now?

As the victor, Ethan accepted the audience's cheers. As the loser, the middle-aged man could only depart in gloom, accompanied by the regrets of a small number of sophisticated women attracted to his bearing.

Under ordinary circumstances, a mature man like him would attract plenty of younger women. Here, however, strength determined everything!

Once defeated, elimination was inevitable.

As far as Ethan was concerned, the middle-aged man's strength had been decent, but nothing more.

They were strangers meeting for the first time. Ethan had no reason to offer him any words of consolation.

Apart from his memorable clothing and the fact that both of his Pokemon came from Kalos, nothing else about him left a deep impression.

Hmm... After today, Ethan would probably cast him from his mind and forget him entirely...

Chapter 441: Jessie's Beautiful Ambition

Ethan left the battlefield and met Erika and the others outside the colosseum.

Although he had successfully advanced to the semifinals, Ash and Misty had both suffered elimination and could no longer compete.

With Ethan the sole survivor, the group's hopes were now concentrated entirely on him.

To be honest, neither Ash nor Misty had expected this before the tournament, when both had been overflowing with confidence. They had believed a local competition like this would let them display their abilities and achieve even better results!

Now it appeared they simply were not strong enough to reach their intended goals.

The result inevitably left both somewhat discouraged, and it struck Ash especially hard.

He had always regarded Ethan as the person he admired most and his greatest rival!

During their travels through the Orange Islands, both Ash and Ethan had defeated Drake and become Honorable Trainers of the Orange League. For a time, that convinced Ash he had once again reached the same starting line and could compete with Ethan!

After reaching Johto, he had caught many Pokemon during his journey, won the Grass Pokemon Tournament, and earned victories in a series of smaller competitions. All of it greatly increased his confidence!

I've become stronger than before! The gap between Ethan and me must be shrinking!

Ash had firmly believed this for quite some time. It was also what gave him the courage to challenge Ethan during the Whirl Cup!

Yet after only a few matches, cruel reality had dragged him back down!

Once again, just as at the Indigo League Conference, his run had ended in the round of sixteen!

His opponent had been Misty, who specialized in Water-type Pokemon, and her Psyduck had defeated him through an unexpected reversal. Even so, a loss was a loss. His own inadequacy was the only honest explanation, and there was no need to make excuses.

Fortunately, Ash had always been broad-minded and had already recovered. What he could not understand was why Misty looked so happy after losing her own match. She practically glowed!

No matter how much he questioned her, Misty merely gave him a smug smile and showed no desire to explain. Only when she looked toward Ethan did some inexplicable emotion seem to pass through her eyes!

The change was so obvious that even Ash could sense it. Unfortunately, in his innocence, he had no idea what the emotion meant.

Unable to understand, he could only suppress the question.

Although Ash and Misty had been eliminated, the three friends had no intention of leaving immediately. They planned to watch Ethan's matches tomorrow before resuming their journey.

As friends, companions, younger siblings, and rivals, they naturally cared greatly about Ethan's progress. With him still competing, how could they abandon him here?

Scratching his head, Ash turned toward Brock. "All of Ethan's matches are finished for today, right? What's tomorrow's schedule?"

Brock took out the guidebook issued by the tournament and flipped through several pages. "Let's see... According to the schedule, the semifinals are tomorrow morning and will determine the last two competitors. The final begins at one in the afternoon and decides the championthe Sea Hero. After that comes the blessing ceremony for the Sea Hero. If everything goes smoothly, we can leave the morning after tomorrow with the trophy and honor."

Like Misty, Brock knew Ethan well enough to believe without doubt that he would become the final champion.

Brock understood perfectly that Ethan was entirely different from Ash and Misty. He already possessed exceptional strength and never gave his opponents the slightest opportunity!

Most of all, they knew about Ethan's red Gyarados. With it available, how could he lose?

Listening to the cheerful conversation around him, Ethan felt exceptionally relaxed and content.

For a time after arriving in this world, he had drifted like a rootless plant, with neither attachments nor support. Now he had friends, companions, and a lover. Their trust and her love made him cherish this world more with each passing day, and they would undoubtedly make him stronger!

White clouds drifted slowly beneath the blue sky, perfectly reflecting his mood.

Yet for some reason, Ethan felt as though he had overlooked something.

Thinking carefully, the tournament had indeed proceeded too smoothly and peacefully. It was like enjoying a delicious feast only to realize it lacked an appetizer, leaving the experience just short of perfect!

Why did he feel that way?

Ethan remained puzzled until he looked at Ash twice and suddenly realized what was missing!

Of course. The Team Rocket trio that's always on Ash's heels hasn't appeared...

Without their interference, this Whirl Cup had undoubtedly been less lively.

But those three could never resist excitement. With such a major event taking place, things should not have remained this quiet.

It was easy to guess that they were hiding somewhere nearby and preparing some grand operation!

...

In fact, Ethan was correct.

Team Rocket had followed Ash and the others to the Whirl Islands long ago. The trio had even disguised themselves as vendors and infiltrated the colosseum. Over the past few days, selling popcorn and cold drinks had already earned them a tidy profit.

Earning money was not their true objective, of course. They had set their sights on the scepter held by Sea Priestess Maya!

The reason they had endured until now without causing trouble was that one of their earlier covert attempts had multiplied the number of guards around the ceremonial platform. Even now, they had not found the right opportunity!

But as the tournament approached its conclusion, they had grown increasingly anxious!

The day's competition was not yet over. Two Trainers were fiercely battling for the last place in the semifinals.

In an unnoticed corner of the stands, the Team Rocket trio crouched in convenience-store uniforms with their heads close together.

"Did you see that just now?" Meowth whispered.

"Of course," James said with a sigh. "Ethan seems even stronger than the last time we saw him. He defeated his opponent so easily again, so the championship is practically his! Ugh. With him here, stealing that scepter will be much harder!"

Jessie glared fiercely at him. "What? Do you two want to give up!?"

Startled by her intensity, James hurriedly ducked his head.

"O-of course not... I only think we should be more careful with our plan..."

"Neither of you is planning to run away at the last moment, are you!?" Jessie narrowed her eyes, a cold gleam within them making the warning unmistakable. "So what if Ethan is here? He's busy with the tournament. How would he have time to meddle in our affairs? And stop being so afraid of him! We're Team Rocket. How can we retreat every time we see him?"

Despite her words, James was deeply unwilling to make an enemy of Ethan.

Under Jessie's oppressive glare, however, he and Meowth hurriedly shook their heads and denied everything. "Of course we aren't afraid of him. We were only thinking... Are we stealing the scepter to sell it for operating funds? We've already made a lot of money over the last few days. Do we really need to take such a risk...?"

Meowth nodded vigorously. "Dat's right... Ethan's bad news. We should stay as far away from him as possible..."

"He's already frightened you out of your wits, hasn't he?" Jessie raised her chin and glanced down at James and Meowth. "I've made up my mind. We are taking that scepter! Look at its golden shaft, and especially that Sea Spirit. How beautiful! I am determined to succeed, and neither of you is allowed to ruin this operation! Ahh, only I am worthy of such a gorgeous gemstone! Hmph, hmph. It exists to make me even more beautiful! Ahahahaha!"

Jessie laughed wildly without the slightest concern for her image, already lost in her fantasy as though the Sea Spirit had fallen into her hands!

James and Meowth were thoroughly accustomed to this behavior. Yet despite Jessie's determination to obtain the Sea Spirit, they could not avoid worrying.

The man and Pokemon exchanged a glance and saw deep concern in each other's eyes.

James cautiously asked, "But... the calling card we left announcing the theft didn't have the intended effect. It only made them increase security..."

"That's exactly the effect I wanted!" Jessie's eyes flashed with confidence. "This is where my brilliance comes in! The stronger their defenses and the more security personnel they have, the safer they'll feel. That means they're even more likely to lower their guard at the crucial moment. And that will be our opportunity to strike!"

Only after hearing her explanation did James and Meowth understand.

"I see! You're a genius! So all we have to do is wait?"

...

Once all four semifinalists had been decided, the next pairings were released immediately.

In the upper half, Trinity would face a female Trainer. In the lower half, Ethan would battle Zhe, the tournament's second favorite!

The winners of those two matches would meet in tomorrow afternoon's final and determine the final Sea Hero.

After eating dinner with Ash and the others, the group remained at their restaurant table to study Ethan's next opponent.

With so many Trainers eliminated, many competitors had chosen to leave rather than remain to watch. Numerous rooms had suddenly opened at the Pokemon Center. Seeing this, Ethan checked out of the hotel and moved there with Erika.

The sleeping arrangements were considerably less comfortable, but the new setting helped him focus more completely on his opponent.

They watched recordings of Zhe's matches several times. Based on his Pokemon's performances, everyone contributed observations and soon discovered a great deal.

Erika's knowledge, Brock's analysis, Misty's eye for detail, and Ash's flashes of inspiration combined so effectively that Ethan barely needed to contribute. They quickly discussed nearly every aspect of Zhe and exposed him down to his underwear.

Ethan could not help observing a moment of silence for the man.

In terms of strength, Zhe was roughly equal to Trinity and perhaps slightly stronger, but he was certainly no match for Ethan. After Ash and the others analyzed him, nearly every strength and weakness of his Pokemon had been identified!

With their help, Zhe's odds of victory plummeted further. Unless Ethan's Pokemon performed abnormally poorly, defeating him would be nearly impossible!

Yes, he was that confident!

That night, both Trinity and Zhe tossed and turned, sleeping very little. Only Ethan slept soundly.

Consequently, when he arrived at the colosseum the next morning and saw his opponent, he noticed the exhaustion on Zhe's face at a glance!

Their semifinal was scheduled first. Ethan examined the man whom the spectators considered his greatest rival in the Whirl Cup.

Zhe was around Ethan's age, roughly twenty. He had short black hair, lightly bronzed skin, a green short-sleeved shirt, and beige shorts. He also appeared calm and steady by nature.

Hmm. Even their styles were somewhat similar.

From the information they had gathered, Zhe was a native of the Whirl Islands and had already earned some local fame before entering. He had spent recent months traveling and, like Ethan's group, was collecting Badges in preparation for the Silver Conference.

Before the spectators learned that Ethan had entered, they considered Zhe the leading candidate for the championship. That belief ended abruptly once Ethan joined the field.

The semifinal rules remained unchanged: each Trainer could still use only two Pokemon.

Against Ethan's Blastoise, Zhe sent out a Quagsire.

From recordings of Zhe's earlier matches, Ethan knew this Quagsire had appeared several times and possessed considerable strength. It was almost equal to Zhe's other Pokemon, and together they had carried him successfully into the semifinals.

Quagsire was a Water/Ground-type Pokemon with a slightly plump, light-blue body that was always slick and slippery. Its two eyes resembled black dots and gave it a vacant expression somewhat similar to Ditto.

Quagsire were ordinarily relaxed and easygoing. They opened their mouths underwater and quietly waited for food to wander inside. Since they scarcely moved, they did not become hungry very often.

Their senses were somewhat dull, and they sometimes showed no concern even after bumping into something.

But no one should underestimate them because of that!

Quagsire were naturally powerful Pokemon. In a Trainer's hands, they could display even greater strength!

Chapter 442: The Semifinal

As the battle began, Ethan and Zhe issued their commands at the same time.

Unlike Zhe, who wanted to engage at close range, Ethan immediately ordered Blastoise to attack from a distance.

Quagsire was too slow to dodge in time, and Zhe was unwilling to let it take a beating without fighting back. He had no choice but to counterattack.

Two streams of water shot from the Pokemon's mouths in quick succession.

Water sprayed everywhere as the thick and thin streams met in midair. The thicker one was naturally Blastoise's Hydro Pump, while the thinner one was Quagsire's Water Gun.

Splash!

As the attacks collided, Hydro Pump crushed Water Gun and scattered it into countless droplets. Its remaining force continued forward and struck Quagsire.

Quagsire swayed slightly under the impact.

Although its Ground typing was weak to Water, Quagsire was also a Water type, sparing it from taking additional damage.

Quagsire had not chosen Water Gun because it was deliberately holding back its more powerful Water-type moves. As a dual-type Pokemon, it also knew a number of Ground-type moves, leaving it with a very limited selection of Water-type attacks!

Seeing Quagsire lose out at long range only strengthened Zhe's determination to bring it closer to Blastoise.

At his command, Quagsire dove into the water and swam toward Blastoise from below, preventing another attack from the surface.

A blue shape streaked through the water.

Several seconds later, Quagsire leaped from the water directly in front of Blastoise. Before it even landed on the stone pillar, it raised both claws and reached for its opponent!

The opening movement made its intention obvious. It was using Grab Throw, a Normal-type move employed by many Pokemon!

Blastoise had no intention of waiting helplessly for the fierce attack. It advanced instead of retreating, turned sideways, and aimed the hardest edge of its shell at Quagsire's abdomen with Tackle!

Bang!

The two Pokemon rushed at each other and immediately became locked in a grapple. But Blastoise's smooth shell offered Quagsire nothing to hold. Its Grab Throw failed, while the heavy impact forced it to stumble a large step backward!

Both of Blastoise's attacks had worked, seeming to set the tone for the battle.
