Quagsire might not appear exceptional in any area, but aside from its extremely poor speed, its abilities were evenly balanced and had no obvious weakness.

That versatility made it difficult for certain opponents to target. Unfortunately, this time it faced a stronger Blastoise and an Ethan who had prepared thoroughly for the battle!

Other than stamina, Blastoise surpassed Quagsire by a wide margin in every area. That advantage made it almost impossible for Quagsire to gain the upper hand in a direct exchange!

The two Pokemon remained on the stone pillar and traded attack after attack. Within only a few breaths, they had already clashed several times!

As the number and frequency of their attacks increased, Quagsire suffered repeated damage, but Blastoise also took several solid hits.

This proved that Quagsire was genuinely strong enough to trouble Blastoise. Zhe clearly had not been idle, either. He had studied Blastoise's fighting style and characteristics as well.

Unfortunately, a gap still separated the two Pokemon, and no tactic could make up for it!

Finally, Blastoise and Quagsire both used Aqua Tail and swung their tails heavily into each other. With a tremendous crack, the water surrounding their tails exploded into spray and rained down through the air. The clash appeared evenly matched, but Blastoise was clearly superior. While Quagsire struggled to regain its footing, Blastoise closed in again and defeated it in one decisive rush!

Splash...

Quagsire toppled backward into the water.

After one look at the unconscious Quagsire, the referee promptly raised his flag and announced the result.

Despite a few twists along the way, Ethan had won the first battle with relative ease.

The audience found the outcome both unexpected and perfectly reasonable.

After all, Ethan was the Indigo League champion. It was only natural for him to win. They simply had not expected Zhe, the tournament's second favorite, to cause him so little trouble.

Was the difference in strength really that great?

In the Trainer's command area, Ethan quietly breathed a sigh of relief as Zhe recalled Quagsire with a helpless expression.

The victory might have looked easy, but the battle had put him under considerable pressure. After its early setbacks, Quagsire had erupted with tremendous fighting spirit in the middle and late stages, even recovering from its disadvantage for a time!

Fortunately, Ethan had prevailed in the end without encountering any serious danger.

While waiting for Zhe to send out his second Pokemon, his ears suddenly caught several familiar voices from the nearby stands.

Turning around, he saw Erika, Misty, Ash, and Brock sitting in the second row and waving enthusiastically at him!

Compared with his earlier matches, they had been fortunate enough to secure excellent seats this time, allowing Ethan to spot them at a glance.

Even more amusingly, Ash's Pikachu and Misty's Togepi each held a little fan in one hand. They bounced up and down as they cheered him on!

Ethan answered them with a broad smile, then turned back toward his opponent.

Zhe had already taken out his second Poke Ball. He drew a deep breath, lifted the ball to his lips, and murmured something to it as though performing a prayer before battle.

Is he preparing to risk everything?

Ethan crossed his arms over his chest without lowering his guard in the slightest.

The more critical the moment, the more sharply he could focus. Even if his opponent displayed a hundred and twenty percent of his strength, Ethan would give him no opportunity!

Come on. Let me see the last of your power!

Only after a long while did Zhe throw the Poke Ball forward. A flash of light revealed a Feraligatr standing upon the stone pillar.

As the final evolution of Totodile, one of Johto's three starter Pokemon, Feraligatr was extremely popular with the region's Trainers. Part of that popularity came from its appearance, which managed to look cool and goofy at once. The other reason, naturally, was its strength!

Feraligatr resembled a crocodile standing on two legs. Blue scales covered its body, together with rectangular plates of armor that strengthened its defense. Compared with its unevolved forms, its forelimbs had grown far more powerful, giving it a much more imposing attack.

Although this pure Water-type Pokemon usually moved at a slow, leisurely pace, it became too fast for the eye to follow when lunging at prey!

Its huge body was difficult to support on land, but by crouching low and driving itself forward with its powerful hind legs, it could move across the ground at great speed. In battle, it opened its jaws wide to intimidate an opponent, kicked off with its strong hind legs, and charged with astonishing speed. It could also catch prey in its enormous, powerful jaws, then whip its neck around and tear the victim apart.

Compared with Ethan's Blastoise, Feraligatr's overall capabilities were no worse; the two Pokemon merely emphasized different strengths. Since both were also pure Water types, their physical attributes alone made the outcome extremely difficult to predict.

Of course, a Pokemon battle depended on more than physical ability. Experience, momentum, and execution all mattered, as did whether the Trainers commanded properly. Even the battlefield and the spectators could greatly affect a match.

That was why many Pokemon performed exceptionally well under ordinary circumstances, only to collapse at a major tournament. Their state of mind affected how well they could display their strength.

But Blastoise had traveled with Ethan for a long time, excelled at major competitions, and spent plenty of time maturing at Cerise Park. Ethan was certain it could defeat this Feraligatr!

At the referee's signal, the second battle officially began.

Before Ethan could give an order, Feraligatr launched an all-out assault.

With his back against the wall, Zhe showed an enormous desire to attack. Under his command, Feraligatr erupted with even more astonishing power!

It flattened itself against the surface and drove all four limbs through the water like a true crocodile. In the blink of an eye, it closed the distance to Blastoise, then attacked ferociously again without even pausing for breath.

At first, Blastoise tried to defend and counterattack. Feraligatr, however, was willing to trade injury for injury and completely ignored whatever damage it might suffer!

The tactic worked. Blastoise was forced entirely onto the defensive. Fortunately, defense was already one of its specialties. Iron Defense, Protect, and the exceptional Withdraw sealed off Feraligatr's attacks without leaving a gap.

As time passed, however, Blastoise inevitably began to struggle under the pressure.

Like its Trainer, Feraligatr seemed to have staked everything on this battle. It ignored its rapidly dwindling stamina, a fire burning in its eyes as it attacked, attacked, and attacked again!

The assault came so quickly that the instant Blastoise blocked one move, another followed. It had no energy left to counterattack!

Even when it used Rapid Spin, Feraligatr merely dove underwater to avoid the move, causing Blastoise to waste its own strength instead.

The sight immediately stirred the spectators into a commotion.

Since Ethan entered the tournament, his Pokemon had always appeared overwhelmingly strong and defeated every opponent by an enormous margin. Now that the semifinals had arrived, someone had finally managed to suppress his momentum!

Perhaps suppress was not quite accurate, but Feraligatr was undeniably attacking without pause while Blastoise scrambled desperately to defend itself!

The audience brightened and instinctively sat straighter, eager to see whether Feraligatr could defeat Blastoise. Even Ash, Misty, and their companions watched wide-eyed, too tense to breathe!

On the field, Ethan narrowed his eyes.

Feraligatr's performance had caught both him and Erika's group by surprise. It had never fought like this in its previous matches. Its style now was completely different.

Zhe had clearly been driven into a corner and changed his approach, casting aside every reservation to risk everything on one desperate assault!

Ethan carefully searched for a weakness in Feraligatr's offense.

Passively taking a beating did not suit him. If the battle continued like this, Feraligatr would probably exhaust itself and stop attacking first. But Ethan could not call it a proper victory if he merely waited for his opponent to collapse from fatigue.

This was the moment to test his ability as a Trainer!

After observing for a while longer, he finally found an opportunity.

The two Pokemon's fierce battle and flying attacks had caused an enormous commotion. Neither side had overcome the other, but the stone pillar beneath them could not withstand such abuse. Without anyone noticing, it had slowly begun to crack!

The fracture was subtle, but it presented an undeniable danger. Better still, it faced Ethan directly, while Zhe could not see it at all.

An idea flashed through Ethan's mind. "Blastoise, stomp your foot, now!"

Blastoise froze for an instant, unable to understand the command. Its absolute trust in its Trainer allowed no hesitation, however. It raised its right foot and brought it down with all its might.

Crack!

Blastoise's body was already extremely heavy. Added to the force of its stomp, that weight shattered the pillar's once-flat surface and opened a large gap!

Both Pokemon instantly lost their balance and began to fall toward the water.

Blastoise had been mentally prepared. It merely stumbled, then used its weight to stand firm upon the pillar. Feraligatr, by comparison, was caught completely by surprise and fell straight into the water!

The sudden difference in elevation gave Blastoise a chance to breathe and sounded the beginning of Ethan's counterattack.

Following the principle of striking an enemy while it was down, Blastoise attacked Feraligatr from above. Water blasted repeatedly from the cannons on its back, striking Feraligatr several times. It struggled in the water but could not climb out, and finally had no choice but to dive below the surface.

Hiding underwater forever was impossible. After Feraligatr remained submerged for a while, Blastoise still revealed no weakness and made no attempt to pursue it. Left with no alternative, Zhe ordered Feraligatr to surface and try to climb back onto the pillar.

Unfortunately, it could no longer approach Blastoise.

The consequences of Feraligatr's earlier frenzy had also begun to show. Its stamina was nearly exhausted, and it had barely climbed onto the pillar before it began panting heavily.

Zhe's expression changed as he realized what was happening.

Ethan had no intention of letting such an opportunity escape!

At his command, Blastoise charged forward and slammed brutally into Feraligatr!

The impact sent Feraligatr tumbling backward. With a loud splash, it fell unconscious into the water just like its partner Quagsire...

Chapter 443: His Opponent Is About to Have a Bad Day

Blastoise had once again defeated two opponents by itself, and its outstanding performance successfully carried Ethan into the final.

The loser left the field in dejection, while the victor received a thunderous ovation from the spectators. Misty's voice rose above all the others, loud enough for Ethan to hear clearly even from some distance away.

When he looked toward her, he saw her fair, slender arm waving excitedly above the crowd as she shouted herself nearly hoarse!

But his attention was soon drawn to Erika beside her, gazing at him with eyes as gentle as water.

Their eyes met, and for some reason, both looked away at the same time.

They could each clearly sense that the longer they traveled together and the more time they spent at each other's side, the more a different sort of emotion wound itself between them...

Ethan gently shook his head, gathered his thoughts, and recalled Blastoise into its Poke Ball.

He already had one foot on the trophy. All he needed to do now was defeat the winner between Trinity and the female Trainer facing her, and the Whirl Cup championship would be his.

Still, despite winning, Blastoise did not look particularly well.

The long series of battles since the preliminary round had left it covered in wounds.

That could not be helped. The injuries had accumulated across many matches, especially during Feraligatr's frenzied assault just now. Blastoise had blocked most of those attacks, but they had still left far too many marks across its body.

The final would take place that afternoon. Judging by Blastoise's condition, even emergency treatment at the Pokemon Center might not restore it to normal in time.

Will I really have to use Gyarados in the final?

After leaving the arena, Ethan met Erika and the others outside, and the group immediately hurried to the Pokemon Center.

When he mentioned his concerns about the final along the way, Erika, Ash, and Brock all looked eager instead.

If Blastoise could not compete, so much the better!

They truly wanted to see Ethan's red Gyarados battle. All three hoped to witness its strength for themselves and discover how far it had developed!

Their reaction left Ethan able to do nothing but smile helplessly.

These people certainly enjoyed the excitement when they were not the ones in trouble!

Even so, Ethan knew perfectly well that if Blastoise continued fighting, it probably could not endure two complete battles the way it had before.

Sigh. It looks like I have no choice but to prepare to send out the red Gyarados...

Once they reached the Pokemon Center, Ethan approached the front desk and handed Blastoise's Poke Ball to Nurse Joy.

He watched her enter the treatment room. While they waited, the group sat in the lobby and watched Trinity's match on a television mounted on the wall.

Just as in her battle with Misty, Trinity used two different Pokemon in the two rounds. She won cleanly by the same two-to-zero score.

The match made it clear that a real gap in strength separated Trinity from her opponent.

Ethan smiled. "It looks like I'll be facing Trinity next. When she first approached us, I could tell she was strong. I never expected her to actually fight her way all the way into the final!"

Erika nodded and analyzed the matchup. "Judging by their strength and their performances in the tournament, there isn't much difference between Trinity and Zhe. But her Chinchou has a major advantage on this kind of Water-type battlefield, especially against other Water-type Pokemon. You need to be very careful!"

"I understand. I'll watch out for it."

At that moment, Misty suddenly leaned closer and whispered sweetly into Ethan's ear, "Ethan, Miss Trinity was the one who eliminated me. You have to avenge me this time, okay?"

Before Ethan could answer, Ash curled his lip from the side.

"Come on, Misty. You lost to Miss Trinity, so you should be the one to settle the score. Why ask someone else to avenge you?"

Slow-witted Ash had clearly failed to understand. Misty might have said that she wanted Ethan to avenge her, but her expression and movements showed that she was really acting spoiled with him.

Ash's interruption shattered the mood and immediately angered Misty. She turned and glared at him, all traces of the gentle, affectionate girl she had been beside Ethan disappearing!

"None of your business! Hmph! Don't forget that you're the loser I defeated in the round of sixteen. If you're unhappy about it, remember to come get revenge on me next time!"

"Darn it, Misty!"

Her words struck a sore spot and infuriated Ash, but his defeat was a fact, leaving him without the confidence to argue.

"Just you wait! The next time there's a tournament like this, I'll definitely beat you!"

Misty raised her chin and dismissed the threat with disdain. "Got it. I'll be looking forward to it!"

With Ash and Misty present, the atmosphere was destined never to become dull.

While the two continued bickering, everyone ate lunch in the Pokemon Center's restaurant. They had barely set down their bowls and utensils when Nurse Joy's voice sounded over the announcement system.

"Mr. Ethan Vale, please come to the front desk. Your Pokemon has finished recovering."

The announcement played several times. By the third repetition, Ethan and the others had already reached the front desk.

When she saw him, Nurse Joy presented a tray and handed Blastoise's Poke Ball back to him.

"Mr. Ethan Vale, your Blastoise's treatment is complete. However, I could only heal its wounds. Battling for several days in a row has left it mentally exhausted, so I recommend giving it a longer rest."

"I understand. Thank you for the warning."

Ethan accepted the Poke Ball and sighed softly to himself.

It appeared that sending Gyarados into battle truly was unavoidable. He could only hope the next match would not leave Trinity with any lasting psychological trauma...

After what had happened with Aya, Ethan was reluctant to offend another female Trainer in the same fashion.

...

At half past one that afternoon, Ethan parted from Erika and the others and entered the competitors' waiting room alone.

He spotted Trinity the moment he entered.

She was sitting on a sofa with her eyes closed. At the sound of approaching footsteps, she slowly opened them.

"You're here?"

Meeting his opponent before the match felt rather awkward. They were hardly familiar with each other, and in a short while, Ethan would probably have to defeat her in a fairly brutal manner.

All he could do was nod politely. Inwardly, he complained about how unreliable the organizers were. If this had been the Silver Conference or another major tournament, the competitors would certainly have been placed in separate waiting rooms. They would never have been allowed to meet beforehand like this!

Fortunately, Trinity paid no attention to his reserved attitude. She rose, walked over to him, and offered a friendly smile.

"According to our earlier agreement, I've now defeated Misty and successfully reached the final. It seems we're destined to decide the winner on the battlefield!"

Ethan had gone from being the challenger to the person others sought to challenge. That proved both the growth of his strength and the results of his journey!

There was nothing wrong with becoming someone else's goal. The more people challenged him, the stronger he would become!

But...

Ethan smiled bitterly to himself.

The friendlier Trinity acted now, the guiltier he would feel once the battle was over.

Sigh. You have no idea what's about to happen. I really hope you can remain this calm after the match...

Chapter 444: Battling Trinity

Looking at the anticipation on Trinity's face, Ethan could hardly bear what was coming. He carefully chose his words and tried to sound as polite as possible. Perhaps then, after Gyarados entered the field, she would not resent him quite so much.

"Miss Trinity, defeating Misty and reaching the final proves that you're an exceptionally capable Trainer. I'm looking forward to our match and hope we can both display our true abilities and give it everything we have. That said, if some accident occurs during the battle or something gets a little out of control, I hope you'll be understanding."

Ethan had phrased the warning as tactfully as possible, but Trinity clearly failed to grasp its true meaning.

"Naturally." She smiled faintly, then grew serious. "Since you've put it that way, Mr. Ethan Vale, I'll be honest too. I don't like admitting it, but you're the strongest Trainer I've ever met! I don't believe I can defeat you, but you won't win easily either!"

Seeing her fighting spirit burn so brightly, Ethan hesitated, then decided to be more direct.

"Um... Can you promise me one thing?"

Trinity froze at his suddenly solemn manner.

"Hmm? What is it?"

Ethan drew a deep breath and said with complete seriousness, "Please promise me that no matter what happens during this battle, you won't hold me responsible afterward..."

Trinity: "?"

...

The final was scheduled for two in the afternoon.

Bang! Bang! Bang...

As the appointed time approached, fireworks once again erupted above the arena. In the daylight, no one could clearly see their flames or patterns, leaving only the sound of explosions rolling across the sky. Even so, the display brought the atmosphere inside the colosseum to its peak.

Everyone waited eagerly for the final to begin.

On the ceremonial platform, the beautiful Sea Priestess Maya stepped forward in a flowing white gauze dress. She offered her blessing to the two final competitors of the tournament.

"After several days of competition, the triennial Whirl Cup has finally reached its championship match, and this battle will determine our new Sea Hero! Both Trainers have already left a deep impression on us with their brilliant performances. Now, let the sea grant them its blessing! May they show us an even more magnificent battle!"

Her voice traveled clearly through the speakers to every listener. As her final words faded, she raised her scepter high. The Sea Spirit once again released a dazzling light that quickly enveloped the entire colosseum, further igniting the crowd's enthusiasm!

On the battlefield, Ethan and Trinity stood in the command areas on opposite sides.

Unlike the semifinal and every preceding round, the final allowed each Trainer to use three Pokemon. That would make the match even more intense, but for Ethan, it was hardly good news.

Apart from Blastoise and his red Gyarados, he would have to include Suicune simply to field three Pokemon. The moment Suicune appeared, it would cause an unprecedented sensation. Ethan doubted it would take until the following day for his name to spread across half of Johto through the internet. Half an hour would probably be enough!

I have no desire to become famous that way. I'd better finish this as early as possible...

At the referee's signal, both Trainers released their Pokemon simultaneously.

Blue light flashed. Ethan naturally sent out Blastoise, while Chinchou appeared on the stone pillar in front of Trinity!

Chinchou had defeated Misty and many other opponents in the earlier rounds. It was no exaggeration to say that Trinity could never have reached the final without its contributions!

But...

Ethan raised an eyebrow.

She's using it right from the start?

Chinchou was the Pokemon with the greatest advantage on this battlefield, yet Trinity had chosen to lead with it. Without knowing what Ethan's final two Pokemon would be, she had adopted an extremely risky strategy in the hope of defeating as many of his team as possible.

While Ethan admired her courage and determination, he could not help worrying a little for Blastoise.

He had no certainty of victory against an Electric-type Pokemon, especially with Blastoise in poor condition. The situation could hardly have been worse.

No matter how many disadvantages he faced, however, he would never lose courage before the battle even began!

Once both sides were ready, the referee swept down his flag, and the championship match officially began!

From the opening exchange, Ethan tried to keep Blastoise out of the water and prevent its body from becoming wet. It remained on a stone pillar, turned the cannons on its back, and repeatedly launched ranged attacks at Chinchou.

Chinchou spat out a stream of water in return, but when the two attacks collided in midair, its stream was scattered with ease!

If they competed using only Water-type moves, Chinchou was clearly no match for Blastoise, the so-called mobile water cannon!

Trinity naturally understood Ethan's plan. She smiled lightly, stopped wasting time in a Water-type exchange, and directly ordered Chinchou to gather electricity!

If it could not compete in overall strength, it would use its type advantage and defeat Blastoise in one decisive assault!

Watching the mass of electricity grow larger in the sky, Ethan's eyelid twitched.

The situation truly looked grim...

On this aquatic battlefield, Blastoise had nowhere to evade or draw out the exchange. It could dive into the water, but an Electric-type move of that magnitude would still inflict tremendous damage.

Waiting helplessly for the attack was clearly impossible. After a moment's thought, Ethan ordered Blastoise to dive into the pool.

Compared with taking the lightning directly, the water would conduct and disperse its current, preventing the entire attack from concentrating on Blastoise.

Blastoise leaped from the stone pillar and struck the water with a tremendous splash. The instant it disappeared beneath the surface, a thick bolt of lightning crashed down!

Crack!

Thunder roared as the lightning shattered the stone pillar into pieces. Fortunately, it only grazed Blastoise and did not strike it directly.

The sight made Misty's heart clench. She had lost to the same kind of attack and feared that Ethan might follow in her footsteps.

Ethan, you have to win...

Trinity was unsurprised that the first attack had missed. She ordered Chinchou to gather electricity again. This time, its power grew even greater, and the attack aimed directly at the water!

I have to stop it immediately!

Ethan's gaze sharpened. At his command, Blastoise sped through the water toward Chinchou's stone pillar. It burst from the pool and slammed toward Chinchou!

Trinity had clearly anticipated such an attack.

Without the slightest panic, she issued her command, and electricity suddenly erupted across Chinchou's body!

The current flashed continuously around it, making the small Pokemon look extraordinarily dangerous!

In the stands, Ash and the others held their breath.

They understood the situation perfectly. If Blastoise continued its charge, it would inevitably touch the electricity surrounding Chinchou. Even if its attack succeeded, Blastoise itself would unquestionably suffer far more severe electrical damage!

Chapter 445: Is This Really His Gyarados?

Ethan naturally saw the electricity surrounding Chinchou, but he remained unmoved. He merely watched calmly as Blastoise slammed toward it!

Compared with Chinchou's small body, Blastoise was like a heavy truck charging forward with unstoppable force. Chinchou could never have dodged in time, and besides, it had no intention of trying.

The instant Blastoise struck, Chinchou's entire body flew seven or eight meters backward. It had no room to struggle before crashing into the water and throwing up layer after layer of spray.

The attack worked exactly as expected, but Blastoise suffered as well. Electricity from Chinchou coursed into it, leaving Blastoise standing in place with pain across its face. It had clearly taken far more damage than Chinchou.

Worse still, the electricity had apparently paralyzed Blastoise, greatly reducing its speed!

Under the present circumstances, that only made a bad situation worse.

Several seconds later, Chinchou's head emerged halfway from the water. It shook its body violently to clear the dizziness from the collision, then looked toward Blastoise as its two bulb-like antennae began rapidly gathering electricity!

Ethan shook his head. Before Chinchou could form the electrical attack, he took out a Poke Ball and recalled Blastoise.

"Oh? Faced with this unfavorable situation, Ethan has chosen not to persist and has voluntarily withdrawn his Pokemon!" The announcer's voice resounded across the battlefield, his excitement unmistakable. "Is it coming!? Is it finally coming? Has someone finally forced Ethan to reveal his second Pokemon!?"

No further encouragement was necessary. Trinity, the spectators, the announcer, the Sea Priestess, Erika, Misty, Ash, Brock, and everyone else focused their attention on Ethan!

At that moment, every eye in the colosseum was upon him!

In the Trainer's command area, Ethan lowered his head and silently returned Blastoise's Poke Ball to the pouch at his waist. Then he drew a deep breath and closed his hand around another Poke Ball that he had prepared long ago.

Since so many people want to see you, come on. Show the world your most ferocious side!

He hurled the Poke Ball with all his strength. Blue light flashed, and beneath the gaze of the entire audience, an enormous red Gyarados appeared, floating upon the water!

This was the first time it had entered the public eye since evolving into a red Gyarados!

Before anyone could even react to its immense size, a deafening roar erupted across the arena!

"ROAR!"

The sound overflowed with dominance, exploding beside everyone's ears as though it could shake heaven and earth. Most of the spectators instinctively covered their ears!

What astonishing presence!

Compared with an ordinary Gyarados, Ethan's Pokemon was unquestionably far more intimidating!

The cameramen closest to the battlefield felt it most keenly. The sudden roar startled them so badly that their bodies jerked, and several nearly dropped the cameras in their hands!

The announcer remained stunned for a long moment before finally returning to his senses and hurriedly beginning his introduction.

"Here it is! As expected, Ethan has sent out his Gyarados! This Pokemon performed brilliantly during both the Indigo League Conference and the Orange League. What kind of performance will it show us today...? Huh? Wait... Why is it red!?"

Only halfway through his introduction did the announcer notice that something was wrong. He frantically flipped through the information in his hands. Ethan had used Gyarados during both the Indigo League and the Orange Islands' Winner's Cup, but the records stated clearly that it had been an ordinary blue Gyarados. Yet this one...

"How strange... As far as I know, Ethan's Gyarados wasn't Shiny. Could this be one he caught recently? B-but... Other than their color, aren't Shiny Pokemon identical to ordinary members of their species? Why is this Gyarados so enormous!?"

The announcer was full of questions, but clearly no one could answer them. In fact, every spectator who knew something about Ethan was wondering the same thing.

Countless wondrous things happened in this world every day, but no one had ever heard of an ordinary Pokemon suddenly becoming Shiny!

Even if its color somehow changed, that would hardly make its body grow to such an outrageous size!

Moments ago, everyone had been filled with anticipation. Now their mouths hung open in astonishment, as though that alone could express the depth of their shock.

After releasing the red Gyarados, Ethan lowered his hand and stood calmly in place.

The spectators could not understand, but he knew that his red Gyarados was entirely different from a Shiny Gyarados. Its crimson scales represented even more ferocious powerand the finest product of Team Rocket's biotechnology!

Even from a distance, the red Gyarados inspired awe in everyone who saw it. But the person under the greatest pressure was undoubtedly Ethan's opponent, Trinity!

Standing in the command area on the opposite side, she felt her entire body turn cold beneath Gyarados's enormous red gaze. Every hair on her body stood on end!

What was this feeling?

Trinity owned a Gyarados herself and believed she knew the species well. Yet staring at the creature before her, she could only wonder what sort of monster it was.

Was this truly an ordinary Shiny Gyarados?

It was two or three times larger than her own Gyarados. Its voice and oppressive presence were both suffocating. Even every breath it took felt like the Grim Reaper gently dragging a scythe across her neck...

Goose bumps covered Trinity's body, and she shuddered. At that moment, an unexpected movement startled her back to awareness.

She looked down and discovered that Chinchou was trembling!

What? What's happening?

Is it frightened too?

As the red Gyarados's first target, Chinchou was shaking even more violently than its Trainer!

It had to tilt its head back merely to see its opponent's enormous face. Chinchou's entire body was not even as large as one of Gyarados's eyes...

"Chinchou, pull yourself together!"

Trinity called out several times. She was certain Chinchou had heard her, but its fear did not ease in the slightest. Her Pokemon even appeared ready to flee!

How can this be happening!?

Trinity understood that such a reaction meant Gyarados must possess the Intimidate Ability. Beyond that, the undisguised killing intent pouring from its body seemed almost tangible and was probably an even greater reason!

My goodness...

How could anyone possibly raise a Pokemon like this?

Chapter 446: A Bloody Scene Reappears

At the side of the field, the referee was the first person in the entire arena to recover. Seeing Trinity still frozen in shock, he hurriedly swept down his flag to signal the start of the battle.

Trinity hastily came to her senses. She forced herself to focus and issued a command, but no matter how loudly she called, Chinchou showed no response!

It's over!

The poor thing has been frightened out of its wits!

Trinity silently cried out in alarm. She immediately took out its Poke Ball and decisively recalled Chinchou.

I'd better let it rest inside for a while...

She sighed and raised her head. After studying the red Gyarados for a long moment with a complicated gaze, she appeared to reach a decision. A look of determination filled her face as she took out her second Poke Ball.

Blue light flashed, and a Gyarados appeared in the pool.

Trinity understood perfectly that an ordinary Pokemon would lose the contest of presence against Ethan's red Gyarados before the battle even began. It might be terrified into helplessness just like Chinchou. At this point, her only option was to confront the red Gyarados with her own!

Fortunately, her Gyarados also possessed the Intimidate Ability. It should be able to withstand the red Gyarados's pressure!

Unfortunately, that assumption was far too optimistic...

Like every other member of its species, Trinity's Gyarados roared when it appeared. Yet compared with the red Gyarados, its voice was unquestionably inferior. Then their gazes met, and Trinity clearly saw her Gyarados recoil despite itself!

What!?

Even Gyarados can't do it?

Trinity's expression changed. If even her Gyarados lost its courage before the battle, there would be no point continuing. She might as well surrender immediately!

Fortunately, it had not been completely frightened out of its wits. Although it recoiled at first, it soon straightened its body again. At the very least, it still appeared capable of resisting, which eased some of the tension in Trinity's heart.

Ethan naturally saw every detail of her Gyarados's reaction.

There were differences even between Gyarados!

No ordinary specimen could compare with his. This absolute monster had fought its way through brutal life-and-death struggles and then undergone further enhancement!

Once Trinity's Gyarados regained its fighting spirit, Ethan had no intention of giving her additional time to adjust.

"Go."

Ethan spoke softly. His low voice seemed unable to reach the red Gyarados across the distance and difference in elevation. Yet the Pokemon appeared connected to him in mind and spirit. Even from the slightest movement of his lips, it understood his intent.

The red Gyarados's enormous body plunged beneath the water, sending rings of waves across the surface.

Trinity's gaze sharpened. Rather than waiting helplessly, she ordered her own Gyarados underwater to search for the red Gyarados.

Currents surged below. On the enormous screen, the spectators could clearly see two shadows, one large and one small, collide beneath the surface!

An ordinary Gyarados was generally about six and a half meters long. That was already enormous compared with most other Pokemon. Yet judging by the two shadows now, the red Gyarados was fully three times its opponent's size. By that estimate, it had to be nearly twenty meters long!

What did that mean?

A six-and-a-half-meter Gyarados was comparable in length to a medium truck capable of carrying eight tons. The nearly twenty-meter red Gyarados was closer to one of the enormous, long and heavy trucks used for the largest loads.

Of course, the comparison was not entirely accurate. Their width hardly resembled that of a truck. More than anything, the description captured the overwhelming impression they created!

When the two Pokemon collided, the water's surface suddenly churned violently. Before the audience could see what had happened, spray exploded upward. The red Gyarados burst from the water with the other Gyarados pinned before it and continued driving it backward. They smashed through two stone pillars in succession before the red Gyarados finally crushed its opponent against the arena's thick outer wall!

Bang!

A web of cracks spread across the wall's stonework, demonstrating the red Gyarados's tremendous strength!

Both Pokemon were famous for their power, yet the red Gyarados had instantly overwhelmed one of its own species!

Before the fragments of the shattered pillars could even fall into the water, a wail of pain rang from Trinity's Gyarados!

While the audience still stared in shock at the red Gyarados's outrageous power, it opened its jaws and bit deeply into its opponent's neck!

Gyarados screamed again, even more miserably than before!

Trinity frowned. At first, she believed the red Gyarados was using Bite, but she immediately noticed something was wrong!

This was no move. It was simply tearing into its opponent with its teeth!

The announcer noticed the difference as well and cried out in disbelief, "What!? The red Gyarados is ripping the scales from Gyarados's body! What kind of move is this!?"

It tore away a large patch of scales. Bright red blood immediately sprayed from the wound and dyed the water beneath Gyarados crimson!

And the attack was not over. The red Gyarados opened its enormous mouth once more and bit into the other side of Gyarados's neck!

Cries of alarm erupted from the stands!

Even Sea Priestess Maya shot to her feet on the ceremonial platform!

No one present had ever witnessed such a bloody scene!

How could this be called a Pokemon battle? It was a primal struggle to the death!

Across the history of Pokemon competition, some ferocious Pokemon had certainly appeared. Yet even those creatures generally followed the rules of battle and used the familiar moves everyone recognized.

But now...

The red Gyarados's fighting style revealed nothing but raw instinct!

There was no technique whatsoever. It simply crushed everything with power!

After only one exchange, Gyarados, a species renowned for its ferocity, had completely lost the ability to fight. The sight demonstrated just how powerful the red Gyarados truly was!

In the command area, Ethan also knew it was time to end the battle. If he allowed this to continue, Trinity's Gyarados would probably die on the spot.

He lightly snapped his fingers. The red Gyarados immediately released its opponent at the far edge of the battlefield and ceased its attack. It dove beneath the water, and when it surfaced again, it had already returned to Ethan's side.

This astonished the spectators all over again!

In their experience, the more ferocious a Pokemon was, the less likely it would be to obey its Trainer. Once battle overwhelmed its reason, it would never stop until its stamina was exhausted!

So why did Ethan's red Gyarados obey him so perfectly?

It defied all common sense!

How had he possibly raised it?

Ethan did not know that Maya was watching from the ceremonial platform. Her thoughtful gaze moved repeatedly between him and the red Gyarados, as though she were deciding something...

Chapter 447: Why Doesn't Hypnosis Work?

Trinity recalled Gyarados with a bloodless face. The Pokemon looked utterly miserable, most of its body stained crimson. It was clearly incapable of continuing the battle.

Besides, could that really be called a battle?

At least in Trinity's entire life, she had never encountered anything like it.

To the side, the referee raised his flag and announced that Gyarados was unable to battle.

This was different from Ethan voluntarily recalling Blastoise. Blastoise had not lost. It still possessed the strength to fight and could return to the field whenever Ethan chose. Gyarados, however, truly could no longer continue.

It had not yet fallen unconscious, but the missing scales exposed large patches of bloody flesh. If the battle continued, it might die in the arena. The referee could never stand by and allow that. Such an outcome would be a major competition accident, and besides the storm of public criticism, he would be held responsible as well.

In her command area, Trinity also knew how dire Gyarados's condition was. She raised no objection to the referee's decision.

She drew a deep breath and looked up at the red Gyarados once more, meeting its blood-red eyes again!

After witnessing the last battle, some of her fear had eased. She still could not face the monster with her usual composure, but she was no longer as terrified as before.

However...

This Gyarados was far too powerful. How could she possibly break through the present situation?

Trinity hesitated.

She had intended to send Chinchou back into the match. Its Electric-type moves would inflict quadruple damage upon a Water- and Flying-type Gyarados, so it should have a chance to defeat the red Gyarados!

But then she remembered that Chinchou had lost even the will to fight in its presence and had been unable to move at all. Helpless, she abandoned the idea.

Forget it. I'd better give Chinchou more time to recover. I can only keep it as my final trump card.

With complicated emotions written across her face, Trinity took out her third Poke Ball.

She threw it, and after blue light flashed, a Poliwrath appeared before the crowd.

The surrounding spectators looked at one another in confusion.

They could not understand Trinity's choice for her third Pokemon.

If even Gyarados was no match for Ethan's red Gyarados, what use could this Poliwrath possibly be?

What they did not know was that Trinity had no desire to make this choice either. She understood that Poliwrath could never defeat the red Gyarados, but it was her last remaining Water-type Pokemon. At this point, she had no choice but to risk everything and hope Poliwrath could delay the battle long enough for Chinchou to recover its courage!

On the opposite side, Ethan also chose not to change Pokemon.

With Chinchou no longer on the field, Blastoise could have returned. But now that the red Gyarados had already revealed itself, there was no need to hide it any longer.

Let's end the battle like this!

When the match resumed, Trinity adopted a different strategy.

She would maintain the greatest distance possible!

At her command, Poliwrath immediately climbed to the top of a towering stone pillar and attacked the red Gyarados from above.

A Water Gun burst from the spiral on its belly. The stream traced a slight curve through the air and struck the red Gyarados squarely on its enormous head.

But the attack seemed no more than a tickle. The red Gyarados showed no reaction whatsoever. It did not even narrow its eyes!

The red Gyarados swam toward Poliwrath's stone pillar, sending circles of ripples across the water.

The response appeared to reveal something to Trinity.

Hmm? It isn't counterattacking from a distance?

Her eyes brightened. She could not help wondering whether the red Gyarados had sacrificed its ranged moves in exchange for its extraordinary strength.

After all, Poliwrath was the evolved form of Poliwhirl, and every one of its abilities was considerably stronger. A Water Gun from Poliwrath should never have been so weak that another Pokemon could simply ignore it.

The red Gyarados's indifference was therefore highly suspicious!

Its performance against the other Gyarados also seemed to support the theory, giving Trinity a tremendous boost in confidence.

Within a few breaths, the red Gyarados arrived before the pillar.

It gave the structure a light bump, and the entire stone pillar shattered. The instant it began to collapse, Poliwrath took a running step, leaped high, and sprang toward the nearest pillar.

Poliwrath was modeled after the frogs of Earth, and its movement now demonstrated that resemblance perfectly.

The pillars stood five or six meters apart, but Poliwrath crossed the gap with ease. The instant it found its footing, it spun around and immediately fired Hypnosis at the red Gyarados!

The waves of light representing Hypnosis raced across the red Gyarados and struck it squarely on the head. Yet just as with Water Gun, the red Gyarados did not react at all!

What!?

This time, Trinity was not the only person stunned. Even the announcer sounded astonished!

"How is this possible!? Why doesn't Hypnosis affect the red Gyarados!? Is it holding some kind of item?"

The stands erupted into discussion. Ash was equally confused. He looked toward his companions and asked, "That's strange. Why isn't Ethan's Gyarados affected by Hypnosis?"

Brock rubbed his chin as possibility after possibility flashed through his mind. Finally, he offered his answer.

"Maybe it has something to do with the red Gyarados's emotions."

Ash and Misty immediately turned toward him.

"Its emotions?"

"That's right." Brock nodded and continued, "You both know that Hypnosis is a Psychic-type move. It affects the brain and forces whoever it hits into a sleeping state. But Pokemon like Gyarados are usually filled with rage, and that powerful emotion affects their minds. It can easily counteract the effect of Hypnosis!"

The explanation seemed quite reasonable. At least Ash and Misty both believed that had to be the cause.

But was simple anger truly the only reason?

Compared with an ordinary Gyarados, Ethan's red Gyarados obeyed his commands far more readily. It displayed no sign of having lost its reason at all!

At the side, Erika pondered for a moment before joining the conversation. "That isn't entirely accurate. Plenty of examples show that Hypnosis can still affect ordinary Gyarados and put them to sleep. If it failed now, the real reason is probably that this red Gyarados is so unusual!"

Because the red Gyarados is unusual?

Everyone focused on it again. Just as Erika had said, no matter how they looked at this Pokemon, it simply could not be judged by common sense...

No matter what happened around it, nothing seemed particularly strange anymore...

Chapter 448: It Was Only Bite

The battle continued on the field.

After discovering that Hypnosis had no effect, Trinity made an immediate decision and ordered Poliwrath to continue attacking with Water Gun.

The stream curved through the air and once again struck the red Gyarados with perfect accuracy.

But the red Gyarados completely ignored the damage from Water Gun. Even when the pillar collapsed and countless chunks of stone crashed against its body, it paid them no attention!

Trinity clicked her tongue inwardly.

This is completely absurd...

Precisely because she also owned a Gyarados, Trinity understood how terrifying this red Gyarados truly was.

Water Gun was one thing. Due to the type matchup, it could inflict only half its usual damage upon a Water-type Pokemon. But the falling rocks caused very real physical damage!

Gyarados did not possess outstanding physical defense. Being struck by so many rocks and continuing as though nothing had happened defied all common sense!

Even an armored vehicle struck from above by so many enormous stones could hardly escape without a mark!

Water Gun might not be causing any visible damage for now, but Trinity firmly believed that if Poliwrath used it often enough, the red Gyarados would eventually reach its limit!

Every little bit of stamina it consumed would help!

In the water, the red Gyarados turned and swam after its escaping prey. Its massive head remained half submerged, red eyes fixed upon its opponent as its enormous serpentine body approached Poliwrath little by little. The pressure was overwhelming!

Once it reached Poliwrath's pillar, the red Gyarados raised its head again and gave the structure a light bump!

Bang!

It did not appear to use much force, but before its immense body, the stone pillar collapsed almost instantly.

At the top, Poliwrath repeated its previous maneuver. The moment Gyarados struck, it took a running start, leaped again, and sprang toward another nearby pillar.

This pillar stood slightly farther away, nearly ten meters from the first. Fortunately, Poliwrath's powerful legs and running momentum allowed it to land on the very top by the narrowest of margins.

Ignoring the falling debris, the red Gyarados turned around and began closing in on Poliwrath once more.

It appeared neither anxious nor hurried, moving like a remarkably patient hunter.

By contrast, Poliwrath barely found its footing before frantically launching another Water Gun. When the red Gyarados drew near, it had no choice but to leap toward yet another pillar.

This was already the fourth pillar beneath its feet. With virtually no time to breathe, it moved, attacked, moved again, and attacked again without pause. Sweat poured from its body. Worse, the next pillar was even farther away than the previous ones, a full fourteen or fifteen meters!

That distance was too great to cross with a simple jump!

Sure enough, Poliwrath began to fall after covering barely more than half the gap!

Fortunately, just before hitting the water, it caught the base of the pillar. It hurriedly climbed the rest of the way with both arms and legs.

But the delay allowed the red Gyarados to close in. This time, Poliwrath did not dare attack. Before it could even catch its breath, it was forced to leap toward the next pillar.

It resembled a frog fleeing in utter panic, but no matter where it went, it could never escape the enormous shadow looming over it!

Stone pillars fell one after another under the red Gyarados's attacks. Soon, every pillar had been destroyed except for the last one beneath Poliwrath.

Poliwrath stood atop the remains of a collapsed pillar and panted heavily. It was completely isolated now, with nowhere left to escape!

The spectators placed themselves in Trinity's position and swallowed nervously, feeling her profound fear and helplessness!

Where could Poliwrath go now?

They looked across the battlefield. Poliwrath's half was filled with piles of broken stone submerged beneath the water. More than a dozen intact pillars still stood on Ethan's side, but reaching them required crossing most of the field. With its remaining stamina, could Poliwrath truly make it?

Even if it possessed enough strength to swim across, the red Gyarados would inevitably catch it!

Difficult. Far too difficult!

Everyone had believed that forcing Ethan to withdraw Blastoise would open a clear road for Trinity and reveal the first light of victory. Instead, she had encountered a boss monster!

Worse, this was the kind of ultimate boss that could not be defeated at all!

Trinity's face was creased with worry, but the battle did not bend to her wishes. Under her helpless gaze, the red Gyarados swam toward the final stone pillar beneath Poliwrath!

Poliwrath looked toward its Trainer and saw the deep concern in her eyes. Yet it understood that with so little stamina remaining, it no longer possessed the strength to keep fighting...

The red Gyarados reached the last pillar. But contrary to the audience's expectations, it did not destroy the structure.

Instead, most of its body rose from the water. Its enormous form climbed higher and higher above the surface until its head towered well past the top of the pillar. Only then did it stop!

At last, the audience gained a true sense of just how enormous the red Gyarados was!

Less than half of its body had emerged, yet it already stood a full head taller than the stone pillar rising from the water!

The red Gyarados looked down upon Poliwrath at the pillar's summit and suddenly opened its enormous jaws. A deafening roar erupted. Poliwrath felt as though a moisture-laden hurricane had struck it and was forced onto all fours simply to keep from being blown off the pillar!

To the spectators, this hardly resembled a Pokemon battle. It looked more like a tiny human attempting to fight some colossal beast!

In the command area, Trinity's heart rose into her throat.

Poliwrath...

By now, she could already imagine the fate waiting for Poliwrath. Even so, she did not choose to recall it.

Defeat was inevitable, and she was deeply worried for her Pokemon, but surrendering outright was impossible!

As a Pokemon Trainer, Trinity possessed her own dignity and limits. With so many spectators watching and the championship at stake, surrendering to an unbeatable opponent would turn her into a mere backdrop. No matter how highly Ethan was praised afterward, everyone who remembered this match would mock her!

Yielding without a fight has never been my style!

"Poliwrath, use Take Down!"

Trinity shook her head and loudly issued her final command.

At the sound of her voice, Poliwrath gathered the last of its strength and launched a charge at the red Gyarados with no thought for its own survival!

It ran forward in long strides, moving faster with every step. Then it leaped and slammed toward the red Gyarados's neck!

For most Pokemon, the neck was one of the body's weak points!

Faced with the attack, the red Gyarados merely opened its enormous mouth, revealed its sharp teeth, and lowered its head. In a single bite, it swallowed the charging Poliwrath whole!

"Poliwrath!"

In an instant, Trinity's scream was the only sound echoing over the entire arena...

"This is terrible!" the announcer's voice suddenly rose. "Poliwrath has been eaten by the red Gyarados!"

The audience clearly saw the red Gyarados close its mouth. A second later, its jaws made an unmistakable chewing motion!

The crowd erupted. People sprang to their feet, unable to believe their eyes!

Was this truly still a Pokemon battle?

Amid the chaos, Ethan alone remained standing calmly in place.

Of course he could see the audience's reaction, but they were imagining far too much. No matter how ferocious his red Gyarados was, Ethan would never train it to behave that way!

Unlike a wild Pokemon, it had long been caught and trained by a Trainer and had left its most primitive habits behind. How could it possibly do such a thing?

It had taken Poliwrath into its mouth only because the red Gyarados was so enormous. The Dark-type move Bite had simply become a much more savage-looking act of swallowing and chewing!

Sure enough, several seconds later, Gyarados abruptly opened its mouth. With a forceful spit, it sent Poliwrath flying out whole.

Like a deflated ball, Poliwrath tumbled onto the stone pillar with blood covering its body and fell completely unconscious.

Only after seeing the red Gyarados spit Poliwrath out did the audience release a collective breath and sit down again with lingering fear. Even Trinity could not resist wiping the cold sweat from her forehead.

They were not making a fuss over nothing. The red Gyarados was simply too frightening, causing everyone to instinctively imagine the worst!

Chapter 449: Surely He Doesn't Have a Suicune Too?

With Poliwrath defeated, Chinchou was the only Pokemon Trinity had left that could still battle.

Watching Gyarados and Poliwrath meet such brutal ends one after another sent her heart plunging to the bottom.

To be honest, after those two battles, Trinity no longer held any hope that she could defeat Ethan.

Even if she somehow defeated the red Gyarados, what would that accomplish?

Ethan still had an exceptionally powerful Blastoise waiting for her. And apart from those two Pokemon, who knew whether he had an even more outrageous monster?

A Pokemon as overwhelmingly powerful as the red Gyarados was not even Ethan's final trump card. Trinity genuinely could not imagine what formidable opponent might appear after it!

A weak Pokemon certainly would not catch this man's attention. So what could it be?

Surely he doesn't have a Suicune too?

The thought made her laugh.

What nonsense am I imagining?

How could anyone encounter and capture Suicune so easily? Besides, perhaps even Suicune could not defeat a Gyarados this powerful!

Trinity brought her attention back to the battlefield and looked toward the red Gyarados again.

She had lost all hope of victory, but that did not mean she would surrender without resistance. Fortunately, Poliwrath had delayed the battle long enough to give Chinchou plenty of time to recover.

Now she could only place every remaining hope upon Chinchou and pray it had regained its composure!

At the very least, I have to give it everything I have and defeat this red Gyarados if I can. I need to recover a little dignity!

Even if I lose, I refuse to be swept aside this easily!

Trinity took out her first Poke Ball and threw it with all her strength. Blue light flashed, and Chinchou appeared upon the water once more!

After calming down inside its Poke Ball, Chinchou appeared far more composed than the first time it faced the red Gyarados. Yet that calm was only superficial. The instant its eyes met the red Gyarados's gaze again, its entire body began trembling against its will!

"Chinchou!" Trinity cupped both hands around her mouth and hurriedly encouraged it. "Don't let its presence frighten you! And don't look into its eyes!"

Chinchou quickly looked away. Sure enough, once it stopped meeting those terrifying eyes, it felt blood flow through its body again. The numbness and pounding in its chest faded. It could still feel the red Gyarados's cold gaze, but at least it was no longer too frightened to move!

Seeing this, Trinity quietly sighed in relief.

Chinchou still could not move as freely as usual, but as long as it did not flee and could continue the battle, she could ask for nothing more!

The referee waved his flag, officially beginning the fourth round!

At Trinity's command, Chinchou floated across the surface and swiftly swam to the side.

The red Gyarados had destroyed every stone pillar on this half of the battlefield. That left medium and large Pokemon with nowhere to stand, but for a small Pokemon like Chinchou, the devastation created a major advantage.

The piles of shattered stone provided endless obstacles it could use to maneuver around the red Gyarados!

Chinchou thrashed its body desperately and reached a heap of debris before the red Gyarados could catch it. In a panic, it slipped through a passage formed by two fallen stones and successfully escaped to the other side.

The red Gyarados was too large to pass through. It could only go around the rubble or smash through it, preventing it from catching Chinchou immediately.

That brief delay gave Chinchou an opportunity.

Both antennae erupted with dazzling light. A second later, an electrical current left their tips and shot toward the red Gyarados!

Crackle!

The electricity struck with perfect accuracy. Perhaps Chinchou had fired too hastily, or perhaps the red Gyarados's body was simply too enormous. The current failed to cover even its entire body before running out of power and dissipating!

The instant it hit, Trinity stared at the red Gyarados without blinking.

She wanted to see whether this terrifying red Gyarados shared the same Water and Flying typing as an ordinary Gyarados and therefore feared Electric-type moves just as much!

Unfortunately, the current had vanished too quickly for her to see any sign of pain. Still, the red Gyarados had paused slightly when struck, so the Electric-type attack had clearly produced some reaction!

Hmm... It seems to have worked, but it also doesn't appear to have done very much...

Was the last attack simply too brief and too weak?

Trinity was about to order Chinchou to use a stronger move, but the red Gyarados had already smashed the pile of rubble aside with its enormous body and appeared before Chinchou again.

This time, Chinchou did not wait for her command. It fled in panic toward another heap of broken stone.

This running battle involved no fierce exchanges of moves, so it was hardly spectacular. Even so, the spectators watched with intense concentration, afraid to miss the slightest detail!

Perhaps out of sympathy for the weaker side, most of the crowd once again placed themselves in Trinity's position. Whenever Chinchou narrowly escaped danger, they found themselves holding their breath for it!

Gulp...

In the stands, Misty unconsciously swallowed.

She was already afraid of Gyarados, and this red Gyarados terrified her even more. As Ethan's companion, she wanted to cheer for him and wanted him to avenge her loss. Yet she could not stop herself from worrying about Chinchou!

When Misty noticed the change in her loyalties, she first froze, then hurriedly reassured herself.

This isn't betraying Ethan! After all... after all, Chinchou is a Water-type Pokemon too. I want to become a Water Pokemon Master, so worrying about it is perfectly natural!

On the field, the red Gyarados had caught up to another pile of stone.

Beside a broken pillar, Chinchou made one agile turn, slipped away from the red Gyarados, and reached another safe position.

It hurriedly turned around and gathered its electrical power with all its strength. When the energy finally reached its peak, an enormous sphere of electricity formed between its antennae.

The terrifying monster approached again. Chinchou did not even have time to aim before hurling the electrical sphere at the red Gyarados in a panic!

The sphere flew through the air.

Perhaps the red Gyarados was simply too enormous to miss. Despite Chinchou's lack of aim, the attack still struck its body.

Crackle!

In an instant, an extraordinarily brilliant burst of light exploded across the red Gyarados!

Chapter 450: Final Victory

This attack was clearly far more effective than the last.

When the electrical light vanished, wisps of blue smoke rose from the red Gyarados's body. Electricity was racing through it while the moisture outside its scales evaporated, combining to create the visible smoke.

Trinity brightened at the sight.

The evidence proved that Electric-type moves truly held a major advantage against the red Gyarados!

No matter how unusual it looked, the red Gyarados was still a Water- and Flying-type Pokemon!

Now that Trinity knew it could be countered, several more attacks like that one would give her a real chance to win!

But before she could celebrate for long, the red Gyarados threw back its head and released a roar that shook heaven and earth!

"ROAR!"

The sound was deafening, making everyone instinctively cover their ears.

The attack had clearly enraged the red Gyarados. Its mind was no longer calm, and it became incomparably violent. Its entire presence changed, finally displaying the madness associated with the name Gyarados.

It fixed its prey with an unwavering stare and surged forward. Its enormous body smashed straight through the rubble, and it opened its jaws as it swam ferociously toward Chinchou!

Chinchou nearly lost its soul from fright. It immediately turned and fled.

Seeing it hide among another pile of rocks and attempt the same trick again, Ethan had no intention of giving it another opportunity.

Nice idea. You got away with that move once, but you think I'll let you do it again?

"Gyarados, stop chasing it. Use Twister!"

At its Trainer's voice, the red Gyarados, which had only just entered a violent frenzy, stopped immediately. The sight left the audience dumbfounded!

Its obedience was absolute!

Forget this terrifying red Gyaradoseven among ordinary Gyarados owned by other Trainers, how many could stop instantly after falling into a rage?

The red Gyarados raised its enormous head. Its anger receded as reason once again took control of its mind. Following Ethan's command, it used Twister in the water.

A gale instantly swept across the pool and formed a huge tornado. Then the water below began spinning with it, faster and faster, violently shaking the entire surface!

An enormous whirlpool appeared within the arena. It covered the entire battlefield and began drawing in seawater with tremendous force.

Anyone could see that Ethan intended to recreate the technique Ash's Kingler had used in an earlier match!

Kingler had used that tactic to create four small whirlpools and defeat Misty's Poliwhirl. Ash had still been eliminated by Misty in the end, but the memorable scene had remained a subject of excited discussion for quite some time.

Compared with Kingler's four small whirlpools, however, the single whirlpool created by the red Gyarados was clearly much larger and far more dangerous!

Trinity naturally remembered the earlier battle well. The moment she saw Ethan use this tactic, her expression changed dramatically!

So the red Gyarados had not sacrificed its moves after all!

With no time to think, she hurriedly shouted, "Chinchou! Find somewhere to hide!"

Chinchou had naturally seen the whirlpool. Even without Trinity's command, it desperately swam in the opposite direction!

Unfortunately, the red Gyarados had already destroyed every pillar on that half of the battlefield. The remaining piles of rubble were submerged in the pool. Even hiding behind them offered Chinchou no guarantee of safety.

The whirlpool's enormous range and suction soon caught Chinchou.

The red Gyarados was also inside the current, its eyes fixed unblinkingly upon its prey. Relying on its immense body, it completely ignored the whirlpool's pull and swam directly across the current toward Chinchou.

As the red Gyarados drew closer, Chinchou thrashed even harder in an attempt to escape. But it was simply too weak to resist the whirlpool's suction. After struggling a dozen times, the rushing water dragged it in.

The whirlpool even affected the command areas on both sides, repeatedly spraying water across Trinity's face.

The distance between the two Pokemon continued shrinking. Faced with such danger, Trinity gritted her teeth and made one final decision.

"Chinchou, use Discharge!"

Within the racing current, Chinchou stopped struggling and allowed the water to carry it toward the whirlpool's center. The instant it passed beside the red Gyarados, every trace of electricity within its body erupted and spread violently in all directions!

Crackle! Crackle!

Light flashed without pause, accompanied by the constant roar of electricity!

The red Gyarados bellowed. It neither dodged nor retreated, but simply opened its jaws and bit toward Chinchou.

The instant electricity struck the red Gyarados, its blood-filled jaws swallowed Chinchou whole!

Trinity closed her eyes in despair.

She had no idea whether Chinchou's final Discharge could defeat the red Gyarados. But once her Pokemon entered those enormous jaws, its prospects were unquestionably grim!

Electric light exploded across the red Gyarados. Once Chinchou disappeared into its mouth, however, the light quickly vanished from view. Even so, the spectators could still see Chinchou struggling inside through the gaps between Gyarados's teeth!

After what had happened with Poliwrath, everyone knew that being swallowed might look terrifying, but Chinchou would not truly be eaten. The knowledge reassured them somewhat.

Sure enough, just as the audience expected, Chinchou's struggles gradually weakened. After only a few breaths, it became completely still.

I've lost...

Trinity collapsed onto the ground, unable even to cry.

She had imagined such a wonderful outcome, but in the end, she failed to defeat this terrifying monster.

It's far too strong...

Her mind returned to Ethan's words before the match. Only now did she finally understand what he had meant.

No wonder he asked me not to hold him responsible. He knew this would happen all along...

But even if Trinity wanted to blame him and seek revenge, how could she ever defeat such a monster, no matter how much she trained her Pokemon?

At Ethan's signal, the red Gyarados opened its mouth and spat the battered Chinchou into the water.

Before Ethan could say anything to Trinity, countless ceremonial cannons fired around the arena, followed by the announcer's ringing voice!

"We have a new champion! Just as we predicted before the tournament, Ethan has seized victory in this year's Whirl Cup with overwhelming strength! Now, let us give him our loudest cheers and applause!"

Chapter 451: Awarding the Prizes

After the announcer finished speaking, the arena fell silent for a moment.

Two or three seconds later, the spectators suddenly awakened. They rose to their feet, applauded, and erupted into wave after wave of cheering!

They might have supported Trinity at times during the match, but once the battle ended and they escaped the red Gyarados's shadow, there was still only one competitor whom they recognized above all others and whom the crowd had most expected to win: Ethan.

Just as most people had confidently predicted before the tournament, Ethan had emerged victorious in the end.

Applause and cheers crashed over him like a tidal wave. Standing in the Trainer's command area with a smile on his face, Ethan waved to the surrounding spectators.

From his position, he could clearly see ceremonial fireworks constantly bursting overhead, the spectators applauding and celebrating in the stands, and countless colorful flags and streamers fluttering along the walls below!

A sight like this sent excitement surging through the heart. No matter how many times he experienced it, he would never grow tired of it...

The celebration continued for quite some time before the announcer's voice sounded again.

"Competitor Ethan Vale, please proceed to the awards platform!"

According to the tournament procedure, the awards ceremony naturally came next. An ordinary person would probably have returned through the competitors' passage, entered the corridor, and climbed the stairs to reach the ceremonial platform.

Ethan chose the opposite approach and decided to put on a show!

He beckoned to the red Gyarados, which swam back to him. As it lowered its enormous head, Ethan took several steps forward, left the command area, and stood directly upon its head!

Before anyone understood what he intended, the red Gyarados swam toward the water below the ceremonial platform. Its entire body slowly rose from the pool, climbing higher and higher. Like an elevator, its enormous head eventually rose above the platform itself!

Countless small streams cascaded between its scales like miniature waterfalls.

Sea Priestess Maya sat in the place of honor upon the ceremonial platform. Six other girls stood to either side, dressed as festival attendants in long white gauze dresses and carrying ceremonial fans. Officer Jenny and more than a dozen police officers formed a guard around them!

The red Gyarados still carried the menace of its recent battle. The instant it appeared, everyone nearby, including the officers, received an enormous fright!

When they met those terrifying blood-red eyes, they instinctively retreated several steps, panic written openly across their faces!

Only Maya and Officer Jenny remained where they were, apparently unafraid of the red Gyarados.

Officer Jenny's composure was hardly surprising. No matter how serious an incident became, members of her family were rarely seen panicking. Maya was clearly no ordinary person either. Although a trace of alarm appeared on her face, she remained seated. The Sea Priestess truly possessed considerable courage!

From other sides of the arena, the red Gyarados appeared to have draped most of its body across the wall, leaving its enormous head above it like a giant ready to break into the platform at any moment!

Ethan first swept his gaze around the platform, then jumped from the red Gyarados's head and landed steadily.

He took out its Poke Ball and recalled it. The moment the terrifying monster disappeared, everyone felt the pressure abruptly ease. The invisible mountain weighing on their hearts vanished, and even the air seemed fresher!

Maya rose and approached Ethan.

"Mr. Ethan Vale, congratulations on winning the Whirl Cup. On behalf of the people of the Whirl Islands, I offer my heartfelt joy at your victory and my thanks for the wonderful matches you have given us! Since you entered the tournament, we have watched you defeat every opponent in succession with tremendous strength. You truly deserve the title of champion!"

"You're too kind..." Ethan smiled. "I simply performed well. Many excellent Trainers also helped me grow a great deal."

Now that he saw her from nearby, Ethan discovered that Maya possessed not only a beautiful face but an excellent figure. Most striking of all was her remarkably pale skin. Combined with her long purple hair, Greek-style clothing, and the scepter in her hand, she strongly reminded him of Athena from Saint Seiya.

Maya offered several more words of congratulations while quietly studying Ethan in return.

This handsome Indigo League champion appeared no older than she was. Yet despite his youth, he had already accomplished so much. Including this victory, he had won three regional competitions of varying size. It was genuinely astonishing.

Most of all, his incomparably ferocious and imposing red Gyarados was absurdly powerful.

Drawing back from her thoughts, Maya noticed Ethan still looking at her. She smiled faintly and gestured to the side.

"I will now present your awards and bestow the blessing of the sea upon you. Please stand upon that platform first."

Ethan walked forward several steps and climbed onto a prepared dais. When he turned to look around from there, the entire arena spread out beneath his eyes!

The view itself had not changed, but the new angle made standing here feel completely different from standing in the Trainer's command area!

How could he describe it? The sight made his blood surge even more strongly and brought an entirely different realization. Only now did it truly strike him that he was the winner of this tournament!

Maya and four attendants approached him.

Ethan looked down and saw that each attendant carried a silver tray. Three different kinds of objects were arranged across the trays.

Maya introduced them. "These four rewards are your medal, trophy, prize money, and the winner's prize for this Cupthe Mystic Water. They all belong to you now."

As she spoke, the four attendants stepped forward one after another and presented the objects on their trays to Ethan.

Maya first lifted the medal and personally placed it around Ethan's neck. It gleamed like gold, though he could not tell whether it had truly been made from the precious metal. Due to its angle, he could see only the front, which bore an engraved whirlpool design.

Next, Maya handed him a heavy golden trophy and a check for one million.

After thanking her, Ethan naturally turned his gaze toward the final reward, the Mystic Water.

Compared with symbolic objects like a medal and trophy, a Mystic Water capable of increasing the power of a Pokemon's moves was unquestionably far more valuable!

In fact, Ethan had already decided who would receive the Mystic Water before he even won the championship.

He currently owned only three Water-type Pokemon. Blastoise had already moved into a more relaxed role, while the red Gyarados rarely battled. The Mystic Water would have a much greater effect in Suicune's possession.

If Ethan encountered another Legendary Pokemon later in his journey, a Suicune equipped with Mystic Water would naturally possess a greatly improved chance of victory.

Chapter 452: The True Sea Hero

The blessing ceremony followed immediately after the awards. Only after receiving the blessing would Ethan truly become this tournament's Sea Hero.

The four attendants withdrew, and Maya approached Ethan with her scepter in hand.

"Mr. Ethan Vale, please kneel here on one knee."

Knowing this was part of the ceremony, Ethan followed her instruction and knelt upon the dais. Maya then raised the golden scepter and rested it against his shoulder.

His shoulder suddenly sank under the weight, and Ethan examined the scepter from the corner of his eye.

The solid-gold staff shone brilliantly beneath the sunlight, while the Sea Spirit set at its tip glittered with an azure radiance!

The scepter was remarkably heavy. Ethan had to admire a woman as seemingly delicate as Maya for carrying it everywhere she went!

A gentle breeze stirred Maya's long purple hair. She held her head high, seemingly enveloped in sacred light, and looked very much like a Greek goddess.

She solemnly proclaimed, "O great God of the Sea! In my name as Sea Priestess, I offer this prayer and ask for your grace. Bestow your blessing upon the warrior before me. Grant him the freedom to travel across the sea and the ability to connect his heart with all Water-type Pokemon!"

The speakers carried Maya's voice across the entire arena, allowing everyone to hear her clearly.

Ethan knelt motionless with a focused expression, apparently accepting the blessing with complete seriousness. Inwardly, however, his thoughts had wandered elsewhere.

Does the God of the Sea mentioned in this ceremony refer to Lugia too?

That fellow's shadow appears everywhere. It isn't just the people of the Orange Islands. Even the people here like calling it the God of the Sea.

When it came to worshiping Legendary Pokemon, people were much the same whether they lived in Kanto, Johto, or any other region.

Still, Lugia was a Psychic- and Flying-type Pokemon. Calling it the God of the Sea did not entirely match what it actually was.

To be honest, Ethan believed another pure Water-type Legendary Pokemon, Kyogre, fit the definition of the God of the Sea much better.

As for why no one called Kyogre by that title, Ethan guessed it was largely because Kyogre usually lived in the deepest parts of the ocean. It appeared far less often than Lugia and was consequently much less familiar to outsiders.

While his imagination wandered, Maya's proclamation reached its end. The Sea Spirit atop the scepter once again released a dazzling light.

Just as during the opening ceremony of the main tournament, magnificent radiance shone forth. This time, however, the pale blue light illuminated Ethan alone!

As before, the Sea Spirit's glow was gentle rather than blinding and appeared no different from the light everyone had already seen.

Bathed in blue, Ethan felt exceptionally calm.

He knew perfectly well that this traditional ceremony had been passed down for several thousand years. Such rituals were almost entirely symbolic and possessed virtually no practical effect. The blessing amounted to a title, proof that by winning the tournament, Ethan had earned the Whirl Islands' highest honor.

Ethan was hardly alone in thinking so. Sea Priestess Maya and nearly every spectator present shared the same belief.

The ceremony proceeded according to tradition and soon approached its conclusion.

But just as the blue light slowly faded and Maya prepared to lift the scepter, the Sea Spirit released a different radiance.

This new azure light shone even more brightly, matching the color of the Sea Spirit itself!

It erupted from the gemstone and instantly wrapped around Ethan!

Under its influence, Ethan suddenly became weightless and floated directly into the air!

After he remained suspended for several seconds, the light abruptly entered his chest, and Ethan descended to the platform once more.

Hmm?
