The sudden change left Ethan completely confused. He lowered his head in astonishment and examined his chest, then looked up at Maya, who appeared equally bewildered.

"Um... I have to ask. Is this supposed to happen?"

"Well..."

Maya remained stunned for a long while. She and Ethan were not the only ones confused. The attendants nearby also found the scene utterly incredible.

Four years had passed since Maya became Sea Priestess, and this was the second Whirl Cup held during her tenure. Yet she had never encountered anything like this!

Neither had her mother or grandmother, the previous two Sea Priestesses. Across more than a decade in office, neither woman had ever witnessed such an event!

Why had the Sea Spirit suddenly released another light and sent it into Ethan's heart?

It was completely unprecedented!

"This is extremely strange. Why would such a thing happen?" Maya frowned, plainly unable to understand it. After thinking briefly, she looked at Ethan and asked tentatively, "Do you feel any different?"

Ethan rose, shook his head, and moved each of his limbs. He felt no change whatsoever.

He asked in return, "Wasn't that an effect you created?"

"Of course not," Maya denied immediately. "The Sea Spirit is a sacred relic passed down from ancient times. The light you saw wasn't some artificial effect. It all came from the Sea Spirit itself, and nothing like this has ever happened throughout its entire history!"

"Nothing like this has ever happened?" Seeing that she did not know the cause either, Ethan smiled. "Then can I take it to mean I'm special? Wouldn't that mean that compared with every previous winner, I'm the one who truly received the God of the Sea's blessing?"

Maya froze at his words. Then something seemed to occur to her, and surprise filled her face as she nodded thoughtfully.

"That makes a great deal of sense. Perhaps... perhaps there truly is something special about you, and you accidentally awakened one of the Sea Spirit's powers. I think... that must be the reason!"

The unexpected incident delayed the ceremony only briefly. Since no one could determine the cause for now, they had no choice but to suppress their questions and continue.

With Maya's blessing and the applause of the spectators, this year's Whirl Cup finally came to an end.

Chapter 453: Something Really Does Seem Wrong

After leaving the ceremonial platform, Ethan returned to the competitors' waiting room.

Erika, Ash, and the others had been waiting there for some time. His arrival naturally brought another round of congratulations. Even Trinity, whom he had only just defeated, had not left and appeared there with everyone else!

Pop! Pop!

Brock and Ash held party poppers and covered Ethan with streamers and glittering confetti. Misty placed a bright garland around his neck. Everyone smiled, clearly delighted that Ethan had won the championship.

Erika stood nearby and applauded softly. Beside her, Trinity approached Ethan with a complicated expression and said sincerely, "Congratulations. Your Pokemon are far too powerful. I accept my defeat completely."

Trinity had suffered such a brutal loss, yet instead of leaving immediately, she had come to congratulate him. The sight left Ethan feeling extremely guilty.

Sigh. If I'd known, I would have switched Gyarados out halfway through. At least then she wouldn't have lost so miserably...

The good news was that, just as Ethan had hoped before the match, Trinity's expression showed none of Aya's former desire to take revenge upon him.

The battle had clearly beaten both the resistance and the courage out of her!

"I'm sorry for hurting your Pokemon so badly. But please don't hold it against me. That's simply how my Gyarados fights. Even if it tries to restrain itself, it really can't..."

Ethan's tone was completely sincere, and the final trace of unwillingness in Trinity's heart vanished.

She smiled. "You can't take all the blame. A Pokemon battle isn't a game played by children. It's dangerous and cruel by nature, so injuries are unavoidable. If you'd held back out of sympathy, I would have felt even more humiliated. Ultimately, I lost because my Pokemon still haven't trained enough. I was also overestimating myself when I imagined I could defeat such a powerful opponent."

Her words left Ethan even more embarrassed.

"Uh... I didn't expect you to possess such perspective. That's admirable. Still, you should go to the Pokemon Center as soon as possible and ask Nurse Joy to treat your Pokemon's injuries. You don't want them suffering any lasting complications."

Trinity naturally understood how urgent the situation was. She should have taken her Pokemon to the Pokemon Center immediately after the match. Even so, she had come here first because she wanted to congratulate Ethan at the earliest opportunity. Otherwise, people might think she was a sore loser who had slipped away without even saying goodbye!

Even in defeat, she had her dignity!

Now that she had offered her congratulations, however, it was truly time to take her Pokemon to Nurse Joy.

"In that case, I'll leave first. I hope the rest of your journey goes smoothly and that you continue catching powerful Pokemon! Oh, rightyour next goal must be the Silver Conference, correct? That's the highest honor in our Johto region! I hope you defeat every formidable opponent and become champion in one decisive run, just as you did today!"

"Thank you for the good wishes. Take care of yourself too, and I hope we meet again someday!"

The two solemnly shook hands.

To Ethan, Trinity was a strong and respectable opponent.

To Trinity, Ethan would unquestionably leave a lasting impression. His red Gyarados in particular would probably remain an inescapable shadow in her mind for the rest of her life.

After watching Trinity depart, Ethan, Erika, and the others felt the atmosphere inside the waiting room become noticeably more relaxed. They talked for a while longer before the conversation turned toward the strange event that had occurred when Ethan received the blessing on the ceremonial platform.

They had all seen the change from the stands and found it exceptionally surprising.

Erika was the first to ask with concern, "What happened just now? Something like that isn't supposed to be part of the normal ceremony, is it?"

"Exactly!" Misty hurriedly added. "I saw that light wrap around you, and then you just went whoosh and flew into the sky! What happened?"

"It wasn't nearly that dramatic!" Ethan grinned and lightly tapped her head. "Whoosh? I'm not some kind of rocket! I only rose about a dozen centimeters above the platform. I was nowhere near floating high in the air!"

After the blessing, Ethan's conversation with Sea Priestess Maya had not been carried through the speakers. Erika and the others had seen the unusual event, but they had no idea what had happened.

Seeing everyone watching him curiously, Ethan shook his head and recounted both his experience and Maya's interpretation.

After listening, Brock rubbed his chin and analyzed the situation. "So unlike the previous winners, who held only an empty title, you actually received the Sea Spirit's blessing?"

Ethan hesitated. "I'm not entirely sure, but according to Maya, the gemstone definitely reacted to me somehow. She went to consult their records and see whether anything similar has happened during the ceremony's long history."

"Do you feel different anywhere?" Misty's eyes gleamed. "You're a Sea Hero! Traveling freely beneath the sea and connecting your heart with Water-type Pokemon are exactly what we Water Pokemon Trainers dream of! Why don't you test it right now? See whether you can truly understand a Water-type Pokemon's thoughts. Then everything will be clear!"

Erika nodded in agreement. "Misty is right. There's no harm in trying."

The instant Erika supported her idea, Misty pulled a Poke Ball from the pouch at her waist without waiting for Ethan's agreement. But just as she prepared to release Poliwhirl, blue light flashed from the pouch, and Psyduck ran out on its own again!

"You little pest!" Misty flew into a rage at the sight. She immediately seized Psyduck by the neck with both hands and shook it furiously. "Why do you always come out without permission? Tell me! Hurry up and tell me!"

Psyduck's face turned bright red, and it looked exceptionally uncomfortable beneath her grip.

Seeing this, Ethan smiled and waved his hand, stopping the rampaging Misty.

"Forget it. Psyduck will do. No matter what else we say, it's still a Water-type Pokemon."

Only then did Misty release it with obvious reluctance. Psyduck, nearly shaken unconscious, collapsed limply onto the floor.

Ethan cleared his throat, approached Psyduck, and crouched to meet its vacant stare.

Psyduck tilted its head and looked at him in confusion, having no idea why this human was staring at it. Then it glanced toward its Trainer, ignored Ethan entirely, and waddled around the waiting room on its yellow legs.

Ethan raised his eyebrows. Astonishment crossed his face. After remaining frozen for a moment, he stood with an equally puzzled expression.

The instant Erika and the others saw his reaction, they realized something must have happened!

Misty asked impatiently, "Well!? Well!? Ethan, could you understand what it was thinking just now!?"

Chapter 454: A Wondrous Ability

Ethan hesitated. "I can't understand what Psyduck is thinking..."

Before he could finish, Ash suddenly burst into laughter.

He glanced at Misty and mocked her without mercy. "Exactly! How could a rock possess such incredible power? Besides, your Psyduck is really special, Misty. Even another Pokemon probably couldn't understand anything it says!"

Misty was about to retort when she heard Ash ridicule her Pokemon. But after opening her mouth, she realized he was right. Her Psyduck truly was abnormal, almost as though something were missing inside its head.

How else could anyone explain a Water-type Pokemon that feared water and had nearly drowned itself on several occasions?

It also constantly emerged from its Poke Ball without permission, ignored commands, and stood around blankly during battle without displaying anything resembling the proper state of mind!

"I... I..."

There were far too many strange things about Psyduck. No matter what Misty wanted to say, all she could produce in the end was a heavy sigh.

Sigh. Forget it. The fact that my Psyduck survived in good health long enough for me to catch it was already an incredible achievement...

At the side, Ethan cleared his throat when he saw the two begin arguing again.

"All right, both of you, stop fighting and let me finish."

His expression clearly suggested that there was more to his answer, and everyone turned toward him.

"However..." Ethan emphasized the word before continuing, "although I haven't connected my heart with Psyduck and can't understand its thoughts, I really can sense its emotions faintly."

"Sense its emotions?" Everyone froze.

"Huh? Seriously?" Ash's eyes widened. "That's incredible!"

"It's true. How should I explain it? The feeling is very subtle." Ethan thought briefly, then continued. "You all know that the eyes are windows into the heart, and a person's expression reflects their emotions. By watching those two things, you can often judge someone's mood without asking. But when I stared at Psyduck just now, I could faintly sense that it felt relaxed without relying on either clue."

Ash and Misty looked at one another. The explanation had already passed beyond their understanding. In truth, they were still young, and much of what adults considered common sense remained unfamiliar to them.

But Erika and Brock both looked thoughtful, so Ash and Misty could only nod as though they understood.

"Ah... ah... So that's how it is..."

"In that case..." Erika mused, "the legend may have been exaggerated, and people today may regard the selection of a Sea Hero as nothing more than a ceremony, but the blessing truly does possess such wondrous power!"

"It seems so. The fact that the ceremony survived until today shows that it wasn't merely a performance." Ethan smiled and shook his head. "But this is obviously far from the legendary ability to connect our hearts."

"It's already extremely impressive," Brock added. "If you can perceive a Pokemon's emotions more clearly and accurately, you'll be better able to care for it. That would be valuable for any Trainer, but especially for Pokemon Breeders and doctors. Isn't this precisely the ability they dream of possessing?"

Only then did Ash finally understand. Eagerness filled his face as he asked excitedly, "Ethan, can you sense the emotions of Pokemon that aren't Water type?"

The emotions of other Pokemon?

The question stirred Ethan's curiosity, and he turned toward Pikachu, who stood beside Ash.

When Ethan looked at it, Pikachu tilted its head in confusion.

"Pika-pika?"

Ethan stared for a long while, but eventually shook his head.

"No. I can't sense anything at all. It appears this much of the legend is true. The ability granted to me by the Sea Spirit can probably sense only the emotions of Water-type Pokemon."

"No matter what, that's still amazing!" Misty wore such a broad smile that her eyes nearly curved into crescent moons. "Does that mean you'll be able to move freely underwater too?"

Her face shone with anticipation. Only moments earlier, a heartwarming scene had appeared in her mind: she and Ethan playing underwater with every kind of Water-type Pokemon, weaving between corals and jellyfish like a pair of happy aquatic spirits!

Wait. If Ethan really has that ability, doesn't that mean he'll start working toward becoming a Water Pokemon Master too?

Then if I want to become a Water Pokemon Master as well, we'll share the same goal and become a match made in heaven!

Hehe. Even the God of the Sea is helping me!

Ethan naturally had no idea what Misty was imagining. If he had known, he probably would have rapped her sharply on the head!

What kind of nonsense is running through that little head?

Water Pokemon Master? Ethan's goal had never been to master a single type!

He shrugged. "Who knows? That stone didn't alter my body. If I want to confirm it, I'll have to find an opportunity to go underwater sometime. But judging by this supposed connection of hearts, I doubt the other ability is as miraculous as Maya described. The legend must be greatly exaggerated!"

...

After the Whirl Cup ended, Ash, Misty, and Brock originally intended to bid Ethan farewell and resume their journey. The moment they heard that Sea Priestess Maya would hold a banquet that evening for Ethan, the Sea Hero, they immediately decided to remain and enjoy a feast. They would leave only after eating their fill and resting for the night.

No one could blame them for being gluttonous. All three were still growing. Brock was an excellent cook, but their constant travel and nights in the wilderness rarely gave them the chance to enjoy a proper banquet. With such a rare opportunity before them, they naturally had to reward themselves!

While they waited for evening to arrive, the group left the arena and headed toward the Pokemon Center.

Along the way, Ash and Misty enthusiastically discussed everything they had seen and experienced during the tournament. Every major competition helped them grow, and many moments were worth remembering.

Before returning to the Pokemon Center, Ethan found a delivery company and mailed his new trophy and medal back to the Cerise Laboratory.

Once he reached the Pokemon Center, he also transferred Blastoise and the red Gyarados back to the laboratory.

The tournament had given both Pokemon an opportunity to stretch their muscles. Ethan would have no need to call upon them again for some time.

Chapter 455: The Evening Banquet

That evening, Ethan brought Erika, Ash, Misty, and Brock to the Temple of the Sea for the banquet.

Stars filled the sky, and the cool sea breeze swept across the group, carrying away the last warmth left after sunset.

The Temple of the Sea stood near the arena, west of Scarlet City on Red Rock Isle. The enormous structure had been built atop a sheer cliff. Looking down from there offered a complete view of the city and, on the other side of the cliff, a vast and violent whirlpool churning across the ocean!

The whirlpool looked extremely dangerous. No one knew when it had formed or how long it had existed. Like a toilet that never stopped flushing, it endlessly drew seawater toward some unknown destination.

The exposed reefs around it had been polished perfectly smooth by the current. The constant rush of water sounded rather harsh, though after listening for long enough, everyone gradually grew accustomed to it.

Despite the banquet's grandeur, none of the Whirl Islands' politicians or merchants had been invited. The guest list included only Ethan, the most important Sea Hero; Maya, the Sea Priestess hosting the banquet; and whichever friends and family Ethan wished to bring.

Seen that way, the banquet appeared remarkably pure. It carried no hidden political or commercial purpose and seemed to exist solely to celebrate Ethan's becoming a Sea Hero.

The group passed several security guards dressed like ancient soldiers and entered the temple together.

Even before drawing close, they noticed that the temple shared the arena's ancient Greek style. The moment they stepped through its doors, they saw a statue of the God of the Sea!

Just as Ethan had expected, the God of the Sea worshiped here truly was Lugia!

The statue reproduced Lugia at full scale. Apart from its color, the sculpture looked astonishingly lifelike, almost indistinguishable from the real Pokemon!

The group stopped and gathered around it for a careful examination.

They had seen the Legendary Pokemon in the Orange Islands, but only from a great distance. They had never been able to observe it as closely as they could now.

"What a beautiful Pokemon... But from this close, Lugia really is enormous!"

Misty looked up and ran a hand across one of Lugia's wings, unable to suppress her wonder.

As a Water Pokemon Trainer, her greatest dream was to catch either a Lugia or a Kyogre one day. With this statue standing before her, for one brief moment, even that dream no longer felt impossibly distant!

"It is huge." Ethan nodded. He was already quite tall for his age, but before this enormous birdlike Pokemon, he still felt exceptionally small. "According to the records, an adult Lugia can reach 5.2 meters in height and weigh 216 kilograms. Its wingspan can exceed ten meters. It's unquestionably a very large avian Pokemon and truly magnificent. Compared with it, my three sacred birds count as only medium-sized. They can't compare at all."

The group continued marveling at Lugia's statue. At that moment, footsteps sounded from the other side. They turned and saw Sea Priestess Maya approaching with graceful steps.

Smiling, Maya joined them and likewise looked toward the statue.

"As you can see, this is the God of the Sea, the being we of the Whirl Islands have always worshiped. Since ancient times, it has protected the islands from outside threats. It is unquestionably our God of the Sea!"

After briefly marveling at Maya's beauty, Misty asked out of her longing for Lugia, "Um... Were the whirlpools outside the islands also created by the God of the Sea?"

Maya gently shook her head. "Well... so much time has passed that no one can verify the truth. You may believe they were, or you may believe they weren't. The generally accepted scientific explanation is that those whirlpools formed because of the ocean trenches and currents near the islands."

Ethan raised his eyebrows. Her answer made him view the beautiful priestess with new respect.

Ordinary religious figures often tried to promote their faith by attributing every unusual event to the deity they worshiped. A priestess like Maya, willing to discuss the facts, was exceedingly rare!

Before Ethan could respond, Maya turned toward his companions.

She naturally knew something about Ash and Misty because both had competed in the Whirl Cup. Erika and Brock had not entered, however, so this was her first time meeting them.

Ethan cleared his throat and introduced both sides.

When Maya learned that Erika and Brock were Gym Leaders from Kanto, surprise filled her face. She smiled. "As expected of a championno, I should say, as expected of our Sea Hero! Your own strength is extraordinary, and even among your traveling companions are powerful Trainers like these Gym Leaders!"

"You've misunderstood." Ethan gently shook his head. "These two friends simply cannot remain at their Gyms for the moment because of certain circumstances, so they decided to travel for a time. They didn't abandon their work there specifically to accompany me."

Maya laughed softly. "Even so, doesn't receiving the recognition of Gym Leaders also prove how exceptional you are?"

...

At eight that evening, inside the Temple of the Sea's banquet hall, a long table overflowed with fruit, pastries, and delicacies. Several attendants played musical instruments nearby. Everything around him reminded Ethan of that night on Shamouti Island.

The scenes were so similar. Even the Sea Priestess seemed to correspond to the festival maiden from that occasion.

Light, beautiful music echoed around the hall.

The banquet had officially begun. Ethan and the others released their smaller Pokemon, and the entire hall instantly became chaotic yet exceptionally lively.

At the long table, Ash, Misty, and Brock devoured the food with abandon. Even Pikachu constantly tossed treats into its mouth. Their ravenous eating looked so comical that the attendants nearby covered their mouths and giggled.

Compared with them, Ethan and Erika ate far more elegantly.

Ethan was willing to spend money and had never deprived himself or his Pokemon when it came to food. Naturally, they did not behave like Ash and the others, who looked as though they had not eaten anything good in years.

Throughout the meal, Ethan and Maya spoke from time to time, creating a relaxed and pleasant atmosphere. Yet he faintly sensed that the banquet's purpose might not be quite so simple after all.

Although Maya wore a smile, some troubling matter seemed to weigh upon her brow.

Chapter 456: Will or Crystal?

The banquet was only halfway over, yet dozens of white plates covered in scraps were already piled high before Ash, Misty, and Brock. The three released enormous burps and lounged lazily against their wooden chairs, patting their swollen stomachs. They clearly could not eat another bite.

Whenever an opportunity like this arose, they showed their bodies no mercy. Unless they ate so much that they needed to support themselves against a wall on the way out, they would never be satisfied!

Now that they had eaten and drunk their fill, the group finally had enough leisure to chat with Sea Priestess Maya.

Brock was especially enthusiastic. In fact, the first time he saw this beautiful priestess, he had stood petrified for quite a while.

Now he held nothing back as he recounted everything they had seen and experienced during their journey. He poured out every amusing and interesting story he could remember, doing everything possible to win the beautiful priestess's favor.

Maya had encountered far too many enthusiastic men who admired her appearance. She possessed her own methods for dealing with them and always maintained a polite but faint distance.

Perhaps because she had been bound to this place since childhood, however, Maya genuinely seemed interested in their travels.

She listened eagerly to their strange and thrilling stories, and an unguarded trace of longing occasionally appeared on her face.

Most of all, Ash described their battle against the three sacred birds on Shamouti Island, their attempt to stop the collector, and how their efforts alongside Lugia, the God of the Sea, finally ended the disaster. The story shocked not only Maya but also the nearby attendants, who stared at the group in astonishment.

"You've seen the God of the Sea with your own eyes!?"

"Of course!" Ash answered honestly without the slightest exaggeration. "We didn't just see itwe even fought beside it! Counting Ethan's Pokemon, there were seven Legendary..."

Before he could finish, Misty suddenly stomped hard on his foot. The movement was so forceful that even Maya glanced toward them.

"Ow!" Ash screamed in pain, then glared angrily at Misty. "Misty! Why did you step on me!?"

This idiot...

Misty rolled her eyes at him in complete exasperation.

He's unbelievably stupid. He almost revealed Ethan's secret!

Those Pokemon are his trump cards. How could Ash expose them to an outsider so casually?

But with Maya present, Misty could hardly explain. Instead, she picked up a large chicken leg and stuffed it directly into Ash's mouth!

"You obviously haven't eaten enough, right? Then have another chicken leg!"

Perhaps Misty used too much strength, because the chicken leg seemed to jab directly into Ash's throat. He made a series of muffled noises and clutched his mouth in pain.

Ignoring the fallen Ash, Misty sat straight and calmly wiped the grease from her hands with a napkin.

Ethan was thoroughly accustomed to their quarrels, but Maya had never witnessed anything like it. She worried that the two might truly become upset. Only when she saw everyone else treating the exchange as completely ordinary did she realize how close Ash and Misty were. Their actions were merely the rough play of companions who trusted each other completely!

Companions... What a wonderful word...

In any case, the interruption allowed Ash's unfinished revelation to pass unnoticed.

Everyone chatted for a while longer. But as the banquet approached its end, Maya's presence suddenly changed, and she became formal.

Ethan understood that serious business was usually discussed at times like this, and he immediately focused.

At the long table, Maya cleared her throat and formally invited Ethan to remain at the Temple of the Sea.

Only then did Ethan learn that when a local Trainer from the Whirl Islands won the Cup, the temple's enormous influence generally persuaded them to stay and assist the Sea Priestess with its work. The arrangement brought fame and benefit to both the winner and the temple, creating an ideal outcome for everyone.

Competitors from outside the islands, however, were not subject to the temple's influence, and very few ever chose to stay.

Ethan refused almost immediately.

Maya regretted his answer but was not surprised.

Even before offering the invitation, she had known that someone like Ethan would almost certainly never remain here. Nevertheless, tradition required her to ask.

Maya sighed, composed herself, and continued. "After returning here from the arena, I consulted a great many records. Although nothing like this has happened during the last two thousand years, the very first Sea Hero experienced exactly the same phenomenon when the Temple of the Sea was founded."

The first Sea Hero?

That's incredibly ancient.

Ethan asked curiously, "Apart from that person, has no one else experienced anything similar throughout all that time?"

"No." Maya shook her head. "A Sea Hero is chosen every three years. Aside from a period several centuries ago when unrest on the islands forced the tournament to stop, nearly six hundred Heroes have been selected in total. The details of every blessing they received were clearly recorded in scrolls. We examined them one by one and found nothing unusual."

At this point, Maya stared intently at Ethan. "After the blessing ceremony, did you notice anything different about yourself?"

Before Ethan could answer, Misty exclaimed excitedly, "We already tested it! Ethan can't truly connect his heart with Water-type Pokemon, but he can sense what they're feeling!"

"I see." Maya remained stunned for a long while. Then she studied Ethan deeply and nodded. "It appears that you are the Sea Hero who truly received the God of the Sea's blessing!"

Ethan could not resist asking, "Miss Maya, what exactly is the Sea Spirit? Why does it possess this kind of power?"

Maya thought for a moment before answering slowly. "According to the records, the Sea Spirit came from the ocean's deepest reaches. It is the brightest and purest existence beneath the sea, formed from the will of the ocean itself. We do not know precisely what it is. Some also claim that it may be a crystal formed after the God of the SeaLugiadied for some extraordinary reason!"

The will of the ocean?

A crystal left by Lugia?

Both possibilities sounded profoundly mysterious.

For a time, everyone fell silent.

They all wondered why Ethan had received the God of the Sea's blessing for the first time in thousands of years.

What separated this man from the hundreds of Sea Heroes who had come before him?

Chapter 457: Team Rocket Infiltrates

"Let's set that aside for now." Maya looked toward Ethan and parted her red lips. "Actually, besides celebrating your becoming a Sea Hero, I arranged this banquet because I have an extremely urgent matter for which I'd like to request your help."

Here it comes!

Ethan silently thought, I knew it. He was about to hear what Maya wanted, but before he could speak, Brock suddenly shot to his feet and thumped his chest loudly.

"Miss Maya! Whatever it is, please tell us! There's no need to be polite!" Brock's eyes had completely transformed into hearts the moment she mentioned needing help. "Whatever your request, we'll brave fire and water and do everything in our power to help! So... is this urgent matter a sweet romance with you?"

Ethan and the others stared at him speechlessly. Misty in particular felt goose bumps rise across her body.

This guy Brock...

He sounded perfectly serious at first. How did he become a completely different person by the end?

Even Misty could never bring herself to say something so embarrassing to Ethan. Yet Brock had shamelessly declared it before so many people!

His skin had to be the thickest in the world. It was as though his entire personality had changed and he had suddenly become a lecher!

Fortunately, Misty knew exactly what he was like. She shoved Brock aside, looked apologetically at Maya, and said, "Sorry. Please ignore him. There's something wrong with his head. What exactly do you need?"

Maya did not answer. Instead, she looked toward Ethan again.

Compared with the others, the Sea Hero's opinion mattered far more to her. In Maya's view, only Ethan, who had received the sea's blessing, was qualified to accept this task and see it through.

Ethan did not agree immediately. He asked first, "Please tell me what you need. Has something happened?"

Only after he spoke did Maya explain. "It concerns the God of the Sea..."

"Lugia?"

"That's right." Maya nodded. "There are signs that an evil organization has targeted the God of the Sea in the Whirl Islands. They're attempting to capture it..."

"Huh? Wait!" Ash and the others froze, then exclaimed in shock, "You mean there's a God of the Sea here too!?"

"Of course." Maya glanced at him. Since Ash was Ethan's companion, she no longer concealed the truth. "Gods of the Sea do live beneath the waters of the Whirl Islands. And there is more than one..."

Misty and Ash looked at each other. The news was simply too astonishing. A Legendary Pokemon coveted by countless people was hiding beneath the nearby ocean!

Ash clicked his tongue. "I thought there was only one Lugia in the entire world..."

"Of course not," Ethan explained. "The same was true of the one we encountered in the Orange Islands. Lugia may be extremely rare in this world, but it isn't unique. That isn't limited to Lugia, either. The same applies to Moltres and the other sacred birds. In fact, another form of the three birds even exists in the Galar region."

"He's correct," Maya agreed. "This is the Temple of the Sea, so naturally the deity we worship is the local God of the Sea from the Whirl Islands. But there is certainly more than one God of the Sea in the world. They reproduce just like other Pokemon."

"I see." Ash scratched his head. "Ethan, you really know a lot."

Ethan merely smiled. It was less that he knew a great deal than that he had played and watched a great deal!

Maya's explanation also caused certain memories to surface in his mind.

According to the animated series, a mother and child pair of Lugia did indeed live in Johto. Judging by their location, they seemed to inhabit the Whirl Islands. Ethan also clearly remembered that the young Lugia was named Silver!

Of course, this Silver had absolutely no connection to Giovanni's son of the same name.

But speaking of Giovanni...

Ethan looked at Maya. "This evil organization you mentioned wouldn't happen to be..."

Maya completed his thought. "Team Rocket, an evil organization causing trouble throughout Johto!"

So it was them after all.

Johto and Kanto were Team Rocket's principal territories. Besides them, Ethan could not imagine another evil organization daring to hunt Pokemon so brazenly in this region!

"Don't worry." After thinking briefly, Ethan accepted the request. "Leave this matter to us. We've dealt with those people many times. Since we've encountered this situation, we would never allow them to succeed even if you hadn't asked for our help!"

...

At nine that evening, after washing up, Ethan lay in a guest room inside the Temple of the Sea.

When the banquet ended, Maya had discussed additional details with the group. By the time they finished, the night had grown late, so she invited everyone to remain at the temple.

The Temple of the Sea was not merely a place of worship. It was Maya's home as well. The office of Sea Priestess passed down through a single family line, and Maya's ancestors had lived here for generations.

In the future, if she married and had children, one of them would inherit the priesthood in turn.

That's quite the secure lifelong position...

Looking through the window at the star-filled sky, Ethan smiled softly.

Becoming Sea Priestess guaranteed food and shelter, earned tremendous respect, offered wealth and privilege, and brought an exceptionally high social position. It was practically a guaranteed route to success in life.

As his thoughts wandered, sleepiness gradually overcame him. Just as he was about to drift off, a dark shadow suddenly emerged from the wall.

Ethan lifted his eyelids and saw that it was his Gengar.

The fellow had wandered all over the temple since the banquet began, grandly calling its excursion an adventure. After so long, it had finally remembered to return.

Ethan yawned and prepared to turn over, only for Gengar to approach his bedside.

"Hey, get up! I just saw Team Rocket!"

Team Rocket!?

The three words instantly banished Ethan's sleepiness and brought him fully awake!

He sat up and asked in surprise, "How did Team Rocket get here? I didn't expect them to reach the temple already. Are they planning to attack Maya, or did they come searching for clues about Lugia?"

"I don't know." Gengar shook its head. "Anyway, those three sneaked inside looking suspicious and are wandering around the place."

"Those... three?" Ethan froze before realizing whom Gengar meant. He curled his lip in disappointment. "Come on... When you said Team Rocket, you didn't mean the executives. It's only James and the other two..."

"What's wrong with them?" Gengar looked at him in surprise. "Why does it sound like you look down on them? Aren't they members of Team Rocket?"

Ethan laughed outright. "How should I put this? Those three may belong to Team Rocket, but they never accomplish anything important. There's no need to worry. Ash and the others are more than enough to deal with them."

He began to lie down again, but after hesitating for a moment, he still draped his jacket over his shoulders.

"Forget it. I'm awake now anyway. I might as well go see what those three came here to do."

Chapter 458: An Eerie Wind Blows

Late at night, inside the Temple of the Sea.

The temple seemed to have fallen completely silent. Almost no sound could be heard except for the violent whirlpool below the distant cliff, which continued rushing tirelessly and filled the night with the endless roar of water.

Ethan quietly moved through the corridors. The surroundings were so still that only his own footsteps echoed again and again. Gengar accompanied him, but the Pokemon made no sound when it moved. Like a shadow, its presence felt almost no different from walking alone.

During the day, the temple had appeared solemn and mysterious. At night, its entire atmosphere transformed, becoming strangely eerie and frightening.

Ethan and Gengar had not traveled far before he noticed that, for some unknown reason, the corridor contained no electric lights or other modern illumination. Instead, an oil lamp hung every few meters. Their hazy flames lit the entire passage and brought a faint, dim glow to the night.

That was not difficult to understand. How could a temple display its mystery without deliberately creating a little atmosphere?

The arrangement also provided another benefit. The burning flames dispersed some moisture from the air and kept the Temple of the Sea's interior dry.

After walking another dozen meters, Ethan turned toward Gengar beside him.

"Where exactly did you see the Team Rocket trio?"

Gengar raised one short, thick arm and pointed ahead. "Not far in front. There's a shortcut nearby that can take us around them. Follow me!"

Under Gengar's guidance, Ethan reached a staircase around the next corner. Gengar manipulated something on a nearby lampstand, and a hidden door suddenly appeared in the wall!

"Go inside." Gengar cackled. "I discovered this secret passage while exploring earlier. It connects to most parts of the temple and is extremely well hidden."

It was hard to imagine that Gengar had uncovered even the temple's secret passages in only a few hours!

Wasn't that practically the same as exposing the other side's greatest secret?

Then again, Pokemon of Gengar's lineage generally enjoyed passing through walls and loved dark places. It was hardly surprising for one to discover such a secret.

Beyond the hidden door, the world grew even darker. A narrow, low passage stretched ahead, just wide enough for a single person.

Unlike the corridor outside, the secret tunnel was so dark that Ethan could not see his hand before his face. Gengar had long adapted to darkness and encountered no difficulty, but Ethan was human and possessed no such ability.

With no alternative, he released Jolteon and had it gather electricity to illuminate the path beneath his feet.

Ethan followed the passage through turn after turn and several intersections. Eventually, they passed through another hidden door and left the tunnel.

Before Ethan could determine where he was, footsteps suddenly sounded in the distance and drew closer little by little. With no time to think, he hurriedly recalled Jolteon and concealed himself in the darkness.

...

Deep within the Temple of the Sea, the Team Rocket trio crept quietly through the nearby passages.

It was far too late to use a flashlight. Without a map and unable to ask anyone for directions, Jessie and James had become completely lost after sneaking inside and had wandered back and forth for a long time.

Both now felt their lower legs aching and weak. They could not take another step.

Finding a stone stair, James simply gave up and sat down. He massaged his legs and frowned. "Hey, Jessie, didn't we already pass through this place? Why does it look so familiar?"

"Did we?" Jessie leaned against the stone pillar beside him and let her tongue hang out like a dog, apparently hoping it would ease her exhaustion. "Everything in here looks the same. You must be mistaken!"

Meowth's expression changed when he heard them. He hurriedly jumped over and made a shushing gesture. "Shh! Keep your voices down! Don't wake the guards!"

"What are you afraid of?" Jessie curled her lip carelessly. "The tournament is over, so Officer Jenny and the police have already left. Only a few women and those guards at the entrance remain. If they dare get in our way, I'll take care of them!"

James hesitated. "But I saw Ethan and the twerps move in here too. If we wake them, we'll be in real trouble!"

"So what if they're here?" Jessie forced out the brave words, though her expression clearly lacked confidence. "We'll leave the instant we get the scepter. It's pitch-black outside. Once we pass through the doors, we can hide behind any tree we like. They won't find us even if they try to chase us!"

Jessie's reasoning sounded convincing enough to James and Meowth, easing some of their concern.

What none of them knew was that Ethan was watching from the shadows beside them with narrowed eyes!

So these people... have set their sights on Maya's scepter?

After overhearing their entire conversation, Ethan finally understood their objective.

The scepter was made from solid gold, while the Sea Spirit mounted upon it was a priceless treasure with tremendous symbolic importance. If Team Rocket truly stole it, the loss would deal a devastating blow to Maya, the Temple of the Sea, and the entire Whirl Islands.

Ethan could only wonder whether targeting the scepter had been the trio's own idea or an order from Team Rocket's leadership.

The resting trio naturally had no idea that the person they feared most was hiding only a short distance away!

After they rested for another moment, a draft suddenly swept through the corridor, making all three shudder at once.

James pulled his clothes tighter and complained, "This miserable place looked perfectly fine during the day. Why does it feel so eerie and frightening at night!?"

"You're imagining things. It's all in your head." Jessie rolled her eyes. "Honestly, how can you call yourself a member of Team Rocket when you're this timid?"

James looked around. The longer he studied the place, the more it made his skin crawl. He urged, "All right, we've rested long enough. Let's hurry and keep moving!"

"Coward..."

Jessie was about to continue when an eerie laugh suddenly reached their ears. It sounded near and far at once, as though something were laughing directly beside them. Yet when they turned to look, they saw nothing!

Even so, the laughter continued to echo clearly in their ears!

Gulp!

All three swallowed unconsciously. After exchanging glances, they hurriedly scrambled to their feet.

Jessie looked at James and forced a dry smile. "Y-you have a point. We really shouldn't stay here. Let's hurry and steal that scepter!"

After what had happened, neither James nor Meowth would agree to walk in front. One grown man and one Pokemon pushed Jessie ahead of them instead.

Jessie wanted to curse the two cowards shoving her forward. She was naturally terrified as well, but since she had proposed the operation, she could only summon her courage and lead the way...

Chapter 459: Maya Is Abducted

As the Team Rocket trio gradually disappeared into the distance, a wicked grin spread across Gengar's face in the shadows.

Both the eerie draft and the terrifying laughter had naturally come from Gengar. It had created them solely to frighten the trio.

Gengar simply had not expected them to be so cowardly. It had barely done anything, yet one small scare had already sent them fleeing in panic!

It spread its hands and shook its head at Ethan. "Come on! They're supposed to be members of Team Rocket. How can they be this timid? They can't withstand the slightest scare. What a disgrace to Team Rocket!"

"All right, enough playing around." Ethan rolled his eyes helplessly. "Let's hurry and drive them out before they cause unnecessary damage."

Leaving the shadows, Ethan and Gengar quickly pursued the trio.

Perhaps the three had been too badly frightened. After Gengar's scare, they fled blindly without caring where they went. By pure accident, they actually found their way to Maya's door!

The moment they saw the magnificent doors, delight filled their faces, and they rushed straight inside.

Just as Ethan arrived outside, a woman's scream came from within!

It's Maya!

Ethan did not hesitate. He kicked the door open and charged inside. By the bright moonlight, he saw Jessie and Maya struggling over the golden scepter!

Both women gripped the staff tightly and pulled in opposite directions, while James and Meowth stood nearby without appearing willing to intervene.

When Ethan entered, the two sides reacted very differently.

"This is bad! It's Ethan!"

James's expression changed dramatically. The tremor in his voice made his terror unmistakable!

He could never have imagined that Ethan would suddenly appear the moment they found their target, before they even managed to seize the scepter!

By contrast, delight flashed across Maya's face. She shouted, "Mr. Ethan Vale, these people are trying to steal the Sea Spirit! Hurry and stop them!"

Perhaps Ethan's sudden arrival gave Maya additional strength. She pulled the scepter closer to herself.

Jessie clearly panicked after seeing him. Combined with Maya's sudden effort, this left her unable to wrench the scepter from the priestess's grasp!

"Darn it!" Jessie cursed under her breath. "Where did this woman suddenly find so much strength!?"

Ethan approached one step at a time. Unable to seize the scepter quickly, Jessie shouted at James and Meowth, "Hey! Stop standing there like idiots! Hurry and stop him!"

"Huh?" James and Meowth stared at her in disbelief. "Us? Stop him? Are you joking? That's Ethan!"

"Enough nonsense! I am taking this scepter!" Veins bulged across Jessie's forehead. When they continued dawdling, she gritted her teeth and shouted, "Hurry! I can't hold on much longer!"

Their partner had given an absolute command. Despite trembling in fear at the thought of facing Ethan, James and Meowth finally placed themselves in front of Jessie.

James threw a Poke Ball and released Weezing. Meowth crossed both arms, and a dangerous cold light glittered along the tips of its claws.

Yet faced with the imposing Gengar, both Weezing and Meowth retreated a step despite themselves!

"Darn it!"

Realizing that its fear had shown, Meowth roared to build its courage, then leaped forward and pounced directly at Gengar.

Gengar merely tilted its body and avoided the attack with ease. Before Meowth could turn around, Gengar extended its enormous tongue and struck with Lick. A deep chill instantly spread across Meowth's entire body, leaving it paralyzed!

A short distance away, James felt a headache coming on. Gengar had merely extended its tongue, and Meowth had already lost the ability to battle.

Even so, he could only steel himself and command Weezing to attack.

"Weezing, use Sludge Bomb!"

Sludge Bomb was a Poison-type attack. Against the Poison- and Ghost-type Gengar, it could inflict almost no meaningful damage.

James had no better alternative. Weezing's typing placed it at an inherent disadvantage against both of Gengar's types!

It could still use certain Normal-type moves, but closing the distance would probably result in it being defeated in one strike just like Meowth.

As Sludge Bomb drew closer, Gengar cackled and gathered a Shadow Ball in its right hand. It threw the attack, which scattered Sludge Bomb instantly and continued forward. With a bang, Shadow Ball struck Weezing and sent it crashing into the wall!

Both Pokemon had been defeated in succession. James lost all will to resist and darted directly behind Jessie.

"You two idiots!"

Jessie was furious at their uselessness, but she managed only one curse before Gengar began approaching her!

She started in alarm. With no time to think and no attention left for stealing the scepter, she released it, reached toward her waist, and pulled out two round objects.

From a distance, Ethan immediately saw that they were not Poke Balls. They were smoke bombs!

Clatter...

The smoke bombs rolled across the floor. An enormous cloud erupted from them and filled the entire room within seconds.

Ethan covered his nose and retreated several steps.

At first, he assumed the trio intended to use the smoke to escape. Then he suddenly heard Maya cry out, followed by a window shattering and glass raining across the floor!

Everything happened in the blink of an eye.

When the smoke thinned enough for Ethan to make out the room, Team Rocket was nowhere to be seen!

Jessie, James, Meowth, and Weezing had all vanished. Even Maya and the golden scepter had disappeared with them!

Ethan hurried through the shattered floor-to-ceiling window and onto the balcony. A crude hot-air balloon was already rising slowly into the sky, and Jessie's triumphant laughter drifted faintly toward him!

Ethan smiled bitterly and shook his head, but he was not particularly angry at the outcome.

No matter what they did, the trio was destined to fail.

He simply had never expected Jessie to be so audacious. Stealing the scepter was apparently not enough. She had abducted Maya as well!

I truly have no idea what goes through that woman's mind...

Ethan sighed and took out a Poke Ball. He threw it into the air, and after blue light flashed, Charizard appeared on the balcony!

Ethan vaulted onto Charizard's back. The Pokemon spread its wings, and its orange body streaked through the sky at tremendous speed in pursuit of the balloon...

Chapter 460: A Dragon-Riding Rescue

Charizard beat its wings and streaked through the sky. The distance between it and the hot-air balloon visibly shrank with every moment.

Inside the balloon, Meowth sensed something behind them. It looked back, and cold sweat instantly covered its body.

"It's Ethan! He's chasing us on Charizard!"

Jessie spun around at Meowth's cry. When she saw Charizard already drawing close, the smile on her face froze!

"What's happening? Didn't we just shake him off?" Her voice was urgent, with none of the triumph she had shown during their escape.

"Idiot! You should've known that was impossible..." James sighed. His tone was gloomy, but his expression clearly said, I expected this all along. "He's Team Rocket's greatest enemy! He isn't as easy to deal with as the twerps. Even the Boss can't do anything about him. How could a couple of smoke bombs possibly hold him back?"

Jessie immediately panicked. "What do we do!? Our balloon can never outrun him!"

"What else can we do? We have to think of something!"

James recovered his composure and pulled a rope with determination. He tried to increase the heat and lift the balloon to an altitude Charizard could never reach, allowing them to escape Ethan's pursuit.

But how could a rising hot-air balloon possibly match Charizard's speed?

An orange blur flashed before the trio's eyes as Charizard swept past them!

The two sides were so close that, under the moonlight, Team Rocket could clearly see Ethan's calm face!

"This is bad! He caught us!" Meowth shouted in complete panic.

James silently groaned. At that moment, he truly wanted to ask who the villains were supposed to be!

How had the glorious Team Rocket been reduced to such a miserable state? They belonged to an evil organization feared wherever its name was heard, yet one man was chasing all three of them away!

Complaints aside, James understood that they had to resolve the situation immediately.

He made a quick decision. "We have to reduce our weight somehow! Otherwise, we'll never escape!"

The instant he spoke, Jessie and Meowth both turned toward Maya in the corner.

Rope bound Maya's hands and feet, while tape covered her mouth. She could neither move nor make a sound.

When she saw the trio looking at her and understood what they intended, Maya's furious eyes became piercing!

Jessie answered without hesitation. "This woman is the heaviest and the most useless thing here. Throw her out first!"

"That doesn't seem right..." A drop of cold sweat rolled down James's face. "She's a living person, and a woman at that. We can't just throw her away. We should get rid of the ballast instead..."

"Are you an idiot? Who has time to worry about that now? Of course we're throwing all of it out!" Meowth scolded James, then turned to Jessie in confusion. "But now that ya mention it... Why did you grab this woman in the first place? Weren't we only supposed to steal the scepter?"

"Well..." Jessie scratched her cheek awkwardly. "She held it too tightly, and I couldn't take the scepter from her, so I brought her along. Anyway, stop wasting time. We only grabbed her by accident, so hurry and throw her out!"

"But..."

James was deeply reluctant. He might be a villain, but no matter what happened, he could never bring himself to throw a woman from the balloon.

The delay gave Charizard enough time to circle the balloon. When it appeared before them again, it suddenly raised its head. A stream of searing fire erupted from its mouth and burned straight through the balloon overhead!

Once the balloon burst, the basket below lost its lift and naturally began plummeting toward the sea.

"Aah!"

The Team Rocket trio screamed miserably. They clung tightly to one another, but as the basket dropped, the violent motion flung all three into the open air!

At least they no longer had to argue about whether to throw Maya overboard. Everyone was airborne now, and no one needed the balloon!

Maya naturally fell with them.

Her hands and feet remained bound. Unable to struggle or call out, she could do nothing but watch the ocean rush closer!

Just as panic filled her heart, a figure flashed before her. Before she could react, she landed within a pair of strong arms!

When Maya recovered and looked up, she was delighted to find Ethan holding her securely!

At the same time, Gengar flew into the air and caught the golden scepter.

Both Maya and the scepter were now safe.

As for Team Rocket, the darkness prevented Ethan from seeing where they had fallen, and he had no time to worry about them.

Even if he had seen them, he probably would have remained unmoved.

Those people had fallen from the sky hundreds of times. Their lives were remarkably durable, so there was no need to worry about whether they survived!

You're on your own.

Ethan was about to speak to Maya when he suddenly noticed the soft, smooth sensation beneath his hands.

He looked down. Maya wore a white silk nightgown. The material was thin and half transparent, and under the moonlight, the contours beneath it were faintly visible.

One of Ethan's hands supported her bottom, while the other held her back!

Both his palms and fingers could clearly feel Maya's firm, warm body.

The vivid sensation struck directly at Ethan's nerves!

Maya noticed the change in his gaze and immediately understood her situation. There was nothing she could do, especially with the ropes preventing even the slightest movement. She lay in his arms like a lamb awaiting its fate!

When Team Rocket entered her room, Maya had been resting. She had possessed no time to change her clothes.

Ethan cleared his throat and looked away. He hurriedly placed Maya on Charizard's back, removed the tape from her mouth, and untied the ropes around her.

"You're safe now."

As he spoke, Ethan removed his jacket and draped it over Maya's shoulders.

"Thank you for saving me."

Maya's face reddened slightly, but she thanked him with natural composure.

She appeared quite calm on the surface, though she inevitably felt shy inside.

Maya might be a Sea Priestess who usually seemed far beyond anyone's reach, but she was still only a woman in her twenties. How could she remain completely unaffected after being held so closely by a man?

Within that atmosphere, she remembered the danger moments ago. Beneath the moonlight, she looked at the handsome face so near her own and suddenly felt her heart, silent for so many years, begin pounding wildly...

Chapter 461: Setting Out for Silver Rock Isle

Beneath the moonlight, Charizard glided in from the distance and finally hovered above the Temple of the Sea.

Holding Maya in his arms, Ethan leaped from Charizard's back and landed steadily on the balcony.

The curtains billowed in the wind. Shards from the broken window still lay scattered across the floor, reflecting faintly in the moonlight.

The tireless rush of the whirlpool continued nearby, but otherwise the surroundings were utterly silent. If not for the wreckage left by the battle, who could have imagined that so much had happened here in such a short time?

To keep Maya's soft, bare feet from being cut by the broken glass, Ethan had no choice but to carry her into the room.

The shards cracked beneath his shoes and splintered into even smaller pieces.

After gently placing Maya on the bed, Ethan finally breathed a sigh of relief.

He had not actually done much beyond riding Charizard back and forth, but anyone forced to remain awake this late and travel so far would inevitably feel exhausted in both body and mind.

Fortunately, the incident had finally come to an end.

"All right, you're safe here now." He smiled. "Team Rocket has been driven off, so they probably won't come back to trouble you again anytime soon."

"So those people were Team Rocket..." Maya nodded dejectedly. "I've heard their name many times, but today was my first encounter with them. I never expected that they would target not only the God of the Sea, but also the scepter in my hands."

She looked at Ethan with a solemn expression. "I know I've already said it, but I must thank you again. If you hadn't been there, the consequences might have been unthinkable..."

"You truly don't need to be so polite." Ethan shook his head. "My Gengar happened to notice them while it was wandering around. Otherwise, I never would've known they'd infiltrated the temple. Once I saw them, of course I couldn't simply stand aside."

He spoke with complete confidence, apparently forgetting that he had hesitated for quite a while before leaving his room.

From another perspective, if Ethan had never interfered, Team Rocket would have simply stolen the scepter and left. They would never have abducted Maya. She could then have awakened the others, and with Ash and his friends' ability to spring into action, recovering the scepter would have been easy. Maya would never have been placed in danger.

If events had unfolded that way, matters might actually have been much simpler.

Regardless, everything had already happened and reached a satisfactory conclusion. There was no need to dwell on possibilities that had never come to pass.

Both of them fell silent, and the atmosphere in the room suddenly felt somewhat strange.

After everything that had just happened, Ethan noticed that the way Maya looked at him had changed.

It was difficult to describe. Her gaze contained something that reminded him both of Sabrina in the past and Erika now.

He did not dare remain for long. After carrying Maya for so long and feeling her soft body against his own, he needed to step outside and calm himself down.

"It's already very late. You should have someone clean this up and then get some proper rest."

After hurriedly leaving those words behind, Ethan turned and walked away, presenting Maya with a dashing view of his back.

Behind him, Maya remained silent. She merely watched him with an unusual look in her eyes until he disappeared beyond the door.

...

Early the next morning, while everyone ate breakfast in the great hall, Maya briefly told the oblivious Ash and the others how Team Rocket had attacked her the previous night.

She glossed over the specific details and said little about how she had been rescued.

Only then did Ash and his friends learn what had happened during the night!

"Those Team Rocket creeps are horrible! How dare they attack Miss Maya at night!" Brock angrily slapped the table, then immediately changed his tone and asked with concern, "Miss Maya, were you hurt?"

"I'm fine." Maya shook her head and glanced at Ethan without drawing attention to the gesture. "Mr. Ethan Vale rescued me in time, so the incident never became any more serious."

Hearing Maya mention him, Ethan lifted another forkful of food to his mouth and stared straight ahead as though she were speaking about someone else entirely.

Despite the enormous commotion the previous night, Ash and the others had not noticed a thing. It could only be said that the Temple of the Sea was truly immense. The roar of the whirlpool had also prevented the sounds of Ethan's battle with Team Rocket from reaching their rooms.

Erika's gaze moved repeatedly between Ethan and Maya. With a woman's intuition, she sensed that the events of the previous night were probably not quite as simple as Maya had described.

Yet both of them behaved perfectly normally, revealing nothing at all.

Once the group finished breakfast, Maya personally escorted them outside the temple's main entrance.

Looking at the group as they prepared to depart, Maya spoke gravely. "Last night's events made me realize that the threat from Team Rocket has become urgent. Stealing my scepter may have been only one part of their plan. We must resolve this as soon as possible. We cannot allow them to capture the God of the Sea!"

"Leave it to us." This time, not only Brock but Ash and Misty also made the same promise. "Don't worry, Miss Maya. We absolutely won't let them succeed!"

Seeing their confidence, Maya finally smiled.

"I believe in you. I'll wait here for your good news!"

After leaving the Temple of the Sea, the group went to the harbor and found a small boat bound for Silver Rock Isle.

According to the clues Maya had provided, the God of the Sea had last appeared in the waters near Silver Rock Isle.

Silver Rock Isle was one of the Whirl Islands' four large islands. Located in the northeast, it was relatively small, nowhere near the size of Red Rock Isle, which Ethan and the others had just left.

Kasado City was the only city on Silver Rock Isle. The island had received its name from the silver rock found there in abundance. It was said that emblems made from silver rock offered some protection and brought their owners good fortune. Unfortunately, their fame also meant that many people in the city fashioned counterfeit silver rock into products for sale.

The group encountered trouble almost as soon as they departed the harbor.

The sea was far from calm that day, and the sky was rather overcast. Strong winds and waves made the small boat pitch constantly.

Apart from Ash and Misty, Ethan, Erika, and Brock all grew more or less dizzy from the motion. Ethan eventually could not bear it any longer. He simply released Charizard and had it carry Erika and him through the sky, which finally eased their nausea.

Fortunately, the two islands were close together. After traveling east for only two or three hours, the boat brought them to the waters near Silver Rock Isle.

As soon as they arrived, the weather abruptly changed. The clouds vanished, and the day became calm and sunny once more.

Chapter 462: The Search and a Reunion with Richie

After reaching these waters, the group did not continue to Silver Rock Isle. Following their map, they instead traveled to another nearby islandOgi Isle.

Ogi Isle was at least two-thirds smaller than Silver Rock Isle. Far removed from the noise of modern society, it retained its original natural environment. There were no human towns anywhere on the island, only a handful of scattered homes.

Several even smaller islands also surrounded Ogi Isle. Large and small, they clustered together to form a relatively modest archipelago.

Once everyone had gone ashore, Ethan paid the fare and watched the boat depart.

From this point onward, they could rely only on themselves.

They had barely stepped onto the island, before their legs could even readjust to the solid ground, when Ash impatiently asked, "What should we do next?"

Ethan considered the question for a moment before sharing his thoughts. "Our immediate priority should still be finding Lugia. We need to protect it before Team Rocket captures it, or convince it to move somewhere else."

"But..." Ash looked around. The same dense forest stretched in every direction, without any visible differences. He scratched his cheek. "Where do we even start looking? It couldn't be hiding on this island, could it?"

At Ash's question, Misty rubbed her chin and offered her own analysis. "Judging from what we saw in the Orange Islands... Wouldn't a Legendary Pokemon like Lugia live in the deepest part of the ocean to avoid being discovered by humans?"

"That's difficult to say." Ethan shook his head. "Many of the Whirl Islands have waterways beneath them. Lakes and underground rivers on the islands can lead directly to the sea, so Lugia could still be hiding somewhere inland. Otherwise, why have so few people discovered any trace of it? Besides, didn't Maya tell us that her clue came from someone who spotted what might have been Lugia on one of these islands?"

Erika agreed. "Ethan is right. Searching for Lugia in the ocean would be like looking for a needle in a haystack. Our only option is to focus on these nearby islands and try our luck. Perhaps we can first find the person who provided the clue and ask them for more details."

Seeing the two of them echo each other with exactly the same opinion, Misty narrowed her eyes.

She might still be young, but she was a girl, after all. Her sensitivity toward romance placed her miles ahead of Ash, and even Brock, who fell in love with every woman he met, could not compare.

Misty had noticed that ever since Erika began traveling with Ethan, their time together had led her down the same path as Sabrina. Erika was beginning to fall for him!

The change was plain for anyone to see!

Sigh... Now I have another rival...

She sighed inwardly, but the small trace of unhappiness vanished as soon as she remembered that Ethan had invited her to travel with him in the next region.

Hehe. There's plenty of time, after all.

I'm still just a little girl. By the time I grow into a beautiful young woman, Erika and Sabrina will both be old ladies in their thirties. How could they possibly be more attractive than me?

I'm the world's most beautiful girl!

Ethan will definitely be mine in the end!!

The group rested beside the sea for a while. Once Brock was no longer dizzy, they chose a direction at random and began exploring the island's interior.

They crossed the beach, continued over a stretch of grassland, and entered a dense forest. Before they had traveled very far, a patch of bushes beside them suddenly rustled.

In the wild, movement like that usually meant a small Pokemon was hiding in the undergrowth. Ash immediately became interested. He cautiously approached the bushes and was about to part the thick grass when a Pokemon emerged on its own. It had yellow fur, long ears, a lightning-bolt-shaped tail, and the appearance of a mouse standing upright!

"Huh? Pikachu?"

Ash exclaimed when he saw the species he knew so well. He had never expected Pikachu to live on such a remote island!

After studying it more carefully, however, he suddenly found this Pikachu familiar. The distinctive tuft of hair on its forehead reminded him of someone in particular.

"You're Sparky, aren't you?" Ash crouched and looked at the Pikachu. Although the words formed a question, his voice brimmed with confidence.

Sparky?

Looking at the Pikachu, Ethan searched his memory and immediately recalled the boy named Richie from the Indigo League.

Sparky also seemed to recognize Ash. It called out to him, then began playing happily with Ash's Pikachu.

Once its identity was confirmed, Brock immediately looked around and murmured, "If Sparky is here, that means..."

Before he could finish, a boy dressed very similarly to Ash stepped out from behind a large tree.

"Sparky, don't wander off..."

Halfway through his sentence, the boy noticed Ethan's group. His words abruptly stopped, and surprise appeared on his face!

"Ash! What are you doing here?"

"Richie! I knew it was you!"

The two shouted almost simultaneously.

Just as they had expected, the newcomer was Richie!

Once everyone came face-to-face, however, the atmosphere inevitably became somewhat awkward.

During the Indigo League, Richie had eliminated Ash and advanced to the quarterfinals. Ethan had then eliminated Richie and moved on to the semifinals.

The three formed something like a food chain. Ethan in particular had defeated Richie decisively, without showing the slightest mercy.

After their battles, Ash and Richie had each shaken hands with their opponents and acted as though neither result bothered them. Yet a thorn still remained in both their hearts. Meeting the opponent who had defeated them again naturally caused some discomfort, even if no one mentioned those matches.

Fortunately, Ash was carefree, and although Richie was more thoughtful, both were passionate young Trainers. After a brief silence, the atmosphere quickly became lively again.

They found a flat rock and sat down, then inevitably spent some time catching up.

Looking at Ash and Ethan, Richie sighed with emotion. "We haven't seen each other since the Indigo League ended. Neither of you has changed at all!"

"You haven't changed either, Richie!" Ash scratched his head. "I really never expected us to meet again somewhere like this. I guess we must be connected by fate! By the way, Richie, what are you doing here?"

Richie answered without hesitation. "I came here to search for a mysterious Pokemon!"

A mysterious Pokemon!?

At his answer, Ethan and the others instinctively looked at one another.

Did Richie come here to search for Lugia too?

But how did he know Lugia was here!?

Chapter 463: Richie Joins the Group

The two Pikachu chased each other nearby, having the time of their lives.

Richie did not notice the strange looks exchanged by the group and continued enthusiastically, "Before coming here, I researched that mysterious Pokemon. I still don't know exactly what it is, but I used the reports and rumors online to work out where it might appear and where it might be headed. Ogi Isle was the most suspicious location, so I came here immediately!"

Richie truly was impressive. Ethan and the others had reached this place using information from Maya, while Richie had uncovered everything entirely through his own investigation!

Since information from two different sources ultimately pointed to the same location, the chances that Lugia was somewhere near Ogi Isle were clearly greatest. It also proved that Ethan and the others had come to the right place.

Only then did Richie belatedly ask, "By the way, why did all of you come here?"

Ash opened his mouth to answer, but suddenly hesitated. He glanced at Ethan and ultimately swallowed his words.

That alone showed how much Ash had grown. He had actually learned to think before he spoke!

In the past, he probably would have answered without the slightest consideration!

Fortunately, there was nothing they needed to conceal. When Ash looked toward him, Ethan chose to tell the truth. "We're actually here for much the same reason as you."

Richie looked at them in mild surprise. "You mean you're also searching for that mysterious Pokemon? I thought I was the only person looking for it."

After hearing the news, Richie's heart instinctively tightened. If both groups shared the same goal, did that mean one side was destined to leave disappointed?

There was only one mysterious Pokemon. No matter who eventually caught it, the result would affect their relationship.

Ethan was one thing. To Richie, he was merely a powerful opponent who had defeated him, and the two had no real friendship to speak of. But Richie and Ash had similar personalities and shared a sense of mutual appreciation. He did not want a dispute over who caught the Pokemon to damage that precious bond.

Ethan saw his concern immediately and explained with a smile, "Although that mysterious Pokemon is our goal too, we're here for a different reason. To be precise, we came to protect it."

"Protect it?" Richie froze, then seemed to realize something and urgently asked, "Does that mean you know what the mysterious Pokemon really is?"

Ethan smiled calmly. "It's Lugia, the God of the Sea."

"Lugia!?" Richie's eyes widened at the name, and he cried out in shock. "The mysterious Pokemon is Lugia!? Is that true!?"

When Ethan nodded, Richie remained stunned for quite some time before finally accepting the truth.

He had imagined all kinds of possibilities for the mysterious Pokemon's identity, but the rarest possibility he had considered was a Shiny Pokemon. Who could have expected it to be the God of the Sea?

Judging from Richie's lingering astonishment, he was still processing the revelation.

Ethan continued, "According to the information we received, Team Rocket has already targeted it. Someone asked us to come here and protect this Lugia."

"I understand." Richie released a long breath, then spoke solemnly. "Please let me join you. I'll help too!"

"What? You don't plan to catch it anymore?"

Richie shook his head with a complicated expression and gave a wry smile. "It's the God of the Sea. A human shouldn't capture it."

Ethan looked at him in surprise.

Possessing that kind of restraint was genuinely admirable.

The last person Ethan remembered meeting with the same quality was Jimmy. When faced with Raikou, Jimmy had remained equally clearheaded. He also believed that Legendary Pokemon should not be captured by humans and ought to live freely in nature.

Unfortunately, Ethan completely lacked that kind of restraint. As a result, that very Raikou was now resting quietly inside one of his Great Balls!

With their goals aligned, everyone ended their rest and prepared to begin searching for Lugia immediately. Before they set out, however, Richie shared one piece of information.

"Before you arrived, I already explored all of Ogi Isle, but I didn't discover any sign of the mysterious Pokemon... of Lugia."

Ethan nodded. "In that case, let's focus directly on the smaller islands nearby."

Following his gaze, the others looked toward the island closest to Ogi Isle. It was a small and uninhabited island, less than half Ogi Isle's size. Two towering mountains stood at its center, surrounded by a dense ring of forest.

Encircled by the sea and even farther removed from humanity, an isolated island like this offered an excellent habitat for Lugia or any other Pokemon.

The group returned to the shore and looked across the broad expanse of water. With their boat gone, they released Pokemon of their own to carry them across the sea.

Ethan climbed onto Charizard and pulled Erika up behind him. Misty took Brock with her, while Ash brought Richie along.

The distance was only a little over two kilometers. It did not take long for the three Pokemon to reach the other island one after another.

Ethan was the first to set foot on its shore. He took out his map, only to discover that the island was not labeled with a name.

Another nameless island...

Once the others came ashore, the group headed into the island's interior together.

They had not gone far when they spotted a young boy floating in a small pool alongside a Lanturn. Both watched the newcomers nervously.

The boy looked about six or seven years old. He wore only a pair of swimming trunks, and his hair had the round style common among young boys. Lanturn, the evolved form of Chinchou, had a distinctly fishlike body and yellow markings across its face that resembled a mask.

Unlike Chinchou, Lanturn had only one antenna on its head, but the stalk branched into two yellow, spherical lights. The larger one hung in front of its head, while the smaller one extended from the branch.

Before Ethan could take out his Pokedex, Ash had already pointed his own at Lanturn.

The Pokedex announced, "Beep. Lanturn, the Light Pokemon. A Water and Electric type. Lanturn inhabits the deep sea and is known as the star of the deep. It releases a dazzling light to blind its prey, then strikes with electricity while the target is unable to move before swallowing it whole. Because prey is scarce on the deep seafloor, it is said to compete fiercely with Lumineon."

Chapter 464: The Boy Named Oliver

When the group reached the edge of the pool, Richie crouched down and asked the young boy, "Hello. Do you live on this island?"

As they studied the boy, he secretly studied them in return. Although his gaze remained full of caution, he slowly nodded.

"More or less. I live on Ogi Isle, but I often come here to play. Why? Is something wrong?"

While he spoke, Ethan's sharp eyes noticed what appeared to be a dark shadow quietly retreating through the water behind the boy.

The shadow vanished beneath the surface in the blink of an eye, but Ethan still caught sight of it.

The boy also seemed to be deliberately hiding it. He positioned his body directly in their line of sight, clearly unwilling to let them discover the shadow!

Unfortunately, it was too indistinct, and the reflection on the water further obscured Ethan's view. He could not tell exactly what it was.

Whatever the case, it had certainly been a Pokemon.

As he considered this, he felt Erika's shoulder gently bump his own.

When he turned toward her, Erika blinked meaningfully at him. She said nothing, but she had obviously seen the shadow too.

Neither of them gave any sign that they had noticed it.

At that moment, Ash heard the boy's answer and eagerly asked, "If you're from around here, have you seen any mysterious Pokemon?"

The question was so blunt that everyone except Ash clearly saw panic flash across the boy's face!

"There's nothing like that around here!" the boy answered stiffly. His wandering gaze, however, made it obvious that he was lying.

Now Misty, Brock, and Richie also realized that something was wrong, not only Ethan and Erika.

This boy definitely knows something!

Careless Ash noticed nothing unusual. Still unwilling to give up, he continued, "Then have you heard any rumors?"

Under Ash's direct questioning, the boy found it increasingly difficult to hold his ground.

"A-Absolutely none!"

The next moment, he seemed to realize that he should not keep retreating. Perhaps afraid that Ethan and the others would doubt him, he forced a smile and added, "Think about it. If there really were some mysterious Pokemon here, it would've caused a huge commotion and been caught a long time ago, right? So I think you shouldn't believe such ridiculous rumors."

"I see..."

Ash appeared completely convinced, without the slightest suspicion.

To Ethan, however, the boy's explanation only made his attempt to hide the truth more obvious.

Of course, Ash's reaction did not mean he was stupid. He was simply too young and immature to read people's expressions, and he lacked experience dealing with others.

As Ethan watched the boy, he tried to recall the plot involving Lugia. Unfortunately, those memories had grown too vague and distant. No matter how hard he thought, he could not remember any more details.

One thing was certain: this boy had to be a key figure. Ethan could even make the bold guess that the shadow that had just departed might have been Lugia!

With that thought, he stepped forward and smiled at the boy. "We've talked for all this time, but we still don't know your name."

Looking at the handsome, cheerful young man before him, the boy believed that his deception had worked and secretly breathed a sigh of relief.

"My name is Oliver, and this Lanturn beside me is my Pokemon."
