Ethan smiled pleasantly. "Then, Oliver, what was the Pokemon that just left your side?"

At Ethan's question, Oliver's expression changed dramatically. Although he was immersed in the cold pool, sweat still ran down his forehead!

"I-I don't know what you're talking about..." he stammered. "You must have seen something else. It's only ever been Lanturn and me here!"

After hearing Ethan's words and seeing Oliver's reaction, the others finally realized that another Pokemon had quietly left while none of them were paying attention!

"Really?" Ethan's smile did not fade. "But I saw it very clearly. A Pokemon swam away from directly behind you."

"There wasn't any Pokemon! Your eyes were playing tricks on you!" Oliver no longer wanted to speak with them. After hurriedly answering, he began swimming away. Even as he swam, he looked back and called, "Oh! I suddenly remembered something I need to do. Goodbye!"

He actually ran away...

Watching Oliver swim farther away, Ethan shouted after him, "Even if you don't tell me, I know the Pokemon that just left was probably Lugia, wasn't it?"

This time, Oliver could no longer pretend to remain calm.

He stopped in the water and looked back at Ethan. He opened his mouth to ask something, only to swallow the words before they emerged.

"Don't worry," Ethan said gently. "We came here to protect it from being captured by bad people. We don't mean it any harm!"

Oliver was only seven or eight years old. Hearing the sincerity in Ethan's voice, he could not resist asking, "Really?"

"I wouldn't lie to you." Ethan suddenly remembered something else. "Oh, right. I forgot to introduce myself. My name is Ethan Vale, and I'm this year's Sea Hero!"

"The Sea Hero!?"

At that title, Oliver's eyes widened with delight!

To children from the Whirl Islands, the Sea Hero represented strength and courage. Sea Heroes were greatly respected and welcomed by the local people, and their status in the children's hearts was every bit as great as that of a League Conference champion!

This did not mean the people of the Whirl Islands were ignorant enough to believe a Sea Hero was equal to a League Conference champion. The Pokemon League simply possessed far less influence here than the Temple of the Sea. Moreover, no Trainer from the Whirl Islands had won a major tournament in a very long time, leaving the local people with little sense of connection to the Pokemon League.

Once Oliver learned that Ethan was the Sea Hero, his attitude reversed completely. Not even the slightest doubt remained.

He swam back to shore and suddenly found the man before him far more agreeable. All his resistance disappeared. He circled Ethan, examining him from every direction as though observing some rare creature.

Ethan waited until Oliver finally calmed down a little, then said, "All right. Can we have an honest conversation now? And could you let us meet Lugia too?"

Chapter 465: Silver

Oliver nodded and dove beneath the water. A short while later, he surfaced again beside a white Pokemon with wings shaped like arms and a blue tail fin.

With a single glance, Ethan and the others immediately recognized the Pokemon as the legendary God of the SeaLugia!

Compared with the Lugia they had encountered in the Orange Islands, however, this one was far smaller. It stood only about as tall as a human child. Even among its own species, it was clearly still very young.

Oliver introduced the two sides. "This is my friend Silver. Silver, this is the Sea Hero and his traveling companions. Go ahead and say hello!"

Lugia's eyes curved into happy crescents as it called cheerfully to them. It did not seem shy around strangers or particularly frightened of humans.

Faced with such an enthusiastic God of the Sea, Ash, Misty, and the others quickly recovered from their initial bewilderment. They hurriedly bowed and nodded in greeting.

"S-Silver... H-Hello..."

"I'm Ash."

"And I'm Misty!"

This was the first time any of them had observed a Lugia from so close. Even Ash and Misty had only seen one from a distance in the Orange Islands. They had never been able to study one carefully at such close range.

For Misty in particular, Lugia and Kyogre were among the Pokemon that every Water Pokemon Trainer dreamed of and ultimately hoped to catch. Now that one had appeared directly before her, how could she possibly remain calm?

Likewise, this was the first time Richie and Brock had ever seen a Lugia with their own eyes. Even though this one was still only a juvenile, the sight brought them tremendous shock and wonder. They could hardly contain the surging excitement in their hearts!

Erika was the exception. Perhaps seeing so many Legendary Pokemon around Ethan had already made such encounters feel ordinary. Although this was also her first time seeing Lugia in person, she was surprised to discover that she felt only a little curiosity toward the God of the Sea. Beyond that, she had no other thoughts, almost as though she were looking at an ordinary Pokemon.

Perhaps this is what it means to have broadened my horizons...

With that thought, she turned toward Ethan. Sure enough, he looked calm and composed. Lugia's appearance had caused almost no visible change in him.

After everyone exchanged greetings, Oliver explained that he and Silver shared a secret base. Whenever other humans appeared, Lugia usually hid there.

When Ethan spotted Silver's shadow moments ago, it had been quietly leaving for that secret base!

Misty studied Silver for quite some time before finally asking with curiosity, "Oliver, how did the two of you meet?"

For some reason, Oliver blushed in front of the bright and beautiful girl. He lowered his head, unable to look Misty in the eyes. "I-It was a little while ago... I was playing beside the sea when I happened to see it... A-And then we became good friends."

Before he even finished speaking, his ears had turned bright red!

Unlike dense-headed Ash, Oliver had clearly awakened to romance much earlier despite being only seven or eight years old. Or perhaps, having always lived among these islands, this was simply his first encounter with such a pretty girl, and the sight had stirred his young heart!

This also proved that although Misty often called herself the world's most beautiful girl with some exaggeration, she truly was very pretty. Combined with her spirited, cheerful personality, she undoubtedly held tremendous charm for innocent young boys!

"I see. You really are lucky." Misty nodded in understanding. "Then you're the one who gave it the name Silver too, right?"

"Th-That's right..." Oliver scratched his head in embarrassment. "Most of its body is silvery white, so that's why I chose the name."

"That makes sense. It looks like Silver really likes the name!"

At Misty's praise, Oliver felt his heart pound so violently that it seemed ready to leap from his chest!

Nearby, Ash tilted his head and asked Oliver in confusion, "If you and Lugia are such good friends, why didn't you tell us it was here?"

The reason was so simple that, among everyone present, perhaps only the innocent and naive Ash still failed to understand it.

Before Oliver could answer, Richie explained for him. "Oliver wanted to protect Silver, so of course he wouldn't reveal anything about it. He didn't know us at all before now. If we'd been bad people with malicious intentions, we would've tried everything possible to capture Lugia the moment we learned it was here!"

"That's right." Oliver nodded, then secretly glanced at Misty again.

Once Oliver and Lugia came ashore, everyone sat together nearby. It was already noon, so Brock naturally took out his cooking equipment and began preparing lunch.

Erika hurried over to help. With two skilled cooks working together, a delicious aroma soon drifted through the air.

Both Oliver and Silver were drawn by the scent and repeatedly swallowed their saliva.

Oliver ate home-cooked meals every day, so the unfamiliar aroma had merely awakened his appetite. Silver, however, had clearly never seen fragrant human food before. It practically drooled with hunger!

Its behavior amused everyone and eased much of their tension around the Legendary Pokemon. Viewed without its divine aura, Lugia was simply another kind of Pokemon!

Before long, lunch was finally ready, much to Silver's eager delight. The instant Brock served it a heaping spoonful of food, it impatiently began devouring the meal.

Everyone exchanged looks and stopped watching it. They sat on the ground, picked up their bowls and utensils, and focused on finishing the food before them.

While they ate lunch, two men in black diving suits hid suspiciously behind a cluster of reefs in the distance. A large red R was printed across each man's chest, and they observed the group through a spy camera.

One of them took out a communication device and whispered, "This is Search Team C. Reporting to Dr. Danbawe've located the target!"

After a burst of electronic static, an elderly but powerful voice sounded through his earpiece.

"It's not Danba, it's Dr. Namba! Honestly, how many times do I have to tell you before you'll remember?"

"Ah... My apologies." The Team Rocket member wiped cold sweat from his forehead and apologized, then reported seriously, "Dr. Namba, we've discovered Lugia on a small island off Ogi Isle. Requesting further instructions!"

Chapter 466: Remember, It's Dr. Namba

Somewhere on the seafloor beyond the Whirl Islands, a secret Team Rocket base lay hidden.

Built from steel atop a broad shelf of level rock, the base was an enormous arched structure more than thirty meters tall. Even in the pitch-black depths, the lights shining from within illuminated a vast area around it.

Countless Water Pokemon swam far beyond the base's perimeter, as though none dared approach.

Through its glass windows, people could occasionally be seen moving inside. A considerable number of Team Rocket members were clearly stationed here.

This was Team Rocket's most secretive research base in the Johto region. Its director was Dr. Namba, a vigorous elderly man already over sixty years old.

The old man's fiery red hair and beard reflected his explosive temper. Baldness had unfortunately left him with hair only around the sides of his head. Despite his remarkable academic achievements, no matter how often he corrected people, everyone somehow instinctively remembered his name incorrectly.

Dr. Namba now sat in the control room with several black-clad Team Rocket members standing on either side. The large screen before him displayed live footage transmitted by the search team.

Although the team continued requesting further instructions, Dr. Namba had no attention to spare for them. Instead, his gaze rested on the people surrounding Lugia.

More precisely, he stared fixedly at Ethan!

He studied Ethan until his brow furrowed deeply, then muttered, "Honestly, isn't that Ethan Vale, the man they call Team Rocket's greatest enemy? Why is he here? This has become troublesome..."

After thinking for a while, he waved over one of the Team Rocket members.

The man approached him and asked respectfully, "Dr. Sanba, what are your orders?"

The instructions Dr. Namba had been about to give lodged directly in his throat. He could only glare fiercely at the man. "It's not Sanba, it's Namba!"

"I'm sorry, Doctor..."

Dr. Namba sighed helplessly. "Have the nearby operations teams converge on that location. Begin with Plan A and attempt to capture Lugia."

The Team Rocket member also glanced at Ethan on the screen, then nodded solemnly. "Yes, understood!"

...

After helping Brock clean up the bowls and utensils, Ethan patted his full stomach and stretched comfortably.

With his hunger satisfied and the warm sun shining down, drowsiness gradually crept over him.

Misty yawned as well, then tilted her head toward Ethan and asked, "Ethan, what should we do now? We can't just sit here doing nothing and wait for Team Rocket forever, can we?"

The moment she finished, Ash sprang upright from the ground with a kip-up. He turned toward Richie, his eyes blazing. "Since we still have time, Richie, how about a battle?"

Looking at his former opponent, Richie shook his head. "Sorry, I'm not in the mood. Now that I've seen Lugia, all I can think about is how to protect it. I really can't summon any enthusiasm for a battle."

"I see..." Ash scratched his head awkwardly and sat down again. "That's fine. We can have a proper match at the Silver Conference instead!"

"I'm sorry again," Richie said apologetically. "I don't plan to enter the Silver Conference..."

"What!?"

Ash was not the only one shocked. Ethan, Misty, and Brock all turned to stare at Richie.

Misty asked in confusion, "Why wouldn't you enter? Everything was going fine."

Brock also tried to persuade him. "Exactly. After everything you learned at the Indigo League, you're sure to earn an even better result at the Silver Conference!"

Faced with their confusion, Richie shrugged. "My loss at the Indigo League helped me fully understand my weaknesses. That's why I'm traveling from place to place now, catching powerful Pokemon and constantly training. Maybe I'll consider entering another League Conference after my strength has improved dramatically."

"How could..." Ash stared blankly at Richie and sighed in disappointment.

He regretted losing the chance to battle Richie and also felt disappointed that he would have one fewer evenly matched rival in the future.

After a long silence, Ethan noticed the gloomy atmosphere and clapped his hands to draw everyone's attention.

"All right, cheer up. It's time to discuss our real problem."

Once everyone looked toward him, Ethan continued, "If we want to protect Silver and foil Team Rocket's plan, we need to hit them hard first. We're exposed while they're hidden, and we have no idea when they'll act. That leaves us extremely passive and puts us at a major disadvantage. I intend to strike first and seize the initiative ourselves!"

Misty was always Ethan's most loyal supporter. She had no objection whatsoever to his suggestion. All she needed to do was support him without a second thought.

"Exactly! Ethan is right!"

"But..." Richie frowned and offered a different opinion. "If we already know that bad people have targeted Silver, shouldn't we keep it as far from danger as possible? Wouldn't taking it away immediately be better? Calling the police might also be a good choice."

Before Ethan could respond, Misty had already retorted, "You're too naive! What good would calling the police do? Wouldn't that be the same as announcing Silver's existence to the entire world!? And even if we flee, where could we possibly go? Knowing Team Rocket, they'll never give up until they capture Silver!"

She turned back toward Ethan with anticipation. "Go on, Ethan. What should we do?"

Ethan glanced at the embarrassed Richie and nodded. "Misty is right. We have to handle this ourselves. My idea is to lure the snake from its hole. We'll draw Team Rocket to a battlefield that favors us, drag them into the open, defeat them, and send them to prison. Then they'll never dare target Silver again!"

"I agree," Erika said first. "Taking the initiative is better than defending passively. I support Ethan's plan."

Brock rubbed his chin. "Ethan's approach really could work. Like Misty said, I don't think calling the police is a good choice either."

Seeing that everyone appeared to approve of Ethan's idea, Richie finally looked toward Oliver and discovered that even he was nodding along.

Apparently, the boy had no objection whatsoever to anything the Sea Hero proposed.

Richie sighed helplessly. As the newcomer to the group, he wanted to ask only one thing: just what kind of magic did the title of Sea Hero possess...?

Chapter 467: The Duo

Near the reefs along the shore, Oliver and Lugia happily played in the sea. The boy and Pokemon splashed water at each other, looking carefree and delighted.

Ethan and Ash sat on a large rock beside them, leisurely watching the pair.

Everything appeared perfectly normal and peaceful, like a simple diversion after lunch.

Strangely, however, no one else was in sight!

Erika, Misty, Brock, and Richie had all seemingly vanished without a trace!

At the same time, a massive submarine lurked silently beneath the water ahead.

Inside its command room, the captain watched the large monitor displaying images transmitted by the submarine's cameras. His brow instinctively furrowed.

One Team Rocket member asked impatiently, "Captain, we've already waited more than ten minutes. Shouldn't we act?"

The captain considered the question but did not issue an order. Instead, he hesitated. "According to our intelligence, this group has seven people. Why are only three left now? Where are the others?"

"We haven't found any trace of anyone else nearby." The Team Rocket member shook his head and ventured, "Could they have already left? This is only a deserted island with nowhere else to go. I think the others probably returned to the city."

They left...?

The captain rubbed his chin, apparently accepting the suggestion. He immediately relaxed somewhat. "If the group truly split up, their strength has undoubtedly been greatly reduced. That man Ethan Vale will still be difficult to handle, but this is certainly a rare opportunity to capture Lugia!"

He glanced at the man and gave his order. "There's no time to waste. Surface immediately and deploy the operations team!"

...

On the rock, Ash looked over the calm surroundings. With no sign that Team Rocket intended to attack, he turned toward Ethan.

"Ethan, will Team Rocket really come?"

"Be patient." Ethan leaned back and lay directly upon the rock. Watching the white clouds overhead, he lazily continued, "This is just like fishing. I'm sure they're watching us from somewhere right now. We've placed the delicious bait directly in front of them, so there's no need to worry. They'll bite."

As though to prove Ethan's words, before Ash could respond, the sea in front of them suddenly churned. A black submarine broke through the surface and rose from the water!

Its arrival was so abrupt that the enormous vessel appeared directly before Oliver and Lugia. The violently surging water instantly left the boy and Pokemon tossing helplessly in the waves!

Ash stood and followed the strategy they had established earlier, shouting at the submarine, "Who's there!?"

The moment he finished, a man's and a woman's voices came from inside.

"Since you asked us so sincerely!"

"Normally, we wouldn't answer!"

"But we'll make a special exception and tell you!"

"To prevent the destruction of the Earth!"

"To protect the peace of the Earth!"

"To carry out the evils of love and honesty!"

"Playful and mischievous villains!"

"Cassidy!"

"Butch!"

"We are Team Rocket, traveling through the universe!"

"A shocking pink, rosy tomorrow awaits us!"

When Ethan first heard the voices, he thought Jessie and James had arrived. But both the lines and the voices themselves were clearly wrong.

Sure enough, part of the submarine opened and an elevator slowly rose, revealing a man and woman who seemed both familiar and unfamiliar to Ethan.

They were familiar because Ethan had watched the animated series and recognized them at once.

They were unfamiliar because this was his first encounter with either of them since arriving in this world!

Both wore black Team Rocket uniforms. The woman had golden hair arranged in two exaggerated pigtails. Although she was fairly pretty, her shrewd expression suggested someone highly skilled at scheming.

The man had short, pale green hair parted down the middle. He looked both handsome and alert.

Cassidy and Butch!

The Team Rocket trio's greatest rivals within the organization had finally appeared!

These two looked somewhat younger than Jessie and James, and their performance within Team Rocket was stronger. The greatest difference was that Cassidy and Butch possessed excellent equipment and enormous operational budgets. They never needed to worry about money!

Of course, that did not necessarily mean Jessie and James were inferior. They had simply pursued Ash for far too long. Whenever they came close to succeeding, Ash ruined their plans, dramatically lowering their success rate, destroying their prestige, and steadily reducing their status within Team Rocket.

When Ash recognized the pair, he apparently worried that Ethan might not know who they were. "Ethan, those two are also from Team Rocket. I encountered them once before. They're just as persistent as Jessie and James!"

"Understood." Ethan nodded. "Stay alert and make sure you protect Silver!"

"Don't compare us with those two useless fools!" Cassidy looked down at them from above and pointed toward Silver with complete confidence. "That Lugia will belong to us today! Leave now if you know what's good for you, or don't blame us for showing no mercy!"

Butch also turned his gaze toward Ethan and snorted coldly. "I hear you've caused Team Rocket a great deal of trouble. Well, your luck runs out today!"

The pair were clearly brimming with confidence. For one thing, they had never dealt with Ethan and knew nothing of his true abilities. Even though they had heard his name, they assumed the stories were exaggerated.

Without witnessing it themselves, how could they believe that a single person had repeatedly foiled Team Rocket's operations?

Moreover, as one of Team Rocket's finest pairs, they had considerable faith in their own strength. Most of all, they had come fully prepared!

The next moment, more than a dozen Team Rocket members poured out behind them in a dark mass. They also glared down at Ethan with intimidating expressions. At the same time, engines roared on both sides of the submarine as more than a dozen speedboats approached from each direction, carrying dozens more Team Rocket members!

In an instant, Team Rocket's force had grown to seventy or eighty people!

They formed a crescent around the entire beach, leaving Ethan and the others no possible route of escape!

Chapter 468: A Faltering Battle Line

A dark mass of people stood before them. Despite being outnumbered more than ten to one, Ash showed no fear and gave no thought to retreat.

Ethan shook his head and addressed the pair atop the submarine in a tone of exaggerated disappointment. "Using superior numbers to bully a smaller group again? You people truly have no imagination. Can't you send a few elite fighters instead?"

He spoke with complete confidence, seemingly forgetting that during his first several encounters with Legendary Pokemon, he had also secured victory through strength in numbers.

Cassidy and Butch sneered.

He truly doesn't know when he's doomed!

Even now, instead of abandoning Lugia and fleeing, he intends to resist?

So what?

No matter how powerful Ethan's Pokemon were, Team Rocket possessed an overwhelming numerical advantage. Even if every member released only one Pokemon, a saturation attack would be enough to drown any opponent!

They had no intention of observing rules or honor. While their Pokemon attacked, the humans would target the Trainers directly!

Even if Ethan's and Ash's Pokemon could not be defeated quickly, Team Rocket needed only to capture the two Trainers. Their Pokemon would then have no choice but to surrender and place themselves at the enemy's mercy!

"I admire your courage," Butch mocked, "but some things can't be accomplished through bravado alone!"

As he spoke, the Team Rocket members took out their Poke Balls. The instant they released their Pokemon, dozens of Zubat and dozens of Weezing appeared in the air!

The winged Pokemon blocked most of the sky. From Ethan's and Ash's perspective, the dense swarm was truly spectacular!

Ash had seen situations like this many times and naturally refused to back down. He took out all his Poke Balls and hurled every one of them at once.

Bang! Bang! Bang! Bang!

The Poke Balls opened one after another. Blue light flashed, and Heracross, Bayleef, Cyndaquil, Totodile, and Noctowl appeared alongside Pikachu, who had remained at Ash's side. All six Pokemon were now assembled!

At the same time, Ethan sent out his own Pokemon.

Gardevoir, Charizard, Jolteon, Dragonair, Scyther, and the Eevee he had received from the Kimono Sisters also appeared before him.

In only moments, more than a dozen Pokemon had formed ranks and prepared for battle!

Tension filled the air. Although the two Trainers' Pokemon were considerably stronger than their opponents, they remained at an obvious numerical disadvantage. Both sides possessed strengths and weaknesses, making the eventual victor impossible to predict.

This balance existed partly because Ethan had not used his full strength. Pupitar and Crystal Steelix still remained in his bag, but neither Pokemon was well suited to fighting along the shore, so he had not released them.

Beyond those two, he also held two trump cardsSuicune and Raikou.

After spending so much time with Ethan, Suicune could now follow his commands. Raikou remained resistant, however, and needed more time before it would be completely subdued. Unless absolutely necessary, Ethan did not dare release Raikou so casually.

Besides, Ethan was certain that Team Rocket also had something in reserve!

Now they would see which side faltered first and exhausted its hidden methods!

At that moment, Gengar also emerged from Ethan's shadow and joined Gardevoir in guarding him from either side.

No matter what happened across the battlefield, these two Pokemon always thought first of protecting their Trainer.

You want to hurt my Trainer?

Then step over my body first!

Along the shore, the atmosphere froze. A great battle could erupt at any instant.

When Oliver saw so many villains and Pokemon trying to steal Silver, fear filled his heart and his legs trembled slightly. Even so, he called from behind them, "Mr. Hero, I'll help too!"

He prepared to have Lanturn swim forward and join Ethan's and Ash's Pokemon.

Ethan glanced at him and shook his head. "Keep Lanturn where it is. Your highest priority is protecting yourself and Silver!"

Oliver opened his mouth. "But..."

"No buts!" Ethan replied in a tone that allowed no argument. "Silver is your friend, isn't it? You're the final line of defense beside it. You have to keep it safe!"

Hearing the Sea Hero's words, Oliver understood the weight of his responsibility and nodded forcefully.

"Yes! I understand. Leave it to me!"

With events having reached this point, there was nothing more to say. In the confusion, no one knew which side moved first. The Pokemon on both sides charged simultaneously!

When the opposing forces collided, the battlefield quickly split into more than a dozen smaller clashes and descended into chaos.

It was not that Ethan's and Ash's Pokemon did not want to cooperate. There were simply too many enemies. They had to guard against hostile moves while taking care not to obstruct their allies' view, forcing each Pokemon to fight alone as the battles gradually spread in every direction.

Dozens of Zubat beat their wings and released piercing shrieks. Their agile bodies darted in every direction with dazzling speed. Each struck from ambush and immediately fled, giving their opponents no chance to respond.

The Weezing, by contrast, floated sluggishly through the air while spewing dense smoke from their mouths. Fearing the poison, the opposing Pokemon did not dare approach and could only attack from a distance.

Cyndaquil breathed fire across the ground. Pikachu fought ten opponents at once, its electricity leaving several Zubat that attempted a sneak attack twitching in agony. Noctowl beat its wings and scattered the thick black smoke...

At first, Ash could still issue a few commands. As the battlefield became more chaotic and the noise grew deafening, however, he could no longer provide much help.

Ethan remained effective. He placed one hand on Gardevoir's shoulder and used its telepathy to transmit his orders clearly and precisely into the minds of his Pokemon, allowing him to direct them from afar at critical moments.

Charizard, use Dragon Rage!

Scyther, hurry and help Eevee! The Zubat have it surrounded!

Jolteon, move farther away before releasing your electricity! Whatever you do, don't hit our allies!

Through the efforts of their dozen Pokemon, Ethan's side suffered occasional wounds, but far more opponents were defeated and fell from the sky.

Unfortunately, too many enemies remained. As Team Rocket released still more Pokemon, Ethan's and Ash's battle line began to falter. Several Zubat even slipped overhead while no one was watching and attacked Silver directly...

Chapter 469: A Three-Sided Ambush and a Hidden Plan

When the Zubat suddenly attacked, Lanturn, which had remained at the very rear, instantly puffed out its cheeks and released a net of electricity that blocked their path.

Unable to evade in time, the Zubat flew straight into the net. They shrieked in pain, then abandoned Lugia and Oliver to attack Lanturn instead.

Lanturn did not dodge or retreat. It immediately battled them head-on.

Although Oliver's Lanturn was not especially skilled at fighting, it was clearly doing everything possible to protect Oliver and Silver!

Ash nervously watched the battle. When he saw the two sides fighting back and forth, he quietly asked Ethan, "Is it time for Misty and the others to move?"

Ethan glanced at Gengar.

"How long has Brock been gone?"

Gengar answered without hesitation, "Almost an hour!"

An hour...

Ethan calculated silently. An hour was not enough for Brock to return yet, but if they delayed a while longer, he should still make it in time!

With that thought, he told Gengar, "Send the signal to Misty and the others."

At his instruction, Gengar immediately formed a Shadow Ball and hurled it into the sky.

The Shadow Ball soared straight upward. At a certain height, it suddenly exploded, unleashing a mass of dark energy across the sky. Against the blue daylight and white clouds, the burst was exceptionally conspicuous. Its black fire could be seen from several miles away!

Cassidy and Butch naturally noticed the flarelike explosion from the submarine.

They looked up at the lingering black flames and sneered.

Calling for help?

This island was extremely remote, and hardly anyone lived even on nearby Ogi Isle. No matter how loudly they called for help, who could possibly rescue them?

Did they expect the police on Silver Rock Isle?

Silver Rock Isle was still a long distance away. Even if the police rushed here, Team Rocket would have captured Lugia and left long before they arrived!

Still, Cassidy and Butch understood that the longer the battle continued, the greater the chance of unexpected complications.

They needed to finish this quickly!

Without further hesitation, they ordered their subordinates to intensify the attack. Then both took out Poke Balls and leaped down to join the battle!

Butch sent out Primeape and Hitmontop, while Cassidy released Houndour and Sableye!

Primeape and Houndour were familiar enough. Ethan had frequently encountered both species during his travels. Hitmontop and Sableye, however, were Pokemon he had never seen alive before.

Hitmontop was a Fighting-type Pokemon with a brown body. Its limbs and tail had bandage-like markings and blue protective structures, while a single spike rose from the top of its head. It fought upside down with both its hands and feet, often performing flips. When it stood upon its head, it resembled a spinning top!

Fighting-type Trainers greatly favored the species. As far as Ethan knew, however, every Hitmontop was male, with no corresponding female species. He had no idea how they reproduced.

Sableye, meanwhile, was a Ghost- and Dark-type Pokemon. Its small body was deep purple, and its sapphire-like eyes gave it a sinister, almost alien appearance. Such a Pokemon certainly suited a villain.

Cassidy's and Butch's four Pokemon were naturally stronger than those of ordinary grunts. They still could not defeat Ethan and Ash in individual battles, but their entry into the fight created considerable trouble.

More significant was the fact that, as soon as the pair joined the battle, the Team Rocket members released dozens more Pokemon, making their assault even fiercer!

The battlefield became overwhelmingly chaotic. Two fists could not defend against four hands, and Ethan's and Ash's Pokemon gradually began struggling to hold their ground!

At that moment, several explosions rang out. Cassidy and Butch turned and saw more than a dozen Pokemon suddenly rush from the forest to the north, northeast, and northwest!

Without saying a word, the newcomers immediately joined the battle and attacked Team Rocket's Pokemon!

Behind them, Erika, Misty, and Richie also emerged from the forest!

At the critical moment, the three had arrived to reinforce the battle!

Cassidy and Butch exchanged looks.

So these are Ethan's reinforcements?

I see. Their companions never left. They were hiding here all along...

Had they anticipated Team Rocket's arrival and prepared an ambush, or did they have some other objective?

Fortunately, the three Trainers' appearance only introduced another variable to the battlefield. Their arrival briefly threw the grunts into confusion, but nothing more.

Even with a dozen additional Pokemon, Ethan's group remained at an overwhelming numerical disadvantage!

Do they truly believe this will be enough to defeat us?

Hmph. How naive!

In contrast, Ethan stood silently upon the large rock and watched the battlefield.

In front of him, a Weezing that attempted to attack was immediately knocked down by Gardevoir's Psychic.

Before the battle began, Erika, Misty, and Richie had remained hidden in the distant forest. Their purpose was to charge out at the signal, surround Team Rocket from three directions, and coordinate with Ethan from within the encirclement to catch the enemy by surprise!

To prevent Team Rocket from detecting them, Ethan had deliberately sent the three far away and instructed them to hide deep within the forest. They were to return only after seeing the signal.

Judging from the result, that part of the plan had clearly succeeded!

Of course, the ambush served more than one purpose.

Ethan's primary objective had been to appear weak enough that Team Rocket would dare act. He fully understood that this small ambush alone could never eliminate the entire force.

Its real purpose was to entangle Team Rocket and prevent them from escaping!

Ethan's true reliance was Brock, whom he had sent to find reinforcements an hour earlier!

What should someone do after encountering criminals?

Call the police, of course!

Even if Ethan defeated all these Team Rocket members, capturing and restraining them afterward would still present a serious problem!

Unfortunately, there was no signal on the island, so Brock had to travel to a nearby city and notify the police. The round trip would take considerable time, and Ethan's group needed to keep Team Rocket occupied until he returned.

Concerned that Officer Jenny might not have enough strength to handle such a large Team Rocket force, Ethan had also given Brock the phone numbers of the International Police officers Anabel and Looker. Brock could request their help directly!

Team Rocket could never have imagined that Maya had warned Ethan about their plan to target Lugia in advance. They believed themselves the hunters without realizing that Ethan had long since turned them into the prey!

With Team Rocket unaware of the trap and the timing working against them, being surrounded by the police had become their inevitable fate!

Chapter 470: Advance or Retreat

The melee continued, but just as Cassidy and Butch had expected, the arrival of Misty's group changed little. Their Pokemon had caught Team Rocket off guard and caused some confusion at first, but that was the extent of their impact.

Each time they defeated one opponent, several more Pokemon surrounded them!

Before long, even the reinforcements were intercepted and drawn into battle by greater numbers of Team Rocket Pokemon, leaving them trapped within the encirclement as well.

With the overall situation seemingly decided, confident smiles returned to Cassidy's and Butch's faces.

Hmph. So what if they have reinforcements?

Against overwhelming numbers, their struggle is ultimately pointless!

While the pair remained at ease, however, the submarine's captain soon detected something unusual on the radar.

A Team Rocket member hurriedly turned around and reported loudly, "Several unidentified helicopters have been detected over the southern waters! They're rapidly approaching this location!"

Helicopters!?

The captain frowned once again and asked in surprise, "Why would helicopters appear in a place like this? Are you certain they're coming for us?"

The Team Rocket member nodded. "Judging by their flight path, they're heading directly toward us!"

"How long until they arrive?"

"Approximately ten minutes!"

"Ten minutes?" The captain sighed, took out his communication device, and contacted Cassidy and Butch outside the submarine. "The situation has changed. An outside force has suddenly intervened. You must end this quickly and resolve the battle within eight minutes!"

An outside force?

Cassidy and Butch exchanged looks, both surprised by the captain's words.

This was a deserted island in a remote area. No one would come here without a reason. From the situation, the approaching force had to be coming for Team Rocket!

But how had anyone else learned they were here?

At that thought, both turned toward Ethan in the distance.

Within Team Rocket, everyone from Giovanni himself to the most ordinary grunt regarded this man as extremely dangerous. No one wanted to deal with him.

They had even heard that the four executives had warned the rank and file that, whenever they encountered Ethan in the wild, they should flee immediately unless they were carrying out a critical mission!

If even the four executives judged him so highly, it showed just how fearsome Ethan's reputation had become within Team Rocket.

Could Ethan have arranged everything, from the earlier ambush to the approaching helicopters?

Otherwise, the timing could not possibly have been so convenient!

With that thought, the pair no longer dared act carelessly, and their wariness of Ethan deepened.

Whatever else happened, their most urgent task was to capture Lugia as quickly as possible and leave before the helicopters arrived!

Eight minutes was neither long nor short, but in a chaotic battle like this, they had no idea whether it would be enough to defeat the opponents before them.

Knowing that time was running out, Cassidy and Butch did not dare delay. At their urging, Team Rocket's Pokemon intensified their assault and launched desperate attacks without regard for their own safety!

Almost immediately, Ethan sensed the change in the atmosphere.

Team Rocket's Pokemon had thrown themselves into a frenzy, attacking without restraint. Something must have happened to provoke such a dramatic shift in their offensive!

There was no need to guess. Brock had to be approaching with the real reinforcements!

His confidence surging, Ethan told Ash, "The International Police are here. It's time for us to fight back!"

Ash's spirits rose at the news. He nodded, then directed the battle with even greater energy.

Both sides fought with renewed ferocity and abandoned all restraint. In only moments, the beach of sand and reef became covered in battle scars of every size, leaving the entire area completely transformed!

Countless rocks were pulverized by the barrage of moves, while powerful energy evaporated the nearby seawater!

Time passed little by little.

One side attacked while the other defended. Their struggle over Lugia became a fierce battle for territory. As Team Rocket attempted to break through to Silver, the ground around it changed hands several times in only a few minutes!

More than a dozen Zubat gathered into a living tornado and swept forward with piercing shrieks, seemingly hoping to reach Silver through sheer momentum. They had traveled only halfway when more than a dozen attacks scattered the formation in every direction.

"...Bzzzt... Cassidy! Haven't you captured Lugia yet!?"

The captain's impatient voice came through Cassidy's earpiece. She checked the time. Five or six minutes had already passed, yet they had neither approached Lugia nor defeated the Pokemon before them!

"Not yet! Please give us a little more time!"

After ending the call, she slammed her fists together and gritted her teeth. "Damn it! Why are these people so difficult to deal with!?"

Butch considered the situation, then asked tentatively, "Should we retreat now?"

"What? Retreat now!?" Cassidy stared at him with wide eyes. "Are you joking? We still haven't captured that Lugia! How can we retreat early?"

Butch sighed and gestured for Cassidy to look around. "Wake up and look at the battlefield. Forget eight minuteseven if we had another hour, there's no telling whether we could defeat these people. Instead of wasting more time here, we should retreat now and prepare for our next attack!"

At Butch's words, Cassidy slowly surveyed the entire battlefield.

Just as he had said, a great many of their members' Pokemon were already injured. Almost every second, another Pokemon fell from the sky, completely unable to battle.

The Pokemon belonging to those brats had also suffered injuries, and their Trainers had recalled some of them into their Poke Balls. Yet the strongest of Ethan's Pokemon, the most troublesome opponents of all, still rampaged across the battlefield like gods of war!

"This..."

Cassidy opened her mouth, but no words came. She knew the situation had turned against them, especially with the helicopters about to arrive. Once that happened, their position would collapse and become even worse!

She simply could not accept it. They had already fought for so long. If they gave up now, all their effort would have been wasted!

Should they continue attacking or retreat?

The two choices flashed repeatedly through her mind. In the end, Cassidy followed reason and chose to retreat.

Just as the pair prepared to give the order, however, they discovered that leaving would no longer be so easy.

After the chaos of the battle, the two sides had become completely intermingled. Misty's group had also formed an encirclement from the outside, trapping Team Rocket's Pokemon and members in a mire. Even if they wanted to flee, they could not safely withdraw at a moment's notice!

The realization instantly left both Cassidy and Butch drenched in cold sweat.

So that's it! Was this that man's true objective!?

He pinned us down from both inside and outside, all so his reinforcements could capture every one of us when they arrived!?

How vicious!

Chapter 471: The First Phase Ends

Rumble, rumble, rumble...

The thunderous roar of helicopter rotors drew closer from the distance. It was clearly audible even amid the chaos of the battlefield.

Cassidy and Butch looked toward the horizon. Four helicopters had appeared in the distance and were rapidly approaching the island.

The roar grew louder and louder until it hurt their ears. By the time the helicopters reached the beach, both could clearly see the enormous International Police insignia emblazoned upon their fuselages!

"The International Police!?"

The pair exchanged looks, shocked to discover who had arrived.

Although they had known helicopters were coming as reinforcements, they had assumed they carried ordinary police officers. Neither had imagined the International Police would appear!

These officers were far more difficult to handle than ordinary police. Their members and Pokemon were all well equipped and highly trained, and their ranks even included experts capable of matching Team Rocket's four executives. They also recruited outside assistance for their operations. Unless they were pursuing major criminals who crossed national and regional borders or organizations like Team Rocket, they rarely took action!

Their presence here could mean only one thing: they intended to wipe out the entire Team Rocket force!

If they had any choice, Cassidy and Butch would have preferred never to confront these people!

The arrival of the International Police shattered their last hope and became the final blow to Team Rocket's morale.

The grunts were visibly thrown into confusion. Those trapped on the front line had no choice but to continue fighting Ethan's group's Pokemon, while the members farther back lost all desire to battle and stared fearfully at the helicopters overhead!

Once their initial shock passed, Cassidy and Butch also began to panic.

"Damn it! Weren't they supposed to be several minutes away!?"

The International Police had clearly arrived faster than they expected.

The timing left them caught between two impossible choices. They could neither seize Lugia from the people before them nor retreat safely in time!

Seeing the situation, Cassidy had no choice but to abandon the mission. She shouted to everyone around her, "Stop fighting! Retreat immediately!!"

With that, she and Butch recalled their Pokemon and led the withdrawal toward the submarine.

Before the pair could reach it, however, the submarine had already begun to descend!

Its crew could hardly be blamed for abandoning their companions. Compared with the ordinary members, the submarine was an extremely valuable Team Rocket asset and could not be allowed to fall into enemy hands.

When the report of the approaching helicopters had first arrived, everyone could have withdrawn immediately and escaped at their leisure. They had delayed for too long, however, and now it was already too late to flee!

The helicopters circled overhead as dozens of International Police officers rappelled to the ground. Their entry into the battle instantly balanced the two sides' numbers, sending the Team Rocket members fleeing in every direction!

They offered almost no resistance. Every Team Rocket member had only one thought: as many of them as possible had to escape, and they had to run as far away as they could!

But this was an isolated island. Other than Cassidy, Butch, and a small number of members who managed to enter the submarine, where could the rest possibly go?

On the other side of the battlefield, Ethan stood atop the large rock and watched the submarine nearly disappear beneath the water. He hurriedly waved to Misty.

"Misty, have one of your Pokemon follow them quietly and find out where their secret base is!"

"Got it!"

Misty nodded, then turned and issued instructions to one of her Pokemon. The next instant, Poliwhirl leaped into the sea and rapidly swam after the submarine!

Poliwhirl drove itself forward, leaving a long wake across the surface.

Ethan watched it catch hold of the submarine's edge and descend into the ocean with it. Only after both vanished from sight did he slowly look away.

If his Blastoise or Gyarados were here, he would not have needed to trouble Misty. For now, he could only hope that Poliwhirl would locate Team Rocket's secret base and return safely with the information.

Across the beach, the arrests continued.

Although the Team Rocket members had scattered in every direction, the helicopters made it impossible for them to hide. As time passed, more and more were captured and placed in handcuffs.

There was no longer any need for Ethan's group to intervene. When Erika and the others approached, everyone reunited and gathered their Pokemon together.

To avoid causing unnecessary commotion, Ethan had signaled Oliver to hide Silver the moment the helicopters appeared.

Silver's existence could not truly be concealed from the officers. A little questioning would be enough to learn about it from Team Rocket. Even so, keeping Silver out of sight for now would still save them considerable trouble.

At that moment, footsteps sounded nearby, and a woman in a black suit approached the group.

"Mr. Ethan, I didn't expect us to meet again so soon!"

Hearing the familiar voice, Ethan turned and saw Anabel, from whom they had parted only recently!

He nodded to her. "Miss Anabel, thank you for all your hard work!"

"There's no need to say that!" Anabel waved a hand. "Arresting Team Rocket is our duty. I wish we had more opportunities like this, so you truly don't need to be polite with us! Still, I should thank you again. You drew out so many Team Rocket members. You're practically our lucky star!"

Lucky star?

I don't want to be anyone's lucky star.

Besides, Team Rocket wasn't even targeting me this time...

Ethan wanted to explain, but the matter involved Silver, so he reconsidered and remained silent.

After they exchanged a few more pleasantries, Brock suddenly came running from the distance, panting heavily.

Although Brock had not participated in the battle, he had also worked extremely hard. Traveling back and forth to report the crime had been an indispensable contribution!

They chatted a little longer before Anabel left to handle the Team Rocket arrests, leaving Ethan and his companions together once again.

Ash wiped the sweat from his forehead and released a long breath. "Whew, it's finally over!"

"You're relaxing too soon." Ethan shook his head. "Team Rocket must have a secret base somewhere nearby. If everything goes well, we may soon be the ones launching an attack and clearing it out. For now, everyone should rest and treat your Pokemon's injuries!"

At his words, the others recognized that he was right and went to care for their Pokemon.

Only Richie remained where he stood. With a complicated expression, he looked at Ethan and said, "That was truly dangerous. I want to knowif the plan had failed, or if the International Police hadn't arrived in time, what would we have done?"

"Failed?" Ethan glanced at Richie as his right hand unconsciously brushed the two Great Balls in the pouch at his waist. "All we could do was make sure this operation had the greatest possible chance of success. But if it truly reached that point, then of course we would protect Silver with everything we had!"

Chapter 472: Lugia, Mother and Child

The arrest operation soon entered its final stage.

As more and more Team Rocket members were captured, only a few stubborn holdouts remained across the beach. Unable to escape, they continued their desperate resistance, but their struggle was destined to fail. The officers subdued them almost instantly.

The officers confiscated the defeated criminals' Pokemon, then bound them together in small groups with rope and escorted them into the helicopters.

While the operation proceeded in an orderly manner, Ethan led Ash and the others to Anabel, who was directing the officers, and told her about their next plan.

"You intend to raid Team Rocket's secret base?" Anabel did not immediately agree. Instead, she first voiced her concerns. "I'm sorry, but we don't have enough personnel to lead another operation. Our highest priority should be taking these captured Team Rocket members back to the station. The round trip will consume a great deal of time, so we truly can't clear out their base as well..."

Unlike Looker's steady but daring approach, Anabel's higher position had made her more cautious. She clearly would not rush into an operation without adequate preparation.

"That's all right." Ethan shook his head. "We plan to handle this ourselves. We may need you to take care of the aftermath when we're finished, though."

Anabel knew how strong Ethan was and how many people were helping him, but the plan still left her uneasy.

"Team Rocket's base must be hidden somewhere extremely well concealed, and it will certainly be heavily guarded. Wouldn't it be too dangerous for only the few of you to go...?"

Ethan glanced at his companions and replied with a relaxed expression, "We should be fine. We aren't going there to fight them head-on. If the situation becomes too difficult, we'll simply escape. Besides, Team Rocket attacked us first. We're only returning the favor!"

Seeing that he had made up his mind, Anabel considered the matter briefly and could only agree.

"Very well. I trust your strength, and I know you wouldn't attempt something you had no confidence in. I can't join your operation, but I'll arrange for several boats to support you as quickly as possible!"

Ethan did not particularly mind that the International Police would not participate.

In fact, this suited him perfectly. He, Ash, and the others would be enough for the operation. Quality mattered more than quantity, and unless they encountered a truly massive confrontation, he would rather not have the International Police accompanying them. Their presence would only restrict what he could do.

His only reason for telling Anabel had been to ensure she could handle the cleanup after they destroyed the Team Rocket base.

Before long, every Team Rocket member on the island had been arrested. Ethan's group waved as Anabel departed aboard a helicopter.

The roar of the rotors faded beyond the horizon, and the entire island became completely quiet.

Once all the outsiders were gone, Oliver dove into the water again. He soon returned with Silver.

Everyone sat together as they waited for Poliwhirl to return. They laughed and chatted cheerfully about how each of them had performed in the recent battle.

Every participant, including Oliver, had done well. Sharing such an experience had also brought Richie and Oliver closer to Ethan's group.

Now that the two knew everyone better, they clearly had more to say. Oliver in particular was no longer so reserved around them and had begun to regard them as true friends.

Looking at the battle scars covering the beach, Richie and Oliver could not help reflecting upon what had happened.

It was the first time either of them had participated in a battle on such a massive scale.

That was understandable for Oliver. He was still young, was not a Trainer, and had spent his entire life on Ogi Isle. Naturally, he had no experience fighting other people.

Richie, on the other hand, had traveled for a long time. He had competed in the Indigo League and faced many powerful opponents, so he had certainly seen something of the world. Even so, this truly was his first chaotic group battle. It made his blood race and left him profoundly shaken!

So these people regularly encounter situations like this, and they even have connections with the International Police...

Seeing how accustomed everyone else appeared only strengthened Richie's determination to stop pursuing League Conferences for now and continue traveling to hone his skills!

As the conversation continued, the subject eventually shifted to Silver.

Silver had become the center of attention. Ash, Misty, and the others all watched it, while their Pokemon surrounded the young Lugia and occasionally reached out to touch it as though observing some rare animal.

In truth, Lugia was an exceptionally rare Pokemon. For ordinary people, the chance to observe one at such close range was a scene beyond anything they could imagine in an entire lifetime!

As Oliver looked at Silver, he suddenly remembered something. He slapped his forehead and exclaimed, "Oh no! I almost forgot! Silver's mother should be coming to pick it up soon!"

"Its mother!?"

Misty's eyes widened. "You mean a real Lugia... I mean, an adult God of the Sea?"

Oliver nodded and rose to his feet. He urgently told the group, "You should hide somewhere. Its mother really dislikes humans. If she sees all of you gathered here, she might attack!"

"Huh? Is she really that bad-tempered?"

Ash scratched his head. Although his expression showed little concern, he obediently stood and prepared to hide with everyone else.

Before the group could move aside, the surface near the shore suddenly exploded. Amid the surging spray, an enormous silver-white figure rose from the sea!

Its appearance was nearly identical to Silver's, allowing everyone to recognize it at oncethe God of the Sea, Lugia!

Compared with the young Silver, the adult Lugia radiated overwhelming pressure!

It spread its arms and looked down upon the humans before it, making no effort to conceal the hostility in its eyes!

At the sight, Oliver hurriedly placed himself between Lugia and Ethan's group.

"God of the Sea! Please don't misunderstand! They're all good people. They just saved Silver!"

Silver also called to its mother several times. Even so, Lugia remained unmoved, and its gaze toward Ethan's group stayed filled with vigilance!

Ethan had initially intended to explain that someone had entrusted him with protecting them.

On second thought, however, even Maya and the other priests of the Temple of the Sea were probably no different from ordinary people in Lugia's eyes.

With that realization, he simply remained silent. He motioned for everyone around him to withdraw slowly and leave the beach to the two Lugia.

Sure enough, their actions caused Lugia's expression to ease slightly, and the tense atmosphere immediately vanished!

Chapter 473: Saying Goodbye to Silver

Any wild Pokemon mother would naturally be highly wary of humans who appeared near her child, especially an entire group of strangers.

As Ethan watched the God of the Sea, a thought suddenly occurred to him. He remembered the blessing he had received upon becoming the Sea Hero and hurriedly focused his mind, attempting to use his new ability to probe Lugia's heart.

Amazingly, although Lugia was not a Water-type Pokemon, perhaps its long life in the ocean allowed Ethan to faintly sense its current emotions!

He felt intense vigilance mixed with hostility.

By comparison, Silver's current emotions were light and joyful, making them much easier for Ethan to perceive.

Beyond that, however, he discovered nothing else!

In truth, emotions like these could easily be identified from the target's expression. There was no need to peer into its heart at all.

Furthermore, this was not a passive skill that allowed him to sense a Pokemon's emotions simply by standing nearby. Ethan had to focus his attention and actively reach out to perceive them!

Sigh. No matter how I look at it, this ability is still far too limited...

Before Ethan could look away, Lugia seemed to sense something and raised its head toward him.

Their eyes met. Ethan coughed lightly and instinctively turned his gaze aside.

Being caught secretly peering into someone else's heart always created a strange sense of embarrassment.

It seemed he should avoid using this ability on Pokemon of Lugia's level in the future. An ordinary Pokemon might never notice, but one as powerful as Lugia would probably detect the intrusion. If that caused a misunderstanding, the consequences would far outweigh any benefit!

Fortunately, Silver reached its mother's side at that moment. The reunion drew Lugia's attention away, and it stopped staring at Ethan.

The two Lugia nestled together in a heartwarming scenealthough it would have been even better without the adult Lugia's intense hostility.

Guided by its mother, Silver leaped into the water. It appeared the two were preparing to leave together.

Before swimming away, however, Silver looked back and waved a wing toward Oliver and Ethan's group in farewell.

"Silver..."

Ash, Misty, and Richie involuntarily stepped forward, their expressions filled with reluctance to part.

Although they had spent little time together, Ash and the others had clearly grown very fond of Silver and did not want to say goodbye so soon.

Unfortunately, Silver's departure was inevitable. Their wishes could not change it.

Silver might often return to play with Oliver in the future, but they would have left this place long before then. Once they parted today, they might never meet again.

The group stood by the sea and watched the two Lugia, one large and one small, swim into deeper water until they disappeared completely.

Seeing Ash and Misty continue staring blankly at the ripples, Ethan tapped each of them on the head.

"All right, stop looking. Silver has already left. No matter how long you watch, it isn't coming back right now."

Misty rubbed her tearful eyes and murmured, "Didn't we come here to protect them? Is it really okay to let Silver leave like this?"

Ethan sighed. "Returning a child to its mother is the greatest protection we can offer. As long as they remain hidden in the ocean, Team Rocket won't be able to find them even if they try."

Seeing that Misty remained dejected, he comforted her. "Don't dwell on it. Both you and Silver still have long journeys ahead. If fate allows it, I'm sure you'll have another chance to meet someday!"

"Sigh... I hope so..."

Without Silver, the earlier cheerfulness did not return, and no one felt particularly inclined to talk. Fortunately, before long, Misty's Poliwhirl suddenly surfaced from the sea.

Ash immediately asked, "Well? Did you find Team Rocket's base?"

Poliwhirl nodded and began croaking at length. Since no one could understand it, they had to ask Gengar to translate.

After listening for quite some time, Gengar frowned at Misty. "Why is your Poliwhirl so noisy and long-winded? It keeps mixing in all these 'croak, croak' sounds and still hasn't reached the point."

Misty's expression darkened. Only then did Gengar provide the translation. "It did find Team Rocket's base. It's beneath the sea, not far from here."

"Beneath the sea!?"

Ash and the others exchanged looks. They had assumed the base would be built upon one of the islands. None of them had expected it to be hidden underwater!

The underwater location also left Ethan feeling that the situation would be rather difficult.

Conditions beneath the sea were extremely complicated. Ferocious Pokemon could lurk in the darkness, while currents and seaweed presented further dangers. Anyone hoping to remain underwater for an extended period would also need proper diving equipment.

Seeing everyone fall silent, Ethan cleared his throat. "Cheer up. Finding the base is good news. Now that we've confirmed it's underwater, we shouldn't waste any more time. Let's set out!"

Richie hesitated. "How are we going to get there?"

"First, we'll find a boat. Traveling by boat will save us a great deal of energy."

At the mention of a boat, Oliver hurriedly said, "I have one! It's tied beneath the trees behind us!"

With Oliver leading the way, they walked to the beach on the other side and entered a small grove. Sure enough, they soon saw a boat tied by rope beneath a large tree.

Only then did Ethan's group learn that whenever Oliver came to this island to play, he sailed here alone through the wind and waves!

They had assumed the boat would be a small wooden rowboat. When they approached, they discovered it was actually a speedboat!

Misty immediately looked at Oliver with newfound respect. "Oh? You can pilot a speedboat!?"

"Heh..." Oliver rubbed his nose and replied shyly, "It isn't that difficult. I've lived beside the sea since I was little, so handling a boat like this is easy for me!"

By now, everyone had rested for quite some time. Their Pokemon's injuries had been treated, and the Trainers had recovered most of their strength. They delayed no longer and boarded the boat.

As Oliver untied the rope, he asked, "Where are we going now? Straight to Team Rocket's base?"

Ethan shook his head. "We'll go to the town on Ogi Isle first. Since the base is underwater, we need to make preparations."

Diving equipment was the highest priority. They could not afford to be careless about it.

Ash, Misty, and Brock all nodded in agreement.

They could not help remembering their experience aboard the S.S. Anne in Kanto, when the ship sank beneath the sea. Their present situation was similar, and they could become trapped underwater at any moment. None of them wanted to experience the same ordeal a second time!

Chapter 474: Underwater Infiltration

The speedboat raced across the sea, leaving two long trails in its wake.

Just as Oliver had claimed, his piloting skills truly were excellent. The boat traveled smoothly and rarely pitched violently, making it clear he was an experienced speedboat operator.

Of course, they also had the favorable weather to thank.

Unlike the conditions during their earlier journey to the island, both the sky and the sea were now calm. The weather was perfect for travel and spared them considerable discomfort.

The sea breeze swept over them, and wild Pokemon occasionally leaped from the water. Everyone's thoughts remained fixed upon the upcoming operation, however, leaving them with no interest in conversation, much less the passing scenery.

Vroom, vroom, vroom...

The speedboat's engine droned without pause.

Before long, the boat stopped at the harbor of Ogi Isle's only town. With Oliver leading the way, Ethan's group disembarked and headed directly into a diving supply shop.

The town might have been remote, but as a coastal settlement, it carried everything one could need.

Faced with the dazzling array of equipment, Ethan immediately paid for a diving mask and compact oxygen tank for each person.

Everyone in the group knew how to swim. Ash and Misty in particular were excellent swimmers and could hold their breath underwater for a long time. With their Pokemon assisting them, they needed little other equipment so long as they could breathe.

To make communication easier, Ethan also purchased several writing slates designed for underwater use and distributed them among the group.

When it was time to pay, the shopkeeper recognized Oliver and offered them a discount without compromising the equipment's quality. Ethan's present finances made the savings largely irrelevant, but the arrangement still spared him a considerable amount of money.

After saying goodbye to the shopkeeper, the group left the store. While they still had a signal, Ethan called Anabel and sent her their coordinates.

The International Police would not be participating in the operation, but maintaining communication remained essential. At the very least, it provided them with a safeguard in case something went wrong!

Once every preparation was complete, they boarded the boat again. Guided by Poliwhirl, they eventually reached another stretch of open sea.

Nothing about the area appeared unusual. Several small reefs rose from the water nearby and could serve as landmarks, but they were thoroughly unremarkable. It was impressive that Poliwhirl had remembered the location so precisely.

At the surface, Poliwhirl repeatedly pointed downward. This time, no translation from Gengar was necessary. Everyone understood that Team Rocket's base had to be somewhere below them.

The group began putting on their equipment. Once Ethan finished adjusting his gear, he turned to Oliver and instructed him, "You shouldn't come down with us. Stay here with Lanturn and support us from the surface!"

Oliver knew he could not offer much help below and sensibly agreed. He also understood that someone needed to watch the boat.

"All right. Please be careful!"

They left their luggage aboard, secured their gear, and reviewed their underwater hand signals several times. Then Ethan, Erika, Ash, Misty, Richie, and Brock sat along the side of the boat and fell backward together.

Splash... Splash...

Several heavy impacts sounded in quick succession. The next instant, Ethan felt the seawater engulf his entire body.

The cold water stung his skin, but after swimming for a moment, he quickly adjusted to the temperature.

Several Water-type Pokemon had already been waiting for them. Under their protection, the group sank beneath the surface and swam toward the seabed.

Visibility remained good when they first entered the water, allowing them to see far into the distance. As they continued descending, however, the light slowly vanished and their visible range shrank. Ethan could also clearly feel the water exerting greater pressure against his body!

The area was not truly deep ocean, so the six people and their Pokemon soon reached the bottom.

Through his diving mask, Ethan surveyed the darkness around them. He had no fear of the deep sea, but the environment still felt oppressive. Fortunately, the companions beside him and his own Dragonair provided considerable reassurance.

Following Poliwhirl, they passed through a coral reef and soon saw a brilliantly illuminated underwater base in the distance.

The base stood on a level stretch of seabed. Although the surrounding water was almost completely dark, the bright lights inside made the facility exceptionally conspicuous beneath the sea!

Everyone beside Ethan was astonished by its enormous scale. It was difficult to imagine that Team Rocket had built such a secret base here!

They remained concealed among the coral and observed the facility for quite some time. Apart from several security cameras, they saw no guards on patrol.

That was excellent news for Ethan's group. If they avoided the cameras, they should be able to enter the base quietly without anyone noticing.

However...

The cameras covered every angle around the facility. Avoiding them appeared almost impossible!

How are we supposed to cross?

Once they recognized the problem, everyone turned toward Ethan and waited for him to devise a solution.

During their long time together, Ash, Misty, Brock, and Erika had all gradually come to regard him as the group's central figure!

Even Richie, who had spent relatively little time with them, would not act recklessly in a situation like this. Whether because he respected Ethan's strength or simply believed he should listen to an adult, his first instinct was also to seek Ethan's advice.

Feeling everyone's eyes upon him, Ethan suddenly sensed an enormous amount of pressure.

He watched the cameras and unconsciously rubbed his chin as he considered their options.

After a moment's thought, an idea truly did come to him!

He took out his writing slate and quickly wrote several words, then gestured toward Misty as he conveyed his instructions.

After reading the slate, Misty nodded and directed her Corsola to swim straight toward the Team Rocket base.

While everyone else watched in confusion, Corsola boldly swam in front of one of the cameras like a curious wild Pokemon. As though fascinated by its own reflection in the lens, it blocked the camera with its entire body and stared intently into it!

Such incidents were common beneath the sea. Wild Pokemon were often attracted by human objects, so the behavior would not alarm anyone monitoring the feed.

At that instant, Ethan hurriedly waved for the others to follow. He led the way through the camera's field of view and rapidly approached the Team Rocket base!

Once everyone had safely reached the wall of the facility, Corsola calmly swam away as though it had lost interest in the camera. Sure enough, the maneuver aroused no suspicion!

Chapter 475: Let's Start Wrecking Things!

The plan proceeded smoothly. Ethan's group waited several more minutes and finally relaxed when the Team Rocket base showed no reaction. They had safely passed the first obstacle.

As Ethan touched the thick wall, however, the question of how to enter the base presented them with a second problem.

If they were willing to be ruthless, they could simply tear several holes through the facility. Seawater would surge inside without pause and flood the entire base in little more than ten minutes, leaving those within no chance to escape and allowing Ethan's group to eliminate everyone in one stroke.

That would be far too vicious. Their primary objective was to capture Team Rocket, not exterminate them.

If they did not damage the wall, however, they would need to locate an entrance to enter the base.

As an underwater structure, the entire facility had to be tightly sealed. Even if they found an access point, opening it would still be a problem.

Ethan explained their predicament to the others through his writing slate. After reading it, Ash and the others merely scratched their heads in confusion, unable to offer a useful idea.

Sigh...

I really can't rely on these people at all...

Ethan helplessly looked away and happened to notice Misty's Corsola once again.

Hmm?

An idea instantly occurred to him. It seemed they would have to ask Corsola for help again!

...

At that moment, two Team Rocket members sat in the underwater base's security room with their legs crossed. They leisurely drank tea and only occasionally glanced over the surveillance screens.

Years of uneventful isolation and tedious work had long since eroded their proper vigilance, leaving both guards thoroughly complacent.

Even so, they remained at their posts and maintained the bare minimum of security.

Then a Corsola appeared and quickly caught their attention.

One guard watched the screen and shook his head helplessly. "How annoying. That Corsola is back again!"

The other guard laughed. "Does it really think the camera is a mirror? Sigh. These wild Pokemon are so adorably stupid!"

On the screen, Corsola swam in front of the camera once again. It looked from side to side, then opened its mouth wide and bit down upon the lens. As it twisted its body and shook from side to side, it actually tore the camera loose!

"Damn it!" One guard immediately sat upright and cursed. He picked up his radio and called, "Maintenance team! A wild Pokemon damaged one of the exterior cameras. Get out there and inspect it!"

"Another one!?" an impatient voice answered through the radio. "Seriously, how many times has this happened this month? Do these wild Pokemon think this place is some kind of treasure trove?"

Despite all their complaints, the maintenance personnel had no choice but to head toward the exit, change into diving suits, and prepare to swim outside to repair the camera.

Meanwhile, Ethan and the others remained hidden against the base's outer wall, waiting quietly for an opportunity to appear.

Fortunately, they did not wait long. A circular passage opened, and a Team Rocket member carrying tools swam out. Without pausing, he headed straight toward the camera Corsola had damaged.

His movements were thoroughly practiced, as though he had experienced the same situation many times before.

The passage had not yet closed. Recognizing that the opportunity could not be missed and seeing that the maintenance worker had already moved away, Ethan's group swam forward with all their strength. They entered one after another and finally made it safely inside the base.

Splash...

Ethan and the others surfaced from the water.

Beyond the passage stood a pressure chamber resembling part of a ship. The group left the water, climbed a ladder, removed their diving masks and underwater respirators, and each took a deep breath.

The air was surprisingly fresh, without the stale quality found inside a submarine. The facility truly deserved to be called a secret base. Its air purification system had clearly been designed extremely well.

Misty asked quietly, "What do we do now?"

Ethan looked in both directions. "They haven't discovered us yet. Let's go farther inside and find out what kind of facility this really is!"

Everyone recalled their Water-type Pokemon and selected partners better suited to fighting within narrow spaces.

Ethan recalled Dragonair, allowed Gengar to emerge, and also released Gardevoir. With these two Pokemon beside him, no one could harm him unless they encountered a Legendary Pokemon!

The group passed through the chamber and silently entered a corridor. Perhaps the base had truly never experienced an intrusion, because they encountered no patrolling guards and saw no further surveillance equipment. A few researchers occasionally hurried past, but Gengar scouted ahead and detected them early, allowing Ethan's group to hide with ease.

They continued forward, passed through several bulkheads, and turned into a room resembling a warehouse. There, they immediately discovered dozens of Water-type Pokemon confined inside metal cages, lying listlessly on the floor.

Misty covered her mouth in shock. "Why are all these Pokemon locked up here?"

"They're probably being used for some kind of research." Seeing no one nearby, Ethan nodded to the group. "Hurry and release them all."

Erika and the others had already intended to do exactly that. The cages were extremely sturdy, however, and they had no keys, leaving them no choice but to have their Pokemon destroy the bars directly.

Naturally, that created unavoidable noise.

Once the wild Pokemon regained their freedom, they paid no attention to caution and fled in every direction. Keeping the operation quiet was no longer possible.

Only seconds later, someone heard the commotion and rushed into the room, colliding directly with the escaping Pokemon!

"Damn it! Intruders! They've released the Pokemon! Sound the alarm!!"

Sirens instantly blared throughout the facility. That no longer mattered. Ethan's group had come to destroy the base, and reaching this point undetected was already a considerable success.

Before the Team Rocket member could take any other action, one of the group's Pokemon knocked him unconscious.

Seeing this, Ethan no longer bothered concealing their presence. He told the others, "This works just as well. Let's wreck the place and defeat everyone we encounter!!"

That was their primary objective. Ash and the others nodded excitedly, ordered their Pokemon forward, and charged down the corridor. Every person who crossed their path was swiftly defeated.

The entire base instantly descended into chaos.

Team Rocket's members could not understand when or how the intruders had entered. They scrambled out of their rooms in confusion, only to run directly into the terrifying group waiting for them!

In front of a large screen, Dr. Namba, Cassidy, and Butch recognized the familiar faces in the footage and immediately realized that disaster had arrived!

Damn it! Why do these people keep haunting us? How did they follow us all the way here!?

Chapter 476: The Base Is Flying!

On the screen, Ethan's Pokemon were charging deeper into the base, smashing through everything in their path. None of their opponents could withstand even a single exchange. Butch frowned. "Dr. Kimba, what should we"

"It's Dr. Namba!" Dr. Namba cut him off before he could finish. He glared at Butch and Cassidy. "You two are useless! Not only did you fail to capture Lugia, you led those people straight here!"

"We didn't lead them here..." Cassidy began to protest, but Butch hurriedly pulled her back.

He knew arguing would accomplish nothing now. With the enemy at their door, they could not afford to start fighting among themselves.

Butch kept signaling to her with his eyes. Cassidy swallowed her anger, sighed helplessly, and stopped arguing with the base's commander.

Once his partner had calmed down, Butch rubbed his hands together and gave Dr. Namba an ingratiating smile. "Yes, yes, you're absolutely right... So what do we do now? Should we retreat?"

"Retreat!?" Dr. Namba rejected the suggestion outright. "Not yet. There's a great deal of important research data and results here. We need time to move them. You two, take every member we have left and stop the intruders. Whatever happens, don't let them reach the core area!"

"Huh? Us?"

Cassidy and Butch froze. After their recent defeat, neither had much courage left to face Ethan's group again.

"Of course you. Who else, me?" Dr. Namba snorted. "Remember, hold them off as long as you can. The data needs enough time to be moved!"
