Butch and Cassidy exchanged a look. They were deeply reluctant, but they understood how important the research was to Team Rocket. They could only steel themselves and obey.

As soon as they had left the command room, Dr. Namba turned to a nearby grunt. "Prepare the submarine. We have to evacuate immediately!"

"Huh?" The grunt stared at him. "Didn't you just order Cassidy and Butch to eliminate the intruders? We're leaving now? What about the data?"

"You're all idiots!" Dr. Namba cursed. Then he tapped his temple. "The data is all in my head. As long as I get away safely, you can consider it moved. Understand?"

"Then why did you send Cassidy and Butch out? Couldn't we just leave now?"

Dr. Namba looked back at the large screen, a cruel expression crossing his face. "Hmph. Giovanni and so many executives have failed to stop these people. How could those two possibly manage it? Sending them out will teach the failures a lesson. Besides, I've prepared a little gift for our visitors from afar. I'm certain they'll enjoy it!"

...

In one of the base's corridors, Ethan and his companions directed their Pokemon through a fierce battle with Team Rocket.

Since being discovered, they had advanced another dozen meters and climbed a staircase to the base's second floor.

Here the resistance was particularly strong. Every few steps, they had to defeat several more Team Rocket members.

Scorch marks, cracks from impacts, and traces of electrical attacks covered the walls. The floors and walls had been damaged, exposing cables in several places. Behind the group lay more than a dozen fallen grunts and dozens of defeated Pokemon.

The fighting had been intense!

Seeing Cassidy and Butch again made Ethan's group realize that the base had probably mobilized every available fighter to stop them.

The pair brought more than a dozen people and completely blocked the passage ahead. Ash and the others were not frightened in the least. They flexed their hands, eager for another fight. Team Rocket's members, on the other hand, feared that a fierce battle might rupture the base and flood it with seawater, so every one of them acted cautiously.

"Damn it! You followed us all the way here!" Butch glared at Ethan's group as though he wanted to tear them apart.

"What, are you surprised?" Ethan smiled and shook his head. "When you fled in such a hurry, you should have known we wouldn't let the matter end there!"

In truth, neither Cassidy nor Butch had expected to be followed. They had escaped in a rush aboard a submarine and had never imagined anyone could track them.

Still, their assignment was to delay Ethan's group for as long as possible. Since Ethan had not attacked immediately and seemed willing to talk, they played along.

Erika saw through their intentions at once.

She leaned toward Ethan and whispered, "They're stalling for time."

Ethan nodded slightly. He had noticed it too. He did not know what Team Rocket was planning, but he had no intention of letting them succeed.

Just as he was about to order an attack, the floor shifted beneath his feet. A violent tremor followed, as though some enormous machine had suddenly started and lifted them all!

"Ethan, look outside!!"

Misty cried out and pointed toward a window in the corridor. She looked as though she had seen something impossible!

Ethan hurried over and looked out at the seabed. Everything below them was falling away. Nothe entire base was rising rapidly toward the surface like a spacecraft!

Ash and the others joined him at the window and exclaimed, "What's going on!?"

At first, they suspected a Team Rocket trap or some secret weapon. But when they looked back, Cassidy and Butch appeared just as bewildered. Clearly, neither knew what was happening.

The two even lost their footing and nearly fell!

Noticing Ethan's group watching them, they quickly regained their balance and pretended nothing had happened.

In private, however, they exchanged an instinctive glance.

Cassidy whispered, "What's happening? Isn't this the base's secret escape system? Why has it been activated already!?"

"I don't know..." Butch shook his head. "Maybe Dr. Rumba has some other plan. Never mind that for now. This place isn't safe anymore. Let's finish our assignment and get out of here!"

Chapter 477: Scattered in Flight

The base was still rising. Ethan had no idea what Team Rocket was plotting, but there was no time to lose. He knew he could not let them succeed, so he immediately ordered Gengar and Gardevoir to attack.

Ash and the others joined in, issuing attack commands to their own Pokemon.

Ash's Pikachu and Heracross, Richie's Pikachu Sparky and Charmander, Misty's Poliwhirl, Erika's Leafeon, and the Forretress Brock had caught in Johto all charged together. A barrage of different moves flew straight toward Team Rocket.

Cassidy and Butch could not withstand the assault. They had no choice but to fall back step by step.

One Pokemon after another was struck down, yet the pair did not panic. Their task was simply to buy time. If they held out until the research data and personnel had all been moved, they would have won.

The base continued its rapid ascent. In just a minute or two, the water outside grew much brighter. Through the windows, they could even make out the faint light of the sun penetrating the surface. At this rate, the base would soon emerge from the sea!

Meanwhile, Oliver waited anxiously in the speedboat above.

He leaned over the side and kept his eyes fixed on the water. He knew he could not see anything below, but watching was the only way he could ease his worry.

Suddenly the water began to churn as though something enormous were about to burst through it!

Startled, Oliver quickly steered the speedboat away, narrowly avoiding the currents that threatened to overturn it.

Splash!!

Seawater erupted high into the air. Beneath the spray, a base resembling a steel fortress rose from the depths!!

The surging water battered Oliver's speedboat.

He immediately recognized the structure as Team Rocket's secret base, but he could not imagine how they had built it.

Inside, Ethan's group fought their way forward another dozen meters. Suddenly, the last rays of the setting sun shone across their faces. They looked up in surprise and realized that the base had reached the surface!

The orange-red sunset was so beautiful that they briefly stopped in their tracks.

Before they could recover, an even sharper alarm sounded!

Unlike the ordinary alarm they had heard earlier, this one blared urgently. A cold female voice repeated the same message over and over: "Warning! The base's automatic self-destruct sequence has been activated. Detonation in five minutes. All personnel must evacuate immediately! Warning! The base's automatic self-destruct sequence..."

Self-destruct!?

Ethan and the others frowned. Cassidy and Butch appeared just as shocked by the announcement!!

Cassidy stood stunned for a moment before bursting out angrily. "Damn it! That old man tricked us! He's going to destroy the base!"

"That can't be right," Butch said in disbelief. "Didn't he tell us to buy time? Why would he destroy it?"

"Idiot!" Cassidy gritted her teeth. "How can you still not understand? The old man never told us the base would be destroyed! He sent us to hold off the intruders so we'd be blown up along with them!!"

"What!?" Butch finally grasped the danger. "Then what do we do now?"

"Do you really have to ask!?" Cassidy seized his arm. "We run!!"

After their hurried exchange, the two abandoned Ethan's group, turned, and fled in a panic.

Seeing them go, the Team Rocket members, whose morale had already collapsed, raced after them. In an instant, the corridor was empty!

Richie watched them disappear and listened to the urgent, cold alarm. Coming back to his senses, he said quickly, "You heard that, right? This place is going to explode. We need to get out too!"

Ethan frowned.

He had not expected Team Rocket to be ruthless enough to sacrifice its own base!

On reflection, it made sense. If the base was about to fall, Team Rocket would rather destroy it than leave it for someone else to claim.

That's extreme...

The group wasted no more time and ran in the direction Cassidy and Butch had taken.

Team Rocket members were fleeing everywhere they looked. The entire base had descended into chaos, and no one had any interest in stopping them.

Still...

As they ran, Ethan could not help glancing out a window.

The more he thought about it, the stranger Team Rocket's actions seemed.

The sea was right outside. Ethan's group could leave through an exit or even break a hole in the wall and escape. Why had Team Rocket deliberately raised the base to the surface, giving them more room to get away?

If the plan was to destroy the base with them inside, Team Rocket could have done it underwater. The surrounding sea would have made escape far harder. So why bring the base up?

Was it merely to let Team Rocket's own people leave safely?

However he examined it, something felt wrong. Yet every part of the plan also seemed reasonable, leaving him unable to find an answer.

They passed through several rooms in succession. Documents lay scattered everywhere, showing how hastily Team Rocket had fled.

Strangely, although this was a research base, Ethan saw only combat personnel. There was not a single researcher anywhere along their escape route!

That deepened his suspicions.

By the time they reached the exit, it was already open. A crowd of Team Rocket members fought to get through it. Cassidy and Butch were nowhere in sight.

When it came to running away, those two were truly in a class of their own!

The countdown continued. Soon the grunts crowded around the exit had all jumped into the sea and were swimming away with all their strength. Ash and the others were about to follow when Ethan suddenly stopped.

Misty, just behind him, asked in confusion, "Ethan, why did you stop? It's about to explode. Hurry!"

Ethan thought for a moment, looked at the others, and shook his head.

"You go ahead. I can't shake the feeling that this isn't so simple. I want to stay and see what's happening before I decide what to do!"

Chapter 478: Taking the Opposite Course

"What!?"

Everyone stared at Ethan in disbelief when they heard he intended to stay!

"Ethan, what are you talking about!?"

Misty even reached out to feel his forehead. Finding no sign of a fever, she asked in astonishment, "There are only a few minutes left on the countdown. We need to leave!"

She took his arm and tried to pull him through the exit.

Ethan shook his head, gently removed her hand, and gave a wry smile. "I'm not joking. Something about this really does feel wrong. Think about it. We haven't done much yet, and we haven't even seen the person in charge of the base. They only resisted for a little while before deciding to blow the whole place up. Doesn't that seem strange? Isn't it an overreaction?"

Erika considered this calmly. "Perhaps... they realized they couldn't hold us off. Or there might be important data in the base that they can't allow anyone to obtain. That would explain such an extreme response."

"Exactly!" Misty hurriedly agreed. "You heard the alarm too. They wouldn't lie about an explosion. And lookTeam Rocket is rushing to escape!"

"Even so..." Ethan shook his head, holding to his judgment. "I still feel that something is unusual. I'll stay and see what happens. Don't worry. I'm not an idiot. If an explosion really does occur, Gardevoir can Teleport me outside at that very moment!"

Despite his explanation, the others could hardly allow him to take such a risk. They all tried to dissuade him.

"That's too dangerous! You're gambling with your life!"

"They're right. Let's hurry and get out of here!"

Their objections surrounded him, but Ethan chose to trust his instincts.

"I've made up my mind. There's no need to keep arguing. Besides, if the base does explode, my Pokemon will protect me!"

Seeing how determined he was, everyone turned to Erika, hoping she could persuade him.

Erika thought for a moment as they watched her. Then, to their surprise, she said, "In that case, I'll stay too."

Her decision was just as firm as Ethan's. She seemed ready to follow him wherever he went.

"Huh?"

"Miss Erika, have you lost your senses too!?"

Everyone was stunned. They had counted on the mature, levelheaded Erika to talk Ethan out of his plan, not to stay and join him!

Erika sighed helplessly at their expressions. "There's nothing else I can do. He's already made up his mind. I can't leave him here alone. Someone has to keep an eye on him."

She turned her gaze toward Ethan.

He met her eyes. Although her decision surprised him, Gardevoir could Teleport them both out together. After a moment, he nodded.

Seeing that Erika was staying, Misty said without hesitation, "Then I'll"

Ethan raised a hand to stop her before she could finish.

"You should all leave. The two of us are enough. Gardevoir can't take more people than that at once."

"But..."

Misty still wanted to argue, but at Ethan's signal, Ash and Brock half pulled, half pushed her out of the base.

Before leaving, she looked back. "I'll wait for you outside. Please be careful!"

Once the others had gone, no one remained nearby except Ethan and Erika. The alarm still echoed through the halls, but otherwise the entire base had fallen silent, as though it had been abandoned.

"Warning. One minute remains until the base is destroyed. All personnel must evacuate immediately. Warning. One minute remains..."

With so little time left, Ethan did not delay. He turned and walked briskly deeper into the base.

Erika had recalled Leafeon as a precaution. Following Ethan, she could not help asking, "How certain are you about this?"

Ethan shrugged. "How could I be certain? It's only a guess. We have to stay ready for the worst."

Erika sighed. "If the whole base explodes at once, we'll never escape. We really could die here together."

Ethan gave a small laugh. "Then why did you dare come with me?"

At his teasing tone, Erika suddenly fell silent.

To be honest, she did not know what she had been thinking when she chose to accompany him into such danger.

Even knowing they might die at any moment, she still felt no regret.

As the silence grew heavy, Ethan realized his remark might have been poorly chosen. He cleared his throat and changed the subject. "Don't worry. This base is mainly a research facility. For safety, the laboratories should be kept away from explosives. If the base really is destroyed, it will probably happen in stages, not all at once. That should give us at least a few seconds to react."

Time passed quickly as they continued forward.

"Warning. Ten seconds remain until the base is destroyed... Ten... nine..."

As the moment approached, both Ethan and Erika grew tense.

For all his confident words, Ethan was far from certain.

Gardevoir took one of their hands in each of its own. At the slightest sign of danger, it would use Teleport.

"Five... four... three... two... one..."

When the countdown ended, Ethan felt a faint tremor beneath his feet. Several explosions sounded in the distance.

Gardevoir was about to Teleport, but Ethan stopped it. He listened closely.

The blasts seemed to be some distance from their position. There had been several in succession, but none felt especially powerful.

"What are you waiting for!?" Startled by the explosions, Erika put a hand to her chest. "The base really is exploding. Your guess was wrong. Come on, we need to leave!"

"Wait a moment." Ethan held a finger to his lips. "Don't go yet. Listen..."

Erika paid close attention. To her surprise, after those first few blasts, the explosions stopped completely!

The alarm had gone silent too!

Huh?

What's going on?

Wasn't the base supposed to be destroyed!?

Chapter 479: The Pokemon Virus

It was as though the whole spectacle had been arranged just to drive everyone out of the base.

The explosions had stopped completely. Now the base seemed to have lost power and was rapidly sinking again.

Given its enormous size and weight, the seawater could not hold it up on its own.

Erika turned toward a window. Water soon covered it once more, the last light of the setting sun disappeared, and the familiar underwater scene came back into view.

She frowned. "It looks as though we're heading back to the seafloor."

Ethan nodded and looked deeper into the base. "Come on. Let's see what Team Rocket is really up to!"

The two advanced cautiously. After walking some distance, they found the facility deserted. The irritating alarm had stopped long ago, and now the only sounds were their footsteps and breathing.

Tap, tap, tap, tap...

Their hurried steps echoed through the empty base.

As they went deeper, they took a quick look inside every room they passed. Each was in the same state of disarray, but nothing else happened.

At the heart of the base, however, they found something different.

This was clearly the research area. It was thoroughly protected: thick bulletproof glass surrounded it, and its only entrance had a blast door.

Through the glass, they could see people moving inside!!

Ethan and Erika exchanged a glance. At Ethan's signal, Gardevoir used Psychic. With a tremendous bang, the force tore the entire door from its frame!

Inside, they first saw a short old man dressed in white. He stood with his back to them, working at a control panel.

Several others nearby wore protective suits. They stood frozen as Ethan and Erika entered, watching them with shock, unease, and panic in their eyes.

The old man turned and regarded Ethan without expression.

"You really are persistent. Even after all that, we still couldn't fool you."

Ethan glanced at the red hair ringing the man's bald crown. "Who are you?" he asked quietly.

The old man smiled faintly. "Allow me to introduce myself. I'm Dr. Namba, the director of this base."

Dr. Namba...

Ethan only vaguely remembered him. The scientist had appeared so briefly in the anime that the storyline had barely touched on him.

Ethan looked around. The laboratory was filled with precision equipment, some of it still operating. Rows of test tubes in different colors made the place look like a chemistry and biology lab.

"You went to such lengths to hide yourselvesexplosions, raising the base to the surface, even fooling your own people. What are you researching here?"

Dr. Namba studied him for a long moment.

"There's no harm in telling you. We're researching a Pokemon virus."

"A Pokemon virus!?"

Shocked, Ethan searched his memory. There had indeed been a story about such a virus in the anime, though he could no longer remember the details. He had a vague recollection that Team Rocket had even kidnapped Professor Oak over the virus research!

Dr. Namba saw Ethan frown and gave a cold laugh.

"Viruses, bacteria, vaccines... They're all essentially the same. People usually want nothing to do with a virus. I see it differently. A virus can change a Pokemon's genes and greatly enhance its abilities. There may be some harm, but on balance, the benefits far outweigh the costs!"

There he goes. Another stubborn old man who has taken an idea much too far...

"So the Pokemon locked up downstairs are your test subjects?"

"Naturally." Dr. Namba snorted, then spoke with regret. "It's a shame we didn't finish organizing and transferring the data. I thought we had plenty of time, but clearly we don't."

He waved to the people around him. The researchers looked as though they had been granted a reprieve and hurried into an elevator to one side.

The elevator descended toward an unknown destination.

Ethan made no move to pursue them.

They were ordinary research staff. The real source of the problem was Dr. Namba.

Even if Ethan arrested every one of those people, Dr. Namba could recruit more to work for him as long as he held to his ideas.

His target was clear: the old man standing before him!

Dr. Namba turned away and made a few more casual adjustments at the control panel.

His composure made Ethan wary of another trick. Ethan started toward him, speaking to keep the scientist's attention divided.

"Aren't you worried?"

"About what?" the old man replied without looking up.

"About being captured and handed over to the International Police."

Dr. Namba shook his head. "You still don't understand. When my research succeeds, the virus will produce Pokemon that are bigger and stronger than ever! What I'm doing will be a great achievement for humanity!! As a Pokemon Trainer, surely you want more powerful Pokemon of your own?"

Before Ethan could answer, Erika, who had remained silent until now, could no longer contain herself. "A great achievement!? You must be joking. You want to use a virus to change their genes. That's a violation of life itself!!"

Dr. Namba glanced at her and snorted. "Young lady, you have a great deal to learn. Humans and Pokemon alike evolved by adapting to their environments little by little. We've been changing our genes all along."

Perhaps realizing that neither of them shared his beliefs, Dr. Namba did not bother explaining further.

He gave Ethan one last look.

"Young man, I know who you are and what you've done. Frankly, you've achieved a remarkable amount at your age. You could go even further in the future. But for now... good luck."

Without hesitation, he pressed a red button on the control panel.

The next instant, the base shook violently and powerful explosions sounded on both sides!

Boom!!

The walls shattered, releasing thick smoke and flashes of fire!

Ethan immediately threw himself over Erika to shield her. Gardevoir raised a barrier around them both!

Smoke filled the room, and fragments of machinery scattered across the floor.

When Ethan raised his head and looked for Dr. Namba, the scientist was already inside the elevator the researchers had used. Its doors were slowly closing.

Before Ethan could give chase, seawater surged in from all sides. In an instant, it covered his feet!

Chapter 480: Rising Water and Underwater Breathing

Ethan had taken only two steps forward when the current nearly knocked him down.

He had no choice but to abandon his pursuit of Dr. Namba. Turning to Erika, he said quickly, "Put on your mask and respirator!"

Fortunately, neither of them had discarded their equipment. They hurriedly put it on, and by the time they were ready, the water had already risen past their waists.

It was rising far too fast!

Watching the level climb, Ethan took out a Poke Ball and recalled Gardevoir, then released Dragonair.

They were already beneath the sea, so Gardevoir could no longer Teleport them away. Dragonair, on the other hand, could move freely underwater and would be far more useful in their present situation.

Only a dozen seconds passed before the water reached their chests. Moving became difficult, and the pressure against them made even breathing a struggle.

Unable to advance, they reached for anything they could hold to keep the current from sweeping them away.

The only handhold nearby was a pillar. Erika wrapped both arms around it first, leaving Ethan to hold onto the pillar and her at the same time. That kept him from being knocked down.

Whoosh, whoosh...

Thick torrents of seawater continued pouring into the room.

With the flood raging around them, they could not worry about the propriety of holding each other so closely. They pressed together and endured the current in silence.

They were so close that, through Erika's soaked clothes, Ethan could feel the warmth of her body!

Erika, in turn, could feel the breadth of Ethan's chest. Even in the middle of this danger, it unsettled her slightly.

Neither made any attempt to separate.

They both knew that if they let go, the current might hurl them against something hard and knock them unconscious.

Whoosh...

Water continued to rush in. Tables, chairs, and other objects were swept from adjoining rooms and hurtled toward them.

Dragonair placed itself in front of the pair and knocked the debris away with its tail before it could strike them.

The situation finally began to change when the room filled completely with seawater.

Ethan felt the force of the current weaken. Knowing their chance had come, he tapped Erika on the waist.

She understood and nodded. One behind the other, they began swimming back the way they had come.

They had walked these halls only minutes earlier, but now every corridor was flooded. The continuing current made each stroke harder and demanded far more strength.

They swam through a long passage and room after room. Erika led the way, and from behind, Ethan had a clear view of her figure and her long legs moving through the water.

Well... At least there's something pleasant to look at while we're escaping...

Even with that distracting view, swimming against the current made the journey seem exceptionally long.

By now the base had sunk, the person responsible had escaped, and their situation seemed incapable of becoming any worse. They both expected to continue swimming until they were safely outside.

Once Ethan adjusted to the effort, he even stole another glance at Erika's graceful figure ahead of him.

They were almost out when a pipe beside Erika burst as she rounded a corner. The blast sent a shock wave through the water and hurled her toward the opposite wall.

It happened too suddenly for even Dragonair to intervene.

Fortunately, Ethan reacted quickly. From where he swam, he was able to seize one of Erika's lower legs before she hit anything. The blast had knocked the respirator from her mouth, however, and the current carried it out of sight in an instant!

Glug, glug...

Bubbles escaped Erika's mouth. Although she could not dodge the shock wave, she managed to close her mouth in time to keep from choking on seawater.

Even so, the air she had been holding escaped at once!

Ethan did not hesitate. He swam to her, removed his own respirator, and handed it over. Erika immediately put it in her mouth and drew several deep breaths, finally regaining her composure.

Once she had enough air, she tried to return it. Ethan waved her off, indicating that he was fine for the moment.

Erika assumed he had taken one last deep breath before giving it to her, so she thought little of his refusal.

As they approached the exit, however, she began to realize something was wrong.

Several minutes had passed. How could Ethan still be holding his breath?

Could his lungs really hold that much air?

Puzzled, she offered him the respirator again. He shook his head and refused once more.

Worried that he was merely trying to act tough, Erika tapped him on the chest.

Her gesture made Ethan realize something was unusual too.

He knew his own body. He should not have been able to hold his breath for so long, yet he still felt no tightness in his chest!

He had gone without breathing far longer than usual. Focusing on the sensation, he could even feel a little oxygen in the seawater being absorbed through the skin around his throat and entering his windpipe!

The discovery immediately reminded him of the blessing he had received as the Sea Hero.

Could this be its second effect?

Curious to discover his limit, Ethan declined the respirator again and continued swimming with Erika toward the exit.

As soon as they emerged from the base, they encountered Misty's Corsola and Ash's Totodile.

After seeing the base sink, Ash and Misty had worried about Ethan and Erika and sent their Pokemon to look for them. The searchers had found them just outside.

Holding on to the Pokemon, Ethan and Erika quickly swam toward the surface with their help.

Then Ethan sensed something. Looking down, he saw an enormous dark shape sweep beneath them.

The view underwater was blurred, but he recognized Team Rocket's submarine immediately!

Dr. Namba and the researchers were probably aboard it.

Sigh. They got away after all...

The Team Rocket members who had fled through the surface exit had been a distraction. This was the real escape route!

Still, the virus research facility had been damaged. That counted for something. At least their trip had not been entirely in vain...

Chapter 481: The Operation Ends

After they swam several dozen meters farther upward, the water around them grew steadily brighter. It was as if two powerful beams had pierced the sea and illuminated everything below.

With visibility improving, Ethan finally felt a tightness in his chest. He asked Erika for the respirator and took several deep breaths.

He had not kept track of the time, so he could not say precisely how long he had gone without it. Still, there was no question that he could hold his breath much longer than before!

By his rough estimate, the time had doubled. It was not an enormous change, but it was enough to let him swim underwater for considerably longer.

They continued upward. At last, they broke through the rolling surface and breathed open air again.

Only then did Ethan realize that the moon was high overhead. Night had fallen completely!

The two bright beams they had seen underwater came from the searchlights of two police patrol boats!

When the officers saw them surface, someone lowered a rope ladder from the nearer boat. Ethan helped Erika onto it first, then climbed after her. Once he left the sea, however, the air felt bitterly cold. His clothes were soaked, and even the light breeze made him shiver.

He endured the chill and climbed toward the top. Several pairs of hands reached down and pulled them aboard.

In the poor light, Ethan could make out only figures gathered around him. Before he could see their faces, someone draped a thick towel over his shoulders.

Its warmth chased away the cold, making him feel almost as though he had been given a new life.

As his eyes adjusted to the darkness, he recognized Ash, Misty, Brock, Richie, and Oliver. Even Anabel was there!

Noticing his look, Anabel gave a soft laugh. "It seems you ran into trouble down there. I could feel the tremors from the seabed even while I was aboard the boat."

"We did have some trouble." Ethan shook his head with a rueful smile. "Those mad Team Rocket scientists set off explosions in the base. Erika and I nearly died in there. Worse, we couldn't catch them. They escaped."

He told the group what had happened below, including the research into the virus.

Ash and the others exchanged astonished looks. None of them had expected Team Rocket to use a diversion to conceal its real purpose!

Misty's eyes shone with admiration. "It's a good thing you insisted on staying, Ethan. Otherwise, we'd never have learned what Team Rocket was hiding!"

Richie scratched his cheek, looking a little embarrassed.

Before the base sank, he too had assumed there was nothing more to the situation. Now he saw how far he still lagged behind this Champion in both strength and experience.

"I only stayed to test a hunch," Ethan said with a sigh. "I happened to be right this time. By the way, how did you all end up together?"

"We were worried about you, of course, so I arranged two boats to support you as quickly as I could," Anabel said with another smile. "As for me, after we landed and handed over the Team Rocket members we'd arrested, I immediately boarded another helicopter. I only arrived here a little while ago."

At the mention of Team Rocket, Ethan hurriedly looked around. "What happened to the members who escaped the base?"

Anabel stepped aside, revealing officers hard at work across the deck.

In one corner, dozens of soaked Team Rocket members crouched in handcuffs. The International Police officers searched and registered them one by one, then escorted the dejected prisoners into the cabin.

Everything proceeded in an orderly manner, another sign of Anabel's excellent command.

"When we arrived, they were just escaping from the base," she explained. "They were all floating on the surface, looking miserable, with no strength left to fight. We pulled them aboard and arrested them without any trouble!"

Ethan was relieved they had not escaped. Then another thought occurred to him. "Did you catch Cassidy and Butch?"

"No." Anabel shook her head regretfully. "We were about to arrest them when a submarine shaped like a Magikarp came out of nowhere and carried them away."

A Magikarp submarine?

Ethan immediately thought of the Team Rocket trio.

They were the only people he knew who traveled around in that homemade Magikarp submarine, causing trouble wherever they went.

But Jessie, James, and Meowth were bitter rivals of Cassidy and Butch. Why would they rescue them?

I can't make sense of that...

"There's nothing we can do now," Ethan said with a sigh. "Those two are persistent, and they're important members of Team Rocket. It would have been good to capture them too."

Anabel was more satisfied with the outcome. "Even so, this operation was a great success. We've dealt Team Rocket another severe blow and weakened them considerably. A few more operations like this, and we may be able to clear their forces out of Johto entirely!"

She studied Ethan appreciatively and added with a half-joking smile, "To tell the truth, I'm growing more impressed with you. Looker was right. You're practically our lucky charm!"

...

At daybreak, after spending the night resting aboard the police patrol boat, Ethan and his companions said goodbye to Anabel. They boarded Oliver's speedboat and set out for the Temple of the Sea on Red Rock Isle.

The matter was settled for now. It was time to return to Red Rock Isle and report to Maya.

In just two days, they had wrecked Team Rocket's base, helped capture a great many of its members, and thwarted its attempt to seize Lugia. Silver and its mother could finally live here without fearing that Team Rocket would disturb them.

They had originally intended to part ways with Oliver. The boy insisted on visiting the Temple of the Sea, however, because he wanted to see the beautiful Sea Priestess Maya for himself. He called his mother and received her permission, so Ethan's group brought him along to Red Rock Isle.

Richie naturally wanted to come and have a look too.

He had come here to train, and the Temple of the Sea was the most famous place in the Whirl Islands. He regretted missing the tournament a few days earlier, but seeing the temple and its surroundings would still be a worthwhile experience.

Chapter 482: The Succession Rite

Maya had already received the news by telephone.

When the speedboat reached the harbor on Red Rock Isle that afternoon, Ethan spotted her from afar. Dressed in a long white robe and holding her golden scepter, she waited at the dock with a group of attendants.

Even standing still, the Sea Priestess drew every eye. Her long purple hair moved in the wind, framing her beautiful face.

As soon as the boat docked, Ethan and the others stepped onto the pier. Maya greeted them with a warm smile that still held a hint of regal reserve.

"Welcome back, my Sea Hero. And welcome to you, the Hero's assistants!"

She offered Ethan the back of her smooth, pale hand.

My Sea Hero...

He found the form of address a little odd, but thought no more of it. Perhaps it was simply how the Sea Priestess addressed the Sea Hero.

Ash and the others noticed that being called the Hero's assistants placed them a step below Ethan, turning companions into followers. None of them minded much.

They had spent enough time beside him to grow used to standing in his shadow.

Ethan recognized the offered hand as a matter of etiquette. He bowed and lightly kissed it.

Behind him, Brock wanted to copy the gesture and steal a kiss for himself. By the time he bent forward, however, Maya had already withdrawn her hand!

He stood there heartbroken, like a statue drained of all color. His misery was so complete that those nearby could almost hear his fragile heart shatter.

Here we go again...

Erika and Ash knew Brock well and had seen this happen often enough during their travels to be entirely untroubled. Richie and Oliver, on the other hand, looked genuinely worried.

"Is... is he all right?"

"Don't worry about him." Misty waved a hand without so much as blinking. "This happens every so often. You'll get used to it."

Meanwhile, Maya looked at Ethan gently and said with a soft smile, "I've heard how you destroyed Team Rocket's base. Thank you for everything you did, and for protecting the God of the Sea. You must be exhausted after that journey."

Ethan and the others responded modestly.

"It was the least we could do."

After a brief exchange, Maya stepped aside. "I've had a lavish dinner prepared to welcome you back and celebrate your success. Before then, please come to the temple and rest."

Ash and Oliver were the most excited by the promise of a feast. Both still had the appetites of children, and no amount of good food ever seemed enough. A chance to eat their fill would be a fine reward for the effort of the past few days!

Escorted by the attendants, the group followed the stone path up the mountain.

Maya and Ethan led the way, with Erika, Ash, Richie, and Oliver following close behind. Only Misty paused beside Brock. With a weary sigh, she seized his ear and dragged him toward the Temple of the Sea while he remained frozen in despair.

Passersby glanced curiously at the procession. When they recognized Sea Priestess Maya and Ethan, the Sea Hero, they stared all the more.

What could have happened to bring the Sea Priestess and the Sea Hero out together?

People murmured among themselves. Fortunately, the Temple of the Sea commanded such respect here that, despite their curiosity, no one dared interrupt the group.

Following the path uphill, they soon reached the temple at the summit.

Like Ash on his first visit, Richie and Oliver immediately found their eyes drawn to the enormous statue of the God of the Sea.

To Oliver in particular, the Temple of the Sea was a sacred place. Simply standing there made him tremble with excitement!

If it could inspire that reaction in a child, it was easy to see what place the temple held in the hearts of the people of the Whirl Islands.

Maya arranged rooms where everyone could rest and recover. At around five in the afternoon, they were invited to the banquet hall.

Gentle music filled the room. A long table was laden with all kinds of food, while attendants played stringed instruments or stood nearby with pitchers of wine, ready to serve their honored guests.

Maya sat at the head of the table and raised a cup in their honor. As at the previous banquet, no other guests attended.

The group took seats along both sides of the table. With little ceremony, the feast began.

They all knew one another now, and even Maya no longer felt like a stranger. The celebration quickly grew lively!

The Whirl Islands produced a fruit wine made from a local grape. Lightly sweet and low in alcohol, it suited the occasion perfectly. Ethan and Erika drank some, and even Ash and the younger guests had quite a bit.

Cups passed around the table as the feast went on in a cheerful atmosphere.

Halfway through the meal, Maya suddenly left her seat and approached Ethan.

"My Hero, could I ask you for one more favor?"

Perhaps because she had drunk some of the fruit wine, a faint blush colored her cheeks. She looked less aloof than usual and a little more alluring.

Ethan set down his knife and fork and looked up at her. "Of course. What do you need?"

They had grown familiar during their time together. Besides, he was the temple's Sea Hero. Unless she asked something unreasonable, he saw no reason to refuse.

Perhaps his eyes deceived him, but Maya's cheeks seemed to redden even further at his answer!

Looking straight into his eyes, she said, "I'd like you to help me carry out the succession rite."

The succession rite?

Ethan glanced at the others and saw the same confusion on their faces.

Judging by its name, it sounded like an ancient ceremony of the Temple of the Sea. Since it was temple business, Ethan had no reason to turn her down.

"Of course. Do you mean now?"

Maya nodded and let out a long breath. She then addressed Erika and the others apologetically. "Please continue your meal. The succession rite will take a long time, so forgive us for leaving you without our company."

Chapter 483: This Isn't a Multiple-Choice Question

Ethan followed Maya out of the banquet hall and deeper into the Temple of the Sea.

Night had fallen during the feast, and the candles in the corridors had been lit again.

Their warm, dim light fell across the stone beneath their feet. Ethan could once more hear the familiar sound of water swirling through the temple.

On the way, he tried to ask a few questions about the succession rite. Maya seemed to have reservations, however, and revealed nothing, making the whole matter feel mysterious.

Oh well...

If she did not want to explain, Ethan saw little point in asking again.

Whatever the rite involved, he trusted Maya not to harm him.

In private, another question kept returning to him. Why had the Sea Spirit's blessing affected him differently from everyone else?

Neither he nor Maya understood the unusual changes.

Sometimes he wondered whether they might have something to do with the fact that he had come to this world from another one. He could think of no other difference between himself and the people who had received the blessing before him.

And so they walked in silence, each occupied with their own thoughts.

At last they reached a room. Ethan glanced at its door and was surprised to recognize Maya's bedroom!

Huh!?

Hadn't she said they were performing a succession rite? Why had she brought him here? Would they hold it in her room, or did she need to collect something first?

Still wondering, he followed her inside.

On his previous visit, the room had been in ruins. Now it had been fully repaired, without a trace of the damage.

Two attendants were present. As Ethan entered, they came forward and removed his coat before he could refuse.

He could no longer contain his curiosity. "Miss Maya, what exactly is this succession rite?"

Maya walked to the balcony and looked at the moon. Then she turned to face him and, apparently ready to stop concealing the truth, began speaking slowly. "Since the Temple of the Sea was founded, the Sea Priestess has always led it. That position has always been held by a woman. It is both our tradition and an unchangeable rule."

Ethan nodded. Oliver had mentioned this while they were aboard the speedboat. As far as he knew, a woman had indeed always served as the temple's leader.

But why bring it up now?

Maya continued, "Compared with men, women are less likely to be swayed by wealth, status, beauty, or other temptations. We can remain more neutral, without a pronounced political allegiance. That has helped the temple avoid losing its way and maintain its special standing in the Whirl Islands. Yet one problem has troubled us throughout our history."

Ethan chuckled. "With all your wealth and influence, you still have problems?"

Maya gave him a long look. "Succession."

Succession...

Ethan stopped smiling and waited patiently for her to continue.

"I'm ashamed to say it," Maya said with a sigh, "but during the temple's first century or two, the position passed to whoever was most capable. A Sea Priestess would hand it over when a suitable successor appeared. Several centuries ago, however, an ancestor of mine wanted to keep that power. She changed the tradition and passed the office to her own descendants. It has remained in our family ever since."

Ethan recalled that Maya had told him she inherited the position from her mother.

Just as Maya said, her family had kept a firm hold on the office for generations.

Moonlight fell over her, lending her a sacred air, as though she wore a veil of silver.

"As a member of that family," she said firmly, "I must someday bear a child and pass on both our bloodline and the office of Sea Priestess."

Her meaning was plain enough that Ethan began to suspect where this was going.

"So..."

Maya took several steps toward him. "So it has long been common for the Sea Hero and the Sea Priestess to join together. Many of my ancestors were Sea Heroes themselves, and the children born of such a union inherited an even more perfect bloodline!"

So that's what she meant by the succession rite...

To be honest, Ethan had never imagined it would mean this!

Then again, perhaps generations of improved genes explained both Maya's beauty and her noble bearing!

"Since you already agreed to the succession rite," Maya began, "we could..."

"I'm sorry..." Ethan interrupted with a rueful smile and shook his head. "I didn't know what the rite meant when I agreed. And I have a girlfriend, so this... I'm afraid I have to refuse."

Maya did not seem surprised by his answer.

"Your girlfriend would be Miss Erika, wouldn't she?"

Ethan opened his mouth to say that Erika was not his girlfriend. Yet their relationship was no longer that of ordinary friends, and to an outsider they seemed inseparable.

But if he called Erika his girlfriend, what did that make Sabrina?

He and Sabrina had never stated their relationship outright, but in both their actions and their feelings, she was the one who should be considered his girlfriend.

After hesitating for a long while, he chose not to explain. "Even if I didn't have a girlfriend, I'm not ready to think about having children at my age."

Maya smiled. "Surely you don't think conceiving a child is so simple? Besides, I won't tell Miss Erika. I know your aim is to challenge the various League tournaments, not to remain here. If a child is born, I'll raise her myself. I won't bring you any trouble!"

"No..." Ethan sighed. "You've misunderstood. This isn't about whether she'd find out..."

Seeing his reluctance, Maya assumed he and Erika were deeply attached and that he did not want to betray her.

"You needn't make this more complicated than it is," Maya said gently. "You wouldn't lose anything. If we have a child, the Temple of the Sea will always stand behind you. I won't cling to you. I only want your help in continuing my bloodline."

Her insistence baffled him. "Why me?"

Maya shook her head. "A new Sea Hero is chosen every three years, so yes, I have other candidates. But you're different. Winning the Indigo League proved your strength. Saving the Gods of the Sea without trying to catch them proved you aren't driven solely by gain. And you saved me, which moved me deeply. Most of all, I like you. I don't want to let my chance with you pass me by in this lifetime!"

Her heartfelt confession moved Ethan.

He could not say what he felt, but reason told him he had to refuse. He could not do this to Sabrina.

Then Erika came to mind.

Nothing had happened between them during their travels together. Even so, both of them knew their relationship had begun to cross the boundary of friendship...

They worked together effortlessly, understood each other's views, and could talk about anything. They had become companions in spirit!

When he fell silent, Maya boldly stepped closer and took his hand.

"My Hero, the man I love, this is my final request. Please don't turn me down!"

Chapter 484: Leaving the Island

Ethan had drunk quite a bit of fruit wine at the banquet, and now he could feel its effects rising.

Maya's expression was so earnest that he could not doubt her sincerity or her resolve. The warmth of her hand in his stirred another feeling that tugged at his thoughts.

Alcohol and impulse gradually wore at his judgment. Fortunately, what remained of his reason still held him back.

He could faintly hear music drifting from the distant banquet hall. Ash and the others were clearly still enjoying the feast.

No...

This is getting out of control. I can't betray Sabrina. I have to leave now...

Before he could say anything, Maya seemed to make up her mind. She tugged gently at the sash around her waist, and her clothes slipped from her body...

Ethan stared at her, eyes wide with disbelief. For a moment, even his thoughts seemed to stop.

The two attendants exchanged smiles, quietly left the room, and gently closed the door behind them...

...

Early the next morning, Ash and the others were eating breakfast in the banquet hall.

Their bags had already been packed and stacked neatly nearby.

From the Whirl Cup through the protection of Lugia, everything they had come to do was finally finished. They could resume their travels.

It had not been very long, yet looking back made the whole experience feel strangely distant.

They waited through breakfast, but Ethan never appeared.

Misty glanced toward the guest rooms and asked worriedly, "It's this late and he still hasn't come. Should we go look for him?"

Erika shook her head. "I don't think he came back to his room at all last night."

"You don't think something happened to him?"

As they spoke, footsteps sounded. They turned and saw Maya approaching with a smile, Ethan beside her and yawning.

Ash immediately asked, "Ethan, did the succession rite go well last night?"

Ethan's expression turned awkward at once.

Before he could answer, Maya said warmly, "It went very well, thanks to Ethan's help."

Misty noticed a subtle difference.

Maya seemed much more intimate with Ethan now.

At the very least, her way of addressing him suggested that something between them had changed.

Curious, Misty asked, "Miss Maya, what kind of rite was it?"

Maya shook her head. "It's an ancient rite. Only a small number of Sea Heroes, those whose courage and strength we recognize, might be chosen by a Sea Priestess to take part."

"Oh..." Ash looked wistful. "I was so busy eating last night. I wish I could have seen it."

"Cough! Cough! Cough!"

Ash's words startled Ethan into a fit of coughing.

That's really not something you should watch, kid...

Sigh. Impulse really can get the better of a person...

With the wine giving him courage, he had crossed that line after all...

Then again, Maya was beautiful, noble, and powerful. She had remained untouched until now, wanted a child with him, asked for nothing in return, and even offered to keep it secret. It was hard not to waver under those circumstances.

In the end, though, he had only himself to blame. His resolve had not been strong enough to resist her beauty...

Noticing that something was wrong with his expression, Erika came over. "You're only arriving now. Have you had breakfast?"

"Mm... I ate a little while ago..."

"You don't look well rested. Are you tired?"

Looking at Erika's lovely face, Ethan could not help coughing again.

"Yes... a little tired. But don't worry. I'll be fine after some rest..."

Sigh...

Erika plainly suspected nothing, and Ethan was filled with guilt and unease as he looked at her.

How was he supposed to face her from now on?

...

At the harbor on Red Rock Isle, Ethan, Erika, Ash, Misty, Brock, Oliver, and Richie prepared to say goodbye.

Their time together had been happy and brief. Parting was another matter.

According to their earlier plans, Ethan and Erika would travel to Cianwood City to challenge its Gym. Oliver would return to Ogi Isle, and Richie would continue his training journey. Ash, Misty, and Brock would set out for other places and the Gyms Ash had yet to challenge.

Maya came to see them off with two attendants. While the travelers exchanged their final farewells, she stood quietly to one side.

Now and then she looked toward Ethan, only to turn her gaze away before anyone noticed.

"Take care, everyone. I'll be going first!"

Richie waved. He was returning to Kanto from here, and because of his schedule, he would be the first to leave.

"You take care too. Maybe our paths will cross again!"

Ethan and the others waved as Richie boarded his boat and departed. Then Oliver untied his speedboat, and Ash, Misty, and Brock climbed aboard with him.

Since their routes all passed Ogi Isle, Oliver could carry the three of them for another leg of their journey.

"Ethan, we're heading out too!"

Ethan nodded to them. "Travel safely. We'll see each other next time."

Their farewell was casual. All of them knew their journeys often crossed, and they would surely meet again.

After the speedboat left the dock, only Ethan, Erika, Maya, and her attendants remained.

Maya approached Ethan and said softly, "As I told you before, this won't be easy. I'll likely need your help several more times."

Neither needed to say aloud what she meant.

Ethan's gaze passed over Maya's neck. Her collar concealed it, but he knew there was a faint red mark there, left by one of his kisses the night before.

He sighed and met her eyes. "I'll come back to see you often. If anything happens, let me know right away."

Whatever Maya had said about not asking him to take responsibility, after last night Ethan could hardly leave her entirely on her own!

Maya nodded with a smile. "I understand. It's getting late. You should be on your way."

Erika sensed something unusual in their exchange, but said nothing. Like Maya earlier, she stood a short distance away and quietly waited for them to finish.

Chapter 485: Chuck, the Human Pokemon

After sailing west, Ethan and Erika reached the docks of Cianwood City around noon.

The city stood on the western edge of Johto, not far from the Whirl Islands. Separated from Johto's mainland, it enjoyed beautiful scenery and a pleasant climate. The city was not especially large, but its streets were clean. It looked like an excellent place for a holiday.

They did not linger and headed straight for the Cianwood Gym.

They had barely left the harbor when shouts of "Hey! Hah! Hey! Hah!" reached them from the beach.

The noise was impossible to ignore.

They turned and saw a shirtless man sparring with a Machoke!

The man had an unusual hairstyle and a thick mustache. Loose white judo trousers covered his legs, while his bronzed skin gleamed in the sun. He looked exceptionally strong.

He was human, yet he traded blows with Machoke without giving an inch. He had to be a formidable fighter!

Erika gave him a glance, lost interest, and started onward. After a few steps, she noticed Ethan was still standing in place and looked back at him curiously.

"What is it?"

"I don't think we need to go to the Cianwood Gym to find its Leader." Ethan tipped his chin toward the man. "That's probably him."

At Ethan's words, Erika studied the man again in surprise.

"Oh? That's him?"

Ethan nodded.

The Cianwood Gym Leader was Chuck, a judo master and a Trainer specializing in Fighting-type Pokemon.

Ethan did not actually remember Chuck's face. The man had so few appearances that he barely stood out even among the Gym Leaders. Still, in a city this small, someone who fit Chuck's description so closely was very likely to be him.

After all, a man who could fight a Pokemon with his bare hands was hardly ordinary. He was practically a human Pokemon himself.

They let Chuck finish his training and watched from a distance. Only when he and Machoke paused to rest did they approach.

Chuck had noticed them some time ago. As they drew near, he wiped his sweat with a towel and turned toward them.

"Excuse me. Are you Mr. Chuck?"

Chuck nodded at the young man's polite question.

"Who are you?"

Ethan got straight to the point. "I'm Ethan Vale, and this is my traveling companion. I've come to challenge the Cianwood Gym."

"Ethan Vale?" Chuck frowned in puzzlement. "I feel like I've heard that name somewhere..."

Unable to recall where, he gave up and looked Ethan up and down.

"If you want to challenge the Cianwood Gym, you must be a Trainer. It's a shame. You're young and should be bursting with energy, but you look exhausted. You haven't got a bit of spirit!"

"Spirit?" Ethan blinked.

He could not deny that he looked exhausted.

After spending the night in Maya's bed, he had barely slept. Then the long, rocking boat trip had done nothing to help. Of course he did not look energetic.

But what did his spirit have to do with challenging the Cianwood Gym?

Seeing Ethan's confusion, Chuck crossed his arms over his chest and declared with booming conviction, "Spirit means vigor and drive! As a Trainer and a man, you ought to train alongside your Pokemon and make yourself just as strong. That's what it takes to be a truly qualified Trainer!"

Ethan had no answer.

He chose to remain silent rather than challenge Chuck's view.

Everyone had their own way of training. Why should a Trainer have to become as strong as a Pokemon?

Such an approach might suit someone like Chuck, who specialized in Fighting-type Pokemon. But were Trainers of other types supposed to match their partners' strength too?

As an ordinary human, Ethan could hardly imagine ever becoming as powerful as Gardevoir or Gengar.

Chuck mistook his silence for agreement. He clapped Ethan on the shoulder and laughed. "Now that you understand, let's start by running to the Cianwood Gym!"

"What?"

"Get moving!" Chuck laughed again. "You can't challenge my Gym without showing some determination!!"

Without waiting to hear whether Ethan agreed, Chuck and Machoke took off toward the city!

Ethan watched them go, speechless.

Erika came to his side with a light smile. "Are you going to run after him?"

Ethan sighed, took off his backpack, and handed it to her.

"Every Gym has its own rules. If I want to challenge Cianwood, I'll have to follow Chuck's. I'll catch up with him. You can take your time getting there."

Chuck was already far ahead. Ethan had little choice but to set off after him at a brisk pace.

He left the beach and entered the city's streets.

Chuck and Machoke raced along like two walking mountains of muscle. The people in the street seemed used to the sight. They greeted Chuck with smiles, and he nodded back as he ran.

At least he was clearly well liked in the city.

But Ethan had been too tired the night before. After running for several minutes, he found that he could not catch Chuck. In fact, Chuck had already vanished from sight!

Gengar drifted out of Ethan's shadow and circled him with a few amused clicks of its tongue.

"That's a primitive way to travel. Want me to carry you? Chuck's so far ahead that no one would notice."

"No thanks." Ethan panted several times and shook his head. "I haven't run in ages. I'll treat it as exercise!"

Normally, his stamina would have served him better. Last night had taken too much out of him, however, and he had not rested properly. Today he was in poor condition.

Fortunately, he adjusted his breathing and changed his pace. Instead of trying to catch Chuck, he slowed to a jog.

Chuck had only said Ethan had to run to the Gym, not race him there. Arriving a little later would make no difference.

The Gym was a little over twenty minutes from the beach. By the time Ethan reached its doors, he was sweating heavily.

Still, although his body was a little tired, the run had shaken off the morning's lethargy. His thoughts were clear again, and he felt much more alert.

Chapter 486: The Cianwood Gym

The Cianwood Gym was the city's official and only Gym. It specialized in Fighting-type Pokemon, and a challenger who defeated Chuck would receive the Storm Badge.

By the time Ethan arrived, Chuck had changed clothes and was waiting outside its doors.

Chuck watched him jog up at an easy pace rather than exhaust himself trying to keep up, as other challengers often did. He nodded approvingly.

"Good. You're not like those fools who never think. You saved your strength by running at your own pace, but you didn't cheat or shirk the work. A clever Trainer who isn't lazywell done!"

Despite the praise, Ethan could not bring himself to feel pleased.

He bent slightly to catch his breath, wiped the sweat from his forehead, and looked up at Chuck.

Chuck was muscular, but he also had a rather large belly. Ethan had assumed that even if this judo master excelled at fighting, running might not suit him. Evidently his stamina was still far better than Ethan's.

Sigh. If I hadn't worn myself out last night and wasted time because I didn't know the way to the Gym, I wouldn't have taken this long...

"Mr. Chuck, can we begin the Gym battle now?"

Chuck nodded and led him inside.

What Ethan did not know was that Chuck had only just arrived himself. For all his talk and his approval of Ethan's effort, he had beaten Ethan here by no more than a few minutes.

Lately, Chuck had developed a taste for sweets, and his body fat had been climbing steadily. The run from the beach had left him drenched in sweat, his calves trembling.

He had gritted his teeth all the way back, then hurried to change into clean clothes before Ethan arrived so he could preserve his image!

He could only pull this off because Ethan did not know the route. Otherwise, Chuck might even have arrived after him!

For all his judgment, Chuck had hardly done much better.

Inside the Gym, a group of children rushed to meet Chuck and bowed together.

"Welcome back, Master!"

The youngest were only seven or eight, while the oldest were fifteen or sixteen. They all wore the same clothes and called Chuck their teacher. They were plainly his students.

Several Mankey, Machop, and Hitmontop stood nearby, surely the students' Pokemon.

Chuck strode past the group with his head held high.

"Did you all practice properly while I was away?"

The students bowed again and answered loudly, "Of course!"

"We didn't slack off!"

Their faces showed genuine trust and respect for Chuck. He managed his students well, and the Gym's atmosphere was clearly a good one.

Only after greeting him did the students notice Ethan behind Chuck. They studied the visitor curiously and, without anyone needing to say it, understood that a Gym battle was coming. Their excitement grew.

Compared with dull daily drills, a lively match was a welcome change!

At Chuck's signal, the students cleared a battlefield for the two Trainers. Then they sat on either side and watched intently.

Ethan had faced enough expectant audiences that their stares did not trouble him.

He and Chuck took their places at opposite ends of the field. The oldest student stepped into the middle to referee the match.

"Each Trainer may use three Pokemon. The Gym Leader sends out his Pokemon first. The challenger wins by defeating all of the Gym Leader's Pokemon!"

Before the match could begin, someone appeared in the doorway. Erika walked in.

She nodded to Ethan, then silently took a seat behind him.

At the sight of the beautiful older woman, several of Chuck's less worldly young students became awkward. They looked away shyly, unable to bring themselves to meet her face.

Erika was not only beautiful; she had the gentle air of an older sister. The younger boys were thoroughly flustered!

Across the field, Chuck regarded Ethan with solemn pride. "Allow me to introduce myself again. I am Chuck, king of Fighting-type Pokemon and Leader of the Cianwood Gym!"

With that, he sent out his first Pokemon.

A flash of blue light faded, and a Primeape stood before Ethan.

Primeape...

Primeape was a common Fighting-type Pokemon in both Kanto and Johto, popular with Trainers. Compared with its unevolved form, Mankey, the bulging cross-shaped vein on its forehead and its frightening glare made it appear even angrier and more intimidating.

After a moment's thought, Ethan took out a Poke Ball and released his own Pokemon.

When the light faded, Dragonair appeared across from Primeape.

"A Dragonair!!"

"Wow! I've never seen one before!"

Several students recognized the uncommon Pokemon and cried out in surprise.

Chuck, unlike his delighted students, frowned. "Young man, you know this is a Fighting-type Gym. Why didn't you send out a Fighting-type Pokemon to battle me?"

To him, matching Fighting-types against each other was the proper way to challenge his Gym. That was a man's idea of romance!

"Sorry..." Ethan shook his head. "I don't have any Fighting-type Pokemon at the moment, so I'll have to battle with another type."

"None?" Chuck's gaze sharpened. "Don't you like Fighting-type Pokemon?"

"It's not that. I just haven't met one I wanted to catch yet."

"What nonsense!" Chuck roared with laughter. "Look at Machamp, Machoke, Machop, Primeape, and Hitmontop. They're all adorable! Go catch yourself a few!"

Ethan smiled wryly.

He had not said there was anything wrong with them. His time and attention were limited, however, and he could not care for an unlimited number of Pokemon. Even if he encountered a wild Fighting-type, he would only catch one he truly liked.

Fortunately, Chuck knew he could not force the matter and let the subject drop.

Both Pokemon were ready. Chuck wasted no more time and ordered Primeape to charge straight at Dragonair!

Chapter 487: Dragonair Evolves

Thud...

After tracing an arc through the air, Primeape crashed to the ground and rolled backward several times. Its limbs went limp. It had fainted and could no longer battle.

Only a few minutes had passed since the match began, yet Dragonair had won the first round with ease.

Chuck's students stared in disbelief. This was nothing like what they had expected! Their master was a Fighting-type expert. How could one of his Pokemon be defeated so easily? The two Pokemon did not even have a type advantage over each other...

Some rubbed their eyes, as though checking whether the Primeape on the floor really was the fierce Pokemon that usually battered other challengers.

Primeape was certainly strong, but among Chuck's Pokemon it was only a reasonably capable member of his team. He had not recognized Ethan and had treated him as an ordinary challenger.

In the end, he had underestimated his opponent.

"To beat my Primeape that easily, you've got real skill. Looks like I'll have to show you a little of what I can do!"

Chuck gave Ethan a surprised look. He took out the Poke Ball he had only recently put away and recalled the unconscious Primeape.

He admitted to himself that he had underestimated this opponent. He had expected an ordinary challenger, never someone so strong. Primeape was often the first Pokemon he sent into battle, and for all the times it had opened a match, it had rarely lost so quickly.

It was time to raise the difficulty.

Chuck waved to the Machoke beside him, the one Ethan had seen at the beach. Machoke leaped straight into the battlefield.

Bang! It landed steadily, and the floor gave a tremendous thump under its weight.

"Young man," Chuck said, "I can see you're no ordinary Trainer. From now on, I won't treat you like one of those green kids who only recently started training Pokemon!"

Ethan nodded and smiled. "Mr. Chuck, you'd better be careful too. My Dragonair is quite strong."

After losing the first round, Chuck's choice to send out Machoke showed just how much confidence he had in it.

Machoke...

Ethan had battled its unevolved form, Machop, many times, but this was his first time facing a Machoke.

Machoke was a pure Fighting-type Pokemon with gray skin and powerful muscles all over its body. It wore a gold belt that restrained its strength. A black marking around its waist resembled briefs, and it had five digits on each hand and foot. Six red marks lined each arm. It looked exceptionally strong.

Ethan did not switch Pokemon for Chuck's second round. Dragonair had barely been hurt in the first, so he left it on the field.

When the battle resumed, Chuck was plainly more serious than before.

If Primeape was a hotheaded amateur that followed its instincts and vented its anger on its opponent, Machoke was a fighting expert with both strength and technique.

As soon as they exchanged blows, Ethan felt how much harder this round would be.

Machoke attacked methodically, often flowing straight from one move into the next. Dragonair struggled to keep up.

Its lack of limbs was part of the problem. Against Machoke's close-range attacks, Dragonair could not block or parry with its body. It had to open up some distance before it could strike back.

"Machoke, use Seismic Toss!"

After its repeated attacks failed to finish the fight, Machoke leaped in front of Dragonair at Chuck's command. It reached out to seize Dragonair in its arms, but Dragonair twisted its body and slipped away before Machoke could grab it.

Dragonair seized the opening and immediately whipped an Aqua Tail at Machoke.

They were too close for Machoke to dodge. It could only raise both hands to shield its head and take the blow.

Smack! Aqua Tail drove Machoke back several steps, but it shifted its weight in time and stopped its retreat.

What a difficult opponent...

Ethan and Chuck had the same thought at the same moment.

The two Pokemon clashed again. Machoke pressed the attack while Dragonair used its long, supple body to keep moving. Each pushed and pulled against the other, trading blows without either gaining a decisive advantage.

Chuck's students watched without blinking. At their level, this was a thrilling battle!

To their disappointment, Machoke landed several solid hits, but Dragonair refused to go down. Instead, Dragonair paralyzed it with Thunder Wave and then defeated it with Hyper Beam!

"He lost again..."

The students shook their heads as Machoke fell. The first round was one thing, but Machoke had had a real chance to win this one. Dragonair had simply proved stronger.

To Ethan, there was nothing strange about the result. Machoke was clearly still not Chuck's strongest Pokemon, and holding its own against Dragonair for so long was already impressive.

Chuck applauded. He was just about to praise Dragonair's performance when a white light suddenly burst from its body!

Chuck knew that light well. It was the glow of a Pokemon evolving!

"Hm? It's evolving!?"

Ethan was delighted by Dragonair's evolution too.

By rights, Dragonair should have evolved long ago. Today, it had finally found the opportunity!

When the light faded, a new Pokemon stood before them.

Its body was orange, its belly a soft cream color. Two small wings grew from its back, and two feelers rose from its head. There was no mistaking the big, plump Dragonite!

Dragonite twisted this way and that for a while, apparently unaccustomed to its new body.

Ethan could not help laughing at the sight. "Congratulations, Dragonite! You might not be as cute as you were before, but you're stronger now!"

Dragonite turned and called back to him, then looked at its two claws. Now that it had hands and feet, it would need quite some time to get used to them.

Chapter 488: Chuck's Ace Conkeldurr

Compared with the joy Ethan and Dragonite felt, Chuck's expression grew heavier after his initial surprise.

He had raised the difficulty and sent out Machoke, yet he had still lost? This young man was no ordinary opponent...

Chuck had to revise his estimate of Ethan's strength upward again.

It had been a long time since he had lost two rounds in a row. To salvage some dignity before his students and win back a round, it was time to show what he could really do!

Under everyone's puzzled gaze, he quietly left the room. When he returned, he was holding a Great Ball.

He took his place in the Trainer's area again and shook his head with a rueful smile.

"I thought I wouldn't need it after becoming a Gym Leader. I never expected I'd fight beside it again."

Ethan's eyes settled on the Great Ball. Chuck had not said so outright, but everyone understood that it must hold his strongest Pokemon!

"Master..."

Several of the older students recognized the ball and crowded around, excited and nervous.

"Is that... your ace Pokemon in there?"

"Master! I've never seen you command it before. You're finally going to let it battle!?"

"I've only heard how strong it is. I can't believe we finally get to see it!!"

Listening to their overlapping voices, Chuck sighed and stroked the Great Ball, as though remembering the past. After a long moment, he came back to himself and waved the students away.

"All right. Save your questions for later. We shouldn't keep our challenger waiting!"

Once the field was clear, Chuck threw the Great Ball with all his strength.

Bang! A blue flash revealed an unusual Pokemon before Ethan. It looked like an old man and held two concrete pillars.

What's that...?

Unfamiliar with it, Ethan took out his Pokedex and pointed it at the Pokemon.

"Beep. Conkeldurr, the Muscular Pokemon. Fighting type. Conkeldurr can swing the two concrete pillars it uses as canes by sheer strength, wielding them deftly in all kinds of moves. When serious, it throws the pillars aside and charges an opponent with its bare fists. It is said that humans learned to make concrete from Conkeldurr two thousand years ago."

Conkeldurr...

It was not a Pokemon native to Kanto, Johto, or Hoenn. You would normally have to go to Unova or another region to see one.

Ethan knew little about the species. He only remembered its evolutionary line: Timburr evolved into Gurdurr, which in turn evolved into Conkeldurr.

This had to be the ace Pokemon that had traveled the world with Chuck in his younger days! Bringing out the ace he had kept in reserve showed that Chuck was giving this battle everything he had.

Ethan glanced at Dragonite. It was eager to fight and still in good condition, so he kept it in the match.

"Dragonite, you can do it."

At Ethan's encouragement, Dragonite turned and nodded firmly to him.

The two Pokemon took their places opposite each other.

Conkeldurr looked every bit the old man it resembled, standing as steady as a mountain. Dragonite, by contrast, was like an excited youngster just starting out. It hovered in the air, beating its little wings, almost bursting with enthusiasm!

At the referee's signal, the battle began.

Now that it had arms and legs, Dragonite took the initiative in close combat. The moment the referee lowered his flag, it rushed at Conkeldurr like a gust of wind.

It was Extreme Speed, a physical Normal-type move that struck before an opponent could react.

Conkeldurr was nowhere near fast enough to dodge and took the hit squarely. But before it could be knocked off the ground, it gripped one of its concrete pillars with both hands. Using the pillar's weight, it managed to steady itself!

And it was not finished. With tremendous force, Conkeldurr swung its other pillar. It traced a full circle through the air with a rush of wind and slammed into Dragonite.

Bang! Dragonite flew backward. It beat its wings frantically and righted itself in midair just in time to avoid being knocked out of bounds.

Both Pokemon had taken damage in their very first exchange, but Conkeldurr seemed to have gained a slight edge!

Chuck's ace lived up to its reputation. A newly evolved Dragonite was no match for its experience!

"Dragonite, stop acting on your own!" Ethan called when Dragonite tried to charge in again. "Listen to me. Use Thunder Wave!"

Hearing its Trainer, Dragonite gradually calmed down.

As it approached Conkeldurr again, its two threadlike feelers released streams of electricity that wound toward the opponent along wavering paths.

Conkeldurr remained calm. It planted one of its concrete pillars in front of itself, and the electricity vanished the instant it struck the pillar.

The concrete conducted the current just enough to draw it down into the ground and disperse it. Conkeldurr clearly had a wealth of experience...

When that attack failed, Ethan promptly changed tactics.

At his command, Dragonite beat its wings rapidly. Energy gathered, and a visible whirlwind began to form between them.

Before the move could fully take shape, something whistled through the air. A concrete pillar flew across the field and struck Dragonite with perfect aim!

Smack! Caught off guard, Dragonite took the pillar squarely in its belly. Fortunately, the thick padding there cushioned the blow. It fell to the floor and suffered some damage, but nothing serious.

The whirlwind it had been building scattered in an instant!

Ethan frowned.

Dragonite was gradually losing ground. With its two concrete pillars, Conkeldurr could both attack and defend, making it a difficult opponent.

This can't go on...

As he thought, Ethan spotted the pillar that had rolled aside after striking Dragonite. An idea came to him.

If the pillars were Conkeldurr's greatest advantage, he only had to take that advantage away!

"Quick, throw that pillar away!" he shouted to Dragonite.

Chapter 489: The Storm Badge

Dragonite hurried forward. Its speed let it reach the concrete pillar before Conkeldurr could retrieve it, and it kicked the pillar out of bounds.

Rumble...

The pillar rolled right off the battlefield. Under the rules, an object that left the field could not be brought back into play.

It was a somewhat unsporting move. Everyone knew that a Marowak's bone club was its weapon. Throwing that club out of bounds might be perfectly legal, but it would still leave a faint impression of an unfair victory.

On the other hand, Conkeldurr had brought its concrete pillars as weapons. Dragonite was fighting barehanded and at a disadvantage. Taking away a weapon first was reasonable enough.

Conkeldurr grew wary. Afraid that Dragonite would throw its remaining pillar out of bounds too, it no longer dared to toss it around as freely as before.

Without an effective long-range attack, interrupting Dragonite's moves would be much harder.

Sure enough, when Dragonite gathered power for Dragon Rage, Conkeldurr hesitated over the pillar in its hand. Rather than throw it, Conkeldurr charged forward.

Dragon Rage formed quickly. A shock wave born of rage burst from between Dragonite's hands, streaked through the air, and engulfed Conkeldurr in an instant!

Boom!

Blue-green light swallowed Conkeldurr.

Conkeldurr held its last concrete pillar across its chest, trying to shield itself from the attack.

But concrete could not withstand a Pokemon's move. After only a few seconds of sustained Dragon Rage, the pillar crumbled into fragments on the ground.

Fortunately for Conkeldurr, the pillar had blocked most of the damage.

When Dragon Rage faded, Conkeldurr, its body scorched by the energy, had already closed in on Dragonite again!

"Conkeldurr, use Dynamic Punch!" Chuck roared.

Conkeldurr poured all its strength into its right fist and swung hard at Dragonite's face!

The two Pokemon were almost touching. With Conkeldurr's pillars gone, Dragonite had no reason to fear a close exchange. Electricity flashed around its hands, and it met the blow with Thunder Punch.

As the Pokemon crossed paths, both fists struck their targets.

Bang! Bang!

Dynamic Punch was a powerful Fighting-type move that always confused an opponent it hit.

Dragonite rocked backward from the blow. It caught its balance, but its head swam and its body swayed where it stood. It was clearly confused!

Yet Conkeldurr could not take advantage of the opening and land a finishing blow.

Dragonite's Thunder Punch had unluckily paralyzed it! Its movements slowed, and when it tried another move, electricity coursed through its body and stopped it in its tracks.

Neither Pokemon could move. They stood like a pair of statues guarding a doorway!

The field fell quiet. Now everything depended on which Pokemon recovered first and finished off the other.

"Conkeldurr! You can do it!!"

"Snap out of it, Conkeldurr!!"

Chuck's students instinctively cheered it on. Of the three rounds, this was its best chance to win. They could not bear to see their master's ace fall to the challenger as well!

If Conkeldurr lost, Dragonite would have fought all three of Chuck's Pokemon on its own. That would be a blow to the Gym's morale and reputation.
