After more than ten seconds, the two Pokemon recovered at the very same moment.

They moved together.

Conkeldurr used the Fighting-type move Hammer Arm!

Dragonite used Aqua Tail!

In the blink of an eye, both moves struck home.

Smack! Bang!

Before anyone could make out what had happened, Dragonite and Conkeldurr flew backward and collapsed on the ground.

What!?

The students sprang to their feet and stared at the field. A long moment passed, and neither Pokemon got up. The student acting as referee looked from one to the other, then decisively raised his flag.

"Conkeldurr and Dragonite are both unable to battle! The challenger wins this Gym match!"

They had taken each other down! Ethan, Chuck, and the students all felt a pang of regret.

Chuck's three Pokemon had all been defeated. Even if the final round was a draw, it could not change his loss.

He looked at the two unconscious Pokemon with mixed feelings.

So Dragonite really did take on all three...

At least Dragonite had fallen too. That salvaged a little dignity.

Ethan walked over to Dragonite and gathered it into his arms.

At the sound of his soft voice, Dragonite slowly opened its eyes.

"You did well," Ethan told it. "That Conkeldurr was a tough opponent. You were amazing to beat it!"

Just as he said, Dragonite had defeated two opponents by itself. Then, with a body it had only just gained through evolution, it had fought Chuck's ace to a mutual knockout. That was an outstanding performance!

Footsteps sounded nearby. Ethan looked up to see that Chuck had recalled his Pokemon and was approaching, applauding.

"That was an excellent battle. Congratulations, you've won!"

As he spoke, Chuck tossed a gleaming badge toward Ethan.

Ethan caught it neatly and opened his hand to examine it.

It was the Storm Badge from the Cianwood Gym.

Shaped like a clenched fist, it symbolized strength and fighting. Beyond that, there was nothing unusual about it.

Chuck smiled. "To be honest, I haven't enjoyed a battle this much in a long time. It's been ages since Conkeldurr last fought, too. This was a rare experience. Next time, I hope you'll bring a Fighting-type Pokemon of your own to face me!"

"I will!"

Erika came to Ethan's side. She took the badge, turned it over in her hands for a while, and then placed it in his badge case for him.

The two were about to say goodbye and leave when Chuck suddenly held out a hand to stop them.

Seeing Ethan's puzzled look, Chuck laughed heartily. "It's already lunchtime. Why don't you eat with us before you go?"

Chapter 490: A Chance Encounter in Azalea Town

Chuck's warm invitation was impossible to turn down, so Ethan and Erika stayed at the Gym for lunch.

Ethan had never expected this before the battle. He had come to the man's Gym, defeated him, and taken his badge. Now he was eating his food too. It felt a little shameless.

Then again, Chuck did not seem to mind. Why should Ethan worry so much about it?

Chuck lived at the Gym. Besides the battle hall, it had dormitories for his students. A few lived nearby in Cianwood City, but most ate and slept at the Gym.

Before lunch, Ethan and Erika met Chuck's wife.

She was a beautiful woman with long red hair and a gentle, capable air.

Frankly, given Chuck's rough appearance, he must have been extraordinarily lucky to marry someone like her!

Ethan and Erika sat down with the students. Chuck took the seat at the head of the table, glanced between his guests, and smiled. "Are you two a couple?"

The question silenced both of them.

Erika had lost count of how many times people had asked her that.

She was about to deny it when Ethan, instead of answering, asked, "Mr. Chuck, did you meet your wife while you were traveling too?"

Chuck nodded. He looked at his wife, sweet memories shining in his eyes. "That's right. Meeting her on my travels was why I wanted to settle down instead of wandering from place to place."

"Oh? I see. That's something to envy..."

Several students brought out plates of food and an enormous bucket of rice. Chuck's wife served everyone a bowl, but for Chuck she used an especially large one.

It was almost the size of a washbasin!

At Ethan and Erika's astonished looks, Chuck laughed. "Nothing strange about it. I get a lot of exercise!"

Once they began eating, Ethan discovered that Chuck was not the only one with a huge appetite. His students seemed to take after him, clutching their bowls and eating as heartily as he did!

It made sense. As Fighting-type Trainers, they trained with their Pokemon every day and burned a great deal of energy. They were growing children too, so large appetites were only natural.

The food vanished from the table in no time.

Over lunch, Chuck and his students grew increasingly curious about Ethan, and they admired him all the more.

After peppering him with questions, they finally learned that this handsome young man was the champion of the latest Indigo League!

"No wonder..." Chuck shook his head with a wry smile. "If I'd known you were the champion, I'd have brought out my strongest team from the start. Maybe I wouldn't have lost so badly."

After lunch, Ethan and Erika left the Cianwood Gym with everyone seeing them off.

As they neared the end of the street, Ethan looked back.

Erika gave him a questioning look. He sighed. "We only knew him for a few hours, but Chuck really is a warmhearted man..."

A few hours after their last visit, the two returned to the harbor.

This time, their destination was the Azalea Gym.

With the Storm Badge in hand, Ethan needed only two more badges before he could challenge the Silver Conference. Goldenrod City was closer to Cianwood, but they had missed the boat sailing there. They had to head for the more distant Azalea Town and challenge its Gym first.

They bought tickets and boarded a small passenger ship, which slowly carried them away from Cianwood City.

They sailed through the afternoon and night, sleeping aboard the ship before finally reaching the Johto mainland the following morning.

A night's rest had fully restored Ethan's energy and stamina. If he raced Chuck again now, he was sure he could keep up!

Unfortunately, there would be no rematch. He could only tuck that regret away in his memories.

Azalea Town was not a harbor town. The ship docked at a small city, and from there they still had a two-hour walk north to reach it.

They disembarked and left the city behind.

Just as they entered the wilds, Erika caught another Sunkern.

It was the second Sunkern she had caught since arriving in Johto.

Ethan could not understand why she wanted two of the same Pokemon. When he asked, Erika gave a little laugh.

"I'm not catching them for battles. They'll help keep the ecosystem in the Celadon Gym's greenhouse healthy and make its Pokemon population more varied!"

"I see..."

As they talked, they passed through the dense Ilex Forest.

It was a paradise for Bug-type Pokemon. The trees grew so thick that their branches blotted out the sky, leaving the forest as dark by day as it was at night.

Here, Ethan used Pupitar and the Eevee he had received from the sisters in Ecruteak City to defeat several overconfident Bug-type Pokemon that attacked them. Both of his Pokemon gained some battle experience.

They also caught a fleeting glimpse of a Farfetch'd. Ethan liked the species and wanted to catch it, but it disappeared deep into the forest before he could try. He could only smile, give up, and reflect that he and this Farfetch'd were not meant to meet.

At last they emerged from Ilex Forest, and the view opened up before them.

Their destination, Azalea Town, was close at hand.

Azalea was a town where people and Pokemon lived together in a simple, peaceful way.

It stood on a peninsula in southern Johto. Once it had been an unremarkable town, but a Trainer had founded the Azalea Gym there a few years earlier, and its name had gradually become better known.

The locals also told a less widely known legend.

Four hundred years ago, a Slowpoke had yawned and brought down rain, ending a long drought. Because of that, Slowpoke held a special place in the hearts of the townspeople.

When Ethan and Erika entered the small town, they spotted a familiar figure before they could even ask where the Gym was.

Ethan looked more closely. It was Professor Elm from New Bark Town!

Professor Elm had seen Ethan too. His eyes lit up, and he waved.

"I never expected to run into you here!"

"Professor, what brings you here?"

They spoke almost at the same time. Their voices overlapped, and after exchanging a glance, they both burst out laughing.

Chapter 491: The Monkey Professor

After they finished laughing, Professor Elm said, "I came here at someone's invitation to help study a certain Poke Ball."

He noticed Ethan's travel-worn appearance and smiled. "Let me guess. You're here to challenge the Azalea Gym, aren't you?"

"That's right." Ethan nodded. "I came to challenge Bugsy, the Azalea Gym Leader!"

Professor Elm adjusted his glasses, tracing Ethan's route through Johto in his mind.

"Given where Azalea Town is, you must have made quite a detour to reach it only now. By the way, how many badges have you collected?"

"I have gone a long way around, but I've gained a lot along the way. As for badges, I've just earned my sixth."

"Six..." Professor Elm said thoughtfully. "That's a good pace. As far as I know, many Trainers who set out from New Bark Town have only four or five by now."

Was it really a good pace?

Ethan smiled and shook his head, but did not explain.

If Team Rocket and other matters had not interrupted him, and he had focused only on challenging Gyms, he would have collected all eight badges long ago.

But he would not have trained his Pokemon as well, or enjoyed the journey nearly as much.

Professor Elm noticed Erika beside him. "And who is this young lady?"

"Let me introduce you." Ethan stepped back to give them room. "This is Erika, the Celadon Gym Leader from Kanto. She's traveling with me now. Erika, this is Professor Elm, one of Johto's leading Pokemon researchers and a former student of Professor Oak!"

Erika greeted him with a graceful bow. Her bearing spoke for itself.

"It's a pleasure to meet you, Professor."

"And you, Miss Erika."

After they had exchanged greetings, Ethan asked, "Professor, that Poke Ball you said you were studying...?"

"It's a remarkable Poke Ball. A Trainer brought it all the way here from Kanto. No one has found a way to open it, so I was invited to study it with them. Since you're here, why don't you come and see it? As a champion, you might be able to help us!"

At Professor Elm's description, Ethan already had a guess.

A mysterious Poke Ball carried from Kanto all the way to Azalea Town could only be the GS Ball! Ash had brought it back from the Orange Islands to Professor Oak's laboratory, and it had then been sent here.

After all this time, they still had not figured it out!

Hmm...

They had nothing pressing to do, and the Gym challenge could wait. Ethan and Erika exchanged a glance, agreed to go with Professor Elm, and followed him toward the western side of town.

Azalea Town was neither large nor bustling. Its streets were nearly empty, with only the occasional passerby. Life seemed to move slowly here.

In truth, most small cities and towns in Kanto and Johto were like this, outside the busy major cities.

As they walked, they saw Slowpoke everywhere. The Pokemon lazed in the sun under trees, on walls and rooftops, and in the streets. Signs reading "Watch Out for Slowpoke" stood all around town!

The townspeople were entirely accustomed to them and lived alongside them in harmony. Even when Slowpoke openly ate fruit from a vendor's stall, the owner paid them no mind.

"Amazing, isn't it?" Professor Elm said. "People here hold Slowpoke in special reverence. Some even regard them as gods!"

"Because of the rain four hundred years ago?" Erika asked.

"Exactly. That rain saved the land and many lives. Slowpoke have been cherished here ever since. Harming one is forbidden, and anyone who does may even be taken to the police station!"

Professor Elm nodded, then gave them an approving look. "You even know that story? You must have done your homework before coming here!"

"Of course. You have to be prepared!" Ethan said. A moment later, he wiped sweat from his forehead and glanced up at the sun. "Speaking of which, it really is hot here."

"It is," Professor Elm agreed with a sigh. "The sun is fierce, and mountains surround the town on three sides. The cool, damp sea breeze can't reach it, which makes the heat worse."

"I see." Ethan understood. "No wonder there was such a terrible drought four hundred years ago."

They passed a Slowpoke lying across the middle of the road. Erika glanced at Ethan and asked quietly, "With so many Slowpoke here, you could catch one easily. Don't you want to?"

Ethan shook his head.

"No. I'm not interested in this species. Besides, if I caught one here, the townspeople would chase me through the streets. It wouldn't be worth the trouble."

The mention of Slowpoke made him think of the Slowking he had caught in the Orange Islands, and then of Sabrina.

What was Sabrina doing at the Saffron Gym right now?

As they chatted, the three crossed most of Azalea Town and reached its northwest corner.

Professor Elm stopped in front of a large, old-fashioned house. "Here we are. This is Kurt's home."

He knocked. Before long, a little girl opened the gate and peered out.

She was only four or five, with her hair tied into two curled pigtails. She looked like someone who took herself very seriously for her age.

"Who are you looking for?" she asked in a clear voice.

"Hello." Professor Elm stepped forward with a kindly smile. "I'm Professor Elm. Mr. Kurt invited me."

"Oh! I know you!" Recognition lit up the little girl's face. "Grandpa told me that if a professor with glasses who looks like a monkey came by, I should let him straight in!"

Professor Elm fell silent.

Ethan and Erika struggled not to laugh. Out of consideration for the professor, neither made a sound.

She called him a monkey...

In fact, when Ethan had first met Professor Elm, his thin frame and the peculiar shape of his hair had given him much the same impression.

"So you're Mr. Kurt's granddaughter..." Professor Elm managed an awkward smile. "How... lively and adorable you are."

Chapter 492: The GS Ball

"Grandpa, that monkey professor you told me about is here!"

As the little girl led them through the courtyard, she called loudly toward the main house, paying no attention to Professor Elm's bright red face behind her.

"You little fool!"

An old man hurried out of the house at her shout. "Don't say things like that in front of people!"

"Huh?" The girl blinked up at him in innocent confusion. "But... aren't you the one who called him that?"

"Ahem..."

The old man choked and rushed forward to cover her mouth. He gave Professor Elm an embarrassed smile. "Sorry, Elm. This is my granddaughter, Maizie. She's too young to know any better and says all sorts of nonsense. Please don't mind her."

Professor Elm scratched his cheek and tried to sound unconcerned. "It's... it's all right. It's been a while, Mr. Kurt..."

Perhaps hoping to move past the awkward moment, the old man turned to Ethan and Erika.

"And who are these two?"

Ethan was studying him too.

The old man wore a traditional kimono. His hair was gray-white, his thick black eyebrows tilted slightly upward, and his eyes were bright. His loose skin gave him a stern look.

Any child who happened to pass him would probably be so frightened by that face that they would hardly dare breathe!

"I asked them to help us study the GS Ball," Professor Elm said. "This is Ethan, the champion of this year's Indigo League, and the young lady beside him is the Celadon Gym Leader from Kanto."

"Oh?" The old man looked them over. "Impressive people. I'm surprised you managed to invite them."

Professor Elm hurriedly shook his head. "You've misunderstood. I didn't arrange for them to come. We met by chance."

He then introduced Kurt to Ethan and Erika.

"This is Mr. Kurt. He's retired now, but he's still a renowned master of handmade Poke Balls!"

He makes Poke Balls?

No wonder Professor Oak had sent the GS Ball to him.

"So you're Ethan!" Recognition dawned on Kurt's face. "My son told me about you. Since you're from Kanto, you must know Professor Oak."

Ethan nodded. "Professor Oak is a respected elder I trust. I've been fortunate enough to know him, and he's helped me several times."

Kurt laughed. "I've known him since we were young. Does he still recite those embarrassing senryu poems? And Agathawe go back a long way too!"

Those shared connections made the group feel much less like strangers.

Ethan still found Kurt's name peculiar. It sounded like a nickname, yet it was his real name!

"You mentioned your son. Who is he?"

"He works at Silph Co.," Kurt said. "A fool who only knows how to make Poke Balls with modern technology. When Team Rocket attacked their headquarters, he said you saved them."

That brought them even closer.

Kurt invited them into the main house. Maizie served them hot tea, then sat quietly to one side.

She kept glancing at Erika. The beautiful woman kneeling beside the older boy looked lovely no matter how Maizie looked at her!

Every movement Erika made was graceful and pleasing to watch. She was just like the well-bred ladies Grandpa was always talking about.

It was a pity that Maizie could never seem to live up to what he hoped for, no matter what she did.

Kurt brought over a red cushion. Resting on it was an unusual Poke Ball, half gold and half white.

"This is the GS Ball," he said with a sigh.

At his words, Kurt and Erika leaned forward slightly to examine it more closely.

It was Ethan's first time seeing the GS Ball too, but he already knew its secret, so it did not stir much curiosity in him.

He glanced at it twice, saw that it matched what he remembered, and looked away. Then he took a small sip of tea.

Ah! Hot!

He set down the cup and turned toward the courtyard. A huge Apricorn tree grew there, its branches full of round fruit.

Those Apricorns were used to make Poke Balls. With heating, hammering, cooling, and other steps, followed by special finishing techniques, a craftsman could turn one into a handmade Poke Ball.

Even now, many older people still usedand trusted onlythese Apricorn Balls, unlike most young people.

From that perspective, Kurt's son had strayed far from the family craft by joining Silph Co. instead of learning to make them!

Professor Elm and Kurt began discussing the ball, drawing Ethan's attention back to the room.

Elm turned the GS Ball over and over in his hands, frowning. He could make nothing of it.

"I heard this ball can't be transferred by machine?"

"That's right," Kurt said. "That puzzles me too. Usually only old-fashioned, handmade Poke Balls can't pass through modern transfer machines."

Professor Elm raised his brows. "Yet its materials don't appear to be handmade. I'm sorry, Mr. Kurt, but I can't tell anything more just by looking. We'll have to examine it with instruments."

Kurt was a little disappointed, though he still held out hope.

"Sigh... We can't open it, and it doesn't react to Pokemon at all. If we knew who made it, we might solve everything. But neither Oak nor Ivy, who discovered it, knows where it came from. They could only name it after the letters 'GS' on its surface."

Professor Elm looked surprised. "Even you can't tell who made it?"

Kurt shook his head. "I'm hardly the only craftsman in the world. Plenty of little-known people are remarkably skilled and use all sorts of strange materials. Without a maker's mark, there's no way to identify them."

When both men fell silent, Ethan gave a small cough. "Actually, I heard a rumor about a special Poke Ball while I was traveling."

Every eye in the room turned to him.

Ethan spoke slowly. "Someone once told me of a unique ball made with a capture net woven from a Rainbow Wing and a Silver Wing. It was crafted specifically to catch an exceptionally rare Legendary Pokemon!"

Chapter 493: A Ball to Catch Time

"A Rainbow Wing and a Silver Wing?"

Kurt frowned at the names. As a master Poke Ball maker, he knew exactly what they were.

Professor Elm and Erika knew less, but their knowledge still gave them a fair idea of where the feathers came from.

Only young Maizie looked to her grandfather in confusion.

"Grandpa, what are those? Are they a Pokemon's feathers?"

Erika liked the girl's innocent, open manner. She answered in Kurt's place. "A Rainbow Wing is a feather from Ho-Oh. A Silver Wing comes from Lugia, the God of the Sea. Both are Legendary Pokemon, so even their feathers hold extraordinary power."

"Ho-Oh... Lugia..."

Maizie murmured the familiar names, her eyes full of longing as her thoughts drifted away.

She had grown up in Johto hearing stories about those Legendary Pokemon and knew how deeply people here revered them.

A Poke Ball made from their feathers must be extraordinary!

Kurt and Professor Elm were far less carefree.

Rare and precious materials did not necessarily make a good Poke Ball. The materials also had to work together. If they clashed, the ball might fail to function even if it could be made at all, and it could pose a safety risk.

Kurt sighed. "One feather represents Ho-Oh's fire, the other Lugia's sea. They're opposing forces. Whoever managed to combine them must be an exceptionally skilled craftsman."

There was one thing he kept to himself: for all his reputation as a master of handmade Poke Balls, he could not have made a ball like this.

Professor Elm turned to Ethan. "Is the ball you heard about this GS Ball?"

Ethan did not answer directly. "I heard that ball has two letters on it. One stands for gold, and the other for silver."

Professor Elm and Kurt looked at the GS Ball again, their eyes resting on its two letters.

It did seem to be the very ball Ethan meant!

"Gold... silver..." Kurt pondered. "But why? Are those the maker's initials, or do they describe the materials?"

Ethan shook his head without committing himself.

He could hardly tell them that the letters referred to the Gold and Silver versions of a game, or that they themselves were characters in games and an animated series!

Professor Elm frowned. "Why go to such lengths to make a single Poke Ball?"

"To catch a powerful Pokemon, of course," Kurt said. "Isn't that why humans make Poke Balls? But Ho-Oh and Lugia stand at the very peak of Pokemon. Obtaining their feathers would already be difficult. What Pokemon could be worth all this effort?"

Professor Elm noticed Ethan's silence and had a sudden thought. "You already have an answer in mind, don't you?"

Ethan nodded. "It's a ball meant to catch time."

"Catch time!?" Kurt and Professor Elm exclaimed together.

"Yes," Ethan explained. "It uses the feathers of two Legendary Pokemon to capture a Pokemon with power over time."

Everyone present except Maizie knew enough about Pokemon to realize which one he meant.

"Celebi..."

Maizie looked from face to face, then asked the beautiful older woman, "What is Celebi?"

Erika gathered what she knew before answering. "Celebi is a Mythical Pokemon. It's said to travel through time and wander from place to place. People also call it the God of the Forest. It can heal wounds and make plants grow thick and strong."

"A Mythical Pokemon?"

Maizie caught on to the unfamiliar term and looked up, her little eyes full of questions.

At her age, she still knew very little of the world. She had heard of Legendary Pokemon, but never of Mythical Pokemon.

Professor Elm nodded. "Mythical Pokemon are extremely rare. Sometimes they're spoken of alongside Legendary Pokemon as a separate group; sometimes they're included among them."

His words left the room heavy with thought once more.

Who would make a ball like this to capture a god of time?

After a long silence, Kurt sighed. "That... makes things rather difficult."

The others turned to him.

Kurt gave a bitter smile. "If it were an ordinary Poke Ball, we could just set it aside if we couldn't understand it. But if the GS Ball has such a history, there could be trouble when people learn about it!"

Professor Elm fell silent.

He was right. Once word spread that such a Poke Ball existed, some people would surely want it for themselves. If someone like that came here...

Elm hesitated. "Perhaps... we should give it to the police."

Kurt shook his head.

The police?

He had lived long enough to know how ugly the world could be. If they handed the GS Ball over, a word from someone in power might have it delivered straight to them.

As soon as he made the suggestion, Professor Elm realized the same thing and sighed inwardly.

Yet keeping it at Kurt's house would bring danger to Kurt.

Even if everyone here kept the secret, the ball had already passed through many hands. Anyone who looked into its trail could discover where it was now.

What a problem...

Elm glanced at Kurt. His face was troubled too; clearly, he had reached the same conclusion.

With a sigh, Elm shook his head. Then his gaze happened to pass over Ethan, and an idea struck him.

"Mr. Kurt, I have a favor to ask..."

"Oh?" Kurt looked at him. "Go ahead, Elm. What is it?"

"Now that we know where it came from, further study may not be necessary. And it isn't safe to keep a ball like this here. I think we should entrust it to the person best suited to guard it."

Kurt had lived long enough to understand Professor Elm's meaning at once.

He followed Elm's gaze, and his eyes came to rest on Ethan.

Chapter 494: An Unexpected Windfall

As the conversation went on, both men's eyes came to rest on Ethan. He raised his brows.

Kurt considered for a moment, then nodded to Professor Elm. "You're right. Keeping the GS Ball here may not be wise."

By now, Ethan could hardly fail to understand what they meant.

They're going to give it to me?

Before he could speak, Kurt continued, "Now that we know what the GS Ball was made for, there's no real need to study it further. It does no good sitting with me."

He turned to Ethan and said solemnly, "So I'm giving this Poke Ball to you."

"I'm not sure I should accept..." Ethan slowly shook his head. "I can't take something so valuable."

Kurt smiled, picked up the GS Ball, and placed it directly in Ethan's hand.

"I'm only a craftsman. I can't protect this Poke Ball. The fact that you came here with Elm tells me he trusts your character. And winning the Indigo League proves what you're capable of. I can feel at ease leaving it with you."

"But..."

Ethan certainly wanted the GS Ball. Still, he had only just met Kurt. They were neither friends nor family; how could he accept such a gift without feeling awkward?

He looked to Professor Elm.

Elm met his gaze with a smile and nodded.

"Mr. Kurt is right. Take it. Neither of us is a Trainer or a collector. The GS Ball has no use sitting with us. It belongs in the hands of a Trainer like you, where it can serve its purpose!"

And what was a Poke Ball's purpose?

To catch Pokemon, of course!

Erika, too, watched Ethan encouragingly.

In the past, she would not have wanted a Poke Ball capable of catching a Legendary Pokemon to fall into a Trainer's hands. Now, though...

"Since Mr. Kurt and Professor Elm both agree, you should take it," she said softly.

Ethan glanced at her. He stopped protesting and accepted the GS Ball.

"Thank you, Mr. Kurt."

Professor Ivy had first found the ball in the Orange Islands. Ash had carried it to Professor Oak, and from Oak it had gone to Professor Elm. Ethan had never expected it to end up in his own hands.

After all those twists and turns, he was the one who benefited!

With a worry lifted from his shoulders, Kurt smiled in relief.

He arranged dinner and treated Professor Elm, Ethan, and Erika as honored guests.

Ethan had hoped to challenge the Azalea Gym while there was still daylight. But Kurt's hospitality was hard to refuse, and after receiving such a valuable Poke Ball, he wanted to thank the man properly.

That evening, drinks passed around the dinner table. With frank, adorable little Maizie there too, the mood was cheerful.

Kurt drank plenty. He even coaxed Professor Elm, who could not hold his liquor, into drinking enough to get thoroughly drunk.

After dinner, Kurt would not let his guests leave. He arranged for them to spend the night in his house.

Perhaps mistaking Ethan and Erika for a couple, Kurt's daughter-in-law did not even ask. She assigned them the same room!

When they came out of the bath and saw two futons laid close together on the tatami, they froze and looked at each other.

Outside, the moon hung high. After the noise of dinner, the house was quiet.

"This..." Ethan, dressed in a bathrobe, scratched his head. "Should we ask them for another room? Or I could sleep in Professor Elm's room..."

Erika's cheeks were faintly red. Perhaps it was the few drinks she had had with dinner, or perhaps something else.

She drew a breath. "Let's not. It's late, and I don't want to trouble them. When you're traveling, you can't insist on everything being just so."

Traveling? We're guests in someone's house!

But Ethan thought she had a point. Kurt and his family were already asleep, and it would be rude to disturb them so late.

Besides, he and Erika had faced situations like this more than once or twice. There was no reason to be embarrassed. During the Whirl Cup, they had even stayed in the same suite.

That suite had had two separate rooms, though. Now they were sharing one!

If they slept here like this, wouldn't everyone else take it as proof that they were a couple?

But the two of them...

While his thoughts circled, Erika went inside and began arranging her belongings. Then she moved their futons a little farther apart.

Well... not much farther. They went from nearly touching to about half a meter apart.

What difference would that make?

Perhaps embarrassed, Erika said as soon as she had finished, "It's late, and we have the Gym challenge tomorrow. We should get some sleep."

Without looking at Ethan, she slipped under her covers. All he could see was the faint outline of her graceful figure beneath the bedding.

Ethan sighed at the sight.

Erika was not a casual woman. She was a young lady from a good family, traditional in her habits and values.

She might be lively and playful in her youth, but at heart she was the very image of a refined, traditional woman.

And now she was willing to...

Ethan shook his head and pushed the thought away. He went into the room.

If Erika said she did not mind, what was he hesitating over?

He turned off the light and slid into his own futon.

Moonlight shone through the glass onto Erika, keeping the room from going completely dark.

Despite the drinks, Ethan tossed and turned. With Erika so close, he could not sleep.

He turned toward her. From where he lay, he could see only her hair and the little patch of pale neck showing above her covers.

Was she asleep?

She lay still and seemed to breathe evenly, but he suspected she was just as awake as he was.

The room was quiet except for their breathing.

Ethan found himself remembering all the time he had spent with Erika. Anyone could see that she had feelings for him beyond friendship. He had felt it himself.

That was no baseless confidence. Their experiences together had made it clear!

In their everyday glances and gestures, they were hardly acting like two people with nothing between them.

He was certain Erika understood how he felt, too.

For now, they were both holding those feelings back.

For an ordinary man and woman who had been through so much together, growing closer day by day, sharing a room like this would have been the natural next step.

Tonight might even have been the perfect chance to define their relationship!

But...

Sabrina came to mind, and Ethan sighed.

He had a girlfriend. How could he betray Sabrina's feelings?

Then he thought of the night he had spent with Maya and sighed again.

Ah. I'd almost forgotten. I already betrayed her once...

Chapter 495: A Detour to Charicific Valley

Lost in his thoughts, Ethan drifted off without knowing when he had fallen asleep.

When he woke, daylight filled the room. Erika's futon had been folded neatly beside his, but she was gone.

He rubbed his eyes. He had just finished dressing when Erika opened the door and came in.

Her white socks made soft tapping sounds on the tatami. She looked at him and said quietly, "You're awake? Mr. Kurt has breakfast ready. He asked me to come get you."

Erika looked as bright and beautiful as ever.

"Did you sleep well last night?" Ethan asked.

Her cheeks reddened slightly. Like Ethan, she had tossed and turned for a long time, torn between shyness and uncertainty. Only after hearing his breathing settle into sleep had she relaxed enough to drift off herself.

"Quite well. It was more restful than sleeping outdoors."

That much was true. A Pokemon Center, guesthouse, hotel, or campsite could not match the warmth of a home. Even as guests staying under someone else's roof, they had woken with much of their fatigue gone.

After Ethan washed up, they went to the dining room for breakfast. Professor Elm, whether because he had drunk too much or for some other reason, was still asleep with a hangover.

Ethan and Kurt ate and talked, chatting about all sorts of things. They drank morning tea too. The sun climbed higher, yet Professor Elm still showed no sign of waking. Ethan asked Kurt to say goodbye to the professor for him, then left the house with Erika while Kurt and Maizie saw them off.

Once they had turned out of the street and Kurt's home was out of sight, Ethan shook his head, lost in thought.

Erika noticed his expression. "What's wrong?"

Ethan sighed. "Meeting Professor Elm in Azalea Town was a pleasant surprise. I never expected to receive a Poke Ball this valuable too. I'm happy, but I also feel as though I owe someone a huge favor."

"Don't worry about it so much." Erika smiled. "As Mr. Kurt said, that Poke Ball was like a ticking time bomb in his house. He never knew when someone might come looking for it. Giving it to you removed the danger. If anything, he should thank you!"

Her words lightened Ethan's mood.

"You always know how to make someone feel better..."

"Not really." Erika blushed faintly. "I'm only telling the truth."

As they spoke, they reached the Azalea Gym. It stood on open land outside town, surrounded by green grass. The sprawling arched building looked less like a Gym than a botanical garden.

Bugsy, the Azalea Gym Leader, specialized in Bug-type Pokemon. Defeating him would earn Ethan the Hive Badge.

Ethan had settled on a strategy during the walk and even chosen the Pokemon he would send out. But as he approached the entrance with eager anticipation, he found the doors shut and a notice posted on them.

Hm?

He read it quickly, surprised by what it said.

Bugsy was not at the Gym. Early that morning, he had gone to a more distant forest to catch Pokemon. He had left a message asking challengers to wait a few days, as he would be gone at least that long.

"Well..." Erika frowned at the notice. "I didn't expect that."

She turned to Ethan. "What should we do? It looks like Bugsy won't be back for days."

Ethan frowned too. Their matching expressions made them look rather like a married couple.

"Sigh. If only we'd challenged him yesterday."

Erika hesitated. "Should we go looking for him?"

Ethan shook his head. "We don't know where he went. With so many forests nearby, finding him would be like looking for a needle in a haystack."

He took out his phone, opened the map, and studied it.

Erika leaned in. They both stared at the map in silence.

Bugsy's absence had caught Ethan off guard, but it was understandable. Gym Leaders had to train and catch new Pokemon from time to time if they wanted to keep improving and stay current.

Still, it meant a delay for Ethan.

His gaze moved over the map. Azalea Town was not far from Goldenrod City, but a round trip there would take more than three days. They might as well stay in the area.

But if they did not go to Goldenrod, where could they go?

His eyes passed over one spot, and an idea slowly brightened his face.

"Let's go here!"

Erika followed his finger. He was pointing to a valley among the mountains, between Azalea Town and Violet City. She read its name.

"Charicific Valley?"

Ethan nodded and smiled. "I've heard the Charizard there are very strong. I wonder how they compare with mine. This is a good chance to find out."

Erika had no objection. In truth, she would gladly go wherever Ethan went. The distance and difficulty of the journey made little difference to her.

With a new destination in mind, they gathered their spirits, changed direction, and set out for Charicific Valley.

The valley was a natural park among towering mountains. Because its terrain was treacherous and many fierce Charizard lived there, ordinary visitors were usually barred for their own safety.

Of course, Trainers had a way of reaching places others could not.

They left Azalea Town and headed north. After half a day's walking, the land gradually rose, the trees and other plants thinned out, and a long mountain range appeared on the horizon.

The mountains looked close, but distances were deceiving. Reaching them on foot would take much longer than it seemed.

Fortunately, the two had time to spare. They walked at an easy pace, stopping now and then to admire the scenery and enjoy the change of mood.

They finally reached the foot of the mountains after dark. Entering the mountains at night would add unnecessary danger.

After discussing it, they decided to pitch their tent at the foot of the mountains and set out again in the morning.

Chapter 496: Liza

Early the next morning, after a simple breakfast, Ethan and Erika entered the unfamiliar mountains with Gardevoir, Scyther, Eevee, and Erika's Leafeon beside them.

Although they had reached the mountains, Charicific Valley lay deep within the range. They still had a long way to walk.

At first, they followed a broad mountain path. After circling the first two peaks, however, it grew narrow and rough. The trail climbed steeply, with sheer cliffs below. One careless step could send them slipping over the edge.

Bare boulders lay everywhere they looked, with hardly any plants among them. Even the view alone made the terrain look dangerous.

That was why they had brought their Pokemon out. If anything went wrong, the Pokemon could keep them safe.

Why not bring out Charizard or Dragonite to fly them straight to the top? As Ethan had said before, climbing a mountain like this was training for him and Erika as well as for their Pokemon.

Ethan crossed a high natural stone bridge first. He looked back, saw Erika picking her way along, and reached out a hand.

"Be careful. The stones can come loose here, so watch your step."

Erika smiled. Without hesitation, she took his hand, and he gently helped her across.

Once she was standing safely, they let go of each other by unspoken agreement, as if nothing had happened.

Their feelings remained unspoken, though both understood them. Deep down, each wanted to be closer to the other.

Holding hands was only a small moment along the way. They continued walking, and as they went deeper into the mountains, Ethan checked the map on his phone against their surroundings to make sure they did not lose their way.

They crossed another low peak and were about to stop for a rest when a woman's voice sounded above them.

"You two down there! You've got Pokemon with you, so I take it you're not ordinary hikers. Are you Trainers?"

They looked up. A woman stood on a boulder overhead, studying them from above!

She looked about twenty-three or twenty-four, perhaps younger. Her thick green hair was pulled into a messy high ponytail. She wore tall red boots, a very short skirt, and a top that left her midriff bare. In one hand she held an odd staff shaped a little like a sword. She had a distinctly rebellious look.

She stood so high that, from Ethan's angle, he could see under her skirt...

He swore he had not meant to look. It was pure chance!

Clearing his throat, Ethan hurriedly looked away. "Uh... who are you?"

The woman laughed and jumped down from the height!

She spun in the air, landed on a lower rock, then sprang to another. After several nimble leaps to break her fall, she landed safely in front of Ethan.

Her quick, fluid movements were nearly a match for Aya the ninja.

Before Ethan could say anything else, she leaned close and sniffed him vigorously.

Erika frowned at once.

"Hee-hee..." The woman straightened and smiled at Ethan. "I can smell something familiar on you. You have a Charizard too, don't you?"

She can tell by smell?

Does she have a dog's nose?

Ethan nodded. "Yes, I do have a Charizard."

Up close, she was quite pretty. Two bright gold earrings caught the light. Her muscles were firm, perhaps from years of training, and together with her hairstyle they gave her a wild air.

At his answer, she looked pleased with herself. "Hah! My nose can always tell when someone has a Charizard. I haven't introduced myself yet. I'm Liza, a Charizard Trainer!"

Liza?

So it was her...

Ethan remembered that a woman Trainer lived in Charicific Valley. Her formidable Charizard had once given Ash a great deal of trouble.

He had wondered before entering the mountains whether he might meet her. Now he had!

He nodded in greeting. "I'm Ethan, and this is Erika."

"So you're Ethan!" Liza exclaimed at his name. "Clair told me about you. She said you have a very strong Charizard. I've wanted to meet you for ages, and here you are!"

"Oh?" Ethan raised his brows. "You know Clair?"

"Of course. We're very close friends. I visit her whenever I can, and she often comes to see me."

As they talked, Erika cast Ethan a discreet glance.

She wanted to ask who Clair was.

And Liza had wanted to meet him for ages?

Erika also noticed that Liza had not called herself a Fire-type Trainer. She had said only that she was a Charizard Trainer.

Did she have nothing but Charizard?

Remembering the valley's name, Erika began to understand.

Before Ethan could ask another question, Liza said excitedly, "If you don't mind, would you like to come with me to Charicific Valley?"

Ethan and Erika exchanged a look. They had only just met her, but both could tell that Liza made friends easily.

"Of course." Ethan turned back to her and nodded. "Charicific Valley is why we came here."

"It is?" Liza asked in surprise. "I thought you were just passing through. Is there something you need there?"

"I've heard that the Charizard in the valley are all very strong. I came to train mine and see how it measures up."

"I see!" Liza laughed. "Then you've come to the right place. The valley's Charizard may be wild, but every one of them is strong! And did you know that another Trainer left his Charizard here not long ago?"

She must mean Ash...

His Charizard had no longer been with him the last time Ethan saw him. Given the timing, it made sense that it was here now.

Chapter 497: Charla

Liza gave a loud whistle. As it echoed through the mountains, a Charizard flew toward them from afar.

It circled overhead several times, then dove and landed neatly beside her.

Liza patted its shoulder and smiled at her visitors. "This is my Charizard, Charla. Charla, say hello!"

Charla politely nodded to Ethan and Erika.

Ethan looked up at the Charizard. A pink bow sat on its head, and its name made it clear that it was female.

A small balloon and gondola were tied behind her by long ropes. The gondola was full of groceries, vegetables, and other everyday supplies. Liza must have just returned from shopping in town when she met them.

Still...

The sight reminded Ethan of a Charizard far across the sea in Alola that spent its days delivering milk from morning to night.

Different regions, but the same lot in life...

Liza climbed onto Charla's back and looked over her shoulder. "Come on, follow me! Would you rather ride in my gondola or on your own Charizard?"

Ethan glanced at the gondola.

Groceries already filled half of it. If both he and Erika climbed in, they would be cramped.

Besides, he had a Pokemon of his own. There was no reason to squeeze in among the supplies.

"Thanks, but I'll ride my Charizard."

Ethan recalled the Pokemon he had brought out for the hike, then took Charizard's Poke Ball from his waist pouch and released it.

Blue light flashed, and his Charizard appeared before Liza.

She examined it closely from head to tail, then nodded.

"You've raised this Charizard well. It's large too. It can hold its own beside an average wild Charizard from the valley!"

Comparing a Trainer's carefully raised, battle-tested Pokemon to a wild one might sound strange, but Ethan knew the Charizard of this valley were all exceptionally strong. They could not be judged by ordinary standards.

After Erika recalled her Leafeon, Ethan helped her onto Charizard's back. He then sprang up and took the seat in front of her.

Liza's eyes brightened at the sight.

A Charizard allowing its own Trainer to ride was nothing unusual. Allowing someone else to ride along was much rarer!

Given how proud Charizard tended to be, that was no small thing.

"Your Charizard trusts and obeys you completely," she said admiringly. "That's impressive!"

Something seemed to occur to her, and she chuckled. "Another Trainer came here before you. His Charizard wasn't nearly so obedient."

Ethan glanced at her. "You mean Ash, don't you?"

Liza was surprised that he knew the name. "Oh? You know him?"

"Of course. We're good friends, and we saw each other just a few days ago!" Ethan nudged Charizard gently with his feet. It took to the air at once.

The two Charizard climbed together. From high above, Ethan could finally see most of the broad mountain range spread out beneath them.

It really is vast.

Liza guided Charla alongside Ethan.

"Charicific Valley is up ahead, but we'll still have to fly for a while," she called. "How about a race?"

The wind forced her to raise her voice so Ethan could hear.

"A race?"

Liza nodded. "The terrain here is tricky. Let's see whether your Charizard can keep up with Charla!"

So that was it. Liza wanted to test him.

She was Clair's friend and had heard Clair praise him. Naturally, she wanted to see for herself how good his Charizard was.

"All right."

At his agreement, Liza's expression sharpened. "Then stay close!"

At her signal, Charla shot forward like an arrow from a bow.

She really is an impatient one...

Ethan's Charizard had heard their exchange and was eager to try. At his command, it hurried after Charla!

One behind the other, the two Pokemon dove between the mountains. The wind at that speed whipped Erika's hair about. She had to close her eyes and wrap both arms tightly around Ethan's waist to keep from being thrown backward.

Her body pressed against his back, and Ethan could feel her curves all too clearly!

She was holding him very tightly.

But this was no time to think about that!

Charla knew the terrain. She flew without hesitation, sometimes clearing a boulder and immediately making a sharp ninety-degree turn.

Each time, Ethan's Charizard had to slow down and steer carefully around the bend before catching up again.

They flew past stone bridges, skimmed over a river, and passed through a rocky tunnel. For all Charla's speed and effort, she could not shake her pursuer.

Liza looked back at Ethan, privately impressed.

He's hard to lose!

No wonder Clair, a Gym Leader from the dragon clan, had spoken so highly of him!

As the two Charizard cleared the mountains, the view suddenly opened. Charla began to slow.

In that instant, Ethan's Charizard accelerated and drew level with her again.

"Not bad!" Liza called. "Keeping pace with Charla proves your Charizard is well trained!"

She turned to face forward. "Here we are. This is Charicific Valley."

Ethan and Erika looked ahead. A broad, clear river flowed between the mountains below them. High cliffs rose on both sides, forming a vast valley.

Dozens of enormous Charizard statues carved from stone stood in the river!

They stared ahead with wings spread wide, solemn and imposing, as though judging the challengers bold enough to come here.

Chapter 498: Charicific Valley

At the far end of the long river stood a majestic mountain. A long flight of stone steps had been built at its foot, leading up to an enormous gate.

The gate stood four or five meters high. Its stone had a faint blue-green sheen, and it looked heavy enough to weigh thousands of pounds. Two huge Charizard statues stood on either side. Facing each other with their claws clasped, they looked as though they were testing each other's strength, or perhaps symbolizing friendship.

The two flying Charizard landed steadily in front of it.

Liza dismounted Charla, walked to the gate, and smiled back at them.

"Welcome to Charicific Valley."

She pressed a button on a remote control, and the massive stone doors slowly slid apart.

Well, would you look at that. They're electric!

Beyond the gate lay a vast green basin. Dozens of Charizard rested, soared, battled, or ate Berries throughout it.

Ethan helped Erika down from his Charizard. At the sight, she could not help saying, "There are... so many Charizard..."

Ethan nodded. It was an impressive sight.

He had seen wild Charizard before, but never so many together. Orange bodies filled the valley in every direction, enough to make his eyes swim.

At the sound of the gate opening, all the nearby Charizard turned to look at them.

These Charizard were large and powerfully built. Some bore permanent scars that made them look fierce. Their cold stares would put pressure on anyone, and even Ethan felt his brow twitch.

They were trying to intimidate him as soon as he arrived!

Liza led them into the valley.

"The Charizard here grow stronger without relying on humans," she explained as they walked. "They compete with one another, spar with their companions, and train on their own. Each wants to become the strongest Charizard in the valley!"

She glanced at Ethan's Charizard. "If you came to train yours, let it battle them. But I should warn you: an ordinary Charizard can't beat the ones here!"

Ethan nodded. Having seen the animated series, he knew these Charizard were far from ordinary.

In game terms, though they were wild, their levels would be high. If a newly evolved Charizard was around level thirty-six, these might be around level seventy.

That was an overwhelming difference.

They owed their strength partly to daily battles and training, just as Liza said. Time was another advantage.

A Trainer's Pokemon might evolve after gaining enough strength or through the influence of an Evolution stone. The Charizard here had spent years building their strength little by little before evolving. They had a far more solid foundation than ordinary members of the species.

Most were in their prime, not newly evolved youngsters. Dealing with the young Pokemon that accompanied many Trainers would hardly trouble them.

Ethan saw his Charizard eager for a battle and was about to choose an opponent when a relatively thin Charizard caught his eye.

It was noticeably smaller than the others. Alone in a corner, it held a large stone and repeatedly lowered itself into squats.

No other Charizard stood within dozens of meters of it. It was clearly isolated.

Ethan had a thought. "That's Ash's Charizard, isn't it?"

Liza needed only one glance to confirm it. "Yes, that's Ash's. That one works so hard. It's been here more than twenty days, and every day it challenges the other Charizard and trains with everything it has!"

Ethan sighed inwardly.

Ash's early ace was now the weakest Charizard here. That was a startling reversal.

How would Ethan's own Charizard compare with the wild ones?

Ash's Charizard noticed Ethan's. Its eyes flickered, but it did nothing more and lowered its head to continue training.

Just as Ash viewed Ethan as his greatest rival, his Charizard naturally regarded Ethan's Charizard as its own rival.

Seeing that rival arrive here only sharpened its sense of urgency.

By then, the group had walked into the heart of the valley.

The wild Charizard nearby had heard enough of Ethan's conversation with Liza to understand why he had come. One after another, they puffed out their chests and eyed his Charizard sidelong.

They had taught one overconfident newcomer a lesson not long ago. Now another had turned up!

Ethan was quietly relieved that he had raised his Charizard well. It was not quite as imposing as these sturdy wild Charizard, but the gap was nowhere near as great as it had been for Ash's.

As for which one to challenge...

He looked left and right. None of them appeared easy to beat.

Unable to decide, he left the choice to his Pokemon.

"Charizard, pick an opponent for yourself."

Charizard nodded and walked toward the most heavily built Charizard in the valley.

Ethan coughed and hurried in front of it.

"You..." he said with an exasperated laugh. "I told you to choose, but you need to know your limits! Why pick the strongest one for your first match?"

Charizard tilted its head, apparently confused. Ethan knew how careless it could be and sighed.

"Even if you're confident, start with a safer match. Choose a relatively weaker opponent. That'll let you get used to how they fight and give us an idea of how strong they are."

Charizard seemed to understand. Ethan added, "And I won't interfere in any of your battles here. You'll have to handle everything yourself, so don't let your guard down!"

Chapter 499: The Strongest Charizard

After Ethan talked it out of challenging the strongest Charizard, his Charizard chose another opponent.

This one looked unremarkable. It was about the same size as Ethan's Charizard, did not stand out among the others, and was not as muscular as some. It seemed fairly young.

Ethan's Charizard crooked a finger at it. That small provocation was enough. The wild Charizard grew restless and strode toward its challenger.

Perhaps they had seen this many times, or perhaps it was simply the valley's custom. Either way, the other wild Charizard moved aside to leave an open space for the fight.

Ethan stepped back to stand with Erika and Liza.

As he had promised, he would not interfere. He intended to watch and leave the battle entirely to his Charizard.

The two Charizard faced one another, their eyes seeming to burn with fire.

A breeze happened to stir the leaves. The instant one green leaf fluttered to the ground, both Charizard lunged.

Orange bodies blurred together. They clasped each other's claws and pushed, the muscles in their arms swelling visibly.

With the same type and moves, sheer strength would decide which was better!

Both faces twisted with effort.

Yet their strength seemed evenly matched. They strained against each other for a long time without either gaining ground!

Refusing to give in, they changed tactics. Each grabbed the other's waist and tried to throw its opponent, but after another long struggle they were still locked in place.

They really are evenly matched...

While the Charizard tried every way they could to bring each other down, Ethan turned to Liza. "Where would this one rank among the Charizard here?"

Liza had said she managed the valley. She knew every Charizard that lived in it.

She thought for a moment. "There are about a hundred Charizard in Charicific Valley. This one ranks somewhere in the lower middle."

The lower middle...

Ethan looked back at the battle.

The two Charizard were rolling together now, bruised and filthy from the dust they had kicked up.

Neither had gained an advantage. Their equal showing gave Ethan a clearer idea of how strong the valley's wild Charizard were.

Becoming the strongest here would take a long time.

Tails lashed, teeth snapped, and claws pulled...

They fought for quite a while longer, but in the end they stopped at a draw.

Ethan's Charizard returned to him panting hard. Even as it caught its breath, it kept staring at its opponent. The two glared at each other, neither willing to admit defeat!

Liza seemed to notice Ethan's dissatisfaction and smiled. "That was a good result. When Ash's Charizard first arrived, it was beaten black and blue. It couldn't even beat my Charla."

Ethan's interest stirred. "And now?"

Liza shrugged. "It still can't beat the other Charizard, but at least it can hold its own against Charla now."

Ethan knew that Charla was different from the valley's wild Charizard. Liza had caught her before she evolved, and she was a Trainer's Pokemon. Here, she ranked near the bottom.

Ash's Charizard could only fight a female Charizard to a draw. No wonder it was training so fiercely by itself in the corner.

It was ashamed!

Nearby, Erika took a spray from the medical kit and quietly cleaned and disinfected the wounds on Ethan's Charizard.

Her thoughtfulness moved him.

No one had asked her to do it. Because she cared about him, she had thought of caring for his Pokemon too.

For the moment, the battle had taken too much out of Charizard. It would not have the strength to challenge another opponent until it recovered.

...

At noon, Liza invited Ethan and Erika into her home.

She had a wooden cabin in the valley. It looked plain from the outside, but inside it was warm and comfortable, with furniture and appliances. She had clearly made it her home.

Lunch was a thick seasonal soup made from seven or eight ingredients. Perhaps because it contained tomatoes, it was red and rather heavy-looking.

It might not have looked appealing, but it smelled wonderful and tasted unexpectedly good!

"Don't be shy. I made a whole pot, so eat as much as you like!"

The soup really was delicious. Ethan had several bowls.

Liza rarely had guests, and she was enthusiastic company. Over lunch she talked at length about life in the valley and listened with equal interest to Ethan's stories from his travels.

She paid close attention even to the smallest incident.

After the meal, while Erika and Liza cleared the dishes, Ethan hesitated, then said, "Miss Liza, there's something I'd like to ask you."

"I know." Liza turned toward him and smiled, as if she had already guessed. "You want to leave your Charizard here too, don't you?"

He had not expected her to know.

"Yes." Ethan nodded. "Now that I've seen this place, I realize there are far stronger Charizard out there and mine still has a lot to learn. I'd like to keep it with me, but I can't give its training all the time it needs. I thought it might grow stronger if it stayed here for a while."

Liza agreed without hesitation.

"Of course! This is a home for Charizard. I'm happy to welcome as many as want to stay."

...

Outside the cabin, Ethan called his Charizard aside and told it about the plan.

At the idea of leaving its Trainer, Charizard immediately shook its head and muttered at length. It clearly wanted to stay by Ethan's side.

"You fool!"

Ethan rapped it hard on the head and gave it a stern look. "I'm not leaving you here forever. Do you think we'll never see each other again? This is a rare opportunity. The Charizard here are strong. Work to beat them all as quickly as you can and become the strongest one in the valley!"

His words made Charizard think of the opponent it had just fought and the others that looked even stronger.

Its eyes grew resolute. It nodded firmly at Ethan, as if promising to meet his expectations!

Chapter 500: Challenging the Azalea Gym

That afternoon, Ethan and Erika walked out of the gate and left Charicific Valley. Another day and night of travel brought them back to Azalea Town.

With Charizard staying behind, Ethan now had ten Pokemon with him: Gardevoir, Gengar, Crystal Steelix, Jolteon, Dragonite, Scyther, Pupitar, Suicune, Raikou, and the Eevee he had received from the Kimono Sisters.

Two open places gave him room to catch more Pokemon in the future.

That did not mean he would catch any Pokemon he came across. He would rather leave those places empty until he found ones he truly liked.

After the long but enjoyable journey, they stood outside the Azalea Gym again on the morning of the third day.

Fortunately, the notice was gone and the doors were open. Bugsy had clearly returned.

Peering inside the round building, they saw something like a botanical garden. Tall trees rose everywhere, with fragrant grass underfoot and shrubs scattered throughout.

From the entrance, Ethan called, "Hello? Is anyone here?"

His voice echoed through the Gym, but no one answered for some time.

He exchanged a look with Erika, then stepped inside.

A narrow path ran through the grass. As they followed it deeper in, they looked around and found that the place was much like an ordinary forest.

To fit a small forest inside a building, the Azalea Gym must have been a huge undertaking. No wonder it stood outside town!

One difference was the number of Bug-type Pokemon hiding therefar more than in most forests.

In only a short walk, they saw a whole crowd of Caterpie, Weedle, Metapod, and Kakuna. The Pokemon hid among shrubs and behind leaves, then poked their heads out when they heard footsteps and watched the newcomers warily.

Erika sighed softly. "It really is a Bug-type Gym. They're everywhere."

The setting was much like the greenhouse at her own Gym, but its Pokemon were entirely different.

Ethan glanced at her and smiled. "As a Grass-type Gym Leader, you must feel uncomfortable surrounded by so many Bug-types."

He was not teasing without reason. Bug-type Pokemon were natural enemies of many Grass-types and had a type advantage over them. A dedicated Grass-type Trainer could hardly avoid feeling that tension.

Erika nodded slightly.

Misty was simply afraid of Bug-type Pokemon. Erika did not like them at all.

They walked a few dozen steps farther into the garden. Then a youthful voice sounded from the side.

"Who are you?"

Ethan and Erika turned. A purple-haired boy in a grass-green shirt and matching shorts was crouching in a thicket a short distance away, watching them.

Ethan stepped forward. "Are you Bugsy, the Gym Leader here?"

Bugsy brushed dirt from his hands and stood. Only then could Ethan and Erika see that he had been tending to a Metapod.

Bugsy looked Ethan over. "That's right! I'm Bugsy, the Azalea Gym Leader and a walking encyclopedia of Bug-type Pokemon!"

A walking encyclopedia?

Ethan hardly knew what to say about the title.

It sounded like one Bugsy had given himself. Did people really introduce themselves with their own nicknames?

"Are you here for a Gym challenge?" Bugsy asked.

Ethan nodded. "We came by a few days ago, but you were away, so we missed our chance."

"Oh? Sorry about that," Bugsy said, looking surprised. "I went somewhere farther away to catch new Pokemon, so I wasn't here these past few days."

Now that he knew why Ethan had come, Bugsy led them deeper into the forest. They passed dense shrubs and an indoor stream before reaching a battlefield among the trees.

Bushes surrounded it. Sunlight fell through the glass roof, and the scent of trees and flowers filled the air. The battlefield felt close to nature and had a character all its own.

Bugsy looked young, perhaps around Ash's age or a few years older. To lead a Gym at that age, he had to be capable.

He was, in fact, an exceptional young man. Quick-witted and knowledgeable, he studied Bug-type Pokemon and hoped to become a Pokemon professor. People across Johto knew him as a gifted youth!

Ethan and Bugsy took places on opposite sides of the field, while Erika sat on a bench.

A staff member came out of a nearby break room to referee.

Seeing both Trainers ready, the referee announced, "The Gym battle between Bugsy, Leader of the Azalea Gym, and the challenger will now begin! Each Trainer may use three Pokemon. The battle ends when all of one side's Pokemon are unable to battle!"

As the defending Gym Leader, Bugsy took out a Poke Ball first.

He threw it hard. A flash of blue light revealed a Pokemon that looked like a green spider.

Bugsy smiled. "My first Pokemonthe silent warrior of Bug-types, Spinarak!"

Spinarak was a Bug- and Poison-type Pokemon less than half a meter tall. Its head and abdomen were pale blue-green, with a white horn on its head and black eyes. It had three pairs of legs marked in yellow and dark blue-green. A pattern resembling a sorrowful face marked its back.

Spinarak were said to be extraordinarily patient. After setting traps with their thin, strong silk, they waited for prey. One could hold the same pose in its nest for days. Even when prey was caught in its web, it might remain motionless until nightfall before acting.

Its silk was sturdy enough to hold a ten-kilogram rock without breaking. Some fishers even wove the silk into nets to catch fish Pokemon!

Chapter 501: Admitting the Gap

Against Bugsy's first Pokemon, Ethan did not hesitate. He sent out Eevee.

He had chosen Eevee for this battle three days earlier, when he first came to the Azalea Gym. He wanted the match to help it train and grow quickly.

Since leaving Ecruteak City with Ethan, Eevee had seen a great deal. It had fought only a few one-on-one battles, but had joined quite a number of skirmishes large and small. It had gained plenty of experience.

It was not exceptionally strong, but it could put up a fight.

Blue light flashed, and Eevee appeared before Spinarak. It glanced this way and that, brimming with excitement.

Bugsy was not especially surprised to see an eager Eevee.

In his time as a Gym Leader, he had seen countless Eevee, as well as Flareon, Vaporeon, Jolteon, and other evolved forms. He had encountered plenty of much stranger, rarer Pokemon too.

An unevolved Eevee was so ordinary that Bugsy began to think the challenger must be ordinary as well.

Why else would a Trainer who had traveled so long still have an Eevee in its first form?

Given enough time together, Eevee could evolve into Espeon or Umbreon even without an Evolution stone. The fact that this one had not evolved suggested to Bugsy that, barring the unlikely possibility that Eevee did not want to, it and its Trainer had not formed a close bond yet.

Bugsy had a good eye. Eevee and Ethan were not close yet. What he did not know was that Ethan had only recently received it, so they had had little time to build trust.

Both Pokemon were ready. The referee swept his colored flag down, and the battle began.

Eevee showed its restless nature at once. Before Ethan could give an order, it rushed eagerly at Spinarak.

Ethan sighed under his breath.

They had not been together long enough. Eevee had also grown used to a relaxed, free life with the Kimono Sisters, and even outside battle it did not listen to Ethan very well.

This can't continue...

He would have to find time to train it properly.

Spinarak braced for Eevee's charge. The white pupils in its black eyes tracked every movement. As Eevee drew close and a hind foot touched the ground, Spinarak suddenly fired a strand of white silk at it.

The silk streaked through the air and reached Eevee almost instantly.

"Dodge it!" Ethan shouted.

Eevee had already thought to evade. It rolled lightly to the side, and the silk skimmed its fur before shooting past!

It had escaped by the narrowest margin. The close call startled Eevee into taking its opponent seriously.

Ethan called again at the right moment. "Eevee! Stop acting on your own and listen to me!"

They had at least spent some time together, and the danger had caught Eevee's attention. It obeyed without hesitation.

"Use Sand Attack!"

Eevee turned and scraped the ground hard with its hind legs. Wave after wave of dust mixed with sand and small stones flew toward Spinarak.

Across the field, Bugsy responded calmly. "Spinarak, use Agility!"

At his command, the normally slow Spinarak became a blur and escaped the Sand Attack in a flash.

Dust and grit covered the spot where it had stood, but did not touch even its shadow.

In their first exchange, Eevee had gained nothing and had nearly been caught by silk. It appeared to be at a slight disadvantage. Bugsy's Spinarak was clearly no weakling.

In most physical qualities, from speed to stamina, Eevee was better than an ordinary Spinarak. If their training were equal, it should have had a good chance of winning. That was why Ethan had dared send it out.

But this Spinarak had been thoroughly trained through its many Gym battles. It could not be judged by the standards of an ordinary member of its species.

The two Pokemon clashed again.

Eevee tried Tackle, hoping to use its greater speed to land a hit.

Spinarak used String Shot to anchor silk to a tree. It swung aside from the attack like a pendulum. When Eevee charged again, Spinarak swung swiftly from tree to tree and reached the far side of the battlefield with ease.

Once more, distance opened between them.

Even Erika, watching from the bench, sensed that something was wrong.

Spinarak seemed stronger, and the trees gave it a terrain advantage. With no favorable type matchup to help Eevee, winning this battle would be difficult.

How will you handle this?

Erika watched Ethan with growing concern.

He considered the situation for a moment and decided not to be stubborn. He took out Eevee's Poke Ball and recalled it.

"Oh? Giving up already?"

Bugsy folded his arms. He looked calm, apparently unconcerned by the switch.

Ethan felt no shame in admitting it. "My Eevee isn't a match for your Spinarak yet. It needs more training. So I'll use a somewhat stronger Pokemon against you."

He threw another Poke Ball. In a flash of blue light, Pupitar appeared before Bugsy.

"Pupitar?"

Bugsy grew a little more serious. Pupitar was rarer than Eevee, and its physical strength was greater. He could not afford to dismiss it.

When the battle resumed, Spinarak had a much harder time.

As Pupitar charged, Spinarak tried the same trick, using its silk to swing across the field and create distance. But Pupitar expelled compressed air from its body and reached Spinarak again almost at once!

Once that escape route failed, Spinarak lost its greatest advantage.

Chapter 502: The Proud Bug-Type Warrior

"I see," Bugsy said. "You used Pupitar's unusual way of moving to keep up with Spinarak's silk swings. Clever!"

In midair, Pupitar slammed into Spinarak and knocked it out of its swing and onto the ground!

Bang! Spinarak landed hard. Its six legs helped it scramble up at once and flee beyond Pupitar's reach before its opponent could follow up.

Thump...

Pupitar landed in front of it. The change in Pokemon had raised the intensity of the battle, and the situation had reversed in an instant!

That did not mean Eevee was weak. Spinarak's way of moving among the branches was almost unfair, and Eevee had too few ways to attack it there.

In a straightforward fight on the ground, Eevee might well have won.

With Pupitar on the field, however, things were different.

Bugsy saw the shift and stopped trying to look unfazed. "Spinarak, restrict its movement!" he called.

Spinarak puffed up its mouth. Ethan knew how sticky its silk was. If Pupitar were bound in it, breaking free would be difficult. He would not let Bugsy have his way.

"Use Sandstorm!" Ethan ordered.

As Spinarak spat out silk, yellow sand swept across the entire field. At first, Pupitar was still faintly visible through the dust. The storm thickened, and in the blink of an eye it vanished from sight!

Spinarak was caught in the storm too.

It fired a few strands of silk toward the place where Pupitar had last been. As the sand grew denser, it lost all sense of direction and could no longer find its target!

Countless tiny stones mixed with the sand. Each sting was mild, but the constant impacts hurt Spinarak and made movement difficult.

Spiders generally had no eyelids to close. Tears kept their eyes moist, but what good were tears in a sandstorm?

Dust coated Spinarak's eyes at once. It rubbed them with its front legs, trying to clear away the sand that kept blowing in.

Each time it succeeded, fresh dust stuck to them less than a second later. The cycle left it unable to do anything else.

Bugsy could not see inside the storm either, but he knew Spinarak was at a severe disadvantage. "Spinarak! Watch out for Pupitar's surprise attacks!" he shouted anxiously.

The wind and sand broke up his words before they reached it.

Spinarak lowered its head and shielded its eyes with its front legs, easing the worst of the dust. It turned slowly, sensing for any sign of Pupitar.

And it found something!

A silver shape was creeping toward it through the yellow haze.

Spinarak had no time to think. It opened its mouth and fired a barrage of Pin Missile at the shape!

In the confusion, it could not tell whether it had hit. Then another silver shape approached from a different direction.

This time, Spinarak fired a Poison Sting. There was a faint metallic clink, and the needle spun away.

Did it miss?

Or did something deflect it?

The Sandstorm began to weaken, and the air slowly cleared. When dust stopped blowing into its eyes, Spinarak looked up. The object it had struck with Poison Sting was a huge rock!

Where did that come from?

Before it could think further, wind rushed behind it. Spinarak turned just in time to see something silver, like an iron mask, flying closer and filling its vision...

It was Pupitar!

Unable to dodge, Spinarak took the impact and was sent flying!

...

In the Trainer's area, Bugsy frowned uneasily. He stared into the Sandstorm and, as the wind finally began to die down, searched the middle of the battlefield.

Before he found his Pokemon, Spinarak flew out of the storm, landed beyond the field, and fainted!

What?

What happened!? How did Spinarak lose during one Sandstorm?

Several large rocks now lay on the field. Bugsy could guess that Pupitar had used a Rock-type move in the storm, but he had no idea what had happened in detail.

He glanced at Ethan across the field. The challenger looked calm, showing little excitement at Pupitar's victory.

Bugsy did not know how the battle had ended, but Spinarak had lost. He took out its Poke Ball and recalled it.

"Unlike your Eevee, this Pupitar is strong. But that's all right. Meet my second Pokemon!"

He threw another Poke Ball.

A green Metapod appeared before Ethan.

Metapod!?

What surprised Ethan was the pairing. Pupitar was in a cocoon-like stage, and Metapod had not completed its evolution either. Neither had hands or feet. Facing each other across the field, they made a comical sight.

Did Bugsy send it out just to make fun of my Pupitar?

As though sensing Ethan's doubt, Bugsy smiled confidently. "Don't underestimate my Metapod. It's a proud warrior among Bug-type Pokemon!"

First he had called Spinarak a silent warrior, and now Metapod was a proud one.

What ordinary person gave their Pokemon titles like that?

Bugsy might have become a Gym Leader at a young age, but he could still sound like a boy caught up in his own grand fantasies!

Ethan looked at the green cocoon and kept Pupitar in the battle.

Metapod, Caterpie's evolved form, was known for the hard shell that protected its soft body while it changed inside.

With two Pokemon in similar stages facing each other, Ethan wanted to see which shell was tougher.

Bugsy's Metapod, or his Pupitar!

Chapter 503: Evolution into Tyranitar

For Bugsy to send out Metapod after losing the first round, he had to be confident in its strength.

Ordinarily, a Trainer's second Pokemon would be stronger than the first or have an advantage against the opponent. Yet Ethan could not understand this choice. At the Metapod stage, its ways to attack were extremely limited. It basically had only Harden, and some Metapod could not even move.

Why send out a Pokemon with such a natural disadvantage?

Bugsy must have his reasons, Ethan decided. Perhaps he had given it some unusual training.

When the battle resumed, Pupitar attacked first.

It released compressed air from its body and shot toward Metapod like an arrow from a bow. In a blink, it reached its opponent, opened its jaws to reveal small pointed teeth, and bit down hard.

Ethan had not ordered it to do that. Pupitar wanted to test Metapod's shell with its own teeth.

A contest of toughness was more than talk!

"Metapod, use Harden!" Bugsy shouted as Pupitar rushed in.

Metapod remained in place, but light flashed over its body. Harden was the one Normal-type move a Metapod could use to make its shell tougher and protect its soft interior.

Pupitar's teeth closed around Metapod with all their strength.

Creeeak...

The scrape of teeth against its shell made a shrill sound like metal grinding on metal.

Protected by Harden, Metapod did not yield. Pupitar nearly broke its teeth. It tried biting several other spots, but could not get through the shell!

Metapod certainly lived up to its reputation for a hard casing!

Bugsy spotted an opening. "Metapod, jump!"

Metapod pushed off sharply with the tip of its body and sprang high into the air, breaking free of Pupitar.

It reached almost to the Gym's ceiling. Pupitar looked up, and the next moment Metapod dropped straight toward it like a cannonball!

Pupitar could not dodge. Metapod slammed into it with a tremendous bang, and the two Pokemon bounced apart.

Only Pupitar's own hard shell let it withstand the blow.

Bugsy saw Ethan's surprise and smiled. "Well? Didn't expect that, did you? My Metapod isn't like the ones you've met before!"

For all the pride in Bugsy's voice, Ethan really was impressed.

Most people's Metapod could hardly move inside their rigid shells. Somehow, Bugsy had trained his to leap and strike!

He deserved his reputation as a Bug-type expert.

Metapod tried another dive from above, but this time Pupitar was ready and dodged.

After those exchanges, Ethan understood its approach. Trusting its shell, Metapod hurled itself around like a solid cannonball!

It had no concern for the risk in either attack or defense.

How could he stop that smooth little sequence?

His gaze crossed Pupitar, and after a moment's thought he had an idea.

When Metapod jumped high again, ready to repeat its dive, Ethan suddenly called, "Pupitar, use Stone Edge!"

At the command, Pupitar formed a huge, solid rock in front of itself. Metapod was already dropping toward it!

"Oh no!"

Bugsy had expected Pupitar to fire sharp stones at the airborne Metapod. When he saw the single massive rock appear, his face changed. He understood what Ethan intended.

It was too late to make Metapod change course!

Before everyone's eyes, Metapod plunged headfirst into the rock.

Bang!

Whether by perfect force or chance, Metapod neither shattered the rock nor bounced off. It punched a small hole and lodged its entire body inside!

Metapod twisted frantically, caught off guard by the turn of events. However hard it struggled, it could not break free.

Got it.

Ethan smiled. "Finish it, Pupitar!"

With a burst of compressed air, Pupitar jumped in front of the rock and aimed at Metapod's exposed back. It unleashed Dark Pulse.

A terrifying wave of energy surged from Pupitar's body and struck Metapod almost instantly. Trapped in the rock, it could not evade. Dark Pulse swept over it, the rock broke apart, and Metapod flew away with the fragments.

Clatter...

Metapod rolled several times and came to rest outside the battlefield.
