Its eyes were spinning. The referee raised a colored flag. "Metapod is unable to battle! Pupitar wins!"

Before Bugsy could speak, white light suddenly enveloped Pupitar.

Bugsy looked startled. Ethan raised his brows too.

Another evolution?

Dragonite had evolved during the Cianwood Gym challenge, and now Pupitar was doing the same. It had happened several times back in Kanto too, always just after one of Ethan's Pokemon defeated an opponent.

In game terms, Gym Leaders' Pokemon were stronger than those of ordinary Trainers. Defeating them meant gaining more "experience points"!

The light faded. A Pokemon more than two meters tall stood on the battlefield, its body protected by hard gray-green armor.

It was Pupitar's evolved formTyranitar!

Tyranitar threw back its head and roared. The deafening sound echoed through the Gym, sending distant Bug-type Pokemon fleeing into the shrubs!

Its entrance reminded Ethan of his Gyarados, far away at Cerise Park. Tyranitar was not as enormous, but it was every bit as fierce a species!

This was not Ethan's first time seeing one. When they had raided a Team Rocket base in Kanto, Apollo, one of Team Rocket's four executives, had commanded a Tyranitar. That Pokemon had struck Erika hard enough to draw blood. Ethan could still remember it clearly!

Chapter 504: Scyther Versus Scyther

Seeing someone else's Tyranitar was very different from owning one himself.

Tyranitar was immensely powerful. Once it had grown to its full strength, Ethan would have another Pokemon that could stand alongside the three Legendary birds or the three Legendary beasts. It was a major addition to his team's depth!

From her seat, Erika looked at the imposing Pokemon and remembered the Tyranitar that had struck her. She was happy for Ethan, though she could almost feel that old pain in her back again.

Ethan admired Tyranitar for a moment. He touched its hard armor and praised it, then recalled it rather than having it continue the battle.

As at the Cianwood Gym, he had planned to use this challenge mainly to train his Pokemon. Fully evolved partners such as Dragonite and Tyranitar were not what he had in mind.

Once Ethan had finished, Bugsy took out his third Poke Ball.

"Impressive. It's been a long time since anyone forced me to use my third Pokemon. Come on out, my magnificent warriorScyther!"

He threw the ball hard. Blue light flashed, and a Scyther appeared on the battlefield!

Magnificent warrior?

Another overblown title. Yet sending it out last suggested that Scyther was Bugsy's ace.

Unlike Gym Leaders who had traveled to other regions, Bugsy used only Pokemon common to Kanto and Johto. They were not weak, but his youth meant he had not yet ventured far from home. Becoming a Gym Leader so early had tied him to this place.

Early fame was not always an advantage.

But if Bugsy was sending out a Scyther...

Ethan searched his waist pouch and drew out his own Scyther's Poke Ball.

When two Trainers had the same Pokemon, a direct contest was too tempting to pass up.

"It's your turn!"

Ethan threw his ball. A Scyther with a scar on its forehead appeared across from Bugsy's.

"Oh?" Bugsy's eyes lit up. He studied Ethan's Scyther, then looked at its scar. "Another Scyther? It looks well trained too. Good! Now we can see which one is stronger!"

Ethan smiled. "Mine may not have a grand title like yours, but it has quite a history. Before I caught it, it lived on an island full of Bug-type Pokemon. Don't let its ordinary looks fool you. They called it 'Scar.' With its two scythes, it cut its way from the south of the island to the north, then from east to west, for three days and three nights without blinking once!"

Huh?

Ethan's Scyther glanced back at him, baffled. When had any of that happened?

Was this "Scar" some other Scyther?

Bugsy failed to recognize the joke. Instead, the island of Bug-type Pokemon caught his interest.

"Where is that island?" he asked.

Ethan had hoped his tired joke would amuse this boastful kid. When his only listener did not play along, he sighed in disappointment.

Is this what a generation gap feels like?

"It's far away, in the Orange Islands," he said, his enthusiasm fading. "It's easy enough to find, but you'll need a boat to get there."

Bugsy nodded thoughtfully. As a Bug-type expert, he was plainly interested.

At the referee's signal, the two Pokemon moved to the center of the field.

They stared at each other, eager to fight!

The colored flag fell. Both Scyther charged at almost the same instant and raised their scythe-like arms together!

They met like master swordsmen. Their blades crossed and threw off bright sparks!

They swung again and again, dozens of strikes flashing by until their scythes were nearly a blur.

As the pace climbed, Bugsy's Scyther seemed to falter first. It jumped back, out of Scar's reach.

Bugsy was startled.

As Ethan and Erika had guessed, Scyther really was his ace. He had complete confidence in it.

Falling behind in the first exchange was the last thing he expected!

It also showed him that, unlike Ethan's unimpressive Eevee, both Pupitar and Scyther were above average.

Scar's eyes turned cold at its retreating opponent. It pressed forward again without giving Bugsy's Scyther a chance to rest.

Bugsy clenched his teeth. He would not meet it head-on. "Scyther, use Double Team!"

Three copies split from Bugsy's Scyther. The move confused Scar, which slashed at the nearest figure.

Its sharp scythe cut through nothing but an image.

A blade whistled behind it. The real Scyther had hidden to the far right and attacked while Scar was swinging.

Clang!

To Bugsy's Scyther's surprise, its ambush failed. Scar turned in time and blocked the blow with its own scythe!

"It's that strong?"

Bugsy frowned. He could hardly believe the sneak attack had failed under those conditions.

"Scyther, use Swords Dance!"

At his order, Scyther whirled and leaped, sweeping its scythes through a dance. Light covered its body, greatly increasing its attack power.

Bugsy must have hoped that extra power would break through Scar's defense.

Ethan smiled and answered in kind.

"Scyther, join it! Use Swords Dance!"

Scar performed the same battle dance, its own attacking strength rising sharply.

Ethan looked from the equally strengthened Pokemon to Bugsy.

There. Now we're both ready. Let's see whose Scyther is stronger!

Chapter 505: The Hive Badge and Goldenrod City

Strengthened by Swords Dance, the two Scyther clashed again, fighting harder than before.

They shared the same type and used much the same moves. For a while, neither could gain a clear advantage.

They battled from the ground into the air and back again. Both used Fury Cutter so often that Ethan heard little but the ring of crossing blades, and his eyes could hardly keep up with their movements.

Perhaps worried that the fight was dragging on, Bugsy grew impatient. He repeatedly ordered Quick Attack followed by X-Scissor, looking for an opening through speed.

Ethan would not give him one. Double Team paired with Agility often let Scar evade and counterattack.

Little by little, Bugsy's Scyther fell behind.

Scar finally caught a gap in its opponent's offense and landed Night Slash, winning the battle.

Thud...

Bugsy's Scyther fell straight to the ground and fainted. Ethan's Scyther was still standing, but all its rapid movement and intense fighting had drained its stamina. Sweat covered its body.

The referee raised the colored flag. "Scyther is unable to battle! The challenger wins the Gym match!"

Bugsy recalled his Scyther and walked over to Ethan with a thoughtful expression.

"I lost. Your Scyther really is remarkable. I never expected to lose to another Bug-type Pokemon when I'm a Bug-type Trainer. I still have a lot to learn."

Scar returned to Ethan, who smiled and stroked its scarred forehead. "Before I caught this Scyther, it led its group. It was strong even among Scyther. And honestly, yours is strong too. If I'd slipped up, I could have been the one to lose."

"So that's how it is..."

Bugsy understood, but his curiosity about the island of Bug-type Pokemon Ethan had mentioned only grew.

I'll have to visit it on my next training trip!

Next month... no, next week!

After a little more conversation, Bugsy took a badge from his pocket and placed it in Ethan's hand.

"This is the Hive Badge, proof that you've defeated me. Take good care of it."

Ethan thanked him. Erika came to his side, and they examined the red-and-black badge in his palm. It looked like a ladybug, much like the ones Ethan had seen on Earth.

With this badge, Ethan needed only one more to enter the Silver Conference!

They chatted a little longer, then said goodbye and left.

After leaving the Azalea Gym, they did not depart town immediately. They found an inn with a hot spring and spent time soaking, easing their fatigue and restoring their strength.

They had walked so many mountain paths on the round trip to Charicific Valley that going on without a rest might have caused trouble.

After a night's recovery, both woke refreshed. The next morning, they set out for the city of Ethan's final Gym challenge!

...

Goldenrod City was a large, prosperous metropolis.

It stood on the coast in west-central Johto. As the region's center of finance, technology, and politics, it was the only international city on the shared Johto and Kanto landmass that could rival Saffron City.

Even the names Goldenrod and Saffron brought wealth to mind. People saw money and opportunity everywhere in both cities, a measure of how prosperous they were.

After a day and a half of travel from Azalea Town, Ethan and Erika finally arrived.

Their destination was the Goldenrod Gym.

Goldenrod City's official Gym was led by Whitney, who specialized in Normal-type Pokemon. Defeating her would earn Ethan the Plain Badge.

They walked through streets lined with tall buildings and busy traffic. Even the people dressed more fashionably here.

For a moment, Ethan could almost forget he was in the Pokemon world. It felt like being back in a great city on Earth.

In any world, people were busy trying to make a living...

Erika noticed him looking around and laughed softly. "Now that you've seen both Saffron and Goldenrod, which do you think is more prosperous?"

Trying to test me, are you?

"They're about the same," Ethan said after thinking it over. "Once cities reach this size, their main differences are the landmarks. One is on the coast and the other isn't."

Erika nodded. Once cities reached a certain scale and level of technology, they did begin to look much alike.

They followed the streets to the Goldenrod Gym.

It stood in the city center and covered an enormous area. From outside, it looked like a large sports arena.

Without the Pokemon League symbol above the entrance, Ethan might have mistaken the imposing building for a football stadium!

But at the entrance, a staff member told them Whitney had just gone out and was not at the Gym.

Ethan was disappointed.

He had had poor luck with Gym Leaders lately. Bugsy's absence had delayed him for three days, and now Whitney was away too.

Had his journey been going so smoothly that fate had decided to make things harder?

Fortunately, the staff member added that Whitney was only wandering around the city. Even if she did not return that day, she would certainly be at the Gym tomorrow. Ethan felt a little better.

Outside, Ethan glanced at the unfamiliar streets and turned to Erika. "It's only noon. Let's find somewhere to stay, then come back later."

"All right." Erika smiled. "Since we have free time and don't often come to Goldenrod, will you go shopping with me?"

Ethan looked at her and felt a pang of guilt.

She had traveled from place to place with him all this time without a complaint. How many people would do that for someone? He ought to make time for her.

"Of course. Where would you like to go?"

Erika thought for a moment. "I've heard the department store here is famous. Let's start there!"

Chapter 506: Evolution into Scizor

The Goldenrod Department Store stood in the southern part of the city. Its plain name might have suggested an old building selling secondhand goods and trinkets, but it was actually Goldenrod's largest shopping center for Pokemon productsand the largest shopping center of any kind in the city!

It had six floors above ground and two below, eight in all. The spacious, bright interior was lavishly decorated, and its merchandise appealed to more than just people shopping for Pokemon supplies.

Ethan and Erika entered and found the place crowded. Trainers were everywhere, but so were fashionably dressed men and women.

Clearly, countless people came to see it every day, just as they had!

The first floor sold cosmetics and jewelry, useful to Trainers whose travels exposed them to wind and sun. Ethan went around it with Erika while she bought a bottle of moisturizing lotion and several face masks.

After so many long days on the road, setting out at dawn and returning after dark, Erika had had little time to care for her skin. Her face felt dry, so the products would come in handy.

The second floor's theme was "Travel Companions." It carried all sorts of things Trainers needed on the road. Ethan restocked supplies there and bought more Poke Balls and medicine for his Pokemon.

The third floor was devoted to "Everything for Victory," selling items for Pokemon battles. Ethan had never been very interested in such things, so he and Erika went straight up to the fourth floor.

The fourth and fifth floors each had their own Pokemon-related themes. Ethan did not spend much time browsing, but he did buy a Metal Coat.

He knew the item well. A Metal Coat had helped his Crystal Onix evolve into Crystal Steelix. Now he intended to use one to evolve Scyther.

By coincidence, the Metal Coat was known to help only Onix and Scyther evolve, and he happened to own both species!

It might as well have been made for him.

After more than an hour of shopping, they reached the sixth floor. Its theme was "When You're Tired of Shopping"a place to rest. It was the busiest, liveliest floor of all. Following an online recommendation, Ethan and Erika ate dinner at a popular restaurant there.

Soft, lovely music filled the restaurant. The setting and mood were just right. They sat facing each other, relaxed, looking very much like a young couple on a date!

Anyone watching their gestures, expressions, and the way they looked at each other would have taken them for a real couple.

They laughed and talked through dinner.

There was still time afterward, so they watched a recently popular Pokemon movie. By the time it ended, night had fallen. They walked shoulder to shoulder back to the guesthouse they had booked earlier.

After checking in at the front desk, Ethan walked Erika to her room. As he was about to turn away, she looked back at him with bright, smiling eyes.

"Thank you for coming with me. I had a wonderful time today!"

Meeting her gaze, Ethan answered before he could think better of it. "If you like it, I'll keep going shopping with you whenever you want!"

As soon as he said it, he felt something was off. Why did that sound so much like a confession?

Erika seemed to think the same thing. She stared at him for a moment, then gave him a radiant smile. Without a word, she went into her room.

That smile made Ethan's heart race.

He drew a deep breath, tried to steady himself, and returned to his own room.

He fell onto the bed and stared at the ceiling for a long time, but his restless feelings would not settle.

Sigh. So much for a purely platonic friendship between a man and a woman...

The longer he traveled with Erika, the deeper their bond grew. It was hard not to want more. Ever since what had happened with Maya, Ethan felt as though an inner restraint had fallen away, and he wanted Erika more than ever.

Thinking back, perhaps agreeing to travel with her had trapped him in a situation of his own making.

The harder he tried to calm down, the more his thoughts wandered. At last he took a cold shower. Only then did he regain his composure.

To keep from dwelling on it, he took a Poke Ball into the courtyard, released his Scyther, and brought out the Metal Coat he had just bought.

He looked his Pokemon over and smiled. "Scyther, let's evolve!"

Scyther looked at the item in his hand and seemed to understand. It nodded firmly.

Once the leader of its group, it was a proud fighter. It had no objection to evolving.

Gengar rose out of Ethan's shadow to watch, interested in the spectacle.

Ethan stepped forward and pressed the Metal Coat against Scyther's forehead. The instant it touched, brilliant white light burst from its body!

Erika noticed the light in the courtyard and opened her window. Fresh from her bath and dressed in a robe, she smiled at Ethan, then turned her attention to Scyther.

She had seen him buy the Metal Coat at the department store and knew what he planned. Its evolution was no surprise to her.

Ethan looked away from Erika and back to his Pokemon.

He had seen the light of evolution many times. He took several steps back, and just as he stopped, the glow vanished.

A cool-looking Pokemon covered in red stood before him. Scyther had evolved into Scizor!

Scyther had two possible evolutionary paths. Using a Metal Coat was one common route.

Scizor was a humanoid Pokemon clad in crimson armor. Two pairs of translucent wings rose from its back, though they were mostly decorative.

The longer Ethan looked at his newly evolved Scizor, the more he liked it. At last he took out his Pokedex and pointed it at the Pokemon.

"Beep. Scizor, the Pincer Pokemon. Bug and Steel type. Scizor's body is as hard as steel, reportedly stronger than even the finest tempered metal. Ordinary attacks cannot harm it. To keep its metal body from overheating and melting during battle, it beats its wings rapidly to regulate its temperature. Despite its slender build, its attacks are astonishingly powerful. Its steel-bearing pincers can crush even the hardest things they catch!"

Chapter 507: Goldenrod TV Station

As the Pokedex had said, Scizor's steel body might be too heavy for flight. The wings on its back could no longer support its weight. At most, they might slow a fall by letting it glide briefly.

In exchange, its new Steel typing had greatly improved its ability to take a hit. It was like a humanoid suit of armor.

Ethan patted Scizor's chest. It rang with a hollow clang that stung his palm, as if he had struck real steel.

"Not bad!"

Smiling, he walked around Scizor several times and admired it. Scizor seemed pleased with its new body too. It raised its large pincers for a closer look. The only thing it found strange was that its blade-like arms had become pincers.

Well, at least it can grip things now...

Ethan released a few of his smaller Pokemon so they could get used to their "new" companion. Then he waved goodnight to Erika and returned to his room, yawning.

All he wanted was sleep. Spending an entire afternoon shopping with a girl was tiring work.

...

After breakfast the next morning, the two left the guesthouse and headed straight for the Goldenrod Gym.

They had walked the route the day before, but in daylight it had a different kind of beauty.

They followed a broad street beside the river, with tall buildings on either side. A few entrances led underground to Goldenrod's shopping district, where visitors could find beauty services, snacks, and fashionable goods.

Erika looked interested. Before she could ask, Ethan offered, "If there's time after the Gym challenge, let's come back and look around!"

His thoughtfulness delighted her. Perhaps she had used the new moisturizer she bought yesterday; her face looked especially soft and fresh, adding to her charm.

They crossed a bridge to the other side of the city. A magnetic levitation train station immediately came into view. Completed only a few years ago, it was a major feat of engineering. Its trains could exceed 550 kilometers per hour and, according to what Ethan had heard, carry passengers across Johto and Kanto to Saffron City in just a few hours.

The station looked futuristic. Elevated tracks ran out of the city like a long zipper, vanishing beyond the horizon.

Farther on stood Goldenrod TV Station, a six-story tower. It was a large broadcaster whose signal covered all of Johto. Nearly every town and village could receive its programs, and its ratings had long held first place.

The tower had originally been an enormous old wooden structure. When age and decay destroyed it, the television station was built in its place.

Ethan and Erika stopped to admire the tower and took a photo together. As they were about to leave, they noticed something wrong.

The street below the station was being cordoned off. More than a dozen police cars stood outside, and officers had put up barriers around the entire building.

Among them, Ethan spotted a familiar figure he had not seen in a long time: Looker!

Looker and several officers stood by the hood of a police car, studying a plan. They spoke with furrowed brows, apparently discussing something serious.

"Something must have happened," Erika said quietly.

Ethan nodded. "When Looker turns up, an evil organization is usually involved. Here in Johto, that probably means Team Rocket."

"Should we go see?"

Ethan hesitated, then shook his head.

"The police are already here. We shouldn't interfere. If we get too involved in matters like this, people may think we're overstepping and trying to take charge of everything."

Two more police cars raced past them and stopped beneath the station.

Ethan and Erika were about to leave when Looker turned around. As if sensing Ethan's presence, he spotted him at once.

They were more than a hundred meters apart. Looker had eyes like radar!

His face lit up. He left the other officers and hurried toward Ethan.

Ethan could no longer simply walk away. He gave Erika a wry smile and went to meet him.

Looker called out before he was close. "Ethan, my friend! What a coincidence! I never expected to see you here!!"

My friend?

When had Looker started addressing him like that?

"I didn't expect to see you either. What's going on?" Ethan asked.

Looker sighed. "Team Rocket broke into the television station this morning. They've taken over the entire building!"

They broke into the station?

Ethan realized this seemed to match a plot from the games.

Looker looked him over and glanced discreetly at Erika. Then he smiled. "You're looking well, Ethan. Anabel told me about your raid on that Team Rocket base not long ago. Thank youyou helped us enormously again. How is your badge journey going?"

"Well enough. I have seven badges, and I was on my way to challenge the Goldenrod Gym. Do you need any help with Team Rocket?"

He offered mainly out of courtesy. The police had surrounded the station. As far as he could see, Team Rocket had no escape; clearing the building was only a matter of time.

To his surprise, Looker laughed. "You'd help? Wonderful! To be honest, I was just worrying about what to do. Running into you now is perfect!"

Ethan fell silent.

Looker did not hesitate to accept at all...

With a sigh, Ethan asked, "Have you run into a problem?"

Looker did not answer immediately. Instead, he led Ethan and Erika over to the police car.

The officers watched curiously. Their commander had rushed away without a word and returned with a young man and woman they had never seen.

Chapter 508: An Unexpected Incident

Several floor plans of Goldenrod TV Station lay across the hood of the police car. They clearly showed the layout of every level.

A video device sat nearby. Looker tapped a few controls and played a recording.

It was security footage from that morning. Employees had just begun arriving, and the lobby was full of people hurrying to work. Everything looked normaluntil the automatic doors opened and dozens of Team Rocket members in black uniforms rushed in. With their Pokemon's help, they quickly seized the lobby.

Terrified workers fled the station. The Team Rocket members occupied it level by level until they had complete control. Then the footage cut off.

When Ethan had seen it all, Looker said grimly, "This is an outrageous incident. I can't imagine what Team Rocket is trying to do. Acting this openlyare they declaring war on the whole world?"

"Can you still see what's happening inside?" Ethan asked.

Looker shook his head. "They cut every security camera feed. We've lost contact with the building. Worst of all, many people didn't get out in time. They're being held hostage..."

A crackle interrupted him. The device's screen flickered, and a new video broke in without warning.

It appeared not only on that device but on electronic billboards outside nearby buildings, on televisions and computers in people's homes, and even on their phones.

A pink-haired woman in a Team Rocket uniform faced the camera. "Attention, everyone in Johto. We are Team Rocket, and today we announce our arrival! All members who hear this, gather here immediately! Boss Giovanni, if you see this message, please join us too!!"

The message ended, and the screens returned to normal. If not for the deep furrows in Looker's brow, the interruption might have felt like an illusion.

"What are they trying to accomplish?" he muttered. "There's no escape from that building. And why ask Giovanni to join them? Was this operation not his plan?"

Ethan thought for a moment. "From that message, they've clearly lost contact with Giovanni. Their bases across Johto have been cleared out one after another. Their local forces must be close to collapse, scattered and desperate enough to try this."

Looker nodded, agreeing with the assessment.

"In any case, after a spectacle this big, Giovanni could appear here at any moment. It might be a once-in-a-lifetime chance to capture all of them together!"

Ethan shook his head slightly, but said nothing.

Giovanni probably would not appear. Since his identity as a Gym Leader had been exposed, he had been keeping a low profile and quietly rebuilding his strength. This public operation did not fit his current approach.

Besides, Giovanni had never been a man who sought attention.

Ethan looked at Looker. "What's your plan?"

Looker hesitated. "I assembled a special police unit to storm the station. I was going to ask you to slip inside first. But after that broadcast..."

He did not finish, but Ethan understood.

Looker hoped to wait for Giovanni to appear, then arrest him along with the rest.

It was an appealing idea. Ethan doubted events would oblige him.

Looker respected Ethan enough to ask his opinion even after forming his own. "What do you think we should do?"

Ethan told him. Looker fell into thought.

At last, he sighed deeply. "You're right. I overlooked Giovanni's character and made this too simple. He would never put himself in danger for an operation this reckless."

"Even if we don't catch Giovanni, it's all right," Ethan said. "These are probably Team Rocket's last substantial forces in Johto. Arrest them, and Giovanni will have almost no one left to carry out his plans here."

The reassurance helped Looker settle on a decision.

"Exactly. We need to arrest this group before they can do any more harm!"

He put his original plan into motion. At his orders, ranks of officers gathered quickly. They wore helmets and carried riot shields, ready for an assault.

Looker returned to Ethan.

"Ethan, I'll need your help. Before my officers enter through the front, I want you to slip in elsewhere. Use the opening to rescue the hostages and arrest whoever is leading this operation."

"No problem. I'm used to this kind of work."

Ethan agreed with a smile. He had done enough of it by now.

He turned to Erika. He knew she would come with him even if he did not ask.

Sure enough, determination shone in her eyes.

They smiled at each other and quietly discussed where they could enter the station.

Team Rocket would be guarding the entrances closely, particularly the back door and roof. They would leave the police few obvious openings.

Ethan studied the plans for a long time, searching for a hidden route. The drains and ventilation ducts were too small for a person. In the end, Erika suggested coming from above and breaking through a window.

Team Rocket had too few members to watch every window on every floor. It could catch them by surprise.

The area around the station was rather open, though. They would need cover to approach unseen.

When they explained the plan, Looker smiled. "That's no problem. I'll launch a feint to draw their attention and use smoke grenades nearby to hide your approach!"

Chapter 509: Surprise Attack

Bang! Bang!

Several smoke grenades burst near the TV station. Thick white smoke spread outward, blocking Team Rocket's view from inside and drawing their attention.

Knowing this usually meant the police were beginning their operation, the Team Rocket members did not dare let down their guard.

Sure enough, officers began trying to attack the front entrance. Team Rocket concentrated most of its members in the first-floor lobby, determined to hold them off.

With their Pokemon providing cover, the two sides fought fiercely. The officers were well trained, but their opponents fought with equal desperation. The assault continued for several minutes without breaking through the defense.

Amid the confusion, nobody noticed a Dragonite carrying a man and a woman. It made a wide detour, climbed high into the sky, then dove and smashed through a window at the top of the tower, bursting into the station!

Crash!

Glass shattered and scattered across the floor. Ethan jumped down from Dragonite's back. Without pausing to look around, he flicked his hand and released two Pokemon.

A flash of blue light, and Gardevoir and Jolteon stood on either side of him. Gengar appeared in front of him at the same time. After setting Erika down, Dragonite rose behind them. The four Pokemon scanned their surroundings, guarding Ethan and Erika from every direction.

Whoever the enemy might be, they would have to get past these Pokemon to harm their Trainers.

Everything around them was quiet. No enemy appeared. Only then did Ethan have a chance to take stock of the place.

They were in the tower above the TV station. The main building stood seven or eight stories below, joined to the tower by a narrower structure. The two sections were separate areas.

Judging by its layout, this was probably a circular observation deck. It was empty now, save for signs of a hurried departure. The station staff had likely been seized by Team Rocket and confined elsewhere.

That suited their purpose. At least they had made it inside without being spotted.

Looker's voice crackled through Ethan's earpiece. "...How are things going?"

"Everything went smoothly," Ethan said quietly. "Team Rocket hasn't noticed us yet."

"Excellent!" Looker let out a long breath. "I've cut the station's internal camera feeds, so they won't see you on the monitors. We'll keep up the attack on the front entrance for a few more minutes. Use that time to make your move!"

"Understood!"

After the call, Ethan sent Gengar to check the area. Once it confirmed there were no Team Rocket members nearby, he and Erika headed down.

Erika released her Leafeon and Bellossom as well. Together, their Pokemon were a force no one could afford to ignore.

That was why Looker had been so pleased to see Ethan. With a Champion involved, one or two people could do nearly the work of an entire elite unit.

They could move quietly, too.

Once they left the room, Gengar went ahead to scout. It could pass through walls without a sound, leaving Ethan little reason to worry that the two of them would be discovered.

They did encounter a couple of patrolling Team Rocket members along the way, but Gengar knocked them out before either could notice anything.

Ethan tore strips from their clothes to gag them, then used handcuffs he had obtained from Looker to secure them to a railing. Leaving them there, he continued downward.

Team Rocket was short on people, and most of its attention was on the front entrance. The infiltration went remarkably smoothly.

After passing through the structure connecting the tower to the main building, they soon found the captive staff in a conference room.

Although fighting was still going on in the lobby, more than a dozen Team Rocket members remained to guard the hostages. Rescuing everyone without raising an alarm would be nearly impossible.

But they had already made it this far. Being discovered now did not matter much.

After a brief discussion, Ethan and Erika split up and approached the conference room's front and rear doors. When Erika was in position, Ethan took out his Gengar mask and put it on for the first time in a long while.

At his command to move, their Pokemon broke through both doors at once. Before the Team Rocket members or their Pokemon could react, attacks flew across the room. Explosions and sparks erupted, sending the defending Pokemon tumbling backward.

It all happened in an instant. The hostages screamed in fright and instinctively crouched low to avoid the attacks.

When the flames and smoke from the explosions cleared, the Team Rocket members and their Pokemon lay scattered on the floor.

A few Team Rocket members had escaped unconsciousness. Shocked to see someone rescuing the hostages, they hurriedly pulled out their radios and alerted the others.

Only then did Team Rocket realize that someone had slipped into the station from another direction while they were fighting at the front.

Damn it! Were these police officers all this devious?

Meanwhile, outside the station, Looker saw a disturbance ripple through Team Rocket's defensive line. He understood at once what had happened. Without waiting to contact Ethan, he made the decision and ordered a full assault.

With the police throwing all their strength into the attack and an enemy striking from behind, Team Rocket came under enormous pressure. Its seemingly solid defense collapsed almost at once.

The Team Rocket members fought as they retreated deeper into the station. The officers pressed forward, quickly took the first floor, and began pushing toward the second.

Ethan could hear the fierce battle clearly, even from the conference room.

Having freed the hostages, he and Erika stayed there to protect them. They could not risk Team Rocket lashing out at the captives in desperation. Only when Looker arrived with his officers did they finally relax their guard.

"Thanks for all your work. Is everyone all right?" Looker asked.

"What could have happened?" Ethan smiled faintly. "They were only ordinary members. It wasn't difficult at all."

Looker nodded. "Rescuing the hostages has removed our biggest concern. But those Team Rocket members have fallen back to the top of the tower. Worse, we've spotted several other executives among them!"

Executives?

Ethan's interest sharpened immediately.

The last time he had encountered a Team Rocket executive was at the Rocket warehouse in the Sevii Islands. He, Sabrina, and Lorelei had faced Lambda, one of the four executives, and eventually captured him and sent him to prison.

So which executive would appear today?

Chapter 510: Cornered Beasts Fight Back

A few officers stayed behind to evacuate the hostages. Ethan, Erika, and Looker led the rest toward the top of the tower.

After losing the station's main building, the Team Rocket members had all retreated there. They were still fighting, like beasts driven into a corner.

Ethan could not understand what Team Rocket hoped to gain from this operation.

Such a public attack was bound to draw trouble. It exposed them to everyone and would surely provoke fear and opposition. For Team Rocket, the harm would far outweigh any benefit.

Was it all just for that announcement? And what came after it?

Ethan could make no sense of it. He could only guess that something had gone wrong within Team Rocket, leaving the executives temporarily unable to contact Giovanni. Or perhaps Giovanni himself had abandoned these people to serve some larger purpose they knew nothing about.

Lost and uncertain, the remaining members might have decided to band together and use the broadcast to find Giovanni.

Still turning the possibilities over in his mind, Ethan retraced his earlier route with the others and reached the passage connecting the main building to the tower.

A spiral staircase rose through it. Two elevators had once run straight to the top, but Team Rocket had locked them down. The long staircase was now their only way up.

Team Rocket's resistance there was fierce. Attacks poured down the narrow stairwell in such numbers that the officers could not advance another step.

The relentless barrage even made the tower tremble. Bits of the walls began to break away.

Ethan sent out his Pokemon too, but no one could withstand an assault like that head-on.

He had no choice but to use the same trick again. Gengar passed through the wall, circled behind the enemy without a sound, and struck. As the Team Rocket members fell into confusion, the officers' Pokemon surged forward. Covering one another in turns, they finally took the staircase after a hard fight.

Team Rocket had no defensible position left. Its members retreated again and again until they reached the very top of the TV tower.

Ethan followed the officers onto the observation deck. At once, he spotted three executives among the crowdApollo, Athena, and Rocket executive Lance!

He rarely came across them at all, yet here were three together. Their faces were grim. Their predicament had stripped away their usual composure.

Some dozen meters separated the two groups. The Team Rocket members glared at them, tense and ready. The final battle could begin at any moment.

Looker pushed through the officers and faced the three executives. "Team Rocket! What was the purpose of this attack? And where is Giovanni now?"

"We'd like to know where he is too," Apollo said with a sneer. "As for our purpose, wasn't our message clear? We wanted the world to see Team Rocket and hear of our great deeds! We wanted you to know we haven't been driven into a corner!"

The destruction of their bases across Kanto and Johto, and the steady arrest of their members, had plainly put Team Rocket under enormous pressure.

"You've lost your minds." Looker shook his head, then fixed them with a stern look. "You're surrounded. Put down your weapons and surrender while you still can!"

Apollo ignored him and turned toward Ethan in the crowd.

"I didn't expect to find you here too. You just keep turning up! If it weren't for you, Lambda wouldn't have been captured. We wouldn't have suffered one loss after another, and Team Rocket's great undertaking wouldn't have met with so many setbacks!"

Ethan's face remained expressionless. He had no intention of answering. This time he had decided to be nothing more than someone who got the job done. Their beliefs were too far apart for an argument to serve any purpose.

Looker saw that Ethan did not want to draw attention to himself. He said no more and gave the order for a full attack.

The two sides' Pokemon collided, and the battle turned fierce at once.

Nearly all the officers' Pokemon were Arcanine. Team Rocket had a much wider variety: Golbat, Weezing, Arbok, and Salandit. They filled the air and the ground, making an imposing sight.

Dozens of Pokemon attacked in the cramped space. Team Rocket had three executives, but Ethan and Erika fought alongside the officers. For the moment, their strongest fighters seemed evenly matched.

Team Rocket's ordinary members and their Pokemon, however, could not match the officers and theirs.

As more Team Rocket Pokemon fell, Apollo glanced around and saw that the battle was turning against them.

He exchanged a look with Athena and Lance. Their purpose had been served. It was time to withdraw.

In fact, Ethan's guess had been right: Team Rocket had undergone a major upheaval.

More than half a month earlier, Giovanni had taken the organization's elite members and vanished completely. No one left behind knew where he had gone.

Those he had abandoned were left to fend for themselves, like bait displayed in plain sight for the International Police and Ethan to pick off one group at a time.

And the tactic had worked to a degree. Over the past few months, almost all their bases and facilities had been cleared out. That success had made the International Police lower their guard. Believing Team Rocket was no longer much of a threat, they had recently stopped actively searching for its remaining members, apart from continuing the hunt for Giovanni.

Team Rocket had moved from operating behind the scenes into hiding deep in the shadows.

Had these members not attacked the TV tower today, Looker might already have left for another region to deal with a different organization.

But the people Giovanni had left behind would not simply surrender. Today's attack on the station was meant to tell their scattered comrades that Team Rocket still had members here. They hoped everyone would reunite, stand together, and fight their way out of their predicament.

Back on the observation deck, Apollo and the other two executives tried to retreat. Ethan had no intention of letting them.

His eyes had been fixed on the three of them since the battle began. The moment he noticed their intention, he directed his Pokemon to engage them and keep them there.

If they escaped today, he might never find them again in a world this vast. Whatever it took, he would use this chance to arrest all three executives at once!

Chapter 511: I Didn't Lie to You

Apollo, Athena, and Lance backed toward the windows. It looked as though they meant to break the glass and escape through the air.

At Ethan's command, Dragonite, Jolteon, and Gardevoir closed on them at tremendous speed. Any Team Rocket Pokemon that tried to block their path was knocked down without mercy.

In mere moments, a number of Team Rocket's Pokemon had fallen before them.

Looker saw what Team Rocket was planning and shouted, "Don't think you'll get away!"

"Get away?" Athena snorted. "This is a tactical withdrawal. We've already done what we came here to do. There's no point staying any longer!"

As she spoke, she took out a controller and pressed it. With a tremendous bang, every pane of glass around the circular observation deck exploded at once!

Shards flew everywhere. The officers' Pokemon instinctively ducked their heads. By the time they looked up, the Team Rocket members had jumped from the tower, opened gliders on their backs, and were sailing away!

They had planned their escape route all along.

"Damn it! After them!" Looker's face changed. He had stationed officers around the TV station, but Team Rocket was clearly gliding farther away. Finding them again in a city this large would be like hunting for a needle in a haystack.

Ethan had kept his eyes on the three executives. As they prepared to leap from the tower, his gaze sharpened. Gardevoir, linked to him telepathically, caught his intention at once. She stretched out a hand and used Confusion, dragging Lance back just as he jumped through the broken window.

"What!?" Lance's face went pale. He tried to break free, but human strength was no match for psychic power. Within seconds, he was hauled back into the tower.

Several nearby officers sprang on him and pinned him down.

Before they had even finished, Ethan whistled and leaped through the shattered window. A yellow figure flashed beside him. Dragonite spread its wings and caught him on its broad back before he could begin to fall.

Gardevoir teleported onto Dragonite's back beside him. Ethan took out a Poke Ball and, while they were still close enough, turned to recall Jolteon.

The whole sequence flowed together and took only a few seconds.

Apollo and Athena had already glided some distance away. When they looked back and saw Lance captured, their expressions shifted.

Seeing Dragonite carry Ethan toward them made their mood heavier still.

The two exchanged a glance and nodded. They broke away from the main group and glided in another direction.

Team Rocket members dotted the sky like paper airplanes, but Ethan ignored the ordinary members. He kept Apollo and Athena in sight.

When they separated from the others, he patted Dragonite's neck, signaling it to change course.

The streets of Goldenrod City lay below. Pedestrians sensed something passing overhead and looked up. Faced with a sky full of gliders, they stared in surprise, thinking some extreme-sports club must be holding an event.

Apollo and Athena glided beyond the city and toward a freight train station in the suburbs. Losing altitude all the while, they finally landed there.

They removed their equipment and had barely found their footing when Dragonite descended in front of them. Ethan swung down and stood in their path.

Apollo narrowed his eyes at him. "You really don't know when to stop chasing us."

Athena folded her arms and snorted. "You came after us alone. Do you think you've already won?"

Ethan gave neither of them an answer. He took out his Poke Balls and released his Pokemon one after another.

Gardevoir, Dragonite, Jolteon, Tyranitar, Scizor, Gengar, and Crystal Steelix stood around him. All seven looked formidable.

Apollo and Athena surveyed them and seemed to abandon the thought of running. They took out their own Poke Balls and released their teams.

Ethan looked from one group to the other. Apollo had Houndoom, Golbat, Persian, Hypno, Tyranitar, and Wobbuffet.

Athena's team consisted of Sneasel, Muk, Arbok, Lickitung, Kabutops, and Vileplume.

In an instant, the Pokemon filled the open space. They watched their opponents closely. None made a sound, but every one of them was eager to fight.

Athena glanced over the teams and sneered. "It seems we have the advantage in numbers."

"Numbers don't decide everything," Ethan replied coolly. "Strength matters more. Besides, the International Police could arrive to reinforce me at any moment. Where are your reinforcements?"

Athena's smile froze. He was right: the International Police could come to his aid at any time. No one would be coming to help them.

"Don't be careless," Apollo warned her with a sidelong glance. "Remember, he still has the three Legendary birds."

"You don't need to worry about them." Ethan smiled and shook his head. "I left the three Legendary birds somewhere else."

What? That he would volunteer the fact that his strongest Pokemon were not with him astonished them both. Why would he leave such powerful Pokemon elsewhere?

Even so, they weighed his claim carefully. How could they know he was telling the truth?

If they believed him and lowered their guard, he might release all three birds at the height of the battle and catch them completely off guard.

Ethan saw their doubt but said nothing more.

Why was it so hard to get anyone to believe the truth these days?

Still...

His fingers brushed the two Great Balls in his belt pouch. The three Legendary birds were absent, but he had two Legendary beasts with him. They could serve as his trump cards just as well.

"Don't worry. I really didn't lie to you. The three Legendary birds aren't with me."

His earnest expression only left Apollo and Athena more baffled. They exchanged a glance. Time was short, so they decided to waste no more of it. They would defeat the man before them and leave.

And if they could finish him here, Team Rocket would be rid of one of its greatest threats at a stroke!

Chapter 512: He Has Two Legendary Beasts Too?

No one could say who attacked first. In a single instant, Ethan's Pokemon and those of Apollo and Athena moved together, charging at one another.

During the standoff, they had already picked out their opponents.

Gengar took on both Hypno and Wobbuffet, the two Psychic-type Pokemon, by itself.

Crystal Steelix, a Ground- and Steel-type, used its enormous body to stop Muk and Arbok.

Ethan's Tyranitar sought out Apollo's Tyranitar for a one-on-one fight. Jolteon set its sights on the fleet-footed Persian.

Scizor rushed at Lickitung and Vileplume. Dragonite faced the two Dark-type Pokemon, Houndoom and Sneasel, alone, while Gardevoir held back Golbat and Kabutops with her psychic power.

Ethan had not specifically arranged these matchups. In their daily training, he had taught his Pokemon to exploit type advantages and create favorable openings in a chaotic battle. When this situation arose, they naturally made those choices themselves.

Of course, these were only the matchups at the start. Once the two sides clashed and the field grew confused, Pokemon would lose track of their opponents. When that happened, Ethan's team would need to work together until the battle steadied enough for each to find its target again.

They had practiced this often. Though outnumbered, they fought in an orderly way.

Apollo and Athena could see that Ethan's Pokemon were not only individually powerful but also well trained. That made them difficult to deal with.

No wonder he was their organization's foremost enemy!

Fortunately for them, the first change in the battle came from the Tyranitar.

Ethan's Tyranitar had evolved far more recently than Apollo's and had much less experience. Their clash shook the ground, keeping every other Pokemon well clear. Before long, Ethan's began to lose and was defeated.

It fell backward and struggled to rise, but it had exhausted its strength and could not stand.

That one defeat tipped what had been a stalemate toward the two Team Rocket executives.

With no opponent to hold it back, Apollo's Tyranitar entered the other fights and quickly disrupted Ethan's formation.

Ethan's remaining Pokemon still worked to defeat their opponents, but Team Rocket's Pokemon were strong in their own right. They would not fall easily. Even when outmatched, they kept moving rather than meeting Ethan's Pokemon head-on. Seeing their comrade win gave them a further burst of confidence.

The two executives could not hide their delight.

"It looks like we'll be the ones winning today," Athena said with a sneer.

"I wouldn't be so sure." Ethan shook his head. "And I'd advise you not to sound so certain. It makes the reversal that much more embarrassing."

He recalled his defeated Tyranitar, then took the two Great Balls from his belt pouch.

Apollo had been watching his every move. Ethan showed no sign of worry despite his disadvantage. Seeing him calmly bring out two more Great Balls made Apollo's eyes narrow.

"Didn't you say you left the three Legendary birds somewhere else?"

"I did." Ethan tossed the two balls lightly in his hands and smiled. "I wasn't lying. I left them elsewhere. But that doesn't mean I have no other trump cards!"

He hurled both Great Balls. Blue light flashed, and two four-legged Pokemon appeared before Apollo and Athena.

The executives recognized their familiar forms and the powerful presence surrounding them at once. Their faces darkened.

Suicune and Raikou!

Damn it. How did he have these two Legendary beasts?

Both executives' expressions changed sharply. Neither had expected this. The speed at which Ethan was growing stronger was astonishing.

Raikou alone might have been understandable. Professor Sebastian's report on the earlier incident had told them that Ethan helped Raikou fight Team Rocket. But when had he captured it? The report had clearly said Raikou escaped!

And where had Suicune come from? Why had they heard nothing about it beforehand?

After the first shock, Apollo studied Ethan, then slowly breathed out.

So that was why he had dared to pursue them alone. He had the strength to back it up.

One detail offered Apollo a little comfort: the two Legendary beasts did not seem to be in the same state of mind.

Suicune simply stood there, watching him calmly. Raikou was much more restless.

Perhaps because Ethan had captured it only recently, Raikou's attention was not on them. It glanced around, as though studying the place for a way out.

Unfortunately for Apollo, it did not flee. After a few quiet words from Ethan, Raikou gradually settled and turned its attention back to him.

When those cold, tiger-like eyes fixed on Apollo, a chill ran down his spine.

Suicune and Raikou were still only standing there, almost as though they had no intention of working. Ethan laughed and scolded them. "You two can stop posing now. Hurry and deal with them while no one else is around! And if you do well this time, I'll let you out for some fresh air more often!"

At his urging, they finally moved together. Suicune was graceful as a doe, mist gathering around it. Raikou sprang like a hunting cat, electricity flickering across its body as it charged straight into the enemy's ranks.

Calling it a tiger among sheep would hardly have been an exaggeration.

The battle shifted almost at once.

With the two Legendary beasts easing the pressure, Crystal Steelix abandoned its opponents and turned on Apollo's Tyranitar. It had been eager for that fight for some time.

It had disliked the look of Tyranitar from the start. Now it would show that Pokemon which of them was truly the fiercer one!

Gengar, on the other hand, grew even less inclined to fight. It floated back to Ethan's side without making any move to attack.

Even during the earlier clash, Gengar had never taken the battle very seriously. It was sure Ethan would win in the end and had done little more than keep its own opponents occupied.

Now that two such powerful Pokemon had joined the fight, Gengar relaxed completely and watched with the air of a spectator enjoying a show.

Chapter 513: The State of the Battle

At the edge of the battlefield, Jolteon chased Persian through the open ground, along pipes, and over shipping containers. The two Pokemon moved so quickly they were almost a pair of blurs.

Persian was agile, but it could not match Jolteon's speed.

Whether Persian sprang a surprise attack or wheeled around to strike from an unexpected angle, Jolteon could evade it with Agility. If Persian closed in and used a move like Fury Swipes, Jolteon answered with Thunder Fang or Double Kick.

Nor was Jolteon afraid of fighting up close. Simply letting electricity run across its body was enough to make Persian wary of touching it.

The two stayed at the outskirts of the battle. Neither had won yet, but at this rate, victory would eventually tip toward Jolteon.

The most fearsome clash in the center of the field was between Crystal Steelix and Tyranitar.

After defeating Ethan's Tyranitar, Apollo's had found itself caught up in a fight with Crystal Steelix.

Tyranitar stood two meters tall and looked like a figure in heavy armor. Crystal Steelix, however, was nearly ten meters long, with a huge head and a body as hard as steel. Tyranitar's presence was no less imposing, but it was plainly outmatched in size.

That size came with immense strength. Crystal Steelix needed only to shift its body for Tyranitar to have to use all its power to resist.

Both Pokemon excelled in strength, and their battle shook the ground. No other Pokemon dared come within a dozen meters for fear of being caught in it.

Still, Tyranitar was a pseudo-legendary Pokemon. Once it fought in earnest, it managed to hold its own against Crystal Steelix despite the size difference.

Elsewhere, Golbat wheeled through the air while Kabutops strode across the ground, swinging its scythe-like forearms. The ancient, shell-backed Pokemon and its flying partner faced Ethan's Gardevoir.

Her psychic power left both of them at a severe disadvantage.

Golbat could not fly under her restraint; it hung motionless in the air. Whenever Kabutops drew close, Gardevoir teleported to another position and struck it with Psychic, knocking it to the ground.

Again and again, she kept both opponents firmly under control.

If dividing her attention between them had not made the fight more difficult, it might already have been over.

In the southern part of the battlefield, Scizor fought Lickitung and Vileplume alone. Vileplume was at a clear type disadvantage. Its attacks did little to Scizor, while Scizor's Bug-type moves punished it so badly it could scarcely fight back.

Lickitung, a Normal-type Pokemon, fared little better. Scizor's Steel typing reduced the effect of its Normal-type attacks, leaving them far less useful than they might have been against another opponent.

Despite fighting two at once, Scizor seemed to grow stronger as the battle went on. When one of its great pincers caught Lickitung's long tongue, the grip left Lickitung in agony.

To the north, Dragonite faced Houndoom and Sneasel.

Both were Dark-type Pokemon. Houndoom was also a Fire-type, while Sneasel was an Ice-type.

Houndoom's Fire-type moves posed little danger to Dragonite. Sneasel's Ice-type attacks, on the other hand, were four times as effective against it.

Fortunately, Dragonite could use its little wings to maneuver nimbly through the air, and Sneasel could not land a hit. Dragonite also knew a varied range of moves and could often surprise its opponents.

That was the state of the battle before Suicune and Raikou joined it. With the two Legendary Pokemon now in the fight, everything changed.

Muk and Arbok were the first to feel it.

They had originally faced Crystal Steelix and had been unable to do much against it. Now Raikou replaced it as their opponent, and their position only worsened.

Raikou barely glanced at them. It leaped past and let loose a Discharge that scorched both Pokemon.

Before they could even fall, a thick Hydro Pump swept across the middle of the field. Houndoom failed to dodge and was knocked down. It was strong enough to survive the powerful hit, though it could not shrug it off.

Seeing three of their Pokemon struck down in an instant made Apollo and Athena's brows twitch.

They had held some hope of winning before Raikou and Suicune appeared. The sight of those two Legendary Pokemon had wiped it away.

They exchanged a glance and saw the same desire to retreat in each other's eyes.

There was no point fighting on. It was time to leave.

At their signal, their Pokemon drew back toward them and began edging out of the open space.

Ethan noticed their intention at once. He had committed his entire team to this fight; letting the executives escape now would make all that effort pointless.

"Surround them!" he called to his Pokemon.

They spread out and blocked Apollo and Athena's routes away. The two executives realized Ethan meant to keep them there and tried to move faster.

But the situation had reversed. Outmatched in both numbers and strength now, how could they simply leave?

Ethan's Pokemon closed around them like a net, leaving only Gengar at his side to guard him. As the circle tightened, the space in which Apollo and Athena could move shrank to a small patch of ground.

Faint police sirens sounded from the street outside. The executives knew they were nearly out of time.

Escape had become almost impossible.

Athena stared at Ethan. With nearly all his Pokemon away from his side, a ruthless idea seized her. "Tyranitar, use Hyper Beam!" she shouted.

Tyranitar was Apollo's Pokemon, but it obeyed her command. It opened its great jaws. Terrifying energy gathered in its mouth, then shot straight toward Ethan!

If they could take Ethan down, his Pokemon would surely lose their composure. Their own crisis would be over at once!

Chapter 514: The Executives Are Captured

Athena's idea was sound enough.

To surround the executives, Ethan's Pokemon had spread out. All of them were some distance away, too far to rescue him at once.

And Tyranitar's Hyper Beam was immensely powerful. If it struck Ethan, it would leave nothing of him behind.

What Athena did not know was why, with so many Pokemon helping to surround them, Ethan had kept Gengar at his side.

Hyper Beam shot toward Ethan, its tremendous energy seeming to warp the air around it.

Ethan did not move. He looked wholly unconcerned for his safety.

Seeing him neither dodge nor try to block, Athena's face twisted into a savage grin.

What a fool. He would regret his arrogance in a moment!

No. He probably would not even have time for regret.

The beam closed the distance in an instant. Ethan could almost feel its heat.

He would have liked to dodge it himself, if he could. But Hyper Beam was too fast and covered too wide an area. How could a human body get clear in time?

At the last possible moment, Gengar flashed in front of him. With a cackling laugh, it formed a Shadow Ball and hurled it straight into the Hyper Beam.

Boom!

The two attacks exploded the instant they met.

A tremendous burst of energy spread outward from the impact. Dazzling light swallowed the Pokemon nearby.

The shock wave whipped Athena's bangs across her face. She raised a hand against the blast, then hurriedly looked toward Ethan as the light faded. He was still standing there, completely unharmed!

Gengar had shielded him from every trace of the explosion's force.

Damn it!

Athena knew Ethan had a Gengar of unfathomable strength, but she had never imagined it could stop a Hyper Beam.

The two moves were not remotely equal in power. Hyper Beam could shatter rocks and melt trees and buildings. Yet that small Shadow Ball had canceled it out!

She could hardly believe her eyes. Gengar was absurdly strong!

The explosion also seemed to guide the police cars in the distance. Their sirens grew louder. Brakes squealed, and several cars entered the open ground and stopped at the edge of the battlefield.

Looker and Erika were first to step out. Before they could take in the scene, two flashes of red light showed that Ethan had recalled something into Poke Balls.

Looker gave it no thought. He hurried over to Ethan and let out a breath of relief when he saw him unharmed.

Then he looked across the battlefield. Ethan's Pokemon had Apollo and Athena surrounded. Looker's face brightened.

"You really are something. You caught them!"

Ethan shook his head. "It's a little early to say I've caught them. I have them trapped, though."

Erika came to Ethan's side as well. She paid no attention to Team Rocket, looking him over carefully instead.

"Are you all right?"

"What could have happened to me?" Ethan said with a smile. "Those two are the ones in trouble."

"Good. That explosion frightened me. I was worried about you."

The more time Ethan spent with Erika, the more certain he became that she would make a wonderful wife and mother one day.

By then, a large number of officers had surrounded the area. Ethan waved his Pokemon back, and the officers' Pokemon immediately took their places.

Looker and his officers could handle what remained. Ethan was no longer needed in the fight.

He stepped back with Erika and watched.

Looker faced Apollo and Athena. "Surrender now. You have nowhere left to run!"

Even trapped, the two executives would not give up without a fight. They ordered their Pokemon to attack again. But they were facing several times their number in trained officers, and even a Pokemon as strong as Tyranitar gradually lost ground.

Golbat and Kabutops fell. Lickitung and Vileplume ran out of strength too.

Finally, the officers' Pokemon subdued Sneasel and Persian. The two Team Rocket executives had no strength left with which to resist.

Officers rushed in and fastened handcuffs around their wrists.

With the matter settled, Ethan felt a great weight lift from his chest.

It was finally over...

Without their Pokemon, even executives were ordinary people.

He still did not know what had happened between Giovanni and the four executives. But with Apollo, Athena, and Lance captured, Team Rocket had undoubtedly lost much of its strength.

The days when Team Rocket could ambush him seemed far behind him. Giovanni, hidden away in the shadows, was unlikely to come looking for trouble either.

Apart from Giovanni remaining at large, everything seemed to be moving toward a happy conclusion.

Looker had the two executives placed in a police car and gave his officers a few more instructions. When he was done, he returned to Ethan.

"Ethan, my friend, I can't thank you enough for your help today!"

Ethan waved a hand lazily. They knew each other too well for formalities.

Looker glanced at Erika, cleared his throat, and put an arm around Ethan's shoulders to lead him aside.

"Ahem. Ethan, my friend, your Pokemon are so powerful that nothing seems beyond them. I admire that. But there's something I ought to tell you. Miss Erika is a fine woman, but Miss Sabrina is wonderful too. Don't try to keep a foot in both camps and end up losing them both."

Ethan was a friend Looker trusted and got along with, and he was especially popular with women. Looker did not want him to make a mess of his relationships.

Ethan felt a little embarrassed. He had not expected even Looker to worry about his love life. "Don't worry. I know what I'm doing."

Yet despite saying it, he still did not know what to do about his feelings for Erika.

He could never bring himself to give her up. Pretending he felt nothing for her would be lying to himself.

But if he followed his heart and accepted Erika's feelings, where would that leave Sabrina?

He sighed. What a headache.

Chapter 515: Whitney and Miltank

After the incident with Team Rocket, neither Ethan nor Erika felt much like challenging a Gym.

It was already noon, and Ethan's Pokemon had spent some of their strength in the fight. He decided to give them a day to rest and challenge Whitney the following morning.

For the rest of the day, he made good on his promise to Erika early. They explored Goldenrod City together, visiting nearly every major sight recommended in their travel guide.

They shopped, ate desserts, and enjoyed the afternoon.

That evening, they took rooms at a hotel near the Gym. After a night's rest and breakfast the next morning, they finally stepped through the doors of the Goldenrod Gym again.

Unlike on their first visit, Whitney was there.

A staff member led Ethan to the battlefield, where he met a cheerful-looking girl with red hair in twin tails.

Like the type Whitney specialized in, the arena looked thoroughly ordinary. Tiered spectator seats surrounded it. The packed earth underfoot was marked with white lines. From every angle, it seemed well suited to a Normal-type Gym.

"Welcome to the Goldenrod Gym. I'm Whitney, the Gym Leader," she said as they approached.

Ethan took a closer look at her. She seemed about sixteen or seventeen, pretty and full of youthful energy. She wore a white short-sleeved shirt, denim shorts, and green-and-black striped socks.

He went straight to the point. "Hello, Whitney. I'm here to challenge your Gym."

"I know who you are," Whitney said with a smile. "I watched your matches at the Indigo League and heard about you from other Gym Leaders. They all said you're an amazing Trainer. It's good to finally meet you!"

Then she added, "And thank you for defeating Team Rocket yesterday and rescuing all those hostages."

"You heard about what happened at the TV station?" Ethan asked in surprise.

"Of course!" Whitney smiled. "There isn't much that happens in a Gym city without its Leader finding out. I should have gone to help, but I happened to be out. By the time I heard, you'd already taken care of everything."

Unlike Chuck and Bugsy, Whitney already knew something about him. That meant he would have to use the second approach to his Gym challenge today.

"I was only nearby and happened to be able to help," Ethan said lightly. Then he explained what he wanted. "If you're willing, I'd like you to use your strongest Pokemon against me."

"Of course!" Whitney nodded. "I was thinking the same thing. I want a real battle with a Champion like you!"

She turned to Erika. "You must be Miss Erika. You're very pretty! I hear you're a Gym Leader too. Is that right?"

"You're too kind, Whitney. You're lovely yourself." Erika gave a small, courteous bow. Since Whitney knew Ethan, Erika was not surprised that she knew of her as well. "I am a Gym Leader. Right now, I'm traveling with Ethan."

It was their first meeting, and their compliments were polite enough. But Whitney noticed the gentle glance Erika cast toward Ethan when she spoke of traveling with him.

Whitney was no sheltered child. She could tell there was more between the two of them.

Were they a couple?

When the introductions were over, a fashionably dressed female staff member came to the middle of the field to referee.

"I'll explain the rules. Each side will use three Pokemon. The first Trainer to defeat all three of the other Trainer's Pokemon wins!"

Ethan nodded. Erika quietly wished him luck, then took a seat nearby to watch.

Once Ethan and Whitney stood in their respective Trainer areas, Whitney, as the Gym Leader, brought out her first Pokemon.

She threw a Poke Ball. Blue light flashed, and a pink, cow-like Pokemon appeared before Ethan.

"This is the partner I trust mostMiltank!"

Miltank looked much like a cow, though pinker and cuter. The species was entirely female; Tauros was its male counterpart.

A Miltank could produce twenty liters of nutritious milk a day. As on Earth, its milk had become part of countless households' daily lives, and demand for it was enormous.

Speaking of milk, Ethan discreetly glanced at Whitney's figure. Perhaps she had grown up drinking Miltank milk; she looked surprisingly mature for her age.

Miltank were common on farms, but Ethan had yet to meet a Trainer who used one in battle.

Not knowing much about the species, he took out his Pokedex and pointed it at Miltank.

"Beep. Miltank, the Milk Cow Pokemon. A Normal-type. Gentle by nature, it does not like fighting people. Children who drink its milk are said to grow into healthy, strong adults. Because Miltank is also sturdy and powerful, some Trainers use it in battle."

Even the Pokedex devoted most of its description to Miltank as a dairy Pokemon. Its battling ability received only a passing mention.

Ethan put the Pokedex away, disappointed, and considered what to send against it.

He still remembered Whitney's Miltank defeating all three of Ash's Pokemon in the animated series. That alone said plenty about its strength.

Yet Whitney had chosen her ace for the first round. Ethan had no idea what other Pokemon she might use afterward. He could not underestimate her.

It also showed that Whitney meant what she had said. She had brought her strongest team and intended to battle him at full strength.

After some thought, Ethan decided to send out Tyranitar.

Against a Pokemon that fought with strength, he would use one that could answer in kind.

Besides, his Tyranitar had lost to Apollo's the day before. It still had plenty of room to grow, and this was a good chance to sharpen its power.

The moment Tyranitar appeared, it showed its imposing nature. It threw back its head and roared toward the high ceiling.

"Tyranitar? That's quite a presence," Whitney said, instinctively covering her ears. She clearly respected a Pokemon this strong.

Seeing both Pokemon ready, the referee raised her flag.

"The Goldenrod Gym badge match between challenger Ethan and Gym Leader Whitney begins now!"

Chapter 516: The Powerful Little Cow

"Miltank, use Rollout!"

At Whitney's command, Miltank broke into a run. It gathered speed, leaped high, and curled into a spinning wheel. When it landed, it rolled straight toward Tyranitar like a living cannonball.

It moved so fast that friction sent sand spraying from the hard-packed ground.

"Tyranitar, use Stone Edge!"

Ethan had seen Rollout before. Rather than meet it head-on, he chose a ranged attack to test how tough Miltank was.

Sharp stones rose from the ground and thrust toward it. Miltank did not even try to dodge. It plowed into the first stone at full speed!

Bang! Bang! Bang!

The force of the impact shattered the stone. Miltank smashed through the others in quick succession without losing momentum and kept rolling toward Tyranitar.

It was called a sturdy, powerful Pokemon for good reason. That body was formidable!

Thud!

Miltank finally struck Tyranitar with a tremendous crash. Tyranitar appeared to have taken the full force of the blow, but its armor was so thick that the attack did little damage.

Whitney was not concerned.

"Miltank, one more time!"

If one hit was not enough, she would keep at it. Eventually Tyranitar would reach its limit.

When Ethan saw Miltank repeat the move, he changed tactics.

"Catch it!"

Tyranitar spread its arms and waited for the right moment. As Miltank closed in, it wrapped both arms tightly around its spinning body.

Scrrrape!

Miltank's body ground against the armor on Tyranitar's arms. Its momentum forced Tyranitar several steps backward, but the hold slowed Miltank's spin until it stopped in Tyranitar's grasp.

"Now's our chance!" Ethan's eyes lit up. "Use Payback!"

Payback was a physical Dark-type move that built power before striking. At this range, there was no way Miltank could evade it.

Tyranitar raised its right hand, gathered energy there, and brought it down hard on Miltank. Miltank shot back toward Whitney's half of the field like a volleyball struck with all one's strength.

Rumble, rumble...

It rolled to a stop in front of Whitney. Its thick hide had spared it serious harm; aside from a few scrapes, it was still in good shape.

"Impressive! You actually stopped that move!" Whitney looked at Tyranitar with approval. Miltank's Rollout had given countless challengers trouble, and many had lost to it outright. She had not expected Tyranitar to break through it so easily.

Ethan smiled. Against overwhelming strength, a clever technique could only do so much.

Once Miltank stood again, Whitney changed her approach.

"Use Zen Headbutt!"

Miltank charged across the field. This time it did not roll. After passing the midpoint, it launched itself forward like a projectile, aiming its large head at Tyranitar.

Charging straight in again?

Ethan shook his head. Did she think the strength of this miniature Godzilla was just for show?

If a Tauros had used that move, its horns might have made the charge intimidating. This was a young cow with no horns at all.

"Use Dark Pulse!"

Tyranitar opened its mouth and fired a wave of Dark-type energy at Miltank.

Miltank could not dodge in midcharge. It plunged into the Dark Pulse, but its sturdy body carried it through the attack and into Tyranitar's lower belly.

Whitney did not stop there. "Jump and use Body Slam!"

Miltank regained its balance, sprang high, and spread its limbs as it came crashing down toward Tyranitar.

Body Slam was a physical Normal-type move whose force depended in part on the user's size and strength. Given Miltank's weight, even Tyranitar would have trouble taking a direct hit.

"Tyranitar, use Iron Defense!"

A blue-green glow covered Tyranitar, greatly strengthening its defenses.

It had barely finished using Iron Defense when Miltank landed on it with crushing force.

Ethan had never been landed on by a cow and did not intend to find out how it felt. Tyranitar's pained expression told him enough. Thanks to Iron Defense, though, it gritted its teeth and held on.

Miltank had now used its three main attacks. It was Ethan's turn to strike back.

As a Normal-type Pokemon that relied chiefly on physical attacks, Miltank did most of its fighting up close. Having failed to defeat Tyranitar early, it had few ways left to overcome it. The battle was turning against it.

"Use Hyper Beam!"

The two Pokemon were almost touching. Ethan had no fear that Miltank would dodge.

Tyranitar opened its jaws and released a powerful blast of energy.

Hyper Beam struck Miltank square in the chest and drove it out of the battlefield into the wall beneath the spectator seats.

When the beam faded, Miltank slid down the wall and collapsed.

The referee raised her colored flag. "Miltank is unable to battle! Tyranitar wins the first round!"

Whitney sighed and recalled Miltank, though she did not look especially downcast. "Everyone was right about you. You really are strong!"

"Your Miltank is strong too," Ethan said courteously. "If I'd used a different Pokemon, those attacks might have beaten it already."

He meant it. Most Pokemon would have struggled to withstand Rollout, Zen Headbutt, and Body Slam in succession unless they could evade Miltank or had exceptional defenses.

Whitney clearly appreciated the reassurance from someone stronger than herself.

"Miltank really is the partner I trust most." Smiling, she took another Poke Ball from her pocket. "Now for my second Pokemon. Come out, Ambipom!"

Chapter 517: Whitney's Mistake

Blue light flashed, and a purple, monkey-like Pokemon appeared before Ethan. It had a forked crest on its head and two long, unusual tails.

Ethan pointed his Pokedex at it.

"Beep. Ambipom, the Long Tail Pokemon. A Normal-type. Ambipom live in large groups high in enormous trees. Their tails can handle so many tasks with such dexterity that they barely use their hands anymore. They link tails to form a ring, sharing their feelings and strengthening their bonds. People are sometimes invited into the ring. If Ambipom wraps both tails around you, it truly feels close to you."

Ambipom could often be found in forests across Johto and other regions. They traveled in groups and attacked people or Pokemon that entered their territory.

Ambipom evolved from Aipom. Though it was seldom seen in the city, Ethan knew something about it.

He remembered Ash catching an Aipom later in his travels, then trading it to Dawn. It eventually evolved into Ambipom.

The species was fast and agile. It would not be easy to fight.

After considering his options, Ethan recalled Tyranitar and sent out Scizor.

If his opponent had strange tails, he would answer with a Pokemon whose pincers were just as distinctive.

Whitney studied Scizor as it appeared before Ambipom.

Scizor's Steel typing would halve the damage from Ambipom's Normal-type attacks. Ambipom also relied on its two tails for most of its offense, and Scizor's huge pincers might leave it little room to use them.

So that was why Ethan had chosen Scizor. It was a clever choice.

When the round began, both Pokemon charged.

Scizor swung in with Slash. Ambipom braced one tail against the ground and lifted itself out of reach, then snapped its other tail at Scizor's head. Scizor blocked with its right pincer.

Suddenly, Ambipom let out a piercing cry. Caught off guard, Scizor startled and froze for a moment. Ambipom seized the opening and struck Scizor over and over with its long tails.

Ethan saw the sequence clearly. Ambipom had used Astonish to create an opening, then followed with Fury Swipes.

The combination flowed so smoothly that it had plainly been practiced many times.

Another Pokemon might have taken serious damage from it. But Ambipom was striking Scizor, whose body was as hard as steel.

Its tails were strong, yet every blow against Scizor's red, armored chest made only a dull thud.

Fortunately, Astonish had not left Scizor flinching.

"Scizor, use Night Slash!"

Scizor swung both pincers at once. But just as it attacked, Ambipom wound a tail around each pincer and bound them together like handcuffs. Scizor could not complete the move.

Ethan had expected Ambipom's tails to be flexible. He had not imagined it could use them like that.

Whitney smiled. "With its hands tied, how will it fight now?"

Ethan remained calm. "Use Iron Head!"

"What!?" Whitney's smile vanished.
