Scizor drew its head back, then yanked its pincers toward its body, pulling Ambipom close. Its hard red head slammed into Ambipom's face.

Bang!

Steel met bone. Ambipom nearly fainted from the impact.

It released its grip without thinking and dropped to the ground. Swaying as if drunk, it could barely stay on its feet.

"Now! Use X-Scissor!"

Scizor readied its attack. Seeing Ambipom still dazed, Whitney cried, "Ambipom, snap out of it!"

It heard her, but its head was spinning. It tried several times to stand steady and could not.

"It's over," Ethan said softly.

He was right. Scizor's X-Scissor struck Ambipom while it could hardly stand. Scizor followed immediately with another Slash and knocked it to the ground.

The referee raised her colored flag. "Ambipom is unable to battle! Scizor wins the second round!"

Whitney sighed with regret. Battles could turn like this. She had been doing well, but one mistaken decision had cost her the round.

Had her strategy really been wrong? She had won against many other Trainers by binding a Pokemon's arms. What she had misjudged was just how hard Scizor's head was.

Against another opponent, perhaps it would have been Ethan's Pokemon lying defeated.

Whitney pushed the thought aside, recalled Ambipom with a rueful smile, and took out her last Poke Ball.

"You're amazing. You've defeated two of my Pokemon so easily. No wonder you're a Champion! Now, my final Pokemoncome out, Lopunny!"

The ball opened, and a fluffy, athletic-looking brown rabbit appeared before Ethan.

Lopunny...

Ethan rubbed his chin. First a cow, then a monkey, and now a rabbit. Whitney's team was like a little zoo!

Lopunny were common in Sinnoh, Unova, Alola, and Galar, but wild ones had not been found in Johto.

As he had done with Ambipom, Ethan took out his Pokedex and aimed it at Lopunny.

"Beep. Lopunny, the Rabbit Pokemon. A Normal-type. It is highly alert and runs with light, bounding steps. If it senses danger, it wraps itself in the soft, fluffy fur at the tips of its ears and leaps nimbly away. Though it dislikes fighting, it can deliver tremendously powerful kicks when threatened."

Chapter 518: The Plain Badge

Lopunny really did resemble a rabbit from Earth. It had pink eyes, a small nose, and two long eyebrows. Most of its fur was brown, while its feet and fluffy tufts were cream-colored.

But Ethan would not underestimate it just because it looked like a rabbit.

People said even a cornered rabbit would bite. In this world of Pokemon, that was all the more reason to be careful.

Whitney had chosen Lopunny for this final round. She must trust its strength.

Tyranitar and Scizor had each fought a round already, so Ethan sent out Dragonite.

All three were still growing. None could yet carry a battle alone the way Gardevoir or Charizard could, so giving each of them a turn to train was important.

The two sides took their positions, ready to begin.

As soon as the referee lowered her flag, Lopunny showed what made it different.

It charged at Dragonite. Its powerful legs carried it across the field in a series of quick bounds, closing the distance with startling speed.

Before it reached Dragonite, it leaped again. In midair it brought both feet together and aimed a flying kick at its opponent.

Ethan could have ordered Dragonite to fly out of reach. Instead, he decided to meet Lopunny head-on.

If it liked attacking from the front so much, he would give it a fight.

"Dragonite, use Dragon Rage!"

Facing Lopunny's airborne kick, Dragonite opened its mouth and released a blue-green shock wave.

Just before Dragon Rage could hit, Lopunny twisted nimbly and spun several times in the air. It somehow held itself aloft long enough for the wave to pass beneath it, then resumed its kick and struck Dragonite in the stomach.

Oh? Ethan's eyes lit up.

That was impressive footwork and an impressive kick!

But this was hardly the time to admire his opponent. Ethan recovered and gave another order. "Dragonite, use Thunder Wave!"

Against an opponent this agile, electricity was the best way to restrict its movement.

Sparks flashed from the two antennae on Dragonite's head and raced toward Lopunny.

At such close range, another Pokemon might have been struck and paralyzed. Lopunny used a sudden burst of strength to spring backward, easily avoiding the current.

Even from that brief exchange, Ethan could tell Lopunny would be harder to handle than Whitney's first two Pokemon.

"Lopunny, use Quick Attack!"

As it came at Dragonite again, Ethan called, "Dragonite, fly higher!"

With Lopunny proving so troublesome, he would have Dragonite use its advantage and attack from above.

Whitney watched Dragonite rise and thought for a moment. This was exactly what she had worried about when Ethan sent it out.

On the ground, Lopunny's jumping ability could let it dance around an opponent. Once Dragonite was in the air, things became difficult. Lopunny could leap up after it, but no jump could give it the same freedom of movement as wings.

"Use Wing Attack!"

Dragonite circled to build speed, spread its small wings, and dove toward Lopunny.

Lopunny was not going to wait for the hit. It ran across the field at speed, trying to shake Dragonite off.

There was no cover here. However it moved, it could not simply outrun an attack from above.

Dragonite closed the short distance in an instant. Just as it seemed about to collide with Lopunny, Lopunny leaped high into the air again.

The same trick would not work on Ethan twice.

As Lopunny dodged, Dragonite climbed sharply alongside it. Electricity crackled around both its fists.

Thunder Punch!

An electrified fist drove toward Lopunny's cheek. Everything happened too quickly for Lopunny to twist away in midair this time.

Bang!

Thunder Punch struck its face and knocked it down to the ground.

Thump...

Lopunny rolled several times. Its thick tufts of fur cushioned the fall, and it had not landed too hard. But as it tried to rise, paralysis seized its body and almost stopped it from moving.

Thunder Punch had triggered paralysis!

"Lopunny, hang on!" Whitney cried anxiously.

Lopunny tried to recover, but determination alone could not shake the effect.

Seeing Dragonite fly toward it again, Lopunny turned and ran, hoping to delay until the paralysis passed. Slowed as it was, it could not escape Dragonite's flying speed. Dragonite closed from behind like a hawk tracking its prey.

"Use Dragon Rush!"

At Ethan's command, Dragonite tucked in its wings and hurtled toward Lopunny like an arrow loosed from a bow.

"Lopunny, dodge!"

Hearing the rush of air behind it, Lopunny looked back. Dragonite was drawing closer, its large yellow head and little horn filling more and more of Lopunny's view.

Bang!

The collision lifted Lopunny off the ground. By the time it landed, it had flown out of the field. Its eyes rolled back, and it lay unconscious.

The referee took one look and raised her colored flag. "Lopunny is unable to battle! Challenger Ethan wins the Gym match!"

Another loss...

Whitney sighed and recalled Lopunny. Disappointment showed plainly on her pretty face.

Those had been her three strongest Pokemon, yet she had not won a single round. She felt frustrated, but there was nothing she could do about it. If she could not win, she could not win.

Though her spirits were low, she quickly gathered herself, smiled, and walked over to Ethan.

Erika reached his side at the same moment. Whitney looked at the handsome man before her and spoke sincerely. "You really are amazing. I couldn't beat you. Here, this is my Plain Badge. Please take it."

Chapter 519: A Third Encounter with the Week Siblings

Ethan looked down at the Plain Badge in his hand.

Like the type favored by the Gym that awarded it, the badge was remarkably plain.

It was a yellow diamond with a white border. Simple and ordinary, much like Olivine City's Mineral Badge, it looked as though no one had seen a need to spend much time designing it.

Ethan took out his badge case and placed the Plain Badge in its last empty space. Looking at the two full rows of eight badges, he let out a breath of relief.

He had collected all eight. Now he only had to wait for the Silver Conference to begin.

After exchanging contact numbers with Whitney, he and Erika said goodbye and left the Goldenrod Gym.

The first thing they did was head for a nearby Pokemon Center. None of Ethan's Pokemon was hurt; he wanted to register for the tournament in advance.

He had learned of the option by chance. Rather than queue at the venue in the days before the tournament, a Trainer with eight badges could register at any Pokemon Center.

At the Goldenrod City Pokemon Center, Ethan told Nurse Joy what he needed.

"You're registering for the Conference? Please give me your badges and Pokedex."

She took his badge case and scanned it. Once she had verified the badges, she connected his Pokedex to her computer.

Ethan's records appeared on the screen. Nurse Joy could see his achievements.

Indigo League Champion.

Orange League Honorable Trainer.

Sea Hero of the Whirl Islands.

He had entered only three different competitions, but he had won every one. What an impressive Trainer!

After a few keystrokes, Nurse Joy returned his badge case and Pokedex.

"You're registered. I hope you do well at the Conference."

"Thank you," Ethan said. "When does the Silver Conference begin?"

"On the first of next month."

"And where will it be held?"

"As in previous years, at Silver Stadium in Silver Town, at Mt. Silver."

So, Mt. Silver on the first of next month. Ethan counted the days in his head. He had more than half a month. That was enough time to reach Mt. Silver and make any final adjustments.

Outside the Pokemon Center, he and Erika stood on the street and discussed where to go next.

"Where should we go now?" Erika asked. "Straight to Silver Town?"

"We have time as long as we arrive before the Conference," Ethan said with a smile. "Why don't I take you somewhere else first? You came to catch Grass-type Pokemon, didn't you? And I'm sure there are other places you'd like to see."

"Finding a Pokemon is partly a matter of chance. But there is somewhere I'd like to go..." Erika took her travel guide from her bag, turned to the second page, and pointed to a picture of a bustling city on the water. "I'd like to see this place."

Ethan read the caption: "Altomare, the City of Waterthe most beautiful city in the world!"

The most beautiful city in the world? That was quite a claim.

Still, if Erika wanted to go, Ethan had no objection.

Altomare lay offshore to the south of the peninsula where Azalea Town stood. It was far enough from the Johto mainland that they would have to travel by ship.

A cruise ship sailed there directly from Goldenrod City. They made their plans and started toward the port, but before they had gone far, several people blocked their path.

It was an odd group: a woman around twenty-four or twenty-five with two very young boys.

"I finally found you! I've been looking for ages!" she said.

Ethan was puzzled. He had never met these three. Why had they been looking for him?

"Who are you?"

Once they introduced themselves, he understood.

"We're the Week Siblings. I'm Monica, and these are my younger brothers, Santos and Sunny."

That one sentence was enough to make Ethan sigh.

He had beaten one sibling and another had appeared. Then he had beaten two, and now all the remaining siblings had come at once! He had finally met every one of the Week Siblings.

"Hello," he said.

Monica smiled. "I expect you know why we're here?"

"You want to battle me?"

"Of course."

"I knew this day would come. Let's go somewhere suitable."

They had only just left the Pokemon Center, so the group retraced its steps and went to the outdoor battlefields behind it.

Several children were already battling there. Ethan's group passed them and took another field.

He knew the rules by now: defeat each sibling to earn their respective badge. Everyone understood, and no one bothered to explain them again.

Even without looking at their faces or ages, the siblings' day-themed names made their relationship apparent.

For example, as Ethan took his place in the Trainer area, the youngest boy hurried to the opposite side. Monica had introduced him as Sunny. He was only seven or eight, and even his name marked him as the last of the seven siblings.

It was fortunate their parents had stopped at seven children. An eighth might have been hard to name.

The children battling nearby noticed another match about to begin and turned to look. They recognized the Week Siblings at once.

"Hey, it's the Week Siblings!"

"That's Monica!"

"I can't believe they're here!"

They gathered excitedly around the field. Here in Johto, the local Week Siblings were evidently better known than a Champion whose victories had come in other regions.

Sunny rubbed his nose, plainly enjoying the attention. He glanced at Ethan and was the first to bring out a Pokemon.

Blue light flashed, and a Heracross appeared before Ethan. It raised its forelimbs as if to show off its strength.

Ethan thought for a moment. He did not look down on Sunny for being young, but sending out one of his usual Pokemon would hardly be fair.

He chose Eevee.

If his opponent was a child, he could battle with a Pokemon that had yet to evolve.

Chapter 520: Oh No, I'm the Villain

The first battle was fairly simple.

Sunny had been full of confidence beforehand, and his Heracross was strong compared with the Pokemon of other children his age. But under Ethan's direction, Eevee kept moving, using its agility to stay out of Heracross's reach. It never gave Heracross a chance to bring its strength to bear. After wearing it down, Eevee won easily with Swift.

Heracross itself had been capable. Sunny's commands, however, reflected his age and experience: attack, attack, and attack again! Ethan had seen the opening that created and used it.

The win had come easily. The difference was less in the Pokemon's strength than in tactics and judgment.

"What? A Week Sibling lost?"

The children watching began to whisper when Sunny's Heracross fell. Only then did they turn their attention to Ethan.

They had been rooting for Sunny and had seen how nimbly Eevee moved, but their confidence in the Week Siblings had made them believe he would somehow turn the fight around.

Instead, his disadvantage had simply grown until he lost. The children stared at Ethan, wondering who he was.

"You idiot! You didn't even touch that Eevee once. How embarrassing. Watch me!"

Santos pushed his younger brother aside. Though only ten, he had more experience and a little more maturity than Sunny, and he was sure he could win.

To him, Ethan's Eevee did not look difficult to handle. Sunny had only lost so badly because he had been foolish.

"Come out, my Pokemon!"

Santos threw a Poke Ball, and a Houndour appeared on the field.

Ethan had fought Team Rocket's Houndoom many times. Houndour was its unevolved form, weaker in every respect, and he was familiar with how to face it.

He did not switch Pokemon. Eevee was still in good condition, so it stayed in the battle.

Once they began, Ethan found that Santos's Houndour was indeed more troublesome than Heracross, despite not yet evolving.

Houndour and Eevee were similar in build and habits. By the sort of classification used on Earth, both were canine-like Pokemon. Ethan could not simply keep circling and evading as he had against Heracross.

This fight would come down to the Pokemon's abilities and their Trainers' commands.

As a battler, Ethan was far more skilled than Santos.

The two Pokemon traded move after move in a long, close fight. Both were covered in scrapes by the end. After one final clash, Houndour collapsed unconscious. Eevee swayed on its feet, but its stronger will kept it standing long enough to claim victory.

All told, the two battles had been fairly straightforward. Ethan showed little excitement over winning.

Santos walked off with the same disappointed look as his brother, and Monica stepped into the Trainer's position.

She had not expected either of the boys to win. Her older and stronger siblings had already lost to Ethan, so these two children had stood little chance.

She did not expect to beat him herself. Even so, a battle against a Trainer this strong would help both her and her Pokemon grow.

"It's my turn," Monica said with a smile. "If you beat me too, every one of the Week Siblings will have lost to you. Not many people can say they've done that."

Ethan did not underestimate a woman five or six years older than himself. As the eldest, Monica was likely to have more experience, a steadier outlook, and more ways to challenge him.

When her Pokemon appeared, Ethan sensed something unusual about it even before he took in its appearance.

It was a Shiny Flygon. Its coloring differed strikingly from that of an ordinary Flygon.

Flygon was not native to Johto or Kanto. Monica's partnership with one suggested that she had traveled to other regions. That was another reason not to take her lightly.

Still...

A Shiny Pokemon. Ethan practically drooled with envy.

When would he finally catch one of his own?

Bringing his attention back to the battle, he considered what to use against this Ground- and Dragon-type Pokemon.

After some thought, he chose Dragonite.

They were both Dragon-types. Neither needed to hold back. This would be a battle between dragons!

Monica was surprised to see him send out Dragonite.

Dragon-type attacks were effective against both of their Pokemon. Neither side had a safe type advantage, and one mistake could easily turn the battle. Was Ethan really that confident?

"Go on, Monica!" Sunny called from the side.

"Avenge usand all our older brothers and sisters!" Santos shouted.

Monica hardly reacted, but Ethan's eyebrow twitched.

Avenge them? Why did that make him sound like the villain?

He had defeated the siblings, yes, but only in ordinary Trainer battles, and he had accepted their challenges rather than seeking them out. How had the two boys decided he was the bad guy?

The children watching joined in after seeing the Week Siblings lose twice.

"You can do it, Monica!"

"The Week Siblings are the best!"

"Beat that man, Monica!"

They were Johto natives. Naturally, they favored the local siblings they had known about for years.

Monica quieted her brothers, then gave Ethan an apologetic look. She understood their wish for their sister to avenge them after a loss. But with the young spectators joining in, the cheering had begun to sound as though everyone had united against Ethan.

That was not what the Week Siblings stood for. Still, Monica did not know the children, and she could hardly lecture them.

Chapter 521: Sandstorm and Rain Dance

Flygon resembled a dragonfly, just as its name suggested. It was no insect, though, but a true Dragon-type Pokemon.

Most of its body was pale green. Two green antennae rose from its head, and two green wings with red edges spread from its back. Its long tail had eight sections, alternating between pale and darker green.

Flygon normally lived in hot, dry regions. Red, dome-shaped structures covered its eyes and protected them from sand.

It was not native to Kanto or Johto, and Ethan had seldom encountered one. He took out his Pokedex and pointed it at Flygon.

"Beep. Flygon, the Mystic Pokemon. A Ground- and Dragon-type. Flygon beats its powerful wings to stir up desert sand and conceal itself, so it is usually surrounded by a sandstorm in flight and rarely appears before people. It sometimes has Krookodile hide in the storm and shares the prey it catches with them. The sound of its wings in a sandstorm is said to resemble a woman's beautiful singing, earning it the name 'desert spirit.' Prey drawn in by the sound lose their senses, are caught in the storm, and become Flygon's food. People have also gone missing in the desert this way."

Ethan put the Pokedex away and rubbed his chin as he watched the great dragonfly-like Pokemon hovering above the ground.

That description made it sound like a remarkably sophisticated hunter. It worked with other Pokemon and even used sound to lure its prey into a trap!

Perhaps the resemblance to a dragonfly went beyond its appearance. Its habits had an insect's ruthless edge. Insects could be far crueler than humans or other animals.

There was no referee for this informal match. As soon as both Pokemon were ready, the battle began.

Flygon beat its thin wings rapidly and lifted its nearly two-meter body into the air. Dragonite refused to be outdone. It flapped its little wings and rose opposite Flygon.

Without waiting for their Trainers' commands, the two Pokemon met and grappled in the air.

The fights with Sunny and Santos had been little more than appetizers, chances to warm up. The battle with Monica was the main course. Both its intensity and the strength of the Pokemon were on another level.

"Flygon, use Supersonic!"

"Dragonite, use Safeguard!"

Supersonic sent out waves that could confuse its target. Ethan had Dragonite use Safeguard to protect itself from that sort of condition.

Visible waves of sound swept over Dragonite, but under Safeguard's protection it remained unaffected.

Seeing that Supersonic would not work, Monica gave another order. "Flygon, use Sandstorm!"

Yellow sand blew in from nowhere and covered the entire area behind the Pokemon Center. It obscured everyone's sight and swallowed both Pokemon.

Monica wanted a battlefield favorable to Flygon, where it could defeat Dragonite from within the sand.

Ethan was untroubled. "Dragonite, use Rain Dance."

Dragonite roared at the sky. Clouds suddenly covered what had been a clear day. There was no thunder or lightning; large drops of rain simply began to fall.

If Monica wanted to change the weather, he could answer in kind. Rain mixed with the sand and fell from the sky as mud.

Ethan had anticipated it and released Gardevoir. She used her psychic power to form an invisible barrier above Ethan and Erika, keeping every bit of mud off them.

The Week Siblings and the children watching were not so lucky.

Monica stayed where she stood to direct Flygon. Mud soon speckled her face and clothes. Her younger brothers were so concerned about Flygon that they kept their attention fixed on the fight.

The children ran in alarm to an awning nearby and watched from a distance, but they had moved too slowly to avoid the mud completely.

They had only seen battles this fierce on television. Now that one was happening before them, they did not want to miss a moment, however unpleasant the weather became.

The two Pokemon in the middle of the battlefield suffered most.

Mud surrounded them and badly obscured their vision. Even Flygon's specially protected eyes were uncomfortable when mud got into them.

Worse for Monica, Flygon's wings were large and thin. Once they were coated in mud, it could no longer stay aloft and had to land.

The packed earth below had softened under the muddy rain and become difficult to cross.

Fortunately, the downpour of mud lasted only a short while before it ended.

The sky cleared again. Apart from the mess left behind, there was little sign that the weather had changed at all.

Pokemon power had its limits. They could alter the weather for a time, but not change nature forever.

Dragonite was coated in mud too, and its flight was growing labored. Ethan called, "Use Dragon Rush!"

Dragonite climbed sharply, shedding some of the still-wet mud. After circling a few times, it dove at Flygon with tremendous speed.

"Flygon, get into the air!" Monica shouted.

A thick layer of mud weighed down Flygon's wings. It struggled to shake them clean, but as it finally tried to take flight, Dragonite struck it with all the force of its dive.

Bang!

Flygon was hurled a long way across the field. The impact also shook most of the mud from Dragonite's body.

With the attack successful, Ethan ordered Dragonite back into the air.

He had no wish to keep battling a Ground-type Pokemon this strong on ground that was difficult to move across.

Chapter 522: Setting Out for the City of Water

Flygon rolled several times across the ground and out of bounds, coming to rest on its back at Monica's feet.

Dragonite stood on the other side of the field, breathing a little hard. After the muddy rain, the two Pokemon had fought another short but fierce exchange. Dragonite had proved the stronger and ended the battle with Aqua Tail.

The match had gone fairly smoothly for Ethan. He had not faced any serious danger.

Monica recalled Flygon with a rueful smile. She and her brothers picked their way around the mud and came over to Ethan.

"You're truly strong. We were no match for you," she said sincerely. Santos and Sunny were plainly less ready than their sister to accept their losses.

Ethan smiled at the boys' childish stubbornness and said to Monica, "Your Flygon is strong too. If I hadn't broken up its Sandstorm, Dragonite might have been the one to fall."

Monica did not know whether he was simply being polite, but the words eased her disappointment.

She took a badge from her coat and offered it to him. "Here. This is my Invigoration Badge, proof that you beat me."

Santos and Sunny each brought out a badge too. Though reluctant, they held them out to Ethan.

"This is my Sound Sleep Badge."

"And this is my Laughter Badge."

Like the badges held by the other four Week Siblings, these three were nearly identical apart from their colors. Ethan accepted them without ceremony.

By defeating these last three siblings, he had collected every one of their badges.

"Thanks."

Monica did not want to linger after losing. "Well, perhaps we'll meet again someday. We should go wash up now."

Ethan had hardly noticed the mud until she mentioned it. He looked them over: all three were filthy, a sharp contrast to his clean clothes.

He watched them leave, and Erika came to his side.

"The Week Siblings are quite well known in Johto. How does it feel to have beaten all of them?"

"How does it feel?" Ethan laughed and shook his head. "I don't feel much, but at least I won't have to worry about them tracking me down again."

They left the battlefield and went straight to Goldenrod City's port.

There they bought tickets to Altomare, the City of Water. A city hailed as the most beautiful in the world drew ships from Goldenrod and many other places. More than a dozen vessels sailed between Altomare and a metropolis like Goldenrod every day.

...

"Long, long ago, an elderly couple lived on the island of Altomare. One day, they found an injured little brother and sister by the sea. They cared for the children, who gradually recovered."

"Then one day, an evil monster attacked the island. Just as it seemed Altomare would be swallowed up, the brother and sister changed before the old couple's eyes."

"They were the Eon Pokemon, Latios and Latias."

"The two Pokemon flew into the sky and called their companions. Together they brought a power that drove away the darkness: a jewel called the Soul Dew. Peace returned to the island. From then on, Latios and Latias often stayed there, and the evil Pokemon never attacked Altomare again."

On the ship's deck, Erika finished telling Ethan the legend and closed her travel guide.

Ethan reclined comfortably in a deck chair, wearing large sunglasses and holding a cocktail. He popped the cherry from his drink into his mouth, but behind the sunglasses, his eyes stayed on Erika.

She was a gifted storyteller. Her voice was gentle, and her tone rose and fell with the tale.

He could not help imagining that if they had children one day, Erika would tell them bedtime stories just like this.

She would make a wonderful wife and mother.

Before Ethan could respond to the legend, a girl nearby laughed. "Miss Erika tells that story beautifully, but it's only a fairy tale, isn't it?"

Her voice sounded familiar. Ethan and Erika turned to find Ash, Misty, and Brock, whom they had parted from not long ago.

"How do we keep running into you three?" Ethan pushed his sunglasses up and smiled at Misty. "The Soul Dew, Latios, and Latias are all real. They're still in that city today. Perhaps we'll even see them this time!"

Then he asked, "Are you going to Altomare too?"

"Of course!" Ash pulled a poster from his coat and showed it to Ethan. "We're entering the annual Pokemon water race. Are you two competing?"

"No. Erika and I are going on holiday." Ethan shook his head. "A Pokemon water race does sound interesting, though."

He took the poster and read it. A race would be held in Altomare soon. Competitors would stand in small boats and be towed by Water-type Pokemon through the city's winding waterways. The first to reach the finish would win a generous prize.

"Since you're here too, come with us!" Ash said eagerly. "Misty and I are both entering. Heh, I can't beat you in a Pokemon battle, but I'll definitely take first place in a race like this!"

"Honestly, where does that confidence come from?" Misty rolled her eyes at Ash, then said proudly, "I'm a Water-type Trainer. A race like this should suit me best. But as for first place... if Ethan decides to enter, he'll definitely win!"

Brock glanced at Misty and sighed helplessly.

He could see that she was Ethan's most devoted fan, beyond any hope of changing her mind. If anyone criticized or underestimated Ethan while she was around, she would mock them without mercy.

How had Ethan managed to win her over so completely?

Chapter 523: Maybe I Can Beat Ethan!

Altomare stood alone amid a vast expanse of sea. Apart from one tiny, deserted island, there was no other land within a hundred and fifty nautical miles.

Canals crisscrossed the city, and most people traveled by small boat. In that respect, it resembled Venice on Earth.

Or rather, Venice was clearly the model from which this city had been made.

Ethan, Erika, Ash, Misty, and Brock left the dock and strolled into the great city.

Before leaving the waterfront, they saw a museum and two stone pillars commemorating Latias and Latios. Perhaps, as Ethan had said, the legendary Pokemon really were close by.

Ash was impatient to enter the race. As soon as they disembarked, he led the others toward the registration desk. On the way they passed one clear, narrow canal after another. Fast boats sped along the water, and brightly colored, old-fashioned European houses with carved decorations lined the streets.

"It really is beautiful here," Misty said, looking from side to side. "No wonder they call it the most beautiful city in the world!"

As a Water-type Trainer, she obviously loved the place.

Ethan saw it differently. Beauty was a matter of taste. Altomare had a character all its own, but plenty of cities in this world impressed him just as much.

Nimbasa City in Unova, Lumiose City in Kalos, and Wyndon in Galar all came to mind.

The race's registration desk was inside the city's arena. After asking for directions, they found it easily.

There, a staff member explained that the water race was a customary part of Altomare's summer festival. Every year it drew crowds, brought the city substantial income, and awarded its winner an Altomare glass winner's medal.

At the mention of a medal, Ash's eyes lit up.

After Ethan, Ash, and Misty registered, Ash grinned at the other two. "Just watch. That medal is mine!"

Misty scoffed. "Don't brag. Ethan will win, and I'll come second. As for you, finishing anywhere but last would be an amazing result!"

"Oh, come on!" Ash groaned. "You never hold back, do you?"

The race was scheduled for nine the next morning. Altomare had been preparing for it for some time; almost every resident and visitor knew a major competition was about to take place.

The group checked into the Pokemon Center. Later they watched a splendid parade of flower-decked boats along the canal. That afternoon Ethan treated everyone to a lavish meal at a local restaurant.

It had become a habit. Almost every time he met Ash and his friends, Ethan bought them a feast.

Over dinner, he learned that Ash had earned seven badges. Once he won the Rising Badge at Blackthorn Gym, he too could register for the Silver Conference.

"Good luck, kid," Ethan said with a chuckle. "The Gym Leader there is Clair. She won't be easy to beat."

They returned to the Pokemon Center as the sun was setting.

Perhaps because he had eaten too much and wanted to work it off, Ash eagerly challenged Ethan to a battle. Ethan agreed.

They went to the battlefield behind the Center. Ethan sent out Eevee again, while Ash chose Pikachu.

The two Pokemon fought for a long time. At last, a panting Pikachu defeated Eevee with Iron Tail.

Ash was delighted. He knew Ethan had not used one of his strongest Pokemon, but beating any of Ethan's team filled him with hope.

Maybejust maybehe could defeat Ethan at this year's Silver Conference?

The thought set his heart pounding. He could hardly calm down.

He had never given up on the idea of beating Ethan!

...

After a night's rest and breakfast the following morning, Ethan and the others put on light shirts and shorts and arrived at the racecourse before the start.

The race would take place on the water. Light clothes would make it easier to move and less troublesome if they got wet.

The organizers provided each competitor with a board and a set of ropes. The racers would stand on the boards, secure themselves, and connect their boards to their Pokemon so they would not be thrown off.

Ethan had temporarily transferred Blastoise over the day before specifically for this race.

With a Pokemon that excelled in both endurance and explosive speed, he was confident he could win.

Erika and Brock were not competing. After cheering the others on, they stood on a nearby bridge, where a large screen showed the race live.

Ethan fitted the ropes around Blastoise and stepped onto his board.

He was in the city's widest canal. About thirty competitors had entered. Like runners at the start of a marathon, they lined up in several rows and waited for the signal.

The course twisted through Altomare's complicated waterways. The start was also the finish: they would loop around the city and return to this spot.

Before the race, Ethan had heard that the favorite was Ross, last year's winner.

Ross's Wailmer was famous for its speed. The previous year, it had led from the front and won by an overwhelming margin.

Ethan happened to stand in the middle of the group. Ross was diagonally ahead of him, while Ash and Misty stood nearby.

Both looked poised and confident, as though the favorite did not concern them at all.

The crowd grew more excited as the start drew close.

Three Natu and a Xatu perched together in a stack like a signal light. They spread their wings one after another. When the Xatu at the bottom gave its cry, the race began!

Chapter 524: The Water Race

More than thirty competitors surged forward almost as one.

Excited cheers rose around them, a confused, buzzing din. Ethan was wholly focused on the race and shut it all out.

With so many racers packed ahead, Blastoise had no room to use its full strength. For the moment, it stayed among the other Pokemon at a moderate pace.

That changed at a sharp ninety-degree turn. Some Pokemon could not steer well enough, while others had charged too hard to take the corner at speed. Their Trainers had to slow down, breaking up the formation and finally opening a gap in the solid wall ahead.

Blastoise accelerated at once. Its large body pushed through the other Pokemon, carrying Ethan past the middle group and up toward the front.

Ash and Misty followed close behind, their Pokemon agile enough to join the leaders.

Ash was racing with Totodile, and Misty with Corsola. Both were small. Once Blastoise had opened a path, they could slip through it easily.

Staff members waited at every turn along the waterways to point the racers in the right direction. No one had to worry about taking a wrong canal.

Spectators lined the banks throughout the course. Their numbers showed how popular the water race was.

The Pokemon swam hard. After another two or three turns, only a handful of competitors remained in the lead group, including Ethan, Ash, and Misty.

Only one racer was still ahead of them: Ross, the favorite, with his Wailmer.

As the reigning champion, Ross had started from an excellent position. With no one blocking him, Wailmer had reached full speed and opened a large gap over the racers behind.

That might seem unfair, but someone had to stand in front. Giving the place to last year's winner was the organizers' way of showing him respect.

Ethan's board cut through the canal, throwing spray to either side.

Ash and Misty kept pace nearby, and the gap between Ethan and Ross steadily narrowed.

When the course straightened again, all three accelerated and drew almost level with Ross.

The four raced abreast. Ethan and the others had speed on their side, but Ross was a local who knew these waterways intimately. He knew where to turn and where to slow down. Even when they briefly passed him, he would catch them at the next corner.

In the second half of the race, none of them held back. They pushed into an all-out sprint and left the next group farther and farther behind.

Then Ash had a mishap.

As they rounded a turn at high speed, Totodile failed to slow in time and towed Ash straight into a wall.

Ash tumbled into the water. A delay like that could ruin a race. By the time he climbed back up, several racers from the second group had passed him, and Ethan and the others were out of sight.

Ethan thought Ash would have little hope of catching up. To his astonishment, only a few turns later, Totodile and Ash's board were right behind them again!

Their speed was unbelievablealmost as though they were flying.

No, perhaps Totodile really was flying.

Ethan looked closely. Totodile was not swimming at all. It was standing on the water and running, its little legs pumping so quickly that sometimes they did not touch the surface.

It looked as though something invisible above the canal was pulling Totodile along.

Ethan looked overhead. At first he saw nothing, but when the sun struck at just the right angle, he caught the faint outline of something large holding the rope behind Totodile.

He understood and gave a helpless smile. Just as one would expect for the animated series' chosen hero, Ash had already caught the attention of Latias and Latios.

Which one was helping him? Latias or Latios?

Judging by their personalities, it had to be the younger sister, Latias.

The rest of the course seemed to pass in a flash. Around another turn, they returned to the main canal. The finish line lay just ahead.

With Latias's help, Totodile moved at astonishing speed. It shot past Ethan and the others and opened a clear lead.

Misty and Ross stared in shock. Neither had imagined Totodile could move like that.

Fortunately for the race, another shadow invisible to everyone else swooped over Totodile. It drew Totodile and Latias together into a narrow side canal.

That canal was not part of the course. Entering it took them away from the finish and left Ash almost no chance of winning.

Apparently Latios did not want his sister meddling in a human competition. He pulled Latias and Totodile off the course until they vanished from sight.

With Ash gone, only Ethan, Misty, and Ross remained in the lead group.

The finish was close. Ethan knew it was time to give everything, and he tugged on Blastoise's reins.

Blastoise understood. Its eyes hardened, and it drove toward the finish with all its strength.

The surge threw up waves that rocked even Wailmer, larger though it was. Misty's little Corsola was affected all the more.

Neither Pokemon gave up. Both pushed as hard as they could. Misty had confidently predicted Ethan would win, but now that the finish was in sight, excitement took over. She gritted her teeth and urged Corsola to sprint.

All three Pokemon fought for every bit of speed. In the end, Blastoise crossed the finish line first by the narrowest margin!

Ethan let out a breath. Before he could even feel the joy of winning, a vast roar of cheers surrounded him.

Chapter 525: A Guide Volunteers

Colored streamers showered Ethan. He smiled and waved to the crowd around him.

Behind him, Misty crouched on her board, a little dejected. She stroked Corsola gently and glanced toward Ethan.

She and Corsola had given everything they had, only to lose to him by the narrowest margin. Of course she was disappointed.

Even so, she was happy for Ethan. Losing to him was something she could accept. If anyone else had beaten her so closely, she would already be pouting and complaining.

Farther behind them, Ross looked thoroughly glum. He had hoped to win for a second year in a row. Instead, he had lost to a younger, more handsome man, and even the girl beside that man had beaten him. Third place was a bitter fall from his expectations.

Speaking of that girl, she really was pretty.

An idea occurred to him. He turned to Misty. "You're visiting from elsewhere, aren't you? To celebrate your second-place finish, how about coming aboard my boat? I could show you around the city."

His enthusiasm made the offer difficult to refuse. Misty thought about it. They had come to an unfamiliar city and could use someone to show them its sights. Ross had volunteered at just the right moment.

"Sure," she said after a pause. "But my friends are coming too."

"Of course!" Ross agreed at once. "And your friends are...?"

Misty smiled brightly and pointed ahead, her gaze softening as it settled on Ethan.

"He's one of them!"

Ross's eyes narrowed. The two were together?

That man was fortunate. He had won the race and had such a pretty girl keeping him company.

The medal presentation, Ethan's remarks, and the photographs took about half an hour. When he found Erika and the others afterward, Ash had already rejoined them, though he had vanished before the finish line.

Ethan immediately noticed Ross beside the group.

Ross was talking animatedly, but apart from Ash, no one seemed especially interested.

Erika and Misty were too focused on Ethan to pay much attention to another man. Brock, for his part, cared more about pretty older women than listening to a man tell stories.

When Ethan returned, Ross approached before anyone else could speak and held out his hand with a broad smile.

"Congratulations on winning the race!"

He was clearly trying to present himself as gracious and good-humored.

Ethan knew Ross's name but had no idea why this stranger was with his friends. He shook Ross's hand, then looked toward Erika in confusion.

What's going on?

Erika shook her head. She did not know either.

Ross looked about twenty-five or twenty-six. Years in the sun had given him a slight tan. He wore his medium-length brown hair parted in the middle and had the easy air of someone who spent his days surfing by the sea.

Misty came over and explained. "Ethan, Mr. Ross has offered to show us around the city."

"I see. That's very kind of you," Ethan said.

"Oh, right!" Ash said excitedly. "Let us see the winner's medal!"

Everyone but Ross looked at what Ethan held. It was a round medallion of clear glass. Sunlight refracted into colors through it. The shapes of two Pokemon were faintly visible inside, along with a green gem set into the glass.

"So that's the Altomare glass winner's trophy?" Misty said. "It's beautiful!"

Ethan smiled and handed it to Erika. For sheer beauty, it surpassed the trophies he had won at the Indigo League, in the Orange League, and at the Whirl Cup.

Then he remembered Ash's disappearance. "Where did you go during the race? How did you end up off the course?"

Ash was baffled himself. He scratched his head and gave an embarrassed laugh. "I don't really know. Maybe Totodile got nervous and took the wrong way."

Latios and Latias had evidently not shown themselves to Ash. Perhaps their interference had been nothing more than a sudden whim.

Misty raised her chin, looking vindicated. "See? I said finishing anywhere but last would be a great result for Ash. Instead, he was the only racer who didn't finish at all!"

Ash blushed at the memory of his boast before the race and could not bring himself to meet her sharp look.

Ross could not get a word in. When their banter finally stopped, he said, "Why don't we talk on the boat?"

Ethan had pictured a speedboat. At the canal bank, however, Ross led them to a wooden boatmore of a narrow skiff. Here it had a proper name: a gondola.

Ross boarded first and took up the long oar at the stern. Ash and Brock climbed in. Ethan helped Erika and Misty aboard one after the other, then jumped in last.

The small gondola was immediately full.

Ross gave the oar a gentle stroke, and the boat drifted along the canal.

The scenery slipped past on either side. Seeing the city at leisure from the water had a different charm from walking its streets.

Brock sighed contentedly. "I've always dreamed of riding an Altomare gondola."

They circled much of the city before returning to the two stone pillars commemorating Latias and Latios, which they had seen when they first arrived.

"They're our guardians," Ross said when he saw them looking. "Legend says they saved Altomare from a disaster. Even now, some people believe they're still hidden somewhere in the city, watching over the City of Water."

Chapter 526: Latias Is Attacked

After circling the city, Ross finally brought the gondola alongside a canal bank.

He had shown Ethan and the others around for quite a while. They had passed nearly every attraction, and at least from the waterways, there was little left to see.

As they climbed ashore, Ross smiled and pointed to a nearby restaurant. "They make the best pancakes in Altomare. Give them a try!"

"Thank you for taking the time to show us the city," Misty said on behalf of the group. "We really appreciate it." Ross had originally invited her aboard, so it made sense for her to thank him.

"Think nothing of it." Ross waved a hand. "We Altomare locals are a friendly bunch. Besides, it was an honor to have the race champion on my boat. Enjoy the rest of your trip!"

They waved goodbye. Watching Ross walk away, Ethan reflected that although the man seemed a little frivolous, he was actually decent company.

What Ethan did not know was that Ross had first invited Misty aboard because she had caught his eye and he wanted a chance to get to know her. When he saw Erika, he had been even more taken with her.

The moment when Ethan had noticed Ross doing his best to be charming and funny was precisely when Ross had been trying to impress them.

Once they were aboard, however, Ross realized that both Misty and Erika had their hearts set on Ethan. He gave up on the idea entirely.

At least he had not kept pestering either of them after that. In that respect, Ethan's impression of him was fair enough.

After Ross left, the group visited the restaurant he had recommended and ordered pancakes in several flavors.

"I want chocolate!"

"Banana for me!"

"I'll have cream and jam!"

They each took a big bite. Ross had been right: the pancakes were delicious.

Just then, Ash glanced around and realized Pikachu had disappeared.

"Huh? Where's Pikachu?"

Everyone helped look. At last they spotted Pikachu around a corner, standing by a fountain in a square, facing a teenage girl.

"Pikachu!" Ash hurried over with a smile. "What, have you made a new friend already?"

From a distance, Ethan caught sight of the girl's face, and his eyes sharpened.

He remembered Altomare well from the movie. Seeing Ash on the cruise ship had made him suspect the movie's events were about to unfold.

Now he recognized the girl at once. She was Latias in disguise. Other details he had forgotten slowly came back to him.

Up close, Ethan studied her appearance. She had short red hair with two odd little pigtails and a pretty face. Her green T-shirt, white shorts, pink boots, and black knee-high socks made her look like any ordinary girl.

The girl turned on the fountain's tap. Clear water spilled out, and Pikachu opened its mouth to drink. Only then did Ash realize it had wandered off because it was thirsty.

"Thank you," he told her.

She said nothing. Instead, she circled Ash several times, leaned in to study his face for a while, then ran toward the canal, leaving him thoroughly puzzled.

Misty came up beside Ash and watched the girl go. She looked just as confused. "Why didn't she say anything?"

At that moment, a speedboat appeared on the canal. Two fashionably dressed women rode in it. They were too far away for Ethan or the others to hear what they said to Latias. The girl suddenly fled in a panic, and the women threw Poke Balls, releasing their Pokemon to pursue her.

Latias darted into an alley. The two Pokemon followed without hesitation.

Before anyone else could react, Pikachu raced after them. Ethan and the others exchanged a glance, then hurried in the direction Latias had gone.

The women's Pokemon were an Espeon and an Ariados. They caught up with Latias near a small bridge. Espeon enveloped her in psychic power and lifted her into the air. Ariados then spat out a mass of silk, binding her hands and feet together.

Ethan and the others arrived in time to see it happen. Beneath the bridge, the two women pulled up in their speedboat.

"What are you doing?" Ash demanded.

Perhaps it was because the girl had helped Pikachu at the fountain, or perhaps he simply could not bear to see someone in trouble. Ash grabbed at the silk and tried to pull it off her.

The two women watched him without any hurry. One smiled. "We're just dressing the girl up."

"Dressing her up?" Ash shouted. "You call this dressing her up? Can't you see she doesn't want it?"

While Ash argued with them, Ethan took a closer look.

Both women appeared to be in their mid-twenties. One had long, wavy blonde hair and wore a pink cropped tube top. The other had short silver hair and a red cropped outfit. Their makeup was immaculate, and both wore bracelets and necklaces. They had a fashionable look with a tough, delinquent edge.

Ethan could not remember their names, but he knew they were notorious thieves.

The silver-haired woman leaned back. "Really? Well, we're enjoying it."

"That's right," the blonde added. "I'm enjoying it too."

Their flippant tone only made Ash angrier. He tore the silk from Latias and shouted at them, "What are you trying to do? Why would you treat a girl like this?"

"Honestly. Is that any way to address a lady?" The silver-haired woman gave a disdainful snort. "Ariados, teach this rude, meddlesome brat a lesson!"

Chapter 527: The Thieves and the Museum

At the silver-haired woman's command, Ariados opened its mouth and attacked without hesitation.

The two were famous thieves, after all. Once they decided to act, they did so at once. Ash had never imagined that pulling off a little webbing and saying a few words would make them attack a stranger.

Caught off guard, he took Ariados's Psychic head-on and fell into the canal.

Ethan had no time to react. Even Pikachu could only watch as its Trainer was struck.

"What was that for?" Ash scrambled out of the water and shouted at the silver-haired woman. Soaked from head to toe, he looked miserable.

The thieves still seemed utterly unconcerned. Ash's anger rose. He clenched his teeth. "Fine. If that's how you want it, we won't hold back either! Pikachu, go!"

At Ash's signal, Pikachu charged headfirst into Ariados. The two Pokemon began fighting at once.

When the blonde woman's Espeon looked ready to join in, Ethan took out a Poke Ball and released Gardevoir.

The two Psychic-type Pokemon exchanged several bursts of power. Their attacks were invisible, but the force of the collisions could be felt in the air, which seemed to warp around them.

The blonde looked from one member of the group to another. "So you're all determined to interfere."

Erika, Misty, and Brock said nothing. They released their Pokemon too, showing Ethan and Ash where they stood.

The thieves' Pokemon were certainly strong compared with most Trainers' partners. Against Ethan and his friends, however, they were outmatched.

After a short fight, the women sensed it too. They exchanged a glance. The silver-haired woman started the speedboat and steered away, while the blonde gave a sharp whistle. Ariados and Espeon broke off their battles at once, leaped aboard, and vanished with the women down the canal.

"What's with them? Why'd they stop?" Ash was baffled by their sudden retreat. After being knocked into the water, he wanted an explanation, and their escape left him frustrated.

Then he turned to check on the girl and found that she, too, had disappeared.

"Huh? Where did she go? When did she leave?"

If Ariados's silk had not still been lying on the ground, he might have wondered whether he had imagined the whole thing.

At Ash's cry, Ethan and the others looked to where Latias had stood beside him. She was nowhere in sight.

Everyone had been focused on the battle. None of them had noticed when she slipped away.

"Maybe she's shy, so she left quietly," Ethan said with a shake of his head. Then he grinned at Ash. "Still, look at you. You've learned how to rescue a damsel in distress!"

"He really has," Misty said, spreading her hands with a theatrical sigh. "I never thought I'd see the day. Too bad she left without a word. She didn't seem all that grateful."

"Stop making things up!" Ash's face reddened as they teased him. "II didn't help her for that! She helped Pikachu, and when I saw Pokemon chasing a girl, how could I just stand there?"

"Of course," Misty said, giving him a sidelong look and waving a hand. "We understand. You don't have to explain."

Once Ash had wrung the water out of his clothes, the incident soon slipped from their minds. They left the canal and continued toward the city center, arriving at Altomare's largest square.

Their destination was Altomare Cathedral, which stood beside the square. It was both a church and the city's only museum. Inside were historical records and artifacts from Altomare's founding onward, as well as fossils on display.

There were many other visitors. When the group entered the main hall, its solemn atmosphere made them lower their voices.

Fine paintings hung on the walls. Set into the floor was a huge Aerodactyl fossil, fully embedded in the marble and protected so visitors could walk over it without causing damage.

"Amazing," Brock murmured. Then he looked down uneasily. "But is it really all right for us to walk on it?"

He had been speaking to himself, but an elderly voice answered from behind them.

"Don't worry. There are other Pokemon fossils farther inside as well, and they're all protected the same way. The surfaces have been treated, and a layer of clear tempered glass covers them. It may feel as though you're stepping on the fossils, but you can't harm them."

Ethan and the others turned. A short, slightly plump old man with a broad bald head and a thick white beard walked toward them.

He looked kindly and round-faced. A badge hung on his chest. Ethan read it: Lorenzo, Guide.

Ignoring their surprised looks, Lorenzo smiled. "This is your first visit to the city, isn't it? Come with me, then. I'll show you around."

He led them deeper into the cathedral. As he had said, they passed more fossils set into the floor, including one of a Kabutops. Each had been protected like the Aerodactyl fossil. Walking above them felt novel and gave the group a vivid sense of the ancient world.

Sunlight filtered through stained-glass windows and spread across the marble.

They reached a circular room. Before them stood a towering machine whose purpose was impossible to tell at a glance.

Colored light fell over Brock. For some reason, he suddenly spread his arms and cried out, "Basking in this sunlightcould it be a sign from the heavens that I'll meet some beautiful older girls in this city?"

Ethan walked past Brock and stood beneath the machine, looking up at it.

It was made entirely of steel and rose more than ten meters high. Four enormous supports surrounded a strange sphere at its center. The whole structure looked both peculiar and mysterious.

Chapter 528: Ash Follows the Girl

Lorenzo continued his explanation. "According to the island's legends, this cathedral and the Tower of the Sun outside were built by the people of old in gratitude to Latias and Latios for protecting the city. The device before you seems to have been made for the sake of peace as well. Unfortunately, it is so ancient that no one knows how it works anymore."

As Ethan and the others listened and examined the machine, Ash suddenly seemed to notice something. He looked up at the gallery on the second floor. A red-haired girl was drawing at a drawing board there. She looked just like the girl who had disappeared beside them earlier.

"It's her!"

At Ash's low exclamation, the others looked up and saw her too.

She had apparently just finished her drawing. She packed up her supplies, turned, and left with her board. For reasons he could not have explained, Ash followed her out.

"Ash!"

Brock called after him. When Ash did not respond, Brock sighed and went after him with Pikachu.

"What's gotten into him?" Misty turned to Ethan. "Should we follow too?"

"Let's go." Ethan nodded. "We know Ash. He can be impulsive, but he has a knack for stumbling into unusual things. Maybe he spotted something."

Even as he said it, Ethan wondered whether the red-haired girl who had left was really the same one they had met by the canalLatias in disguise.

He vaguely remembered that Latias had taken on the appearance of a girl before showing herself to people. And they had only just arrived at the cathedral, while this girl seemed to have spent a long time drawing upstairs.

Whatever the answer, following Ash seemed sensible.

Ethan, Erika, and Misty hurried through a side door, taking the route Brock had used to leave the cathedral.

Outside, they saw Brock trailing Ash beyond the cathedral grounds. They quickened their pace, crossed the square and a broad bridge, and followed them a long way through the city.

The red-haired girl walked at an unhurried pace. Ash nearly caught up with her several times, but he did not know the streets. Each time a canal blocked his path, he had to circle around to another route to keep her in sight.

Brock and the others, despite leaving later, managed to catch up with Ash first.

When the girl reached the opposite bank once more, Ash called across the water, "Please wait!"

She turned toward him. "Are you talking to me? What do you want?"

"Why did you leave without saying anything earlier? And who were those women?" Ash asked.

"What are you talking about?" She stared at him in confusion, then gave a cold laugh. "If this is some new way of trying to pick me up, you've chosen the wrong girl."

With that, she turned and walked away without another glance.

Misty covered her mouth, unable to resist teasing him. "Ash, I guess rescuing her didn't have quite the effect you hoped. Now she's got the wrong idea about you!"

"I wasn't trying to rescue her to impress her!"

Red-faced, Ash hurried onto the bridge and set off after the girl again.

This time she entered a more tangled residential district. Ash lost sight of her after only a moment's distraction.

Ethan and the others found him standing there, dejected. Misty caught her breath and asked, "Seriously, we ran all this way. Why are you so determined to find her?"

"I don't know..." Ash scratched his head. "She just gives me this special feeling. It's like... like..."

He tried several times but could not put the feeling into words.

Ethan glanced at him and smiled. "Like when you meet a Pokemon you really like?"

"Yes, exactly!" Ash's eyes lit up as he nodded. "That's it!"

"A Pokemon?" Misty burst out laughing. "So that's what liking a person feels like to you, Ashliking a Pokemon!"

By now, Ethan was almost certain that the girl who had just brushed Ash off was an ordinary human, not Latias.

The two looked alike, but there was one clear difference: this girl spoke, while the one they had met earlier had remained silent.

Of course, calling her ordinary was not entirely right. Even if Ethan could not remember the plot, Latias had chosen her appearance for a reason. The two must have some close connection.

With the girl gone, the group could only keep walking. Altomare had struck them as beautiful since their arrival, but its crossing canals, little bridges, and alleys made its streets a maze.

As they discussed where to go next, they spotted the red-haired girl watching them from a nearby bridge.

They were astonished. She had just shaken Ash off so impatiently, yet now she seemed to be waiting for them.

Ethan alone noticed that the look in her eyes was entirely different.

This must be Latias in the girl's form again. It was hard to explain such a change otherwise.

While they stood there in surprise, Latias waved to them, then slipped into an alley beside the bridge.

Ash looked at the others. "What does she mean by that?"

"You idiot," Misty said with a sigh. "Isn't it obvious? She wants us to follow her."

"But..."

Ash hesitated. The other girl's sharp words were still fresh in his mind, and this sudden invitation left him thoroughly confused.

"What are you waiting for?" Ethan lightly tapped Ash on the head to snap him out of it, then smiled. "You chased her all the way here when she told you to leave her alone. Now that she's asking you to follow, you're suddenly afraid?"

"I'm not afraid! Come on, let's go!"

The tap brought Ash back to himself. He stopped hesitating and hurried after Latias, Pikachu at his side.

Chapter 529: The Secret Garden and Latios

As they talked, the group followed the girl. This time Latias seemed to be guiding them. Whenever she came to a fork, she waited until they caught up before running deeper into the neighborhood.

The chase stretched Ethan, Ash, and the others into a long line.

Ethan and Erika were at the back. When no one else was close enough to hear, Erika said softly, "That girl isn't the same person we saw just now, is she?"

"Huh?" Ethan stared at her. "How did you know?"

"At first it was just a woman's intuition. Then I noticed the small differences in their expressions. But the clearest clues were her hat and what she was carrying."

"Her hat and what she was carrying?"

Ethan remembered that the girl at the cathedral had worn a white hat. The one running ahead of them wore no hat and carried no drawing board.

He had overlooked both details. Erika had not.

She had been sharp enough to notice the difference all along.

"You're right. They aren't the same person." Seeing how far ahead Ash and the others had run, Ethan leaned close enough to whisper so they could not hear. "Actually, I think the girl in front of us is Latias in disguise."

He did not tell Erika everything. If he seemed to know too much about what would happen, she might start wondering how he could possibly have known it.

Latias?

After her first surprise, Erika understood. "No wonder. I thought it was strange that you'd keep following Ash around just to chase some girl. I knew there must be a reason, but I didn't expect her to be Latias."

Considerate as ever, Erika did not ask how Ethan knew. He had revealed unexpected information like this many times before. In her view, a good partner did not need to question him about everything; she could simply listen.

"Otherwise, I wouldn't have played this chasing game for so long," Ethan said with a wry smile. Then his expression grew serious. "Be careful, though. Remember those two women? Latias is their target too. They might be watching us from somewhere right now."

In fact, he was right.

The thieves had only just been driven off and had no intention of giving up. Unseen by Ethan's group, a small spider-shaped robot clung to a nearby rooftop. Its camera sent everything it saw back to the women.

Latias led them through turn after turn in the complicated residential district, finally reaching a vine-covered passageway. She ran into it and, to everyone's astonishment, passed straight through what looked like a solid wall. Then she was gone.

As she crossed it, faint colored light shimmered over the wall, like a barrier.

Ash stopped in front of it, unsure whether he dared try the same thing. He looked toward Ethan when Ethan reached his side.

"Let's go." With everyone watching him, Ethan stepped toward the wall first. "The answers to what we've been wondering are on the other side of this barrier."

He touched it. It resisted his hand like a thin film. Without hesitating, he took another step and passed through.

When Ethan vanished, Ash and the others exchanged uneasy looks. Then they gathered their courage and followed.

The darkness lasted only an instant. On the other side, Ethan found himself in a vast circular garden. Old-fashioned walls enclosed it, and a huge glass dome arched overhead. Sunlight poured through the panes onto lush trees and plants.

Footsteps sounded behind him as Ash and the others emerged. They, too, marveled at the hidden world beyond the wall.

The garden covered an enormous area and was remarkably quiet. Apart from their group, there was no sign of human activity.

Small Pokemon played in the grass on either side. Flocks of Butterfree fluttered overhead. Everything seemed peaceful and unhurried.

They descended the stone steps and headed farther in. Latias, still in the girl's form, stood near the center. She had stopped running and smiled at them before walking toward a broad pond.

As they approached, they saw her sitting on a swing in the distance. Each time she kicked her legs forward, it swept through a wide arc.

They had just drawn near and were about to speak to her when a westerly wind rose beside them. Before they could react, water burst from the pond and a transparent Pokemon flew toward them at tremendous speed. Its body could still be traced by the way it distorted the space around it.

It rushed past them, spraying water into the air. Then it wheeled around and charged at them again.

This time Pikachu reacted. Apart from Misty's Togepi and the Gengar hidden in Ethan's shadow, it was the only Pokemon currently at anyone's side. It leaped in front of the group to protect them.

Crouching low, Pikachu fixed its eyes on the transparent Pokemon and unleashed a stream of electricity.

The attacker drove through the electric attack and sent Pikachu flying. It rolled a long way across the ground, completely overpowered. The transparent Pokemon turned its attention back to Ethan and the others, ready to attack againuntil Latias, still in the girl's form, suddenly stepped between them.

At the sight of her, the Pokemon stopped at once. Its invisibility faded, revealing its true form.

It was about two meters long, white in front and blue behind, with a sleek body, wings like those of a jet, and feet resembling fins. It looked part bird, part fish, and part dragon.

There was no mistaking it. This was Latios, the Pokemon Ethan remembered seeing at Latias's side in the movie.

The others had never seen this Legendary Pokemon in person. Even so, they immediately connected it with the two statues at the harbor and recognized it.

Chapter 530: Dream Projection and the Soul Dew

"Why is Latios here?" Misty exclaimed.

Brock's eyes widened too, though even at their widest they still looked rather narrow. He nodded uncertainly. "It really is unbelievable. And... it looks angry!"

"You people!"

As they stared at Latios, an indignant girl's voice rang out behind them. They turned to see someone hurrying toward them who looked exactly like the girl Latias had become.

She carried a drawing board and wore a white hat. This was the human girl.

"Huh?" Ash looked from the red-haired girl standing in front of them to the one in the white hat behind them. "There are two of you? You look exactly alike!"

The girl in the hat glared at him. "How did you get in here? Are you thieves?"

"Of course not!" Ash shook his head quickly. "We're Pokemon Trainers from Pallet Town and other places. We followed this girl inside!"

Her gaze swept across Ethan and the others, then settled on Ash. Perhaps remembering his strange attempt to talk to her earlier, she said coldly, "You seem very suspicious. Latios, drive them out!"

Latios rose at her command, ready to attack. Then an elderly voice called from nearby.

"Stop!"

They turned again. Lorenzo, the guide they had met at the cathedral, was walking toward them.

The round, grandfatherly man approached the girl and Latios. "Bianca, Latios, the boy is telling the truth."

"But Grandpa..." Bianca began.

Lorenzo raised a hand to calm her, then looked at the other girl. "Latias, did you want to play with them?"

"Latias?"

Ash, Misty, and Brock followed his gaze to the girl. Why had the old guide called her Latias?

Could she really be Latias in disguise?

With everyone watching, Latias nodded. Then she took Ash by the hand and led him to the swing. They climbed onto it together.

She pressed Ash into the seat and stood behind him. With a gentle push, she sent the swing moving back and forth with both of them on it.

Then her appearance changed. The girl vanished, replaced by a Pokemon several sizes smaller than Latios, with a red back half.

"Whoa!"

Startled by her transformation, Ash jumped off the swing.

Misty and Brock stared, stunned. At last they understood why the girl had said nothing along the way. It was not that she had refused to speak. As a Pokemon, she could not speak human language.

Even Bianca murmured, watching Latias play with Ash, "She seems to like that boy."

Lorenzo nodded. "She's so happy. She really must have led them here herself."

With the misunderstanding cleared up, Latios went over to Pikachu and licked its wound. It seemed to be offering an affectionate apology for hurting it earlier.

Ash and Pikachu soon grew friendly with both Legendary Pokemon. Latias and Latios carried Ash through the air as they flew around the garden. Togepi, watching from Misty's arms, squirmed free and jumped onto Latios's back as well.

Ethan took the opportunity to tell Lorenzo and Bianca how they had rescued Latias from the two thieves.

"I see." Lorenzo was grateful. "Thank you for helping her."

Bianca looked apologetic too. "I'm sorry. My name is Bianca. I was too quick to judge you."

"It's all right," Ethan said, shaking his head. "If strangers appeared here, I'd try to drive them off to protect the Pokemon too."

At Lorenzo and Bianca's invitation, they went to sit nearby. On the way, Lorenzo explained, "For generations, our family has protected this Secret Garden for the Latios and Latias who visit the island. Their power created it, and it is their home while they're here."

"A secret garden for Legendary Pokemon," Brock said with a knowing nod. No wonder its entrance had been protected by a barrier.

At a table, Bianca made tea for everyone. "This Latios and Latias are brother and sister. Latios is the older brother, and Latias is the younger sister. She's much livelier than he is. She often takes on my appearance and goes out to explore the city."

Just then, both Pokemon's eyes glowed white. Latios dove into the water, and Latias came over to the group. As the light flickered in her eyes, the scenery around Ethan and the others changed.

They seemed to be underwater, surrounded by clear water. Everything looked so real that they felt as though they were actually there.

Seeing Ash's astonished face, Bianca smiled. "This is one of their powers. They can link their minds and let us experience what Latios is seeing. We call it dream projection."

"Dream projection?" Brock murmured. "So everything we're seeing now is really happening around Latios?"

"That's right," Lorenzo said. "I think they're doing this to welcome you."

Ethan stayed seated and took in the scene. He could feel solid ground under his feet and hear birds in the garden beside him, yet the view before his eyes was like a three-dimensional movie. It almost convinced him he was underwater.

After they had enjoyed it for a while, Latios returned to them, and the projection ended.

Perhaps no one had ever been invited inside by Latias before, or perhaps Bianca felt she owed them patience after her mistake. Either way, she led them over to some stone tablets and continued explaining.

"Long ago, Latias and Latios brought a power that could drive away darkness: a jewel called the Soul Dew. Legend says one was left on this island after they saved it. The two thieves you told us about may have tried to capture Latias because they're after that Soul Dew!"

Chapter 531: The Soul Dew and a Sudden Crisis

Ethan noticed something familiar carved into a nearby stone tablet. He pointed it out to Lorenzo. "Isn't that the device we saw in the cathedral?"

"It is," Lorenzo said with a nod. "My ancestors built it to draw on the Soul Dew's power and protect this island. The tablet shows how the Soul Dew is truly meant to be used."

He led them to a small, separate pool and asked them to look at its bottom.

In the clear water rested a round, transparent orb on a stand. Countless glimmers of light flowed through it like drops of water.

"Is that...?"

"The Soul Dew," Lorenzo said. "It is the treasure Altomare has protected for generations."

"That's the Soul Dew?"

Ash, Misty, and Brock had never expected the mysterious jewel from the legend to be sitting so openly in a pool, with almost no visible protection. Then again, the barrier outside hid the garden, and two Legendary Pokemon lived here. Where could it be safer?

Still, was this really the Soul Dew? It looked very different from the splendid gem they had imagined.

They leaned forward together for a closer look. A railing kept them back, however, so they could only make out its general shape.

Bianca smiled. "Latios trusts you, and meeting you here must be fate. But please promise me you won't tell anyone that the Soul Dew is here."

"Don't worry," Ethan said. He and the others nodded firmly. They understood how important the treasure was and had no intention of spreading word of it. "We won't tell a soul."

They played with Latias and Latios for a while longer. When evening came, they finally said it was time to leave.

Latias immediately looked disappointed and reluctant to let them go.

Even so, Ethan and the others waved goodbye to the two Legendary Pokemon and left the Secret Garden.

Lorenzo and Bianca guided them away. Instead of heading back through the city, they took them to the nearest canal bank and into a wooden workshop.

It was Lorenzo's workplace. Besides serving as a guide, he repaired gondolas and spent his spare time here working on them. In truth, gondola repair was his profession; guiding tourists and telling them about Altomare and its Legendary Pokemon was something he did out of interest.

Lorenzo pointed to a speedboat in the canal. "Bianca, take them back to the Pokemon Center."

Ethan and the others were about to decline. They felt bad asking Bianca to take them all the way back. But a look around showed them how far they had wandered from the city, so they accepted. On foot, they might not reach the Pokemon Center before dark.

Everyone boarded the speedboat. Bianca handled it expertly, steering them smoothly along the canal toward the city center.

They did not know that, soon after they left the Secret Garden, the thieves' spider-shaped scout had already slipped inside.

The motor droned steadily. Ethan and his friends were absorbed in the scenery along the banks, so the sound hardly bothered them.

The boat continued down the canal. A gentle breeze brushed their faces, making the ride wonderfully pleasant.

It would have been even better if they had not been so hungry.

They reached the Pokemon Center before nightfall. After arranging their rooms, they hurried to a nearby restaurant and ordered a table full of food.

At their warm invitation, Bianca stayed for dinner too.

When the dishes arrived, Ash's way of eating startled her at first. She had spent enough time with him to see that he was a straightforward boy who acted on whatever came to mind. So she ate at a more measured pace and watched him devour his meal as though she were watching an eating show.

After dinner, they chatted and exchanged contact details. By the time they left the restaurant, the moon was high. Altomare looked beautiful in a different way under its evening lights.

They waved Bianca goodbye and returned to the Pokemon Center.

From the morning's water race to dinner, it had been a long day. Tired out, they said good night and went to their rooms.

Ethan took a hot shower to wash away the day's fatigue. When he returned, Ash and Brock were already snoring. He shook his head, lay down, and picked up his phone.

He was still concerned about the two thieves. He could not remember the plot clearly, but he knew they would cause more trouble.

With nothing else to do, he searched online for information about them.

There was almost nothing on the internet about thieves of their caliber. Ethan finally sent Looker a message.

Only a few minutes later, Looker sent back two files. Ethan opened them and found photographs of the women at the top.

They were sisters. The blonde was named Annie, and the silver-haired woman was Oakley. They ranked as the world's foremost thieves. Both were agile, and neither had failed a job since beginning her career.

Below the photographs was a list of their crimes. Ethan skimmed it. Most of their targets had been valuable jewelry, paintings, calligraphy, and other works of art.

As he read, drowsiness overtook him. He could not remember when he fell asleep.

The stars glittered beneath a high moon.

Deep into the night, the whole city was quiet. At some point, a cool breeze brushed Ethan in his sleep and woke him. As soon as he opened his eyes, he saw Latias flying toward him in a rush. Her anxious expression and the scratches on her body told him something had happened.

Before he could turn on the light, Latias tumbled into the room and struck the floor with a loud crash. Ash and Brock woke at once.

Ethan switched on the room light. Ash and Brock stared at Latias in surprise.

"Latias, why are you here? What happened?"

Chapter 532: The Defense Mechanism

Latias spoke to them urgently, but Ethan and the others could not understand Pokemon language. Her expression alone told them something serious had happened.

Ethan already had a suspicion. The Secret Garden must have been attacked, and the attackers could only be the two thieves.

Ash and Brock looked at him. Ethan understood what they wanted and addressed the shadow at his feet. "Gengar, stop sleeping. Time to work."

They needed Gengar, who had so often served as their interpreter.

At Ethan's urging, Gengar slowly rose out of the shadow. Absurdly, he was yawning, wearing a nightcap, and hugging a large pillow.

"Hey," Gengar grumbled, glancing at Ethan. "Do you know what time it is? It's the middle of the night! I need my beauty sleep to take care of my skin."

"Enough," Ethan said with a helpless sigh. Then he turned serious. "Something's wrong. Translate for us. What is Latias saying?"

Latias realized this unusual Gengar could speak human language and repeated her account.
