Gengar dropped the jokes after listening. He turned to the others. "There was trouble in the Secret Garden. The two thieves who attacked Latias during the day broke in. They captured her brother and stole the Soul Dew!"

Ash and Brock's expressions changed at once.

"How could that happen?" Ash asked. "Wasn't there a barrier protecting the garden? How did they find it?"

"They must have followed us without our noticing," Brock said, resting a hand under his chin. Then he sighed. "I still can't believe they succeeded with two Legendary Pokemon there."

"That isn't so strange," Ethan said, shaking his head. "Being Legendary doesn't guarantee a Pokemon is strong. Even two of the same species can differ enormously. Their condition, experience, and surroundings all affect how well they can fight."

None of them could go back to sleep after that. Erika and Misty were in a separate room, so Ethan called Erika to explain. Then he, Ash, and Brock hurried to get dressed.

By the time they reached the Pokemon Center lobby, Erika and Misty were rushing in too, their clothes hastily thrown on. People said women took longest to get ready, but in an emergency they had kept things simple.

Though Ethan had told them about Latias over the phone, seeing her there still surprised them. Fortunately, the lobby was empty at this hour, so she had no need to worry about being seen.

Even if someone else had been there, she could have taken Bianca's form again.

Erika thought a step further. "What about Lorenzo and Bianca? Are they all right?"

As guardians of the Secret Garden, neither would have stood by while it was attacked.

Latias shook her head. Then her eyes began to shine, just as they had in the garden. She was using dream projection.

In an instant, the scene around them changed. Through Latios's eyes, they saw Bianca and Lorenzo bound together in spider silk. Annie and Oakley stood nearby, murmuring to each other beside Latios. They seemed puzzled by the sudden change in his eyes.

"Why does this place look familiar?" Misty frowned at the view around them. "It looks like some kind of hall..."

"You don't need to guess." Ethan pointed to something nearby. "It's the cathedral. Look at that machine. Isn't it the one we saw today?"

The others looked around. He was right. They were seeing the cathedral they had toured that afternoon.

"Then let's get over there!"

They were about to leave to rescue everyone when the projection showed Oakley slipping deftly into the sphere at the center of the machine. Somehow, with Latios and the Soul Dew, she set it in motion.

As it turned, the fossils embedded in the floor stirred. Before their eyes, they rose as though alive.

The Soul Dew's power was astonishing.

"We have to hurry," Ethan said. "Whatever those two intend to do, they're almost ready."

The others nodded. As soon as Latias ended the projection, they ran for the Pokemon Center entrance.

Before they could reach it, iron hooks shot up from beneath the paving stones outside, surrounding the doorway.

The same sharp hooks blocked street entrances, bridges, and narrow alleys throughout the city. Fortunately, it was late enough that few people noticed the change.

Misty had been running so fast she nearly scraped herself against them. Ethan pulled her back just in time. Shaken, she stared at the sudden obstruction. "What are these?"

Latias called out several times. Gengar translated immediately. "She says it's an ancient defense mechanism, built when her ancestors saved the island!"

"A defense mechanism?" Ethan shook his head. "It looks like our enemies have turned it into a weapon against us."

The hooks were too sharp and densely packed to push through. Fortunately, they had Pokemon to help. One Shadow Ball from Gengar blasted a large hole through the seemingly sturdy barrier.

Outside the Pokemon Center, Ethan surveyed the silent street. He took out a Poke Ball and turned to the others. "Walking will take too long. Let's split up. Erika and I will fly ahead on Dragonite. You find a boat and take the canals."

Misty and Brock knew their own Pokemon could not carry them through the air as Ethan's could. They nodded and ran toward the canal.

As Ash was about to leave with them, Latias caught his clothes in her mouth and indicated that he should climb onto her back.

Ash hesitated only a moment. Knowing how urgent this was, he climbed aboard. Latias spread her wings and took to the air beside Ethan's Dragonite. Together they raced toward the cathedral.

Chapter 533: Breaking into the Cathedral

Dragonite and Latias carried them through the night sky. At their speed, they crossed most of the city in a flash.

Within minutes they reached the cathedral and landed in the square before it. Ethan had barely begun to take in his surroundings when several Pokemon lunged out of the darkness.

Looking closer, he recognized the Aerodactyl and Kabutops they had seen revived in the dream projection. It was too dark to count them. Shadows darted all around the square, and pairs of pale eyes watched them coldly. The Soul Dew's power appeared to have revived every fossil.

Several Kabutops charged at them, brandishing their sharp scythes. Before they could strike, Gengar hurled one Shadow Ball after another and drove them back for the moment.

Ethan, Erika, and Ash seized the chance to jump down from Dragonite and Latias.

Erika surveyed the situation and volunteered to cover them. "Leave this to me. Hurry inside and save Lorenzo and Bianca!"

Ash hesitated. Erika was a Gym Leader, but there were so many hostile Pokemon that leaving her here alone still seemed dangerous.

Ethan trusted her. He did not try to talk her out of it. Instead, he took several Poke Balls from his bag and placed them in her hands.

"Let these guys help too."

However urgent the rescue was, he would not leave Erika to face that danger by herself.

She accepted the Poke Balls without ceremony, brought out her own, and released both their teams.

Blue light flashed. Erika's Pokemon were Leafeon, Vileplume, and Bellossom. She had caught several others since coming to Johto, but they had little training and experience. This was no time to send them into such a fight.

The Pokemon Ethan had lent her were Crystal Steelix, Tyranitar, and Scizor.

They were tough enough to hold the front line. Together with Erika's Grass-type Pokemon, they could handle the attackers here.

More importantly, Ethan's Pokemon knew there was something romantic between their Trainer and Erika. None of them objected to taking her orders.

Ethan and Dragonite were already running toward the cathedral doors alongside Ash and Latias.

An Aerodactyl swooped at them, but Dragonite slammed it aside before it could reach them.

There were too many revived Pokemon. No sooner had that one been repelled than two or three Kabutops leaped into their path.

Pikachu fired an Electric attack at once. Kabutops was part Water-type, so the attack should have been super effective. Under the Soul Dew's influence, however, it did far less than expected.

Ash stared. Pikachu, too, seemed stunned for a moment.

The three Kabutops showed brief signs of pain but did not stop. They came down with their scythes ready to strike. Something flashed across Ash's vision, and all three were knocked away by a tremendous force.

He turned and saw Ethan's Crystal Steelix drawing back its tail. It had saved him.

Even while directing the fight farther away, Erika had kept an eye on Ethan and Ash.

"Stay alert," Ethan called as he pressed toward the doors. "The jewel's power has changed them somehow. Bring out the rest of your Pokemon!"

Ash nodded and quickly released Totodile, Bayleef, Cyndaquil, and his Shiny Noctowl. Protected by their Pokemon, he and Ethan fought off more attacks and finally reached the cathedral entrance.

Sharp iron hooks guarded these doors too. At a signal from Ethan, Gengar formed a Shadow Ball and smashed through them by force.

Bang!

Iron fragments flew backward. The Shadow Ball kept going and destroyed the lock on the cathedral doors as well.

Ethan kicked the doors open. There was no time to worry about damage to the building. He charged inside first, heading straight for the room with the machine.

As he had seen in the projection, Lorenzo and Bianca were bound together in spider silk. Hope lit their eyes when Ethan's group burst in, but silk covered their mouths. They could only struggle, as though trying to tell the rescuers something.

Before the machine, Latios was trapped in a frame of more than a dozen iron rings. The device was steadily draining power from his body.

"You pests again!" Annie, the blonde thief, stepped into Ethan's path. "This time you can't stop us!"

At her words, more than a dozen revived fossil Pokemon rushed in. Ethan could only conclude that the two women had gathered up fossils from all over Altomare; otherwise there could not be so many attackers.

Those fossils were valuable relics, important for research and display. That made Ethan and the others reluctant to attack them without restraint.

But rescuing the captives and Latios mattered most.

Ethan took out two Poke Balls and released Gardevoir and Jolteon against the advancing fossil Pokemon.

His and Ash's Pokemon met them in battle. Latias used the opening to fly to Latios and repeatedly ram the device holding him.

"It's no use." Annie glanced at her. "You can't overcome the Soul Dew's power. You were lucky to escape us twice before. I never thought you'd come straight to us this time!"

At her gesture, Espeon and Ariados charged at Latias together. While everyone's attention turned to them, Ethan's Gardevoir used Teleport and appeared beside Lorenzo and Bianca.

Ethan had never forgotten that rescuing the hostages was his most important aim.

Chapter 534: The Power of the Soul Dew

Annie was focused on the fight in front of her and did not notice that the hostages had been freed. Inside the machine, Oakley was busy operating something and paid Ethan's group no attention either.

Gardevoir took Lorenzo by one hand and Bianca by the other, then used Teleport to carry them behind the battle.

Before she had even found her footing, Bianca said urgently, "Ethan, Ash, please save Latios!"

Lorenzo was more concerned about the Soul Dew. "Be careful," he warned Ethan. "They've figured out how to use the jewel and the machine. The entire city of Altomare is under their control now!"

Ethan nodded. They had already seen what the Soul Dew could do: raise barriers throughout the city and revive fossil Pokemon. Both were powerful abilities, and he had no idea what else the women might unleash.

From across the room, Annie heard Bianca and Lorenzo and finally realized they had escaped. She did not care. She and Oakley already had Latios and the Soul Dew. The hostages had served their purpose.

Jolteon used its speed to keep the fossil Pokemon from getting close, attacking with a variety of Electric-type moves from a safe distance. Ash's Totodile, Bayleef, Cyndaquil, and Noctowl were fighting well too.

Pikachu stood out most of all.

Its small body let it dart among the larger Pokemon. It sprang onto a Kabutops's head, leaped to an Aerodactyl's back, and unleashed Thunderbolt, knocking out several nearby fossil Pokemon at once.

Working together, they brought down one attacker after another. The revived Pokemon had numbers on their side, but little else. The battle seemed to be turning in Ethan's favor.

When another Aerodactyl fell, Annie looked toward Oakley inside the machine. "If you don't do something soon, we're going to be in trouble!"

"I know!" Oakley's voice came from the sphere. She sounded entirely calm. "Don't worry. They're about to see the Soul Dew's true power!"

At first, Ethan and the others noticed nothing. They kept fighting the fossil Pokemon. Then they realized something was wrong.

Seawater was flowing in from every direction, through the doors and windows in ways water should not move. In moments, it gathered into a small waterspout that surged toward them.

"Noctowl, blow it apart!"

Ash recognized the danger before Ethan could act. He ordered his Shiny Noctowl to disperse the spinning water.

Noctowl beat its wings and sent a fierce gust across the room. The waterspout twisted under the force. Spray scattered everywhere and fell across the floor.

But as soon as the wind stopped, the water gathered again. With more seawater still pouring in, the vortex grew larger.

"You two, get outside!"

Ethan turned to Lorenzo and Bianca. They understood how dangerous the fight had become and knew they could do little by staying. After one anxious look at Latios, they nodded and ran out of the cathedral.

The waterspout pulled at everything around it. As it moved, it tore up the floor and sent pieces flying, drawing nearby objects into its center.

Even the mindless fossil Pokemon, intent only on attacking, were smashed by their own side's waterspout. Many of their fossil bones were sucked into it.

Ethan turned to Ash. "We can't let it grow any bigger. Let's break it apart together!"

"Got it!"

They called their Pokemon to them and ordered a combined attack. Multicolored bursts of power flew toward the waterspout at once.

Ethan had Gengar add his strength, hoping to destroy it completely.

Seven or eight attacks struck almost simultaneously. The waterspout burst into a shower of water that rained onto the floor. A moment later, the seawater flowed back together and formed the vortex again.

"It's useless!" Oakley poked her head halfway out of the sphere and laughed at them. "It's made of seawater, and the sea has more water than you could ever use up. Break it apart once, and it'll simply come back!"

Ash lowered his voice. "Ethan, what do we do?"

"If attacking the waterspout won't work, we'll stop them at the source." Ethan pointed at the rings holding Latios. "You free Latios. I'll smash the machine."

"Okay!"

They split up and ran around the massive vortex toward their separate targets.

At Ash's command, his Pokemon attacked the iron rings restraining Latios. The rings were made of something extraordinarily tough, and they seemed to absorb the power of every move that struck them. Electric attacks, flames, and water all disappeared into the metal.

Ash gritted his teeth. "Use Tackle!"

Noctowl dived from above and struck the rings. But they could discharge electricity too. The moment Noctowl hit them, the energy they had absorbed erupted as an electric shock.

Crackling sparks filled the air.

Light blazed around Noctowl. It was thrown backward and knocked out by that single shock, its feathers scorched.

"Noctowl!"

Ash rushed over and lifted Noctowl into his arms. He looked back at the machine, helpless and frustrated.

Meanwhile, Ethan was closing in on the other side.

To keep anyone from disturbing her younger sister, Annie sent Corsola and Ariados to block him.

Those two Pokemon were no match for Ethan's Gardevoir and Jolteon, especially with Gengar nearby, ready to join in.

After only a few exchanges, both defenders went down. Only Annie remained between Ethan and the machine.

Chapter 535: A Giant Waterspout

Gardevoir and Jolteon passed Annie on either side. Neither paid any attention to the thief now that she had no Pokemon left to fight with. They headed straight for the machine.

As the partners of a legitimate Trainer, they would not attack a human without an explicit order.

The machine appeared unguarded. But just as the two Pokemon drew close, the great waterspout swept in front of them.

It had already done irreparable damage inside the cathedral. It had cracked countless floor slabs and battered the walls, pillars, and everything else nearby.

That the building had not collapsed yet was a testament to its strength. In an island city like Altomare, the builders had probably taken wind and earthquakes into account.

"Go around it!" Ethan called.

Gardevoir used Teleport to cross the barrier of water. Jolteon raced around its side.

In the next instant, two streams split from the waterspout and blocked them again, threatening to close around them.

The Pokemon attacked the streams, but the result was the same as before. More seawater flowed in to replace everything they broke apart.

They had no choice but to retreat.

Ethan glanced toward Ash. He had not managed to free Latios either. Thinking quickly, Ethan called, "Let's get out of here. If this keeps up, the cathedral will collapse!"

Ash hated to leave, but he knew he could not free Latios alone. He nodded and followed Ethan out.

The fighting outside was nearly over. With help from Ethan's three Pokemon, Erika had taken some time but had defeated the revived fossils without anyone getting hurt.

Lorenzo and Bianca had taken shelter in a corner of the square. When they saw Ethan and Ash emerge, they hurried over.

"Did you save Latios?"

Before Ethan could answer, the cathedral's huge wooden doors exploded outward. The waterspout smashed through them, tore away half a wall, and surged into the square.

They needed no answer now.

"Don't stand there. Get clear!"

Ethan called Lorenzo and Bianca out of their shock and led them to the middle of the square, where they joined Erika.

Only now could he see countless thin streams rising from canals in every direction and converging on the cathedral. They were feeding the waterspout and making it grow.

"Ethan!"

Misty's voice came from behind them. They turned to see her Pokemon pulling a wooden boat toward the bank. Misty and Brock stood aboard.

The two jumped ashore and ran over. Seeing Lorenzo and Bianca with the group, they let out relieved breaths.

"Are you all right?"

After splitting from Ethan, they had found a gondola and had Misty's Corsola pull it along the waterways. They had needed to break through iron hooks blocking their route and fight off several fossil Pokemon. Those delays were why they had only just arrived.

"We're fine, but..." Bianca looked toward the cathedral with worry. "Latios and the Soul Dew are still inside."

In the dark, Misty and Brock had not noticed the waterspout looming over the square. Now they stared at it. "Why is there a waterspout on land? And how did it get so big?"

"Those two women made it using Latios and the Soul Dew," Ethan explained grimly. "It keeps drawing in seawater. We haven't been able to stop it."

Erika frowned as she understood the problem. "Then we have to break the link between them."

"But..." Ash looked downcast. "I already tried. I couldn't break the iron rings holding Latios."

Misty realized how serious the situation was. "What do we do?"

Ethan looked around and saw Annie coming out of the cathedral. His eyes brightened.

"This might be our chance," he said quickly. "The waterspout and the blonde thief are both out of that room. With fewer guards inside, someone could sneak up to the machine and pull the silver-haired woman out of it."

He turned to Misty and Brock. "You're the only two she hasn't seen here yet. You're best placed to do it."

"Understood!"

They nodded and hurried to one side of the square, approaching the cathedral out of sight.

Latias followed them. She seemed just as eager to free Latios.

In the middle of the square, the waterspout kept swelling. Under the same mysterious power, clouds began to cover the sky. Lightning flashed, and raindrops struck the group.

Rain fed the water; wind drove it wilder.

The waterspout stirred the surrounding air into something like a small hurricane. Anyone who knew nothing of the Soul Dew might have mistaken it for extreme weather. Only Ethan and the others understood the danger they faced.

They had to raise their voices to be heard over the wind and rain.

Ethan ignored his soaked clothes and shouted to Erika and Ash, "We have to break up that waterspout. We can't let it get any bigger!"

Both nodded. At their orders, their Pokemon concentrated their attacks on the spinning water.

They could not disperse it completely, but repeated hits tore holes through it. Water sprayed everywhere, and the vortex steadily shrank.

Fresh seawater still flowed in, yet they were holding its growth back.

"It's working!" Ash cried.

Ethan nodded. He knew this could not last, but it might buy Misty and Brock the time they needed.

"Keep going!"

While the Pokemon dodged the waterspout and chipped away at it, Misty and Brock reached a side window of the cathedral.

No one had spotted them on the way. The room inside seemed quiet. They exchanged a look, then climbed through the window with Latias.

Chapter 536: A Massive Tsunami

The hall was quiet. Even Misty and Brock's faint footsteps were lost beneath the wind and rain outside.

They met no resistance. Feeling their way through the dark, they reached the room with the machine unhindered.

It was the only room still lit in the cathedral. They had been anxious all the way there, but found no fossil Pokemon standing guard. Peering inside, they saw the machine still running. Latios remained trapped in the iron rings beside it, his power continually drained away. He was plainly in pain.

Latias could not wait to save him. She rushed toward Latios before Misty or Brock could stop her. By the time they reacted, she had reached his side.

Her movement gave the two intruders away early, costing them their chance to take Oakley by surprise.

"What rats have crept in here?"

Oakley, the silver-haired thief operating the machine, snorted. She drew on the Soul Dew to revive several fossil Pokemon that had already been defeated, sending them against Misty and Brock. Under her control, the waterspout raging in the square also turned back toward the cathedral.

Ethan and the others outside noticed at once. Certain something had gone wrong with Misty and Brock's mission, they followed the waterspout toward the building.

Inside, Misty and Brock knew they had no time to lose. They released their Pokemon and ordered them to attack the huge machine beneath Oakley.

Ancient builders had made it entirely of steel, but it still proved vulnerable to Pokemon attacks.

After barely a dozen blows, the machine began to fail. It tilted badly, throwing Oakley off balance inside its controls.

"You little pests!" Oakley shouted. "Why do you keep interfering?"

She tried to draw on the Soul Dew again. Instead, the console inside the sphere flickered and spat sparks.

The situation spun out of control. The sphere carrying Oakley began rotating over and over. The rings holding Latios drained his power even faster, like a pump pulling up water, and he cried out in agony.

Latias grew frantic. She slammed into the rings again and again, ignoring the electric shocks that struck her.

Before she could free Latios, a flash of black light came from the sphere. Misty looked up. The once flawless Soul Dew had somehow turned dark purple. A deep violet glow pulsed inside it, ominous even from a distance.

"Oh no!" Misty remembered Lorenzo's warning. "The Soul Dew has been corrupted!"

When they first saw it in the Secret Garden, Lorenzo had explained that Latias and Latios had used the jewel to repel an ancient monster and that it stood for purity. If someone with evil intentions used it, the Soul Dew would become twisted and corrupted. It would lose its original power, and the island itself might disappear. Misty had thought it was only a story. Now the darkened jewel looked as though it might explode at any moment.

Bang!

With the machine's hold weakened, Latias finally broke through the rings and freed Latios. He was in dreadful shape, badly hurt and utterly drained.

Misty looked at Brock. "Latios is free. Let's get out of here!"

Brock nodded. Supporting Latios between them, they headed for the cathedral doors. Annie, the blonde thief, came toward them as they left the room.

She had no time to deal with them. She saw the machine still spinning behind them and ran toward it in alarm.

"Oakley! Are you all right?"

The groups passed with little more than a glance. Neither tried to stop the other.

Misty felt some relief as Annie hurried away. She and Brock helped Latios outside, where Ethan and the others were coming to meet them.

Bianca brightened when she saw Latios. "You saved him?"

Misty nodded. Then she noticed how strangely quiet it was. "Wait. Where's the waterspout?"

"We don't know," Ash said. "It suddenly vanished."

The word reminded Misty of the jewel. "The Soul Dew looked corrupted. It turned black!"

"That's terrible!" Lorenzo's face changed. "Once the Soul Dew is corrupted, it will disappearand trigger a tsunami!"

Ethan frowned. "Can it be purified?"

Lorenzo shook his head. "The Soul Dew was formed from the souls of Latios and Latias. It is utterly pure. Once corrupted, it cannot be restored."

"Look around," Erika said suddenly. "Something else is wrong."

At her urging, they looked about. The rain had stopped, and the water in the surrounding canals was slowly receding.

It drained quickly. Small boats that had been afloat settled onto the exposed canal beds. Altomare was an island in the middle of the sea; even if the canals emptied, seawater should flow back into them. It should not all be withdrawing like this.

Lorenzo seemed to realize what it meant and hurried toward the shore beside the square. Ethan and the others followed his gaze. The sea beyond the city was pulling away too, as though an enormous tide were going out.

Broad stretches of reef and seabed appeared around the entire island. Countless shells and Pokemon were stranded by the sudden retreat of the water. Farther out, the ruins of a castle emerged.

The sea had covered those crumbling ruins for centuries. Only now could anyone see that such a building had once stood near the island.

Lorenzo watched the receding sea, a pale line moving steadily away. "This is bad. A tsunami is cominga massive one unlike anything we've ever seen."

"A massive tsunami?" Brock, who came from inland, did not entirely understand. "You mean there'll be a huge wave?"

"Yes." Lorenzo's face was full of worry. "The sea has never retreated this far. Even a conservative estimate puts the wave at a hundred meters high when it comes back."

"A hundred meters?"

They looked at one another. None of them thought Lorenzo was exaggerating.

"Grandpa..." Bianca's voice trembled as she asked what they were all thinking. "Can the city survive a wave that big?"

"No." Lorenzo sighed, his face ashen. "The whole city would be submerged. The people here would probably die as well..."

Chapter 537: Breaking the Wave

As Ethan watched the enormous tsunami rise like a wall, he remembered how the movie ended. It, too, had brought a wave against Altomare. To save the city and its people, Latios had spent all his strength and given his life to stop it. He had become a new Soul Dew, replacing the corrupted jewel and continuing to protect Altomare.

Now Ethan was here. Surely there was something he could do.

He had to prevent that tragedy from happening again.

Thinking it through, Latios was a Legendary Pokemon. The reason stopping the tsunami had cost him his life must have been the injuries he had suffered in captivity and the power the machine had drained from him.

Even with Latias helping, the two of them had only so much strength left.

What if another Pokemon with extraordinary power over water joined them? Could that change the outcome?

Lugia, the God of the Sea, would have been ideal. Ethan had dealt with several Lugia, and he knew they would gladly help in a crisis like this. Unfortunately, every one of them was too far away.

He did have another Legendary Pokemon skilled with water.

Ethan took a Great Ball from his bag and weighed it lightly in his hand. "It's our turn to save this city," he said to the Pokemon inside.

Not far away, Latias and Latios had noticed the tsunami too.

They exchanged a look, then flew up and circled above the Tower of the Sun. From the tower, they had a clearer view of the wave's size and destructive force.

Latios floated there, breathing hard. He and Latias could have flown away and escaped it. But they had lived in Altomare so long, and perhaps it was simply their nature: Latios would not watch the wave destroy the city.

He seemed to reach a decision and was about to fly toward it when a man's voice came from behind him.

"Latios, wait! I have an idea we can try!"

Latios turned quickly. Somehow a man had appeared at the top of the Tower of the Sun.

He recognized the young man Latias had brought into the Secret Garden earlier, though he did not know his name. Dragonite hovered beside him; it must have carried him up there.

Latios had sensed something unusual about Ethan when they first met that day. It was not his manner. He had felt two powerful presences at the man's waist.

They were not others of his own kind, but he believed they belonged to other Legendary Pokemon.

Latios called weakly to Ethan. This time, Ethan understood the gist without Gengar translating.

He opened the Great Ball. In a flash of blue light, Suicune appeared beside him.

Resting a hand on Suicune's long crest, Ethan turned to Latios. "This wave threatens all of us. You don't have to face it alone. My Pokemon will help you and Latias."

Latios and Latias regarded Suicune. It was noble-looking and calm, and both could feel the abundant power within it.

Ethan pointed toward the sea. "The wave is coming mainly from one direction. Were you planning to fly above it and break its structure, so the section headed straight for the city would collapse?"

Latios gave a small nod. It was the only solution he could think of.

"It can work," Ethan said. "I had the same idea. But in your condition, it may cost you dearly. Let Suicune help."

He waved Dragonite over and climbed back onto its back.

"We can settle the details on the way. There's no time to spare. Let's get ahead of the tsunami while it's still far from the city."

Latios and Latias followed Dragonite without objection. Suicune leaped down from the tower, touched lightly against one rooftop after another, and bounded toward the coast.

At the seafront railing by the square, Ash and the others looked up as Dragonite carried Ethan overhead with Latias and Latios. They placed their hopes in him.

Lorenzo and Bianca saw Suicune leap past them and only then realized that Ethan had caught a Pokemon so powerful.

Erika alone watched him with worry. The danger ahead was immense. She did not know how he meant to help the city survive it.

The night sea wind was cold, especially with Ethan still soaked from the earlier rain and seawater.

The exposed seabed flashed by below. After only a dozen or so seconds, they were already far from Altomare.

Ahead of them, the towering wave advanced.

From this close, it was terrifying. Ethan looked up. The wall of water rose above him until it seemed to fill the sky.

"Here!" he shouted to Latios and Latias. "Use all your strength. Suicune will work with you!"

The roar of the wave forced him to yell for them to hear.

Suicune had reached the ground below them. Latias and Latios glanced down at it, nodded, and drew on all the power they had left.

Brilliant white light burst from their bodies. Together they shone like a small sun as they flew straight at the enormous wave.

Suicune acted at the same moment.

Its command of water was unparalleled. That was the reason Ethan had trusted it with this task.

After gathering its strength, Suicune opened its mouth and sent a thick beam of energy toward the point Latias and Latios were approaching.

One force came from the air, the other from the ground. They struck the same spot on the wave almost simultaneously.

A thunderous impact followed. The water erupted as though a bomb had gone off, tearing a huge gap in the wave.

Chapter 538: A Temporary Measure

The shock wave from the impact erased most of the wall of water headed toward Altomare. The rest of the tsunami continued toward the city.

Suicune's body shone brightly. It opened its mouth again, resonating with the seawater. More than a dozen waterspouts rose from the remaining wave and twisted toward the sky. They were much smaller and weaker than the one the Soul Dew had made, but there were many of them. Water flowed upward along their spirals, breaking up the wave's movement from within.

The three Pokemon could not make the tsunami vanish altogether. They had, however, weakened the part bearing down on Altomare enough that the city could endure it.

Ethan did not hesitate. Just before the water reached Suicune, he returned it to its Great Ball. Dragonite carried him above the wave, where he searched for Latias and Latios.

Perhaps they had spent all their strength in the collision. Neither Legendary Pokemon had flown back up. They might be floating on the surface or sinking below it.

Finding them in such a huge, dark sea was no easy task.

Ethan searched without success for some time. At last Dragonite spotted them: Latias and Latios, pressed close together on the surface, drifting with the current.

At Ethan's signal, Dragonite descended. Only when they drew near could Ethan see that both Pokemon were exhausted and unable to move.

Dragonite suddenly cried out. Following its gaze, Ethan saw that the wave was about to strike the ruined castle on the exposed seabed. If he did not get Latias and Latios out of the water, the current would smash them against the stone.

"Dragonite, lift them!"

Dragonite flew above the pair and reached down with its short arms to take hold of Latios. But Latios was a large Pokemon, two meters long. After several attempts, Dragonite still could not get him into the air.

It tried Latias instead. She was smaller, yet carrying her was still a struggle.

And even if Dragonite managed to take Latias away, Latios would be left behind.

Ethan saw Dragonite's distress and felt his own frustration rising.

If Charizard were here, the two flying Pokemon could carry both Latias and Latios. But Ethan had left Charizard at Charicific Valley.

He had left Gengar on shore too, to protect Erika and the others. Gengar's powers might have lifted the pair clear of the sea if he were here.

Now Dragonite was Ethan's only flying Pokemon.

This was a problem.

The wave drew closer to the ruins. Knowing he could not wait, Ethan gritted his teeth and took two Poke Balls from his coat.

"Latios, Latias, please stay in these Poke Balls until I can get you ashore. I promise I'm not trying to catch you while you can't resist. I'll let you out as soon as we reach land!"

Latios barely had the strength to raise his head. He looked at Ethan and gave a faint nod. He seemed to understand the danger and that there was no other choice.

Beside him, Latias merely watched the Poke Balls in Ethan's hands with innocent curiosity, blinking at them.

Ethan aimed the two balls at them. Red light enveloped Latios and Latias and drew them inside.

The balls rocked only slightly in his hands. Neither Pokemon struggled. Two soft clicks sounded, and the balls fell still.

With both safe, Ethan nudged Dragonite's belly with his legs. Dragonite climbed and flew back toward Altomare.

As they left, the remainder of the tsunami struck the castle ruins. Under that immense force, the crumbling structure collapsed instantly, without raising so much as a visible splash.

The wave continued toward the city.

Dragonite flew fast. It soon landed in the square, and Ethan immediately took out the Poke Balls and released Latias and Latios.

He had meant what he said. Taking them into the balls had been a temporary measure to save them, not an attempt to take advantage of their helplessness. He let them out the moment he reached shore.

When the blue light faded, everyone crowded around the two very weak Pokemon on the ground.

"Latios! Latias! Are you all right?"

The others were a little surprised to see them emerge from Ethan's Poke Balls, but no one said anything. Even Lorenzo only sighed, his expression complicated.

Everyone understood that the rescue must have been dangerous. Ethan would not have done it unless he had no other way to save them.

Erika and Brock knelt to examine them. Finding no visible wounds, they nodded to the others.

"They've just exhausted their strength."

Before Ash could say anything, a deep rumble sounded behind them. They turned. The wave was nearly at the city. It still looked fierce, but after being weakened, it was nowhere near as terrifying as before.

"This square is low-lying," Lorenzo said. "We should get to higher ground."

They realized he was right and hurried up into the city. With everyone there to help, Ethan did not need to put Latias and Latios back into the Poke Balls.

The wave arrived quickly. It crashed against the city's seawall and poured into the canals, raising the water level visibly.

Wooden boats that had rested on the exposed canal beds were swept deeper into the city.

But the wave truly had lost much of its force. It flooded some low areas without causing further destruction.

Ethan and the others climbed a dozen or so steps. At that height, the seawater could no longer reach them.

About half an hour later, the water began to recede. The overwhelming danger seemed, at last, to have passed.

Chapter 539: The Best Outcome

The seawater slowly receded.

Although it did not seem to have caused a disaster, it had still left its mark.

The ground floors of some buildings had flooded, soaking furniture and appliances in seawater. Many small boats had vanished too. No one knew whether they had drifted into the city or been carried out to sea as the water withdrew.

For the people who owned them, the losses were considerable. Fortunately, no one had been hurt in the tsunami. That was a stroke of luck amid the misfortune.

The commotion woke the city's residents. They switched on their lights and leaned out from their balconies to look around. Seawater had risen above the canals and spread half a meter deep into the city. They were baffled, but none of them knew what had happened.

Perhaps when day broke, they would hear on the news that a great tsunami had struck in the night, only to be stopped by something and dissipate.

On a rise above the city, Misty watched everything settle back into calm and let out a sigh. "It's finally over..."

"Wait!" Brock suddenly remembered something. "What happened to those two thieves?"

The sky was already beginning to lighten. While there were still few people about, Ethan had Lorenzo and Bianca take Latias and Latios, who were too weak to change their appearances, back to the Secret Garden. He and the others hurried straight to the cathedral.

But Annie and Oakley were long gone. All that remained were fossils scattered across the floor and the damaged machine.

As for the corrupted Soul Dew, it had shattered into fragments strewn everywhere.

"Damn it!" Ash said angrily at the sight. "They caused all of this, and in the end they just got away!"

"It is a shame," Ethan agreed. "But we couldn't help it. All our attention was on the tsunami. One mistake could have been disastrous. How could we have spared anyone to guard them? I believe we'll meet them again someday, though. When we do, we'll bring them to justice."

Brock hesitated. "Earlier... I thought the woman called Oakley had suffered a backlash from the Soul Dew too. She looked awful. It seemed like she was seriously hurt."

"Hmph." Misty raised her head with a snort. "They brought it on themselves. Serves them right!"

"All right." Seeing that they were about to say more, Ethan cut them off. "We can't stay here. Let's go before someone sees all this and decides we're the ones responsible. We'd never be able to explain ourselves."

They left the cathedral and returned to the Secret Garden.

When Bianca saw them come back, she prepared hot tea and brought over towels and some pastries.

"Come and dry yourselves off. After everything you've been through, you must be hungry and tired."

She was right. Latias had woken them in the middle of the night, and they had not had so much as a sip of water since. If they had not eaten a large meal before bed, they would have been ravenous by now.

With the tension finally gone, everyone's eyelids grew heavy and their energy drained away.

After a little care, Latias and Latios had recovered some strength. They were no longer in danger. The two Pokemon lay close together, dozing as they drifted off to sleep.

The sight filled Ethan with relief.

Compared with the ending of the movie, he had saved Latios's life and spared Latias the pain of losing her family.

After eating a little, the group stayed in the garden rather than returning to the Pokemon Center. They lay down fully dressed in one of its wooden cottages. Bianca found several blankets for them, warm and snug, and Ethan lost consciousness almost the moment he lay down.

He slept soundly.

When Ethan woke, everyone else was already up and out of the room. He rubbed his groggy head and stepped outside. Ash and Pikachu were playing with Latias and Latios.

"You're awake?"

Erika, some distance away, was the first to notice him.

She was brushing his Jolteon's fur. His Gengar had shamelessly attached itself to her as well, pestering her to scratch it.

It looked as though his Pokemon had already taken Erika for the lady of the house. They showed no reserve around her at all.

Looking around, he saw Misty and Ash helping Bianca prepare food. The mood was as relaxed and cheerful as ever, just as it had been when they first came to the Secret Garden.

Ethan nodded to Erika, then walked to the pool where the Soul Dew had once rested. He turned to Lorenzo. "What will you do now that the Soul Dew is gone?"

Lorenzo shook his head. "Even without the Soul Dew, having Latias and Latios here is the best outcome we could have hoped for. I'm sure they'll continue to protect this place, and I'll make sure the legend of the Soul Dew lives on!"

Speaking of Latias and Latios...

Ethan took out their Poke Balls and held them out to Lorenzo.

"These are their Poke Balls. I'd like you to keep them here."

"Oh?" Lorenzo did not take them at once. He looked at Ethan curiously. "You aren't taking them with you?"

"Taking them?" Ethan shook his head. "They belong here, and they like it here. Where would I take them? Besides, I already have plenty of Legendary Pokemon at my side. Let them go on living here without a care."

Lorenzo remembered Suicune leaping past them earlier. He knew Ethan was not boasting. With a Legendary Pokemon like that beside him, Ethan had less reason than most people to covet others.

But another question still troubled him. "Why give me their Poke Balls instead of releasing them completely?"

"It's a precaution," Ethan said with a small smile. "I expect more people like those two thieves will set their sights on them someday. Even ordinary people who happen upon them might try to catch them. Since they're already registered to these Poke Balls, at least no one with bad intentions can capture them in another."

"I see!" Lorenzo said as understanding dawned. "Because of how Poke Balls work, no one else can catch them with one now. And even if someone gets hold of them, we can call them back into these balls!"

Ethan smiled and nodded. That was exactly what he meant.

Latias and Latios seemed to sense something. They left Ash and Pikachu, flew over, and saw the two Poke Balls.

Under their gaze, Lorenzo accepted the balls. With solemn care, he placed them where the Soul Dew had once been.

"Then this is where they'll stay..." He looked at the two Poke Balls side by side and spoke from the heart. "From now on, they'll take the Soul Dew's place in guarding this Secret Garden!"

Chapter 540: Leaving Altomare

After a generous lunch prepared by Brock and Bianca and another night's rest, they had fully recovered from the previous day's exhaustion.

What a remarkable visit to Altomare it had been. They had entered a water race and won the championship, toured the beautiful city, and met Latias, Latios, Lorenzo, and Bianca. They had thwarted the schemes of two thieves said to be the best in the world and saved the city from a massive tsunami.

Any one of those events would have kept them busy under ordinary circumstances. Yet all of them had happened within twenty-four hours!

Now that everything had settled, it was time to leave the city and continue their journey.

They told Lorenzo and Bianca they were going. Lorenzo took the news calmly, but Bianca's face showed how reluctant she was to see them leave.

They had known one another only a short time, but everything they had been through had forged a strong friendship. Of course she wished they could stay longer.

She also knew they were Trainers with places to go. They could not remain in one city for long.

"I have something for you."

With that, Bianca dashed away. A dozen or so seconds later, she returned carrying a sheet of drawing paper.

"I drew this while you were sleeping. Thank you for saving my grandfather and me, and for saving Latias and Latios. Thank you for saving the city too. I don't have anything valuable enough to show how much that means to me, so I made you this picture."

"A picture?"

Ash was about to reach for it, but Ethan took it first.

The others crowded around to look. It was a crayon drawing of all seven of them, standing side by side with the water city of Altomare behind them. Latias and Latios flew above their heads, while Pikachu perched on Ash's shoulder. Bright colors filled the page, and everyone wore a broad smile. The picture was full of life. Bianca was clearly a skilled artist, and she had put her heart into it.

"It's beautiful!" Misty said. "Thank you, Bianca."

"Oh, it's nothing..." Bianca blushed. "Compared with what you've done, this hardly counts. I just hope you like it."

"Don't say that," Ethan said with a smile. "What could matter more in a gift than the thought behind it? We'll treasure your picture."

He had said we, but he ignored the look on Ash's face that said he wanted it too. Ethan tucked the drawing inside his coat.

It was a precious memory, and there was only one copy. How could he possibly hand it over to that kid? When he had the chance, he would get it framed and hang it in his room.

Hearing that Ethan and the others were leaving, Latias and Latios came over as well. Latias in particular hated saying goodbye. She rubbed her cheek affectionately against Ash and Pikachu, then circled the rest of the group a few times.

Latios was steadier than his sister. He simply watched them with gratitude before turning his gaze to Ethan.

He was not oblivious to what had happened. Last nightno, in the early hours of this morningEthan had taken him and his sister into Poke Balls. From that moment, they had ceased to be wild Pokemon. Their lives might look much the same as before, but they were bound to those balls, and Ethan could return them to them whenever he wished.

Did that mean he and his sister were now Ethan's Pokemon? Still, Latios knew it had been the only way to save them, and the man seemed decent. He did not particularly mind.

Leaving the Secret Garden, the group went back to the Pokemon Center for their luggage and then headed to the harbor.

They would take a ship back to the Johto mainland and resume their travels.

Lorenzo and Bianca saw them all the way onto the ship. When the passenger ferry pulled away, the two waved goodbye. As it sailed farther and farther out, their figures finally disappeared from view.

Goodbye, Altomare. Goodbye, Bianca.

A sea breeze brushed across the group.

Standing on deck, they watched the water city shrink in the distance. They could not help feeling sad to leave. Who would not want a little more time with friends, if they had the chance?

But that was life. After saying goodbye to yesterday, they still had an unknown tomorrow ahead of them.

"Look!"

Misty suddenly pointed toward the sky. The others looked up and caught glimpses of two shapes among the clouds, one blue and one red. They immediately realized that Latios and Latias had come to see them off.

"Goodbye!"

Ash waved at the clouds and shouted. The other passengers looked skyward at his strange behavior. A few gasped as something seemed to flash past.

"Huh?" A man in a flowered shirt, with a gold chain around his neck, rubbed his eyes. "I think I just saw Latias and Latios!"

"What are you talking about?" His girlfriend rolled her eyes. "Latias and Latios are only legends. This is a busy city. Why would they be here?"

"I did see them! I'm telling you!" The man pursed his lips in annoyance and pointed upward. "Look for yourself... Huh? Where did they go?"

The woman looked up. The sky was just the sky; there was no Pokemon in sight. She shook her head helplessly. "You had too many cocktails. You must have imagined it. Why would there be Legendary Pokemon here?"

Ethan and the others exchanged knowing smiles as they listened.

Like the statues on Altomare's shore, the legend of Latias, Latios, and the Soul Dew would live on in the city, giving its people something to talk about for years to come...

...

The ferry did not retrace the route they had taken to Altomare. It sailed straight to a small harbor outside Cherrygrove City.

It was a slow ship. After a night at sea, Ethan and the others finally set foot on the Johto mainland the next morning.

They parted ways at the harbor. Ash, Misty, and Brock were heading off to earn Ash's final badge, while Ethan and Erika would make for Silver Town.

Knowing they would meet again soon, they kept their goodbyes casual and simply waved.

"Then I'll see you at the Silver Conference!" Ethan said with a smile.

"That's only a few days away." Ash rubbed his nose, unconcerned. "As soon as I've challenged Blackthorn Gym, I'll come find you!"

"Clair won't be easy to beat. Don't get so confident that you slip up," Ethan said with a chuckle. "It's settled, then. I'll be waiting for you in Silver Town!"

Chapter 541: Ethan Makes His Move

Cherrygrove City was a small seaside town on the southern coast of Johto. It had no Gym, and it was not even as well known as Azalea Town.

The scent of flowers and the sea breeze were its defining features. Ethan had passed through on his way from New Bark Town before, but he had not spent much time looking around, and the place had left little impression on him. Erika, on the other hand, seemed perfectly suited to it.

She liked the city as soon as she set foot in it.

From the harbor, Ash and his friends headed north. Ethan and Erika needed to go east, then turn north at New Bark Town toward Mt. Silver and Silver Town.

After parting from the others, they did not linger in the little city. They headed straight out.

Erika had some luck. Shortly after leaving Cherrygrove, she came across another Grass-type Pokemon on a plain and caught it.

Her trip through Johto had been rewarding. She had set out hoping to catch Pokemon, and by now she had caught five or six, more or less meeting her original goal.

There was still some time before the Silver Conference, so they were in no hurry. When they reached New Bark Town that evening, they visited Professor Elm. At his warm invitation, they stayed the night at his home.

There Ethan met the professor's wife and son. The boy looked so much like his father that Ethan would have recognized the relationship without an introduction.

Ethan and Erika gave the family the gifts they had brought for the visit, earning an even warmer welcome.

At dinner, Ethan and Professor Elm shared a few drinks. Perhaps Kurt was not there to keep filling his glass, or perhaps his wife was watching him. Either way, the professor did not get thoroughly drunk again as he had at Kurt's house.

At bedtime, however, Ethan and Erika found themselves in an awkward situation they had faced more than once before.

Maybe Professor Elm's wife had noticed how they looked at each other and how close they stood. Or perhaps Elm had seen them stay under the same roof at Kurt's house and told her about it. Whatever the reason, she had put Ethan and Erika in the same room.

Once inside, they exchanged wry smiles. They had lost count of how often this had happened.

They were used to it by now and made no attempt to explain themselves to Professor Elm. This time, though, their hearts beat a little faster. The room held only one double bed, and there was only one blanket.

"Well..." Ethan looked at Erika. "Should I sleep on the floor tonight?"

Erika's ears reddened slightly. "It's all right. We can share the bed. We don't have to stand on ceremony when we're traveling."

At that, Ethan did not insist. He had only offered as a way of edging toward what he wanted anyway. With a soft bed right there, why would he sleep on the hard floor?

Erika bathed first. When Ethan had finished washing too, she was already lying in bed.

He turned out the light and slipped under the blanket. In the moonlight, Erika had her back to him. Her faint fragrance reached him, and with the drinks giving him courage, he could no longer hold back his desire.

He turned toward her and slowly reached out, resting his hand on her waist beneath the blanket.

Erika was clearly still awake. He could feel her body trembling slightly, and her breathing quickened.

He waited several seconds. When she made no other move, he grew bolder.

His hand slid down and slipped inside her pajamas, coming to rest on the smooth skin of her stomach.

The touch made his pulse race. Erika still did not respond, so he slowly moved his hand upward toward her breasts. Just before he reached them, she raised an arm and pinned his hand with her elbow through the fabric of her pajamas.

The room was frighteningly quiet. With Erika facing away, Ethan could not see her expression, but the warmth rising from her body told him she must be blushing.

He pressed a little harder, slipped past her elbow, and cupped one of her breasts in his hand.

This time Erika did not stop him. Her lips parted, and amid her heavy breaths Ethan could even hear a faint moan.

That gave him all the courage he needed. He moved closer, then turned her toward him. Her eyes met his, hazy in the dim light.

As they looked at each other, Ethan could see the fluster in Erika's face. She could hardly meet his gaze. Looking at her, he acted on impulse and pressed his lips to hers.

...

The next morning, Ethan came to the dining room yawning. The moment he sat down at the table, he found Professor Elm smiling at him.

With his wife cooking in the kitchen, Elm cleared his throat and spoke quietly. "You're young and full of energy, but you should pace yourself. Some things shouldn't keep you up so late!"

Erika had just entered the dining room and heard him. She stopped in her tracks, her face turning scarlet. Ethan gave an embarrassed smile. He knew exactly what Elm meant.

Spurred on by the drinks last night, he had finally made love to Erika. She was a little fuller figured than Sabrina and Maya, and he had been so taken with her that they had gone at it several times. Before he knew it, they had stayed up well past midnight.

They must have disturbed Professor Elm's sleep.

Erika sat beside Ethan, keeping her head down. She had just stripped the disheveled, bloodstained sheet from the bed and tucked it into her bag. If she left it here for the professor and his wife to find, she would never be able to face them again.

Fortunately, Elm's wife brought in the food, giving Erika a reprieve from her embarrassment.

After breakfast, they formally took their leave of the couple.

"I hope you win the championship!" Professor Elm said with a smile. "I'm sure you can do it. If I can find the time, I'll come and watch your matches in person!"

"Thank you for your good wishes," Ethan said. He and Erika stood outside and bowed slightly to the couple seeing them off. "And thank you for having us. We'll be on our way now!"

"Have a safe trip!"

They waved goodbye, then headed north from Professor Elm's house and left New Bark Town.

After that night, both their feelings and their relationship had changed completely.

Chapter 542: Ho-Oh Temple

After leaving New Bark Town, Ethan and Erika headed north. They traveled all day, leaving the plains behind and reaching the mountains around Mt. Silver by nightfall.

They passed a Pokemon conservation area along the way, but Ethan had no interest in going in. After another half hour of walking, they found a level spot beside a stream and pitched their tent just before dark.

After dinner, Erika grew restless under Ethan's increasingly heated gaze.

She knew what was about to happen.

Last night, he had made his move after drinking, and she had found it hard to refuse him. Tonight it was just the two of them. If she let it happen again, she would be accepting what he wanted.

But given how they felt about each other, she could not bring herself to turn him away.

Besides, she had already given herself to him the night before. There was little point in holding back now.

For Ethan, being alone meant he could finally relax and enjoy himself without worrying about anyone interrupting.

It had been Erika's first time last night, and they had been guests in someone else's home. He had not been able to do all he wanted. Now she was a little more accustomed to him, and no one was around to listen through the walls. He could give himself over to the night.

After they washed up by the stream, he grinned and led Erika into the tent early. As he lowered the flap, he glanced at Scizor and Jolteon, who were keeping watch outside, and motioned for them to move farther away and leave him alone.

The flap fell shut. By the light inside, Gengar, which had been sent out too, could see Ethan's shadow eagerly pulling Erika down. It turned to Scizor and Jolteon and spread its hands.

"See that?" Gengar grumbled. "Young people. It's barely dark and they're already in there having fun, leaving us out here in the cold!"

Gengar had lived for more than two thousand years. It had seen just about everything and was used to this sort of thing between humans.

It was only mating. What was there to be embarrassed about? Did they really have to make Gengar leave? Did they honestly think it wanted to watch?

Gengar poked the burning wood with a stick. Scizor and Jolteon merely yawned, found comfortable spots beside the campfire, and lay down. They did not seem to mind keeping watch at all. Gengar let out a long, helpless sigh.

You two obedient fools deserve to sit out here in the cold.

Ah...

It looked up at the sky and sighed to itself.

My companions aren't too bright. This team is hard to lead...

Inside the tent, Ethan laid out the bedding and gazed at Erika before slowly moving closer.

"Wait..." Erika's face turned bright red. "Turn off the light first..."

Ethan smiled. That was an easy request to grant. He reached over and switched off the camping lamp, plunging the tent into darkness.

Fortunately, moonlight filtered through the fabric, so it was not completely black inside.

He guided Erika down onto the bedding, then reached into his bag and took something out.

It was the pack of condoms he had left over from his time with Sabrina. She had departed so suddenly that they had not used them all. He had not expected to use them with Erika.

Well, at least they would not go to waste.

...

After a night's rest, the two packed up and set out for Silver Town.

Ethan had certainly enjoyed himself the night before.

He was tired, though.

Erika looked more radiant than ever. When she glanced at Ethan, her gaze was so gentle it seemed ready to melt.

Their relationship had advanced quickly. In both body and heart, she now felt she belonged to him, and everything she did showed a tender, caring side of her.

Even the way she spoke to Ethan had grown softer.

Mt. Silver stood in eastern Johto. Strictly speaking, it was part of the same mountain range as the Indigo Plateau, not far from the site of the Indigo League. It belonged to Johto by location, however, placing the two tournament sites in different regions.

Silver Town sat at the foot of Mt. Silver beside a lake. It had Johto's largest Pokemon Center, several competition venues, and a fully equipped village for the competitors. The whole town had been built around the Silver Conference.

Before entering Silver Town, however, Ethan and Erika passed Ho-Oh Temple.

It was said that the ceremonial flame for each year's Silver Conference came from this temple. Some Trainers considered it a sacred place and visited before the tournament to pray for a good result.

Ethan had not come to pray. He was simply curious and wanted to look around.

They walked through the open gate into the temple grounds.

As they had expected, a few other Trainers were there. There would probably be more as the tournament drew near.

On the day before the opening, crowds of Trainers would flock here to watch the flame carried to the stadium.

Erika opened her travel guide again and smiled. "There's a legend about this temple. Long ago, a terrible battle was fought here, and countless Pokemon were killed or wounded. The fighting grew worse until the land was barren. Ho-Oh, furious, burned the humans' weapons, then restored the lake and the earth. Seeing that, the people reflected on what they had done. They called the fire that remained the sacred flame and kept it in the temple, passing it down from generation to generation. Now it serves as the source of the Silver Conference flame. That's how the temple got its name!"

"Another legend about Ho-Oh... Why does it turn up everywhere?"

Ethan pursed his lips at the name. He still held quite a grudge against Ho-Oh. If it had not interfered, he would have caught all three Legendary beasts by now!

Erika chuckled at his expression. After only a few laughs, she saw the suggestive way he was watching her lips. Remembering the night before, she blushed and quickly stopped smiling.

They climbed a long flight of stone steps and finally reached a shrine building.

But just as they stepped onto the hilltop, before they could approach the shrine, two Pokemon suddenly sprang out and blocked Ethan's path.

On closer inspection, they were a Machoke and a Machop.

"Huh?" Ethan stopped and looked at them in puzzlement. "What's this about?"

Machoke and Machop made threatening gestures at him. Then a dark shape flashed before his eyes, and a catlike Pokemon leaped between them!

Chapter 543: Sneasel Rules the Temple

Ethan had seen this black, catlike Pokemon more than once. It was Sneasel, a Dark- and Ice-type Pokemon.

Sneasel's appearance might have been inspired by the Japanese kamaitachi, or perhaps by a mix of a kamaitachi and a cat. Its body was mostly black, with a red tail, silvery white claws, and small gold markings on its forehead and chest. Sharp claws hid in its fingers.

Although Ethan had encountered Sneasel many times, he had never really learned much about it.

Now one had leaped in front of him with a vicious look. He raised his Pokedex and aimed it at the Pokemon.

The Pokedex chimed. "Sneasel, the Sharp Claw Pokemon. Dark and Ice type. Sneasel generally live in cold places and are cunning and vicious. They suddenly extend their sharp claws to intimidate attackers. They often hide in the dark to stay inconspicuous and hunt cooperatively at night. One draws the parents away while another steals an egg, though they may quarrel endlessly over who gets to eat it. In Alola, they have even been recorded preying on Sandshrew."

Ethan put the Pokedex away and looked at the Sneasel again.

It was plainly wild. It had its mouth open and seemed to be saying something to him, while Machoke and Machop flanked it like bodyguards or underlings.

Ethan glanced down at his feet. "Hey, Gengar, what's it saying?"

Gengar poked half its head out of his shadow. "It says this place belongs to it, and you aren't allowed to trespass."

"Your territory?" Ethan stared at Sneasel in surprise. "Isn't this a temple? How did it become yours? Are you one of the temple's Pokemon?"

The question seemed to provoke Sneasel. With a sudden roar, it sprang at Ethan and slashed at his face.

Ethan dodged backward, avoiding the attack. He frowned.

"What are you doing?"

Sneasel spoke again, and Gengar translated. "It says it's no Pokemon of you despicable humans, and you should leave at once."

Hearing the disturbance, a young man in black training clothes ran out of a nearby building and hurried over.

"Are you all right?" he asked Ethan. He glanced at Sneasel too, his face full of worry.

He appeared to work at the temple, so Ethan asked, "What's the story with this Sneasel?"

The man sighed. "It's a wild Pokemon from around here. It moved in and won't leave. We haven't been able to do anything about it."

Ethan was astonished. "Why don't you drive it away?"

"Well..." The man scratched his cheek awkwardly. "We've tried several times, but we can't beat it. Even the Trainers we asked for help lost to it. Recently it made that Machop and Machoke its followers, so now there's even less we can do!"

Erika spoke up. "So it has taken over the place?"

"It's causing us a lot of trouble," the man said with a sigh. "The Silver Conference is coming soon. With it occupying the temple, we can't even get close, let alone bring out the sacred flame!"

"I see." Ethan nodded. "Since we're here, I'll help. I just need to drive it off, right?"

"...I'd appreciate it."

The temple attendant gave a polite smile, but he did not look hopeful. As he had said, other Trainers had offered to help and made bold promises. In the end, they had accomplished nothing and only gotten their Pokemon hurt. Perhaps this would end the same way.

Ethan took several Poke Balls from his belt pouch and studied Sneasel again.

It had driven off that many Trainers, so it clearly had some ability. He would not underestimate it.

Besides, this was a good chance to train his own Pokemon.

He threw the Poke Balls. Blue light flashed, and Dragonite, Tyranitar, Scizor, and Eevee appeared before Sneasel.

Against Machop, Machoke, and Sneasel, each of the four faced at least some disadvantage in type matchups.

Ethan had chosen them deliberately. He wanted them to practice turning a battle around when the types were against them.

Of course, he did not want to lose. Sending out four Pokemon against three gave them a better chance of winning.

At the sight of Ethan's team, Sneasel roared and charged before they could make a move.

Machoke and Machop rushed in with it, closing on Ethan's Pokemon from both sides.

No wonder it had beaten so many Trainers. Even outnumbered, Sneasel dared to attack first.

Ethan thought a little more highly of it.

"Tyranitar, Scizor, keep Machoke and Machop busy! Eevee, help Dragonite deal with Sneasel!"

At his command, the four split up and faced their assigned opponents.

As Fighting types, Machop and Machoke had a decisive type advantage over Rock- and Dark-type Tyranitar. Scizor's Bug typing, at least, offset some of the weakness its Steel typing had to their Fighting-type attacks.

Dragonite and Eevee closed in on Sneasel together. Eevee, a Normal type, was in better shape. Against a Dark- and Ice-type like Sneasel, Dragonite's Dragon- and Flying-type combination put it at a severe disadvantage, just as Tyranitar was against the Fighting types.

Erika surveyed the matchups with concern. "Are you sure this is a good idea?"

"If they win, they win," Ethan said casually. "It isn't a tournament match. If they can't manage it, I have other Pokemon to back them up. Think of it as training."

Erika had nothing more to say, though she still worried. They were Ethan's Pokemon, and because she cared about him, she did not want any of them hurt.

Fortunately, his Pokemon were strong, while Machoke and Machop were not especially formidable. Tyranitar and Scizor soon gained the upper hand.

Dragonite, however, was in trouble.

It had failed to dodge one of Sneasel's Ice-type attacks, and the hit left it in poor condition. If Eevee had not kept drawing Sneasel's attention away, Dragonite might already have been defeated!

Chapter 544: In Pursuit

Sneasel stood less than a meter tall, but it was quick and agile. It dodged a Fire Punch from Dragonite, then darted in and raked its sharp claws across Dragonite's body, leaving long scratches.

Before it could press its advantage, a shadow flashed before it. That energetic Eevee had charged in again.

What a nuisance. Eevee was not especially strong, but Sneasel could not shake it. It seemed to enjoy chasing Sneasel, as though the pursuit itself were a game. Whenever Sneasel had Dragonite where it wanted it, Eevee jumped in and disrupted its rhythm.

Sneasel found a moment to look at its two followers. They were not doing well either.

To its surprise, Machop and Machoke had the type advantage, yet they still could not beat the human's Tyranitar and Scizor.

The gap in strength was too wide for type advantage to make up.

Seeing that, Sneasel pushed itself to its limit. It forced Dragonite and Eevee back for a moment, then leaped in front of its followers.

It bared its teeth and barked a few threats at Tyranitar and Scizor. Then, without looking back, it led Machop and Machoke into the mountain forest.

"It... it ran away?"

The temple attendant's face brightened. Had the Sneasel that had troubled them for so long really been driven off?

He had seen the fight clearly, though. Sneasel had barely been hurt. Why had it chosen to flee?

Still, its departure meant the shrine that held the sacred flame was back in the temple's hands.

Ethan glanced at the attendant and shook his head. "Don't celebrate yet. Sneasel has only gone away for now. If we don't settle this properly, it'll come back sooner or later."

The attendant's face fell. He looked hopefully at Ethan. "Could you help us drive them away from here?"

Compared with the Trainers he had asked before, this man's Pokemon seemed much stronger. For the first time, the attendant felt hopeful.

Ethan considered the request and did not answer at once.

Sneasel was a wild Pokemon. Perhaps it had come here because it had nowhere else to go and had made the shrine its territory.

It had never gone down the mountain to attack people. It only fought when someone approached. That suggested it was not malicious; it simply wanted others to keep away.

If they drove it off, where would it go? Would it have to wander in search of another home?

But leaving it in control of the temple was no solution either.

Ethan explained his thoughts to the attendant, who was silent for a while.

"I see. I hadn't thought it through," the attendant said with a sigh. Working at a temple, he knew he ought to show compassion. "I was only trying to make it leave. I never considered things from its point of view. Now that you've pointed it out, I realize Sneasel must have left its own group to make a home here."

Erika thought for a moment. "Then why not call it back and talk? If it truly likes this place and doesn't want to leave, it could stay and live alongside you, as long as it agrees not to interfere when you take the sacred flame to the tournament."

The attendant hesitated. "But you saw it. It won't talk to us."

"That's easy enough," Ethan said. "If it won't talk, we'll battle it until it will."

With that, he led his Pokemon into the forest. Erika went with him, following the direction in which Sneasel had fled.

Mt. Silver's forests were known for their thick growth and sturdy trees. Towering trunks stood everywhere, and anyone unfamiliar with the terrain could easily get lost by venturing too far in.

Fortunately, Sneasel, Machop, and Machoke had entered only moments earlier. Ethan could follow the fresh footprints they had left behind.

Most were Machoke's. Its feet were large, and its body was packed with muscle. Wherever it stepped on soft ground, it left a clear print.

Perhaps Sneasel had not expected anyone to follow.

After only a few hundred meters, Ethan and Erika found all three Pokemon resting beneath a tree.

They were startled to see the humans and scrambled into a fighting formation.

"Sneasel, wait. We aren't here to fight. We only want to talk about the temple!"

Ethan tried words before force. He held off on ordering an attack, hoping they could settle the matter by talking.

But he had underestimated how wild Sneasel was. He had barely finished speaking when it growled, and all three charged.

So much for that. Just as Ethan had said, they would have to beat Sneasel before it would listen.

"Dragonite, you and the others, go!"

Ethan waved his Pokemon forward again. This time he changed the pairings to give them different practice. Dragonite and Eevee faced Machoke and Machop, while Tyranitar and Scizor took on their leader, Sneasel.

The change, combined with the strength of Ethan's Pokemon, immediately made a difference.

Dragonite, Tyranitar, and Scizor were no longer facing opponents that countered their types. They could fight at full strength, and their opponents gave ground almost at once.

Sneasel, for example, had been comfortable against Dragonite. Now Tyranitar and Scizor confronted it together. It would have struggled with either one alone, let alone both of them.

Before long, it was panting and drenched in sweat from dodging their attacks.

When Sneasel found a chance to look at its followers, Dragonite and Eevee had already beaten them.

Panic threw it off. In a moment of inattention, Scizor caught it by the neck with one huge pincer and slammed it against a tree trunk.

With the fight decided, Ethan walked over and looked at Sneasel.

"Well? Ready to behave?"

Sneasel turned its head and snorted. It clearly was not happy about losing.

Ethan paid no mind to its attitude. He smiled and motioned to his Pokemon. With the others escorting them, Scizor carried Sneasel back toward Ho-Oh Temple in its pincer.

He left Machop and Machoke alone. He had their leader; there was no reason to concern himself with the two underlings.

Chapter 545: Just Like a Married Couple

As they escorted Sneasel back, Erika leaned close and asked Ethan quietly, "This Sneasel seems special. Aren't you going to catch it?"

Ethan thought for a moment, then shook his head.

"No. It looks cool and it's strong, but I'm not especially interested in this kind of Pokemon. I'd rather wait until I meet one I really like."

Erika smiled. He had said more than once that too many Pokemon would stretch his attention thin. If he was going to catch one, he needed to truly want it.

Clearly, this Sneasel was not to his taste.

They were only halfway back when Dragonite gave a soft cry. It had spotted something.

Following its gaze, they looked up. Far away, a large yellow bird wreathed in flames flashed through the clouds.

Ethan had seen it often enough to recognize it almost immediately.

"Huh? Is that Moltres?"

Erika was surprised too. "There's a Moltres here?"

Ethan nodded. There were tales of Moltres being seen in the mountains around Mt. Silver. He had not expected them to encounter one themselves.

Moltres appeared for only a moment before vanishing from sight.

After that brief interruption, they continued down the mountain and soon reached Ho-Oh Temple again.

The attendant could not hide his delight when he saw that Ethan had brought Sneasel back.

"We'll leave Sneasel with you, then. We won't get in your way any longer."

At Ethan's signal, Scizor handed Sneasel over to the attendant. How they talked things through was up to them; Ethan did not intend to take part.

To thank them, the attendant invited Ethan and Erika to stay for a vegetarian meal while he spoke with Sneasel. After they had eaten, he returned with the news that Sneasel had agreed to their proposal. It would continue living near the shrine, try to coexist peacefully with people, and neither disturb visitors nor interfere with the sacred flame.

Ethan was glad to hear it. Many people devoted their lives to helping humans and Pokemon live together. Seeing the temple and Sneasel set aside their mistrust and share a place was the best outcome he could have hoped for.

He and Erika said goodbye and continued toward Silver Town.

The town was close to Ho-Oh Temple. After another half hour on the road, they arrived at the site of the Silver Conference.

The town truly had been built for the tournament. Advertisements, souvenirs, and decorations bearing the Silver Conference theme were everywhere.

They followed the broad main road around the stadium to the Pokemon Center behind it.

Ethan had already completed the final registration formalities, so there was little to do. He collected a guide to the Silver Conference, checked in, and went to the competitors' village.

Few entrants had arrived yet, although some Trainers who had collected all their badges in previous years were already there.

Even that small crowd made the atmosphere livelier.

The competitors' village was behind the Pokemon Center, down a short street lined with snack stalls and vendors. There were tempting things to eat and little amusements everywhere.

They had plenty of time to explore later. For now, they went straight to their lodgings.

At the Indigo League, the competitors had stayed in separate little houses. Here, everyone stayed in one large hotel, with each entrant given a spacious private suite. Every suite had a living room and bathroom, like a luxury apartment.

Ethan took out the keycard. When he and Erika saw the room they had been assigned, they exchanged a smile.

It looked comfortable, far better than they had expected. It felt like a home.

And speaking of home...

Ethan gazed at Erika. She would make a wonderful wife. A home and a wife: everything was here!

Erika felt his eyes on her and seemed to have the same thought. Deliberately avoiding his gaze, she set their bags aside and began putting away their clothes. Once she had arranged their things, it looked as though they lived there together.

"Ahem... Well." Ethan cleared his throat. "We've been walking a long time. We're both dirty. Why don't we take a bath first?"

Erika blushed. She knew exactly what he was thinking. "No... It's still daytime..."

Despite her words, she let herself be persuaded, and Ethan pulled her into the bathroom. How they bathed, and what else they did there, was nobody else's business.

...

Over the following days, Ethan and Erika lived much like a married couple. He trained his Pokemon, devised strategies, and worked on their weaknesses. Erika looked after him and prepared nutritious food for his Pokemon.

There was a dedicated restaurant at the competition grounds, but they never visited it. Erika prepared all three meals each day, and she clearly enjoyed doing so.

In their free time, they walked arm in arm through the area, buying small trinkets and gifts or stocking up at the supermarket. Each time, Ethan would buy several boxes of condoms under Erika's embarrassed gaze. They were going through them quickly, using two or three almost every day, sometimes more.

As they enjoyed their time together, the days passed and the start of the tournament drew closer.

Finally, on the day before it began, Ash and his two friends arrived at last.

Ethan had no idea what had delayed them. Blackthorn Gym and then Silver Town should have taken only a few days, yet somehow they had not arrived until now.

All three looked surprised when they saw Erika. Misty could not help saying, "That's strange, Erika. It's only been a few days, but you look so well. Your skin is glowing, and you seem positively radiant!"

Even though she was speaking to children, Erika could not help feeling shy.

She gave Ethan a sidelong look.
