What else could it be? Ethan had been satisfying her every day.

Chapter 546: The Competitors Gather

"All right, that's enough talk for now," Ethan said with a smile. "You look worn out from the road. Go register before it closes, then get back to your room and wash up."

Ash remembered that this was the final day to register. He wasted no time and hurried into the Pokemon Center with Pikachu.

Ethan, Erika, Misty, and Brock stayed outside to catch up. They had barely begun talking when Ash came rushing back.

"All done!" He gave them a thumbs-up, grinning broadly.

"Let's go," Ethan said. "I'll show you to your room. Then, as usual, dinner's on me!"

"Yeah!" Ash and Misty cheered together.

They were about to leave when another familiar face came toward them.

"Ash! Ethan! I didn't expect to see you here. It's been a long time!"

They turned toward the voice. It was Gary.

Ethan remembered meeting him shortly after arriving in Johto. Gary had been passing through and had said he intended to enter the Silver Conference. Ethan had heard nothing of him since. Now here he was.

But something had changed.

Whatever sort of journey Gary had been on, he looked steadier than before. His sports car was gone, and so were the cheerleaders who had once followed him everywhere. He stood alone with a small bag on his back.

The sight of his fellow Pallet Town Trainer and rival filled Ash with energy.

"Gary!" Ash pointed at him in delight. "So you're entering the Silver Conference too!"

Gary sighed. "You really don't pay attention, do you? After the Indigo League, we battled at my grandfather's house. I told you that day I was going to enter the Silver Conference."

"Huh?" Ash scratched his cheek awkwardly. "Did you? Sorry. I forgot..."

"Honestly..."

Gary turned away from Ash and fixed his gaze on Ethan.

"This time, I'm going to avenge my last loss. I'll beat you!"

He was still bothered that Ethan had knocked him out of the Indigo League.

Ethan was not intimidated. He smiled lightly. "I'll take you on whenever you're ready. First you'll have to reach me. Don't let someone else eliminate you along the way!"

"Don't worry," Gary said, shaking his head. "I've staked everything on this tournament. I'm going to be the champion."

"No, I'm going to be champion!" Ash cut in, unwilling to back down. "I'll battle both of you and beat you both!"

"Is that so?" Gary smiled. "I could say exactly the same. I'll defeat the two of you and win it all."

The tournament had not even begun, yet Ash and Gary were already competing with each other. They each wanted to beat the other, but both clearly saw Ethan as their strongest opponent.

After their brief exchange, Gary left wearing a confident smile.

Ethan looked around. Silver Town was much busier than it had been when he and Erika arrived.

Trainers entering the tournament had gathered here, along with countless spectators who had come early to watch. Some places were already crowded enough to slow everyone down.

Ethan spotted a few faces he recognized, though he did not know the people. He had glimpsed some of these Trainers at different Pokemon Centers and had seen others compete in the Whirl Cup.

He even saw Jimmy and Marina. They were far away and had not noticed him, so he did not go out of his way to greet them.

The group left the Pokemon Center and headed down the shopping street toward the competitors' village.

The street was bustling too. There were far more vendors and goods for sale than before.

Ash and Misty looked from side to side. Snacks, Pokemon masks, pillows, and all the other little items caught their attention. Their youthful excitement was plain to see; they seemed to wish they had more eyes to take it all in.

Brock was more composed. He narrowed his eyes and looked only at the pretty older girls.

Halfway along the street, they saw a crowd of young children surrounding an elderly man, chattering as they asked him for something.

As they drew closer, they recognized him. It was Charles Goodshow, the Pokemon League president whom they had met before. He held a bunch of balloons and handed them out to the five- and six-year-olds around him. Being short himself, he almost disappeared among the children.

Once the children had gone, Ash approached him first.

"President Goodshow!"

Goodshow's eyes lit up at the sight of Ash and Ethan behind him. "Oh, it's you two!"

Now Ash was surprised. "You remember us?"

"Of course." Goodshow pointed first at Ash, then at Ethan. "I remember every competitor who leaves an impression. Ash, you reached the top sixteen at the Indigo League. You often won by surprising your opponents and battling against the type matchup. And you must be our Indigo League champion!"

Goodshow could not help laughing heartily as he finished.

No wonder he had risen to lead the Pokemon League. Ethan, as champion, was easy to remember. But Goodshow still recalled Ash so clearly after all this time. His memory was impressive.

"President, what are you doing out here?" Ethan asked.

Goodshow smiled. "As you can see, I'm in charge of the tournament, and I'm doing what I can to give our young supporters a little present."

"A present? You mean the balloons?"

"That's right." Goodshow nodded. "They may be inexpensive, but the thought matters. Didn't you see the smiles on all those children's faces when they received one?"

He was right. The children had been excited about the tournament already. Now they chased one another with their balloons, happier still.

"My, the last time I saw you was at the Indigo League." Goodshow stroked his beard. "And here you are entering the Silver Conference. I hope you perform brilliantly in every match ahead and give the crowd something to cheer about!"

Chapter 547: The Screening Trials and Travis

Ash had arrived late, so his room was on the top floor of the competitors' hotel. The view was better up there, though getting in and out would be less convenient.

Once they had put away their luggage, Ash and his friends took the elevator back to the lobby to meet Ethan. Together they headed to the outdoor battlefields for the screening trials.

The trials gathered more than two hundred registered Trainers for an initial selection, reducing the field to forty-eight. They were group matches held before the preliminaries, away from the public tournament. Each entrant had three chances to battle different opponents. Judges assessed their performance, so even someone who lost a match might still reach the preliminaries.

After Ethan explained the rules, Ash nodded. "So if I do well enough to impress the judges, I could advance even if I lost two matches?"

"That's right," Ethan said with a smile. "You can use only one Pokemon in each match, though, which makes it easy for a battle to go wrong. If you want to get through, you have to give every match your best."

Every entrant had to take part. Trainers would reach Silver Town on different days, so the Pokemon League had scheduled the trials for the day before the tournament opened.

Ethan, Ash, and all the other Trainers had to compete. Even though Ethan had arrived well ahead of time, he could only take part today alongside everyone else.

At the venue they found more than a dozen battlefields enclosed by wire fencing, lined up side by side. The other two hundred or so entrants were arriving too.

At the service desk, Ethan drew his match assignments.

He looked down. He was in Group A, scheduled for matches two, four, and ten.

All even numbers. He wondered whether that was a good sign.

"Let's wish each other luck."

Ethan and Ash went to their separate fields. Erika naturally accompanied Ethan, while Brock went with Ash. Misty looked between the two, silently apologized to Ash, then followed Ethan.

The three reached the Group A field at an easy pace. The two Trainers ahead of Ethan were already battling. They were young men of about the same age. One had sent out Nidoking, the other Hitmontop.

The Pokemon seemed evenly matched, trading attacks while neither gained a clear lead. Both Trainers shouted encouragement at the top of their lungs, determined not to lose their first match.

After Ethan watched for a while, Hitmontop landed a Rolling Kick squarely in Nidoking's chest and knocked it down.

Before Nidoking's Trainer could return his Pokemon, the referee signaled Ethan and his opponent to enter.

"Good luck, Ethan!" Misty said, raising a little fist to cheer him on.

Ethan smiled at her and walked onto the field, studying his opponent.

It was a boy of about ten, wearing a blue baseball cap and dark clothes, with a Pikachu at his side. If Ethan had not just parted from Ash, he might have thought Ash was standing opposite him.

The boy's face and expression looked remarkably like Ash's, and he even had a Pikachu. He resembled Ash more than Richie did.

Once both Trainers had reached their positions, the referee raised a colored flag. "Next is Group A's second match: Ethan versus Travis!"

Travis?

Ethan had heard that name somewhere.

Wait...

A memory flashed through his mind. "Travis, are you from the Orange Islands?" he asked.

"Huh?" Travis looked at him in surprise. "Yes. How did you know?"

"So it's you." Ethan smiled as he realized who the boy was. "What a coincidence. When I challenged the Gyms in the Orange Islands, I met your mother on Kumquat Island. She asked me to tell you, if I happened to meet you in Johto, that she misses you and hopes you'll come home soon."

Misty nodded. "Luana asked Ash and me too. I never imagined you'd be here at the Silver Conference!"

"Mom..." Travis's thoughts flew back to the island where he had grown up. He could almost see his mother. His eyes grew damp, and he nodded gratefully to Ethan. "Thank you for telling me. I really have been away a long time. Once I'm done with the Silver Conference, I'll go home!"

Ethan had not expected much to come of the request. Johto was vast; how was he supposed to find someone he did not know? Now that he had delivered Luana's message, he felt the satisfaction of fulfilling a promise.

He had never imagined that Travis would be his first opponent in the screening trials. What a twist of fate.

Travis collected himself and looked at the handsome man before him again. He was grateful for the news of his mother, but he would not hold back in the battle ahead. He had left home to get away from a comfortable life and achieve something through his own efforts.

His gaze turned resolute, and he took a Poke Ball from inside his jacket.

"That's the look I like to see..."

Ethan met his eyes and took a Poke Ball from his belt pouch.

At the referee's signal, they threw their balls together. Blue light flashed, and two Pokemon appeared on the field.

Travis had sent out Kingler, a Pokemon commonly found along the coast.

His Kingler was unusual, though. It stood about a meter and a half tall, a full size larger than most of its kind, and looked powerfully built.

Ethan had chosen Dragonite.

"Please be careful," Travis said. Perhaps he felt a little guilty about battling Ethan so soon after receiving his kindness. "Apart from Pikachu, Kingler was the first Pokemon I caught. It came with me from the Orange Islands, and it's very strong!"

"Is that so?" Ethan had some idea of what Travis was feeling. He smiled. "Then you'd better be careful too. My Dragonite is no pushover."

Chapter 548: Two Wins in a Row

Because they had chosen their Pokemon without knowing what the other Trainer would send out, neither side could predict the matchup.

No one knew what kind of opponent they would face.

For Travis, the problem was that Kingler was a pure Water type. Dragonite did not have a type advantage over it, but Kingler's Water-type attacks would deal only half their usual damage to a Dragon type.

That was not good news.

As the battle began, Kingler hurried toward Dragonite. Dragonite took off and rose into the air.

Kingler could not reach it, so Travis called, "Kingler, use Water Gun!"

He knew a Water-type move would do little to Dragonite. But Water Gun was one of Kingler's few ranged attacks, and on an open field it was one of the few options Travis could rely on.

Hitting a flying target was difficult. Dragonite rolled lightly aside, and the long stream of water missed.

"Dragonite, use Dragon Rush!"

At Ethan's command, Dragonite glowed faintly blue-green. It circled in the air a few times, then dived toward Kingler.

"Protect!"

Travis shouted at once. He knew Kingler was not fast enough to dodge Dragon Rush, but he had another way to meet it.

Kingler raised both claws before its chest. A strange light surrounded its body just as Dragonite slammed into it with tremendous force. Kingler skidded several meters, yet when it stopped, it did not have a scratch.

That was the power of Protect. Ethan had not expected one blow to bring Kingler down, however.

Before Kingler could steady itself, Ethan pressed the attack.

"Don't give it time to recover. Use Thunder Punch!"

Dragonite was versatile at close range. Alongside the Normal-type Slam and Water-type Aqua Tail, it could use both Fire Punch and Thunder Punch. Ethan usually favored Thunder Punch over Fire Punch.

The two punches were equally powerful, but Thunder Punch could paralyze its target. Ethan liked that extra effect.

A moment's paralysis could change the course of a battle.

"Kingler, use Crabhammer!"

Kingler was strong in close combat too. Seeing Dragonite come in rather than retreat, Travis did not hesitate.

Kingler stepped forward and swung its two uneven claws. They collided with Dragonite's electrically charged fists, and the Pokemon traded blows.

In raw power, Crabhammer surpassed Thunder Punch. Kingler's enormous claw could even land a critical hit.

But Ethan's plan paid off. After the two Pokemon had exchanged several attacks, Thunder Punch paralyzed Kingler. An electric jolt ran through its body, and just as it tried to move, it froze.

That was the opening Ethan had been waiting for.

"Dragonite, Aqua Tail, then Hyper Beam!"

Water wrapped around Dragonite's tail. It spun and struck Kingler, knocking it into the air. At the same time, energy gathered in Dragonite's mouth. The instant Kingler landed, Dragonite opened wide and fired a thick beam that hit it squarely.

The smooth combination knocked Kingler to the ground.

The referee raised a colored flag. Only then did Travis seem to realize what had happened.

A moment ago, the two Pokemon had looked evenly matched as they traded blows on the ground. How had Kingler lost so suddenly?

After his surprise faded, Travis sighed, returned Kingler, and walked over with a wry smile to shake Ethan's hand.

"I lost..."

"You fought well." Ethan patted his shoulder. "But like I told you, my Dragonite is strong too."

Ethan could have kept Dragonite in the air and beaten Travis easily with ranged attacks. But he had met Luana and knew Travis had traveled far from home to pursue his dream. He liked the boy and did not want to crush his confidence, so he had met Kingler head-on instead.

It had carried some risk, but the result was good enough.

With his first match won, Ethan returned Dragonite and left the field.

Erika and Misty came over to meet him.

"Congratulations, Ethan! Only two matches left before you advance," Misty said first.

As a Gym Leader, Erika had noticed more about the battle. She looked toward Travis and said approvingly, "That boy is strong too."

Ethan nodded. She was right.

Travis had real skill. Ethan had seemed to hold a large advantage and win with relative ease, but the battle had shown him that his own strength made the difference. Against another Trainer, Travis might well have won.

If Travis maintained that level in his remaining matches, he should have no trouble advancing.

Ethan sat on a nearby bench to collect himself and wait for his second battle.

He had drawn Group A's fourth match. After watching the third, he was called back to the field.

This opponent was an older man who looked like an employee at a large company. He wore thick round glasses and had a dull expression, as though life had worn him down and he hoped a Pokemon tournament might revive his lost enthusiasm.

The man sent out Houndoom. Ethan chose Tyranitar.

But...

Ethan had no idea how long ago the man had earned his badges. The moment they began, it was clear that he had not trained his Pokemon in a long time. His Houndoom was nowhere near Travis's Kingler in strength; it was below even the standard of an ordinary Trainer's Pokemon.

Ethan won easily. Once he understood the difference between them, he barely gave any commands for the rest of the match.

Tyranitar was merciless. It showed its fiercest side, battering Houndoom until it howled again and again.

In the end, even Ethan could not bear to watch and turned his head away.

Only after facing this office worker did Ethan truly understand why the Pokemon League held the screening trials before the main tournament. They filtered out entrants who were only making up the numbers, leaving more exciting battles for the spectators.

Chapter 549: Into the Preliminaries

Ethan's third battle was Group A's tenth match. It would not begin until around two in the afternoon, so he, Erika, and Misty left the Group A field to visit Ash in Group C.

The timing was fortunate. When they arrived, Ash was in his second match, pitting Phanpy against a woman's Machoke.

They did not call out and distract him. Instead, they found Brock watching nearby.

"You're here?" Brock asked when he saw them. "How did Ethan's battles go?"

"How do you think?" Misty said with a smile before Ethan could answer. "Ethan won two in a row without much trouble! What about Ash? Don't tell me he's already lost a match."

Brock shook his head. "No, but..."

He told them about Ash's first battle. Ash had won, but his opponent's Furret had used clever burrowing tactics, attacking again and again from underground. It had cornered Pikachu, and Ash had nearly lost. Then inspiration struck. He had Pikachu grab hold of Furret and go underground with it. Pikachu used Thunderbolt beneath the surface, stopping Furret's tactic and defeating it.

It had been a dangerously close match.

At least Ash had pulled through.

No opponent could be taken lightly. Among the entrants, there might be someone capable of a real surprise.

Ethan shook his head, worried on Ash's behalf.

Sending Pikachu underground too was the sort of idea only Ash would have.

Back on the field, Ash seemed to have taken the lesson to heart. He fought with unusual focus, and Phanpy performed well. Working together, they finished the match when Phanpy struck Machoke in the head with Tackle and knocked it unconscious.

"I won!"

Ash cheered before his opponent had even returned her Pokemon. His narrow escape in the first match had clearly shaken him, and he had stayed anxious throughout the second. Now that he was one win away from advancing, he could not contain his excitement.

When Ash came off the field and saw Ethan and the others, he hurried over with a broad smile.

"Congratulations." Ethan led the applause. "You did well."

"Heh, that one was easier than the first," Ash said, grinning even wider. "What about you, Ethan? You won too, right?"

"Yes. I haven't faced anyone too troublesome. Come on, let's have lunch."

They went to a nearby restaurant. While Ethan ordered, Misty told Ash about meeting Travis. Once the food arrived and they had eaten heartily, Ethan and Ash talked about their matches and traded a few observations.

There was not much advice to exchange, really. Mostly they encouraged one another.

The break was short. Soon after one o'clock, before they had even digested lunch, an announcement called Ash back to his field. Ethan did not go to watch this time. He returned to Group A with Erika and Misty.

They watched another match from the seats, and then Ethan's turn came.

His opponent was a recent graduate of a Pokemon school. Rather than collect badges, the student had qualified for the Conference by passing an exam at school.

Every region had a route like that.

Pokemon school graduates generally knew more theory than the average entrant. Overall, though, they tended to have less hands-on experience and were not always good at improvising.

They would never learn Ash's rough-and-ready style of battling in a classroom.

Ethan sent out Scizor against the student's Cyndaquil. Despite fighting at a type disadvantage, Scizor won. It was a vivid lesson for a young Trainer just setting out into the world.

Even against an opponent with a fourfold type advantage, a wide enough gap in strength could make victory easy.

The student returned Cyndaquil and left the field with a quiet sigh. His record in the trials was one win and two losses, a poor showing. Losing to Scizor despite having the favorable type matchup counted against him too. He would probably miss the preliminaries.

Ethan, by contrast, felt pleased.

He left the field, gave Misty a light high-five as she jumped up, and headed for the League hall.

Before parting earlier, he and Ash had agreed to meet there after their last battles. They were both likely to advance, and there was no need to gather at the fields first.

By the time Ethan reached the hall, Ash had already won his final match and was waiting for him.

They met each other's eyes. Neither needed to say anything. Both looked relieved; their last battles had evidently caused little trouble.

They waited as the other Trainers returned from their matches. Compared with the more than two hundred who had registered, far fewer people were left in the hall.

Photos of those who had advanced to the preliminaries appeared on a large screen. Ethan and Ash found their own pictures there, along with Gary's, Jimmy's, Marina's, and many other Trainers they had met while traveling.

Ethan searched more closely and spotted Travis's photo too.

Travis had reached the preliminaries despite losing his first match to Ethan. He really was strong.

Once everyone had gathered and seen the results, they began looking at the other Trainers around them.

With the field reduced, people who knew one another naturally began to notice familiar faces.

Gary spotted Ethan and Ash first. He did not come over. He glanced at them, confirmed that they had advanced, then leaned alone against a pillar and closed his eyes. He carried himself as if he stood apart from the crowd.

Ethan had just looked away when footsteps sounded nearby. Jimmy and Marina, whom he had met during the Raikou incident, approached with a chubby boy.

Jimmy's hearty voice reached them before he did. "Mr. Ethan! So you're entering the Silver Conference too, and you've made the preliminaries!"

Chapter 550: The Buzz Builds

"Let me introduce everyone..."

Ash and his friends had not met Jimmy's group, so Ethan made the introductions.

"These are Ash, Misty, and Brock. They've traveled together since Kanto and came to Johto for the Silver Conference, just like I did. These two are Jimmy and Marina, Trainers who set out from Professor Elm's lab in New Bark Town. We met during an incident and became good friends. And this is..."

Ethan looked at the chubby boy and furrowed his brow.

Marina had introduced him before, but they had known each other for such a short time, and it had been so long, that Ethan had forgotten his name.

The boy did not mind. Seeing Ethan at a loss, he smiled and quickly said, "Hello, I'm Vincent. Jimmy, Marina, and I have been friends since childhood."

"Childhood friends!" Misty's eyes lit up. "That sounds wonderful."

Ethan smiled at the three of them. "You all made the preliminaries. Professor Elm will be pleased when he hears. I stayed at his house the last time I passed through New Bark Town, and he mentioned you. He said you were mischievous as children and often came to play at his laboratory."

"Those were good days," Vincent said wistfully. "We didn't have a care in the world. It's a shame we've grown up and left."

As he spoke, Vincent stole a glance at Marina, apparently hoping she would share the memory. She did not look at him. Her eyes had turned to Jimmy.

Ash and the others might not have thought anything of it, but Ethan and Erika had enough experience to read what those looks meant.

Ah, the misery of a love triangle...

Everyone was friendly and close in age. After just a few words, the two groups were chatting easily.

While they were talking, someone else came over.

"Ethan! Ash! We meet again!"

It was a young girl's voice. Ethan and Ash turned and immediately recognized the white baseball cap and distinctive yellow jacket.

"Casey? You made the preliminaries too?"

Casey rubbed her nose and puffed out her chest proudly. "Of course! Nothing is too hard for a fan of the Electabuzz baseball team!"

After all this time, Casey had not grown much taller, and her devotion to the team had not changed at all. She truly was a passionate fan.

She stole a glance at Ethan, and her heart fluttered.

Casey had actually seen Ash more often than Ethan, and she and Ash had become friends. Once, when they met again at the Bug-Catching Contest in National Park, Ash had even given her a Beedrill he had caught.

Casey's battling ability was only fair, though. She had needed a good deal of luck to reach the preliminaries.

She was about to say something else when applause suddenly broke out in the hall. Everyone turned. The short Pokemon League president, Charles Goodshow, walked onto a raised platform under the competitors' gaze, his hands behind his back.

Goodshow cleared his throat. "Congratulations on passing the screening trials and reaching the preliminaries. I'll explain the preliminary rules now."

The hall fell silent as everyone waited for him to continue.

"The forty-eight Trainers will be divided into sixteen groups of three," Goodshow said. "In each group, the Trainer who earns the most points from victories will advance to the final tournament."

A wave of discussion broke out as soon as he finished.

Sixteen groups with three Trainers each meant only one place from each group was available. The elimination was harsh.

Then again, compared with previous years or tournaments in other regions, it was only a different format. Anyone aiming for a strong result would have to defeat their opponents sooner or later.

When the noise faded and the hall quieted again, Goodshow said, "Those are the rules. I hope you perform to your true ability, make this year's wait worthwhile, and give the spectators your very best!"

With that, he walked off, hands still clasped behind his back, as though he had come simply to take a look at the competitors.

After he left, a staff member explained the schedule for the next two days.

The day's battles were finished. The Silver Conference would officially begin at noon tomorrow. Before the matches, as at other sporting events, there would be a torch relay carrying the sacred flame, followed by Goodshow's opening address.

From then on, there would be no more closed trials like today's. The competitors would battle in public, before spectators and cameras.

Meanwhile, advertisements and promotions would spread throughout Johto, filling the streets and appearing on televisions and people's phones, so everyone would know the event was beginning.

The chatter in the hall went on for some time before the Trainers gradually left.

With so many friends gathered, Ethan made good on his promise from that morning. He led them to a nearby restaurant, ordered plenty of food, and treated everyone to a lively meal.

Some of them had barely known one another before. By the end, they were much more at ease together.

During dinner, Casey kept looking for a chance to speak to Ethan. Misty, already watching her closely, saw every attempt coming and headed it off. Casey never found an opening.

While they ate, photos of the forty-eight Trainers who had reached the preliminaries were posted online. Interest in the tournament surged.

People began guessing who would win this year's championship.

Support for many local Johto entrants climbed, but Ethan's rose even faster, putting him in first place.

Many people had not known who he was. Once other fans explained that he was the previous Indigo League champion, they took notice.

His good looks and strength won over a wave of new admirers. Their high hopes pushed his popularity still higher, well ahead of the pack.

Of course, no one would believe the Pokemon League had not helped promote him behind the scenes.

Chapter 551: The League's Promotional Push

It was nine at night by the time Ethan and Erika returned to their suite in the competitors' village.

They bathed together and lay down. Ethan did not press for sex tonight. Wanting to save his strength, he held Erika close and went over the day's battles in his mind.

Overall, he was pleased with his performance. His Pokemon had fought well and met the expectations he had set for them before the matches.

Erika rested her cheek on his chest and listened to his strong heartbeat. Seeing him lost in thought, she asked softly, "What are you thinking about?"

"The matches the day after tomorrow."

Ethan breathed in the scent of her hair and smiled. "After tomorrow's opening ceremony, the real battles begin. Then we'll be facing strong Trainers who fought their way out of their groups. It won't be as easy as it was today."

"Are you worried about what's ahead?"

"No." He stroked Erika's smooth back, his expression serious. "My goal is the championship. However strong my opponents are, and whatever round I meet them in, I'll give everything I have to beat them. The only question is whether we meet sooner or later."

It was a bold claim, but Ethan had good reason to trust the strength of his Pokemon.

...

While Ethan fell asleep with Erika in his arms, full of hopes for the future, the lights still burned in the nearby Pokemon League building. An intense debate was under way.

League officials disagreed over how to run this year's tournament.

Perhaps they remembered the benefits of Ethan's popularity at the Indigo League. John, the broadcast director, and many others wanted high ratings. They hoped to repeat what they had done there: promote Ethan as a favorite for the title and shape his tournament path so that he would meet opponents of similar strength, making every battle exciting.

President Goodshow and those who sided with him wanted a fairer competition. The League should not interfere with the schedule or manipulate matchups. They also thought it was bad for the League if one person monopolized the championship. Every competitor deserved equal attention.

The two sides argued until their faces were red. Neither would yield.

When the meeting broke for a rest with no decision reached, John went to the smoking area with several of his relatives. In private, he made no secret of his frustration with Goodshow.

"The old man ought to step down," he told them. "Ratings are what matter most! Ethan looks good and he's an outstanding Trainer. If I don't put the spotlight on him, should I put it on ordinary entrants who don't look remotely like champions?"

Somehow, his words eventually reached Goodshow. The president only shook his head helplessly.

The two men simply saw things differently. No amount of persuasion would settle that.

Fortunately, when the meeting resumed, the moderates helped them reach a compromise. Goodshow allowed John to give Ethan a larger share of the publicity resources. But the League would not interfere with the tournament schedule or match selection. The competition had to remain fair.

Ethan would never know about that discussion, though he soon noticed changes around him.

The next morning, he had barely finished breakfast when several League staff members arrived and invited him to shoot promotional videos.

There was nothing improper about the invitation. A few popular local Johto entrants had been asked to come to the shoot as well.

Compared with them, however, Ethan received more elaborate makeup, more time before the camera, and several changes of setting.

Even in the group photo, he stood right at the center.

Ethan did not like drawing this much attention, but the League had arranged it, so he followed the staff's directions.

By the time he escaped the shoot at noon, a large crowd of reporters was waiting for him.

Like sharks scenting blood, they had already marked the popular entrants as their targets. More reporters had their eyes on Ethan than on anyone else.

He had little choice but to answer a few questions in careful, official language.

"Ethan, what's your goal for this tournament?"

Looking at the microphone thrust almost into his face, Ethan replied earnestly, "To work hard and reach the next round, of course. If I make the final, all the better."

Someone else asked, "Are there any opponents here who have left a strong impression on you?"

"I think everyone who has reached the preliminaries is strong and deserves respect."

"Is there anything you'd like to say to them?"

"I only hope we all perform at our best and give the audience the most exciting battles we can."

His answers were modest and careful, giving the reporters nothing they could twist into a story.

When they looked ready to ask more, Ethan called over some League staff. With their help, he slipped away quickly.

He had not gone far when his phone rang.

It was Alexa, the beautiful reporter from Lumiose City who had interviewed him during the Indigo League.

Ethan found an empty corner and answered.

A woman's voice came through at once. "Hello, Mr. Ethan. Do you remember me?"

"Of course." Ethan recalled meeting her in Kanto. "How could I forget the famous reporter from Lumiose Press? What brings you to call now, Alexa?"

Even as he asked, he had already guessed what she wanted.

Alexa laughed. "The same thing as last time. I'd like another exclusive interview with you. Please don't turn me down!"

So it was another interview.

Ethan thought for a moment and agreed.

Alexa had interviewed him at the Indigo League, and the two had formed a friendship of sorts. Refusing her now would feel unkind.

"All right. There's still some time before the opening ceremony, and I'm free at the moment."

"That's wonderful!" Alexa sounded delighted. "We're at a cafe nearby. Could you come over now, if it's convenient?"

Chapter 552: Alexa's Second Exclusive Interview

When Ethan reached the cafe beside the competitors' village, Alexa and two colleagues wearing Lumiose Press vests were already waiting outside.

She had crossed the sea alone with two Pokemon to report on the Indigo League. This time, she had brought a professional team and was clearly well prepared.

"Mr. Ethan, it's been so long!" Alexa smiled and offered her hand.

"Hello, everyone."

Ethan shook hands with all three. Then he smiled at Alexa. "Sent to Johto this time? It seems no League tournament can do without you. You must be busy!"

"I can't help it. It's part of the job."

After a brief exchange, Alexa and her colleagues welcomed Ethan into the cafe.

To give the interview a relaxed, elegant setting and keep strangers from interrupting, Alexa had rented the whole place. Apart from the four of them, only one employee remained behind the counter.

Ethan sat on a sofa. Alexa set a steaming cup of coffee before him while her colleagues prepared the equipment.

They aimed the camera at Ethan and arranged the microphone, lights, and reflector. Then they gave Alexa an okay sign.

Alexa nodded, sat opposite Ethan, and crossed her legs at an angle.

His eyes were drawn to them. Alexa was beautiful, and she had a lovely figure too.

Her close-fitting pants showed off the shape of her legs in particular.

After only a glance, Ethan looked away without giving himself away.

"Mr. Ethan, may we begin?" Alexa asked, unaware of his glance. "If you're nervous, don't worry. This is recorded, not live. We can make small edits afterward if anything doesn't turn out as you'd like."

"No problem. I'm ready."

Seeing how calm he was, Alexa smiled. "Then let's begin."

The camera started rolling. Alexa faced the lens. "Welcome, viewers, to this year's Silver Conference. I'm special correspondent Alexa. Today we're honored to have a remarkable competitor with us: the previous Indigo League champion and an old friend of ours, Mr. Ethan Vale!"

The camera turned to Ethan, who smiled and waved.

"Hello to everyone watching in Kalos. I'm Ethan, and it's good to see you again."

After his greeting, Alexa asked her first question. "What are you hoping to achieve at the Silver Conference?"

"My goal?" Ethan answered without hesitation. "To go as far as I can. I think I should at least try to match my result at the Indigo League."

Alexa could not help smiling.

Match his Indigo League result? Ethan had won that tournament. Was this his way of saying he intended to win the Silver Conference too?

He was not being modest at all.

With the reporters outside, Ethan had been cautious and formal. He did not know them and worried they might misrepresent his answers. Lumiose Press was no gossip tabloid, and Alexa had earned his trust, so he felt no need to hide behind rehearsed phrases.

That was why his manner with her was so different.

Alexa did not know exactly what he was thinking, but she liked the answer.

Viewers enjoyed an interview with some humor. Nobody wanted a string of stiff questions and answers that sounded prepared in advance.

Ethan was handsome, but he was also relaxed and lively.

What audience would not like a competitor like that?

Alexa asked many more questions, and Ethan answered each in the same easy tone.

They talked comfortably. Nearly twenty minutes later, the interview ended, and Alexa was delighted with how it had gone.

At her request, Ethan then brought out Dragonite, Scizor, and Tyranitar, the three Pokemon he had used in the screening trials. They posed for several photographs to use in the interview video and news cover.

It was much like their first interview.

Now, though, they knew each other better, and Ethan was more at ease with the process.

...

Once everything was finished, Ethan said goodbye to Alexa and headed for Silver Stadium to meet Erika and the others.

He felt drained. The shoot and interview had exhausted him more, in body and mind, than a whole day of directing his Pokemon in battle.

Given the choice, he would rather deal with Ash's Pokemon every day than sit through another shoot and interview.

Silver Town was even busier than it had been yesterday. The opening ceremony was about to begin, and a crowd packed the area in front of Silver Stadium.

Ethan went through the competitors' entrance to the stadium's waiting room. Erika and the others had been looking out for him for some time.

"You're finally back!" Misty said, relieved. "What took so long? The opening ceremony is about to start. I thought you might miss it!"

"Don't worry. I was watching the time."

As one of the Trainers who had reached the preliminaries, Ethan had to take part in the ceremony. He and the other forty-seven would enter the stadium through the competitors' passage, face the crowd, welcome the arrival of the sacred flame, and listen to Goodshow's speech.

Those steps were both mandatory and an honor. Even if he found them tedious, he would have to be patient.

But...

Ethan glanced around. "Where's Ash?"

"I don't know." Misty shook her head. "I saw him leave with two staff members. Maybe he's taking part in some activity."

Ethan was about to say more when other staff entered the waiting room and began lining up the competitors for the procession. He stopped asking questions, said goodbye to Erika and the others, and joined the crowd.

"We'll see you later!" Misty waved. "We'll be in the stands, enjoying the show!"

Chapter 553: The Silver Conference Opens

Ceremonial cannons sounded, and fireworks burst high overhead.

At three in the afternoon, Silver Stadium was packed with spectators from across Johto. Television stations switched to live coverage of the annual Pokemon League tournament.

Friends and family of the competitors and ordinary viewers alike turned their attention to the event. Huge screens in shopping centers and along the streets showed the broadcast without pause.

Office workers sneaked a look while on the job, and students secretly took out their phones. Some bosses and teachers let it pass, because they were just as interested in the Conference.

With so many people watching, the announcer's voice rang through the stadium, clear to everyone there.

In front of a television, Sabrina sat comfortably on a sofa, one leg crossed over the other. She had just finished a Pokemon battle and was watching the broadcast at her leisure.

"...The opening ceremony and the competitors' procession will begin in this very stadium shortly. The audience here can hardly wait. This year's Silver Conference has brought together powerful Trainers. Their contests of strength and skill begin tomorrow. Who will take the championship? Stay with us and find out!"

Sabrina watched the screen and remembered the first part of her journey through Johto with Ethan. If the Pokemon League had not pressed her to return so urgently, she would surely still be at his side.

The thought soured her mood.

If Ethan had not urged her to stay, and her father had not pleaded with her, she would have resigned as Gym Leader and continued traveling the world with him.

Just then, Sabrina's father entered the room. "Sabrina, another challenger is here. Could you..."

He stopped when his daughter rose, her face like ice. She had been fine a moment ago. Who had upset her now?

As she walked coldly toward the battlefield, he could only feel sorry for the challenger.

He hoped Sabrina would not go too far and would remember to hold back.

Others were watching too: the Cerise family at the Cerise Laboratory in Vermilion City, including assistants Ren and Parker; Professor Ivy in the Orange Islands; Melody on Shamouti Island; Maya at the Whirl Islands' Temple of the Sea; the Kimono Sisters in Ecruteak City; and even people as far away as Kalos.

Some were only Ethan's friends. Others had a much closer bond with him.

As they watched, the broadcast cut to a torchbearer raising the sacred flame high. He had left Ho-Oh Temple and was running toward Silver Town between rows of spectators.

In Silver Stadium's waiting area, Ethan stood in line and followed the staff's directions toward the field.

The moment the competitors emerged, every spotlight swung toward them. Cheers and shouts erupted from the stands.

Like the others, Ethan smiled and raised his right hand to acknowledge the crowd.

A camera caught his smile and put it on the giant screen, drawing even louder cheers.

Thanks to the Pokemon League's promotion, he was the most popular competitor here. Nearly every commentator and news outlet listed him among the favorites to win.

Ethan saw himself on the screen. He had nerves of steel and showed no stage fright; if anything, his smile grew wider.

He searched the stands for Erika, Misty, and the others. But Silver Stadium held eighty thousand people. Finding them in that crowd was all but impossible.

His search led him to something else instead.

In a small section near the front of the stands, more than twenty people waved banners and flags. They wore matching outfits, some with hair dyed bright colors, and cheered at the top of their lungs.

Ethan's sharp eyes picked out the words on a banner: Boss Ethan Is Number One!

Huh?

He looked again. The flag bearers wore black leather jackets and had unusual hairstyles. They looked like a biker gang.

Those people at the front seemed especially familiar...

Wait. They were...

Misa, Masha, and the rest of the biker gang! They had come all the way to Johto to watch the opening ceremony?

No one had told Ethan they were coming. They had certainly surprised him.

The camera found them too. The broadcast director gave them a close-up, putting their banner and flags in front of viewers across Johto.

Soft laughter rose from the stands. No one was mocking them; their bright, enthusiastic display was simply too funny and out of place.

When Misa, Masha, and the others saw themselves on the giant screen, they waved their flags even more vigorously.

Those guys...

Ethan smiled wryly to himself.

That banner had made him a target. Even competitors who had paid little attention to him before would take notice now.

It might make things troublesome, but these lovable fools had come only to support him. There was little he could do to repay them.

All he could do was win every match and give them performances they could be proud of.

The competitors' procession lasted more than ten minutes. Once everyone was in position, the stadium gradually quieted.

Now they awaited the sacred flame. It would enter the stadium and light the great cauldron.

As time passed, the sky slowly darkened.

Tens of thousands waited expectantly. At last an athlete carrying the torch came running out of a stadium passage and onto the field.

But when he emerged, the spectators were startled. This was not the young man who had set out from Ho-Oh Temple. The torchbearer was a small boy in casual clothes and a baseball cap, holding the sacred flame with a determined face. A Pikachu ran beside him.

"Ash?!"

Everyone who knew him stared in surprise. No one had expected Ash to become the torchbearer.

Only Ethan shook his head with a rueful smile.

There was only one reason Ash would have gone missing and then appeared with the torch: Team Rocket's trio must have caused trouble somewhere out of sight.

Chapter 554: Lighting the Sacred Flame

Ash's entrance had eclipsed every other competitor. All eyes in the stadium were on him.

There was only one way to describe it: he looked incredibly cool.

Ethan and the others, who had entered in the ordinary procession, could not compete for attention.

The announcer received an update and explained, "We've just learned that the original torchbearer injured his ankle and couldn't complete the relay. The boy you're watching now is Ash, who passed the screening trials and has also reached the preliminaries!"

After a pause, the announcer continued, "The flame in his hands is the undying sacred fire of the legendary Pokemon Ho-Oh, which ended a war and brought life back to the land and forests. And now Ash has carried it to the cauldron..."

Inside the stadium, Ash held the torch high and ran across most of the field. He climbed the steps to the great cauldron. When he touched it with the torch, a roar sounded and the whole cauldron burst into flame. The Silver Conference had truly begun.

The crowd broke into its loudest cheers yet. Even Ethan and the other competitors applauded as they looked up at the blazing flame.

Every Trainer felt a surge of excitement. Ethan was not alone in silently hoping for a perfect result at this Silver Conference.

Amid that excitement, Pokemon League president Charles Goodshow approached the podium.

He was a short man, but under the lights and in the charged atmosphere, he looked imposing.

Standing before the microphone, he cleared his throat and smiled. "To everyone who has advanced from the screening trials: Ho-Oh's sacred flame is here to watch over you. Give all you have, battle fairly, and leave no regrets!"

Goodshow never gave long speeches. A few simple words, straight to the point, were enough to stir the crowd.

...

By the time they left the stadium, the moon was high and stars dotted the sky.

Outside, Ethan met up with Ash, Erika, and the others. Misa, Masha, and the rest of the biker gang came hurrying toward him with brilliant smiles.

"Boss!"

They called out from far away, drawing looks from the people nearby. Some fans had recognized Ethan and wanted an autograph or a photo with him. When they saw the fierce-looking bikers converging on him, none dared approach.

In that respect, Misa and Masha were helpful.

"You lot..." Ethan shook his head with a wry smile. "You came all this way without telling me. If I hadn't spotted you in the stands, I'd still have no idea you were here!"

"Heh." Misa smiled sheepishly. "It's such an important tournament. Of course we had to come and cheer for you in person!"

"Exactly!" Masha said. "We wanted to surprise you. And we knew you had the screening trials yesterday, so we didn't dare interrupt!"

Misty, Ash, and Brock had met the bikers at the Indigo League, so they were not surprised. Erika alone looked from Ethan to the rough-looking group and back, unable to see how they fit together.

And why were they calling him Boss?

"How did you get here?" Ethan asked.

"We rode," Masha said. "All the way from Vermilion City!"

"Thanks to the money you invested," Misa added with a smile, "our club is making a profit. We're not the same as we were before. We even traded in all our bicycles for motorcycles!"

Ethan nodded. Going from bicycles to motorcycles was certainly progress.

Motorcycles suited a biker gang better too. What sort of gang rode bicycles every day? Their peers would laugh at them for years if word got around.

Still, riding all the way from Vermilion City to Silver Town could not have been easy. They had traveled a great distance to support him, and Ethan was touched.

"Come on. Let's all have a good dinner."

Ethan led the group to a nearby restaurant. The owner looked alarmed when so many bikers came through the door at once, fearing they were there to wreck the place. Their conversation soon put him at ease.

With Ash's group included, nearly thirty people squeezed around two large tables. The tables filled with delicious food. Most of the party were adults, so they ordered plenty of alcohol. Even Brock and Ash drank quite a bit in the excitement.

Over dinner, Ash told them how he had become the replacement torchbearer. As Ethan had guessed, Team Rocket's trio was responsible.

They had lured Ash away, stolen Pikachu, and locked him in a room. Luckily, Gary had arrived in time to free him.

Then, as Team Rocket fled, they collided with the original torchbearer. After rescuing Pikachu, Ash had to take the man's place.

"And that's how you ended up stealing the show," Misty said with a smile.

"Heh." Ash smiled bashfully. Even at his age, he knew that carrying the torch was a great honor.

He had carried one at the Indigo League too, though, so this time he was not quite as overwhelmed.

Everyone ate, drank, and talked merrily. From time to time, Misa and Masha glanced at Erika.

During the Indigo League, their boss had been with Sabrina, the beautiful psychic girl. They knew that. Now, after so little time, he was with another beautiful woman.

When they learned Erika was the Celadon Gym Leader, they gave Ethan a private thumbs-up.

As expected of their boss. He was a League champion, and the women in his life were Gym Leaders too. How could they not admire him?

Dinner lasted until ten at night. Then everyone said goodbye and returned to their rooms.

With matches beginning tomorrow, Ethan and Erika bathed quickly when they reached their suite and went to bed.

But Ethan was too excited to sleep. He lay awake for a long time. Ash, Gary, and most of the other competitors were much the same that night, tossing and turning in their beds.

Unable to fall asleep, Ethan spent a long while making love to Erika. Only after he had worn himself out did he drift off.

Chapter 555: The Preliminaries Begin

Early the next morning, Ethan met Ash and the others and went down to the ground-floor lobby of their lodgings. The match schedule for the preliminary groups was already displayed on the large screen.

Sixteen groups had been drawn, with three Trainers in each one. A photograph appeared beside every name.

"There I am!" Ash spotted his picture at once. Pointing at the screen, he said, "I'm in Group H. Let's see who I'm up against... Huh?"

At his surprised voice, Ethan and the others turned to look.

"What is it?"

A closer look showed that Ash's group included a young girl and a slightly chubby older boy. The boy was Vincent, Jimmy and Marina's childhood friend from New Bark Town.

"So it's him." Misty gave Ash a teasing pat on the shoulder. "Marina told me Vincent is really strong. What bad luck to end up in his group."

Ash looked eager for the challenge. "It doesn't matter who I face. I won't lose!"

Once they had checked Ash's group, everyone searched for Ethan's name.

Misty narrowed her eyes and found it first. "There he is! Ethan's in Group C!"

Following her finger, Ethan found his photograph. His two group opponents were Trainers he had never seen before.

"That's not bad luck. I didn't draw Jimmy or the others."

He was relieved not to be grouped with anyone he knew. Only one Trainer could advance from each group, and he would feel bad if he had to eliminate a friend himself.

They were bound to meet if they kept winning, but the later it happened, the better his friends could place. He would feel less guilty about knocking them out then.

He did not even want Gary eliminated this early.

After checking the draw, they read the rules more carefully.

Each group would play a three-person round robin. A win earned three points, a loss none, and a draw one. The Trainer with the most points would advance to the final tournament.

"There's a small chance of a complication," Brock said, rubbing his chin. "If every match ends in a draw and the points are tied, they'll hold tiebreaker matches until there's a clear winner."

"That..." Ash tried counting it out on his fingers, but the scoring was more than he wanted to work through. He gave up before he strained his limited supply of brain cells. "Anyway, if I beat both of them, I definitely go through, right?"

"Exactly." Ethan smiled. "You're here to compete. Don't get bogged down in the details. That's the spiritgo straight at them!"

Once they knew where to go, Ethan parted ways with Ash and took Erika toward Group C.

Misty had traveled with Ash all this way, and with such an important competition beginning, she could hardly leave him on his own. She and Brock accompanied him to the Group H venue.

...

Beside the main Silver Stadium were four smaller arenas, A through D. The sixteen preliminary groups would compete in those four arenas.

Group C, Ethan's group, had been assigned to Arena A according to the schedule.

When Ethan emerged from the competitors' tunnel, Arena A was already full of spectators. Judging by the crowd, it had drawn the most attention of the four venues.

Misa, Masha, and their friends had claimed conspicuous seats early. As soon as Ethan entered, they waved their flags wildly.

They were impossible to miss. Erika sat quietly beside them, her gentle gaze fixed on Ethan across the arena.

One of Ethan's opponents was a popular local Trainer from Johto. He had taken his place in the red Trainer's box before Ethan arrived, but while the others seemed relaxed, his expression was grim.

No one else could quite understand the pressure of standing before the Indigo League champion and the favorite to win this year's Silver Conference.

When he learned he had been drawn into Ethan's group, he had made a point of watching Ethan's earlier matches. They had left him feeling as though he could scarcely breathe.

Gardevoir, Charizard, Blastoise, Venusaurevery Pokemon he had seen Ethan use was formidable, and his other Pokemon seemed no weaker. Their strength was worthy of a champion. Gyarados in particular had frightened him.

He had no idea how to fight an opponent like that.

Now Ethan walked toward the blue Trainer's box, waving to the crowd with an easy expression. The other Trainer could only pray that Ethan would leave his strongest Pokemon out of the preliminaries.

Once Ethan was in position, the referee stepped to the center of the field.

"We'll now decide who sends out a Pokemon first!"

Unlike the usual matches, these preliminaries used a spinning wheel to decide the first Trainer to send out a Pokemon. The method was not entirely fair, but it reduced some uncertainty and offered a measure of protection to the weaker side.

On the other hand, if the weaker Trainer drew the first move, the battle would likely end faster and more decisively against him.

A small wheel appeared on the nearby screen. Red and blue sections representing the two Trainers were spaced evenly around it. As the pointer began to turn, both Trainers watched intently.

When it slowed and came to rest on Ethan's blue section, his opponent could not help breathing a sigh of relief.

The referee glanced at the result and gestured to Ethan. "Ethan, please send out your Pokemon first."

Ethan nodded, showing no disappointment. He trusted his Pokemon. Even at a type disadvantage, they would not go down easily.

He took a Poke Ball from the pouch at his waist. He had made his choice before the match. He threw the ball, and in a flash of blue light, a Pokemon appeared on the field. Green leaves and a red flower rose from its back, above its blue-green limbs.

It was Venusaur! Once a star of Ethan's battles in Kanto, it had spent a long time at Cerise Park without appearing in a match.

Chapter 556: Two Very Different Battles

Venusaur's appearance was no spur-of-the-moment decision.

That morning, Ethan had contacted Chloe and asked her to send Venusaur through the laboratory's transfer machine.

He was not going to leave a Pokemon he had caught behind and forget about it the way Ash sometimes did. Venusaur had gone a long time without battling, so Ethan could not be certain of its present strength. But the foundation it had built remained, and it should have no trouble in the preliminaries.

When Ethan's opponent saw Venusaur, his expression turned hopeful and conflicted at once.

From the Indigo League matches he had watched, Venusaur had seemed the most conventional of Ethan's Pokemon. It had no obvious weakness, but it had not done anything especially dazzling either.

Compared with facing Charizard, Gyarados, or Gardevoir, facing Venusaur ought to be easier.

But Venusaur was still powerful. This would be no easy battle.

When the Trainer failed to act, the referee glanced at him and urged, "Kimura, please send out your Pokemon."

Only then did Ethan learn his opponent's name.

It had been listed on the match schedule, but the man was not a notable Trainer or someone Ethan recognized from the animated series. Ethan had not bothered to remember it.

The referee's reminder brought Kimura back to himself. He quickly considered which Pokemon he should use against Venusaur.

After a few seconds, he took out a Poke Ball with a grave expression.

When he released his Pokemon, the spectators saw that Kimura had made careful use of his advantage in choosing second. He had sent out Ledian, a Flying-type Pokemon with a type advantage over Venusaur!

"A fine choice! Flying beats Grass, and it looks as though Ethan faces a tough challenge!" the announcer called, his voice ringing over Arena A. "Both sides are ready. Let's see who takes the first victory!"

...

Preliminary matches were three-on-three. In his first match of the preliminaries, Ethan fought carefully. Venusaur, Scizor, and Tyranitar defeated Kimura's Ledian, Magmar, and Jumpluff in turn, giving Ethan a clean three-to-zero win.

Kimura's Pokemon had fought hard in all three rounds, but none had caused Ethan much trouble.

Anyone could see the clear difference in strength between their Pokemon.

"Boss is as strong as ever!" Masha was excited, though the one-sided match had left him a little unsatisfied. "Even a type disadvantage barely slowed him down. No one's going to stop him from taking the title!"

"I wouldn't go that far," Misa said. She was more cautious than her younger brother. "These are only the preliminaries. The competitors' strength varies a lot. Once we reach the last eight, we'll see the truly dangerous ones."

Ethan shook hands with the dejected Kimura, nodded to the crowd, and left Arena A through the competitors' tunnel.

His first preliminary win had earned him three points. If nothing went wrong and he beat the other Trainer in his group, he would advance to the last sixteen.

For Kimura, advancing was now possible only in theory. Ethan would have to lose to the third Trainer, Kimura would have to beat that Trainer, and then Kimura would have to face Ethan again in a tiebreaker and win.

The chances were vanishingly small. Kimura could hardly imagine Ethan losing to the third Trainer, and he had no confidence that he could beat Ethan himself in a rematch.

The spectators cheered warmly for Ethan as he left. His victory was what most of them had hoped for and expected. If he ever lost a match, that would be the result they found unbelievable.

Ethan met Erika outside the arena. Side by side, they returned to the ground-floor lobby of the lodgings and watched Ash's match on the large screen.

It had reached its crucial stage.

Ash's opponent was a girl about his age named Macey. She wore her hair in two braids and had rosy cheeks. She was plain-looking, and at first glance she did not seem especially clever.

But the state of the battle surprised Ethan: Ash had been driven to the brink of defeat.

The score was one to two. Macey had lost her Magcargo, while Ash's Phanpy and Totodile had both been knocked out!

Erika stared at the screen in surprise. She had battled Ash herself and had known him long enough to understand his ability. She had never expected to see him in this position.

"This..." She searched for the right words. "I thought he might fall behind, but I didn't expect such a hard fight."

Ethan studied the battle and sighed. "Look at Macey's team. She's revealed all three Pokemon: Magcargo, Quilava, and Electabuzz. Ash chose Totodile and Phanpy in response. Totodile has the advantage against her two Fire-types, while Phanpy's Ground type gives him an answer to her counterattack."

"True." Erika nodded. "Thinking that far ahead doesn't sound like him."

Ethan shook his head. "Brock and Misty probably helped him plan it. But even with all that preparation, Macey isn't easy to beat. Now we'll see how Ash gets out of this."

As they watched, Ash sent out his last Pokemon.

It was not Pikachu, the partner he had trusted for so long. It was Squirtle, whom he had left with Officer Jenny to lead a firefighting squad!

That was a surprise.

Against Macey's Electabuzz, however, sending a Water-type as his final Pokemon hardly looked like a good choice.

Fortunately, Ash was at his best when fighting against a type disadvantage. He showed his tenacity once again.

Squirtle performed brilliantly, defeating Electabuzz despite the unfavorable matchup, then taking down Quilava with its type advantage. Ash came through the battle with a narrow victory!

Chapter 557: How Their Friends Fared

When Ash and the others returned to the lobby, they were all smiling. To Ethan's surprise, Macey had come back with them.

Huh? What was going on?

Ethan quickly pulled Misty aside and asked in a low voice. Only then did he learn that Ash and Macey had met before entering the arena that morning, after the two groups had parted ways.

Macey had approached him to pick a fight. She wanted to find out whether Ash was worthy of being her opponent.

Just then, Team Rocket's trio had attacked. They happened to capture Ash's Pikachu and Macey's Vulpix, but Ash used his other Pokemon to defeat them and rescue both captives.

That had won Macey's heart on the spot.

Even after Ash beat her in their match, she felt no resentment. She admired him more than ever, which was why she now kept following him around.

"I see." Ethan could not help laughing. "So Ash is finally having some luck in love!"

When Ethan and Misty rejoined the others, he greeted Macey politely. Only then did she learn that Ash and Ethan were good friends.

With her standing right there, Ethan could hardly congratulate Ash. He made a few minutes of casual conversation instead.

Eventually Macey's attention became too much for them. Misty coaxed her away on the pretext of going to the restroom, giving Ethan and Ash a chance to breathe.

"She really is..." Ethan shook his head with a wry smile, leaving the thought unfinished. Then he teased Ash. "Only you could have girls falling for you wherever you go."

Ash rubbed his hair awkwardly, his face turning a little red.

He wanted to retort, Doesn't Misty act the same way around you? But with Ethan and Misty to answer to, and Erika standing nearby, he did not dare say it aloud.

Seeing him blush, Ethan pressed on. "Why not make it official and ask her to be your girlfriend?"

"What are you talking about...?" Ash's face grew redder. "I... I haven't thought about that..."

Ethan shook his head, half amused and half exasperated. "You're such a kid."

"That's enough." Erika saw how embarrassed Ash was and caught Ethan by the arm. "Stop teasing him. He is still a kid."

At Erika's intervention, Ethan dropped the subject and talked to Ash about the day's matches instead.

Both of them were finished competing for the day, and both had won their first match. It was a happy result for them, but every winner meant a loser. The defeated Trainers who returned to the lobby all looked weighed down by worry.

They were already on the brink of elimination. One more loss would end their Silver Conference run.

"Your match was close," Ethan told Ash. "You nearly lost to Macey. Good thing Squirtle held up under the pressure and beat Electabuzz despite the type disadvantage."

"It was tense," Brock agreed with a nod. "Watching from the stands, I was worried for Ash the whole time!"

Just then, other competitors Ethan knew began returning.

Their expressions revealed how their matches had gone. Gary was among the first through the door. As composed as ever, he wore a small backpack, spared no one a glance, and walked straight to the elevator with his chest out.

He had plainly won, and won easily.

Jimmy and Marina entered after him, talking and laughing together. Their matches had evidently gone well too.

Casey and Travis were scheduled to compete tomorrow. Neither had battled today, so their results would have to wait.

Watching their two group opponents battle today had given them a chance to prepare more thoroughly and tailor their teams for tomorrow.

That might not be entirely fair to the other competitors, but it was how the tournament schedule worked.

Highlights from the day's battles spread quickly online. Some media outlets even put together a top-five list.

Surprisingly, not one of Ethan's battles made the cut. His matches had been so one-sided that there had been little suspense to make them exciting.

Interest in the preliminaries remained high. Some spectators enjoyed the matches so much that they watched the replays again and again.

For now, none of that mattered much to Ethan and the other competitors.

After a night's rest, the second day of the preliminaries arrived. Ethan had no match scheduled.

From the stands, he watched Kimura battle the other Trainer in their group, a young woman named Hui. The contest was fierce, but at the end Kimura's Magmar lost to Hui's Feraligatr. With two defeats, Kimura was out of the Silver Conference. He would never get the chance to avenge his loss to Ethan.

Hui had watched the first day's matches and seen that Magmar was Kimura's strongest Pokemon. She had prepared a counter for it, and that preparation won her the decisive exchange.

With her win over Kimura, Hui had three points, the same as Ethan.

Tomorrow they would battle for the place in the last sixteen. The winner would advance; the loser would be eliminated.

After leaving the arena, Ethan met his friends again and heard how their matches had gone.

Vincent, who shared Ash's group, had made an entrance intended to look cool in his match with Macey, only to take a spectacular tumble. He then lost the battle too.

That left Ash and Macey on three points each. If Ash beat Vincent tomorrow, he would advance outright.

If he lost, though, he would have to face Macey again in a tiebreakera battle tangled up in their new affection and rivalry.

Travis had also lost his match today. He still had one more chance tomorrow, so advancing was not out of reach.

Casey had better luck. Her opponent today was not especially strong, and she won without much trouble.

With that, the second day of the preliminaries ended. Everyone awaited tomorrow's final matches.

Chapter 558: Fate's Cruel Draw

"Hui's Ursaring is down! Incredible! Ethan's Tyranitar has shown its tremendous strength, easily overpowering its opponent in a contest of raw power!"

The announcer's ringing voice carried over Arena A, but it could not drown out the crowd's thunderous cheers.

As the referee raised his flag, the announcer continued, "Another clean three-to-zero! Ethan has dominated once again and secured his place among the final sixteen!"

On the field, Ethan calmly took out a Poke Ball and recalled Tyranitar. He glanced at the dejected young woman opposite him, waved to the spectators, and turned to leave.

He had given Hui no room to breathe, defeating her with a powerful lineup of Blastoise, Dragonite, and Tyranitar.

Hui was about as strong as Kimura had been. Neither had caused Ethan much trouble.

Ethan and Erika returned to the ground-floor lobby. They had barely sat down when their friends began to arrive, bringing news of the day's preliminary results.

Jimmy and Marina came first. The childhood friends from New Bark Town had each won their second match and advanced together to the next round.

Gary returned next. As cool as ever, he wore a faint, enigmatic smile. It looked as though he had won easily again.

Then came Travis and Casey. Both had beaten their opponents today. Their matches had not gone quite as smoothly, but the results were good.

Ash was the last to return. He had fought brilliantly against Vincent. After losing two rounds, he sent out Bulbasaur, which defeated two of Vincent's Pokemon in succession and brought the match to a draw.

Ash had more points overall, so the draw was enough to put him among the final sixteen.

Vincent was the only one of the three childhood friendsJimmy, Marina, and himselfto lose out in the preliminaries.

It was a severe blow to his confidence. After saying goodbye to Marina, he felt too ashamed to stay and hurried away from Silver Town.

Life rarely went exactly as one hoped. Those who had been eliminated would have to try harder next year.

With so many competitors gone, the lobby suddenly seemed empty. But the remaining Trainers had little time to reflect. The large screen flickered, displaying the next round's matchups.

From the final sixteen onward, the competition would be a knockout tournament. The bracket was split into upper and lower halves. Competitors in different halves would not meet until the final; each half would produce one finalist.

The format had advantages and disadvantages. Ethan could not say whether it was good or bad.

When everyone gathered around to read the bracket, though, the pairings stunned them.

First was the seemingly fated clash between Ash and Gary. Friends and rivals who had set out from Pallet Town together, they would finally face each other here.

For both of them, it had come much sooner than expected. Neither had been mentally prepared.

As if sensing the other's reaction, they looked at each other. Their eyes held a tangle of emotions.

That was not all. Whether or not the Pokemon League had arranged it deliberately, Jimmy and Marina, the childhood friends from New Bark Town, had also been paired against each other!

Their expressions were even more revealing than Ash's and Gary's.

They liked each other, yet now they had to fight for the one place in the next round.

Ethan looked away from those two pairings and searched for his own name.

When he found it, he could only sigh. It felt as though the League had it in for him too.

His opponent was Casey, a good friend to both him and Ash.

He had barely finished laughing at Ash's and Jimmy's misfortune before the same thing happened to him.

Worse, he had landed in the same half of the bracket as Ash, Gary, Jimmy, and Marina. Whoever won those matches would be on course to face him in the rounds ahead.

Ethan shook his head with a rueful smile and searched for the other familiar names.

Travis, whom they had only recently met, was the one person to escape this knot of friends.

He had been placed in the other half of the bracket. For him, though, it hardly mattered. He knew Ethan and the others, but they were still acquaintances rather than close friends.

Everyone reacted differently to the draw. For most of them, these were the matchups they had least wanted.

The matches were tomorrow, and no one felt like chatting now. After brief goodbyes, they returned to their rooms.

"Let's go too," Ethan said.

As the others dispersed, he and Erika went back to their room.

Once inside, Ethan walked straight to the sofa and sat down in silence. Erika came up behind him and gently pressed her hands to his shoulders.

"What's wrong? Something on your mind?"

Ethan nodded and sighed. "Did you see their faces? Everyone was happy to reach the final sixteen. Then they saw the bracket and didn't know what to say. None of them expected this draw."

"It couldn't really be helped." Erika sat beside him and settled against his chest. "Seven of the sixteen competitors are from your group of friends. Some of you were bound to be paired together."

Ethan knew that. He would give his all against whoever stood across from him. For now, he simply felt bad for his friends.

"Enough thinking about it. Let's watch the recordings and see how strong Casey has become."

They rose and headed toward the computer. Walking behind Erika, Ethan admired her figure and suddenly wrapped his arms around her from behind.

"What are you doing?" Erika blushed at once. They had slept together many times now and shared a room for several days, but every intimate advance still made her shy. "It's the middle of the day!"

"So what if it is?" Ethan slipped a hand beneath her clothes and squeezed her as he kissed her. "I think daytime makes it even more exciting."

Chapter 559: The Final SixteenFacing Casey

Early the next morning, Ethan left the lodgings with Erika, refreshed and in excellent spirits. They stopped outside the competitors' entrance to Silver Stadium.

The final tournament would use full six-on-six battles. Each Trainer could field six Pokemon, leaving more room to recover from a mistake than in the previous days' matches and offering a better measure of the strength of an entire team.

For the spectators, more battles to watch were an even better reason to welcome the change.

Before Ethan went in, he happened to meet Casey at the entrance. Her expression grew complicated when she saw him, but she still walked up to him, fidgeting.

"Mr. Ethan..." She wished she could call him Ethan the way Misty did, with a more familiar form of address, but she had never found the right moment to make that change. They were not as close as Ethan and Misty. "I never thought we'd be opponents. I... I barely slept last night. I don't know how to face today's match. I really don't want to meet you like this..."

"That doesn't sound like you." Ethan saw the dark circles under her eyes and shook his head, interrupting her. "The Casey I know doesn't dwell on things like this. I'd rather see you full of energy, the way you usually are."

"Full of energy... me?" Casey's eyes widened. She had not expected him to say that, and she felt a rush of warmth.

He was right. She was so unlike her usual self that she could hardly recognize herself.

"That's right." Ethan smiled. "Don't put any pressure on yourself. Treat it like a practice match, or any ordinary battle. Whatever the result, give everything you've worked for a chance to show. Don't let your nerves leave you regretting today's match!"

He was her opponent, yet he was trying to encourage her. Moved, Casey pressed a hand to her chest and declared in her strong Kansai accent, "I understand! I'll give this battle my very best! And... and you do your best too!"

She bowed deeply, gave Ethan one last look, then ran off with a blush on her face.

Erika laughed softly as she watched her go.

She was not jealous of a child, nor upset that Ethan had encouraged a young girl in front of her.

She was amused because his words had restored Casey's confidence in an instant. The girl would probably fight all the harder now. Ethan had created trouble for himself that he need not have faced.

Then again, his willingness to do it showed how confident he was in his own strength.

Ethan and Erika entered through the competitors' tunnel and went to a private waiting room.

When Ethan's match began, Erika would not have to sit in the stands. She could stay here and watch.

Ethan had specially requested it from the League. In fact, every Trainer who reached the final sixteen received better accommodations. They had private rooms to prepare in, where friends and family could watch the matches and wait for them afterward.

The battles had also moved from the four smaller arenas into the main Silver Stadium. It had better equipment, held a larger crowd, and drew far more attention.

In the waiting room, the atmosphere grew heavier as the start of Ethan's match approached.

He stopped joking with Erika. Instead, he opened recordings of Casey's earlier matches on the computer and reviewed the Pokemon she had used.

For a Trainer who had only recently begun her journey, Casey had grown enormously.

Across her previous matches, she had used five Pokemon: Meganium, Pidgey, Rattata, Beedrill, and Elekid. She had suffered setbacks now and then, but her team was strong overall.

Reaching the final sixteen as a newcomer showed real talent. At the very least, she had matched Ash's result from the Indigo League.

After skimming several of Casey's matches, Ethan lay back on the sofa and turned to the waiting room's large screen.

The day's first match was underway.

One of the competitors was Travis, who had been placed in the other half of the bracket. His opponent was another Trainer from that half, Jon Dickson.

Their battle was nearing its end. Ethan had fought Travis before and knew his ability. Though Travis was about Ash's age, he was a little stronger than an average Trainer. Yet Jon was overwhelming him.

That surprised Ethan and made him wary of Jon Dickson.

He had not seen everyone else battle yet, but he had a feeling Jon might win that entire half of the bracket.

Erika had noticed his strength too. She frowned. "He's worth watching. I think he's a local Johto Trainer, and I've heard spectators say he's one of this tournament's favorites, apart from you."

Ethan nodded and committed Jon Dickson's name to memory.

On the screen, Travis's Pikachu was fighting Jon's Rapidash. Pikachu was extremely agile, but Rapidash was fast too, and its charges carried tremendous force. It soon drove Pikachu to the brink.

"He's going to lose..." Erika murmured, watching the battle turn against Travis.

She was right. Pikachu resisted fiercely, but in the end it fell beneath Rapidash's blazing hooves.

Travis had defeated only one of Jon's Pokemon in the entire match. The gap between them was unmistakable.

On the screen, Travis gathered Pikachu into his arms, looking desolate. He had traveled across the sea from the Orange Islands to Johto, but his Silver Conference journey had to end here.
