He had not achieved the result he wanted. He would have to return to the Orange Islands disappointed and full of regret.

Ethan had no time to dwell on it. At the announcement over the speakers, he rose and headed for the battlefield.

His match with Casey was next. One of them would follow Travis out of Silver Stadium, carrying their own disappointment.

Chapter 560: Casey's Own Trap

Ethan and Casey walked to their respective Trainer's boxes amid a roar of cheers.

While the announcer introduced them to the crowd, they looked at each other across the field.

Casey had regained her composure since their meeting outside. Her face was bright with energy, and none of her earlier anxiety showed.

She had recovered quickly.

"Ethan!" Perhaps she had finally overcome her hesitation about speaking to him more familiarly. Like Misty, she addressed him without the formality of before. "I'm ready. Please give me a real battle!"

Ethan smiled and nodded. "Of course. Give me everything you've got."

Seeing that both Trainers were ready, the referee announced, "We'll now decide who sends out a Pokemon first!"

They looked at the large screen. The wheel spun through more than a dozen rotations before slowing to a stop, its pointer settling on Ethan's red section.

Ethan sighed.

His luck with the draw had been poor throughout this tournament. Every time, he had been chosen to send out a Pokemon first. He did not care much about the disadvantage, but drawing first again and again was still irritating.

"Red side, please send out your Pokemon first!"

At the referee's signal, Ethan took out the Poke Ball he had prepared and released his first Pokemon without hesitation.

A flash of blue light revealed Jolteon on the field.

Just as Ethan had studied recordings of Casey, she had reviewed his team before the match. Jolteon's appearance did not surprise her.

The announcer flipped through his notes and raised his voice over the stadium. "Ethan has sent out Jolteon! As everyone knows, it performed superbly in both the Indigo League and this year's Silver Conference. How will Casey answer?"

Casey looked at Jolteon, steadied herself, and took a Poke Ball from the pouch at her waist.

"Go, Meganium!"

She threw the ball far out. Blue light flashed, and Meganium appeared before JolteonCasey's first and most trusted partner.

Of the few Pokemon on Casey's team, it was a sound choice.

Meganium did not have a type advantage on offense, but as a Grass-type it resisted Jolteon's Electric-type moves. That improved its chances considerably.

Even from across the field, Ethan could see Casey smile. Her resolve and confidence were unmistakable.

That was more like her.

But...

Casey had grown quickly, yet Jolteon had trained longer and fought in many more battles. Beating Ethan would still be difficult.

He had no intention of giving her an easy chance, either.

Sure enough, Jolteon's performance surprised Casey as soon as the battle began.

The fastest of Eevee's evolutions showed extraordinary agility. Meganium's Magical Leaf and Tackle could not land while Jolteon raced around the field.

Even Razor Leaf, with its swiftly spinning blades, missed as Jolteon dodged each leaf.

"It's so fast..."

Watching from the sideline, Casey could barely follow Jolteon with her eyes.

Worse, Meganium could not use Vine Whip to restrain it as some other Grass-type Pokemon might. Its short, thick limbs could not keep pace with Jolteon. Jolteon repeatedly found openings and struck with Electric-type attacks.

Meganium's resistance to Electric-type moves was all that had kept it in the fight.

Seeing her partner pushed back, Casey searched anxiously for a way to reverse the battle. Then an idea came to her.

"Use Poison Powder!"

At her command, Meganium sprayed a cloud of purple powder. The move was too obvious to catch Jolteon.

But hitting Jolteon directly was not Casey's aim.

She ordered Meganium to keep releasing Poison Powder. Soon the purple cloud covered nearly half the battlefield. Jolteon dared not rush into the dense haze and could only pace outside it, giving Meganium a chance to catch its breath.

"A clever response from Casey!" the announcer praised her. "If Jolteon closes in now, it will enter the poison cloud and risk being poisoned. Meganium has time to recover. What will Ethan do?"

Ethan raised his eyebrows at the haze.

It did keep Jolteon from approaching easily. Yet the scene looked familiar. Had he seen something like this before?

He could not remember which battle it had been, but he remembered how to respond.

"Jolteon, use Thunder Shock!"

Jolteon leaped back to widen the gap, then fired a current from its body. The instant the electricity touched the suspended Poison Powder, a deafening boom sounded and the entire cloud exploded.

The blast engulfed Meganium. When the powder cleared and the crowd could see again, the Pokemon that had looked healthy moments before was barely able to stand.

Casey's face changed. She stared at the field in disbelief. "How...?"

An experienced Trainer would know that a cloud of powder could explode when it met a spark or an electric current. Casey had never encountered that danger before.

"Oh no!" the announcer cried. "Casey released so much Poison Powder that she gave Jolteon the perfect opening. Her own strategy has backfired!"

Ethan did not need to give another order. Seeing Meganium in that state, Jolteon dashed forward and knocked it out with a single Tackle.

The referee raised his flag, and Casey finally came back to herself.

She recalled the unconscious Meganium with a rueful smile, scolding herself for her mistake.

When she saw Ethan looking helplessly amused too, she stuck out her tongue at him and took a second Poke Ball from her clothes.

"You're next! Go, Pidgey!"

Chapter 561: Don't Joke About Professor Oak

Against Casey's Pidgey, Jolteon had a clear type advantage. But Ethan wanted his Pokemon to gain experience as they battled, so he took out its Poke Ball and recalled it.

Casey noticed.

She smiled. Despite losing the first round, she had chosen a Pokemon at a type disadvantage for a reason.

From recordings of Ethan's recent matches, she knew he rarely kept the same Pokemon on the field for consecutive rounds, regardless of the matchup. She had decided to take a gamble.

She had guessed right. When he saw Pidgey, Ethan withdrew the Jolteon that could have beaten it so easily instead of pressing his advantage.

Good! Without the type disadvantage, she had a chance to win.

A moment later, her smile vanished.

Ethan threw his second Poke Ball, and an elegant Pokemon appeared before Pidgey.

Casey recognized it at once: Ethan's Gardevoir.

Oh, this was bad...

Gardevoir was the first Pokemon Ethan had ever caught. Casey knew it was his ace and the partner he trusted most.

Sending a Pokemon like that against her Pidgey was almost unfair!

As Casey's delight turned to dismay, Ethan shook his head with a helpless smile.

His newer Pokemon from Johto needed to keep training through tournaments like this, but his long-standing partners from Kanto also needed an occasional battle to stay sharp. Every one of them deserved a chance on the field.

It simply happened to be Gardevoir's turn.

When the round began, Gardevoir fought as though it had decided that knowing its Trainer's opponent was no reason to hold back. It dispatched Pidgey cleanly.

The announcer and spectators could only imagine how helpless Casey must have felt.

Pidgey had no chance to fight back. Gardevoir used Teleport to evade its Quick Attack. When Pidgey launched Twister from a distance, Gardevoir dodged that too, dragged it to the ground with Confusion, and finished it with a rapid combination of attacks.

The gap between them was unmistakable. The round had been entirely one-sided.

The score was two to zero. Casey had lost two Pokemon without putting Ethan under any pressure.

"How can Casey turn this around?" the announcer asked, his voice subdued with concern for her.

Casey looked across at Ethan, drew a deep breath, and took out her third Poke Ball.

"Go, Rattata!"

...

"She's going to lose again..."

In a plaza outside the stadium, Ash, Misty, and Brock sat on a bench, each holding an ice cream. A nearby screen showed the match inside. Casey had now lost five rounds. Her last Pokemon, Beedrill, was fighting Ethan's Scizor.

Beedrill was in poor condition, its body covered in wounds. A moment's mistake let Scizor catch it in its great pincers. It looked close to defeat.

"Ethan's as strong as ever," Ash said enviously. "Casey can't fight back at all."

"Of course she can't." Misty tilted her head up proudly. "None of you competitors can beat him, if you ask me!"

Misty and Casey were about the same age, and Misty could sense Casey's vague affection for Ethan. Perhaps they bristled at each other because of that, or perhaps it was just their personalities. They had never quite gotten along since they met.

Brock glanced at Ash. "You know this isn't good news for you, right? If Ethan wins, then whoever wins your match with Gary will have to face him next."

"What?!"

Ash hurriedly pulled out the bracket the League had given him. Sure enough, his match with Gary sat beside Ethan's match with Casey. The winners would meet in the quarterfinals.

Misty covered her mouth to hide a laugh. "Fate really is playing tricks on you. Well, I'm looking forward to watching you do what you promised: beat Gary first, then knock Ethan out!"

Before Ash could reply, someone called his name from a distance.

"Ash!"

He turned and saw his mother, Delia, approaching with Professor Oak.

"Mom! Professor Oak!" He ran over to them in surprise. "What are you doing here?"

"We've come to cheer you on, of course." Delia looked at him with pride. "Reaching the final tournament is already a wonderful achievement. How could I miss the chance to support you in person?"

Professor Oak clasped his hands behind his back and smiled kindly. "I hear you and Gary have been drawn against each other?"

"Yes."

"Then both of you must do your best." Oak turned toward the screen. Ethan's Scizor had beaten Casey's Beedrill, and the camera had settled on Ethan's handsome face. "You're both excellent young Trainers, so I wouldn't be surprised whichever of you wins. Compared with him, though, you're still a little inexperienced. I hope you'll push past your limits and defeat him in the next round."

...

Ethan and Erika were leaving through the competitors' entrance when they met Ash's group coming toward them.

He was a little surprised to see Delia and Professor Oak there, but it made sense. With such an important match ahead, of course Ash's mother had come to watch.

"Professor, Aunt Delia. It's been a while."

"Congratulations on your victory," Oak said with a warm, grandfatherly smile. "You were remarkable. I still remember when we first met. You were so inexperienced then. After all your travels, you've grown tremendously. You're not only much stronger but more composed too."

They chatted briefly. Then, as Ash's match time approached, the group said goodbye and went into the stadium with him.

Erika watched them go. "Isn't Professor Oak Gary's grandfather? Why isn't he with Gary? He seems so close to Ash and his mother."

"Can't you tell?" Ethan laughed and repeated a joke he knew from his life on Earth. "Oak and Ash must be close because Oak's an old bachelor, and Ash's mother is a beautiful woman who's been single for years. Maybe he's hoping to court someone much younger!"

"Honestly." Erika rolled her eyes and gave his waist a light pinch. "At first I thought you actually knew something. Then you started talking nonsense. Don't joke about them like that. Imagine if they heard you! Delia seems such a kind, capable woman, and Professor Oak is so respected. Why would you think that about them?"

Chapter 562: Ash and Gary's Battle

Ethan and Erika returned to the ground-floor lobby of their lodgings. They settled on a sofa in the lounge, ordered two cocktails, and watched Ash's match with Gary at their leisure.

In the final tournament, the battlefield was randomly chosen for each match.

There were four possibilities: grass, rock, water, and ice. Each field could change a Trainer's tactics, strategy, and even how a Pokemon performed. The random draw made the matches less predictable and more exciting to watch.

Ethan and Casey had drawn the grass field. They had battled among dense greenery, though neither had made much use of the terrain.

On the screen, the announcer was introducing Ash and Gary.

"...Incredibly, both Ash and Gary come from Pallet Town in Kanto, and they set out on their journeys from there at the same time! Now these friends and rivals finally meet in what seems a fated clash in the final tournament!"

Gary's cheerleading squad, absent for so long, had appeared again from somewhere. Behind him in the section for friends and family, they performed a cheering dance.

The tall, beautiful young women drew nearly every man's gaze and made Gary impossible to forget.

The announcer continued, "And we've learned that Gary is the grandson of Professor Oak, a highly respected figure in Pokemon research! Ash, meanwhile, reached the final sixteen at the Indigo League. Their match today is sure to be one of the most watched and exciting of the tournament! Both Trainers are ready, so let's see the sparks fly!"

The camera cut to Professor Oak. Seeing himself on the screen, he froze for a moment. He had clearly not expected to be mentioned. Sitting beside Delia, he looked terribly awkward. But he had weathered plenty of public attention before, and a second later he managed a stiff smile and waved at the camera.

When the audience's enthusiastic applause died down, the announcer returned to the match.

"Before the battle begins, let's find out which field they'll draw!"

Everyone watched the wheel on the large screen spin. When it stopped, the pointer indicated the rock field.

The ground before Ash and Gary began to change. It parted to either side, opening a dark pit below. A huge lifting platform rose from the darkness, carrying a battlefield strewn with giant boulders into place.

Next came the draw for who would send out a Pokemon first. Ash was lucky enough to go second, leaving Gary, on the red side, to choose first.

Gary looked indifferent. It seemed he did not care which of them had to lead.

When the match began, Gary sent out Nidoqueen. Ash thought for a moment and answered with Tauros. Both Pokemon had plenty of strength; a contest of raw power seemed inevitable.

Erika glanced away from the screen. "Which one do you think will win?"

"Probably Ash," Ethan said, rubbing his chin.

If he had to judge only from knowing the two boys in person, Ethan could not say which would win. But he also remembered the animated series, and that made him favor Ash.

"Ash..."

Erika frowned slightly as she weighed their strengths.

Before the Indigo League, both boys had challenged her at the Celadon Gym. Gary had seemed stronger then. He had since shed much of his arrogance and become steadier, which likely made him an even tougher opponent.

Yet Ash was a more astonishing boy. As Erika traveled with him and came to know him better, she saw how unpredictable his ability could be. He could be slow to catch on and rash in his actions, but he also had a way of producing miracles.

She still did not know who would win, but she was willing to trust Ethan's judgment.

On the screen, Nidoqueen and Tauros had already begun fighting.

Nidoqueen opened with a powerful strike, slamming its fist into the ground. A wide fissure spread toward Tauros. The force shattered the towering boulders, sending smaller stones raining down on it.

Tauros took some damage, but at Ash's command it charged straight at Nidoqueen with astonishing force, aiming its two horns directly at its opponent.

Gary's Nidoqueen was no weakling. It seized both horns with brute strength and stopped Tauros in its tracks.

At that close range, Nidoqueen fired a Hyper Beam straight into Tauros. The blast hurled it through several boulders before it collapsed on the ground, unable to rise.

Seeing Tauros unconscious, the referee raised his flag.

The crowd erupted in surprise. No one had expected Tauros to be knocked out so quickly. Hadn't the announcer just promised an exciting match?

Was that it?

The announcer himself had not expected this outcome and fell silent in embarrassment.

The Pokemon had barely exchanged blows. The audience had not even settled into the match before the first round ended.

Ash was not shaken. He calmly recalled Tauros and took out his second Poke Ball.

This time he sent out Heracross. Whether out of caution or for some other reason, Gary recalled Nidoqueen and chose a second Poke Ball too.

A flash of blue light revealed Magmar opposite Heracross.

It was a strong choice. Magmar's Fire-type attacks had a clear advantage against Heracross's Bug typing. Gary was taking the match seriously and had no intention of holding back.

Chapter 563: Oak's Pokemon Are Impressive

The second round between Ash and Gary began.

Heracross attacked first. It landed several moves on Magmar in succession, then used its great strength to knock Magmar into the air, taking an early advantage.

Magmar answered with a startling maneuver. While airborne, it used Fire Blast, then plunged into the flames of its own attack. Like a blazing fireball, it hurtled down at Heracross.

The impact drove Heracross backward until it struck a huge boulder. Gary gave another command, and from point-blank range Magmar hit Heracross with Flamethrower.

Flames swallowed Heracross. Its silhouette was barely visible inside them.

Just when everyone thought it had lost, Heracross beat its wings and raised a powerful gust. The wind blew out the flames around it in an instant.

That gave Ethan an idea. Watching other Trainers battle could always teach him something new.

With the fire extinguished, Heracross launched its counterattack. It charged through Magmar's Flamethrower and struck with Megahorn, one of the strongest Bug-type moves, knocking Magmar out.

"Ash really is a master of fighting at a type disadvantage," Ethan said, watching the wounded, panting Heracross on the screen. "It hung on through sheer determination, ignored the matchup, and turned the battle around. I have to admire that."

Hearing the envy in his voice, Erika smiled. "Some things can't be learned. That's his talent."

With the score tied at one apiece, Ash and Gary moved into the third round.

Perhaps hoping to take control of the match, Gary sent out Blastoise. It was his first Pokemon and his strongest. Bringing it out now was surely meant to establish a lead and widen it.

Ash kept Heracross on the field against Blastoise. But when Blastoise fired Hydro Pump, determination alone could not save the exhausted Heracross. It went down easily.

Two to one. Blastoise had put Gary ahead as soon as it entered.

Ash's third choice was Muk.

The two Pokemon traded attacks. Muk even found an opening and enveloped Blastoise completely in its soft, mudlike body. But Blastoise kept firing Hydro Pump from within. As water built up inside Muk, it could no longer hold on and was forced to release its opponent.

Ash made a quick decision. Rather than let Muk continue fighting, he recalled it.

"What a match!" the announcer cried. "Both Trainers are showing everything they've got. Gary's Blastoise has been trained evenly across the board, with no obvious weakness. What Pokemon will Ash choose to face it next?"

Ash considered for a moment and sent out Bayleef.

Ethan was surprised. He had expected Ash to bring out Pikachu for a battle between their two aces, but Ash clearly had another plan.

Then again, if Ash thought the way Ethan did, he would not so often fight at a type disadvantage and create so many memorable moments.

Pikachu was not even beside Ash. It sat with Misty, Brock, Togepi, and the others, cheering him on. It seemed Ash had no intention of using it in this match.

Grass-type Bayleef had a clear advantage over Water-type Blastoise. But that was the sort of advantage other Trainers could rely on. When Ash used the favorable type, he seemed to lose nine times out of ten.

He really was that unpredictable.

At first, Bayleef and Blastoise looked evenly matched. Then Blastoise found an opening. It bit down on Bayleef, swung it around, and hurled it out of the field. Bayleef struck the wall beneath the stands and fell unconscious.

"Incredible!" the announcer shouted. "Gary's Blastoise has taken down three of Ash's Pokemon in a row! Who can stop its winning streak?"

Gary still had five Pokemon available. Ash had only three left.

Back in the lobby, Erika turned to Ethan. "Gary's Blastoise really is strong. I battled it before, and I still remember it. Ash is in trouble now. What if Gary wins?"

"Have faith in him." Ethan was not especially worried. The battle appeared to be turning Gary's way, but Ethan held to his earlier judgment. "It isn't over. Either one could still win, and I believe Ash has the strength and luck to come back."

After a five-minute break, the match resumed.

Ash opened the second half with Snorlax. Gary gave Blastoise a rest and sent out Arcanine.

Arcanine was another of Gary's signature Pokemon. He had trained it exceptionally well, and it was not to be underestimated.

But Ash's Snorlax was powerful too. Arcanine trapped it in Fire Spin at the start of their clash. Snorlax answered with a Hyper Beam that knocked Arcanine out in one blow.

Gary, the announcer, and the spectators were all stunned.

The crowd erupted. After losing three Pokemon, Ash had begun the second half by taking a round back with Snorlax's overwhelming strength.

Gary's expression did not change. He recalled Arcanine and, instead of returning Blastoise to the field, sent out Nidoqueen, which had performed so well against Tauros in the opening round.

Ethan understood the choice. Gary was giving Blastoise time to recover.

Gary knew Ash would not be easy to beat. He intended to save Blastoise for their final confrontation.

But he had underestimated Snorlax. Nidoqueen fought well under Gary's direction, yet before long Snorlax found its chance. It dodged Nidoqueen's Hyper Beam with unexpected agility and knocked it out with a single Ice Punch.

"S-so strong!"

The announcer could scarcely believe that the heavy, placid-looking Snorlax had such ability.

Applause burst from the stands. Even Erika praised it. "Ash has raised that Snorlax remarkably well. It has strength and agility. I wonder how he trained it."

Ethan laughed. "Rather than Ash, maybe you should credit Professor Oak for raising it so well!"

"What?" Erika blinked.

"Didn't you know?" Ethan smiled. "Ash leaves the Pokemon he's caught at Professor Oak's Laboratory. Oak looks after them and helps train them. Compared with other Trainers who leave Pokemon there, he clearly pays Ash's partners more attention. Even his own grandson Gary doesn't get that treatment!"

Chapter 564: Advancing Together

The battle seemed to be turning Ash's way again.

But just when everyone expected Snorlax to keep dominating, Gary sent out Scizor. With its extraordinary speed, it knocked out Snorlax and then Muk, swinging the advantage back to Gary.

More importantly, Ash had only one Pokemon left that he had not sent out, while Gary still had three available. From any angle, Gary seemed more likely to win.

The broadcast cut to Misty and Brock in the section for friends and family. Both looked tense and worried for Ash.

The spectators, in contrast, were delighted by a match whose outcome they could not predict. The announcer's promise before the battle had proved true: this was a fierce contest worth watching.

On the field, Ash took out his last Poke Ball with a solemn expression. He threw it high, and Charizard appeared before the crowd.

"Huh?" Erika stared at it in surprise. "Wasn't Charizard at Charicific Valley? How did it get here?"

"That's not so surprising," Ethan said with a smile. "Ash must have felt uncertain about facing Gary and called it back for this match."

Since leaving his own Charizard at Charicific Valley, Ethan had often exchanged messages with Liza, who ran the place. She kept him informed about its training.

Both his Charizard and Ash's were hardworking Pokemon. In only a little over two weeks at the valley, they had climbed considerably in its rankings.

Ethan's Charizard had reached the upper ranks and was challenging for a place in the top twenty. Ash's was in the middle ranks and could now fight the valley's ordinary residents on even terms.

Back on the field, Gary seemed to have expected Ash's Charizard. He did not switch Pokemon and left Scizor in the battle.

Perhaps he wanted Scizor to test how strong Charizard had become. But Scizor was four times as vulnerable to Fire-type attacks. The round had barely begun when it fell to Charizard's flames.

Gary's expression did not change. He sent out another Pokemon.

With a booming thud that shook the ground, a round, heavy Golem landed on the field.

As a Rock-type, Golem could withstand Charizard's fire. But Charizard could fly while Golem remained on the ground, leaving each with its own possible path to victory.

Then came an amusing moment. Knowing fire would do little to Golem, Ash ordered Seismic Toss. He had underestimated its weight. Charizard managed to lift Golem only a short distance before losing its grip and dropping it back to the ground.

Charizard was still the stronger of the two. As Golem used Rollout, Charizard struck it with Dragon Rage and knocked it out.

With two consecutive wins, Charizard had brought the match level again.

Each Trainer now had only one Pokemon remaining: Ash's Charizard, already on the field, and Gary's ace, Blastoise. Their round-of-sixteen match had come down to its final clash.

The matchup favored Gary. Blastoise's Water type countered Charizard, and it had rested while Charizard fought two rounds.

As the final battle began, everyone watched closely.

Just as expected, Blastoise took the early advantage. Even when Charizard flew into the air, Blastoise fired Hydro Pump from both cannons on its back. The streams formed a kind of antiaircraft barrage that kept Charizard from approaching.

But Ash rarely fought by the expected rules.

At that disadvantage, he suddenly ordered Charizard to breathe fire over the rocks around the field.

The spectators looked at one another in confusion. Gary and Blastoise were just as puzzled by what Ash was trying to do.

As Charizard kept breathing fire, the field grew hotter. Smaller rocks broke apart in the heat, and the whole rocky surface became so hot that it visibly reddened.

Gary did not know Ash's plan, but he knew he could not let it continue.

At his command, Blastoise sprayed water across the field to cool it. The cold streams struck the hot rocks and instantly raised great clouds of steam that covered nearly the whole arena.

"I see..." Ethan understood what Ash intended.

The steam hid the battlefield from view. Fortunately, it dispersed almost as quickly as it had formed.

When the spectators could see again, Charizard had somehow closed the distance. It and Blastoise had locked their four limbs together and were struggling for control.

The announcer took a moment to recover. "Charizard couldn't get near Blastoise before, but the steam let it approach safely! Ash's strategy is astonishing!"

More importantly, with Blastoise's arms pinned, it could not turn its body and aim its cannons at Charizard.

That was bad news for Gary.

Still locked together, Charizard carried Blastoise into the air and used Seismic Toss again. It spun rapidly several times, then dove and drove Blastoise hard into the ground.

Boom!

Dust billowed upward. The spectators strained to see. Both Pokemon rose from the ground, but Blastoise was covered in injuries. It swayed a few times and then toppled backward.

The referee raised his flag. After trailing earlier in the match, Ash had fought back to win.

The stands burst into cheers. Delia jumped up and down with joy beside a visibly awkward Professor Oak, who seemed unsure how to react.

"He really won!"

Erika covered her mouth in surprise. Ethan had predicted Ash's victory before the match, but as the battle grew fierce, she had thought Gary was ahead. She had not expected Ash to turn it around.

"Gary made a mistake," Ethan said with a shake of his head. He sounded a little sorry for him. "He panicked during that last Seismic Toss and didn't give the right command. I'd have told Blastoise to withdraw into its shell. The impact would still hurt, but it wouldn't have gone down so easily."

While the people around him celebrated, Ash stood motionless on the field, staring in a daze. He seemed unable to believe that he had won.

Gary took the loss more easily. He looked at Ash, then left the battlefield without a word.

In the lobby, Ethan drained the last of his cocktail and stopped watching the screen. He would wait there for Ash to return.

Four matches were scheduled for the day. Three had finished, sending Jon Dickson, Ash, and Ethan into the quarterfinals. The two Trainers in the next match were both in the other half of the bracket. Ethan did not know them well, and neither was an immediate rival, so he had little interest in watching.

Jimmy and Marina's match, along with the remaining battles, would take place tomorrow. That gave Ethan time to study Ash's team carefully.

Chapter 565: Ethan Versus Ash

It was not long before Ash and the others returned to the ground floor of the lodging building.

Ash's broad smile was visible even before he came through the door. He had reached the quarterfinals, his best result in two League tournaments. More than that, he had finally beaten Gary, his longtime rival, for the first time. Winning on a stage like this meant something special.

"Congratulations." Ethan applauded with a smile. "Just as I 'predicted,' you won."

"Thanks." Ash scratched his head bashfully at the praise. Then he remembered who his next opponent would be and grew serious. "Ethan, we battle the day after tomorrow. I'll do my best!"

Ethan's expression turned peculiar.

He had come over to congratulate Ash, and Ash had responded by announcing his determination to beat him. Ethan did not know whether to laugh or sigh.

Well, Ash was a child and the story's chosen hero. Ethan would let it pass.

A celebration meal for both their victories was only natural.

Besides their own group of five, Ethan invited Delia, Professor Oak, Jimmy, Marina, Misa, and Masha. They crowded into a private room at a nearby restaurant and ate their fill. Afterward, Oak, the eldest among them, offered to pay despite the pained look on his face. He discovered Ethan had already settled the bill.

Oak stood before the smiling server and sighed to himself. What a thoughtful young man.

That night, after everyone returned to their rooms, Ethan stood on the balcony and happened to see Ash leave the building alone. He headed toward the lake beside Silver Stadium.

"What are you looking at?" Erika came up behind Ethan and slipped her arms around his waist. Following his gaze, she said, "Oh, isn't that Ash? Where is he going so late?"

"He's going to find Gary. Who else?"

"Gary?" Erika was surprised for a moment, then nodded. "Their relationship is complicated. I suppose Ash wants to comfort him."

Ethan turned and wrapped his arms around her, breathing in her perfume. "If Ash had been eliminated, Gary as he is now would have gone looking for him too. After tonight, I think Gary will entrust his dream to Ash."

"Why do you say that?" Erika had scarcely finished speaking when Ethan opened her collar and slid a hand beneath her clothes. Her face reddened.

Ethan offered little explanation. Caressing her, he said with a smile, "If things go as I expect, Gary will turn to scientific research. I doubt we'll see him competing in future League tournaments. Anyway, it's a beautiful night. Let's celebrate properly."

...

The next day, Ethan and Erika had no match of their own. They stayed in their room.

The day's battles played on the television while they used the computer to review Ash, Jon Dickson, and several other possible opponents. They went through the Pokemon those Trainers had used, concentrating on each one's abilities so they would know what to expect.

As on the previous day, four matches would determine the remaining quarterfinalists. Of the Trainers Ethan knew, only Jimmy and Marina still had a match today, and they would have to face each other.

To anyone else, their pairing might have looked ordinary. To Ethan, who knew a little about their feelings for one another, it was emotionally harsher than Ash and Gary's match.

Once the battle began, it fell into three distinct stages.

At first, they tested each other carefully. Perhaps neither had worked through their feelings or knew how to face the other. They held back and fought so cautiously that it hardly looked like a match between the final sixteen.

The announcer was baffled, and the spectators began murmuring. Some even wondered if the match was fixed.

The conflict on Jimmy's and Marina's faces was plain on the screen. Fortunately, it did not last long. Marina seemed to make up her mind and launched a fierce attack. Jimmy responded in kind, and soon both were fighting freely, exchanging blows.

That second stage settled the crowd. At least now there were moments worth cheering for.

After the halftime break, they stopped holding back entirely and fought with everything they had.

Jimmy was the stronger of the two. In the final exchange, his Typhlosion defeated Marina's Feraligatr despite its type disadvantage, securing his place in the quarterfinals.

Unlike Ash, Jimmy showed little excitement at advancing. Marina, though she had lost, seemed happy for her childhood friend.

Ethan sighed. What a complicated relationship.

One more match in their half of the bracket followed. It was far less tense; the gap in strength was considerable. A Trainer from Hoenn named Harrison won decisively.

With that, all four quarterfinalists in Ethan's half were set: Ethan, Ash, Jimmy, and Harrison. Ethan would face Ash, while Jimmy would face Harrison. The winners would advance to the semifinals.

In their room, Ethan and Erika spent the rest of the day preparing. They drew up several plans based on their opponents' Pokemon and made the final choices for Ethan's team tomorrow.

...

The quarterfinals followed the same knockout-tournament rules as the round of sixteen.

Each match would be a full six-on-six battle. The battlefield and first Trainer to send out a Pokemon would be drawn beforehand. Once either Trainer had lost three Pokemon, there would be a five-minute halftime break.

The only real difference was how fiercely people online debated who would make it through and eventually reach the final.

Ethan's half of the bracket had left a strong impression on the spectators. He led the polls by a wide margin, but Ash and Harrison had plenty of supporters too. Jimmy came last, largely because he and Marina had held back during the first half of their match.

In the other half, Jon Dickson was the only standout. Most people expected the final to be between him and Ethan.

After a night's rest, Ethan and Ash stood opposite one another inside Silver Stadium at nine the next morning.

Ash looked well rested. His eyes were determined, and he seemed eager to begin.

Beating Gary yesterday had given him a great deal of confidence. He was ready for today's match.

Two matches were scheduled today: Ethan against Ash in the morning, then Jimmy against Harrison in the afternoon. By day's end, their half of the bracket would have its two semifinalists.

Once both Trainers were ready, the referee called, "We'll now draw the battlefield for this match!"

Ethan and Ash looked up together. The wheel spun on the large screen and, when it stopped, pointed once again to the rock field.

That was good news for Ash. He had fought on the rock field only yesterday and performed well there. Familiarity with the terrain gave him a slightly better chance.

The next draw decided who would send out a Pokemon first. Once again, Ethan had the bad luck to be chosen.

He looked untroubled. By now, he was used to it.

Before the watching crowd, the battlefield changed. Ethan's match against Ash had begun.

Chapter 566: Oak Says to Trust Ash

Ethan took out a Poke Ball, tossed it lightly in his hand, and threw it onto the field.

Blue light flashed, and Gardevoir appeared.

From yesterday's review, Ethan knew Ash had around twelve Pokemon available, leaving aside his thirty Tauros. Any of them might appear today. Ethan had always treated Ash like a younger brother, but he could not underestimate his strength. One careless choice could cost Ethan the match.

He had to be cautious.

So he opened with the partner he trusted most, aiming for a steady first round.

Ash had spent all of yesterday studying Ethan's team with Brock. He knew most of Ethan's Pokemon were formidable. Gengar and the red Gyarados were particularly terrifying. He could not afford to let his guard down.

At the sight of Gardevoir, Ash drew a deep breath. Following the plan he and Brock had made, he took out a Poke Ball.

"Go, Donphan!"

Ash threw hard. A sturdy Pokemon resembling a small tusked elephant appeared before Gardevoir.

Donphan? Ethan had not expected that.

On reflection, though, it made sense. Neither Pokemon had a type advantage over the other, and Ash had few better answers to Gardevoir.

With the crowd watching, the battle began at once.

At Ash's command, Donphan curled into a ball and rolled straight at Gardevoir with tremendous momentum.

"Gardevoir, stop it!"

Gardevoir reached out with its psychic power, trying to restrain Donphan. But Donphan moved quickly while rolling, and rocks of different sizes blocked its path from view. Catching it was not so simple.

Rumble, rumble...

The ground trembled beneath Donphan. It rolled straight up the sloping side of a huge boulder, launched into the air, and dropped toward Gardevoir.

Surprising an ordinary Pokemon might have made the attack work, but Gardevoir saw it coming. A single Teleport carried it safely out of Donphan's path.

Donphan had barely landed and had not yet turned around. Gardevoir seized the opening, raised a hand, and used Psychic to hurl it into a distant rock.

Crash!

The impact shattered the rock. Donphan's ringed armor protected it, however, and it took little damage.

In Ash's section of the stands, Brock sighed helplessly.

He and Ash had worked hard on their plans yesterday. Of all Ethan's Pokemon, they agreed that Gardevoir would be the hardest to face apart from Gengar.

Gengar was absurdly strong, but they knew Ethan rarely sent it into tournament matches unless the situation was desperate. That offered some reassurance.

Gardevoir was another matter. They could not expect to avoid it. It stood like a mountain between Ash and the semifinals.

After considering Ash's Pokemon one by one, they had chosen Donphan to face Gardevoir if it appeared. There was no type disadvantage between them, which improved Ash's chances a little. Gardevoir's psychic attacks also tended to lift opponents and slam them into the ground. Donphan could curl up to soften those impacts.

In theory, it was a sound plan. Brock had been especially relieved when today's battlefield was drawn as the rock field.

The boulders might limit Donphan's movement, but they also blocked Gardevoir's sight. That should hinder its psychic attacks even more.

Now that the battle was underway, the plan had helped somewhat, but the reality was far from what Brock had expected.

All he could do was hope Ash would adapt.

He hoped Ash could survive this round.

Misty sat in the same section, but her two good friends were on opposite sides of the field. She tried to remain neutral and did not cheer especially hard for either one.

In a small, casual match, she might have teased Ash without harm. At an important tournament like the Silver Conference, she did not want to unsettle him and affect his focus.

She had even stayed out of Ash and Brock's planning yesterday so there would be no question of taking sides.

She could not help having a preference in her heart. When she saw Ethan take the lead, she felt glad for him.

On the field, Gardevoir went on the offensive at Ethan's command.

Waiting passively had never been his style.

The great boulders did restrict Gardevoir, but an opportunity could be found if they watched for one.

Donphan rolled forward again, trying the same launch from a boulder. Gardevoir timed its move before Donphan could land. A forceful burst of Psychic sent it flying out of the battlefield.

Donphan sailed past the referee and struck the wall behind him before finally stopping.

The referee raised his flag. "Donphan is out of bounds! Ethan wins the first round!"

"How did that happen...?"

Ash scratched his head as he looked at Donphan beyond the boundary. The round had ended before he was ready. Donphan was hardly injured, yet it had been eliminated like this. It was frustrating.

He recovered quickly, recalled Donphan, and drew a second Poke Ball.

"Go, Noctowl!"

Blue light flashed, and Ash's golden Shiny Noctowl appeared over the field. Ethan could not help feeling envious all over again.

He wanted a Shiny Pokemon too.

Ethan shook off the thought, recalled Gardevoir, and chose his second Poke Ball.

As before, he was fighting cautiously but still wanted to train his team before the final. He tried to give every Pokemon some time on the field.

Jolteon would face the Shiny Noctowl. Now the terrain could work in Ethan's favor.

As the next round began, Jolteon darted through the rock field with nimble steps. Noctowl had the advantage of flight and was fast in its own right, but it could not pin Jolteon down.

Each time Noctowl dived, Jolteon sprang from a boulder and changed direction sharply. It opened the gap again before Noctowl could catch it, leaving the bird to sail past.

"Ash..."

In the stands, Delia watched her son struggle and grew worried. She had brought a professional camera to photograph his best moments, but so far his Pokemon had scarcely had a chance to show what they could do.

"Trust him," Professor Oak said beside her. "Remember the match the day before yesterday? Ash fell behind early, then came back and beat Gary. I believe he can do it today too."

Delia nodded, but the worry did not leave her face.

She had not known Ethan for long, yet she liked him. And she could see that Gary, in both his Pokemon's strength and his own composure, was not Ethan's equal. Could Ash truly beat a Trainer like this?

Chapter 567: The Unbeaten Streak Ends

Noctowl and Jolteon were still battling on the field.

Jolteon ran behind a huge boulder, stopped sharply, and turned to face Noctowl. A dazzling Electroweb burst from its body and spread toward the bird.

But Ash's Noctowl was clever. It had read Jolteon's intention before Jolteon even turned. With a slight twist and a beat of its wings, it flew clear of the web.

The Electroweb brushed past Noctowl and dissolved in the air.

From his place in the Trainer's area, Ethan watched Noctowl's response and nodded in approval.

Ash's Shiny Noctowl was a little smaller than others of its kind, but it was remarkably intelligent. It could think for itself and even direct other Pokemon in battle.

Ash had worked hard to catch it. Unlike most Pokemon, Noctowl made its own judgments on the battlefield, assessed the situation, and seized openings that lasted only an instant.

Now, as soon as it escaped Electroweb, Noctowl spotted Jolteon's brief pause. Without waiting for Ash's command, it beat its wings and counterattacked with two Air Slashes.

"Jolteon, dodge!"

Jolteon sprang to one side. It avoided one blade of air, but the other struck it.

Ethan raised an eyebrow. He had expected Noctowl to be smart, but seeing it in action was still impressive.

Another Pokemon might lose this opening in the time it took to hear its Trainer's command and act on it. Noctowl could recognize the chance and move on its own.

It could fight, it could lead other Pokemon, and, above all, it was Shiny. Ethan could hardly contain his envy.

He pushed the thought aside and called out, "Jolteon, let's get serious too! Use Agility!"

A faint glow surrounded Jolteon. Its movements seemed lighter, and its speed surged. It raced up another rock and leaped toward Noctowl from the higher ground.

"Thunder Fang!"

At Ethan's command, Jolteon opened its jaws, baring fangs that crackled with electricity, and lunged for Noctowl.

Agility made it terrifyingly fast. Noctowl began to dodge the moment Jolteon jumped, but Jolteon still caught its left wing in its teeth.

Crackle!

Electricity flashed. Noctowl cried out in pain and, enduring the shock, shook Jolteon loose.

The bite had also paralyzed it. Its wing would barely move, and its body wobbled in the air. It could scarcely keep flying.

"Darn it..."

Ash gritted his teeth, took out his Poke Ball, and recalled Noctowl himself.

"Rest in there for a while. I'll send you out again once the paralysis wears off," he murmured to the ball. Then he took his third Poke Ball from his belt and threw it onto the field. "It's your turn now! Go, Charizard!"

Blue light flashed, and Charizard appeared in the air. The crowd had barely made out its shape when it let out a fierce roar.

Charizard had not always acted this way. After spending so long among the wild Charizard of Charicific Valley, it now showed a wilder side when facing a major battle.

"Here it is! At last!" the announcer cried. "Ash's Charizard showed astonishing strength in the round of sixteen, helping him defeat Gary and winning over a great many fans. Facing tournament favorite Ethan today, can it put on another incredible performance?"

Charizard...

Ash was bringing it out against him already?

Ethan had thought Ash would save Charizard as his final trump card. Instead, Ash had lost patience and sent it out in the third round.

Still, Ethan had seen Charizard fight the day before yesterday. When Ash had not sent it back to Charicific Valley afterward, Ethan knew it would appear in today's match. That much had gone exactly as he expected.

He recalled Jolteon and took out his own third Poke Ball.

"Come out, Dragonite!"

Charizard was not a Dragon type, but it looked just as people imagined a dragon should. Once Ethan knew Ash would bring it, he had decided to arrange a clash between two dragonlike Pokemon.

It would draw plenty of attention, and the Pokemon League would surely welcome the spectacle.

Sure enough, the sight of the two dragonlike Pokemon flying above the field brought the audience to its feet. Cheers rolled through the stadium.

High above the rocks, Charizard and Dragonite locked eyes. Both seemed to burn with the desire to fight. The referee waved his flag, and before either Trainer gave an order, they charged at each other.

Charizard had struggled against the Charizard in Charicific Valley, but that was only by their standards. On a tournament field it was exceptionally strong, and Ethan had to be wary of its Seismic Toss in particular.

The two Pokemon tangled in the air. Charizard struck first with Dragon Tail, whipping its tail toward Dragonite. Dragonite answered with a Dragon Tail of its own.

Crack!

The tails collided with the sound of a snapping whip. The air itself seemed to shudder from the impact. Neither attack got through. They separated, spread their wings, and slammed into each other again.

"The same move, the same power!" the announcer shouted. "Incredible! It's as though these two can read each other's minds. They've opened with the very same tactics. Is it coincidence, or do they understand each other?"

That exchange lasted only a moment. Once their Trainers intervened, the two Pokemon began to show their different styles.

"Charizard, use Flamethrower!"

"Dragonite, Dragon Rage!"

Red and blue energy burst from their mouths and met in midair. A violent explosion hurled both Pokemon back toward their respective sides of the field, where they faced each other in a brief standoff.

This was easily the strongest opponent Ethan had faced since entering the Silver Conference.

Charizard's strength and experience were both first rate. With a Trainer as unpredictable as Ash directing it, even Ethan found the battle difficult.

Under their Trainers' commands, the fight swept from sky to ground, smashing so many boulders that the rock field nearly became a plain. Then the two rose into the air and grappled again.

The audience watched, stunned and delighted. At a glance, the battle looked evenly matched. Anyone who knew what to look for, though, could see a difference in the Pokemon's condition.

Charizard was covered in wounds, yet it remained spirited, growing fiercer as the fight went on. Dragonite was just as battered, but it panted heavily. Its strength was running out.

With Ash, Brock, Delia, Professor Oak, and everyone else who cared for Ash watching, Charizard came through in the end. One final Flamethrower knocked Dragonite out!

"It won!"

The announcer's roar set off the loudest cheers yet. From the sound of the crowd, anyone might have thought Ash had won the final and lifted the trophy.

"Unbelievable!" the announcer went on breathlessly, without waiting for the cheers to die down. "After that grueling battle, Charizard has won! And that means the legend of Ethan's unbeaten run, stretching from the Indigo League to this Silver Conference, has finally come to an end!"

Chapter 568: An Impressive Dig

Compared with Charizard, Dragonite had less battle experience and had evolved more recently. Overall, it was a little weaker. Losing the round was a shame, but Ethan could accept it.

He did not care much about his winning streak, either. Everyone lost sometime. His earlier opponents simply had not been strong enough to trouble him, allowing the streak to grow. Ash breaking it now did not mean much.

Ethan recalled the unconscious Dragonite and took Jolteon's Poke Ball from his belt.

The score stood at one to one. Although they were tied in knockouts, Ethan still held an advantage in the condition of their Pokemon.

Most of all, Charizard had spent so much strength defeating Dragonite that it could hardly manage another intense fight.

"Let's see which Pokemon Ethan will choose next... Oh! It's Jolteon again!" the announcer said. "That makes sense. It took little damage against Noctowl, and after that warm-up, it's in excellent shape!"

Seeing Jolteon, Ash wanted to recall Charizard and send out someone else. Charizard's stubborn spirit had been stirred, though, and it shook its head firmly at him. Ash could only let it stay in the battle.

Jolteon was plainly stronger than Dragonite, and Charizard was already badly worn down. They had barely begun to fight when Jolteon's Electroweb shocked Charizard unconscious before it could mount a counterattack.

Charizard had not shown the same heroic strength it had against Gary. Its run ended here, without defeating another of Ethan's Pokemon.

"What a shame..." The announcer shook his head. "Charizard did bring down Dragonite, but it used up so much energy doing it that Jolteon defeated it before it could show us anything more. I'm sure the audience would have loved to see more of its power in this arena. I certainly would!"

The announcer was right. Charizard's performance two days earlier had won it many fans. They had expected another display of strength today, perhaps one that would put Ash on the path to victory. Instead, it had struggled to beat one Pokemon and then fallen easily to Ethan's next choice.

If the crowd wanted to see Charizard fight again, they would have to hope Ash advanced to the next round.

After a moment's thought, Ash took out his third Poke Ball.

He threw it forward, and a round, sleepy-looking blue Pokemon appeared on the field, as large and soft-looking as a giant stuffed toy.

It was Ash's Snorlax.

Ethan narrowed his eyes.

Of the dozen or so Pokemon Ash could call on, Ethan considered three especially dangerous: Pikachu, Charizard, and this Snorlax.

Pikachu and Charizard were both famously strong, capable of astonishing upsets. Any opponent had to treat them with care. Snorlax looked dull and slow, but its strength was as enormous as its appetite.

Even among Snorlax, this one was unusual.

For one thing, it could swimand it used the butterfly stroke. It was also faster than most of its species.

A Pokemon with that kind of physical power called for another powerhouse.

Ethan recalled Jolteon. After considering his options, he took out his fourth Poke Ball.

"Go, Crystal Steelix!"

He had considered both Crystal Steelix and Tyranitar. But Tyranitar had not yet reached its full strength, and Ethan did not want another result like Dragonite's. Crystal Steelix was the steadier choice.

"Rooar!"

Crystal Steelix roared at Snorlax as soon as it appeared. Spectators seeing its huge, translucent body for the first time gasped in wonder.

"There it is! Ethan's Crystal Steelix!" the announcer exclaimed. "Ladies and gentlemen, we heard before the match that Ethan had an extraordinary Steelixone with a body as beautiful as crystal and tremendous destructive strength. It's quite unlike an ordinary Shiny Steelix. Seeing it in person is breathtaking!"

Some people had seen this remarkable Pokemon before, but only a few. Now it was on display before the whole city at a major tournament, causing a sensation.

It was far more striking than a typical Shiny Pokemon. Countless spectators learned that a Pokemon could have an extraordinary body like this as well as a different color.

The crowd's reaction did nothing to slow the battle.

As the referee waved his flag, Crystal Steelix slithered forward and charged Snorlax with the force of a heavy truck.

Snorlax still wore its placid, vacant expression. At the instant Steelix was about to hit, it raised both arms and braced them against the giant head.

Steelix's massive body already had momentum behind it. It kept driving forward, pushing Snorlax through several boulders and toward the boundary line.

"Snorlax, don't let it beat you!" Ash shouted.

The muscles in Snorlax's arms bulged visibly. It clenched its teeth and dug its feet in, straining until at last it stopped just short of the line. It had escaped being forced out of bounds.

Before Ash could relax, Crystal Steelix opened its jaws and snapped toward Snorlax.

Snorlax was broad and more than two meters tall, yet Steelix's open mouth seemed large enough to swallow nearly its whole body.

Now Snorlax showed its surprising agility. Before Steelix had fully opened its jaws, Snorlax rolled neatly to the side and escaped them.

That was close...

In the section reserved for friends and family, Brock wiped cold sweat from his brow. As a Trainer who specialized in Rock- and Ground-type Pokemon, he knew how formidable Ethan's Crystal Steelix was.

Had Snorlax reacted a moment later, it would have ended up entirely inside Steelix's mouth.

Snorlax moved alongside Steelix, gathered power in its right fist, and swung a mighty Mega Punch at it.

"Crystal Steelix, burrow underground!"

At Ethan's command, Steelix plunged headfirst into the earth. It avoided the punch and, with astonishing speed, bored a hole so deep its bottom could not be seen.

"What...?" Ash's eyes widened.

He had challenged the Orange League too, and he had fought its Supreme Gym Leader, Drake. He could tell at once that Ethan's Crystal Steelix could dig as fast as Drake's Onix. He remembered all the trouble that Onix's digging had caused him.

So Ethan had taught his Pokemon the same technique?

Ash had beaten Drake's Onix in the end and had some experience dealing with Dig. But Squirtle's Water-type attacks had won that fight. Snorlax had no way to force Crystal Steelix out of the ground, much less deal it any effective damage down there.

What should he do now?

Cold sweat gathered on Ash's forehead.

Should he switch to another Pokemon to face it?

Chapter 569: Ash at a Disadvantage

Before Ash could decide what to do, Crystal Steelix burst out of the ground beneath Snorlax and drove it into the air with its head.

Broken stone and hard-packed earth scattered. Snorlax's huge body tipped backward, and its usual vacant expression gave way to unmistakable alarm.

"Crystal Steelix, use Iron Tail!"

At Ethan's command, Crystal Steelix swung its pointed tail with tremendous force. Snorlax could not dodge while airborne. It could only watch the glittering tail sweep toward its belly.

"Quick, use Protect!" Ash shouted just in time.

Snorlax hurriedly raised both hands before its chest. A faint glow enveloped it an instant before Steelix's tail struck.

Crack!

Protect spared Snorlax any damage, but Steelix's strength still sent it flying to the center of the field. It smashed through a boulder before coming to a stop.

After all the rounds the two Trainers had fought, the rock field was a wreck. Almost no boulder remained whole. It was turning into a field of rubble.

Ash knew he could not keep fighting this way. As soon as Protect faded, he called, "Don't let it go underground again! Use Headbutt!"

Snorlax broke into a run toward Crystal Steelix. Its heavy steps shook the loose stones around it. Nearing Steelix, it accelerated again, lowered its head, and struck hard.

This time, Snorlax's strength prevailed.

Crystal Steelix swayed under the impact. But before Ash could celebrate, its tail coiled around Snorlax and held it fast.

"Break free, quick!"

Snorlax strained with all its strength against Steelix's Bind. Both were powerful Pokemon, but Steelix was several times its size. It had no intention of letting go.

Snorlax struggled for a long time without escaping. The more it fought, the tighter Steelix's coils became. Its face reddened, and it looked close to its limit. Ash took out its Poke Ball to recall it, but Steelix's body blocked the red beam. The light could not reach Snorlax.

"How can that be?"

Ash tried aiming from different angles, growing more anxious each time. He still could not recall it.

Trapped in the coils, Snorlax found it harder and harder to breathe. Its awareness faded. Only when it had lost consciousness did Crystal Steelix fling it off the field.

"Ethan wins this contest of strength!" the announcer declared. "With Snorlax's defeat, Ash has now lost three Pokemon. We'll take a five-minute break before the second half of the match!"

"Well done."

Ethan praised Crystal Steelix, recalled it, and returned to his rest area.

He sat down, drank some water, then leaned back with his eyes closed and waited for the break to pass.

Across the field, Ash returned to his own rest area looking dejected. Brock handed him water as soon as he sat down.

"Don't be discouraged. We prepared for this before the match, remember? We knew there was a good chance he'd beat you. If you show everything you can do, you'll already have done well!"

Even Misty could not bear to see Ash so downcast. "Haven't you always wanted to beat Ethan? Your Charizard took down his Dragonite. Come onthis is the closest you've come to that goal since you started traveling. Don't waste the chance!"

Their encouragement eased Ash's mood. He calmed his impatience, and when the five minutes were over, he walked back to the field with resolve in his eyes.

"After that short break, our Trainers are ready to continue!" the announcer said. "What kind of exciting battle will they show us next? Let's find out!"

Ethan and Ash took their places in the Trainer areas on opposite sides of the field.

Ash opened the second half by sending out his Shiny Noctowl again.

By holding back a new Pokemon, he seemed to want to keep one last surprise in reserve.

After a long rest, Noctowl had recovered enough to move despite its earlier paralysis. This time Ethan did not send Jolteon against it. He took out his fifth Poke Ball instead.

"Go, Blastoise!"

Ash was startled to hear Blastoise's name. He knew Ethan had not been keeping it with him and had never expected him to bring it to this match.

Ethan smiled at Ash's surprise.

Just as Ash had called on Squirtle, Ethan had brought Blastoise for the tournament as part of his team rotation. He had not chosen it to counter Ash. This simply happened to be its turn to fight.

In the friends and family section, Brock was troubled. He and Ash had spent all of yesterday studying the Pokemon Ethan currently had with him. Neither had imagined that Ethan would bring in Blastoise instead.

Ash might have been surprised, but he was not afraid of facing a different opponent.

When the battle began, Noctowl flew straight into the air. To Ash's astonishment, Ethan adopted the same tactic Gary had used: Blastoise fired a steady barrage of Water Guns from the cannons on its back, filling the air above the rock field with streams of water.

It was the same field, and once again Blastoise faced a Flying-type Pokemon. The difference was that Noctowl had no way to break through the barrage as Charizard had.

Noctowl was smaller and harder to hit than Charizard. Water-type attacks were not especially effective against it, either. Even so, its position was far from good.

Whoosh! Whoosh, whoosh!

Blue streams of water streaked through the air, skimming past Noctowl.

It dodged left and right as best it could. But it had already fought once and spent some of its strength, and Jolteon's attack had paralyzed it. The rest had helped, yet the aftereffects lingered. After only a few evasive moves, a stream struck it head-on and knocked it from the air.

"Noctowl!"

Ash cried out anxiously. To his relief, the one hit had not badly hurt it. But it was soaked through. It tried several times to take off and could not.

A bird that could not fly was in a sorry position on the ground.

Blastoise closed in, struck with Tackle, then followed with Bite and knocked Noctowl down.

"Noctowl is unable to battle! Blastoise wins!"

Ash's expression did not change when the referee gave the result. He quickly recalled Noctowl and immediately took out his fifth Poke Ball.

This time he sent out Bayleef. Unlike most gentle Bayleef, Ash's was known for refusing to give up. It would keep fighting even against a strong opponent, no matter how many wounds it suffered. It had a fierce spirit of its own.

It was a good choice.

Whether Ethan used Blastoise, Crystal Steelix, or Jolteon, each would be at some degree of type disadvantage against Bayleef.

But those were not Ethan's only Pokemon. Without hesitation, he settled on the last member of his team for this match.

He threw his final Poke Ball onto the field. Blue light flashed, and his Scizor appeared before Bayleef.

Chapter 570: Ash Is Eliminated

Bayleef was one of Johto's three starter Pokemon and a pure Grass type. Against Scizor's Bug and Steel types, it was at a severe disadvantage both attacking and defending.

Ash often fought well despite a type disadvantage, but against Ethan this time, he produced no miracle.

Razor Leaf and Magical Leaf barely troubled Scizor. Even when Bayleef landed Normal-type moves such as Tackle and Body Slam, they did only half their usual damage.

Scizor, meanwhile, pursued Bayleef without pause. Slightly faster and aided by its small wings, it swung its enormous pincers at Bayleef again and again.

Bayleef could neither overpower it nor shake it off.

With no other choice, Ash recalled Bayleef before Scizor could knock it out.

He had only one fresh Pokemon left. Ash glanced down at his feet, and his yellow Pikachu understood at once. It dropped to all fours and ran toward the center of the field.

"Oh?" The announcer sounded surprised. "At this crucial moment, Ash is sending in a Pikachu? Compared with Charizard and his other Pokemon, this little one looks perfectly ordinary. Why save it for last? Is there something special about it?"

That was only how outsiders saw Pikachu.

Anyone who knew Ash knew Pikachu was the partner he trusted mostand his strongest.

Its performances were wildly unpredictable, though. Pikachu could stand up to a Legendary Pokemon one day and lose to a rookie's starter the next. Not even Ash could be sure which Pikachu would show up today.

Pikachu reached the middle of the field and called brightly to Ethan. Confidence shone on its face.

It looked just like Ash when he was feeling sure of himself. Perhaps Pokemon really did take after the humans they spent so much time with.

Ethan stroked his chin as he watched it.

Knowing Pikachu as he did, he hesitated to send out a Pokemon with an obvious type advantage against it. That might be exactly what triggered one of Ash's improbable comebacks. The safer choice was to let Scizor continue and see how Pikachu fought.

"Scizor, I'm counting on you for this round. Be careful!"

Despite its Bug and Steel types, Scizor was not especially vulnerable to Electric attacks. Its Steel-type moves would be less effective against Pikachu, but otherwise the matchup posed little problem.

Scizor nodded to Ethan, walked up to Pikachu, and looked down at it.

Pikachu refused to be intimidated. It planted all four paws, raised its tail high, and readied itself for battle.

"Ash is on the brink now!" the announcer called. "If Pikachu falls, all he'll have left is an injured Bayleef. But he's chosen to put his faith in Pikachu, so let's cheer it on and see what it can do!"

At the start signal, both Pokemon rushed forward almost together.

Scizor reached out with one huge pincer. Pikachu nimbly jumped onto its arm, twisted, and swung its tail toward Scizor's face.

Most fighters avoided going for the face. Pikachu had tried it at the very first opportunity.

Scizor calmly brought up its other pincer to shield its head. Thunk! Pikachu's Iron Tail struck the steel claw with a dull metallic clang.

The move caught the announcer's attention. "Oh! This Pikachu is different from others of its kind. It's quick on its feet and surprisingly strong. There really is more to it than meets the eye!"

They separated after that first exchange.

"Pikachu, use Thunder Shock!"

"Scizor, use Double Team!" Ethan ordered.

As Pikachu began its attack, Scizor produced five copies of itself. Six identical Scizor now stood before Pikachu, leaving it no way to tell which one was real.

Pikachu looked from one to another, then chose the Scizor standing where the original had been before Double Team. Golden electricity shot from its body toward that figure. It had guessed wrong. The current passed through an illusion and struck a rock behind it.

At the same time, the other Scizor images rushed Pikachu. Every one raised its right pincer and swung down.

"Pikachu, dodge!"

Pikachu glanced frantically between them, trying to pick out the real Scizor. It found out only when a steel pincer struck it and sent it tumbling aside.

Pikachu fell toward the shattered rocks. The moment it landed, it sprang up, raised its tail, and formed a large ball of electricity at the tip. It hurled the Electro Ball at Scizor.

From the Trainer's area, Ethan could see that Pikachu's gaze was steady and its attention fixed. It was giving this battle everything it had.

The Electro Ball still missed. Scizor used Agility as Pikachu released it and escaped the attack's path. Pikachu's counterattack struck nothing.

That exchange set the pattern for the rest of the fight. Both Pokemon battled fiercely, trading blows until they were covered in wounds and gasping for breath.

Against a weak opponent, Pikachu seemed to grow weak too. Against a strong one, it rose to match that strength.

At the height of the struggle, both Pokemon used Quick Attack and charged straight at each other. They crossed in a blurand a moment later, both collapsed.

The referee stepped forward. After confirming that neither could battle, he crossed his flags before his chest.

"Scizor and Pikachu are both unable to battle! This round is a draw!"

The crowd erupted in cheers. Both Pokemon had fought brilliantly, giving the spectators everything they could have hoped to see.

The simultaneous knockout surprised them even more, leaving the match poised on a knife's edge.

The announcer praised Pikachu too. "Incredible! Ash's Pikachu was far more formidable than it looked. It brought down Ethan's Scizor! Even though the round ended in a draw, that performance deserves our admiration!"

And yet...

Many spectators felt a pang when they remembered that Ash had only one Pokemon left, and Bayleef was already hurt.

Ash's unpredictable, varied style had won him many fans during the tournament. They believed he had the strength to reach at least the semifinals. Now that elimination by Ethan seemed inevitable, they could not help feeling sorry for him.

Against someone else, perhaps he might have gone further.

Ash walked onto the field and picked up Pikachu, which could barely move.

"Pika..."

Pikachu managed to open its eyes and weakly call to him.

"I know." Ash smiled gently. "You brought down Ethan's Scizor. You did great. Rest now."

He meant it. Ash had ended Ethan's unbeaten run and knocked out two of his Pokemon, an achievement beyond most Trainers. Even if he was eliminated, he could be proud of that.

Ash carried Pikachu to the friends and family section and entrusted it to Misty. Then he returned to his position, turned his cap backward, and took out Bayleef's Poke Ball with a determined look.

He knew as well as anyone that his injured Bayleef could not realistically defeat Ethan's four remaining Pokemon.

But Ash was not the kind of Trainer to surrender. As long as one of his Pokemon could still fight, he would fight beside it to the end.

"Go, Bayleef!"

He threw the Poke Ball across the field. Blue light flashed, and Bayleef appeared again. Ethan gave Ash an approving smile, then slowly took out a Poke Ball of his own.

"Unless something unexpected happens, this should be our last round in this tournament," Ethan said. His voice was encouraging. "You've grown so much, and you've given me an exciting battle. To thank you, I'm going to fight you with everything I have."

Ethan threw the ball. When Ash saw what emerged, he could only shake his head and laugh.

Gardevoir. Of course Ethan had chosen Gardevoir.

Even now, he was bringing out a Pokemon like that. He was giving Ash no mercy at all!

...

"Congratulations to Ethan! He has defeated Ash and advanced to the semifinals!"

As the announcer called the result, Ethan recalled Gardevoir. He walked forward through the audience's cheers and shook Ash's hand.

"Ethan, you're amazing. I lost to you again."

Ash was not dispirited as some might have expected. He scratched his cheek and smiled sheepishly.

"You were amazing too," Ethan said with a smile. "You beat my Dragonite and Scizor, didn't you? Keep going. I'm sure you'll be even stronger by the time you reach the next region."

Ethan had mentioned in an earlier conversation that he planned to travel through Hoenn after the Silver Conference. Ash had been eager to go as well and had already made plans. He looked forward to meeting Ethan there.

"I will!" Ash clenched his fist. "I'll get stronger, and then I'll challenge you again!"

Ethan left through the competitors' tunnel and returned to the lounge, where Erika greeted him with a radiant smile.

"Congratulations! You've made the semifinals!"

Now that they were alone, Ethan no longer hid his happiness. He drew her into his arms and celebrated with a long, passionate kiss.

He felt a little bad for Ash, but he had won, and he was happy about it.

There were two matches today. Ethan's battle with Ash had been the first. Jimmy and Harrison would meet in the afternoon.

The winner would face Ethan the day after tomorrow.

They left the stadium for the Pokemon Center on the ground floor of the dormitory building. Ethan handed his injured Pokemon to Nurse Joy, and then he and Erika ate lunch at the restaurant.

Ash's group soon came into the lobby with Delia and Professor Oak.

With Ash eliminated, Delia had no reason to stay. She had wanted to take him back to Pallet Town, but Ash refused.

Having come all this way, Ash wanted to remain until the tournament ended. He especially wanted to see Ethan win the championship. Unable to persuade him, Delia packed her bags and returned to Kanto with Professor Oak.

After seeing them off, the others gathered together. By one in the afternoon, both Ethan's and Ash's Pokemon had been treated and regained their strength. Jimmy and Harrison's match began just then.

"Who do you think will win?" Misty asked, watching the screen.

Only then did Ethan learn that Ash, Misty, and Brock had visited Ho-Oh Temple before entering Silver Town. They had met Harrison there and had become friends of a sort.

Harrison was a Trainer from Hoenn. Like Ethan, he had come to Johto specifically to challenge the Silver Conference.

"Probably Harrison." Ethan leaned back on the soft sofa. He had never met Harrison, but he gave his judgment anyway. "Jimmy's still a little young. Harrison has a steadier style, and his Pokemon are stronger overall."

The others nodded. They could see Jimmy was still somewhat inexperienced and would likely have trouble beating Harrison.

They ate dessert while watching the match. Just as they had expected, Jimmy fell behind early.

Compared with his match against Marina, Jimmy began this one in top form.

Even so, while the exchanges looked close, his Pokemon could not match Harrison's across the board. When Jimmy finally sent out his ace, Typhlosion, it faced Harrison's Blaziken. Jimmy had never seen this Hoenn Pokemon before and was plainly at a loss.

Chapter 571: A Pokemon from Hoenn

Jimmy was not the only one surprised by Blaziken. Ash, Misty, Brock, and Erika had never seen a Pokemon like it either.

"What kind of Pokemon is that?" Misty asked.

When Ethan had visited Ho-Oh Temple, he had dealt with the Sneasel causing trouble there. Ash and his friends had still met Harrison at the temple, but without that incident or an interruption by Team Rocket, there had been no reason for Harrison to show them his Blaziken.

He had kept it hidden through the preliminaries and the round of sixteen as well. His matches had gone smoothly enough that he had not needed it until now.

Its first appearance caused a stir among people who knew little about the Pokemon of other regions. They stared and exclaimed at the unfamiliar sight.

Ash took out his Pokedex and pointed it at the upright, striking Pokemon on the screen. It gave him only one answer: "Sorry. No data available."

"No data?"

Ethan sighed at their reactions. "You can stop scanning. That's Blaziken. Its main habitat is Hoenn, the region we're going to visit next. Like my Gardevoir, it isn't found on the Kanto or Johto mainland. It's from a later 'version,' you could say."

"Blaziken?" Erika ignored his remark about versions. She studied the vivid red on its body. "Then it's a Fire-type Pokemon?"

"Fire and Fighting. Like Charizard and Typhlosion, it's the fully evolved Fire-type starter of its regionHoenn's, in this case."

"A starter from Hoenn..." Ash murmured. His eyes grew brighter. He longed to set out at once and begin a new adventure there.

On the field, Jimmy had never seen Blaziken before, but its coloring told him it was probably a Fire type.

When two Fire-type Pokemon faced each other, their Fire attacks would do less damage. The contest would come down to their other strengths.

Jimmy had not realized Blaziken was also a Fighting type.

That mistake let Blaziken get close. It seized the chance, unleashed a series of Fighting-type attacks, and knocked out Typhlosion.

Typhlosion was Jimmy's ace. Losing it in its first exchange all but settled the match.

Harrison went on to defeat Jimmy's remaining Pokemon without much trouble. Only a strong showing by Jimmy's Beedrill saved him some pride. Without it, Harrison might have swept the match six to zero.

There was a gap between their abilities, but it should not have been this wide. The unfamiliar Pokemon and Typhlosion's defeat had shaken Jimmy's confidence so badly that he failed to bring out his team's true strength.

"What a shame," Ethan said after watching the whole match. He shook his head. "Against Marina and now against Harrison, Jimmy never got his mind settled. He worked too hard during his travels to let that hold him back."

Erika sighed too. "It's hard to avoid. Most people would be affected by something like that."

"True. Jimmy was unlucky to meet this opponent."

Ethan turned and stared directly at Ash. Ash looked back, baffled.

"Why are you looking at me, Ethan?" Ash glanced down at his clothes. They were not dirty.

"No reason." Ethan smiled. "I was just thinking that only someone as oblivious to feelings as you could keep his head clear no matter what a girlor anything elsedid."

The others understood his implication and laughed softly. Ash, looking perfectly serious, said, "Of course! Whoever my opponent is, I'll give the battle everything I've got!"

That made Misty and the others laugh even harder.

After the match that afternoon, Ethan's group found Jimmy in the ground-floor lobby. He looked dejected. Marina stood beside him, speaking quietly and trying to comfort him.

"Ethan..." Jimmy gave them an awkward smile. "Well, I lost."

Ethan did not know what to say, so he patted Jimmy's shoulder.

Jimmy knew Ethan would face Harrison next. "Please be careful," he said. "Harrison is strongespecially his Blaziken. Watch out for it!"

Only after the battle had Jimmy learned the Fire Pokemon's name. By then it was too late. What good could that knowledge do him now?

"Thank you for the warning. I will."

Ethan shook Jimmy's hand and watched him and Marina enter the elevator.

Like Vincent before them, the two childhood friends from New Bark Town would probably leave this place with regrets.

What a cruel tournament...

The night passed quietly.

The following day's two matches belonged to the other half of the bracket. By the end of them, Ethan had seen that Jon Dickson really was strong. He defeated his opponent by a wide margin.

The afternoon match, by contrast, was unremarkable.

Even the winner was not especially formidable. Their battle drew the lowest ratings of the quarterfinals.

If Ethan beat Harrison, it seemed his opponent from the other half would indeed be Jon Dickson.

The Pokemon League noticed the same possibility. Its promotions began playing up Ethan and Jon Dickson, building anticipation for a meeting between two strong competitors.

Interest in the Silver Conference rose again as the semifinals approached.

During the break, Ethan filmed a promotional video. Alexa also pulled him aside for another exclusive interview, leaving him busy from morning to night.

He was surprised she had stayed in Silver Town so long. Even now she was still working outside the stadium.

By the time everything was finished, Ethan returned to the dormitory somewhat tired. At last he had a chance to rest and prepare for tomorrow's match.

The building felt deserted compared with the first days of the tournament.

Apart from staff and the rush at mealtimes, he hardly saw any competitors. The Silver Conference was nearing its end.

...

Boom! Boom!

Fireworks burst one after another above Silver Town, stirring the crowd's excitement.
