After breakfast, Ethan and Erika entered the waiting room at Silver Stadium. Even through the walls, he could faintly hear the announcer.

He leaned back in a chair and rested with his eyes closed. Before long, an announcement summoned him to the field. He opened his eyes and stood.

"Good luck," Erika said.

She came over and straightened his collar. Ethan drew her into his arms and kissed her lightly.

"Don't worry. Wait here for the news that I've won!"

They smiled at each other. Ethan said goodbye, left the waiting room, and walked through the competitors' tunnel. To the cheers of the crowd, he reached his position opposite Harrison.

It was the first time Ethan had studied Harrison properly. They had seen each other in the dormitory lobby before, but had never spoken.

Harrison looked three or four years older than Ethan. Perhaps from traveling so long, his skin was a little tanned. He was tall and broad, with short brown hair and an ordinary face made cheerful by a bright smile.

As strangers, they exchanged friendly nods but no words. Then both turned to the referee.

"We'll now draw the battlefield and decide who sends out a Pokemon first!" the referee announced.

The wheel on the big screen began to spin. Ethan and Harrison watched its pointer closely. When it finally slowed, it came to rest on the Ice Field.

The Ice Field?

It was a decent field. The thick ice would not trouble the Pokemon, but standing beside it for a whole match could give an underdressed Trainer a cold.

Next came the draw for who would send out first.

For once, Ethan escaped his run of bad luck. Harrison drew the first move.

Harrison shook his head in disappointment. He had studied Ethan for a long time and knew how strong he was. Facing him would be difficult enough; having to reveal his first Pokemon made it worse.

Those were the rules. Harrison gathered himself and took out his first Poke Ball.

The arena transformed. The open ground in front of them parted, and a field covered in thick ice rose into place.

Before Ethan could adjust to the expanse of white, cold air slipped inside his clothes. He shivered.

"Both competitors are ready, and the field is set!" the announcer cried. "The long-awaited Silver Conference semifinals are finally beginning! Let's cheer for our favorite Trainers!"

Harrison could not match Ethan's popularity, but Ethan's supporters applauded him too.

Harrison hurled his Poke Ball forward. "Go, Kecleon!"

Another Pokemon from Hoenn.

An ordinary Johto Trainer might have been as bewildered as Jimmy when faced with an unfamiliar species. Harrison's opponent was Ethan, though. He had never set foot in Hoenn in this world, but back on Earth he had cleared the Hoenn games and their Ever Grande Conference countless times. He knew its Pokemon well.

The Kecleon before him stood only about a meter tall. Its grass-green body might make it look like a Grass type, but it was actually a Normal type.

It resembled a chameleon from Earth. Kecleon could change its body's color to blend into its surroundings and approach prey unseen. It had one limitation: the pattern across its belly never vanished, so its camouflage was never complete.

Others might not know how to deal with it. Ethan needed only a moment to settle on a plan.

He took a Poke Ball from his belt and sent out his first Pokemon. Blue light flashed, and Tyranitar appeared on the ice.

"Rooar!"

Like his red Gyarados, Tyranitar liked to roar on entering a battle, spreading its intimidating presence. Its tall, armored body was enough to make Harrison's Kecleon take a frightened step back.

Harrison frowned. Starting a battle afraid was a bad sign.

Tyranitar looked down at its much smaller opponent. A cruel smile crossed its face, and contempt flashed in its dark eyes.

Seeing that it was taking Kecleon lightly, Ethan warned it. "Don't underestimate this one. It can turn invisible. Be carefuland watch its long tongue. That's its main way of attacking."

Tyranitar did not think much of the warning. Harrison, on the other side of the field, looked alarmed.

How did Ethan know Kecleon's traits? Had he been to Hoenn and seen one before?

That was bad news. Harrison had never used Kecleon in an earlier round, just as he had held Blaziken back. He had meant to surprise a strong opponent with it.

Instead, Ethan seemed to see through it the moment it appeared.

This would be troublesome. Harrison knew he had to give the battle everything he had.

As the match began, he gave the first command. "Kecleon, disappear!"

Before the crowd's eyes, Kecleon's body began to fade. Within a second or two, its color blended with the white ice beneath it, and it vanished from sight.

Spectators gasped and stared. Even the announcer cried out in astonishment. Most of them were used to Johto Pokemon; seeing such a strange ability for the first time showed them how varied Pokemon could be.

Ethan remained still. He narrowed his eyes and studied the place where Kecleon had disappeared. Sure enough, he could make out a red pattern shaped like a wave.

The mark was faint, but it stood out against the white ice. It was the one part of Kecleon that could not disappear.

Chapter 572: Gengar Wants a Turn Too

"Tyranitar, see that red pattern? Aim there and use Dark Pulse!"

At Ethan's command, Tyranitar opened its mouth. A wave of black energy formed there and shot toward the place where Kecleon had vanished.

The attack startled Harrison all over again.

Now Ethan even knew the flaw in Kecleon's camouflage. Harrison felt certain Ethan must have been to Hoenn. How else could he understand Kecleon so well?

"Kecleon, move!"

Harrison had barely spoken when the invisible Kecleon darted aside. His training deserved credit. Kecleon was not the slowest of Pokemon, but it was hardly known for speed.

Harrison's Kecleon, however, moved with astonishing quickness. In a flash, it escaped the path of Tyranitar's attack.

Boom!

Dark Pulse struck the thick ice and blasted out a deep crater. Shattered pieces sprayed in every direction.

Kecleon reappeared on the other side, unharmed.

He could fight this!

Harrison let out a long breath, and some of his tension eased.

Ethan had frightened him into a moment of panic. Thinking clearly now, Harrison realized that seeing through Kecleon's camouflage did not decide the battle. Kecleon could still use its speed to keep Tyranitar at a distance.

"Kecleon, look for an opening!"

Kecleon began circling Tyranitar. It moved so fast, and its body blended in so well, that it was almost impossible to follow with the naked eye.

Even its visible belly pattern became a blur at that speed, making up for the weakness in its camouflage.

It ran around Tyranitar more than a dozen times. Tyranitar turned to follow, but it could not keep up. By the time it spotted Kecleon, the smaller Pokemon was gone again.

Without a target, Tyranitar could not attack.

Kecleon suddenly stopped and lashed out with its long tongue. Harrison was certain Tyranitar had not noticed in time.

The supple tongue stretched several meters. Its tip struck like a fist, carrying surprising force, and hit Tyranitar in an instant.

Harrison frowned. With a dull smack, the tongue bounced off Tyranitar's armored body.

Was its armor that hard?

At least Kecleon slipped away again before Tyranitar could retaliate, giving its opponent no opening.

Speed was testing itself against defense.

In his Trainer's area, Ethan considered how to defeat such an opponent. He glanced across the smooth ice and suddenly had an idea.

"Tyranitar, use Earthquake!"

Tyranitar raised its right foot and stamped down. Cracks raced outward from beneath it in every direction.

The sharp, alarming sound of breaking ice filled the stadium. Deep fissures opened across the once-solid field, leaving the surface uneven. One move had permanently changed the terrain.

Kecleon lost its footing. Its small body rocked with the tremor. As it recovered, another Dark Pulse came straight toward it.

"Dodge!"

Kecleon jumped aside and narrowly escaped.

It tried to run again, but the broken surface slowed it badly. Cracks and raised slabs of ice stopped it from moving as freely as before.

This was bad.

Harrison saw the danger too. "Use Psybeam!"

He seemed to want Kecleon to attack from a distance and perhaps confuse Tyranitar. But preparing Psybeam forced Kecleon to stop, giving Tyranitar an opening.

Just as Kecleon fired, several pointed rocks broke through the ice and thrust toward it.

The moves met in the middle of the field. Psybeam struck the stones and never reached Tyranitar. Kecleon, meanwhile, was hit and launched high into the air.

The blow broke its camouflage. As Kecleon fell, a huge shadow covered it.

It looked up to find Tyranitar towering over it with a cold stare.

"Got you." Ethan smiled. "Finish it with Hyper Beam!"

Tyranitar opened its mouth. A fierce column of energy formed inside.

"Get out of there!" Harrison shouted.

Kecleon struggled to its feet and tried to run. Hyper Beam erupted before it could take a step, engulfing it completely.

Boom!

The glare faded. At the center of the field, Hyper Beam had melted a great hole in the ice. Kecleon lay motionless beside it.

The referee raised his flag. "Kecleon is unable to battle! Tyranitar wins the first round!"

"Yes!" Misty waved a flag and cheered from the stands. She was much more openly enthusiastic than she had been during Ethan's match against Ash.

Both competitors had been her friends then, and cheering for one would have felt unfair to the other. Harrison was another matter. She hardly knew him.

Harrison recalled Kecleon and took out his second Poke Ball with a grave expression.

He threw it, and the crowd saw a black Pokemon resembling a lean hound. Two large curved horns rose from its head, and its long tail had a devilish shape. It was Houndoom, a Dark- and Fire-type Pokemon familiar to Johto audiences.

They were disappointed and relieved at the same time. Houndoom brought less novelty, but seeing too many Pokemon from elsewhere made this feel less like the Silver Conference.

Ethan had faced Houndoom many times before. He knew the species well.

He recalled Tyranitar and sent Jolteon back out.

If Harrison chose a canine Pokemon, Ethan would answer with one of his own.

Jolteon did not look like an ordinary dog, but its appearance called to mind a sheepdog, a fennec fox, or a coyote. It belonged among the canines in Ethan's eyes.

As the round began, both Pokemon raced across the field.

Houndoom was slower than Jolteon, but it was still quick compared with most Pokemon. The shattered ice made the terrain difficult, yet neither agile fighter was troubled by it.

They skipped over protruding chunks and deep fissures without slowing.

For some reason, Jolteon fought on the move. It avoided meeting Houndoom head-on, attacking as it retreated and darting back and forth across the field.

Harrison did not understand the tactic, but he ordered Houndoom to chase it.

Flames swept through the arena as they fought. Heat and energy raised the temperature of the Ice Field. Some broken pieces began to melt.

Harrison noticed nothing at first. Then Houndoom stepped through a puddle, and the splash made him realize why Ethan had chosen Jolteon.

Oh no!

Before he could give another order, Ethan shouted, "Now! Use Discharge!"

Jolteon's stiff fur stood out. Brilliant electricity burst from its body and traveled across the wet ice toward Houndoom.

Ordinarily, Houndoom could have dodged an attack like that. Water now carried the current along a faster, less predictable path, leaving it no chance to avoid the shock.

Crackle!

Electricity raced through Houndoom. It endured until the shock subsided, then coughed out a puff of black smoke. Before it could recover, Jolteon was already in front of it, raising both forelegs.

Double Kick!

Thump! Thump!

Both kicks struck Houndoom's head. It fell and did not rise again.

Another victory for Ethan.

In the stands, Misty turned to Brock, puzzled. "Why does Ethan's match against Harrison seem easier than his match against Ash? He's making it look effortless..."

"I wouldn't say that," Brock replied. "Harrison's real ace, Blaziken, hasn't appeared yet. Maybe we haven't seen everything he can do."

"Hey, you two!" Ash lifted his head proudly between them. "Don't you know how strong Ethan is? Just think about the Indigo League. Not even the finalists managed to knock out one of his Pokemon! This is normal for him. Heh, only my Charizard and Pikachu really gave him trouble!"

"You..." Misty rolled her eyes, amused. "Are you getting a big head just because you beat two of Ethan's Pokemon? You're easy to satisfy."

The match had reached the third round of the first half. Harrison still did not send out Blaziken. Instead, he chose Miltank.

Many people wondered why he would hold back his ace while falling behind. Ethan understood as soon as he saw the choice: Harrison was saving his gamble for the second half. He wanted to face Ethan with everything he had after the break.

Knowing Harrison's plan did not make Ethan dismiss Miltank. He gave it proper respect and sent Crystal Steelix onto the field.

Crystal Steelix's appearance drew a surge of cheers. Beautiful and imposing, it had won over many spectators just as Ash's Charizard hadperhaps even more.

Harrison's Miltank was a nimble, sturdy close-range fighter. It battled differently from Whitney's Miltank at the Goldenrod Gym.

Both knew Rollout, but Harrison's did not rely on it. It closed with Crystal Steelix again and again, meeting the giant Pokemon head-on with Tackle, Stomp, Zen Headbutt, and Body Slam.

Miltank attacked fiercely, but it never broke through Crystal Steelix's defenses. Steelix caught it in a Bind, bit it, and finally drove it into a large block of ice with Double-Edge. Miltank lost consciousness.

Ethan had won all three rounds of the first half with three different Pokemon.

At halftime, Harrison sat in his chair looking grave. Nervous sweat ran down his forehead.

He had reached the semifinals. One more win would take him to the final. No one wanted to be eliminated now.

But...

He looked across at Ethan. Ethan sat with his eyes closed, resting calmly. Harrison found that composure almost as daunting as Ethan's team.

His opponent was too strong. It felt as though they were not even on the same level.

How had Ash managed to knock out two of Ethan's Pokemon in the previous match?

In the other rest area, Ethan waited for halftime to end.

The first half had not been difficult for him. Of Harrison's Pokemon, the one he truly needed to watch was Blaziken.

Then the shadow at his feet trembled. Gengar floated out of it and came to his side.

"Let me fight in the next half too!"

Ethan opened his eyes in surprise. "You?"

"Yes!" Gengar nodded. "I've watched the others battle for days. To be honest, I can't sit still anymore!"

Ethan shook his head with a wry smile. "I could let you, but wouldn't that be a little cruel to Harrison?"

Gengar laughed and thumped its chest. "Just pick the weakest one for me. I only want to stretch my muscles. Don't worryI'll go easy on it!"

Ash and the others had been watching Ethan from the stands.

His halftime rest had seemed perfectly ordinaryuntil Gengar rose from his shadow and began whispering beside him. Then they sensed something was amiss.

Chapter 573: Gengar's Game

Misty stared at Ethan's rest area. "Waitis his Gengar going to battle?"

"It can't be..." Ash's mouth fell open. "How is Harrison supposed to fight if Gengar joins in?"

As Ash had said before, knowing Ethan's team made him fear Gengar more than any of the others.

Brock rubbed his chin and sighed. "It looks like Gengar will fight. What worries me is that Harrison barely knows Ethan, much less how frightening that Gengar is. How will he face it?"

The three fell silent and looked toward Harrison with helpless sympathy.

Harrison knew nothing of their concern. When the break ended, he slapped his cheeks to steady himself and walked resolutely back to the field.

Whatever happened next, he had to win!

Then he saw Gengar beside Ethan and stopped short.

What was this Gengar doing here? Harrison had watched every one of Ethan's tournament matches and had never seen it battle.

Was it another hidden ace? And why did the look it gave him seem almost malicious?

More urgently, Harrison had planned to send out Hypno in the fourth round. With a Gengar there to counter his Psychic-type Pokemon, he abandoned the idea.

The referee called for his choice before he could work out another strategy. Harrison decided quickly and took out his fourth Poke Ball.

"Go, Swellow!"

He tossed the ball high. Blue light flashed, and a large bird Pokemon soared into the sky.

The announcer took a moment to identify it. "Oh! Another Pokemon from Hoenn! Harrison has brought us another surprise!"

Given a choice, Harrison would have preferred not to rely on Pokemon caught in Hoenn.

He had come to Johto to catch new Pokemon and challenge the Silver Conference. What was the point of doing that if he fought only with his old Hoenn team?

But Ethan was too strong. Harrison had to use everything he had if he wanted a chance to beat him.

Ethan looked up at the bird.

Swellow, the evolved form of Taillow, resembled a swallow. Most of its plumage was dark blue, with red markings on its forehead, neck, and the tips of its tail feathers. It was said to roam in search of warm lands, wheeling gracefully high above the ground. When it spotted prey, it dived and caught it in sharp claws.

As with Kecleon, Ethan knew this species well.

He had played many modified versions of the games. Apart from Kanto's Pokemon, those of Hoenn were the generation he knew best. Ash would also catch a Swellow when he traveled through Hoenn in the animated series Ethan remembered. Many viewers would recognize it.

It was a shame Ethan had no bird Pokemon. He would have liked to stage a battle between two of them.

His other Pokemon had all fought recently and needed no special training.

There was nothing for it. Gengar could take this round.

Ethan turned to it and tipped his chin toward the field. "This one's yours."

"Heh, heh, heh..." Gengar grinned and floated forward. "Leave it to me. I finally get to have some fun!"

Once it reached the center, Gengar did not speak again in front of the crowd. That would have caused an uproar. It simply crooked a finger at Swellow, wearing a mocking half smile. The challenge was plain enough to make Swellow furious.

Its proud nature had been there since it was a Taillow. After evolving, Swellow was even less willing to let another Pokemon challenge it.

Harrison chose an aggressive opening.

At his command, Swellow used Focus Energy, sharpening its concentration so its next attacks would be more likely to strike a vital point. Then it used Aerial Ace, streaking over Gengar's head before turning sharply and diving at it.

Ethan stood in his Trainer's area with his hands in his pockets. He said nothing.

He had left the entire round to Gengar.

Just as Swellow reached it, Gengar changed shape. Its body became a bird-catching net, and Swellow flew straight into it.

"What?!"

Harrison's face changed. The announcer and spectators were just as astonished.

"Incredible!" the announcer shouted. "How did it do that? It changed the shape of its body! Did it use Hypnosis on all of us?"

Ash and his friends knew better. They had seen how powerful this Gengar was.

Back at Maiden's Peak, when it was still a Gastly, it had already shown remarkable transformations. It could become people, Pokemon, or even inanimate objects. It could speak human language too, unlike any other Gastly they had met.

Harrison recovered from his first shock. "Swellow, get out of there!"

Swellow struggled inside the net, trying to tear it open. But the net was Gengar's own body. It had no intention of letting Swellow break through.

Gengar was only teasing it. After letting it struggle for a while, Gengar laughed, returned to its usual shape, and released it.

Swellow hurried into the sky and stared down at Gengar, still shaken.

Its instincts told it Gengar was immensely strongand had a nasty streak.

Harrison rubbed his temples. He wanted to tell himself he had imagined what had happened. He could not.

He forced himself to settle down and called up to Swellow. "Don't be afraid. Attack from a distance this time. Use Air Slash!"

Swellow beat its wings and sent two crescent blades of compressed air toward Gengar.

Gengar grinned and sank into its own shadow. The blades cut through the place where it had stood and struck nothing.

"It... disappeared!"

The announcer searched the field with wide eyes. Unlike Harrison's Kecleon, Gengar truly seemed to have vanished. Could it turn invisible too?

"Where did it go?" Harrison asked. The spectators might be excited by the spectacle, but he was frightened.

He had faced Pokemon stronger than his own before without feeling this way. Gengar's unknown abilities left him with no confidence at all.

Fear came from what he did not understand.

Swellow searched from above with its sharp eyes. It could not find Gengar either.

Then it heard a sound behind it. Before it could turn, Harrison shouted, "Behind you!"

Swellow twisted around. A giant flyswatter came down on it. The heavy blow darkened its vision and sent it plunging into the ice.

It shook its head. The dizziness had barely begun to pass when it looked up and saw Gengar in its normal form floating overhead.

Now Swellow understood. That wretched Gengar was not trying to fight properly. It was playing with it.

Swellow screeched and took off. Its pride fed its anger until it could no longer think clearly.

Blue flames seemed to flare around it. Its power rose, its wings folded, and it hurled itself at Gengar.

"Brave Bird!" the announcer cried. "After Gengar's tricks, Swellow has lost patience. It wants to settle this head-on!"

Swellow was one of the Pokemon Harrison had saved for the second half. It was strong enough to know an advanced move like Brave Bird.

Even so, it would not be easy to hurt Gengar.

Gengar faced the charge without concern. Rings of light appeared in its eyes and traveled toward Swellow. Too angry even to consider dodging, Swellow flew straight through them.

"Swellow..."

Harrison recognized the rings. Gengar was using Hypnosis, a move many Pokemon knew.

He watched anxiously. He wanted to recall his enraged Swellow but hesitated.

Swellow had used Brave Bird without his command. It was not quite as powerful as the similarly named Sky Attack, but it was still formidable. If it hit Gengar, it might knock it out at once.

Hypnosis did not always land. At Swellow's speed, and in its anger, perhaps it could push through the attack.

But Brave Bird would also hurt Swellow through recoil. Harrison hated the thought of that, and if Gengar dodged, the round was almost certainly lost.

While he wavered, Gengar watched Swellow close in and gave a cold smile.

Did it think it could break through his Hypnosis like this?

It was underestimating him.

Gengar opened its eyes wide. The rings that had been flowing slowly from them suddenly came faster, and their color deepened to purple-black.

Swellow's gaze wavered for an instant.

That instant was enough for Hypnosis to take hold. Its thoughts seemed to freeze. Sleepiness dragged at it, and its target grew hazy.

At its tremendous speed, the remaining distance disappeared in a heartbeat. Swellow dipped downward as it lost focus. It fought to open its eyes, only to find it was no longer heading toward Gengar. It was diving at the ground.

It was too late to correct course. Hypnosis took its consciousness, and a hundredth of a second later Swellow slammed into the ice.

Boom!

The impact shattered the ice and exposed the frozen earth below. Apart from a spray of snowflakes that landed before Gengar, the crash did not touch it.

"Swellow!" Harrison cried. Everything had happened too quickly for him to react. He should have recalled it when he had the chance.

Regret would not help now. Even if he had withdrawn Swellow, he did not know which of his Pokemon could face this strange Gengar.

"That was an... unusual battle," the announcer said, stumbling over the word. "Ethan's Gengar has defeated Swellow in a most surprising way. As with his Crystal Steelix, Ethan has shown us something none of us expected!"

Gengar floated back to Ethan wearing an enormous grin.

"Not bad," it said before Ethan could speak. "It wasn't enough to stretch my muscles, but I had fun."

Ethan shook his head helplessly. It was one thing to say that privately. If Harrison heard it, he would be furious.

His strong Pokemon had been hurt, mocked, and driven to a desperate last attack, and Gengar called it a game. Anyone might lose their temper at that. A hotheaded Trainer might even try to fight Gengar himself.

Ethan found the remark provoking too, but Gengar was his own Pokemon. He let it pass.

Fortunately, after Swellow's defeat, Harrison saw Gengar staying beside Ethan. It did not seem ready for another round, and he quietly breathed a sigh of relief.

At least he would not have to face it again.

His position was worse than ever, though. Four of his Pokemon were down. Elimination was drawing close.

Chapter 574: Ace Blaziken

At the referee's reminder, Harrison recalled Swellow and took out his fifth Poke Ball.

But the Pokemon that appeared was still not his ace, Blaziken. It was another from Hoenn: Linoone.

It bore little resemblance to a bear. Barely half a meter tall and weighing a little over thirty kilograms, it looked much like a badger from Earth.

Linoone's streamlined body reduced drag as it ran. Most of its fur was light brown, marked by darker stripes, and its head tapered like an arrow. Its coat was resilient and soft. It was said that people in cold places liked to wear coats made from its fur.

True to its name, Linoone was fast enough to reach a hundred kilometers per hour. It was poor at turning, though. To avoid an obstacle, it had to make a sharp right-angle turn; without slowing abruptly, it could hardly turn at all.

Ethan studied the Pokemon and searched through the Poke Balls on his belt. He could not decide whom to send out.

His Pokemon had all taken several turns in recent battles. Every one of them was in good condition and comfortable in the arena. None particularly needed another round.

Who should he choose? Perhaps he still had too few Pokemon available.

This was where the privileges of a star competitor showed. Harrison was a semifinalist too. The referee had not spoken while he chose his Pokemon, but he had kept his eyes on Harrison as if urging him to hurry.

When Ethan stood thinking for much longer, the referee showed no impatience at all. Ethan's popularity, strength, and the League's favor brought him that small advantage.

He did not delay too long. After a little thought, he selected Crystal Steelix's Poke Ball.

"This round is yours. Go, Crystal Steelix!"

Rather than trying to match Linoone's speed with another fast Pokemon, Ethan chose one with extraordinary defense.

Thud.

Crystal Steelix's massive body shook the field as it landed.

Although this was the Ice Field, the long match had already melted much of its surface. Large stretches of frozen earth lay exposed.

"There it is again!" the announcer exclaimed. "No matter how often I see Ethan's Crystal Steelix, I can't help admiring its beauty and strength. Sunlight and the remaining ice make that clear body shine. What a sight!"

This was Crystal Steelix's third appearance since the tournament began. Each time it entered the field, spectators cheered.

Who would not love a Pokemon like this?

At the start of the round, Linoone rushed into motion. As Ethan expected, it ran straight and fast but struggled with turns.

Harrison was badly behind and could not afford to wait. He ordered an all-out attack.

Linoone mainly fought at close range. Against a giant with Crystal Steelix's defenses, that gave it no advantage.

There was little suspense. Linoone had traveled with Harrison for years after he caught it in Hoenn, yet it too fell to Crystal Steelix.

Given the difference in their size, the result was hardly surprising.

"Linoone charged! And Linoone is down! It barely did any damage!" the announcer cried. "That's Harrison's fifth Pokemon defeated. Has Ethan recovered from his last match with Ash? Will he start another unbeatable run?"

As the announcer went on, Harrison looked at his fallen Pokemon and shook his head helplessly.

He had done everything he could.

After Linoone's defeat, he no longer believed he would advance. Still, he wanted to defeat at least one of Ethan's Pokemon.

He had crossed the sea to get here. How could he return to Hoenn after losing six to zero? He had to win one round.

Resolve returned to his eyes. He took out his final Poke Ball. Everyone knew which Pokemon it held: his ace, Blaziken.

Harrison threw it. Blue light flashed, and the imposing Blaziken appeared on the field.

Blaziken was the striking final evolution of Hoenn's Fire-type starter. It was powerful and popular; even those who knew nothing about it could be won over by its appearance.

Ethan did not hesitate this time. He had already chosen an opponent for Blaziken.

He recalled Crystal Steelix and sent out his own ace.

"Go, Gardevoir!"

Gardevoir lifted its head proudly as it appeared. The two Pokemon faced each other across the battered remains of the Ice Field.

Harrison looked at Gardevoir and shook his head. "A familiar Pokemon. Two Pokemon from outside Johto, meeting and battling hereit almost feels like I'm back in Hoenn. This is my last chance, so I'm going to give it everything I have!"

"Come at me," Ethan replied with a smile. "I received this Gardevoir in Kalos. It was my first Pokemon, and it's very strong. I won't hold back either!"

They fell silent and focused on the battle.

If Gardevoir defeated Blaziken, Harrison would be eliminated and Ethan would advance to the final. If Blaziken won, Harrison would still have five more of Ethan's Pokemon to overcome. That was nearly impossible, and Ethan had no intention of giving him the chance.

Once both Trainers and Pokemon were ready, the referee waved his flag. The final round of their semifinal began.

Harrison went on the offensive again. The instant the flag dropped, Blaziken ran at Gardevoir.

Gardevoir sensed Ethan's instructions in its mind and prepared to defend, then counterattack.

"Blaziken, use Flamethrower!"

Before Blaziken reached the middle of the field, it opened its mouth and fired a stream of searing flames from a distance.

The attack came plainly from the front. Gardevoir raised a hand, forming an invisible psychic barrier before it. The flames struck the wall and spread around its sides.

Harrison had meant the flames as a distraction. While Gardevoir blocked them, Blaziken leaped out through the fire at one side and drove a raised knee toward it.

As a Fire- and Fighting-type Pokemon, Blaziken excelled at close combat. Against a Psychic-type like Gardevoir, closing the distance could deny it room to use its powers.

Ethan made a decision without speaking. Gardevoir immediately raised its other hand. A stronger force burst out, and Psychic knocked Blaziken back into the flames.

That was the benefit of their mental connection. Ethan could command Gardevoir with a thought, saving the time it would take to speak.

Blaziken stumbled into the fire but charged back out seconds later, running at Gardevoir with great speed.

Gardevoir tried Psychic again. Blaziken leaped high from a standstill and cleared the attack.

"Good opening! Use Fire Punch!" Harrison shouted.

Flames engulfed both of Blaziken's fists. It dropped from above and swung at Gardevoir with all its strength.

Ethan showed no alarm. One hand remained in his pocket; he merely narrowed his eyes. Gardevoir used Teleport and vanished from before Blaziken.

Bang!

Fire Punch struck the frozen earth, drying a patch of ground in an instant.

Blaziken straightened and turned. Gardevoir had appeared on Ethan's half of the field, putting a wide gap between them again.

Harrison frowned. Blaziken had spent so much energy only to return to the starting point. They had merely swapped sides.

He could not let that continue.

He knew Teleport was a common tactic for some Psychic-type Pokemon. If Gardevoir kept using it, Blaziken would tire first. Harrison had to limit its movement.

"Blaziken, once more! Use Flamethrower!"

The same attack had failed before. Ethan knew Harrison was not foolish enough to repeat it without a plan.

Blaziken was dangerous both at range and up close. If an attack landed, Gardevoir would take serious damage.

Ethan stayed alert. This time, rather than block the incoming flames, he had Gardevoir Teleport farther away.

That was the opening Harrison had wanted.

The moment Gardevoir vanished, he shouted, "Watch all around you! Be ready to use Quick Attack!"

So that was his plan. Ethan shook his head with an amused smile. Did Harrison think this was enough to defeat Gardevoir?

Gardevoir appeared nearby. Blaziken, already prepared, rushed at it. Quick Attack drove it forward even faster.

Harrison knew Gardevoir could not Teleport a second time immediately. But that brief gap would not be enough. Gardevoir was Ethan's ace because of its strength, not merely because it was his first Pokemon or knew Teleport.

As Blaziken closed in, Gardevoir raised both hands. Its expression was as calm as Ethan's. A strange pink-purple beam shot from its palms straight toward Blaziken.

Psybeam!

At such close range, Blaziken could not dodge. The attack struck it at once.

Its body jerked and its charge slowed. It did not become confused, but the interruption gave Gardevoir another opening.

Gardevoir brought its hands together and raised them. An invisible force lifted Blaziken helplessly into the air.

Oh no! Harrison saw that Gardevoir had caught it with Confusion. "Break free!"

Blaziken struggled, but Confusion worked differently here than in the games. Its ability to hold and move a target was formidable. Without a special way to escape, a small or medium-sized Pokemon could not break free by force alone.

Blaziken rose higher. Unlike the way he had won a round against Ash, Ethan did not plan to throw it out of bounds. He would defeat Harrison in a direct fight.

Gardevoir thrust its arms down. Blaziken plunged into the ground.

Bang!

Ice chips and dust scattered. When the cloud cleared, Blaziken slowly stood.

It had already taken some minor damage, but that one impact was not enough to finish it.

As its strength fell, its fighting spirit seemed to rise. Its feathers stood on end, and fire appeared to burn in its eyes. Blaze, its Ability, had activated, making its attacks much stronger.

Gardevoir met its stare calmly, showing no reaction to the change.

Harrison took a deep breath. This was the decisive moment. If Blaziken was going to beat Gardevoir, it had to do so now.

"Give it everything you've got, Blaziken! Use Flare Blitz!"

Chapter 575: Into the Final

Flames covered Blaziken from head to toe, making it look like a huge fireballa meteor ready to race across the ground.

Perhaps the heat of its own flames was too much even for it. Blaziken coughed out a wave of hot air. Then it fixed its gaze on Gardevoir and ran.

The last patches of ice and snow, and even the damp earth nearby, dried in an instant.

Blaziken had poured everything into this move. The strain on its body would be immense, but if it hit and happened to burn Gardevoir, an impossible victory might become possible.

Harrison placed all his hope in the attack. As Blaziken drew closer, his worry grew so sharp that he shut his eyes without meaning to.

Please, let it hit!

Across the field, Gardevoir could use Teleport again. It could leave the path of Flare Blitz whenever it wished. Out of respect for Harrison, Ethan chose not to do that.

The result seemed settled. At least he could let the final exchange be a worthy one.

At Ethan's thought, Gardevoir responded.

It lifted both arms and used Psychic to drive Blaziken back. Blaziken gritted its teeth and forced its way forward against the invisible power.

It looked ready to collapse, its awareness beginning to blur, but fierce resolve kept it moving.

"Persistent," Ethan murmured, shaking his head. He sounded impressed, not alarmed.

Gardevoir's eyes flashed. It drew on its power to the limit, and a brilliant light burst from its palms toward Blaziken.

Dazzling Gleama powerful Fairy-type move.

Even in daylight, the light blazed like the sun. It almost blinded Blaziken. Under its force, Blaziken felt as if its body might melt. Every step and every breath became agony.

Worse, it could not keep its eyes open or tell which way to charge.

It's over, Ethan thought with a sigh.

Gardevoir Teleported behind Blaziken and struck its back with Psychic.

This time Blaziken could not endure. It flew forward, losing consciousness before it hit the ground.

"Blaziken is down!" the announcer cried.

Harrison, who had been looking down with his eyes closed, snapped them open. His Blaziken struck the ground. Behind it stood Gardevoir, slowly lowering its arms.

He had not seen how Gardevoir avoided the charge or delivered the final blow, but the scene told him enough.

He sighed. He had not won. Even at the end, Blaziken had never touched Gardevoir.

"What a decisive victory!" the announcer said. "Congratulations to Ethan, the first Trainer through to the final! His opponent will be decided in this afternoon's other semifinal!"

Harrison recalled Blaziken, walked over to Ethan, and shook his hand.

He looked at the handsome young man, several years his junior, with sincere admiration. "You're incredible. I was no match for you. After fighting you, it feels as though we're on different levels altogether."

"It's not quite that bad," Ethan replied with a warm smile. "My Pokemon have been through trials most Trainers' teams haven't faced. They grew stronger from them, and they did their best today."

In truth, Harrison was probably a little stronger than Ash overall.

Their teams emphasized different strengths. Ash's Pikachu and Charizard stood apart from his other Pokemon, which were somewhat weaker.

Harrison's Blaziken was clearly his ace, but the rest of his team was strong too. His Pokemon were more evenly matched.

Ash had an extraordinary upper limit, though his performance depended heavily on the day. Harrison had a higher baseline. If he could defeat Charizard and Pikachu, he would likely beat Ash.

Against Ethan, that balance led to a different result.

Ash had made Ethan work for his win, while Harrison had been overwhelmed. Ethan's Pokemon were, on average, stronger than Harrison's.

There was another reason Ethan had lost two rounds to Ash: he had sent Dragonite and Scizor, neither of which had finished growing into its strength. He had not used his strongest partners.

Had he chosen veterans like Gardevoir or Jolteon for those rounds, Ash would have had no chance to win them.

Still, losses had value. Ethan believed Dragonite and Scizor would grow stronger because of what they had experienced at this tournament. One day, they might stand beside his veteran Pokemon as equals.

He turned his attention back to Harrison. They did not know each other well, so their conversation was brief. A photographer took a picture of their handshake, and then they went their separate ways toward the waiting rooms.

Inside, Ethan spotted Ash, Misty, and Brock beside Erika.

"When did you get here?" he asked, surprised. The route from the stands was much longer than his walk from the field. Somehow the three had arrived first.

"We ran the whole way!" Misty smiled brightly. "Congratulations on reaching the final, Ethan!"

"Heh, heh!" Ash was grinning too, with none of Misty's grace. "A feast! I can't wait!"

Ash knew that Ethan treated them to a hearty meal whenever he advanced. As soon as Gardevoir won, he had dragged Misty and Brock out of the stands, without even waiting for Ethan to shake Harrison's hand.

Ethan laughed at his eagerness. Nothing except a battle or a big meal could make Ash move that fast.

"Of course. Come onlet's eat until we're full!"

They found a nearby restaurant and ordered a generous spread. Ethan was not very hungry at midday. He watched the television and chatted with Erika, Misty, and Brock.

Ash and Pikachu were the only ones eating as fast as they could.

It was already one in the afternoon. The main lunch rush had passed, and the restaurant was fairly quiet.

The television on the wall showed the day's other semifinal. It had only just begun, with the competitors being introduced. Jon Dickson faced a Trainer named Yamashita from the opposite half of the bracket.

Jon stood with a confident little smile. Brock watched him and said, "Unless something unexpected happens, Jon should win this, shouldn't he?"

"I think so," Misty agreed. She glanced at Jon on the screen. "Then the final really will be Jon against Ethan, just as we thought. He can smile now, but he won't be a match for Ethan!"

"You..." Ethan lightly flicked her forehead. She stuck out her tongue, and he shook his head with a smile. "Don't tempt fate for me. If I lose to him after you say that, everyone will laugh."

Misty was unconcerned. "I believe in you!"

The match began as they spoke. Even Ash stopped eating and turned toward the television.

The field at Silver Stadium had been drawn as a Grass Field. Jon, sending out first, chose Exeggutor to take advantage of the terrain. Yamashita answered with Magcargo.

Judging by Jon's earlier dominance in his half of the bracket, everyone expected him to win by a wide margin, just as Ethan had. The opening round startled them.

Exeggutor used the thick grass and its Grass- and Psychic-type moves to give Magcargo trouble early on. But Magcargo's Fire type had the advantage. Once it counterattacked, repeated blasts of flame scorched Exeggutor badly.

Perhaps Jon had grown careless. Perhaps the League's promotion of him as Ethan's equal had made him underrate the other competitors. Instead of switching Pokemon, he tried to fight through the unfavorable matchup.

The decision cost him. Magcargo's flames knocked Exeggutor out.

The referee raised a green flag. Yamashita had taken a one-to-zero lead.

Even then, no one realized how serious Jon's trouble was.

The announcer sounded amused. "It seems Jon Dickson may have underestimated his opponent, and the type matchup worked against him. The first round went badly, but I'm sure he'll adjust as the match continues!"

One loss was surprising, nothing more. Jon's strength was well known, while Yamashita had shown little in earlier rounds. No one believed Yamashita could beat him.

Jon himself thought the same.

The second round astonished them again.

Jon took Yamashita seriously and sent out Ampharos, which was not at a type disadvantage against Fire. Yamashita trusted Magcargo and kept it on the field.

Jon attacked fiercely from the start. Under his commands, Ampharos dealt Magcargo considerable damage. Then Magcargo spewed flames across the Grass Field, setting the whole surface alight.

Fire surrounded Ampharos in an instant. Its cries carried through the blaze.

The grass fed the flames, and the flames spread through the grass.

That was fire's destructive nature. Electric attacks and streams of water would fade into the air or earth when they missed. A flame could catch on fuel and keep burning until that fuel was gone.

The Grass Field gave this blaze more than enough to consume.

Jon frowned. He had not foreseen this. He wanted to recall Ampharos, but his Poke Ball's red beam could not penetrate the fire. He could not even see where Ampharos was inside it.

His composure vanished. However badly he wanted it to stop, the flames spread until the entire field had become a sea of fire.

Heat reached the spectators nearest the arena. They leaned back in alarm, trying to escape the hot air blowing toward them.

When the flames finally weakened, Jon searched the field. Ampharos lay blackened and motionless. He rushed out to check on it.

The burns were severe. Ampharos could not move, and its life was in danger. Without prompt treatment, it might die.

A medical team with two Chansey began emergency care at once. Then they lifted Ampharos onto a stretcher and carried it to the nearby aid station.

After the frantic interruption, the match resumed.

The accident was unexpected, but it fell within the rules. Different fields brought different risks.

Jon had lost two rounds. Now he had to focus and treat Yamashita with real caution.

At last he understood that Yamashita's plain earlier performances did not mean he was weak. Every Trainer in the semifinals had earned a place there. Any one of them might have held back a surprise. Underestimating an opponent could end his own tournament.

Fortunately for Jon, there was still a difference in their overall strength.

He sent out his strongest remaining Pokemon and did not relax again. He won the later rounds and reached the final after all, where he would face Ethan.

Chapter 576: You Call That Admiring Me?

The semifinals were over. Ethan and Jon Dickson had reached the final, exactly as most people had predicted.

Each had dominated the other Trainers in his half of the bracket.

Pokemon commentators boasted about their accurate forecasts on television. Ordinary spectators found that amusing. Even people who rarely watched a match could have guessed the finalists from what they had shown before the semifinals.

What made those commentators experts? They had said what everyone else was thinking.

The final was scheduled for the day after tomorrow. The date had been set long ago, and it would be the last battle of this Silver Conference.

Whoever won would be the champion.

The day between matches gave spectators more time to anticipate the final. It also let both Trainers study their last opponent more closely.

Ethan, however, intended to take the match as it came. He had already studied what he needed to know and saw no reason to wear himself out thinking about it again. He had a limited team to choose from; Jon could worry about which Pokemon he would send.

The Pokemon League increased its promotion for the final. Advertisements were everywhere, pushing public interest to its peak.

As people compared the finalists, Jon's two early losses in his semifinal became a subject of argument.

Some said he had no chance against Ethan. His side of the bracket had been weaker; had Ash or Harrison been placed there, Jon might not even have reached the final.

Others insisted Jon would win. They believed the League could not allow the same Trainer to take two regional titles in succession and would surely arrange something behind the scenes.

Online opinions went in every direction, but about eighty percent still expected Ethan to become champion.

The rest day arrived amid all that talk.

More spectators poured into Silver Town. Tickets for tomorrow's final were nearly impossible to get, and scalpers charged outrageous prices.

Several more of Ethan's friends arrived to support him, joining Ash and his group.

Professor Elm came first. After arranging his work, he had found two days free and brought his wife and child to watch the final in person.

The Kimono Sisters' arrival was more unexpected. The five were public figures in Johto, and people followed what they did. By coming to the tournament, they risked being recognized.

Ethan was pleased to see them all. He booked a private room at a Japanese restaurant and invited both groups to dinner.

Although they all lived in Johto, a scholar like Professor Elm had no reason to know performers like the Kimono Sisters. The sisters were easy to get along with, though, and Ash and his friends helped keep the conversation moving. Soon everyone was comfortable together.

Professor Elm's wife might have been the one exception. Seeing so many beautiful women in one room made her a little jealous, even though none showed any interest in her husband.

"Mr. Ethan," Miki, the eldest sister, said as she raised her cup. "I hope you win tomorrow and take the championship!"

Perhaps to avoid recognition, the sisters wore ordinary clothes rather than their familiar kimonos. They had also left off their heavy stage makeup. From a distance they looked like five attractive young women out for dinner.

"I hope so too. Thank you for coming so far to cheer me on!"

Ethan drank his sake. Truthfully, he did not care for its taste. He would have preferred beer or a cocktail, but neither suited this dinner as well.

"Sister," Zuki said from across the table. She smiled at Miki but spoke with pointed seriousness. "Mr. Ethan is an outsider. Jon Dickson is the local Trainer from Johto. Are you sure you're cheering for the right person?"

Her words had a sharp edge. Ethan glanced at her.

Zuki was the sister who had battled him in Ecruteak City. Even now, he had the feeling she was singling him out.

Sensing the change in mood, Kuni covered her mouth and laughed softly before Miki could answer. "Mr. Ethan is our friend. Of course we can cheer for a friend."

Naoko agreed. "Besides, this isn't a battle between regions. The championship belongs to an individual Trainer."

Zuki rolled her eyes at them. She had not expected her sisters to take Ethan's side.

The conversation moved on. Apart from Zuki's odd attention toward Ethan, everyone got along well. Erika, whose manner suited theirs, quickly became close to all five sisters.

But then Miki and Kuni exchanged a glance.

Neither was married, yet both could see that Erika and Ethan were closer than when they had last met. Warmth filled Erika's eyes whenever she looked at him. There was a new softness about her, too.

Together, the signs suggested that she and Ethan had recently become intimate.

The sisters saw the same surprise in each other's eyes. They liked Erika and thought of her as a traditional woman. They had not expected her to sleep with Ethan before marriage.

On reflection, it was hardly unbelievable. In the sisters' view, pure friendship between a man and a woman was rare unless neither had looks nor money. Ethan and Erika had traveled alone together; it would have been more surprising if nothing had changed.

Had they not known how close he was to Erika, the sisters might have been drawn to him themselves.

...

That night, after making love, Ethan lay in bed with Erika in his arms.

The room was warm from their exertion. Moisture clouded the windows, and a distinct scent lingered in the air.

They leaned against the pillows together, enjoying the quiet afterward.

Breathing in the scent of her hair, Ethan asked casually, "What did Miki and Kuni want to talk to you about after dinner?"

Professor Elm and his family, along with the Kimono Sisters, had returned to their respective hotels after the gathering. Before leaving, the five sisters had drawn Erika aside. Ethan had seen them laughing together but had been too far away to hear.

"Nothing important. Just things women talk about. You wouldn't be interested." Erika smiled. "They invited me to visit them after the tournament, though."

She hesitated, then added, "Actually... Zuki isn't trying to pick on you. She just..."

"She just what?" Ethan asked lazily.

"She admires you."

"What?" Ethan coughed and stared at her. "Admires me? Are you joking? Is giving me trouble over and over her way of showing it?"

Erika hid a laugh behind her hand. "Some proud girls do act like that. It's how they try to get a man's attention."

"Seriously?"

Ethan frowned. Zuki certainly was proud, and most people probably could not catch her interest. But deciding that her barbs were meant to attract him seemed awfully presumptuous.

Erika did not look as though she was joking. Could it be true?

Then he looked down at her bright eyes and had a sudden thought.

Was she testing him? Did she mean something else by bringing this up?

He cleared his throat and shrugged with studied indifference. "Who cares? We can't control how other people act. If you want to visit the sisters after the tournament, we'll go. As for Zuki, I'll keep my distance."

...

Salutes boomed and fireworks burst over Silver Town. Colorful flags fluttered around Silver Stadium, where the sacred flame burned and a packed crowd filled the stands with cheers.

"Everyone, after a long Silver Conference, the final has arrived!" The announcer's voice rang with its usual energy. "Two Trainers have fought through round after round to stand here today. Now they'll give everything they have for the honor of becoming champion!"

After warming up the crowd and introducing the finalists, the announcer welcomed them to the field. Ethan and Jon Dickson walked out of their respective tunnels, both wearing serious expressions.

They shook hands in the center, then went to their Trainer areas.

Pokemon League President Charles Goodshow gave a brief opening speech. Ethan paid little attention. He studied his opponent instead.

Jon was about Ethan's age. He had brown hair and wore a T-shirt and shorts. His looks were unremarkable, but his strength showed in his confident smile.

Ethan had heard Jon came from Cherry Town in Johto, known for its large, plump cherries and the bright blossoms that covered the town each spring.

In the waiting room, Erika was no longer alone. Ash, Misty, Brock, Professor Elm's family, and the Kimono Sisters sat with her, watching the big screen.

Every stadium ticket had sold out before they could get one. Ethan had brought his friends and family here instead. It lacked the atmosphere of the stands, but they had soft sofas, cool air, and fruit to eat.

Miki looked at Ash. "Mr. Ethan will win this match, won't he?"

She performed onstage and had an Eevee of her own, but knew little about competitive battles. Professor Elm's family looked to Ash as well. They wanted a Trainer's judgment rather than another guess.

"Of course," Ash said with conviction. "Apart from people like Lance, Ethan is the strongest Trainer I've met. I don't think anyone can beat him!"

Miki and the Elms relaxed a little. They had traveled far to support Ethan. No one wanted to watch him lose.

Only Zuki stood apart with her arms folded, leaning against a wall. As she watched Ethan on the screen, the faintest smile touched her face.

On the field, the opening formalities finally ended.

"We'll now draw today's battlefield and decide who sends out first!"

The rules were the same as in the earlier tournament rounds.

Ethan and Jon watched the screen. The pointer spun past Grass, Rock, Ice, and Water before slowing to a stop on the Water Field.

The next draw gave Ethan the second choice again.

Overall, he could hardly complain. Jon's ace was Rapidash, and the Water Field would restrict a Fire-type Pokemon. By sending out second, Ethan could also choose a good response to Jon's opener. Both draws seemed to favor him.

"Jon Dickson, on the green side, send out your first Pokemon!" the referee called.

The final was underway. Jon took a deep breath, lifted the Poke Ball he had already prepared, and threw it toward the center.

"Go, Rhyhorn!"

Blue light flashed. A sturdy Rhyhorn, built like an armored vehicle, appeared on the field.

Ethan had watched footage of Jon's matches. He knew this Rhyhorn had helped eliminate many competitors with its sheer strength. It had left an impression on him.

Sending it first showed Jon wanted an early win and hoped to seize the momentum of the match.

Chapter 577: Jon Is Stunned

Today's Water Field had a broad patch of land in the center, surrounded by a pool.

There was enough room on that central ground for Rhyhorn to run. That was why Jon had felt safe sending it out.

Against a Ground- and Rock-type Rhyhorn, Ethan chose Crystal Steelix.

Thud.

Crystal Steelix landed heavily to another roar from the crowd. Rhyhorn showed no fear of the enormous opponent. It scraped a front hoof across the ground, eager to fight.

Its confidence was not groundless.

With a body like a cross between a rhinoceros and a horned dinosaur, covered in armor, Rhyhorn looked tremendously hard. Once it got moving, the force of its charge would be frightening.

Jon smiled when Ethan brought out Crystal Steelix.

Just as he'd hoped. He had been studying Ethan's team for a long time. Every one of Ethan's Pokemon had looked strong in tournament footage.

He had never faced them directly, though, and believed he could handle them.

More importantly, Ethan had changed since the Indigo League. At the Silver Conference he seemed less interested in exploiting type advantages and more willing to meet opponents head-on. That gave Jon room to use his own strengths.

There was a reason he had opened with Rhyhorn. Now Ethan had responded exactly as he had expected, sending the rare Crystal Steelix for a direct contest of strength.

Steelix was huge, but Jon's Rhyhorn had trained for that kind of clash. It had never feared a test of raw power.

The referee checked both sides and swung his flag.

"The first round of the Silver Conference final begins now!"

At Jon's command, Rhyhorn started to run.

It earned its comparison to an armored vehicle. The ground trembled under its hooves.

Rhyhorn was not fast, but the momentum of its charge was imposing enough that Ethan took it seriously.

He had no intention of avoiding it.

Crystal Steelix feared no Pokemon in a contest of strength. "Stop it!" Ethan called.

Steelix lowered its center of gravity and coiled its body. Rhyhorn had built up momentum, so Steelix needed the friction of its coils against the ground to resist the impact.

Under the crowd's tense gaze, they collided.

Bam!

The force drove Steelix's front half backward. Its tail braced hard against the earth, though, and no matter how Rhyhorn pushed, it held its position.

Rhyhorn shuddered as though it had struck a small mountain. It could not advance another step.

Neither Pokemon had won the first exchange. Ethan remained calm, while Jon raised his eyebrows.

Even that charge had not moved Steelix. He had underestimated its strength. A pity, but the result was still within what he could handle.

"Rhyhorn, use Bulldoze!"

Rhyhorn lifted both front hooves to begin the Ground-type attack. Ethan did not give it the chance.

Ground-type moves were dangerous to Crystal Steelix. Even it could not take many direct hits.

"Don't let it. Use Iron Tail!"

Steelix swept its huge tail through the air with a rush of sound. It struck Rhyhorn with a sharp crack.

Rhyhorn staggered sideways. Its low stance let it catch itself before it fell.

Its thick hide did its job. The blow had interrupted it without dealing much damage.

Even so, Jon had been warned. He withdrew Rhyhorn to a safer distance and changed tactics.

From there, he ordered Earthquake. The whole field shook, and rings spread across the surrounding pool.

Now!

Crystal Steelix rocked with the ground and struggled to keep its balance. Jon saw his opening.

"Push it in!"

Rhyhorn charged again. Steelix had no time to brace as before. Rhyhorn drove it to the edge of the central ground, gave one more push, and sent it crashing into the pool.

Splash!

Water rose high and closed over Crystal Steelix. Its huge body vanished below the surface.

It worked! Jon celebrated inwardly. He tried to hide it, but he could not quite keep the smile from his face.

Most Ground-, Rock-, and Steel-type Pokemon could not swim. Anyone with a little knowledge knew that. Once they fell into water, they rarely got back out.

"This is bad!" the announcer cried. "Crystal Steelix has fallen into the pool around the field. Is Ethan about to lose the very first round?"

The spectators gasped. Ethan was the tournament favorite, with a huge following. Could he stumble at the opening of the final?

The referee looked over the water. Bubbles rose, but the splashing was fading.

He was about to call the result when something caught his eye. A vast shape seemed to be moving below the surface.

The stadium screens showed it too. The crowd quieted, staring in disbelief.

Jon noticed the change in mood and frowned. He looked carefully at the pool. A huge shadow really was swimming there.

No. Surely not.

Water suddenly erupted. Crystal Steelix's enormous head broke the surface. It coiled, pulled itself upward, and climbed back onto land.

Jon stood numb with shock.

How? Steelix could swimand climb out again?

Most of the audience was just as stunned. Even Professor Elm and the Kimono Sisters in the waiting room stared. Only those who knew Crystal Steelix well, like Ash, were unsurprised.

"Incredible," Elm murmured, adjusting his glasses. "That Steelix can swim. I never expected it."

Steelix did not give Jon time to recover. It rushed forward, wrapped its body around Rhyhorn, and lifted it from the ground.

"Oh no! Break free!"

Jon finally shook off his surprise. Without room to run, though, Rhyhorn was helpless in the coils.

Creak... creak...

Crystal Steelix tightened its grip. Rhyhorn's armorlike hide could withstand punishing attacks, even flames, but constant crushing pressure was another matter.

Its struggles grew weaker. Steelix squeezed harder. Rhyhorn's eyes rolled upward, and its body went limp.

The referee raised his red flag. "Rhyhorn is unable to battle! Crystal Steelix wins!"

Jon had gone from complete confidence to doubt in a single round.

He did not seem to realize he had lost until the referee reminded him to choose his next Pokemon.

Jon could accept a loss. He had lost the first two rounds against Yamashita, after all. This felt different.

"You can't understand how strong Ethan is until you've fought him yourself."

Jon remembered reading that online. The person who wrote it was a Trainer from the Whirl Islands. Ethan had apparently beaten him so thoroughly at a recent Whirl Cup that he had lost much of his desire to continue as a Trainer.

Jon had dismissed the comment as an excuse from a weak opponent. Now he began to understand it.

Ethan's match videos had not conveyed this pressure. Facing him in person felt suffocating.

Victory always looked possible, yet somehow slipped away. Why?

Jon recalled Rhyhorn. His expression heavy, he took out his second Poke Ball.

"Go, Golduck!"

He threw it with his usual motion, but his voice had lost its earlier certainty.

"After that first-round defeat, Jon Dickson is choosing a Water-type to use the field to his advantage!" the announcer said. "That's quite a change from his usual style!"

Jon had reached the final through skill, not luck. A Trainer with his record had pride. He had not usually bothered to build his choices around the field or a type matchup.

Now he had deliberately chosen a Water type on the Water Field. The match was changing him already.

Golduck was a pure Water type, but like Psyduck it could also use some Psychic-type moves. It was far more alert and imposing than its absentminded pre-evolution.

Ethan liked the species. He had never encountered a wild one, though, and had not caught one of his own.

His fingers passed over Jolteon's and Dragonite's Poke Balls. After thinking for a moment, he chose Blastoise.

Several days earlier, Ethan had asked Chloe to send him all his Pokemon from Cerise Park apart from the red Gyarados. He had kept them with him after each match instead of sending them back, ready for any matchup.

"Go, Blastoise!"

Blue light flashed. The larger Blastoise and smaller Golduck faced each other across the field.

"Two Water types!" the announcer said. "Now experience, stronger moves, and how well they use this field will decide it!"

As the battle began, both Pokemon attacked from a distance.

Blastoise fired Hydro Pump. Golduck did not answer with a Water-type move. It used Confusion.

Ethan almost laughed at the trick. He had brought a Water type for a Water-type duel, and Jon had chosen this?

Hydro Pump struck Golduck squarely. It endured the hit thanks to its own Water type. Blastoise, meanwhile, suddenly felt light as Confusion lifted it high into the air.

The red gem on Golduck's forehead flashed rapidly. It pushed both hands downward, and Blastoise plunged toward the ground.

It was a standard way to use Confusion here: hurt the target, lift it, then slam it down for a second impact.

An ordinary Pokemon might have had no answer. Blastoise had a shell.

Ethan did not need to give an order. After many similar experiences, Blastoise knew exactly what to do.

Just before it hit, Blastoise withdrew into its heavy shell, letting the armor take the force.

Crash!

A crater opened beneath it. A moment later, Blastoise poked out its head and shook off its dizziness. It had taken no meaningful damage.

Even so, Ethan did not want Jon to repeat the move. "Blastoise, jump into the water!"

Underwater movement and refracted light would make it much harder for Golduck to catch Blastoise with Confusion again.

Jon sighed when his surprise attack failed. He did not lose heart. He ordered Golduck into the pool as well.

If they were both Water types, they could settle the round in the water.

Chapter 578: Champion

Both Pokemon vanished beneath the water. Underwater cameras gave the audience a fixed view of what happened below, but the Trainers could no longer see their partners directly. Their commands could not reach through the pool, either.

Now the battle depended on the Pokemon's own judgment.

On the stadium screens, Golduck's streamlined body, long tail, and webbed feet made it look swift in the water.

Blastoise was no less capable.

It had helped Ethan win the racing competition in Altomare. A straight sprint might not be its strength, but its powerful muscles gave it tremendous force and bursts of speed.

Glub... glub...

The crowd could not hear the fighting underwater. The images still showed how fierce it was.

Golduck used its agility to circle Blastoise, darting in from one side and then another to rake at it.

Blastoise had its hard shell for protection. It needed only to face Golduck's attacks. Whenever it turned a little, Golduck had to swim a much wider arc and spend more energy finding another opening.

As the fight continued, Jon noticed something was wrong.

Blastoise drew its head and limbs into its shell. The great shell began spinning, faster and faster. Soon the water in the pool was turning with it.

Oh no! "Golduck, get away from there!"

Jon shouted toward the bottom of the pool, but Golduck could not hear him.

Fortunately, it sensed the danger for itself and swam for the shore. It was already too late. A whirlpool had formed underwater.

Golduck was not large enough to fight the powerful current. It had barely made any progress before the suction pulled it back toward the center.

The whirlpool's effect spread to the surface. Even without the screens, spectators could see a huge spiral opening in the water and guess what was happening below.

Then water roared upward. A waterspout rose from the pool and climbed high into the air.

Golduck was caught at its top, battered by the rushing water.

It was an underwater tactic Ethan had used to win many battles. Now Jon was experiencing its power.

Jon's face changed. He took out Golduck's Poke Ball to recall it, but the waterspout rose beyond the ball's range.

When the column finally dissolved and Golduck fell, it dropped too fast for Jon to aim the recall beam. He tried several times and missed his chance.

Bang!

Golduck struck the ground hard. As the dust cleared, it lay unconscious.

Splash!

Blastoise jumped from the pool and landed on the central ground.

The referee raised his red flag. "Golduck is unable to battle! Blastoise wins the second round!"

Applause filled the stands. After only two rounds, many spectators felt Ethan's championship was becoming inevitable.

Jon recalled Golduck, his expression grave. While Ethan seemed at ease, Jon's spirits sank.

He looked across at Ethan, clenched his teeth, and reached for his ace.

"Go, Rapidash!"

"Oh? Jon is sending out his strongest Pokemon already!" the announcer exclaimed. "Rapidash has been unbeaten in his earlier matches and carried him through this tournament. But we're only at the third round, still in the first half. Is this too soon?"

Too soon? Jon could only smile bitterly.

Against another Trainer, he might not have needed Rapidash at all. His other Pokemon could have carried him through.

Now he had to stop this run of defeats.

If he kept losing, what good would a win in the final round do? He would have nothing left to face Ethan's remaining team. Better to stake everything on a fight now.

Ethan knew Rapidash was Jon's strongest Pokemon, even though it had not been his first partner.

He could leave Blastoise on the field and take advantage of the type matchup. That would be straightforward. Such an easy choice no longer interested him much.

What should he choose instead?

"This round is yours." Ethan recalled Blastoise and threw another Poke Ball. "Go, Dragonite!"

Dragonite, Tyranitar, and Scizor were the newer generation of his team. They would carry his next regional journey, so he wanted them to gain as much battle experience as possible.

Jon breathed easier when he saw Dragonite.

From Ethan's matches, he knew that Dragonite and some of the other newer Pokemon were a little less formidable than veterans like Gardevoir, Jolteon, Crystal Steelix, and Gengar. He had a better chance against one of them.

If he could turn the match around, it had to begin here.

Both Trainers looked satisfied with their choices. At the signal, they ordered their Pokemon forward.

Rapidash was a Fire type; Dragonite was Dragon and Flying. Neither held an obvious type advantage.

That did not tell the whole story. Their individual abilities mattered too.

Rapidash, a running Pokemon, had an impressive speed in the Pokedex. Dragonite's listed speed was lower, but its wings let it fly fast enough to keep pace with Rapidash.

Rapidash relied mainly on Fire- and Normal-type attacks. Dragonite had a wider range: Dragon and Flying moves, along with some Electric and Water moves. Even a single Aqua Tail could surprise Rapidash at close range.

Both had paths to victory. The uncertainty made the round more exciting.

Dragonite twisted aside in midair and dodged Rapidash's Fire Blast. Then it dived.

Rapidash ran, trying to leave it behind.

They chased and clashed all around the field. Dragonite did not always have the initiative. Rapidash lived up to its reputation as Jon's ace, finding chances to strike back.

When Dragonite missed one dive, Rapidash kicked it with its front hooves.

The struggle remained close. Both had taken damage after only a short while.

Then one of Rapidash's Fire attacks burned Dragonite. Every movement brought it fresh pain.

Another Trainer might have recalled it until the burn subsided.

Ethan hesitated when he saw the determination in Dragonite's eyes. He shook his head and let it continue.

Dragonite wanted to win. Recalling it now would hurt its confidence.

It had a way to ease the pain. Dragonite dived into the pool and leaped out again. Water clinging to its body soothed the burn.

As with rinsing a burn under clean water, the relief was immediate.

"A clever choice!" the announcer said. "The water won't remove the burn completely, but it has eased the pain!"

Dragonite returned to the fight with even greater ferocity. It ignored its injuries and closed the distance instead of attacking from afar. The burn had already taken hold; it might as well press the attack.

Thunder Punch met Rapidash's Flame Wheel, and an unexpected Aqua Tail lashed across Rapidash's body.

Perhaps Dragonite's relentless assault rattled Rapidash. It could neither outrun its pursuer nor break away. In the end, both Pokemon exhausted each other and fell together.

The audience gasped as they collapsed.

A draw? Rapidash was Jon's strongest Pokemon, while Dragonite was considered one of Ethan's less experienced partners. Few had expected them to bring each other down.

Ethan was surprised too. He had already been ready to send out his next Pokemon, only for Dragonite to give him this welcome result.

It really was growing fast through this tournament.

Jon shook his head helplessly. Losing his ace took much of the fight out of him. He knew it would be harder than ever to stop Ethan.

So it proved. After halftime, Jon lost his earlier aggression. His Quagsire, Hitmontop, and Marowak fought cautiously, defending far more often than they attacked. Jon's commands became cautious tooa complete reversal of his usual style.

Ethan answered those three Pokemon with Scizor, Tyranitar, and Gardevoir. Each won its round. Three successive victories ended the match.

Marowak had barely fallen when salutes thundered around Ethan. Before he fully realized he had won, cheers rose from the stands and ribbons flew through Silver Stadium.

"We have our champion!" the announcer shouted. "The favorite has delivered! Congratulations to Ethan, winner of this year's Silver Conference. After the Indigo League, he has now won two championships in a row!"

Ethan stood still for a moment. He was happy, though not as excited as he had been after his first title.

He had won already?

The rounds had passed almost routinely. The match had held few surprises.

Jon simply had not challenged him enough. Ethan judged him to be roughly as strong as Harrison, and neither had been especially difficult to face.

Kanto and Johto shared a continent and had close ties with little cultural difference. In Ethan's view, they scarcely needed separate League tournaments. One combined competition could bring all their strongest Trainers together.

They even shared the Elite Four. A combined tournament would be more exciting than one in which, apart from a few standouts, the competitors varied so widely in strength.

On the other hand, the Indigo and Silver Conferences had been good first stages for Ethan. They had given him experience and helped train his Pokemon for harder battles ahead.

He came back to himself, smiled broadly, and waved to the cheering crowd.

Jon shook his hand with visible disappointment. Then the referee directed Ethan to the awards platform.

League President Charles Goodshow was waiting. He placed a gold medal around Ethan's neck, took a shining trophy from an attendant, and handed it to him.

"Congratulations, young man," Goodshow said with a kindly smile. Ethan thought he detected a trace of bitterness beneath it. "You've won the Silver Conference. That's your second championship. Quite an achievement!"

Goodshow's words were not entirely wholehearted. He sincerely congratulated Ethan, but part of him was disappointed.

As League president, he had to think about the competition as a whole. Two consecutive titles were a great honor for one Trainer. For the others, watching the same person win again could be discouraging.

"Thank you, President Goodshow." Ethan had not noticed his conflicted mood. "Don't worry. I'll keep working hard on my travels and try to win another trophy!"

Goodshow's smile faltered. That was not what he had meant. He could hardly say so aloud, though. "Then... good luck. I'm sure you'll do well."

Chapter 579: Another Familiar Movie Plot

The winner of this years Silver Conference is Ethan Vale of the Kalos region! This is his second championship trophy since the Indigo League! Lets congratulate him!

The announcers ringing voice echoed through the stadium. The result was settled, and the tournament had truly reached its end.

Of course, Ethan still had to take a commemorative photograph with the Pokemon who had won him the title.

He brought out Gardevoir, Dragonite, Scizor, Tyranitar, Crystal Steelix, Jolteon, Blastoise, and Venusaur, all of whom had battled in this tournament. Gengar could not contain itself either. It hurried to Ethans side with a huge grin.

The Pokemon gathered around him. With the enormous trophy in his arms, Ethan heard the click of the camera, and the moment was preserved forever.

After leaving the field, Ethan returned to the waiting room.

He had braced himself before opening the door. It did him no good. Streamers burst over him the instant he stepped inside.

Congratulations, Ethan!

You won the championship!

Congratulations!

Voices came from every direction. Ethan pulled a streamer from his hair and saw familiar face after familiar face, all smiling their heartfelt congratulations.

Thanks, everyone.

They crowded around him as he came in. Until then, the victory had not quite felt real. With everyone talking at once, he felt as though he were floating on a cloud, his limbs light and weak.

Then came the part everyone enjoyed: a celebratory feast.

Winning the Silver Conference also brought Ethan another cash prize. It was about the same amount he had received for winning the Indigo League, and it swelled his savings considerably.

With the money he had now, he could stop being a Trainer, settle somewhere quiet, and live comfortably for the rest of his life.

That was not a path he was considering yet. If the day came when he was tired of traveling and wanted to settle down, the option would be there.

The whole group headed to a restaurant, where Misa, Masha, and their friends were already waiting. They had heard the news and arrived ahead of them.

The meal lasted until late at night. The worst of it was that Misa, Masha, and the other bikers kept filling Ethans glass. He was in such a good mood that he drank more than he should have.

By the end of the night, he had no idea how he got home.

When he woke again, it was eleven the next morning. His head throbbed from the hangover, and he reeked of alcohol. Only after a cold shower did he feel a little better.

Here.

Erika handed him a glass of warm water. As he drank it slowly, she smiled and said, Professor Elms family, Miki, and the others have already gone home. You were still asleep, so they didnt come in to say goodbye.

Ethan set the glass aside and tried to empty his mind. Thinking made it feel as though something were stirring around inside his skull.

What about Misa and Masha?

They just left too. I asked them to take your medal and trophy to Cerise Laboratory. Ive packed our luggage as well. Only Ash and the others are still waiting for you.

Ethan looked around. The room was spotless, and their things were ready to carry out. Having a thoughtful woman beside him certainly made life easier. Erika had taken care of everything without him having to worry about a thing.

He dressed, picked up his luggage, and went downstairs with her to the competitors village lobby.

The lodging was deserted. Apart from the staff, Ethans group seemed to be the only people left. The Trainers who had lost had long since gone, taking their disappointment with them.

Ethan, youre awake!

Misty was the first to turn at the sound of footsteps. One look at his weary face told her how he felt.

You slept forever, Ash grumbled. Weve already eaten lunch!

Can you blame me? Ethan said. Those people kept pouring me drinks last night. My head still feels like its going to split open.

Once they were together, they wasted no more time at the village and set off.

At yesterdays celebration, they had agreed to leave Silver Town as a group. They would travel to a town not far away, then part ways there.
