He held Celebi tightly. It struggled, but his gloves were specially made. They gave off a faint dark energy that kept it from escaping or attacking him.

He had not flown far when he heard something behind him. Ethan was pursuing him on Dragonite.

That man was impossible to shake.

Vicious gritted his teeth and pushed the jetpack to full power. Flames roared from it, and his speed surged.

He was foolish to think that would leave Dragonite behind.

Dragonite might look slow on land, but it was extraordinarily fast in the air. Even Viciouss sudden burst of speed could not open a gap.

More importantly, a jetpack had limited fuel. Before long it ran dry, forcing Vicious to descend.

As he landed, an orange shape flashed before him. Dragonite came down opposite him.

Ethan dismounted and smiled. Youre out of options. Stop struggling and let Celebi go.

Chapter 587: Across Time

Vicious stared at Ethan with hatred.

He held Celebi in one hand and felt around his vest for a Dark Ball with the other. His fingers found nothing.

Only then did he remember that he had not recalled Dark Tyranitar, Dark Sneasel, or Dark Scizor during the battle. Their balls had been lost as well.

Cursing under his breath, he searched the other side of his vest and pulled two Dark Balls from the bottom.

They held ordinary Pokemon he had caught almost casually. Even enhanced by dark energy, they could not compare with his Sneasel or Scizor, much less Tyranitar.

But they were all he had left to fight with. Perhaps they could buy him a little time.

He threw both balls. Dark Poliwhirl and Dark Graveler appeared before Ethan, each wrapped in black light.

Ethan did not send Dragonite into the battle. He took two Poke Balls from his belt instead.

Gardevoir, Jolteon, go!

Blue light flashed, and they faced Poliwhirl and Graveler. Ethan had chosen two of his best partners. He was taking Vicious seriously and holding nothing back.

Once the fight began, however, Vicious surprised him.

As all four Pokemon moved, Vicious turned and ran. He vanished behind a tree. Gardevoir and Jolteon knocked the Dark Pokemon down almost as soon as they had engaged them.

Ethan understood. Vicious had reached the end of his resources.

He hurried after him with his Pokemon. Passing the two fallen opponents, he rounded the tree and found a Dark Ball flying straight at them.

Vicious knew he could not outrun Ethan. He had hidden to ambush him. If he could steal even one of Ethans Pokemon, the Trainer would have a serious problem.

But Ethan expected a desperate trick. As the ball came toward him, a stone rose from the ground beside him and struck it.

Smack!

The Dark Ball did not break, but the blow knocked it off course. It fell to the ground without opening or releasing its black light.

Ethan had learned the trick from Ash. He could not fight the Dark Balls light once it opened, but a well-aimed object could deflect it while it was still flying.

Only Gardevoir, linked closely enough to understand his thought without an order, could have moved the stone in time.

His ambush failed. Ethans Pokemon surrounded Vicious, who now had no other way to resist.

Footsteps sounded behind them. Ash and Sammy arrived, breathless from running.

They had made remarkable time, though Ethan and Vicious had not flown far. Ethan had already spotted Ashs Shiny Noctowl following them from above, so their appearance did not surprise him.

With the boys there too, Vicious had no hope of escaping.

Y-you! Ash bent forward, struggling for breath. He looked from Vicious to the Celebi in his hand. Let Celebi go!

You pests... Vicious shouted bitterly. I had Celebi! I was so close to leaving Team Rocket and becoming the ruler of this world! This is all your fault!

Leaving Team Rocket? Ethan raised his eyebrows.

He had not known Vicious harbored that ambition, though it made sense. Team Rockets executives were hardly selfless people. A Pokemon hunter with power enough to change the world would not be content to serve under someone else.

But Vicious would never achieve that dream.

Its over, Ethan said. Hand Celebi to us. I promise youll reach the police unharmed.

Vicious laughed. When he stopped, he fixed them with a savage look. You really think youve won?

He looked almost deranged. Ethan wondered what else he could possibly have planned. Unwilling to let him create another surprise, he ordered his Pokemon forward and stepped closer himself.

Vicious slowly drew his last Dark Ball.

Ethan, Ash, and Sammy all watched the ball. Was he about to release some powerful Dark Pokemon, or try to catch one of theirs?

He did neither. He pressed the Dark Ball toward Celebis head.

Oh, no.

Ethan grasped his plan in an instant. Vicious meant to control Celebi again, then force it to carry him into another time.

If he succeeded, everything they had done would be wasted. Once he left their time, they might never encounter him again.

They had to stop him. Ethan shouted an order to his Pokemon and ran toward Vicious.

Sammy moved too.

Ash had not yet understood what Vicious intended, but Sammy had. The moment the Dark Ball approached Celebi, he guessed the danger and sprinted forward.

Hearts pounded. For a moment, time itself seemed to slow.

Vicious raised his arm. His finger moved toward the balls switch. Ethan and Sammy rushed closer, urgency plain on Sammys face, but the distance looked too great. They would be too late.

Everyone had overlooked the most important one there.

Celebi.

Hunter and rescuers alike had focused on it. Celebi saw the Dark Ball nearing its head and remembered what it had just suffered under its control.

It would not endure that pain again.

I wont let it control me!

Celebi gave a piercing cry. Power erupted from its body. The light and sound of time travel spread out from it, enveloping both Celebi and Vicious, then expanding farther.

Vicious took the first impact. Even through his mask, the flash blinded him. He turned his head away, felt a powerful force strike him, and lost his grip. Celebi broke free.

Ethan and Sammy had no time to understand what was happening before the blue-green light swallowed them too.

Farther away, Ash shielded his eyes and turned from the glare. When it faded enough to look again, Ethan and the others had vanished.

The forest fell silent. If Viciouss two fallen Dark Pokemon had not still been lying behind him, Ash might have thought he had imagined it all.

Ethan... Sammy... Celebi... Where had they gone?

...

Ethan felt weightless and unsteady, as though gravity had disappeared.

Before he could understand it, he heard a man scream. It was not Celebi. The voice was painfully familiar: Vicious.

What had happened to him?

When the light around Ethan vanished, he looked ahead. Vicious lay on the ground, rolling and clutching his eyes.

My eyes! My eyes!

His cries echoed through the trees and startled several bird Pokemon into flight.

Ethan looked around. His Pokemon were there, and Sammy stood nearby with the same bewildered expression. Ash was nowhere to be seen.

Had they traveled through time?

He turned toward Celebi. It was already flying away.

Celebi, come back!

Sammy called too, but Celebi kept flying as though it had not heard either of them.

It must be frightened, Ethan said with a frown. Stay here and watch him. Ill bring Celebi back!

Without waiting for Sammys answer, he recalled Gardevoir and Jolteon, mounted Dragonite, and flew after Celebi.

Wait... Sammy took two hurried steps, but Ethan was already high above him. He sighed.

He did not mind keeping an eye on Vicious. He simply did not know whether his Charmeleon could handle such a dangerous hunter alone.

For now, Vicious seemed hurt. He kept rolling on the ground, apparently no longer a threat.

Sammy sent out Charmeleon. Fighting down his fear, he approached and kicked the last Dark Ball away from Vicious. Only after it rolled well out of reach did he feel a little safer.

...

High above the trees, Ethan and Dragonite followed Celebi.

Frightened, it fled without choosing a direction. Celebi flew fast enough that Dragonite had to give everything it had to keep up.

Ethan did not know which time they had reached. He did know that Celebi was his only way home. He could not lose sight of it.

He had wanted to catch Celebi before. Now he had another reason he could not let it escape.

At last Celebi seemed to tire, or perhaps it calmed down. It descended into the forest.

Ethan let out a long breath and directed Dragonite after it.

Celebi landed in a fruit tree, picked several berries, and ate. At the sound of wings behind it, it turned quickly. Seeing Ethan on Dragonite, it relaxed.

From their time together yesterday, it knew he was not a bad person. It did not know that, although his methods differed from Viciouss, Ethan also hoped to catch it.

Out of the wolfs den and into the tigers jaws, one might say.

But Ethan had no evil use in mind. He liked Celebi and did not want to spend the rest of his life regretting a missed chance to catch this Mythical Pokemon.

He smiled, trying to appear as friendly as possible.

Celebi, where are we? Can you take me back to the time we came from?

Bi!

Celebi tilted its head. Its eyes shone as it answered, but Ethan could not understand a word.

Fortunately, he had a translator for moments like this.

Gengar, come on out. Time for work!

Gengar emerged from his shadow, stretched widely, then floated around Celebi with interest.

It says this is the time it originally lived in. It left here a few days ago.

Its original time? Ethan understood at once. This must be the world Sammy had come from. Had they traveled forty years into the past?

Can it take me back?

Celebi nodded gently. Bi, bi-bi.

Gengar translated. It can. But it wants to know why you dont want to stay here.

Because my friends and the woman I love are in that time, Ethan said, relieved that he could return. If I stay, I may never see them again. Theyll be worried too.

Celebi nodded as though it partly understood. To it, any time and any forest seemed much the same. Time had changed little about its home.

It raised its hands to use its power. Ethan stopped it.

Wait. Sammys back there waiting for me. I cant just leave him. At the very least, I need to go back and speak to him first.

Chapter 588: Catching Celebi

Ethan rode Dragonite back with Celebi, searching for Sammy and Vicious.

The forest below looked the same in every direction. Fortunately, Dragonite remembered their approximate route. Before long, they heard Sammy calling and found him.

But when Dragonite landed, Ethan saw only Sammy and Charmeleon. Vicious was gone.

Wheres Vicious?

Im sorry. Sammy looked ashamed. His eyes seemed badly hurt, so I let my guard down. He jumped into the river while I wasnt watching. I wanted to follow him, but I was afraid you wouldnt find me when you came back, so I stayed here.

Vicious had escaped again?

It was regrettable, but not Sammys fault. Ethan did not reproach him. Was he pretending to be blind?

Sammy shook his head. No. I saw blood coming from his eyes. He was really hurt. He found the river by listening for it, then stumbled in.

Ethan had nothing to say to that. Vicious had nerve.

If Ethan were blind, he would never dare jump into a river without knowing where he could get out. It was almost a death sentence. Vicious would rather gamble on the current than be captured. He must have feared losing his freedom more than dying.

But even if he reached the shore, how would a blind man without Poke Balls or Pokemon find his way out of this forest?

Then Ethan remembered something else. Vicious had not seen the blue-green light and heard the voice of Celebis time travel before today. No one had explained it to him. He probably did not even know he had landed forty years in the past.

Perhaps he hoped to find the spider-shaped robot he had left behind and escape in it. He could search this forest forever and never find a machine that belonged to another era.

For all he had done, it was a miserable end.

Sammy noticed Celebi beside Ethan and brightened. Ethan told him they had returned to his original time.

So Im back forty years ago? Back where I belong?

Thats right. You

An engine roared nearby. A motorcycle burst from behind the trees.

Its rider was a thin-faced man in his thirties or forties. He wore an old-fashioned jacket and a deerstalker hat that had long since gone out of style in Ethans day. A black patch covered his injured right eye. He did not look friendly.

A Scyther and a Houndoom ran beside the motorcycle. The man and his Pokemon stopped in front of Ethan and Sammy.

His gaze passed over Celebi and settled on Sammy. I thought youd disappeared. So this is where you went. You made me search everywhere. Whats wrong? Too frightened to run anymore?

Sammy took an instinctive step back, and Celebi moved away too.

Bewildered, Ethan looked at Sammy. Who is he? Why does he talk as though he owns the place?

Hes the Pokemon hunter who was chasing Celebi in this time! Sammy started to pull Ethan away, then remembered the strength of Ethans Pokemon and Suicune in particular. He steadied himself. He cornered us. Thats why Celebi had to take us to your time.

I see. Ethan faced the hunter with a smile. Picking on a child isnt impressive. Would you like to battle me?

Who are you? The man studied him, hearing the confidence in his voice. Another meddler?

Then he spotted Dragonite and laughed. This is my lucky day. Ill catch Celebi and a rare Dragonite. That one will fetch a fine price.

Ethan had heard enough. He whistled.

Dragonite, already angry, flew at the hunter. The man opened his mouth to threaten the reckless young Trainer, but his Scyther and Houndoom were knocked down in a few swift blows.

What?

Dragonite rammed him off his feet and planted a foot on him before he could rise.

Thats it? Ethan shrugged. I thought youd be more of a challenge.

Sammy and Celebi breathed easier at the sight of the hunters effortless defeat.

Who are you? The man stared up at Ethan with his one visible eye.

That doesnt matter. What matters is that your luck just ran out. Ethan turned to Dragonite. Break up his motorcycle, destroy his Poke Balls, and throw him in the river. He can keep Vicious company. They may even get along.

Dragonite nodded and obeyed. It kicked the hunter into the river, then tore his motorcycle apart. Finally it found the Poke Balls on the bike, released every Pokemon inside, and crushed the empty balls underfoot.

It dusted off its hands and returned to Ethan with a proud look.

With the danger handled, it was time to part from Sammy.

Ethan offered him a hand. Celebi will take me back to my time now. You should continue your sketching journey.

Sammy shook his hand. He had a thousand things he wanted to say, but none would come out.

He had met Celebi, traveled forty years into the future, seen the girl who had once given him bread as an old woman, and helped rescue Celebi from a hunter. He had only just made friends with Ash and could not even say goodbye to him. It all felt like a dream: precious, and hard to wake from.

At last he bowed deeply. Thank you so much. Please say goodbye to Ash and Towa for me. Ask them to forgive me for not being able to do it myself.

I will.

Ethan patted his shoulder and smiled knowingly at the young Professor Oak. The future authority of the Pokemon research world had just bowed to him. He could not help feeling a little pleased.

After their farewell, Sammy stepped back beyond the reach of Celebis power.

Blue-green light shone, and the ethereal voice sounded once more. Ethan and Celebi vanished before Sammys eyes.

Sammy stood looking at the empty ground for a long time. When he had calmed himself, he turned with determination and resumed his travels.

...

When the light faded, Ethan was back where he had left his own time.

Traces of their battle remained, but Ash was gone. He had probably returned to the lake to meet Misty and the others after seeing them vanish.

Ethan did not hurry to find Erika. With no one around, he put his plan to catch Celebi into motion.

First he brought out Eevee to play with it. He had seen how well the two got along. Eevees company would help Celebi relax.

Then he set down his bag, filled a kettle from the river, and heated the water. With Celebi watching, he opened a cup of noodles and poured the hot water in.

Yes, he intended to use food again to tempt Celebi into coming with him.

The tactic rarely failed with a glutton. A Pokemon that had lived in the wild for years could find human food especially hard to resist.

He and Celebi were on friendly terms now, and it had no reason to fear him. They were alone in a peaceful forest, with time and opportunity on his side.

If he still failed to catch it, he might as well bang his head against a block of tofu.

When the noodles were ready, he peeled back the lid. A savory smell rose into the air. Celebi, already eager, was nearly drooling.

Want some? Ethan asked.

Celebi nodded repeatedly.

Ethan held the cup toward it. As Celebi leaned in, he drew it back and sighed as though disappointed.

Celebi looked up, not understanding.

Such a shame, Ethan said.

He left the thought unfinished. Celebis stomach growled at the smell, and it chirped to ask what he meant.

Im about to leave this forest. We wont be able to stay friends.

Before Celebi reacted, Dragonite turned its head away. It had heard this sort of speech before and could guess what would come next.

Celebi looked downcast. It had known Ethans group for only two days, but those days had held more excitement than its quiet life ever had. Even with so little experience of the world, it understood that people had to part.

If only you could travel with us, Ethan went on. You could leave this forest and see the wide ocean, bustling cities, and all kinds of wonderful food...

At the mention of food, Celebi swallowed and stared at the noodles. Until recently, it had eaten only wild fruit. It wanted to devour the fragrant meal in one bite.

Ethan handed it the cup. Celebi forgot all the dignity expected of a Mythical Pokemon and began gobbling the noodles.

Cup noodles smelled and tasted good, even if most people tired of them after eating too many. To Celebi, tasting them for the first time, even the cup itself looked tempting.

It finished the noodles, patted its round belly, and still seemed to want more.

Ethan judged the moment right and spoke in an enticing voice. Its a pity you can only stay in this forest. If you came with us, Id treat you to even better food. Youve never had strawberry cake, have you? Bright red strawberries on top, smooth cream underneath... And theres something called ice cream...

As Ethan talked, Celebi drooled. Even Dragonite smacked its lips at the description.

Eevee called to Celebi too, backing up what its Trainer said. Before joining Ethan, Eevee had lived with the five Kimono Sisters in Ecruteak City and tried plenty of delicious food. It spoke from experience.

Trainer and Pokemon continued painting a picture of life beyond the forest. When Ethan saw interest brightening Celebis eyes, he finally asked, Would you like to travel with us?

Celebi hesitated. The outside world sounded wonderful, but it still wanted to remain in its forest.

Eevee redoubled its efforts. Its calls reminded Celebi of the fun they had shared yesterday and of all the advantages Eevee had described in living with humans.

Dragonite added a few words of encouragement.

Seeing Celebi waver, Ethan took out the GS Ball and held it before the Pokemon.

What do you say? Come with me and see the world outside?

Everything went quiet. Ethan had finally shown what he wanted. Dragonite and Eevee watched Celebi, waiting for its choice.

Neither Pokemon was foolish. They had understood from the beginning that their Trainer wanted to catch Celebi and had been helping him persuade it.

After all three had made their case, Celebi gave Ethan an innocent smile and nodded.

Good. They had talked it into it.

Ethan touched the GS Ball to Celebis forehead. Blue-green light sprang from the ball and enveloped it.

Celebi entered. The ball rocked a few times, then fell still.

At last Ethan let out a breath. He had caught Celebi.

He barely had time to celebrate before footsteps and voices sounded nearby.

As he stood, Erika and the others emerged from the trees, looking worried.

Huh? Misty froze at the sight of him and turned to Ash. You said Ethan disappeared! Hes standing right here!

Ash had panicked when Ethan and Sammy vanished. After searching the area without finding them, he had run back to the lake and told the others. Erika and the group had hurried here.

Ash looked around. Ethan, where did you go? And where are Sammy and Celebi?

You might not believe this, but I went forty years into the past. I helped Sammy defeat the hunter who had been pursuing him and Celebi.

I see. Ash scratched his head. So where are they? Didnt they come back with you?

Sammy stayed. Thats where he belongs. Ethan smiled. He asked me to say goodbye to you and Towa. He hopes you wont mind that he couldnt do it in person.

Sammy... Ashs face fell. They had only just become friends, and already they had parted.

Dont be sad, Ash, Towa said. Sammy comes from another time. Too much contact between you might change the present. We know he got home safely. We should be happy for him.

Youre right. Ash nodded, then looked back at Ethan. What about Celebi?

Celebi... Ethan smiled faintly. It went where it belongs.

That was a riddle. Ethan was not unwilling to tell Ash, but Towa, Diana, and White were there. They lived beside the forest. He did not know how they would feel about him catching its guardian. He could explain to Ash another time.

With that, the matter was finally settled.

Ethan and Ashs group had journeys to continue.

They waved goodbye to Towa, Diana, and White. The three villagers turned back toward Arborville while the travelers headed for the other side of the forest.

Perhaps they would never meet again. None of them would forget what had happened here.

They walked on without much conversation. Beyond the forest, they reached a town below the Indigo Plateau. It was time for Ethan and Ash to part too.

Standing opposite Ash, Misty, and Brock, Ethan smiled. Im leaving for Hoenn. Once youve been home and rested a few days, come as soon as you can. Otherwise Ill get far ahead of you.

Dont worry. Ash thumped his chest. Ill go back to Pallet Town, talk with Mom, and head straight to Hoenn!

They smiled at each other. Ethan said goodbye to Misty and Brock as well.

Brock took the parting easily enough. Misty smiled at Ethan. You wont be waiting long for me. Ill return to the Cerulean Gym, let my sisters know Im safe, and come find you right away.

Ill wait for you. Ethan and Erika waved once more. See you in Hoenn!

(End of the Johto Arc)

Chapter 589: A New Region, a New Adventure

A long ship's horn echoed across Littleroot Town's harbor. When the liner that had carried them across the sea docked, Ethan and Erika followed the other passengers down the gangway and stepped onto a land neither had visited before.

Hoenn, here we come!

Littleroot Town was the starting point for Hoenn's new Trainers. A few days earlier, after parting from Ash and the others in Johto, Ethan and Erika had gone to the nearest port and boarded the ship that brought them here.

True to its name, Littleroot was a country town surrounded by fresh, unspoiled nature, as though it had yet to be colored by anything else.

It was still a town with a small harbor, though, and there were even a few tall buildings near the waterfront. The countryside and the city met here.

At the other end of town stood Professor Birch's home and laboratory. Like Professor Oak in Kanto and Professor Elm in Johto, Birch was Hoenn's leading professor and the one entrusted with giving starter Pokemon to new Trainers.

As someone entirely new to Hoenn, Ethan meant to begin his next journey here too.

He and Erika did not drop in on Professor Birch, however. They had never met him, had no particular reason to visit, and had no one to introduce them. They could get acquainted another time.

Ethan's first task in Hoenn was to register for the Hoenn League. Only then could he challenge the region's Gyms. When they asked people nearby, however, they learned that Littleroot had no Pokemon Center. He would have to register in neighboring Oldale Town.

What a bother. Ethan shook his head. This is where so many new Trainers set out, but the League hasn't put a Pokemon Center here. You'd think they could make an exception.

Erika shook her head. They must have their reasons. The Pokemon League may be the world's largest organization, but its funding is limited. It can't provide everything everywhere.

After several days aboard ship, both were full of energy. They did not linger in Littleroot, but headed north for Oldale Town.

Hoenn lay southwest of Johto, with an ocean between them. Although the regions occupied different landmasses, their customs and general feel were much alike.

Hoenn had all sorts of natural environments, from tropical rainforests to deserts, and islands of every size surrounded the mainland. Overall, its climate was warmer and its vegetation more varied than in Johto or Kanto.

Ethan remembered that Hoenn was supposedly based on Japan's Kyushu island, turned in a different direction. He also recalled that its name came from the characters for abundant bonds, a place rich in connections. Whether that was true, he could not say.

They took their time along the country road out of Littleroot, enjoying the scenery and watching the Pokemon they encountered. Most were familiar from Kanto and Johto, but this was their first time seeing species such as Poochyena and Zigzagoon.

Of course, Ethan had known those Pokemon from games and anime for years. Seeing living creatures with his own eyes instead of cold electronic data was another matter. In that sense, this really was his first encounter with them.

As they drew near Oldale, they spotted ancient ruins in the distance.

More than a dozen huge oval stones stood on a stretch of barren ground. Half buried, they surrounded the remains of several buildings, almost as if guarding them.

Curious, Ethan and Erika went over for a closer look.

Nothing fenced the ruins off; anyone seemed free to visit. Behind the standing stones were the remains of low houses built from rock. No one could tell how long they had stood there. Parts had weathered away, leaving the marks of age everywhere.

Several people dressed like scholars were busy among the ruins. One looked up, noticed the visitors, and came to meet them.

Hello. He was a man of about twenty-seven or twenty-eight, with tanned skin, work clothes, and a short ponytail. To Ethan, he looked a little like Brock with his eyes open. The man glanced between them and smiled. Have you come to see the Oldale Ruins?

Oldale Ruins?

That's right. These are the Oldale Ruins. The town nearby was even named after them. He caught himself. I forgot to introduce myself. I'm Alden, a researcher studying the ruins here.

Nice to meet you. I'm Ethan, a Pokemon Trainer.

And I'm Erika.

Would you like to look around? Alden asked. Perhaps afraid they had the wrong idea about his archaeological work, he added, People know very little about this place, and it hasn't received much attention. I'm trying to help more people learn about the Oldale Ruins.

I see.

Now Ethan understood why Alden had approached them. He exchanged a glance with Erika, and they followed the researcher into the ruins.

Alden's explanation gave them a general picture of the site. Ethan noticed, though, that the researchers were using instruments to probe what looked like an ordinary ruin.

Mr. Alden, he asked, is there something here that hasn't been discovered yet?

Alden nodded. These ruins conceal a doorway linking the ancient Pokemon world and the modern one.

A doorway?

An actual door. It stands outside a stone chamber and has a peculiar mechanism we haven't been able to open. If we force our way in, the mechanism will trigger and destroy the whole structure. So we still know nothing about what's behind it.

Ethan nearly spoke, then held his tongue.

As far as he could see, they did not need to break the door to get into the chamber. A Ghost-type Pokemon could pass through the wall.

A person could not follow, of course, but the Pokemon could at least see what was inside.

Then again, if the doorway held some strange power and transported whoever passed through it elsewhere, that would be a different matter.

Erika asked, What did you mean by a link to the ancient world?

Ancient Pokemon, Alden said with feeling. I suspect there may be extinct Pokemon behind the chamber door, like Aerodactyl or Kabutops. There might even be species we haven't discovered yet.

He looked at Ethan and smiled. I guessed you were Trainers as soon as I saw you. I've invited several others into the chamber before, hoping their Pokemon could help me solve the door's mystery without damaging it.

He did not have to finish. Clearly, none of those Trainers had succeeded.

By then they had reached the chamber entrance.

No one knew what kind of stone had been used to build it, but unlike the rest of the ruins, the chamber remained remarkably intact and solid. It had stood for thousands of years and looked capable of standing for thousands more.

Ancient builders' ingenuity was nothing to dismiss.

Ethan and Erika stepped closer. The door was a single heavy stone slab with no handle or keyhole, only several grooves. Something apparently needed to be fitted into them to open it.

Ethan pushed against the cold stone. It felt immensely heavy and did not move an inch.

Alden was right: they would need to find the proper way to open the chamber.

Looking at the door, Ethan suddenly remembered something. Wasn't this the first mystery Ash encountered after arriving in Hoenn and meeting May?

Thinking it over, he vaguely recalled that the chamber led underground. There was a subterranean lake inhabited by an ancient fish Pokemon, along with a few murals worth studying. Beyond that, there was nothing else.

What was the fish Pokemon called again?

RightRelicanth. It was an ugly-looking Pokemon about which people knew little. They had not even found an evolved form for it.

More importantly, it was not unique to these ruins. Relicanth could also be found in deep undersea caves.

Once he remembered that, Ethan lost all interest in opening the chamber.

He would leave it to Ash. Ash would be here in a few days, and Ethan had no need to wear himself out prying open this stone door.

He and Erika made a show of examining it. After a while, they both shook their heads at Alden. The researcher was used to disappointment and did not seem too disheartened.

They spent a little longer exploring the site. As the day grew late, they said goodbye to Alden and continued toward Oldale Town.

Oldale was a place where little things gathered into something greater, a lovely town of colorful flowers and green trees.

It lay in southern Hoenn. Petalburg City was to the west, while the main road north led toward Mauville City and Slateport City. Many routes passed through Oldale.

New Trainers leaving Littleroot would part ways here, setting out in different directions to challenge Hoenn's Gyms and begin their adventures.

By the time Ethan and Erika arrived, dusk had fallen.

They went straight to the Pokemon Center. As in Kanto and Johto, Nurse Joy worked there, caring for Pokemon and the Trainers who stayed overnight.

Welcome, she said, greeting them with a sweet smile.

Hello, Nurse Joy. I'm here to register for the Hoenn League. Ethan introduced himself and handed her his Pokedex.

One moment, please.

Nurse Joy took the Pokedex and entered a few things into her computer. Then she saw Ethan's record: champion of both the Indigo and Silver Conferences, plus victories in the smaller Orange Islands and Whirl Islands tournaments.

What an incredible record!

She gave Ethan a surprised glance, but kept her composure. After completing his registration, she returned the Pokedex.

You're registered, Mr. Ethan. Good luck with your Hoenn challenge!

Ethan accepted it, but did not leave yet. He went to a transfer machine nearby and contacted Chloe at the distant Cerise Laboratory.

Now that he had reached a new region, it was time to adjust his team.

He and Chloe exchanged a few pleasantries. Then he transferred Blastoise, Venusaur, Jolteon, and Crystal Steelix back to her. All four had distinguished themselves at the Silver Conference and no longer needed more training on the road.

They were already strong enough to compete in a major tournament. He only had to make sure they did not lose their edge.

That left nine Pokemon with him: Gardevoir, Gengar, Dragonite, Scizor, Tyranitar, Eevee, Raikou, Suicune, and Celebi.

Gardevoir and Gengar were permanent members of his team. He would never swap them out; wherever he traveled, they would remain by his side.

Celebi was a new companion. He needed to strengthen their bond and keep his promise to let it taste more delicious food.

He had told Erika aboard the ship that he had caught Celebi. She had not seemed surprised. Instead, she had been sincerely happy that the man she loved had managed to catch it.

After his three legendary birds, Suicune and Raikou were his other trump cards for the journey. Naturally, he wanted to keep them close.

That left Dragonite, Scizor, Tyranitar, and Eevee as the four regular Pokemon he planned to train most in Hoenn. He wanted to bring them up to the level of Jolteon and Crystal Steelix.

Of course, four regular Pokemon would not be enough for the Ever Grande Conference. He would need to catch several more.

Night had fallen by the time they left the Pokemon Center, so they found a hotel in Oldale for the evening.

After dinner, they walked arm in arm through the quiet town, taking their time to feel what made this new region different from Kanto and Johto.

But the wind felt the same, and the forests were just as thick.

If the town's name had not told Ethan he was in Hoenn, he might never have known the difference.

Chapter 590: Catching Torchic

After a night's rest and breakfast the next morning, Ethan and Erika left Oldale Town.

Apart from the Oldale Ruins, there was little else to see. They had no reason to spend more time there.

They put their heads together over the route for a while. In the end, Ethan decided to visit Petalburg City first, then make a wide circuit through Rustboro City, Fallarbor Town, Fortree City, Lilycove City, Mossdeep City, Sootopolis City, and Pacifidlog Town. From there they would return to Hoenn's mainland and challenge the Gyms in Slateport City and Mauville City.

It was only a preliminary plan. If anything changed, they could alter the route whenever they needed to.

Before challenging a Gym, though, Ethan wanted to catch a few Pokemon and expand his team.

He could not keep using Pokemon that had already fought in a conference. They would win him badges easily, but the battles would do little to develop his team.

Where nearby might he find a Pokemon he liked?

His gaze settled on the mountains in the distance.

Trainers had already searched the roadside woods and grasslands thoroughly. There might still be rare Pokemon hidden deep in those mountains.

After packing supplies, Ethan and Erika left the main road and headed into the hills.

The farther they went from town, the rougher the way became. They often had to change direction through ankle-high grass, keeping watch as they waded across streams or pushed into dense forest.

Both were used to such journeys. They could still chat as they walked, hardly troubled by the obstacles.

The landscape around them grew greener and greener.

With no one else likely to see them this far from town, Ethan let Celebi and Eevee out together.

Eevee was one of the Pokemon he hoped to train most in Hoenn, and he expected a great deal of it. It had far too much energy to stay quiet, though. One moment it sniffed something to the east, the next it was nosing around to the west, and between discoveries it played with Celebi.

With those two beside them, Ethan and Erika never felt bored.

After a long walk they reached the foot of a mountain. Just as they were about to climb, something flashed through the grass at their side and ran off.

They looked up in time to see a wild Ralts disappear into a distant thicket.

Ralts...

The familiar sight stirred a rush of feeling in Ethan.

That was right: wild Ralts lived in Hoenn. They were still rare here, but a small number of Trainers had already caught them.

Ralts was Gardevoir's first form, and Gardevoir had been Ethan's very first Pokemon. She had stayed with him through the hardest part of his journey.

But both he and Gardevoir had grown so much since then. They could never go back to how they were.

He sighed.

It was a fond memory, and a bittersweet one.

When his thoughts settled, Ethan and Erika began climbing.

There were noticeably more wild Pokemon on the mountain. The lower slopes still held mostly common species, though. Even by the time they reached halfway up, they had passed dozens of different Pokemon without wanting to catch any.

That was hardly surprising. If rare Pokemon were so easy to find, they would be everywhere.

Ethan had caught some of his own Pokemon because he knew the anime's story and where to look. Searching a mountain like this was a matter of lucka blind chance of stumbling upon the right one.

Habitats and territory mattered too. Unless a Pokemon wandered or migrated, turning over every stone on a particular mountain or around a lake would reveal only the few species that lived there.

The path grew steeper. Ethan and Erika stopped talking and concentrated on the climb.

By the time they reached the summit, Ethan had broken a light sweat despite the stamina he had built over his long travels.

They had found no rare Pokemon, but the view was worth the effort. Oldale Town and the Oldale Ruins lay spread out below them.

After enjoying the mountain breeze, Ethan grew hungry. He and Erika set up a temporary camp.

They meant to eat lunch, rest a while, and then head back down. But just as the meal finished cooking, its aroma spreading through the air, a nearby patch of grass rustled.

Something was hiding there.

Celebi noticed it first and clutched its food protectively, as if afraid the newcomer would steal a bite.

Eevee ran up to the grass and barked at it.

The grass shook again. Startled by Eevee, a tiny Pokemon like a young chick leaped out in a panic.

Wait, wasn't that...?

Although he had never seen one in person, Ethan recognized it at once: Torchic, the first form of Blaziken.

It had a small chick-like body covered in fluffy orange feathers and two tiny wings. It clearly could not fly.

Ethan took out his Pokedex and pointed it at Torchic.

Beep. Torchic, the Chick Pokemon. Fire type. Torchic has a flame sac inside its body, and the fire burns for as long as it lives. Holding one is as warm as holding a hot-water bottle. When attacked, it spits fireballs formed in its belly. These scorching fireballs can reach one thousand degrees Celsius and burn an opponent. Torchic fears nights so dark it cannot see its own feet. It pecks at the ground to swallow small stones that help its digestion and raise the temperature of the flames it breathestwo benefits from one stone.

Back at Cerise Laboratory, Ethan had asked Professor Cerise to download information from regions around the world onto his Pokedex. He did not need an update in Hoenn; it worked here as usual.

He liked Torchic and both of its evolutions, Combusken and Blaziken. Even before arriving in Hoenn, he had put Blaziken on his list of Pokemon he absolutely wanted to catch.

And now he had found a Torchic here. It was as if a pillow had appeared the moment he felt sleepy. The hard trip into this remote place had paid off.

Still...

What was Torchic doing up here?

Most Fire-type Pokemon preferred drier places. Few would come alone to a mountaintop like this.

When Torchic started to flee, Ethan quickly called Eevee back. Did the smell draw you here? Would you like some?

Torchic had not yet reacted, but Celebi hurriedly shielded its plate. It seemed terrified that Ethan might give away its portion.

Torchic hesitated at Ethan's words. It knew nothing about these humans and did not really want to approach, but the food smelled too good. The aroma had drawn it here before it could stop itself.

Seeing its uncertainty, Ethan smiled. How about this? Have a battle with me.

He pointed to Eevee. If you beat Eevee, you can eat anything here. If you lose, you'll come with me and become my Pokemon. What do you say?

Torchic looked up at Ethan, then at the eager Eevee. Its little brow furrowed as it weighed the offer.

Ethan did not want to give it too long to think. What's there to decide? Don't tell me you're scared. Or do you doubt you can win?

At being called frightened by a human, Torchic flared up.

It was bold by nature. Otherwise, it would never have followed the smell and hidden so close to them in the first place. It would not let this human look down on it.

It cried out fiercely at Ethan. He did not need Gengar to translate: I'm not scared! Come at me!

Ethan and Erika exchanged a glance, and both smiled.

Ethan was pleased his provocation had worked. Erika shook her head in amused exasperation.

For a grown man to resort to such a childish trick! He could have let Eevee attack, defeated Torchic, and caught it outright.

A patch of open ground lay beside their camp. Torchic strode over with its head high, and Eevee bounded out to face it.

Ethan gave no commands for this capture battle. He sat comfortably to one side and watched.

He looked almost like a spectator.

That did not mean he was indifferent. Both Pokemon were still in their first forms, but Eevee had traveled with him for some time and fought in battles large and small. It had the experience to handle this without his help.

The two Pokemon faced one another with a dozen or so meters between them. Neither backed down. As though they had reached the same decision at once, they suddenly charged.

Ethan sat up a little straighter and watched Torchic's movements closely.

When it reached Eevee, Torchic lifted a claw and swiped at its face. Eevee was a little faster. It twisted aside and avoided the blow.

Then Eevee slammed into Torchic. The little Pokemon stumbled and nearly fell, but regained its balance after several steps to the side.

It did not retreat. Its belly swelled, and a burst of sparks flew from its open beak toward Eevee.

At such close range, the flames caught Eevee. It had learned how to deal with fire during its earlier travels, though. It rolled across the ground until the sandy soil smothered the flames.

The brief injury did not slow Eevee much. It got up and grappled with Torchic again.

After watching for a while, Ethan saw that Torchic kept returning to the same few attacks. It had no unusual moves, and at this level it could not defeat Eevee.

Sure enough, as the battle continued, Torchic visibly tired. At last it fell to Eevee's Swift.

Ethan took out the Poke Ball he had prepared and threw it at the fallen Pokemon.

Bang!

Red light wrapped around Torchic and drew it into the ball. The ball shook a few times, then clicked and fell still.

Good. He had caught Torchic!

Ethan picked up the Poke Ball and immediately let his new Pokemon out again.

Erika tended to both Pokemon's injuries and gave Torchic a taste of her cooking. Within minutes of meeting them, it had become completely at ease.

Ethan laughed softly as he watched Torchic play with Eevee and Celebi, with none of its earlier awkwardness left.

A Pokemon with a nature like that was easy to befriend. Treat it kindly, and it would return that kindness.

Thanks to Torchic's temperament, Ethan's long search had not been wasted. The trip had brought him an unexpected new Pokemon.

Counting Torchic, he had obtained nineteen Pokemon over the course of his travels. If he included Latias and Latios in the Water Capital, the total was twenty-one.

It was not an enormous number, but every one of those Pokemon was exceptional.

They rested at the summit until their strength returned. Then Ethan packed their things, and he and Erika started down.

They had come with hopes and were leaving satisfied.

He was so pleased that he hummed through most of the descent.

At the foot of the mountain, he recalled Celebi and Eevee to avoid attracting attention. He kept Torchic beside him so they could spend more time together and deepen their bond.

By the time they regained the main road and reached Petalburg City that evening, Torchic was entirely comfortable with Ethan. It looked like a Pokemon that had lived with him all along.

Petalburg stood in southwestern Hoenn. It was neither large nor populous, yet it was famous far beyond its borders.

That was because Norman, the Petalburg Gym Leader, was so strong that many novice Trainers hesitated to challenge him.

People said Norman's family had originally lived in Johto and had moved to Hoenn only so he could fulfill his duties as a Gym Leader.

He had pursued strength all his life. People often said he seemed born for Pokemon.

It was too late for Ethan to call at the Gym and issue a challenge now. He would have to wait until the next morning.

Chapter 591: May and Max

Early the next morning, Ethan and Erika visited the Petalburg Gym.

The Gym stood on the outskirts of the city, backed by two green mountains. It looked like an old Japanese estate, enclosed by tall white walls. Without the sign reading Petalburg Gym over its entrance, most people would never have guessed it was a Pokemon Gym.

They climbed the steps. The doors were open and no attendant was in sight, so Ethan walked in.

Inside was an enormous traditional dojo. It was deserted and very quiet; the only sound was Ethan and Erika's footsteps echoing on the floor.

Hello? Is anyone here?

Ethan called out. After waiting a while without an answer, he raised his voice and called again.

At last, someone came running from the other side of the building.

But Ethan saw that it was only a boy of about seven. The child was short, with black-framed glasses, bushy eyebrows, and medium-length hair. He wore a T-shirt and shorts and looked like the sort of youngster who knew every bit of Pokemon theory.

He looked almost exactly as he had in the anime. Ethan recognized him at once: May's younger brother and Gym Leader Norman's son, Max.

Coming! Coming! Max ran up to Ethan. As soon as he saw Ethan's face clearly, he pointed at him and cried, Oh! It's you!

Ethan tilted his head. You know me?

Of course! I've been watching the Silver Conference for the past two daysthe live matches and the replays. You're Ethan, the Champion!

Ethan was a little surprised that Max recognized him, but it made sense. The boy loved learning and knew a great deal about Pokemon. In the anime, he had recognized Ash the first time they met and even known which match had knocked Ash out of the tournament.

That's me. Ethan smiled. Is Mr. Norman here? I've come to challenge the Petalburg Gym.

Challenge my dad... Max started to answer, then remembered something and smiled sheepishly. Oh, I almost forgot. Dad went out early this morning. He might not be back for several days.

What? Ethan stared at him. He's gone?

Yeah. He left only half an hour ago. He told me to close the front doors and put a notice outside, but the match I was watching was getting exciting and I forgot.

Well, that was unfortunate.

Ethan and Erika exchanged a helpless look. Half an hour earlier, and they might have caught him.

But while Ethan looked disappointed, Erika shot him a sharp glare.

Whose fault was this?

His, of course. They had both woken early and were almost dressed for breakfast when he had suddenly felt amorous and insisted on pulling her back into bed.

If he had not kept them there for so long, they would have arrived in time.

Ethan understood her look. He gave a rueful smile and shook his head.

He had meant well. Calling at the Gym too early might have disturbed Norman, so he had deliberately delayed them. Who could have predicted Norman would leave?

I see. Ethan sighed. Did Mr. Norman say what he was doing, or where we could find him?

Well... Max scratched his head. I'm not sure exactly. My sister might know. I'll go get her!

He dashed across the Gym and vanished through a door before Ethan could respond. The boy really was eager to help him.

Before long, Max returned, using both hands to pull a pretty young girl into the dojo.

She was about Misty's age. Shoulder-length brown hair curled outward at the sides, and her lovely features promised that she would grow into a beautiful woman.

Ethan knew her immediately. She was May, the popular traveling companion who would join Ash in the anime's third generation after Misty left.

May was every bit as pretty as Misty, but quieter without being dull. She could be quite clever too.

Ethan had reached Hoenn a few days before Ash. May would ride her bicycle to Professor Birch's laboratory in Littleroot Town to receive her first Pokemon around the same day Ash arrived.

They would meet there as though by fate and begin traveling together.

Ash was still two or three days away. That was why Ethan could meet May here now.

Max had dragged her toward the battlefield so suddenly that she did not know what was happening. She was about to scold him for rushing around when she saw the man and woman waiting there. Understanding the situation, she composed herself.

I'm sorry. May bowed lightly to Ethan and Erika. The Pokemon League called my father away on urgent business. Before he left, he said he might not return for three days.

Three days...

Ethan could not wait here that long. If he left, though, he would have to visit other cities first and come back to challenge Norman after his return.

There's nothing for it, then. I'll come back another time.

He shook his head and was about to turn away when Max called out again.

Mr. Ethan, wait!

Ethan and May both turned to look at him.

What is it? Ethan asked.

As if by magic, Max produced a pen and notebook from behind his back. He held them out hopefully. Could I have your autograph? I'm a fan!

Ethan laughed. He had not expected his Johto victories to win him a fan all the way in Hoenn, let alone a boy who would become an important character in the anime.

Of course. He took the pen and notebook. Although he already knew, he asked, What's your name?

Max straightened to attention. How rude of me! I'm Max, and I'm seven. I want to travel like you and become a great Trainer like my dad!

That's an excellent dream. Mr. Norman is strong and respected, so you couldn't ask for a better example. I'm sure he'd be proud to hear you say that.

Ethan signed the notebook's first page with a few quick strokes. When Max opened it, he read: May you always remember why you began, and may your dream come true. Your friend, Ethan.

Max trembled with excitement.

Ethan handed back the pen and was about to leave when he noticed May looking down curiously at his Torchic. An idea came to him.

Do you like it?

May glanced at Ethan, then back at Torchic. She neither agreed nor disagreed.

It's cute. What is it called?

Despite being a Gym Leader's daughter with a younger brother who loved Pokemon and knew so much about them, May knew surprisingly little herself.

After receiving her starter from Professor Birch, she would encounter a wild Pokemon and naively throw a Poke Ball at it, thinking she could catch it without a battle.

In battle, she would also fail to understand type matchups, leaving her Pokemon knocked down. Ash, a master of fighting against type disadvantages, would have to explain the basics to her from his own experience.

It was quite remarkable.

And May's first Pokemon would, of course, be a Torchic too.

It's called Torchic. It's a Fire-type Pokemon.

A Fire-type Torchic... May nodded without entirely understanding. Its feathers look so fluffy and warm. I bet it feels nice to touch.

It's strong too. You're about the right age, and you're a Gym Leader's daughter. You'll be getting your first Pokemon and setting out soon, won't you?

May's eyes brightened at the mention of travel. The prospect of seeing the world clearly appealed to her more than Pokemon did.

That's right. Once Dad comes back from his League business, I'll go to Littleroot Town and see Professor Birch.

I thought so. Ethan nodded. Treecko and Mudkip are good choices too, but if you can't decide, consider Torchic. Believe me, you won't regret it.

Torchic...

May looked again at the little orange chick beside Ethan's feet.

Whatever its type, its appearance suited her tastes.

Yes, like that man's Torchic. It could be a good choice.

After Ethan and Erika left the Gym, May gathered her thoughts. Turning around, she found Max grinning foolishly at his notebook.

You asked him for an autograph. Is he famous?

Come on! Max shot her an exasperated look. You don't know him? He won both the Silver Conference and the Indigo Conference! He overwhelmed his opponents with sheer strength, and you don't know who he is?

Really? He's that strong?

May pictured Ethan again. To her, he had looked like a handsome, gentle man. She could hardly connect him with a Champion.

Oh, right, Max said. What did he tell you?

Nothing much. He suggested that I choose Torchic as my first Pokemon.

Torchic... Max frowned and thought it over. He can't be wrong. I was going to recommend Treecko, but if Mr. Ethan says that, maybe Torchic really is stronger. And Fire beats Grass, so when you choose...

He trailed off, looked at his sister again, and thought about her personality. Then he nodded firmly.

I see it now. Why didn't I think of that? Maybe Torchic really would suit you better.

...

Outside the Gym, Ethan and Erika paused by the entrance and brought up a map on their phone.

If they followed the route they had planned, missing the Petalburg Gym now was no great problem. They would circle Hoenn and return here eventually; Ethan could challenge Norman then.

It would change the order of his Gym battles, but there was nothing to be done.

They put the disappointment behind them and headed out of Petalburg City.

Like Oldale and Littleroot, Petalburg was no major tourist destination and had no especially famous scenery. With the Gym challenge postponed, they had no reason to stay.

Next was Rustboro City to the north, where another Gym awaited Ethan.

Getting there would take them a long way past the sea and through the famous Petalburg Woods. It would not be an easy trip.

But that was what traveling meant: covering dull stretches of road while learning about the world, meeting new people, and training Pokemon.

Leaving Petalburg, they continued west along the main road. Before long, they reached Hoenn's long, winding western coast.

Ethan did not know what lay across the water. But as he looked over the broad blue sea, his regret at missing Norman that morning faded away.

Golden sand stretched along the shore, and many Trainers were out on the beach. Erika suggested, Shall we walk by the sea? We might find a Water-type Pokemon native to Hoenn.

Ethan nodded. He had no objection.

They slowed and headed toward the sand. In his mind, Ethan ran through all the Water-type Pokemon of Hoenn.

Except for Kyogre, they seemed common enough. None struck him as worth searching for specifically.

He glanced at Erika and saw how interested she was. Smiling, he let the thought go.

Forget searching for Pokemon. He could spend time with the woman he loved and relax.

Chapter 592: Catching Feebas

The beach was broad and close to both the main road and Petalburg City. It was a natural place to raise Pokemon.

New Trainers were everywhere, turning over gravel and rocks in search of Pokemon hidden beneath them.

They were not demanding. A Krabby, Tentacool, Shellder, or almost any other Pokemon would make them happy for a while.

Some Trainers were even battling nearby, testing their skills against one another.

For beginners, this was a hunting ground and one of the easiest places to find wild Pokemon outside forests and grasslands.

Trainers were not the only visitors. Families of three and young couples wandered along the shore too.

Ethan and Erika looked like an ordinary couple. No one paid them much attention beyond a passing thought that they made a good-looking pair.

After enjoying the sea breeze and wading in the shallows, they watched Torchic pace at their side, dodging the waves as though terrified of getting its feathers wet. They both found it funny.

They stood there quietly for a while. Then Erika turned to Ethan. Since we're here, aren't you going to turn over a few rocks like the others? You might find a surprise.

What rare Pokemon would be in a place like this?

Ethan shook his head, unconvinced. But with nothing else to do, he left the sand and made his way among the rocks.

They had moved away from the crowd earlier to avoid being disturbed. No one else was near this secluded part of the shore. The tide was going out, exposing much of the rock that usually lay beneath the sea.

Stepping from one rock to the next, Ethan looked down at his feet.

Seawater remained in the hollows, forming little pools after the tide had retreated. Pokemon that had not escaped in time were stranded in them.

Even on a short walk, he saw quite a few.

A wild Horsea was hiding between two rocks. As Ethan leaped over it, the Pokemon unexpectedly squirted ink at him.

He barely dodged. Frowning, Ethan jumped down and paid it back with a kick that sent it toward the sea.

Horsea spun through the air a dozen times before landing in the water with a splash.

Hmph. Rough as that looked, he had saved its life.

A few steps later, two tentacles lunged at him. Ethan seized them and found a Tentacool trying to ambush him.

He frowned again, pulled the tentacles up, wrapped them around a small rock, and tied a knot.

That would teach it to attack him. Let it see what it could do without free tentacles. It could wait there for someone else to catch it.

After those two encounters, Ethan lost interest in searching. Seeing that he had strayed far from Erika, he found a relatively flat route back.

He had gone only a few steps when he heard a faint flapping sound nearby.

Something was stranded in the shallows, struggling to save itself. He could hardly ignore it. Ethan changed course and went around a huge rock.

On the other side, a fish Pokemon lay in a tiny, shallow pool. Most of its body was above the surface, and it beat its tail repeatedly, trying to work its way back to the sea.

So it had been stranded by the tide.

The sea was still some distance away, separated from the pool by a wide stretch of rock. The fish could barely move now. Even if it could, it would likely dry out before it reached the water.

Ethan looked closer. Its body was dull yellow-brown and uneven, like an ordinary fish made uglier. It had a vacant stare, thick lips, and fins that looked torn and ragged.

Erika came around the rock just then. She had seen Ethan start back toward her and suddenly veer away, so curiosity had brought her over.

She saw the Pokemon, whose appearance was far from her idea of beautiful.

What Pokemon is that? It looks a little... strange.

Erika's good manners let her put her surprise gently. Someone else might have simply called it ugly.

Ethan smiled. Have you heard of a remarkable fish that's terribly ugly before it evolves, but becomes a beautiful Pokemon with scales that shine in different colors under the sun?

There is a Pokemon like that? Erika looked down at the stranded fish. You mean this one?

As a Trainer, she knew plenty about Pokemon, but her expertise was mostly in the Grass types of Kanto and Johto. She had never met this species or even heard of it.

Ethan nodded. It's called Feebas. It can survive even in a filthy ditch. It looks dull, and it's easy to catch, but most Trainers want nothing to do with something so ugly and ragged. Few know how beautiful it becomes after evolving.

He took out his Pokedex and pointed it at Feebas.

Beep. Feebas, the Fish Pokemon. Water type. Feebas lives in many habitats and gathers in large numbers in rivers rich with aquatic plants or on the seabed. Although abundant, they prefer to live in groups. They have remarkable vitality and swim well. This hardy Pokemon will eat anything and does not mind polluted water, making it a subject of study for many researchers.

Ethan called up an image of Milotic and handed the Pokedex to Erika.

See? This is what it becomes. Beautiful, isn't it?

Erika looked at the lovely Pokemon on the screen, then at the Feebas in the pool. She could hardly believe they were connected.

Incredible, she said. There's such a difference before and after evolution. I can't see a trace of its old appearance.

Exactly. Ethan put the Pokedex away. Most people don't know Milotic evolves from Feebas. They treat it as an extremely rare Pokemon in its own right.

Erika glanced around. There was only one Feebas here. She understood.

The Pokedex said they live in groups. It must have been left behind accidentally when the tide went out.

That seems likely. Look at these rocks. They're low, but together they form a wall around the pool. Even though the water receded slowly, it trapped Feebas until the sea was gone and left it exposed to the air.

After all that explanation, Erika saw Ethan take out a Poke Ball. You're going to catch it?

He nodded. I need another Water-type Pokemon. Feebas is weak, and its looks put most Trainers off, but with enough care it will evolve into Milotic. Milotic is beautiful and quite strong.

Ethan threw the ball. Feebas looked so weak that he expected no resistance. But as soon as the red light drew it inside, the ball shook once and Feebas burst back out.

Unwilling to believe it, he picked up the ball and tried again. This time, too, Feebas escaped after barely two seconds.

What a stubborn will to live.

Ethan finally understood why scholars studied the species. Even stranded in a tiny pool, this one still had strength to struggle.

No wonder Feebas could survive in ditches and polluted water.

He waved Torchic over. This one's up to you. Knock it out.

Torchic tilted its head, then opened its beak and used Ember. The little flame struck Feebas without doing much harm and quickly went out in the pool.

Ethan sighed. Don't use Ember. Get closer and use Scratch.

Torchic approached and swiped with a claw. It took two scratches to knock Feebas unconscious.

Ethan threw his Poke Ball at the motionless fish. This time, the capture succeeded.

Good. He had caught his twentieth Pokemon!

Satisfied with his find, Ethan left the beach with Erika.

Before coming here, he had not expected to catch anything. Yet in only two days in Hoenn, he had already caught two Pokemon.

Hoenn really was a treasure trove. There were so many wild Pokemon here. Perhaps that was why its Gym Leaders and Trainers were a little stronger on average than those in Kanto and Johto.

Back on the main road, they headed north and soon reached the entrance to Petalburg Woods.

Night was approaching. They were far from the city, with no houses nearby, so it seemed they would have to camp outdoors.

Since that was settled, they entered the woods while there was still daylight.

If they had to sleep outside, what difference did it make whether they camped in grassland or forest?

Petalburg Woods reminded Ethan of Viridian Forest in Kanto. Dense branches shut out much of the light, leaving the interior dim and easy to get lost in.

Both forests held plenty of Bug-type Pokemon. Petalburg Woods had other species too, giving it a wider variety of life.

And almost as many Trainers came to catch Pokemon here as in Viridian Forest.

They walked for a while. As the sun sank, the whole forest darkened.

Ethan and Erika chose a level spot near water and stopped for the night.

They had barely pitched their tent when a huge Zigzagoon approached their camp in a zigzagging path.

Ordinary Zigzagoon were small, less than half a meter tall and weighing a little over thirty pounds. This one was nearly six feet tall, almost the size of a person.

Ethan wondered if they had met a dominant wild Pokemon and trespassed on its territory. He was about to warn his team to be ready when the Zigzagoon rose onto its hind legs and stood like a human.

Before he could recover from that surprise, it reached up with both hands and pulled off its own head.

In the fading light, Ethan stared. But as the figure stepped closer, he saw it was no Zigzagoon. It was a big boy wearing a Zigzagoon costume. The head he had removed was only a mask.

Hey, you two!

Before Ethan could speak, the boy called out, Don't camp here! You're ruining my plan!

His angry tone made Ethan narrow his eyes.

Why? Does this forest belong to you? he replied coldly. We'll camp where we like.

The boy ran up to him. I've been hiding here for half the day trying to get close to the Zigzagoon! Then you arrived and scared them all away!

Before setting up camp, Ethan had seen several Zigzagoon on the clearing. He had paid them little mind. He had simply sent Torchic charging forward, and they had fled into the trees. Looking back, he supposed this was their habitat.

Who would have imagined someone dressed like this was hiding nearby?

Up close, Ethan noticed that the boy looked remarkably like Ash. Apart from his slightly different hairstyle, he might have been a larger, equally impulsive version of him.

If Ethan had not known Delia had only one child, he might have mistaken this boy for Ash's long-lost older brother.

So what? Ethan glanced at him. If the boy had spoken politely, Ethan would have been friendly in return. With that attitude, he saw no reason to smile. If they ran off, go after them. Or can you only catch them by dressing up and sneaking close enough for an ambush?

Chapter 593: Nicholai and Team Magma

What are you talking about? The boy did not seem to hear Ethan's mockery at all. Do you know how hard I worked to get close to those Zigzagoon? Look at this outfit. It took me ages to make!

Ethan had the impression that the boy was not terribly bright.

Who tried to approach Zigzagoon like this? He was not a Pokemon Watcher. Even if they failed to spot him, what would he do once he got close? He would still need to battle them to catch one.

Besides, it was hardly Ethan's fault. The Zigzagoon had moved away when he arrived. He had not driven them off.

If even one of them had tried to stay or defend the clearing, Ethan would not have pitched his tent here.

Shaking his head, Ethan said, Instead of wasting time arguing with me, you could go after them. They may not have gone far.

The boy did not leave. He looked at Torchic beside Ethan.

You're a Trainer too, aren't you? he called. Then battle me!

Battle you?

Ethan looked him over. The boy wore every thought on his face. His mood changed in an instant, and whatever came into his head came out of his mouth. He could hide nothing.

There was no point getting angry with someone like that. He would drag Ethan down to his level and beat him with experience. But words alone were unlikely to make him go away.

You really are persistent. Ethan rose from his folding chair and walked to an open patch of ground. I suppose you won't leave until we've battled.

The boy's irritation vanished the moment Ethan agreed. Great! Let's start!

He took out a Poke Ball, aimed it at the ground, and pressed the button. A flash of blue light released a Mudkip in front of Ethan.

Despite its fishlike appearance, Mudkip was no fish at all.

One of Hoenn's three starter Pokemon, it was every bit as popular as Torchic. It looked soft and slippery, like an amphibious mud salamander from Earth.

Mudkip had slick blue skin and a small, nimble body. An upright fin rose from its head, bright orange gills marked its cheeks, and its tail fin was enormous.

It usually rested buried in the mud of a riverbed. In water, it breathed through its cheek gills. The fin on its head was a sensitive radar, detecting movements in water and air without relying on sight.

It was remarkably strong. It could swim at great speed and push against the ground with all four legs. When threatened, its muscles alone could break a rock larger than its body.

This Mudkip looked as though it had not been traveling long. It was still young and had not evolved into Marshtomp.

Then again, like Ash's Pikachu, it might have chosen not to evolve despite having great strength.

Strong or weak, one battle would tell Ethan what he needed to know.

After a moment's thought, he took a Poke Ball from his belt pouch and sent out Eevee.

The opposing Pokemon did not look especially formidable. Eevee should be able to handle it.

The two Pokemon took their positions, with Ethan and the boy standing behind their partners.

Personality shaped battle style. At the start, the boy threw himself into commanding Mudkip. At his order, it charged Eevee headfirst.

Eevee, dodge!

Ethan knew Mudkip was strong and had no intention of letting it land that hit. Eevee slipped aside, then counterattacked.

It twisted clear of Mudkip's rush, bared two rows of sharp teeth, and bit into its opponent.

Ethan did not know what Mudkip tasted like, but from its pained expression he knew Eevee had bitten hard.

Shake it off! the boy shouted.

Mudkip thrashed, but Eevee held on. However much Mudkip twisted, it could not break free.

At last Eevee let go on its own, giving Mudkip a moment to breathe.

Seeing that Eevee was faster, the boy changed tactics. At his command, Mudkip fired a Water Gun from farther away.

The stream curved through the air toward Eevee.

Eevee was a little faster than Mudkip, but it could not normally move quickly enough to dodge a Water Gun. On its own, it would be hit.

Ethan had an answer.

Eevee, Quick Attack!

Eevee accelerated sharply, slipped past the water just before it struck, and rammed into Mudkip again.

Mudkip staggered backward. Without waiting for another command, it scooped up a clump of mud and hurled it at Eevee.

It had understood the problem too. To win, it needed to slow Eevee down.

But the movement was obvious. Ethan saw it coming and would not let the attack land.

He had Eevee dodge calmly, then use Swift. The stars struck Mudkip and knocked it down.

Huh? The boy rubbed his eyes at the sight of Mudkip fallen. He seemed unable to believe he had lost so easily.

For Ethan, after all the high-level tournaments he had entered and the earthshaking battles he had seen, this was a beginner's match.

It was not arrogance. The battle simply had not been hard. His opponent's attacks were straightforward, and Ethan could predict nearly every move.

The boy recalled Mudkip and studied Ethan with new admiration.

You're amazing. What's your name?

Ethan shook his head. By now he could see that the boy was simple and spoke without thinking, often offending people, but meant no harm.

Shouldn't you introduce yourself before asking for someone else's name?

The boy paused, then nodded vigorously. Oh! You're right. Listen up, then! Sometimes I'm a Zigzagoon running through the forest! Sometimes I'm a Tentacruel with lots of tentacles! Other times I'm a Bellossom with magnificent dance steps! But my true self is Nicholai, the boy known as the Shorts Boy!

Zigzagoon? Tentacruel? Bellossom? Shorts Boy?

As he spoke, Nicholai pulled one costume after another from the huge pack on his back and changed at astonishing speed. Ethan felt his temples begin to throb.

This was exactly the kind of person he least wanted to deal with.

He could feel his blood pressure rising.

He could not follow Nicholai's pace or way of thinking, much less understand what went on in his head.

Without answering, Ethan turned and walked toward the camp.

Nicholai stared after him for a moment, then called, Wait! You still haven't told me your name!

Ethan kept walking. When did I say I would tell you? Now please leave us alone. Goodbye.

But... Nicholai's mouth fell open. But you said I should introduce myself before asking yours!

That's right. Ethan glanced back with narrowed eyes. I never said I'd introduce myself.

I...

Nicholai started to reply, then thought about it. Ethan really had not promised anything.

He was about to follow, but Ethan's cold expression plainly said he wanted no company. Nicholai stopped awkwardly.

He was not so oblivious that he could miss such clear distance. He could hardly keep pestering Ethan now.

It was a shame, though. Someone that strong, and he would never learn his name.

Well, no use dwelling on it. He would think of another way to get close to the Zigzagoon.

By the time Ethan returned to camp, Erika had finished dinner.

The rich smell of curry rose from the metal pot. It made his mouth water and his stomach growl.

Erika smiled gently. All done?

Mm. Ethan sat beside her and sighed. A simple-minded fool whose mouth keeps getting him into trouble. That's exactly the sort of person I hate dealing with. Better to keep my distance.

Seeing how determined Ethan was to avoid Nicholai, Erika could not help laughing.

He feared no Pokemon, yet someone with that personality made him want to run away. She had not expected that.

...

It was noon the next day when they left Petalburg Woods.

While they were there, Erika had found a Seedot and a Shroomish. Both were Grass-type Pokemon with no habitats in Kanto, so she had caught them both.

In a short time in Hoenn, Erika too had added two Pokemon to her team. Both she and Ethan had gained plenty.

They continued north. Before long, Rustboro City came into view.

Rustboro was a city that sought to bring nature and science together.

A major city in western Hoenn, it was much larger than Petalburg in population, size, and economy. It had a Pokemon school, and several world-famous companies were based there.

Before they reached the outskirts, they saw three hooded figures in matching red uniforms kick a man in a suit to the ground, snatch his briefcase, and run down the road toward them.

Huh? A robbery?

One of them saw Ethan standing in their way. His eyes hardened. Move if you don't want to die! Get out of our way!

Behind them, the man in the suit shouted, Catch them! They stole my briefcase!

There was no time to think. The three men were already in front of Ethan. He silently took one step back.

They thought he had decided not to interfere. But as they congratulated themselves, his shadow rippled. A long arm emerged, stretching across their path like a rope.

Unable to stop, all three tripped over it and fell headfirst onto the road.

They scrambled up, furious, and glared at Ethan.

You dare get in our way?

One threw a Poke Ball. In a flash of light, a Houndoom appeared and immediately sprang at Ethan with its jaws open.

Ethan kept one hand in his pocket. He did not move.

The Houndoom leaped, its mouth wide and foul-smelling saliva dripping from its teeth. Just before it could bite him, Ethan's shadow rippled again. Two huge claws rose from it and caught Houndoom in midair.

What?

The three men finally looked at the ground beneath Ethan. Behind the claws, Gengar floated slowly out of the shadow with a mischievous grin.

Gengar cackled. You thought it would be that easy to touch him? You're underestimating us.

A... a talking Pokemon? The men were even more shocked.

The suited man had caught up, panting. Apparently wary of the three men's strength, he stayed a short distance away and called to Ethan. Sir, I work for the Devon Corporation. These people grabbed my briefcase without warning. There's something important inside. Please help me get it back!

Devon Corporation?

Ethan nodded in understanding. He studied the three men again, his gaze lingering on their red uniforms and hoods.

He knew which story this was.

Those matching, attention-grabbing clothes belonged to one of Hoenn's two famous criminal organizations: Team Magma.

Though it was called a criminal organization, Team Magma was not evil in quite the way Team Rocket was.

Its members operated mainly in Hoenn. They believed humanity's development was tied to the happiness of the world as a whole, and that living alongside Pokemon hindered human progress. Their goal was to expand the land and give people more room to live.

Finding the Legendary Pokemon Groudon was one of their most important aims.

Chapter 594: Devon Corporation's Bad Day

Ethan had not expected to run into Team Magma here.

Like Team Rocket, whose roots ran deep in Kanto and Johto, Team Magma was powerful in Hoenn. It was locked in fierce rivalry with another organization, Team Aqua, and neither side could overpower the other. Only a still larger organization, the International Police, could take them on.

Team Magma and Team Aqua might not be as strong as Team Rocket, but in Hoenn they dominated.

Seeing the first Houndoom caught, the other two Team Magma members frowned and released their own Pokemon.

Like their matching uniforms, their Pokemon matched too: two more Houndoom.

These were different from ordinary Houndoom. Armor covered their bodies and heads, making them look fiercer and offering some protection.

The two charged Ethan from left and right.

Only Gengar and Ethan's newly caught Torchic stood beside him. Torchic was far too inexperienced to beat Houndoom like these.

Even so, it bristled and did its best, breathing Ember toward the attackers.

They easily dodged the little flames and kept coming.

But a small chick was not Ethan's only defender. Gengar looked left and right at the two black dogs trying to split its attention. A Dark Pulse surged from its body like a black wave and swept over both.

The Houndoom already in Gengar's claws was struck too. All three flew backward and fell at their Trainers' feet.

Gengar had defeated the other two with one attack. A Gengar a thousand years old really was formidable.

That's... incredible!

The Devon employee stared in amazement. The Team Magma members went pale.

What kind of power was that? Even Team Magma's three executives might not be able to knock out a Houndoom in a single strike.

Was this man as strong as their leader?

They reached for a second set of Poke Balls, but Gengar did not give them a chance. At Ethan's command, it used Hypnosis and put all three to sleep.

Only then did the Devon employee approach cautiously.

Thank you so much, he said to Ethan.

It was nothing. Ethan smiled and shook his head. Check whether anything is missing.

At the reminder, the man hurried to retrieve his briefcase and examine its contents.

While he did, Ethan turned away. He did not ask what in the case had been worth stealing in broad daylight.

Unless it held a Master Ball, neither valuable documents nor secret researchor anything else he could imagineinterested him much.

After searching the case, the man let out a long breath.

The robbers had only just taken it. They had not had time to remove or tamper with anything. Apart from some damage to the outside, nothing had been lost.

Everything is still here. I can't thank you enough, he said. Oh, I forgot to introduce myself. My name is Kennedy. I'm secretary to Mr. Stone, the president of Devon Corporation.

A secretary? Ethan had taken him for an ordinary employee.
