Devon was no small company. Only a few years ago it had been a modest business mining iron ore and refining steel. Now it had grown into a giant that could rival Silph Co.

Most of its products were made for Pokemon Trainers. It had developed new kinds of Poke Balls and, Ethan had heard, was making remarkable progress on a project to revive Pokemon from fossils.

More recently, a machine that generated energy using magma as fuel had brought the company's reputation to new heights.

Ethan waved off Kennedy's thanks. Anyone who could help would have stepped in.

He found some rope, tied up the three Team Magma members, and called the police.

Before long, Officer Jenny arrived with several police cars. The officers woke the sleeping men and took them away.

As far as Ethan was concerned, the matter was over. But after Kennedy had given his statement, he sought Ethan out again.

He bowed. I've told our president what happened. He asked me to invite you to the company as his guests so he can thank you.

Ethan did not want to intrude, but Kennedy insisted and had been sent by Mr. Stone himself. After discussing it with Erika, Ethan agreed to visit Devon.

The Gym would still be there. Challenging it a little sooner or later made no real difference.

Kennedy told them more about the company as they entered Rustboro City and made their way toward its headquarters.

So Devon's head office is in Rustboro? Erika asked.

Devon products were common even in Celadon City, far away in Kanto. She had heard of the company but had not known its headquarters was here.

They reached the street outside the Devon Corporation building.

Ethan saw an imposing tower long before they reached it. It had more than sixty floors and looked at least two hundred and sixty meters tall. Sunlight shone on the gleaming glass exterior. A huge fountain sprayed water in front of the entrance.

There was no question that Devon's tower was the tallest building in Rustboro.

Its wealth astonished Ethan. How had a small company grown to this scale in only a few years?

Inside, a lavish lobby had a thoroughly modern feel. Kennedy led them into an elevator and up to the top-floor office of Devon Corporation's president, Mr. Stone.

President meant he was, in effect, the company's chief executive.

His full name was Joseph Stone. Despite his silver hair, he was only in his fifties. Perhaps he took good care of himself: his eyes were bright and he looked healthy.

He was sitting in a spacious, well-lit office. When Kennedy brought Ethan and Erika in, he promptly rose to welcome them.

Let me introduce myself. I'm Stone, president of Devon Corporation. Welcome, both of you. Thank you for helping Kennedy recover those documents. On behalf of Devon, you have my sincere gratitude.

Before Ethan could answer, Kennedy complained, This only happened because you insist on wandering off into town to play with those children. I had to carry the documents out to find you!

He sounded almost as if he were scolding his boss. Surprisingly, Mr. Stone merely laughed, entirely unbothered.

Perhaps he was used to it.

A company president would normally expect a secretaryespecially a male secretaryto follow his instructions without argument. Seeing Kennedy talk to Mr. Stone this way opened Ethan's eyes.

Oh, don't make such a fuss. Mr. Stone waved a hand at Kennedy. We have the documents back, and no one was hurt. That's what matters.

Kennedy could only sigh. He seemed to have no way of curbing his president's whims.

They had only just met, but Ethan could already see that Mr. Stone put on no airs.

Remarkable. Perhaps that helped explain Devon's rapid rise.

When Mr. Stone turned to him, Ethan nodded. Hello, Mr. Stone. I'm Ethan, a Pokemon Trainer.

Erika greeted him gracefully. And I'm Erika.

At Ethan's name, both Mr. Stone and Kennedy paused.

Ethan? Mr. Stone asked. Are you the young man who helped Silph Co. take back its building from Team Rocket in Kanto and won two League conferences?

People in Mr. Stone's position might not watch Pokemon tournaments, but they knew Ethan's name. Reports of important events around the world reached them quickly.

Yes, that's me.

What a coincidence. Mr. Stone marveled at the meeting. No wonder you had the strength to recover our documents from Team Magma so easily. You've accomplished a great deal for someone so young.

Kennedy, too, had not realized that the stranger who saved him was a conference Champion.

They grew still warmer toward Ethan. Mr. Stone showed Ethan and Erika around Devon, including its work on a technology that could change the age: reviving fossil Pokemon.

In a vast laboratory stood a precision machine, Devon's pride. The Fossil Reviver could bring Pokemon back from fossils.

It was an extraordinary achievement. People might once again see ancient Pokemon that had gone extinct. For Trainers and for society as a whole, the possibilities were immense.

The technology was not yet fully mature. Revivals were costly, and Devon could not perform them on a large scale. Successful experiments had proved it was possible, though.

Ethan was still admiring the company's work when an alarm rang out. Before anyone understood what was happening, several people in blue-and-white striped clothes burst from the laboratory next door and ran toward a floor-to-ceiling window.

What?

Mr. Stone and Kennedy stared, as confused as the researchers around them.

Ethan was already running after the intruders.

His encounter with Team Magma had put him on his guard. One glance at these people told him they belonged to its notorious rival, Team Aqua.

Devon had dreadful luck today. Team Magma had robbed an employee outside, while Team Aqua had managed to infiltrate the company itself.

The alarm was sounding, but the Team Aqua members appeared to have succeeded already.

If he had not known the two teams would sooner destroy each other than cooperate, he might have thought they had planned this together.

The Team Aqua members carried devices like jetpacks on their backs. They had plainly planned to escape through the window.

They might have got away if Ethan had not been there. He had no intention of letting them leave.

As he ran, he took a Poke Ball from his pouch and released Gardevoir.

Through their telepathic bond, she understood without a spoken command. She used Confusion to raise a barrier in front of Team Aqua.

Caught off guard, the intruders slammed into the invisible wall and fell in a daze. By the time they shook off the dizziness and got to their feet, footsteps sounded behind them. They turned to find a handsome young man and a Gardevoir waiting there.

Damn it!

They assessed their position and felt the barrier behind them. Devon's security team would soon reach this floor and surround them, with more people waiting outside. If they delayed, escape would be far harder.

But Ethan blocked their path now. They would have to defeat his Gardevoir to get out.

Ethan noticed a bulging pouch at each intruder's waist. Several vials of amber liquid stuck out of them. They had clearly taken something important from the laboratory.

Kennedy ran up behind Ethan and spotted the vials. His face changed. Mr. Ethan, that's our culture medium! It's essential for reviving fossil Pokemon, and extremely valuable. Please don't let them take it. Help us get it back!

For the second time today, Kennedy had asked Ethan to stop criminals for him.

Without Ethan here, Devon Corporation might have suffered a disastrous loss.

But with him here...

Chapter 595: Team Magma, Then Team Aqua

The Team Aqua members wore bandanas and looked rather like pirates. Three were plainly ordinary grunts. From the way the fourth stood at the front and carried himself, Ethan guessed he was an officer.

He wore a bandana too, but it was clear that he was bald. His cheeks were gaunt, and his narrow eyes made him look thoroughly untrustworthy.

One of the grunts whispered to him, Sir Amber, what do we do?

Amber studied Ethan and gritted his teeth. Don't be afraid. There's only one of him. Beat him, and we can leave!

He reached for a Poke Ball. The others released their Pokemon too.

Several flashes of blue light filled the corridor. When they faded, lobster-like Pokemon stood before Ethan.

He recognized them at once: Crawdaunt, the Water- and Dark-type Rogue Pokemon. Just as Team Magma used Houndoom, Team Aqua issued Crawdaunt to its ordinary members.

Each stood more than a meter tall. Its shape suggested an American lobster from Earth. Most of its body was red, with two blue markings on its chest. Perhaps the similarity to Team Aqua's uniforms was why the organization had chosen it.

A yellow five-pointed star marked each Crawdaunt's forehead, and a huge pincer sat on either side of its body. They had fierce tempers, picked fights readily, and were notoriously difficult to raise.

They brandished their claws constantly, grabbing other Pokemon from their ponds and throwing them out. Any challenger approaching their territory was beaten without mercy. Few other creatures could live in a pond occupied by Crawdaunt.

Psychic attacks would not work on these Dark-type Pokemon. Seeing the aggressive Crawdaunt, Ethan took out another Poke Ball and released Scizor.

The Crawdaunt lifted their pincers. Across from them, Scizor raised its own. Both sides waited for their Trainers' commands.

They all had powerful claws, but even before experience and strength came into it, Scizor's Bug type gave it an advantage against Crawdaunt's Dark type.

The Crawdaunt had numbers on their side, at least. Amber, the officer, also sent out his own Pokemon.

It was a Pelipper.

Pelipper's beak was larger than the rest of its body. Like a pouch, it could hold things the Pokemon swallowed whole.

Pelipper built nests on seaside cliffs and protected their young inside their beaks. On calm days they floated on the water to rest. They flew low over the sea looking for food, dipping their great beaks into the water to scoop prey and seawater up together.

There was nothing wrong with Pelipper itself. But a flying Pokemon was a poor choice in the cramped space of an office building. It could barely spread its wings here, much less fly to a safe height.

Unless...

Just then, the Pokemon in the corridor moved together and charged.

Despite their advantage in numbers, the three Crawdaunt had no coordination. They crowded toward Scizor, blocking one another's paths and attacks.

Scizor moved like a silent warrior, using X-Scissor again and again. Its great red pincers traced crossing cuts through the air. By the time it passed the Crawdaunt, all three had fallen.

The Team Aqua grunts stared, stunned. Only now did they realize they had met a powerful opponent.

Only Amber's Pelipper remained between Scizor and them.

What are you waiting for? Amber snapped at the others. Use your other Pokemon!

Huh? Ohright!

The grunts fumbled for their second Poke Balls. While the next flashes of blue light appeared, Pelipper suddenly flew toward a window.

Amber sprinted after it, threw his arms around its body, and tried to crash through the glass with it.

So that had been his plan. The moment the battle went badly, he meant to escape amid the confusion.

He was abandoning his subordinates. The three grunts gaped as their officer fled.

Before they could react, Pelipper hit something invisible with a thud and came to a halt.

Beside Ethan, Gardevoir slowly lowered her arm.

She had used Confusion to block Pelipper's path. Ethan had guessed what Amber intended; he was not about to let him escape.

The failed attempt left Amber where he had begun. For Team Aqua's morale, though, it was a heavy blow.

The officer in charge had tried to leave them behind and save himself. How were they supposed to keep fighting?

One of the grunts stared at him in disbelief. Amber! Why would you do that?

You fools, Amber said with a weary sigh. Don't you recognize him? He just won the Silver Conference. How could we beat him here? If we all get captured, who will deliver the culture medium we stole to our leader?

Amber really had recognized Ethan. Faced with such a difficult opponent, he had weighed his options and chosen to flee.

His loyalty to Team Aqua was no less than anyone else's. Getting the stolen culture medium to its leader had been his first thought.

Still, however necessary he believed it was, leaving his own people behind was a betrayal that would chill them.

To Amber, the organization's great plan outweighed any one member. Given the choice again, he would do the same thing.

The grunts wanted to argue, but Ethan gave them no time.

At a wave of his hand, Scizor and Gardevoir advanced together. They knocked out Pelipper and brought the Team Aqua members under control.

Chapter 596: Steven Stone

After Ethan brought down the Team Aqua members, Mr. Stone and Kennedy came over and stood behind him.

Those people... they must be from Team Aqua, Mr. Stone said. I can't believe they slipped all the way in here. Mr. Ethan, thank you. Without you, we might have suffered a terrible loss today.

In a short time, Ethan had helped Devon Corporation through two crises, one involving Team Magma and the other Team Aqua. Mr. Stone could hardly help being moved.

Ethan had done more than defeat a few criminals. By opposing both dangerous organizations, he had drawn their attention and might have brought considerable trouble upon himself.

There's no need to thank me, Ethan said. I couldn't stand by after seeing it happen.

He sighed to himself all the same.

He did not fear Team Magma or Team Aqua. The International Police stood behind him, and he had many powerful Pokemon. Even if both groups came after him, what could they really do?

What bothered him was the security at companies like this one.

Silph Co. in Kanto and Devon here in Hoenn were multinational giants with armed guards. Perhaps because they had never faced such attacks before, they guarded their entrances and neglected the inside of their buildings.

At that moment, a light came on above the elevator at the end of the corridor. The doors opened, and more than a dozen security officers hurried out toward Kennedy.

You lot! Kennedy scolded. You're too late! If Mr. Ethan hadn't been here, they would have escaped!

The guards looked miserable, but the delay was hardly their fault. They had responded as soon as the alarm sounded. Devon Tower was enormous; gathering, setting out, and riding the elevator up to this floor all took time.

Only four or five minutes had passed. Arriving already showed that they were well trained.

Ethan spoke up for them. Mr. Kennedy, please don't be angry. No one expected Team Aqua to appear inside the tower. I happened to be right here. If I'd been elsewhere, I couldn't have caught them so quickly either.

The guards gave him grateful looks. They did not know who he was, but they could see that he had caught the intruders. Instead of taking all the credit, he was defending them.

Kennedy calmed a little, though he still glared at the security team. Even so, letting Team Aqua slip into this building unnoticed was a serious failure. I want a report from every one of you after this.

The reports were a nuisance, but better than losing their jobs. Relieved, the guards nodded and tied up the Team Aqua members. Kennedy recovered the stolen culture medium from their bags.

Then the elevator opened again. A young man strode quickly down the corridor.

Father! Mr. Kennedy! What happened?

Ethan turned. The newcomer was about his own age, dressed in a well-fitted suit. He had medium-length blue-gray hair, pale skin, and refined features, like a young aristocrat.

Kennedy stared for a moment, then greeted him respectfully. Young Master Steven, what brings you here?

Steven?

Ethan knew Steven from the anime and games. Now that he had met this immensely popular character in person, he studied him with surprise.

He also remembered that Steven was Mr. Stone's son.

Sure enough, Mr. Stone smiled. Mr. Ethan, let me introduce my son, Steven Stone. He's a Trainer too. You're close in age; I'm sure you'll have plenty to talk about.

He called Steven over and told him, This is Ethan, Champion of the conferences in Kanto and Johto.

Ethan? Steven paused, then approached with a warm smile and offered his hand. I live in Hoenn, but I've heard your name. I know you're a remarkable Trainer, and I've wanted to meet you.

Steven was the son of an extraordinarily wealthy man. Yet he was so well mannered that Ethan saw none of the arrogance people often expected from someone born into money.

On meeting him, Ethan's first impression was simply of a courteous young man. No wonder Steven was so popular in the anime and games.

Ethan shook his hand. Steven was a little shorter than Ethan, who stood over 180 centimeters tall, and looked lean and well proportioned.

You're very kind, Mr. Steven. The truth is, I've heard far more about you.

It was no empty courtesy. Steven's name was famous in the anime and games, and he played an important part in both. Few people familiar with them would fail to recognize him.

Steven did not hear Ethan's deeper meaning. He took it as a polite compliment.

After their greetings, Mr. Stone smiled. Today was my first meeting with Ethan too, yet he's already helped us twice.

Twice? Steven had only just arrived. What do you mean?

Kennedy told him about Team Magma stealing his briefcase and Team Aqua taking the culture medium.

Steven's gratitude grew as he listened, and he looked at Ethan with new warmth.

I had no idea, he said sincerely. You helped my father and Mr. Kennedy. That makes you my friend. If you ever run into trouble, please come to me.

Chapter 597: Unexpected News

In the president's office on the top floor of Devon Corporation, Steven sat in the main guest chair. Ethan and Erika sat together on one side. Erika listened as Ethan and Steven talked at an unhurried pace, adding a few words now and then. The atmosphere was easy and pleasant.

Steven was unfailingly polite. He was not naturally a talkative man, but in company he showed the social grace of a well-raised heir. He made sure everyone felt included. The way he spoke was impressive, and his effortless elegance never felt forced.

Apart from the three of them, only Mr. Stone was in the office.

Kennedy had work to do and the Team Aqua incident to handle. Mr. Stone, by contrast, sat at his desk watching the young people chat with a smile, as though he hoped someone as accomplished as Ethan would become his son's friend.

Steven pushed cups of tea toward his guests. I've spent this past while traveling and collecting all sorts of stones. I only happened to return so I could send the ones I found to Devon for study. I'd barely come through the door when I heard what had happened.

What kind of stones? Erika asked.

Remarkable stones with different powers, Steven said with a smile. They're hidden in mountains, caves, and under the sea. Some have names already. Others don't, and we still have no idea what they can do. You've heard of Mega Stones, haven't you? Before anyone discovered their power, no one knew their true value. The same was once true of Evolution stones. I want to find out what potential other stones might hold.

It was an unusual hobby and meaningful research. If Steven discovered something important, it might change the world for people and Pokemon alike.

Speaking of stones...

Ethan had seen plenty on his travels. Most were common, well-understood things like Fire Stones, Leaf Stones, and Everstones. The only truly precious one he had encountered was the Soul Dew formed from Latios and Latias in Altomare.

When he told Steven about it, Steven was astonished.

What? You've seen the Soul Dew?

Yes. We saw it in the Water Capital. It held incredible power: it could revive fossils and even cause a tremendous tsunami. It was beautiful to look at, too.

I've heard of it, Steven said eagerly. They say the Legendary Pokemon Latias and Latios gave their lives and all their power to create it. I thought it was only a legend. To think it truly existed! I should go there and see it myself.

For someone who loved collecting stones, a marvelous crystal like the Soul Dew held immense appeal, even if it had not formed naturally.

Now that he knew one had really existed in the Water Capital near Johto, how could he sit still?

You'll be disappointed, Ethan said. The Soul Dew was polluted and destroyed. It's gone. You won't see it if you go.

He told Steven the broad outline of what had happened in Altomare, leaving out the fact that he owned Suicune and had caught Latias and Latios in Poke Balls.

What an enviable experience, Steven said. Then he looked at Ethan. You came to Hoenn for the Ever Grande Conference, I assume?

Of course. Ethan smiled. I want to catch Hoenn Pokemon, challenge its Gyms, and enter the Ever Grande Conference.

Then be careful. Steven's eyes brightened. Hoenn Trainers are strong. The Ever Grande Conference is even more competitive than the Indigo and Silver Conferences. Winning here won't be easy. As it happens, I won the last Ever Grande Conference. If you need advice, you can ask me anytime.

That man...

Ethan nearly laughed. All the talk of caution sounded fine, but Steven really wanted him to know he was the previous Champion.

...

After exchanging contact information with Steven, Ethan and Erika waved goodbye as he saw them out of Devon Corporation.

Steven had wanted a friendly battle to see which of them was stronger. Ethan had politely declined.

Most of his main Pokemon were elsewhere. With a team built around Dragonite and Tyranitar, he could not be sure how the match would go.

Winning the Silver Conference had also given him a chance to challenge the Elite Four, but he had turned that down too.

It was not a lack of confidence. He wanted to save such challenges for last. Once he had competed in every conference, he would visit the Elite Four one after another and test himself against them.

They left the street where Devon stood and were about to head for Rustboro Gym when Erika received a video call from another region.

The caller worked at the Celadon Gym. Ethan had seen her at Erika's perfume shop before and knew she and Erika were close friends.

Erika! The Gym repairs are finished. Someone from the Pokemon League came to ask where you were. When we told them you're traveling in Hoenn, they said to contact you right away. They want you back to run the Gym!

Ethan and Erika both frowned.

When Erika had left Celadon, she had explained that a fire had damaged the Gym badly enough to close it while the Pokemon League rebuilt it.

That closure had allowed her to travel with Ethan.

So much time had passed that they had both known this news would come. Hearing it now still unsettled them.

What they had been expecting had finally arrived.

Chapter 598: Erika Leaves, Misty Joins

The sudden video call changed Ethan and Erika's lighthearted mood at once. They looked at each other, weighed down by the news.

They could do nothing about it. Unless Erika resigned as Gym Leader, she had to follow the Pokemon League's instructions. Giving up her work to travel with Ethan indefinitely was not realistic.

He sighed.

Ethan had been through a separation like this when he parted from Sabrina. It had not made him used to it. If anything, this hurt more.

Erika looked so sad that she could not speak. Ethan took a deep breath, gathered himself, drew her into his arms, and comforted her softly.

Then you should go home. You've been away a long time. Your perfume shop and your Gym both need you. There are more people who depend on you than just me.

Erika buried her face against his chest and held his waist tightly. She said nothing.

It was the first time Ethan had seen this vulnerable side of her so clearly. Usually she was gentle and thoughtful, with the composure of a traditional Japanese lady. She seldom let her feelings show this freely.

It made plain how unwilling she was to leave him.

Ethan held back his own pain and kept speaking gently until she calmed a little.

The Rustboro Gym battle was out of the question now. Ethan had no heart for it. Rustboro had no international airport, so Erika could not fly straight to Kanto. They would have to leave the city, pass through Petalburg, return to Littleroot Town, and buy her a ticket aboard a passenger ship.

They made the journey mostly in silence.

Ethan could not go back with her; he had his own travels to continue. At least he could see her safely to the harbor.

They crossed Petalburg Woods, passed through Petalburg City, and reached Littleroot Town the following evening.

The starting town looked much as it had when they first arrived. But the confidence and anticipation with which they had begun their Hoenn journey had gone. They felt entirely different now.

They had been so eager to set out and so sorrowful to return.

They had missed the day's sailing. They checked into a hotel, rested overnight, and planned to go to the docks the next morning.

That night Ethan saw how fierce Erika's passion could be.

Perhaps she poured her reluctance to part into their lovemaking. She kept reaching for him until he had filled her. Only then did she lie in his arms with faint tear tracks on her cheeks and seem to fall asleep.

But Ethan could not sleep.

The strength he had shown during the day fell away. Erika did not want to leave him; he wanted her to stay just as badly.

He had tried to be steady throughout their return, giving her warmth and someone to lean on when she needed it without adding to her pain.

Now that she lay beside him, he finally let himself feel what he had hidden.

His eyes grew wet as he stared without blinking at the moonlight beyond the window. Then a soft hand brushed the moisture from the corner of his eye.

He looked down. Erika was watching him with tender eyes.

She had been awake all along. She had only pretended to sleep so he would not feel worse.

Their eyes met. They smiled and kissed again.

...

After breakfast the next morning, Ethan took Erika to the harbor.

They embraced one last time. He whispered in her ear, Wait for me in Celadon. I'll contact you every day. And don't worrymy travels won't last forever. When I take a break, I'll come see you.

I know. I'll be waiting. Erika kissed his cheek, stepped back, and bowed deeply with her hands before her chest. I wish you victory in every battle. May all your hard work lead you to win every conference you enter.

Erika boarded the ship. She looked back again and again, but the liner departed on schedule and carried her out of sight.

Ethan stood on the dock for a long time. It felt as though she had taken half his soul with her. Memories of their time together kept rising in his mind, surrounding his heart with warmth.

When he had steadied himself, he sighed and turned to leave. Then someone called to him from a distance.

The voice was so familiar that he knew who it belonged to before he looked around.

Ethan! A pretty, energetic girl with a side ponytail came running up, a small backpack on her shoulders. She was out of breath but still spoke brightly. What are you doing here? Did you come to meet me?

Of course it was Misty.

Unlike before, she was alone. Ash and Brock, usually at her side, were nowhere to be seen.

As they had agreed, she had spent a little time at the Cerulean Gym after returning home, then crossed the sea to join Ethan in Hoenn.

Before Ethan could answer, Misty frowned and looked around. Huh? Where's Erika?

Her smile eased much of Ethan's sorrow. He shook his head and told her about the call that had forced Erika to return to Kanto.

What? Misty's eyes widened. Just now? Then I missed my chance to say goodbye!

Misty had come to Hoenn by ship too. By chance, hers docked just after Erika's had sailed.

For a moment the two ships had passed each other, as though their passengers' paths were changing places.

I didn't expect to find you here either. When I heard your voice, I thought I was imagining it. Ethan reached out and ruffled her hair. Why didn't you tell me you were coming?

Hee hee. Misty looked up at the face she liked so much, her heart racing. I wanted to surprise you. I was going to call once I reached Hoenn, but I found you right away!

Then she realized what Erika's departure meant. From now on, she and Ethan would travel together alone, with no one else around.

No Erika, no Ash, no Brock. She really would have Ethan to herself.

Was she dreaming?

The surprise left her dazed. Everything felt almost too wonderful to be real.

Yes!

Her delight showed on her face. She almost shouted it aloud.

This was perfect. Even fate seemed to be helping her.

Chapter 599: The World's Strongest Pokemon

Ethan and Misty left Littleroot Town and headed toward Petalburg City.

He had traveled this road back and forth several times in only a few days. By now he knew the area better than many Trainers native to Hoenn.

They crossed the open countryside. Like Ethan when he first arrived, Misty looked around at everything on this new continent with eager curiosity.

After a while, though, she realized that apart from a few different Pokemon, Hoenn looked much like Johto and Kanto.

The mountains were mountains, and the trees were trees.

As her initial excitement faded, she turned her attention to Ethan and talked with him while they walked.

When he asked what Ash was doing, Misty thought for a moment. I heard he was getting ready to leave too. He'll probably reach Hoenn tomorrow or the day after. But he left all his Pokemon at Professor Oak's lab. It sounds like he's traveling with only Pikachu.

That did not surprise Ethan. Ash would follow the same pattern on later journeys to Sinnoh, Kalos, and elsewhere, setting out with Pikachu and little else.

Ethan himself had given Celebi to Erika when she returned to Kanto, asking her to care for it at the Celadon Gym for now.

Like leaving his three legendary birds with Sabrina, it gave him and Erika a bond across the distance. It also gave Celebi a more comfortable place to stay.

Erika would care for it, feed it plenty of delicious things, and let it enjoy the familiar natural setting of the Gym's greenhouse. Celebi would be more relaxed and happier there.

If Ethan needed it, he could have Celebi transferred back at any time. Showing it more of the world would have to wait for another opportunity.

After they passed Oldale Town, Ethan guessed Norman might not yet have returned to the Petalburg Gym. This time he chose a different road toward Rustboro City.

It was longer and more remote than their earlier route, but it gave him new sights to enjoy instead of making him retrace every familiar step.

Beyond a small, unnamed village, they came to a Y-shaped crossroads with a huge signboard.

It stood conspicuously in the grass. Anyone passing by would be sure to notice it.

They stopped, and Ethan read the words aloud: The Gym with the world's strongest Pokemon lies ahead!

The world's strongest Pokemon? Misty's eyebrows rose in anger. Her family ran a Gym too, and she could not stand such a boast about another Gym and its Pokemon. That Gym Leader has some nerve. I want to see what Pokemon he dares call the strongest!

Ethan had won two conferences and had the three legendary birds and Suicune, yet he never called any of his Pokemon the strongest. What gave the owner of a little Gym near a remote village such confidence?

Ethan found her indignant look funny.

He was curious too. He wanted to see which Pokemon could supposedly live up to that claim.

With both in agreement, they left the main road and followed the side path toward the far end of the village.

They reached the wall of a large enclosure. Before they made it to the gate, a boy of about ten came out crying, clutching his Pokemon.

Ethan and Misty exchanged startled looks.

What had happened in there? Had some extraordinarily strong Pokemon beaten the boy so badly he cried?

They entered the yard. A modest building stood ahead, with an outdoor battlefield in front of it.

On one side of the field, a Pelipper and a man of about thirty-five or thirty-six were strolling back toward the building. The man had a crew cut and wore a gold belt.

He heard Ethan and Misty's footsteps and turned to look them over.

Oh? Two more challengers? he said casually. It's a busy day.

With her hands on her hips, Misty called, Is this the Gym that claims to have the world's strongest Pokemon?

That's right. The man nodded. I'm Anthony, the Leader here. And this Pelipper beside me is, without question, the strongest Pokemon in the world!

Ethan and Misty looked at Pelipper.

Ethan had battled Amber's Pelipper at Devon Corporation not long ago. He knew a little about the Water- and Flying-type species, but he could see nothing different about this one.

Misty eyed it skeptically too. She had seen many Legendary Pokemon, and she traveled with a two-time conference Champion. An ordinary-looking Pelipper hardly seemed worthy of the title strongest.

Besides, this place looked more like a private Gym than an official one.

She had plenty of questions, but she asked, Good. You're who we came to find. Will you accept a challenge?

With Misty at his side, Ethan's travels had taken on a different rhythm. She called herself the world's most beautiful girl and met every situation with energy and a stubborn streak. Apart from Bug-type Pokemon, almost nothing intimidated her.

Of course! Anthony laughed. We've just had a match, but Pelipper barely exerted itself. It has plenty of energy left. Which of you wants to go first?

He had just made a challenger cry and still sounded completely confident.

Misty exchanged a glance with Ethan and stepped forward.

Ethan doesn't need to handle this. I'll take you on first!

Seeing that his opponent was only a girl in her early teens, Anthony shrugged and led Pelipper back to the Trainer's position.

Your choice, he said with a smile. If Pelipper makes you cry, don't blame me.

Chapter 600: The Amazing Pelipper

Misty and Anthony took their places on opposite sides of the field. Anthony, of course, would battle with Pelipper. After a moment's thought, Misty sent out Starmie.

Apart from Psyduck, which needed a headache to bring out its true power, and the Gyarados she had caught later, Starmie was perhaps her strongest Pokemon. It had accompanied her throughout her travels and was one of the partners she trusted most.

The two Pokemon stared at each other. Starmie was wary; Pelipper looked far more confident.

Misty studied Pelipper for a while, still skeptical. Even now she could sense nothing particularly powerful about it.

She glanced at Anthony and found him looking just as confident as his Pokemon. She decided to stop worrying about it and gave her first command.

Starmie, use Swift!

The large gem at Starmie's center flashed. A shower of glittering stars shot from one of its points toward Pelipper.

Both Pokemon were Water types, so Misty had chosen not to attack with Water-type moves. She intended to rely on Starmie's Normal- and Psychic-type moves to settle the battle.

Pelipper flapped its wings and rose into the air, easily evading Swift.

Misty was not surprised. She stayed alert for its counterattack.

What came when Pelipper flew above Starmie astonished her. It was no Flying-, Normal-, or Water-type move. It was an electric shock!

Golden light suddenly flared inside Pelipper's enormous bill. A bolt shot through the narrow opening between its jaws and struck toward Starmie at tremendous speed.

What!?

Misty stared in shock. As a Trainer who specialized in Water types, she had made a point of studying Hoenn's Water-type Pokemon in the Pokedex before coming here. Pelipper had left a strong impression on her.

But she clearly remembered that Pelipper was a Water- and Flying-type Pokemon. How could it suddenly use an Electric-type attack? It made no sense!

Starmie tried to dodge, but the current moved too fast. It struck in an instant.

Electric attacks were strong against Water types. Sparks crackled across Starmie's body, and though it had no visible face, Misty could still feel its pain.

Starmie!

Before she could do anything else, Pelipper opened its bill a fraction again. A second bolt of electricity shot out and knocked Starmie down.

What kind of Water-type Pelipper was this? It might as well have been an Electric-type Pokemon!

Misty hurried onto the field and gathered Starmie into her arms.

She looked back at Anthony, baffled. Why can your Pelipper use Electric-type moves?

Anthony lifted his chin proudly. What's so strange about that? I told you my Pelipper is the strongest Pokemon in the world! Well? Now you've seen what it can do!

Being beaten by an attack that seemed to defy common sense left Misty dissatisfied.

She recalled Starmie and took out another Poke Ball. Before she could send out her second Pokemon, however, a flash of blue light came from her waist. Psyduck had let itself out again!

Psyduck wandered around the field, looking this way and that. It seemed oblivious to the tense atmosphere, and even to the fire in its Trainer's eyes.

You little! Misty fumed. Why do you always come out and cause trouble at the worst possible moment?

Anthony shook his head and laughed. Seriously? You can't even keep your own Pokemon under control. Can you really call yourself a proper Trainer?

That made Misty even angrier. After what Anthony had said, she could hardly switch Pokemon now. She shouted, Fine! Since you're already out, you can battle! Go, Psyduck! Show him what you can do!

Psyduck tilted its head, looked at Misty, then turned to Pelipper. Only then did it belatedly realize that Misty was in a battle.

It showed no fear. Quacking excitedly, it charged at Pelipper.

That's it! Misty cried, thrilled to see Psyduck actually eager to fight for once. Show it your strength! Use Zen Headbutt!

Psyduck ran at Pelipper with long strides, wearing an expression that was somehow both dopey and fierce. It made strange noises all the way, looking surprisingly aggressive.

But it had only crossed half the distance when two vines suddenly emerged from Pelipper's bill. They reached Psyduck, bound it tightly, lifted it into the air, and slammed it hard against the ground.

Now Misty was truly stunned.

Vines could come out of Pelipper's mouth? Was it some new variety? Or were all Hoenn's Pokemon this outrageous?

While Misty stood at a loss, Ethan watched from behind her. After observing the battle, he had begun to understand what was happening.

There had to be an unseen reason for Pelipper's impossible attacks.

The secret lay inside the enormous bill that could swallow a small Pokemon whole.

Unlike an ordinary Pelipper, Anthony's kept its bill barely open during the battle. No matter what situation it faced or who its opponent was, it never opened wide. It seemed to be taking great care to avoid doing so.

There could hardly be anything but a secret inside it.

The sight also stirred Ethan's memory. Hadn't Ash encountered something like this in the anime? A man named Anthony had come up with the absurd idea of hiding Poke Balls containing Pokemon of different types inside Pelipper's bill. During a battle, he would command Pelipper to release whichever Pokemon had the type advantage, using those favorable matchups to win.

Anthony had certainly put his scheming mind to work to devise a trick like that.

A Trainer who did not know what was happening could easily be caught off guard. This was what gave Anthony the nerve to call his Pelipper the world's strongest Pokemon.

Psyduck went down before it even had a chance to unleash its powerful psychic abilities.

Misty was still unwilling to concede. As she reached for a third Poke Ball, Ethan stepped beside her and stopped her.

Forget it. You're no match for him. Let me take over from here.

Chapter 601: Then I'll Play Along

Misty recalled Psyduck and gave Ethan her place in the Trainer's area.

Across the field, Anthony took the change of opponent in stride. Whoever he faced, he was convinced his Pelipper could not lose.

That's quite an impressive way to battle, Ethan said with a smile, clapping his hands. But it's a cheap trick, and hardly sporting. Someone is bound to expose it sooner or later. When that happens, won't you be ashamed to face all the Trainers you've beaten?

His words struck Anthony like a spike. His expression changed, and his heart began to pound.

Impossible! Had this man discovered Pelipper's secret?

That could not be. Pelipper had never opened its huge bill all the way, or even wide enough to reveal anything inside. No one could have spotted it by watching the battle.

Yet what Ethan had just said made it sound as though he knew something.

What are you talking about? Anthony demanded. He forced himself to keep his voice steady. I'm not using any trick. Pelipper can do all this because it trained hard!

Is that so? Fine. I'm not going to argue with you. If that's what you say, so be it.

Ethan shook his head. Anthony's excuse did not concern him. In truth, once he realized that this supposedly strongest Pokemon was little more than a contrived combination, he had lost interest. Still, since he had come all this way, he might as well battle it and experience this combination's strength for himself. Then the time he had spent here would not be entirely wasted.

Besides, Anthony had beaten two of Misty's Pokemon in succession. Ethan had to help her settle the score.

Misty had heard the implication in Ethan's words. Ethan, are you saying there's something wrong with his Pelipper?

He pressed a hand down gently, signaling her to be patient. Rather than explain, he smiled. Watch and you'll see. I'll show you what he's really up to.

Seeing Ethan so sure of himself made Anthony uneasy. For a moment, he even thought of backing out.

Then he caught Ethan's knowing half smile, gritted his teeth, and held his ground.

So what if this man knew something? Anthony's scheme had helped him beat at least a hundred Trainers. Which of them had ever defeated him?

As long as no one could win, his Pelipper was still the strongest Pokemon in the world!

This match would be like all the others. Pelipper would use those same methods to defeat this man and teach him a harsh lesson.

Ethan had no idea Anthony was wrestling with his doubts and had resolved to make him pay. Choosing to be cautious, he passed over the newly caught Pokemon, including Torchic. Instead, he took out a Poke Ball and sent out Dragonite.

Anthony's brow furrowed as soon as Dragonite appeared.

After running this private Gym for so long and battling Trainers of every sort, he had begun to recognize patterns.

Young children with unseasoned faces and restless movements were usually beginners who had only just set out. Most of their Pokemon were weak and unevolved.

Anthony could beat those Trainers easily, often without resorting to his special methods at all.

At the other end were Trainers weathered by long days on the road. They were much harder to deal with.

They had more experience and a wider variety of Pokemon. Some were formidable enough that Anthony had to give everything he had and exploit type advantages just to scrape out a win.

But even those Trainers were not the most troublesome. The handful he truly dreaded looked very much like the man standing before him.

They met any situation with an air of calm indifference. Their Pokemon had been through countless battles and had grown into their final forms. With that much experience, even an unfavorable type matchup did not seem to hinder them as much.

Ethan and his Dragonite clearly belonged to that group.

And Ethan had all but named his secret. Anthony's eyelid twitched as a bad feeling rose in his chest.

There was no backing out now. If he made an excuse and refused to fight, word would spread. The reputation and business he had spent so long building would be ruined, and he would become a laughingstock.

But he had little confidence in winning, either.

All he could do was hope Pelipper performed as usual and beat this man.

While Anthony fretted, the two Pokemon took their positions.

There was no referee and there were no special rules, so no one needed to announce the start. As soon as Pelipper was ready, Ethan whistled. Dragonite skimmed low over the ground and charged straight at it.

Anthony snapped back to the battle and hurriedly focused on the field.

Pelipper, use Wing Attack!

He had never battled a Dragonite before, but he knew it was a Dragon- and Flying-type Pokemon. Pelipper's electric shocks, vines, and any Water- or Fire-type attacks it might use would not give him the type advantage against a Dragon type.

Fortunately, Pelipper was a Flying type too. Its Flying-type attacks would still work normally, so he was not without options.

Pelipper had barely raised a wing before Ethan understood Anthony's plan. He did not change his command. Dragonite continued closing in.

The two Pokemon crossed paths low in the air and separated again after only a brief clash.

That single exchange set off alarm bells in Anthony's mind.

Both Pokemon had used Wing Attack. At the moment they met, however, Dragonite had turned slightly and avoided Pelipper's strike. Pelipper was not so lucky. Dragonite's small wing hit it, sending it wobbling so badly that it nearly fell to the ground.

Anthony had seen enough battles to judge their strength from that first exchange. Dragonite was unquestionably stronger and more skilled than his Pelipper.

Chapter 602: It's a Matter of Character

After landing its first blow, Dragonite kept up its momentum and wheeled back toward Pelipper. This time Anthony did not dare meet it head-on. He attacked from a distance instead.

His retreat told Ethan how little confidence lay behind his bluster, and Dragonite pressed its advantage.

Pelipper parted its bill slightly, sending a bolt of electricity at Dragonite. With a small turn and its tremendous flying speed, Dragonite dodged easily. It closed the distance and drove its head into Pelipper's belly.

The impact dented Pelipper's stomach. Its bill flew open in spite of itself, nearly exposing its secret. It caught itself just in time, clamped its bill shut, and fled farther away.

Ethan traced a circle with his finger. Dragonite caught the gesture with a glance from above and immediately gave chase.

High over the battlefield, Pelipper was fleeing toward the other side when it looked back and saw Dragonite bearing down on it again. It opened its bill a fraction. A dazzling jet of fire burst out: Flamethrower!

Along with the Grass-type Vine Whip and Electric-type Thunder Shock it had used earlier, this Fire-type attack brought its displayed repertoire to five types when its own Water- and Flying-type moves were counted. It certainly seemed versatile.

Anyone who did not know its secret might have been fooled.

Dragonite met the flames calmly. It beat its wings and used Hurricane, blowing the Flamethrower straight back toward Pelipper.

Pelipper was startled. It had not produced those flames with its own power, and they could burn it just as easily as anything else.

Fortunately for Pelipper, the wind from Hurricane was fierce. Though it blew the fire toward Pelipper, the opposing gust also lifted the bird and carried it clear of the flames in an instant.

But Pelipper had barely steadied itself when Dragonite drew close without a sound. Water wrapped around Dragonite's long tail. It twisted and lashed out with Aqua Tail, striking Pelipper squarely across the face.

Smack!

The hit landed hard. This time Pelipper could not keep its bill closed. It opened wide, and three conspicuous Poke Balls flew out amid a spray of saliva.

Pelipper crashed to the ground. The three balls fell beside it and bounced several times.

One rolled all the way to Misty's feet. She stared at it for a moment before she understood what it was and what Ethan had meant earlier.

So you're a fraud! She glared at Anthony. I actually thought your Pelipper was something special. All you've been doing is fooling people with this trick! And you still dare call it the strongest Pokemon in the world? You have no shame!

Anthony's face went pale. With his lie exposed, he said nothing. He did not dare defend himself.

He took out a Poke Ball and recalled his unconscious Pelipper, then hurried onto the field to gather the three fallen balls. Without stopping, he slunk away from the battlefield.

He looked nothing like the arrogant man who had stood there a moment ago.

The secret behind Pelipper's Electric-, Grass-, and Fire-type attacks was simple: Anthony had hidden several Poke Balls inside its bill before the battle. Whenever it needed a particular attack, Pelipper moved its tongue to release the appropriate Pokemon.

Once that Pokemon had used its move, Pelipper moved its tongue again to recall it into its ball. An opponent watching from outside would be none the wiser.

The technique took skill. Anthony and Pelipper must have practiced it extensively to perform it so smoothly, without anyone noticing and without Pelipper being caught by the attacks inside its own bill.

If Anthony had devoted that time and effort to training instead of tricks, Pelipper could have grown much stronger. With that dedication alone, it might have been able to beat ordinary Trainers honestly.

In the end, Anthony's attempt to take a shortcut had only hurt him.

Misty was still talking indignantly at Anthony's retreating back. Ethan shook his head and patted her shoulder.

Come on. Let's go.

Huh? Misty looked at him in surprise. We're just leaving? He's deceived so many people. If we walk away now, he's getting off far too easily!

What else can we do? Ethan said with a shrug. Ultimately, this is a problem with his character. The people he beat haven't really suffered any loss. What would calling the police accomplish? And did you see his face when he left? He was embarrassed that he'd been exposed, but he wasn't ashamed. Once we're gone, he won't change his ways. He'll keep using the same trick to fool people.

Then what are we supposed to do? Misty grew angrier. Just stand by while he keeps beating Trainers who have no idea what's happening?

Misty. Ethan rubbed the top of her head. The world isn't made up of right and wrong alone. People have their dark sides too. We can't stand by when we face truly bad people, but with someone like him, there's little we can do. One day he'll meet someone he can't push around, suffer a serious loss, and get the lesson he deserves.

Then let's tell everyone what he's doing! Misty said, unwilling to let it go. Once they know how underhanded he is, no one else will fall for it!

Ethan shook his head. That would take us a great deal of time. Anthony could simply move somewhere else, and all our effort would be wasted. Come on. Don't let someone like him trouble you any longer.

Between reassurance and persuasion, Ethan finally led Misty away.

The encounter showed him how differently the women in his life would have reacted. If Erika had been beside him, she would have shaken her head, laughed, and put the matter behind her, just as he had.

Only Misty, so young, energetic, and full of a sense of justice, would keep arguing over it.

With Sabrina, it would have been simpler still. A wave of her little hand, and Anthony would have become a doll, left in a corner for a few years!

Fortunately, Misty's anger never lasted long. Once they were back on the road, she soon forgot Anthony altogether. Before long, she was her cheerful, lively self again.

Chapter 603: A Conversation and Roxanne

That evening, Ethan and Misty found themselves between towns with nowhere to stay, so they camped beside a small lake nearby.

Ethan pitched his tent and invited Misty inside. Unlike the nights he had shared a bed with Sabrina or Erika, there was a lamp between them, and they each slept on one side with plenty of space. The tent merely kept out the wind and rain.

Even so, Misty's cheeks burned, and she could not help imagining where the night might lead.

With Erika gone, Ethan naturally took charge of dinner. His cooking was only average, but after spending so much time with Erika, he had learned a thing or two. He made a hearty seasonal soup for the main course, and it turned out surprisingly delicious.

He was pleased with it, at least, and Misty praised it enthusiastically.

They and their Pokemon all ate their fill. After the sun had disappeared, darkness settled around the lake and the moon climbed high. They cleared away the dishes, then sat in front of the tent, chatting as they watched the still water.

The campfire crackled. Starlight lay across the lake, its reflection stretching like a river of stars.

Nearby, Eevee and Torchic played with several of Misty's Pokemon. Gengar sat to one side like a meditating monk, admiring the beauty of the night sky.

Ethan stirred the lively fire with a stick and turned to Misty. I'm surprised your sisters agreed to let you leave again so easily.

Why wouldn't they? Misty smiled, though it looked a little strained. They support my travels. Besides, even if they didn't, it wouldn't matter. I wouldn't listen to them!

In fact, Misty had rested at home for a few days after returning to the Cerulean Gym. When she announced that she intended to set out for Hoenn, Violet and Lily had strongly opposed it.

The three Cerulean sisters were now wholly focused on their underwater ballet. They had long wanted to hand the Gym's work over to Misty as soon as they could.

Fortunately, Misty had spoken to their eldest sister, Daisy, in private. After Misty appealed to both her feelings and her reason, Daisy persuaded Violet and Lily to allow her a little more time to travel.

When that time ran out, Misty would have to return and take over the Gym.

She kept all this from Ethan. Even though the agreement came with a condition, she had long known that none of her sisters wanted to be Gym Leader. Cerulean Gym belonged to their family and could not simply be abandoned. Sooner or later, the position would fall to her.

For now, she was glad to have won herself more time.

Ethan took her answer at face value. Yet he had seen the anime, and even without Misty telling him, he understood that she might soon return to Cerulean Gym, take over her sisters' duties, and truly become its Gym Leader.

Thinking about Cerulean Gym reminded him that Misty was a Trainer who had grown up around Water-type Pokemon. He took out a Poke Ball and released the Feebas he had recently caught on the beach outside Petalburg City.

Even Misty, a Water-type specialist, frowned at the ugly, yellow-brown fish Pokemon.

Ethan, is this one of your new Pokemon? Why does it look so... so...

Knowing what she was trying to say, Ethan laughed. He brought up a picture of Milotic on his Pokedex and showed it to her.

It may be ugly now, but look how beautiful it is after it evolves.

His explanation made Misty realize she had judged Feebas by its appearance. Embarrassed, she stuck out her tongue.

Ethan then asked her for advice on caring for a fish Pokemon like this one.

He had raised Magikarp before, but holding Magikarp aloft and swinging it into other Pokemon was hardly a suitable way to handle Feebas.

Misty was delighted and flattered that he had asked. She contained her excitement and shared everything she knew. Having grown up in a Gym, she understood little details Ethan had never noticed. He learned a great deal from their conversation.

With Misty's help, he also tried several more specialized Water-type training methods in the lake, with good results.

By the end of the evening, he felt more confident about raising Feebas.

...

Early the next morning, they packed their belongings, buried the campfire ashes, and set out again.

After walking for a little over an hour, they left the plain behind, and Ethan arrived in Rustboro City for the second time.

With Misty beside him, he went straight to Rustboro Gym.

The official Pokemon League Gym stood in an open part of the city. Yellow earth and rocks surrounded it, clearly placed there to distinguish it from the busy streets nearby and tell challengers at a glance what type of Pokemon they would face.

The building itself looked like an immense imitation mountain, with the Gym carved into its base.

Its Leader, Roxanne, specialized in Rock-type Pokemon and was known as a talented student devoted to rocks. She also taught at a Pokemon Academy. Both jobs commanded respect and a measure of social standing, and she had a considerable reputation in Rustboro City.

Ethan composed himself, took a deep breath, and entered the Gym with Misty.

After greeting the receptionist, they were led directly to the battlefield.

Before they reached it, Ethan spotted a girl on the rock-strewn field. She wore a blue-gray skirt, red stockings, a red bow tie, and a matching ribbon in her hair. She was directing several students in matching uniforms as they cleaned up the field.

To be honest, it was hard to judge Roxanne's age.

Her clothes suggested a girl of seventeen or eighteen, but her face made her look about Ethan's age.

If he had to put it into words, Ethan thought she looked as though she were trying to dress younger.

He did not mean that as a criticism of her taste. Perhaps she simply had a youthful outlook and an image of herself she liked to hold on to.

Roxanne heard their footsteps and noticed them. She came forward a few steps, stopped before Ethan, and gave a small bow.

Hello. I'm Roxanne, the Gym Leader here. Welcome to Rustboro Gym!

Chapter 604: Ethan's Standards Have Risen

Hello, Roxanne. I'm Ethan, and I've come to challenge Rustboro Gym.

And I'm Misty, she added. I'm traveling with Ethan.

When Ethan introduced himself, Roxanne looked closely at his face. Surprise crossed her expression.

It's you! she said, her voice brightening. Only a few days ago, my students and I watched recordings of your Silver Conference battles and analyzed them together. I never expected to meet you in person so soon!

The students around her hurried over as though a celebrity had appeared. Excitedly, they asked Ethan for photos, and one of them even produced an autograph pen as if by magic.

Their enthusiasm was overwhelming, but understandable. These students had not yet left school. They rarely had a chance to meet a Trainer who had already achieved so much in Pokemon tournaments.

Beside Ethan, Misty proudly puffed out her still-small chest.

Seeing the person she liked held in such high regard made her happy too.

Ethan could only spare a little time to satisfy the students' requests. When their excitement finally eased, he turned his attention back to Roxanne.

She smiled. So you've come to Hoenn. Are you planning to enter the Ever Grande Conference? I can't wait to see how you perform there. Since it's you, would you like to battle my strongest Pokemon? To be honest, after watching your matches, I've wanted to face you myself.

Sorry, Ethan said, shaking his head. I've left my main team in someone else's care. This journey is mostly about training my new Pokemon. Please don't make any special arrangements for me. Treat me like a Trainer who's only just started out.

A beginner with two conference trophies? That's quite a remarkable beginner. Roxanne covered her mouth as she laughed, then nodded. All right. I'll treat you like an ordinary challenger and use my usual Gym team.

The students perked up at the prospect of a Gym battle. They moved to either side of the field and began setting up recording equipment.

Roxanne gave Ethan an apologetic smile. Would you mind if we record the match? As you can see, I teach at a Pokemon Academy as well as lead this Gym. These are my students and assistants. We usually record our battles with challengers, then discuss and analyze them afterward so the students can gain experience. I'd like to keep a recording of this one too.

Of course, Ethan said with a nod.

His tactics and other secrets were not at stake, and the Pokemon he would use were still new. If the students wanted to watch, he saw no reason to refuse. He could consider it a contribution to the Academy.

After a little more conversation, he and Roxanne took their places in the Trainer's areas on opposite sides of the field.

One of the older students served as referee and announced the rules.

The Rustboro Gym battle is about to begin! Each side may use two Pokemon. This is an elimination match, and only the challenger may switch Pokemon during the battle!

They were ordinary Gym rules. Most Gyms used much the same format.

With the rules settled, Ethan looked at Roxanne again.

At first glance, her clothes suited a quiet, dignified young woman. Once she stood on the battlefield, though, she showed another side: confident, with a different look on her face.

As Gym Leader, Roxanne sent out her Pokemon first. She threw a Poke Ball, and Geodude appeared on the field.

Geodude was a very common Rock-type Pokemon. For Trainers who specialized in Rock and Ground types, like Brock and Roxanne, having one on the team was hardly unusual.

Even Trainers outside those specialties often caught a Geodude if they favored a tougher battling style.

But being Gym Leaders did not mean Brock and Roxanne had Geodude of equal strength. Ethan would have to battle Roxanne's to find out which was stronger.

As for what to use against it...

After a moment's thought, Ethan sent out Eevee.

Of the Pokemon he had caught recently, Eevee was the one most ready for a Gym match. It had not evolved yet, but it had already built up plenty of experience and strength. All it lacked was the right item to trigger its evolution.

Once he found one and Eevee evolved, Ethan was sure it could rise to the level of Dragonite, Scizor, and Tyranitar on his current team.

Eevee appeared, eager to fight, and studied its opponent intently.

Roxanne smiled again. Unlike you, your Eevee doesn't seem very composed. It looks impatient.

That's true. Eevee's lively, Ethan said, looking at it fondly. But that's no bad thing. Pokemon with different personalities can bring out different tactics.

The Pokemon on the field were tense and ready to fight, but their Trainers were relaxed enough to joke with each other.

The one person who was not enjoying herself was Misty, seated in the stands.

Perhaps she was imagining things, or perhaps she had grown too quick to worry. Roxanne was so friendly toward Ethan that Misty feared the Gym Leader might develop designs on him if they spent more time together.

After all, Ethan's charm had already won over Sabrina and Erika. Misty herself had fallen for him too.

What reassured her a little was that although Roxanne had the same standing as Sabrina and Erika, she was nowhere near as beautiful.

Ethan would never fall for her!

Misty felt rather pleased with that thought. With Sabrina and Erika setting the standard, and the world's most beautiful girl sitting right here beside him, why would Ethan be interested in someone so ordinary-looking?

Ethan was focused on the battle and had no idea what Misty was thinking.

If he had known, he would surely have given her a sharp knock on the head!

Still, she was right about one thing. After Sabrina and Erika, and even Maya, Ethan's standards had indeed risen. Girls who were not especially striking no longer caught his eye.

Roxanne looked fairly ordinary at first glance and pretty enough on a closer look, but she did not make his heart stir at all.

Chapter 605: Cheering for the Challenger

At the referee's signal, the Gym challenge began.

Geodude raised its enormous fists and came toward Eevee, looking eager for a fight.

Perhaps some magnetic force inside it was responsible. Though it had a round body and no legs, Geodude could move forward in little hops and even float briefly in the air. It was a strange sight.

As a Normal type, Eevee had no advantage against Geodude. In fact, Geodude's Rock typing halved the damage it took from Normal-type attacks, which was bad news for Eevee.

Geodude's hard body was both reliable armor and a source of considerable force when it used attacks such as Tackle.

With one Pokemon's attacks weakened and the other's blows strengthened, Eevee seemed to be at a clear disadvantage. Roxanne found Ethan's choice puzzling.

As a Gym Leader and Pokemon Academy teacher, she understood type matchups better than most Trainers. She would never willingly send out a Pokemon at such a disadvantage, and a two-time conference champion like Ethan should know better too.

Why, then, had he chosen Eevee? Was he trying to train it to battle through an unfavorable matchup?

Before she could think further, the two Pokemon engaged.

Geodude used Mega Punch. Each swing of its fist seemed to carry tremendous weight, cutting forcefully through the air.

Eevee was not suited to trading close-range blows, and Ethan had no intention of letting it do so. He used Eevee's speed and the rocky terrain to approach from different directions, keeping Geodude occupied while looking for an opening.

But Geodude's fists guarded it so thoroughly that Eevee could find no gap.

Roxanne's students watched without blinking. Both Pokemon were unevolved, and neither was using especially advanced moves. Still, this was a battle between a champion and a Gym Leader. Ethan's name alone made it worth their full attention.

As the Pokemon exchanged attacks, Ethan considered how to break through.

His gaze passed over the large boulders on the field, and an idea came to him.

Eevee, jump onto those rocks!

Eevee leaped up. Geodude immediately followed so it could keep attacking. The short delay gave Eevee time to prepare.

Use Sand Attack!

Eevee turned its back to Geodude and kicked off the rock with both hind legs. A spray of grit and chips rained down into Geodude's face.

Geodude raised its hands to shield its eyes. For a moment it could neither continue its attack nor see where Eevee had gone.

When the spray cleared and Geodude looked up, Eevee's large head was already rushing toward it. Eevee slammed into its body.

Geodude had been climbing toward the rock where Eevee stood and was still suspended in the air. Without firm footing, it was knocked straight toward the ground.

Before it could recover, Eevee turned and kicked backward with both hind legs. Its Double Kick struck Geodude twice.

Bang!

Geodude flew back and did not stop until it hit a boulder behind it.

Its toughness deserved praise. An ordinary unevolved Pokemon might already have been knocked unconscious, but Geodude's stony body gave it remarkable resistance to physical blows. It looked battered, yet it could still fight.

Good work! Roxanne called. Geodude, hang in there! Use Rollout!

Geodude shook its head to clear the dizziness, wrapped its arms around its body, and rolled toward Eevee.

Ethan studied it. Geodude had already used up much of its strength. Rather than have Eevee evade again, he decided to meet it head-on and settle the round.

Eevee, use Take Down!

Take Down could inflict heavy damage, but it also hurt the Pokemon using it.

Ethan would not have taken that risk at a critical moment. Eevee, however, had come through the battle almost unhurt and still had plenty of energy.

Geodude rolled faster and faster, gathering formidable force. Eevee was no less determined. It burst forward and threw itself at Geodude without holding back.

Before everyone's eyes, they collided head-on.

The impact boomed through the spacious battlefield. Both Pokemon stopped short, then fell away to opposite sides.

It had been a brutal collision.

Fortunately, Eevee suffered little beyond a dizzy head and some aches. It was first to rise and immediately took a fighting stance again.

Geodude rolled backward a dozen times.

Ethan thought the round was over, but to his surprise, Geodude shakily pushed itself up once more.

An ordinary Trainer's Pokemon would have been unable to continue after a hit like that. Roxanne's Geodude could clearly take an exceptional amount of punishment.

Some of its endurance might be due to its resistance to Eevee's Normal-type attacks, but even so, it looked close to falling.

At Ethan's command, Eevee used Swift. The stars struck Geodude, and this time it finally went down.

That was one tough Pokemon...

Ethan smiled helplessly. Without a favorable type matchup, Ground- and Rock-type Pokemon were hard to bring down. They could absorb punishment and stubbornly keep fighting.

In her Trainer's area, Roxanne smiled as she recalled Geodude.

Although her opponent had used an Eevee, the result did not surprise her. The Trainer mattered as much as the Pokemon in a battle, and Ethan belonged among the very best.

Even Roxanne's students, whose Gym had just lost a Pokemon, showed no disappointment. Instead, they whispered excitedly about Eevee's performance.

Neither side had done anything particularly dazzling, but watching Ethan battle up close thrilled them all the same.

It was like seeing your favorite athlete perform a simple warm-up in front of you. Even that could set your heart racing.

Some of the students had already switched their loyalties in spirit. They were actually happy to see the challenger win!

Chapter 606: Eevee: I'll Take It On!

Roxanne took out her second Poke Ball. A flash of blue light revealed a Nosepass in front of Ethan.

It was an unusual Pokemon, as if a huge boulder had come to life. Its whole body was blue, with arms, legs, and a large red nose.

Nosepass was a pure Rock type. The magnet in its nose never failed and always pointed north. If someone became lost in the mountains, one look at a Nosepass's nose would tell them which way to go. That was how the Pokemon got its name.

There was another curious fact about the species. Because like magnetic poles repelled each other, two Nosepass could not bring their faces close together. Wild Nosepass were said to move only one centimeter in a year, though they could spin and dive underground in an instant when threatened.

A Nosepass could remain perfectly still and draw prey toward it with the powerful magnetism its body gave off. That magnetism grew stronger in colder seasons. Sometimes, however, it attracted a predator instead: Metang.

Ethan called Eevee back to his side and studied the Nosepass.

He remembered Roxanne's Nosepass well from the games. It was her signature Pokemon and had left a strong impression on him.

It was no pushover. When he challenged her in the games, a team without sufficiently strong Pokemon or a type advantage could easily need several Pokemon just to beat it.

Like Geodude, this Nosepass had a cold, stony body and looked difficult to damage. Eevee might not even be able to break its surface.

Ethan did not want Eevee to batter itself against a rock like that. After a moment's thought, he decided to answer Nosepass with a Pokemon that could meet its toughness head-on.

Before he had quite settled on his choice, something brushed against his trouser leg. He looked down. Eevee was gazing up at him, eager to go.

He raised an eyebrow. What? You still want to battle?

Eevee nodded emphatically and cried out.

The great stone Pokemon was much larger than Eevee, and Eevee's claws and teeth might not be able to scratch or bite through it. But Eevee was not afraid.

Ethan knew Eevee was unlikely to win. Even so, he agreed to let it take the field again.

Earning a Gym Badge was only one purpose of this challenge. More than that, he wanted to develop his Pokemon's abilities.

Even if Eevee lost and got hurt, it could still learn something from the defeat.

As soon as Ethan nodded, Eevee ran back to the middle of the field.

Roxanne had seen their exchange and understood what Ethan intended. She said nothing, merely smiling a little.

Once the battle began, she held nothing back and focused on directing Nosepass. Ethan, by contrast, fought much more cautiously.

Under his commands, Eevee gave everything it had. It raced around the rocky field, attacking from different angles and trying to bring Nosepass down. But it could not overcome the type disadvantage. At last, Nosepass used Rock Tomb, and Eevee fell.

The student serving as referee raised a colored flag. Eevee is unable to battle! Nosepass wins the second round!

With Eevee's defeat, the score stood at one to one.

Misty watched without much concern. Eevee was unevolved, had limited ways to attack, and faced a poor type matchup. It was never likely to hurt Nosepass badly. Its defeat had been predictable, but she knew Ethan would send in a stronger Pokemon to turn the battle around.

From his Trainer's area, Ethan recalled the unconscious Eevee.

The match had been brief, but it had not been pointless. Eevee had gained more battle experience, and Ethan had learned something about Nosepass that would help him in the next round.

He returned his attention to the field. This time he did not hesitate. With a sweep of his arm, he sent out Tyranitar.

Like the red Gyarados and Crystal Steelix before it, Tyranitar threw back its head and let out a deafening roar the moment it appeared.

Raaah!

Several of the more timid students went pale and stepped back. Even Misty, sitting in the stands, covered her ears.

No matter how many times she saw a fierce Pokemon like this one, its temper still frightened her.

Its strength aside, that sheer presence was impressive.

Roxanne nodded when she saw Ethan's choice.

Unlike Eevee, Tyranitar had the type advantage. Its Ground-type moves could hit Nosepass hard, and its armored body would not fare badly against stone. It was a sound choice.

Even so, Roxanne knew the match would be difficult for her.

She had watched Ethan's Silver Conference battles and seen how well this Tyranitar performed.

She could not be confident against a Pokemon capable of competing at that level. Perhaps her strongest Pokemon could give it a fight, but Nosepass...

Nosepass had helped her defeat many challengers, yet Roxanne knew it would probably struggle against Tyranitar.

It was not fear before the battle. It was the conclusion her experience and judgment had led her to.

The referee raised the flag again, and the third round began. If Ethan beat Nosepass, he would earn his first Hoenn Badge. If he lost, he would have to return and try the Gym again tomorrow.

Nosepass remained motionless. Tyranitar stamped a foot. Energy surged, and more than a dozen sharp stones burst up from the ground and thrust toward Nosepass.

Almost at the same instant, Nosepass used Stone Edge too. One wave of stone spikes raced from east to west and the other from west to east, until they crashed together.

Bang, bang, bang!

The two Stone Edge attacks shattered against each other, spraying fragments into the air. The chips fell back onto both Pokemon, striking their hard bodies with a series of little clinks.

As the dust and stones cleared, both Pokemon opened their mouths almost at once and launched their second attacks.

Chapter 607: The Stone Badge and Meteor Falls

Nosepass fell.

Just as Roxanne had expected before the battle, it could not beat Tyranitar. Ethan had also used Eevee's round to get a general sense of Nosepass's abilities, so the outcome was hardly surprising.

Tyranitar had not won effortlessly, though. Nosepass had given it some trouble, and the fight had been far from meaningless.

Applause rose from outside the field. Roxanne's students clapped for Ethan's victory.

They were cheering against their own teacher, but they could hardly help themselves. Today's challenger was far too popular.

Roxanne glanced at the students and smiled helplessly. She recalled Nosepass and walked over to Ethan.

She took out an earthy yellow Badge and held it out to him.

Congratulations on winning. This is the Stone Badge, proof that you defeated me. Please accept it.

Ethan thanked her and took the Badge. Curious as ever, Misty hurried over to examine this Hoenn Gym Badge with him.

It looked like two triangular pieces of ore set slightly out of alignment. The design was distinctive, and, like most Hoenn Badges, it used a gradient of color. Ethan thought Hoenn's Badges were prettier and more finely made than those of Johto and Kanto.

He placed the Stone Badge in his Badge case and put the case back in his bag.

Nurse Joy had given him the plain case at the Pokemon Center in Oldale Town after he registered with the Pokemon League. With his first Badge inside it, Ethan had taken a firm first step toward the Ever Grande Conference.

A journey of a thousand miles began with a single step. Catching the first Pokemon and earning the first Badge were good beginnings.

With the challenge finished, Ethan said it was time to go.

Roxanne and her students warmly invited him and Misty to stay for lunch and talk more about battling, but Ethan politely declined.

Erika had only just left, and he was not in the mood. His backtracking over the past several days had cost him time, too. Ash would arrive in Hoenn soon, and the thought made Ethan feel some urgency.

He could not help it. Ash improved so quickly that Ethan had to keep pushing himself if he wanted to stay ahead.

Ethan and Misty left Rustboro Gym and headed out of the city.

Their destination was Lavaridge Town, surrounded by mountains to the northeast. It had Lavaridge Gym, the nearest Gym town apart from Petalburg, and its famous hot springs could ease sore muscles before the next stretch of their journey.

They traveled north.

As they went, the broad road narrowed into a path and then a winding track of loose stone. By noon, when they were ready for a break, they had reached the foot of an unbroken mountain range.

They looked out at one towering rocky mountain after another, with no end in sight.

Oh no. Looks like we have another climb ahead of us...

They exchanged weary looks, then sat on rocks beneath a large tree to rest.

After drinking some water and eating their packed lunches, they stared at the seemingly endless mountains and lamented the time and effort it would take to cross them. Then an old man in a straw hat, carrying a bamboo basket on his back, strolled out from another direction.

Misty spotted him. An idea came to her, and she approached with a bright smile.

Excuse me, sir, she asked sweetly. Do you know a shortcut through these mountains?

She clearly did not relish another mountain trek. Despite her habit of calling herself the world's most beautiful girl, she was a delicate young woman with soft arms and legs. Given a choice, why would she want to scramble along a mountain trail?

The man looked to be over seventy. He lowered his gaze to Misty, and her smile won him over. Without hesitation, he nodded and pointed to a concealed cave not far away.

Of course. See that cave entrance? It's a shortcut. He looked at them kindly and added, You two are Trainers, aren't you? Be careful inside. Don't get separated, and don't go chasing after any Pokemon. There are passages leading every which way, and it's easy to get lost. Once you do, finding your way out is hard. Stay on the main path and you'll get through safely.

Stay on the main path? Misty repeated, then nodded. Don't worry. We'll be careful!

They thanked the old man. Misty returned to Ethan with a delighted expression and raised her eyebrows at him triumphantly.

He knew how pleased she was to avoid the climb and gave a helpless smile.

He was glad of the shortcut too. Walking through a cave would be more comfortable than struggling over high mountains under the sun and wind.

Once they had rested enough, they set out again.
