From a distance, the opening had looked small. Up close, they found the entrance was five or six meters high. The level gravel beneath their feet looked maintained, suggesting people used this route often.

That reassured them further. The cave really did seem to be a shortcut.

The temperature dropped sharply when they entered, but they had put on thicker clothes beforehand and were comfortable enough.

The old man had said the main path would take them through safely. Even so, Ethan released Eevee and Torchic as a precaution.

The farther they went, the darker it became. They turned their flashlights up to their brightest setting so they could see the way ahead.

Fortunately, the cave was neither a limestone cavern nor an icy tunnel like others Ethan had traveled. The path was easy enough to walk. The only discomfort was a damp draft that blew from somewhere deeper inside and slipped through their collars and sleeves.

Ethan pulled his clothes tighter and swept his flashlight from side to side.

The old man had been right. Beyond the main trail, countless passages branched off in both directions. Some entrances were large, but most were small enough only for little Pokemon to pass through.

How had the first person to discover this shortcut ever found their way out?

That thought made Ethan turn to Misty. Did the old man tell you what this place is called?

Misty thought for a moment, then nodded. I think he called it... Meteor Falls.

Chapter 608: The Twenty-First Pokemon and the Key Stone

Meteor Falls?

The name sounded familiar to Ethan. He thought the place appeared in the games, though he could not remember the details. But a place called a waterfall must have plenty of water, and water would attract more wild Pokemon.

Could they find a rare species here?

He held his curiosity in check, and the two continued along the main path.

As he had guessed, the deeper they went, the more Pokemon they encountered. There were more kinds of them too.

Some, like Diglett, Dugtrio, Geodude, Graveler, Onix, and Golbat, were common in Kanto and Johto. Others, such as Lunatone and Solrock, were Pokemon neither of them had seen before.

Ethan even caught a glimpse of an Aron darting into a small cave.

Misty watched it disappear. If Brock came here, he'd think he'd found paradise!

Ethan laughed and was about to answer when his flashlight illuminated a small, unusual Pokemon floating a short distance away.

Is that...?

Startled, he quickly aimed his Pokedex at it. Though the cave was dim, the device soon returned an entry.

Beldum, the Iron Ball Pokemon. A Steel- and Psychic-type Pokemon. Its cells are said to be magnets, with magnetic force circulating through its body in place of blood. By repelling the planet's magnetic field, it can float in the air. Beldum gathered in groups move together with the coordination of a single Pokemon and communicate through changes in their magnetic fields. In battle, Beldum sends out magnetism from its rear to pull an opponent close, then pierces it with its sharp claw. When angered, it may rampage and release a powerful magnetic field that damages machinery. If you encounter a Beldum in poor condition, give it a magnet.

Beldum?

Misty studied it with interest after hearing the entry. She walked closer until she could see it clearly.

Despite its name, it looked more like a stone security camera than a dumbbell to her. A crest rose above its almost round head, and its long body ended in a large claw. The head sat at the front of the body like a ball in a socket, with one large red eye at its center.

Misty often met Pokemon that resembled animals or plants, but she had never heard of one shaped like a dumbbell.

The world held all sorts of things. Then she remembered Magnemite, a common sight in Kanto. If there could be a Pokemon that looked like screws, a dumbbell-like Pokemon was not so strange after all.

She was about to keep walking when she turned and saw Ethan striding toward Beldum, already reaching for a Poke Ball at his waist.

Ethan, do you want to catch it? she asked in surprise.

Of course! He took a ball in hand and sent Torchic toward Beldum. Then he turned back to Misty. It may be small and unremarkable now, but its final evolution, Metagross, is incredibly strong.

Metagross? Misty gave a half-understanding nod. She had never seen one, but if Ethan said it was strong, she trusted his judgment.

Torchic ran up to Beldum on its two little legs.

It cried at Beldum excitedly. Beldum merely glanced at it, turned away, and floated into a side passage.

Ethan followed without hesitation, with Torchic at his side. After a moment, Misty hurried after them. Ethan, wait! Have you forgotten what the old man said? We have to stay on the main path or we'll get lost!

Ethan kept walking. He looked back and laughed. We're Trainers. Why let rules like that stop us? Don't worry; we'll find a way through. A few confusing paths are no great obstacle. Come on, before it gets away!

Perhaps his smile was infectious. Misty nodded firmly, put the warning out of her mind, and followed with quick steps.

Why worry? As long as she was with Ethan, what would it matter if they spent weeks trying to get out of this cave?

Beldum floated ahead, Torchic close behind. Ethan and Misty followed a little farther back.

They did not lose ground, and Beldum was not particularly fast. But it could fly over obstacles while they had to watch the uneven path beneath their feet, so they could not run at full speed.

They chased it for some time, turning left and right, crossing an underground river, and heading deeper into the cave. By the time Beldum stopped, they were so far from the main path that they could no longer find their way back.

Ethan had no attention to spare for that now. Seeing Beldum hovering in place, he realized they had reached its habitat.

Many unusual minerals lay nearby. They appeared to be magnetic, and that magnetism was Beldum's food.

Ethan glanced at Torchic. Chirping, it charged Beldum again and used Ember, sending hot sparks from its beak.

Beldum hung in the air, watching the people and Pokemon with its single eye. Its expressionless face gave Ethan no clue what it felt.

Perhaps it was confused. People might occasionally pass through the cave, but Beldum had probably only ever seen them from afar. This was likely the first time anyone had chased it and stood in its path.

Maybe no one had ever disturbed it, or maybe it had no predators here. It seemed to have lost all caution. Beldum did not even try to dodge before Ember struck it.

Ethan frowned. After finally finding a Beldum, had he found a foolish one?

Only when the flames burned it did Beldum seem to understand that it was under attack. Belatedly, it twisted to extinguish the fire and lunged at Torchic.

Torchic did not need a command to avoid that attack. It simply hopped aside.

Then Torchic raised one claw and scratched Beldum, jolting its whole body.

Beldum turned and used Tackle again. Torchic dodged as before and landed another hit.

After this happened several times, Misty looked at Ethan. She hesitated before asking, Ethan... why does Beldum keep using the same attack? Doesn't it know any other moves?

No, it doesn't. Wild Beldum that haven't been trained only know Tackle, despite being Steel and Psychic types. It looks weak now, but like Magikarp, it'll gain tremendous strength after it evolves.

The comparison to Magikarp gave Misty a clearer picture. Beldum's Tackle was rather like Magikarp's Splash.

She had still not overcome her fear of Gyarados, but she knew that a Pokemon weak at first could change dramatically through evolution.

Once Torchic understood Beldum's simple pattern, it handled the battle with ease.

Before long, another Ember knocked Beldum to the ground.

Ethan threw the Poke Ball he had been holding at it.

He and Misty watched as a red beam drew Beldum inside. The ball rolled several times on the ground, then came to rest with a click.

After so long on the road, Ethan no longer showed much excitement when he caught an ordinary Pokemon, unlike when he captured a Legendary Pokemon. Still, he was pleased, and a faint smile appeared on his face.

Misty clapped happily. Congratulations, Ethan! Which number Pokemon is this for you?

My twenty-first, he answered without hesitation.

Including Beldum, he now carried eleven Pokemon, leaving only one place below his limit of twelve.

He had not expected to catch them so quickly. He had been in Hoenn only a few days and had already added three new Pokemon.

Ethan picked up the ball and was about to leave, but he looked around the area once more.

Minerals of many kinds lay scattered about. He recognized some and could not name others.

In one corner, something glinted in the beam of his flashlight.

Curious, he went over and picked up a small, round stone as clear as crystal.

What's this? Misty came closer. A mark like a crescent moon showed on its surface. It doesn't look natural. More like a carved gemstone.

Ethan studied it for a while before saying uncertainly, I think it's a Key Stone.

A Key Stone? Misty had clearly never heard the name. What's that?

Remember the Mega Stones I found earlier? Ethan asked.

Of course.

This is what works with them. It's a natural stone, though no one knows exactly how it forms. What people do know is that it holds a mysterious power. It resonates with a Mega Stone carried by a Pokemon and lets that Pokemon Mega Evolve.

Mega Evolution! Once Misty heard what the stone was for, she forgot her questions about how it had formed.

She crouched and searched the ground carefully. Before long, she had found another seven or eight Key Stones.

Delighted, she divided the stones into two shares. She kept one and gave the other to Ethan. Whether they used them later or gave them away, the find was an unexpected prize.

Misty eagerly searched the area again but found nothing else. Satisfied with what they already had, she gathered her things and turned back with Ethan toward the way they had come.

They had walked barely a dozen steps when the first fork brought them to a halt.

Which way did we come from? Misty looked left and right. They had run so quickly after Beldum that she had paid no attention to the details.

Ethan shook his head too. He had been focused on Beldum and had not watched the route.

Misty sighed. We should have marked the way.

It's all right, Ethan said with a smile. There's a little trick for situations like this. If we keep going in the same direction, we'll generally reach an exit, as long as this isn't a particularly complicated maze.

It was a technique he knew from exploring outdoors. And if it failed, their Pokemon could help. They would not be trapped here forever; the question was only how long it would take to get out.

After discussing it, they chose the passage farthest to the right. They walked for a long time before noticing that the ground beneath their feet was growing damp. Somewhere ahead, they heard flowing water.

They exchanged a look. This was not the route they had taken in. But after coming so far, neither wanted to turn back, so they followed the sound.

The path sloped gently upward. The rush of water grew louder. They turned a corner, ducked through an opening only just high enough to pass, and suddenly found themselves in bright light.

Before them, more than a dozen waterfalls of different sizes formed a vast cascade inside the cavern. Water thundered down. A huge opening in the cave roof let sunlight pour in, driving away the gloom.

At the foot of the falls lay an enormous round pit. Its shape did not look like the work of running water. It looked more like the mark of a meteorite impact.

Misty looked up at the falls. Over the roar, she had to raise her voice as she spoke near Ethan's ear. This must be Meteor Falls, right?

Ethan did not know the waterfall's name for certain.

Still, this must be the place. With a crater like that, the connection to meteors was hard to miss. And when he looked closely, droplets sprayed from the highest falls like countless shooting stars. The sight was magnificent.

Chapter 609: I'll Catch Them Both Off Guard

They could leave the cave through the opening overhead and find their bearings on the surface at once. But that would defeat the purpose of taking this shortcut through the mountains.

Misty had thought of that too and was about to discuss it with Ethan. Before she could speak, he came closer and put a finger to his lips.

She blinked in confusion. Ethan pulled her behind a boulder and pointed into the distance.

On the far side of the waterfall, more than a hundred meters away, a group in matching blue-and-white uniforms was pushing and dragging a bespectacled man toward a cave entrance.

Misty's eyes widened. Someone was being kidnapped!

She turned to ask Ethan what they should do, but the frown on his face suggested he recognized the group. Ethan, do you know those people?

He nodded. They're Team Aqua.

Team Aqua?

They're an organization in this region, something like Team Rocket. But they aren't evil, and they don't go around stealing other people's Pokemon.

Huh? Misty raised an eyebrow. That doesn't sound so bad.

Ethan shook his head. Their ultimate goal is to expand the ocean. They say they want to restore habitats Pokemon have lost to human greed. They believe the sea is the source of all life, and they want to reclaim it and create an ideal home for Pokemon.

Oh. Misty's mouth fell open. So that means...

Exactly. They want to control Kyogre, one of the ancient Pokemon and ruler of the sea, flood the land, and increase the ocean's size!

Misty understood now. Team Rocket wanted to capture the strongest Pokemon and rule the world. Team Aqua had a narrower aim, but it intended to upset the existing ecological balance and remake the world.

Why did every organization like this cause so much trouble?

As she was thinking that, another group arrived quietly. They wore cloaks of the same color as one another and slipped into the cave after Team Aqua.

Who are they?

Team Magma. Ethan told her about his earlier encounter with them in Rustboro City. They're another organization here. Like Team Aqua, they want to control an ancient Pokemon. Their target isn't Kyogre, though. It's Groudon, the ruler of the land.

Another ancient Pokemon, Misty said flatly. Don't tell me they have the same sort of plan?

You've got it. Ethan gave her an approving thumbs-up. Team Magma wants to expand the land and give humans more room to live. They believe human progress is closely tied to the world's happiness, and that coexistence with Pokemon holds that progress back. With their opposing beliefs, the two groups are always at odds in Hoenn. They fight often.

Misty rubbed her temples.

It was all too complicated. Given a choice, she would rather face Team Rocket than an argument about how the world should sustain life.

Do you know the man they took?

Ethan shook his head. He had not been in Hoenn long and knew few people here. He had also forgotten some of what happened in the anime and games; even characters who had appeared there were hard to recall clearly.

Whatever the details, Team Aqua and Team Magma had both come to this remote part of the cave. Something important was clearly happening.

For the world's ecological safety, and for his own, Ethan could not ignore it.

They waited a little longer. When no one else appeared, Misty called out Starmie. With its help, they slipped into the pool and crossed quickly and silently to the other side of the falls.

The thunder of falling water covered what little noise they made.

At the entrance the two groups had used, Ethan and Misty peered inside. The others were already out of sight.

Team Aqua apparently had no idea anyone was following them. Team Magma thought it had stalked its prey unseen, but it did not know someone was following it in turn.

Ethan recalled the Pokemon beside him, then sent out Gardevoir and called Gengar forward.

They entered cautiously, leaving their flashlights off. Gengar scouted ahead. After a while, they spotted Team Magma hiding behind a cluster of rocks farther down the passage.

Team Aqua stood beyond them.

Its members were saying something to the man they had kidnapped, but they were too far away for Ethan to hear.

He signaled to Gengar, which understood at once, sank into the ground, and headed toward them from below.

Before it reached them, the situation changed.

Perhaps Team Magma had grown impatient or decided the moment was right. Its members burst from cover and attacked Team Aqua.

The surprise worked. Team Aqua had not expected an assault. Several members fell before they could organize a proper defense.

While everyone was distracted, Ethan and Misty crept to the rocks Team Magma had just left. From there, they could hear the voices and the sounds of fighting clearly.

They could see the members of both teams properly now, too.

Each side had about a dozen people in matching uniforms. Only the two women leading them stood out from their teams.

Team Aqua's leader was a tall woman of about twenty-six or twenty-seven. She wore sunglasses on her head instead of a bandanna and no standard uniform. A top left her midriff bare, and her trousers exposed the outsides of her thighs. Slightly wavy black hair fell down her back. Her skin was a little dark, and although Ethan did not consider her particularly beautiful, she looked sharp and capable.

Team Magma's leader was also a woman, but much younger, perhaps eighteen or nineteen. She wore a red hood like her teammates. Pale purple hair and a delicate face showed beneath it. Her red short skirt and high boots gave her a look both demure and cute.

The two leaders clearly knew each other. While their teams fought, they stood in place and stared coldly across the field.

The hooded young woman called to the taller one. You weren't expecting us, were you? Team Magma has an intelligence network too. Don't think you're the only ones who found this lead!

The tall woman was unmoved. You caught us off guard. Do you really think that's enough? How naive. We surveyed this place a week ago. We know where every passage leads. If we decide to leave, none of you can stop us.

Leave? It won't be that easy, the young woman said. Enough talk. Hand over that man!

She meant the bespectacled man Team Aqua had kidnapped. Ethan looked at him more carefully. He appeared to be around forty, with small round glasses, untidy hair, and a vest. He had the look of a scholar.

Rope bound him, and he stood behind the tall woman with a panicked expression, as though he had no idea what was happening.

The tall woman gave her younger rival a sidelong glance. Dream on. We went to a great deal of trouble to bring Professor Cozmo here. Why would we give him to you? Courtney, I know what Team Magma wants. You plan to find the meteorite, stir up the volcano here, and make it erupt, all for that ridiculous dream of yours!

Our dream is ridiculous? Courtney frowned. Shelly, yours is just as absurd! Why are you after the meteorite? For your own laughable dream, of course!

What did you say?

You heard me!

The two traded barbs with satisfaction, but their argument also told Ethan and Misty what was going on.

There must be a meteorite with unusual power somewhere here, and the kidnapped professor was an expert on it. Both teams wanted his help finding it for their hidden plans.

The fighting inside the cave continued fiercely. Pokemon fell on both sides. Team Magma had the advantage, but Team Aqua was recovering from its initial confusion and retreating toward a side passage as it fought.

Ethan and Misty exchanged a look.

What do you want to do? Misty whispered.

Isn't it obvious? Ethan grinned and took a Great Ball from his waist pouch. Neither side is here for anything good. We'll use the confusion to give them both a big surprise.

Misty looked at the ball. You're bringing out a Legendary Pokemon already?

She knew Ethan well enough to recognize that he kept his Legendary Pokemon in several Great Balls, apart from his other powerful partners. The ball in his hand told her what he intended.

We've crossed these people before, Ethan said. There's no reason to worry about offending them again. Let's make this count.

He quietly opened the Great Ball. Blue light flashed, and Raikou appeared beside him.

Raikou shook its head, seemingly unaccustomed to the darkness.

Ethan stroked its head and whispered instructions into its ear. Then he pointed ahead. Raikou sprang away like a streak of lightning, racing toward Team Magma and Team Aqua.

The golden electricity drew Courtney's and Shelly's attention almost at once.

Who's there? they shouted together.

They looked up and saw Raikou racing toward them amid crackling lightning. It was almost upon them.

Is that... a Pokemon?

Both women frowned. Neither recognized it immediately.

That was understandable. Raikou was a Legendary Pokemon of Johto, rarely seen even by people who lived there. These two were from Hoenn. Even if they had heard of Raikou, they would not necessarily connect the name to the Pokemon before them at a glance.

While they hesitated, Raikou reached the teams.

A dazzling burst of electricity erupted from its body and spread in every direction. The members of both teams and their Pokemon were caught unprepared and struck by the current.

No one had expected this turn.

When the teams first saw the extraordinary stranger, its grace and mystery had drawn their attention. They thought they had found a rare Pokemon. None expected it to attack without warning.

Damn it! Are we under attack?

Courtney and Shelly both looked toward the direction Raikou had come from, but they saw only darkness.

No one?

Was this a wild Pokemon attacking them because they had entered its territory? They had never heard of a Pokemon like this living near Meteor Falls.

Raikou's arrival changed the balance of the fight at once.

Team Magma was closest to the first burst and suffered the heaviest losses. But Raikou's attacks struck indiscriminately. A second wave of electricity brought down many Team Aqua members and Pokemon too.

Realizing how powerful the unknown Pokemon was, Courtney and Shelly gave the same order almost together. Stop staring! Catch it!

The teams broke off their fight and turned their Pokemon against Raikou.

Raikou was agile, though, and its electric attacks were fierce. Their ordinary Pokemon were no match for it. As soon as they engaged, more of them fell.

Meanwhile, Ethan and Misty slipped toward the battlefield.

In the confusion, no one noticed two dark figures drawing closer to Professor Cozmo.

Chapter 610: Zinnia

The broad cave, strewn with loose stones, suited Raikou well.

Team Magma and Team Aqua had plenty of Pokemon, but Raikou used the uneven ground to stay ahead of them. Fighting alone meant it did not have to avoid an ally's attacks, and that freedom became an advantage.

Courtney and Shelly frowned when all those Pokemon failed to bring it down.

They could see that their people were trying. The stranger was simply too strong. Even its ordinary electric shocks seemed far more destructive than those of most Electric-type Pokemon.

Courtney was the first to lose patience. She raised a hand and sent out her own Pokemon.

It was a large creature with long orange-red fur, a head rather like a donkey's, a camel-like body, and two rocky humps on its back.

Camerupt, a Fire- and Ground-type Pokemon that lived in tropical regions.

It stood almost two meters tall. The moment it appeared, its presence set it apart from the other Pokemon on the field.

At Courtney's command, Camerupt advanced slowly toward Raikou and opened its mouth to spray a stream of scorching flame.

Across the battlefield, Shelly was about to send out a Pokemon of her own. But something felt wrong. She stopped and scanned the cavern carefully instead.

Courtney had once been a scientist and was now a field commander. Shelly, meanwhile, was regarded as Team Aqua's strategist. Despite her daring, revealing clothes, she was observant and known for her sharp mind. Only the team's leader held more influence within Team Aqua.

That was why the sudden appearance of a Pokemon that hurled electricity had bothered her from the start. There had to be more to this than it seemed.

Her close watch rewarded her. At the edge of the battlefield, two figures, one taller and one shorter, were creeping up behind her. They were not Team Magma members. One was a man she had never seen before, the other a girl in her teens.

Who were they? Where had they come from?

Her eyes narrowed. Stop! Who are you?

The shout exposed Ethan and Misty and drew Courtney's attention to them as well.

Courtney could see they had sneaked in behind her team. They must have been followed. She glared at the pair with open hostility.

Ethan was not particularly surprised to be caught. Between the dark cave and the chaotic battle, he had managed to get closer than he expected.

With both women's eyes on him, he shouted, Now!

Before anyone understood what was happening, Gengar rose from the ground in the middle of the battlefield. It gave a chilling cackle, holding a sphere of dark energy in each hand, and hurled both into the crowd.

Bang! Bang!

Boom! Boom!

The spheres exploded among them. It happened so quickly that even Raikou's sudden arrival seemed tame by comparison. Team Magma and Team Aqua had no time to defend themselves; their members were blown off their feet.

At the same moment, Raikou redoubled its assault. It roared and gathered power in its mouth. A moment later, a brilliant electric blast like a cannon shot out, dividing the battlefield in two.

It was Zap Cannon, a powerful Electric-type move.

It might not be the single most damaging Electric attack, but it could still bring a battle to an end.

Working together from inside and outside the groups, Gengar and Raikou brought down most of the nearby people and Pokemon. Even Courtney and Shelly were caught in the shock wave and fell backward onto the ground.

Ethan and Misty used that moment to hurry to Professor Cozmo. They cut the ropes around him with a knife, took his hand, and led him back the way they had come.

Electricity and the exploding dark spheres broke apart many of the rocks. The whole cavern trembled faintly.

Dust filled the air. Shelly and Courtney covered their mouths and noses. They now knew for certain that the unfamiliar Pokemon had been sent by someone.

Its Trainer had to be one of the two people escaping with Professor Cozmo.

By the time the dust settled, the pair had vanished. So had Raikou and Gengar.

Damn it!

Courtney sprang up, ready to lead a pursuit, but Shelly suddenly burst into laughter beside her.

What are you laughing at? Courtney demanded coldly.

Shelly laughed so hard that tears gathered at the corners of her eyes.

At you, of course. You went to all the trouble of following us here, only to end up doing someone else's work for them!

Courtney glared. And you didn't? Your team put even more effort into this than ours!

I don't care. Shelly spread her hands. Our main objective has always been in the ocean. The meteorite would only have given us another way to achieve it. Losing it won't hurt us much. But seeing how badly this upsets you? Nothing could make me happier.

The rival organizations hated each other so much that one side's setback pleased the other more than its own success might have.

Courtney knew Shelly was provoking her, yet she could not keep her anger down.

Team Magma had spent a long time planning this operation, moving people into place and watching Team Aqua closely. Courtney had expected to deal its rival a serious blow. Instead, a stranger had taken the prize.

She had no time to argue. With a wave of her hand, she rallied her team and led them after Ethan.

Once they were gone, a Team Aqua member helped Shelly to her feet. Boss, what do we do?

Her smile vanished, and anger flashed in her eyes. We go after them too, of course!

For all her talk about not caring, she had only been trying to mislead Team Magma and infuriate Courtney. Team Aqua had spent weeks on this. Losing Professor Cozmo mattered very much.

Shelly intended to find out who was bold enough to cross Hoenn's two largest criminal organizations at the same time.

And this time, she would follow Team Magma's example and wait for a chance to benefit from someone else's fight.

She gathered her scattered members and led them after Ethan and Team Magma.

Elsewhere in the maze of caves, Ethan, Misty, and Professor Cozmo were running back toward Meteor Falls along the route they had taken.

When they reached the waterfall, Ethan started toward another passage. Professor Cozmo called him back.

Wait! This way!

The professor was beckoning from a different opening. Ethan and Misty followed him into a narrow cave where only one person could move sideways through at a time.

They had barely turned into it when Courtney and her team reached the waterfall behind them.

The delay had cost Team Magma sight of their quarry.

More than a hundred openings of different sizes surrounded the falls. Anyone could be hiding in any one of them. Most pursuers would have been at a loss, but Team Magma was accustomed to operating underground and had its own way of tracking people.

Its members released several Houndoom. The fierce, dog-like Pokemon, at home around caves and lava, sniffed the ground before racing toward the narrow passage Cozmo had chosen.

Excitement flashed in Courtney's eyes. There! After them!

Ethan heard the commotion and looked back. They had found his trail again. He shook his head helplessly.

They were persistent. No wonder Team Magma had managed to follow Team Aqua so long without being discovered. Those noses were useful.

One group fled, the other gave chase.

Professor Cozmo seemed to know the cave. He led Ethan and Misty through one turn after another, deeper inside.

It was not enough to shake Team Magma. The gap narrowed until Ethan could almost hear their labored breathing.

He was considering stopping to hold them off when he heard stones shifting overhead.

He looked up. A huge boulder fell from above and landed behind them, sealing the passage completely.

Before they could recover from the surprise, a girl's voice called from a ledge high above.

Come this way!

A vine dropped down in front of them.

It was too dark for Ethan to see the speaker's face, but her clear voice sounded young.

Professor Cozmo, who was leading, seized the vine and climbed without hesitation. Ethan recalled Raikou, then he and Misty climbed after the professor onto the ledge.

Only there did Ethan see the girl clearly.

She looked seventeen or eighteen and was strikingly beautiful. Short black hair fell below her jaw. She wore a cape over a black T-shirt, shorts that exposed the tops of her thighs, and a strange-looking band around one ankle. There was something mysterious and a little wild about her.

Most distinctive of all was the odd, scale-shaped collar visible at her neckline.

Her appearance was so recognizable that Ethan knew her almost at once. This was Zinnia, a character with an important role in the games.

At her feet stood a round pink Whismur with large ears. It had evidently pushed the boulder down to block the passage.

Before Ethan could say anything, Zinnia quickly drew up the vine. This isn't the place to talk. Follow me!

She turned and went into a deep tunnel behind her. At that moment, Team Magma smashed through the boulder below. Ethan and Misty wasted no time. They followed Professor Cozmo into the tunnel.

The passage was only a little taller than a person and stretched a long way into the darkness. Yet Zinnia moved quickly without a flashlight, as though she could see perfectly well.

After a long walk and a crossing of another underground river, she finally stopped.

Ethan looked around. They had reached a stone chamber furnished with a stone bed, stone cabinets, and other belongings. Someone appeared to live here regularly.

Zinnia lit an oil lamp on a stone table, illuminating the room.

She looked first at Professor Cozmo and shook her head. I didn't expect Team Aqua to catch you. That was careless.

Those words alone told Ethan that Zinnia and the professor knew each other.

Professor Cozmo sighed without answering her. He turned to Ethan and Misty instead.

Thank you for saving me. I haven't even asked your names.

I'm Ethan, and this is Misty. We're Trainers passing through. We saw Team Aqua abduct you at Meteor Falls and followed them. That's how we ended up there.

I see. Cozmo thanked them again. Without their help, Team Aqua or Team Magma would likely have held him captive and forced him to help them find the meteorite.

Then something seemed to occur to him. He pushed up his glasses and asked eagerly, Ethan, was that Raikou, the Legendary Pokemon from Johto?

As a Pokemon researcher, Cozmo had recognized more than the two commanders had. His words were a question, but he already sounded certain.

Zinnia looked at Ethan with curiosity when she heard the name too.

Yes. Ethan nodded. He had sent Raikou into the open and had no reason to hide it. That was Raikou. It's my Pokemon now.

Cozmo looked at him with newfound respect. The man standing before him had caught a Legendary Pokemon. Even Zinnia could not help studying Ethan with greater interest.

Chapter 611: The Tables Turn

As Zinnia studied Ethan, he happened to turn toward her. Their eyes met.

She did not seem embarrassed to be caught looking. Instead, she smiled slightly and introduced herself. Hello. I'm Zinnia, a descendant of the Draconid people.

The Draconid people?

Misty had only recently arrived in Hoenn and had never heard the name. Most people in the region probably had not heard of them either.

Zinnia turned to her and waved the question away. We're just people whose families have lived near Meteor Falls for generations. We have a different name, that's all. It's nothing special.

It was hardly that simple, Ethan thought.

Despite Zinnia's casual explanation, he knew the Draconids were more than ordinary people living apart from the world. They were Trainers who specialized in Dragon-type Pokemon.

They lived in the hidden Draconid Village beneath Meteor Falls, reached by an underground waterway.

The reason they had remained here went back two thousand years, to a battle between Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre.

According to the records, the two ancient Pokemon had fought fiercely, causing devastation as meteors streaked across the night sky. Their battle ended only when a third ancient Pokemon, Rayquaza, appeared.

A thousand years later, a meteor fell on what was now Sootopolis City and awakened Groudon and Kyogre. The Draconids' Lorekeeper of that time stood upon a rainbow stone and prayed for Rayquaza's return. Her wish brought about Rayquaza's Mega Evolution. After the ensuing battle, Groudon and Kyogre returned to the depths, and Rayquaza went back to the sky.

Afterward, the Draconids built Sky Pillar to honor their god and painted murals on its walls. They foretold that another meteor would strike the world after the next thousand years. When it came, helpless people would have to call upon Rayquaza again to protect the planet.

They sounded like guardians of the world and devoted followers of Rayquaza.

Professor Cozmo heard Zinnia's modest description and, worried that Ethan and Misty might not know the truth, explained the Draconids himself. His account was much the same as what Ethan already knew.

For Ethan, it was a familiar story. Misty finally understood what sort of people Zinnia came from.

Groudon... Kyogre... and Rayquaza... Misty murmured, longing in her eyes. Hoenn has so many incredible Pokemon.

Ethan smiled. It's no stranger than Ho-Oh and Lugia in Kanto and Johto. Pokemon like them possess immense power, remain hidden in the world, and are often revered as gods. Raikou is a Legendary Pokemon too, but those three are on another level.

Thinking of Ho-Oh and Lugia helped Misty grasp what Groudon and the others might be like. Ho-Oh could bring the dead back to life, and Lugia was called the god of the sea. These Hoenn Pokemon must have their own extraordinary powers.

They talked for a while longer. Ethan and Misty learned that Cozmo and Zinnia had met only recently. Cozmo had come alone to investigate meteorites, lost his way, and happened to be rescued by Zinnia. Team Aqua had taken an interest in him around that time, leading to his abduction.

By the way, Misty asked belatedly, Professor Cozmo, what field do you study?

Me? He shrugged. Meteorites. All kinds of meteorites. Did you know that wormholes can even send a meteorite to another universe?

Perhaps he rarely had anyone to discuss his work with. Once he began, he talked without stopping. Zinnia finally coughed a few times, and Cozmo realized he had been going on too long. He fell silent in embarrassment.

They stayed in the chamber for a long while without Team Magma or Team Aqua finding them, and gradually relaxed their guard.

By the time it was around three or four in the afternoon, they left the hiding place by another passage and headed for the surface.

With Zinnia guiding them through the caves she had known since childhood, they no longer had to worry about getting lost. She soon led them toward the nearest exit.

The journey had been peaceful. As they drew closer to daylight, their steps grew lighter.

Then, near the exit, Team Magma ambushed them.

After losing their trail in the maze, Courtney had stopped to think rather than search blindly. The tunnels were complicated, but only a few openings led outside. If her team waited long enough at one of them, they might catch their quarry.

Now they had.

Dozens of Houndoom lunged at Ethan's group from every direction. Misty and Cozmo were startled. Ethan had expected Team Magma to keep pursuing them and had stayed alert, so their appearance did not surprise him much.

What did catch his attention was Zinnia. She remained steady in the face of the ambush, showing no sign of panic.

She had nerves of steel.

Courtney stepped out from among her Team Magma members and watched the surrounded group coldly.

While setting the ambush, she had called for reinforcements. Members stationed nearest Meteor Falls were on their way. The group had a powerful Pokemon, but once those reinforcements arrived, she was confident she could keep them all here.

Her one concern was Shelly and Team Aqua. They would surely come after Team Magma in retaliation, just as Courtney had followed them earlier.

Inside the ring of Houndoom, Ethan and the others sent out their Pokemon.

Misty chose Starmie and Politoed.

Politoed had been with her since it was a Poliwag. It had evolved into Poliwhirl, battled Ash in the Whirl Cup, and later evolved again into Politoed. It was a strong partner.

Professor Cozmo was not helpless in a fight either. He threw a Poke Ball, releasing a strange Pokemon that floated in the air. Its orange body resembled a meteorite, with eight pointed rocks projecting from it.

It was Solrock, a Rock- and Psychic-type Pokemon. Ethan had never seen one in person before, but this was no time to study it.

Almost as soon as Cozmo sent out Solrock, Zinnia released her own Pokemon.

It was a fierce-looking Salamence. The Dragon- and Flying-type Pokemon planted all four feet on the ground, spread its red wings, and growled at the Houndoom. Its open mouth showed rows of sharp teeth.

Finally, Ethan assessed the field and threw two Poke Balls in succession, bringing out Dragonite and Tyranitar.

Courtney sneered when she saw those were the only two he had sent out. Where's your electric Pokemon? Why aren't you using it? Afraid?

Ethan smiled. His answer shook the confidence of her team.

Of course not. I'm keeping it ready for Team Aqua. As you know, Electric-type moves have the advantage against Water-type Pokemon.

Courtney's face darkened. She glanced to one side.

He was right to worry about Team Aqua. She had been worried about them too. She had already assigned a squad to guard their rear in case Team Aqua appeared and disrupted their formation.

For now, however, capturing Cozmo was the urgent task.

At her command, twenty or thirty Houndoom closed in from several directions. In an instant, the battle began.

Courtney soon realized it would not be as simple as she had imagined.

Apart from Cozmo's Solrock, which was only moderately strong, the other three Trainers' Pokemon were unexpectedly difficult to handle.

Dragonite, Tyranitar, and Salamence were especially formidable. The Houndoom fell after only a few exchanges. The opposing Pokemon seemed to belong to an entirely different class.

Alarmed, Courtney wondered who these people were and where they had come from.

She waved Camerupt into the fight and called out, Who are you?

Ethan was busy directing his two Pokemon and had no interest in answering. Zinnia looked at Courtney, who seemed about her age, and spoke instead. I'm a friend of Professor Cozmo. And this is Draconid territory. How could I let you do whatever you please here?

Draconids?

Understanding flashed in Courtney's eyes. She had thought those people had disappeared long ago. So they still existed.

That single answer told her she would have to defeat the group before she could take Cozmo.

She said nothing more and signaled for everyone to attack at once.

She had clearly taken Ethan and Misty for Zinnia's companions, and thus for Draconids as well.

There was no more to discuss. Ethan's group had to break through the encirclement and get Cozmo away. Team Magma was determined to capture the professor.

The Pokemon clashed in a chaotic melee.

One Houndoom bared its fangs and leaped at Dragonite. Dragonite sent it flying with a sweep of its tail.

Several others spat flames at Dragonite, but Politoed and Starmie fired Water Guns together and drove the fire back.

Zinnia's Salamence stood out as well. It held off four or five Houndoom at once and still managed to defeat them one by one.

Yet Tyranitar was the most imposing Pokemon on the field.

It resisted Fire-type attacks, and its thick armor gave it excellent protection. It charged through the Houndoom like a moving tank, scarcely acknowledging their presence.

Team Magma's Pokemon were no match even for many ordinary Trainers' partners, let alone this group.

They did not collapse the instant fighting began, but they could not stop Ethan and the others for long. Their sheer numbers forced Dragonite's group to dodge the many attacks coming their way, and that was almost the only reason Team Magma was still holding out.

Courtney's Camerupt entered the fight and recovered some ground for her side.

That reprieve would be brief. Once Misty's two Water types were free, they could turn their attacks on the slow-moving giant.

Courtney frowned as she surveyed the field. This was not how she had expected the battle to go.

During the earlier surprise attack, everything had happened too quickly for her to judge Ethan's strength. She had noticed only the power of his Electric-type Pokemon. Now, fighting him directly, she understood how dangerous the group was.

Hurried footsteps sounded behind her.

Courtney brightened. Her reinforcements must have arrived. She turned to order them into battle and froze.

They were not Team Magma. It was Shelly, leading Team Aqua toward them.

How had they got through? Courtney had stationed a squad behind her to watch for exactly this. Her heart sank.

Shelly took in the battle and burst out laughing.

Courtney, the tables really have turned! Now we're the ones who can profit from the fight. Did you imagine this would happen when you ambushed us earlier?

The happier Shelly looked, the angrier Courtney became.

With enemies on both sides, Courtney knew Team Magma could not win today. She cast a hard look at Ethan.

That man had attacked them from behind. Without him, victory today would have belonged to Team Magma!

Chapter 612: Why Are We Back Here Again?

Team Magma retreated.

Courtney had come full of expectations and left in disgrace. None of her plans had succeeded. The operation was a complete failure.

Shelly did not know that Courtney had already been losing before Team Aqua arrived. She assumed Courtney had seen her and withdrawn rather than face her, and she felt pleased to have taken her revenge.

Well? Courtney had ambushed her earlier, and now it was Shelly's turn. At last Courtney knew what defeat felt like.

Shelly glanced at Professor Cozmo, then waved Team Aqua's members forward. They took the places Team Magma had just abandoned and continued the assault on Ethan's group.

Cozmo had escaped her once, but he would still end up in her hands.

As soon as the fighting resumed, Shelly realized something was wrong.

Misty, Zinnia, and Cozmo kept the same Pokemon on the field: Politoed, Starmie, Salamence, and Solrock.

Ethan alone made a change. He recalled Tyranitar, which faced an unfavorable type matchup, and sent out Scizor to fight alongside Dragonite.

Team Magma and Team Aqua were much alike in strength, from their commanders down to their ordinary members. Like Courtney, Shelly had badly misjudged Ethan's group.

She had felt relieved at first when the mysterious Pokemon that spread electricity everywhere did not appear. Assuming Team Magma had beaten it, she paid little attention to the others.

Her team outnumbered them by far. And after the battle they had just fought, how much strength could Ethan's group have left?

Then she watched Team Aqua's Pokemon fall one after another.

Shocked, she realized the people in front of her were nowhere near as weak as she had thought.

She took out her own Poke Ball without delay and threw it hard.

A blue Pokemon resembling a sea lion appeared on the battlefield. It had two long tusks.

It was Walrein, an Ice- and Water-type Pokemon. Its thick layer of fat protected it from bitter cold, leaving it comfortable even below freezing, and could cushion an opponent's blows. Its two powerful tusks grew throughout its life and could shatter an iceberg weighing ten tons in one strike. If a tusk broke, it would grow back.

Walrein was not exceptionally tall, but it stood out among Team Aqua's Crawdaunt.

A red Aurora Beam shot from its mouth toward Dragonite. Ethan had been watching Shelly, though, and was ready.

Scizor darted into the beam's path. It swept its huge pincers across its body and used X-Scissor. A cross-shaped wave of energy struck the Aurora Beam.

Boom!

The two moves collided in a violent explosion, canceled each other out, and faded in the air.

Seeing how difficult the group was to fight, Shelly asked the same question Courtney had.

Who are you people?

This time Zinnia stayed silent, and Ethan answered. You don't need to know. All you need to know is that while we're here, you won't take anyone away.

Shelly studied him for a long moment. Recognition dawned.

I remember you! You're the one who ruined our operation at Devon Corporation a few days ago. Now you've taken someone from us again. Are you determined to make an enemy of Team Aqua?

Ethan remembered that the police had taken away everyone who broke into Devon, including one of Team Aqua's officers. Even if Team Aqua knew the operation had failed, he had not expected its people to know his part in it. Yet Shelly had heard and recognized his face. Their intelligence network was impressive.

He had crossed groups like this often enough that being identified did not trouble him much.

Zinnia and Cozmo looked at him with surprise. They had not known he had dealt with Team Aqua before.

Old grievances and the new rescue made Shelly hate Ethan even more.

But hatred did her little good. Her members' Pokemon kept falling, and even Walrein was driven back again and again.

Then the field changed once more.

Ethan took out a Great Ball and released Raikou. The sight made Shelly's heart sink.

Now she understood why Courtney and Team Magma had withdrawn so decisively.

She gritted her teeth and gave the order to retreat too. She was clever enough to decide quickly when a fight could not be won.

Before leaving, she said coldly to Ethan, Don't celebrate yet. This isn't over. No one who angers Team Aqua gets away with it.

She waved an arm, and Team Aqua fell back. Within moments, every member was gone.

It's finally over...

Misty let out a long breath and dropped onto a nearby rock.

She had faced threats like that several times before. Like Ethan, she paid Shelly's warning no mind.

After all, even Team Rocket's enormous organization had never managed to stop Ethan. He was stronger now than he had been then.

Professor Cozmo alone looked troubled. I'm sorry I dragged you into danger, he said.

It's all right. Zinnia shook her head. No matter how powerful they are elsewhere, they won't be a match for us at Meteor Falls.

By us, she seemed to mean the Draconids. Ethan guessed that Zinnia was not the only one with considerable strength among her people. That would explain her confidence in facing Team Aqua.

It's fine, he told Cozmo. You heard Shelly. I'd already made an enemy of Team Aqua. They'd come after me whether or not this happened.

Cozmo gave a rueful smile. Even so, you saved me. I don't know how to thank you.

Once they were certain both teams had gone, Zinnia escorted them back to the cave's main passage. There she stopped.

Ethan, Misty, and Cozmo said goodbye to her and headed together for the exit.

Before entering the cave, Ethan had expected nothing more than a convenient crossing. Instead, he had caught a Beldum, found several Key Stones, and rescued Cozmo from two rival teams.

It had been quite a journey.

They walked for a long time. By the time they emerged under the open sky, stars filled the night. Ethan checked the time: it was already past nine o'clock.

He turned to Cozmo. What will you do now?

Go home, of course, the professor said at once.

Where is home?

Fallarbor Town. It's not far. Would you like to visit?

Fallarbor Town... Ethan thought for a moment, then shook his head.

I'd better not. There isn't a Gym in Fallarbor, and I'm short on time. I won't trouble you.

That's a pity. Cozmo sounded disappointed but did not press him. Good luck with your Gym challenges, then!

After a little more conversation, they parted. Cozmo had not gone far when Misty cupped her hands around her mouth and called after him, Professor! Be careful, and don't let anyone kidnap you again!

Cozmo turned and waved. He only smiled, then continued alone toward Fallarbor Town.

Ethan and Misty watched until he vanished along the mountain road. They exchanged a smile and set off too.

They feared Team Magma or Team Aqua might still be nearby and attack in the night, so they did not camp there. They continued downhill under the moonlight instead.

Fortunately, the moon was bright enough for them to make out the path without flashlights.

They walked until midnight. Only when they were sure they had left the cave far behind did they pitch the tent, eat a quick dinner, and crawl inside.

Between the long trek, two battles, and the late bedtime, they slept until the sun was high overhead. They emerged from the tent yawning.

Ethan rubbed his eyes, sat outside in a daze for a while, then heated water and began making breakfast.

It was dull work that demanded patience.

At times like this, he particularly missed Erika and Brock. They both cooked delicious food and took care of every part of the meal. Ethan only had to sit down and enjoy it.

Now he had to feed Misty as well as himself.

After they and their Pokemon ate their late breakfast, they prepared to leave. That was when Ethan noticed something wrong.

They had hurried through the darkness the night before without checking their overall direction. Somehow, they had circled back near Rustboro City.

They stared at the map in silence.

How? Misty rubbed her eyes in disbelief. I remember heading east yesterday. How did we end up back here?

However much they wanted to deny it, the map and their surroundings were clear.

It must be the terrain, Ethan said, rubbing his temples. Our general direction was right, but the path wound downhill. Last night we had nothing to navigate by but the moon, so we circled back.

Even with an explanation, it felt uncanny. How many times had he come to Rustboro now? Why did he keep ending up here?

If he had known this would happen, he might as well have gone with Cozmo to Fallarbor Town. Fallarbor had no Gym, but at least it would have carried them forward.

They had lost still more time.

There was nothing to do but check their bearings and set out again.

Fortunately, they were near Rustboro only in the broad sense. They were far from the city itself, at the edge of a forest. Crossing it would take them to the other side of the mountain.

That was some consolation. They put the mistake behind them and entered the trees.

Ethan did not know the forest's name, but it looked broad and dense on the map. They had not gone far when someone suddenly sprang from the bushes ahead.

After yesterday's fighting, Ethan first thought Team Magma or Team Aqua had found them. A closer look showed only a young boy.

He had a round face, seemed about Misty's age, and had innocent-looking eyes. A small pack rested on his back. He was probably another traveling Trainer.

A Heracross taller than the boy stood beside him. It was plainly his Pokemon.

The boy looked just as surprised to see Ethan and Misty and stopped where he was.

Oh. Misty patted her chest. I thought you were a bad guy or a wild Pokemon!

Even as she spoke, she took a few steps back and hid behind Ethan. Heracross looked sturdy and impressive, and it was not especially furry, but a Bug-type Pokemon was still a bug. She could not keep her skin from crawling.

The boy saw nothing amiss. He looked them over and asked, Are you Trainers too?

Of course.

Ethan nodded pleasantly and was about to walk past. The boy brightened. If we're all Trainers and we've met out here, how about a battle?

Ethan stopped and hesitated.

Normally he welcomed a challenge, but he had not recovered from yesterday and felt little enthusiasm for another match.

Still, making eye contact and then battling was a well-worn custom among Trainers. It was hard to refuse.

The boy looked eager, and the huge Heracross stood ready beside him. Ethan nodded at last.

All right. One on one.

The boy beamed. Let's introduce ourselves first. I'm Jiro Sawama. I only started traveling recently, and I'm training here in the forest!

Ethan could hear the boy's youthful energy. After journeys through two regions, he felt some of that freshness fading in himself.

He was about to give his own name when another person emerged behind Jiro, looking exactly like him.

Huh? Misty stared. You're twins?

Chapter 613: I'm Never Teaming Up With Psyduck Again

That's right. As you can see, we're twins.

The boy who had appeared second stepped beside Jiro and nodded to Ethan and Misty. Hello. I'm Ichiro Sawama, his older brother.

Ethan and Misty looked from one identical face to the other. They could hardly tell the twins apart. Fortunately, the boys wore T-shirts of different colors beneath their outer clothes and had different Pokemon beside them, giving the travelers a way to match names to faces.

When Ichiro heard that Jiro had challenged them, he grew interested too.

Let me join in! Like my brother, I haven't been traveling long. Since there are two of you and two of us, let's have a Double Battle!

Ethan had been in Hoenn only a few days, but he had already noticed that Double Battles were more popular here than in Kanto and Johto. In Rustboro City, he had glimpsed several pairs of Trainers battling together on outdoor fields.

He and Misty exchanged a look. She smiled and discreetly covered her mouth.

One of them was a conference champion, the other almost a Gym Leader. The twins had chosen formidable opponents.

In a playful mood, Ethan and Misty kept their identities to themselves and agreed to the match.

They found a relatively level clearing in the forest and stood on opposite sides.

We're visiting from other regions, Ethan said. We don't know much about Double Battles here. Are there any special rules?

Ichiro had only recently begun his travels, but he knew the rules. He shook his head. Nothing special. It's the same as anywhere else: knock out all the Pokemon on the other side to win.

Ethan nodded and studied the brothers again. Since they were both beginners, he had no need to show his true strength. He could simply enjoy the match with them.

Misty seemed to have the same idea. One look was enough for them to understand each other.

Ethan and Misty each took a Poke Ball from a waist pouch. The twins needed none: they sent the Pokemon already at their sides onto the field.

Jiro's choice was the large Heracross beside him. Ichiro's partner was an Ariados.

Blue light flashed as Ethan and Misty released Torchic and Psyduck.

Ethan had chosen Torchic at least partly to train it. Misty's choice of Psyduck showed that she was treating the Double Battle as a bit of fun.

All four Pokemon looked eager, even Psyduck, whose eyes held an unusual excitement.

That was understandable. Misty rarely chose to send it into battle deliberately. After so long with her, Psyduck was thrilled to have the chance and resolved to do its best for her.

Ichiro picked up a small stone and tossed it high. The instant it struck the ground, the battle began.

Torchic darted forward first. It chirped fiercely and headed straight for the largest opponent, Heracross.

Its Fire-type attacks were strong against both Bug types, Heracross and Ariados, so Torchic had a good chance in this matchup.

Besides, it was a young chicken. Bugs hardly frightened it, however large they were.

As it drew close, Torchic opened its beak and used Ember.

Heracross did not dare meet the flames. It beat its thin, cicada-like wings and glided away.

Torchic chased after it, looking determined not to stop until it managed to burn Heracross.

Psyduck, meanwhile, lived up to Misty's expectations in quite a different way. Its performance was as consistent as ever.

It wanted to impress her, but as it waddled toward Ariados, the spider shot silk around its legs. Psyduck tripped and fell with ease.

Misty pressed a hand to her forehead and sighed. Trusting Psyduck had been foolish.

Still, she could not leave it there. Psyduck, use Water Gun!

Psyduck fired a hurried stream of water. Ariados dodged nimbly, closed the distance, and lowered two fangs glinting with poison toward Psyduck's neck.

A shadow flashed past. Ariados looked up just as Heracross slammed into it.

Torchic had chased Heracross across the clearing. It had ended up here by accident and crashed into its teammate, saving Psyduck in the process.

Thanks, Misty said to Ethan with a grin. She quickly had Psyduck strip the silk from its legs so it could move again.

The battle continued.

The forest clearing was small for four Pokemon, limiting how freely they could move.

Burning patches left on the ground by Torchic's flames narrowed Heracross's and Ariados's options still further.

Before Ethan could enjoy that advantage, Psyduck started spraying Water Gun at random and put the hot embers out.

Ethan stared at it in silence.

Was Psyduck secretly on the other team? Why was it making things harder for them?

He gave Misty a speechless look. She stuck out her tongue in embarrassment and hurried to order Psyduck to stop firing Water Gun so freely.

The battle went on.

Unlike Ethan and Misty, who had shown almost no teamwork, the twins knew how to cooperate.

Since Heracross struggled against Torchic, both brothers turned their attention to Psyduck.

They had seen that it was not very bright and kept getting in its partner's way. If they knocked it out first, they could deal with Torchic together afterward.

The combined attack put Psyduck in immediate danger.

Heracross charged into Psyduck and knocked it down. Before it could rise, Ariados came in and bit it on the rear.

Psyduck howled, sprang into the air, and ran wildly around the field, clutching its backside.

Any thought of impressing Misty had vanished from its mind.

Misty had hoped the attacks might give Psyduck a headache and unleash its powerful psychic abilities. But neither Heracross nor Ariados had struck its head. Psyduck was hurting, yet the source of its psychic power remained untouched.

Did it have to offer them its head to hit?

Its panicked running disrupted Torchic too.

When Heracross and Ariados came close together, Torchic saw a chance to catch them both with Ember. It had barely opened its beak when Psyduck charged blindly toward it, still clutching its backside.

Torchic chirped and jumped aside to avoid being hit by its own teammate. It lost the best moment to attack the two Bug types.

How did it come to this...?

Misty's face fell. Ethan could only shake his head. Psyduck's lack of control had made the battle much harder.

Thanks to Psyduck, Ethan realized this match was proving more difficult than yesterday's fight against Team Magma and Team Aqua.

Fortunately, the twins did not know Psyduck always behaved this way. They remained intent on knocking it out before confronting Torchic together.

That gave Torchic a little breathing room and kept it from facing both opponents at once.

Ethan knew he did not have much time. He needed to bring down one of them soon.

He focused on the field, searching for a way to win.

After countless battles over a long journey, he had learned to read what was happening quickly. This time, too, he spotted an opening.

Heracross and Ariados kept pursuing Psyduck. Its own panic made its movements so unpredictable that even the twins could not anticipate where it would run next. Otherwise, they would already have beaten it.

When Psyduck ran toward Torchic again, Ethan did not order Torchic to dodge. He told it to use Ember.

Misty was astonished. The twins stared too.

They soon saw what happened. At the last instant, Psyduck changed direction. Torchic's Ember struck the place it had been heading toward and engulfed Heracross, which had been close behind it.

A rare chance! Ethan had Torchic close in and knock the struggling Heracross to the ground with a headlong charge.

Yes!

Misty raised a hand and cheered. With one opponent down, she could finally relax a little. She would have felt terrible if Psyduck's antics had cost them the match.

She turned to Ethan admiringly. That was amazing! How did you know Psyduck would change direction there?

Ethan laughed. Do you really think I can predict everything? That's Psyduck. I can't understand what it's thinking on a normal day, let alone when it's running around like that.

Huh? Then the timing...

What timing? He waved the question away. I was treating Psyduck as a target too.

What? Misty's eyes widened.

Ethan shrugged. It would have been fine even if Ember hit it. Psyduck's a Water type; a little fire isn't much of a threat. It might even have calmed down.

That made a kind of sense, and perhaps he had had no other option, but Misty could only smile ruefully. She had thought Ethan had found exactly the right moment.

Whatever his intention, the result was good. Heracross was down.

Ichiro and Jiro had only Ariados left. With its poor type matchup against Torchic, the battle had turned completely around.

Psyduck was no help, but under Ethan's commands, Torchic soon defeated Ariados with another burst of fire.

Ethan wiped cold sweat from his forehead. That Double Battle had taken more effort than he expected.

It had been hard on Torchic too. It had battled two Pokemon while its own teammate caused trouble, and it was exhausted.

If there was a next time, Ethan would never team up with Psyduck again. It was far too much trouble!

Ichiro and Jiro recalled their Pokemon. Ethan was about to go over and speak with them when white light suddenly surrounded Torchic.

He knew that light at once. Torchic was evolving! The unexpected delight brought a smile to his face.

The glow did not last long. When it faded, a Pokemon much larger than Torchic stood before them.

Torchic had evolved into Combusken.

Its main colors were much the same, but its claws were sharper and its body stronger. It looked rather like a fighting rooster from Earth.

Misty had never seen a Combusken, so she aimed her Pokedex at it.

Combusken, the Young Fowl Pokemon. A Fire- and Fighting-type Pokemon. It runs through hills and fields to strengthen its legs and hips. In battle, it uses scorching flames from its beak and powerful kicks. The fire inside it burns fiercely as it fights. Its legs combine speed and strength, allowing it to deliver ten kicks in one second. Its sharp cry focuses its mind and intimidates opponents. With a strong fighting instinct, it keeps battling until its opponent gives up.

Chapter 614: A Chance Meeting with Bea

Torchic's evolution into Combusken filled a gap in Ethan's team: he now had a Fighting-type Pokemon.

If he came across another Fighting tournament, he could enter instead of watching the excitement from the stands.

Of course, Combusken was not a pure Fighting type. In a tournament restricted by type, that might limit what it could do compared with a Pokemon that had only Fighting typing.

Never mind. He had a Fighting-type partner now!

Ichiro and Jiro approached Ethan. Both looked downcast, clearly dissatisfied with losing the Double Battle.

It was understandable. Psyduck had been such a hindrance that they felt one more push would have knocked it out. Ethan's victory seemed to owe everything to Torchic's type advantage. With a different Pokemon, the twins believed they could have won.

What the inexperienced brothers had not yet realized was that battles offered no such convenient ifs. Had Misty chosen someone other than Psyduck, they might have lost much sooner.

Ichiro sighed. We lost. Your Torchic was strong, and congratulations on its evolution into Combusken.

Jiro was less willing to let it go. I'm not satisfied with how that ended. Will you battle us again?

Ethan checked the time and shook his head.

Sorry. We've been delayed too long already. He spoke before Jiro could argue. You're Trainers too, so I imagine you're aiming for the Ever Grande Conference. If you want a rematch, we can have a proper one there.

The Ever Grande Conference?

The brothers looked at each other. Jiro was disappointed, but he could hardly insist. He watched as Ethan and Misty recalled their Pokemon.

The match is over, so we'd better be going, Ethan said.

They said goodbye and headed farther into the forest.

This time they met no more novice Trainers or wild Pokemon. They crossed without trouble and reached another town by dusk.

The map named it Verdanturf Town. It sat at the foot of the mountains. Not far to the north stood Mt. Chimney, and at that mountain's base was Lavaridge Town and its Gym.

After so much travel, Ethan and Misty were glad to spend a night resting in a town.

Nature seemed to surround Verdanturf. It lay in a valley with lovely scenery and wonderfully fresh air.

Misty breathed in deeply. It even smells faintly sweet. Isn't this close to the volcano? Shouldn't there be ash everywhere? The air's so clean, and I can't see any dust at all.

Ethan looked toward the faint outline of Mt. Chimney. Misty was right that nothing here felt unpleasant. Yet the mountain was a dormant volcano, and despite its long quiet spell, volcanic ash still drifted down from it. Verdanturf was close enough that it ought to feel the effects.

He held out a hand and paid attention to the air. Soon he understood.

It's the wind, he said with a smile. There's a warm, gentle breeze here most of the time. It keeps the ash from blowing into town.

Misty felt for it too. A light wind passed over her hand, just as he had said. It was not strong, but it carried the ash and other particles away from Verdanturf.

As they walked through town, they noticed its unusually unhurried pace. People sat together drinking tea and talking. Most were lively older residents; few young people were in sight.

They bought food and other necessities at a shop, then headed for the Pokemon Center to stay the night.

Verdanturf was small, with few buildings. From the town center, they could already see the Pokemon Center ahead.

They had barely come through its automatic doors when they met a girl on her way out.

She looked seventeen or eighteen, with fine features, short silver-gray hair cut to her ears, and a broad band over her head. She wore close-fitting black-and-white athletic clothes. Her tan skin and firm muscles gave her an air of health and strength.

A panel of black mesh covered her midriff. It was thin enough that Ethan could faintly see her navel.

He and Misty stood in the doorway, blocking her path. They stepped aside to let her pass.

The girl paused, nodded politely, and went straight out of the Pokemon Center.

Misty had never seen a woman quite like her. She turned to watch until the girl disappeared.

She looked so cool! Misty told Ethan, her voice excited.

He nodded. The girl had a cool, capable air about her.

Although he had seen her only briefly, she had made enough of an impression for him to recognize her. It was Bea, the Fighting-type specialist and Gym Leader of Stow-on-Side in Galar.

She was no ordinary Trainer. People called her a prodigy of Galar's century-old karate tradition.

But what was she doing here?

After a moment's thought, Ethan had an idea. In the anime, Bea spent her free time traveling the world to sharpen her skills and those of her Pokemon. She challenged famous Fighting-type Trainers wherever she went, in Kanto and beyond. Hoenn was no stranger a destination.

Misty noticed that he was still looking toward the door. Jealousy rose at once.

She's gone. What are you still looking at?

Ethan heard the edge in her voice. He turned and lightly rapped her on the head with his knuckles. What are you thinking? She was carrying a backpack, so she's clearly setting out somewhere. I'm just wondering where she'd go this late, when traveling is so inconvenient.

It was only a passing encounter. They checked in with Nurse Joy and soon put it out of mind.

Nurse Joy also told them Verdanturf would hold a Pokemon Contest in a little over ten days. That gave them something else to talk about.

A Pokemon Contest? Misty asked, puzzled. What kind of competition is that?

Nurse Joy smiled at the visitor from another region. Unlike a regular battle tournament, it's a competition that showcases a Pokemon's appeal. Trainers and Pokemon perform, judges give them scores, and those scores decide the winner.

That sounds interesting. Misty's eyes lit up, then she sighed. But it's not for another ten days or more? That's too bad. We're leaving tomorrow.

Don't be so disappointed, Ethan said. If we have time, we can come back when it starts. And our journey has only just begun. Even if we miss this one, we'll have other chances to watch a Contest.

That made sense to Misty. Her mood lifted, and Ethan's words, our journey has only just begun, made her secretly happier still.

She and Ethan had only recently started traveling together. There was no need to rush anything.

...

After a night at the Pokemon Center and breakfast the next morning, they left Verdanturf and headed toward Mt. Chimney.

The rest had cleared away their fatigue. Both looked lively again.

Mt. Chimney stood in north-central Hoenn and rose more than fifteen hundred meters. Even before they began climbing, the air seemed hotter.

Sweat soon soaked their clothes and dripped to the ground.

Travel near the mountain was more tiring than on the other roads. This time, however, they were not headed up the volcano. After more than half a day's walk, they reached Lavaridge Town at its foot.

Though Verdanturf was not far away, the two towns felt as if they belonged to different climates: one cool and refreshing, the other hot.

Verdanturf was a pleasant place for older people to spend their later years at leisure. Lavaridge was a hot-spring destination. Geothermal heat fed hundreds of springs, large and small, making it attractive to older residents too.

Misty had read in a travel guide that the springs had separate baths for men and women, as well as mixed baths. Her heart beat faster. She remembered the time she and Ethan had spent at a hot spring on Cinnabar Island in Kanto.

Would she have another chance to bathe with him here?

The thought made her face grow hotter. Fortunately, the weather already had both of them flushed, so Ethan was unlikely to notice.

They entered town and headed straight for Lavaridge Gym.

Despite its name, Lavaridge Town looked more like a small city than Verdanturf did.

Tall buildings stood beside older ones. The two styles blended naturally, climbing and dipping with the ground at the foot of the mountain. Hot-spring water flowed beneath bridges, sending up fine wisps of steam and giving the streets a layered look.

Everywhere they turned were men and women in yukata, laughing as they admired the scenery or stopped at stalls to bargain with vendors.

Some people lay buried in warm river sand, enjoying its fine grains and heat. A few dozen minutes there could wash away the fatigue in their bodies.

There was something related to the hot springs along every street. Misty looked around eagerly and bought a hot-spring egg for a snack.

After making their way through town, they reached Lavaridge Gym and were startled by its size.

The Gym stood beneath Mt. Chimney. Behind its high courtyard walls rose a four- or five-story building with white walls and red roof tiles. From outside, it looked less like a Gym than a hot-spring resort.

They had barely entered the courtyard when they spotted a beautiful red-haired woman training with two Slugma.

The Slugma were breathing fire at her. She was using herself as the target, repeatedly dodging their attacks.

Ethan had often seen Trainers practice alongside their Pokemon, but never one who had the Pokemon attack her directly.

The woman heard their footsteps and turned. At that moment, a burst of fire struck her and set her clothes alight.

She yelped and ran about in alarm.

Misty stared. She had assumed the woman was skilled enough to make herself a target. Apparently she was as vulnerable as anyone else.

Recovering, Misty quickly sent out Starmie.

Starmie, use Water Gun!

Water poured over the red-haired woman and put out the flames.

Ah... I'm saved. She wiped sweat from her forehead. Without even checking for injuries, she hurried toward them. Thank you so much! You helped just in time. Who are you? What brings you here?

Her questions came so rapidly that Ethan seemed to feel her heat even from more than a meter away.

He took a step back from her enthusiasm. Hello. I've come to challenge Lavaridge Gym.

The woman jumped in excitement.

Wonderful! I've waited so long for someone to challenge the Gym! she said. Oh, I forgot to introduce myself. As you can see, I'm the Gym Leader here: Flannery!

Chapter 615: Flannery, the Rookie Demon Gym Leader

Flannery looked about Ethan's age. She was pretty and had a good figure, with a black cropped T-shirt above her jeans. Her bright red hair had been arranged into several broad sections, like the petals of a flower in full bloom.

As a Trainer who specialized in Fire-type Pokemon, she seemed every bit as fiery as her chosen type. Her enthusiasm was infectious, though the way she treated strangers like old friends could be a little overwhelming.

What Ethan couldn't understand was why hearing that someone had come to challenge the Gym had provoked such a reaction from her.

Isn't Mr. Moore the Lavaridge Gym Leader? he asked hesitantly.

Moore was the previous Lavaridge Gym Leader and a former member of Hoenn's Elite Four. He was an elderly man with glasses and a kindly appearance.

Before coming to Hoenn, Ethan had read a Trainer's travel guide that clearly named Moore as the Lavaridge Gym Leader. He hadn't expected the position to change hands in the few days since then.

My grandpa? Flannery shook her head. He's retired and passed the Gym on to me. Come on, let's battle already! I feel like I'm on fire!

Her grandfather?

So she was the new Gym Leader.

Flannery was plainly impatient and excitable, but she was cheerful too. From this brief exchange alone, Ethan could tell she would be easy to get along with. Perhaps that was a common trait among Trainers devoted to Fire-type Pokemon.

The change of Gym Leader didn't really matter to him. His only regret was missing the chance to face a former Elite Four member.

Before he could say anything else, Flannery took out a Poke Ball and threw it. A large turtle with orange-brown skin appeared before them.

Enough talk! Let's have a great Gym battle!

She was about to order the turtle into action when Misty hurriedly stopped her.

Wait! Misty stared at her. Miss Flannery, shouldn't an official Gym battle take place on the Gym's battlefield?

Oh, I forgot. Flannery paused, then smiled awkwardly. I got carried away. Sorry! I've only been Gym Leader for a few days, and I'm still getting used to things.

Her explanation did little to reassure Misty.

Still getting used to things? Surely everyone knew where a Gym battle belonged. Her grandfather had run this very Gym, yet she'd forgotten something so basic!

Having grown up in a Gym family herself, Misty knew more about the job than most people. Flannery's lack of professionalism left her unimpressed.

Ethan said nothing. It wasn't that he was more forgiving because Flannery was beautiful. Everyone started out inexperienced, and unfamiliar work could make anyone flustered. He could also see how much she loved being a Gym Leader. Her excitable personality simply made her seem rather scattered.

Flannery led them into the Lavaridge Gym. Beyond its spacious entrance hall lay the battlefield. When Ethan and Misty saw it, both frowned again.

Perhaps because the Gym stood at the foot of Mt. Chimney, or because Lavaridge itself was so rocky, its Fire-type battlefield was covered with stones. At the moment, however, it was a wreck. The ground was pitted, the rocks had been smashed into countless pieces, and signs of battle were everywhere.

Noticing their expressions, Flannery gave another embarrassed laugh.

Ahaha... I had a challenger yesterday, and then I forgot to clean up the field. So this is how it ended up...

She had forgotten that too? Misty was speechless.

Repairing a battlefield normally wasn't a Gym Leader's personal responsibility. The Pokemon League provided substantial funding each year, enough for a Gym to hire people to handle such work.

Brock was an exception. With so many younger siblings to support, he had needed to spend the Gym's money on his family and couldn't afford other employees. But judging by its size, the Lavaridge Gym was hardly short of funds. It shouldn't have been run in this state.

Flannery wasn't merely careless; she seemed to have no management skills at all.

She was about to ask Ethan and Misty to rest while she fixed the battlefield, but Ethan stopped her.

It's fine. He shook his head. The field's damaged, but I think a battlefield that's already seen a fight will be more complicatedand more interestingthan another ordinary rocky field.
