Flannery regarded him with new respect. Most Trainers would have waited for repairs, whether they wanted a fairer match or lacked confidence in their own strength. His indifference suggested he trusted his abilities.

Only then did she take a proper look at him. He was about her age and remarkably handsome, especially his eyes. Her impression of him improved at once. She let the repairs wait, and they took their places on opposite sides of the field.

First, the rules. Flannery finally sounded like a professional. She straightened up as she spoke. When my grandpa was here, he'd decide how many Pokemon to use and which ones to send out after judging the challenger. That sounds too complicated, so I've decided to make this like other Gym battles: three Pokemon each!

Then she remembered one more detail. Oh, and only you can switch Pokemon during the battle. Is that okay?

Ethan nodded. Those rules were much the same as at other Gyms.

What her grandfather had done was another matter. Adjusting a challenger's match to their ability on the spot required both considerable strength and a wealth of experience. Flannery didn't yet have either, which explained why she hadn't adopted his approach.

Ethan introduced himself, and Flannery quietly repeated his name before directing her large turtle onto the field. Ethan and Misty both studied it.

Though the turtle stood only fifty centimeters tall, it was remarkably heavy. Dark gray rings marked its limbs and long neck, each foot bore three claws, and a short tail protruded behind it. Its shell was mostly dark gray, with five fiery red hollows around it that seemed to vent excess heat from its body.

Misty had never seen one before, so she took out her Pokedex and aimed it at the Pokemon.

Beep. Torkoal, the Coal Pokemon. Fire type. Torkoal are often found in abandoned coal mines. They continually dig up coal and burn it in the holes in their shells. When attacked, they release black smoke and escape. Smoke from their nostrils makes a sound like a train whistle.

So it was called Torkoal. Misty nodded, put away her Pokedex, and turned her attention back to the match.

From the Trainer's area, Ethan considered which Pokemon to send out. By its presence and condition, Torkoal was clearly no weakling. It might even be one of Flannery's strongest partners. Eevee, Combusken, and Beldum weren't ready to face it.

Instead of making his choice immediately, he asked, Miss Flannery, is that your strongest Pokemon?

My strongest? Flannery thought for a moment and smiled. One of them! I have a Magmortar too. Those two are the partners I trust most!

Just as he'd suspected. As a new Gym Leader, Flannery still had much to learn. She hadn't prepared any ordinary Pokemon for beginner challengers; she had sent out an ace instead.

He glanced at the scarred field and asked cautiously, What sort of Trainer challenged you yesterday?

A little girl who hadn't been traveling long, Flannery said with a smile. She was adorable. She told me Lavaridge was the first Gym she'd ever challenged!

Did she win?

Of course not! Flannery looked puzzled by the question. She used all three of her Pokemon and only just managed to beat my Magmortar. Then I sent out Torkoal and told her it was about as strong as Magmortar. I don't know why, but she started crying. She ran away without even battling it!

Ethan had no words.

How cruel! Looking again at the marks all over the field, he could picture a novice Trainer who had worked hard to catch three Pokemon and arrived full of hope for her first Gym challenge, only to run straight into the Gym Leader's best team and be overwhelmed.

After giving everything she had to defeat a single Pokemon, she hadn't even had a chance to catch her breath before facing another of equal strength. No wonder she'd been devastated. That battle must have left a lasting shadow over her journey.

What a frightening woman.

Still, knowing that Torkoal was one of Flannery's strongest Pokemon made Ethan's choice simpler. He took a Poke Ball from his waist pouch and threw it across the field. A flash of blue light released Tyranitar.

An ordinary opponent called for one approach; an ace called for another. Apart from Gardevoir and Gengar, all the non-Legendary Pokemon currently traveling with Ethan still needed training. Whatever his opponent sent out, he had someone to meet it.

As soon as Tyranitar appeared, it threw back its head and roared, just as it had before.

ROAR!

The sound echoed through the enclosed Gym, loud enough to shake their ears.

Flannery might have been careless about running a Gym, but she had an unusual eye for Pokemon. One look at Tyranitar told her it was no ordinary opponent.

Oh? She frowned and examined it, her voice turning unusually grave. That Tyranitar looks strong. I've only felt something like this from my grandpa's Pokemon!

Was Tyranitar strong? Ethan merely shook his head without answering.

He already had two exceptionally powerful and ferocious Pokemon in his red Gyarados and Crystal Steelix. Beside them, Tyranitar was only averagemiddle of the pack for its species at best. It had yet to distinguish itself, much less satisfy Ethan.

That was why he had brought Dragonite, Tyranitar, and Scizor on this journey: he wanted to concentrate on training them.

Tyranitar fixed its gaze on Torkoal. The two Pokemon stared each other down, their fighting spirit rising until both were ready to strike.

Flannery, fiery as ever, settled into battle after her moment of admiration. Her eyes grew serious, a complete change from the excitable young woman of a moment ago. Now she looked like a proper Gym Leader.

With no other staff present, she served as the referee herself.

Begin!

At Ethan's command, Tyranitar attacked from across the field. It roared, and a succession of sharp stones surged up from the ground toward Torkoal.

Stone Edge, a Rock-type move.

Torkoal was far too slow to evade it. Instead, it resorted to a turtle Pokemon's most familiar defense: it drew its head and limbs into its shell, letting the hard casing absorb the Stone Edge.

Chapter 616: The Battle at Lavaridge Gym

Torkoal's shell had protected it from injury, but Stone Edge still knocked the withdrawn Pokemon into the air.

Ethan knew that Torkoal was dangerous even with its head and limbs tucked away. Its hard shell guarded it, and it could use Rapid Spin from that position. Getting close would be a mistake.

Rather than order Tyranitar to follow up, he called, Tyranitar, use Sandstorm!

Billowing yellow sand came from nowhere and swept across most of the battlefield, hiding Tyranitar within it. Ethan had used this tactic before and knew it well.

Flannery lost sight of her target. Torkoal landed safely, but Tyranitar did not reappear. After waiting a while, she had no choice but to make Torkoal emerge from its shell.

Torkoal, use Flamethrower over there!

She dared not rush into the sandstorm, so she tried to force Tyranitar out with an attack from a distance. The field was large, though, and all she could do was aim at the place Tyranitar had last stood. Ethan had anticipated that. As soon as the sand concealed Tyranitar, he had told it to change position.

Flames poured into the storm, lighting a broad patch of sand red. When the fire died away, there was still no movement inside. The attack had missed.

Flannery ordered Torkoal to fire again, with the same result.

Tch. At this rate, she wouldn't see her opponent unless she got closer. She glanced across at Ethan, gritted her teeth, and sent Torkoal into the sandstorm.

As the Gym Leader being challenged, she could have waited patiently for Ethan to attack. She could even have waited until the storm passed. But she lacked the experience to recognize that advantage and was still treating the match like an ordinary battle between Trainers. Defense didn't suit her personality, either. She pressed forward instead.

Torkoal's thick shell protected most of its body. Only its head and limbs were exposed to the storm, and its excellent defenses made the sand's damage little more than a nuisance. Even so, Flannery had deliberately sent her Pokemon into danger. Her recklessness was about to cost her.

With both Pokemon hidden in the storm, neither Trainer could see exactly what was happening or give precise directions. Inside it, Tyranitar and Torkoal would have to fight on their own judgment.

Torkoal was one of Flannery's aces, but she herself had not traveled widely. Tyranitar had competed in a Pokemon League tournament and fought in many major battles. It had a slight edge in strength and experience, with the terrain and surrounding sandstorm firmly in its favor.

Torkoal plodded into the sand and vanished. Before long, orange flashes flickered within the storm, followed by several of Tyranitar's roars. The two Pokemon had clearly met, though no one outside could tell which had the upper hand.

Ethan listened calmly. Flannery was anything but calm. She craned her neck and cupped a hand around her eyes, trying in vain to glimpse what was happening. Her face betrayed her anxiety.

The ground shook inside the storm. Even at a distance, Flannery felt the tremor. Tyranitar must have used a Ground-type move. More worried than ever, she shouted, Torkoal, get out of there!

Her command disappeared into the storm without a response. A bad feeling settled over her.

After another anxious wait, the sounds of battle ceased. The sand slowly thinned, and at last she could see the field again.

Tyranitar was standing in front of a deep fracture in the ground. Torkoal was wedged in the crack, apparently unconscious.

Torkoal!

Flannery stared in disbelief. She knew her own Pokemon's strength better than anyone; she hadn't imagined it would lose like this. She studied Ethan again and raised her estimate of him. He was incredibly strongperhaps every bit as strong as her grandfather!

She recalled Torkoal and took out her second Poke Ball.

Here's my second Pokemon. Go, Magmortar!

A red-and-yellow Pokemon appeared on the field, its vivid body seeming to burn with flames. This was the Fire-type Pokemon Flannery had said was as strong as Torkoal.

Compared with its earlier form, Magmar, Magmortar was bulkier. The markings all over its body looked like fire, its breath seemed to burn, and its arms ended in huge cannonlike tubes.

They had seen Magmar many times on their travels, but Misty had never encountered a Magmortar. Curious, she pointed her Pokedex at it.

Beep. Magmortar, the Blast Pokemon. Fire type. Magmortar usually live near volcanic craters. It is said that only one pair lives at each volcano. Life near a crater makes its body increasingly like a volcano, with organs resembling magma chambers. It fires fireballs from its tubular arms at temperatures reaching two thousand degrees Celsius, hot enough to melt an iron pot in an instant. Its body may glow faintly white with heat, and repeated firing can even cause its wrists to melt slightly.

The description alone made clear how formidable this Pokemon was.

Ethan called Tyranitar back to him and patted its armored body in encouragement before returning it to its ball. Then he took out a second Poke Ball.

Anyone who knew Ethan knew that, except in special circumstances, he rarely made the same Pokemon fight consecutive rounds. Misty thought nothing of the switch, but Flannery was surprised. Tyranitar looked so strong and had suffered only minor burns. It could surely keep fighting. Had Ethan forgotten that Magmortar was also one of her strongest Pokemon?

Her doubts lasted only until Ethan threw the ball. Dragonite emerged in midair, and she sensed the same imposing strength she had felt from Tyranitar.

So he had good reason to make the switch! Naturally, she took both Dragonite and Tyranitar to be his ace Pokemon.

It's been ages since I faced anyone as strong as you, Flannery said, one hand on her hip. I'm completely fired up now. I'm going all out to beat your strongest Pokemon!

She thinks Tyranitar and Dragonite are my aces, Ethan realized. He smiled but didn't correct her. Telling her that they belonged to his second tier would probably crush her confidence.

The field was even more battered after the first round, though neither Trainer's resolve had suffered. For Magmortar, which had to move on the ground, the broken terrain would make things harder.

Flannery called, The second battle begins now!

The moment she finished speaking, Magmortar attacked on its own. It lifted its cannonlike arms and launched clusters of fireballs from both barrels at Dragonite in the air.

Dragonite twisted sideways. Two fireballs about the size of basketballs brushed past it. A fraction slower, and they would have hit.

It steadied itself and answered with Dragon Rage, turning the exchange into a contest of ranged attacks.

Neither Ethan nor Flannery had ordered those opening moves. Their Pokemon had reacted for themselves. Waiting for a command could cost a precious moment, and both were experienced enough to recognize an opening and act on it.

Of course, Trainers allowed that freedom only to Pokemon they could trust. If Misty's Psyduckor another Pokemon that regularly ignored ordersacted on its own, it would probably earn a shouted reprimand instead.

After that quick exchange, the Trainers took control again. At Flannery's order, Magmortar sent out another burst of flame to cancel Dragon Rage. Ethan commanded Dragonite to dive toward it with Dragon Rush.

Magmortar's attacks were powerful, and its two arm cannons let it fire from both sides. Trading shots at a distance would put Dragonite at a disadvantage. Closing in was the wiser choice.

Dragonite was fast, and Dragon Rush drove it faster still. Radiating a fierce, almost murderous pressure, it charged straight at Magmortar.

Flannery welcomed the challenge. She knew Magmortar couldn't dodge, so she chose to meet Dragonite head-on.

Use Flame Wheel!

Fire surged over Magmortar's body. Instead of retreating, it ran toward Dragonite. Moments later they collided with a tremendous bang. They pressed against each other, glaring and gritting their teeth.

Both had been hurt, but neither was willing to give ground. Dragonite was taller and heavier; Magmortar's searing skin made the contest painful all the same. After only a short struggle, Dragonite was beginning to suffer.

Ethan's next command came in time. Dragonite, use Aqua Tail!

Dragonite beat its small wings and lifted into the air. Water wrapped around its great tail, and it turned to whip the tail into Magmortar.

Flannery refused to yield. Magmortar, Fire Punch!

Dragonite's surging tail struck Magmortar, while one of Magmortar's blazing cannon arms hit Dragonite. The Water-type blow made Magmortar recoil, its expression changing as it staggered back several steps.

Dragonite was hurting too. After two Fire-type attacks in succession, it had the bad luck to be burned. Both Pokemon had taken damage: Dragonite now faced a lingering status condition, while Magmortar had suffered a super-effective hit for double damage. In that respect, the contest seemed even again.

Flannery found herself in a difficult position. Where had this man come from? How could he be so strong? But she had no time to dwell on it. The battle continued.

Magmortar and Dragonite clashed again. Perhaps the pain had made them angry, for each threw itself into the fight with its attention fixed solely on the other. Moves flew one after another. Their reckless exchange quickly reached a fever pitch.

As their injuries mounted, both Pokemon tired rapidly. In the end, Dragonite proved the stronger fighter. Another Aqua Tail knocked Magmortar to the ground.

Torkoal's defeat had happened out of sight in the sandstorm. This time Misty had been able to watch every thrilling exchange, and both Trainers were satisfied with how their Pokemon had performed. Flannery's only disappointment was that she had lost.

Even that could not dampen her excitement. It had been an intense match between powerful partners, and her admiration for Ethan had only grown.

You're amazing! Stars seemed to sparkle in her eyes. She looked delighted rather than dejected. Apart from my grandpa, you're the strongest person I've ever met! Come on, let's have the third battle. I can't wait!

Chapter 617: The Pink Demon Returns!

Flannery's third Pokemon was a Camerupt.

Ethan had battled Courtney's Camerupt not long ago. Its abilities were still fresh in his mind, so this time he felt better prepared. Having faced one before did not, of course, guarantee a victory.

He sent Scizor against it.

Frankly, it was a terrible matchup. Scizor was both Bug and Steel type, and Fire-type attacks were four times as effective against it. One blast of flame could leave it in a dreadful state, if it didn't knock it out outright. Even Ash, for all his enthusiasm for battling at a type disadvantage, would rarely choose a Pokemon with a fourfold weakness to its opponent.

Flannery frowned when she saw Ethan's choice. She wanted to ask whether he'd lost his senses or grown overconfident. But his eyes were as calm as ever. He must have done this deliberately.

Either he had tremendous faith in Scizor, or he had some other plan. After seeing Tyranitar and Dragonite fight, Flannery preferred the first explanation. Was Scizor his strongest Pokemon?

Once they began, she realized she had overestimated it. Scizor was certainly strong. Its attacks and mobility were impressive, especially against a slow Pokemon like Camerupt. It twisted and darted around the field, finding plenty of openings. Double Team and Agility helped it avoid attack after attack. It was giving everything it had.

But it could not overcome the type disadvantage. Scizor could succeed a thousand times; it couldn't afford a single mistake.

Camerupt was not one of Flannery's aces, but it was no weakling. Even under Ethan's careful direction, Scizor could hardly fight an opponent like this without leaving an opening. As it kept moving, its stamina fell and its speed began to drop.

Flannery seized the chance. She predicted where Scizor would land and ordered Camerupt to unleash a wide-ranging burst of flame over that part of the field.

Fire swept across it. Scizor had nowhere to go. The flames engulfed it, and it cried out in pain. The hit was devastating.

After finally finding a path to victory, Flannery held on to it. Before Scizor could escape, she had Camerupt pour out more fire. Another wave of searing heat brought Scizor down.

She had won!

Ethan could only shrug helplessly. He hadn't thrown the round on purpose. After Tyranitar and Dragonite, Scizor had simply been next in the order he'd chosen. He had also wanted to see whether it could win despite a fourfold weakness. Evidently it still needed more training.

Flannery jumped with excitement. She was so openly delighted to have won a round that she seemed not to consider her opponent's feelings at all. Ethan couldn't help smiling.

She really did act exactly as she pleased. That could be troublesome for the people around her, but it was also appealing. He meant that as simple appreciation, not romantic interest.

He recalled Scizor and looked again at Camerupt. It seemed every bit as strong as Courtney's; the two were probably evenly matched. That said something about the resources behind Team Magma and Team Aqua. If one of their commanders could command a Pokemon at a Gym Leader's level, it was no wonder those organizations had operated so brazenly in Hoenn for so long.

Ethan's fingers hovered between Tyranitar's and Dragonite's Poke Balls. At last he chose Dragonite, the more exhausted of the two.

Yes, the more exhausted Dragonite. The less favorable the situation, the more he wanted his Pokemon to fight through it. That was how he could build their strength.

Flannery was startled to see Dragonite return. This was the last battle, and Tyranitar was in better condition. Why send out Dragonite? After a moment's thought, she finally understood: Ethan was using their Gym battle to train.

She had only been a Gym Leader for a short while, but she knew how most challengers prepared. They chose Pokemon to exploit the Leader's type, made sure their team was rested, and came to the Gym only when everything was ready. Ethan seemed to feel none of that pressure. He treated a Gym challenge like an ordinary battle he might find anywhereand was even looking for a chance to train.

What nerve.

Another Gym Leader might have felt looked down on. A proud one might have taken offense. Flannery felt only more curious about him. No wonder his Pokemon were so strong: he never wasted a chance to improve them.

Curiosity would not win the match for her, though. When Dragonite was ready, she put the thought aside and focused on the field.

This round was different. Ethan no longer had to worry about a disastrous type matchup, and he attacked without restraint. Flannery's good mood quickly vanished as the battle turned against her.

Dragonite's advantage over a ground-bound opponent was obvious. It had been injured earlier, but Scizor had worn Camerupt down as well. Dragonite had also rested for a while in its Poke Ball. Neither Pokemon entered this round in much better shape than the other.

Unlike Magmortar, Camerupt couldn't keep Dragonite at bay with overwhelming firepower. Under Dragonite's fierce assault, it belched thick smoke and sprayed great quantities of magma in resistance, but neither was enough.

It did not last long. Dragon Rage struck Camerupt. Its massive body wavered, then toppled.

Thud! It landed against a huge rock with a dull crash.

Ethan could feel the difference Flannery had described. This Camerupt really was a step below Torkoal and Magmortar. The round had been less intense than the first two, and he had won it more easily.

I lost. You're really good.

Flannery recalled Camerupt and strode over to Ethan with an open smile. She had lost the match, but accepted it wholeheartedly. That alone set her apart from many Gym Leaders. Some pretended not to mind when a challenger beat them, yet their tone and movements betrayed their discomfort. Flannery showed none of it.

Your Pokemon were impressive too. I got lucky this time, Ethan replied politely.

Then the two stood looking at each other, each apparently waiting for the other to speak. An awkward silence settled over them.

Misty finally cleared her throat. Um, Miss Flannery? Aren't you forgetting something?

Forgetting what? Flannery turned to her in confusion. Only when Misty said badge did realization dawn.

Oh! I forgot! She slapped her forehead and hurriedly searched her jeans pockets.

Ethan and Misty exchanged speechless looks. After spending this long with Flannery, they should have expected it. There was little they could do about having met such a forgetful new Gym Leader.

After searching for a while, Flannery realized she didn't have the badge on her. Sorry! Please wait here. I must have put it somewhere else. I'll go look...

Before either of them could answer, she dashed out of the room.

Oh... Misty sighed at her retreating back. She turned to Ethan, worry in her voice. Can she really handle being a Gym Leader?

Probably... maybe... I hope so. Ethan couldn't be sure. Her enthusiasm was precious, at least. He hoped she would keep it.

They waited long enough for Misty to grow impatient and consider going to check on her. At last Flannery came running back, out of breath.

She stopped before Ethan and, without waiting to catch her breath, held out an orange-red badge shaped like a flame.

Here! The Lavaridge Gym's Heat Badge!

Ethan took a closer look. Its colors shifted from a bright red circle at the bottom to a flame rising above it. It was strikingperhaps the best-looking of all the badges he had collected.

Thanks!

He placed the Heat Badge in his badge case. Then he and Misty said goodbye and left the Lavaridge Gym. Flannery accompanied them all the way to the entrance, waved, and went back inside.

With his second Hoenn badge won, Ethan was one step closer to the Ever Grande Conference. It was already late, so he and Misty decided to spend the night in Lavaridge Town.

Ethan saw the anticipation on Misty's face and knew what she had in mind. He smiled. I know, I know. We're in a town famous for its hot springs. It would be a shame not to have a soak.

Yes! Hooray! Misty cheered. Her delight lifted Ethan's mood too, and he laughed.

They went first to the Pokemon Center and left their injured Pokemon for treatment. Then they headed to the hot spring district and checked into a guesthouse that looked especially clean.

The guesthouse had its own hot springand, as it happened, it was a mixed bath. Misty was thrilled. Whatever she was imagining made her cheeks turn red, and she kept stealing glances at Ethan.

Ethan had no idea what she was thinking. After a generous dinner, they washed and wrapped themselves in towels before going out to the open-air spring behind the guesthouse.

Lavaridge had so many hot springs that, despite the crowds of tourists in town, the two of them appeared to be the guesthouse's only visitors that night.

Ethan tested the water, stepped in, and sank until only his neck and head remained above the surface. He leaned back against a natural stone and gazed at the stars.

Misty took a deep breath to gather her courage. She slowly entered the spring and sat beside him. Neither spoke. She edged a little closer, then followed his example and looked up at the night sky.

What a beautiful night.

The scene reminded her of the hot spring inn on Cinnabar Island. She had shared a spring with Ethan there too, sitting almost this close. Close enough that she could have touched him simply by reaching out.

What had happened after that? She thought back and suddenly remembered the pink demon, Jigglypuff. It had appeared beside the spring and sung until both of them fell fast asleep. When they woke, their faces had been covered in drawings, exactly as one might expect.

Ah, those were good memories. How had Jigglypuff's song gone again?

Something like...

Jigglypuff, Jigglypuff... Jigglypuff...

Yes, that was it! The song sounded just as comforting as she remembered, enough to make her want to drift straight to sleep. Misty nodded as the fading memory came back to her.

Jigglypuff, Jigglypuff... Jigglypuff...

The singing came again. Misty's eyelids grew heavier, and her thoughts began to blur. Through the haze, she heard a sudden splash beside her.

Startled, she turned and saw Ethan plunge headfirst into the water. Before she could understand what he was doing, he surfaced again, looking around with a grave expression.

Misty, get up. Listen! I think that's Jigglypuff's voice!

Chapter 618: Catching Jigglypuff

Jigglypuff?

Misty stared. Had the voice really been more than her imagination? She came fully awake, hurried out of the water, and searched for the pink demon she remembered.

Listening carefully, she realized the song wasn't coming from nearby or even from inside the guesthouse. Jigglypuff seemed to be some distance away. She relaxed a little. That explained why they hadn't fallen asleep as soon as they heard it. If Jigglypuff had been any closer, they would already be out cold, just as before.

She turned to Ethan. What should we do?

Go and take a look, of course. He gritted his teeth. Who knows how many people will suffer if we leave it alone? And it drew all over our faces last time. I haven't forgotten that!

He sounded as though he had quite a grudge against Jigglypuff. Was he planning to catch it?

They left the spring, hurried to the changing rooms, put on their everyday clothes, and met again in the guesthouse courtyard. They also put on headphones to protect themselves from the song. The headphones couldn't block it completely, but they might at least weaken its effect.

Following the sound, they went out onto the hot spring street. It was about ten at night. The street should still have been lively, but people lay sprawled everywhere, fast asleep. They wore blissful smiles; one sleeper even had a bubble at his nose.

The singing continued and grew louder as Ethan and Misty approached the end of the street. Beneath a huge rock, they spotted a round, pink Pokemon. It had set down its microphone, taken the cap off a black marker, and was drawing on the sleepers' faces.

Jigglypuff, all rightand unmistakably the same one from the anime, the one that had followed Ash from Kanto through Johto and on to Hoenn.

If it was here, Ash must have arrived in Hoenn too. Ethan didn't know where he was yet, but he had surely started traveling the region.

To be safe, Ethan released both Gengar and Gardevoir and sent them around to flank Jigglypuff. He wasn't letting it get away this time. Then he took out Combusken's Poke Ball.

Misty had guessed correctly: he meant to catch Jigglypuff. Unlike his previous captures, he wasn't doing it to strengthen his team. He simply wanted this particular Pokemon. In all his travels, only this Jigglypuff and the Celebi in the mysterious forest had inspired that feeling.

Combusken's appearance caught Jigglypuff's attention. It had relied on its sleep-inducing song for so long that other Pokemon usually fell before they could threaten it. It gave Combusken no thought until it came close, then puffed out its cheeks and glared up at it with wide eyes.

Before Jigglypuff understood what Combusken intended, Combusken raised a clawed foot and kicked it. Jigglypuff rolled backward more than a dozen times and struck a rock.

Combusken looked at Ethan in puzzlement. Was that all? Its expression suggested it had expected a stronger opponent.

Jigglypuff had appeared many times, but it wasn't especially powerful. It knew few moves and was more of a mascot than a formidable fighter. Ethan remained cautious anyway, signaling Gengar and Gardevoir to close in from either side.

Jigglypuff swayed where it stood until its head cleared. Then it glared at the Pokemon that had attacked it for no apparent reason and ran angrily toward Combusken. It thrust out its little pink hands, aiming a Double Slap at Combusken's face.

Jigglypuff stood only fifty centimeters tall, while a Combusken was normally around ninety. It had to stretch up even to reach. After announcing its attack by charging straight in from a distance, it stood little chance of landing a hit. Combusken didn't need an order; it simply stepped back.

Jigglypuff refused to give up. It ran forward again and charged headfirst.

Use Detect!

A light flashed in Combusken's eyes. Jigglypuff's motion seemed to slow, every opening suddenly plain. As it came close, Combusken put a hand on its round head and guided its momentum toward a nearby rock.

Thud! Jigglypuff hit the stone and reeled. When it recovered enough to rub its aching head, it finally understood that this opponent would be hard to beat.

Without hesitation, it reached behind itself and pulled its microphone from wherever it kept it.

That was the moment Ethan had been waiting for. He caught Gardevoir's eye. Without a spoken command, she used her psychic power to snatch the microphone away.

Jigglypuff felt it leave its hand as though an invisible hand had seized it. The microphone floated toward the human man. Startled, Jigglypuff chased it, only to find Combusken blocking the way again.

Great! Misty breathed easier at the sight of the stolen microphone. Without it, the pink demon couldn't use that overwhelming song to put them to sleep.

Jiggly!

Jigglypuff puffed up with anger until it looked bigger, but anger couldn't change its predicament. Combusken's belly swelled, and it spat a burst of fire. Faced with the scorching flames and knowing it couldn't win, Jigglypuff turned to flee.

Ethan had no intention of allowing that. Gengar and Gardevoir came in from both sides and drove Jigglypuff back to where it had started.

Combusken, Double Kick!

Combusken sprinted up and launched two flying kicks. Both struck Jigglypuff, sending its round body through the air like a kite with its string cut. It tumbled onto the ground.

Ethan promptly threw a Poke Ball. Red light enveloped Jigglypuff and drew it in. Under Ethan and Misty's gaze, the ball rocked several times. Then another flash of red light burst out, and Jigglypuff escaped.

Oh? It still has strength left? Ethan was a little surprised, but it changed nothing.

He was about to tell Combusken to finish the battle when an idea occurred to him. Instead of throwing another ball, he took out Beldum's.

He released Beldum beside him. Misty had wondered why he'd stopped, but the moment she saw Beldum, she understood and couldn't help laughing.

Ethan picked Beldum up and walked toward Jigglypuff with a pleasant smile. This was a rare opportunity. Beldum knew only Tackle and normally couldn't defeat anyone, but Jigglypuff could barely fight back now. He wasn't about to waste the chance to give Beldum a win.

Besides, he'd done this sort of thing once before. And Jigglypuff had drawn all over his face; now he finally had a chance to take revenge with his own handsor close enough.

Beldum deserved its name. Though less than fifty centimeters tall, it weighed a staggering ninety-five kilograms. Fortunately it could float; otherwise Ethan could never have lifted it alone.

He raised Beldum high over Jigglypuff's round body and brought it down hard. Combusken's attacks had left Jigglypuff strong enough to break out of a Poke Ball once, but no longer able to resist. Lying there, it could only watch the man loom above it and drop a dark shape toward it.

The rock-hard Beldum struck the soft pink Jigglypuff with a loud smack. Under that weight, Jigglypuff's eyes rolled back and it fainted.

Done!

Ethan dusted off his hands, picked up the Poke Ball, and pressed it against Jigglypuff. This time it had no strength left to struggle. The ball gave one slight wobble, then its button locked.

Excellent. He had taken his revenge and caught the pink demona double victory. Better still, it wouldn't be free to harass them again.

He turned to Misty, who was smiling back at him. Only then did he notice that in her hurry to get dressed, she had fastened her buttons crookedly. He had rushed too, afraid Jigglypuff would escape.

Around them, its victims lay asleep in every imaginable position. Jigglypuff had already covered many of their faces with strange drawings. They would probably wake soon, so Ethan and Misty left them undisturbed and returned to their guesthouse.

Neither felt like going back into the hot spring after all that. Misty looked a little disappointed as they said goodnight and went to their separate rooms.

...

The next morning, after a generous Japanese-style breakfast, they went to the Pokemon Center to collect the partners they had left there for treatment.

They left Lavaridge Town and entered Jagged Pass at its northeastern edge. One branch of the mountain route led toward Mt. Chimney's summit; the other passed through Lavaridge and out of the mountains. As its name suggested, Jagged Pass was full of steps and uneven stones. It was hard going, but for Trainers used to long, strenuous walks, it was mostly a matter of getting a little more tired.

Still, as they reached the middle of the pass, Ethan had the persistent feeling that unfriendly eyes were watching them. He thought back and vaguely remembered that Team Magma had a base somewhere around here.

He was in no mood to seek trouble with them and hoped they wouldn't come looking for it either. He remained tense and watchful all the way through. Fortunately, nothing happened. After half a day of walking, they reached the plains safely.

Their next destination lay to the southeast: Mauville City. It was a central Hoenn hub, one of the region's largest cities, and home to the Mauville Gym. They still had more than a day's walk ahead.

On the plains, they met far more Trainers. In a single day they encountered at least a dozen people traveling with Pokemon. Many were eager to battle. When they recognized Ethan and Misty as fellow Trainers by their clothes and gear, they came over to issue challenges. None of them had identified Ethan himself; they simply wanted a fight.

Ethan was in a good mood and accepted them all. Thanks to those matches, Combusken and Eevee steadily grew stronger. Feebas even had one chance to battle, though it lost badly, defeated almost as soon as the match began.

Ethan and Misty teamed up for several Double Battles as well. Their coordination improved with practice, and they beat everyone who faced them. At Ethan's insistence, Misty kept Psyduck firmly inside its Poke Ball.

All those battles made their progress unusually slow. By nightfall they had covered barely a quarter of the route. At that pace, Mauville was still another day or two away.

Chapter 619: Jigglypuff Won't Give Up

Eager to make progress, Ethan and Misty missed the next town where they could have stayed. That night they had to pitch their tents in the wilderness again.

Setting up camp, gathering firewood, boiling water, cooking, and laying out the dishes all went smoothly. They had done it so many times that each step came naturally.

When dinner was ready, Ethan let out Gardevoir, Gengar, Dragonite, Scizor, Tyranitar, Eevee, Combusken, and Beldum. They ate together around the campfire, enjoying one another's company until the meal ended.

Only then did Ethan release Jigglypuff.

It was still indignant, unable to believe it had been caught so easily. The moment it appeared, its eyes darted around and it bolted.

There was a reason Ethan had brought it out last. His other Pokemon were sitting all around it. Except for Beldum, Jigglypuff couldn't hope to beat any of them, and before it had gone far one of them blocked its path.

Stop struggling, Ethan said with a smile. I've already caught you. Running won't change that, so you might as well accept it.

Jigglypuff tried another direction and found a different Pokemon in its way. After several failed attempts, it plopped down on the ground and sulked, cheeks puffed out. Misty giggled.

Ethan, Misty, and the Pokemon teased it for a while longer. When it finally seemed to have given up trying to escape, they left it alone.

Jigglypuff, however, had only been waiting for them to lower their guard. While everyone was talking, it slipped over to their bags and began searching through them. It wanted its microphone back.

It turned both Ethan's and Misty's bags inside out without finding it. As it wondered where the human had hidden the microphone, a shadow fell across it.

Jigglypuff looked up with a start. Gengar stood there grinning, its microphone in one hand.

Jiggly!

Its eyes lit up and it reached for the microphone. Just as its short hands nearly touched it, Gengar lifted its arm. That tiny extra distance put the microphone out of reach. Jigglypuff jumped; Gengar jumped too. It still couldn't get it.

Jiggly!

Now it understood it was being toyed with. It glared up at Gengar, whose face wore the same infuriating smile as the human's.

...

Mauville City was a colorful, lively metropolis where past and present met. It was home to the Mauville Gym, the Mauville Game Corner, Mauville Park, and Mauville Food Court. Young visitors to the city rarely missed those well-known sights.

On the morning of the third day, Ethan and Misty finally reached Mauville. Rather than sightseeing, they went straight to the Gym.

The Mauville Gym was one of Hoenn's official Gyms. Its Leader, Wattson, specialized in Electric-type Pokemon. From a distance, the building looked five or six stories tall. Its outer walls were painted gold, several electrical towers rose from the roof, and an enormous lightning-bolt sign hung outside. It looked more like a power station than a Gym.

Unfortunately, when they arrived, they found it closed for the day. They had missed their chance to challenge it. At least the closure ended that night; the Gym would open for challenges again the following morning.

With no other choice, they looked at each other and set off to find somewhere to stay.

Following the street toward the Pokemon Center, they came to Mauville Park in the middle of the city. Outside the park stood a tall tower modeled on Lumiose City's Prism Tower. It was a symbol of friendship between Lumiose in Kalos and Mauville in Hoenn. According to local stories, the tower shone brightly whenever something went wrong at New Mauville, warning the city.

They had time to spare, so they changed plans and decided to walk through the park first.

Just inside, they saw a small boy arguing with a middle-aged man. Ethan and Misty glanced at them and kept going, but as they passed, the boy suddenly ran over.

Excuse me, sir! Please wait!

Ethan and Misty stopped and turned, eyebrows raised.

What's the matter? Ethan asked.

The boy came up to him, bowed politely, and asked in an almost pleading tone, Are you a Pokemon Trainer?

Of course.

As he answered, Ethan took a better look at the child. He seemed about ten, with thick, pale green hair and neat features. Dressed in long sleeves and trousers, he looked like a diligent student and was a little shy.

Um... The boy hesitated. Would you have a battle with me?

Ethan had never met a challenger who was so polite, even when asking for a battle. He looked toward the man, then asked before agreeing, I could. But what was going on between you two just now?

The boy relaxed at the possibility of a match. I was arguing with my uncle. He thinks I'm not ready to challenge the Mauville Gym. I want to battle you in front of him and show him what I can do!

So that was it. But why choose Ethan? How did the boy know he could win? If he lost, that would hardly prove he was ready. Unless the boy thought Ethan looked weak.

Ethan glanced from the uncle to the boy once more and finally nodded. All right. I accept your challenge.

The boy brightened and pointed nearby. There's a battlefield over there. Let's go!

He returned to his uncle and spoke quietly to him. Ethan exchanged a look with Misty, shook his head with a helpless smile, and led the way toward the open-air battlefield.

Chapter 620: Battling Wally

Ethan and the boy took their places on opposite sides of the battlefield. Misty and the middle-aged man stood behind their respective Trainers to watch.

Mauville Park was busy, but most visitors were skateboarding, walking dogs, or jogging. No one else was using the battlefield. As soon as people noticed a battle was about to begin, those with time to spare gathered around. More and more came until over twenty spectators stood outside the field: men and women, young and old, all curious about the two Trainers and which Pokemon they would choose.

Ethan had been watched often enough to ignore a crowd. The boy across from him plainly hadn't. He looked around nervously, growing more uncomfortable as the audience swelled.

Only when he saw Ethan calmly take a Poke Ball from his waist pouch did the boy pull himself together. He took a deep breath and focused on the match.

Then he bowed to Ethan again. My name is Wally. It's a pleasure to meet you!

Since his opponent had introduced himself, Ethan replied in kind. He didn't need to bow to a child, so he nodded and smiled. I'm Ethan, a Trainer traveling around the world.

Wally took out his Poke Ball. This was an informal battle in a public park. Apart from sending out their Pokemon at the same time, they had no elaborate rules and no need for a referee.

They threw their Poke Balls almost together. Two flashes of light revealed their choices. Ethan had selected Combusken, which had only recently evolved. He wanted it to gain experience in battle.

Wally's choice surprised him: a Ralts.

Only then did Ethan vaguely recall that a boy named Wally had appeared in the games. What a coincidence to meet him here.

Ethan turned his attention back to Ralts. Having raised one himself, he could tell at a glance that Wally had cared for it well. It looked healthy and spirited. The boy was a capable Trainer.

He also remembered that Wally's Ralts was male and would eventually become a Gallade, showing remarkable strength later in the games.

Ethan studied the matchup. Ralts was still in its first evolutionary stage and couldn't match a second-stage Combusken physically. But Ralts's Psychic typing gave it a super-effective advantage over Combusken's Fighting type. The battle would not be as easy as it looked.

Several spectators noticed the type matchup and murmured to their companions. They didn't seem optimistic about Combusken. Wally relaxed a little too. He had issued the challenge himself, and the result mattered to his hope of challenging the Gym. Seeing the type advantage naturally pleased him.

When both Pokemon were ready, Ethan and Wally exchanged a glance and called their commands in unison.

Ralts, use Confusion!

Combusken, Sand Attack!

One Trainer had chosen to attack, the other to hinder his opponent. As Ralts used Confusion, Combusken kicked a spray of sand toward it.

Both moves landed. Sand filled Ralts's eyes, while the psychic force knocked Combusken backward.

At first glance, Ralts seemed to have won the exchange. Combusken had only recently evolved, though, and Ethan had not had time to train it in all the moves it could learn. Confusion was an invisible attack with decent reach, difficult to evade on foot. Knowing that, Ethan had chosen Sand Attack to limit what Ralts could do next.

It worked. Combusken had been hit, but Ralts could not follow up while its eyes were full of sand. It rubbed at them, trying to clear its vision.

Get close, Combusken! Ethan called. Combusken ran into Ralts's half of the field. By the time it arrived, Ralts had rubbed the sand away. It looked up, and their eyes met.

Ralts, Confusion, quickly!

Quick Attack!

Wally tried the same move again. This time, with the distance greatly reduced, Ethan had more options. Combusken burst into a sudden sprint, zigzagging toward Ralts. Confusion missed.

Wally's heart jumped. Quick, use Double Team!

His haste was understandable. If a Fighting-type Pokemon reached Ralts, it could be dangerous. Ralts resisted Fighting-type moves, but it would be hard to break away once Combusken was close.

Ralts split into four identical figures, each moving in exactly the same way. Looking at them alone, it was impossible to tell which was real.

Ethan had anticipated it. As Ralts used Double Team, Combusken opened its mouth and sprayed Embers over all four figures at close range. The fire passed harmlessly through three copies and caught the real Ralts.

Ralts cried out in pain. Combusken was already upon it. A Double Kick struck home, followed by a slash from its claw that knocked Ralts to the ground.

The battle had not lasted long. Most of the spectators were surprised that Combusken had won despite its type disadvantage.

Wally's face fell at the sight of his defeated partner. Ethan smiled faintly. He knew what Wally had hoped to prove, but he had never intended to let the boy win.

Wally had only recently become a Trainer, yet he had raised Ralts well. Against another beginner, he might truly have won. Unfortunately, he had picked the wrong opponent.

Ethan, rather mischievously, had said nothing about the gulf between their abilities. He had simply treated the match as practice for Combusken.

Chapter 621: The News Duo

Wally had lost. By rights, that meant his hope of proving himself to his uncle had failed. To everyone's surprise, though, the man began to applaud.

That was an excellent battle, his uncle said with a smile. I saw how hard you've worked. You lost because your opponent was too strong.

Wally's eyes lit up. He watched his uncle hopefully, waiting to hear what would come next.

His uncle met his gaze and nodded with satisfaction. I agree. You can challenge the Gym and pursue your dream.

Yes!

Wally jumped for joy. The shy boy would only show so much excitement in front of a crowd when something mattered this deeply to him.

Combusken had already returned to Ethan's side. Well done. Ethan stroked its head in encouragement. Then he looked up at Wally's beaming face and shrugged at Misty.

Well, we should be going.

They took Combusken through the crowd and soon disappeared. By the time Wally recovered enough to thank Ethan, the older Trainer was gone. Wally didn't dwell on it; he was too happy about his uncle's decision.

Ethan and Misty were about to continue their walk through Mauville Park when a voice called from behind them.

Please wait!

It was an energetic woman's voice. At first Ethan didn't realize she was addressing him. Then he heard footsteps hurrying after them and turned. A man and a woman were approaching together.

The woman looked about twenty-five or twenty-six. She was pretty, with short light-brown hair, subtle makeup, and pearl earrings. She wore a blue strapless top, fitted white trousers, and white heels, and carried a microphone. She looked every bit the big-city reporter.

The man seemed about the same age. In a cap, gray T-shirt, and jeans, he carried a video camera on his shoulder. Their equipment made it obvious that they worked for a television station.

The woman's eyes brightened when Ethan faced her. It really is you! You're the champion of both the Kanto and Johto Leagues!

Shh... Ethan quickly gestured for her to lower her voice. People recognized him from time to time now, but he had only just arrived in Hoenn and didn't want to draw attention yet.

Oh, sorry. She smiled apologetically. We're reporters from TV Mauville. We were conducting interviews nearby, happened to see your battle, and took the liberty of following you.

I see. Ethan nodded. What are you covering? Has something interesting happened here? Any big news?

No, the man said without thinking. It's just a feature about parents and children

The woman interrupted him with a loud cough and an awkward smile. We're really just looking around. We don't have a particular story in mind.

Before Ethan could ask anything more, she hurried on. I've talked so much without introducing us. How rude of me! I'm Gabby, and this is my partner, Ty. Would you be willing to give us an exclusive interview?

Gabby and Ty? Ethan thought for a moment but couldn't place them. He could tell Gabby was avoiding the subject of their current assignment, though, and let it go.

Sorry. I don't want to do an interview.

Really? Gabby looked startled. Didn't you give exclusive interviews during the Silver Conference and the Indigo League?

She meant the two interviews Alexa had conducted with him. Ethan wasn't surprised she knew about them; a reporter would have better access to that information than most people.

He shook his head. Those were late in the tournaments, after I'd achieved something worth talking about. I've only just arrived in Hoenn. I have one badge and haven't even qualified for the Ever Grande Conference. What grounds do I have for an interview now?

You're too modest, Gabby said with a smile. With your ability, collecting eight badges and entering the Ever Grande Conference should be easy. You might even win the whole thing!

Ethan only smiled and shook his head, leaving that prediction unanswered. An interview this early would expose him to other competitors before he was ready. It could also leave viewers thinking he had started boasting before he had even collected the badges.

Gabby saw that he had reservations, but she kept asking. Ethan held firm. Eventually, worn down by her persistence, he offered a compromise.

An interview now is out of the question. When the Ever Grande Conference comes around, if the opportunity is there, I'll consider you first.

Well... Gabby hesitated. She could tell that was as far as he would go, so she smiled and accepted. It's a deal. Let's exchange contact details.

Her determination made her ambition plain. With a resigned sigh, Ethan exchanged phone numbers with her, made an excuse, and left with Misty.

Watching him go, Gabby raised her brows triumphantly and clenched a fist in excitement.

Why are you so happy? Ty asked.

You idiot! She gave him an exasperated look. This is a rare opportunity. Do you want to spend the rest of your career standing in parks interviewing parents about time with their children?

Ty still looked puzzled. What's that got to do with him?

Everything! He won both the Silver Conference and the Indigo League. He's obviously come to Hoenn aiming for another championship. He's mysterious, hardly ever appears in the media, and audiences love him. If we can build a connection with him and land even one interview, our standing at the station will soar. We might finally get back into the studio!

Oh, I see! Ty's eyes lit up. We can't let a chance like that slip away.

Now you understand. Gabby lifted her chin, then looked in the direction Ethan had gone. Determination filled her eyes. Whatever happens, I'm holding on to this opportunity. I'm tired of standing outside in the wind and sun!

Chapter 622: Traps and Raikou at Mauville Gym

After strolling through the park and unwinding, Ethan and Misty checked into the local Pokemon Center. They didn't eat lunch there, though. They went to the nearby Mauville Food Court instead.

Despite its name, the food court was an indoor restaurant area on a basement level. Stall followed stall; there appeared to be a hundred of them, selling food from Hoenn and other regions alike. They arrived at lunchtime, when the place was packed. Almost every one of the hundreds of tables in the central hall was occupied.

With so many stalls cooking at once, their combined fumes made the air smell strange and a little sharp. Ethan and Misty worked through the dense crowd, looking over the stalls. After a long search, they chose a few meals with peculiar names.

Misty ordered a Village Sandwich. It contained sliced meat, bacon, ham, tuna, and egg, none of which explained the name. Had someone brought the recipe from a village?

Ethan chose Magnemite-yaki. Despite the name, it didn't contain a Magnemite. It was simply a selection of okonomiyaki, akashiyaki, imagawayaki, dorayaki, tonpeiyaki, and takoyaki.

Carrying their food, they searched again before finding half an empty table in a corner. At last they could eat. The food court's reputation was deserved: besides its enormous size, the food was delicious. They finished their lunches, still wanted more, and each ordered a bowl of miso ramen. Only then were they full.

To walk off the meal, they visited another of Mauville's famous attractions: the Mauville Game Corner. Like the Celadon Game Corner in Kanto, it was large and equipped with novel machines. They bought tokens and spent a happy while trying almost every kind of game. Before leaving, Ethan won a Starmie plush for Misty from a claw machine.

They returned to the Pokemon Center thoroughly satisfied. They hadn't challenged the Gym, but the afternoon had been full all the same. Misty especially felt as though she had been on a date with Ethan, and she could hardly have been happier.

...

After a night's rest, Ethan and Misty returned to Mauville Gym early the next morning. The notice had been removed from the door. The Gym was open again, and this time they could go inside.

The moment they entered, the building had a surprise for them. A long, enclosed corridor stretched beyond the entrance. As soon as they stepped into it, the floor trembled, then began to move like a horizontal elevator, carrying them along a barely visible track into the Gym.

Whoa! Misty staggered in surprise and grabbed Ethan's sleeve to keep from falling. She wasn't timid. Anyone would be startled by a moving floor with no warning.

The platform sped down the corridor and passed through an electric gate. Then the track sloped upward, and they began to climb.

What is this? Misty grumbled. Isn't this a Gym? Why does it feel like an amusement park?

It's an Electric-type Gym, Ethan said with a smile. Its Pokemon probably give it plenty of power. They might as well find a use for the electricity instead of wasting it.

Maybe, but... The platform kept rising, and Misty had a bad feeling. Don't tell me this is

It reached the top before she could finish. Then it lurched forward and hurtled downhill like a roller coaster.

Aaaah!

Misty screamed. A roller coaster in an amusement park wouldn't normally frighten her this much. Here they were simply standing on a moving platform, without seats or even safety belts.

Ethan caught a handrail with one hand and wrapped the other arm around Misty's waist. That kept them from being thrown off as the platform raced through the narrow passage.

A dozen or so seconds later, the space ahead opened into a large room. They thought they had reached the end of the ride, but the track stopped at the entrance. Beyond it lay a deep pool.

The platform shook as it left the rails. It skipped violently across the water like a flat stone, nearly bouncing them into the pool. Even Ethan lost his grip. Both of them flew into the airthen, as though the whole contraption had been carefully designed for this, landed safely back on the platform.

It crossed the room, caught another track at the far side, and carried them deeper into the Gym. They got up and rubbed their aching backsides.

Before Misty could complain, another electric gate opened at the end of the passage. Beyond it stood a magnificent golden Pokemon. Ethan recognized it immediately; he owned one himself.

Raikou? Misty cried. She had never imagined seeing a Legendary Pokemon from Johto inside a Hoenn Gym.

The moving platform began to slow, but its momentum still carried them right up to Raikou. It roared and opened its mouth. Electricity flickered insidea clear warning that an attack was coming.

They had nowhere to dodge while standing on the platform. Whatever this Gym was trying to do, Ethan guessed the encounter was some sort of test for challengers. He wasn't going to sit still for it.

Misty reached for a Poke Ball, but Ethan held out a hand to stop her and threw one of his own. Blue light flashed, and Tyranitar appeared before Raikou.

Tyranitar roared and charged without caring whether its opponent was a Legendary Pokemon. Ethan used the moment to study the Raikou more closely.

He knew how unlikely it was for one to appear in Hoenn. Even if Raikou existed as a small population rather than a single Pokemon, they were extraordinarily rare. Finding a second one in Johto would be difficult enough, let alone finding one captured by a Gym Leader here. Ethan already carried a Raikou in his own Poke Ball, making the coincidence even less plausible.

Now that he looked carefully, he spotted something wrong. The figure before him had Raikou's imposing appearance, but lacked its living presence. Its eyes were empty, like those of a cold machine.

A replica might fool someone who had never met Raikou. It could not fool Raikou's own Trainer.

Chapter 623: Battling Wattson

Tyranitar lumbered toward the Raikou. The imitation's attack came first: a huge stream of electricity burst from its mouth and struck Tyranitar.

The blast looked powerful, but Tyranitar's typing did not leave it weak to Electric-type attacks. It hurt, yet Tyranitar kept advancing, step by heavy step.

Ethan could have ordered a ranged attack such as Hyper Beam. In the narrow corridor, the Raikou could hardly have dodged it; it would have needed a move of similar power to cancel the beam. But Ethan knew this was a Gym test, and he didn't want to damage the building. He chose to fight up close.

Once Tyranitar reached its target, it opened its jaws and used Bite. The false Raikou lacked a living Pokemon's judgment. It stood still and let Tyranitar sink its teeth into it.

Rrrip!

Tyranitar's teeth were small and not especially sharp, but they easily tore a piece from the Raikou's body. Misty saw wires inside and finally realized it was a fake. Perhaps the damaged circuitry failed, because its eyes went dark and it stopped moving.

That's it? Misty put a hand on her hip and shook her head. It made such a dramatic entrance, but it broke after one bite.

It was probably only a small test, Ethan said. If it were as strong as a real Raikou, most Trainers would never get through the door.

As he spoke, a hidden door opened in the wall. Two men came out.

The first was an elderly man in his seventies, short and rather round, with a prominent belly. He had styled what little white hair remained on his head, and a matching white mustache and beard covered much of his lower face. He wore a camouflage vest marked with a lightning-bolt symbol over work overalls. Despite his age, he seemed full of energy and came out laughing.

Behind him walked a younger man with round glasses, apparently his assistant.

The old man had evidently heard them from the other side of the door. He grinned at Ethan. You're right! It's only a little test. That's my Laughing Million-Volt No. 2, a welcome for challengersa little jolt to charge up your lives! Well? Did it scare you?

Hardly, Misty said with a dismissive look. She had been startled, but she wasn't going to admit it. Your imitation is nowhere near as strong as a real Raikou.

Oh? The old man raised his eyebrows. You know what it's called, so you must be from outside Hoenn. And from the sound of it, you've seen a real Raikou before?

Misty realized she had said too much. Her expression changed, and she glanced at Ethan.

He stepped forward with a smile. We have. I fought one while traveling in Johto.

That wasn't a lie, merely half the story. He had fought Raikouand then caught it.

The old man had no reason to doubt him. He stroked his beard. You've battled a Legendary Pokemon? Your travels must have been exciting!

Ethan recalled Tyranitar. To move away from the subject and get to the reason for their visit, he asked, Are you Mr. Wattson?

That's right. The man nodded. I'm Wattson, Leader of the Mauville Gym. This is Watt, my assistant.

Watt gave them a friendly nod. Hello. Welcome to Mauville Gym.

It's a pleasure to meet you. I'm Ethan, a traveling Trainer, and this is Misty, my traveling companion. I'm sure you know why we're here, Mr. Wattson. Would now be a good time for a challenge?

Of course! Follow me.

Wattson and Watt led them out of the corridor and into a spacious room. It was plainly the Gym's battlefield. Unlike a rocky field or a pool, the Electric-type Gym's arena was simply flat ground.

Misty chose a seat in the stands. When she used to travel with Ash, every Gym battle had made her worry. Watching Ethan was different. She rarely had to fear for the result; she could cheer a little and enjoy the match. It was one of the greatest differences between the two Trainers.

Ethan and Wattson took their places in the Trainer areas, and Watt stepped forward to referee.

The Mauville Gym battle is about to begin! he called. Each side may use three Pokemon. The Gym Leader may not switch Pokemon freely during the match. When all three Pokemon on either side are unable to battle, the match is over!

They were standard Gym rules, identical to the ones Roxanne had used at Rustboro. Once Watt had finished, Wattson threw his first Poke Ball.

A Voltorb appeared before Ethan.

This is my Voltorb, Wattson said cheerfully. A warning: it can fight for a long time. If you want to beat it, you'd best finish the battle quickly!

His warning showed Ethan how cheerful the old man was and how much confidence he had in his partner.

Thank you. I'll keep that in mind.

Ethan smiled politely and sent out his own Pokemon without much deliberation. Blue light flashed, revealing Combusken.

Wattson looked surprised. Why didn't you use that Tyranitar? It seemed very strong a moment ago. Oh, I seeyou must be saving it for last!

Chapter 624: Misty: Nice Shot!

Voltorb looked remarkably like a Poke Ball. Even now, some people claimed that humans had modeled the first modern Poke Balls on it. The story might be nothing more than a rumor or a joke, but plenty believed it. Voltorb certainly resembled a Poke Ball.

It had no arms or legs, only a round body with a red upper half, a white lower half, and a pair of eyes. Stranger still, people had discovered Voltorb around the same time Poke Balls first went on sale. The earliest sightings were said to be inside a company that made them. Voltorb also appeared in power plants. Why it looked so much like a Poke Ball remained a mystery, which only encouraged the belief that the two were connected.

One theory held that Voltorb had come into being when a Poke Ball was exposed to a powerful pulse. Its resemblance to the ball served as camouflage. People sometimes mistook it for one and touched it, only to receive a numbing shock. The slightest provocation could even make it explode. Experienced Trainers handled Voltorb carefully.

Despite the risk, it remained popular with Electric-type Trainers. Wattson's willingness to use one in the opening round showed how well he knew his own Voltorb. He wouldn't put himself in danger lightly.

At the edge of the field, Watt saw both Pokemon were ready and gave the signal. The Gym battle began.

Combusken immediately ran toward Voltorb on its two strong legs. Since catching it, Ethan had noticed its gift for speed. It enjoyed running and was good at it. If Charizard, his other Fire-type Pokemon, was strong and unwilling to yield, Combusken was quick and restless. Ethan already had a general idea of how he wanted to train it, including after it evolved into Blaziken.

Wattson watched it close in and gave his first command without concern. Voltorb, use Screech!

Screech, sometimes called a piercing noise, lowered the target's Defense. Starting with it suggested Wattson meant to weaken Combusken before finishing it with a powerful attack. Ethan had fought enough battles to see the plan from that one move.

Voltorb flashed blue. The air around it shuddered as a violent sound spread outward in every direction. Combusken could not dodge an invisible attack that covered the whole area. And whether it meant to use fire or a close-range Fighting move, it needed to get nearer to Voltorb.

Screech passed through Combusken just as it reached the middle of the field. At the same time, Combusken opened its mouth and sprayed Embers toward Voltorb.

The sound reverberated through Combusken's body. It grimaced and dropped to one knee. Across the field, Wattson took the oncoming flames seriously. Voltorb could be unstable; even a small injury might trigger an explosion, and fire was hardly a small threat.

Voltorb, use Rollout!

It was a smart command. Rolling away would evade the Embers and bring Voltorb closer to Combusken. Combusken could use Fighting-type moves up close, but Voltorb had Electric attacks such as Discharge and the threat of an explosion. It needn't fear close combat. At worst it could blow itself up and take its opponent down with it, a tactic Voltorb Trainers often used against difficult foes.

Voltorb rolled forward. Its smooth, round body picked up exceptional speed on the flat field. In a blink it passed beyond the flames and raced toward Combusken.

Ethan smiled faintly. He had already seen what Wattson intended and prepared an answer. As Voltorb drew close enough to collide, he called, Double Kick!

Combusken sprang up and kicked the oncoming Voltorb. It was like kicking a soccer ball: Voltorb shot back the way it had come. Before it could use Discharge, it was rolling toward its original position.

Nice shot! Misty blurted from the stands. Embarrassed, she quickly fell silent. This was a Pokemon battle, not a soccer match.

Voltorb finally stopped spinning and looked upjust as another wave of fire came toward it. This time it could not use Rollout to escape. The Embers hit directly, and Wattson's heart leaped.

Even after raising Voltorb for years, he could not know exactly how much damage would make it explode. It might endure several attacks without trouble, or a collision with a small stone while rolling might set it off. As he watched the flames cover it, he could only hope it would hold together a little longer.

Perhaps his silent plea worked. When the Embers faded, Voltorb had a few scorch marks but was otherwise unharmed.

Excellent! Wattson laughed again, his hearty voice filling the Gym. He hardly sounded like an old man. Now it's our turn to fight back!

That was easier said than done. Voltorb and Combusken stood at an awkward distance: close enough for Combusken's Embers to reach, but beyond the range of Voltorb's Discharge. If Voltorb tried Rollout again, Combusken would simply kick it back as before.

They tested that standoff several times. Wattson frowned. It clearly wasn't working, and for a moment he couldn't decide what to do next.

Chapter 625: Winning the First Round

Wattson had spent many years as a Gym Leader and had a lifetime of experience to draw on. After a moment's thought, he found a way out of the stalemate. Defense did not suit a man who laughed as freely as he did. To beat Combusken, he would attack.

Voltorb, use Spark!

If Rollout alone wasn't working, he could add electricity to the charge. With Spark, electric current would cover Voltorb's body as it struck its opponent. Combined with the way Voltorb moved, it would be a rolling ball of lightning.

Combusken couldn't simply kick it away again. Touching it would mean taking an electric shock, perhaps even being paralyzed.

At Wattson's command, visible currents began to dance over Voltorb's body and leap into the surrounding air. It looked dangerous even before it moved. When it rolled toward Combusken again, its speed and force were plainly different.

Ethan became more cautious. He would not have Combusken kick it casually this time, but meeting it head-on wasn't wise either.

Combusken, use Ember!

Combusken spat fire. Now that Voltorb was rolling at full speed, though, it slipped out of the attack's range before the flames hit the ground.

Ethan's gaze sharpened. He could no longer intercept it midway. First Combusken needed to avoid Spark. He changed plans at once. Dodge it!

Combusken obeyed without hesitation, turning and running toward the far end of the field. For a while the distance between the two Pokemon remained steady.

The average Combusken might not be exceptionally fast, but an individual could have a particular talent. Ethan's Combusken was a gifted runner. Its powerful legs gave it a burst of speed that it couldn't necessarily maintain forever, but for now that burst was enough.

Combusken ran. Voltorb pursued.

Wattson had not expected it. He was an Electric-type specialist, but years of facing challengers had taught him the capabilities of many other Pokemon, Combusken included. He had been sure Spark combined with Rollout would connect. This one was faster than he had imagined.

As Voltorb used up its energy, the electricity around it weakened and finally disappeared. It was slowly gaining on Combusken, but without Spark it was merely rolling again.

Wattson's heart sank. Why had the electricity faded at that very moment? His reactions were a little slower with age. Before he could give another command, Ethan called from the opposite side of the field.

Now! Quick Attack!

Combusken braked, spun around, and raced straight back at Voltorb. It moved even faster than before. In a flash, it was upon its opponent.

Oh no! Wattson opened his mouth, but Combusken had already collided with Voltorb. The impact sent the round Pokemon rolling far across the field before it finally came to a stop.

Wattson watched it wobble. Then Voltorb exploded violently.

Boom!

Combusken's collision had pushed Voltorb past the point at which it would explode. The worst part for Wattson was the distance: Voltorb was much too far away for the blast to catch Combusken.

What a shame. If only it had been a little closer. Wattson sighed and shook his head.

Watt raised his colored flag. Voltorb is unable to battle! Combusken wins!

Well done! Ethan called. Combusken answered with a cry.

Wattson was disappointed to lose the first round, but he composed himself. He recalled the unconscious Voltorb and took out another Poke Ball.

You're good. I never expected your Combusken to run like that. But the next battle won't come down to speed!

He threw the ball. In a flash of blue light, a Magneton appeared before Ethan.

Ethan had faced its unevolved form, Magnemite, many times in the wild and in matches. This was his first encounter with a Magneton, though he knew what it was.

It looked much like three Magnemite joined together. According to what people said, strong magnetic forces bound them so tightly that they could no longer separate, giving rise to a new Pokemon.

The combination changed the placement of its magnets. Two lower magnets projected forward, while each Magnemite at the sides bore only two screws. It had three heads instead of one, but it was not three times as intelligent. Its electrical power, on the other hand, had increased considerably.

Magneton could produce powerful magnetic fields and high voltages, strong enough to evaporate moisture nearby. Getting close to one could cause severe ringing in the ears. It also emitted mysterious electromagnetic waves that disrupted communications. Precision machines sometimes failed wherever Magneton lived.

Because of that, some large cities even had rules requiring Trainers to keep Magneton in its Poke Ball. Those who let one roam freely could receive a warning from the police.

Ethan understood why Wattson had sent it out. After the trouble Voltorb had had closing the distance, the Gym Leader had chosen a Pokemon that excelled at fighting from medium to long range against Combusken.

Chapter 626: Wattson: Young Man, You're Too Trusting!

Ethan saw what Wattson had in mind and indulged him. He kept Combusken on the field instead of switching Pokemon. Wattson was an old man, after all; a little consideration seemed only polite. More importantly, Combusken had taken little damage in the first round. It had spent some energy but could still fight.

Seeing that Ethan had not switched, Wattson smiled in a way he hadn't before. Ethan noticed but gave it little thought. He sent Combusken to its starting position for the second round.

Both sides were ready. Watt waved his flag, and the second round of the Mauville Gym battle began.

Let's show them our new move! Wattson called with a laugh. Magneton, use Zap Cannon!

Zap Cannon?

Ethan started. This wasn't a move just any Pokemon could use. Among Electric-type attacks, its power stood below only Bolt Strike and Electro Shot, matched Volt Tackle and Double Shock, and even exceeded Thunder. Wattson's Magneton had learned something that formidable?

It must be a very strong Pokemon. Now Ethan understood that odd smile. Wattson had sprung a powerful partner on him without warning. The man really was crafty beneath his cheerful manner.

Ethan shook his head ruefully. He had kept Combusken in partly to spare Wattson's feelings, only to be met with this at the start of the round. That hearty laugh had fooled him.

Still, a move as strong as Zap Cannon took time to launch, giving Combusken a chance to escape. They had begun on opposite halves of the field, far apart. Combusken wasn't immobilized or trapped, had plenty of stamina, and had flat ground beneath its feet. Hitting it from that distance would be difficult. Ethan realized Wattson also wanted to make an impression and frighten him a little. He relaxed slightly, though Magneton was plainly no easy opponent.

All those thoughts passed through his mind in an instant. At the same time he shouted, Dodge, quickly!

Magneton charged for a moment. All six of its U-shaped magnets exerted force together, forming a thick beam before it. The Zap Cannon fired toward Combusken like a rectangular shell of electrical energy, trailing lightning as it flashed across the field.

Combusken had already begun to run. As the attack neared, it used Quick Attack and accelerated just enough to slip past its edge. The hot glow of the current faded in the air, having singed only a few feathers.

Combusken kept the momentum from Quick Attack and closed the distance. At Ethan's command, it spat Embers toward Magneton, as it had against Voltorb in the previous round. Wattson had more options this time.

Thunder Shock!

Magneton stayed where it hovered, choosing to trade blows. Lightning and fire crossed in midair. Neither canceled the other; both passed through and struck their targets. Combusken and Magneton cried out almost together. Fortunately for each, neither attack caused an additional status condition.

Magneton was stronger overall than Voltorb. It could contend with Combusken from long, medium, or short range and lacked many of Voltorb's limitations. Winning would take a hard fight.

Double Kick!

Combusken rushed Magneton and launched a fierce, sustained assault. A long battle favored the troublesome Magneton, so Ethan wanted Combusken to give everything it had now. Wattson noticed the change of pace and raised his brows, directing Magneton to answer each attack.

Embers, electrical discharges, and Combusken's heavy breathing echoed around the battlefield. Combusken pressed close, alternating its clawed feet and using Fighting- and Normal-type moves. Magneton struggled against the pressure.

With no arms, it could not catch or block Combusken's Fighting moves. It had to keep sliding aside. Movement interrupted some of its attacks, forcing it to defend and trapping it in a worsening cycle.

Scratch, Double Kick, then Peckwithin seconds Combusken landed several hits.

Magneton was strong enough to retaliate even in that position. A Thunder Shock struck Combusken.

Crackle!

Electricity flashed over Combusken, making all its feathers stand on end. In the end, Magneton, already on the verge of falling, managed to bring Combusken down with it. Both collapsed.

Ethan could accept a draw. Wattson found it much harder to take. He had caught the young Trainer off guard and still lost the round. A defeat was a defeat, though. At least Magneton had taken down one of Ethan's Pokemon with it.

There was something worth noting about Wattson's first two Pokemon. In the anime, both Voltorb and Magneton had seemed capable of strong attacks but unable to endure much damage. When Ash challenged this Gym, his Pikachu absorbed electricity from the Raikou robot, then defeated each of Wattson's Pokemon in a single hit. Three easy wins earned him the badge.

It was probably Ash's easiest Gym battle from the start of his journey all the way to his eventual championship. Even more remarkable, Pikachu had done it against fellow Electric types, which resisted its attacks. That showed how little punishment those Pokemon could take.

Chapter 627: Ethan: As You Wish

After losing two rounds, Wattson's hearty smile faded. Even Watt looked at him with concern. His boss was getting on in years; a strong emotional shock would do him no good. If he lost all three rounds and fell ill from it, the match would hardly be worth the cost.

Wattson appeared unaware of his assistant's worry. He recalled Magneton and took out his third Poke Ball with a grave expression. Blue light flashed, revealing his final Pokemon.

An Ampharos.

It resembled a large kangaroo. Its skin was yellow, with a white belly, flat hands and feet, and a single toe on each foot. A red orb sat on its forehead and another at the end of its tail. Black bands marked its neck, ears, and part of the tail.
