The tip of that tail produced an intense light. After dark, its glow could be seen far out at sea, serving as a beacon for ships. In ancient times people had even used Ampharos's light to send signals to companions in the distance.

Ethan had battled an Ampharos in Johto, so it wasn't unfamiliar. His experience with the games told him something else that most challengers might not know: Ampharos was one of Wattson's ace Pokemon.

The old fox. Wattson had quietly raised the difficulty again. An ordinary challenger might never have realized it.

Ethan recalled Combusken and assessed Ampharos. Despite dragon in its Chinese name, it was purely an Electric-type Pokemon. Even so, it was versatile and knew moves of several types beyond Electric.

With Wattson using an ace, Ethan had to choose more carefully. His fingers passed over the Poke Balls at his waist. He considered Dragonite and Tyranitar, then stopped on Tyranitar's ball.

Wattson showed no surprise when Tyranitar appeared. I knew you'd send it out! When it broke my Laughing Million-Volt No. 2, I could tell it was strong. I was sure you'd use it in this battle.

Sure I'd use it? Ethan shook his head with a faint smile but didn't argue. Anyone who saw a challenger with a strong Pokemon would assume it was the greatest threat and keep watching for it. To Ethan, Tyranitar had merely been one of several choices.

Tyranitar gave its customary roar. Many of Ethan's more ferocious Pokemon seemed to have developed that habit.

Wattson's Ampharos was rather timid. The roar and Tyranitar's greater size made it instinctively take a step back. Wattson's heart sank.

Don't be afraid! he called quickly. Fight the way you always do. Have confidence in yourself. You're the best!

His encouragement worked. Ampharos calmed down and even met Tyranitar's gaze. Its nerves might be a little fragile, but it clearly had a close bond with Wattson and trusted him.

When both Pokemon were ready, Watt waved his flag again. The third round began. Each side had sent out a powerful partner, and the battle promised to be fiercer than the first two.

They opened with a clash of ranged attacks. Ampharos's Signal Beam and Tyranitar's Dark Pulse, two differently colored bursts of energy, met in the air and exploded violently.

Smoke spread over the middle of the field. Ampharos was preparing to fire through it when the ground began to tremble. Tyranitar burst from the smoke and charged. The tremors came from that armored tank of a Pokemon pounding toward it.

Startled, Ampharos fired a Thunder Shock. Electricity struck Tyranitar, but it roared and kept coming through the damage.

Ampharos was not incapable of close combat. With moves such as Fire Punch and Thunder Punch, and Thunder Wave to paralyze an enemy, it could stand up to most Pokemon. But something about Tyranitar's intimidating presence made it lose heart. It desperately wanted to stop Tyranitar at a distance.

Wattson sensed what his partner was feeling. The opponent was already coming close, though, and Ampharos knew how to fight there. It couldn't run from the exchange.

Pull yourself together! Thunder Punch!

Ampharos gritted its teeth and went forward. That was exactly what Ethan wanted.

As electricity flashed around Ampharos's fists, he smiled. Tyranitar, keep going. Ram straight into it!

Tyranitar set its armored shoulder and head forward and ran harder. Ampharos tried to sidestep the charge before striking with Thunder Punch, but Tyranitar was larger and could burst forward over a short distance. It hit before Ampharos could clear its path.

Bang!

Ampharos felt as though a truck had struck it and went flying. The impact looked tremendous, though it did less damage than its force suggested. Ethan was not finished. Before Ampharos could land, he sent Tyranitar after it.

Now, let's make a mess of things! Thrash!

Thrash was a familiar move: the user launched into a reckless flurry, striking without restraint and ending up confused afterward. Its power came with a cost, so it was best used when the target couldn't get away. Even if it did not finish the battle, it could cause serious damage.

Ampharos had just hit the ground and could not escape. It looked up to find Tyranitar towering above it. As Ampharos watched, Tyranitar's eyes turned bloodred. It raised both arms high and brought them down.

Chapter 628: That Old Man Retired?

Tyranitar brought its arms and legs down in a wild barrage. Dust filled the air as it hammered Ampharos into the ground.

One Thrash would not be enough to finish Ampharos. When the move ended, Tyranitar became confused. It did not stop attacking; it simply began striking at everything around it. That gave Ampharos the chance to escape.

Ampharos scrambled out of the crater and fled to a safe distance. It looked back at Tyranitar, which had finally gone still, and let out a shaken breath. Only then did it register how badly its whole body hurt, as though every bone had been broken.

Ampharos, don't just stand there! Counterattack! Wattson called.

His partner came back to its senses and gathered energy for a move. Ethan saw it preparing to attack, but all he could do was wait for Tyranitar's confusion to pass. The aftereffect was unavoidable; worrying would not make it end sooner.

He had to admire Wattson's ace. Ampharos had been rammed hard, then pounded into the ground, and it could still fight back. It was far tougher than an ordinary opponent.

A powerful Thunder Shock shot from Ampharos's tail and struck Tyranitar. Electricity crackled over its body. Tyranitar cried out in pain, but the jolt also cleared its head.

There was no need to close the distance again. Ampharos was wounded and had already spent much of its energy. At Ethan's command, Tyranitar attacked from afar with Dark Pulse.

Ampharos answered with the Bug-type move Signal Beam. This time Ethan deliberately changed Tyranitar's angle of fire. The two attacks skimmed past each other instead of colliding, and each struck the opposing Pokemon.

Both swayed. Ampharos's remaining strength gave out first, and it fell.

Watt raised his flag. Ampharos is unable to battle! The challenger, Ethan, wins the Mauville Gym match!

With Ethan's current team, this had been a difficult Gym challenge. That wasn't because Wattson's Pokemon were overwhelmingly strong. The difficulty lay chiefly in the way he had chosen and ordered them.

Other Gym Leaders often sent out their Pokemon from weaker to stronger, but Ethan had rarely seen such obvious gaps between their abilities. Wattson had made matters worse by giving no warning. Luckily, Ethan's partners had come through for him.

It was a small matter in the end. Wattson had tested challengers with the mechanical Raikou before letting them reach the battlefield. Anyone who passed that entrance test would be capable enough that he could adjust his team to match.

Wattson had lost, and losing with Ampharos clearly disappointed him. Still, his familiar hearty smile returned as he came over to Ethan.

Impressive! You may not know it, but Ampharos is one of my strongest Pokemon. Beating it proves you're ready to compete in the League tournament!

Wattson plainly did not know much about Ethan. If he had, he would not have felt quite so downcast about losing. Ethan had no reason to volunteer that information.

You're too kind, he said with a smile. My Pokemon still have a long way to go. They need more training.

Wattson was pleased by the lack of arrogance. Then keep working hard, young man. I have high hopes for you!

Watt came over with a badge. Wattson took it from him and passed it to Ethan.

Here. The Dynamo Badge, proof that you defeated me.

The badge was a fairly plain yellow ring shaped like an electromagnetic coil. Ethan thanked him and put it in his badge case.

With the Dynamo Badge, he had defeated three Hoenn Gyms and collected three badges. One more would bring him halfway to the eight he needed.

Wattson had sharp eyes. As Ethan opened the case, the old man spotted the Heat Badge and laughed.

So you beat that fellow Moore too?

Ethan thought he heard a note of satisfaction at someone else's misfortune. Wattson was bound to be disappointed.

No. Mr. Moore had retired by the time I reached Lavaridge Gym. His granddaughter Flannery was running it.

He retired? He really gave up that Gym?

Wattson looked stunned. It was evidently the first he'd heard of it. Moore was about his age. If Moore had retired, perhaps Wattson ought to give his own future some serious thought.

Watt smiled and tried to persuade him. Sir, you're getting older, and you've hurt your back. Why not retire like Mr. Moore?

Hmph! What nonsense are you talking? Wattson pursed his lips. I'm still going strong. Retirement can wait another ten or twenty years! Though Moore should have told me something this important. The next time I see that old fellow, I'll give him a piece of my mind!

The way he spoke made clear that he and Moore shared a long, close friendship. Their history was not Ethan's concern. He put away his badge case, recalled Tyranitar, and exchanged polite nods with Wattson. Then he and Misty left Mauville Gym.

They were traveling Trainers. With their business in Mauville finished, it was time to head for their next destination.

The city had left a strong impression on Misty. A little way beyond its limits, she turned for one last long look at the city at the heart of Hoenn. It was her first visit, and perhaps her last.

Goodbye, Mauville City.

Chapter 629: Ash: Misty, What Are You Doing Here?

Ethan had two possible routes ahead of him. After passing through Rustboro City three times and losing so much time, the itinerary he had planned when he first arrived in Hoenn no longer made much sense.

He was now near the center of the region. Whichever direction he took to challenge another Gym, he would eventually have to double back toward the opposite side. That meant wasting time.

He thought it over and talked with Misty. In the end they decided to head south to Slateport City, then take a ship to the island in the southwest and challenge the Dewford Gym. After that they would face the Petalburg Gym and finish the western part of their Hoenn journey.

Misty had no objection. They left Mauville City and followed the main road south. The city's tall buildings gradually fell behind them, replaced by dense forest.

Slateport was a long way from Mauville, with a bridge across the sea along the route. Walking alone would take at least two days, more when meals, rest, and camping were counted. But they were traveling; there was no reason to complain about the distance. As long as they kept going, they would arrive.

They crossed the forest in half a day and reached the coast. Far across the water stretched a winding bridge whose end they could not see, as though it reached the horizon.

That's a long bridge... Misty stared into the distance. How far do we have to walk to reach the other side?

It was Ethan's first time there too, so he could not answer. Fortunately, a bicycle rental shop stood beneath the bridge. They could ride across much faster and with less effort.

There was no reason to pass up that convenience. They went in, paid a deposit, and rented two bicycles.

The owner had a clever business. Customers rented at one end of the bridge and returned the bicycles at the other, in either direction. He had almost cornered the trade. As long as the bridge stood, he could make a living from it.

Ethan mentioned that to Misty, who laughed softly. Are you jealous? When you get tired of traveling, you could open a shop like this. I'd definitely come work for you!

To take that as a simple joke would have missed her meaning. Beneath I'd come work for you, she was telling Ethan she wanted to stay with him whatever he did in the future.

Ethan seemed not to hear the hint. Spend my whole life beside one bridge? No thanks. I'd rather settle on a deserted island than waste my time here.

Once they rode onto the bridge, their pace improved. Damp, salty sea air brushed their faces. They cycled side by side and left many pedestrians behind.

Wide rest areas appeared every few kilometers, presumably for people crossing on foot. Because the bridge connected two cities, many Trainers used it each day. Some battled in those rest areas, making full use of the available space.

A few people tried to stop Ethan and Misty for a match. Ethan did not want to be stuck on the bridge after dark. He shook his head and rode past.

It proved the right choice. The sun was setting and the sky turning to dusk when they finally rolled off the bridge and onto land. Anyone who had lingered to battle behind them would have to hurry through the night against the hard sea wind or sleep on the cold bridge. The more fun the battles had been, the more miserable that journey would be.

...

Slateport City was a port where people, Pokemon, and nature met.

On Hoenn's southern coast, it had first grown around clean water, plentiful food, and a thriving market. It remained an excellent place to shop. Over time it had expanded into a major harbor, with ships coming and going every day.

After more than a day on the road, Ethan and Misty arrived on the morning of the third day. From a distance they could see an enormous lighthouse on the city's southern side. Not far away stood the famous Oceanic Museum, with a Pokemon Contest venue nearby.

They were about to head for the harbor when several familiar figures appeared on the opposite side of the street.

The boy in front wore a blue hoodie and a red cap. He had a cheerful, not especially thoughtful-looking face, and Pikachu sat on his shoulder. The clothes, backpack, stride, and Pikachu were all familiar. Who else could it be but Ash?

Three people walked with him. The tallest was Brock, the lecherous squint-eyed oddball Ethan knew so well. On the other side were a brother and sister: May and Max, whom Ethan had met at the Petalburg Gym.

They were here too? And, just as expected, the four had begun traveling together.

As Ethan and Misty recognized Ash, Ash spotted them. Ethan! Misty too?

His eyes lit up, and he ran over. Pikachu was just as delighted. As soon as Ash came close, it leaped from his shoulder into Misty's arms.

What a coincidence, Ethan said, looking Ash over. When did you get here?

A few days ago. I've already got two badges! Ash lifted his shirt at one side to show the Stone Badge and the Knuckle Badge. Then, before Ethan could reply, he turned to Misty with an indignant look.

Misty! You said you weren't going to keep traveling with me because you had to stay at the Cerulean Gym. So what are you doing here with Ethan?

Chapter 630: Misty Meets May

Misty lifted her chin at Ash's question. Is there a problem? I can go wherever I want. Do I have to report to you first?

She had been Ash's first traveling companion, and they had spent a long time together. With him, her sharper side came out in full force. Ash was never quick with words. Faced with that reply, he stammered and could find nothing to say.

Brock, May, and Max caught up a few steps behind him. Brock's reunion with Misty was every bit as dramatic. After the Silver Conference, the three of them had returned to Kanto and firmly parted ways. Now they had somehow run into one another again in Hoenn.

Brock! Didn't you say you were going home to look after your brothers and sisters?

Weren't you going back to help your sisters at the Gym?

They pointed at each other, shocked and incredulous. Neither had expected to see a recently departed companion here. May and Max looked from one to the other, unable to follow the argument.

So this is how you take care of your siblings? Misty asked, giving Brock a sideways look.

And I don't see your sisters anywhere, Brock said with a smile.

Caught between them, Ash wiped sweat from his forehead. If this was going to happen, we might as well have kept traveling together.

Hmph. Who wants to travel with you two? Misty lifted her head proudly. I'm traveling with Ethan now. Just the two of us!

May and Max didn't know Misty, but they could tell that beneath the bickering, the three old companions cared deeply about one another. Unable to join in, the siblings went over to Ethan.

Good to see you again, Mr. Ethan. May looked up at him with a wide smile. I didn't expect to meet you here. Where's Miss Erika?

She went back to Kanto. Ethan shook his head, then asked a question he already knew the answer to. How did you end up traveling with Ash and Brock?

It's a long story. May sighed. Not long after we last met, I went to Professor Birch's lab to get my first Pokemon. That's where I met Ash. Pikachu was sick at the time and accidentally wrecked my bicycle. I ended up traveling with them. Max insisted on coming along after we reached the Petalburg Gym, and we met Brock out in the wild.

At the word bicycle, Misty immediately turned toward her. Wait. Ash wrecked your bike too?

Too? May studied this pretty but rather fierce girl. What do you mean, too?

Misty shot Ash a look. Exactly what it sounds like. When I first met him, he took my bicycle to save Pikachu. It was destroyed, and he still hasn't paid me back. I only traveled with him afterward for Pikachu's sake.

What? May stared. He's done this before?

If Misty had traveled with Ash for so long and still never received a replacement, what hope was there for May's bicycle? Ash could only smile awkwardly at the direction the conversation had taken. Even Pikachu looked uncomfortable.

Misty had long since stopped caring about the bike. She held out her hand to May. Hi. I'm Misty.

May paused, then quickly shook it. Hi. I'm May.

So the two girls who accompanied Ash through different regions in the anime finally met. It was as though one generation of traveling companions had passed the torch to the next, while each continued on her own path.

Ash had endured enough embarrassment. Afraid the others would find another story to tell at his expense, he turned to Ethan. How many badges have you got now?

Ethan saw what Ash was doing and was glad to help. I only just finished the Mauville Gym. I have one more than you.

Just one more? Ash's spirits rose. Ethan had set off much earlier, yet he was only a badge ahead. Maybe Ash could catch up soon. He would have to work even harder.

That's perfect timing, Ash said with a grin. I've just finished the Dewford Gym, and I was on my way to challenge Mauville!

It is good timing, Ethan agreed. We're going in opposite directions. You're heading for Mauville City, and I'm going to Dewford Town. Meeting here wasn't easy.

Oh, come on, Misty said with a wave. Once or twice might be a coincidence. How many times have you two run into each other by now? I've stopped being surprised. We shouldn't stand in the street talking. Let's find somewhere to sit.

She had a point. Their chance meetings had grown familiar even to Ethan and Ash, and the group was blocking foot traffic. They chose a nearby cafe and went inside.

Over coffee and desserts in a corner booth, they caught one another up on their travels. May and Misty grew more comfortable together as they talked.

You're in for a rough time, Misty told May, laughing behind her hand with the authority of experience. You'll find out how painful it can be to travel with Ash. Worst of all, Team Rocket's trio shows up everywhere!

Brock nodded emphatically.

May thought back over everything that had happened since meeting Ash. So being attacked by strange people, getting lost, and going hungry weren't unusual? That happened all the time before?

Chapter 631: Becoming Close Friends

As they slowly finished their coffee and a few pieces of dessert, the initial excitement of their reunion settled. Conversation became easier, and they talked about why May had come to Slateport.

There was no Gym in the city, but Ash's group had not arrived without a purpose. May had begun her travels unsure of what she wanted. After some time on the road, she had found her direction and resolved to become a top Pokemon Coordinator.

Coordinators took a different path from conventional Trainers like Ethan. They caught and raised Pokemon for Pokemon Contests, traveling to events in different cities to earn Ribbons rather than focusing on ordinary battles.

They cared about their Pokemon's appearance and condition. They groomed them and gave them Berries, Pokeblocks, and Poffins to improve their condition. They trained moves too, paying attention to how beautiful and polished each performance was. It was a different road, but every bit as demanding.

There's a Pokemon Contest here? Misty's eyes lit up. She was still new to Hoenn and curious about these performances. She had regretted missing the last one; now, so soon afterward, another opportunity had appeared.

Yes, May said. It's tomorrow, and I've entered.

Misty grew even more excited. She turned to Ethan with shining eyes. Can we go watch?

Of course. Traveling meant seeing all sorts of people and events. They had arrived at the right time, so why miss this one? Ethan also wanted to see what a real Pokemon Contest was likeand how May, the future Princess of Hoenn, would perform.

He looked at May again. She was the girl who traveled with Ash in the third generation of the anime, and she was as pretty as Misty, though in a very different way. They had one thing in common: both were still flat-chested. At their current age, they were still growing up. They might be more mature in thought than boys their age, but neither looked like an adult yet.

May would earn the title Princess of Hoenn and a following after entering only a few Contests. Her choice of path was clearly right for her. She must have remarkable talent.

May noticed Ethan's gaze from across the table. He wasn't embarrassed to be caught looking. He met her eyes, gave her a friendly nod and smile, then turned away as though nothing had happened.

Though young, May could tell he had been studying her. She didn't read anything into it and went back to talking with Misty.

She felt an immediate connection with the other girl. Misty could be rather forceful, but their views were much alike. May had a feeling that the girl who called herself the world's most beautiful young woman might one day become a close friend.

There was a reason May wanted that friendship. She had only recently settled on her goal. She was eager to pursue it but not yet confident, and the thought of her first Pokemon Contest made her anxious.

Her traveling companions were all boys. Ash was oblivious, Brock lost his head whenever a beautiful older woman appeared, and Max, though her own brother, was a bookworm. None quite understood what troubled her. She had kept worries she couldn't sort out to herself. Now she had met an outgoing girl her own age and finally had someone to confide in.

Misty felt much the same. She had three older sisters, but their age difference and different dreams left them little to talk about. Most days they argued instead. She had kept her own private feelings to herself. Meeting Maythe girl who had inherited the hardships of traveling with Ashfelt like meeting an old friend.

They talked eagerly about their interests, hobbies, and shopping. By the time everyone left the cafe, May and Misty were walking arm in arm.

The boys, Ethan included, were too slow to understand how the friendship had formed. They could hardly believe two girls meeting for the first time had become so close, so quickly.

They needed somewhere to stay, so after leaving the cafe's street, the group headed for the Pokemon Center.

On the way, Ash excitedly told Ethan about the Pokemon he had caught. When Ethan mentioned that his Torchic had evolved into Combusken, Ash could hardly wait to battle him.

Ethan shook his head at the boy's eagerness. What's the rush? Even if we're going to battle, shouldn't we check in first?

Heh. Ash rubbed his nose, suddenly realizing how impatient he sounded. Right. We can do it after we get to the Pokemon Center. Go, go, go!

Saying that did little to calm his desire for a match. He hurried the group across much of the city until they finally reached the Pokemon Center.

But when they opened the door, Ash stopped short. The lobby was packed with people of every age, height, and appearance. All of them had a Pokemon at their side.

Why are there so many people? he murmured.

Isn't it obvious? Ethan walked past him toward the counter. They must be here for the Pokemon Contest. Come on, let's check in before every room is taken.

Chapter 632: Preparing for the Contest

At the front desk, Nurse Joy looked over the group before Ethan could explain what they needed. You arrived just in time, she said with a smile. We have exactly one men's dorm room and one women's room left. A little later, and you would have had to share with other Trainers.

That was welcome news. None of them wanted to stay with strangers. Sharing would make everything less convenient and less comfortable.

That's great, Ethan said. Could you assign us those rooms, please?

Certainly. Nurse Joy worked at her computer. Without looking up, she added, Judging by your group, you're here for the Pokemon Contest too, aren't you?

Ethan felt the atmosphere shift. Trainers who had been grooming or feeding their Pokemon in the lobby turned their eyes toward the group, trying not to seem obvious.

Misty and May, the only two girls among the travelers, noticed as well and instinctively moved closer together.

May glanced around. Why is everyone looking at us? she whispered.

Isn't it clear? Ethan replied without turning. There are already plenty of entrants, and the number of places is limited. They see our group and think the competition just got tougher.

May swallowed. Being watched by so many people made her more nervous than ever.

Fortunately, Brock had no sense of the mood. He leaned across the counter toward Nurse Joy, his face full of longing. You've misunderstood! Only May is entering the Contest. But if you wished it, beautiful Nurse Joy, I'd sign up just for you!

Ugh. Misty couldn't stand such a syrupy declaration. She grabbed one of Brock's ears to pull him awaythen realized Max had taken hold of the other.

Oh? Misty remembered May introducing her rather serious little brother at the cafe. Why was Max tugging Brock's ear too? The answer came to her at once: he was as tired of Brock's embarrassing declarations as she was. At least someone could take over this job when she wasn't around.

Misty and Max exchanged a grin. Together, they hauled Brock back into the group. His cry filled the lobby, distracting the other Trainers and allowing May to breathe easier.

...

After putting their luggage in the dorm rooms, Ash was eager to drag Ethan outside for a battle.

But seeing all those other entrants had weighed on May. She shook her head. You go ahead. I want to find somewhere to practice a little more.

She had prepared during their travels, yet with the Contest almost upon her, she felt less certain than ever.

I'll come with you, Misty said with a smile. I can already guess how their battle will end. Ash isn't going to beat Ethan. Besides, I'd like to see how someone trains for a Pokemon Contest.

May understood that Misty had offered to keep her company, and she was touched. Thank you.

So the group split up. Ethan, Ash, and Brock went to the battlefield behind the Pokemon Center for a battle between the boys. Misty and Max accompanied May to the beach to practice.

We'll see you later! Misty waved to Ethan. Come find us at the beach when you're done.

I will.

Ethan watched them go, then followed Ash and Brock through the Center's back door to the open-air battle grounds.

Except in very remote places, an outdoor battlefield was standard at a Pokemon Center. Even in an unfamiliar city, a Trainer could expect to find somewhere to battle there.

Because Slateport was a coastal city and many local Trainers had Water-type Pokemon, this Center also had a simple pool for water battles.

Only two children were using the grounds. They were battling on the ordinary field farthest away and seemed to be local kids playing rather than traveling Trainers.

That was one difference between Pokemon Contest entrants and League competitors. If this had been a League tournament, every battlefield would already have been occupied, with more battles breaking out in any open space nearby. Dozens of Pokemon would be taken to the treatment room each day before anyone called the place lively.

Contest entrants, by contrast, quietly attended to their own preparations. Those who wanted to practice, like May, often sought an unseen corner, unwilling to reveal what they had planned.

The children were too caught up in their battle to notice the newcomers. Ethan watched with interest. One boy commanded a Poochyena, the other a Zigzagoon. Perhaps they had little experience, or perhaps their Pokemon were too young, but their entire exchange consisted of Tackle, Growl, and Tail Whip. They shouted their commands with enormous enthusiasm all the same.

What a wonderful childhood.

Ethan shook his head and went to one side of the water field, facing Ash across it.

Huh? Ash looked surprised. We're having a water battle this time?

I caught a Water-type Pokemon recently, Ethan said. It hasn't had many chances to fight. This is a good opportunity to train it.

Sure, let's do a water battle. Ash took his place opposite Ethan, rubbed his nose, and grinned. Come on, Ethan! I'm ready!

Under Ash's watchful eyes, Ethan took a Poke Ball from his waist pouch and tossed it lightly. A yellowish-brown, remarkably ugly fish Pokemon appeared in the pool.

Chapter 633: Ash: Is That It?

There was no mistaking Ethan's Water-type Pokemon. It was the Feebas he had caught not long ago.

Ash had only recently arrived in Hoenn, and most of the region's Pokemon were still unfamiliar to him. What was this one?

Seeing the astonishingly ugly yellow-brown fish with its thick lips for the first time, he took out his Pokedex and scanned it. Once he had heard the description, he had a few basic facts about Feebas.

Feebas? Ash put his Pokedex away and nodded. It doesn't look very strong. I'm surprised you'd catch a Pokemon like that, Ethan. In that case, I'll use this one!

He pulled out a Poke Ball and threw it forward. A flash of blue light appeared, and a Corphish landed in the pool.

Ethan had never battled a Corphish, but he knew its evolved form, Crawdaunt, very well. He had lost count of how many Crawdaunt belonging to Team Aqua he had defeated.

As Crawdaunt's unevolved form, Corphish looked even more like a small crayfish. It had an orange shell, a white belly, three pointed projections on its head, and two large claws. Its little beadlike eyes gave it a rather vacant expression.

Corphish was said to be full of energy wherever it went. It could adapt to almost any environment, ate whatever it found, and was hardy enough to multiply even in filthy rivers. Like Feebas, it could live in a muddy, foul-smelling ditch. It seized prey with its sharp claws, and once those great pincers closed, it would never let go, no matter what happened.

The two Water-type Pokemon swam a few laps around the pool.

After warming up, Ethan's Feebas returned to its own half and prepared to battle. Ash's Corphish, however, swam right up to Ethan and sank to the bottom of the pool!

Hey! Corphish, what are you doing?

Embarrassed, Ash hurriedly called it back to his side. He scratched his cheek and forced a smile. Sorry. I only caught it recently, and this is its first battle like this. It doesn't understand all the rules yet.

It's doing fine. Ethan waved away the apology. You should have seen Feebas when I first let it out after catching it. It didn't even understand what I said. It just kept swimming wherever it pleased, as clueless as a Magikarp. It took a lot of work to train it to behave like this.

Sure enough, Ash looked much less embarrassed. He breathed out and asked, Ethan, how many Pokemon have you caught since coming to Hoenn?

Combusken, Feebas, and a Beldum. Three Hoenn Pokemon in all.

Only three?

Ash counted up his own team. Besides Pikachu, he had caught Taillow, Treecko, and Corphish since arriving in Hoenn. He had only earned two badges so far, but his three captures matched Ethan's.

Ethan had started several days earlier, yet the gap between them was nowhere near as large as Ash had imagined. Even in badges, he was only one behind Ethan!

Just then, Ethan drew out his words with a note of relief. Though besides those three, I did catch someone else. A memorable little troublemaker, and an unexpected bonus.

Memorable and troublesome? Ash stared at him. Did you catch another Legendary Pokemon?

Of course Ash envied Ethan for having so many Legendary Pokemon. He wasn't jealous, but when Ethan mentioned a memorable troublemaker, Ash immediately assumed another Legendary had joined his team.

Of course not. Ethan shook his head. Come on, Legendary Pokemon aren't that easy to find. You can't just catch one whenever you feel like it. All right, I know I've already caught several, but I haven't even encountered one since coming to Hoenn. Have another guess. You've run into this Pokemon many times on your travels. You'd definitely remember it!

He turned to Brock with a grin. You know it too. Why don't you guess?

Brock's eyes widened a little. Huh? I know it?

What could it be?

Ash and Brock frowned and thought hard. They had traveled through two regions and seen so much along the way that neither could bring to mind a Pokemon that fit Ethan's description.

At last Ash gave up. What is it? Come on, Ethan, tell us! Stop keeping us in suspense!

You still can't guess? Ethan laughed helplessly. I'll tell you after the battle. Let the mystery last a little longer.

Ash was itching to know, but Ethan clearly wasn't going to say more. He held back his curiosity and turned his attention to the pool.

Both Pokemon were ready. At Brock's signal as referee, the battle began!

Ash took even this informal match seriously. He brought the same concentration he showed at a League tournament and was fully engaged from the first exchange.

But as they traded attacks, something seemed wrong.

It wasn't that Feebas was too strong. Quite the opposite: after several rounds, Ash realized with surprise that it kept using only simple moves like Splash and Tackle. Compared with his Corphish, Feebas had almost no attacking options at all!

What? Ash deflated like a punctured balloon, the light vanishing from his eyes. I was really looking forward to this battle. Is that it?

Chapter 634: Fooled by the Same Trick Twice!

As expected, Feebas lost its battle against Corphish.

But Ash showed no joy at winning. If anything, he felt as though he'd been tricked.

Feebas had used a fish Pokemon's natural agility to dodge many attacks in the water, and it had landed several Tackles on Corphish. Even so, Corphish's two large claws quickly brought it down.

The match had gone so smoothly that Ash felt little satisfaction in his victory. A faint disappointment lingered. This was nothing like the battle he'd imagined!

Ethan, your Feebas is so weak! That wasn't hard at all. This isn't like you!

Ash grumbled, and he had a point. In his experience, every one of Ethan's Pokemon was immensely strong. Ash had to give everything he had to beat even one of them, and compared with those Pokemon, this Feebas was hardly worth mentioning.

Like me? Ethan, on the other hand, was perfectly at ease. He smiled. What's strange about it? Every Pokemon starts out weak and grows stronger. Feebas might not look like much now, but perhaps the next time you meet, it'll surprise you.

Ash thought about it and had to agree. Every Pokemon went through a stage like this. He stopped dwelling on the match, and his mood brightened.

Besides, whatever else had happened, he'd defeated one of Ethan's Pokemon. Most people couldn't say that!

And yet...

No matter how he tried to console himself, he couldn't quite shake his disappointment.

Ethan saw his expression and smiled. If that battle wasn't enough for you, how about I give you another?

Ash's eyes lit up. He nodded eagerly. Sure! Bring it on! This time I'm really going all out!

Seeing Ash fired up again, Ethan pointed toward the open ground beside them instead of taking out another Poke Ball. Let's change fields. My second Pokemon isn't a Water type, so we won't need the pool.

Ash had no objection. Ethan's serious preparations only made him look forward to their second battle more. On a different field, Ethan certainly wouldn't use Feebas again. Ash went to the ordinary battlefield and took his place opposite Ethan in the other Trainer's box.

Under Ash's expectant gaze, Ethan unhurriedly took a second Poke Ball from his waist pouch and threw it.

Blue light flashed. A Pokemon resembling a stone gauntlet appeared before Ethan, floating in midair.

What was that? Ash's eyes shone. He had never seen this Pokemon either, and he immediately pulled out his Pokedex.

It soon told him that the unusual creature was Beldum, a Steel- and Psychic-type Pokemon.

Steel and Psychic? Ash nodded. Psychic Pokemon were often powerful, and with Steel as well, Beldum could surely attack from a distance and defend itself up close. This one had to be something special! His anticipation for the second battle grew.

That pleasant feeling lasted only until he actually fought Beldum.

Ash sent out the Treecko he had caught recently. Its Grass type put it at a disadvantage against Beldum's Steel type, but Ash wasn't worried about that.

Once the battle began, though, something felt wrong again.

Beldum hovered in midair and looked impressive, yet all it seemed able to do was Tackle. It had even fewer options than Feebas! And the open field made its straight-line charges easy for Treecko to block or dodge. Beldum couldn't make any use of its type advantage.

Wait a minute...

Ash frowned. He was about to ask why Beldum seemed so weak too when Treecko knocked it down before he could speak!

Even Ash now understood what had happened.

Hey! He jumped up in anger, waving his arms like a child. You tricked me again! This wasn't what I expected!

Hahaha! Ethan couldn't help laughing at his reaction. How did I trick you? I only said we'd have another battle. I never said which Pokemon I'd use. You're the one who made an assumption. How is that my fault?

Ash opened his mouth to argue, then realized Ethan was right. He had never promised to use a particular Pokemon. Ash had simply assumed that, after Feebas, Ethan would send out someone stronger.

He'd been had again!

How annoying!

Those two...

Brock, who had seen exactly what was going on, shook his head helplessly. Unlike the oblivious Ash, he knew Ethan was using him as a practice partner, giving Feebas and Beldum battle experience. Only someone as straightforward as Ash would fall for the same trick twice.

Still, Ethan had a childish side too. He really ought to act a little more mature.

Just then, Beldum, lying on the field but still conscious, was enveloped in white light.

The glow drew all three of their eyes. Even the two little boys battling on the other field turned to look.

Brock recognized it at once: the light of evolution.

A battle gave the winner plenty of experience, but the loser gained some too. If a Pokemon was close enough to evolving, even a defeat could push it over the threshold.

Ethan's Beldum had evidently reached that point. He watched it evolve with a pleased smile.

Ash, in stark contrast, stood there with a long face, torn between anger and the miserable feeling that he'd been used.

That was all thanks to me!

Chapter 635: I'm Done Battling

Before long, the light surrounding Beldum faded completely. A Pokemon with a new form stood before Ethan, Ash, and Brock.

Its blue-green body resembled a flying saucer. It had two arms, a silver spike on its face and another on its back, and two pairs of silver blades extending diagonally backward from its sides. It looked a little like two Beldum joined together.

What Pokemon is that?

Ash had been upset about the battle and thought Ethan had fooled him, but the sight of Beldum evolving swept those feelings away. He picked up his Pokedex and aimed it at the new Pokemon. It responded almost at once.

Metang, the Iron Claw Pokemon. Steel and Psychic type. Metang has two brains connected by magnetic nerves, which produce powerful psychic energy, though its intelligence does not change. Its steel body can collide with a jet without injury. The claws on its hands can tear through thick iron plates as if they were silk. It floats using magnetism and can rotate its arms backward to move at high speed, flying through the air at one hundred kilometers per hour and passing swiftly over rugged mountains. When it spots prey, it grips it with sharp claws and uses powerful psychic energy to stop it moving, leaving no escape. Metang is especially fond of minerals that emit magnetic forces, and it will pursue a Nosepass at one hundred kilometers per hour.

The long description made Ash realize that Metang was nothing like the weak Beldum he had just faced.

He had challenged the Rustboro Gym himself and battled Roxanne's Nosepass, so he knew how formidable that Pokemon could be. Metang hunted even a troublesome Nosepass! It had to be strong.

His excitement returned. Ethan, how about another battle? Use this Pokemon!

But although Ash wanted to fight, Ethan had no intention of battling him again.

He had agreed to the earlier matches to help his two weak Pokemon, each with only a narrow range of attacks, evolve sooner. Now one of them had evolved. Why spend more time here?

Ignoring Ash's eagerness, Ethan laughed and turned him down. Let's leave it. It's getting late. We should go see how May and the others are doing with their practice.

He took out a Poke Ball and recalled Metang without hesitation. Ash's expression froze.

But...

Before Ash could say more, even Brock nodded enthusiastically.

I agree! Brock's eyes opened wide and shone with excitement. There are bound to be lots of beautiful women in swimsuits on the beach. Let's hurry over!

You two... Ash was about to ask if either of them was really a Trainer, but Ethan and Brock had already set off together, talking and laughing. Hey! Don't leave me here by myself!

He watched them walk away, sighed helplessly, and ran after them.

...

When Ethan and the others reached the shore, the long beach was crowded with visitors. Just as Brock had hoped, along with families and older vacationers, there were plenty of pretty young women in bikinis. Some lay sunbathing on the sand; others sat beneath parasols sipping cold drinks. It was quite a sight.

Brock clasped his hands, drooling as he gazed around in delight. Wow! No wonder this beach is such a famous summer destination. It really does have so many beautiful women!

Ethan and Ash ignored him and searched the beach. Even after looking for some time, they couldn't find May, Misty, or Max.

That's strange, Ash said. Where are they? Didn't they say they were coming to the beach to practice?

Ethan glanced at the crowd. There are too many people here. They probably went somewhere quieter. Let's check nearby.

Each taking one of Brock's arms, Ethan and Ash pulled him away from the beach and headed farther along the shore.

The visitors grew fewer and fewer. After five or six hundred meters, they reached a huge rock where hardly anyone else was around.

As they were about to search farther, they heard unusual sounds from the other side of the rock, as though someone was talking. They went around it and immediately spotted Misty and the others.

So this is where you were hiding! Ethan said. You were hard to find.

Misty smiled when she saw them. The main beach was too crowded. We had to come here to practice in private.

A dark gray butterfly Pokemon fluttered gently around May.

Ethan hadn't seen it in person before, but he knew it was May's Beautifly, the Pokemon she planned to enter in the Contest.

Beautifly had pale blue compound eyes and brilliantly patterned wings. It was about the same size as the Butterfree they had seen so often in Kanto and Johto, but Ethan thought it far more beautiful.

Beautifly gathered in flower fields to collect pollen and traveled on spring breezes in search of more. When flowers filled a garden, they flew from bloom to bloom. They loved sweet pollen so much that one would come to a flowering pot set by a window and use its long, needlelike mouth to draw pollen from it.

Despite its lovely appearance, Beautifly was aggressive and loved a fight. When angered, it attacked fiercely, piercing opponents with its slender proboscis and draining their bodily fluids. Greedy for nectar, it would even drive away Combee already feeding on flowers so it could have the sweet food to itself.

Ethan had learned while chatting at the cafe that May had caught this Beautifly only recently. In just a few days, it had evolved all the way from a Wurmple into its present form. Bug-type Pokemon really could grow at a remarkable speed.

But from the look of things, May and Beautifly still weren't working together very smoothly...

Chapter 636: Misty Loses Her Temper

How's the practice going? Ethan asked them directly.

Misty and May exchanged a glance. For an instant, they both looked utterly dispirited. Neither said a word, but Ethan could feel the sudden awkwardness in the air.

Max had no such reservations. He spread his hands and shook his head as he criticized his sister. Terribly. Her poses are a mess, she and Beautifly can't work together, and Beautifly's moves are a mess too!

Huh? Ash and Brock stared at May. If things were really as bad as Max said, how could she enter the Contest?

May blushed under their gaze. She wanted to defend herself, but ever since they had arrived at the beach, her practice really had been awful. Misty and Max weren't the only ones who thought so. Even May could barely stand to watch herself.

Beautifly hadn't fully mastered its moves yet. Earlier, just after they reached the beach, it had used Gust and sent a whole group of innocent visitors running. That was one reason they had retreated here.

Ash and Brock could tell from May's expression that Max hadn't been exaggerating. Neither wanted to say anything that might discourage her further. Ash clenched a fist and said, Don't give up! You've just got to keep practicing and do your best when the Contest starts!

I know that! May shot him a look. Her gloom vanished, replaced by determination. Do you think a little setback is enough to stop me? I was practicing the whole time before you arrived. I haven't been slacking off!

She picked up three flying discs and threw them into the air at once. Beautifly, use Gust!

The spinning discs soared toward Beautifly. It beat its broad wings, raising a powerful gust almost at once. The wind caught the discs, lifted them, and sent them back toward May along a new course.

May leaped lightly. Her arms swept through graceful arcs, and she caught the first two discs with ease. Her pose was lovely, and a calm, confident smile rested on her face.

Oh? Ethan and the others brightened. Their coordination looked far better than Max had claimed.

The thought had barely formed when the third disc whistled over May's head. She was still in the air with a disc in each hand and had no way to catch it.

Everyone turned to follow its path. A rise of rocky ground stood behind the beach, with a staircase linking it to the sand. On those steps was a boy about Ash's age, with slightly wavy green hair. He had one hand on the railing and was watching them.

No one had noticed him arrive. They had no idea how long he had been standing there, and May's missed disc was flying straight at him!

Look out! May cried, her face changing. She had thrown it. If it struck someone, she would feel awful.

Ethan raised a hand, ready to have Gengar intervene at any moment. Not everyone was as tough as Ash. A disc spinning that fast could leave a nasty bruise even if it missed anything vital.

The next instant, Ethan lowered his hand. Without so much as lifting his eyes, the green-haired boy reached out and caught the disc smoothly. The effortless catch astonished Ash and the others.

Relieved that he wasn't hurt, May ran a few steps toward him. I'm so sorry! Are you all right?

The boy straightened without looking at her. He flicked the disc and let it spin on his finger, then tossed it down at May's feet.

You don't plan to enter a Pokemon Contest with a simple trick like that, do you?

May looked down at the disc, then up at him. Her apologetic expression froze, and her brows drew together.

With his hands in his pockets, the boy came slowly down the steps and stopped in front of her. They stood face-to-face. His next words cut straight through her composure.

There's nothing beautiful about you.

May flared with anger. Before she could reply, he raised a hand to stop her and continued in a smug, superior tone. My name is Drew. I'm a Pokemon Coordinator too, but don't compare yourself to me. Neither you nor your Pokemon is the least bit beautiful. Give up that ridiculous dream of entering the Contest.

What did you say? May was furious now. Anyone could see that a boy who kept throwing the word beautiful at her had come looking for a fight.

Ethan was the oldest there. Seeing May bullied, he couldn't just stand back and watch. He started forward to support her, but Misty darted past him first.

Misty strode up to Drew. She was far less inclined than May to let an insult pass. So you're here to pick a fight? Fine, let's battle. We'll see whether your Pokemon is as impressive as your mouth!

She and May had known each other only a short time, but they were already close friends, almost like sisters. Misty wasn't about to let some obnoxious kid treat May this way.

Battle? Drew looked Misty up and down and shook his head with disdain. I see. You're one of those savage Pokemon battle Trainers. Always wanting to fight. How crude. And just like her, there's nothing beautiful about y

A dark blur flashed before his eyes. Drew blinked, then opened them wide as he realized it was Misty's fist!

He forgot all about acting cool and hurried to dodge. He had barely turned his head when pain struck his cheek. She had punched him.

Chapter 637: We're Friends

When Misty had first met Ash, she'd been fierce enough to slap him just for seeing Pikachu hurt. After Drew's insults, there was no chance she would let him off lightly.

Drew was stunned. He stepped back and stared at her, eyes wide. Only when his cheek began to swell and burn did he seem to realize he'd actually been hit.

You... you dared to hit me?

He held his face in disbelief. Perhaps his upbringing stopped him, or perhaps Misty's forceful manner intimidated him, but he didn't strike back. He only glared at her furiously.

Consider that a lesson! Misty lifted her chin and put a hand on her hip. Make fun of my friend again, and I'll give the other side of your face the same treatment!

She had held back. If she'd aimed for Drew's eye, she could easily have ruined the fairly handsome boy's looks. The punch had been so sudden that Ash, May, Brock, and Max were as astonished as Drew. None of them had expected Misty to throw a punch so quickly.

Only Ethan gave a helpless smile. He hurried forward and put himself between Misty and Drew.

He hadn't recognized the boy by appearance alone, but as soon as Drew introduced himself, Ethan remembered who he was and what lay ahead for him.

Drew would become May's greatest rival in Pokemon Contests. After this meeting, the two would cross paths many more times; eventually, Drew would even begin watching May's progress quietly from afar.

For all his scorn, Drew was rather like Gary had been early on: sharp-tongued, but decent beneath his cool exterior. Ethan had remained calm during the provocation because he knew what Drew was really like. Misty's punch, however, had probably turned the boy against them for good.

That wouldn't matter much to Ethan and his friends. They were traveling Trainers and would leave Hoenn after the Ever Grande Conference. For May, who lived here, making an unnecessary enemy of a wealthy and capable Coordinator was another matter.

But what was done was done. Ethan wouldn't waste time hesitating over it. He stepped up and took responsibility. That's what happens when you insult people. You need to learn some basic respect.

You! Drew's face went red. No one had ever spoken to him that way, let alone dared to do it. He glared at the group. Get out of here! You're not welcome!

Misty rolled her eyes. Why should we leave just because you say so? We were here first!

Drew pointed behind him. This is the private beach belonging to my family's resort hotel. It's not a place for you to do whatever you please!

They followed his finger and saw a four-story hotel nearby. The stretch of sand lay within its grounds. So that was why there were no other visitors: it was a private beach. They had wandered onto the property, which also explained why Drew had come over.

Ethan and the others exchanged glances. Misty turned to leave first, and the rest followed.

Only after they had gone a long way and returned to the crowded public beach, with Drew nowhere in sight, did May quicken her steps to catch up with Misty.

Misty, thank you for what you did back there!

It's nothing. Misty waved it off. We're friends. How could I stand there while he talked to you like that? I couldn't stand his arrogance either, as if everyone else were beneath him. And he had the nerve to say we weren't beautiful! Does he have any idea how insulting that is to a girl?

Misty... May was deeply moved. Even Ash and Max thought Misty looked incredibly cool just then.

They left the beach and found another secluded spot to help May practice again. With Ethan and the others joining in, they could try more kinds of training. Ash even volunteered to face May in a mock Contest battle.

That suited Ethan and Misty, who had never seen a Pokemon Contest in person. They could learn more about its rules before the real event.

They chose an open space outside the city. Ethan and Misty sat on a large rock and put a kettle of tea on to boil nearby. May and Ash took positions on opposite sides of the field, as they would for an ordinary Pokemon battle.

Brock stepped into the middle to referee. After looking from one Trainer to the other and seeing that both were ready, he called, The mock Pokemon Contest battle begins now!

Having run a Gym himself, Brock made a convincing referee. He looked every bit as capable as a professional.

As soon as Brock finished speaking, Ash threw a Poke Ball with an excited grin. Taillow, I choose you!

Ash's energy and enthusiasm were hard to match. He had already battled Ethan twice, yet he was still eager to face May. With that much love for Pokemon battles, he truly did seem like this world's destined protagonist.

May sent out the Beautifly she had been practicing with.

As they watched, Ethan explained to Misty that a Pokemon Contest had two stages: an appeal round and Contest battles.

In the appeal round, Coordinators displayed their Pokemon's moves beautifully to impress the judges and audience. Those with high scores advanced.

Compared with other regions, the Grand Festivals in Kanto and Hoenn had two appeal rounds. In the first, Coordinators showed their Pokemon using moves; in the second, they could use moves freely.

During the battle stage, Coordinators had to bring out the beauty of both themselves and their Pokemon in combat. The battles followed double battle rules, and a computer selected each Coordinator's opponent at random. A loser was eliminated; whoever won the final match took the championship.

The rules sounded complicated to Misty. What a lot to keep track of... She shook her head with a wry smile. Our Pokemon battles are simpler. Beat your opponent and you advance. There aren't so many extra rules.

Chapter 638: May: Excuse Me?

As soon as the battle began, May eagerly gave Beautifly its first command.

Beautifly, use Tackle!

Beautifly rode the wind, gliding toward Taillow before charging at it. Glittering scales shed from its beating wings caught the sunlight and traced a long, shimmering path behind it.

It was a distinctive trait of butterfly Pokemon. Nearly all of them left some of that sparkling powder in their wake when they flew hard, and it was lovely to see.

Taillow, dodge!

A simple charge was never going to be easy to land on another Pokemon in flight. At Ash's command, Taillow twisted nimbly away from the Tackle.

Then Ash ordered a Tackle of his own, countering with the same move. But just as Taillow had dodged, Beautifly could avoid a straightforward charge too. It tilted its body at the last moment, narrowly slipping past Taillow. May breathed a long sigh of relief.

She had only recently begun traveling with Pokemon. When one of her partners was attacked, she couldn't remain as calm as Ethan, or even Ash. Her emotions rose and fell with Beautifly's every move.

Yet under that pressure, May showed the instincts of a Gym Leader's daughter. Beautifly, use String Shot! she called at just the right moment.

Beautifly's long, needlelike mouth expelled a strand of silk about as thick as a little finger. The thread seemed to move of its own accord; in an instant, it had wrapped around Taillow's wings and bound them together.

The spectators brightened. Max blurted out, That was great timing, May!

Unable to spread its wings, Taillow couldn't fly. It was too small to tear the silk apart by sheer strength, but the thread holding it up kept it from falling to the ground.

That surprise would have troubled an ordinary Trainer. Unfortunately for May, her opponent was Ash, who had a knack for inventing a way out.

Taillow, find the gaps in the silk and break free! he shouted.

Taillow darted this way and that within the threads, never letting them tighten completely. Beautifly couldn't quite hold it fast. The struggle reached a stalemate, and May, still a novice, began to panic.

She wanted to change the situation, but no matter how urgently she thought, she lacked the experience to see what to do. Then she remembered some of the battles she had watched at her father's Gym. An idea struck.

Use Gust!

Beautifly beat its wings. A powerful gust laden with countless glittering scales swept toward Taillow. It snapped the silk connecting the two Pokemon and drove Taillow into the ground with a hard thud.

Well done! Ethan and Misty cheered together. From their excitement, it was obvious whose side they were on.

Ash had no attention to spare for their favoritism. His eyes were fixed on Taillow lying motionless. Taillow, get up!

Perhaps Ash's voice reached it, or perhaps the silk around it had cushioned the fall. Either way, Taillow opened its eyes.

That's it! Ash grinned. Break those threads!

May had been delighted, thinking the fall would finish Taillow. Seeing it struggle to its feet sent her into a panic again.

Use Silver Wind!

Ethan raised an eyebrow. That was a poor choice. Misty had mentioned when they found May that Beautifly had tried Silver Wind many times already, failing every time. Betting the battle on a move it had yet to perform successfully would give Ash an opening.

Just as Ethan expected, Silver Wind failed again. Beautifly beat its wings, but the wind it gathered quickly dispersed in midair.

Taillow seized the chance to tear free of the silk. It flew back into the sky and struck Beautifly with Wing Attack, knocking it down.

Beautifly hit the ground and fell completely unconscious. Ethan felt a pang of regret. May had been so close to earning that remarkably common achievement: beating Ash as a novice Trainer!

Ethan and Misty rose and went over to the others. They were about to speak when a voice sounded behind them.

That was a fine performance. With that kind of skill, you should have no trouble entering a Pokemon Contest!

It was a man's voice, and it came from nearby. They turned to see a man around thirty, wearing a white headband and traditional clothes, walking toward them while applauding.

Oh, no... May smiled bashfully at the praise. I still have a long way to go. You're too ki

Before she could finish, the man strode straight past her and stopped in front of Ash.

May stared.

The man patted Ash's shoulder and smiled. Your Taillow did wonderfully. You're entering this Pokemon Contest too, aren't you?

What? May was dumbfounded. He had been praising Ash, not her!

Ash looked surprised as well. He scratched his head awkwardly. Um... you've got the wrong person. I'm not entering. The girl standing in front of me is.

The man finally realized his mistake and turned to May.

She nodded uncomfortably. Y-yes. I'm the one entering.

I see! Sorry, I got that wrong. He laughed without looking embarrassed. Your Beautifly performed well too. But I can tell that neither of you has entered a competition like this before, have you? You both seem very nervous!

Chapter 639: Kind Mr. Big

From the man's tone, it was clear he wasn't just a casual passerby. He knew something about Pokemon Contests, or perhaps even worked in that world.

Before Ethan and the others could ask, he introduced himself. Oh, I forgot to tell you my name. I'm Mr. Big. I live nearby, and I used to be a Pokemon Coordinator.

A Coordinator? Mr. Big?

Ethan thought carefully, but neither the man's face nor his name was familiar. Even if he had been a Coordinator, he couldn't have been a particularly famous one.

Beside him, May, Misty, and Ash introduced themselves in turn. When it came to Ethan, he gave Mr. Big a nod of greeting.

I heard your battle and came over to have a look, Mr. Big said with a smile. I didn't expect such a good match. That Taillow in particular used its moves with real flair!

Ethan and the others weren't sure exactly what he meant by flair, but they could tell it was praise.

Mr. Big and Drew were both Coordinators, yet their personalities could hardly have been more different. One was warm and friendly; the other was aloof and sharp-tongued. Drew had youth and looks on his side, but the group found Mr. Big much easier to like.

Learning that he had competed in Contests, May couldn't help asking, Um... how many Ribbons did you win?

It wasn't a very polite question for someone she'd just met. Such a personal subject could easily touch a sore spot and offend him.

Fortunately, Mr. Big didn't mind. With a hint of pride, he answered, Three Contest Ribbons altogether!

Three! To most people, and especially to May as a newcomer, that was an impressive record. A Contest Ribbon wasn't like a Gym Badge, which a Trainer could earn by challenging and defeating a Gym Leader. A Coordinator had to compete against other entrants and win through judging. The competition was fierce. Three Ribbons meant this man really knew what he was doing.

May's eyes shone. Mr. Big, can you tell me the secret to competing?

Her excitement was understandable. Ethan and Ash were Pokemon Trainers surrounded by other Trainers who were both friends and rivals. When one of them had a problem, a few words from someone else might point the way forward.

May had no other Coordinators beside her. She had been figuring everything out by herself, and there were things even an experienced Coordinator might consider common knowledge that she still didn't know. Of course she was thrilled to meet someone who had won three Ribbons.

Mr. Big looked from May to her Beautifly and rubbed his chin. The most important thing for a Coordinator is to learn to stay calm. I watched your battle. You were flustered and kept scrambling to respond. That's a serious mistake for a Coordinator. Your state of mind affects your Pokemon's confidence and performance. Even actions and moves they can usually manage are much more likely to fail.

It was heartfelt advice. Ethan could tell from those few words that Mr. Big had experience and genuinely wanted to help May.

Ethan had noticed the same problems, but he followed a different path from May. As an outsider to Contests, he had hesitated to speak too bluntly. He'd intended to say something after the battle, but having a senior Coordinator explain it to her was better.

May frowned and thought back over her performance. There had indeed been many moments she wished she'd handled differently.

She went on to ask Mr. Big about other things that had puzzled her. He answered each question patiently, and his explanations made things fall into place for her.

May straightened and bowed deeply. Thank you so much! I've been wondering about these things for ages, and now I finally understand!

As confidence gradually returned to her face, Ethan and the others exchanged smiles.

Pokemon Contests and ordinary battles both involved Pokemon, but they were different fields. Specialist knowledge was best taught by someone who knew the field well.

Perhaps May's willingness to learn moved Mr. Big. Wanting to help his young fellow Coordinator further, he reached inside his clothes and brought out a rectangular container that looked like a candy box. He handed it to her.

If you want to become an excellent Coordinator, you need to pay attention to more than training. Your Pokemon's food and nutrition matter too. That helps them look healthy and beautiful. These are Pokeblocks, made from a mixture of different Berries. They can improve a Pokemon's condition. You can give your Pokemon one from time to time.

I... I couldn't take these...

It's all right. I've made plenty, and I hardly need them anymore. Please, don't be shy.

May tried to refuse at first, but Mr. Big insisted. Since she truly needed something like this, she finally accepted it.

Everyone could see that May had met a kind man today. Max often bickered with his sister, but he was happy for her.

Then something Mr. Big had said struck him. Mr. Big, you said you used to be a Coordinator. Have you stopped?

Mr. Big smiled and nodded. I'm getting older. I can't dance across the stage the way I did when I was young. These days, I make fireworks.

Fireworks?

That's right, exactly the sort you're thinking of. My daily work is making fireworks in the shapes of Pokemon!

May hadn't expected that. A man with three Contest Ribbons had changed careers. But it did nothing to weaken her resolve. She bowed again and asked loudly, Mr. Big, would you help me practice now?

He stared at her in surprise. He hadn't expected the girl to ask him that.

Perhaps her earnest expression touched him. After thinking for a moment, he sighed. All right. I've finished my work for the day, and there's still time before tomorrow's Contest. I'll give you a little guidance...

Chapter 640: The Oceanic Museum

May took Beautifly and followed Mr. Big off to one side to continue practicing.

With a professional helping her, there wasn't much Ash, Misty, or even her younger brother Max could do. They all stepped back.

Seeing May concentrate on her training, Ethan turned to the others. She doesn't need us for the moment. Instead of standing around, why don't we explore somewhere else?

Everyone agreed. They told May they'd meet her at the Pokemon Center that evening, then headed back toward the city.

Without anyone noticing, the day had slipped into afternoon. Warm sunlight fell across the streets, making the air pleasant.

After wandering for some time in the sea breeze, Misty stopped at an intersection and looked both ways. Do you know anywhere good to go? she asked Ash and the others.

She and Ethan had only arrived in Slateport that day. She knew nothing about the city and had no idea where they should spend the time.

Max didn't hesitate. I want to go to the Oceanic Museum!

The Oceanic Museum? The others turned to him.

That's right! Max adjusted his glasses. It's famous. There are all kinds of displays about the ocean, and models of lots of unusual Pokemon. I've wanted to see it for ages, but we never had time. It's supposed to be open today, so this is our chance!

That was Max for you. Most boys his age would choose an amusement park or a playground. Few were as eager to learn as he was.

Ethan and the others had no objection. But just as they were about to set out for the museum, Brock stayed where he was. You go ahead. I need to buy ingredients and supplies at the market. Like May, I'll meet you at the Pokemon Center tonight.

Sometimes Ethan envied Ash. With Brock taking care of everything like a full-time caretaker, Ash hardly had to worry about daily necessities. He could focus entirely on his battles.

Ethan had enjoyed that sort of help only briefly, when Erika was still traveling with him.

Ah, another day without Erika. As always, he missed her...

...

Slateport's Oceanic Museum stood on open ground beside the sea, not far from the lighthouse.

As Ethan's group approached, they saw three tall glass-domed buildings joined together into one enormous museum.

Max walked ahead, so excited he was humming. But the moment he reached the entrance and read the notice there, his face fell.

How could this happen...?

He backed away, devastated. Ethan raised an eyebrow and stepped up to read the notice. The museum was normally open today, but it had been closed temporarily because its curator had something to attend to.

Looks as though we came for nothing.

The others were disappointed, but it wasn't a serious loss. They could treat the trip as a walk. Max, however, couldn't accept it. He looked around, ran to a museum window, jumped, and caught the sill with both hands.

Hey... Misty raised an eyebrow in a way that looked remarkably like Ethan. What are you doing? That's dangerous! Get down!

I don't care! Max gritted his teeth and tried to pull himself through the window. I'm going into that museum today! There's so much for me to learn in there! I've been looking forward to it forever!

He had completely lost his head over this.

Worried he might hurt himself, Ethan started toward him to lift him down. Just then, Max's arms gave out. His fingers slipped, and he fell from the windowsill.

Thump.

He landed on his backside. Fortunately, there was grass beneath him and he hadn't climbed very high, so the fall did him no harm.

Ash helped him to his feet. Come on, let's go. If they're closed today, we can come back tomorrow.

Perhaps their voices had been too loud. The folding window suddenly opened from the inside, and a neatly dressed man in his forties leaned out to look at them.

May I ask what you're doing?

None of them had expected anyone to be in the room. Max looked embarrassed, but answered honestly. We came to visit the museum, but the front door was locked. I thought I could get in this way!

If an adult had done what Max had just tried, it would have looked very much like trespassing. Coming from a child, the frank confession sounded different. The man merely smiled and nodded.

I see. He glanced at Ethan and the others. I'm Captain Stern, the curator of this museum. There is a reason we're closed today. Still, since you've come all this way, I wouldn't want you to leave disappointed. I'll make an exception and let you in.

He disappeared from the window. A little later, a side door opened, and he stood there beckoning to them.

Max was overjoyed. He ran over at once. Ethan and the others exchanged surprised looks. Their luck had turned, and the man offering to let them in was the museum's curator himself.

May and Max had both been fortunate today. Each had met someone willing to help.

They followed Max into the museum. Although they entered through a side door, it was near the main entrance, and a few steps brought them into the central hall.

The sight that greeted them stopped everyone in their tracks: a life-size Wailord model suspended from the ceiling.

It's huge...

Looking up from below, they saw its great blue body hanging over nearly the entire hall. It made them feel how small a human being was beside such a vast Pokemon.

Ash couldn't help asking, Captain Stern, that Wailord isn't real, is it?

Chapter 641: The Scorched Stone

Of course it isn't real, Captain Stern said with a smile. It's only a replica. It is somewhat larger than an ordinary Wailord, though. That's why it makes such an overwhelming impression.

They left the main hall and entered the next gallery. Unlike the entrance area, which served mainly as a place for visitors to gather and pass through, this was a proper exhibition space.

Display cases stood in rows on either side. Inside were models of dozens of Pokemon that lived in the sea.

They weren't limited to Hoenn species. The collection included sea Pokemon from Johto, Kanto, Sinnoh, and Unova as well. Every model was so lifelike that it might have been a real Pokemon standing still.

This is wonderful! Misty exclaimed. No one in the group loved Water-type Pokemon more than she did. Seeing so many of them, even as models, delighted her more than winning a battle.

But the fact that they were models made her curious. Captain Stern, why don't you keep real Pokemon here? Wouldn't that be better to look at?

This is a museum, not an aquarium, Stern said. I also study marine Pokemon. With models, I can examine their body structures more closely and do it safely.

For a researcher like Stern, living Pokemon were unpredictable and difficult to control. Even so, could studying models alone truly teach him much?

They passed through the gallery and went deeper into the museum. In Exhibition Hall No. 2, they found an orange submarine model.

Before anyone could ask about it, Stern took on the role of guide. This is my multipurpose submarine. I designed it myself and built it at my shipyard. With it, I can go down to the seafloor and observe wild Pokemon firsthand!

His tone held a touch of pride. He was clearly pleased with his design.

Max had been excited the entire way. After praising the submarine, he turned to the others. It's such a shame May and Brock didn't come! They're missing so much!

Misty gave him a look. May has something more important to do, and Brock specializes in Rock- and Ground-type Pokemon. He might not be interested in a marine museum. You shouldn't assume everyone sees things the way you do.

Max fell silent as soon as Misty spoke. Perhaps it was the punch she'd thrown at Drew, or perhaps it was her occasional fierce manner. Either way, he was a little afraid of this pretty older girl. He wouldn't argue with her as he did with his sister; he barely dared meet her eyes.

As they talked, they reached the room where Stern had first heard them outside the window. Only now did they see it was his office.

Stern went to his desk, picked up an elegant small leather case, and set it before them. This is the reason I closed the museum today. I needed to study it.

He opened the case. Everyone leaned in, only to find that it contained a single black oval stone.

It was no larger than a palm and looked thoroughly charred. Apart from that, there seemed to be nothing special about it.

What's that? Ash asked. Some kind of rare gem?

No. Stern shook his head. It's an unidentified stone discovered by chance on the seafloor. It may not look like much, but it isn't ordinary. Those scorched marks come from heat inside the stone. Even in the deepest water, it continues to give off heat.

Intrigued, Ethan and the others reached toward it. They felt a fierce warmth before their hands even came close. In the short time the case had been open, the room itself seemed to grow a few degrees hotter.

Ethan looked more closely at the case. It had a thick insulating lining. No wonder they hadn't felt anything while it was closed.

Stern turned on a nearby computer and showed them a scan of the stone. At its center, the image revealed an unidentified source steadily radiating heat.

That doesn't make scientific sense... Max pushed up his glasses and leaned toward the screen. Why would a stone give off heat? It should be inert...

I've considered many possibilities, Stern said. I still don't know how it formed, but I don't believe it formed naturally. I think a Pokemon's power created it.

A Pokemon made it? Ash's eyes widened. An ordinary Pokemon couldn't create something that defied common sense like this. Only a Legendary seemed capable of it.

But Ash didn't know much about Hoenn yet. He couldn't even identify all its ordinary Pokemon, let alone its Legendaries.

Fortunately, Stern didn't make them guess. Do you know Groudon?

Groudon? Ash was about to ask what that was, but Ethan looked perfectly calm. Ash caught himself and nodded. Of course. It's a Legendary Pokemon, right?

Before Stern could answer, Max eagerly displayed what he knew. Groudon is one of the ancient Pokemon! They say it's the embodiment of the land, the Pokemon that created land and expanded the continents!

You know a great deal, Stern said approvingly. He's right. And I believe Groudon's power may have formed this stone.

Ethan rubbed his chin. He hadn't expected an ordinary museum visit to lead back to Groudon.

And Groudon inevitably brought Team Magma to mind. Stern's discovery might not stay secret from them. Judging by their usual methods, they could come to steal it at any moment.

It seemed Ethan and his companions might soon cross paths with Team Magma again.

Chapter 642: Cacnea and Seviper

Captain Stern still had work to do, so Ethan and the others left his office rather than keep bothering him. They wandered through the museum on their own.

Despite the museum being closed, Stern seemed to be the only person on the premises. There were no other staff members in sight, not even a security guard making rounds. Yet he trusted them to explore without worrying that anything would go missing. He was a remarkably openhearted man.

Without a guide beside them, they could relax. They went wherever they liked and talked freely about the exhibits.

Beyond the displays they had already seen, the museum covered seawater quality, samples of sand and sediment from different depths, and electronic audio presentations about the ocean.

Max learned a great deal during their visit, and even Ethan and the others felt more knowledgeable by the time they finished exploring.

Before they realized it, dusk had settled outside the windows. How quickly the hours had passed.

Then a soft click sounded nearby. Everything went dark. The lights across the museum had gone out at once.

Huh? Ash looked around in confusion. Did the power go out?

Probably, Misty replied casually. She wasn't worried.

None of them panicked. Outages were unusual, but everyone had experienced one. Ash had run into several during his travels and thought little of it.

Ethan, however, suspected that someone had broken into the museum. The question was whether it was Team Magma or Team Rocket. Either was possible.

The last daylight coming through the windows kept the room from growing completely dark. Ethan beckoned to the others. Let's go back to Captain Stern's office. I think something's happened.

Something's happened? Misty asked. What makes you think that?

This is a museum in a thriving coastal city. Its power shouldn't fail easily, Ethan said. And even if it did, there should be a backup generator. The lights still haven't come on. If the generator isn't working either, something's wrong.

The others realized he was right. They hurried back along their route to Stern's office.
