At the doorway, they found the room in disarray. Someone had clearly searched it roughly. Stern and the case were both gone, and a large hole had been smashed through the window. Sea wind blew in, scattering papers from the desk across the floor.

What happened here? Ash said.

Ethan exchanged a glance with the others. Without hesitating, they jumped out through the broken window one after another.

Outside the museum, they spotted two groups facing off a short distance away.

One was the familiar Team Rocket trio. The other wore matching red uniforms: Team Magma.

What were both groups doing here, and how had they ended up confronting each other?

Before Ethan could get closer, he heard Jessie shout, You lot! Hand that treasure over to us!

That single line told Ethan what had happened. Team Rocket must have seen Team Magma enter the museum and leave with the case. Mistaking its contents for treasure, they had decided to rob the robbers.

Fortunately, their interference had stopped Team Magma from getting far.

But where was Stern? Ethan looked around and couldn't see him anywhere.

Apparently, Team Rocket had already delivered its introduction to the Magma members before Ethan arrived. That was a relief. He had heard their motto so often that his ears had grown tired of it.

As Ash started forward, Ethan caught his arm. Wait, he said quietly. If we rush them, they'll run. Let Team Rocket keep them occupied. You two circle around and block their escape.

At his direction, Ash and Misty slipped off in opposite directions, each taking a different path around the two groups. Max stayed behind Ethan as they approached slowly from the front.

The dusk gave them cover. Neither Team Rocket nor Team Magma noticed they were being surrounded; both groups were focused entirely on each other.

This was Ethan's first encounter with the trio since they had followed Ash into Hoenn. Their Pokemon lineup had changed in the new region. Besides Meowth and Wobbuffet, Jessie and James had two unfamiliar Pokemon standing guard before them: a Cacnea and a Seviper.

Cacnea, a Grass-type Pokemon, looked just as its name suggested: a walking ball cactus.

It had a round body, sturdy arms, three dark green diamond-shaped patterns on its chest, a yellow flower atop its head, and sharp spines all over. Its light green color gave it a healthy look.

Cacnea usually lived in dry places with little rain and favored harsh environments such as deserts. It stored water inside its body and could survive thirty days without a drink.

The yellow flower on its head bloomed only once a year. The drier and harsher its surroundings, the more beautiful and fragrant the bloom became.

Its spines were extremely sharp and could snag all sorts of things by accident. It lured prey with the flower's strong scent, then fired its spines to bring them down. It could also fight by swinging its thick, needle-covered arms.

Seviper was another matter. It resembled a black snake, with a golden lower jaw, gold armor on its head and back, six small gold markings on its belly, sharp red fangs, and a bladelike tail.

Seviper and Zangoose were said to be eternal enemies, their rivalry continuing through generations. The scars on Seviper's body marked their fierce battles. It was relentless and dangerous: poison seeped from the sharp blade of its tail. Lurking in grass, it could bite prey with its venomous fangs, then slash an opponent with its tail and spread more poison into the wound.

To be honest, Ethan thought it ugly. It didn't suit his tastes at all. Only someone like Jessie would take a liking to that sort of snake Pokemon.

Chapter 643: Battle for the Case

The Team Magma members all had the same Pokemon: Mightyena.

They might have been standard-issue partners, but once the fighting began, it was Team Rocket's trio who came off worse.

Their strength was as consistent as ever. The museum intruders weren't commanders, only a few elite grunts, yet Jessie and James somehow couldn't beat them. Even Wobbuffet, whom some called the Wobbuffet God, couldn't keep them from falling behind almost immediately.

At Jessie and James's commands, Seviper and Cacnea attacked with Poison Tail, Bite, Pin Missile, and Needle Arm. The Magma members' Mightyena were stronger, however. Using only Tackle and Double Team, they stopped the attacks and countered. In a single exchange, they knocked out both Seviper and Cacnea.

The two Pokemon flew backward into the Team Rocket trio, sending all of them tumbling into the sea.

In moments, the water swallowed them. They vanished from sight, leaving only their screams echoing over the waves.

As useless as ever. When it came to disappointing people, Team Rocket never disappointed!

At least, however unintentionally, the trio had bought Ethan and the others time to get close.

The Magma members disposed of the strangers who had appeared from nowhere and turned to leave. Then a boy and a girl suddenly emerged from opposite sides of their path.

They frowned. There was no need to ask why the two youngsters were there.

Stop! Ash shouted. Leave the case behind! And what have you done with Captain Stern?

Ash had encountered Team Magma before. Not long ago, he'd fought both them and Team Aqua, and he knew something of what they were after.

The male grunt leading the group glanced at Ash and Misty without answering. He tried to step around them, only to see another man approaching head-on with a bespectacled little boy.

Tch. The grunt scowled. You keep popping up one after another. What a nuisance.

Ethan was about to speak when footsteps sounded behind him. He turned. Captain Stern was running toward them, breathing hard.

The curator looked disheveled. His suit was wrinkled and his hair singed. He had clearly been through something unpleasant.

Wait! Stern called. These people are my opponents!

Ethan noticed the Poke Ball in Stern's hand. Perhaps he hadn't had his Pokemon with him when the thieves took the case, making it easy for them to overpower him. Now he had returned with a partner, ready to settle matters himself.

Could he really defeat these Team Magma members? Ethan wasn't sure, but he held back and gave Stern the chance. The victim had asked to handle his own fight; for the moment, the rest of them could watch.

Go, Sealeo!

Stern threw his Poke Ball. Blue light flashed, and a plump blue Pokemon resembling a sea lion appeared.

Sealeo was an Ice- and Water-type Pokemon with a cream-colored front and a blue back. It had two short upper fangs, a pair of front flippers, a short flipperlike tail, and thick white whiskers on either side of its mouth. Those whiskers made it look like a kindly old grandfather.

Sealeo lived in groups on drifting ice and always seemed to be spinning something on its nose. It could distinguish a prey Pokemon's scent while swimming, locate it, and catch it. Round objects delighted it: whether a Poke Ball or a Spheal, it could balance one on its nose and spin it at will.

As soon as Sealeo appeared, Stern ordered it to attack. Use Aurora Beam!

Sealeo opened its mouth and fired an energy-filled beam of ice. It struck a Mightyena precisely and drove it back. The blast's shockwave knocked the Magma grunts off balance, and the case containing the stone flew from their hands.

The case arced high through the air. Max spotted it, jumped without a thought for his own safety, caught it, and hugged it tightly against his chest.

Ethan marveled at Max's agility. He also understood why Stern had insisted on fighting for himself. Sealeo was genuinely strong. Stern had clearly spent time training it, and it was certainly more capable than Team Rocket's trio. His confidence was justified.

But the elite Magma grunts weren't helpless. The sudden attack had surprised them, not frightened them away. At their urging, their Mightyena bared their teeth and advanced little by little toward Stern.

Team Magma! Ash demanded. What do you want with that stone?

I'm not telling you anything! one grunt snapped, pointing at the case. Hand it over if you know what's good for you, before we have to take it!

Not a chance! Max hid the case behind his back and glared. You criminals! This is important research material. We would never give it to you!

The grunts hadn't explained themselves, but their purpose was obvious. They must have heard about the stone and wanted to search it for clues to Groudon.

Their efforts were bound to be fruitless. They had spent years searching across the land, never realizing that Groudon had been hidden beneath the sea all along.

Ethan stepped in front of Max. There was no point talking further. They had recovered the case. If they drove off or captured the Magma members and made them reluctant to return, the immediate problem would be solved.

He threw a Poke Ball, and Combusken and Metang appeared before him. Ash and Misty also released Pokemon on either side.

The air grew tense. Seeing that the group meant to protect the case, the Magma members exchanged glances. Then their Mightyena rushed forward together!

Chapter 644: Sometimes You Don't Have a Choice

On their own, Ethan's Combusken and Metang weren't especially powerful yet. They were about as strong as an ordinary Trainer's Pokemon, which put them at a disadvantage against Team Magma's elite grunts.

But Ethan wasn't fighting alone.

Ash sent out Pikachu and Corphish. Misty added Politoed and Starmie, and Captain Stern had his Sealeo. Together, they matched the Magma members in both numbers and strength.

No one could dismiss what they could do as a team.

At their Trainers' commands, the Pokemon attacked in succession. A burst of multicolored moves flew at the Mightyena from several directions at once.

The Mightyena couldn't block or dodge every attack. Even when they countered one incoming move with another, a different attack slipped through. After a few exchanges, they were close to defeat.

Just as Ethan's group thought they could finish the fight easily, rotor blades roared overhead. A helicopter appeared high above them.

The prominent emblem on its body marked it as Team Magma's.

Reinforcements? Stern frowned. After a moment's thought, he called to the others, They've brought help. We should leave for now!

He had recovered the case. If they could get away safely, the thieves could do nothing more to him. Once back in the city, he could call the police and leave the intruders to them.

Ash and Misty looked to Ethan. They understood Stern's concern, but did they really have to retreat?

If they had been on their own, Team Magma's reinforcements might have forced them to withdraw. Ethan was here, though. Ash and Misty knew better than anyone how strong he was and what powerful partners he still had in reserve.

Ethan looked up at the helicopter and marveled again at the wealth of these regional organizations. Team Rocket, Team Magma, and Team Aqua all seemed to have endless money, plenty of members, and every kind of advanced equipment. They were equipped like armies, perhaps better even than the International Police.

Unfortunately for Team Magma, that wouldn't change the outcome. It was time for Ethan to get serious.

His fingers passed over the Poke Balls in his waist pouch. He selected two and threw them onto the field.

Blue light flashed twice. Dragonite and Scizor appeared!

There was no need to bring out a heavier force than the situation required. These grunts didn't warrant Gardevoir or Gengar, much less Raikou or Suicune. Dragonite and Scizor were more than enough.

At a gesture from Ethan, Dragonite beat its wings and charged straight for the helicopter. Scizor joined the fierce attack on the Magma members on the ground.

The grunts, who had been barely holding on, rallied at the sight of their incoming support. Each sent out another Pokemon. But Scizor's arrival left them no better off. Its bladed arms struck again and again, and their Pokemon fell one after another.

Damn it! How is this happening?

The grunt leading the squad stared at Scizor, then at the Trainer behind it. How had an ordinary theft brought them up against someone like this? Their intelligence had missed a serious threat. A commander, or even a leader, should have been sent to deal with him!

He glanced skyward. The support helicopter they had pinned their hopes on was trailing smoke under Dragonite's assault and looked close to falling. Its crew fought back as best they could, but they couldn't hit the Dragonite circling around them.

The squad leader gritted his teeth. The mission couldn't end as planned. Fortunately, he still had a way out.

He exchanged looks with the other grunts. They all pulled out smoke bombs and threw them down. Thick, choking black smoke flooded the area.

They couldn't even think of a new way to escape. Ethan shook his head. Scizor, use Air Slash!

Scizor swept its bladed arms forward. Two nearly transparent, crescent-shaped blades of air cut through the smoke.

The blades parted it, revealing the grunts recalling their Pokemon and sneaking away through the opening.

They thought they could run? Ethan stepped forward, ready to order Scizor after them, but Stern suddenly held him back.

Let them go. Don't chase them.

Ethan gave him a puzzled look. Seeing the worry on Stern's face, he understood.

Unlike Ethan and his traveling companions, Stern had a museum here. If they angered Team Magma further, it would be Stern's property at risk of retaliation after the travelers left.

Ethan sighed. People's lives were tied together in ways that made every action affect something else. No one could simply do as they pleased. Everyone had worries and obligations of their own.

In the brief delay, the Magma grunts escaped. Ethan lost interest in bringing down the helicopter as well. He whistled for Dragonite to return.

Dragonite didn't understand, but it obeyed faithfully. It let the helicopter go and flew back to Ethan's side.

Its rotors thundered as the smoking aircraft departed. Quiet returned. Without the marks of battle beneath their feet, it might have seemed that nothing had happened at all.

Thank you so much, Stern said, breaking the silence. He thanked the group, then took the case from Max.

When he opened it, he frowned. Max cried out, How could this happen?

Ethan, Misty, and Ash came closer and looked inside. The stone was gone!

Max could hardly believe his eyes. He removed his glasses and wiped them again and again, but the case was still empty when he put them back on.

That's impossible! His face turned red. I guarded the case the whole time. I never let it go! How did the stone disappear?

They fooled us, Stern said with a sigh.

Isn't it clear? Ethan shook his head. Their act convinced us the stone was still in the case. They must have taken it out earlier.

He regretted letting them escape. If he'd insisted on stopping them, they might have recovered it.

Stern was pained by the loss, but he didn't despair. He drew a black fragment no larger than a fingernail from his pocket and gave Max a reassuring smile.

Luckily, I cut off a piece earlier. We haven't lost everything. This should be enough for me to continue my research.

Stern really did have a good attitude. If Ethan had been in his place, he would have gone after the thieves by now.

Still, perhaps this could work in his favor. With the stone, Team Magma might narrow down Groudon's location. Ethan could follow that trail and see the magnificent ancient Legendary Pokemon with his own eyes.

Chapter 645: What Have You Swallowed Now?

At ten that evening, Ethan, Ash, Brock, and Max sat on the lower bunks in the boys' dormitory on the Pokemon Center's third floor. Misty had sneaked in as well. Snacks lay in a heap before them, and they ate while they talked.

Max glanced at the wall clock. It's so late. Why hasn't May come back yet?

Should we go look for her? Ash suggested. The light in his eyes showed that sneaking out at night appealed to him.

I don't think we need to. Ethan glanced at the darkness beyond the window. May knows her own mind. If she thinks she's practiced enough, she'll come back on her own.

The others had traveled with May long enough to know he was right. She wasn't someone they needed to worry about constantly.

Then Ash remembered something. Oh, Ethan! What was that other Pokemon you said you caught? Come on, stop keeping us in suspense!

Brock remembered too and looked at Ethan curiously.

Ethan smiled. He had no reason to hide it any longer. He took out Jigglypuff's Poke Ball.

You can see for yourselves.

With Ash, Brock, Max, and Pikachu watching, Ethan opened the ball. Blue light faded, and Jigglypuff's round figure appeared before them.

J-Jigglypuff!?

Ash recognized it at a glance. This was the Jigglypuff they had crossed paths with so many times before! He sprang up, backed away several steps, and pointed at it, too frightened to get a word out.

Brock and Pikachu were hardly calmer. Both retreated, remembering the terror of Jigglypuff's song and its marker.

Only Max looked from one face to another in confusion. Why were they so afraid? Jigglypuff looked adorable.

Misty covered her mouth to hide a laugh. She remembered how she had reacted when she'd first seen it again; she hadn't done much better.

Calm down. Ethan pressed his hands downward. Look. It isn't holding its microphone.

Ash and Brock looked at Jigglypuff's hands and saw that the microphone was indeed gone. They let out a breath of relief. Without that essential prop, Jigglypuff couldn't deliver its irresistible lullaby!

Finally at ease, they sat down again and examined it with curiosity.

That's amazing, Ash murmured. I never thought you'd manage to catch it, Ethan.

Ethan nodded. I've rid the world of a menace. No one has to worry about suddenly being put to sleep by a song coming from nowhere anymore!

The group laughed and talked about Jigglypuff, recalling all the trouble it had caused them. Looking back, those painful memories were funny too.

Max pieced together the story from their conversation. He had never imagined this cute Jigglypuff was nicknamed the pink demon and had caused so much astonishment.

He kept watching it with interest. Almost as soon as it appeared, Jigglypuff went straight to a corner, opened Ethan's backpack, and began rummaging inside. It moved with such practiced ease that it clearly had done this before.

What is it looking for? Max asked.

Its microphone, of course, Ethan answered without turning around. Don't worry. I've hidden it. It won't find it.

Ash and Brock relaxed even more. They stopped watching Jigglypuff and went back to talking with Ethan and Misty.

Jigglypuff alone refused to give up. It turned the backpack over, determined to search every last corner. One by one, it tossed out the contents: medicine, unused Poke Balls, and spare clothes.

A pair of Ethan's boxer shorts landed beside Misty. She glanced at them and blushed. Not wanting Ash and Brock to see and embarrass Ethan, she quietly hid them behind her back.

When she was sure no one had noticed, she let out a breath. She considered stopping Jigglypuff from emptying the bag, but Ethan didn't seem concerned, so she said nothing.

Jigglypuff searched more than half the backpack without finding its microphone. In a sulk, it dropped down beside the bag.

Then it noticed a bare stone at the bottom of the pack. Was its microphone hidden underneath?

Hopeful, Jigglypuff picked up the stone. There was nothing below it. That made it even angrier. It hurled the stone hard at the dormitory wall.

Bad luck for Jigglypuff. The stone struck the wall with a bang, bounced back, and flew straight at its face.

It was too busy sulking to notice. Something flashed across its vision, and the hard, smooth stone shot directly into its mouth.

Gulp!

Before Jigglypuff could react, it swallowed the stone.

It gagged and coughed, clutching its throat as it rolled across the floor. The fright was bad enough, but the stone was so large that it seemed lodged in its throat. Jigglypuff couldn't breathe.

The commotion caught the others' attention. They had heard the stone strike the wall, and when they turned, they saw something rebound into Jigglypuff's mouth.

Hey, hey! Ethan hurried over, exasperated. What have you swallowed now?

He checked his backpack. Everything else was there. Only the Everstone he had picked up during his earlier travels was missing.

This was bad.

Ethan knelt beside Jigglypuff, patted its back, then held it upside down and shook it. No matter what he tried, the Everstone wouldn't come out!

Chapter 646: Poor Jigglypuff

Jigglypuff looked more uncomfortable by the second. We'd better take it downstairs to Nurse Joy, Brock said quickly.

Ethan nodded. This was beyond anything he could handle. He carried Jigglypuff down to the Pokemon Center's front desk, with the others hurrying beside him.

Misty rang the desk bell. A little later, Nurse Joy came out from the back, yawning.

Before Ethan could explain, she spotted Jigglypuff's condition. Her sleepiness vanished, and she rushed over. What happened to it?

Misty quickly told her the whole story. Joy nodded, called for an assistant Pokemon, and had Jigglypuff placed on a stretcher and taken into the treatment room.

The red light over its door came on. Only then did the group feel they could breathe. They sat on the benches nearby.

Ash looked at Ethan. Why did you have a stone in your backpack?

It wasn't an ordinary stone, Ethan said with a rueful smile. It was an Everstone.

An Everstone?

I know what that is! Max pushed up his glasses. Unlike Evolution stones, the books say a Pokemon holding an Everstone can't evolve. It stays in its present form!

Huh? Ash stared. So if Jigglypuff swallowed one, does that mean it can never evolve?

Would that be so terrible? Misty asked. Your Pikachu keeps refusing to evolve into Raichu. Besides, I think Jigglypuff is cuter than Wigglytuff.

While they waited for Jigglypuff to be treated, May returned.

She entered the Pokemon Center and saw them gathered around the benches by the desk. The mood seemed subdued. Puzzled, she came over. What are you all doing here so late? Haven't you gone to bed?

Only then did they notice her arrival. It was almost eleven at night.

It's a long story, Misty said, and gave her an outline of what had happened. Remembering the stone bouncing off the wall straight into Jigglypuff's mouth almost made her laugh.

What? May stared. Is Jigglypuff all right?

I think it will be, Ethan said. Then he asked, How did your practice go? You're back late.

May made an OK sign, brimming with confidence. No problem! Just watch me tomorrow!

The others exchanged glances. What had she practiced in those few hours to become so sure of herself?

They were about to ask when the red light went out. The treatment-room door opened, and Nurse Joy emerged. Everyone hurried to their feet.

Nurse Joy, how is Jigglypuff?

She looked apologetic. It isn't in immediate danger, but the Everstone is in its stomach. I've tried several ways to remove it without success.

They hadn't expected even Nurse Joy to run into a problem she couldn't solve. What can we do now?

There are two options. A specialist hospital could break up the stone inside its stomach and remove the pieces, but that requires surgery there. Or we can wait for Jigglypuff to bring it up or pass it naturally. With a stone that large, that could take a long time.

Everyone looked at Ethan, waiting to hear his choice. He didn't hesitate. Is there a hospital here that can do the procedure?

Joy shook her head. This city has hospitals for people. For that kind of Pokemon surgery, you'd need to go to a larger city.

Then we don't have much choice. Ethan sighed. As long as Jigglypuff isn't in immediate danger, we'll arrange treatment when we reach a larger city. Until then, we can only hope it gets the stone out on its own.

...

They rested at the Pokemon Center overnight. The next morning, Ethan, Ash, Brock, and Max finished breakfast in the dining room, but Misty and May still hadn't come downstairs.

Today was Contest day. Everyone knew girls sometimes took a while getting ready, whatever their age, but this was taking far too long.

Ethan called Misty. Only then did he learn that May had been unable to sleep for half the night. Misty had stayed up talking with her, and both had finally gone to bed late. They were still asleep. Without Ethan's call, they might have slept even longer.

He ended the call and checked the time: 9:07 a.m.

The Contest itself began at one in the afternoon, but entrants had to arrive at the Contest hall before ten to confirm their registration and draw a number. Anyone late would be barred from competing.

Ethan told the others. Their answer was a chorus of helpless sighs. After all May's hard work, missing the entry deadline would be unbearable.

Fortunately, only a few minutes passed before May and Misty came flying down the stairs.

Beside Ethan and the others, who were ready to go, the girls looked rushed. Their clothes were wrinkled from being put on in a hurry, and water still glistened on their faces from a quick wash. Even so, they were naturally beautiful.

We're going to be late! We're going to be late! May didn't spare the group a glance or stop for breakfast. She ran straight out of the Pokemon Center.

Misty hurried after her, and the sight made Ash and the others nervous enough to follow. In a moment Ethan was alone, watching their figures disappear. He shook his head.

He had already decided that if May came down too late, he would have Dragonite fly her ahead to the Contest hall so she could confirm her place. But they had rushed away before he could say a word.

Traveling with Ash had evidently rubbed off on the whole group. Now they all charged into things in the same frantic way...

Chapter 647: My Idol Is Your Fan?

May and the others hurried through the city, arriving breathless at the Pokemon Contest venue. From a distance, they saw Ethan leaning against the wall by the entrance. He had a cold drink in hand and was sipping it at his leisure.

Huh? May stopped short. Ethan? Weren't you behind us? How did you get here first?

Just then Dragonite strolled out from the other side of the wall, happily licking an enormous ice cream cone.

Ash jumped. You flew here on Dragonite? That's cheating!

How is it cheating? Ethan lifted his chin. It's making good use of a Pokemon's abilities. You could have thought of it yourselves. Anyway, the deadline's almost here. May, you'd better get inside.

She knew he was right. Without stopping to wipe the sweat from her forehead, she nodded and went straight into the hall.

Ash and the others filed in after her. Before they reached the doorway, Ethan handed each of them a cold drink. I bought these for you. Catch your breath before you drink, or the cold will be hard on your lungs.

Slateport's Contest venue stood on a square in the city center. Its hexagonal dome made it resemble an old circus tent, but it was a solid five-story building.

A crowd of spectators had already gathered outside. The show wouldn't start until one in the afternoon, but they had come early to enjoy the atmosphere.

Ethan was the last of the group to enter. From the doorway, he saw May at the counter, completing her check-in with a staff member.

A clock in the hall read 9:57. She had arrived only three minutes before the deadline. May really was lucky. This was the same girl who had encountered a Duskull in a forest in broad daylight!

May rejoined them and let out a long breath. Only then did she notice her stomach rumbling and remember how disheveled she must look. She gave them an embarrassed smile.

Sorry for all the trouble...

It's fine. Misty waved it off, then cast a pointed glance at Ash. We've dealt with this sort of thing plenty of times before. We're used to it!

Her meaning was obvious to everyone but Ash. He was too busy gulping down his drink to notice.

Where do we go now? he asked.

Isn't it obvious? Misty patted her empty stomach. We get something to eat!

They left the hall and walked, talking and laughing, to a nearby restaurant.

It had opened only recently, and there was just one other customer, a woman sitting in a corner. Yet the moment May saw her, she stopped.

Oh? May looked again to be sure, then hurried over. Excuse me... are you Dr. Abby?

The woman had long green hair arranged in twin ponytails over her shoulders. She looked about Ethan's age and was quite beautiful. In a white T-shirt and jeans, she seemed bright and a little playful.

She looked at May curiously and nodded. I am. And you are...?

It really is you! May exclaimed. I'm a fan! Oh, sorry, I forgot to introduce myself. My name's May, and I'm a Pokemon Coordinator too!

Before Abby could reply, Brock flashed past Ethan. In an instant, he was kneeling on one knee before her, offering a rose he'd somehow found.

Beautiful lady! Do you believe in love at first sight? The moment I saw you, Cupid's arrow struck my heart. I'm sure you felt it too!

Huh? Abby stared at the squint-eyed man. Before she could make sense of him, Misty and Max stepped up, each seized one of his ears, and dragged him away.

May breathed easier once he was out of the way. I'm sorry, Dr. Abby. My friend bothered you. Please don't mind him.

It's all right. Abby smiled gently. Are you here to compete or to watch?

To compete, May admitted with a shy smile. This is my first Pokemon Contest, though. To tell the truth, I'm nervous.

Misty, Ash, and the others looked puzzled, so May introduced them. This is Dr. Abby, the legendary Pokemon Coordinator! She won a Grand Festival, and Coordinator Monthly ran a feature on her. She's my idol and one of Hoenn's most popular Coordinators!

She turned to Abby. These are my friends. They've come to support me.

Hello, Dr. Abby. I'm Misty.

I'm Ash, and this is my partner Pikachu.

Pika!

I'm Max, May's little brother!

Greetings! I'm Brock, and I'm currently single!

They crowded around Abby to say hello. Only Ethan stayed quiet, casting May a curious look.

A few days ago, she had known almost nothing about Contests. Now she had an idol? Either she had been studying furiously, or Mr. Big had told her about Abby the previous evening. May was clearly eager to put everything she'd just learned to use.

It's nice to meet you all, Abby said warmly. She seemed as kind as she looked. Those achievements are in the past. I'm no longer a Coordinator, only an ordinary Pokemon doctor.

A Pokemon doctor? Misty asked. Do you work here?

No. My clinic is in Foothill Town, not far from Verdanturf Town. I only came to Slateport to watch the Contest.

I see.

A doctor... Misty suddenly remembered something. She turned to Ethan. Ethan! Abby is a Pokemon doctor. Bring out Jigglypuff. Maybe she can get that Everstone out!

Ethan realized she was right. He hurriedly took out Jigglypuff's Poke Ball and released it.

Jigglypuff looked much as it normally did, though a little less energetic.

Dr. Abby, could you take a look? Jigglypuff swallowed a stone by accident, and we haven't been able to get it out.

Abby immediately focused on the sick Pokemon. She asked for the details, examined Jigglypuff, and reached the same conclusion as Nurse Joy.

There really are only those two ways to remove the stone. I'm sorry, but my clinic and its equipment aren't here, so I can't operate now. If you like, you can come with me to Foothill Town after the Contest.

Ethan considered it. Going with Abby would mean retracing their steps, away from the route he had planned.

Let's wait for now. Jigglypuff isn't in immediate danger, and I still need to challenge the Dewford Gym. After that, I'll visit you in Foothill Town.

Challenge a Gym? Abby blinked. You're a Pokemon Trainer?

That's right.

She looked Ethan over. The more she studied him, the more familiar he seemed. Then she remembered Misty calling him by name, and her face lit up.

Oh! You're the Champion of both Kanto and Johto!

Her sudden cry startled the group. She had been so gentle since they met that nobody expected her to burst out like that, as excited as May had been a moment earlier.

Yes, that's me... Ethan was taken aback. You know who I am?

Of course! Abby said eagerly. I watched your matches on television not long ago. You were incredible! Champion of two regions! I'm a fan. Could I have your autograph?

Misty and the others exchanged glances. May looked as though her world had been turned upside down. She had just told her friends how accomplished Abby was, and now her idol was a fan of Ethan?

Then what did that make May? A fan of a fan?

Even Ethan hadn't expected it. They had won championships in entirely different kinds of competition, yet Abby admired him.

He might need her help later, so he agreed at once. Of course. Where would you like me to sign?

Abby opened her wallet, took out a photograph of herself, and offered it with both hands. Here, please!

Ethan studied the picture. It seemed to have been taken at an amusement park, with a tall Ferris wheel behind her. Abby smiled brightly at the camera.

He had a pen in his backpack. On the back of the photograph, he wrote: May your healing hands bring health and your kind heart bring comfort. Ethan Vale.

It was a simple blessing inspired by the congratulatory banners he'd often seen in hospitals back on Earth. The words were a little conventional, but they suited a Pokemon doctor.

Abby read it, beamed, and carefully returned the photograph to her wallet. Thank you for your kind words. I'll remember them and try to live up to them!

She had even become more respectful in the way she addressed him. Conventional or not, the message had pleased her and brought them closer.

At Abby's invitation, they joined her at her table.

This was a rare opportunity. At Misty's encouraging glance, May forgot about breakfast and asked the renowned former Coordinator several questions.

Like Mr. Big the day before, Abby held nothing back. She shared her experience and insights with May.

The conversation went on until noon. With the Contest drawing nearer, they finally had to stop.

Thank you so much! May stood and bowed deeply. I'm sorry I took up so much of your time.

Not at all. Abby smiled. It's a pleasure to see a young Coordinator working so hard. Now concentrate on the Contest ahead. I'll be cheering for you from the audience!

After saying goodbye to Abby, May realized how hungry she was. She ate a few hurried bites at the restaurant, then rushed back toward the venue.

She had spent the entire morning hurrying from one thing to another. In a way, that helped: she had barely had time to feel nervous or imagine everything that could go wrong.

That calm didn't last long. Once she was ready and seated in the contestants' waiting room, her heart began to pound.

The rules allowed her friends to accompany her, so Ethan and the others could enter the waiting area and watch the Contest from there.

On their way through the corridor, Ethan saw far more Coordinators than he had seen at the Pokemon Center the day before. Each was preparing in a separate room, and tension spread through the whole area.

May wasn't the only anxious one. Many newcomers, and even some who had competed once or twice before, looked unsettled.

Ethan was much more relaxed. It wasn't his competition. Although he sat in the same waiting area, he was only there to watch. For him, the whole experience was new and interesting.

At 12:53, even the corridor fell quiet. As the start drew close, every contestant seemed to feel the pressure. The noisy waiting area went still.

Then music sounded, followed by a woman's voice echoing throughout the venue.

The Slateport Pokemon Contest had begun!

Chapter 648: The Pokemon Contest Begins

The television in the contestants' waiting room was showing the Contest live.

Ethan and the others sat on the sofa. On the screen, a beautiful woman in an elegant red gown stood at the center of the arena with a microphone in hand. She had curly blonde hair and a beauty mark beneath one eye.

Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for waiting! Her sweet voice carried clearly through the room. The Slateport City Pokemon Contest is about to begin! First, please welcome today's three judges!

The camera turned toward the judging table. Two men and a woman sat there. Ethan recognized the woman immediately from her familiar face and uniform: Nurse Joy.

Her presence at a Contest didn't surprise him. After a glance, he turned his attention to the men beside her.

The one nearest Nurse Joy was remarkably short. Even seated, he didn't reach her shoulder. He looked at least fifty years old and kept his eyes narrowed. Despite his black suit, he had a quiet, unassuming air and hardly stood out at all.

The other man was about the same age, perhaps a little younger. He wore a burgundy suit and a bow tie. His hair was swept back, with a section in the middle dyed silver-gray. He looked quite fashionable.

As you can see, the host continued, our judges today are Mr. Sukizo, Mr. Contesta, and Nurse Joy! Let's give them a warm welcome!

Applause rolled through the arena.

Ethan looked over all three judges. Even without the introductions, he knew these were important people.

Leaving Nurse Joy aside, the short man, Mr. Sukizo, was the president of the Pokemon Fan Club. He regularly judged Pokemon Contests and appeared at venues all over the circuit.

Mr. Contesta was the director of the Pokemon Contest Committee, the person in charge of the entire competition.

Compared with them, Nurse Joy was the one people saw most often, and probably the one they found easiest to approach.

Once the introductions were over, the host explained the prize. The winning Pokemon and Coordinator will receive the Slateport Ribbon! Coordinators who earn five Ribbons from Contests in different locations qualify for the Grand Festival!

A picture of the Slateport Ribbon appeared on the big screen. It was a gleaming gold circle like a medal, with a green ribbon tied into a bow around it. The design seemed simple at first, yet it had a distinctive charm.

And now, the competition is about to begin! I'm your host, Vivian. Please welcome our first contestant!

With that, the Slateport Contest was officially underway. Under countless watching eyes, contestant number one made a dazzling entrance with their Pokemon.

Gulp!

In the waiting room, May swallowed nervously as the Contest began. Ethan and the others heard her and turned. She was trembling.

May, what's wrong? Misty asked with concern. Are you nervous?

May nodded. I don't know what's happening. I thought I'd prepared myself, but now that it's really starting, I can't make my legs stop shaking...

With her turn approaching, Misty and the others weren't sure how to encourage her. They could only keep cheering her on.

Fortunately, Ethan had enough experience with competitions to know how to steady her. Take your time. Breathe slowly. Didn't Mr. Big tell you last night? If a Coordinator gets too nervous, their Pokemon can pick up on it.

May drew a deep breath and let it out slowly. She repeated it several times, and her racing heart began to settle.

Thank you, everyone...

Contestants were already taking the stage on the television. A male Coordinator and his Wingull were showing off the beauty of their moves beneath the spotlights.

When their performance ended, the three judges gave them a score of 27.6.

It wasn't a poor score, but it wasn't especially high either. The performance had made no real mistakes, yet nothing had stood out. Unless the pair did something much more impressive in the second round, winning would be difficult.

Several more contestants performed after him. Their scores stayed between 25 and 28.

That didn't mean their performances were bad. Each Pokemon appeared to have received careful training. None had quite managed to make a lasting impression.

Then contestant number twenty-four was called, and that changed.

Next up, contestant number twenty-four!

As Vivian introduced him, a green-haired boy walked onto the stage. His face and manner were unmistakable: it was Drew, whom they had met the day before.

So he really did enter!

May's gaze sharpened. Misty even gritted her teeth at the sight of him.

His good looks and confident manner might have won over plenty of girls in the audience, but May and Misty had already put him firmly on their list of people they disliked.

Once Vivian had finished introducing him, Drew made a dramatic entrance beneath the spotlight, complete with a pose so exaggerated it looked like something out of a fantasy show.

Watching him put on airs, Ethan couldn't help thinking that if Drew ever became a battle Trainer and visited Alola, he would perform a Z-Move pose without the slightest embarrassment.

It was a natural gift!

After striking what he clearly thought was a dazzling pose, Drew began his performance.

His partner on stage was a Roselia, a small, humanoid Grass-type Pokemon with arms and legs. Three spikes rose from its head. Pale green skin and leafy growths draped its body like a dress, with a touch of yellow among the leaves on its chest. Its eyes were usually closed beneath long lashes. A blue rose adorned its left hand, and a red one its right. It looked like a little spirit of the forest.

Whatever offense Drew's sharp tongue had caused, Ethan had to admit the boy had chosen his partner well.

Compared with the Pokemon that had performed before it, Roselia's humanlike form could make its dancing much more graceful and pleasing to watch.

Chapter 649: Which Pokemon Is Most Beautiful?

On the television, Drew's Roselia had begun its performance.

It leaped into the air and used Petal Dance, sending petals swirling across the stage. As the petals floated overhead, Roselia spun and sprayed Stun Spore toward the ceiling, then followed it with Magical Leaf. The moves blended into one another. Powder and glowing leaves intertwined beneath the spotlights in a dazzling display.

The sequence was as beautiful as it was intricate. Vivian praised it, and the audience burst into applause. Drew had brought the arena to life.

Roselia wasn't finished. It used Petal Dance again, vanishing from sight amid the cloud of petals. Before the spectators could wonder where it had gone, Roselia reappeared and launched another Magical Leaf. The sharp-edged leaves shredded the airborne petals into countless tiny pieces. They spun down slowly like pink snow.

Amid that snowfall, Roselia and Drew bowed to the audience in perfect unison and left the stage.

Clap, clap, clap!

Thunderous applause filled the arena. Screens before the three judges displayed their scores: Mr. Contesta gave Drew 9.8, Mr. Sukizo gave him 9.9, and Nurse Joy gave him 9.7. Together, they made an impressive 29.4 points for the round. Drew had taken the lead over every contestant before him.

Vivian was surprised by the score, but she didn't call the next contestant yet. Instead, she went to the judging table to interview all three judges.

You each gave him a very high score. Could you tell us why?

It was an important part of the show. For viewers watching their first Pokemon Contest, the judges' explanations would make Drew's score easier to understand.

Nurse Joy looked at her screen and smiled. The Coordinator and his Pokemon worked together beautifully. Of all the performances so far, theirs was the most pleasing to watch. That's why I gave them 9.7.

When Vivian offered the microphone to Mr. Sukizo, the short Pokemon Fan Club president simply smiled. No special reason. I liked it.

Mr. Contesta, the director of the Pokemon Contest Committee, offered a more technical explanation. It was an excellent stage performance. Roselia is clearly well trained, and that kind of skill takes a great deal of practice. Combining some of those moves requires precise timing. A mistake could easily have spoiled the whole effect.

In the waiting room, Misty frowned after hearing the judges' comments.

He really does have some talent. No wonder he's so confident.

May said nothing. Drew's performance had put a great deal of pressure on her. Could she really stand up to him after a showing like that?

The Contest continued. Not long after Drew left the stage, the door to May's waiting room opened. Drew walked in with his hands in his pockets.

Oh, you made it after all. He looked over the group, then fixed his eyes on May with a sneer. You saw my performance, didn't you? That's real beauty. A beginner like you couldn't hope to manage it.

At his mention of beauty, Misty's temper flared. Did you come here to pick a fight? Do you want me to hit you again?

Drew remembered her punch all too well. He stayed by the doorway rather than coming any closer, though his tone remained defiant.

Pick a fight? I have better things to do. As a more experienced Coordinator, I only came to wish you luck. I hope you at least make it through the first round. It would be a shame if you were eliminated right away!

Everyone could tell he had come to boast and taunt her.

May privately admired his performance, but she wasn't going to admit that to his face. She stood up and answered firmly, I will make it through! Just watch me!

At that moment, a tremendous cheer rose from the television. They all turned toward the screen.

A man with long blond hair and a purple suit was performing with his Pokemon. He carried himself with the same sort of elegance as his partner: a Milotic.

Under the spotlights, Milotic seemed wrapped in a mysterious radiance. Its whole body shimmered.

Milotic doesn't even need to perform! Vivian cried excitedly. Its beauty alone has set the whole arena alight!

Milotic?

Ash stared openmouthed at the colorful Pokemon on the screen. Its long body reminded him a little of a Dragonair. It's so beautiful. What kind of Pokemon is that?

You don't know? Misty gave Drew a dismissive glance, unwilling to waste another word on him, then turned to Ash. Didn't you battle Ethan's Feebas before? Milotic is what Feebas evolves into!

What?!

Ash was stunned. That ugly, weak Feebas evolved into something this beautiful? Milotic wasn't humanoid, but even Ash could appreciate its looks.

Ethan was the only person in the room who felt little excitement at the sight of it. To him, Milotic was elegant, certainly, but he wasn't convinced it was exceptionally beautiful.

When he had caught Feebas, he had mainly wanted to make up for the shortage of Water-type Pokemon on his team.

If he had to name Pokemon he genuinely found beautiful, he would choose Gardevoir, Pheromosa, and Meloetta.

Even when it came to elegance, he thought Latias surpassed Milotic. She was more beautiful too.

That reminded him of Latias. After all, she had once been inside one of his Poke Balls. What were she and her brother Latios doing now? Had any humans disturbed them?

Then he thought of Bianca and her grandfather looking after them, and the barrier protecting their home. They were probably still living as carefree as ever in Altomare, the City of Water.

While Ethan's mind wandered, the performance on the screen came to an end. The audience cheered just as loudly as it had for Drew. Even the score was the same.

Only then did Ethan hear Vivian announce the man's name: Robert.

Chapter 650: Should I Lend You a Pokemon?

Robert's appearance put Drew under tremendous pressure too. He realized that Robert might be his greatest rival in this Contest.

No longer in the mood to mock May, Drew turned away with a grim face. Without another word, he left the waiting room and disappeared down the corridor.

Ethan and the others didn't notice him slip out. Their attention was still fixed on the television.

Several contestants performed after Robert, but perhaps his near-perfect showing had shaken them. A few made mistakes they normally wouldn't have made. Such basic slips were the last thing a Coordinator wanted, yet they kept happening. Robert had clearly put them under pressure.

May had no time to worry about the other contestants. The appeal round was nearing its end, and her own turn was coming.

Good luck! The announcement called her to the stage, and Ethan and the others offered their encouragement. Believe in yourself. You can do it!

Vivian lifted her microphone to introduce the final contestant. Only one Coordinator remains in our first round! Please welcome contestant number fifty, May of Petalburg City!

May took a deep breath. Under her friends' encouraging gazes, she straightened her small frame, nodded to them, and marched out of the waiting room with the determination of someone who had decided there was no turning back.

None of them had expected her to draw the last number. She would have to close the round.

After so many performances, the audience and judges might already be tired of watching. Unless she offered something special, the previous contestants could throw her off, and even a good appeal might fail to make an impression on weary viewers.

But she had drawn number fifty. Whatever she thought of the position, she had to go out and perform.

Misty clasped her hands, her eyes glued to the screen. She looked almost more nervous than May. Come on, May. You can do it!

May came through the contestants' entrance and walked to Vivian's side.

Vivian smiled at the crowd. This is May's first Pokemon Contest, and she looks a little nervous. But once the performance begins, I'm sure she'll leave that feeling behind. Now let's welcome her Pokemon and see what they've prepared for us!

Mr. Big and Dr. Abby had both offered May advice, and her friends had cheered her on. Once the appeal began, she quickly found her rhythm.

She threw a Poke Ball and released Beautifly. At the start of the performance, Beautifly merely fluttered its wings, scattering the fine scales unique to butterfly Pokemon. Beneath the spotlights, they drifted down like a tiny galaxy.

May tossed a flying disc. Beautifly used String Shot to flick it back into her hand like a whip. They repeated the exchange several times, showing the audience how well they worked together.

On May's final throw, Beautifly used Gust to send the disc back along a wide arc. May leaped high, spun neatly, and caught it. The audience applauded.

Misty and the others breathed easier. May had performed smoothly so far. Unlike Drew, who had let his Pokemon display its beauty alone, she interacted with Beautifly throughout the act. Their almost acrobatic routine gave the audience something different to enjoy.

It swept away the spectators' and judges' fatigue. They watched closely again.

May didn't disappoint them. For the finale, Beautifly used Silver Wind and began to spin. A small silver vortex formed around it, spreading glittering powder outward. The wind carried that powder across the stage until everything seemed bathed in silver light.

Under that glow, May struck a stylish pose and bowed to the audience. Beautifly landed behind her, and together they completed their curtain call.

Applause thundered through the arena.

Back in the waiting room, Ethan and the others were relieved that May had finished so well. Before they could celebrate, the camera turned toward the judging table, and their eyes followed it.

The audience could applaud all it liked, but these three people would decide whether May advanced.

Nurse Joy spoke first, smiling. That was a very good performance for a first Contest!

She tapped her screen. Her score appeared: 8.7!

Mr. Contesta, the director of the Pokemon Contest Committee, spoke next. I agree. Such a smooth and accomplished performance is a pleasant surprise. She hardly looked like a beginner. She has a promising future, and I'll be watching her progress!

His score appeared: 8.9!

That left Mr. Sukizo, the president of the Pokemon Fan Club. Vivian held the microphone out to him. As before, he offered just one short sentence.

I liked it.

His score was 9.1!

It was the highest of the three and the only score above nine. Crossing that mark felt like clearing a difficult threshold; a score over nine carried a different weight. May's appeal had truly won the club president's approval.

The computer added the judges' scores and displayed her total.

26.7!

May jumped for joy. Was it a high score? Not especially. It was well behind Drew's and Robert's scores in the twenty-nines, and it was comparable to the totals of several unremarkable contestants.

But this was May's first Pokemon Contest. As Mr. Contesta had said, she showed real promise. With more competitions and experience, she could become an excellent Coordinator.

Ethan felt proud of her. He clearly remembered May's first Slateport Contest in the anime: she had made a mistake during her appeal and received a slightly lower score.

His presence had affected her performance, even though he hadn't personally done much to train her. In the anime, she hadn't practiced with Mr. Big or met Dr. Abby and received her advice. A good beginning would help both her confidence and her growth.

All fifty contestants have now completed their first-round appeals, Vivian announced. Please wait a moment while we determine which Coordinators will advance to the second round!

May left the stage and returned to the waiting room. The moment she came through the door, Ethan and the others greeted her with enthusiastic applause.

Congratulations! You did really well!

Yeah, Sis! That was even better than you usually do! Max added.

May was happy, but her face still showed her worry. I wonder if my score will be enough to get me into the second round...

Don't worry. Ethan smiled. I worked it out. Your score is a little above the middle of the field. Unless something unexpected happens, you should advance.

She couldn't relax until she saw the official list. After a short, anxious wait, Vivian announced the results.

Thank you for waiting! Eight Coordinators have been selected for the second round. Here they are!

Eight portraits appeared on the big screen. Ethan and the others spotted May almost immediately, in the last position.

I made it!

Now that she knew she had advanced, May jumped up. She and Misty held hands, bouncing and laughing with excitement.

Ethan looked over the other finalists. There were both men and women, most of them fairly young.

As expected, Drew and Robert occupied the top two places. The remaining finalists had also delivered noteworthy appeals. The list was much as Ethan had predicted. The judges had seen their merit, and the audience could see it too.

Brock chose that moment to temper May's excitement. It's great that you made the second round, but the next part is a battle. May isn't used to battling yet. That could be a problem for her.

May fell quiet. He was right. Almost all her practice had gone into preparing an appeal strong enough to clear the first round. She had little experience with Contest battles.

It's okay, she said, seemingly untroubled. I'm already happy to have reached the second round. I never even dreamed of winning the whole Contest.

She knew her own abilities. Rather than aiming for the highest prize at once, she was ready to improve one step at a time.

Now we'll randomly assign the matchups for the second round! Vivian announced.

On the big screen, the eight portraits shuffled and flashed through different positions. A few seconds later, they settled into a tournament bracket.

The Contest battle round was split into two halves. Coordinators on opposite sides would not meet before the final.

May searched for her opponent. She found Drew's portrait almost at once, facing her own.

What?! she cried. I have to battle him?

Misty and the others exchanged startled looks. What were the chances?

That's bad luck, Ash sighed. Drew won't be easy to beat, May. You...

A sharp look from Misty cut him off. May was already frowning. Misty didn't know what to say, so she stood silently beside her.

Ethan shifted in his seat and smiled. If you don't want to lose, should I lend you one of my Pokemon? They're pretty strong. I guarantee one of them could teach that boy a lesson for you!

Ash's eyes lit up. In that case, May, you can borrow my Pikachu too!

Ethan! Misty said helplessly. Stop teasing her. You know cheating isn't allowed. And Ash, don't make it worse!

Ethan laughed. He hadn't meant the offer seriously. He only wanted to lighten May's mood.

After competing in so many tournaments, he knew the consequences of cheating. If anyone discovered it, May would lose her result and might even be banned from future Contests for life. Even if she had agreed to borrow one of his Pokemon, he wouldn't have done it.

More importantly, a Coordinator couldn't switch Pokemon between the appeal and battle rounds. They had to use the same partner throughout. Almost everyone knew that rule, so they understood Ethan was joking. Only Ash had taken him seriously.

Sure enough, May looked a little happier. I'll be all right with my own Pokemon. If I can't beat him this time, there'll be a next time and a time after that. I know I'll win someday!

The tense mood lifted.

The disappointed contestants left the venue while those who had advanced waited eagerly. After a brief interval, the Contest battles began.

One match in the upper half of the bracket went first. The second brought May and Drew onto the battlefield.

A Contest battle was quite different from an ordinary Pokemon battle. There was a five-minute time limit. Each Coordinator had to use dazzling moves to reduce the opponent's score as much as possible. The one who did the better job before time ran out would win.

May and Drew stood facing each other. Drew looked confident, even arrogant. May didn't expect to win, but she refused to show him any weakness.

After all, she believed Beautifly's Flying type gave it a twofold advantage over Roselia's Grass type. She had a chance.

With both Coordinators and their Pokemon ready, Vivian signaled the start of the battle. The clock began to count down, and Drew gave the first command without hesitation.

He knew the type matchup was against him, but he didn't seem worried. He ordered Roselia to use Magical Leaf, opening the attack from a distance.

Chapter 651: The Pokemon Contest Ends

Beautifly met Roselia's Magical Leaf with Gust. It beat its wings, and a powerful current of air scattered the oncoming leaves.

But Drew had clearly trained Roselia for just such a response. Rather than panic at the strength of the Gust, he gave a faint, confident smile.

Roselia's eyes snapped open. The Magical Leaves still flying toward Beautifly split into two streams, curved around the wind head-on, and attacked from either side!

May stared in shock. The spectators' eyes widened too. Even Ash, Brock, and Misty could scarcely believe it.

That wasn't something Roselia could learn simply by repeating the move over and over. How had it done it?

Ethan touched his chin. He was the only one among them who understood.

Magical Leaf dealt Grass-type damage, but it didn't behave like an ordinary Grass move. Its enchanted leaves could home in on a target instead of flying straight ahead. When they encountered an attack like a strong wind, they could drift with the air and then use that tracking ability to reach the opponent from another direction.

May, unfortunately, was still a beginner. She couldn't even recognize every move yet, let alone understand the principle behind this one. Its sudden change of course left her at a loss for a command.

Dodge it!

Watching May stand frozen on the battlefield, Ash and the others clenched their fists in the waiting room. They were so anxious they wanted to take over the battle themselves. While May hesitated, the leaves struck Beautifly.

Fortunately, Magical Leaf did little physical damage to Beautifly. It wasn't a disaster in an ordinary battle.

But a Contest battle wasn't only about knocking out the opponent.

Ethan looked at the big screen. The red bar showing May's points had fallen by about a fifth. Drew had taken the early lead.

He checked the clock too. A minute and a half had passed, leaving May only three and a half minutes. That was no help to her.

Drew's smile widened. He kept pressing the attack, ordering Roselia to use Stun Spore.

The powder spread across the battlefield and closed in on Beautifly, limiting where it could move.

May could have ordered another Gust to blow it away. In her panic, though, she chose a different response.

Beautifly fired String Shot to restrain Roselia. Roselia used Magical Leaf again, slicing through the silk. The leaves kept going and struck Beautifly.

May had now been caught by the same move twice. Her point bar dropped further, almost to half its original length.

Misty and the others felt their hearts sink. At least May hadn't given up. She ordered Beautifly to use its strongest move, Silver Wind.

But Drew's Roselia was plainly the stronger Pokemon. Its Petal Dance canceled the rush of Silver Wind, then sent petals sweeping straight toward Beautifly.

This time May reacted in time. Beautifly barely managed to avoid the attack.

Before she could breathe easier, Roselia took the opening stance for Solar Beam. May's face changed. She knew Beautifly couldn't withstand that attack in its present condition, so she hurriedly ordered String Shot to stop it.

She was too late.

The silk had only just left Beautifly's long mouth when Roselia unleashed Solar Beam. A dazzling pillar of light surged across the field and swallowed Beautifly. For an instant, it lit the entire arena.

Beautifly had no chance to react. Its body vanished completely inside the beam.

She's lost... Brock shook his head and sank onto the sofa in the waiting room.

He wasn't alone. Anyone watching could see that Beautifly's battle was over.

Sure enough, when the beam faded, Beautifly fell headfirst to the floor, battered and unable to rise.

Beautifly is unable to battle, Vivian announced regretfully. This match is over! Congratulations to Drew, who advances to the next round!

The arena erupted in applause for the winner.

Drew glanced at May. This time he said nothing. He and Roselia turned and walked away, leaving the crowd with a pair of cool, retreating silhouettes.

May recalled Beautifly, her expression troubled. She gave the battlefield one lingering look, then returned to the waiting room by the opposite entrance.

The mood there was subdued. When she came in, Misty and the others wanted to comfort her, but none of them knew quite what to say.

May...

Sis...

Seeing their worried faces, May forced a small smile. It's okay. You don't need to comfort me. I'm fine... Really, I'm all right...

They could all see how disappointed she was.

From the sofa, Ethan watched them stumble over their words and spoke coldly. She lost once. Why are you all moping around as though it's the end of the world?

What?

Ash and the others stared at him. Shouldn't he be trying to comfort May gently?

Ethan ignored their looks and turned to her. His voice was stern. Pull yourself together! Drew beat you decisively. His appeal and his battle were both better than yours. Everyone saw it.

May's eyes reddened, but Ethan continued without softening his words.

There's no shame in that. He started earlier than you, and his Pokemon is stronger. Those are facts, which means you have to work harder. You're upset because he mocked you before the Contest and then beat you in the battle, aren't you? This was your first Contest, and you already did well. If you can't bear a setback this small, you might as well give up becoming a Coordinator now!

It was a merciless speech, unlike the Ethan they were used to. Yet it had an immediate effect.

May's disappointment gave way to the words echoing through her head. She knew he was speaking for her sake, so she wasn't angry.

She wanted to tell him that she understood all of that. She wasn't as fragile as he thought; she just felt bad for the moment and would soon recover. But when she opened her mouth, all she managed was, I understand. The next time we meet, I'll do better than I did today!

Max stared at his sister, shocked that she had accepted the scolding so readily. Then he looked at Ethan.

His idol could actually keep May in line! When had that happened? It was incredible.

Vivian's startled cry came from the television, drawing their attention back to the Contest.

On the screen, another second-round battle was underway: Drew, who had just eliminated May, was facing Robert.

What surprised Ash and the others was Roselia's condition. It had seemed so powerful against May, but now Robert's Milotic had left it covered in injuries.

Three minutes had passed. Milotic had taken only one hit, losing about a fifth of its point bar. Drew had only a fifth of his own bar left.

Robert pressed his advantage, ordering Milotic to use Iron Tail. The blow sent Roselia flying again.

Milotic didn't have a favorable type matchup against Roselia. To dominate it this thoroughly, it had to be strong enough to overcome that disadvantage.

It was much like Drew's battle with May: the Coordinator with the type advantage was losing. Only now Drew was the one forced to feel May's frustration.

Like May, he kept searching for a way to turn the battle around. With the end of the match approaching, he ordered another Magical Leaf.

This time it brought him no luck. Milotic answered with Twister, sweeping every leaf aside at once.

May immediately understood the difference between herself and Robert. Magical Leaf could be stopped. Beautifly's Gust simply hadn't been powerful enough to do it.

Ring, ring, ring!

Before Drew could try anything else, the bell sounded to end the match. His face changed as Vivian announced, Time is up! Robert and his Milotic advance to the final!

Drew lost? Ash and the others exchanged incredulous looks.

They had expected either Drew or Robert to win the Contest, but they hadn't imagined such a one-sided battle. There was no time even to enjoy Drew's defeat.

Ash watched Robert on the screen. He's that strong?

Ethan nodded. Even outside a Pokemon Contest, Milotic's battle strength could carry Robert far in an ordinary competition.

On the field, Drew stood motionless, as though he still couldn't believe the result. Only minutes ago, he had gone to May's waiting room to mock her. Now he had been eliminated himself. The reversal was so swift it must have stung.

Ethan glanced at May and shrugged. See? There's always someone stronger. You thought Drew was your biggest opponent, but he couldn't beat Robert. Look at himhe's taking it even harder than you did. Maybe he'll lie in bed tonight and secretly cry into his pillow.

The others all pictured Drew doing just that. They shuddered. It was an image they would rather not see.

After Drew's defeat, the last match in the other half of the bracket soon produced its winner. Robert met a female Coordinator in the final and won again with overwhelming strength, taking the Contest title as expected.

Ethan and the others stayed in the waiting room to watch Robert receive his prize. Only when the entire Contest had ended did they leave the venue.

It was dusk outside. Spectators poured out through every exit. Ethan's group came out by the contestants' passage, and soon spotted Dr. Abby waiting in the distance.

She wore a sunhat and large sunglasses, so she had no need to worry about being recognized. When she saw May, she came straight over.

That was a wonderful performance, she told May gently. For a beginner to score 26.7 in her first Contest and reach the second round is an excellent result!

Thank you, Dr. Abby. May had had time to recover and could now face her loss calmly. Your advice helped me so much. I would have done much worse without it.

They talked for a little while. Then, as the light faded, Abby waved goodbye. She had come to Slateport only to watch the Contest. Now it was over, she needed to return to Foothill Town. She had waited outside solely to say farewell to them.

If you ever come to Foothill Town, you must visit me, she said.

Ash nodded vigorously. We will!

Until we meet again, then!

Have a safe trip, Dr. Abby!

They watched her leave, then Misty and the others headed back toward the Pokemon Center.

Ethan turned to follow. Out of the corner of his eye, he noticed the Team Rocket trio crouched before an elderly man beside one of the venue's walls. What were they doing?

He watched for a moment. Jessie and Meowth were crouching there half asleep. Only James was writing furiously in a notebook, recording everything the old man said as he talked without pause.

Well, that was rare. Team Rocket had followed them here but hadn't caused any trouble. The sun must have risen in the west. Something had kept the trio occupied.

Ethan shook his head and looked away. He wasn't going to interfere.

The Contest was over. Tomorrow morning, he would set out again and continue his own adventure.

Chapter 652: Meeting Bea Again

At eight the next morning, outside the Pokemon Center, Ethan and Misty stood opposite Ash and his friends. They had eaten breakfast and were saying goodbye.

Ethan, Ash, and Brock were used to parting ways. For Misty and May, this farewell was much harder. They held hands, embraced, and clung to each other as though they might never meet again.

At last Ash couldn't stand it. You'll see each other again before long. It might only be a few days. Do you have to make such a fuss?

What would you know? Misty wiped at the corner of one eye and glared at him. Someone as clueless about feelings as you could never understand a bond between women!

Women? Brock looked Misty and May up and down and shook his head. It's a little early for you two to call yourselves women. Try again in ten or fifteen years...

Misty threw her backpack at his face before he could finish. Brock fell over at once.

Max regarded him without sympathy, adjusted his glasses, and turned to May. Sis, if you two hate saying goodbye so much, why don't we all travel together?

Travel together? Misty and May both brightened for a moment. They looked at each other, then sighed in unison.

They would have loved to. But Ethan and Ash were friends and rivals. Meeting now and then was one thing; traveling as a single group was another. It simply wasn't going to happen.

And if one of the girls left her own group for the other? Misty couldn't leave Ethan, while May couldn't abandon her little brother. Each had her own reason to stay. Neither could switch traveling companions on a whim.

They would have to wait for another chance someday.

At least the discussion eased their sadness enough for them to talk normally. Ash breathed a sigh of relief and waved to Ethan. See you next time, Ethan!

Ethan nodded, smiling as he looked over Ash's group. See you next time.

They went their separate ways, one group heading west and the other east. Soon they were out of sight of one another.

As Ethan had planned, his next destination was Dewford Island, a small island off the Hoenn mainland.

It lay in Hoenn's southwest. A short mountain range ran through its center, with three or four peaks that drew stone collectors to climb there every day. The busy town of Dewford stood at the foot of the mountains.

At Slateport's harbor, Ethan and Misty soon found a small passenger boat bound for the island. They bought tickets, boarded, and spent an uneventful half day at sea. They reached Dewford Town at three in the afternoon.

There was still daylight, so Ethan checked his navigation device and headed straight for the Dewford Gym with Misty. She had no time to take in how the island differed from the mainland towns. Hurrying after him, she crossed the town center in short order.

The Gym stood on a seaside cliff outside town. They followed a path through palm trees and arrived at a striking gate.

A gold-painted sign gleamed above it. At the top was a relief of a Machamp and a Machoke running together. The two Pokemon were shoulder to shoulder, wearing broad smiles. To Ethan, they looked almost comically intimate.

Odd as the design was, anyone could tell at a glance that this was a Fighting-type Gym. That was what made the gate so distinctive. Its strangeness served a purpose.

The Dewford Gym lay beyond it: an ordinary square, two-story building apart from its roof. Three ridges rose along the top, like those on the heads of the Machop evolutionary line, making the whole roof resemble a giant Machamp's head placed over the building.

What an unusual sense of style... Misty stared up at it. The Gym Leader isn't another strange older man like Chuck in Johto, is he?

Ethan gave her a look. Careful, or Chuck will visit your dreams tonight and beat you up. Then he grinned. The Leader here is Brawly. He's a fashionable guy, a professional surfer as well as a Gym Leader. He favors direct physical attacks, like waves crashing in from the sea. That's why he's called a big wave in fighting.

A big wave in fighting? Misty blinked. That's a good nickname. I just can't picture someone like that with a team of heavily muscled Fighting-type Pokemon.

They reached the Gym doors as they talked. Ethan raised a hand to knock, then noticed the doors were slightly ajar. Through the gap came the sounds of a battle.

Another challenger today?

Curious, Ethan pushed the doors open without knocking and went in with Misty. The battle court lay directly inside. Two women were battling there.

On the left stood a woman of about twenty. She wore a red athletic swimsuit and had long, lake-blue hair tied in a large ponytail. She was attractive, with the firm, well-defined muscles of someone who exercised constantly.

Her position suggested that she belonged to the Gym, though Ethan couldn't tell how she was connected to Brawly. Perhaps she was acting as Leader while he was away.

Then Ethan looked at her opponent and stopped. It was Bea! He and Misty had met her briefly at the Pokemon Center in Verdanturf Town.

She still wore her racer-like training outfit and the black headband tied to resemble rabbit ears. Her face was as serious as ever, as though it had no other expression. What was she doing here?

Then again, Bea specialized in Fighting types and traveled around the world. Of course a Fighting-type Gym would draw her. Ethan simply hadn't expected to encounter her again so soon after Verdanturf.

The woman from the Gym was using a Meditite. It was a Fighting- and Psychic-type Pokemon with gray-blue skin, a head shaped as though wrapped in a large turban, creamy ring patterns on its arms, and large black-pupiled eyes. It looked a little like a monkey from India.

Meditite trained at yoga deep in the mountains and could float in the air. Daily yoga was essential to it. Meditation strengthened its mind, and it could spend hours at a time doing nothing else. It was said to eat only one Berry a day; enduring hunger was another way to discipline itself.

Bea's Pokemon was a Pangoro. Though it came from outside Hoenn, its appearance suited its name: it resembled a panda, only larger, fiercer, and stronger. A long bamboo shoot stuck out of its mouth like a cigarette. At first glance, it looked like a member of a street gang.

Pangoro could be hot-tempered and impulsive, but it was bold and deeply loyal to its companions. That drew many Trainers to it. Winning its respect, though, meant negotiating with fists, so few people managed to train one.

It was a wild Pokemon proud of its arm strength, the sort that preferred to solve problems with a punch. One blow could turn a large dump truck into scrap metal. Yet it would not tolerate anyone bullying the weak in front of it. Even when attacked, it charged forward without flinching, swinging arms strong enough to snap a utility pole. By watching the sway of the leaf in its mouth, it could also read an opponent's movements. It had a rough sense of justice as well as a fierce nature.

Those two Pokemon were the source of the sounds Ethan had heard outside. Neither Trainer noticed him and Misty enter. Both were completely absorbed in their battle.

On the court, Meditite and Pangoro fought at close range. They exchanged Fighting-type moves, advancing and countering without pause.

Their types didn't give either one a simple advantage. Meditite's Psychic-type attacks couldn't hurt the Dark-type Pangoro, but its Fighting-type moves were twice as effective. Pangoro's Dark-type attacks were strong against Meditite's Psychic type, while its Fighting-type moves would do only half damage.

Bea, however, made no attempt to win with Dark-type attacks. She kept Pangoro on Fighting moves alone. The woman facing her did the same with Meditite.

There was less dazzling move work than in a battle of ranged attacks, but every exchange had the force of fist meeting flesh. It was no less compelling to watch.

Thud! Thud! Thud-thud!

Each of Pangoro's punches seemed to push a wave of air ahead of it. The blows looked immensely heavy.

Meditite was smaller and lacked Pangoro's raw strength. It had to circle and maneuver to stay in the fight, and it began to lose ground in their direct exchanges.

Fists met fists, palms struck palms, elbows collided. Detect, Arm Thrust, Karate Chop, Circle Throw, Vital Throw, and High Jump Kick followed one another in rapid succession. In little more than ten seconds, the Pokemon traded over a dozen blows.

Pangoro was the stronger of the two. Meditite held its own early on, but as the battle continued, its strength failed. Pangoro knocked it to the floor.

The woman sighed at her Pokemon's defeat. All right, you win. You've earned the right to challenge Brawly. But as I said, he's out surfing. If you want to battle him, you'll have to come back tomorrow morning.

Bea frowned slightly but said nothing. She recalled Pangoro and headed for the door. Turning, she came face to face with Ethan and Misty.

Her steps paused. She clearly remembered seeing them somewhere, but after a polite nod, she walked out of the Dewford Gym without another word, leaving behind a strikingly cool silhouette.

She really was rather cool.

Before Ethan could look away, the woman from the Gym noticed him and Misty. Who are you? she asked in surprise.

Sorry, Ethan said with a smile. We came in without knocking. I'm Ethan Vale, a traveling Trainer. I came to

She waved a hand before he could finish. I know, I know. You're here to challenge the Gym, right?

Of course.

She shrugged. Then you probably heard what I told the last challenger. The Gym Leader is away right now. You'll have to wait until tomorrow. And before you can challenge him, you have to beat me.

That's fine, Ethan said. I haven't asked your name, though. You are...?

Oh, I forgot to introduce myself. The woman drew herself up proudly. I'm Shauna, Brawly's top student and his girlfriend. I also act as Gym Leader when he's away!

I see. My apologies. Can we start our match now?

He said the right words, but Shauna heard very little respect in his voice. How irritating! The woman with Pangoro had been the same.

Didn't these people know how famous Brawly was in Dewford? He was the most popular man on the island, a star surfer as well as a Gym Leader. Almost every girl in town wanted to be his girlfriend.

So why did challengers react with such indifference when she told them she was his top student and girlfriend?

Chapter 653: Before the Typhoon

Ethan had no idea what Shauna was thinking. If he had known, he would probably have shaken his head at how little of the world she had seen.

That was one benefit of traveling: it kept a person's view from being limited to a single place.
