To the people of Dewford Town, Shauna certainly had something to boast about. But however famous Brawly was on the island, his reputation barely reached beyond it. Across Hoenn, he was one Gym Leader among many. He couldn't compare with an Elite Four member or a Champion, and other Gym Leaders were just as admired in their own hometowns.

Ethan had won the Leagues of two regions, while Bea was a Gym Leader herself. Neither was lesser than Brawly. Why would his local fame impress them? Shauna was only claiming to be his student and girlfriend.

Ethan stepped to the place where Bea had stood, facing Shauna across the field.

After its battle with Pangoro, Shauna's Meditite clearly couldn't fight again. Perhaps she underestimated Ethan, or perhaps she had no stronger Pokemon available. Either way, she sent out a Machop.

It wasn't that Ethan looked down on Machop. Since his time in Kanto, he had fought so many Machop and their evolved forms that he knew their moves and abilities well. They no longer felt particularly difficult to face.

Shauna knew none of that. My rules are simple. Beat me in a one-on-one battle, and you'll be allowed to challenge Brawly in an official Gym match tomorrow.

She stressed Brawly's name, hoping Ethan would realize how hard it was to earn an audience with the Gym Leader. He remained impassive, apparently missing the point altogether.

What a blockhead.

Understood. Ethan took out a Poke Ball. Since he had come to a Fighting-type Gym, he felt like following its custom. As it happened, he had a Fighting-type Pokemon of his own.

Come out, Combusken!

A blue flash released Combusken opposite Machop. Neither Pokemon stood a meter tall, and they stared at one another as though sparks were passing between them.

Oh, Combusken? Shauna put her hands on her hips. What an ordinary Pokemon.

Ethan glanced at her Machop. She was calling his Pokemon ordinary? Combusken lived mainly in Hoenn, with only a few elsewhere. Machop could be found in practically every region.

He couldn't be bothered to argue, so he ignored the remark. Shauna's smile froze awkwardly. She let it pass and focused on the field.

As acting Gym Leader, she would referee her own battle as well as compete. Once Combusken was ready, she collected herself and called, Begin!

At once she sent Machop charging straight toward Combusken.

Ethan didn't use a Fire-type move to wear it down from a distance. Combusken, Bulk Up!

Bulk Up was a Fighting-type move that tightened the user's muscles, raising its Attack and Defense. Ethan's choice made his intentions clear: like Bea, he wanted to settle this at close range with Fighting-type moves.

Combusken raised its arms and struck a bodybuilder's pose. Its muscles seemed to tense all at once.

Shauna understood what he was doing and laughed. Come on, then! That's just what I want. Let's really go at it!

Really go at it? She probably meant nothing suggestive, but was that how she wanted to phrase it?

Even from their brief meeting, Ethan could tell Shauna was rather like Ash: open and impulsive, with just a little cunning. Every feeling showed on her face. Fighting someone like that was both exhausting and easy.

While Combusken used Bulk Up, Machop crossed half the field. It leaped and kicked toward Combusken's head.

Ethan had watched it closely. As Machop raised its leg, he read the attack and ordered Combusken to meet it with Double Kick.

Bang!

Their feet collided in midair, apparently evenly matched. Before Machop could fall, Combusken spun and raised its other leg, driving the second kick into Machop's lower stomach.

Machop had stopped the first kick, but the second caught it badly. Strengthened by Bulk Up, the blow sent it stumbling several steps back before it could regain its balance.

Be careful! Shauna called. Don't trade blows with it yet. Find a way to get close!

Machop charged again. Having learned from the first exchange, it kept its movements compact until it reached Combusken, then picked its moment to strike.

It feinted, lifted its right hand high, and brought it down sharply. Karate Chop looked like a simple strike, but it carried considerable force.

To Shauna's surprise, Ethan gave his command almost the instant Machop moved, as though he had known what was coming. Combusken raised both arms, blocked the chop, and kicked Machop in the lower stomach again.

What?!

Hit in the same place twice, Machop could no longer hide the pain. It clutched its stomach and staggered back several more steps.

Shauna stared at Ethan. How did you know what move I was going to use?

What's so strange about it? he asked. If you'd battled as many of the same Pokemon as I have, you'd have a fair idea of what they can do and how they fight. Your Machop isn't especially strong, and it hasn't shown any unusual moves. It's fairly easy to predict.

He was trying to explain that experience against Machop had helped him anticipate its attacks. Shauna, simple-minded in much the same way as Ash, missed the point. All she heard was that he'd called her Pokemon weak.

She would teach him a lesson! Shauna ordered Machop to attack without holding anything back.

She did, after all, have the nerve to stand in for a Gym Leader. When she pushed Machop harder, Combusken found it difficult to defend. The two Pokemon exchanged more than a dozen blows. Machop took hits, but it gritted its teeth and refused to retreat. Neglecting its own defense, it landed several punches and kicks on Combusken too.

A wild barrage could trouble even an experienced fighter. For the moment, Ethan couldn't shake Machop off and had to keep Combusken trading blows with it.

But Shauna's approach carried a cost. Combusken's Bulk Up had made it tougher and increased the force of its attacks. Meeting it head-on while ignoring defense was a poor choice, however fierce Machop looked.

At first Ethan wondered if Shauna had a plan or a last-minute move that would turn the match around. As the fight went on, he realized he had given her too much credit. Like Ash when Ethan had first met him, her strategy was simply to attack, attack, and keep attacking.

That style had its uses, but this was not the time for it.

Combusken used Double Kick again, catching Machop in the chest. Already battered, Machop could take no more. It toppled backward and hit the floor unconscious.

Yes! Misty sprang up and applauded before Shauna could announce the result. She made no effort to hide her delight.

She had been irritated with Shauna for a while. The woman's opinions of herself and Brawly were so self-important that Misty had wanted to argue with her. She had held back only because Ethan was in the middle of a battle. Now that he had won, she saw no point in a debate and merely raised her eyebrows at Shauna.

You win, Shauna said dejectedly, ignoring Misty's triumphant look. Come back tomorrow morning and you can challenge Brawly.

Before and after the battle, she seemed like two different people. Combusken's last kick had knocked down her pride along with Machop.

Pokemon battles came down to strength. A Trainer whose Pokemon was stronger had reason to feel confident. Shauna had now suffered two defeats in a row, decisively losing to Bea and Ethan. It had plainly affected her.

Ethan didn't know her well, and he had achieved what he came for. He and Misty exchanged a glance, said goodbye, and left the Gym.

They hadn't met Brawly, but Ethan had at least earned the right to challenge him. He wouldn't need another qualifying battle tomorrow.

The sky was growing darker. Outside the Gym grounds, once she was sure Shauna couldn't hear them, Misty complained, I've never seen a Gym where you have to qualify just to challenge the Leader! What a big deal they make of him. You'd think we were here to face an Elite Four member!

Ethan smiled, then shook his head. Who knows? It must be a local custom. Brawly's a surfer as well as a Gym Leader, and he probably can't spend all his time here. Maybe the preliminary battle is how they screen challengers.

They passed back through the distinctive gate and started down the gentle path from the cliff. Before they reached town, they saw a bank of heavy clouds stretching along the distant horizon and drifting toward the island.

Looks like a downpour is coming. Let's hurry to the Pokemon Center.

Unlike its counterpart in the games, Dewford Town in this world was a busy and important Hoenn town. It had no forest of skyscrapers, but many tall buildings rose over lively streets.

A sudden gust swept through. The endless bank of clouds seemed closer already.

They quickened their pace to avoid the rain and reached the Pokemon Center before nightfall. After checking in, they sat in the dining area to wait for dinner. Around them, other Trainers were beginning to talk about a typhoon and heavy rain.

Outside the window, rows of palm trees lining Dewford's streets swayed. Their broad leaves shook in the wind, silently bearing the force of the approaching weather.

Misty listened for a while, then lowered her voice. From what they're saying, that cloud bank we saw is part of a typhoon.

Ethan had heard them too. He nodded. That's not unusual for an island town. The weather can turn extreme without much warning.

Will it affect tomorrow's Gym battle?

He looked outside again. The Pokemon Center stood high enough for him to see flashes of lightning within the clouds. At their present distance and speed, the typhoon might not make landfall until well after midnight.

He sighed. I hope not, but I can't say. If it does, there's nothing we can do. Even after the Gym battle, we may have to wait for the storm to pass before leaving. No boat can sail in a typhoon and its heavy rain.

So we might be stuck here. Misty stuck out her tongue, but she didn't seem worried.

A seaside Pokemon Center would surely have been built to withstand storms. At worst, they would stay a few extra days. What was so bad about that?

Chapter 654: A Sudden Downpour

The wind blew almost all night.

Ethan slept badly. Again and again, the howling outside his window startled him awake.

Misty had fared no better. When they met in the dining room the next morning, each could see dark circles beneath the other's eyes.

Ahh... Misty yawned widely and rubbed her eyes. The wind was so loud last night. I kept worrying it would break my window!

Same here. Ethan shook his head. Even headphones didn't help.

There was good news, at least. Despite the night of high winds, the typhoon hadn't reached Dewford Island as expected. Endless dark clouds still hung in the distance, but its center appeared to have shifted from the island's eastern side toward the west. It remained a threat, though for the moment they seemed safe.

Let's eat quickly, Ethan said. While we can, we should get to the Dewford Gym. If the storm changes course again, we won't be able to go out at all.

Misty knew they had little time and didn't argue. They ate in a hurry, fed their Pokemon, and set out lightly, leaving their backpacks behind at the Pokemon Center.

The town looked nothing like it had the day before. It was only a little after seven, but the streets were empty. Not a single pedestrian was in sight.

A broadcast from somewhere nearby kept warning residents to shelter at home and stay off the streets in case the typhoon made landfall. Every door was shut. Through some windows, they could even see tape placed across the glass as a precaution.

Ethan and Misty exchanged a look. The urgency was clear. They picked up their pace and hurried toward the Gym.

Whoosh!

Wind struck them. Perhaps it was their imagination, but it seemed stronger than when they had left the Pokemon Center.

They looked up and saw they hadn't imagined it. The distant cloud bank had turned again and was moving toward Dewford Town.

Just what they had feared! They had only just left town. The remaining distance to the Gym was about the same as the distance back to the Pokemon Center.

Ethan couldn't bring himself to turn around now. They had already come this far; going back would make the trip a waste. Besides, what was a typhoon and heavy rain to a Trainer? If he couldn't endure a little hardship, he might as well give up and become a Coordinator! Every ordeal was another chance to grow stronger.

Resolved to challenge the Gym, he pressed on into the wind. He didn't even consider asking Dragonite to fly them there.

That made the journey harder for Misty. Her slim build left her at the mercy of the gusts, and several times she nearly fell. Ethan caught her each time. Before long, they were walking arm in arm, supporting one another.

Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh...

They left town and started up the slope toward the cliff where the Gym stood. The higher they climbed, the harder the wind seemed to blow.

Ethan... Misty opened her mouth and caught a lungful of air. She covered it with her hand before trying again. You have Suicune, don't you? Couldn't it stop this typhoon?

Probably. Ethan lowered his head against the wind. But don't count on it. The storm formed naturally. We shouldn't interfere with it too much, or we'd upset the ecological balance.

How would stopping it upset the ecological balance? Misty asked.

A typhoon's formation and path are complicated. There's more to them than we can see. It often brings heavy rain. That rain may cause some damage on the coast, but it also supplies water farther inland and nourishes the land. If I stopped this storm now, it could set off a chain of effects in those inland ecosystems.

He paused, then added, Besides, the damage here should be small. Coastal towns like Dewford have drainage systems. Rainwater that pours into town will soon flow back out to sea.

At ten years old, Misty had never thought about storms in those terms. Once she understood his reasoning, she stopped suggesting it. Ethan really did know a lot. Someone more simple-minded might have used a powerful Pokemon just to show off, without considering any of that.

Walking against the wind wasn't easy, but the Gym wasn't far. After several dozen minutes, they reached it.

Just beyond the unusual sign they had seen the day before, they spotted someone standing at the Gym doors. It was Bea!

Like them, she must have hoped to challenge Brawly before the typhoon arrived. They had all had the same idea. But why was she standing outside?

Bea heard their footsteps and turned. Ethan approached her, looked at the doors, and understood. They were shut tight, with a large padlock hanging from them. The Gym hadn't opened. Was no one inside?

He checked his phone. It was already 8:47. By normal business hours, the Gym should have been open.

Oh, come on... Misty sighed. I wanted to get inside and out of this wind. If it keeps blowing like this, my skin will crack!

Ethan signaled for her to be patient, then asked Bea, How long have you been here?

Bea looked startled that he had spoken to her. They had met before, though. After a moment's hesitation, she answered, Half an hour.

Half an hour? Misty stared. You've been standing here at the door the whole time?

Bea nodded faintly.

My goodness, you're really stub I mean, you're very patient. Misty caught herself just in time. Calling Bea stubborn would have been rude.

Bea didn't seem to mind. She said nothing more and appeared willing to keep waiting.

Ethan shook his head, then walked around the Gym a few times. He remembered its general layout from yesterday and wanted to see if there was a back entrance or contact information posted somewhere. He found neither.

When he returned to the front, Misty hesitated. Ethan... do you think the people who work here might not come in today?

Both Ethan and Bea looked at her.

She cleared her throat. When we left the Pokemon Center, the town was broadcasting a warning for everyone to stay home. Maybe Brawly listened and decided not to come to the Gym.

Ethan frowned. The possibility hadn't occurred to him. Even a careful person could miss something, and he had never claimed to be exceptionally wise.

Before setting out, he had thought only about himself. As a traveling Trainer, he wasn't going to let a typhoon stop him from reaching the Gym, however hard it rained.

But running the Gym was only one part of Brawly's life. He wasn't a traveler trying to toughen himself through every hardship. Staying home during extreme weather would be perfectly reasonable.

Brawly loved surfing and the sea, but he had no reason to brave a typhoon merely to get to work soaking wet.

Maybe I'm worrying over nothing, Misty added, seeing Ethan's thoughtful expression. Don't mind me.

He knew she meant to comfort him. Still, she was probably right. All he could do was hope Brawly was committed enough to open the Gym in this weather.

On second thought, Brawly had arranged for an acting Leader so he could go surfing. Expecting him to turn up during a typhoon seemed unlikely.

You have a point. Ethan nodded to Misty. Let's wait until nine. If the doors are still locked, they're probably closed for the day. We'll go back to the Pokemon Center.

Bea listened silently. She offered no opinion, but she stayed where she was. Apparently she too had decided to wait until nine.

Ethan and Misty found a level stone step sheltered from the wind and sat down. Bea remained standing. Gusts sent her silver-gray hair flying, and the black, rabbit-eared headband above it swayed back and forth.

Would you like to sit with us? Misty asked her.

Bea glanced over and gently shook her head. Standing in the wind was training for her endurance. In any case, it was only a dozen or so minutes until nine. She had already stood there for half an hour without moving.

In that short time, the typhoon drew closer. The entire palm grove outside the Gym began to sway violently.

Ethan checked the time. A few minutes still remained, but he decided not to wait.

Let's go back.

Huh? Now that he wanted to leave, Misty hesitated. Are you sure? There's still a little time. Shouldn't we wait?

If Brawly were coming, he'd already be here. A few more minutes won't change it. He isn't opening today. We'll have to challenge him after the typhoon passes.

All right... Misty stood and started downhill beside him.

As they passed Bea, Ethan called, Don't keep waiting. Come down with us. The storm's almost here, and if you stay much longer, you could be trapped on the cliff.

Bea looked toward the horizon. The typhoon had reached the waters just off Dewford Island. Landfall now seemed inevitable; the air already smelled heavy with moisture.

Waiting would change nothing. She nodded and followed Ethan and Misty down the hill.

The three moved briskly along the path, Ethan and Misty ahead of Bea. They deliberately slowed a little so she wouldn't fall behind, but after a few hundred meters, they realized they had misjudged her.

Her toned muscles showed how often she trained. She was fitter than either of them and had a faster stride. She caught up in moments.

Once they reached the foot of the hill, the town would be another ten or fifteen minutes away. They had underestimated the typhoon's speed.

Rain began without warning. A few small drops pattered against them, then within seconds the shower turned into a downpour.

They had traveled light. Neither Ethan nor Misty had brought a bag, and Bea carried only a small backpack. None of them had a raincoat or even an umbrella.

Their clothes soaked through instantly. Water poured over their heads and streamed down their faces as though someone had turned a faucet on them.

It was too late to race all the way into town. Going back to the Gym and breaking a window for shelter would take too long as well. The rain was so hard that speaking was difficult, visibility was poor, and they could scarcely keep their eyes open.

Fortunately, Ethan remembered a cave nearby. He had noticed it on the way up, and it was close enough to offer temporary shelter.

He waved to Misty and Bea, left the path, and ran toward the rocks. Misty knew the cave too and understood at once; she hurried after him. Bea didn't know why they had changed course, but guessed they had found somewhere to escape the rain. She followed without hesitation.

Chapter 655: Three People Shelter from the Rain

Beside the road rose a low, bare hill of rock. It was only a dozen or so meters high. Halfway up, behind several boulders, a narrow black opening hid in the stone. Only one person could pass through at a time.

The three climbed the hill in the downpour and hurried inside one after another.

The cave was small, oval-shaped, and had no other entrance. Ethan estimated its floor space at little more than a dozen square meters.

It might once have been a wild Pokemon's den. Its occupant had apparently moved elsewhere long ago. Thick, dry grass remained, but there were no recent signs of habitation and no unpleasant smell.

Small though it was, the cave could hold all three of them. Best of all, its entrance faced away from the typhoon. The wind couldn't reach inside, and even the torrential rain ran downhill past the opening.

The cave mouth felt like an invisible barrier separating them from the storm. Out of the wind and rain at last, all three let out relieved breaths.

Ethan and Misty looked at each other's bedraggled appearance and burst out laughing. Their laughter was contagious. Even the corners of Bea's mouth lifted slightly. They had escaped danger, and for a moment they could simply enjoy that.

Then Misty shivered. They were soaked from head to toe. If they didn't warm up, they would soon be in trouble.

Ethan looked around. There are plenty of dry twigs and grass here. Let's get a fire going.

Misty immediately gathered the grass and arranged it with the twigs. Bea hesitated, but before she could kneel to help, Misty had finished. The ease of her movements told Bea that Ethan and Misty were accustomed to camping outdoors.

Ethan took out a Poke Ball and released Combusken. Combusken, use Ember.

Combusken breathed a burst of fire into the kindling. Flames leaped up, lighting the cave and filling it with warmth.

The fire was a start, but they needed to dry their clothes. Wearing wet fabric would be miserable and could leave them chilled and ill.

There was an awkward problem: Ethan was sharing the cave with two girls. He had a way around it.

He released Dragonite. The large Pokemon sat down in the middle of the cave, forming a living screen. More than two meters tall with a broad belly, Dragonite separated Ethan from Misty and Bea.

Someone could still see around it by leaning forward, but as long as everyone stayed in place, it blocked most of their view of one another.

All right. Take off your wet clothes and lay them on the rocks by the fire to dry.

Ethan went first. He removed his clothes, shoes, and socks, keeping his shorts on, and spread the wet things near the flames. Then he leaned against Dragonite. Dragonite wrapped an arm around him and warmed him with its own body heat.

That was why he had chosen Dragonite rather than the equally large Tyranitar. Tyranitar's armor was hard and cold. Dragonite was soft, comfortable, and warm.

On the other side, Misty followed his example. She set her clothes by the fire, stayed in her underclothes, and leaned against Dragonite's opposite flank. She felt no need to make a fuss. She and Ethan had visited hot springs together more than once. She liked him, and she had never been shy by nature. She could treat it like a trip to the swimming pool.

Bea was the only one who hesitated. She knew drying her clothes was sensible, but a man she had met only a few times was just beyond Dragonite. After making sure he couldn't see her, she changed out of her wet clothes too and kept her underclothes on.

Misty glanced at her without thinking. Bea was older and more developed than she was, though not nearly as much as Erika. Bea's firm muscles and taut stomach caught her attention as well. Her skin had the healthy tone of someone who exercised regularly.

Misty wondered why Bea trained her own body so hard. Weren't Trainers supposed to train their Pokemon? Up close, she could also see that Bea was quite pretty, with delicate features, even if she wasn't the sort of beauty who stunned a room at first sight.

I'm Misty, she said, setting those thoughts aside. That's Ethan over there. I don't think we know your name yet.

Bea looked at the smiling girl. They had met a few times now and had gone through the storm together. They were no longer complete strangers.

I'm Bea. She offered nothing more.

From your accent, I'd guess you're not from Hoenn? Misty tried again.

Bea nodded. I'm from Stow-on-Side.

Stow-on-Side? Misty searched her memory. Where's that?

Galar.

And where's Galar?

Far to the west.

What brought you all the way here?

I came to challenge the Fighting-type Gym.

Misty was doing all the work in the conversation. Bea answered each question and never opened a new topic. It was exhausting.

They had known each other only briefly, but Misty could already tell Bea was quiet and rarely spoke more than she had to. After a few dry exchanges, Misty gave up and turned toward Ethan.

How long do you think the typhoon will last?

Ethan had heard the whole exchange and found it funny. Bea was exactly the sort of person Misty struggled to talk to. He didn't tease her about it.

We'll have to wait and see. It's only just begun, so it won't end right away. But don't worry. The sky will clear eventually.

I know, but I wish it would clear sooner, Misty sighed.

Crackle, crackle. The fire went on burning. The cave was shallow, so Ethan wasn't concerned about carbon dioxide building up inside.

After another half hour by the fire, their hair and skin were dry. The clothes on the rocks were warm too. They dressed again and gathered around the flames.

Misty checked her phone. There was no signal.

Rain continued to roar outside, without any sign of easing. With little else to do, Ethan and Misty talked to pass the time.

Bea sat apart from them, making no attempt to join in. Misty had to admire how comfortable she seemed with silence. But Misty and Ethan traveled together every day. They had already discussed most of the things that came to mind, and before long the conversation ran dry.

For someone as restless as Misty, sitting in the cave became torture. She got up and stretched. After moving around for a while, she looked back. Ethan was grooming Dragonite's and Combusken's feathers, while Bea was doing push-ups. Both had found something to occupy themselves.

Those two might actually get along. Misty shook the thought away at once. What was she thinking? Ethan was hers!

She wandered around some more. When she checked the time, it was only noon. The storm still hadn't weakened, and now she was thirsty.

Where could she find water? She had expected to challenge the Gym and return promptly to the Pokemon Center. Apart from her phone, wallet, and Poke Balls, she had brought nothing.

Ethan noticed her discomfort and took a lidded water bottle from the pouch at his waist. He was in the habit of carrying water, which had come in handy.

He poured a little into the lid. Then he looked at Bea and offered it to her first. You must be thirsty too. Have some.

Bea licked her dry lips. She thanked him, accepted the lid, and drank.

Misty had already reached out for it and pouted when Ethan handed it to Bea instead. Her smile returned when he passed her the bottle itself.

She took it carefully and tried a small sip. The water was lukewarm, but her heart felt light. Ethan used this bottle himself. Did drinking from it count as an indirect kiss?

Under his gaze, she pushed the thought aside, drank a little more, and handed it back. Ethan took the bottle and, without looking, drank deeply from it.

That was the spot where my lips touched... Misty's face flushed. Now she was certain it counted. Fortunately, the orange firelight flickered over her face, hiding her embarrassment.

Then her stomach growled. Ethan glanced at it. He was hungry himself.

Bea returned the empty lid and set her small backpack in front of them. She unzipped it and took out a surprising amount of food. Keeping some for herself, she pushed more than half the snacks toward Ethan and Misty.

Oh! Misty realized the food was for them. Thank you so much! Her opinion of Bea, previously no more than lukewarm, rose at once.

Ethan hadn't expected her to carry food or share so generously. He had water, Bea had snacks, and Misty had brought only her appetite. Between them, they were managing nicely.

He examined the packages: egg rolls, pudding, chocolate bars, strawberry cake. Almost everything was sweet. The food would supply plenty of energy, but that was a lot of sugar. Then he remembered that Bea in the anime loved sweets. No wonder she carried so many.

He glanced unobtrusively at her lean waist. With the amount she ate, her daily training must be what kept her fit.

Neither he nor Misty worried about sugar just then. They opened the packages and quickly ate their share. The snacks were a little cloying, but they filled them up. The rush of sweetness lifted their spirits too. Even the rain outside seemed less gloomy.

Sharing food brought the three closer. Misty tried talking to Bea again. Bea still answered as briefly as before, but Misty no longer minded. It simply seemed natural to her now.

The fire began to die. They had burned all the dry wood in the cave, leaving only embers. The air cooled quickly, and dampness crept inside.

Misty edged toward Ethan. He called Dragonite over and had it spread its arms around all three of them.

Misty sat in the middle, with Ethan on her left, Bea on her right, and Dragonite's soft, warm belly behind them. The chill vanished at once.

Before today, sitting so close to a near stranger like Bea might have made Misty uncomfortable. After what they had shared, it didn't trouble her at all.

Chapter 656: Brawly Meets a Cold Reception

Ethan opened his eyes, groggy. He had fallen asleep without realizing it. Sitting in one position for so long had stiffened his shoulders. Misty was asleep too, holding one of his arms. On her other side, Bea's eyes were closed and her breathing even.

He checked the time. It was already three in the afternoon.

Outside the cave, the rain had stopped at some point. The wind still howled now and then, reminding him that the typhoon might not be over. But with the rain gone, they could finally leave.

He was about to wake the others when he eased his arm free. Misty felt him move and opened her eyes at once.

Huh? She rubbed them, bewildered. When did I fall asleep?

Her voice woke Bea as well. Bea blinked drowsily. Compared with her usual unreadable expression, she looked almost comically dazed.

The fire had gone out, but Dragonite's warmth had kept them comfortable. Listening to its strong heartbeat, all three had drifted off without noticing. Ethan turned to Dragonite. It smiled at him, apparently unbothered by having sat still for so long.

Thanks for putting up with us, he told it.

Misty got to her feet and stretched. When she saw that the rain had stopped, she exclaimed, Has the typhoon passed? I thought we'd spend the night in here!

Ethan glanced sideways at her. You sound a little disappointed.

I don't! Misty stuck out her tongue.

To be honest, she was a little sorry to leave. Being trapped had been boring, but it had also given the three of them an unusual memory. After hours in the cave, cut off from the outside world, she had grown used to it. Returning to ordinary life felt oddly sudden. Still, they couldn't stay there forever.

They gathered their rubbish, stamped out the last embers of the fire, and left the cave.

The wind continued to blow, though much less fiercely. In the distance, the seemingly endless dark clouds were moving away. This time the typhoon really did appear to have left Dewford Island behind.

Let's go back to town first, Ethan said.

Huh? Misty looked toward the Gym. Now that the storm's gone, shouldn't we check whether it's open?

We'll challenge it tomorrow. It's already late, and I doubt the staff will rush over to open up as soon as the typhoon passes. Besides, our clothes may be dry, but we still look a mess. Let's clean up at the Pokemon Center first.

Misty agreed. Rain had left an unpleasant smell on them even after they dried.

They went down the hill and reached Dewford Town after another ten or fifteen minutes. It looked as though someone had washed it clean.

As Ethan had predicted, the town's drainage system had worked well. Despite the long downpour, hardly any water remained in the streets. They were merely damp.

The town had not escaped entirely. Some signs and trees leaned at odd angles, and debris carried in from who knew where littered the roads. Residents had come out of their houses and were cleaning up together.

The Pokemon Center was crowded with dozens of Trainers. Ordinarily scattered across Dewford, they had all gathered here because of the storm. Ethan hadn't realized there were so many in town.

Nurse Joy looked relieved when she saw the three return. Where have you been? Your luggage was in your rooms, but none of you were here. I was terribly worried!

As the person responsible for the Center, she could hardly ignore three missing guests. If something had happened to them during their stay, it would have affected her too. She had been anxious since the head count.

Sorry we worried you, Misty said. We were stranded outside and couldn't come back until the storm passed.

I see. I'm glad you're all safe. Nurse Joy nodded. Go and rest. I've prepared ginger soup in the dining room to help everyone warm up.

Thank you.

They left the counter and went to their separate rooms. Ethan took a hot shower first, washing away the smell of rain. He put his dirty clothes in the washing machine, changed, and went to the dining room.

From a distance he saw Bea sitting alone in a corner. Misty hadn't arrived yet; she was apparently still getting ready. Ethan walked over and sat across from Bea.

She gave him a brief glance, then went back to minding her own business. After their time in the cave, she seemed to have quietly accepted Ethan and Misty as friends.

Neither of them had much to talk about. A Chansey helping in the dining room brought over ginger soup, and they sipped it in silence.

Several bolder Trainers had been considering approaching Bea while she sat alone. Seeing a man join her, they sighed in disappointment.

Misty arrived after they had finished their bowls. She too had just showered, and her hair was still damp. When she spotted Ethan sitting face to face with Bea, her gaze sharpened.

Why did this feel familiar? As though she were the extra person?

Then she reconsidered. Ethan was impressive, but not everyone would fall for him. Bea was so reserved that surely things wouldn't turn out as they had with Sabrina or Erika.

Surely not...

The next morning, after breakfast and a night's rest, Ethan and Misty set off for the Dewford Gym again. Bea went with them.

The town had recovered completely. There was scarcely a sign that the typhoon had passed through.

Outside Dewford, they followed the mountain path past the cave where they had sheltered. Misty looked at it fondly. Even Ethan and Bea glanced its way more than once.

They continued uphill to the Gym's unusual entrance sign. To their surprise, it had vanished. The wind must have blown it away.

They exchanged looks. Misty felt a flash of satisfaction. She wasn't being cruel, exactly. If the Gym had opened yesterday, they could have sheltered inside instead of being stranded in a cave. She felt little sympathy for the missing sign.

Bea looked disappointed. As a lover of Fighting-type Pokemon who owned Machop, Machoke, and Machamp, she had liked the sign's design. It suited her taste.

They passed the place where it had stood and reached the main doors. Unlike yesterday, the Gym was open. Someone was finally there to take challenges. At least the trip hadn't been wasted.

Inside, a dozen or so young women sat beside the battle court where Ethan had fought two days earlier. They wore swimsuits and had surfboards beside them. The youngest looked about eighteen or nineteen, the oldest in their early twenties. Their athletic figures and sun-browned skin suggested they spent a great deal of time surfing.

One man sat among them, surrounded on every side. He had spiky blue hair, sunglasses, a sports T-shirt, and shorts. He too was suntanned and fairly handsome.

Only one person could sit there so comfortably, receiving so much attention: Brawly, Leader of the Dewford Gym.

Ethan couldn't help feeling a little envious. Not all the girls were striking, but there were certainly a lot of them. Brock would probably have burst into tears at the sight.

NoAsh had already challenged this Gym. Brock had probably done exactly that.

Brawly noticed the three enter. Oh? Challengers this early? I thought today would be perfect for surfing, with the typhoon gone. Looks like I'll have to put that off for a bit.

Surfing again? Misty planted her hands on her hips. We won the qualifying matches two days ago! Weren't you supposed to accept our challenges yesterday? Why was the Gym locked? We came all this way, got drenched, and ended up trapped in a cave!

Brawly looked baffled. Qualifying matches? What qualifying matches?

Misty frowned. Don't pretend you don't know! We battled your acting Gym Leaderyour top student and girlfriendto earn the right to face you!

Brawly understood. He gave a rueful smile, turned toward the crowd, and called quietly, Shauna!

Shauna was among the women. She had already realized she was in trouble. Flushing with embarrassment, she pivoted and ran into another room as fast as she could.

Misty watched her go, completely confused.

Brawly sighed and turned back to the challengers. I'm sorry. We don't have any qualifying matches here.

What? Misty stared. But two days ago...

Shauna isn't my acting Gym Leader. The Dewford Gym doesn't have one. She took it upon herself to watch over the place while I was away.

Ethan could only marvel at Shauna's nerve. Without anyone's permission, she had fought them and made her invented rules sound official. He wasn't angry so much as aware that he had been fooled.

She had probably wanted to impress the man she liked. Her feelings for Brawly had driven her to quite a bit of trouble.

Brawly was embarrassed too. He said nothing more about surfing. Instead, he whistled for the women to clear the battle court, then asked the three visitors, Are all of you here to challenge me, or only one?

Ethan glanced at Bea just as she looked at him. He smiled and offered her the first match. Ladies first.

Bea nodded. Without a speech, she walked straight to the challenger's side of the court.

Hostile looks followed her. She was considerably prettier than most of the women around Brawly, and they felt the threat at once. What if Bea liked him, or he liked her? They wouldn't stand a chance.

On the other hand, the man who had come with her was handsome tooyounger and better-looking than Brawly. Together, they made an enviable pair. Surely someone with a companion like him wouldn't be interested in Brawly. The women felt both relieved and strangely disappointed.

Brawly faced Bea and studied her with open appreciation. Something about her felt familiar. Even before they battled, he could tell she was a Trainer devoted to Fighting-type Pokemon, just as he was.

The oldest of the women stepped to the edge of the court to referee.

The Dewford Gym battle is about to begin! Each side will use two Pokemon. The Gym Leader may not switch Pokemon freely during the match. When both Pokemon on either side are unable to battle, the match is over!

They were ordinary Gym rules, with nothing unusual about them.

Once the referee finished, Brawly flashed what he thought was a dashing smile at Bea. You already know who I am, but I'll introduce myself anyway. I'm Brawly, the Gym Leader here and an excellent surfer!

He gave her another brilliant smile. Bea's expression didn't change at all. Brawly's confidence hit a wall, and for a moment he stood awkwardly in place.

He recovered enough to ask, And what's your name?

Bea said nothing. He waited, but she still didn't answer. This time Brawly couldn't hide his embarrassment, especially with the other women watching him.

They had never seen him pay so much attention to someone. Their glances turned complicated.

Misty had to stifle a laugh. After a day with Bea, she knew her well enough. If Brawly thought this sort of flirtatious introduction would get Bea chatting, he was setting himself up for disappointment.

Chapter 657: A Contest of Strength

Brawly dressed fashionably, was fairly handsome and outgoing, and had no shortage of admirers. The girls who spent every day with him at the Gym were proof of that. If he had tried to talk to someone else, he might have succeeded. He had simply chosen the wrong person.

After an awkward silence, he rubbed his nose and took out a Poke Ball, pretending nothing had happened. Whether he felt embarrassed was anyone's guess but his own.

He threw the ball. A plump Pokemon resembling a sumo wrestler appeared on the field.

Misty had never seen one before. From the sidelines, she pointed her Pokedex at it.

Makuhita, the Guts Pokemon. Fighting type. Makuhita loves to train. It builds up energy by eating well, sleeping well, and exercising every day, growing stronger through repeated, rigorous practice. It enjoys strengthening its body more than anything. By charging into thick tree trunks, it toughens both its body and its determination. It practices slapping over and over. Its perseverance lets it withstand attacks and rise again, no matter how many times it is knocked down.

It sounded like a Pokemon born to fight. Being solely a Fighting type could leave it at a disadvantage against certain opponents, but it also let it specialize in fighting.

On the other side, Bea released the Pangoro that had battled Shauna two days earlier. It had performed well then, so Ethan wasn't surprised. He knew Pangoro wasn't even Bea's strongest Pokemon. Her real ace was a tremendously powerful Machamp capable of Dynamaxing.

Brawly seemed eager to show off his knowledge of a Pokemon uncommon in Hoenn. Stroking his chin, he said, A Pangoro! You rarely see one in this region. Here in Dewford Town, years may pass between visits from Trainers who have one. But I'm familiar with them. I encountered plenty while traveling in other regions, and I know how strong they are.

Someone else might have replied politely, perhaps downplaying Pangoro's strength, saying she had caught it by chance, or asking where Brawly had traveled. Bea remained as impassive as ever. She showed no interest in continuing the conversation.

In that respect, she reminded Ethan a little of Sabrina. Both kept strangers at a distance with a cool manner. But silence was not the same as rudeness. When Brawly sent out his Pokemon, Bea bowed with perfect courtesy.

He blinked and hurriedly bowed back. After several failed attempts to talk to her, he was beginning to understand that she simply didn't say much.

He also noticed that although she had come with Ethan, the two barely interacted. They didn't seem close, let alone a couple. With that settled in his mind, he calmed down a little.

He knew he had been too eager earlier and had upset the women around him. Easy now. No need to rush.

He could show Bea what he was capable of by defeating her Pangoro in battle instead.

With both Pokemon ready, the referee raised her flag. The match begins now!

As the flag dropped, both Trainers acted.

Feel the force of my wave! Brawly made an exaggerated surfing motion on dry land. At his shout, Makuhita charged straight at Pangoro.

Pangoro didn't even lower its head. Its eyes shifted down toward the approaching Pokemon while it slowly chewed the bamboo shoot in its mouth.

Bea took a karate stance in her command area. At nearly the same moment, Pangoro assumed the identical stance with its back still turned to her, as though it had sensed her movement.

Here it comes, Ethan thought, narrowing his eyes.

Of all the things he disliked in a Pokemon battle, the coordinated posing and dancing some Trainers did with their Pokemon ranked near the top. He would never do it himself.

Bea drove a fist forward. Pangoro moved in perfect unison, throwing its right fist into Makuhita. It was a style Bea hadn't shown against Shauna. Perhaps Shauna hadn't been strong enough to draw it out; only against Brawly was Bea revealing how seriously she could fight.

Ethan didn't know what the gestures accomplished. Maybe mimicking her Pokemon helped Bea feel the battle through its movements while she trained herself and gave commands.

The blow caught Brawly and Makuhita by surprise. Bea hadn't spoken a command, so neither had expected Pangoro to attack just then.

Makuhita was well trained, though. It quickly recovered, rubbed its aching chest, and lunged again. Both Pokemon favored direct physical attacks. There were no dazzling effects as they closed and traded blows.

As the exchange went on, Brawly sensed that something was wrong. Pangoro was much too strong.

Makuhita wasn't his best Pokemon, but it had won many Gym matches and helped him defeat more than a dozen challengers. He had always considered it capable.

Against Pangoro, it was outmatched. Its strength, technique, durability, and reactions all fell short. It even had less battle experience.

After only a dozen exchanges, Pangoro seized an opening. One Vital Throw slammed Makuhita onto the floor, and it could not get up.

The girls watching from the sidelines covered their mouths in shock. They were used to seeing Brawly as the stronger Trainer, whatever challenger stood opposite him. When had they last seen one of his Pokemon lose so decisively?

Brawly hadn't expected Makuhita to fall so fast either, but he didn't panic. He had traveled enough to know that the world held many powerful Trainers and Pokemon. Losing a round or two wasn't the end of anything.

Still, he had resolved to defeat Bea's Pokemon, and she had beaten his almost immediately.

The referee took a moment to recover her composure before raising her flag. Pangoro wins the first round!

Yes! Misty applauded from the spectator area. As Bea's friend, she was on her side. Brawly's unsubtle attempts to flirt with Bea had also irritated her. The angry looks from the women around him didn't bother her at all.

Your Pangoro really is strong, Brawly said. He had lost the round, but refused to sound defeated. It's been a long time since I've met an opponent like you. You've impressed me. The next round won't be so simple, though. I'll have to get a little more serious.

He recalled his unconscious Makuhita and took out a second Poke Ball.

Come out, Hariyama!

Blue light flashed. A Pokemon larger, stronger, and fiercer-looking than Makuhita appeared on the field. Misty scanned it with her Pokedex too.

Hariyama, the Arm Thrust Pokemon. Fighting type. The evolved form of Makuhita. Known for its immense strength, Hariyama loves testing itself against very large Pokemon. It can stop an oncoming train with one palm and send a ten-ton truck flying with a slap. Despite its love of contests of strength, it is kindhearted and courteous, and it honors its opponents.

Misty had guessed the relationship from their appearance, but still looked surprised. Hariyama evolves from Makuhita? If he had this stronger option, why didn't he send it out first?

Ethan hadn't expected Brawly to use Makuhita's evolution in the second round either. He had assumed the Gym Leader would choose a different species. Most Trainers didn't raise two Pokemon of the same kind unless they had a particular reason to. Evolution rarely changed a Pokemon's battle style as much as it changed its strength, so an opponent who had seen the first form could often anticipate the second.

Unless Brawly had great confidence in Hariyama, sending it out now seemed unwise.

The women at the Gym reacted quite differently. The moment they saw Hariyama, they stirred. The challengers might not know it, but this was Brawly's ace. He was bringing out his strongest Pokemon against Bea. Was she really that formidable?

The women spent more time surfing than studying battles. Still, after watching so many Gym matches, they had learned to recognize some things. Bea's Pangoro was unlike most of the challengers' Pokemon they had seen.

Ethan and Misty exchanged smiles. Brawly had claimed he was getting only a little more serious, yet he had already brought out his ace. He clearly didn't want to lose face in front of Bea.

Makuhita stood about a meter tall. Hariyama reached two meters and thirty centimeters, roughly twenty centimeters taller than Pangoro. It weighed nearly twice as much too: a genuine heavyweight.

Everyone looked to Bea. Would she switch Pokemon, or send Pangoro into another round?

She seemed oblivious to their attention, but her decision was clear. Pangoro returned to its starting position on her side of the court.

It wasn't surprising. Bea had won the first round and still held the initiative. Even if she lost this one, she would have another Pokemon for the deciding battle. Pangoro could still fight, so why withdraw it?

Brawly breathed a little easier when he saw she was keeping Pangoro in. He needed to regain some ground. If she switched now, beating two fresh Pokemon would take longer and make it harder to show her how strong he was.

Both Pokemon readied themselves. The referee waved her flag again, and the second round began.

Hariyama, use Arm Thrust!

Hariyama strode toward Pangoro, raising its enormous red palms as it ran.

Bea took her karate stance a second time. Pangoro matched her, and the two towering Pokemon collided.

Their large hands locked together. Both pushed with all their strength, but neither gained ground. Their muscles bulged, their bodies trembled, and strain showed at their temples. What looked like a simple test of strength had both Pokemon giving everything they had.

At first, Hariyama's greater size left Brawly feeling confident. Only a few seconds later, Pangoro roared and began forcing Hariyama backward.

In the contest of strength, Pangoro had come out ahead.

Chapter 658: The Fighting Spirit He Once Followed

Pangoro drove a Sky Uppercut into Hariyama's chin. The powerful blow lifted its massive body clear of the floor and sent it flying.

Hariyama! Brawly cried in alarm. There was nothing he could do but watch. Hariyama's eyes rolled upward, and it fell backward with a heavy thud.

The Gym fell silent. The women watching stared wide-eyed at the motionless Hariyama. They could hardly believe Brawly's ace had lost.

The two Pokemon had fought for some time. At points the battle had seemed evenly matched, with both landing hard blows and taking injuries. Yet Pangoro had won.

How? Brawly stepped back, stunned. He had entered the fight brimming with confidence. Now even his strongest Pokemon had fallen to Bea's Pangoro. He couldn't understand how her Pokemon was powerful enough to defeat both of his.

Ethan, watching from the side, thought the answer was plain. Both were Gym Leaders, but Brawly spent his days surfing and let his Pokemon spend much of their time playing in the water with him. Bea trained alongside her own Pokemon with relentless discipline. Why would Brawly expect to win?

Hariyama and Pangoro had looked evenly matched during the exchange, but Pangoro was stronger and tougher. Its determination was exceptional too. More than once, it had gritted its teeth through a hit and counterattacked. Losing to such an opponent was only natural.

Pangoro returned to Bea's side and raised its head proudly. It swept a defiant look over the girls who had been so certain Brawly could not lose. They instinctively looked away.

Its Trainer said little, but Pangoro could stand up for her. Beating an opponent was the clearest way to do it.

At last the referee recovered and raised her flag. H-Hariyama is unable to battle! The challenger wins this Gym match!

Brawly quickly composed himself and applauded. What a fine battle. He felt the defeat keenly, but put on a smile as he approached Bea. Your Pangoro is remarkable. I knew it was strong. In fact, you're the strongest female Trainer I've faced since I first received a Pokemon!

He took a badge from his pocket and offered it to her. Please accept this as proof you defeated me.

Bea didn't even look at the badge. She bowed to Brawly, turned, and headed for the exit. When she passed Ethan and Misty, she hesitated, then sat beside Misty instead of leaving the Gym.

Brawly stared after her. Why hadn't she taken the badge? Winning a Gym match and accepting its badge was perfectly normal. Had he done something wrong?

Ethan stood and walked over. Sorry. She doesn't talk much, so let me explain. She didn't come for a badge or to enter the Ever Grande Conference. She challenged you to train her Pokemon.

Oh, I see... Brawly finally understood.

He was about to say more, but Ethan continued toward the challenger's side of the court. Brawly's interest stirred. Are you here to challenge me too?

That's right. Ethan glanced at Hariyama, still lying on the floor, and feigned sudden realization. Oh! Were those your only two Pokemon? Without them, can you still defend the Gym?

Ha, of course I can! What a question... Brawly's eyebrow twitched. He was a Gym Leader. Did this man really think he owned only two Pokemon? Ethan's tone was irritating too.

He looked Ethan over. The younger man seemed a few years his junior and perhaps a little more handsono, about equally handsome.

Then he glanced at the spectators. Apart from Bea, who had caught his eye, Ethan had arrived with another pretty girl. She was still young, but Brawly could tell she would grow up to be beautiful. Ethan seemed fortunate in his companions, which only annoyed Brawly more.

You want a Gym battle? he asked again.

Of course. Ethan smiled innocently, as though he hadn't noticed the hostility in Brawly's voice. I'm nowhere near as strong as she is, though. I don't have any especially powerful Pokemon. Please go easy on me.

Not very strong? Brawly's eyes lit up. Perfect. Bea's victory had embarrassed him in front of her and all the women at the Gym. Here was his chance to recover some pride.

He softened his expression, afraid of scaring the challenger off. No problem. I have a few Pokemon that aren't especially strong either. Let's have the match.

Misty laughed from the spectators' seats. Ethan's act was so obvious! Yet Brawly had swallowed it and taken him for an easy opponent.

She could see that Brawly wanted to make up for his loss by defeating Ethan. He had no idea whom he was facing. Ethan was younger and had achieved far more. Sabrina, Erika, and Misty herselfthe world's prettiest girl, in her opinionwere all more beautiful than Brawly's admirers. Most of all, Ethan's Pokemon were nothing like the weak team he claimed to have.

She had no intention of warning Brawly. Go, Ethan! she called, then sat back with her legs together to enjoy the show.

Bea turned a curious look on Misty. She had left after her battle with Shauna and hadn't seen Ethan fight. Brawly had seemed only somewhat stronger than Shauna today; perhaps Ethan could manage him. But why had Ethan said he wasn't very strong?

Misty caught Bea's gaze and shook her head, suppressing a laugh. If she explained, she would sound as though she were boasting about Ethan. Bea could discover his abilities for herself. Misty was more interested in whether Bea's calm expression would survive learning that Ethan was Champion of two regional Leagues.

Ethan and Brawly faced one another on the court. Unlike before, a few of the Gym's women cheered for the handsome challenger. Brawly grew more irritated. These women usually gathered around him. Why were some of them changing sides?

The rules had already been announced, so the referee didn't repeat them. Each side would still use two Pokemon.

After a moment's thought, Brawly chose his first.

Come out, Hitmontop!

Blue light flashed, and a Pokemon with the look of a streetwise fighter appeared. With Makuhita and Hariyama defeated, Brawly still had more than a dozen other Pokemon. Only a few were strong enough for this sort of match, and Hitmontop was one of them.

Ethan had fought Hitmontop before. He knew how skilled it was with its legs. Among the Pokemon he wanted to use here, he had just one Fighting type that also specialized in kicking.

I'm counting on you, Combusken!

Combusken emerged. Brawly relaxed at the sight. Hoenn newcomers could choose Torchic as a starter, and he had faced Torchic and Combusken often while running the Gym. This one hadn't even evolved into Blaziken.

Ethan had told the truth, Brawly thought. His Pokemon really was on the weak side. At least it wasn't some unfamiliar Pokemon from another region, or a fully evolved powerhouse like Bea's. Everything seemed under control.

Brawly! You can do it!

Shauna appeared in the second-floor gallery at last. She hadn't watched Brawly's match with Bea after running away, but she had heard he lost. Of all the girls at the Gym, her support for him was the most unwavering. Now she came out to cheer for the man she liked.

Her voice encouraged Brawly. Not everyone had lost faith in him. He decided to set aside her unauthorized attempt to act as Gym Leader, smiled broadly, and waved back.

Thank you for loving me so steadfastly, Shauna. Watch me beat this man and give you a reason to be proud!

His confidence returned. This time he didn't ask the male challenger for his name. He went straight to the battle.

Hitmontop, close in and use Triple Kick!

Ethan would not underestimate someone who specialized in Fighting types, especially while using a Fighting type himself. Combusken, use Detect!

His safest approach was to prepare before Hitmontop reached him, watch the attack, and counter from defense.

Combusken's eyes sharpened. For an instant, Hitmontop's movements seemed slower to it. Hitmontop spun forward upside down like a top and thrust a spiked foot high toward Combusken's face.

At Ethan's command, Combusken sprang back out of the way. Then it caught the opening after Hitmontop's kick and countered with Double Kick.

The battle was on. Unlike Bea's contest of raw strength, this was a test of technique.

After several exchanges, Brawly saw that Combusken wasn't overwhelmingly powerful. It was difficult, but not impossible, to handle. His Hitmontop seemed evenly matched with it, unlike Makuhita against Pangoro.

That was still more troublesome than he had expected. Why were all his challengers today so hard to beat?

The Pokemon kept exchanging kicks. Both favored attacks with their legs, so the action stayed low: a kick, a clash, a retreat, then another kick and another clash.

In only a few minutes, they had traded more than a dozen attacks. Most were blocked or countered, but each Pokemon found openings and landed several blows. Their stamina ebbed. Soon both were panting and looked ready to fall.

Hang on... Brawly watched Hitmontop wobble. It could no longer spin as smoothly as when it entered the field. His heart was in his throat.

Combusken, by contrast, stood its ground through sheer Fire-type fighting spirit. Its sharp eyes remained fixed on Hitmontop.

That determination startled Brawly. Only then did he remember the perseverance and grit he had once held so dear.

Have I spent too long taking it easy on this island, far from the mainland? Have I strayed from the path of fighting I used to follow?

Chapter 659: Taking On Machamp

Hitmontop fell.

Combusken had defeated its opponent, but it clearly could not continue either. Ethan had won the first round, though both sides had paid for it. For Brawly in particular, that was a result he could live with.

And yet...

Brawly's brow twitched. He had a growing feeling that he might fail to live up to Shauna's expectations today.

Then Ethan sighed and said apologetically, Sorry. I would have liked to battle you with Fighting-type Pokemon, but Combusken can't go on, and it's the only one I have. Please let me use a Pokemon of another type for the next round.

Another type? Brawly felt a flicker of hope.

He had to admit that Combusken was somewhat stronger than his Hitmontop. Losing was disappointing, but there was nothing he could do about it now. If the next Pokemon wasn't one with a type advantage against Fighting-types, though, Brawly still thought he had a good chance of winning.

He nodded. Of course. This is a Fighting-type Gym, but challengers aren't required to use Fighting-type Pokemon. Choose whichever one you like.

Ethan smiled. After challenging so many Gyms, he knew the rules perfectly well. He had brought it up in advance so no one could complain that he had fought unfairly if Brawly lost.

Brawly recalled Hitmontop and took out another Poke Ball. This would be his fourth Pokemon to battle today. If he kept losing, he might brood over it for a long time.

But a Gym Leader had to be ready for that. He would either defeat a challenger or be defeated. He could blame no one else; such matches were part of his life.

He threw the ball, revealing his fourth choice: a Machamp.

Ethan immediately remembered the unusual sign outside the Gym. The Machamp carved into it must have been this very one. He hadn't expected to meet the model in person.

Off the court, the girls from the Gym began to talk at once.

Oh! I didn't think Brawly would send Machamp out!

Neither did I. I haven't seen it battle in ages, not since Hariyama became his ace!

With Machamp out there, he'll definitely win this one!

Ethan understood. Before Hariyama had taken its place, Machamp must have been Brawly's strongest Pokemon. Hariyama's rise had gradually pushed it into a supporting role. To beat Ethan, Brawly had brought out even the Pokemon he usually kept in reserve.

Did he think that would be enough?

Ethan recalled Combusken and ran his fingers over the Poke Balls in his waist pouch. He considered how to face a muscular Pokemon with four arms.

If he chose a Pokemon with a type advantage, the girls would probably dismiss his victory as a matter of favorable typing. He wanted to win so decisively that they would have nothing to say.

He ruled out several Pokemon and took out Tyranitar's ball. Fighting-type attacks were four times as effective against Tyranitar. If he beat Brawly with that disadvantage, surely no one could object.

Go, Tyranitar!

The light from the thrown ball faded, and Tyranitar's enormous body appeared on the court. It gave Machamp a thunderous roar.

Brawly narrowed his eyes. Tyranitar had an imposing presence, fierce and domineering. It looked like a formidable Pokemon. But why had Ethan sent it out? Surely he knew Machamp had a type advantage. Was he underestimating Brawly, or did he truly have no better choice?

Whatever the reason, Brawly's chances had improved considerably.

The Gym girls brightened too. Machamp's Fighting-type attacks would be four times as effective. How could it lose?

In the stands, Bea frowned at the sight of Tyranitar. She couldn't make sense of Ethan's choice either. But his calm expression suggested he had selected it deliberately. Perhaps he wanted to train it under difficult conditions.

Only Misty, who knew what Tyranitar could do, had a good idea of Ethan's intention. He wanted this match to silence everyone who might question his victory. She sat up straight, eager to watch.

As for the possibility that Ethan might lose? What a joke.

After a brief pause, the referee gave the signal, and Ethan's second battle began.

Tyranitar, Stone Edge! Ethan ordered at once.

Sharp rocks thrust up from the floor toward Machamp. They would be difficult for it to dodge, but Machamp had another answer. Just as a pointed stone rose beneath it, Machamp extended all four arms and stopped the rock with sheer strength.

That's impressive. Ethan nodded to himself. Brawly had trained this Machamp well if it could catch an attack like that.

But how many times could it do so?

Tyranitar, again!

As long as Machamp couldn't close the distance, Ethan thought, all that strength would be of little use. Tyranitar gathered energy and unleashed a second Stone Edge.

Machamp did not wait for the next rock to reach it. With all four arms, it lifted the stone it had just stopped and hurled it at Tyranitar without even taking time to aim.

The rock traced an arc through the air. Ethan understood why Machamp had seemed so unhurried about approaching. It had a way to attack from a distance after all.

Its throw was remarkably accurate too. Though it had barely looked, the stone flew straight at Tyranitar. Machamp must have practiced this countless times. Still, a rock like that would do little to Tyranitar.

As it arrived, Tyranitar lowered its head and struck it with the armor-hard spikes at the back of its skull. The stone shattered. Fragments streamed down through the gaps in Tyranitar's armor, leaving its head unmarked.

Meanwhile, the second Stone Edge reached Machamp. Its arms were still extended from the throw, and its balance had not yet recovered. It could not brace against the new rock as it had before. It leaped to the side and barely avoided it.

That first exchange gave both Trainers a clearer sense of their opponent's strength. Simple attacks would not decide this battle.

At Brawly's command, Machamp charged toward Tyranitar. Ethan had no intention of letting it approach unopposed. At a sweep of his hand, Tyranitar summoned a Sandstorm and hid itself in swirling yellow sand.

The sand spread across the court, despite the Gym being indoors on an island.

Brawly did not hesitate. He ordered Machamp straight into the storm. What could a mere Rock-type move do to it? Poor visibility made surprise attacks a danger, but close combat was Machamp's specialty. He had no reason to fear a fight at that range.

Machamp strode into the sand and vanished. Soon roars from Machamp and Tyranitar sounded one after the other. They had found each other and begun to fight.

Yet something about the sounds unsettled Brawly and the Gym girls. Tyranitar's roars remained as fierce as ever, while Machamp's cries grew lower and increasingly pained.

Brawly's heart lurched. Was Machamp struggling? That made no sense. It held the type advantage. If either Pokemon was in trouble, it should be Tyranitar.

The storm hid the battle from everyone outside. Another troubling thought struck Brawly: perhaps the gap between the two Pokemon was so great that Tyranitar's disadvantage no longer mattered.

But that did not fit what he had seen. Ethan's Combusken had defeated Hitmontop, one of Brawly's stronger Pokemon, but had been injured badly enough that it could not fight again. His Pokemon did not seem overwhelmingly powerful. Tyranitar looked strong, certainly, but how much stronger could it be?

Brawly was so desperate to know what was happening that he wanted to rush into the Sandstorm himself. Of course, he couldn't. The wind and dense sand swallowed the light and sounds of the moves within it. The spectators could only guess at the fight from the rising and falling roars.

Time passed under that tense uncertainty. The storm gradually thinned, and everyone peered into it.

Through the hazy sand, they made out two shapes still fighting. As they had expected, it was a close-quarters battle. A wall of rocks surrounded Machamp, restricting its movement. Broken stones lay scattered nearby, crushed during the struggle.

Both Pokemon bore wounds, but Machamp was covered in them. Tyranitar had suffered far less. The fight within the storm had plainly been fierce, and Machamp had taken the worst of it.

Brawly and the Gym girls frowned. Machamp was losing? How was that possible?

Bea was just as astonished. Anyone who knew her well knew that her strongest Pokemon, the one that best represented her, was a Machamp, not Pangoro. She understood the species well enough to grasp how startling this result was.

Ethan watched their reactions with his hands in his pockets. From a distance, Machamp looked built for close combat: muscles everywhere, four powerful arms, and every apparent advantage in a grapple. But it had a weakness. Compared with its upper body, its legs were less formidable.

Tyranitar had exploited that weakness in the Sandstorm. It used Rock Slide to raise obstacles around Machamp and restrict its movements. With visibility so poor, Machamp had found itself trapped among the rocks.

The greater reason for the result, however, was Tyranitar's own strength. Machamp excelled at close combat, but Ethan had never meant to match it technique for technique. Machamp had its advantages, and Tyranitar had its own.

Tyranitar could not fight with four humanlike arms, but it had sharp claws and fangs. It could bite and tear like a wild beast. The Sandstorm gave it cover to unleash its savage strength.

Low Sweep, Karate Chop, Vital Throwwhatever Machamp tried, it still had to withstand Tyranitar's collisions and Thrash.

Ethan had never intended to defeat Machamp with Dark-type or Rock-type attacks. His real answer was the powerful Normal-type moves Tyranitar's tremendous strength made possible.

Chapter 660: An Unexpected Request

With everyone watching, Machamp spread all four arms and charged at Tyranitar again. This time, they could see exactly how it had fallen behind.

Machamp broke through a rock blocking its path with a light shove of its shoulder. A few strides brought it in front of Tyranitar. It reached out as if to grab Tyranitar and use Seismic Toss. If it succeeded, the move would do serious damage.

Just before Machamp could touch it, Tyranitar turned. Its tail was not especially long, but it was immensely thick. It swept the tail straight into Machamp's legs.

Pain shot through Machamp's lower body. Caught off guard, it lost its balance and fell backward.

Oh no! Brawly's expression changed. He knew what was coming.

Machamp hit the floor with a heavy thud.

Now's our chance! Hyper Beam! Ethan called.

Everyone understood what he intended. Some of the Gym girls turned away, unable to bear watching. Others covered their faces, and a few even shed quiet tears.

Tyranitar lowered its head slightly. Energy gathered in its mouth and burst forth at point-blank range, striking Machamp squarely in the chest. The blazing white beam poured into it with a fierce, crackling hiss.

Under the tremendous impact, Machamp's body convulsed. Its eyes rolled upward, and it soon lost consciousness.

The referee raised her flag almost immediately. Machamp is unable to battle! Tyranitar wins! The challenger wins the Gym match!

As soon as she finished, Brawly shouted at Tyranitar. Stop!

But Tyranitar was not going to obey him. It continued pouring out the remaining energy of its Hyper Beam. Alarmed, Brawly kept looking toward Ethan.

When Ethan saw that the match was over, he waved a hand. Tyranitar closed its mouth at once, and the beam cut off.

Brawly hurried over to examine Machamp. Satisfied that it had suffered no serious injury, he recalled it.

I lost...

He was frustrated, but he arranged his face into an unconcerned expression. Your Tyranitar is strong. That attack on Machamp's legs was especially clever. I can tell you must have trained specifically for this challenge. You came well prepared.

Trained specifically? Ethan wondered. For what? Attacking legs?

He shook his head helplessly. Brawly really couldn't stand to lose without finding an excuse. Ethan could understand why. Two challengers had arrived today, and Brawly had sent out four of his best Pokemon across their matches. He had lost every round. In front of the Gym girls, his pride had taken a beating. He needed some way to save face.

Ethan had no desire to argue. He recalled Tyranitar.

Brawly took Ethan's silence as agreement. So the man really had researched his team before coming here. The thought made Brawly feel a little better.

He approached Ethan and offered him the same badge Bea had refused earlier. This is my Knuckle Badge. Please take it.

He watched Ethan closely. What if this man, like the woman before him, had come only to train and refused the badge too? To Brawly's relief, Ethan accepted it without hesitation.

Ethan looked down at the Knuckle Badge in his palm. True to its name, it resembled a boxing glove. Most of it was blue, forming the body of the glove, while an orange circle at the bottom looked like a protruding thumb. There was nothing more elaborate about it.

He put the badge into his badge case, gave Brawly a nod, and headed for the exit. Misty and Bea rose from the stands to join him, and the three left the Gym together.

Brawly let out a long breath as he watched them go. At last it was over. Those matches had been exhausting. It was only morning, yet he felt drained and thoroughly gloomy.

First he would get his Pokemon treated. Then he could go surfing and relax. His only regret was that he had never learned Bea's name or got her contact information.

What a shame. Still, Brawly's disappointment faded almost as quickly as it had come. Life went on, and there was no sense giving up a good day at the beach.

Girls, the weather's great! Let's go surfing!

He turned to invite them, only to find them huddled around one girl's phone, chattering as they stared at its screen. Brawly raised an eyebrow, put on a bright smile, and walked over.

What are you looking at?

Brawly, come here! the girl holding the phone said excitedly. We found out who that man was!

What? Brawly stopped. Hadn't Ethan been an ordinary challenger? Curious, he hurried over.

I thought he looked familiar, the girl continued. I searched for him just now, and sure enough, he's no ordinary Trainer!

On the phone, a video showed an awards ceremony. The man standing on the podium was the same one Brawly had just battled. Its headline read: Congratulations to Ethan Vale on Winning His Second Pokemon League Tournament!

What? A tournament champion? His second?

Brawly rubbed his eyes and looked again. There was no mistake. The man smiling on the podium was Ethan. He had won tournaments in two regions. No wonder his Tyranitar had been so strong.

Then Brawly remembered his claim that Ethan had studied his team in advance, and his face grew hot. A Trainer with two tournament titles had no need to research him specially just to challenge one Gym.

Fortunately, the girls were too busy praising Ethan to notice how flimsy Brawly's excuse had been. But hearing all that admiration made him jealous. Until a short while ago, those admiring looks had belonged to him.

...

After leaving Dewford Gym, Ethan, Misty, and Bea followed the familiar path out of Dewford Town. With their Gym challenges behind them, it was time to part ways.

Ethan turned to Bea. Where will you go next?

There are other well-known Fighting-type Trainers in Hoenn, she replied without hesitation. I'll visit and challenge them all. Then I'll travel to another region.

I see. I hope our paths cross again.

They had only just met, so after exchanging contact information, they said a simple goodbye and watched Bea leave.

While they exchanged numbers, Misty quietly watched their faces. Neither Ethan nor Bea showed anything unusual. She let out a relieved breath.

Once Bea had gone, Ethan and Misty returned to Dewford Town. At the Pokemon Center, Nurse Joy treated Combusken and Tyranitar. They had lunch there as well before heading to the harbor.

Ethan now held four badges: the Stone Badge from Rustboro Gym, the Heat Badge from Lavaridge Gym, the Dynamo Badge from Mauville Gym, and the Knuckle Badge from Dewford Gym. He was halfway to the eight he needed for the Ever Grande Conference.

They boarded a passenger ship bound for the mainland. Standing on deck in the sea breeze, with the blue water stretching around them, Misty asked, Where are we going next?

Ethan took out his map and studied it. Petalburg Gym. I went there before, but Norman was away on business, so I missed my chance to challenge him. Petalburg isn't far from Dewford either. It makes sense to go now.

Norman is May's father, right? Misty nodded. I wonder what he's like.

Ethan looked toward the horizon. A man who lives for Pokemon. Serious, meticulous, and well liked. Most of all, he's strong.

...

The ship sailed for much of the day. By evening, Ethan and Misty stepped onto Hoenn's mainland again. Though the island was part of Hoenn too, solid ground here felt different. It was reassuring to be back.

The voyage had been dull, and they did not push on after disembarking in the port city. They took a room at a hotel for the night.

They had arrived late, and the hotel had only one room left. Ethan and Misty had to share it. At check-in, Ethan spent a long time explaining himself under the shocked gaze of the receptionist. Only after the lobby manager examined the situation did they finally allow him and Misty to take the room.

That was one of the difficulties of traveling with a minor. Given a choice, Ethan would rather have stayed at a Pokemon Center or a small inn.

As the elevator doors closed behind them, he caught one last glimpse of the receptionist and manager. They were still staring at him as though he were a pervert.

Oh well. I'll get used to it eventually...

Nothing happened that night. Early the next morning, Ethan barely touched breakfast before hurrying Misty out of the hotel and heading straight for Petalburg City.

Misty had no idea why he was acting that way. Mature as she was compared with others her age, there were still things she did not quite understand.

The road toward Petalburg City was busy with Trainers who had only recently set out from New Bark Town. Ethan accepted every challenge offered along the way to give his Pokemon practice. With Eevee, Combusken, and Metang, he swept through the beginners. By the time they reached the outskirts of Petalburg City, he had won seventeen battles without a loss.

Misty found the whole thing hilarious. Ethan, why are you picking fights with beginners? Did you see their faces after you beat them? Some of them looked so crushed they might take ages to recover.

What do you know? Ethan shrugged and gave her a look. I've been traveling for a long time, but those three Pokemon are still fairly new to battling. If they're beginners too, what's wrong with sparring against them to sharpen my team's skills?

Of course, of course. You're right. Misty hid a laugh behind her hand. But aren't you worried someone will find out? Lucky for you they didn't know your name. Otherwise we'd see headlines like, Shocking! Tournament Champion Crushes Beginners Near Their Starting Town!

Ethan gave her a light knock on the head. Laughing, he entered Petalburg City in high spirits.

Just then his phone rang. The caller was Kennedy, the Devon Corporation secretary he had once rescued.

Ethan paused. Why would Kennedy call him out of the blue? They were unlikely to have much to do with each other again. Something must have happened.

He answered. Hello?

Mr. Vale? Are you still in Hoenn?

I am. I'm near Petalburg City. What's going on?

Kennedy sounded relieved to hear he was near Devon's headquarters. He came straight to the point. That's wonderful. If it's convenient, could you come to Rustboro City? Mr. Stone has something very important to ask of you!

Chapter 661: Target: Deoxys!

On a stretch of level grassland outside Petalburg City, Ethan and Misty sat on a rock and waited.
