After Kennedy's call, Ethan had looked at the city almost within reach and decided to put off his Gym challenge. Norman and his Gym would still be there later. First he would deal with Mr. Stone's request.

He wished he knew what was so urgent. Kennedy had told him nothing over the phone, only that someone would come to pick him up right away. The secrecy had made Misty curious too.

Just over twenty minutes later, the rumble of rotors sounded overhead. They looked up to see a medium-sized helicopter descending toward them.

A helicopter? Ethan had expected a car. Devon Corporation had sent an aircraft instead. He was impressed by the company's resources, and more curious than ever about what Mr. Stone wanted.

...

The helicopter landed on the rooftop helipad of Devon Corporation's headquarters in Rustboro City. As Ethan and Misty climbed out, Ethan spotted Kennedy waiting for them. After all this time, the secretary looked much the same, neatly dressed in a suit.

Mr. Vale. Kennedy glanced at Misty and gestured toward the building. Mr. Stone is waiting for you. Please follow me.

Ethan nodded and followed him toward the elevator without asking questions. Misty lingered a step behind to take one last look at the view from the roof before catching up.

She couldn't help being impressed. Ethan knew the president of a major company well enough for the man to send a helicopter for him. Traveling with Ethan felt nothing like traveling with Ash.

The elevator stopped on the fifteenth floor. Ethan had visited before, so he knew Mr. Stone's office was elsewhere. This floor housed the company's most tightly guarded research facilities.

Security was visibly stronger than on his last visit. Guards patrolled with Pokemon, cameras watched the corridors, and reinforced doors divided the area. Several guards glanced curiously at the unfamiliar man and girl Kennedy was escorting through.

This looks better, Ethan said to Kennedy with a smile. It finally looks as though security means business.

We have you to thank for that. Kennedy gave a rueful smile. Team Aqua would have succeeded last time if you hadn't been here. Mr. Stone was furious afterward. He ordered a complete overhaul so it couldn't happen again.

As they spoke, Kennedy led them into a large control room. Computers and monitors filled it. Among more than a dozen researchers, Ethan immediately spotted Mr. Stone.

The president came forward smiling. Mr. Vale. We meet again!

Hello, Mr. Stone. Ethan got straight to the point. What's so important that you needed me here?

Mr. Stone did not answer immediately. His gaze shifted to Misty. And who is this?

Hello. Misty introduced herself with easy confidence. I'm Misty. I'm traveling with Ethan.

Noticing that Erika was no longer with him, Mr. Stone asked, Where is Miss Erika?

She went back to Kanto, Ethan said. Why did he ask? Is there something you need from her?

Mr. Stone's brow creased. He looked disappointed, though he shook his head. I wasn't looking for her specifically. I had hoped to draw on both of your strengths.

Ethan understood that he meant their strength as Trainers. What problem required both him and Erika?

Don't underestimate Misty because she's young, he said with a smile. Her sisters are the Gym Leaders of Cerulean Gym in Kanto. After this trip, she's going home to inherit the position. She's an excellent Water-type Trainer, and she's my best partner when I need help.

Misty felt a rush of emotion. His best partner? Was that really how Ethan saw her?

Oh? Mr. Stone looked at her anew. Then I misjudged you. I should have known that anyone traveling with Mr. Vale would be exceptional.

He had not expected a girl who looked barely into her teens to be so capable, much less to become a Gym Leader. But he trusted Ethan's judgment. The young man's skill and character had both been proven. If Ethan said Misty was strong, she was strong. Mr. Stone relaxed.

Now Ethan was more puzzled than ever. Mr. Stone, can you tell us why you called me here?

Of course. Mr. Stone led them to a large screen and nodded to a researcher. After a few keystrokes, a video appeared.

It showed a satellite's view of space. Stars glimmered against the dark, and Earth filled much of the frame. Its oceans, continents, mountains, and snowfields were clearly visible.

Is that our Earth? Misty asked.

She used the same name Ethan had used for the planet where he had lived before coming to this world. Here, though, it meant the planet they lived on now.

Yes, said Mr. Stone. That's our planet.

Misty nodded, wondering why he wanted to show them a view of Earth. Then she realized that Earth was not the subject of the recording.

An enormous object raced in from deep space. It looked something like a meteorite, though not quite. In an instant it struck the satellite's solar panel and destroyed it. The force sent the satellite tumbling.

Through the spinning view, they saw the strange meteorite continue toward Earth and strike a continent. Then the recording ended.

Misty was bewildered, but she recognized the shape of the land where it had fallen. That was Hoenn, wasn't it? Do you want us to find the meteorite?

Yes, Mr. Stone said. Though we've already located it. We ran into trouble when we tried to bring it back for study.

What kind of trouble? Misty asked. Radiation? Something else?

By then, Ethan had a good idea where this was going. Meteorites were not particularly rare in the Pokemon world. Research institutes studied them in hopes of discovering something useful inside. But one kind of meteorite was unlike the others.

Such a meteorite often carried a Pokemon from space within it. It could serve as the Pokemon's home and its means of travel, carrying it across the cosmos until it reached some far-off destination or fell like a shooting star onto an unfamiliar planet.

That Pokemon was Deoxys, the Mythical Psychic-type Pokemon.

After a pause, Mr. Stone asked, Have either of you heard of Deoxys?

Ethan said nothing. Misty glanced at him, then shook her head. Deoxys? Is that a Pokemon?

It is, Mr. Stone said. A friend of mine named Professor Lund encountered something extraordinary four years ago while conducting research in Antarctica. He had established a research station there when a meteorite landed nearby. A Pokemon no one had discovered before emerged from it. That Pokemon was Deoxys.

Ethan knew the incident Mr. Stone meant. It was the story of one of the Pokemon movies from his previous life.

Deoxys were not vanishingly few on this planet, either. At least five had appeared across the animated series and films Ethan knew, and two had appeared together in one film. Those were only the ones people had discovered. More might have landed in uninhabited regions or in the sea.

A Pokemon from space... Misty nodded. So there's a Deoxys inside that meteorite. You want us to catch it for you?

No. Mr. Stone sighed. I'm interested in the meteorite, not in catching a Pokemon. As you saw, it destroyed one of Devon's experimental satellites. The satellite is useless now, but that loss is minor. The meteorite's research value is what matters to me.

He went on. Rare elements, rare forms of energydiscovering and using them could teach us more about the universe and advance our technology. Once we identified the impact site, we sent armed teams several times to recover the meteorite. Deoxys defeated them all.

Why not ask the police for help? Misty asked.

Mr. Stone glanced at her. This is a matter of business competition. We received the information first and located the meteorite first. Naturally we want to retrieve it before anyone else. If we bring in the police, other interested parties will hear about it, and then...

He did not need to finish. Misty understood. She had simply never had to think about such corporate maneuvering before.

I see.

Mr. Stone turned back to Ethan with a smile. I imagine a Pokemon like Deoxys interests you too, Mr. Vale. So will you help us?

Of course I will, Ethan said, smiling.

Deoxys was rare, and Ethan genuinely liked it. He could hardly ignore the chance to meet one. Mr. Stone had probably counted on that. A Trainer of Ethan's ability would not be tempted by an ordinary Pokemon, but Deoxys was another matter.

Still, one question occurred to him. This is important. Why didn't you send Steven? I'm sure he could bring the meteorite back.

Mr. Stone gave a strained smile and said nothing. Kennedy answered for him.

We don't know where Master Steven has gone this time. We can't reach him by phone, and even satellite tracking has failed.

Ethan shook his head. Steven was probably deep in some cave, digging for stones. No wonder no signal could reach him there. If he loved digging so much, why hadn't he become a miner?

All right. There's no time to waste. I can leave now. Do you have a Poke Ball transfer machine here?

We do, Mr. Stone replied. What do you need it for?

To bring in some reinforcements. Ethan smiled. Deoxys won't be easy to face. If I'm going to beat it, I'll need some of my old team with me.

...

Every minute of delay gave someone else a chance to reach the meteorite first. Ethan accepted the assignment, exchanged the Poke Balls he needed, and left promptly with Misty. Mr. Stone saw them off as the helicopter rose from Devon's roof and headed toward the impact site.

Mr. Stone also supplied them with new equipment for the operation. Deoxys could alter magnetic fields, rendering ordinary communications and other devices useless nearby. Even many Electric-type Pokemon had been affected to some degree. The helicopter would have to land before it reached the worst of it.

Without equipment designed for those conditions, Ethan and Misty might find themselves living like modern-day primitives before they even found Deoxys.

Chapter 662: Fly! Dance!

Deep in the mountains near Lavaridge Town, in southwestern Hoenn, a helicopter flew over the foothills of Mt. Chimney. Meteor Falls was not far away.

Ethan looked out the window. After challenging Lavaridge Gym, he had planned to leave these mountains behind. Yet here he was again so soon. Things rarely went as expected.

He remembered catching Beldum here, encountering Professor Cozmo after Team Magma and Team Aqua kidnapped him, and then meeting Zinnia of the Draconid people during their escape. It all felt as though it had happened yesterday.

After a while, the helicopter descended onto a stretch of level ground. The person in the copilot's seat turned and raised his voice over the rotor noise.

The magnetic interference ahead is too strong. We can't fly any farther. You'll have to go on foot. Our people have set up an observation post farther along. Follow this path and meet them there first!

Ethan nodded. He and Misty gathered their equipment, climbed down, and set off in the indicated direction. Behind them, the helicopter took off again and soon vanished into the distance. The roar of its rotors faded at last, giving their ears a welcome rest.

Unlike Mt. Chimney's bare main slopes, these foothills were green. Trees covered the mountains, grass grew underfoot, and wild Pokemon appeared from time to time.

They had not walked far when Ethan saw a few simple tents ahead. Several men in Devon security uniforms stood guard outside. This had to be the observation post.

As they approached, a man who appeared to be the team leader came to meet them. Mr. Vale and Miss Misty?

He already knew who they were. Headquarters had sent word of their arrival, along with their photographs. He knew, too, that Ethan's strength far exceeded that of anyone on his team.

When Ethan nodded, the leader said, The meteorite is at the bottom of a small lake not far ahead. Would you like us to take you there?

No. There may be a battle. Leave it to us from here. Wait for me to contact you, then come and transport the meteorite.

Understood. Good luck, sir. Deoxys is extremely strong. It has injured a great many of our people, so please be careful.

Ethan and Misty left the post and followed the path toward the lake. Almost at once, they sensed that something was wrong. It was too quiet.

Before the observation post, they had seen wild Pokemon. Here there were none, and not even a cry broke the silence.

For once, Gengar emerged from Ethan's shadow on its own. Lately it had been absorbed in manga, showing itself only now and then at mealtimes. Ethan had barely spoken to it in ages.

It still held a manga volume, but it was no longer reading. It frowned at the surroundings. Something's wrong here. It makes my whole body feel uncomfortable.

Probably the magnetic field, Ethan said. Deoxys and its meteorite can alter it. Mr. Stone wouldn't have gone to all this trouble or asked me to help otherwise.

Ahead, a clear lake lay quietly among patches of forest. Nothing about it looked unusual.

Gengar stared toward it for a long moment. Be careful. I can feel a powerful presence up ahead. It should be Deoxys. I've felt something like this from only two other Pokemon.

Which ones? Ethan asked.

Mewtwo and Ho-Oh!

Mewtwo and Ho-Oh? Misty's eyes widened. Deoxys is that powerful?

Gengar shook its head. I mean the feeling it gives me, not necessarily its strength. It might have something to do with the magnetic field.

Ethan said nothing as he considered the warning. The movies had shown him how formidable Deoxys could be. It had even gained the upper hand for a time against Rayquazawhat Ethan jokingly thought of as Caterpie's ultimate evolution.

Deoxys could switch freely among Normal, Attack, Defense, and Speed Formes. It was highly intelligent, could alter the magnetic field around it, fly, dive into the sea, and regenerate at astonishing speed. Its powers were outrageous. An ordinary Pokemon would have little chance against it. That was why Ethan had changed his team before leaving Devon.

As they neared the lake, he sent out Gardevoir as a precaution. With her and Gengar beside them, he could at least be confident that he and Misty would be safe.

To his surprise, they reached the shore without being attacked.

Ethan checked his phone. There was no signal, and the battery was draining rapidly. Only seventeen percent remained. Kennedy's special communicator had been affected too, though it could still carry a broken conversation. Ethan had no idea what material it was made from.

Misty glanced from side to side. What do we do now? she asked softly. She looked as if she expected Deoxys to leap out at them at any moment.

Kennedy said the meteorite fell into this lake. I think Deoxys is hiding here too.

Misty studied the water. Pieces of a boat or aircraft drifted on its surface. They must be the remains of Devon's equipment, destroyed in the earlier attempts to retrieve the meteorite. Those fights had been disastrous, almost a complete rout.

How will you lure it out? she asked.

Lure it? Ethan shook his head and drew a Poke Ball from his pouch. I'm going to force it out.

He aimed the ball over the lake. Come out, Gyarados!

A flash of blue light revealed a gigantic red Gyarados above the water. For this mission, Ethan had brought back some of his strongest Pokemon. Once Kennedy told him the meteorite had landed in a lake, he knew there might be a battle in the water. He had contacted Chloe and asked her to transfer his red Gyarados to him.

He had brought other Pokemon too, but there was no need to reveal them yet.

Misty knew Gyarados belonged to Ethan and would obey him, but the sight of the terrifying giant still made her uneasy. It was simply so big.

Ethan had no attention to spare for her fear. He met Gyarados's red eyes and swept his right hand downward.

Do what you do best. Stir up the lake and drive that thing out!

Gyarados roared and plunged headfirst beneath the surface. Great waves rolled outward. At first they spread in regular circles, but as Gyarados churned the water below, the lake began to heave wildly. Nothing living down there could avoid the disturbance.

Ethan and Misty saw a red light flash beneath the surface. Then came a second, and a third. Water exploded upward. An orange-red, humanoid Pokemon flew out first, while Gyarados's vast jaws followed close behind, snapping at it.

The newcomer moved too quickly. Gyarados's bite closed on empty air.

Is that...? Misty hurriedly aimed her Pokedex at it.

Deoxys, the DNA Pokemon. Psychic type. No further data available.

So it was Deoxys.

Up close, it hardly looked like a Pokemon from Earth. Its orange-red body had an alien shape. Its arms twisted like strands of DNA, and its blue-green face resembled a mask. White circular eyes sat within rectangular black sockets. A crystalline structure ran through its chest, where a round, jewel-like core was embedded.

Misty found it frightening. It reminded her of the hunters in science fiction films: beings from an advanced civilization that regarded humans as prey and cared nothing for their lives.

She turned to Ethan, about to speak, and found his eyes shining with excitement.

As soon as Deoxys appeared, Ethan reached into his pouch again. Three Great Balls filled his hand. He tossed them high and called, Come out, my Pokemon!

Three large birds appeared in the sky: one red, one blue, and one yellow. They were Moltres, Articuno, and Zapdos.

Ethan had brought out the first of his hidden trump cards to face Deoxys. Before setting out, he had contacted Sabrina and had the three Legendary birds transferred back to him, just as Chloe had sent Gyarados.

The birds flew in wide circles overhead. Even while still inside their balls after the transfer, they had sensed their Trainer's purpose. Now they could feel the power of the unfamiliar Pokemon in the air with them. They recognized their target at once, and the prospect of battling it fired their fighting spirit.

On the ground, Ethan watched those familiar shapes and let out a long breath. His blood was stirring in a way it had not for some time.

He fixed his gaze on Deoxys. Fly! Dance! Let's defeat it!

At his signal, all three birds cried out and turned toward Deoxys. Zapdos loosed lightning. Moltres breathed fire. Articuno fired an Ice Beam. Powerful attacks of three different types converged on Deoxys from three directions.

Deoxys hovered in place, its cold eyes on the approaching birds. From their magnetic fields, it could tell they were unlike ordinary Pokemon. That was all the notice it gave them.

It raised its arms across its chest. A spherical barrier sprang up around it and easily stopped all three attacks.

Then its DNA-like arms drew together. A great ball of energy formed between them and shot toward Moltres, flying in the middle. Moltres could not dodge in time. The ball struck it head-on and exploded in a blinding flash.

Moltres was wounded, but strong enough to endure the blow. Furious now, the Fire-type broke away from the others. With Agility, it accelerated in an instant and lunged at Deoxys, claws extended. Articuno and Zapdos attacked from the sides to cover it.

Deoxys remained calm. Its barrier stopped the two supporting attacks. Then it changed from Normal Forme to Attack Forme, its arms dividing into four. As Moltres closed in, Deoxys slipped aside and lashed it with an arm like a whip.

Moltres was injured again.

The brief exchange made one thing clear: Deoxys was stronger than any one of the Legendary birds. But Ethan had not sent out all three so they could take turns fighting it alone.

They were too far away to hear him directly, so he had Gardevoir carry his command by telepathy. Don't get caught up fighting it one at a time. Use Tri-Bird Assault!

The combined technique of three Legendary Pokemon could deliver devastating force. The birds did not hesitate. They climbed higher, circling in wide, upward spirals.

A chill touched Misty. She looked up, and the sky had suddenly darkened. Clouds had gathered from nowhere, covering most of it in a thick black mass.

Her bangs stirred lightly.

The wind was rising...

Chapter 663: Defeat Them All!

We should get away from here, Ethan told Misty.

He signaled the red Gyarados to dive beneath the lake and shelter from the wide-ranging attack that was coming. Then he called Gardevoir to him through telepathy. She used Teleport to take Ethan and Misty to a distant peak.

Lightning, frost, and fire blazed in three colors against the dark clouds. A vortex of wind had formed and was drawing the clouds inward.

At Devon's observation post, several guards stared at the sky. They were too far away to see how Ethan was fighting Deoxys, or even which Pokemon he had sent out. But they had no doubt that the vast bank of black clouds was his doing.

He's incredible... a young guard said. Those clouds appeared out of nowhere. Is that what a tournament champion can do?

Don't be ridiculous, the team leader said, giving him a sideways look. A Pokemon League tournament winner is stronger than an average competitor, and luckier too, but could one normally make all this? A small patch of cloud, perhaps. This...

He looked up again. A change in the weather on this scale means those aren't ordinary Pokemon. It has to be them. Only they could do this.

The young guard swallowed. You mean Legendary Pokemon? Can someone really find and catch them, then bring them into a battle?

Who knows? People aren't all alike. It's a big world. Things beyond anything we can imagine must happen every day.

I still can't believe someone could encounter a Legendary Pokemon so easily.

You can't? The leader shook his head. What about Deoxys? Most people have never seen one. We've been fighting it for the past two days. Isn't that proof enough?

I suppose it is...

Above the clouds, Moltres, Zapdos, and Articuno flew with the rolling vapor as though performing a strange dance. With each beat of their wings, energy flowed from their bodies into the cloud mass.

Below them, Deoxys sensed the danger. Perhaps it could see in the clouds the powerful magnetic fields that now threatened it. It brought all four arms together and fired an energy ball larger and stronger than the first one into the sky.

The ball raced toward the Legendary birds. But they were far enough away to see it coming, and dodged with ease. It exploded in the clouds, scattering a broad swath of them. More clouds rushed in to fill the gap. The attack had achieved nothing.

Then the birds' dance stopped. Tri-Bird Assault was ready. This would be only the second time they had shown it before other people.

Water, lightning, and fire particles broke apart, reformed, and joined in the clouds. A brilliant column of energy, more than ten meters across and wider still as it poured downward, fell like a waterfall from the sky. Its radiance lit the dark day like a sun beneath the black clouds.

Deoxys hovered at the center of the attack's path. The glare forced it to shield its eyes with an arm. Most Pokemon would have fled from a strike they could not withstand. Deoxys did not move. It meant to take the attack with its own strength.

It was stubborn, at least.

Deoxys changed from Attack Forme to Defense Forme. Its body grew heavier, as though sheathed in thick armor. Then it raised its arms before its chest and formed another spherical barrier.

The barrier had barely appeared when Tri-Bird Assault reached it. Energy crashed down like a wave, engulfing Deoxys completely. The next instant, an explosion sent a terrible mushroom cloud rising from the ground.

The earth shook. A shock wave swept all the way to Ethan and Misty. On the peak, Misty ducked behind Ethan. Gardevoir and Gengar protected them both.

Once the blast passed, Ethan peered out at the devastation. He had seen this attack once before, yet its destructive power still astonished him.

Deoxys couldn't have died in that, could it? Misty asked.

Died? No. It's not that fragile. I'm wondering whether it was injured at all.

Not injured? Misty stared at him. How could anything withstand an attack like that?

Back at the observation post, Devon's guards still gaped at the distant blast. A violent gust blew dust into their open mouths. Before they could spit it out, the ground trembled beneath them and they nearly lost their footing. When the shock finally subsided, they cleared their mouths and hurried to look toward the battlefield again.

C-c-captain!

Quiet! I see it!

Before, they had only suspected Ethan had a Legendary Pokemon. Now they were certain. No ordinary Pokemon could cause an explosion like that. Only human technologyor a Legendary Pokemoncould do it.

Even that immense explosion finally faded. A great crater had opened beside the lake, and water poured into it. The last smoke drifted away from its center. Before they could make out what lay behind it, a pair of cold eyes opened.

Misty looked hard. There was Deoxys, covered in wounds, with only half its body remaining.

It... She stopped, horrified by its condition. Then the missing parts began to grow back before her eyes.

Rapid regeneration! In only a few breaths, Deoxys had restored itself. It looked just as it had before the attack.

That's unbelievable, Misty said. It really survived that hit.

Ethan nodded, his face impassive. This was what made Deoxys so formidable.

Was Tri-Bird Assault strong? Unquestionably. Three Legendary Pokemon combined their power in a technique far greater than the sum of three separate attacks. Even other Legendary Pokemon would have reason to avoid it.

He believed Mewtwo, Ho-Oh, Groudon, and Kyogre could survive a direct hit, though each would be hurt to a different degree. Perhaps none but Arceusnot even Eternamax Eternatus or the ice pillar Regicewould come through it as well as Deoxys had.

Defense Forme, the energy barrier, and changes within its DNA and cells had all reduced the force that reached its body. But those defenses were secondary. Deoxys's real advantage was its regeneration.

As long as its core remained intact, it could eventually recover from almost any injury, even the destruction of its head, limbs, or body. Sometimes that took seconds; at other times it might take three or four years. It would return whole, without a scar on the surface, though the process cost it a great deal of mental energy.

Every Pokemon had its distinguishing traits. Deoxys, born from a mutated virus from space, had a capacity to heal that seemed to defy reason.

That did not mean it could not be defeated or killed. If it suffered enough attacks in a short time, its mental energy would run out. That was the possibility Ethan was counting on. He could keep attacking until Deoxys could no longer endure it.

He looked up at the three Legendary birds. Tri-Bird Assault had drained most of their energy. They could still fight, but they could no longer carry the battle. Ethan had never intended to depend on them alone.

He reached into his pouch and took out two more Great Balls. Misty knew what they held: Suicune and Raikou. She marveled at how many powerful Pokemon Ethan could call upon. His second wave of attacks was about to begin.

But before he could release them, something unexpected happened.

Thirty or forty people emerged along a ridge to the left of the battlefield. Their matching orange-red uniforms marked them as Team Magma. Ethan recognized the hooded young woman leading them: Courtney.

That was not all. A second group appeared on a ridge to his right, more than fifty people dressed in blue and white stripes. Team Aqua had arrived too. At their head stood Shelly, whom Ethan also knew.

Wonderful. Everyone he had hoped to avoid had shown up. Not long ago, he had been the one disrupting their operations. Now they had come to make trouble for him.

Ethan lowered the two Great Balls and watched coldly.

Shelly surveyed the battlefield with a hand on her hip and a smug smile. Well, well. What have we found? A Pokemon we've never seen before, three Legendary birds, and one irritating rat. What an unexpected treat.

Courtney said nothing. She turned and fixed Ethan with a cold stare.

After he had disrupted their plans repeatedly, both teams had investigated him. They knew he was a two-time tournament champion from Kanto and Johto, and they had learned just how powerful he was. Courtney intended to settle their scores today.

Ethan felt their undisguised hostility and smiled. I'm rather busy. Could you leave?

Shelly regarded him with an amused half-smile. What do you think?

Dream on, Courtney said flatly.

So there's no room to negotiate? Ethan spread his hands.

Of course there is. Shelly licked her lips, danger flashing in her eyes. Once I've caught you, we can negotiate exactly how I should punish you.

Before Ethan could answer, Courtney said, That won't happen. He's mine.

Yours? Shelly turned toward her with a laugh. You'd better leave while you can. Both the man and that Pokemon are already Team Aqua's.

She had reason for her confidence. Team Aqua had brought more people and Pokemon than Team Magma. She had also seen Ethan and Deoxys fighting. They had been at it for some time, and both sides appeared depleted. To Shelly, the advantage was hers.

Three sides now faced one another, each determined to defeat the others and claim whatever could be won here. Yet both teams had underestimated something.

Surrounded by them all, Deoxys had had enough.

Blue light shot from its core into the sky. A vast blue aurora appeared from nowhere and spread over most of the battlefield. Strange, winding curtains of light hung down. It was beautiful.

Everyone looked up instinctively. At the same moment, Deoxys changed from Defense Forme back to Attack Forme and began to attack without distinguishing friend from foe.

An energy ball formed at the end of each of its four arms. With a slight motion, Deoxys launched them toward Ethan, the three Legendary birds, Team Magma, and Team Aqua.

It would defeat them all.

Chapter 664: A Four-Sided Battle

Boom! Boom! Boom! Boom!

The four energy balls exploded one after another, and the battlefield fell into chaos.

The ball aimed at the three Legendary birds came from too far away to catch them. They dodged it easily. Gengar met the one aimed at Ethan and Misty with a Shadow Ball, canceling it out. Gardevoir raised a barrier with her psychic power to stop the remaining shock wave before it reached the two Trainers.

The other two explosions, aimed at Team Aqua and Team Magma, caused much more trouble. Their members stood close together, and none had expected the Pokemon they had surrounded to strike first. They tried to scatter when they saw the energy balls, but some were inevitably caught in the blasts.

That was the signal for the battle to begin in earnest.

Courtney and Shelly had both escaped the attacks. Each looked back to assess her team's losses. The damage was still manageable, but they could no longer afford to wait. The two commanders issued orders to attack almost at the same moment.

Remarkably, both teams set aside their hostility toward each other. Neither attacked its longtime rival. They focused instead on Ethan and Deoxys.

Ethan had foiled their plans repeatedly. As long as he remained free to interfere, neither organization could rest easy. Deoxys, meanwhile, was a Pokemon of extraordinary power. Capturing it would give either team a stronger position when the time came to face Groudon or Kyogre.

Water from the lake surged through the breach into the enormous crater left by Tri-Bird Assault. Some flowed through collapsed ground toward other parts of the battlefield. In a short time the lake level dropped noticeably, and much of the ground became muddy. Soon the waterlogged areas would join into one. No one paid attention; Courtney and Shelly had ordered all their people forward.

Hundreds of flashes of blue light appeared. Almost every member of both teams released two or three Pokemon at once. The ridges on either side filled with Water-type and Fire-type Pokemon. There was no reserve. The teams meant to overwhelm their opponents with numbers and Pokemon that were, individually, capable enough.

It was a simple, old-fashioned plan. Sometimes that was all it took to catch an enemy off guard.

Seeing roughly half the people on each ridge rush toward him, Ethan threw the two Great Balls in his hands. Raikou and Suicune appeared, one on either side.

Their types were exactly what he needed. At his signal, Raikou charged toward Team Aqua while Suicune moved to stop Team Magma. Electric and Water attacks gave them an advantage against the two organizations' Pokemon.

Even so, two Legendary Pokemon could not face such numbers alone. Concentrated attacks would eventually drive them back, type advantages or not. Fortunately, Ethan had brought more of his old mainstays.

He drew four Poke Balls from his pouch and threw them. Charizard, Venusaur, Blastoise, and Jolteon appeared before him. All four had traveled through Kanto with Ethan. Every one of them was strong.

Chloe had sent Blastoise, Venusaur, and Jolteon from Cerise Park along with the red Gyarados. Ethan had also contacted Liza, who sent his Charizard from the Charicific Valley. With so many longtime partners at his side, Ethan's team was as strong as it had ever been. Even one of the Elite Four would have to take it seriously.

Through Gardevoir's telepathy, Ethan told the three Legendary birds to draw back a little from Deoxys. They could keep it occupied, but he wanted them out of the two teams' attacks as much as possible and conserving their remaining strength.

He kept Gardevoir and Gengar close to protect himself and Misty. Then he sent out the four newly released Pokemon to support Raikou and Suicune. Charizard and Blastoise headed for Team Magma; Jolteon and Venusaur raced toward Team Aqua.

The four-sided battle was underway.

Most of Team Magma's Pokemon were Houndoom, Mightyena, and Golbat, with some Magcargo and Camerupt among them. Except for the flying Golbat, they moved slowly across the spreading lake water. They had to pick their way from one dry patch to another to keep their bodies out of it.

Team Aqua advanced faster. Its force consisted mostly of Crawdaunt and Walrein, with a smaller number of Pelipper. The flowing water helped them close the distance. They were the first to reach both Ethan's Pokemon and Deoxys, and the first to engage them.

More than a dozen Walrein fired Water Guns at Raikou together. Raikou leaped aside and gathered electricity, ready to send a shock back through the streams. Before it could do so, several Crawdaunt charged in with their huge claws raised.

Raikou frowned and sprang away again. The moment it landed, more Water Guns came at it. The attacks were relentless and irritating.

Then two Vine Whips lashed in from the side and broke the jets into sprays of droplets. Raikou glanced back to find Venusaur and Jolteon arriving. It nodded to them and turned its full attention to the fight.

With partners beside it, the pressure eased. Raikou no longer had to guard every direction at once. Powerful electricity flashed across the field each time it attacked. None of Team Aqua's Water-type Pokemon could take a direct shock from the Legendary Pokemon without being badly hurt.

Jolteon fought differently. Smaller and faster than Raikou, it darted back and forth through the crowd. No Water-type could keep up, and it struck Pokemon with electric attacks as it passed.

Venusaur lacked their speed and was too large to avoid becoming a target. It held its ground beside Raikou instead, each covering the other's back as they dealt with opponents one at a time.

In any small encounter, the three had the advantage. Team Aqua, however, had brought far too many Pokemon. Even with half its force attacking Deoxys and another portion occupied by Raikou's group, plenty of them used the spreading water to circle around toward Ethan and Misty.

When more than a dozen Team Aqua Pokemon bore down on them, Gengar and Gardevoir stepped in front of Ethan. They were his most reliable guards. Even a Legendary Pokemon would struggle to hurt their Trainer while they stood beside him.

Before they could act, Misty raised her hand and threw her own Poke Balls. Starmie, Politoed, Corsola, and Psyduck appeared.

Ahem... Misty promptly recalled Psyduck, which had let itself out again without permission. She turned to Ethan as if nothing had happened. Don't forget me. Let me help too!

Ethan smiled. How could I forget you? I was just about to ask.

At Misty's direction, her other three Pokemon joined Gengar and Gardevoir and met the approaching Team Aqua force.

Across the battlefield, Team Magma's Pokemon had engaged Suicune, Charizard, and Blastoise. Suicune was more measured than the fierce Raikou, but its attacks were no less powerful.

The first opponents they met were Golbat flying overhead. The nimble bats kept their distance like a swarm of flies, harassing Suicune with Air Slash and Supersonic. It worked. Suicune grew frustrated, while its Water Guns struggled to hit such agile targets.

Charizard soon dived through them like a dragon, scattering the Golbat. During its time away from Ethan at the Charicific Valley, it had grown considerably. Ethan did not yet know exactly how strong it had become, but it was visibly larger and more muscular.

Liza had told him that his Charizard and Ash's were now challenging the strongest Charizard in the valley. They had yet to succeed, but both were steadily improving.

Charizard breathed fire and drove the Golbat back. A few stubborn ones tried to attack it. Charizard wheeled in the air, caught one with a claw, and squeezed until the Golbat went limp. Then it tossed it to the ground.

Below, Blastoise stood beside Suicune and filled the defensive role Venusaur played on the other side of the battlefield. Its thick hide and shell let it take punishment. The two heavy cannons on its back poured out Water Guns at any of Team Magma's Fire-type Pokemon that dared come close.

With the Golbat no longer harassing it, Suicune could use its power freely. Where Blastoise fired from its cannons, Suicune needed only to guide its energy with an elegant motion to send great waves of water surging over Team Magma's Pokemon.

That side of the battle also seemed to be turning in Ethan's favor. Yet, as with Team Aqua, Team Magma had so many Pokemon that some could always slip around the defenders and attack Ethan. Each one added pressure to the last line protecting him and Misty.

For the moment, Ethan was safe. He looked past the fighting around him toward Deoxys.

It faced nearly half of Team Magma and Team Aqua on its own, while still having to guard against attacks from the three Legendary birds. Deoxys showed no fear. In Attack Forme, it was devastating. Whenever one of its strikes landed, an opposing Pokemon fell.

The sight worried Shelly and Courtney, but tempted them too. Every injured team member or defeated Pokemon was a loss to their organizations' fighting strength. Yet Deoxys's terrible power could help either woman fulfill her team's ambitions if she captured it.

They needed to work out how to catch Deoxys and defeat Ethan. Their greed was already costing them. Had either team committed most of its strength against one opponent and left only enough Pokemon to keep the other from escaping, it might have beaten them in turn. Instead both teams wanted Ethan and Deoxys at once. Neither dared leave an opening for its rival. Their forces were stretched thin, the battle was stalling, and they were slowly losing ground.

It was not the result either commander had expected. After a moment's hesitation, both women led their elite squads into the fight.

Shelly took Team Aqua's best members straight toward Deoxys. Courtney led Team Magma's best toward Ethan.

They noticed their different choices at the same time. Each glanced back across the field, surprised and baffled by the other's decision.

To Shelly, the obvious move was to catch Deoxys first, then deal with Ethan. He had five Legendary Pokemon in his possession. Despite her confident talk before the battle, she thought securing Deoxys was the safer choice. If Ethan escaped, Team Aqua would at least have gained something.

Courtney saw it differently. Deoxys was valuable, but it was not essential. Her main target was the infuriating man who had ruined their operations again and again. This was a rare chance to capture him. Then he would be at her mercy, and his Pokemon would belong to Team Magma. With so many Legendary Pokemon under their control, catching Deoxys afterward would be easy.

Neither plan was plainly right or wrong. But once each woman saw the other pursuing a different target, both were satisfied. They could concentrate on their own objectives without worrying quite as much about a knife in the back.

They led their squads forward. Each had six or seven elite members beside her, people better trained than the ordinary grunts and equipped with stronger Pokemon.

As soon as Courtney joined the assault, Ethan felt the pressure rise sharply. Why did she hate him so much? She was ignoring Team Aqua and Deoxys to come after him. Weren't the two organizations supposed to be bitter enemies?

On the Team Magma side, the new arrivals tipped the battle against him. Strong as his Pokemon were, Suicune, Charizard, and Blastoise could not face so many attackers at once.

Ethan frowned and told them through Gardevoir's telepathy to fight as they withdrew toward him. Then he surveyed the rest of the battlefield.

Team Magma had pulled some of its people away from Deoxys to reinforce Courtney. Only a smaller group remained there, mostly to watch Team Aqua press its attack. Courtney truly meant to defeat Ethan in one push.

Team Aqua, meanwhile, was drawing members away from its fight with Ethan to help Shelly surround Deoxys. The few who stayed behind fought cautiously to keep Ethan occupied. That shift had at least eased the pressure on his other flank.

Ethan used Gardevoir's telepathy to send new orders across the field. Raikou and Venusaur would stay and attack the Team Aqua Pokemon that remained. Jolteon would return and join the fight against Team Magma.

He also told the three Legendary birds to stop attacking Deoxys and target only the Team Aqua force surrounding it.

They really have underestimated me. Team Aqua wanted Deoxys? He was not going to let them take it.

Ethan turned back to his own position. Suicune, Charizard, and Blastoise were still fighting as they retreated. They were now only a few dozen meters away. At his signal, Gengar and Misty's Pokemon moved up to support them, joining the front line. Only Gardevoir remained beside Ethan and Misty for protection.

Misty hesitated. The fight no longer looked as easy as it had before; their side seemed to be at a disadvantage. She took out Psyduck's Poke Ball and released it again.

Oh, fine. You may be an idiot, but surely you can help protect Ethan and me...

Chapter 665: Meeting Zinnia Again

Courtney still had her Camerupt, but this time she had also released a Weezing. One fought on the ground and the other in the air, working together.

The other Team Magma elites used the same kinds of Pokemon as their ordinary members, but theirs were noticeably stronger. Their arrival lifted the morale of the grunts, whose earlier attacks had failed to break through. Ethan had to devote most of his attention to stopping them.

Through Gardevoir's telepathy, he sent precise orders to his Pokemon.

Charizard, drive those Golbat overhead away with Flamethrower. Don't let them attack from above.

Blastoise, switch from Water Gun to Hydro Pump. Aim at the Camerupt. They're slower and easier to hit.

Jolteon, use your speed to draw the Mightyena after you.

Suicune, use your strongest attacks wherever the enemy Pokemon are thickest.

And Gengar, stop holding back. Show them what you can really do!

His Pokemon moved into their assigned roles. With Misty's Pokemon helping, they barely held Team Magma's charge. The line shifted back and forth, but they kept the fighting near the foot of the peak where Ethan stood.

A stalemate was not what he wanted. He turned to Gardevoir. Go down and help them.

She hesitated. Ethan understood why and laughed. Don't worry. Psyduck is still here. I'm sure it can protect us.

Psyduck? Gardevoir gave the vacant duck a cool glance. It stood there looking at her with its head tilted. She could not bring herself to entrust Ethan's safety to it. Her worry reached him through telepathy.

Ethan's smile faded. He patted her shoulder. It's all right. I still have one more card to play. If things turn bad, I'll take care of myself.

She did not trust Psyduck any more than before, but she reluctantly turned and joined the battle. Her arrival could not reverse the situation on its own. It did ease the pressure on the Pokemon at the front.

The enemy still had an overwhelming advantage in numbers. No matter how well Ethan's Pokemon fought, they could not cover every gap.

Courtney and two elite grunts broke through. They climbed the peak and came face-to-face with Ethan.

When Misty saw them, she pulled Psyduck in front of her and stepped before Ethan. You've always looked after me and protected me, Ethan. Today it's my turn.

She faced the hooded girl with purple hair. You won't hurt Ethan while I'm here!

Courtney gave Misty no more than a glance. Her eyes paused for a second on Psyduck, then moved past them to Ethan.

Why go to all this trouble? Ethan asked Courtney, shaking his head. Despite the enemy reaching him, he remained remarkably calm. Team Aqua is surrounding Deoxys. Aren't they your sworn rivals? Are you really going to ignore them?

Them? Courtney's mouth twisted in a cold smile. Shelly thinks she's clever. She believes one Pokemon can change everything. I know better. People like you are the greatest obstacle to Team Magma's goal.

She had seen the problem clearly. Finding Groudon would be difficult, but if Team Magma searched carefully and followed every clue, they would find it eventually, provided it still lived. What truly hindered them were powerful Trainers who repeatedly interfered with their plans. Each intervention made success harder and failure more likely. Removing Ethan was the wiser priority.

Ethan shrugged. Then I have one last question. Were you hiding here waiting for me to show up?

It was a reasonable concern. Devon had asked him to help recover the meteorite only an hour or two ago, yet both teams had arrived with substantial forces and seemed ready for him. Had they learned where he was going, assembled their people, and located him that quickly? If so, something was badly wrong. There might even be an informant inside Devon.

Courtney did not answer. She was close enough to attack him now; she had no reason to explain herself. At her signal, the two elite grunts ordered their Pokemon forward too.

Psyduck, stop them! Misty shouted.

Psyduck tilted its head and did nothing, as though it had not understood a word.

Its inaction did not make it safe. It stood between the attackers and their target, so Team Magma's Pokemon chose it first. Several streams of fire surged toward Psyduck.

It might be foolish, but it could recognize danger. Psyduck dodged frantically. One stream still caught its tail. As a Water-type, it took only half the usual damage from the flames, but the burn hurt enough to send it running in circles with its tail clutched in its hands.

Courtney and the grunts stared. On their way up the peak, they had seen how powerful the Pokemon defending Ethan were. How could this one be so helpless? Did it really belong to the same side?

Whatever the explanation, Courtney welcomed it. How could such a weak Pokemon protect anyone?

Misty grew desperate. Psyduck, pull yourself together! Use Confusion!

Psyduck heard none of it. It kept racing around, holding its tail.

I'm such an idiot, Misty thought. Why did I trust Psyduck? I shouldn't have brought it on this journey. Regret was useless now. She had no other Pokemon left with her.

Ethan had never depended on Psyduck to keep him safe. He watched the Team Magma members close in and touched his wrist, ready to speak. Then he heard a sound behind him.

As he turned, a blue, winged Pokemon with four limbs rushed past. It slammed headfirst into a Mightyena that had been about to attack Ethan and sent it flying.

What?

Ethan was startled. Courtney frowned and looked sharply past him. A black-haired girl in a cape braced her hand on a rock and vaulted out from behind it.

Ethan and Misty recognized her at once: Zinnia of the Draconid people, whom they had met near Meteor Falls.

So she was here too. Why?

Ethan finally got a clear look at the Pokemon that had struck Mightyena. It was a Salamence, surely Zinnia's.

Zinnia! Misty's face brightened. Did you come to save us?

To Misty, they had been on the verge of being overwhelmed. Zinnia's timely arrival felt like a rescue.

Zinnia hurried to their side. She first directed Salamence to drive back several Pokemon pressing in on them, then turned to Ethan and Misty.

I've been here for a while. I was watching you from behind that rock. She studied Ethan with amazement. You kept a lot hidden. I saw Raikou last time, but I never imagined you had this many Legendary Pokemon.

Born and raised in these mountains, Zinnia was evidently good at hiding. Ethan had not noticed her at all.

Everyone has secrets. He lowered his right hand from his left wrist and smiled at her. Why are you here? You didn't come just to watch, did you?

Zinnia admired his composure. Psyduck was the only Pokemon left beside him, and the rest were fighting at the front. Yet he showed no fear with enemies so close. Where did his confidence come from?

Perhaps she had stepped in too soon. If she had waited a little longer, she might have discovered whether Ethan was bluffing or had another way to turn the fight around. But she could not have watched silently while he and Misty were attacked.

Of course not, she said. The thoughts passed quickly, and she looked Ethan in the eye. You don't really think Devon was the first to find that meteorite, do you?

Ethan understood what she was suggesting. You found it?

Zinnia did not answer immediately. She glanced at Salamence, still battling Team Magma. It was strong enough to hold its own against Courtney's Camerupt and the two elite grunts' Pokemon together. Satisfied, she turned back to him.

I found it three days ago, when it fell here. I saw the powerful Pokemon that came with it too.

Ethan knew she meant Deoxys, so he waited for her to continue.

Remember when we talked about Rayquaza in that cave?

Of course. Ethan knew more about Rayquaza than Zinnia realized.

Zinnia drew a breath. After that Pokemon appeared, Rayquaza came. It dropped out of the sky and fought it. Their battle shook the mountains and frightened away all the wild Pokemon nearby.

Now Ethan understood the unnatural silence beyond Devon's observation post. The wild Pokemon had fled the area three days earlier.

What happened next? Misty asked.

Both were injured. The other Pokemon went back into the water and fought Devon's people the next day. Rayquaza returned to the sky, and I haven't seen it since.

Ethan realized why Zinnia had stayed. As one of the Draconid people, she wanted to see Rayquaza again, perhaps even speak with it. She had been waiting here in hope of its return. Instead she had watched Ethan and Misty arrive.

Misty swallowed. Do you think Rayquaza will really come back?

It will! Zinnia nodded firmly. It's territorial, and it doesn't let a defeat go. It left wounded. Once it heals, it'll return for revenge.

Ethan could not say whether Rayquaza would return. It might, or it might not. Zinnia, though, needed to believe it would. For the Draconid people, this might be the closest they had come to Rayquaza in hundreds of years. Her chance to meet it could come only once in her lifetime.

Misty saw the sudden light in Zinnia's eyes and wisely kept her question to herself: Would you try to catch Rayquaza if it came?

Rayquaza and the Draconid people's plans were not her concern. She wanted Ethan and herself to survive this battle. Legendary Pokemon were beyond her ability to catch anyway.

Ethan glanced at Courtney nearby. What about these people? When did they arrive?

Team Magma and Team Aqua? Zinnia shook her head. They got lucky. They've been roaming these mountains since you rescued Professor Cozmo. They noticed the fight between Rayquaza and that Pokemon a few days ago, so they came to see what they might find.

Chapter 666: Rayquaza's Grand Entrance

Once Zinnia explained how the two teams had come here, Ethan breathed easier. Thank goodness. Team Aqua and Team Magma had stumbled on the situation by chance and tried to take advantage of it, much as Ethan had disrupted their plans before. That was far better news than a leak inside Devon.

No wonder Courtney had refused to answer his question. It was hardly an impressive plan to boast about.

The fighting below had settled into another stalemate. Team Magma could not break through, and Ethan's Pokemon could not yet push them back.

Close to Ethan, Zinnia released an Altaria to join Salamence. Zinnia might have been a little stronger than Courtney, though not so much stronger that she could overwhelm her. With Salamence and Altaria working together, she could hold Courtney and the elite Team Magma members to a draw despite their greater numbers.

On the other side of the valley, Team Aqua had made no real progress against Deoxys either. They had tried to account for its power and still underestimated it. With the three Legendary birds harassing Team Aqua, Deoxys was wreaking havoc. Even the elite members' Pokemon fell quickly before it. Only Shelly's Pokemon posed any meaningful threat.

Team Aqua did have numbers. Like ants wearing down a snake, they might eventually exhaust Deoxys's stamina and mental energy. They could defeat and capture it, though at a terrible costif the Legendary birds stopped interfering.

Ethan had not recalled the birds even when his own position was in danger. He clearly had no intention of giving Team Aqua that chance. As far as he was concerned, their dream of catching Deoxys could remain a dream.

Water continued spreading through the valley. In places, it was already more than half a meter deep. Battles raged everywhere. Fire and Water-type attacks reflected in countless pools, coloring one side of the valley fiery red and the other blue.

Then the sky changed again.

A great mass of dark clouds appeared overhead. Almost at the same moment, Deoxys, Raikou, Suicune, Moltres, Zapdos, and Articuno all raised their heads. The other Pokemon followed their gazes, and some stopped fighting altogether.

Ethan had nothing to do with this change in the weather. He sensed the disturbance and looked up with Misty. Courtney and Zinnia paused as well.

Before everyone's eyes, a Pokemon burst through the clouds and descended.

It was enormous and long-bodied. Green segments ran down its dragonlike form. Two long, flat, hornlike structures rose from its head, with two smaller ones below. Its two limbs ended in three-clawed hands. Red-edged, rudderlike fins projected from its shoulders and lower body, with a similar fin at the tip of its tail. Yellow rings patterned its length.

Most people present had never seen it before. Even so, one name came to mind for all of them: Rayquaza.

It's Rayquaza! Misty cried. It really came back!

Ethan glanced down beside him. Zinnia was trembling with excitement. She had believed Rayquaza might return, but even she had not expected it to appear so suddenly. This time, she vowed to herself, she would not miss her chance.

Team Aqua and Team Magma reacted very differently. At first, they had merely been searching the Mt. Chimney area for their own purposes. Even when the meteorite fell nearby, neither team had cared. Their goals were Groudon and Kyogre. What use was a mere space rock?

Only after hearing that a powerful Pokemon had appeared near the impact site did they gather their forces and come to capture it. Finding Ethan already fighting that Pokemon had delighted them. They might take the creature and eliminate a persistent enemy in one operation.

The rival team's arrival had been a surprise, but each group knew the other well enough to put it aside and focus on its own target. Despite some setbacks, the plan had seemed to be progressing.

Rayquaza's appearance changed everything. Capturing one Deoxys was already taking all their strength. How could they deal with another Pokemon of that caliber? Neither team had come to capture Rayquaza, but having it above them filled everyone with dread. Even the aftershocks of a fight involving it could kill them.

Rayquaza did not pause after breaking through the clouds. It flew straight at Deoxys. Shelly's expression changed. As Zinnia had said, Rayquaza was territorial and quick to seek revenge. Wounded in their earlier battle, it had now returned to settle the score.

Deoxys reacted at once. It abandoned the Team Aqua Pokemon surrounding it, rose into the sky, and met Rayquaza head-on.

Beside Ethan, Zinnia suddenly sprinted toward the ground beneath the two. Salamence and Altaria broke away from Team Magma and followed her.

Gardevoir! Ethan called.

Gardevoir, still fighting Team Magma farther away, used Teleport and appeared at his side. Ethan did not try to stop Zinnia. Instead he quickly told the three Legendary birds through telepathy to withdraw.

Deoxys and Rayquaza would fight until one fell or both were badly hurt. Ethan did not want his Pokemon caught between them. He could conserve their strength and watch for a chance to benefit from the outcome. With Zinnia gone, the birds could also return to protect him and Misty.

Above them, Deoxys and Rayquaza were already fighting. They seemed to see only each other, recognizing an opponent of equal standing. They chased, struck, and defended from sky to mountain, from mountain to ground, and back into the sky.

Their blows shook the earth. Mountainsides collapsed, trees were destroyed, craters opened, and even the shape of the land changed. Nothing nearby escaped the effects of their battle.

The three Legendary birds beat their wings and returned to Ethan. Courtney saw them arrive and immediately withdrew her people from his position.

She had struggled badly enough against one Raikou before. Facing three Pokemon of that same legendary rank with only her two grunts would be absurd. She did not leave the area, though. She drew the rest of Team Magma out of the fighting and gathered them together nearby.

Ethan glanced at her and looked away. Courtney apparently intended, as he did, to wait and make a move when the struggle overhead was over.

Team Aqua had it worse. Rayquaza and Deoxys were fighting right beside its people. After surrounding Deoxys earlier, they could not retreat even if Shelly ordered it.

Deoxys fired an energy ball that missed Rayquaza and blasted several Team Aqua Pokemon away instead. Rayquaza charged with its enormous body. Deoxys turned aside, leaving several Team Aqua members on a rock in its path. Rayquaza struck the rock and sent them flying into the air with it.

They were paying dearly for being so close.

With the birds guarding them and Ethan's other Pokemon withdrawing, Misty finally felt safe enough to take out her Pokedex. She aimed it at Rayquaza.

Rayquaza, the Sky High Pokemon. Dragon and Flying type. It is said to have lived in Earth's ozone layer for hundreds of millions of years. Flying at night, it resembles a shooting star. It lives so high above the clouds that it cannot be seen from the ground. It appears to feed on water and particles in the atmosphere, and it also eats meteorites.

Humans knew far more about Rayquaza than they did about Deoxys, partly because technology had improved. Satellites, spacecraft, and other objects sent skyward sometimes caught glimpses of it passing through the ozone layer. Repeated sightings and observation had given researchers a rough picture of its habits.

That was still only a rough picture. Its abilities, origins, birth, and reproduction remained mysteries.

Rayquaza... Misty lowered her Pokedex and watched it intently. She knew it belonged among Pokemon of Ho-Oh's stature and that the Draconid people had long revered and guarded it.

Thinking of the Draconids, she searched for Zinnia. The cloaked girl was running across broken rocks and flooded ground toward the other battlefield, forcing her way through every obstacle.

What is she trying to do? Misty asked.

Isn't it obvious? Ethan watched too. Whether they call it protection, inheritance, or something else, the Draconid people have always wanted one thing...

He did not finish, but Misty understood. Deoxys could be right in front of Zinnia, as could Kyogre or Groudon, and she would not care. She wanted to catch Rayquaza.

Zinnia had already reached the center of the battle. Explosions burst nearby, and other Pokemon blocked her path, but none stopped her from running toward Rayquaza. Her resolve carried her through.

Could she truly catch it on her own?

Above the valley, the fight had reached its fiercest point. Rayquaza's attacks had destroyed parts of Deoxys's body several times. Each time, rapid regeneration restored it. Rayquaza was suffering too. Deoxys's blows in Attack Forme were powerful enough to hurt even a Legendary Pokemon.

Still, Rayquaza appeared to hold a slight advantage.

Another collision shook the mountains. A small hill in the distance was flattened outright.

Zinnia tried calling to Rayquaza. She held up several bright, shining objects to catch its attention. Rayquaza ignored the tiny human beneath it, absorbed in the fight. Her voice vanished beneath the explosions.

Desperate, she ordered Salamence and Altaria to attack Rayquaza. They had barely entered the space where Rayquaza and Deoxys fought when the two Pokemon struck them down.

Zinnia had no way into the battle. Ethan shook his head. She had acted too hastily. How could she hope to catch Rayquaza amid this chaos without clearing away the people and Pokemon around it? Even speaking to it would require a better place and time.

He turned his attention back to the two combatants. Their furious exchange was draining them quickly. After only a few minutes, Deoxys had spent much of its stamina. Its movements and attacks visibly slowed. It was finally tiring. It had fought for a long time and regenerated more times than anyone could count.

Rayquaza was covered in wounds of different sizes and had begun to breathe heavily as well.

Almost everyone's eyes brightened. Both Pokemon were nearing their limits. If anyone meant to act, this was the moment.

Chapter 667: Mega Red Gyarados!

Team Aqua had been close to collapse. Seeing Rayquaza and Deoxys tire, Shelly gritted her teeth and ordered an all-out attack.

She could no longer afford caution. She could retreat in disgrace, as Team Aqua had before, and accept another defeat. Or she could stake everything on one last attempt. Withdrawing now would waste all they had done, leave them with heavy losses, and crush their morale. Continuing might fail toobut after a few tense seconds, Shelly made her choice.

Gather everyone we have left! Ignore Rayquaza. Target that powerful Pokemonattack!

At her urging, the remaining Team Aqua members regrouped and launched a final assault on Deoxys.

The shift caught the attention of Ethan and Team Magma. Ethan had the best view from his peak, and little on the battlefield escaped him. Shelly's choice did not surprise him. He would have been reluctant to walk away empty-handed too.

What would Team Magma do?

Though they were far apart, Ethan could almost see Courtney's hesitation. In the middle of Team Magma's gathered force, the elite grunts turned to her.

What do we do now, Commander Courtney? one asked.

Courtney considered her options. With all Ethan's Pokemon back at his side and Team Aqua no longer drawing his attention, his position was stronger than ever. Raikou, Suicune, Moltres, Zapdos, Articunoeach was difficult enough to face, even without the rest of his team. Together they were beyond what Team Magma's remaining force could defeat. Capturing Ethan was no longer possible.

She had to change her plan. Her eyes moved to Deoxys. Shelly's decision made sense. In a situation they could no longer control, they should seize whatever prize they still could.

Change targets. Forget the man. We're going after Deoxys too!

Are we competing with Team Aqua for it? an elite grunt asked.

Yes. We can't stand by and let them have it. Even if we can't catch Deoxys ourselves, we won't let Team Aqua succeed!

Understood!

Courtney gathered her people and led them toward Deoxys and Team Aqua. The attack on her flank infuriated Shelly.

That wretched woman! Shelly had thought Courtney had finally shown some sense by going after the most dangerous human opponent. Now she was coming after Team Aqua again. Shelly should have known better than to trust anyone from Team Magma.

Her force wavered, but the move was not wholly unexpected. The organizations were sworn enemies. A shared opponent could never make either one stop watching the other. Shelly split off some members to hold back Team Magma, then urged the rest to attack Deoxys and Rayquaza harder.

The melee reached its peak. The earlier battle lines had vanished. Deoxys, Rayquaza, Team Aqua, and Team Magma were all fighting in the same space. Zinnia, near its center, found enemies on every side and was soon in serious danger.

For the moment, Ethan's position was untouched.

Ethan... Misty was growing anxious. They're all going after Deoxys. Could one of them catch it?

Her fear was reasonable. Team Aqua alone had kept Deoxys occupied, and now it faced Team Magma and Rayquaza too.

Ethan rubbed his chin. If I stood aside, one of them would certainly get it. But why would I stand aside?

He looked to either side. Gengar and Gardevoir would stay with him as guards. He waved the rest of his Pokemon forward into the battle.

Keep fighting. The more confused it gets, the easier it will be for me to take what I want.

Ethan's Pokemon plunged into the melee like tigers among sheep. The fight had entered its final stage. Apart from Ethan and Misty, everyone was caught up in it now.

After so much fighting, nearly every Pokemon on the field was wounded and exhausted. A fresh, powerful Pokemon appearing at this moment could change the balance decisively. Team Magma, Team Aqua, and Zinnia seemed to have no such reserve.

Ethan walked a few steps to the edge of the peak. A light breeze stirred his bangs. From here he could see the whole battlefield.

High above, Rayquaza and Deoxys were the two most conspicuous fighters. Yet each had to face the other while watching for attacks from below. Their power drew much of the other Pokemon's fire.

On the ground, Team Magma and Team Aqua fought across the valley, red uniforms clashing with blue. At this distance Ethan could not make out individuals, but the colors marked each side clearly. Nowhere in the valley was peaceful.

What a sight, he murmured. Misty could not tell whether he sounded impressed or regretful.

She sensed there was more behind his words and came to stand beside him. Do you still have a way to turn this around?

I don't know whether it'll settle everything, Ethan said. But I can promise it will surprise the people and Pokemon down there.

A surprise? Misty frowned. She had stood beside him when he exchanged his Pokemon before departure. Every one of them was already on the field. What else could he have?

Before she could ask, Ethan looked down and exposed his left wrist. A band was fastened there. Misty immediately noticed the bright, rounded stone set into it.

Isn't that the Key Stone we found at Meteor Falls?

She was about to ask when he had made the wristband and why he wore the stone there. Ethan smiled.

It's time...

What? His voice had dropped almost to a whisper, and she had not caught it.

Ethan glanced at her and laughed. It's time they saw just how savage things can get!

He thrust his arm into the air. The Key Stone on his wrist began to shine.

Before Misty understood what he was doing, a brilliant light flashed beneath the lake at the edge of the battlefield. It shone through the water for long enough to draw everyone's attention. Rayquaza, Deoxys, Zinnia, Team Magma, and Team Aqua were all startled.

The glow suddenly vanished. The lake exploded upward, and a gigantic red shape broke the surface.

Only then did Misty remember Ethan's red Gyarados. After it had driven Deoxys out of the lake, it had disappeared below the water. The battles that followed had completely pushed it from her mind.

Ethan had kept a formidable Pokemon hidden all this time. But as the water streamed off it, Misty saw that its shape had changed.

It was no longer than before, yet it looked far heavier and much thicker. Its skin was darker and more solid, as though covered by armor. The horn on its forehead was larger and harder, and its two whiskers had grown very long. The gray structures along its back had become one enormous dorsal fin. It looked fiercer than ever.

What happened to it? Misty's eyes widened. She looked from the changed Gyarados to the stone on Ethan's wrist. Wait... Could it be...?

That's right. Ethan smiled. Mega Evolution. Gyarados just became Mega Gyarados.

Mega red Gyarados! Misty's heart raced. Ethan had told her of this temporary evolution, discovered and widely used in Kalos. It could greatly increase a Pokemon's strength in battle. But how had he managed to use a power from another region?

Ethan read the question on her face. Mega Evolution takes two things. The Trainer needs a Key Stone that resonates with the matching Mega Stone held by the Pokemon. And the Trainer and Pokemon need a deep bond.

Misty understood. Ethan had caught Gyarados back in Kanto when it was a Magikarp. Since its evolution, they had fought countless battles together. Their bond was beyond question.

They had found the Key Stone at Meteor Falls only recently. Long before that, in the Orange Islands, the Pokemon Watcher Quincy T. Quackenpoker had given Ethan a Gyaradosite beside the Lake of Birth and Evolution. He had both stones.

But how did you learn to use them? she asked.

That wasn't hard. I looked through Kalos Trainer forums. Some generous Trainers had explained the method in their posts.

Misty remembered seeing him on his phone often during their travels. She had thought he was chatting with someone, perhaps a girl in Kalos whom he treated like a younger sister. It seemed she had helped him look for information too. So that was what he had been doing.

On the battlefield, Mega Gyarados crashed back into the lake. The splash from its enormous body swept nearby Pokemon aside.

No one else had expected it. The teams had arrived too late to see Ethan use Gyarados to drive Deoxys from the water. They did not even know a Pokemon was hiding below. At the sight of the red giant, they assumed the melee had enraged some terrifying creature that lived in the lake.

Let's begin. Through Gardevoir's telepathy, Ethan sent his command across the battlefield to Mega Gyarados. Use all your strength. Tear this place apart!

Raaah!

Water exploded outward again. Mega Gyarados sprang from the lake with its huge mouth open and lunged at Rayquaza and Deoxys in the air. It rose dozens of meters, showing the tremendous power in the muscles of its lower body.

Neither airborne Pokemon dared dismiss this newcomer. Both sensed its strength and extreme ferocity. Rayquaza dodged one way and Deoxys the other. Mega Gyarados missed them and fell back into the lake.

The people and Pokemon nearby were less fortunate. Huge waves swept through them. Even Team Aqua's Water-types lost control in the surge and were dragged under; the Fire-types fared worse.

As in Rayquaza and Deoxys's battle, the small fry were not Mega Gyarados's targets. They suffered from the force of its attack all the same.

Chapter 668: Capturing Deoxys!

Gyarados, use Twister!

Ethan sent Mega Gyarados its first direct command through Gardevoir's telepathy. Gyarados plunged into the lake and rolled its enormous body through the water. Its power drew the air into a huge tornado at the center of the battlefield.

Wind dragged the dark clouds along with it. Compared with a Twister made by another Pokemon, this one was broader, thicker, and far more destructivejust like Mega Gyarados itself.

The wind howled. The tornado swept unpredictably through the valley, tearing up trees and hurling broken rocks in every direction. Many Pokemon could not resist it. Some were lifted into the air; others disappeared beneath the flying debris.

Misty stared at the devastation. Only after a long moment did she think to aim her upgraded Pokedex at Mega Gyarados. She had updated it on arriving in Hoenn and had not expected it to contain information on this form.

Mega Gyarados, the Atrocious Pokemon. Water and Dark type. Mega Evolution places a heavy strain on its body, driving it to rampage even more violently. It sprays water from vents on its sides to skim across the surface at speeds faster than sound. Anything caught in its path, even a large ship, may be broken in two. Instinct drives it to destroy everything, but it will obey a Trainer it truly trusts.

The entry helped Misty understand what she was seeing. She also noticed a bright stone hanging beneath the red Gyarados's neck. That had to be its Gyaradosite. When had Ethan put it there?

Back on the battlefield, lake water rose into the Twister. It became a waterspout wandering erratically through the valley. No one could continue fighting under those conditions.

Team Aqua and Team Magma, with so many people gathered together, took the worst of it. They fled as sheets of water fell from above, soaking their clothes and blinding them. A misstep could send someone into the waterspout.

Their formations collapsed. With water and sky seemingly joined around them, they could hardly tell which way to run, let alone find their teammates or Pokemon. The two teams were in disarray.

The waterspout separated Rayquaza and Deoxys too. Both still wanted to fight until one of them won, but neither could get close. They were strong enough to force their way through the storm, yet neither wanted to do that.

Rayquaza tried to charge at Deoxys. Before it reached its opponent, a Mightyena came hurtling out of the waterspout with a terrified howl and struck Rayquaza's head.

Rayquaza shook the Pokemon off and pressed on. Half a tree trunk spun toward it next. It angrily knocked the wood aside with a claw, only to find the wandering waterspout directly in its path again.

The interruptions kept coming. At last Rayquaza lost patience. It circled the sky furiously, roared, and abandoned Deoxys. Then it flew upward and away.

No!

Behind a large rock, Zinnia was sheltering from the storm. She reached toward Rayquaza as it departed, hoping to call it back. The wind scattered her cry before it could reach anyone. She could barely hear herself.

On the distant peak, Ethan watched Rayquaza leave without a change in expression. Its arrival had been unexpected. He had never planned to capture two top-tier Legendary Pokemon at once, and he believed he would have another chance to encounter it. Letting it go did not trouble him.

His objective had always been Deoxys. In fact, driving Rayquaza away was part of the decision he had just made. He felt a little sorry for Zinnia, but he could not risk his chance to capture Deoxys safely for her sake. She had lacked the strength to hold Rayquaza's attention and had missed her brief opportunity.

The confusion had reached its height. Ethan judged the time right and sent another series of telepathic orders.

First, the three Legendary birds were to occupy Deoxys again so it could not escape as Rayquaza had. The rest of Ethan's Pokemon would strike Team Aqua and Team Magma while they were struggling and drive them off the battlefield.

The plan worked. Neither organization could withstand the renewed assault. They retreated step by step until Ethan's Pokemon forced them to the edge of the valley.

When Shelly and Courtney counted their people, each found only a dozen or so nearby, with just twenty or thirty Pokemon at hand. Some members had been scattered and could not be found. Others were trapped among the ruins and rock piles still covering the battlefield.

Even the people who remained with the commanders were wounded, and their Pokemon were in miserable condition.

How had this happened? Though they stood in different places, Shelly and Courtney looked up at the enormous Pokemon still rampaging through the valley almost at the same time.

Neither had seen its form before, but they could tell it had something to do with Gyarados. Both had investigated Ethan's team. With a moment to think, they realized this monster must be his. How it had changed hardly mattered now. Neither team had the strength to continue.

They had not lost every person or Pokemon, but they had come close. Their only thought was to leave as quickly as they could. The two forces departed as bedraggled as they had arrived confident. In only a few minutes, the battle had turned completely.

Ethan paid them little attention. With Team Magma and Team Aqua gone, the contest had returned to where it began: Ethan against Deoxys.

There was Zinnia too, though she no longer seemed part of the fight. Once Rayquaza left, she walked silently toward the edge of the valley without even saying goodbye. She was not blaming Mega Gyarados for driving it away. She felt lost and needed somewhere quiet to collect her thoughts.

With the other teams out of the way, Ethan knew the capture battle was truly nearing its end.

The earlier destruction had spread lake water over much of the valley. Mega Gyarados moved freely through the shallow flood, leaping out at intervals to attack Deoxys.

Stay here, Ethan told Misty.

He called Charizard through Gardevoir's telepathy. As it swept past, Ethan jumped onto its back. Before Misty could answer, Charizard carried him toward the center of the battlefield.

After raging for so long, the vast waterspout finally dissipated. Its pull had cleared the remaining dark clouds. The wind died, the rain stopped, and blue sky returned.

Ethan's other Pokemon gathered nearby. They did not attack. They stood guard and watched Mega Gyarados face Deoxys. Ethan circled high on Charizard, far enough away to avoid being caught between them. He would leave the rest of this fight to Gyarados.

He was determined to capture Deoxys. If he succeeded, it would become the strongest Pokemon on his team. Gengar, Raikou, Suicune, Zapdos, Moltres, Articunonone could beat it alone. Only Mega Gyarados could contend with it for a short time.

Mega Evolution had changed Gyarados into a Water and Dark-type. Deoxys's Psychic-type moves no longer threatened it. Deoxys could still use Normal, Dark, and Ghost-type moves, though those were less formidable than its Psychic attacks. It was not helpless.

Mega Gyarados burst from the water, its jaws open wide, and lunged at Deoxys. Deoxys tried to dodge, but all its earlier fighting had left it slow. For once, it did not move in time.

It barely managed to raise an energy barrier before Gyarados's huge jaws closed around it.

Splash! Both Pokemon crashed into the lake and vanished beneath the surface.
