Ethan leaned forward, trying to see what was happening below. From his position, he could make out only Gyarados's massive dorsal fin slicing wildly across the water and great streams of bubbles rising around it. The unseen struggle had him as unsettled as the churning lake.

Then the surface exploded. Deoxys flew out, half an arm missing, and stopped in the air. It hovered there panting, watching the water beneath it.

It was in terrible shape. Its rapid regeneration, which had saved it again and again, did not restore the severed arm. No new tissue appeared at all. Deoxys had finally spent so much energy that it could not even heal itself at once.

The odds were turning Ethan's way, but he needed one more decisive blow.

Gyarados! Don't let it rest. Finish it with Hyper Beam!

Mega Gyarados gathered power. When it had drawn in enough, it opened its jaws and fired a thick, blazing column of energy straight at Deoxys.

Deoxys did not dodge. Everyone could see that it lacked the strength. Instead it gathered what power remained for one last clash. Its two arms came together before its chest, and it fired a blazing beam of its own.

Deoxys had used Hyper Beam too.

The two beams met in midair, one rising from the lake, the other descending from above. The collision exploded in a dazzling flash. Ethan's eyes were overwhelmed. Then a shock wave struck him and Charizard, sending them tumbling through several turns in the air.

Charizard beat its wings and caught the current before they could fall into the water. As soon as the blast passed, Ethan looked toward the center of the battlefield.

Both Pokemon had been thrown backward. Mega Gyarados fell into the lake and resurfaced. Deoxys tumbled away like a kite with its string cut, smashed through several rocks, and landed on its back in the valley.

Ethan's eyes lit up. The chance he had been waiting for had arrived.

He urged Charizard forward. It flew straight toward Deoxys. Ethan took out the Ultra Ball he had prepared and hurled it with all his strength.

The ball traced an arc and struck the fallen Deoxys. Red light enveloped it and drew it inside. The Ultra Ball shook violently under Ethan's anxious gaze. Its movements gradually weakened.

At last, with a soft click, it fell still.

Joy flooded Ethan. He had spent so long on this, fielded almost all his strongest Pokemon, driven off Team Magma and Team Aqua, forced Rayquaza away, and even used Mega Evolution.

At last, he had captured Deoxys!

Chapter 669: Astonishment

Ethan jumped down from Charizard's back and crossed to the Ultra Ball. He picked it up from a puddle.

Who would have guessed that this one ball now held a Pokemon powerful even among Legendary Pokemonone that had fought Rayquaza to a standstill for a time?

He heard splashing footsteps and turned. Misty was running toward him, out of breath.

Ethan, you're amazing! You really caught Deoxys!

In her excitement, she threw her arms around his neck and clung to him. Ethan could feel how genuinely happy she was for him. That was the gift of traveling with someone who truly cared. Many people would have envied him; Misty celebrated his capture as though it were her own success.

All right, come down, he said, setting her gently on her feet. Her sudden embrace had left him flustered. I'm not even making that much of a fuss. How did you get so excited?

Misty smiled broadly. She had noticed his awkwardness and blushed, but she was pleased that he no longer seemed to see her as only a child.

Of course I'm excited. I helped too, you know!

You did. Ethan patted her head. You helped me a great deal, and your Pokemon fought well. This couldn't have gone so smoothly without you. Psyduck aside, of course.

At the mention of Psyduck, Misty laughed. That's not fair. If Psyduck hadn't held Team Magma up, would Zinnia have arrived in time?

She had a point. Psyduck had accomplished little deliberately, but it had taken several attacks and bought them time until Zinnia stepped in. Without that delay, Ethan might have had to Mega Evolve his red Gyarados before Rayquaza appeared, revealing it early. Zinnia might never have come out of hiding, and Gyarados would have lost the element of surprise. Who could say whether the ending would have been the same?

Ethan laughed, in an even better mood. That's why I told Mr. Stone not to underestimate you before we left. I was right. For helping so much today, I'll buy you a gift when we get back to town.

A gift? Misty's eyes lit up. What is it?

Whatever you want! Ethan swept a hand out grandly. If it's sold in a store, you can have it. I'm paying today.

I have to pick it myself? I thought you'd already chosen something for me. Oh wella gift is still a gift!

They chatted and laughed until their excitement gradually settled.

Their Pokemon were all around them, enjoying the aftermath of victory. The lively ones played together, while the quieter ones found places to rest alone.

Mega Gyarados changed again. A faint light flashed over it, and its body returned to its ordinary form.

It's a shame Mega Evolution can't last forever, Misty said. Imagine always having a Pokemon that strong.

What we have is already good enough, Ethan said. If it lasted forever, Kalos would be full of Mega Evolved Pokemon. If everyone had the same advantage, how different would anything be?

He had a point. If everyone started from the same place again, Mega Evolution would no longer set anyone apart.

Ethan recalled his Pokemon one by one, leaving only Gengar and Charizard with him. He took out the special communicator Kennedy had provided and contacted Devon's people. His part of the work was finished. The remaining recovery was best left to professionals.

The landscape had been devastated and would take a long time to recover. But Deoxys was captured. Devon could retrieve the meteorite safely now.

Ethan and Misty sat side by side on a nearby rock, looking out across the valley and enjoying a brief spell of quiet.

More than twenty minutes later, several Devon helicopters appeared overhead. The security guards from the observation post arrived around the same time.

Standing in the middle of the ruined battlefield, the team leader looked around in amazement. Mr. Vale, you're incredible. You even managed to capture a Pokemon that powerful!

Ethan smiled at him. You saw it?

We did! another guard said before his leader could answer. We couldn't see much at first, but we dared to move closer later. We saw everything! You had all those Legendary Pokemon, drove off Team Magma and Team Aqua, chased Rayquaza away with that powerful Gyarados, and caught Deoxys!

The guard was still breathless with excitement. The battle had plainly shaken him. He had never imagined one person could possess so many Legendary Pokemon.

The helicopters drew nearer, rotors thundering and throwing strong gusts across the valley. Ripples spread through the puddles around their feet.

Ethan glanced up at the descending aircraft, then back at the guards. Those Pokemon are something I've kept private. I don't want word of this to spread. Would you keep it to yourselves?

The guards looked briefly surprised. Then they nodded firmly.

Of course, Mr. Vale. You can count on us. We won't tell anyone.

Chapter 670: Norman and Caroline

The helicopter settled slowly onto the ground. As soon as its door opened, Kennedy jumped out first.

Mr. Vale... He stared at Ethan in amazement. You really did it!

From the helicopter, Kennedy had seen that no part of the valley was untouched by battle. He had not witnessed the fighting, but he could imagine what Ethan had faced.

Ethan merely nodded. It took a few unexpected turns, but I got the job done. He had no need to boast.

And Deoxys...? Kennedy asked carefully.

The fact that you landed here safely should tell you. I've caught Deoxys. It won't cause any more trouble. You can recover the meteorite from the lake.

Thank you so much! Kennedy bowed deeply to them both. Mr. Stone will be delighted. On behalf of Devon Corporation, I sincerely thank you for your help.

Kennedy offered to fly them back to Rustboro City, but Ethan declined. After giving him a few details about the site, he and Misty climbed onto Charizard and headed straight for Petalburg City.

Ethan had already spent too much time away from the Gym he had passed several times without managing to challenge. He did not want to delay again. A return trip to Rustboro could bring any number of distractions. Better to finish the Gym match first.

Rustboro had a strange way of drawing him back no matter how many times he left. He did not want to test that pull again. Nor did he want another ride in a helicopter; the noise had been more than enough.

Would Mr. Stone thank him in person or give him another material reward if he returned to Devon? After capturing Deoxys, Ethan no longer cared. Deoxys was the greatest prize he could have wanted.

Charizard spread its wings and carried them past the clouds. Fatigue finally caught up with Ethan and Misty, and they said little during the flight.

By the time they reached Petalburg City, it was too late to challenge the Gym. They went to the Pokemon Center and took rooms for the night. Almost all Ethan's Pokemon needed treatment, and he wanted to adjust his team before the Gym match.

It was not that his current team could not win. With Pokemon strong enough to compete for a championship, though, a Gym challenge would lose much of its point.

At the counter, Ethan handed all his Poke Balls to Nurse Joy. Her eyes widened when she saw them.

Th-these Pokemon...

She had worked at the Petalburg City Pokemon Center for years and treated countless Trainers' teams. Never had she seen a roster quite like this one.

Ethan put a finger to his lips. Please keep this quiet. If possible, could you treat my Pokemon in a separate room? Some of them shouldn't be seen by the public.

Nurse Joy recovered her composure. Of course. We protect our patients' privacy behind the scenes at every Pokemon Center. Your secrets are safe here.

Thank you.

He watched her wheel the Poke Balls into the treatment area. Then he and Misty went to their separate rooms, showered, changed, and met again in the Center's lobby.

To celebrate their victory, they decided to eat at an upscale restaurant rather than have dinner at the Center. Before that, they stopped at the city's largest shopping mall. Ethan had promised Misty a gift to thank her.

Misty took her time deciding. In the end, she chose a fairly expensive set of cosmetics. Ethan paid, and she walked ahead carrying several bags, delighted with her purchase.

He found himself reflecting that he might not have expected someone her age to care about such things. Then again, people liked to look their best at any age, especially around someone whose opinion mattered to them.

...

Early the next morning, Ethan ate breakfast, collected all his Poke Balls, and began exchanging his team.

He sent the red Gyarados, Blastoise, Venusaur, and Jolteon back to Cerise Park. Charizard returned to the Charicific Valley to continue its training.

He sent the three Legendary birds back to Sabrina. After a moment's thought, he sent Jigglypuff to her as well. He had no intention of traveling with that disobedient Pokemon. Sabrina could deal with it.

Ethan was curious which would prevail: Jigglypuff's sleep-inducing song or Sabrina's psychic power. Would Jigglypuff draw a ridiculous face on her, or would Sabrina tame it completely? Either result would be entertaining.

He then retrieved Dragonite, Scizor, Tyranitar, Eevee, Combusken, Metang, and Feebas from Cerise Park. These were the Pokemon he meant to train on his journey through Hoenn.

Once everything was settled, he and Misty headed for Petalburg Gym.

They followed the main road there without difficulty. It was only a little past eight in the morning, but the Gym doors were already open. Norman was ready for challengers. His dedication was a marked change from Brawly at Dewford Gym.

In most respects, this visit felt much like the last one. The greatest difference was that May and Max were gone, leaving the Gym unusually quiet.

They entered and walked toward the battlefield. In the distance, a middle-aged man was training his Pokemon. He appeared to be in his late thirties, lean, with thick eyebrows and alert eyes. Even standing still with his arms folded, he gave the impression of strength.

Neither Ethan nor Misty had met him before, but they knew who he was: Norman, May and Max's father and the Leader of Petalburg Gym.

Norman noticed them almost at once. Before Ethan could speak, he smiled. You've finally come. I've been waiting for you.

Huh? Misty looked puzzled. You know us?

Of course! Norman laughed. May and Max have talked about you several times. This is our first meeting, but they've told me plenty over the phone.

Oh, I see.

Norman turned to Ethan, rubbing his chin. You've come to challenge Petalburg Gym, haven't you?

That's right. Can we begin now?

Norman shook his head with a smile. No need to rush. You're May and Max's friends. Come have some tea first.

Tea? Ethan and Misty exchanged baffled looks.

Norman turned toward the rooms inside the Gym. Caroline! We have guestsMay and Max's friends!

Coming! a woman called back. A moment later she walked out.

Caroline looked to be in her thirties. She wore her long reddish-orange hair in two sharp, zigzagging ponytails. She was pretty, fair-skinned, and fashionably dressed, with pearl earrings. She looked more like a stylish woman from the city than someone Ethan had expected to find managing a household.

She was Norman's wife and May and Max's mother. Ethan could see where May had inherited her good looks.

He and Misty had come to challenge a Gym. They had not expected to meet May's mother before the battle even began. It felt a little like an unexpectedly formal introduction to the family. They managed polite greetings.

Hello, Auntie, Misty said.

Hello, Miss Caroline, said Ethan.

Misty's greeting placed her among May's friends, but Ethan's choice of Miss delighted Caroline even more.

Chapter 671: Challenging Petalburg Gym

In Petalburg Gym's reception room, Ethan and Misty sat a little stiffly before a low table laden with fruit and snacks. Norman and Caroline sat across from them.

Ethan took a sip of tea, paused, then continued. ...And that was when Misty punched Drew in the face. She sent him stumbling and gave May the satisfaction of seeing someone stand up for her!

He was talking about the unpleasant encounter with Drew before they had joined May at the Slateport Contest.

May spoke to her parents every day, but Ethan doubted she had told them about any of this. She would not have wanted them to worry.

Sure enough, Norman and Caroline frowned as they listened, then turned to Misty.

May only tells us the good news, Caroline said. She never mentioned that she'd been treated like that. If you hadn't told us, we still wouldn't know. Misty...thank you so much! May is lucky to have a friend like you.

Misty shifted awkwardly and gave an embarrassed smile. You're too kind. May and I haven't known each other long, but we got along right away. That boy was acting so superior. I only did what a friend should do!

Her modest answer made Norman and Caroline like her all the more. She was as pretty as their daughter and about the same age, and they appreciated her frankness, even with that slightly fiery streak.

Caroline turned eagerly back to Ethan. What happened after that?

After that...we met Mr. Big and Dr. Abby. Their help made a big difference to May. She improved enough to reach the second round in her very first Contest. I expect she's told you that part, but there are details you might not know. Misty can tell you about those.

Ethan handed the story over to Misty. His mouth was dry after talking for so long, despite all the tea he had drunk. Besides, Misty knew May better than he did. Before Norman and Caroline asked him something he could not answer, he might as well let her take over and enjoy a rest.

Misty had no idea what he was thinking. She launched into a lively account of the day of the Contest, adding her own opinions as she went. For May's parents, it was an entirely new view of events, full of things their daughter had never mentioned.

They listened with interest. The conversation went on for most of the day.

The clock's hands made their rounds. Outside the window, white clouds drifted past, sometimes fast and sometimes slow. It seemed to be a fine day.

Yawn...

Ethan had lost count of how often he had yawned. His cup had been refilled several times, he had been to the bathroom three times, and his legs had gone numb. Still, Norman and Caroline showed no sign of bringing the conversation to a close.

He was bored out of his mind.

How could Caroline and Misty have so much to talk about? They had gone from May to Max, from Max to their own interests and hobbies, and somehow circled back to May. There seemed to be no end to it.

He had got up especially early and arrived that morning to make sure nothing delayed the battle. Somehow, the battle had been delayed anyway.

He glanced at Norman. The man listened to his wife and Misty with a faint smile, nodding now and then. When he noticed Ethan looking, he returned his gaze warmly.

Norman could listen to every little detail without a trace of impatience. He really was a good man, a good father, and a good husband.

Ethan thought of the several women with whom his own relationships had grown complicated. Compared with Norman, he felt himself edging closer to being a scumbag.

At last, a loud growl from his stomach brought the long conversation to an abrupt halt.

Everyone looked at him. Ethan rubbed his stomach and smiled ruefully. I didn't eat much this morning. I'm hungry.

Oh! Caroline glanced at the clock and smiled apologetically. It's noon already? I'm sorry I've kept you so long! Please wait here while I make lunch. You don't visit us often, so we must treat you properly today!

Before Ethan or Misty could decline, or even make a polite protest, Caroline was on her feet and gone.

Once she had left, Norman turned to them. I'm sorry. You must have been ready to get up ages ago. Caroline's been lonely since May and Max left to travel. She hasn't quite adjusted. That's why I let her keep you talking. As a man, I can't talk with her about these things the same way, and you're May's friends. I couldn't bring myself to interrupt her.

So that was it. Ethan and Misty understood at last.

That explained why Norman, who normally would never keep a challenger waiting this long, had allowed the visit to go on without getting to the battle.

...

Lunch was a lavish seafood meal that filled the whole table. Caroline clearly knew how to prepare it: there was plenty of variety, and everything tasted fresh and delicious.

Ethan and Misty ate happily. If only Caroline had not kept asking them questions throughout the meal, they might have enjoyed it even more.

After lunch, Ethan finally got his Gym battle with Norman.

They took their places in the Trainer boxes on opposite sides of Petalburg Gym's battlefield. A very young apprentice stepped out to serve as referee.

Before the apprentice could explain the rules, Norman stopped him. Folding his arms, he addressed Ethan. I don't need to go over the rules for you, do I?

Ethan shook his head. Before parting with May and Max, he had heard Max talk at length about the Gym. He knew the match would be three against three. If Ethan had not stopped him, the boy might even have listed the weaknesses of every one of his father's Pokemon. Max admired Ethan that much.

What a disloyal son.

How would you like to battle? Norman asked. Do you want us both to use our strongest teams? To be honest, I'd like to face a Champion who's won in two regions.

Please don't. Ethan shook his head. I've come to challenge the Gym, but I mainly want to train my Pokemon. Treat me like an ordinary challenger.

Norman was a Trainer close to Elite Four level. Ethan had no intention of testing himself against someone like that yet. After he had traveled around the world and challenged the Gyms in each region, he could return for a serious battle.

I see. Norman did not seem to mind. He nodded. Then I understand.

He took a Poke Ball from his jacket and threw it. A flash of blue light revealed the Pokemon Ethan had seen Norman training when they arrived.

It was a Slakoth.

It looked like the sloths Ethan knew from Earth, with a vacant face, gray-brown fur, and darker stripes across its back.

In the stands, Misty aimed her Pokedex at it.

Beep. Slakoth, the Slacker Pokemon. Normal type. Slakoth spends most of every day asleep, lying down for more than twenty hours. Three leaves are enough to satisfy it for a day. Its heart beats only once per minute, and it is almost never seen moving.

Chapter 672: A Surprising Slakoth

This was Ethan's first battle against a Slakoth.

In all his travels, he had rarely seen a Trainer use one, whether in a street battle or a formal match. The reason was simple: Slakoth was too lazy.

Its evolved forms, Vigoroth and Slaking, were another matter. But whatever modest advantages Slakoth had were overshadowed by its laziness, leaving it little chance to shine in battle.

Most people lacked the patience to raise one. Slakoth hardly wanted to move and preferred to stay in one place, while Trainers needed to travel constantly. It was difficult to accommodate both.

Worse, when Slakoth fell asleep, nothing seemed to wake it. A Trainer who sent one out at such a time would make a laughingstock of themselves.

Only a Gym Leader like Norman would take the trouble to train one so carefully.

Ethan chose his own Pokemon. His Poke Ball opened, and Metang appeared on the battlefield.

In terms of type, Metang could not exploit a weakness in Slakoth. But Metang's Steel typing meant that Slakoth's Normal-type moves would deal only half their usual damage.

Slakoth was also in its first evolutionary stage, while Metang had already reached its second. Metang's body was far stronger. On those two points alone, the advantage seemed to belong to Metang.

Yet although Ethan had trained his Metang privately, this was its first Gym battle. Its lack of experience might bring the two Pokemon closer to even footing.

Once both Trainers were ready, the referee signaled the start of the match.

Metang, use Confusion!

Slakoth, Shadow Ball!

Norman was every bit the near-Elite Four Trainer Ethan had expected. Perhaps he had guessed Ethan's opening move: he issued his order at the same moment.

Invisible psychic force struck the Shadow Ball in midair, setting off a violent explosion. Norman had anticipated the attack and countered it immediately.

Then a shape burst through the smoke.

Metang had slipped forward under its cover and floated across the middle of the field toward Slakoth. As it drew near, it raised both iron claws and slashed down with Metal Claw.

The claws gleamed as they came in, swift and precise. Just before they connected, Slakoth sidestepped with startling agility and avoided the blow with ease.

Oh? Ethan raised an eyebrow, but gave it little thought. He ordered a second attack.

Metang swept its claws at Slakoth again. This time Slakoth took a single shifting step and dodged once more.

Now Ethan had to pay attention. He narrowed his eyes and studied the Pokemon's movements. Norman's Slakoth was unusual.

People tended to think of Slakoth as slow and clumsy because the species rarely moved. What Ethan saw before him was entirely different.

Slakoth swayed and drifted from side to side, evading every one of Metang's attacks with an almost weightless ease.

So that's it... Norman must have trained it specifically to compensate for its weakness. No wonder it could move like that.

Close combat would not work. Ethan needed another approach. He told Metang to move back toward his half of the field.

Norman, however, had no intention of letting it leave. Seeing Metang retreat, he ordered Slakoth to stick close.

That's it! Slakoth, use Feint Attack!

Slakoth suddenly thrust out an arm at Metang. Ethan had been watching for a counterattack and had Metang float upward just in time. The strike missed by a narrow margin.

Just as Norman had read Ethan's intentions, Ethan understood Norman's. He was defending and waiting to counterattack. There was nothing mysterious about it.

The exchange finally gave Metang enough room to break away and return to its side of the field. Slakoth did not follow. Its nimble steps let it dodge close-range attacks, but they had not made it any faster over a distance. On a field this wide, catching a floating Metang would be another matter.

Metang, Confusion!

Ethan repeated his opening attack. He did not believe Slakoth could intercept Confusion with Shadow Ball every time. One mistake would give him an opportunity to press.

Norman understood the plan, but he had another answer.

Slakoth, Blizzard!

Slakoth opened its mouth and blew out glittering snowflakes. They grew larger and thicker in the air until a fierce blizzard swept across the field toward Metang.

Ice-type Blizzard would deal only half damage to Steel-type Metang. Norman was aiming for something else.

Among the countless flakes, the previously invisible path of Confusion suddenly took shape. Slakoth saw where it was going, twisted aside, and dodged it easily.

That was not all. The freezing snow coated Metang's metal body with frost. As the ice built up, its joints began to lose their freedom of movement.

So that's what he's after! Ethan understood with a glance.

Metang was not a warm-bodied creature. It might not even have blood to circulate; it was more like a cold stone, with a very low surface temperature. Once snow and ice covered it, Metang could neither melt the coating with its own warmth nor easily clear it away.

A moment later, Metang wobbled in the air. Even the simple act of floating seemed to have become difficult to control.

Norman really was something. He had given a Pokemon usually seen as weak a distinctive way to evade attacks, taught it an Ice-type Blizzard, and perhaps kept still more surprises in reserve. He had raised his Pokemon exceptionally well.

That tactic might have defeated another Trainer. Against Ethan, it was not quite enough.

The thought flashed through his mind as he gave his next order without hesitation. Use Zen Headbutt!

Zen Headbutt concentrated psychic power in the user's forehead for a charging attack. The force of the blow could even make an opponent flinch.

Protected by psychic energy, Metang rushed toward Slakoth again. Retreating only to charge back in had wasted the distance it had gained, but Ethan had little choice. Of the moves Metang currently knew, this was his best option.

The space between them gave Metang time to accelerate. By the time it reached Slakoth, its momentum had built to a peak.

But a Gym Leader's Pokemon would not be so easily intimidated. At Norman's command, Slakoth shed its lazy manner. Its presence changed sharply, and instead of dodging, it drove forward to meet Metang head-on.

Ethan, Norman, Caroline, and Misty watched the two Pokemon close the gap. At last, they crashed into each other...

Chapter 673: What Did You Teach It?

Slakoth and Metang are both unable to battle! The first round is a draw!

The referee held both flags out to his sides, confirming that Ethan and Norman's first battle had ended with both Pokemon knocked out.

There had been no avoiding it. After their head-on collision, the two Pokemon had fought on for some time. Their early testing of each other gave way to the simplest and most brutal stage of the match: close combat, face-to-face.

Norman had raised his Slakoth exceptionally well. In performance, strength, and experience, it had the edge over Metang.

But Metang relied on its excellent defenses and its resistance to Slakoth's Normal-type attacks. Trading blows with its Steel-type moves, it managed to take Slakoth down with it.

Ethan was pleased with the result. Norman could only smile ruefully. There was little he could have done. When two Pokemon were not far apart in strength, a type advantage could decide the outcome, just as it had here.

Well done, Norman told Ethan. My Slakoth may not have evolved, but it's strong. Plenty of challengers before you have underestimated it and paid the price.

Ethan knew Norman was neither boasting nor trying to save face. Slakoth had shown enough to give an inexperienced or overconfident Trainer a very memorable surprise.

Metang certainly benefited from its type advantage, Ethan said with a smile. I'm happy it managed a draw.

Norman nodded, pleased by the young man's modesty. Someone who had won two regional League tournaments in succession really was exceptional. At the very least, his attitude deserved praise. Ethan was worthy of the admiration Max had for him; he would make a good example for Norman's son.

Both Trainers recalled their Pokemon. Norman took out his second Poke Ball.

On to round two. I should warn you: this Pokemon is stronger than the Slakoth you just faced.

Understood. Let's see it, then. Now that the warm-up's over, I should get a little more serious myself!

Perhaps I spoke too soon about his modesty, Norman thought. He smiled and threw his Poke Ball.

A flash of blue light revealed a white Pokemon standing like an ape. It had a tuft of red hair on its head, sharp claws, and a tail.

From her seat beside Caroline, Misty raised her Pokedex again.

Beep. Vigoroth, the Wild Monkey Pokemon. Normal type. The evolved form of Slakoth. Unlike the lazy Slakoth, Vigoroth is always restless and eager to make a commotion. It cannot sit still for even a minute. Its heart beats ten times faster, and its blood races through its body. If it does not move, stress builds up and its health deteriorates.

Slakoth's evolved form? Misty lowered the Pokedex and studied the agitated Pokemon in front of her.

Judging by the description, Slakoth and Vigoroth were complete opposites. It was hard to believe they belonged to the same evolutionary line. Maybe it had so much energy because it had slept too much before evolving?

While Misty speculated, Ethan considered something else. At Dewford Gym, Brawly had sent out Makuhita and then its evolved form, Hariyama. Now Norman was using two stages of the same line too.

Will he send out Slaking after this one? Is this some kind of Hoenn Gym Leader tradition?

Even as he wondered, Ethan took out the Poke Ball he had prepared.

Go, Combusken!

He hurled the ball, and Combusken entered the field for the first time since the Dewford Gym battle. Ethan's frequent use of it showed how seriously he was training it.

Combusken took one look at its opponent and felt its fighting spirit flare. Vigoroth was not about to back down. It glanced sideways at Combusken, then wiggled its backside in an unmistakable taunt.

Combusken's inner fire burned hotter. The tension between them made the second round feel explosive before it had even begun.

The referee gave the signal. Both Pokemon rushed forward. As they met, Combusken kicked high and Vigoroth drove out a straight punch. Leg and fist collided.

Vigoroth was plainly stronger than Slakoth. But Ethan's Fire- and Fighting-type Combusken had a better matchup than Metang had had, and it was no newcomer to battle. After several hard fights, it had experience Metang lacked.

Vigoroth, Slash!

Combusken, Double Kick!

They clashed again without either gaining ground.

Then Combusken sprang back to create some distance and used Flamethrower, hoping to wear Vigoroth down from farther away. To Ethan's astonishment, Vigoroth used the very same move.

The two streams of fire met between them and swelled into a huge ball of flame. Ethan and Combusken stared at it in disbelief.

What? Vigoroth knows Flamethrower?

Ethan thought of Slakoth's Blizzard and fell speechless. What other strange moves had Norman taught his Pokemon?

Norman smiled at their expressions. He had seen that same shock on countless challengers' faces.

He taught his Pokemon moves outside their own types precisely to catch opponents off guard and give them an unexpected experience in battle. It was a small pleasure of his, and part of his style as a Trainer.

Vigoroth raised its brows at Combusken and muttered something taunting. It might as well have been saying, Didn't expect that, did you? I can use your move too. What are you going to do about it?

Furious, Combusken charged. Ethan did not stop it. A little anger could sharpen a Fire-type Pokemon's fighting spirit, though it was a double-edged sword; the Trainer had to know how to use it.

Sure enough, Combusken's attacks became faster and fiercer. Scratch, Peck, Double Kick, Quick Attackmove after move poured out in a relentless assault.

Even Vigoroth, with its agile limbs and boundless energy, struggled to keep up. It discovered that Combusken could match its speed, which came as a shock. Vigoroth had faced other Combusken in Gym battles, but none had been this fast.

Defending against it grew harder. Norman saw the problem too. His brow furrowed as he searched for a way out.

In its current state, Combusken was attacking as quickly and as hard as it could. With Vigoroth's strength and the moves it knew, Norman could see little chance to break through yet.

He would have to wait until Combusken tired. He could only hope Vigoroth held out that long.

Ethan did not know what Norman was thinking. While Norman looked for a way to defend, Ethan searched for Vigoroth's weakness. He knew his own Combusken better than anyone, and he knew it could not maintain this furious assault for long.

The question was whether Combusken would break through Vigoroth's defenses before its stamina faded, or Vigoroth would endure and turn the match around.

So where is your weakness?

Ethan frowned and watched Vigoroth's every move. And as he looked more closely, he really did notice something.

Chapter 674: Just as I Thought!

Vigoroth simply could not keep still.

Ethan noticed that every movementattacking, defending, or runningcame with something extra. Vigoroth paced, bounced on its toes, pawed at the air, scratched its cheeks, or thumped its chest. It was acting on instinct without realizing it.

He ordered Combusken to attack again and watched Vigoroth closely. Sure enough, those little motions followed a pattern. They were unconscious habits.

A plan formed at once. There was no time to weigh whether it would work. Combusken was already slowing down, so Ethan had to take a chance and test his idea.

Combusken, use Scratch!

He had deliberately chosen an attack Vigoroth could dodge easily. As Combusken raked its claws toward it, Vigoroth slipped aside and, just as Ethan expected, bounced twice on its toes.

Ethan seized the opening. As Vigoroth landed, he shouted, Behind you, at an angle! Double Kick!

Combusken was puzzled but obeyed without looking back. It kicked behind itself twice.

Thud! Thud!

Both kicks struck Vigoroth squarely in the chest. It staggered back, clutching the spot and grimacing in pain.

Norman raised an eyebrow. At first he thought Ethan had guessed right by luck. What happened next made him reconsider: Ethan repeated the same trick, and it worked again.

Another pair of kicks hit the same spot. This time Vigoroth broke out in a sweat from the pain.

Norman frowned. Ethan had clearly seen through Vigoroth's movements and anticipated where it would go. But how?

Across the field, Ethan smiled faintly at Norman's baffled expression. Sometimes the person closest to a thing was the last to see it.

Pokemon had been named for their habits and traits since people first came to know them. Vigoroth had earned its name because it was always in motion.

Norman knew his own Pokemon so well that he had grown used to its restlessness. Familiarity had made him overlook the important detail.

Ethan was surely not the first to notice. Other Trainers might have dismissed the habit, or seen it but lacked the ability to seize such a brief opening. Over time, even Norman had stopped treating it as a weakness.

His experience and keen eye soon served him. Norman followed Ethan's gaze, then studied Vigoroth and understood.

So that's it!

Yet understanding did not mean he could fix it. Vigoroth had been restless ever since it evolved. A few shouted commands would not change a lifelong habit.

Under Combusken's continued assault, Vigoroth could no longer hold out. One more Fighting-type strike landed, and its eyes rolled back. It toppled onto its back.

Vigoroth is unable to battle! Combusken wins!

The match had been evenly contested at first, then turned quickly once Ethan found the weakness. Without that discovery, Combusken and Vigoroth might have knocked each other out, as Slakoth and Metang had.

Even the Pokemon Norman used against ordinary challengers were formidable. His strength as a Trainer was plain to see.

Combusken was panting hard too. Ethan recalled it and waited for Norman's third Pokemon.

Norman did not reach for another ball immediately. He applauded. You anticipated Vigoroth's movements. Excellent observation!

It's hardly something to celebrate. Ethan shook his head regretfully. I still have a long way to go. If my observation were really that good, I'd have noticed it at the start of the battle. Things would have been much easier.

He wants to be better still? Norman studied him with mixed feelings.

Few people could win a battle and immediately reflect on their own shortcomings. Ethan had already won two regional League tournaments. If he kept growing like this, what kind of Trainer would he become?

Norman wanted to see how far he could go.

He put the thought aside and took out his third Poke Ball.

This is my last Pokemon. It's one of my stronger partners. Many challengers have lost their Gym battle to it.

Ethan fixed his eyes on the ball. Norman's first two Pokemon had increased the difficulty step by step. The last would surely be the strongest of the three. If Norman himself considered it powerful, Ethan expected a serious challenge.

Norman threw the ball. Blue light flashed, and a gorilla-like Pokemon appeared on the battlefield, lying on its side.

Ethan stared at it, speechless. He had guessed right after all: Norman's last Pokemon was Slakoth's final evolution, Slaking.

Norman was meticulous to a fault. He had Pokemon from all three stages of the same evolutionary line and had put real effort into raising each one. Just how much did he like this species?

Slaking had a pink, pig-like nose and beige skin. Brown rings surrounded its half-lidded eyes, giving it a lazy, sleepy look. Two white tufts of hair sprouted from its head, while a collar of white fur circled its neck and body. Brown fur covered its limbs. It reminded Ethan of a baboon as much as a gorilla from Earth.

He shook his head and rested a hand on the Poke Balls at his waist, considering what to send out.

Misty aimed her Pokedex at Slaking. She had the same question Ethan did about Norman's choice of Pokemon. She wanted to ask Caroline why he had raised all three forms, but it felt too personal, so she kept quiet.

Beep. Slaking, the Lazy Pokemon. Normal type. Slaking is the world's laziest Pokemon and spends most of its life lying down. It eats whatever food is within reach, including grass. Only when it has eaten all the grass around it will it reluctantly roll over and move elsewhere. This leaves regular circles of bare ground wherever it rests. Although it appears to be doing nothing, Slaking stores energy for a counterattack. Releasing that energy at once gives it astonishing power.

Misty was close enough that Ethan heard the entry too, though he already knew most of it. That knowledge was exactly why he understood how strong Slaking could be.

It really was powerful. It hit hard, defended well, and could endure tremendous punishment. For all its lazy appearance, it could move with surprising speed, keeping up with many quick opponents. A careless Trainer who underestimated it could be caught completely off guard.

Choosing a Pokemon to face it was the crucial question.

Ethan reviewed his team and ruled out the partners that were still too weak. That left only Dragonite, Tyranitar, and Scizor.

His third battler would have to be one of them...

Chapter 675: One Move After Another

Slaking was one of Norman's signature Pokemon. Ethan knew it would be difficult to handle even without Norman's warning.

Fighting such a powerful opponent at close range seemed unwise. Of the three Pokemon Ethan was considering, he ruled out Tyranitar first.

Tyranitar's Rock typing gave it some protection against Slaking's Normal-type attacks. Both Pokemon relied on strength, so they might have been able to clash head-on. But Tyranitar was simply too slow.

Slaking would keep its distance and wear Tyranitar down. Rock Tomb might slow Slaking's movements, but an ape-like Pokemon would have no trouble climbing over the obstacles. The move would not achieve what Ethan needed.

He hesitated between Dragonite and Scizor, then chose Scizor.

The next battle is yours. Go, Scizor!

Scizor's Steel typing would blunt Slaking's Normal-type moves. Slaking also knew many Fighting-type moves, but Scizor's Bug typing would offset its Steel typing's weakness to them. The matchup gave Scizor an advantage from the start.

More important, Scizor had the body to withstand Slaking's attacks. Its strength, speed, and stamina might fall short of Slaking's, but its steel-hard frame could take a beating, and it hit hard itself. Its small wings gave it a little more room to maneuver. Slaking might still keep it at a distance, yet Scizor would have ways to respond.

Blue light flashed as Scizor appeared and moved into position. It tried to study its opponent. Slaking remained sprawled on the ground, barely moving. It only lifted its eyes for a brief glance, as if Scizor were not worth its attention.

That might have angered Combusken. Scizor merely took its stance and remained calm. It did not seem to care that Slaking was ignoring it.

Its composure was remarkable. Scizor was not easily provoked, a trait Ethan associated with many Bug-type Pokemon: cool and unsentimental.

The third round of the Petalburg Gym battle begins now! the referee announced.

Scizor, X-Scissor!

Ethan began with a probing attack from some distance rather than rushing in. Scizor crossed its blade-like arms and swept them forward. An X-shaped cutting wave shot out toward Slaking.

Block it, Norman said quietly.

Slaking lazily extended both hands and caught the attack barehanded. Bang! Bang! The cutting waves broke against its heavy palms.

They still left two swollen red marks. The hands Norman had trained to be hard as steel felt the sting. Slaking could no longer dismiss the Pokemon facing it. It rose from the ground, half-opened its eyes, and settled into a fighting stance.

Norman had learned something too. This Scizor was in a different league from the Metang and Combusken Ethan had used before. It had the strength to compete in a League tournament and contend for the championship.

He stopped watching and gave his own attack order. Slaking, Hammer Arm!

Slaking's right fist shone brightly. It surged across the field at startling speed, lifted that fist high, and brought it down on Scizor.

Scizor showed no fear. It raised both bladed arms to meet the blow.

Clang!

Slaking's massive fist struck the two arms with a ringing sound like metal on metal. Scizor retreated two steps, its arms numb.

Slaking's strength was terrifying. One blow had nearly overwhelmed Scizor's guard. But that was all. Scizor's defenses and type advantage kept the damage modest; it had only to catch its breath.

Slaking began thumping its chest. The gesture signaled that it was taking the fight seriously.

Slaking, Earthquake!

Another move outside Slaking's Normal type. Ethan was used to that by now. After Norman's earlier surprises, he might have been more startled if Slaking had used only ordinary attacks.

Slaking leaped high, landed heavily, and stamped the ground over and over. The force shook the whole battlefield. Scizor, standing directly before it, felt the tremors first. Ethan did not panic.

Scizor, jump and use Slash!

The small wings on Scizor's back came into play. Its weight prevented it from truly flying, but the wings could help it jump farther and glide briefly. They could even soften a fall from above.

Scizor sprang high above the violently shaking ground. While suspended in the air, it raised its right arm and slashed down at Slaking.

Slaking had felt the force of Scizor's earlier attack and did not take this one lightly. Its Earthquake had failed to catch Scizor, so it stopped stamping and lifted its broad hands to block the descending strike.

As Slaking swung an arm to counter, several copies of Scizor suddenly appeared. For a moment it could not tell which was real. Norman could offer no help from his position; Slaking had to trust its instincts.

It punched the nearest image. Its fist passed straight through.

A blade cut through the air behind it, headed for its back. Without turning, Slaking reached one hand behind itself and caught Scizor's surprise attack cleanly.

Ethan could only admire Slaking's ability. It was strong indeed. Despite their long exchange, neither Pokemon had gained a clear advantage.

Compared with an ordinary Slaking, Norman's was remarkably energetic. It had been lazy only for the brief time before the battle began. Ethan wondered how Norman had trained it.

To win, Scizor would have to bring greater force to bear. Ethan called it back to his half of the field and ordered Swords Dance.

As Scizor began building up its strength, Norman smiled. Don't give it the chance. Slaking, Hyper Beam!

Slaking opened its mouth. Before Ethan could react, a column of devastating energy erupted from it and shot straight at Scizor.

Ethan had not expected Slaking to have another attack of this kind in reserve. Scizor was halfway through Swords Dance, caught at the worst possible moment. It had no time to dodge before Hyper Beam struck.

The enormous surge of energy swallowed Scizor. Ethan frowned, unable to do anything about it now.

At least Scizor had taken little damage in the fight so far. Barring another surprise, it should be able to withstand this attack.

Chapter 676: That Shouldn't Have Happened

After several seconds, Slaking's Hyper Beam faded.

Just as Ethan had hoped, Scizor was still standing. Its body was covered in marks, but its steel-hard shell and determination had carried it through the flood of energy. Ethan finally let out the breath he had been holding.

Good! Scizor, Quick Attack!

Scizor breathed out a puff of dark smoke, then accelerated sharply toward Slaking. Despite the hit it had taken, it had managed to complete Swords Dance.

With its strength raised, Scizor drove its gleaming bladed arms at Slaking from two different angles.

Norman would not let it land an easy blow. Block it!

Slaking swung its heavy hands into position. Scizor used Double Team again, splitting into several images and confusing its judgment.

Slaking looked left and right. Just as before, it could not tell which Scizor was real. With an angry roar, it clawed wildly at the images, trying to break them all. But Scizor was already too close for Slaking to deal with every copy in time.

Its claws scattered two images in front of it. As it turned toward the others, a sharp pain struck its lower back.

Slaking looked around. Scizor had appeared behind it again, in the same place and the same stance as last time. Slaking had guessed wrong once more.

This time, boosted by Swords Dance, Scizor's attack did real damage. It followed up with Fury Cutter, its bladed arms moving so fast they blurred as it struck Slaking again and again.

Slaking cried out in pain and hurriedly dodged away.

Hm? Its reaction surprised Norman. Slaking's defenses were formidable. Even with Swords Dance, Scizor's attacks should not have hurt quite this muchunless...

He understood and looked up at Ethan. Your Scizor has Swarm, doesn't it?

Ethan nodded. That's right.

From the name alone, Swarm sounded to some people like a heightened sense that helped a Pokemon spot and dodge attacks. Its real effect was different. When the Pokemon's stamina fell low, Swarm strengthened its Bug-type moves, much as Blaze, Torrent, and Overgrow strengthened moves of their respective types.

Slaking's Hyper Beam had worn Scizor down enough to bring that Ability into play.

The two Pokemon faced each other again. Both had taken damage in the exchange, and they seemed nearly even once more.

In the stands, Misty swallowed nervously. Even she could see that Petalburg Gym was the toughest Ethan had challenged so far. Metang still needed more training, but Norman was also an exceptionally strong Gym Leader. His experience and Pokemon surpassed those of most Leaders. Judging by Vigoroth and Slaking alone, he was far stronger than Brawly at Dewford Gym.

Ethan assessed the field. Neither Pokemon had much more stamina than the other. The next moment might decide the match.

Almost together, he and Norman called out their orders.

Scizor, X-Scissor!

Slaking, Hammer Arm!

Both Pokemon charged, arms raised. Every eye followed them. Misty and Caroline could no longer stay seated; they stood beside each other, each hoping the person she cared about would win, though neither could say so with the other right there.

Scizor sent another X-shaped cutting wave toward Slaking. This time Slaking knew better than to catch it with its bare palms. With Swords Dance behind the attack, its power had grown too great. Yet Scizor could not simply withstand Slaking's Hammer Arm either.

The moves met in an instant and canceled each other out. Scizor followed with both bladed arms, but Slaking caught them in its hands. Relying on its greater size and strength, it lifted Scizor and threw it away.

Scizor beat its wings in the air, landed steadily, and rushed back, slashing with both arms again.

Everything happened in seconds. The Pokemon traded several blows so quickly that Ethan and the others could barely follow them. The furious pace drained their strength.

At last both slowed, unable to keep up the same intensity. Ethan spotted an opening.

Double Team!

Scizor split into multiple images. Slaking recognized the move that had hurt it twice already. It was frightened of guessing wrong again, and furious enough to want to knock Scizor down before it could ever use the trick once more.

But the question remained: which one was real?

Slaking scanned the images. Having been fooled twice, it thought it knew the answer. It clenched a fist, spun sharply, and punched toward the spot behind it at an angle.

Didn't expect me to turn around, did you? I won't fall for the same trick a third time!

It could almost picture Scizor flying away when its punch landed. The heavy fist struck Scizor square in the faceand passed straight through its head.

Another image. Slaking had guessed wrong again.

How is that possible? It froze in disbelief. Scizor had attacked from that very spot the last two times. Why had it changed position now? It made no sense.

There was no time to think. Slaking heard a blade cut through the air behind its head, but its fist was still extended and it could not dodge. Pain exploded across its back. Its eyes rolled up, and it collapsed forward.

The referee took one look and raised his flag. Slaking is unable to battle! Scizor wins!

It's finally over... Ethan breathed a quiet sigh of relief. That had been hard.

If even he had struggled this much, how many challengers could win a badge here when Norman held nothing back? Then again, a region with Gym Leaders like this would produce stronger Trainers. At the Ever Grande Conference, Ethan might face fewer beginners than he had at the Indigo and Silver Conferences. Hoenn's tournament could be his most challenging yet.

Norman recalled Slaking. He, Caroline, and Misty all applauded.

That was a wonderful battle, Norman said. Scizor's last Double Team trap completely fooled Slaking. Did you train it to do that?

Yes. I developed that tactic earlier. I've trained my other Pokemon that know Double Team to use it the same way.

Mixing real and false attacksthat makes you genuinely hard to predict. You deserve your Champion titles.

After a few more words of praise, Norman took a badge from his jacket and held it out. Please accept the Balance Badge, proof that you've defeated Petalburg Gym.

Ethan thanked him and took it. The badge was an odd shape. Rather than a simple circle, it looked like a pair of scale pans joined togetheror perhaps a set of headphones. Strange taste.

He put the Balance Badge in his badge case, thanked Norman again, and headed for the Gym entrance with Misty.

Oh? Are you leaving already? Caroline sounded disappointed. I thought you might stay a little longer. At least have dinner with us.

Stay longer? Ethan shook his head. If they did, his ears would be ringing from another long conversation.

Thank you for offering, he said politely, but I still have other Gyms to challenge, and I'm short on time. Perhaps we can visit again another day. We could come back when May and Max return.

I understand. Caroline knew a Trainer could not remain in one place for long, and she did not press them. I should thank you for today. Norman hasn't enjoyed a battle this much in a long time. Thank you, truly.

So that's why it was such a difficult battle. Norman was giving it his all...

It made sense. If he fought every challenger with this much strength, hardly anyone would win his badge.

Norman laughed at his wife's disclosure and shook Ethan's hand. Keep going. I have high hopes for you, and I believe you'll win the Ever Grande Conference too. When the day comes, Caroline and I will be cheering you on from in front of the television.

Thank you...

Ethan and Misty waved to Norman and Caroline, who had accompanied them to the door. After adjusting their bags, they left the Gym.

With that, their journey through western Hoenn had come to an end. Ethan had won his fifth badge and taken another step toward the Ever Grande Conference.

It was not yet two in the afternoon. With plenty of daylight left, they walked out of Petalburg City without delay.

After they had gone some distance, Misty said, May's parents are such lovely people. Caroline cooks so well, they're funny, and they're both so stylish...

Ethan stayed quiet and walked beside her. From her tone, he sensed a little envy. It was not a subject he wanted to handle carelessly. As far as he knew, Misty had grown up with her three older sisters, and he had never seen their parents. One wrong comment could hurt her.

Fortunately, Misty had only meant to voice a passing thought. Her smile soon returned. Where are we going next?

Ethan took out his phone and opened the map. The nearest Gym from here is Fortree Gym in Fortree City. But getting there means crossing central Hoenn, and it's a long way on foot.

So we'll take a ship?

He nodded and pointed to another city on the map. Let's sail to Sootopolis City and challenge Sootopolis Gym first. From there, we can travel to the other two Gym cities. The distances and transport connections will be much easier to manage.

Misty had no objection. Ethan had made the decision, and she was happy to follow.

They left Petalburg City and reached the seaside town beside Petalburg Woods before sunset. There they bought tickets for a luxury cruise ship bound directly for Sootopolis City.

It was too late to board that evening. The ship would dock the next morning, take on supplies, and then depart again, so they spent the night near the port.

After dinner, they walked along the shore. Ethan gazed at the sea in the dark and said, Once we're aboard, it may take several days to reach Sootopolis. Could you help me train a Pokemon during the voyage?

Huh? Misty was surprised he had asked her, but she agreed readily. Which one? I can help, but you know I'm best at training Water-type Pokemon. I'm not very good with the others.

That's fine. I want to train Feebas, Ethan said with a smile. I don't have enough Pokemon ready for battle yet. I caught Feebas ages ago, but without a suitable place to train it, I've hardly had the chance. I want to see it evolve into Milotic soon. More than that, Milotic would give me another dependable member of the team. Then I wouldn't have to keep relying on Combusken and Metang in battle.

Chapter 677: Out of Body

With a long blast of its horn, the great luxury liner left port and headed into the deep blue sea.

Once aboard, Ethan and Misty went to the passenger cabins to put away their luggage. They would be at sea for two days and two nights. It was a long journey, but a comfortable one: they could rest, train, or battle other passengers along the way.

On an upper deck, they found their room by its number. Ethan swiped the key card and opened the door. Misty immediately spotted the bright floor-to-ceiling window. Beyond it lay the wide sky, the endless ocean, and an unobstructed view of the deck.

Wow! She dropped her bags, hurried to the window, and leaned against it to look out. What an amazing view!

Of course. Ethan smiled. I paid a lot for it. It's not the best suite on the ship, but it's far better than a standard cabin.

The room was luxurious. It had a living room, bathroom, bedroom, and kitchenette, along with appliances, a massage chair, and everything else they needed. With that view, it could have passed for a room in an expensive hotel.

Why spend so much? They had more than two days at sea ahead of them. A comfortable place to stay would make the trip more pleasant. Ethan considered it money well spent.

Misty had moved on to the wide, soft bed and was rolling across it with a delighted expression. Ethan shook his head, put away their luggage, and beckoned her to join him. Together, they explored the ship.

It was the most luxurious liner Ethan had ever boardedbigger, taller, and grander than the S.S. Anne or any other ship he had traveled on.

The cabins were nearly full. Four or five thousand people shared the vessel, making it feel like a small city. Passengers filled its cabins, decks, swimming pools, ballroom, playground, movie theater, and gym. Everywhere was lively.

The largest crowd gathered around a Pokemon battle on deck. A man and a woman were directing their Pokemon while spectators watched. Ethan and Misty stopped for a while, but the Trainers were not especially skilled, and neither showed anything remarkable. The two moved on.

The liner sailed steadily onward. Behind it, the harbor had shrunk to a tiny dot.

After their tour, Ethan kept the promise he had made the night before. He and Misty found an empty pool toward the stern and began training.

Ethan released Feebas first. It swam contentedly around the pool. When Misty released her Staryu, the two Pokemon played together in the water for a while.

Misty looked up at Ethan. How do you want to train it?

By battling, of course. But Feebas only knows Tackle and Splash so far. Staryu will need to go easy on it and give it attacks it can learn to answer, a little at a time.

Got it. I'll hold back. Let's begin!

...

Over the next few hours, several of Misty's Water-type Pokemon took turns as Feebas's training partners. Even while holding back, they were much stronger than Feebas could handle.

By the end of the morning, Feebas was exhausted. It floated motionless on the water like a dead fish.

Ethan found the sight funny but did not press it further. He understood that rushing would only make matters worse. Training required rest as well as effort.

By the time they had eaten lunch, the ship had completed a third of its voyage. While they stood at the rail afterward, looking out over the sea, Misty noticed something like a wreck in the distance.

What's that? she asked.

Sea Mauville, I think, Ethan said.

Sea Mauville? What is it? It sounds as though it has something to do with Mauville City.

Ethan searched his memory of the games he had played before coming to this world. It used to be some sort of large research facility. It was abandoned for reasons I don't remember. Now anglers love it. The currents there are complicated, and people travel all the way out from the mainland to catch rare Water-type Pokemon.

Someone leaned against the rail beside him. A woman's voice said, You know quite a bit. Not many people remember Sea Mauville now.

Ethan turned. The stranger wore a red leather jacket over a bandeau top, shorts, and knee-high boots. Her long blonde hair fell in styled curls. Heavy makeup made her exact age hard to judge; she looked somewhere between her late twenties and early thirties. She was fairly attractive, and there was a faint scent of perfume and tobacco about her.

Ethan and Misty exchanged a glance. Neither had met her before, and they did not know why she had approached them. Misty was especially wary of a pretty woman dressed so boldly coming up to Ethan.

But the stranger showed no sign of being interested in him that way. Looking toward Sea Mauville, she said, What you said isn't quite right. Sea Mauville was an undersea energy extraction platform owned by Greater Mauville Holdings. When the New Mauville project was canceled, the company suffered a severe blow and eventually went bankrupt. The platform was abandoned.

She continued, Before it could be dismantled, investigators found that it had developed a unique ecosystem. They preserved it as a nature reserve. Over the years, the ruins and their surroundings became part of the same landscape. That unusual sight led to its later renovation as a tourist attraction.

Misty was surprised by how much she knew. How do you know all that?

My father worked there before he died.

That brief answer explained it. As they spoke, the liner drew close enough for them to see the whole site from the upper deck.

The broken structure did look like a drilling platform. Its rear half had sunk beneath the sea, leaving only part of the ruins above the surface. Many Water-type Pokemon lived in the shallows nearby, treating the place as their own refuge.

Human construction had changed the ocean. In turn, the ocean had changed what people had built.

The liner continued on, and Sea Mauville slowly disappeared from view.

The woman turned back with a smile. I'm Diane, a magician's assistant. You two are Trainers, aren't you?

Huh? How did you know? Misty asked. She glanced at their clothes. Nothing about them seemed to give it away.

Diane shrugged. I saw you at the pool on the aft deck this morning, training Feebas. I figured only Pokemon Trainers would use battles to train it like that.

Oh, I see. Misty's eyes brightened. You said you're a magician's assistant? I've loved magic shows since I was little! I didn't expect to meet someone from one today. You must be really good!

The truly talented one is over there. Diane tipped her chin toward a deck chair in the distance. A silver-haired man lay in it, sunbathing behind oversized sunglasses. He's my partner, Butlerone of the finest magicians in the world.

Butler? The man was reclining and wearing sunglasses, so Ethan could not see his face clearly. The name meant nothing to him. He knew little about stage magic and had no reason to know its stars, though Butler must be accomplished to have such a reputation.

Where are my manners? I'm Ethan Vale, and this is Misty. You saw correctly: we're Trainers, preparing for the next part of our journey.

Misty asked, Where are you and Butler going?

Forina. We're meeting the rest of our troupe there before a performance.

Forina was another unfamiliar name to Ethan. From the map, he thought it lay somewhere inland in Hoenn, but he knew little else about it.

What caught his attention was Butler. When Ethan introduced himself, the magician had stolen several looks at him. Ethan was certain he had felt the man's gazeand something faintly hostile in it.

It made no sense. If Butler was annoyed that Diane had approached Ethan, it was hardly Ethan's fault. She had come to him.

Then Ethan reconsidered. Butler had seen him talking to Diane earlier without reacting. It was only after Ethan gave his name that the hostility appeared. Butler must know who he was, or at least have heard something unfavorable about him.

Perhaps Diane's approach had not been accidental either. Ethan had no proof; it was only a suspicion. Still, it was enough to put him on guard.

He kept smiling and gave no sign of what he was thinking. The three chatted casually for a while. Everything looked ordinary. Butler, too, turned away and stopped watching them, as though nothing had happened.

After they parted, Ethan took Misty back to their cabin. As soon as the door closed, he called Gengar out.

What is it? Gengar had been reading a comic. It drifted out of Ethan's shadow and looked at him in confusion.

Ignoring Misty's equally puzzled expression, Ethan asked, Can you temporarily draw a person's soul out of their body?

He remembered Ash's visit to the Pokemon Tower in Lavender Town. Hoping to catch a Ghost-type Pokemon to face Sabrina, Ash had encountered Haunter and Gengar. They had separated his spirit from his body, and he had spent a long time in the tower that way.

Of course I can, Gengar said. But why? It's dangerous. If anything goes wrong, you could really die. The ability is unstable during the day, too.

Ethan told Gengar and Misty what he had noticed and what he suspected. I want to find out what's going on. If those two are planning something against me, I'd rather know in advance.

So that's it! Misty said, only now putting the pieces together. I had a feeling Diane might have an ulterior motive. If you're right, they could be hiding something.

They both looked at Gengar. It hesitated, then nodded. All right. I'll be careful.

Ethan took a deep breath, told Misty to watch over his body, and lay down on the bed without changing his clothes.

Before closing his eyes, he turned to her uneasily. Stay here. Don't let anyone come in. And...don't do anything strange to my body.

What kind of person do you take me for? Misty waved him on. Leave this to me. Go find out what those two are doing!

Ethan almost said something else. Had he seen a glint in her eyes? Never mind. He pushed the thought away, relaxed, and closed his eyes.

Gengar floated over his head and reached down. The instant it touched him, Ethan felt weightless. Then his soul drifted out of his body, beyond his control.

Chapter 678: Nothing to Do with Me

It was a strange feeling.

Ethan looked at his own body on the bed. His heart was still beating, yet from outside it he could no longer feel even his breathing.

Misty saw him lying there as though asleep. She knelt on the bed and nudged his arm. Ethan? Have you gone?

Gone? You make it sound as if I died... Ethan turned to Gengar. She can't hear me now, can she?

A spirit can't speak to ordinary people, Gengar said. She won't hear your voice. You could still play a prank on her, though.

Ethan shook his head. He had no interest in playing tricks on Misty. But then he noticed something else.

When he did not answer, Misty seemed to assume he had left. Wearing a curious little smile, she slowly reached toward his chest.

Ethan stared. What is she trying to do?

He frowned at Gengar. Tell her I haven't gone anywhere yet. She needs to behave herself.

Gengar had been grinning, eager to see what Misty would do. Now it sighed in disappointment, cleared its throat, and relayed Ethan's message.

Huh? Misty snatched back her hand like a startled bird. Embarrassment flooded her face. I was just going to straighten his clothes. They looked a little messy.

Even as she spoke, she berated herself. I'm such an idiot! Gengar hasn't even left. Of course Ethan hasn't either! Why did I try anything now? I got impatient and he caught me. I hope he believes that excuse...

Hovering above her, Ethan believed none of it. Her flushed face had told him enough. He should have let Gardevoir out to guard his body.

Before he could say more, Gengar urged him on. We don't have time for this. I told you a spirit is unstable outside its body during the day. Go and do what we came to do.

Ethan cast one last uneasy glance at Misty, then followed Gengar through the cabin wall. They drifted into the corridor. He could not properly control his spirit form, so Gengar pulled him along.

Where are we going? Gengar asked.

Back to the deck where we met them. They should still be there. Can other Pokemon see me like this?

Only Ghost types. Are you trying to avoid them?

This is supposed to be discreet. It's better to avoid people and Pokemon if we can. That will spare us trouble.

Then we'll approach quietly through the air.

Without being noticed, they reached the deck where they had met Diane. She and Butler were still there, reclining in deck chairs. Other passengers were nearby, and the pair said nothing to each other. They simply sunbathed.

Their behavior looked perfectly ordinary. Somehow, that only deepened Ethan's suspicion.

Gengar glanced up at the blazing, cloudless sky. They could stay here for ages. Are we going to wait? Spend too long away from your body and you really will die.

Then make them leave. Ethan thought for a moment. Find a way to drive them inside.

I knew that job would fall to me, Gengar muttered. It slipped to a spot no one was watching, transformed into a giant electric fan, and sent a powerful gust across Diane and Butler's chairs.

Whoosh!

Hair flew everywhere. Hats were blown from passengers' heads. People scrambled against the sudden wind. Diane and Butler could no longer sunbathe comfortably, so they got up and went inside.

They appeared to take the gust for an ordinary change in the weather. When Gengar returned, Ethan followed them discreetly into the ship.

He did not get too close. They might have a Ghost-type Pokemon that could see him. He stayed more than ten meters behind, far enough to give Gengar time to react if something unexpected happened.

Their cabin was not far from his, though it lay two decks higher and looked rather more expensive. A magician can clearly afford a fine room, Ethan thought.

Diane and Butler stopped at a door, swiped their card, and went in. Gengar passed through first to check for danger, then pulled Ethan through the wall.

The moment he entered, Ethan heard a man's voice. You shouldn't have risked approaching him.

Butler had removed his sunglasses. Ethan could finally see him clearly. He looked at least in his thirties, handsome enough and graceful in his movements. His elaborate hairstyle gave him a slightly frivolous air.

What does it matter? Diane went to the drinks cabinet, poured herself a glass of red wine, and sipped it. You've left Team Magma. He's no longer your enemy.

Team Magma? Ethan's suspicion had been right. Butler knew him and had once belonged to Team Magma. But why had he left?

You're inviting trouble, Butler said darkly. If he becomes suspicious, our entire plan could fail.

Would that be so bad? Diane laughed softly. Then you could give up that impossible dream and finally let it go.

Never! No one will stop me from taking revenge on the people who mocked me. Once we reach Forina and find Jirachi's crystal, my wish will come true!

Jirachi. Ethan understood.

Butler had been a member of Team Magma. Something had happened there that left him humiliated; he had departed and now sought Jirachi to fulfill a wish.

Jirachi was a Mythical Steel- and Psychic-type Pokemon. An old legend said that once every thousand years, a clear singing voice could wake it for seven days. Upon waking, it would grant any wish written on the tags attached to its head.

Most people treated that story as a charming legend. Few believed it literally. Butler seemed obsessed with making it real.

Now Ethan vaguely remembered where he had seen these two before. They were characters from the Jirachi movie, and Butler was its villain. Their names had been unfamiliar, but their faces had stirred a memory.

Having learned what they were doing, Ethan lost interest. He had no designs on Jirachi and no wish to travel all the way to Forina. He would leave the rest for Ash to deal with.

He signaled to Gengar. They left the cabin and followed their route back.

When they entered their own room, Ethan found Misty asleep beside his body, her head resting against him. Her Starmie stood nearby, bored but keeping watch.

Honestly... Ethan shook his head and slipped back into his body. He opened his eyes.

The movement woke Misty. She rubbed her sleepy eyes and stared blankly for a moment before realizing what had happened. Ethan, you're back?

He regarded her uncertainly. You didn't do anything to my body, did you?

She was instantly wide awake. Of course not! Is that really what you think of me?

He was still suspicious, but his clothes were where they should be. He kept his doubts to himself.

Eager to change the subject, Misty asked, What did you find out?

Nothing that concerns us. Those two do have another purpose, but I'm not their target. We don't need to spend any more time on them.

...

For the rest of the voyage, Ethan set the matter aside and continued training Feebas with Misty. It did not evolve, but it gained a great deal of experience and improved noticeably.

Diane came to watch one of their sessions and chatted casually with them. She seemed unaware that Ethan knew about her and Butler. He remained polite but kept his distance.

The voyage ended when the ship docked at Sootopolis City and Ethan and Misty disembarked.

Sootopolis was a mysterious city where history slept. It stood in eastern Hoenn on a large island apart from the mainland. Ethan had heard that its real-world model was Santorini in Greece.

The city lay inside a volcanic crater. Long ago, an undersea volcano had erupted and risen above the ocean. Rainwater collected in the crater and formed a lake. People found the climate warm and pleasant, and built Sootopolis within its walls.

Ethan came down the gangway intending to head for Sootopolis Gym. Before he could leave the harbor, he glimpsed someone passing in the distance. The sight was brief, but his sharp eyes recognized her at once: Shelly, the Team Aqua commander he had encountered several times.

What is she doing here? Planning another operation?

Ethan called to Misty and hurried after Shelly instead of going to the Gym. His conflict with Team Aqua had gone far beyond a passing rivalry. If he heard they were nearby, he would seek them out; when one walked right in front of him, he would certainly not let the opportunity pass.

Shelly seemed preoccupied. She did not notice she was being followed. No other Team Aqua members accompanied her; she was alone. Even Misty thought something was wrong.

What's happened to her? Did losing Deoxys last time shake her up?

For a senior Team Aqua officer to walk openly through a public port while looking so distracted, something must have changed.

I doubt she's that fragile, Ethan said. It must be something else.

They followed Shelly out of the passenger terminal and toward the cargo area. When they reached a deserted stretch, Ethan stopped trailing her. He and Misty moved ahead and behind to cut off her escape.

Whatever had brought Shelly here, he would not ignore a chance to confront an enemy.

She startled when Ethan stepped into her path. Recognition made her look even more shocked.

Didn't expect to meet me here, did you? Ethan smiled as he reached for a Poke Ball at his waist. It's a shame for you, but today you're the one with nowhere to run.

W-wait! Shelly's expression changed. She raised both hands to show she did not intend to fight. I have something important I must do. Could you let me go this once?

She seemed like a different person from the arrogant opponent Ethan remembered.

Oh? His smile did not quite reach his eyes. You look as if something has happened. I'm curious. Will you tell me what it is?

Chapter 679: An Agreement with Shelly

Let you go? Ethan looked Shelly up and down. That depends on what you can offer me in return. Start by telling me where you're going.

He looked threatening enough that Shelly, remembering his strength, had no thought of resisting. But she hesitated over her purpose, plainly reluctant to speak.

Ethan shook his head. You still don't understand your position. If you won't tell me, I won't waste time arguing. Once I've handed you over, you can explain everything to the International Police from a cell.

He drew two Poke Balls and threw them. Dragonite and Tyranitar appeared on opposite sides of Shelly, trapping her between them.

W-wait! I'll tell you! she said quickly.

She knew he was serious. After another moment's hesitation, she seemed to make a difficult choice.

After our last operation against youno, after we fled from youI took a group to the Weather Institute near Fortree City. We occupied it, and I used its equipment to investigate and simulate the ocean's effect on Hoenn. Only then did I realize how ignorant and absurd the goal Team Aqua has pursued since its founding really is.

She meant the vision promoted by Team Aqua's leader, Archie: to make the world an ideal home for Pokemon by awakening and controlling Kyogre through Primal Reversion.

Team Aqua had thrown itself into that supposedly noble cause even though the world saw it as an evil organization. Hearing one of its commanders reject the goal now surprised Misty. Ethan, who knew the games' story, had long understood the danger.

What did you discover? he asked.

Shelly shuddered. Archie was naive. Primal Kyogre would never obey anyone. It would keep raising the sea and creating extreme weather. Its whirlpools could swallow everything!

Ethan sighed. Wasn't that obvious? How did it take you this long to see it?

Shelly looked embarrassed. Archie was openhearted and had won his followers' trust. None of them had questioned his dream. If she had not investigated it herself a few days ago, she might still believe in it.

So you're going back to stop Archie? Ethan asked.

She nodded. I left the group and hurried here. I have to stop him before he wakes Kyogre.

Ethan caught the implication. Archie knows where Kyogre is?

Shelly hesitated again. Ethan's grave expression made her answer. Yes. And some time ago, he obtained a blue orb with a strange power from Mt. Pyre. They say it can awaken Kyogre and cause its Primal Reversion.

That complicates things. Ethan rubbed his chin.

Mt. Pyre was a resting place for departed Pokemon, much like Pokemon Tower in Kanto, Lost Tower in Sinnoh, or Celestial Tower in Unova. Mist, the wishes of the dead, and many Ghost-type Pokemon kept most people away. Those same qualities made it a fitting place to guard objects that should not fall into human hands.

Ethan did not know how the Blue Orb had been made or who had placed it there. He knew only that it had a counterpart, the Red Orb, and that their powers could awaken Kyogre and Groudon and drive them into their primal forms.

With both the Blue Orb and Kyogre's location in Archie's hands, awakening Kyogre was only a matter of time. If the Pokemon broke free and threw all Hoenn into chaos, who could stop it?

How do you plan to stop Archie? Ethan asked.

I...I'll try to talk him out of it. Shelly looked troubled.

Talk him out of it? Do you really think he'll listen?
