She fell silent. Archie was charismatic but stubborn. He had pursued this dream for years and was now close to achieving it. A few words from her were unlikely to change his mind.

Her expression told Ethan she had no confidence in her plan. He sighed, signaled Dragonite and Tyranitar to step back, and made an offer.

I'd like to be rid of Team Aqua's interference for good, but this concerns all of Hoenn. Let's make a deal.

A deal? Shelly stared at him. She had always treated Ethan as Team Aqua's greatest threat. She had never imagined working with him, though she could guess what he wanted.

What kind of cooperation? she asked cautiously.

I'll pretend I never saw you and let you go. In return, you take me to Archie.

And what will you do when you find him?

What I do best. Defeat his Pokemon, put an end to this fantasy, and return the orb to Mt. Pyre.

Shelly's brow tightened as she wrestled with the choice. Bringing Ethan to Archie would betray her leader and Team Aqua. Even if it stopped him, she would have no place in the organization afterward; her comrades would despise her.

Yet without Ethan, she had no real way to stop Archie. Letting him proceed could doom Hoenn and betray the reason she had joined Team Aqua in the first place.

Ethan gave her time to decide. He looked toward the distant sea. He did not suspect a trap. He knew the broad course of these events from the games and what might happen if no one intervened.

As a traveling Trainer, he could have left the matter to the authorities, the Pokemon League, or the Elite Four. He was not obliged to handle every crisis himself.

But could he, someone who thought of himself as a decent person, truly ignore a danger unfolding in front of him? He might be closer than anyone else to the heart of itand best placed to stop it.

There was another reason, too. He wanted to see Kyogre for himself, to learn how it compared with the Pokemon of the games and anime, and how overwhelming it really was.

Shelly took a deep breath and nodded firmly. All right. I'll take you to Archie. But promise me one thing: don't attack the other members

You still don't understand your position, Ethan cut in coldly. Are you so used to being a commander that you think you can give me orders? What gives you the standing to set terms? I'm the one holding the advantage.

Shelly went still. She remembered that she had nothing with which to bargain. After a long breath, she said dejectedly, I understand. Can we leave now?

She had faced the situation and made her choice. Ethan was satisfied, though he quietly told Gengar to watch her in case she changed her mind or tried to escape.

After discussing their next steps, they agreed to follow Shelly's original plan: go to the cave where Kyogre was hiding, find Archie, and decide how to act from there.

Before they left, Ethan sent Anabel a message outlining the danger. He could not guarantee success. If Kyogre did cause a tsunami, advance warning might at least give people at sea time to get clear.

The three of them continued through the cargo warehouses toward a secret Team Aqua facility. Only senior members knew of the small base. It held supplies and, Shelly said, a craft they could use for the journey.

As Shelly led the way, Misty fell back beside Ethan. Do you really trust her? Something about this feels wrong.

Don't worry. Ethan patted her head. I think she's telling the truth. Even if it is a trap, I can get you out safely.

That's not what I mean. She changed her mind so quickly. Is Kyogre really powerful enough to drown all of Hoenn?

Don't underestimate Legendary Pokemon. Ethan glanced at Shelly, who seemed too preoccupied to hear, and lowered his voice. You saw Rayquaza fight Deoxys. Rayquaza was incredibly strong, but it wouldn't be enough against Primal Kyogre without taking on a stronger form itself. Kyogre could raise the sea and create enormous whirlpools with a flick of its tail.

Misty stuck out her tongue in alarm. That strong? Can we really stop it? Your strongest Pokemon aren't with you right now.

That's what worries me too. But if we take the orb before Archie makes his mistake, I don't think Kyogre will undergo Primal Reversion.

I hope we can stop him. Misty paused. Waityou aren't doing all this because you want to catch Kyogre, are you?

Of course not. I know which Pokemon I can catch and which I shouldn't. Kyogre and Groudon should be left undisturbed in their corners of the world.

What about Rayquaza? You looked very interested in the one we saw.

That's different. Having one more or one less Rayquaza wouldn't change the world. But I'm not after the one we met. I want a cooler-looking one. Ethan waved the subject away. That's for another day. We need to focus on this crisis.

They reached a warehouse at the far end of the cargo district. Shelly entered a code, and its heavy door opened automatically.

In the center lay a pool connected to the sea. A small submarine bearing Team Aqua's emblem rested in the water.

Shelly did not start the submarine yet. She went to a shelf, took down two sets of clothes, and handed them to Ethan and Misty.

To avoid unnecessary trouble and get close to Archie more easily, put these uniforms on first.

Ethan had not expected her to think of that, but he had no objection. Reaching Archie quickly mattered most. Team Aqua's uniforms looked ugly to him, yet the thought of infiltrating their ranks in disguise gave him an odd thrill.

Chapter 680: You Should Choose a Better Path

Wearing Team Aqua uniforms, Ethan and Misty followed Shelly into the small submarine.

It was smaller than a minibus and shaped rather like a shark. Unlike Team Rocket's crudely built Magikarp submarine, though, it carried sophisticated equipment. A huge round window at the front gave a clear view ahead.

There was room for six people, including the pilot. Neither Ethan nor Misty knew how to handle a submarine, so they sat behind Shelly and watched her work the controls.

A short while later, the craft trembled gently as its engines started. Through the window, Ethan watched it sink until water covered the glass. Once they were fully submerged, the cabin felt strangely oppressive. Perhaps it was only his imagination.

Shelly steered through a channel excavated beneath the warehouse and out to sea. She found her bearing without consulting a map and guided them past the shallows into deeper water.

The submarine was small but fast. Coral and schools of fish Pokemon slipped behind them almost at once. After confirming their course by satellite navigation and nautical chart, Shelly engaged the autopilot.

She leaned back, wanting a moment to rest and consider what lay ahead. Remembering the two enemies seated behind her kept her tense.

Ethan noticed. He still needed her help, so he chose a casual question to ease the atmosphere. How long have you been with Team Aqua?

Shelly recognized that he was making conversation rather than interrogating her. Many years. I was among the first to follow Archie.

Then you must be one of the people he trusts most.

After a pause, she said, No. He has never truly trusted me or the other commanders. The only person Archie trusts completely is himself.

Ethan nodded. That did not surprise him. A leader might value his followers without trusting them in everything; he still needed authority and a clear head.

Can you tell me about the other commanders?

Shelly hesitated. Ethan smiled. I'm not asking because I plan to target them. We may have to deal with them soon. It would help to know who they are.

She fell silent again. Leading an enemy toward Archie was already a betrayal. Giving away information about her comrades would make her feel still more like a traitor.

What difference would it make? she said at last. Your Pokemon are stronger than ours. None of us could beat you.

At least tell me their names. We're supposed to be sneaking in. If I don't know who anyone is, I'll give myself away.

She could not argue with that. Fine. Apart from me, Team Aqua has two other commanders and some senior members. You don't need to know the senior members. Remember the commanders.

Their names are Matt and Amber. You met Amber at Devon Corporation. Thanks to you, he's still in prison, so you won't have to worry about seeing him.

Matt is a big, strong man. He isn't much of a thinker, but he acts decisively. Archie helped him years ago, and Matt has made Archie's dream his own. He would give his life for it. Apart from Archie, he'll be the hardest person for us to handle.

I see. Ethan nodded. So there's no talking either of them around. If we clash, I'll have to stop them by force.

It was a reasonable conclusion, but Shelly did not like hearing it.

The silence grew heavy. Ethan tried another question. Now that you know Team Aqua's goal was wrong, do you still intend to stay?

What do you mean? Shelly asked. Are you trying to persuade me to leave? Our methods were wrong, but our ideals weren't. What's wrong with striving to make an ideal home for Pokemon? Even without Kyogre, we'll keep working toward it.

Will you? Ethan shrugged. The world seems pretty wonderful already. We could take better care of it and stop damaging it. There's no need to remake it completely. If you want change, why use a Pokemon's power? Work on the economy, environmental protection, construction, or how people treat one another.

In the round window's reflection, he saw Shelly give a faint, cold smile. You have your reasoning, and we have our beliefs. I can't make you agree with me, but you can't change my mind either.

Stubborn woman. Ethan shook his head. I think it's a waste. You're intelligent and capable. You shouldn't follow one path all the way into darkness.

What? Are you trying to recruit me?

Recruit you? Ethan laughed. I don't run an organization or have some grand plan to carry out. What would I recruit you for? We're talking, that's all. Do you intend to spend your whole life in an outlaw group, hiding from the world? You should think about what kind of life you want later.

Shelly said nothing for a long time. Ethan could not tell whether his words had reached her.

At last she murmured, That's quite a speech from someone your age. She was plainly older than him and did not enjoy being lectured.

Ethan heard the barb. He shifted in his seat, put his feet on an empty chair, rested his hands behind his neck, and looked out the window.

I don't have another motive. If you don't want to hear it, forget it. I just don't want to watch you sink further into this until you end up like Amber, alone in prison for the rest of your life.

Shelly had no answer.

Misty sat quietly, doing her best not to draw attention. This exchange felt like something between adults, far beyond what she knew how to join. She turned back to the view outside.

The submarine remained quiet for a long while. Ethan thought the conversation was over when Shelly asked softly, Do I...really still have a chance to leave?

Of course. He looked toward her, but from behind he could see only her long hair. You recognized the danger and set out to stop Archie. Most people wouldn't even admit they were wrong. That ought to count in your favor. If it comes to an accounting later, I'll speak for you.

What would I do afterward?

Whatever you want, as long as you obey the law. Surely you've had some ambition of your own. If you can't settle into an ordinary life, I could suggest somewhere else.

Where?

I know a group of people in Kanto. Ethan considered his words. They're friends, not followers of some cause. They're good people. If you need a place to belong, you could meet them. But that only makes sense if you genuinely want to leave Team Aqua. Decide that first, and I'll tell you where they are.

Shelly seemed about to reply, but Ethan ended the subject. We can talk about the future later. Look at the chartthe submarine's slowing down. Are we close?

She checked and found they had reached the coordinates she had entered. Taking a breath, she set aside her thoughts, turned off the autopilot, and took the controls herself.

The submarine rose until sunlight poured through the window again. Ahead lay a maze of hundreds, perhaps thousands, of tiny islands and coral reefs. None was very high; even the tallest rose only a few meters above the sea.

With no visible markers, Shelly turned left and right from memory, threading the craft through the complicated channels toward the islands' center.

Stay alert, she said. We'll see the others soon. If someone recognizes you, don't say I didn't warn you.

Don't worry, Ethan said lightly. I can always fight my way through.

Shelly fell silent. He had left her speechless more than once, but she knew he was capable of doing exactly that. She concentrated on steering.

After several minutes, Team Aqua members came into view, guarding a larger islet. Shelly stopped the submarine at the water's edge and opened the hatch.

Before she climbed out, Ethan warned her, We're in this together now. No tricks.

I'm more worried than you are, she replied, rolling her eyes.

She climbed onto the submarine and greeted the guards. Matt, where's Archie?

The hatch remained open, so Ethan could hear them. He studied the man at the front of the group. Matt was tall and heavily muscled, built like a boxer. His hair was cropped short and his chest bare. Thick chains hung at his neck and waist, and a large Team Aqua emblem marked his chest.

Matt frowned at Shelly. Before answering, he peered into the submarine. He could make out only two figures in Team Aqua uniforms and lost interest.

Why are you back? he asked. Weren't you leading a group near Mt. Chimney?

That can wait. Where's Archie? I need to speak to him urgently.

He took a team to the entrance of Kyogre's cave. He should be there by now.

Shelly's face changed. She jumped back into the submarine, sealed the hatch, and started it toward the deeper part of the island maze.

Once Matt was out of sight, she turned to Ethan. We're too late. Archie has already gone to Kyogre.

I heard. Ethan sighed and checked his equipment. We'd better prepare for the worst.

On the other side of the islands, open water appeared again. Ethan glanced at a larger island nearby and noticed a lighthouse.

Where exactly is Kyogre?

Under this island. Hold on. I'm going at full speed.

Shelly shoved the control lever forward. Ethan felt a jolt as the submarine plunged rapidly into the deep water beneath the island.

After more than a minute of descent, a well-hidden cave entrance emerged from the dark seafloor.

Ethan had to admire Team Aqua's persistence. How had they found a place like this in the vast ocean? It must have taken years of work by hundreds, perhaps thousands, of people.

Chapter 681: The Fight for the Orb

The tunnel beyond the entrance was deep, narrow, and almost completely dark. Even with the submarine's powerful searchlight, Shelly could barely see the way ahead.

She drove as fast as she dared, but they did not catch Archie. After several hundred meters, light appeared ahead and the tunnel curved upward. The passage was nearing its end.

The submarine broke through the surface inside an underground cavern. Before Ethan could take in the surroundings, he saw another submarine of exactly the same design moored nearby. It had to be Archie's.

No one remained aboard. A single Team Aqua member stood guard on the shore.

Shelly opened the hatch and climbed out first. The guard stared, then saluted. Boss, what are you doing here?

His eyes moved to Ethan and Misty as they emerged behind her. They looked unfamiliar, and he wondered who they were.

Shelly calmly stepped into his line of sight. Where's Archie?

He pointed deeper into the cavern. He left a moment ago. He can't be far.

Without another word, Shelly led Ethan and Misty after him into the darkness. They walked faster and faster, soon nearly running as they clambered over protruding rocks and crossed channels of water.

Even their flashlights did little to improve the visibility. A careless step could send someone sprawling. Shelly lost her footing while climbing a rock and nearly fell; Ethan caught her in time.

She did not thank him. She simply hurried on. Ethan found it faintly amusing. Days ago they had been fighting fiercely over the same Pokemon. Now, for the moment, they were on the same side. Fate could change things quickly.

After several minutes, dim light appeared ahead. Ethan heard water rushing, with voices beneath the sound. They quickened their pace. Four figures came into view near the light, and a man's loud, rough voice rang through the cavern.

Ha ha ha! Kyogre, the Legendary Pokemon of ancient times! After all these years, I've finally found you!

Even before he saw the speaker, Ethan knew it must be Archie.

Closer up, Archie proved strongly built, though not as enormous as Matt. He wore a blue bandanna over his head and had a full beard. His blue, sharkskin-like diving suit and the anchor-shaped chain on his chest made him resemble a pirate. He looked tough and formidable.

Three senior Team Aqua memberstwo men and a womanstood beside him.

Before them lay a brightly lit pool whose water gave off a strange blue glow. In its center floated an enormous blue Pokemon that seemed part whale, part bird, part fish.

It was Kyogre, the embodiment of the sea. Myth credited it with command over water and with expanding the ocean by drowning land beneath torrential rain and mighty waves. Pokemon as rare as Lugia were beyond most people's hopes of ever seeing; Kyogre was rarer still.

Archie stood before it, exultant. Listen, Kyogre! I'm Archie, leader of Team Aqua! I've waited for this day for years. The world has gone wrong. Everyone cares only about their own interests, and nature and Pokemon suffer for it. Together, we'll put the world back the way it should be!

He took out a crystal-bright orb about the size of his fist and held it toward Kyogre.

Shelly could contain herself no longer. She ran toward him, shouting, Archie! Wait!

Hm? His hand stopped in midair. He turned and frowned. Shelly? Why are you here? No mattercome and look! Everything we've pursued is right in front of us. Our dream is about to become real!

Listen to me first! she pleaded. The world you imagine and the world Kyogre would create are completely different!

Archie's face darkened. What nonsense are you talking?

His sudden harshness made Shelly flinch. She forced herself to continue, her voice shaking. I studied it at the Weather Institute. I simulated what would happen when Primal Kyogre wokewhether your ideal world could exist, how far its power would reach. Every result led to the same thing: a disaster we couldn't escape. All living things would sink beneath the sea it brings!

The three senior members looked stunned. Archie merely snorted.

Simulations? Research? Cold figures and your guesses, nothing more! He raised the Blue Orb. With this in my hand, Kyogre will serve me!

This was Ethan's first meeting with Archie. The man showed him only immovable stubbornness and a near-hysterical certainty. He would hear no one else's warning. He was like a gambler who had placed everything on one final card and believed he alone would win.

Ethan sighed and stepped up beside Shelly. It looks as though talking to him failed. We should try my way now.

Only then did Archie notice the man in a Team Aqua uniform beside her. He knew most of the members who worked closely with his commanders, but he had never seen this one.

Who are you?

Who am I? Ethan took off his bandanna and smiled. I've crossed paths with your people plenty of times lately. I thought your leader would recognize me on sight. Even the ordinary members have managed that. Have you been so absorbed in finding Kyogre that you don't know who Team Aqua's greatest enemy is?

What? Archie stared, confused. Two seconds passed before recognition struck. You! You're Ethan Vale?

Before Ethan could answer, Archie turned his fury on Shelly. Traitor! You brought him here?

I... Shelly tried to explain. Archie waved an arm before she could. The three members beside him released their Pokemon.

Several Mightyena, Golbat, and Crawdaunt surrounded Ethan, Misty, and Shelly.

Shelly had known this might happen. Facing it for real still left her heartsick. Ethan and Misty had come prepared. They threw their Poke Balls, and their own Pokemon appeared.

Ethan sent out Gardevoir, Dragonite, Scizor, Eevee, and Metang. Misty released Starmie, Staryu, Politoed, Corsola, and Psyduck.

Wait. Psyduck? Misty startled and immediately recalled it.

The two sides faced each other. Battle was moments away, but Shelly tried one last time. Wait! Don't attack! Archie, I haven't betrayed Team Aqua. Ethan came here to

Archie had already decided she was a traitor. At his order, the senior members hesitated only briefly before attacking. Until seconds ago, Shelly had been their commander, the organization's strategist and second only to Archie. Their loyalty to him overrode it.

Powerful jets of water swept toward the three of them. Shelly stood frozen. Ethan pulled her out of their path, while Gardevoir teleported in front of her and stopped the Water Guns with Confusion.

Seeing Ethan protect Shelly only confirmed Archie's belief that she had betrayed him. He had trusted her enough to make her a commander, and now, he thought, she had turned against him.

The sight of Kyogre and the supposed betrayal drove him into a shark-like frenzy. Shelly's warning had planted a trace of doubt before; now he dismissed it as a lie invented to steal his orb.

Archie turned back toward Kyogre to use the Blue Orb. Ethan urged his Pokemon to attack faster. These senior members were much tougher than ordinary grunts, however, and their coordinated defense held.

The narrow cavern lay deep underground. Ethan could not risk using his Legendary Pokemon or attacks strong enough to bring the roof down and bury them all. His strongest regular partners were elsewhere. Given enough time, he might break through; right now he did not have it.

He called out Gengar. Go through the ground and take that orb!

Got it! Gengar understood the urgency. It sank into the cave floor without another joke and slipped toward Archie.

Team Aqua's senior members, though weaker than Ethan, continued to work together and refused to yield an inch.

Everything you've done is for nothing! Archie laughed wildly and hurled the Blue Orb toward Kyogre.

No! Shelly cried.

Time seemed to slow. The orb spun through the air toward the motionless Pokemon. Ethan followed it with his eyes, his heart in his throat. Gengar was still underground, too far from Archie to stop the throw.

Will Kyogre really undergo Primal Reversion?

Then the orb stopped in midair, as though an invisible hand had caught it. Everyone froze. Ethan recovered first and turned to Gardevoir. It had one hand outstretched, holding the orb in place with psychic power.

Beautifully done! Bring it here!

Archie's face changed. The orb flew over his head toward Ethan. He grabbed at it but could not reach its height.

Desperate, he pointed toward the cavern roof. You threeattack that!

The members followed his gesture. A huge stalactite hung above the center of the battlefield. They directed their Pokemon's attacks at it just as the orb passed underneath.

Several moves struck the stone. An explosion tore it free. The stalactite crashed down, burying the Blue Orb beneath it as smoke and dust blotted out the view.

That's bad!

Ethan and Archie both lunged toward the fallen stone. Pokemon on each side tried to stop the opposing Trainer, only to be intercepted by their counterparts. The cavern dissolved into chaos.

Both men reached the shattered stalactite almost together. But the Blue Orb lay somewhere among the rubble, and neither could spot it.

Chapter 682: Run, Keep Running!

Archie spotted the Blue Orb first among the broken stones. To his delight, it lay closer to him than to Ethan. He needed only a few steps to reach it.

He grinned fiercely, strode forward, and bent to pick it up. Just as his hand touched it, the orb lifted off the ground on its own.

What?

Archie looked up. Gengar had appeared above him, cradling the orb. Heh heh heh! This shiny stone is mine now! It flew back to Ethan.

Damn you! Archie roared. He threw a Poke Ball, releasing a Muk in front of Ethan.

Ethan smelled it before he could see it clearly. The stench made his eyes sting. After several coughs, he forced himself to look at Muk.

People sometimes claimed that the more a Muk reeked, the stronger it was. There was no scientific proof, but Archie's Muk was the foulest Ethan had ever encountered. Perhaps the rumor had some truth.

Muk, Sludge Bomb!

Muk reached into its own body and hurled a murky purple mass at Ethan. Gengar met it with Shadow Ball. The attacks exploded together, spraying foul droplets and scraps in every direction.

Ethan hurried back while Archie prepared to pursue him. Then a deep, whale-like call echoed through the cavern.

Kyogre had woken.

The noise of the battle had disturbed its sleep. It opened its eyes to find strangers invading its home. Whether from anger, territorial instinct, or simple irritation, it reacted furiously.

It did not even use an attack. Merely turning its body shook the whole cavern. Everyone realized they had provoked the ancient Legendary Pokemon, the embodiment of the sea.

Stalactites broke from the ceiling in such numbers that no one could avoid every falling stone. One enormous piece came straight toward Ethan. Gengar moved above him and caught it with its body.

Everyone else scrambled for safety. Misty and Shelly were in the path of the rockfall too, but Gardevoir was beside them and kept them safe. The other Pokemon defended themselves as best they could. Ethan spared Archie and his senior members no attention.

Another, larger rock fell. Gengar blocked it as well, but grunted under the impact. The orb slipped from its hands, struck the ground, and rolled away.

It came to rest near Shelly. She reacted quickly and picked it up.

The shaking stopped, and the stalactites ceased falling. Kyogre paid the intruders no further attention. It turned, dove into the pool, and vanished.

No! Archie cried in despair. Bruised from dodging the falling stone, his bandanna gone, he looked almost unrecognizable. He turned blazing eyes on Shelly. This is all your fault! Give me the orb!

Fortunately, everyone had the instincts of a Trainer and none had been seriously injured.

I'm sorry... Shelly stepped back. She looked pained but sounded firm. I can't stand by and let you drag Team Aqua and all Hoenn into ruin.

Traitor! Archie ordered his Pokemon to charge her without restraint.

Shelly still seemed ready to explain herself. Ethan called to Misty, grabbed Shelly's hand, and pulled her toward the way they had come. The three fled.

He could have tried to capture Archie here, but two risks stood in his way. Shelly had not turned on Team Aqua. Even after Archie called her a traitor and attacked her, she refused to strike back. Her loyalty was still with the organization. If Ethan tried to arrest Archie, Shelly might attack Ethan from behind.

And they were deep underground. If a desperate Archie brought down the cavern, no one might escape. The chance was small but too serious to ignore.

Kyogre was gone and the Blue Orb was in their hands. Leaving now and making a new plan was the sensible choice.

Being pulled away finally brought Shelly back to herself. The upheaval had shaken even her usual composure.

Covered by their Pokemon, the three ran back to the place where they had moored the submarine. The Team Aqua guard was waiting anxiously. His eyes lit up at the sight of Shelly, but before he could ask a question, the three recalled their Pokemon and climbed aboard without stopping.

He had no idea what had happened farther inside. The tremors only made him more curious. Had Archie fought Kyogre? Why had Shelly returned alone?

The submarine was already diving when Archie and the senior members finally arrived.

Where's Shelly? Archie demanded.

She left in her submarine.

What? Why didn't you stop her?

Why would I? The guard stared at him.

Archie ignored him and boarded his own submarine. Only after everyone was inside did one of the senior members tell the guard that Shelly had betrayed Team Aqua.

That can't be right, the guard murmured after a long silence. There must be some mistake.

His disbelief showed how highly Team Aqua regarded Shelly. He would sooner believe Archie and the others had misunderstood or were playing some kind of cruel joke.

Enough, Archie snapped. Pursue her! Contact Matt and tell him to stop that traitor!

The guard hurried to open a channel. Matt answered almost at once. Archie, have you brought Kyogre under control?

Archie exploded. Stop the traitor!

Traitor? What are you talking about?

Don't let Shelly escape! She betrayed me and all of Team Aqua! She brought that man Ethan Vale to Kyogre and stole the Blue Orb!

What? Matt was stunned. As a commander, he recovered faster than the guard. He doubted Shelly had truly betrayed them, but stopping her until they understood would do no harm. He waved his people into their submarine.

...

Shelly steered through the same long, narrow underwater passage. She had stopped Archie from using the orb, yet her thoughts were in turmoil. How had she become a traitor?

Ethan did not need to see her face to sense it. He glanced out the window. I know what you're thinking. But if you let it distract you from piloting, Archie will catch us before long.

She stiffened slightly. After several seconds, she gave a curt reply. I know.

The submarine surged forward, moving faster than before. The delay had already cost them, though. Archie's craft was closing in; its bright searchlight swept over their stern. Their communicator lit up.

Shelly hesitated, then accepted the call. Archie's furious voice filled the cabin. Shelly! You dared betray Team Aqua! I'll tear you apart!

I didn't. Please listen

He cut the connection before she could finish. Only the dead tone remained.

Ethan shook his head at her back. You can't reason with someone who's lost control. Besides, he has expelled you. You don't have to stay involved with Team Aqua now.

I'm not a traitor! This happened because of you!

Because of me? Ethan shot her an irritated look. Without me, Archie might already have caused Kyogre's Primal Reversion. Which would you choose: seas swallowing the world or being called a traitor?

Shelly had no answer. Angry, she ignored him and focused on piloting.

The tunnel brightened, and the submarine emerged into deep water. Almost immediately they saw another craft waiting outside the entrance.

Shelly reacted with a sharp turn, barely avoiding a collision. Matt, she said through her teeth.

The failed interception let them slip past, but Matt and Archie both chased after them. Neither submarine fell far behind.

They may follow us to the ends of the earth. Ethan glanced back. Does this thing have weapons?

A harpoon launcher and two torpedoes. They all fire forward.

That's unfortunate. Their submarines seem to be the same model. They can attack us from behind, and we can't fire back.

Relax, Shelly said without a trace of panic. I'm Team Aqua's best and fastest pilot. They won't catch me.

Ethan's phone rang. Anabel was calling. He answered immediately.

Thank goodness, I finally reached you, she said with relief. I'm aboard a maritime police vessel near the area. Where are you?

Her timing could not have been better. I'll send you my coordinates. Send me yours too. We stopped Archie, but he's chasing us now. We need support.

After the call, Ethan told Shelly about Anabel. To his surprise, she seemed unmoved.

You think I need help from the police? she scoffed. We're Team Aqua. We don't work with them, and we certainly don't ask them to protect us.

Are you still Team Aqua? Ethan gave her a knowing look. Archie threw you out in the cave. Right now you're on your own.

Again, Shelly had no answer. However unwilling she was to admit it, could she still call herself a member?

Even so, I don't need the police! she declared. Even if they catch me, even if they blow this submarine to pieces, I won't ask for help. I'll lose them myself!

Chapter 683: As Though He Were in Control

Anabel stood on the deck of the maritime police ship, scanning the blue sea through binoculars. Before long, a shark-shaped submarine surfaced and sped toward her.

She lowered the binoculars and called to the crew behind her. They're coming. Ready the crane!

It was the submarine carrying Ethan, Misty, and Shelly. Ethan had persuaded Shelly to change course and meet Anabel by using a firmer approach, reminding her who held the advantage.

The submarine slowed and stopped alongside the police ship. The trained crew quickly secured it and began lifting it from the water.

As it rose, Ethan looked out of the window. Far away, Archie and Matt's two submarines had stopped, unwilling to approach.

Archie might have lost his temper, but he had no appetite for a direct fight with the maritime police. Compared with Team Rocket, Team Aqua still lacked nerve.

Escaping Archie did not end the matter. Ethan turned his gaze elsewhere. A larger danger still demanded attention.

He had prevented Archie from capturing Kyogre or causing its Primal Reversion. But the battle had angered and woken it. After leaving its cave, Kyogre had created a terrifying whirlpool in the surrounding sea.

The ocean was indifferent, and so was its embodiment. Perhaps Kyogre had not meant to target the intruders at all. Perhaps the disturbance was an accidental consequence of its passing, or perhaps it meant to teach the humans and their followers a lesson. Whatever the reason, the whirlpool had formed.

It was enormous. It encompassed the entire maze of islands and the waters around them. Sea rushed toward its center and dragged at everything nearby. The low parts of some islands were submerged, leaving weaker Water-type Pokemon helpless as the landscape changed around them.

Fortunately, Kyogre had not undergone Primal Reversion. Sea level had not risen violently as Shelly's simulations predicted. The consequences could have been far worse.

Clang. In little more than ten seconds, the submarine had been hoisted level with the deck. Ethan opened the hatch, climbed out first, and jumped onto the police ship.

Anabel was waiting for him. She froze at the sight of his Team Aqua uniform. Why are you dressed like that?

It made the operation easier, Ethan said. He turned and helped Misty onto the deck.

Shelly emerged last, moving slowly. Anabel recognized Team Aqua's second-in-command and immediately reached toward her belt.

Easy. Ethan raised a hand. She's working with me now. She isn't an enemy.

Working with you? Anabel looked as if he were joking. Shelly was one of Team Aqua's chief strategists, second only to Archie. How could Ethan have won her over?

Yet Shelly stood there beside him. Anabel could hardly deny what she saw. Had Ethan somehow started dismantling Team Aqua from within?

She was about to ask her officers to take Shelly aside when Ethan stepped in front of her. He had read her intention.

Sorry. I still need her. I can't hand her over yet.

He did not say it outright, but Anabel understood: he meant to protect Shelly.

His sudden firmness took her aback. She would have warned most people against speaking that way to the International Police. With Ethan, she had no wish to cause a rift. His strength mattered, but so did the friendly cooperation that had begun with Looker and continued over time.

You've misunderstood, she said with a light laugh. We only need to ask a few questions. We should register her change of status too. Otherwise it may complicate matters for her when everything is reviewed later.

Ethan nodded. Anabel had decided how to handle it, and he was glad she understood. Thank you. But as I said, I can't hand her over until this is fully settled.

All right. Anabel was not troubled. If Shelly really was cooperating, a short delay would change little.

Throughout their conversation, Shelly listened silently as though they were discussing someone else. Anyone from Team Aqua who knew her would have been astonished to see her so subdued.

She looked out at the raging whirlpool. Kyogre's power was astounding. It also brought back the memory of what had happened in the submarine minutes earlier.

After she had refused to change course or accept police protection, Ethan had shown her a side of himself she had not expected. He had asserted his will in a way she could not resist.

It was different from Archie's rough temper, which always seemed a step from violence. Ethan's manner remained outwardly courteous, much like her first impression of him. Yet his anger could be frightening too. In that moment she had understood that, in one respect, he could be more intimidating than Archie.

She was accustomed to power struggles within Team Aqua and respected strength. Her thoughts had gone blank, and she had followed Ethan's instruction. Thinking back, it felt as though he had taken control of her.

The police ship set off after Archie and Matt. Both submarines dived and soon vanished, leaving Archie at large once again.

Anabel returned with nothing to show for the chase. The whirlpool still churned ahead. Kyogre had gone, but its power continued to disturb the sea without any sign of stopping.

At least Ethan's earlier message had given Anabel time to warn other vessels in the area. Any losses should be limited.

While Anabel and her crew worked, Ethan, Misty, and Shelly stood at the rail, watching the whirlpool. After a long silence, Shelly glanced at Ethan.

Aren't you going to do something? You have a Suicune. Surely it could calm a whirlpool like that.

Why do you think I should? Ethan asked.

She looked at him in surprise. Isn't it obvious? WeI've looked into your history. You've worked with these people since Kanto, then Johto and Hoenn. You've stopped one crisis after another. Isn't this what you do?

You've got me wrong. Ethan smiled faintly. Most of the time, I acted because someone asked me to. On the few other occasions, including this one, leaving things alone would have put all Hoenn at risk. Primal Kyogre would have been a catastrophe for its people and Pokemon, and I couldn't have escaped it either. Look at the situation now.

Shelly turned back to the sea. The whirlpool was frightening, but unlike what she had modeled at the Weather Institute, its effects were limited to this stretch of water. At worst it might affect Sootopolis City to some extent. Human society had the means to handle that danger.

I see. You aren't quite as overflowing with sympathy as I thought.

People who can't restrain their sympathy end up playing savior, Ethan said, narrowing his eyes. I've always considered that an insult. I might have a little sympathy, but that's all.

...

After more than two hours, the whirlpool gradually subsided. Anabel's ship had patrolled its perimeter throughout, keeping watch and searching for distress calls. Fortunately, everyone remained safe.

Ethan said goodbye to Anabel. He, Misty, and Shelly boarded the submarine again.

He had gained no prize from the expedition, but stopping Archie's plan was success enough. He had also turned an enemy into someone who might stand with him.

Shelly had nowhere obvious to go after leaving Team Aqua. She had not declared a new allegiance, yet Ethan expected that she would seek him out eventually. She was used to a dangerous, hidden life and unlikely to settle easily into ordinary society. Unless she joined another organization, he might be her only remaining refuge.

Could she disappear under a new name and live quietly? That would require a complete change of character.

The submarine traveled unseen through deep water and reached Sootopolis City safely. Archie did not appear again. Ethan found that odd at first, then understood. Unable to recover the Blue Orb for now, Archie would be following Kyogre before it vanished from sight. Otherwise he might spend another decade finding it again.

It was a frustrating but sensible choice for him.

Back in Sootopolis, the submarine surfaced inside Team Aqua's secret warehouse. Ethan stepped onto solid ground and voiced his concern.

Aren't you worried Archie could have people waiting here for us?

No. I built and maintain this warehouse myself. No one else knows about it, not even the other commanders. Archie doesn't know how many members Team Aqua has; he certainly doesn't know about this place.

Ethan understood. It had been Shelly's private base all along. While she belonged to Team Aqua, it served Team Aqua. Now that she had left, only she knew where it was.

Shelly took out the Blue Orb and offered it to Ethan. It still shone brightly, its flat, diamond-like faces casting colored light around the warehouse.

Ethan glanced at it but did not reach for it. Keep it.

What? Shelly stared. You're giving it to me? Aren't you taking it back to Mt. Pyre?

Archie stole it from Mt. Pyre once. He could do it again. Returning it there wouldn't solve anything.

Then why leave it with me? Aren't you afraid I'll disappear with it?

Where would you take it? Back to Archie? Ethan gave a short laugh. Besides, it's like a lamp with endless power that you can't switch off. If I carried it while traveling, I'd draw attention everywhere.

So you want me to keep it?

Yes. He met her eyes. You've shown me I can trust you with something important. Whatever else we disagree on, you can tell right from wrong when it matters. You led me to Archie. I think you're the right person to hold the orb.

After a long silence, Shelly put it away, almost as if she were following an order. What should I do with it?

Keep it safe for now. Ethan sighed. This isn't over. There's also the Red Orb, which can awaken another ancient Pokemon. If all else fails one day, we may need the Blue Orb to hold that Pokemon in check.

Chapter 684: A Champion Battles the Kids

After exchanging contact numbers with Shelly, Ethan and Misty left the warehouse district and walked from the harbor into central Sootopolis City.

Sootopolis was an island city that drew both traveling Trainers and many tourists. It was far busier and more prosperous than remote Dewford Island.

Its buildings were distinctive too. Nearly all of them were white, and their style reminded Ethan of Santorini in Greece. The city had an unmistakably Mediterranean feel, unlike the rest of Hoenn. He could see why visitors came from far away.

Evening was approaching, so they went to the Pokemon Center instead of challenging Sootopolis Gym. After checking in and eating dinner, they turned to training.

Ethan had a feeling Feebas was close to evolving. It seemed to need only one last push. He had no scientific proof, but years as a Trainer had taught him to trust that feeling.

As it happened, Sootopolis was preparing for a major festival. Excitement filled the city. The most anticipated finale was said to be a performance by the Sootopolis Gym Leader.

That Leader was Juan, not Wallace, who would take the position later. Juan might have an ordinary-sounding name, but he was an accomplished man: a Gym Leader, a Pokemon Coordinator, and Wallace's teacher.

Wallace, known as the Prince of Water and the Artist of Water, carried himself with an air of elegance. He had won the Ever Grande Conference and become a leading Coordinator. Juan had trained a remarkable student.

Now in his forties, Juan was elegant in manner and dress, witty in conversation, and devoted to beautiful battles. He was especially popular with local women. With someone so admired as the festival's star performer, Sootopolis was clearly taking the celebration seriously.

None of that was Ethan's immediate concern. He wanted to keep training Feebas.

In the pool behind the Pokemon Center, Misty's Pokemon again served as training partners. Ethan and Misty worked with Feebas late into the night.

Their effort paid off. Ethan had just ordered Feebas to use Tackle against Misty's Starmie when it stopped in the water. Brilliant white light enveloped it.

Ethan felt a surge of emotion. At last. He had waited a long time for this.

Pokemon such as Beldum and Feebas, or Magikarp before them, had required much more attention and unusual methods to evolve than partners ready to battle from the start. He had spent enormous effort on each. Now that work had paid off.

The light faded. An elegant Milotic floated in the pool.

Misty had seen and scanned a Milotic before, so she was not quite as overwhelmed as on her first encounter. Its beauty still astonished her. It's gorgeous! I could look at one again and again.

It's all right, I suppose. Nothing that special, Ethan said with a laugh. His pleased voice gave away how proud he was.

Misty had an excited thought. If you ever need to leave Milotic somewhere, could you send it to me?

To you? At Cerulean Gym?

Of course! Her eyes curved with delight. I helped it evolve, didn't I? And I love Milotic. It would be happier with me than at Cerise Park!

You're planning awfully far ahead. Ethan gave her a look. It only just evolved. It needs a lot more growing and training before it's where I want it. Even after Hoenn, it'll probably travel with me through the next region, maybe longer. You're already claiming it?

I'm just happy for you! she said with a grin.

They spent a long while admiring Milotic. When it was nearly two in the morning, they finally recalled their Pokemon and went to their separate rooms.

Ethan was physically exhausted, but too delighted to fall asleep at once. Milotic had evolved and could now battle properly. It was time for the next stage of its training.

...

Ethan slept until nearly noon. His body had rested, but he still felt sluggish when he woke. One occasional late night was manageable at his age.

He washed, met Misty in the dining room, and ate lunch. Then, instead of going to Sootopolis Gym, he sought out battles.

Juan was often away from the Gym during festival preparations, so Ethan might have arrived to find it empty. Meanwhile, the Pokemon Center was full of Trainers. Newcomers and their Pokemon were out on the streets too. Their varying levels of experience offered exactly what Milotic needed.

The second stage of training would still mean repeated battles, but now Milotic would face other Pokemon in real matches instead of simple practice sessions.

Ethan gave Misty the afternoon to explore the city and enjoy the festival atmosphere. He went to a nearby park on his own.

Children chased each other through the grounds, as they did in any park. Ethan looked around and soon found what he wanted.

Sootopolis was a seaside city with pools and waterways throughout its streets, and this park had one too. In a simple aquatic battlefield at its edge, two boys of perhaps seven or eight were battling with Water-type Pokemon.

They looked young and innocent. Ethan approached them with a broad smile.

One wore a baseball cap; the other had rosy cheeks. Both had a little runny nose. Their Pokemon were Poliwag and Krabby. Neither was especially strong, but they were putting up an energetic fight.

The boys stopped to stare at the handsome stranger. Adults had never shown much interest in their games before.

Ethan turned Milotic's Poke Ball in his hand. You two look strong. Would either of you like a battle?

Recognition from an adult thrilled them. They nodded eagerly, though they had never met him. Sure!

The boy in the cap hurried to one side, and Ethan took his former place. I should warn you: I have only this one Pokemon, and it just evolved. It's not very strong yet, so don't expect too much. Which of you wants to go first?

Me! The rosy-cheeked boy shoved past his friend and sent Krabby toward the middle of the pool. Come on!

Krabby brandished its great pincers at Ethan, as spirited as its Trainer.

Ethan nodded approvingly and released Milotic. Blue light flashed, and it appeared in the water.

Both boys squealed with delight. Milotic!

Wow, it's so pretty!

They forgot about battling and crowded Ethan with questions. Where did you catch it? Can I touch it?

Their sudden shrieks made his ears ring. One thing at a time. Let's battle first.

Children could be distracted by anything new. Reminded why Ethan was there, they finally refocused.

All right! I'll beat it! the rosy-cheeked boy declared.

Once both Pokemon had taken their places, the park battle began.

Krabby, Bubble!

The boy ordered an attack immediately. At his age, he had little sense of strategy, type matchups, or how to adjust during a fight. Whoever the opponent was, his answer was to attack straight ahead.

Krabby scuttled across a shallow platform in the pool, spraying bubbles as it went. They expanded until some were as large as basketballs, then drifted toward Milotic.

Krabby and its young Trainer were not strong, but the move could still hurt. Most of Ethan's other Pokemon would have dodged or countered on their own.

Milotic, however, had evolved from a rather vacant Feebas only the night before. Its body was stronger, but it had even less battle experience than Krabby and still carried some of Feebas's habits. It might dodge by instinct; it could not yet judge the fight for itself.

That was no problem as long as it followed Ethan's instructions. Milotic, dive, then use Water Gun!

Both Pokemon were Water types, so their Water-type moves would do less damage to each other. Milotic nevertheless had plenty of ways to use the water around it.

Its smooth body slipped beneath the surface. Like a water snake, it swam past the bubbles and surfaced behind Krabby. A strong stream from its mouth struck Krabby's back.

Water Gun did little direct damage, but its force knocked Krabby into the pool.

Don't let it climb out. Use Wrap!

Crab-like Pokemon could not swim through the water as swiftly or nimbly as fish and many other Water types. Krabby's powerful claws could still keep an enemy awayif its Trainer knew how to use them.

The rosy-cheeked boy did not. Before he could react, Milotic coiled its long body around Krabby. As the hold tightened, Krabby waved its pincers helplessly, unable to reach Milotic at that angle.

The boy's expression changed. The more anxious he became, the harder it was to think of a useful command. Krabby, shake it off!

Krabby could not. The pressure mounted. It blew a stream of tiny bubbles and fainted in Milotic's coils.

The match had been so easy that Ethan had scarcely needed to think. A few simple commands had won it.

I...I lost, the boy said. His face reddened as he hurriedly recalled Krabby.

His friend pushed him aside and sent out Poliwag. You idiot. Watch me!

For all his confidence, the boy in the cap lost even faster. Milotic dodged Poliwag's Water Gun, used Disarming Voice to catch its attention, and then trapped it with Wrap. The same hold ended the second match.

The boys stared at Milotic in admiration. Ethan smiled calmly. Milotic had gained confidence in those two battles and grown comfortable in its new body.

A familiar voice sounded behind him. Honestly, Misty said, laughing. I wondered what you'd do after sending me off. I never expected to find you here beating up little kids!

Chapter 685: One Challenger Leads to Another

Ethan turned. Misty stood on a low wall behind him with an ice pop in her mouth. When he looked her way, she jumped down, came over, and handed him a second one.

Why didn't you explore? Ethan asked. I gave you the day off. You didn't have to stay with me.

There wasn't much to see. Misty took the ice pop from her mouth. The buildings have different shapes, but after a while they all start to look the same. And the festival's still several days away. Nothing much is happening yet.

She gave him a teasing look. I'm glad I came back, though. Otherwise I'd have missed your fierce struggle against these children.

What struggle? I swept the field!

Of course you did, she said, grinning wider. Against two little boys. Very impressive.

Ethan ignored her and turned to the boys. Well? Want another battle? I'm ready whenever you are.

They glanced at each other and shook their heads. No. We can't beat you. But beating us doesn't mean we've given up!

You don't want to battle, but you won't admit defeat. What do you want?

The boy in the baseball cap said, Beating us is nothing. If you can beat Kinta, then we'll admit you're better!

Kinta?

He's the strongest of us, the rosy-cheeked boy explained. Neither of us can beat him. You won't either!

Ethan gathered that Kinta was the leader among the local children. All right. Go and get him. I'll wait here.

The boys dashed away. Only then did Ethan accept the ice pop from Misty and sit beside the pool. He called Milotic over and reviewed the battles with it while they ate.

Going over a match was an important part of a Pokemon's growth. It helped Milotic recognize what it needed to improve and remember what to watch for next time.

They finished their review, but the boys still had not returned. Ethan began to think they had stood him up. Then Misty pointed across the park.

The two boys were coming back, breathless, pushing a third boy between them. This must be Kinta.

Ethan studied him. Kinta was a year or two older than the other boys, perhaps around Misty and Ash's age. He looked thoroughly unwilling to be dragged here. Ethan heard him complaining long before they arrived.

Slow down! I'm busy. I don't have time for one of your little play battles.

It's different this time! the boy in the cap pleaded. We met someone really strong. We can't beat him. You have to help us!

Despite Kinta's resistance, they pushed him in front of Ethan. He wore an aloof, self-important expression.

I hear you're strong, Ethan said before Kinta could speak.

Kinta raised an eyebrow and studied him cautiously. He had expected another child, not an adult. Why would an adult battle his two younger friends?

You're the one who bullied them? he asked.

Bullying? Ethan laughed. We had a friendly battle. When they lost, they said only you could beat me. That's why they fetched you.

And you call that friendly? You're a grown man battling little kids. Aren't you embarrassed? Kinta sighed with exaggerated maturity, broke free of his friends, and took the other Trainer's position.

I thought they'd found another child, someone who wasn't worth my time. But you're an adult, and you beat my friends. I can't ignore that.

Ethan stared. Kinta had a remarkably big mouth for a boy. This was the second time someone had criticized him for battling children. What was wrong with battling them? Kinta was a child too.

Back on Earth, Ethan had heard sayings about never dismissing a young person for what they had yet to become. The words themselves might not exist here, but the meaning did. Who could know whether one of these children might turn out to be a talent like Garyor someone like Ash?

Ethan could battle Legendary Pokemon one day and children at a park the next. Taking every opponent seriously was part of how he had come this far. In their youth, these boys had the good fortuneor misfortuneto meet him.

Kinta glanced at Milotic, then threw his Poke Ball. A Tentacruel appeared on a step in the water.

The sight stirred Ethan's memory of the giant Tentacruel he had faced in Kanto. Back then, handling it had been difficult. He had traveled and grown so much since that he could deal with it easily now. He even had more Legendary Pokemon than many new Trainers had ordinary partners. Seeing Tentacruel again made him feel how much time had passed.

He set the thought aside and directed Milotic into position.

Go, Kinta! the rosy-cheeked boy shouted. His friend in the cap stepped forward to serve as referee.

Begin!

The battle started at once. Ethan quickly saw that Kinta was more experienced than the younger boys. His commands were sharper, and Tentacruel was much stronger than their Pokemon. Kinta had reason to be confident.

Even so, he was still a child. He did not yet match Trainers who traveled and battled regularly. Ethan judged him only a little stronger than Wally had been when they met.

Early on, Tentacruel's many tentacles and poison put Milotic under pressure. Once Ethan understood Kinta's attack pattern, he brought the match under control. Milotic used Refresh to clear the poison, leaving little to threaten it. Ethan took the opening and finished the battle in a decisive series of attacks.

Kinta went still. The younger boys stared, unable to believe the result.

K-Kinta...you lost? the rosy-cheeked boy asked.

Kinta flushed. Idiot! I didn't lose. I just let my guard down!

He turned to Ethan. That one doesn't count. Battle me again!

The reluctant, careless air he had worn before was gone. Now he wanted badly to defeat Ethan in front of his friends.

Another battle? Sure, Ethan said. He was here to train Milotic. A stronger opposing Pokemon would make the practice more useful.

Kinta breathed in, recalled the unconscious Tentacruel, and took out a second Poke Ball with a serious expression.

He had claimed carelessness, but he knew he had fought with everything he had. Milotic itself had not seemed overwhelmingly strong. Ethan's commands were the problem. One moment the battle had been even; the next, Kinta had been unable to respond.

He had felt that suffocating helplessness only once before, against a man he admired. Could this stranger really be that strong? Nosomeone who went around challenging children could hardly compare with his hero.

Ethan knew none of Kinta's thoughts. He watched the boy's expression shift before Kinta finally threw the ball.

Marshtomp appeared.

Marshtomp was the evolved form of Mudkip, one of Hoenn's three starter Pokemon. It usually lived on thick, muddy ground and buried itself in mud to sleep. Over time it had developed strong hips and legs, letting it stand and walk steadily even on soft terrain.

A thin membrane covered its body, helping it survive on land and move quickly through mud. In the right conditions, it could make full use of its abilities.

For Kinta to bring Marshtomp out now, it was probably stronger than Tentacruel. Its eagerness to fight and the determined look on Kinta's face suggested something more: Marshtomp was likely his first Pokemon and his ace.

Have I become some great rival he has to overcome? Ethan smiled and sent Milotic out again.

Come on, Kinta! The two younger boys cupped their hands around their mouths and shouted so loudly that people nearby glanced over. When they saw only an adult battling a group of children, they lost interest.

The second match began. Kinta stayed focused and cautious, but the pattern repeated. After their opening exchanges, Ethan read his movements and commands. Suddenly Kinta's attacks no longer posed a threat, and Milotic defeated Marshtomp with apparent ease.

Once again Kinta felt unable to breathe under Ethan's control of the battle. How...? He stepped back, pale-faced, and stood stunned.

His two friends sat down hard, as though the sky had fallen. Misty leaned lazily against a bench and yawned. After the battles she had seen, this little match gave her no urge to applaud.

Ethan called Milotic back to him and stroked the scales on its head in encouragement. Then he looked at Kinta.

Well? Another round? I'm ready whenever you are.

It was the same tone he had used with the younger boys. Ethan meant nothing by it, but it made Kinta's temper rise. Of all people, he did not want to lose to a man who sought out children to battle.

Yet both his Pokemon had been beaten. He could no longer deny the difference between them. He took a deep breath and forced himself to calm down.

Don't get smug. Beating me doesn't mean much. If you can beat the person I bring back, then I'll admit defeat.

Haven't I heard that before? Ethan glanced at the two younger boys, then nodded. Fine. Go find whoever you like. I'll wait here.

You said it! Kinta shot him one last resentful look and led his friends out of the park.

Ethan laughed as he watched them go. He had only wanted two easy opponents to let Milotic practice. Instead, one challenger had led to another.

That suited him. As the opponents changed, the battles grew harder, saving him the trouble of searching for Trainers at the right level. He wanted to see who they would bring back next.

Chapter 686: The Spirited Idol

This time Ethan and Misty waited even longer than before.

How much longer? Long enough for Ethan to spot another little boy who had just entered the park, challenge him, and defeat him in short order. The boy left looking miserable.

Milotic gained more experience, while the boy acquired a defeat he would have trouble forgetting. Misty's teasing had come true: Ethan really was sweeping through the local children.

I, Ethan, am incredibly strong!

It might not have been the fairest way to find opponents, but the battles were useful. Milotic had grown completely comfortable with its evolved body and was beginning to move with ease. If it kept improving at this rate, it would soon catch up to Eevee and Combusken. That would give Ethan another powerful choice for his team.

At noon, Ethan and Misty bought hot dogs and coffee in the park and ate lunch there. Only afterward did Kinta finally return.

The two younger boys were with him, along with a girl Ethan had never met. Even from a distance, she seemed to radiate youthful energy.

She looked about Misty's age, pretty and a little playful. Long locks framed either side of her face, and a ponytail rose from her blue-green hair like a bolt of lightning.

Her dark blue miniskirt was dotted with tiny stars. She wore a matching top that left her midriff bare, a white stocking on one leg, blue boots, cloudlike decorations at her wrists and ankles, and large earrings. The other leg was bare. She looked like someone from an idol group.

Kinta, so aloof earlier, now led the way with a broad smile. He kept turning to speak to her, with none of his former swagger left. The two younger boys trailed behind, blushing and staring at the ground. Neither dared say a word.

The girl herself showed no sign of arrogance or spoiled behavior. She had simply drawn all three boys' admiration.

Yet something about her bothered Ethan. Why did she look familiar?

As he tried to place her, Misty stepped up beside him without a word. Her face was blank, but Ethan could feel her hostility toward the approaching girl.

Kinta stopped in front of him and puffed out his chest. This is the help I went to find! If you can beat her, I'll admit you're strong.

Ethan nodded. He did not particularly care who his next opponent was. He beckoned Milotic toward the starting position, but before he could give it a command, Kinta frowned.

Wait. Don't tell me you don't know who's standing in front of you?

Ethan looked at the idol-like girl again. Their eyes met. He still could not identify her, though she seemed to be studying his face with the same uncertainty.

Kinta could bear his ignorance no longer. You really don't know her? She's the most popular and famous Pokemon Contest idol in all HoennLissi Lisia!

Lisia? An idol? The name meant nothing to Ethan. He was sure he had seen her in the anime back on Earth, but he could not remember which series she had appeared in or what had happened around her.

Misty, however, reacted to the nickname. I've heard of you! Aren't you the beautiful Coordinator who sings CharmLove?

Since becoming friends with May, Misty had learned a great deal about Pokemon Contests and their best-known performers. She had seen Lisia in reports and on the news more than once. Only a few nights ago she had listened to CharmLove before bed and thought it was a good song. Finding its singer here in the park was astonishing.

Lisia gave them a bright smile. Hello! I'm Lisia, and yes, I'm a Contest idol. Lissi is just what my fans like to call me. And that song is my current theme song.

Then she looked Ethan over again. Um...have we met somewhere before? I feel as though I've seen you.

Misty's heart gave a jolt. She studied their expressions, searching for some sign that they knew each other. She could do little about the older women in Ethan's life, but she did not want another pretty girl her own age getting close to him. I was here first!

Ethan was certain he had never met Lisia. Today was the first time he had even heard her name. She must have seen footage of him competing in a League tournament. As an idol, she would probably encounter news and popular topics more often than most people. One of his battles might have left an impression.

He had no wish to draw attention to his identity. You must be mistaken. This is the first time we've met.

I suppose so. Lisia accepted that and turned to the reason she had come. You're the one who beat Kinta?

That's right. So you're my next opponent?

Of course! she said. Kinta and I have been friends since we were little. He came to ask me for help, so I can't let him down.

Facing a Coordinator would be a new experience for Ethan. He had never imagined himself battling one. Let's see what difference there is between your battles and ours.

He was about to send Milotic into place when something on Lisia's hair ornament caught his eye: a Key Stone.

He had not expected to see one in Hoenn. A Key Stone was crucial to a Pokemon's Mega Evolution, and hardly anyone would wear one merely for decoration. Lisia, then, could Mega Evolve a Pokemon too.

That made her more interesting. Neither of them was likely to use such power in this match, but it suggested she was far more capable than Kinta or his two younger friends.

Lisia noticed where he was looking. Does he recognize it? she wondered. This power comes from another region...

Before she could think further, Kinta folded his arms and addressed Ethan. Don't say I didn't warn you. Lisia doesn't battle very often, but she's strong! She's Mr. Wallace's niece, too. If you want to surrender, now's your chance.

Wallace's niece? Ethan was surprised again. A casual chain of park challenges had brought him from two little boys to an idol related to a Gym Leader and Champion. The world sometimes felt enormous and sometimes remarkably small.

But did Kinta really think a famous relative's name would frighten him off? That was childish. He would not be afraid to face Lisia, Wallace himself, or anyone else in Hoenn.

Before Ethan could reply, the two younger boys chimed in. That's right! Lisia's really busy. She was filming when we found her. She only slipped away because Kinta begged her over and over. If you're scared to battle, just surrender!

They meant to impress Ethan with how much trouble she had taken to come. To Kinta, their words sounded awful.

You two, shut up! he snapped, face reddening as he glared at them. Had he really looked that desperate when he asked Lisia? Why did they have to tell Ethan he had begged?

A quick glance showed that Ethan seemed not to care, and Kinta relaxed. Then he caught Misty looking at him with an amused expression. His spirits sank again. So much for saving face.

Ethan took his place in the Trainer's area and directed Milotic to the starting position. Across the pool, he and Lisia faced one another while they waited for her Pokemon.

Even her voice reminded Ethan of Casey in Johto. Both girls seemed full of energy. Perhaps their Pokemon were the same.

Lisia did not take out a Poke Ball. Instead, she snapped her fingers toward the sky.

A moment later, a Pokemon swooped down and landed beside her. Lisia patted the Altaria's shoulder and smiled. Here's my partner for the battle!

Ethan saw nothing unusual in the choice, but Kinta looked alarmed. Lisia, you're using Ali? Are you sure that's a good idea?

Why wouldn't it be? she asked.

Kinta glanced at Ethan, then leaned close to her ear. You have a festival performance in a few days and Contests in other cities after that. He's no easy opponent. What if Ali gets hurt?

He was genuinely worried for her. Lisia shook her head with a smile. You can't be afraid of an injury every time you battle. Besides, Ali is strong. We won't lose easily. And even if Ali does get hurt, Nurse Joy can heal Ali in no time.

Kinta was about to argue, but Lisia had already turned to Ethan. All right! Let's have a sparkling, gorgeous battle!

Ethan raised an eyebrow. Where had that sudden burst of excitement come from? Then he remembered Casey. Perhaps this was simply what an energetic girl was like when a battle began.

This time Kinta took the role of referee. Once both sides were ready, he cast one more worried look at Ali and brought his arm down.

It was a battle between a Pokemon in the water and one in the air. Milotic was a Water type; Altaria was Dragon and Flying. At first glance, Milotic seemed to be at a disadvantage. Altaria's Dragon typing resisted Water attacks, and it could strike downward from above while Milotic fought upward from the pool.

But the pool also posed a danger to Altaria. Apart from the two circular platforms, the field was almost entirely water. If Altaria's fluffy feathers became soaked, it would lose its aerial advantage and might be unable to take off again for a while. Stranded on a platform, it would be at Milotic's mercy.

Milotic, meanwhile, could dive beneath the surface whenever it needed to evade an attack. Both Pokemon had ways to use the field. The question was which Trainer would seize the initiative.

Chapter 687: Wallace, the Water Prince

Milotic, use Water Gun!

Altaria, use Sing!

Sing was a Normal-type move that could lull its target to sleep. In effect, it was much like Hypnosis or any other sleep-inducing move; the difference lay in its type.

From those first commands, the difference between Ethan's approach and Lisia's was already clear. Most Trainers preferred a direct attack. If they could defeat an opponent with sheer force, they would. Only when a battle turned against them, or an opponent proved difficult to break down, did they tend to vary their tactics.

Coordinators gave more thought to how a battle looked. A simple attack held less appeal than a complicated, dazzling move. Neither approach was inherently right or wrong. They were different ways to battle, and only a match between them would show how they fared together.

Milotic opened its mouth and sent a thick jet of water at Altaria. With a quick beat of its cloudlike wings, Altaria barely dodged the Water Gun and began to sing.

But Lisia's Altaria did more than sing. As its lovely voice filled the park, it traced graceful circles through the air, almost dancing.

Years of Pokemon Contests had likely made that movement a habit. Lisia encouraged it: judges and spectators enjoyed a performance that gave their eyes as much to follow as their ears. Here, however, those extra movements gave Ethan openings.

The two younger boys watched openmouthed. They had only seen performances like this on television. Now a beautiful idol's Pokemon was dancing directly above them. At last they understood why people found such performances so thrilling.

Ethan could appreciate its beauty too, but the elaborate display also gave him ample time to react. Milotic's eyes began to droop under the soothing music.

Underwater, Ethan ordered.

Milotic plunged into the pool. Cold water closed around its body, washing the drowsiness away. When it surfaced again, Altaria was still dancing.

Much too slow.

Lisia did not seem concerned. Sing had only been a test. The main performance was still to come.

She spun in place like a cheerful sprite, struck a cute pose, and smiled. Now our blue-green moves and our grand performance can begin in dazzling style!

...

Splash!

Altaria, soaked through, fell from the sky like a stone and struck the pool. It did not resurface. Their park battle had ended in Milotic's victory.

Victory had cost Milotic dearly. Scratches marred its beautiful scales, its strength was nearly spent, and it panted so hard that it clearly could not battle again.

For all Lisia's elaborate style, her Altaria had been formidable. Ethan would put her near Drew, the strong young Coordinator they had met recently. Both were far ahead of most people their age.

As the exchange grew fiercer, the Pokemon had fought almost evenly. For a while neither could gain a decisive advantage. Ethan's sharp commands let Milotic attack or defend at just the right moment, but Lisia had a strength of her own.

Altaria's experience had grown through countless battles. It could read a situation, dodge, and counterattack without waiting for an order, often faster than Milotic. An instinctive response took less time than a Trainer seeing a move, deciding what to do, and calling out a command.

Each side had fought to its own rhythm, which was why the contest remained close until the end. As Ethan had expected, though, repeated Water-type attacks soaked Altaria's feathers. Their growing weight hindered its flight. Once it lost its advantage in the air, Ethan found his chance and finished the match with Water Gun.

Those cloudlike feathers gave Altaria its distinctive beauty and helped it in the air. This time they had also brought it down.

That's impossible. Lisia lost...?

Kinta spoke before either Trainer did. He had swallowed his pride and brought Lisia here to avenge his defeats. He had placed all his hopes in her and never considered that Ethan might beat her too.

Lisia was a Contest idol and a skilled Coordinator. Kinta had battled her many times without winning once. Even some adult Trainers on Sootopolis Island could not beat her, especially when she used Ali, her strongest Pokemon. Could this man really be that good?

Ethan, meanwhile, was pleased with Milotic. It looked battered, but a narrow victory was still a victory. It had only recently evolved and did not know many moves yet. Beating an opponent like Altaria, even with Ethan's guidance bringing out everything it had and more, was a great step forward.

Lisia hurried to the edge of the pool and peered into the water. Ethan signaled Milotic to dive after Altaria and bring it up.

Milotic carried Ali to the bank. Altaria was in a sorry state. Its fluffy feathers hung flat and wet, and it looked nothing like the beautiful Pokemon that had taken to the sky at the start of the match.

Ali... Lisia knelt to check on it. Finding it conscious and in no serious danger, she finally relaxed. Then she looked at Ethan with open admiration. You're really good. I lost this battle.

Let's call it a draw. Ethan smiled and shook his head. I know you were holding something back. If you'd used that, my Milotic would have lost.

He tilted his head toward the Key Stone in her hair. Misty, Kinta, and the two younger boys followed his gaze and noticed it at last.

So you do know what it is! Lisia's eyes brightened. Have you been to Kalos or another region? Or do you have one too, like I do?

To Kinta and the boys, their conversation made no sense. Only Misty understood. Kinta scratched his head. Wasn't the thing in Lisia's hair just an ornament?

I have one, Ethan said. I've even used it. It worked rather well.

Lisia opened her mouth to reply, but hurried footsteps sounded nearby. A woman in her twenties was rushing toward them.

Oh, that's my manager! Lisia stuck out her tongue at the others. She must have found out I slipped away. I have to get back, and I need to have Ali treated too.

She said goodbye, recalled Altaria, and went to meet the woman.

With Lisia gone, the rest had little reason to stay. Kinta and his friends had now seen even the person they had called for help defeated. They exchanged glances and slunk off in Lisia's direction without saying whether they admitted defeat.

Ethan was still watching them leave when Misty spoke in a sour voice. Still looking? She's out of sight already.

What are you thinking? Ethan gave her a light knock on the head.

Am I wrong? Misty pouted. She's pretty, her skin's fair, and she's an idol. Everyone likes her. Did you see Kinta and those two boys? They practically wanted to put her on a pedestal.

Come on. Ethan rubbed her hair. Do you think I'm interested in her? She's about your age. Why would I fall for little girls who haven't grown up yet?

That struck Misty harder than he realized. She huffed, straightened her back, and glanced down at her chest. Then her shoulders sagged.

Just wait. I'll grow up someday!

Milotic was injured too badly to keep training. Ethan took it to the Pokemon Center for Nurse Joy to treat, bringing the day's plan to an end.

He had managed only five battles, fewer than he had hoped. Still, each opponent had been stronger than the last. Milotic had gained a great deal and was beginning to catch up with the rest of his Pokemon.

...

The Sootopolis Gym stood in the north of the city at the foot of an extinct volcano. Its height gave it one of the city's finest views; from there, nearly all of Sootopolis could be seen.

Juan, the official Gym Leader, specialized in Water-type Pokemon. Defeating him would earn a Challenger the Rain Badge.

After a night's rest, Ethan went there with Misty early the next morning, hoping to find Juan. As they had heard, he was a busy man. With the festival approaching, he spent most days away from the Gym. A visitor either had to arrange an appointment or hope to catch him by chance.

The Gym resembled a grand estate. Neatly tended gardens surrounded its handsome main building, making it look more like a nobleman's home than a place for Pokemon battles.

Before entering, Ethan noticed several middle-aged women lingering outside. What were they waiting for? Was Juan truly so charming that women their age gathered wherever he went?

Curious, Ethan and Misty went inside. The interior was just as elegant: statues, framed art, fine chandeliers, and polished marble floors. Whoever had decorated it had excellent taste.

But they saw no one. In the hall, their footsteps were the only sound. There was not even a staff member in sight. Had they come all this way for nothing?

Can I help you? a man called from above.

They looked up. A man with blue-green hair stood by the railing of the second-floor gallery, looking down at them. He wore a round white hat, a white outfit, and two long green drapes over his shoulders.

Ethan recognized him at once: Wallace, Hoenn's former Champion and the former Leader of the Sootopolis Gym. He was one of the people of Sootopolis, a distinguished Pokemon Trainer and top Coordinator, the elegant man known as the Water Prince.

What a surprise. Ethan had come looking for Juan, only to find Juan's even more accomplished student.

Sorry to disturb you, Ethan said with a smile. I'm here to challenge the Sootopolis Gym. Is the Gym Leader in?

Wallace was about to answer when light footsteps approached him. A familiar girl appeared at his side.

She followed Wallace's gaze down to the hall. The moment she saw Ethan, she pointed at him in surprise. Oh! It's you!

Chapter 688: So That's What You're Like, Juan!

The girl who had called out was Lisia, the idol Ethan had battled only yesterday. He had not expected to find her here too.

Kinta had said she was Wallace's niece. Standing side by side, their matching blue-green hair and similar features made the family resemblance plain. They must both have taken after Lisia's mother's side of the family.

Ethan smiled and waved to her. Misty pursed her lips and looked away. Why does this girl keep turning up?

Wallace looked from his niece to Ethan in surprise. You know each other?
