Of course! Lisia told him all about the previous day's battle, complete with gestures and dramatic detail.

When she finished, Wallace laughed. You say the match ended in a draw?

It did! Lisia nodded. I lost, but he said himself that we could call it a draw.

Then you did very well. Not many people can hold a man who's won the championships of two regions to a draw!

What? Lisia stared at her uncle. What do you mean?

You still don't see it? With a flourish, Wallace pointed at Ethan. This is the man everyone's been talking aboutthe winner of the Indigo League who went on to win the Silver Conference!

What? Lisia turned to Ethan in shock. She had battled the Champion of two regional tournaments without knowing it.

Now she remembered why he had looked so familiar. She had seen videos of his battles and posters promoting him.

You really kept that from me!

Kept what from you? Ethan smiled. I told you the truth. Yesterday was our first meeting. You recognized me from somewhere else, and you never asked my name. How could I have hidden it?

Lisia was ready with a retort, but a moment's thought stopped her. Neither she nor Kinta had asked his name, even after the battle. Strictly speaking, Ethan was right. She still felt deceived, and her cheeks puffed out in protest.

Ethan found the expression amusing. He shook his head and spoke more formally. Then let me introduce myself now. I'm Ethan Vale, a Trainer. I came today to challenge Mr. Juan, the Leader of the Sootopolis Gym.

That's better. Lisia's irritation vanished as quickly as it had come. But my teacher isn't here. He's been so busy lately that he hasn't attended to the Gym for days.

Her teacher? Ethan had known Wallace was Juan's student. So Lisia had studied under him too. Uncle and niece had learned from the same master, an unusual arrangement. Both had become outstanding in their own fields. Their talent mattered, but Juan must have been an excellent teacher as well.

Still, Juan really was absent. Had Ethan come for nothing? He exchanged a disappointed look with Misty.

Wallace and Lisia came down the red-carpeted marble stairs to meet them. Unlike yesterday, Lisia circled Ethan with unabashed curiosity. When she saw his troubled expression, she smiled.

You don't have to worry. You're lucky you ran into me today! One call from me, and my teacher will come straight back, wherever he is.

Would that be all right? Ethan asked. You said he's busy. The festival's large enough that the whole city has spent days preparing. Everyone I saw outside seemed to take it seriously. I wouldn't want him to change his plans just for me.

Don't worry. Lisia waved away his concern. They hold this festival every year. My teacher knows it inside out. He doesn't need endless rehearsals. Besides...

Her smile turned mischievous. He only looks busy. Really, he's hiding from those women who are a little too enthusiastic about him. That's why he hasn't dared come back to the Gym!

So that explained the middle-aged women waiting outside. Ethan had learned a little piece of local gossip. Being popular could be troublesome too.

...

Lisia called Juan. While they waited, she and Wallace showed Ethan and Misty around the Gym. Few visitors would receive a personal tour from them, but they treated Ethan as an equal.

As they talked, Ethan learned more about both of them. Wallace, for one, was extremely busy. He offered few details, yet Ethan sensed that he was investigating something important. His return to Sootopolis was only a short pause to rest and consult some information. He might leave again that afternoon or the next day. Meeting him now had been fortunate.

Lisia's schedule was little easier. She was touring and performing around the world, spending most of her time outside Hoenn. The coming festival had brought her home: as an idol from Sootopolis, she had been invited to film a short promotional piece. It also gave her a brief chance to rest with her familyand had led to yesterday's encounter in the park.

Fame kept both of them busy. The admiration they enjoyed came with demands on their time.

Ethan wondered what he would do when his own travels ended. Would he settle somewhere quiet and enjoy an early retirement, or keep himself occupied as they did? He put the thought aside. That decision lay far in the future. For now, he had enough to do.

After the tour, Wallace had other matters to handle and left the Gym. He had wanted to watch the man who had won two regional tournaments battle his teacher, but his schedule would not allow it.

Without her uncle there, Lisia grew even more inquisitive. She asked Ethan how he had begun as a Trainer, which rare Pokemon he had met, and what adventures he had experienced. He could hardly keep up with her questions.

Perhaps a life planned around performances made travel sound especially appealing. With each answer, her eyes seemed to shine brighter.

Misty grew more annoyed by the minute. She had already been wary of a pretty girl her own age. Now Lisia's interest in Ethan seemed suspicious to her. Eventually she had had enough, idol or not, and began making pointed remarks.

Only then did Lisia give the equally pretty girl at Ethan's side her full attention. From the first moment, Lisia had liked Misty no more than Misty liked her. Perhaps two equally outgoing girls, one sharper and the other more playful, were bound to rub each other the wrong way.

How strange, Misty said coolly. You're a Coordinator, yet you're so interested in a Trainer's travels. Aren't you crossing into someone else's territory?

What she meant by territory was clear enough to her, if no one else.

Coordinators and Trainers both travel with Pokemon, Lisia replied, giving her a sidelong look. How is that crossing a line? Speaking of lines, I think distance is far more frustrating. You can see someone but never reach them. However hard you try, you're still standing in the same place.

They were young, but neither missed the meaning behind the other's words. Ethan listened to them trade barbs and felt a headache coming on. How had the conversation turned into this?

Rapid footsteps from the hall interrupted them. Before Ethan saw who was coming, a strong, slightly resonant voice rang through the Gym.

Little Lisia, your teacher is here! Why did you need me back so urgently?

Ethan turned. A man around forty was hurrying toward them in an ornate blue suit with a white bow tie. He had a neat little mustache and a white feather ornament on his head.

This was Juan: the current Sootopolis Gym Leader, teacher to Wallace and Lisia, a Trainer and Coordinator, and the man the local ladies called their ravishing Gym Leader.

Ethan could see why Juan had so many admirers. Even to another man, his charm was obvious. It was more than his handsome face; it came naturally from the way he carried himself. Like Wallace, Juan had gathered a remarkable collection of titles and admirers. Ethan could imagine Lisia doing the same when she was older.

But why was Juan speaking to her with such extravagant affection?

Juan reached Lisia, dropped to one knee like an actor on a stage, and lifted his voice. The moment you called, I set everything aside! Little Lisia, it's been so long. You grow more beautiful and adorable every time I see you.

Ethan understood. Juan was hopelessly fond of young girlsor, more accurately, doted on Lisia like a daughter. He wondered what the women outside would think if they saw this display.

Lisia seemed used to it. She smiled sweetly. I didn't call you here for myself. He did. She indicated Ethan. He's here to challenge the Gym. You were away, so I took the liberty of contacting you.

Juan seemed to notice the other visitors for the first time. His eyes settled on Ethan, a handsome man standing close to Lisia, and his expression changed at once.

Who are you? How do you know Lisia?

He studied Ethan with the alarm of a father who had just seen a prized daughter approached by a flashy young delinquent. Ethan felt the hostility and could not resist teasing him.

Sorry to trouble you, he said pleasantly. I am here to challenge the Gym. Lisia saw you were out and kindly called you for me, just as she said. As for how we met, perhaps you should ask her.

You've got some nerve! Juan thought. His first suspicion had only been a wild guess. Now he was convinced this young man was trying to charm his precious student.

I see. Juan spoke through clenched teeth. A Gym challenge, is it? Good. I haven't had a proper chance to stretch in quite some time. Since you've come to me, let me see what you can do!

He snorted, turned, and strode deeper into the Gym without giving Ethan a chance to answer. One teasing reply had been enough to make him angry. At this rate, Ethan would not need to ask Juan to use his strongest Pokemon. Juan would choose them himself.

Chapter 689: Unexpected Battle Rules

After learning a little about Juan, Ethan wanted a proper battle with him. A man who had trained both Wallace and Lisia had to be an exceptional Trainer, even if his students had since surpassed him. This Gym challenge was an opportunity Ethan would regret missing.

As Juan strode ahead, Lisia stuck out her tongue and spoke quietly to Ethan. Sorry. My teacher is usually elegant and composed. He only acts childish like that around me. Has he made things difficult for you?

I should be the one apologizing, Ethan said. A challenger shouldn't provoke a Gym Leader. I did it because I want to face him when he's serious and using his best Pokemon, not a second-string team.

So that's why you suddenly changed your tone. Lisia nodded, then grinned. Be careful, though. My teacher is strong. You might get more than you bargained for.

They followed Juan into the Sootopolis Gym's battlefield. Compared with the luxury of the other rooms, it was surprisingly plain: a rectangular pool, like one used for swimming. More than a dozen circular platforms of various sizes floated on its cold, deep water, giving land-bound Pokemon places to stand.

Misty and Lisia went to the spectator seats. Despite their dislike of each other, appearances obliged them to sit together. Each edged away to her own side of the bench to avoid even brushing shoulders.

Ethan and Juan took their places at opposite ends of the pool. Each Trainer's platform rose about two meters above the water, like a diving board reached by stairs. From there, they could see the whole field clearly.

An elderly man with silver hair appeared at the side of the field. His well-fitted black suit made him look like a butler. He probably served the Gym in that capacity and refereed challenges as well.

I will explain the rules, he told Ethan. Each side may use five Pokemon. The Gym Leader may not freely switch Pokemon during the battle. The match ends when all the Pokemon on one side are unable to battle.

Five? Ethan had visited many Gyms, but none had allowed so many Pokemon in a challenge.

The butler seemed accustomed to that reaction. Yes. In the first round, each side must send out two Pokemon together for a Double Battle. That round ends when both Pokemon on one side are unable to battle. The winning side's Pokemon continue into the second round. After that round, the remaining battles are one against one until one side has lost all five Pokemon.

It sounded complicated, but Ethan nodded to show he understood. Most Gyms had similar rules, apart from Leaders who adjusted the conditions to suit their own needs. Ordinarily he only had to check whether a match used two Pokemon or three. Sootopolis was a rare exception.

When the butler had finished, Juan glared at Ethan. The rules require me to introduce myself. I am Juan, Leader of this Gym. We may now begin the official challenge. Are you ready?

If the League had not required the formalities, Juan would not have wasted another word on the man he thought was leading his precious student astray. He wanted to send out his best Pokemon at once, teach Ethan a humiliating lesson, and show Lisia how strong her teacher really was. Not just anyone can sweet-talk my student away!

Don't worry. Ethan patted the Poke Balls at his waist. The rules surprised me, but I came prepared.

Juan fell silent. This fellow had not even introduced himself, yet he claimed to be prepared for rules he had only just heard. How arrogant could he be?

Juan drew several sharp breaths. He could not remember the last time he had wanted so badly to defeat an opponent. After all these years, Ethan had stirred his competitive spirit.

In the stands, Lisia realized her teacher had not recognized Ethan and was treating him like an ordinary challenger. She worried Juan would be overconfident and suffer an ugly defeat. She shifted, ready to warn him.

Misty spoke before she could. What? Don't you trust Mr. Juan? It's only a battle. Surely he doesn't need a warning.

Lisia settled back into her seat. I was just getting comfortable. I wasn't going to warn anyone.

Really? My mistake. Misty smiled without quite smiling. Ethan never uses his strongest team for Gym challenges anyway. He brings Pokemon he's still training. Even if he loses, it'll be close. You needn't worry about your teacher.

What? Lisia forgot their quarrel for a moment. He uses only Pokemon he's training? That might work against weaker opponents, but wouldn't it make a loss much more likely against someone strong?

That's why his commands matter so much. Misty lifted her chin proudly. Every decision, every quick idea can pull his Pokemon out of danger and turn the match in their favor. Ethan is that kind of Trainer.

I see. Lisia considered this, then smiled. Now I'm worried about Ethan instead.

Misty looked at her in surprise. What do you mean?

Didn't you hear Sebastian explain the rules? Lisia nodded toward the butler. This Gym asks more of a challenger than most. There are five Pokemon to manage, and two must battle at the same time. A Trainer needs the skill to command both together.

She paused while Misty thought it over. I agree Ethan is excellent, perhaps among the very best. But this match also demands teamwork and strength from his Pokemon. If he uses partners who are still developing, he really could lose.

Misty's confidence faltered. Lisia had laid out the difficulty too clearly to dismiss. Even so, she chose to trust Ethan. Do your best.

...

On the battlefield, Juan sent out his Pokemon first. He threw two Poke Balls together. In flashes of blue light, a Walrein appeared on a platform and a Kingdra in the pool.

He folded his arms and addressed Ethan. A Trainer aiming for the Ever Grande Conference must be as adaptable as water, taking the shape of whatever vessel it enters. Show me which Pokemon you'll choose to challenge my Gym.

Ethan looked over the pair. Juan was plainly using Pokemon he trusted. Ethan did not know the details of Juan's team, but two fully evolved partners would be formidable.

Which of his own Pokemon should he use? Setting aside Gardevoir, Gengar, and his Legendary Pokemon, he currently had seven to choose from: Dragonite, Tyranitar, Scizor, Eevee, Metang, Combusken, and Milotic.

Five would have to battle today. The first decision was the hardest. Winning the opening Double Battle would put him ahead, an advantage he badly wanted with a team that was not his strongest.

His choices also had awkward type matchups here. After considering them, Ethan sent out Dragonite and Milotic, one for the air and one for the water.

Most of his other Pokemon would face unfavorable types. Scizor had a somewhat better matchup, but its steel-heavy body was dangerous on a field surrounded by deep water. If it fell in, it might not be able to swim back out. Eevee faced no obvious type problem either, yet it would struggle to move freely around this pool.

Ethan was not overly worried. He had spent plenty of time practicing battles against unfavorable types. This was exactly the sort of situation that training was meant to prepare him for.

Juan was surprised by Ethan's choice, then disappointed. Living on an isolated island, he followed Sootopolis and Hoenn news more closely than events in other regions. He had heard a little about them, but he did not know who Ethan was.

Without that knowledge, the choice seemed dreadful to him. Dragonite was Dragon and Flying, making Walrein's Ice-type attacks especially dangerous. A single hit could do tremendous damage. Milotic was a pure Water type facing Walrein and Kingdra, both of which also had Water typing. Their Water attacks would do reduced damage to one another. What did Ethan hope to gain from that exchange?

Most of all, Juan's own ace was a Milotic. He knew the species intimately. One look at Ethan's Milotic's scales and bearing told him it had evolved only recently. Bringing such an inexperienced Pokemon to a Gym challenge looked reckless.

Judging only by type matchups, Juan would have given Ethan's opening pair a terrible score. He began to think less of his opponent. Was the handsome young man all appearance and no substance?

Had Lisia been free to warn him, or had Wallace stayed, Juan would never have relaxed his guard. But Misty had kept Lisia occupied and Wallace was gone. Juan took Ethan for just another challenger.

Even so, he had not forgotten why he had chosen Walrein and Kingdra. Whatever Ethan's abilities, Juan intended to teach him a lesson.

Dragonite circled overhead while Milotic swam a few delighted laps. Once all four Pokemon were ready, Sebastian gave the signal to begin.

Juan meant to watch his opponent's first move. Before he could, Ethan swept an arm forward and issued an order. Dragonite and Milotic both used Twister at the same time.

Two thick waterspouts rose from the pool and surged toward the ceiling. Their combined force churned the water, sending waves across the entire battlefield.

Chapter 690: Fishing in Troubled Waters

The waves spread across the entire pool, reaching Walrein and Kingdra at the far end. Kingdra was swept along by the current, unable to hold its position. Even Walrein, standing on a platform, was battered by the surging water.

Both were Water-type Pokemon, at home in the sea, but these waves were too violent for them to keep their balance.

Ethan slipped his hands into his pockets. There was an old saying about fishing in troubled waters. His two Pokemon faced unfavorable matchups, so he had upended the entire field. Now no one could fight comfortably. In the confusion, he could look for a way to win.

He had plenty of experience with chaotic battles, whether people or Pokemon were involved. Juan was older, but Ethan doubted he had faced many situations like this.

Sure enough, Juan frowned. For all his composure and elegance, he could hardly believe what he was seeing. What sort of tactic endangered both sides? Was this how a normal Trainer battled? Twister was supposed to attack an opponent, not turn the whole battlefield against everyone. It was anything but graceful.

The two waterspouts had reached their full strength. They roamed unpredictably around the pool, throwing up spray and churning the currents. Neither distinguished friend from foe. Together, two uses of the same move had become far more destructive than either alone.

Water rained down on the field. It soon soaked Juan's elaborate suit, fitting his mood. He looked at his Pokemon. In a pool this enclosed, simply holding their positions was difficult, let alone attacking. All the plans he had made before the match dissolved like the water falling back from the spouts.

Things had changed faster than his plans could. Seen another way, though, Ethan's approach was clever. Juan himself would never have made such a decision. His opinion of the challenger shifted again.

Through a gap between the waterspouts, he saw Ethan standing calm and almost enjoying himself. The young man was difficult to read. But Juan could not stand there reflecting while the field spun out of control.

Walrein, use Aurora Beam!

Aurora Beam was a ranged Ice-type attack that could badly hurt Dragonite. Juan, however, aimed it at the nearest waterspout. With both spouts in the middle of the field, even standing still exposed his Pokemon to their force. He needed to stop them and calm the pool before he could fight on his own terms.

Walrein's beam could freeze water. If it froze a waterspout solid, it would be the quickest, simplest solution available to him.

Walrein opened its mouth. A blue-green beam shot out between its long tusks and struck the closer spout almost at once. Ice crackled over the point of impact and spread through the moving water. Given enough time, the whole column might freeze.

Before Juan could relax, the second waterspout drifted near. Its pull tore at the growing ice. Thick pieces broke away and crashed into the pool.

Juan's brief smile froze. The idea had not been wrong, but Aurora Beam had barely been enough for one waterspout. It could not freeze both together.

Still, the effort had not been wasted. The spout Walrein had struck had visibly weakened. Juan prepared to try again.

Before he could give the order, the water beside Walrein's platform burst open. Milotic surged up, leaped high, and rammed Walrein off its footing. Both crashed into the pool.

At almost the same moment, Dragonite beat its wings overhead and fired Dragon Rage at Kingdra. While Juan concentrated on stopping the waterspouts, Ethan had sent one Pokemon through the air and the other beneath the surface to attack from opposite directions.

The currents troubled Ethan's partners too, but they had experience fighting amid disorder. Ethan only had to account for the spouts as another hazard. Juan, by contrast, was so intent on ending them that he had diverted his attention from the opposing Pokemon.

Falling spray obscured his view, and he had to command two partners at once. Those pressures gave Ethan's attacks their opening.

Walrein splashed into the water. Once submerged, it was far less agile than Milotic. Milotic kept it occupied, preventing it from surfacing, escaping, or using another Ice-type move to freeze the waterspouts. The two struggled beneath the pool, and Walrein lost the advantage it had held on the platform.

Kingdra dove beneath Dragonite's Dragon Rage. Juan considered sending it deeper to help Walrein. Together his Pokemon might surround Milotic and change the battle's course. In a Double Battle, helping a partner in trouble was usually the right choice.

But the water below was as turbulent as the surface. Walrein might not be fast enough to catch Milotic and set up a two-on-one attack. The currents could also draw either of Juan's Pokemon into a waterspout and fling it into the air. Their sturdy bodies would not protect them from that.

If Kingdra stayed underwater, Dragonite would have the air to itself. The next time Kingdra surfaced, it could be attacked from above without restraint. Worse, Ethan might simply raise another waterspout when these died away and keep Juan trapped in the same situation.

Juan made his choice. If Ethan could fight beside the spouts, then the Leader of a Water-type Gym could too. He had resolved to teach the challenger a lesson and would not retreat now, least of all in front of Lisia. Watch me, little Lisia. I'll show you how elegantly your teacher fights.

He kept Kingdra at the surface rather than sending it after Walrein. Kingdra, use Hydro Pump!

A heavy jet of water shot from Kingdra's mouth. It swept an arc across the air, tracking Dragonite's flight. Ethan understood Juan's decision at once: he would meet him head-on.

Kingdra's attack looked imposing, but taking down Dragonite would not be so easy. Dragonite had traveled with Ethan for a long time, fought countless battles, and competed at the Silver Conference. It had grown to roughly the strength Charizard possessed before training in the Charicific Valley.

Among Ethan's second-tier Pokemon, Dragonite held the leading place and was nearing the level of his top team. It was not yet in the extraordinary class of his red Gyarados or Crystal Steelix, but it could defeat the ace Pokemon of most Gym Leaders. Tyranitar and Scizor were at about the same level as Dragonite, and all three were central to Ethan's plans for the Ever Grande Conference.

If Juan thought Dragonite's type disadvantage made Ethan the weaker side, he was badly mistaken.

Dragonite dodged left and right in the air until Kingdra's Hydro Pump ran out. Then it turned sharply and streaked toward Kingdra.

Dragonite, use Dragon Rush!

Dragonite accelerated again. It folded its wings, wrapped itself in a surging wave of power, and flew straight at Kingdra like an arrow loosed from a bow.

It's fast! Juan's eyes widened. Dive, quickly!

His warning came too late. Dragonite skimmed so low over the water that its rounded belly seemed to touch the surface. In a blink, it was face-to-face with Kingdra. Kingdra felt the heat of its breath and the terrifying Dragon-type energy gathered around its smooth head.

Bang! Dragonite struck with the force of its full speed. The super-effective blow knocked Kingdra out of the water. It skipped across the surface four or five times before flying toward the waterspout behind it.

Kingdra slammed into the rotating column. The current caught it, carried it higher and higher, and hurled it toward the ceiling.

Juan looked up in alarm. Kingdra shot free of the spout and fell back toward the pool like a kite whose string had snapped. Dragonite had already turned and was racing after it.

Only now did Juan realize how powerful Ethan's supposedly ill-chosen Dragonite was. That was the confidence behind Ethan's decision. Juan had understood it too late.

Kingdra had no way to evade in midair. Dragonite caught it with Wing Attack, changing its course once again and driving it down toward the water. Kingdra had been reduced to a helpless target by the chain of attacks.

The battle should never have become so one-sided. Juan's initial misjudgment had started a series of mistakes that Ethan kept exploiting.

Smack! Kingdra struck the surface. From that height and at that speed, the water might as well have been solid ground. It floated unsteadily, dazed by the impact, and did not recover for some time.

Juan watched anxiously. Dragonite hovered above Kingdra and began gathering energy in its mouth. Juan recognized Dragon Rage, the move Kingdra had dodged once before. Against Kingdra, it was the last attack he wanted to see coming.

Chapter 691: We Have to Leave Right Away!

Hurry, dodge! Juan shouted to Kingdra.

Kingdra heard him, but it was too dazed from the fall to control its body. It could neither dodge nor sink beneath the surface in time. Dragonite gave it no chance to recover.

Dragon Rage swept down in a blue-green wave and struck Kingdra.

Boom! Water exploded around it. The shock wave spread across the pool and collided with both waterspouts. Their energy had already begun to fade after several minutes of violence; the blast broke most of what remained. Only weak, scattered gusts continued to turn.

All the water they had lifted into the air fell back into the pool at once, raising an even larger wave. The Trainers' elevated platforms protected Ethan and Juan from the spray.

A minute earlier, Juan would have welcomed the end of the waterspouts. Now he watched their last traces disappear without relief. Kingdra floated unconscious on the surface. He had lost one Pokemon, and the battle was in worse shape than before. His promising opening position had been overturned completely.

One thing offered him a little comfort. While both Trainers had focused on the fight above the pool, Walrein had used its greater battle experience to break free of Milotic underwater. It had hurt Milotic and resurfaced.

Juan's first judgment about Ethan's team had been partly right: Milotic was much weaker than Dragonite. But Walrein had escaped too late. If it had surfaced sooner, it might have helped Kingdra defeat Dragonite before turning on Milotic. Regret could not change the result.

For Ethan, the situation was straightforward. Two against one was an advantage he had no intention of wasting. Milotic's injuries were manageable. On his command, it and Dragonite attacked Walrein from the water and the air.

Walrein was an evenly capable Pokemon, without a glaring weakness in its abilities. Juan's was also strong. It hauled itself onto a platform and defended from both directions, holding out longer than Ethan might have expected.

But Dragonite was stronger, and Milotic kept pressing it too. Walrein blocked a close-range Thunder Punch from Dragonite. As Dragonite flew past and climbed, Walrein prepared to counterattackonly for Milotic's Water Gun to strike it in the back.

It could not defend both sides forever. The combined assault soon brought it down after Kingdra.

Sebastian announced in his aged voice, The challenger wins the first round!

Misty smiled in the stands. She did not celebrate openly; she only gave Lisia a sidelong, triumphant look. To her surprise, Lisia showed no disappointment at her teacher's defeat.

Misty's smile faded. It seems you were worrying for nothing. Ethan fought as steadily as ever. We won the first round.

Lisia turned toward her, eyes shining with an expression Misty knew too well. She had seen that look from Melody, the festival maiden on Shamouti Island, and from Casey, the young Trainer at the Silver Conference. Alarm bells rang in her mind.

He's amazing! Lisia said, excited admiration spilling out of her voice.

Misty's eyelid twitched. She no longer wanted to discuss Ethan at all, but Lisia was too absorbed in the battle to notice.

I've never seen anyone beat my teacher so easily! Even my uncle couldn't do that. Is this what winning two regional tournaments looks like? And those two Twisters becoming waterspoutsI had no idea you could battle that way! It opened my eyes. It was so exciting!

Juan had lost on the battlefield. Misty was the one suffering in the stands.

It wasn't anything special, she said, though she did not believe it. She hoped to cool Lisia's sudden admiration. Lots of Trainers use unusual tactics. One of my old traveling companions did something unexpected in almost every match. If you met him, you'd really see something new.

Lisia hardly heard her. She rested a hand under her chin and nodded to herself. So that's what a two-region winner is like. He's given me an idea, too. Perhaps I could make a beautiful effect with two Twisters in my next stage performance.

Oh no. Misty rolled her eyes. Juan charmed the middle-aged women of Sootopolis, and Ethan seemed to charm girls wherever he traveled. Lisia was beginning to fall for him too.

That could not continue. Misty made a firm decision: from now on, she would watch every pretty girl they met on the road much more closely. And as soon as this Gym challenge ended, she would get Ethan away from Sootopolis.

She had wanted to stay for the festival in a few days. Now Lisia made the city feel far too dangerous. They could not stay here and let her follow Ethan around. We have to leave. Right away!

...

On the field, Juan recalled both of his defeated Pokemon without a trace of expression. The first round had gone nothing like he expected, and the second was about to begin before he could reflect on it.

He still had to face Dragonite and Milotic. What if Ethan used Twister again, raising two more of those dreadful waterspouts? Juan could almost imagine surrendering rather than fighting through that a second time.

Yet he could not ask Ethan to stop using a move. A Gym Leader who demanded such a condition would lose face. Worse, little Lisia might think he was afraid of the challenger. That would sting more than any embarrassment before the women who admired him.

Juan took a breath and sent out his next two Pokemon. If he wants another chaotic fight, I'll give him one.

Blue light flashed from the Poke Balls. A Politoed and a Whiscash appeared on the field.

Misty straightened at the sight of Politoed. She had one herself and wanted to see how Juan's compared with her own.

Ethan glanced at Politoed, then studied Whiscash. This was the first time he had encountered one in person.

It resembled a large catfish. Its back was dark blue, its belly yellow, and its body stood less than a meter high. Sponge-like pale blue lips framed its mouth. Two long yellow whiskers hung from the corners, and a W-shaped mark sat on its forehead. Altogether, it looked rather vacant.

Whiscash were said to be fiercely territorial. They nested at the bottom of swamps and claimed the surrounding waters. When something intruded, they could shake the ground violently before attacking.

During the day, they often slept motionless in the mud while waiting for prey. They ate almost anything. Their eyesight was poor, so they sensed vibrations in the water with their whiskers to locate food. They might then shake the ground to frighten an opponent and swallow prey from the swamp bottom, mud and all.

Some people saw groups of Whiscash leaping at the surface and took it as a warning of an earthquake. Over time, the story spread until people believed the Pokemon caused the quakes themselves.

Ethan examined Juan's Whiscash carefully. Even in the games, he had rarely dealt with the species; few Trainers used it. He recalled that it was Water and Ground type, but he knew little about its Abilities. He would have to learn as they fought.

At his signal, Dragonite and Milotic returned to their positions. Before Sebastian could announce the start of the second round, Ethan looked over at Juan. The Leader's grave expression told him exactly what was worrying him.

Don't worry, Ethan said with a smile. I won't make waterspouts again this round.

Juan stared. Why would Ethan give up an advantage voluntarily? Yet he seemed sincere. Perhaps Juan had misjudged him. Perhaps he was a decent man after all. Juan felt a little more respect for the challenger.

That feeling vanished as soon as the round began.

Ethan kept his promise: he raised no waterspouts. Instead, before Juan could issue an order, Milotic dove out of sight. Juan expected an attack from below. A long moment passed with no sign of it.

Then the water in the center of the pool began to turn. At first Juan did not grasp what Ethan was doing. The rotation grew faster until a vast whirlpool opened before him.

No waterspoutsjust a giant whirlpool! What difference did that make? One disruption had risen above the surface, and the other churned below it.

Juan was about to protest. Ethan had said he would not use that move! But he stopped himself. Both effects came from Twister, yet a whirlpool was not a waterspout. Ethan had kept the exact promise he had made. Somehow that made it more infuriating.

Juan still had a battle to fight. He had encountered whirlpools before and could deal with one more easily than with the twin waterspouts. This time he ignored Dragonite at first and ordered Politoed and Whiscash to attack Milotic together.

They knocked Milotic out. Only then did Juan turn both Pokemon against Dragonite. For a while, the decision worked. The balance shifted toward him, and another strong push might have won the round.

But he had underestimated Dragonite again. Even facing two opponents alone, it held its ground. The struggle lasted a long time. Then Dragonite surged forward and, in one fierce stretch of fighting, defeated Politoed and Whiscash both.

Chapter 692: Hopes Rising and Falling

Juan had not expected this result. He had recognized Dragonite as his greatest threat, dealt with Milotic first, and focused both his remaining Pokemon on it. Even then, he had underestimated its strength.

Dragonite's performance had been astonishing. Walrein had struggled under a two-on-one attack in the first round. Dragonite, by contrast, fought more fiercely as the pressure mounted. It took the initiative and drove Politoed and Whiscash back. Their attacks sometimes reached it, but anyone watching could see that Dragonite held the advantage.

How could it be so strong? Juan thought it could enter the Ever Grande Conference today and make at least the quarterfinals. Was it Ethan's ace?

He sighed at his two motionless Pokemon floating on the pool and recalled them. Their defeat was not entirely bad news. Dragonite had battled through two rounds, ending the second against two opponents alone. It looked too exhausted to fight the third.

Juan's final Pokemon would be his own ace. Without Dragonite, how would Ethan respond? Juan felt a little betteruntil he remembered that Ethan had three Pokemon he had yet to send out. His Milotic would have to face all three by itself. His spirits sank again.

Juan no longer dreamed of an overwhelming victory or of teaching Ethan a lesson. He hoped he could win somehow, or at least force a draw. Two rounds had changed his ambitions that much.

Ethan recalled his Milotic. When Dragonite returned to his platform, he rubbed its round belly. Well done. Rest now. He recalled it too, then looked up as Juan released his last Pokemon.

The third round would be a series of one-on-one battles. Juan had no reason to hold back. His final choice was his ace, Milotic.

Since arriving in Hoenn, Ethan had now seen three Milotic, including his own. The other belonged to Robert, the Coordinator at the Slateport Contest. Ethan's newly evolved Milotic could not yet compare with either Robert's or Juan's. He wondered which of those two was stronger. This battle might give him an answer.

Juan's Milotic stretched gracefully across a platform. Its scales glittered beneath the Gym lights. Like its Trainer, it knew how to make an entrance. Ethan could easily imagine how many admirers Juan had won while performing with it.

What should Ethan use against it? His fingers passed over the Poke Balls at his waist. He still had three Pokemon to try, so he decided to use this rare opportunity to test one of them against a powerful opponent.

He threw a Poke Ball and sent out Metang.

Juan stared at the Pokemon, which had not yet reached its final evolution. He had thought Ethan's Milotic looked newly evolved. Did sending out Metang mean Ethan had no stronger partners left? Or did he believe a Metang alone could beat Juan's ace?

Whatever Ethan meant, Juan saw a chance to recover his standing in front of Lisia and perhaps turn the match around.

Sebastian signaled the start. Both Pokemon attacked at once. Floating above a platform, Metang opened with Confusion. In a field surrounded by water, though, that approach was hard to make work. Milotic simply dove beneath the surface, evaded the move, and slipped closer for an attack from below.

Ethan had expected that tactic and kept Metang from being caught completely off guard. Even so, Milotic had closed the distance and could make full use of both the pool and its superior strength.

The two fought in earnest. Ethan directed Metang well, and Metang performed admirably, but after several exchanges Juan's ace found an opening and knocked it down.

Metang fell toward the pool. Ethan recalled it before it struck the water.

Only when Sebastian confirmed his win did Juan breathe easily again. His Milotic was still in good condition. If it beat the next Pokemon too, victory would draw much nearer.

Ethan's expression did not change. He had known Metang was unlikely to win. That was no lack of faith in it. The first two rounds had shown him that Juan's Pokemon were well trained. They had lost because Dragonite was exceptionally strong, not because Juan's team was weak. His ace would be stronger still, and Metang was not ready to defeat it.

Ethan selected another Poke Ball. Blue light flashed, and Eevee appeared on a platform. It began hopping eagerly from one platform to another.

Juan raised an eyebrow. Metang at least had evolved once. Eevee had not chosen an evolution at all. Was Ethan taking this challenge seriously?

He suspected Ethan had sent out a weak-looking Pokemon to insult him. Fine. Keep doing it. When I beat every one of your partners, we'll see how you feel.

Once the next one-on-one battle began, Juan realized he had judged Eevee too quickly. It performed even better than Metang. Its attacks, defense, and leaps were exceptional for its species. The little Pokemon was far more dangerous than its innocent appearance suggested.

Even when Milotic knocked it into the pool, Eevee paddled back to a platform. It made Juan's ace work for every opening. Milotic could move freely through the water and was the stronger Pokemon, however. After a harder fight than Juan had expected, it defeated Eevee.

Juan could not smile at the result. Milotic had taken more damage. It was not seriously injured, but its condition was now roughly as poor as Dragonite's had been after the second round. If Juan had to face a rested Dragonite now, he doubted Milotic could win.

This might be the most emotionally exhausting Gym challenge of Juan's career. His hopes had risen and fallen too many times already.

Ethan recalled the unconscious Eevee and reached for another Poke Ball. Juan's heart rose into his throat as Ethan threw it.

The fifth Pokemon was not Dragonite. It was Combusken. Juan exhaled in relief, then immediately frowned. What was Ethan thinking? Why send a Fire-type Pokemon into a Water-type Gym, especially on a field covered by water?

Could this Combusken, like Eevee, be strong enough to overcome the type disadvantage? Juan doubted it. Even a Blaziken should struggle against his Milotic here.

He glanced at Milotic's worn condition and faltered. Perhaps, after all, a Blaziken could do it now.

Ethan's eyes sharpened. Metang and Eevee had worn Milotic down. He had chosen Combusken to settle the match.

From the start, Juan felt a hunger to attack that had been less obvious in Ethan's previous two battles. Metang and Eevee had searched for openings, but this was different. Combusken leaped from platform to platform, looking for its chance at every step.

If Juan had kept a cool head, he could have stayed in the water and worn Combusken down with ranged Water-type attacks. Time and the field would have favored Milotic.

But he was impatient to beat Ethan in front of Lisia and prove himself. He knew Ethan might have sent out a Fire type to provoke him, yet he could not bear to retreat from the man he imagined was leading his dear student astray.

Instead of hiding beneath the surface, Juan had Milotic fight half-submerged beside the platforms, trading attacks as Combusken jumped from one to the next.

At first glance, the decision was reasonable. Water beat Fire, and Juan's Milotic had the better field. His mistake was allowing Combusken close. He had also underestimated how quickly Ethan could spot an opening.

One fleeting chance appeared. Combusken struck with Double Kick while leaping and knocked Milotic out of the water onto a platform.

What? Juan had been preparing his next command. He stared, then paled as he understood what had happened.

Milotic was like a fish stranded beside a Pokemon skilled in close combat. Misty and Lisia both stood up in the stands. They knew this was the decisive moment.

Combusken landed, turned, and reached Milotic before it could slip back into the pool. Quick Attack closed the last gap and dealt the first hit. Peck and Scratch followed in a tight combination.

The blows left marks across Milotic's once-beautiful scales. It tried to break free, return to the water, and find time to recover its strength. Ethan would not let such a hard-won chance go. Combusken cut off its route and drove another Double Kick into its face.

Milotic fell into the pool at lastbut only because Combusken had kicked it there. The battle was over.

Juan's mouth moved without words. Defeat had left him dejected. Then a white light enveloped Combusken, making the sight even harder for him to bear.

He knew that light. Combusken had met the conditions to evolve, and the change had begun naturally. Losing his best Pokemon was painful enough. Now the Pokemon that defeated it was evolving before his eyes.

For Juan, it was a second blow on top of the first.

Chapter 693: Will We Meet Again?

Sebastian announced the result everyone could already see. Milotic is unable to battle. The challenger wins the Gym match!

Two sets of applause sounded from the stands. Misty was clapping, but so was Lisia. Her eyes sparkled with excitement at Ethan's victory. Misty glared at her.

Why are you clapping? Your teacher lost. Aren't you cheering for the wrong person?

Lisia turned to her with a look that said, So what? I'm happy for my friend. Ethan won. Why shouldn't I applaud?

Your friend? Misty seethed. How long had Lisia known Ethan before claiming that? Give her a few more meetings and she might start calling him Ethan with the same familiarity Misty used. Did being an idol make her this shameless?

Misty could not control what Lisia said, so she strengthened her own resolve. Once the challenge was over, she and Ethan had to leave Sootopolis immediately. Lisia must not get another chance to approach him.

Both girls rose and headed down toward the field. The passage from the stands narrowed, and they reached it together. Neither gave way. After exchanging a look, they pushed forward at the same time.

Lisia had stamina from singing and dancing, but Misty was stronger. She squeezed through first, then looked back with a triumphant expression. She said nothing, yet her meaning was clear: Whether it's this passage or Ethan, you won't beat me.

Lisia glared back. You may have won this time. We'll see who wins in the end.

Ethan knew nothing of the contest in the stands. All his attention was on Combusken. The light of evolution faded, revealing a new form: Blaziken.

Its types remained Fire and Fighting, but its body and abilities had matured. White feathers crowned its head above a V-shaped crest. Its eyes were blue, its claws seemed wrapped in bandages, and powerful legs supported its taller frame.

Blaziken would face opponents bravely to the last. Ethan recalled that it burned off old feathers every few years to grow bright new ones. In battle, hot flames could burst from its wrists, burning more fiercely against stronger opponents. Its legs and waist were said to be so strong that it could scale a thirty-story building in only a few leaps.

The evolution strengthened Ethan's regular team. At his signal, Blaziken cleared the broad pool in a single jump and landed on the bank. Together they approached Juan.

Misty and Lisia had reached the field as well. Misty stood beside Ethan. Lisia stood by her defeated teacher but smiled at Ethan, leaving Juan to bear his loss without her comfort. Juan's expression grew more complicated.

However reluctantly, Juan had to admit Ethan had beaten him. He cleared his throat and adopted an easy tone. Well, you performed nicely. About as I expected. Don't let it make you overconfident, though. You're young, and you have a long road ahead. There is plenty of room for you to grow. I hope you keep working hard.

Juan delivered it like an elder encouraging a promising junior. Anyone who had missed the battle might think he had allowed Ethan to win.

Ethan listened with a smile and let the words pass. He had achieved what he came for. There was no reason to needle Juan again. The man was trying to save face, and Ethan was happy to give him that much. Juan had lost the match; a few grand words would do no harm.

Misty felt less charitable. They had only just met Juan, and their encounter had hardly been friendly. Why was he lecturing Ethan now? She was about to say so when Lisia cut in first.

That's enough, Teacher. Lisia gave Juan an exasperated look. After battling him, do you still not know who he is?

Juan paused. Was there more to this challenger than he realized? Oh? Then tell me who he is.

Lisia was about to answer, but Ethan raised a hand to stop her. He knew she meant to tell Juan about his victories in two regions. He did not mind people knowing. Yet having the same achievements announced wherever he went would eventually make it sound as though he were showing off, even when someone else spoke for him. Relying too heavily on his reputation could do more harm than good.

Who am I? Ethan smiled at himself. Just an ordinary challenger who arrived in Hoenn not long ago and is preparing for the Ever Grande Conference. Nothing remarkable.

Lisia stared, then understood why he had stopped her. She wanted more people to know and love her as an idol. She knew how many others sought fame too, along with the respect and money it could bring. Ethan seemed untouched by the temptation to announce his achievements. She admired him all the more.

He really is captivating. She looked at him happily, then turned to urge Juan to fetch the Gym Badge.

Juan still wanted an explanation, but with Lisia pressing him, he put off the question until he could ask her later. Why was his dear student taking the challenger's side already?

He took a badge from inside his coat and tossed it toward Ethan. Take it. The Rain Badge proves that you defeated me.

The badge spun through the air. Juan's throw was a little high. His irritation showed in the angle; if Ethan wanted to catch it himself, he would have to step back.

Before it reached him, a sturdy gray claw closed around it. Blaziken had caught the badge for its Trainer. It fixed Juan with a fierce stare, fire seeming to burn in its eyes. Without an order from Ethan, it did nothing more. After a few moments it turned and placed the badge in Ethan's hand.

Ethan examined it. Three teardrop shapesone blue, two fading from blue to pinkformed a larger triangular drop. The design was simple. He put it away and shook his head at Juan's petty throw, then said goodbye to Lisia.

She seemed to want to say more. Ethan left with Misty and Blaziken before she found the words.

They had only just stepped outside the Gym when quick footsteps sounded behind them.

P-please wait! Lisia called, a little out of breath.

Misty had been silently hoping never to see her again. She took a deep breath and turned with Ethan.

What is it? he asked gently. He liked Lisia. She was pretty, cheerful, and full of youthful energy. Talking with her had been easy and pleasantapart from her constant sparring with Misty.

Lisia caught her breath. About my teacher...please don't take his behavior to heart. He's really a good person. He's afraid someone will deceive me, so he doesn't like me getting close to men. That's why he was so hostile when he saw you.

Don't worry, Misty said before Ethan could answer. Ethan won't be angry over something so small. He won't give Juan another thought.

I didn't ask you! Lisia shot back. You don't have to answer for him.

Here they went again. Were these two born to quarrel? Ethan pulled Misty gently behind him and asked her to be quiet for a moment.

Misty's right, he told Lisia. I don't mind. I've met all sorts of people on my travels, including plenty whose attitudes were worse than your teacher's. By tomorrow, I may have forgotten the whole thing.

I'm glad. Lisia let out a long breath. She met his eyes, then looked down shyly. Um...will we see each other again?

Misty nearly protested, but she remembered Ethan had asked her to stay quiet. She fumed behind him instead.

I think we will, Ethan said. There's a long road ahead. We might cross paths anywhere, someday. And as a Coordinator, you'll visit cities that host Contests. That gives us plenty of chances to meet.

You're right! Lisia brightened. After the Ever Grande Conference, when you leave Hoenn, where will you go?

If nothing changes, Sinnoh.

Sinnoh? Her eyes lit up. Really? That's wonderful! My work will be centered there next. It must be fate. We can meet in Sinnoh too!

Lisia insisted on exchanging contact details with Ethan. Only then did he and Misty finally leave the street where the Gym stood.

Misty remained gloomy as they walked. She had failed to shake Lisia off. Now Lisia could contact Ethan, and they might meet again in the near future. Why was she so hard to escape?

Lost in thought, Misty followed Ethan for some time before she noticed where they were going. This was not the way to the port. They were heading back to the Pokemon Center.

She pouted, hurt and suspicious. Why are we going back there? Do you miss that girl already? Are we staying a few more days?

Ethan flicked her forehead. What nonsense. Several of my Pokemon are injured. They need treatment first. There's also something important I haven't taken care of. I need somewhere we won't be disturbed.

Strangely, the little flick swept away Misty's annoyance. She returned to her usual spirited self. Ethan was right: despite the time his Feebas training had taken over the past few days, another unfinished matter was waiting for him.

Chapter 694: So You're a Quick One!

When we parted, I thought it would be ages before you contacted me again. Yet here you are only a few days later, visiting me on a night like this.

Shelly leaned against the wall of her secret warehouse, arms folded, and teased Ethan. It was past seven in the evening. Darkness had fallen, and the cargo district outside was silent.

He ignored her tone. When I was here last time, I think I saw a place inside that would suit me. Do you still have it?

Shelly's expression changed. She covered her chest with one hand and watched him warily. What are you planning? I knew your reasons for helping me weren't entirely innocent. I even expected a day like this, but I didn't think you'd be in such a hurry!

Ethan stared at her. After two puzzled seconds, he realized what she thought he meant.

Don't flatter yourself. He rolled his eyes. I need somewhere private to handle something without being interrupted. I hoped I could use a room here.

Handle something? Shelly did not believe him. Something physical, you mean? I wondered why you came so late without that little girl who's always with you. Now I know.

Ethan sighed. He could see why she might suspect him. A man had appeared at her quiet warehouse after dark, faintly smelling of the glass of red wine he had drunk at dinner, and had pushed his way inside. It was an unusual visit however she looked at it. Explaining further would only make it sound worse.

He walked past her toward the indoor pool that still held her shark-shaped submarine. Beyond a partition, a hidden staircase led him to the warehouse's second floor.

The warehouse was roughly 160 meters long, 80 meters wide, and seven meters high. Among dozens of similar buildings near the docks, its exterior looked unremarkable. Shelly had transformed the inside into a fully equipped secret base.

She had made the second floor difficult to notice from outside by cleverly dividing the tall interior. It held several rooms for living: a bedroom, a bathroom, even a dining room with everything she needed. Another section remained open and spacious, perhaps reserved for a project she had not had time to finish after leaving Team Aqua.

Ethan opened the door to that empty area without asking and stepped inside. He released Gardevoir, Raikou, and Suicune from their Poke Balls, then called Gengar out of his shadow.

Shelly arrived a few steps behind him. The two Legendary Pokemon took positions in opposite corners. Gardevoir, Ethan's first partner, and the powerful Gengar that could speak human words stood to either side of him. All four looked ready for danger. Shelly understood at once that he truly had something important to do here.

All right, I take back what I said. You didn't leave the girl behind and come here to try anything with me.

Take it back? Ethan gave her a helpless look. She had sounded entirely serious a moment ago. Now she wanted to call it a joke. She was a convincing actress.

Good. Would you mind keeping watch outside for anything unexpected?

You want me out of the room. You can say it plainly. Shelly snorted. I know what you're going to do, even without watching. But this place is small and not especially sturdy. Don't put it through too much.

I know what I'm doing, Ethan said. He admired how quickly she had understood his concern. There won't be a problem.

Shelly gave him one last look and left. Ethan took out an Ultra Ball and aimed it at the center of the room.

All guard Pokemon are in position. The third communication with Deoxys begins now.

He said it steadily, almost like a researcher recording an experiment. Then he pressed the ball's release button. Blue light flashed, and Deoxys appeared.

Since defeating and catching it by the lake, Ethan had tried to speak with Deoxys twice in private. Communication with an intelligent Pokemon from outer space had been difficult. He could only approach it little by little through Gardevoir's telepathy, taking care not to provoke it. At least it did not resist him as its Trainer; he had beaten it openly in battle.

Deoxys emerged calmly. It looked over the Pokemon guarding the room before turning its gaze to Ethan. A small blue aurora shone from its chest and appeared before him.

That light was why he needed a hidden room. Outdoors, even somewhere remote, the aurora could attract notice from kilometers away. A busy Pokemon Center offered still less privacy. Here the light could not escape to draw anyone's attention.

Because of that need for seclusion, Ethan had not yet come to understand or work with Deoxys as naturally as he did with his other Legendary Pokemon.

He had tried asking Gengar to translate. Gengar could speak with many Pokemon, but Deoxys's alien language meant nothing to it. Gardevoir's telepathy was the only way Ethan could converse with Deoxys clearly.

Ethan nodded to Gardevoir. It placed a hand on him. An odd sensation reached his mind immediately. Having experienced the connection before, he knew Gardevoir had linked him to Deoxys.

...Friend...

Loneliness filled the faint thought that reached him.

Don't worry, Ethan answered silently. As I told you before, you weren't the only one to land on this planet. Our journey has barely begun. We'll find others like you someday. And remember, my Pokemon and I are your companions and friends now too.

From the films and anime Ethan remembered, Deoxys traveled vast stretches of space alone. Cold meteorites were the closest things it had to a home. No wonder it longed for friends, and perhaps even crossed the stars looking for its own kind.

...Promise...

Yes. That's our promise, Ethan said. In return, I need you to fight strong opponents alongside me.

At the thought of a strong opponent, Deoxys seemed to remember Rayquaza, with whom it had battled twice. Its emotions flared, and the feeling rushed through Gardevoir's link into Ethan.

Easy, he urged. I don't mean Rayquaza. I mean other opponents of comparable strength: Ho-Oh, Groudon, Kyogre, and others we haven't met yet. I may have to face them someday.

...I understand. I will help you...

Ethan smiled. Of their three attempts to communicate, this had been the easiest and most productive. He and Deoxys seemed, at last, to have reached an understanding.

...

When Ethan left the room and descended the stairs, he found Shelly leaning against a wall, bored. She looked up at his footsteps, noticed his lighter expression, glanced at the clock, and shrugged.

Finished already? That was quick.

Perhaps she meant something else. Perhaps Ethan was reading too much into it. Either way, he felt insulted.

Quick? he said. Impossible. I'm young, strong, full of energy, and never tire. My record speaks for itself. Anyone would tell you so. How could I be quick?

Shelly's lips curled. So you really are that kind of man. I knew it. You were upstairs less than seven minutes. Take out the time you spent getting ready and walking up and down, and you managed barely more than three. What would you call that?

Efficient! It proves I'm good at what I do.

Is that so? Shelly stretched, then walked past him toward the stairs. If I'd known, I wouldn't have bothered sending you upstairs. You could have finished right here even sooner.

Without turning around, she raised a hand to stop his reply. Don't come looking for me for this sort of thing again. It wouldn't be worth the trouble. I'm going to bed. Turn out the lights and lock the warehouse when you leave. Good night, quick man.

She was doing it on purpose. Ethan watched her go upstairs in an excellent mood and knew she was teasing him.

He had played a part in bringing her to this life. Without his intervention in the struggle over Kyogre, Hoenn might have suffered badly, but Shelly would probably still be with Team Aqua, the group she had regarded as home. Her jokes suggested her feelings toward him had changed. Perhaps she was also letting out some resentment over the pressure he had once put on her.

Fine. Things are improving, so I'll let the insult go this time. But if she called him a quick man again, he would have something to say about it.

...

When Ethan returned to the Pokemon Center, Misty was already asleep. He went to his room, washed, and soon fell asleep himself.

After the talk with Deoxys, he could imagine facing Pokemon at the very peak of the world without needing to overwhelm them with a group. He might still lose, but compared with before, it was a considerable step. As Deoxys grew stronger, only a few opponents would remain beyond his confidence.

The night passed quietly. After breakfast the next morning, Ethan and Misty went straight to the port and took a ship away from Sootopolis Island.

The festival was still several days off, and Ethan could not wait there indefinitely. Knowing Juan would perform the finale gave him even less reason to stay. Leaving early suited Misty perfectly.

They would pass several smaller islands before returning to the Hoenn mainland and heading for the next Gym city. The journey was short compared with their voyage from Petalburg; they expected to reach the mainland in about a day.

As Ethan's badges accumulated, the Ever Grande Conference drew nearer. He could almost imagine smelling the flame of the opening ceremony.

Chapter 695: A Chance Meeting with the Elite Four

Lilycove City was said to be where the land ended and the sea began. On Hoenn's eastern coast, it was the largest and busiest city on that side of the mainland.

Its port was crowded, and it was known for both a department store and an art museum. Lilycove was only a little smaller than Mauville City, yet it drew even larger crowds. Every year, when summer was at its hottest, tourists flocked to its broad white beaches to enjoy the city's energy.

After a day's short voyage, Ethan and Misty arrived early the next morning. Before they could leave the harbor, they passed an area filled with moored yachts and heard someone calling from a distance.

Hey, young man over there!

Only when the call came a second time did Ethan realize it was meant for him. Under a sunshade some way off, an old man was waving from a deck chair.

He had a silver beard and wore a broad-brimmed white sailor's hat, a long black coat over his bare chest, jeans, and heavy boots. He looked like a retired ship captain, perhaps in his seventies or eighties. His frame was still sturdy and his gaze sharp.

I think he's calling you, Misty said. Do you know him?

No. Let's see what he wants.

They followed the narrow steps toward the sunshade. Before Ethan could speak, the man stood and looked him over. You're that Ethan fellow, aren't you?

Standing, he was about as tall as Ethan. He must have been powerfully built in his youth; age had only made him somewhat leaner. An unmistakable presence remained.

I am. Ethan was about to ask how the man knew his name. Then he took a closer look. Are you...Drake of the Elite Four?

The old man stared, surprised, then burst into laughter. Well, that's unusual. You recognized me!

Misty covered her mouth. She had sensed there was something special about him, but she had never guessed he belonged to Hoenn's Elite Four. What a coincidence to meet him here.

Ethan understood why Drake had known his name. Anyone familiar with his tournament results might recognize him. A man who still called him young fellow despite those victories must not be impressed by the title of Champion. Along with the sailor's clothes and his age, that had made Drake a reasonable guess.

Hoenn's Elite Four were capable, but less familiar to the public than their counterparts in other regions. Even many locals knew their names without having seen them. They mostly kept to themselves.

Drake, for instance, had become one of the Elite Four when he was young. His tenure stretched back to the generation of Agatha in Kanto, Bertha in Sinnoh, and Drasna in Kalos. Few people anywhere had held such a position longer. Yet he was also a captain and an explorer who spent much of each year at sea. How could ordinary people get to know him?

The other three had their own reasons for staying out of the public eye. Sidney's name might sound feminine, but he was a man: a former troublemaker who specialized in Dark types. A single tuft of red hair rose from his otherwise shaved head, and his fierce expression hardly made him look approachable.

Phoebe and Glacia were women with very different images. Ethan thought they also had fewer chances to make public appearances. Phoebe was young and looked like an island dancer in a grass skirt. Glacia carried herself like a distant, aristocratic lady. Each had admirers, but neither drew the broad public enthusiasm that a visible figurehead might.

Hoenn lacked someone like Lance: a prominent figure with an impressive manner, a widely admired Pokemon specialty, and an appearance that inspired trust. Ethan kept the thought to himself. Fame aside, an Elite Four member deserved respect, and he was pleased to meet one by chance.

Recognizing you isn't strange, Ethan said. Anyone who knows much about Hoenn's Pokemon has heard of you. You're practically a living piece of its history, and highly respected. How did you recognize me?

Drake laughed. My crew, that's why! Long voyages can be dull. With little else to do, the lads watch tournament matches from other regions. I learned about you from them.

I see.

You're in Hoenn to compete at the Ever Grande Conference?

Yes. I have six badges. Two more and I can enter.

Just as I thought. Drake nodded with satisfaction. The boys have been guessing which region you'd challenge after Johto. I was the only one who said you'd come to Hoenn. I also told them you'd win the championship.

That was a high opinion indeed. You're giving me too much credit. Hoenn's Trainers are stronger overall than those in Kanto or Johto. I can't promise I'll win.

Too much modesty saps a young man's spirit, Drake said with a snort. They may be strong, but do you think you've stood still? Anyway, your greatest obstacle at this tournament won't be the other Trainers. It'll be the Pokemon League itself.

Why do you say that?

You've probably guessed. The League won't sit by while one Trainer wins championship after championship in different regions. When the tournament starts, expect obstacles at every step. They'll put the toughest opponents in your path.

Ethan smiled. Wouldn't that be fine? To win, I have to defeat them all eventually. What difference does it make whether I face them early or late?

Drake watched him for several seconds, then laughed again. I take back what I said. You have plenty of spirit. You just keep it quiet. I knew I was right about you.

His expression grew serious. I haven't met someone this interesting in a long time. Why don't you battle me while we're both here? If you become Champion, you'll have the opportunity to challenge the Elite Four anyway. As you said, early or latewhat difference does it make?

Not now. Ethan shook his head. This was my plan in Kanto and Johto too. I won't challenge any of the Elite Four until I've competed in every regional tournament I intend to enter. Only then will I turn my attention to all of you.

Drake looked a little surprised but understood. Fair enough. I won't press you. I only wonder whether I'll live long enough to see that day.

You will. You're still strong. I expect you'll reach a hundred.

Misty had listened quietly. Now she asked, Mr. Drake, if you're a captain, where is your ship?

There. Drake pointed across the harbor.

They followed his finger to a huge wooden sailing ship with five masts.

A sailing ship? Misty had imagined that an Elite Four member would own a luxury yacht.

What would youngsters like you know? Drake scoffed. A sailing ship is the romance of the sea! No modern machinery, only the wind and currents carrying you across the water, over great waves and through whirlpools. That's an adventure worth chasing!

He looked ready to set out that instant. Misty did not share his enthusiasm. To her, a boat was a place to relax on deck in the breeze. She loved Water-type Pokemon, but she would rather stay away from storms and huge waves.

Ethan could sympathize a little. Before coming to this world, he had enjoyed pirate films and their ships. He also understood the older captain's nostalgia. Modern vessels were useful, but this one could still make Drake feel like the young adventurer who had first pursued the sea.

After they had admired the ship, Drake turned back to Ethan. If we aren't battling, come aboard and look around. Quite a few of my crew are your fans. They'll be pleased to meet you.

Ethan accepted the invitation. He and Misty followed Drake to the ship. Up close, it was larger and more imposing than it had looked from the dock: a black hull below white sails, with ropes everywhere like a pirate vessel.

A rope ladder dropped from above. Ethan looked up. A man in his late twenties, wearing a white shirt and a light tan from the sun, waved to Drake.

Captain! Preparations are complete. We can depart!

Not yet. Drake climbed the ladder with practiced ease. We have guests.

Guests? The sailor stared. Apart from a few old friends, he could not remember Drake bringing visitors aboard. He studied Ethan with open curiosity.

On the dock, Ethan tugged the ladder to make sure it was secure, then told Misty to climb first. He would follow below her in case she slipped.

She did not need the help. After traveling through two regions with Ash and enduring all kinds of rough weather and trouble, she found a rope ladder easy enough. What made her self-conscious was having Ethan climb behind her while she wore shorts. She wondered whether he would look upand found she did not entirely mind the idea.

Ethan urged her onward before she could dwell on it. She climbed with a blush, and he followed. He could hardly avoid looking upward altogether, but he kept his attention on the rope in front of him. He regarded Misty as a younger sister and had no interest in treating her otherwise. Looking straight ahead also avoided an awkward misunderstanding.

When Ethan reached the level of the deck, Misty offered him a hand. She wore a small, expectant smile, as if hoping to see something in his eyes. He took her hand without changing expression and stepped aboard.

At Drake's call, the sailor who had lowered the ladder and several of the others gathered around them.

Chapter 696: What Are Friends For?

Lads, look who I've brought aboard! Drake laughed to his assembled crew, drawing every eye to Ethan.

As Drake had said, the sailors had watched videos of Ethan's tournament matches. They had talked about him more than once. Several recognized his face immediately.

No way! It's Ethan Vale!

What's he doing here?

He's in Hoenn?

Are you entering the Ever Grande Conference?

They crowded around him, delighted and astonished. One sailor even touched his arm, as though checking whether he was real.

He really is here!

Of course he is, idiot.

I know! I just can't believe I'm meeting him in person.

Their excitement startled Misty. She knew Ethan's looks and his Pokemon made him popular with girls. Where had he acquired so many male fans? Ethan, too, had trouble with the attention. It reminded him of the enthusiastic biker gang he had met back in Kanto. If he had to be surrounded, he would have preferred a group of pretty girls to a circle of brawny sailors.

The man who had lowered the ladder stepped forward. Welcome aboard. Will you be battling the captain?

The other sailors perked up. A winner of two regional tournaments against a member of the Elite Four would be a match worth seeing.

Drake introduced the man. This is Liangguang, my leading student and the ship's first mate. He's a reliable fellow. He sails with me and helps me hunt for treasure.

A pleasure. Liangguang offered Ethan his hand. I watched all your matches at the Indigo League and the Silver Conference. You're an exceptional Trainer. It's an honor to meet you.

Ethan shook his hand. Liangguang was slightly tanned by the sun, but otherwise looked polished and carried himself calmly. It was easy to see why Drake trusted him as both student and first mate.

You're too kind, Ethan said. I was only testing myself in those tournaments. It helped that I didn't meet too many opponents I couldn't handle.

Drake watched their friendly introduction with satisfaction. He could deny it aloud, but he knew he was old and did not have endless years ahead. He had invited Ethan aboard because he liked him, and because he wanted Liangguang to know a capable Trainer who might be useful to him later. A man devoted to the sea could still plan sensibly for his student's future.

He waved the sailors back and cleared his throat. There won't be a battle today, so stop pestering him. Ethan is my guest. Give him room to breathe.

The crew obeyed. With Drake leading and Liangguang accompanying them, Ethan and Misty toured the deck. The five-masted ship felt steeped in history. Even Misty began to see some of its appeal.

They eventually went belowdecks. Away from the crew's curious stares, the four could speak more freely. Ethan learned that Drake and his ship would soon depart on another long voyage in search of unknown treasure.

Treasure hunting was Drake's chief pleasure between his duties with the Elite Four. Each return to land was often little more than preparation for the next departure. He truly lived for the sea.

The visit was pleasant, but Drake had a voyage ahead and Ethan had his own journey. After a little more than half an hour, Ethan rose to leave.

During their conversation, Drake had treated them to his special hot Moomoo Milk. It was sweetastonishingly sweet. Ethan guessed he had added at least five heaping spoonfuls of sugar, far beyond what anyone needed. Beneath that sweetness, the milk itself had a rich flavor. Misty seemed to like it.

Only a kid would enjoy this much sugar. Ethan shook his head and forced himself to drain the cup. When he set it down, Drake looked satisfied. Liangguang wore a practiced, obliging smile. Being Drake's first mate might not always be easy.

...

Back on the dock, Ethan and Misty waved as Drake's ship spread its sails and left Lilycove Harbor. Their meeting with an Elite Four member had been a pleasant interruption to the trip.

Knowing Drake might make little practical difference. The world was vast, and the sea vaster. Unless Ethan arranged a formal challenge, meeting him by chance again would be like searching an ocean for a needle. Not everyone had Ash's knack for crossing paths with the same people.

They left the harbor and walked into Lilycove City. It was attractive, but it had no official Gym. They could stop briefly, then move on.

Signs, mascots, and advertisements lined the streets. Misty noticed a coming event. There's a Pokemon Contest here soon! Maybe we'll see May.

Ethan was studying the map on his phone as he walked. She travels from Contest to Contest, so she probably won't miss this one. But it doesn't start for another day or two, and we aren't staying that long. I doubt we'll meet her.

True. Misty looked disappointed. I wonder how much she's improved.

Ethan glanced at her. You haven't talked privately? Didn't you exchange contact details?

We made a promise. She won't tell me how she's doing in advance. The next time we meet, she wants it to be a big surprise.

That's an unusual kind of friendship, Ethan thought, and returned to the map.

He still needed two Gym Badges. The remaining Gyms lay in different directions: one far out at sea, the other on the mainland. Now that they had returned to land, the immediate choice was clear. They would go to Fortree City and challenge the Fortree Gym.

It would be a long walk from Lilycove, through a large Safari Zone. The journey would not be effortless. They visited a nearby shop to replenish their supplies. As they were about to set out, Ethan's phone rang.

It was Anabel. That can't be good. An International Police officer rarely called him without needing help. He answered.

Ethan? I heard you're in Lilycove City, Anabel said urgently.

Who told you? Don't say you've had a satellite following me.

Drake told me. She ignored the joke. I called him just now to ask for help with an urgent matter, but he'd already sailed. He recommended you, and that was how I learned you were in Lilycove. If I'd known, I would have called you first.

Drake told her? They had only just met and said goodbye. Already the captain had sent trouble Ethan's way. This was a fast return on a new friendship. Still, a man who loved the sea would hardly turn his ship around just after setting sail.

We've helped each other before, Ethan said. Tell me what happened.

That's why you're our friend, Anabel said, then grew serious. Phoebe of the Elite Four has asked for help. Team Magma is after a remarkable stone on Mt. Pyre, like the one you stopped Team Aqua from using a few days ago. It's said to awaken Groudon and cause its Primal Reversion. We can't let Team Magma take it.

Ethan considered the information. If Phoebe asked the International Police, why can't you handle it yourselves? You have the resources.

We're still at sea, Anabel admitted. After helping you stop Team Aqua, we found several of their secret bases nearby. We're dealing with those and can't spare a force right now.

So they had turned to Drake, only for the request to come around to Ethan.

Another question, he said. Why is Phoebe at Mt. Pyre? Being in the Elite Four doesn't oblige her to guard two stones most people have never heard of.

You don't know? Her grandparents guard the mountain. They've always protected the stones. Team Aqua injured them when it stole the Blue Orb, so Phoebe came back to protect the remaining one in their place.

That explained it. Ethan remembered the guardians from the games but had not known they were Phoebe's family.

Then I need to meet Phoebe at Mt. Pyre and stop Team Magma.

Yes. I'll gather officers to support you as soon as I can. Until then, I'm counting on you.

Ethan ended the call and shrugged helplessly at Misty. She covered her mouth and laughed. She had heard enough to know Fortree would have to wait.

You stay busy, she teased. Your travels, that international company, criminal organizations, the International Policeapparently everyone needs you.

What can I say? Ethan grinned. The more capable you are, the more people ask of you.

He considered stopping at the Pokemon Center to change his team before a possible fight. Then he remembered that he had Deoxys now. Who in Team Magma could defeat it? With Raikou and Suicune alongside him, his strength was at least comparable to what he had brought to the battle in which he caught Deoxys, perhaps greater.

He felt a surge of confidence. There was no need to visit the Center. He led Misty toward Mt. Pyre instead.

...
