Mt. Pyre lay southwest of Lilycove, near the coast but tucked among remote, continuous hills. Most Trainers had heard of it, yet few had gone there. Those who had loved a Pokemon deeply might make the long journey after its death, crossing mountains and water to bury it there, hoping it could rest in peaceor simply to keep a place where they could remember it.

Chapter 697: Tomboy Phoebe

Neither of them knew when Team Magma would arrive. To be safe, Ethan sent out Dragonite as soon as they left Lilycove City, and they flew toward Mt. Pyre.

White clouds seemed close enough to touch. The ground swept past beneath them.

The mountain looked nearby on a map, but reaching it on foot would take most of a day. They would have to cross a stretch of water, then make their way through rugged hills. Even the paths vanished as the terrain grew steeper.

With Dragonite carrying them, they avoided all of that and made much better time.

After several hours in the air, Dragonite reached a peninsula. Ethan could see all of Mt. Pyre below.

It was nothing like the bare, lifeless mountain people might imagine. A high, green peak rose above dense forest, with rivers and the sea in the distance. Fog veiled its summit year-round, hiding every trail. The scenery was beautiful, yet the mountain felt strangely gloomy and dangerous. Perhaps that was only because so many Pokemon had been buried there.

People even said terrible things appeared on Mt. Pyre after dark. Some villagers at its foot had made a rule never to climb it once night fell.

Ethan suspected Ghost-type Pokemon were responsible for most of the stories, perhaps with the occasional rare Pokemon mixed in. There was little to fear once one understood what was happening. People who did not had plenty of room for their imaginations to run wild.

Following the coordinates Anabel had sent, Ethan directed Dragonite to land halfway up the mountain. The summit was still some distance away, but flying into the thick fog risked a collision with the rocks. Walking would be safer.

He also wanted to use the weak signal they still had to update Anabel on their progress.

His relationship with the International Police had never been better. They worked together readily, each helping the other. Ethan had repeatedly involved himself in their investigations and helped bring down criminal organizations. Anabel and Looker, for their part, had been just as willing to offer him their goodwill and cooperation.

They kept Dragonite beside them as a guard and began climbing.

Forest covered much of Mt. Pyre's surface, while its interior was riddled with connected caves. Together they formed a vast maze in three dimensions. The mountain was a natural Pokemon graveyard, and its caves also sheltered the Ghost-type Pokemon that appeared and vanished so mysteriously.

They had walked only a few hundred meters above the landing site when they had already passed several cave mouths. Some were just large enough for a person to squeeze through. Others were so small that only a Pokemon like Rattata could enter freely.

A chill seemed to rise from nowhere. Misty shivered. If we weren't here for this, I don't think I'd ever set foot in a place like this.

Ethan climbed onto a rock, then turned and helped her up. It used to have a different name. People called it Mt. Fire, and it wasn't a burial place for Pokemon. At some point that custom began, and over time people started calling it Mt. Pyre instead.

As they climbed, tendrils of fog appeared around them. Misty gripped Ethan's arm and looked from side to side, afraid something frightening might emerge without warning.

Using a few obvious landmarks, they found a narrow, secluded trail. Phoebe's grandparents had probably worn it into the mountainside over decades of walking. They followed the rough path, crossed several caves, and finally reached the summit.

For some reason, the fog that had blanketed the mountain below did not reach this area. Sunlight poured down on an open space that seemed cut off from the rest of the mountain. The eerie feeling was gone as well. The air was fresh, the sun warm, and the view lovely. Ethan could understand why Phoebe's grandparents had wanted to stay.

Better still, they had seen no sign of Team Magma on the way up and no trace of a battle. The group apparently had not reached the summit yet.

But where was Phoebe?

Ethan was about to look for her grandparents' home when something whistled through the air beside him. He turned and saw a small stone flying toward his head.

He did not need to dodge. Dragonite swept a wing through the air and knocked the pebble away.

Only then did Ethan and Misty see who had thrown it. A girl about Misty's age stood on the branch of a large tree, watching them with dark eyes.

Her clothes were striking. Two large red flowers adorned her head. A blue bandeau covered her chest, leaving her collarbones, arms, and waist bare. A blue skirt with a high opening shifted in the breeze, revealing a glimpse of her leg. Such an outfit would hardly draw notice by the sea, but it seemed daring on this mountain.

Ethan recognized her almost immediately: Phoebe, one of Hoenn's Elite Four, and the person they had come to meet.

You're Phoebe, aren't you? he called up. Anabel asked us to help you deal with Team Magma.

Of course I know you're here to help. Otherwise, I wouldn't have greeted you with only a pebble.

Phoebe came down from the branch with the agility of a monkey and landed on the ground. Ethan glanced at her feet. The thick grass helped muffle her steps, but the straw sandals she wore made them quieter still.

Misty stared. This girl was one of the Elite Four? She looked about Misty's own age!

Back in Sootopolis City, Misty had resolved not to let any more girls get close to Ethan. Looking at Phoebe, though, she felt no jealousy at all. It had nothing to do with Phoebe's rank. In Misty's private and admittedly unkind opinion, Phoebe was ordinary-lookingmore like a tomboy than anything else. Even the two red flowers could not soften the impression made by her short, boyish hair.

Her outfit showed off her legs and waist, but her skin was slightly dark and she had little in the way of curves. Misty could not imagine Ethan being attracted to her. He cared about looks, after all, and the girls around him were beautiful. With Mistythe world's prettiest girl, by her own reckoningalready at his side, why would he look at Phoebe?

Feeling completely at ease, Misty gave Phoebe a warm look.

Phoebe knew nothing of the appraisal Misty had just made. She came up to them, studied the two of them with curiosity, then shook her head.

I told Anabel how serious this is. Why did she send only you two? Where's Drake? Didn't she say he was nearby?

Clearly, Phoebe did not know Ethan or what he could do. She had expected more than a young man and a pretty girl. That was understandable. Not everyone followed events in other regions as closely as Drake and Wallace did. Even an Elite Four member had her own concerns, and Phoebe was young.

Ethan knew little about Phoebe in return. She had a remarkably low profile. Like Sidney and Glacia, she had not even appeared in the main anime. She seemed to receive little attention from its creators, either.

Since she plainly doubted them, Ethan said, There are only two of us, but we're both strong.

Exactly! Misty added. We've dealt with Team Magma plenty of times. We know them well. We'll be fine.

Phoebe watched them for a moment, then nodded. I suppose you're right. Anabel wouldn't have sent you here if she didn't trust you. If she believes you can handle this, I have no reason to doubt you. We shouldn't talk out here, though. Come with me.

She led them to a wooden cabin. It was small, with a vegetable garden outside where ripe produce hung among the plants. A drying rack and farming tools made the place feel lived in. It was plainly her grandparents' home.

The cabin was silent. Through an open window, Misty could see that nobody was inside.

Where are your grandparents? she asked. Aren't they supposed to guard this place?

Guard it? They're just an ordinary old couple who live here, Phoebe said. They don't have the strength to protect anything. I've already driven off several small Team Magma attacks. There could be another fight at any time, so I sent them somewhere safe at the foot of the mountain.

She did not enter the garden. Instead, she guided Ethan and Misty past it and deeper into the summit.

Before long, they reached a stone shrine. It resembled the one Ethan had seen on Shamouti Island: a small tower of weathered stones stacked together. A slab inside seemed intended to hold offerings. Two hollows had been carved into its center. One was empty; the other held a stone shaped like the Blue Orb, but glowing red.

That's the Red Orb, isn't it? Ethan asked.

Yes. Phoebe nodded. The Blue Orb was in the other hollow. Team Aqua stole it, and we still don't know where it is. One is gone already. I absolutely won't let anyone take this one too.

Ethan hesitated. He did not tell her that Shelly had the Blue Orb.

When Anabel's police vessel had rescued them from the submarine at sea, Ethan had deliberately asked Shelly to hide the orb before she left the submarine. Apart from the few of them and the members of Team Aqua involved, no one knew it was in her possession.

Now, with Phoebe talking about it, Ethan chose to keep quiet. Team Aqua and Team Magma were both after the orbs, and leaving them here had plainly failed to protect them. With two Legendary Pokemon involved, it would be better to return the Blue Orb once everything had settled.

Misty noticed that Ethan did not want to reveal its whereabouts. She changed the subject, feigning ignorance. If the orb is so important, why don't you take it away or hide it somewhere else?

She had a point. Hiding it would seem safer than standing guard over it.

But Phoebe answered without hesitation. Hiding won't solve this. When something like this happens, you need to deal with it instead of running away. Defeat the people coming after the orb, and the matter will truly be over.

For all her youth, Phoebe was ready to take responsibility. Ethan and Misty were reminded that she was no ordinary girl. She was one of the Elite Four who represented Hoenn.

Chapter 698: Team Magma, Move Out!

The Red Orb gave off a gentle, warm light, tinting the shrine around it a faint red.

Ethan looked around. No wonder Team Aqua had stolen the Blue Orb so easily. There was no security here at all. Nobody had even tried to conceal the light of the orb that remained.

Fortunately, few people even in Hoenn knew the two orbs existed, much less came looking for them. Phoebe's grandparents lived here mainly to stop mischievous wild Pokemon, or the occasional lost visitor who stumbled upon the shrine, from carrying an orb away without understanding it. Their role was as much to keep the tradition and watch over the place as to guard it against thieves.

Ethan drew his gaze away from the Red Orb. Do you have any news about Team Magma?

Phoebe sat on a broken stone railing, swinging her legs. When I drove those people off earlier, I heard them mention Maxie. It sounds as though their leader is coming in person.

Maxie... Ethan stroked his chin.

Unlike Archie, Maxie did not strike him as a particularly charismatic leader, despite commanding a large organization. He could be neurotic and fixate on tiny details. He even had a habit of using numbers in place of ordinary descriptions. Most of the time he appeared cool and composed, but when he pursued a goal he could be merciless. If necessary, he would sacrifice anyone or anything but himself.

Ethan had always found the names of the two leaders amusing. In the language of his previous life, Maxie's name paired a red flame with a pine tree, while Archie's paired water with a tung tree. Fire and water suited bitter enemies. Yet both names ended in trees. Their methods and ideals differed, but perhaps their aims were more alike than either would admit.

For someone whose name evoked fire, Maxie rarely entered a battle himself. He usually sent his subordinates instead. If he had come for the Red Orb personally, word that Team Aqua had taken the Blue Orb must have reached him and put him under enormous pressure.

Phoebe mistook Ethan's silence for fear. Don't worry. I'll handle the commanders. You two just keep the ordinary members off me.

That's quite a promise, Ethan thought. Misty met his eyes, and he could tell she had heard the same confidence in Phoebe's voice. They had come to help. If Phoebe wanted the harder opponents, neither of them had reason to argue.

Maybe this will be easy. Ethan smiled at Misty, then said, All right. Leave the grunts to us.

Phoebe seemed pleased. A moment later, she remembered something. I don't even know your names.

I'm Ethan.

And I'm Misty.

Just as they had expected, Phoebe showed no reaction to Ethan's name. She really had never heard of him. That suited him. Everywhere else he went, people recognized him and treated him differently. Here, for once, Phoebe was the one looking out for him.

After their introductions, Phoebe took charge of assigning tasks. Her plan was simple: they would hold the only entrance and prevent Team Magma from entering the summit.

Ethan considered it, then objected. We'd have the advantage of waiting for them, but we'd also be completely passive. They know where we are, and we don't know when they'll attack. If we stand guard for half a day, we'll be worn out before they even appear.

Even without knowing his strength, Phoebe looked at him with new respect. You're thinking further ahead than I did. What do you suggest?

Ethan surveyed the summit and the three of them. First, send a Pokemon down to scout. We should at least learn what they're doing. Team Magma doesn't know Misty and I are here, which gives us an advantage. We can hide and strike when they show themselves.

Phoebe thought it through. It was a better plan than hers. She had powerful Pokemon and the rank of an Elite Four member, but she was still young; strength in battle did not automatically give her the experience to consider every part of a defense.

Let's do that, she said. But you should know the mountain is complicated, and there are Ghost-type Pokemon everywhere. Anyone who didn't grow up here could get lost or have trouble shaking them off. My Pokemon need to stay ready for Team Magma, so I can't send them all the way down to scout.

Ethan understood. Phoebe could not let her Pokemon stray far from the orb. She needed one of theirs for the reconnaissance, though she plainly doubted how well it would manage.

Don't worry. I have exactly the Pokemon for this. The wild Ghost types won't bother it, and it can scout without anyone noticing.

He clapped his hands. Gengar slowly rose from his shadow.

Mt. Pyre would feel like home to Gengar. Ethan was less concerned that the wild Ghost-type Pokemon would harass it than that it might decide to harass them.

Oh! You have a Ghost-type Pokemon too?

As Hoenn's Ghost-type Elite Four member, Phoebe was naturally fond of them. Some even said she could communicate with Ghost-type Pokemon. Her eyes lit up. She circled Gengar, smiling. You've raised it well. Look how round it is! You must feed it wonderfully.

She reached out to pet it. Gengar slapped her hand away before she could touch it.

Little girl, you can compliment me without calling me round. What's round about me? I'm perfectly slim!

What? It can talk? Phoebe pointed at Gengar, her eyes wide.

You're shouting, kid. Gengar stuck a finger in its ear, then turned to Ethan. You just want me to watch those people, right?

Gengar spent almost all its time in Ethan's shadow, except when Ethan made it leave for certain private moments. It heard the conversations around him and needed no further explanation.

Ethan smiled. As long as they don't discover you, feel free to play a few pranks. Give the coming battle an appetizer.

Got it! Then I'll have some fun!

With a cackling laugh, Gengar sank into the mountainside and disappeared.

When Ethan turned back, Phoebe was still staring in the direction Gengar had gone, her eyes shining. She wiped a trace of drool from her mouth as soon as she noticed him watching.

It's so special! I love it. Would you trade Pokemon with me? I have lots of strong Ghost types. You can choose any of them!

Trade my Gengar? In your dreams.

Absolutely not. Ethan shook his head, his voice cool and firm. Gengar is my partner. I would never trade it. Forget about it.

...

A large number of Team Magma members had gathered in a thick forest at the foot of Mt. Pyre. Their orange-red uniforms stood out sharply against the green trees and undergrowth.

The loose formation suddenly stirred. Courtney, at the rear, rose to see what had happened. Maxie was approaching the front of the group with another commander, Tabitha. Courtney hurried to meet them.

Maxie looked about Archie's age, but had none of Archie's fierce bearing. He wore black half-rim glasses and a neat Team Magma uniform. His long red hair was combed back, and his slim figure gave him a scholarly air. Behind the lenses, though, his eyes were cold. His pale face showed no expression. He looked like a snake waiting to strike, and nobody underestimated him.

Beside him walked Tabitha, a tall, heavy man in a loose Team Magma jacket. His eyes remained narrowed, and a sly smile seemed fixed at the corners of his mouth.

With both of them here, their objective could only be the Red Orb. Ethan had guessed correctly: a spy had told Maxie that Team Aqua had stolen the Blue Orb, and the news had made him anxious. He would not allow Team Aqua to awaken Kyogre first.

It puzzled him that so much time had passed without news of Team Aqua's next move. Still, their theft had revealed where the orbs were kept.

Team Magma had searched for so long, never suspecting that the Red Orb lay on a mountain where people buried their Pokemon. The discovery was surprising, but they were not too late. If they seized it, they could find and awaken Groudon before Team Aqua managed to awaken Kyogre.

Maxie would not permit this operation to fail. He stopped before Courtney. What's the situation?

We've searched the whole mountain below the summit, including the caves, Courtney said with a slight smile. The orb isn't anywhere there. It must be at the top.

Good. Maxie nodded. And the woman?

He meant Phoebe.

As I reported, the Elite Four member drove off several of our probes. She's still on the summit.

Then she must be the guardian. Is she alone? Has anyone else approached the mountain?

She's alone. I placed hidden lookouts all around Mt. Pyre. None of them has seen anyone go up.

That was a lucky accident for Ethan. He had not known Team Magma had surrounded the mountain. By descending from the air straight onto the mountainside, he and Misty had avoided every lookout.

Well done. Maxie surveyed the gathered members, then raised his voice. You know our objective is on this mountain. Once we have it, we'll be one step from realizing our great dream! A child whom people call one of the Elite Four thinks she can stand in our way. Show them that even the Elite Four cannot stop us. Team Magma, move out!

Chapter 699: Courtney: Now We're in Trouble

Team Magma began climbing the mountain.

They had brought more than thirty people for the operation. That was scarcely more than the force they had once sent against Ethan, but this time every member was among Team Magma's best. They were far stronger than ordinary grunts.

One Elite Four member could hardly fight them all. With Maxie and two commanders present as well, Maxie had every reason to believe the operation would succeed.

They shared a destination, but split into three groups to keep Phoebe from escaping with the orb. Maxie, Courtney, and Tabitha each led one group toward the summit from a different direction. Special communicators kept all three leaders in contact. If one group encountered trouble, the other two could hear about it at once and come to its aid. They had prepared for every eventualityor so they thought.

Groups this large could not climb as quietly as one or two people. Footsteps and voices carried through the mountain air. Maxie did not mind. He had never intended to hide such a force. Let Phoebe hear them and understand the consequences of opposing Team Magma. If she realized resistance was pointless, she might even hand over the orb and spare herself a beating, along with everyone else's time.

But she seemed unlikely to do that. Maxie was disappointed. Why can't people understand our great dream? He gave a cold smile and turned his attention to leading his group uphill.

At first, the climb went smoothly. Mt. Pyre made him uncomfortable, as if countless eyes were watching him. He had heard about the many Ghost-type Pokemon that harassed visitors here. A few delays would be acceptable if he obtained the Red Orb in the end.

Then the fog changed. It had once covered only the summit, but now it spread downhill. His group had barely reached the halfway point when thick mist swallowed them.

Maxie initially dismissed it as a shift in the weather. A succession of mishaps soon convinced him something in the fog was attacking them.

A huge rock rolled down from above and knocked one member's Pokemon off the mountainside. Before they recovered, a tree fell across their path, nearly crushing two Pokemon clearing the way.

And his group was not alone. Through the communicator, Maxie heard the other two groups reporting their own bizarre incidents. Alarmed shouts and confusion filled his earpiece.

Wild Ghost-type Pokemon had to be behind it. Nobody saw an attacker, and few other Pokemon could play tricks without leaving a trace. Yet Ghost types usually bothered people traveling alone. Why would they suddenly target three armed groups?

It felt as though someone had singled them out.

Uneasy, Maxie ordered his people to clear the fog around them. They blew it aside, only for more mist to flow immediately into the opening.

He frowned. The climb had become a real problem.

...

On the summit, Ethan lay in the soft grass, resting in the warm sun before the coming battle. Misty had settled beside him and was watching the clouds. Phoebe had disappeared after they agreed on their tasks; neither of them knew where she had hidden.

More than half an hour passed before Gengar returned.

The moment it appeared, Phoebe sprang from a distant tree. She swung and leaped between branches with the agility of a jungle explorer, then landed beside it.

Well? Did you find Team Magma? she demanded before Gengar could speak.

Gengar edged away from her eager face and smiled at Ethan, who had sat up. I did. They're on their way.

How long until they get here? Ethan asked.

Hard to say. Gengar laughed. I asked some new friends to make a little trouble for them. They should be busy trying to deal with the pranks.

New friends? Who else is here? Misty asked. Then she understood. Oh, the wild Ghost-type Pokemon!

Of course. There are plenty of Duskull, Shuppet, Sableye, and Misdreavus on this mountain. They're a fun bunch. I told them what was happening, and they were delighted to help.

Ethan shook his head with an amused smile. Sending you was the right choice. He looked at Misty and Phoebe. The wild Pokemon won't stop Team Magma for long. Let's get ready to fight.

Maxie, Courtney, and Tabitha eventually reunited near the summit. Each looked over the others' disheveled troops. The pranks had left the members miserable, though at least few had been lost along the way.

We should never have split up, Maxie thought. We didn't catch Phoebe trying to escape, and all we gained was this trouble.

The commanders seemed about to speak, but Maxie's face stopped them. He surveyed the force and snorted. Don't stand around. Keep moving.

The thirty-odd elite members advanced again under the protection of their Pokemon, filing through the narrow entrance to the summit. The climb had been troublesome, but they had made it. Defeat Phoebe, and the orb would be theirs.

Still, the accidents had cast a shadow over Maxie's confidence. Perhaps the rest of the operation would not be as simple as he had imagined. He narrowed his eyes and beckoned Tabitha over.

Tabitha looked puzzled. Maxie whispered a few instructions in his ear. The commander was visibly surprised, but nodded and left with several trusted members.

Courtney watched them go without comment. Maxie was the sharpest mind in Team Magma. He must have had a reason.

The others soon reached the fog-free part of the summit and saw Phoebe's grandparents' cabin in the distance. They searched it, found no orb, and continued to the stone shrine.

There, Maxie saw Phoebe waiting calmly in front of the shrine. His gaze moved past her to the Red Orb, shining softly inside.

It really is here! Delighted, he started forward. Phoebe stepped into his path.

Team Magma, you don't belong here. Leave now, or don't blame me for what happens next!

Maxie checked his surroundings. Phoebe appeared to be alone. He smiled instead of attacking. Young lady, don't you understand? The world needs people like me to make it better. The oceans cover an enormous area while humanity crowds onto the land. If we awaken Groudon and bring about its Primal Reversion, the seas will dry and the land will expand. We'll have more room to live and can build an ideal world for humankind.

Phoebe was young, but his obsessive vision did not impress her. What nonsense. I may favor Ghost-type Pokemon, but even I know the ocean is the cradle of humanity. Our climate and ecosystems depend on it. If you did what you're proposing, we'd be the first to suffer.

So I can't persuade you. Maxie shook his head in feigned regret. I was going to offer you a chance to join Team Magma. But someone so shortsighted could never understand our great dream. Now give us the orb behind you.

Phoebe answered by throwing Poke Balls. Six Ghost-type Pokemon appeared before Team Magma: Mismagius, Banette, Drifblim, Chandelure, Dusknoir, and Sableye.

Maxie looked them over. He had never dealt with Phoebe before, but he knew she was a Ghost-type specialist. Her team confirmed it.

Do you really think those six can stop us just because you're one of the Elite Four? he asked with a contemptuous snort.

The elite members behind him grinned and sent out their Pokemon. Blue flashes filled the clearing. In moments, sixty or seventy Pokemon surrounded Phoebe and her team.

Most Trainers would have panicked at the sight of so many hostile Pokemon ready to pounce. Phoebe did not hesitate. She attacked first.

Even Maxie had not expected that. Foolish girl. His members gave their own commands without waiting for him.

He did not expect to need Courtney's help, much less to fight himself. Surely their elite members could overwhelm her. At the start, Phoebe's stronger Pokemon knocked several opponents down. But the crowd closed around them, and they began to struggle.

There were simply too many foes. Team Magma could not easily withstand their attacks, but Phoebe's Pokemon could not defend against strikes coming from behind and both sides. The elite members' partners were strong, too. They were nothing like the wild Pokemon Phoebe might casually drive away. At this rate, her defeat seemed only a matter of time.

Yet the more the battle went Maxie's way, the more uneasy he felt. He studied the clearing and glanced at Courtney, who was also watching without taking part. He could see nothing wrong.

Perhaps I'm imagining it.

Two explosions sounded at once, one to either side. Several Team Magma Pokemon flew into the air with the blasts.

Maxie whipped his head around. More than a dozen Pokemon burst from the forest on both flanks and joined the battle.

An ambush. His heart jolted, then he felt relief. This was what had troubled him. They had caught him off guard, but now their hidden force had revealed itself. There was nothing else to fear.

Then he noticed Courtney's expression.

What is it?

She was staring past the newly arrived Pokemon at a familiar man. Her voice sank. Now we're in trouble. That's Ethan Vale.

Chapter 700: Leaving No Opening

Ethan Vale?

Maxie stared for a moment before he realized whom Courtney meant. That infuriating man who keeps ruining our operations?

Unlike Archie, Maxie usually worked behind the scenes. He had never met Ethan, but he knew the name well. It had appeared again and again in Team Magma's recent reports. Ethan had disrupted so many plans that the organization regarded him as its greatest threat.

Maxie knew how dangerous he was. He had simply never imagined he would appear here. Why is he everywhere?

What's going on? he demanded of Courtney. Why is he here? You told me no one had come up the mountain to help her!

I don't know. For once, the usually composed Courtney sounded shaken. The patrols and lookouts didn't see him. I really don't know how he... Her voice failed.

No one in Team Magma had dealt with Ethan more often than she had. She knew what his arrival meant. He had so many Legendary Pokemon, and after the battle involving Deoxys there were even rumors that he had caught it. Their operation might fail. They might struggle merely to get away unharmed.

Meanwhile, Ethan drove his Pokemon into Team Magma's line. The surprise attack had already spread confusion, and they pressed their advantage.

With Phoebe bearing the brunt of the enemy's attention, Ethan had not called on his Legendary Pokemon. He sent out only his usual team. Even so, they struck together like a clenched fist, too powerful for Team Magma's Pokemon to stop.

Misty was his one worry. She had sprung her own ambush from the other side, but her Pokemon were not as strong as his. The first rush had gone well. If the fight dragged on and Team Magma regrouped, she could become their easiest target. Joining her mattered more to Ethan than reinforcing Phoebe.

Misty's Water-type Pokemon had a favorable matchup, and the attacks from three directions kept Team Magma too confused to notice that her side was the weakest. She could not rely on that forever. Ethan ordered his Pokemon to push toward her.

As it turned out, he had worried too much. Team Magma's members might have faced Phoebe or an unfamiliar reinforcement with determination, but the man attacking them was Ethan Vale. Many had fought in the disastrous clash over Deoxys. The defeat was fresh, and the mere sight of him shook their courage. Some lost the will to battle at once.

Maxie saw his line falter and shouted, furious. Don't be afraid! Don't retreat! Our ultimate dream is right in front of us. Once we have the Red Orb, Groudon will be ours! We cannot turn back now!

His authority and conviction had their effect. The wavering members steadied. They were one step from realizing Team Magma's dream. They could not give up here.

Under Maxie's urging, they recovered their formation and held their ground. These elite members were strong, roughly the equal of ordinary Trainers. Working together, they put Phoebe under heavy pressure.

Maxie and Courtney sent out their Pokemon and joined the battle as well. Phoebe saw that Ethan's team was strong enough to ease some of the burden on hers. In fact, the moment he had appeared, much of Team Magma's attention had shifted from her to him.

She noticed the change immediately. I'm the Elite Four member. Why are they ignoring me to attack him?

Misty had said they had clashed with Team Magma many times. Perhaps their history ran deeper than Phoebe knew, and the members were eager to settle it.

Maxie seldom joined operations himself, but a leader's Pokemon were hardly weak. He had brought out five Houndoom. Perhaps he wanted to exploit their advantage against Phoebe's Ghost types; perhaps he simply meant to bring her down and seize the orb at once. Unlike Courtney and most of the members, Maxie aimed his team at Phoebe.

The black, hellhound-like Pokemon worked together and forced her backward. She was one of the Elite Four, but five of them, with other Team Magma Pokemon nearby, were difficult to handle.

The shrine stood behind her. Her grandparents had protected its treasure, and she understood what losing it would mean. She clenched her teeth and refused to give ground. Her title had been earned young because of her exceptional strength and talent, not by chance. Under her commands, her Ghost-type Pokemon withstood the unfavorable matchup and kept the shrine secure.

Then Misty arrived to support her.

Of the three defenders, Misty was the least powerful, but she had met the lightest resistance. Most of Team Magma was focused on Ethan and Phoebe. Apart from a few members directly in her path, almost no one paid attention to her, and she made use of the opening.

In a straightforward battle, she would have struggled against even one or two of these elite members, let alone a crowd. She had come from a Gym and might someday lead the Cerulean Gym, but that future was still ahead of her. In the confusion of this battle, she could choose opponents one at a time.

Traveling with Ethan had made her stronger. She had also witnessed enough large battles to keep her head now, answering each threat without panic. That composure helped her reach Phoebe so quickly.

The fighting had torn apart the beautiful scenery around the shrine. Maxie watched Phoebe hold out long enough for Misty to join her, and his earlier excitement cooled. He studied the field again. The sides were still locked together, but the longer the battle continued, the worse his position would become.

Ethan had not used any of the Legendary Pokemon mentioned so often in Team Magma's reports. He was plainly holding back, while Maxie's force was already fighting at full strength. A direct assault would not take the Red Orb now.

It was time to see whether the plan he had arranged before the battle would work. He was glad he had acted on his misgivings.

Maxie ordered a fighting withdrawal. It was no panicked rout. His people gave ground slowly, holding their formation as they moved toward the summit entrance. The battle would continue, drawing Phoebe's and Ethan's Pokemon farther from the stone shrine. That would give Tabitha his opportunity.

The maneuver went smoothly. The fight shifted toward the entrance. Phoebe and Misty noticed the change, but assumed Team Magma was finally being forced to retreat.

Ethan was less certain. Maxie's withdrawal was too orderly. Ethan could see the fight turning against Team Magma. If Maxie saw it too, why did he neither make one last desperate attack nor break away? He seemed content to prolong a fight he could not win.

Ethan was quick to notice small changes on a battlefield, and the movement felt wrong. He did not know the plan, but he would not follow Maxie's lead. As Misty and Phoebe drifted farther from the shrine, he shouted, Don't chase them! It could be a trap!

Misty and Phoebe heard only a warning. Maxie felt a jolt of fear. Has he seen through it?

He had heard stories about Ethan, but meeting him made the threat real. Ethan had not even revealed the Legendary Pokemon from the reports, yet his alertness alone marked him as a dangerous opponent. No wonder Courtney and Team Aqua had failed against him.

To Maxie's relief, the orange-haired girl stopped advancing, but Phoebe pressed on. His plan could still work. It needed only one more push.

He nodded to several nearby members. Their Pokemon immediately attacked Phoebe's grandparents' cabin. Flames caught the garden fence and began to spread toward the house.

You monsters! Phoebe cried.

She had grown up there. It was her grandparents' home. The fire burning through their garden kindled her own anger. She would not let the people who had set it escape. She drove her Pokemon forward after them.

Ethan wanted to stop her, but they were separated by the battle. By the time he saw the flames, Phoebe was almost out of sight.

Why does the League appoint children to the Elite Four? he thought with a sigh. She may be strong, but she needs more experience. Couldn't they have waited until she was fifteen or sixteen? Phoebe had charged straight into an obvious attempt to lure her away from the shrine.

He could not abandon her now. He had accepted Anabel's request, and if Phoebe came to harm, he would have failed her. But leaving the shrine unguarded was no better.

Ethan called Gengar over. Stay here and guard it. Then he shouted to Misty, You stay too. Put out the fire first, then protect the orb. I'm going after Phoebe!

I understand. Leave this to me, Misty said. Be careful!

It was not a perfect defense, but it kept the orb protected. Ordinary Pokemon would have trouble getting past Gengar, and Misty would be there as well.

Unlike Phoebe, Ethan had no objection to moving the orb if the situation demanded it. Should anyone break through, Gengar could simply take it underground. Team Magma could dig up the whole mountain and still fail to find it.

He would leave them no opening at all.

Chapter 701: Fire Behind the Lines

Phoebe was already far ahead. Ethan gave Misty and Gengar brief instructions at the shrine, then followed with his Pokemon.

He crossed a dozen shallow craters left by the battle and soon reached the narrow approach to the summit. Everyone coming or going on foot had to pass through it.

Phoebe had said before the fight that the altitude and fog made the rest of Mt. Pyre's upper slopes dangerous. This was the only entrance she knew. Her original plan had been to block it and keep Team Magma below. Ethan's proposal had changed that. Their ambush had driven Team Magma back faster and hurt them more, but her home had caught fire. Phoebe could hardly call the outcome a success. Without that loss, she might have thought the plan perfect.

The narrow passage had slowed Team Magma's many Pokemon. Phoebe had caught up with them and was attacking fiercely. They fought back, filling the air with moves and explosions. Their advantage was in numbers; hers was in the strength of her Pokemon. Both sides took losses, though Team Magma continued to retreat, inching downhill. Before long, they would reach the halfway point and find escape easier.

Ethan and his Pokemon joined Phoebe. Stop chasing them. Our job is to protect the orb. Even if we defeat all of Team Magma, we don't have enough people to hold them prisoner.

Phoebe did not turn. I won't let them get away with burning my grandparents' house! At the very least, I'm capturing Maxie!

She was furious and meant to pursue him. Her family's home mattered more to her than anything. Still, she heard Ethan's concern and answered with confidence. Relax. This is the only way onto the summit. We've driven them out of it, so they can't reach the orb. And you left Misty guarding it, didn't you?

So she had noticed that Misty stayed behind. Her anger had not made her forget the larger situation entirely. But Ethan did not share her certainty about the single entrance.

Fog made it risky for a flying Pokemon to approach the summit from the open sky. Without a clear view, it could fly straight into rock. Yet there was another way. A Pokemon could stay close to the mountainside and climb along it. It would not need to navigate the fog at all.

Team Magma favored Fire types, but it also had flying Pokemon such as Koffing and Zubat. They might be too small to ride, yet some could carry a person by the claws or on a harness. A strike from behind was possible.

Ethan glanced at Phoebe and shook his head. He would follow her lead for now and hope his suspicion came to nothing.

He could have eliminated the risk. A few Legendary Pokemon guarding the shrine could withstand even Team Magma's full force. But he wanted to see what Maxie had planned. He also suspected that merely holding the orb was not his best opportunity. This might be a chance to destroy Team Magma's force in one blow. Better to turn the tables than wait for them to keep coming after him.

He let the battle continue and watched for what came next.

...

At the rear of Team Magma's line, safely away from the fighting, Maxie watched Phoebe and Ethan follow his retreat. He sneered. Strong as they were, they had taken his bait.

Even Ethan, whom the reports portrayed as such a menace, had come after them. Maxie had expected more thought from him. What could they accomplish by chasing Team Magma? They could not capture everyone. In the end, they would have to turn back empty-handed.

Team Magma's earlier failures must have owed something to Ethan's strength, but perhaps more to the simpleminded subordinates who had faced him. Maxie could not beat him head-on; he admitted that much. Ethan had nevertheless failed to notice the maneuver behind him. Strategically, Maxie considered it a victory.

The orange-haired girl still guarded the orb, but he had seen her struggle against his elite members. She had managed to fight a pair at a time largely because her Water-type Pokemon had the advantage. A commander would be more than she could handle.

Maxie checked the time. The move he had arranged should be under way.

An explosion shook the summit behind them. Phoebe's face changed.

No! She turned. Smoke rose in a thick column from the direction of the shrine. Only then did she realize that someone had attacked it. But Team Magma's people were right in front of her. Where had the attackers come from?

She hurried back with her Pokemon. Maxie ordered his members to counterattack. They pressed forward without regard for losses, entangling her team and preventing her from taking a step toward the summit. A moment ago, she had refused to let them leave. Now they would not let her go.

Maxie watched Ethan as well. Will you finally call out those Legendary Pokemon?

To his surprise, Ethan's expression did not change. Even with the shrine under attack and Team Magma holding them here, he showed no urgency and summoned none of his Legendary Pokemon.

Doesn't he care that the orb is being stolen?

Maxie did not know what Ethan was thinking. All he needed was to delay them long enough for Tabitha to seize the orb. Before entering the summit, he had told Tabitha to watch the battle from the flank and wait for an opening if they reached a stalemate. The order had now paid off.

Team Magma could delay two powerful Trainers, but not indefinitely. Even using his regular team, Ethan gradually fought a path back to the summit with Phoebe. Maxie's members did not pursue. They withdrew instead.

From a distance, Ethan saw flames engulfing Phoebe's grandparents' cabin. Misty was nowhere nearby. Only her Starmie remained, spraying water at the blaze with little effect.

Phoebe's heart sank at the sight. She had no time to fight the fire. She ran past the house toward the stone shrine.

The trees and bushes around it were burning too. Heat rolled outward, fierce enough to feel before they reached the clearing. Smoke billowed as branches crackled in the flames.

Ethan searched frantically for Misty. After scanning the area several times, he spotted her beyond the ring of fire, shielded by Gengar and several Water-type Pokemon.

She was sitting on the ground, smeared with mud. Her knees were bruised. Tears filled her eyes when she saw Ethan and Phoebe.

Ethan, someone stole the orb! she cried, pointing toward the shrine.

They looked up. Above the shrine, a heavyset man in a Team Magma uniform was rising into the air, carried by two Weezing. One arm clung to a Pokemon; the other cradled the Red Orb.

The orb! Phoebe shouted. She tried to send her Pokemon after him, but the flames leaped higher and cut them off.

The man smiled down at them, apparently untroubled by the heat, as the Weezing carried him farther away. Team Magma's orange uniforms were more than decoration. Their members worked constantly around Fire-type Pokemon, flames, and lava. The fabric resisted high temperatures, allowing them to operate close to a blaze.

In moments, Tabitha and the Weezing vanished into the fog.

Phoebe turned to Misty. What happened?

With Ethan's help, Misty got to her feet. I was putting out the fire when that man suddenly reached the shrine and took the orb. I tried to stop him, but several others attacked me from the side and set fires everywhere. It took everything I had to get out. By the time I looked up, he'd already flown away. Her voice was full of self-reproach.

Neither Ethan nor Phoebe blamed her. She had been alone, unable to guard two places at once. She had not expected to be ambushed, especially when their side had been the one to spring the first ambush.

Ethan looked at Gengar. It shook its head helplessly. It could not be in two places at once either. The attackers had appeared without warning, and Tabitha had set a fire the moment he arrived, preventing Gengar from reaching the shrine immediately.

Gengar might still have found a way to take the orb back. But when it saw Misty attacked and surrounded by flames, it made its choice: save her first. Her life mattered, and Gengar knew what she meant to Ethan. Even with the orb gone, it would make the same choice again.

This is my fault. Phoebe lowered her head. If I hadn't insisted on chasing them, we could have put out the fire sooner and kept the orb safe. I was too impulsive.

Her decision had been a mistake, but she was still young and had already done a great deal. Ethan was less despairing than either of them. In fact, he felt a little disappointed in Maxie.

That was it? He had expected something more clever than a simple lure. If Gengar had stood a little closer to the orb, Team Magma might have failed. One extra instruction from Ethan could have changed the outcome. He and the others had let their guard slip.

Then again, a simple plan could be effective. He assessed the fires and spoke quickly. This isn't the time for blame. A house can be rebuilt, and we can take the orb back. You two stay and put out these fires before they spread. I'll pursue Team Magma. Tabitha vanished into the fog, so I can't track him directly. Maxie can't have gone far. If I follow him, I'll meet Tabitha again sooner or later.

Chapter 702: A Suspicious Pokemon Approaches!

I'm coming with you!

Phoebe's face tightened when Ethan said he would follow Team Magma alone. She immediately offered to accompany him. Ethan had other plans.

Stay and help Misty put out the fires. She has Water-type Pokemon, but too few to handle a blaze this size by herself.

Phoebe looked around. The fire was at its fiercest. Her grandparents' house and the area around the stone shrine were both engulfed. If they let it spread, flames might consume the whole summit. Mt. Pyre would become a mountain of fire in more than name.

The cliffs around the summit kept it somewhat isolated, so the blaze could not easily travel downhill. A strong wind might still carry embers over the edge and start a much larger fire below. They could not wait.

Phoebe sighed. All right. But be careful. Team Magma isn't easy to deal with. Keep them in sight. Once we put the fires out, we'll come and join you. Then we'll face them together.

She had seen enough of Ethan's Pokemon to know how capable they were. Team Magma had gained no advantage against him, and several times he had broken a stalemate. His strength might be no less than hers. That made it easier for her to accept his decision to go alone.

Misty looked at him. Ethan met her gaze. I'm leaving this to you.

I understand! She drew herself up. Don't worry. You can go in peace!

Ethan stared at her. Why did that sound like something to say to a dying man?

He beckoned Dragonite over and climbed onto its back. Then he recalled his other Pokemon. Under Misty's and Phoebe's eyes, Dragonite took off and plunged into the fog beyond the summit.

Misty drew a deep breath and faced the flames. All right. Let's get started.

...

Visibility was almost nothing for several dozen seconds. Then Dragonite broke through the thick fog into clear air, and Ethan's view opened.

Blue sky stretched above him, the sea lay far ahead, and green forest covered the ground below. No flames burned here. No stubborn fog obscured the scenery.

Looking down, he spotted Team Magma hurrying down Mt. Pyre's middle slopes.

He patted Dragonite's neck. Fly higher. Follow them from a distance, and don't let them see us.

Dragonite climbed into the clouds and hid high above them.

Team Magma noticed nothing. Since leaving the summit, Maxie had been too delighted by the operation's success to think calmly. Tabitha had rejoined the group carrying the Red Orb. They really had it. Once they found Groudon, their great dream could be realized. The thought made Maxie's blood race.

As for where Groudon was, Team Magma had recently uncovered important clues, much as Team Aqua had with Kyogre. They had a rough idea of its hiding place. Without a way to control it, they had not dared approach. The orb changed that. It was time to act.

At the foot of the mountain, the whole group boarded jeeps hidden among the trees. The convoy drove northeast, presumably toward a base.

Maxie had arranged precautions against anyone following. Two vehicles brought up the rear, and the group used other measures to check for a tail. From above, Ethan saw it all. He kept his eyes fixed on Maxie's jeep and ignored the distractions.

The vehicles raced along the ground while Dragonite flew through the clouds.

More than two hours later, the convoy entered another rugged mountain area close to the coast. The vehicles slowed. Ethan directed Dragonite down and landed on a small hill some distance away.

He recalled Dragonite, sent out Gardevoir and Scizor, and called Gengar from his shadow. He watched the convoy carefully. None of Team Magma's members seemed to have spotted him.

The jeeps disappeared into a dark tunnel.

Ethan did not rush after them. That must lead to a Team Magma base, he told Gengar. They'll have the tunnel heavily guarded. Going straight in would alert them. Slip inside and see whether there's a hidden entrance nearby.

Leave it to me.

Gengar was used to the troublesome, covert jobs Ethan gave it. It sank into the ground and headed toward the tunnel.

Ethan sent their location to Anabel and Phoebe, then examined the surrounding terrain. On the map, he was not far from Lilycove City. After all that travel, he had circled back toward it.

The tunnel ran into a low mountain. Team Magma must have hollowed out much of its interior. Dense trees surrounded it, but the forest's peaceful appearance was misleading. Cameras and patrols were likely hidden among the foliage. A few more steps could bring him into view.

This won't be easy.

He studied the mountain from one end to the other. On the far side, a cliff dropped to the sea. Forest concealed the approach, the mountain itself made a solid fortress, and water protected the rear. It was an excellent place to defend. Could this be Team Magma's main base?

Ethan began moving carefully toward the coastal cliffs. A base like this might have a secret exit below them, and such an exit would probably be less heavily guarded than the front tunnel.

He left a marker for Gengar, then traveled through the trees with Gardevoir and Scizor. To avoid alarming Team Magma, he took a wide, indirect route.

The forest was thick. Scizor went first, cutting vines Ethan could not pass with its pincers. That was why he had brought it. Whenever they encountered a gully or a rise too difficult to climb, Gardevoir carried Ethan across with Teleport. The detour took little time.

At the cliff's edge, Ethan looked down. At least thirty meters separated him from the water. Waves struck the rock face and withdrew, exposing hard reefs of many sizes.

Something rustled nearby. Gardevoir and Scizor turned toward it, ready for a fight. Gengar emerged from the forest, following the marker Ethan had left.

It shook its head before Ethan could ask. It is their base. But I found only one entrance, and it's guarded closely. I can get in, but I can't take you through without being noticed.

Ethan took the news calmly. Still scanning the cliff for anything that resembled an opening, he sent Gengar down to search.

Gengar floated along the rock face and soon returned. I went around it. There's no entrance above the waterline that I could find.

That surprised Ethan, though it also made sense. Team Magma had built a secure base and left no easy way in.

Only one option seemed to remain. Then we'll have to attack the front. A base like this probably has a self-destruct system. Go back, find anything they could use to destroy it, and disable it before we start. I don't want a surprise halfway through.

What a life, Gengar sighed. You're the boss, so you give an order and I run around until my legs give out. Being a Pokemon is hard.

It complained, but had already turned toward the base.

That one... Ethan shook his head with a smile. Come on, he told Gardevoir and Scizor. We're going back. This time we hit the front with everything we have.

...

Inside Team Magma's surveillance room, two members watched the monitors covering the tunnel approach.

This was the organization's main base, and its guards were well trained. They did not slack off. Word had just arrived that the operation was a success, but they had also been ordered to watch for anyone following the convoy. Every unusual movement mattered.

They had seen nothing for a long time. Neither let his attention wander.

Then one of them leaned toward a screen. Hey. Is that a person?

His partner looked. A figure was moving slowly toward the tunnel entrance. It was too far away to make out. As it came closer, they saw it was no human being but a creature neither recognized.

What is that? A Pokemon?

Must be. I've never seen one like it.

The strange Pokemon was vaguely human-shaped. Its body was orange, with long, tube-like legs and no visible feet. A blue-green mask seemed to cover its face, leaving only its eyes clear. Its arms looked like tentacles twisted together.

That's bizarre. Is it wild? Did somebody send it?

They swung the camera to check behind it. All they saw was dense forest.

Let's have the entrance guards take a look. The member picked up a radio and reported the approaching Pokemon.

A strange Pokemon near the entrance? Understood. We'll check it out.

Several guards in the tunnel exchanged weary looks after their colleague put down the radio.

How many times is that now?

The surveillance room makes a fuss over every Pokemon. They sit in the air-conditioning while we have to keep walking back and forth.

Bet it's just another one that wandered in by accident.

They complained, but sent several members toward the exit. This happened every few days. Usually, they simply drove away a wild Pokemon that had strayed too close. The surveillance room's strange one was probably just a rare species.

The guards walked out at an easy pace and looked into the distance. The monitors had been right: a Pokemon none of them had ever seen was floating slowly toward the entrance.

Chapter 703: Sacrifice and Premonition

What is that?

The Team Magma guards stared at the unfamiliar Pokemon. Could it be an extremely rare species? No human appeared behind it, so it might even be wild. They exchanged eager looks, each thinking of catching it first.

Their captain studied it. Confusion gave way to recognition, and his face changed. No! That's Deoxys! We're under attack!

He knew more than the ordinary guards. He had not joined the force sent against Ethan and Deoxys, but he had heard the survivors talk about that battle many times. He had watched the footage they brought back, too. Ethan's Pokemon had astonished him, and Deoxys had stayed in his memory. Some members later speculated that Ethan had caught it after the others withdrew.

The recognition had taken him a moment. Now all those reports rushed back at once.

What? The other guards did not know what Deoxys was, but they understood under attack. They reached for their Poke Balls.

Deoxys struck first. It did not even change form. Energy gathered before its chest, formed a sphere, and shot into the group. The blast took all of them out of the fight.

Wailing alarms sounded throughout the base.

Chaos broke out. The combat guards moved toward the entrance to stop the intruder. Noncombat staff began packing and preparing to flee. A secret base ceased to be secret once an enemy found it. Even if Team Magma repelled this attack, they could no longer use the place.

Outside, Ethan stepped from behind a tree with Gardevoir and Scizor protecting him. He walked toward the tunnel. Deoxys alone could break through every defense and force open the base.

Waves of guards rushed out, their Pokemon attacking as fiercely as they could. Deoxys overwhelmed them. It advanced at a measured pace, leaving unconscious people and Pokemon behind it, along with the marks of its energy blasts.

News of the breach soon reached Maxie.

They found us after all. He was surprised by the speed of the counterattack, but not shocked. His exhilaration over the Red Orb had subsided, and he could think clearly again. He made his decision at once: abandon the base.

He regretted losing it, but the orb mattered far more. Once Team Magma controlled Groudon, they could build as many new bases as they wanted. This one was a small loss beside Groudon's strategic value.

Prepare the submarine, he told a nearby member. Evacuate the noncombat staff. Move any files we can carry and destroy the rest.

Yes, sir!

...

Sector One has fallen!

They've breached Sector Two!

The intruder is in Sector Three and engaging the guards!

Ah!

He's too strong. We can't stop him!

Fall back! Fall back!

Sector Three is lost! He's heading for Sector Four!

Orders, screams, and explosions crowded Team Magma's communication channels until voices blurred together. One fact remained clear: the intruder was driving deep into the base, and no one could hold him.

Scizor struck a heavy blast door with X-Scissor. Its pincers cut the door into four sections. As the pieces fell, Ethan entered the inner part of the base.

He had added Blaziken, Metang, and Eevee to the Pokemon beside him. The fighting would give them experience, and they could protect his rear from surprise attacks. Deoxys led far ahead like a spearpoint, clearing everyone who resisted from the front. Ethan's other Pokemon dealt with stragglers and any counterattack. With that formation, he had crossed the first three sectors easily.

The layout grew complicated near the core. Ethan had never been here before and no longer knew which way to go. He wanted Maxie, but had seen neither him nor either commander. They were probably keeping out of his path on purpose.

Gengar emerged through a wall. It made an okay sign with one hand. All done. I slipped into their control room and cut the circuits. I don't think they've even realized there's a problem.

Good work. Ethan had one less threat to worry about. Do you know where Maxie is?

I heard a call while I was in there. He's gone to some underground harbor. Sounds like he's leaving on a submarine.

So there was a hidden harbor after all. Ethan had missed it from outside. If he had entered through it, he might have blocked their escape completely. But he knew about it now, and he could still catch them before they left or soon afterward.

Do you know the way?

Not exactly, but I know roughly which sector has the entrance.

Then lead me there.

Gengar guided Ethan in a new direction. He drove his Pokemon forward faster, aware that time was running out. As they approached the harbor route, the guards fought harder. That told him they had chosen the right way. Team Magma was making its last stand, but Deoxys broke through it.

...

An enormous orange submarine waited in Team Magma's underground harbor.

One might imagine that Team Magma, with its interest in land, volcanoes, and magma, would have no use for a submarine. But it was one of Hoenn's major criminal organizations. It needed ways to travel. It also owned helicopters, though their conspicuous size kept them grounded much of the time.

This submarine was more than a simple transport. Its orange hull and unusual shape resembled a Crawdaunt. A huge drill protruded from the bow, promising considerable destructive power.

Maxie entered the harbor through several heavy doors with Courtney, Tabitha, and dozens of elite members. A member waiting by the dock hurried to meet him.

Boss, the submarine is ready. We can depart whenever you say.

Maxie nodded to the people behind him. Board.

You heard him. Come on! Tabitha led the members up the gangway. Courtney was about to follow when Maxie stopped her.

Wait.

She turned. You stay here, he said.

Courtney stared, startled. Before she could speak, Maxie continued. That man will arrive soon. We can't let him pursue us. Hold him here and buy time for what comes next.

But I... I can't stop him.

Then delay him. Maxie tossed her a controller. You've dealt with him longer than anyone else. You can manage that much.

Courtney caught it and recognized the base's self-destruct control. Pressing it would set off explosions throughout the facility. No one inside would escape.

He wants me to die with Ethan? Has he cast me aside?

She looked up. Maxie's eyes were calm. There was no pity, regret, or other feeling in them. She understood his words as a judgment on her failures: the earlier operations, and now her lookouts missing Ethan on Mt. Pyre. Team Magma's predicament had followed from her mistakes.

After several silent seconds, she nodded. I understand. You have my word: I won't let him leave here alive.

Maxie passed her with his hands behind his back and climbed aboard. As he reached the hatch, Courtney called from the dock.

Boss! She looked up at him, her voice full of expectation rather than fear. I look forward to humanity's progress. Change the world!

Maxie stopped and looked down at her. Everything will unfold as I've planned. Until we meet again.

He entered the submarine. Its hatch closed slowly, separating them like the walls of two different worlds.

Boom!

An explosion sounded in the distance. The fighting was still going on, and by the sound of it Ethan was getting closer. Courtney stood watching the submarine start and sink until it vanished beneath the water. The ripples had barely settled when a series of blasts shook the harbor entrance.

Deoxys floated through rolling smoke. Ethan hurried in behind it, guarded by his other Pokemon.

He searched the harbor for Maxie. Only Courtney stood on the dock. The last ripples on the water were disappearing.

Too late? Ethan walked toward her. Where's Maxie?

Courtney did not seem to hear. She stared at the flashing alarm light on the wall and murmured, The red warning lights are beautiful. I can see the wonderful world after our dream comes true.

Ethan frowned. Was she ill? She was talking nonsense. Her eyes brightened, and a strange smile spread across her face. Beneath her usually calm manner lay something wild. Had that always been there?

Then her expression changed. Her eyes widened as though she had seen something terrifying.

Groudon, beyond anyone's control. Destruction. Fury. Even the boss dying at its hands...

What is this? Why would it turn out that way?

She came back to herself before she could understand the vision. Deoxys was right in front of her. Only then did she seem to grasp that Ethan had arrived.

Chapter 704: Turning an Enemy into a Friend

Courtney looked at Deoxys floating beside Ethan and knew she could not beat him. This Pokemon had fought Rayquaza to a standstill. Even without it, Ethan's usual team was probably beyond her.

She would not have felt that way against most people. She would have challenged even Phoebe of the Elite Four and judged the outcome after they fought. Ethan was different. Courtney knew too well how frightening he could be.

Her purpose in staying was to hold him hereor die with him. She would give her life for Team Magma's dream, and to make up for her own mistakes.

It's my fault, just as the boss said. She had failed to keep Ethan from rescuing Professor Cozmo. She had failed to defeat him and stop him from catching Deoxys. Her lookouts had missed him on Mt. Pyre, almost ruining the operation. She put every setback on her own shoulders.

She had made so many mistakes. Now she had one chance, perhaps her only chance, to redeem them. She would not let Ethan interfere with Maxie again. She gripped the controller Maxie had given her.

Ethan could not hear her thoughts. He approached and asked in an even voice, I doubt you'll tell me, but I have to ask. Where is Maxie going?

Courtney had attacked him more than once. In the battle over Deoxys, she had even ignored the Legendary Pokemon to aim at Ethan himself. Yet he thought somewhat better of her than of Shelly. Courtney was less cunning, but her determination had value, even if it sometimes became stubbornness. She was beautiful, too, and Ethan knew he was more inclined to forgive a beautiful woman.

As he expected, she did not answer. A strange half-smile appeared on her face, touched with something frantic. Light seemed to flicker in her amber eyes.

Hee hee... Her laugh sounded unlike her usual voice and made the air feel colder. You're too late. The boss is taking the orb to Groudon. I won't let you go any farther. You can't stop him now. You and your Pokemon will be buried here with me.

Ethan glanced at the object in her hand and shook his head. Maxie left you here. No, he abandoned you. Do you really think you can stop me by yourself? Or are you counting on that thing?

He seemed to understand both her position and what she was about to do, yet remained calm. Courtney was surprised. Was he not afraid? She decided he must be pretending. No one could survive the explosion she could trigger. Everything here would be crushed in an instant.

A great plan requires sacrifices, she said. You're too dangerous. To us, you're the greatest threat and the greatest uncertainty.

Ethan understood that she meant to kill them both. He was glad he had sent Gengar ahead to disable the base's destructive systems. As a further precaution, he recalled every Pokemon except Deoxys and Gengar. Too many partners around him would make a sudden emergency harder to manage. Those two could protect him.

I know what you're thinking of doing. Don't. He held her gaze. We're not the only ones in this base. There are members of your own team who are unconscious or haven't escaped yet. Their Pokemon are here too. Do all of them need to die for this dream?

Courtney's smile froze. She had been thinking only of dying with Ethan. She had forgotten her teammates and friends who might still be inside. Was she going to take them with her? The thought struck like cold water.

Ethan kept talking because he needed information. Maxie was already at sea; searching its vast expanse blindly would be nearly impossible. Courtney could tell him where the submarine was headed. And after seeing Shelly leave Team Aqua, he wanted to help Courtney step away from Team Magma as well.

Both organizations would fall sooner or later. Courtney had ability, despite her failures against him, and he did not think she had a cruel heart. Helping her change course would be a good deed.

That's the reason, he assured himself. It certainly isn't because she's pretty.

Seeing that his words had reached her, he stepped closer. Courtney reacted like a startled rabbit and raised the controller.

You're right. I can't drag the others into this. It will be enough if I'm the only one who dies with you!

She pressed a small button.

Gengar smiled. She doesn't know I cut the wires in their control room.

Explosions sounded one after another. Before Gengar could understand what had happened, the ceiling above the underground harbor collapsed. Rock, soil, and broken equipment poured down.

Ethan's heart lurched. He had not expected Courtney to press the button so quickly, or for the blast to work after Gengar's sabotage. But he had prepared for the worst when he recalled his other Pokemon. Gengar was a Pokemon, not an engineer. It could break machinery; it could not guarantee that every device in the base had been disabled.

You lunatic! Ethan shouted. How much did she hate him to choose this?

The ceiling fell rapidly. The lights went out as a broad section of the harbor roof gave way. Emergency lamps snapped on. In the same instant, Deoxys used psychic power to hold a barrier above them. Gengar floated over Ethan, ready to catch anything that broke through.

Courtney had closed her eyes to await death. Ethan cursed and pulled her under the barrier. Darkness fell around them as rubble struck its surface with a series of heavy crashes.

The ground shook, but the blasts were limited to this part of the base. Courtney had detonated the underground harbor, not the entire facility. Its destruction system must be separate from the one Gengar had sabotaged.

Deoxys had stopped the first fall, though stones and soil kept dropping. The mountain was solid. Two enormous slabs had lodged against each other in an inverted V, temporarily holding back more of the collapse. They were sliding downward, however. In seconds they could give way.

Courtney opened her eyes and saw that Ethan had saved her. Why... why did you do that?

You wanted to die. I couldn't stand there and watch it happen, even after you tried to take me with you.

She stared at him, then shook her head. It's pointless. The exit is blocked. We'll be buried alive anyway.

Ethan looked back. Rubble filled the entrance through which he had come. There was no gap.

Gengar knocked an incoming stone aside and saw Ethan still talking. Hey! Stop trying to charm her and find a way out. This place is coming down!

Gengar could sink through the ground and escape. Its panic was for Ethan. But charm her? Ethan shot it a glare. This was hardly the moment. Then he looked toward the water.

There is another way. We go through the sea. He pulled Courtney toward the edge.

She peered into the black water below. What are you doing? You're taking me with you?

Of course. Did you think I'd leave you here to die?

You've got to be joking. I just tried to kill us both. And I've half succeeded.

Then let's make sure the other half fails. Besides, I've always been good at turning enemies into friends. Ethan urged her closer. We have no time. This is the only way out.

Wait! Courtney held back. I can't leave. And... I can't swim.

You can't swim? You were ready to die, but you're afraid of this? Or do you not want to die after all?

The words struck her. She had made her decision and pressed the button. She had thought herself unafraid of death. Why, then, was her heart pounding and her body trembling?

Ethan would not give her more time to argue. He took Milotic's Poke Ball from his belt, drew a deep breath, and jumped, pulling her with him.

Splash!

The harbor water was icy. Ethan shivered. Milotic emerged from its ball and swam to them.

Courtney had managed one breath before he pulled her in. Now she squeezed her eyes shut, held that breath, and flailed for something to grasp. Ethan released her hand. Panic surged through her, but his arm immediately caught her around the waist. Her hands found Milotic's scales, and the Pokemon swept them forward.

Ethan kept his eyes open underwater. One hand held Milotic, the other kept Courtney securely against him. Few creatures could carry them through water as fast as a Water-type Pokemon. Milotic was their best chance to leave before the harbor collapsed completely.

Since receiving Maya's blessing, Ethan had felt far less discomfort underwater. There was even something strange and almost familiar about the sensation now.

Only Deoxys remained beside him. Gengar disliked the water and had slipped back into his shadow the moment Ethan jumped.

Rocks continued to splash into the harbor and sink toward the seabed. Deoxys followed behind them, holding up another psychic barrier to keep the falling debris away.

Milotic drove through the passage like a sea serpent at the greatest speed it could manage, carrying both humans toward the far end.

Chapter 705: Convincing Courtney

The underwater passage to the open sea was longer than Ethan expected. Light strips ran along its walls, so they could at least make out the way ahead.

Milotic swam with determination. The water it displaced washed over Ethan and Courtney.

After only a dozen seconds, a deep crash sounded behind them, audible even underwater. The underground harbor must have collapsed completely. They had escaped with barely any time to spare.

A shock wave traveled through the water. Ethan felt the sea shudder and push against them. It did little to slow Milotic, but Courtney could not swim and had kept her eyes shut. The jolt startled her into losing her breath. Bubbles streamed from her mouth.

Ethan could have held on for several more minutes. The blessing he had received as the Sea Hero had changed his body in a remarkable way. Whenever it helped him underwater, he silently thanked Maya, the Sea Priestess with whom he had shared a night.

Courtney was another matter. He watched her anxiously, hoping she could endure a little longer.

Milotic finally emerged from the long tunnel and headed upward. Sunlight shone through the water above them.

Courtney could not hold out. She coughed, and seawater rushed into her mouth.

A dozen or so seconds later, Milotic broke the surface with a leap. They were still at sea. Ethan leaned against Milotic, wrapped both arms around Courtney from behind, and pressed hard against her abdomen. She brought up a mouthful of seawater.

Her eyes stayed closed and she did not wake, but her heart was still beating faintly. Ethan did not think she was in immediate danger of dying.

Deoxys rose from the water beside them. It had protected itself with psychic power and moved that way through the sea, though more slowly than Milotic.

Take us up there, Ethan told it.

Without moving, Deoxys wrapped psychic power around Ethan, the unconscious Courtney, and Milotic. It lifted them all to the top of the cliff.

By chance, it was the same cliff Ethan had examined before entering the base. Their footprints were still there. He had searched its face for an opening, but never looked beneath the water and had missed the tunnel.

He laid Courtney flat, removed her cloak, and opened the front of her uniform. Gengar floated out of his shadow and made an appreciative clicking sound.

I know it's been a while since you've been with a human female, and you're young and full of energy, Gengar said, but is this really the time? Should we give you some privacy?

What are you talking about? I'm trying to save her.

Really? Then why are you taking off her clothes? It looks just like what you do with your women at night.

Go away. Ethan refused to explain further. He moved Courtney's clothes aside and pressed both hands against her swollen abdomen. After a couple of thrusts, she coughed again and brought up more seawater. Her abdomen relaxed.

She opened her eyes weakly. She could not even lift a finger. After looking at Ethan, she stared at the sky for a long while without speaking.

A light breeze crossed her exposed stomach. She noticed her clothes, pulled them back into place, and sat up sharply. Ethan spoke before she could.

You died.

She blinked. What do you mean?

Ethan leaned back against a rock. Without me, you would have died in the base or drowned in the sea. So this life of yours is mine now.

Courtney frowned. You think that will make me tell you where the boss went?

How do you plan to repay me for saving you, then? I don't think you're the sort of person who'd answer a good deed with betrayal.

She had no reply. Courtney was not cruel by nature. In Team Magma, she had followed orders, but had done little that she considered unforgivable. She could not easily turn on someone who had saved her. And after narrowly surviving, she understood that she had not truly wanted to die so miserably. She had come out of the dark place her thoughts had trapped her in.

Then another image flashed before her eyes.

On an island covered in volcanic rock, Groudon rose roaring from the stone, its body seemingly bathed in magma. A blast of energy from its mouth destroyed several nearby islands. The sea glowed red. Fire spread while Pokemon fled in every direction. Maxie and his people came ashore from the submarine and approached Groudon.

Before they could act, Groudon opened its mouth. A surge of energy struck them.

Courtney jerked back to the present. Ethan was in front of her again.

What was that? She had seen a similar image in the underground harbor, and now it had returned. Was it a premonition? A warning?

Why am I seeing this? she murmured.

Ethan noticed her expression. What is it?

I... I... Courtney hesitated. Should she tell him? She did not know whether the vision was real or just something her exhausted mind had invented. But what if it was about to happen? Maxie and the others would be in danger.

Ethan interrupted her thoughts. Remember what I said. Your life is mine now.

No one had ever said anything like that to Courtney. She was a Team Magma commander, but in Maxie's eyes she had been a piece he could discard. She looked at Ethan with complicated feelings. If their places had been reversed, Maxie would never have saved her.

I think I saw something, she said at last.

Saw what? Ethan looked around. Nothing unusual was nearby.

An image appeared in my mind. Soon, the boss and his people will be attacked by Groudon. None of them will survive.

Ethan raised his eyebrows. A premonition or a hallucination? Have you ever had an ability like this before?

She shook her head. She could not explain it. It felt as though something was trying to warn her.

Then part of you already suspects Maxie's plan won't go smoothly, Ethan said. If you're worried, tell me where he's headed. We can go there and find out what's really happening.

Courtney fell silent. She wanted to know whether Maxie and the others were safe. She had done all she could to delay Ethaneven tried to die with him. But giving him Maxie's destination would mean betraying Team Magma.

Ethan's phone rang. Shelly was calling.

He had replaced his phone long ago with one suited to his travels. It could withstand water and connect briefly by satellite, allowing calls even from remote places. He answered in front of Courtney. Shelly's departure from Team Aqua had not become public, but it could not stay secret forever. Ethan saw no need to hide their contact.

Have you found out where Maxie is going? Shelly asked at once.

Courtney recognized her rival's voice. Why was Shelly calling Ethan?

Not yet, Ethan said, glancing at Courtney. I caught Courtney, but she won't say a word.

Shelly fell quiet for a moment and sighed. Let me talk to her.

Ethan turned on the speaker and held out the phone. This might be what changed Courtney's mind.

Courtney, listen, Shelly said calmly. She told her what had happened at the Weather Institute and later in the undersea cavern. Groudon and Kyogre are alike in this. Once either undergoes Primal Reversion, it will bring destruction to the world.

Courtney stared, trying to absorb the news. Team Aqua's second-in-command had left the organization and was now with Ethan? Archie had failed to control Kyogre because of him? Most unsettling was what Shelly said about Kyogre. Would controlling Groudon lead to ruin rather than the better world Team Magma promised?
