Ethan watched her until he thought the moment was right. Will you work with me now?

She studied him. I'll take you to the boss. But I need to see for myself whether what you've said is true.

Ethan shrugged. Her doubts did not matter for the moment. She would show him where to find Maxie and the orb.

Courtney drew a breath and gave him a set of coordinates. Shelly heard them and ended the call.

Ethan sent out Dragonite. Come on. We should leave. He climbed onto its back and offered Courtney his hand.

She had never imagined traveling with him like this. Still uncertain, she gritted her teeth and took his hand. He pulled her up behind him. Dragonite leaped and beat its wings, carrying them into the sky.

Ethan messaged Misty. She and Phoebe had put out the fires on Mt. Pyre and were on their way toward him. Without a flying Pokemon to ride, they had to walk through the remote area. He had no time to wait. He asked Misty to head for Lilycove City instead; they could reunite there after he dealt with Maxie.

Misty replied almost immediately. She understood she could do little more here. She agreed, urged Ethan to be careful, and promised to wait in Lilycove for his victorious return.

With Courtney guiding them, Dragonite flew southeast. Maxie had a head start, but a submarine was not especially fast. Dragonite drove forward like an arrow, covering hundreds of meters in moments.

Chapter 706: You Made a Move on Her Too?

Dragonite carried them more than ten kilometers from shore and out over the open sea. Flying let them cross straight over the islands below, and at Dragonite's speed they caught up with Maxie in little more than half an hour.

The enormous orange submarine, shaped like a Crawdaunt, was traveling underwater. It was not very deep. From the sky, Ethan could see its outline and the broad shadow cast by its hull. It would have been hard to notice from the side, but from above it stood out clearly.

He breathed easier. He had known they were following the same route, yet he could not relax until he found Maxie. Now there was still a chance to prevent Team Magma from awakening and controlling Groudon. Even if he could not recover the orb, he could at least ruin this operation.

Courtney's feelings were far less simple. She had led an enemy straight to her boss. She could not bear to imagine his face when he saw her with Ethan. Would he be angry? Shocked? Disappointed?

Ethan sat in front and could not see her expression. Even if he had known her thoughts, he would only have smiled to himself. It was too late to think of returning to Team Magma. Maxie would see them together and conclude, as Archie had with Shelly, that his commander had betrayed him.

Courtney could offer a hundred explanations and still fail to remove the suspicion. Even if Maxie eventually chose not to punish her, could he trust her as he once had? Would he give her important assignments? If he distanced her or stripped her of her rank, she would feel the change and begin to question her place in Team Magma herself.

Ethan was doing this openly. He wanted to force a break between Courtney and Team Magma and weaken the organization. Only complete trust from Maxie could prevent it, and Maxie was hardly that generous.

Smiling, Ethan let Dragonite overtake the submarine and fly on toward its destination. They knew the route now. There was no need to keep following from behind. Maxie would be surprised to find Ethan there first, with Courtney beside him. That, too, would make her supposed betrayal look certain.

Neither spoke as they flew, each occupied by different thoughts.

Another half hour passed. At about four in the afternoon, they reached a remote cluster of eight or nine volcanic islands. Even the largest was only two or three soccer fields across. There was almost no vegetation and no visible crater. The land rose no more than five or six meters above the sea. At a glance, there was nothing remarkable about the place.

If Courtney had not confirmed the coordinates, Ethan would never have guessed that Groudon lay hidden here.

A message arrived from Shelly. Sootopolis City was farther away than the Hoenn mainland, but not by muchonly a dozen or so minutes more by their routes. After driving her submarine hard, she had entered the island group.

They agreed on where to meet. Ethan guided Dragonite down to the largest island.

He dismounted and surveyed the place. Apart from the wind and waves, he heard nothing. He could not see a single Pokemon. The island felt dead.

Are you certain Groudon is here? he asked Courtney as she climbed down.

She nodded. We don't know its exact position. But our instruments have confirmed it repeatedly. Groudon is deep below us somewhere.

Maxie has a lot of patience. If you've found it, why haven't you tried catching it? You have enough members. Surely you could do it without a Master Ball.

Courtney was quiet for a moment. We only located it a few days ago. We also lost some Pokemon in our last battle with you, and they haven't all recovered. We couldn't be completely sure of capturing Groudon before it escaped, so we didn't rush in.

So I helped delay you? Ethan laughed. That was lucky.

The ground seemed warm beneath his feet. Perhaps Groudon's presence explained why nothing grew here.

A shark-shaped submarine broke the surface nearby. Its hatch opened as it approached the island. Shelly leaped out and crossed the rocks in a few nimble bounds.

Her gaze passed over Ethan and settled on Courtney. Courtney stiffened.

Well, well. Shelly's voice was teasing. I never expected us to meet like this. She turned to Ethan. Was having me around not enough? You've made a move on her too?

Courtney stared at Ethan. Was that the sort of relationship he had with Shelly? Had he saved Courtney for reasons beyond stopping Maxie?

She's joking. Don't take her seriously, Ethan said quickly. He frowned at Shelly. Stop saying things that sound like something else. She'll get the wrong idea.

Did I say anything untrue? Shelly snorted. You brought both of us to this point. You can't expect me to believe your motives were entirely pure.

Her attitude toward Ethan still puzzled him. She came whenever he called and did not try to flee when she was away from him, yet she continued to needle him. Perhaps the teasing was her last form of resistance. If it stopped, she might have no resistance left at all.

If anything, you should thank me for helping you avoid a miserable end. Ethan shot her a look. Before she could unsettle Courtney further, he changed the subject. Enough. We need to decide how to keep Maxie from controlling Groudon.

Shelly quieted at his look, but could not resist one more remark. What's to decide? This is what you're best at. Send out your Pokemon. What could stop you?

Ethan rubbed his chin. That won't work this time. Right now, we know they're coming and they don't know we're here. If we reveal ourselves too early, Maxie could leave with the orb. We can't guard these islands forever. Sooner or later we'd miss him.

Courtney looked as though she wanted to speak, then held back. Until recently, Team Magma's fortunes had been hers. Now two people were discussing how to defeat her boss and her comrades in front of her. It was uncomfortable to hear.

Ethan and Shelly were too absorbed in their discussion to notice.

What do you want to do, then? Shelly asked.

That's what I'm asking you. You're supposed to be the cleverest person in Team Aqua. This is your chance to offer a plan.

Now he remembers that? Shelly grumbled inwardly. Still, she considered how to stop Maxie and recover the orb. An idea came to her quickly.

She leaned close and laid it out in a low voice. Ethan frowned. He weighed it for a while before asking, Isn't that too risky? If it goes wrong, we could make things worse.

Then don't use it, Shelly said. It's your choice.

Ethan thought again and decided to trust her. The worst likely outcome was that Maxie escaped with the orb. As long as he did not control Groudon, Ethan would have accomplished the essential part of the mission.

...

Shelly left Ethan an earpiece for communication and returned to her submarine. It sank out of sight. She would remain hidden as their last safeguard. If Maxie escaped, she would track him until Ethan could act again.

Courtney went to the far side of the island and concealed herself behind a pile of stones. Ethan was not counting on her help. Watching without interfering would be help enough. He wanted to see what she would choose: rush to Maxie's aid despite everything, or heed both her vision and Shelly's warning and side with the truth.

He watched her go. I hope she makes the right choice.

Gengar rose from his shadow. It had seen and heard everything. Are you sure it's wise to trust those two women?

Who knows? Ethan shrugged. I can't read their minds. But I do know that neither of them can go back to the way things were, whether they want to or not.

With both women in position, Ethan had to act. Maxie would arrive soon. He took a Poke Ball from his belt.

Tyranitar appeared on the island with a roar.

Ethan pointed to the highest pile of volcanic rock. Let's force Groudon out. Tyranitar, make some noise!

Tyranitar roared again and gathered energy in its mouth. It fired Hyper Beam straight into the rocks, blasting the pile apart. Turning its head, it swept the beam across the island. Explosions tore through the stone. Fragments rained down.

When the attack ended, the ground under Ethan remained still. That didn't wake Groudon?

Once Tyranitar had recovered from the recoil, Ethan gave another command. This time it used Earthquake. A shock wave spread from its feet. Volcanic rocks toppled, the sea around the island churned, and the entire island trembled.

Ethan nearly lost his footing. Gengar lifted him into the air.

As he rose, a rock formation in the distance burst apart under an immense force. A huge red figure surged up from beneath it.

Shelly's voice came through the earpiece at the same moment. Radar just picked up a suspicious contact. Be careful. They're here!

Chapter 707: An Easy Operation

Team Magma's enormous submarine rose slowly and broke the surface in less than half a minute. The hatch opened. Maxie came out at once with Tabitha and the other members.

They had not even stepped off the submarine when they saw a huge red figure roaring amid flowing magma in the center of the island. They knew Groudon well enough to recognize it immediately.

What? Tabitha cried. Groudon? Wasn't it supposed to be underground? How did it get up here?

Maxie's face darkened. Groudon should have been asleep. Their instruments had tracked its stable energy for some time. Without an outside disturbance, it might have slept for months or even years. Why had it awakened now, at the worst possible moment?

Controlling a dormant Groudon and controlling an awake one were very different undertakings. He scanned the islands, but saw no person or Pokemon besides Groudon.

Boss, what do we do? Tabitha asked. He knew this change threatened the entire plan.

Maxie had to choose: take his force in and attempt to capture Groudon despite the danger, or withdraw and try again after regrouping. He made his decision in less than two seconds.

We can't wait. We have to control Groudon before that man catches up.

Tabitha stared at him. You think Courtney can't stop him?

Of course she can't. We've sent many people against him before, and they failed. She can't do it alone.

But you gave her the controller to destroy the base. You know her. She'll use it. How could he survive an explosion that wipes out the entire place?

Don't underestimate him. I doubt an explosion would kill him easily. If he were that simple to deal with, he wouldn't be a threat to both us and Team Aqua.

Then why leave Courtney there and sacrifice the base?

Maxie gave him a cold look. Once an enemy discovers a secret base, it has no value. Better to blow it up ourselves than let them dismantle it. At least the destruction might delay him and keep him from following us.

Tabitha nodded. For all his broad build and easy smile, he could be cruel. Neither he nor Maxie mentioned the members who might still be inside the base, as though their lives barely mattered.

They moved cautiously onto the island. Every eye settled on the ancient Legendary Pokemon. Even members who knew little about Groudon were awed by the sight.

It stood more than three meters tall. Its head looked helmeted, while overlapping red plates armored its back and tail. Its gray underside appeared softer. Spikes covered its powerful body. Cold eyes and sharp teeth made it formidable, and its heavy, spiked tail looked strong enough to dig through the earth.

Some said Groudon's design recalled Behemoth from the Hebrew Bible, an unconquerable primordial lord of the land. In Hoenn's legends, Groudon embodied the earth and made new land. It could clear rain clouds, and its harsh light and heat evaporated water to extend the continents. People suffering from floods had once hailed it as a savior.

Other stories said it battled Kyogre repeatedly in pursuit of nature's energy until Rayquaza stopped their struggle. Afterward, it slept in magma beneath the earth, gathering strength. Its waking could cause volcanoes to erupt. However often someone saw it, its presence remained overwhelming.

Now Groudon was visibly furious at being awakened. Magma welled out of the hole it had torn in the ground and spread across the island, making it look more imposing still.

Hidden behind volcanic rocks at a distance, Courtney watched with wide eyes and held her breath. Her heart raced. She had seen this scene in her mind more than once. Soon she would learn whether those images had been hallucinations or true glimpses of the future.

Maxie and his people followed the same path toward Groudon that she remembered. Their movements matched her vision exactly. She was almost certain now: she had seen what was about to happen.

Boss... Her fists tightened.

Groudon noticed the intruders. Energy gathered in its mouth. It fired Hyper Beam, carving a terrible path across the island and the sea. Then it turned toward the approaching group. The beam swept toward them.

Danger! Courtney could not stand and watch Maxie and the others die as she had foreseen. She rose without hesitation. Boss, look out!

Maxie and Tabitha thought for an instant that they had imagined her voice. Courtney? She was supposed to be at the base holding Ethan back. How could she be on this island?

Her warning gave them just enough time. They threw themselves clear as the beam reached them. The members behind them did not. The explosion hurled Maxie and Tabitha a considerable distance, but their quick escape kept them from serious injury.

When they recovered and looked back, a crater marked the place where their members had stood. None had survived. Groudon's power was terrifying. Maxie's face changed color. An instant later and he would have died with them.

Before he could demand an explanation from Courtney, he sensed something beside him. He turned. Gengar floated at his shoulder, grinning.

The shocks had slowed Maxie's reaction. Gengar snatched the pouch from his belt before he moved.

The orb! The pouch looked ordinary, but it held the Red Orb. Maxie had thought it safest on his person. He reached for it, too late. Gengar rose with a cackling laugh and flew away.

A man stepped out from behind volcanic rocks and caught the pouch. Ethan Vale.

Maxie understood at once. He looked between Ethan and Courtney, fury contorting his face. Courtney! You betrayed me! You betrayed all of Team Magma!

Courtney stood rigid, unable to answer. Betrayal had not been what she wanted. Circumstances had brought her here. But who would believe that?

Ethan took the Red Orb from the pouch, checked it, then put it back and secured the pouch behind him. Your commander is my prisoner, Maxie. I had her guide me here. You didn't expect me to escape your base, reach the island first, and take back the orb, did you? Your plan is over.

That made Maxie angrier. Prisoner? Courtney was walking freely, with no one forcing her. Ethan's explanation only deepened his suspicions. Everything made sense now. Courtney had told Ethan where they were going. Ethan had awakened Groudon. She was a traitor.

He opened his mouth to accuse her again. Groudon did not give him the chance.

It attacked whatever moved before it. Ethan had revealed himself and become another target. Groudon fired Hyper Beam toward him, Courtney, and Maxie.

Halfway there, a second Hyper Beam shot in from another direction. The beams met in a violent explosion. Groudon turned toward the attacker.

Tyranitar came out from behind the volcanic rocks and stared it down. Groudon was larger and far more imposing, but Tyranitar did not flinch. The two Pokemon stepped toward each other. A fierce battle was about to begin.

Tabitha limped to Maxie's side. A stone fragment from the explosion had cut his knee. The wound was not grave, but it made walking difficult.

Boss, what now?

Maxie had no ready answer. His members were dead, Courtney had apparently betrayed him, the orb was gone, and Groudon was raging beyond their control. He had arrived confident and lost everything before the operation could truly begin.

He took a breath and forced himself to think. We withdraw for now.

Withdraw? Tabitha glanced at the fallen members. Leaving like this felt unbearable.

Maxie looked toward Ethan. He wins this time. It isn't over. We need to rebuild our strength, then find a chance to take the orb back.

Ethan could not hear their words, but he read their intent. He had no intention of letting them escape. So far the operation had been easier than any he could remember. Shelly's plan had barely begun, and he already had the orb.

He was about to send Gengar after Maxie and Tabitha when something flashed across his vision. The next instant, his Tyranitar slammed into a volcanic boulder.

Chapter 708: Team Aqua Arrives

Even after all its travels and training, Tyranitar could not defeat Groudon one-on-one. It was outmatched in size, defense, speed, and power.

In the games, their numbers might not look far apart. This was a living world, not a table of statistics. Without Mega Evolution, Tyranitar could not easily cross the gulf between them. Nor was Ethan directing it. Two Tyranitar relying on brute-force collisions might still have failed.

That was the terrible strength of an ancient Legendary Pokemon. Its presence alone could make most Pokemon hesitate to approach.

Rocks rattled as Tyranitar pushed itself up from the pile. The short exchange had already left wounds across its body. Its eyes held no fear. It roared and charged Groudon again. Whether it could win or not, it had the courage to fight.

Ethan glanced over. He had not watched the exchange closely, but the result was no surprise. Tyranitar's collision had delayed Gengar's pursuit, giving Maxie and Tabitha a little more distance. That was inconvenient, not decisive.

Maxie had been Ethan's true objective all along. He was dangerous because of his ideas and the large organization he led, not because his own battling strength frightened Ethan. Capture him, and Team Magma would lose its leader. The organization might fall apart soon afterward, sparing Hoenn much harm and Ethan a persistent enemy. He did not want to miss this rare opportunity.

Ethan had no plan to catch Groudon or settle a contest of strength with it. Keeping it occupied long enough to secure Maxie would do.

He told Gengar to continue the chase. Tyranitar alone could not hold Groudon for long, so Ethan reached for more Poke Balls. Shelly's urgent voice sounded in his earpiece.

This is bad. Team Aqua! They've found me!

Team Aqua? For a moment Ethan thought he had misheard, or that Shelly had said the wrong name in her alarm. Why would Team Aqua be here? Then he realized she meant exactly what she had said.

Her submarine surfaced in the distance. The hatch flew open, and she jumped down and hurried toward him. She had brought the Blue Orb with her.

Since obtaining it, Shelly had guarded the orb carefully. She usually kept it close to prevent Team Aqua from stealing it again. It was awkward to carry outside, so she often left it aboard the submarine. Bringing it onto the island now showed how urgent the situation had become.

As she reached shore, another vessel broke the surface behind her: a huge blue submarine shaped like a shark. It was as imposing as Team Magma's orange craft. Its color and markings left no doubt who owned it.

Shelly ran up, breathless, and pressed the pouch holding the Blue Orb into Ethan's hands. I was careless. Archie matched his signal and frequency to mine. My radar never showed him closing in. He followed me here without my noticing!

Both submarines had come from Team Aqua. Archie had found a way to hide his approach from Shelly's instruments. He had caught them off guard while they were focused on Maxie.

How had Team Aqua found Shelly so quickly? She had kept hidden and done nothing conspicuous. Ethan could not answer the question now. He had both orbs in his hands.

That was dangerous. If someone took them from him, both would be lost at once. Few could steal anything from Ethan, but he could not ignore the possibility. He tied both pouches securely behind him.

Then he sent out Raikou and Suicune to help Tyranitar occupy Groudon. He turned back to the blue submarine. Team Aqua was here; he would have to see what they intended.

Gengar had nearly reached Maxie and Tabitha. They sent out Pokemon to fight back. Gengar was much stronger than most of its kind, but could not capture the two immediately. Their struggle stalled.

Across the island, Raikou and Suicune pressed Groudon from opposite sides while Tyranitar attacked with them. The three of them working against it brought to mind three heroes facing a single mighty warrior. Groudon sensed that the two Legendary Pokemon were exceptional. It did not consider them its equals, but it gave them its full attention.

The first part of Shelly's plan had worked. Waking Groudon had drawn Maxie to the island and set up Ethan's ambush. Team Aqua's unexpected arrival now trapped Ethan in the struggle he had hoped to control. Groudon was tying up his own forces.

Two broad-shouldered men climbed onto the top of the blue submarine: Archie and Matt.

Archie looked toward Ethan and Shelly with mocking eyes. Didn't expect to see us again, did you? His amplified voice carried clearly across the water.

Archie! Shelly called to her former leader, conflicted. Why are you here?

He bared his teeth in a grin. To pay you back for last time, of course. And to take back what belongs to me.

He nodded to Matt. Tubes emerged from the submarine's hull. At Matt's order, dozens of guns of different calibers opened fire, blanketing the island.

Boom! Boom! Boom!

Shells struck rock and burst all around them. Archie's idea was clear. If his Pokemon could not beat Ethan, he would try human weaponry.

Ethan could not simply stand through an attack covering the whole island. He sent out Gardevoir and had it shield him and Shelly with psychic power, then recalled Raikou, Suicune, and Tyranitar from their fight with Groudon. He still ordered Gengar to pursue Maxie despite the shelling.

Smoke and dust swallowed the island. The bombardment had begun so suddenly that Ethan had lost track of Courtney. He hoped she had found cover. Soon he could no longer see Groudon or Gengar either. All he could do was keep Shelly safe behind his Pokemon's defense and wait out the barrage.

Groudon would not suffer the attack quietly. After several shells struck it, it roared and fired Hyper Beam through the barrage. The thick energy column crossed the island and the sea in an instant and hit the blue submarine's port side.

The submarine lurched. Its guns went silent.

Archie dropped to one knee on the roof. Once the vessel stopped shaking, he stood and glared at Groudon. Every one of you gets in my way! Fine. I'll destroy you first, then deal with that man and the traitor!

He shouted down through the hatch, Everyone out! Finish them all!

A lower hatch opened. More than a dozen speedboats full of Team Aqua members roared toward the island. Their sailor scarves, fierce eyes, and wild shouting made them resemble pirates. They rode motorboats rather than wooden ships, and their weapons were Poke Balls rather than muskets and cutlasses.

Archie and Matt jumped into a speedboat and followed. They had come prepared, with both people and equipment.

As the smoke thinned, Ethan and Shelly saw the boats racing in. Ethan looked first toward Maxie's escape route. Archie had arrived with a formidable force; beating him would take a hard fight. Maxie was the easier capture if Ethan could still catch him.

But the shelling had changed that, too. Gengar lay overturned after taking a hit. Maxie and Tabitha had reached their submarine.

They did not depart. Maxie saw an opportunity in the confusion and ordered the members still aboard to attack. The enormous drill at the submarine's bow began spinning. It slammed against the island, tearing into the volcanic rock.

Maxie knew his position was poor. Ethan and Team Aqua both threatened him, and he could not let either side take Groudon. Better to disrupt everything than wait for defeat. If he could not have Groudon, neither would theyespecially Team Aqua.

Ethan sighed. A few minutes had turned an easy operation into a battle on two fronts. The one advantage was that Groudon had stopped targeting him. Its attention had shifted to Team Magma's submarine, and particularly to the drill chewing through the island.

Groudon had been woken in anger. Now these humans were making an even greater racket. It walked toward the orange submarine, intent on destroying the noisy machine, whether or not anyone held the Red Orb.

Team Aqua's boats reached the shore. Members leaped out, shouting, and sent their Pokemon at Ethan. He and Shelly exchanged a glance and called out their own.

Neither Team had any intention of stopping short. The whole operation was out of Ethan's and Shelly's control. With both orbs in his possession, Ethan could still leave the island. But Courtney was missing. He had finally shaken her faith in Team Magma; abandoning her here would undo everything.

Chapter 709: Trading for Her Life

Shell craters of every size scarred the island. The taller piles of volcanic rock had been blasted apart. The bare little place looked more desolate than ever.

Among the flattened ruins, Ethan finally spotted Courtney. She was crouched in a crater. Her Camerupt stood over her, shielding her with its body. Scorched marks still smoked on its back. It had protected its Trainer through the barrage.

Courtney's orange-red uniform stood out against the dark stone. She looked shaken and disheveled, but unhurt. Ethan felt some relief. Courtney, are you all right?

She stood and shook her head. Ethan turned back to the fight. There was no time to look after her further. Archie and his members had reached him and Shelly.

Old enemies needed no more threats. The battle began at once. Moves crossed the air, and Pokemon collided.

Ethan held nothing back. Shelly still had complicated feelings about being called a Team Aqua traitor, but she attacked her former comrades without hesitation. She knew this was no time for mercy. Team Aqua showed her none in return.

Archie came straight for Ethan. Matt, the other commander, met Shelly. The two people who had once served together now fought a battle that could cost them their lives.

Then the sea erupted. A huge shape rose amid flying spray.

Groudon turned as if it had sensed the newcomer. A massive blue Pokemon, shaped like a winged whale, leaped from the water, rolled in the air, and crashed back down. Waves towered around it. Everyone looked toward the sound.

Its identity was unmistakable: Kyogre.

The two ancient Legendary Pokemon had met here. Ethan, Shelly, and Maxie were astonished. Team Aqua's members looked less surprised.

Archie had not initially followed Shelly. He had been tracking Kyogre's wake through the sea. Near these islands, he lost it and instead detected Shelly's concealed submarine. Then he saw the battle ashore. He chose his new target immediately. Now Kyogre had appeared of its own accord.

Its arrival was no accident. Kyogre and Groudon had fought since ancient times. Apart from sleeping and feeding, they seemed to spend much of their existence struggling against one another. Since its earlier awakening, Kyogre had been searching for Groudon. It could sense its rival somewhere in this stretch of sea but had not found the exact place. The recent fighting revealed the island and drew it here.

Kyogre's appearance transformed the battle. Groudon abandoned Team Magma and strode toward its old enemy. Kyogre rose from the sea and floated toward Groudon. They had eyes only for each other.

Ethan, Team Aqua, and Team Magma suddenly mattered very little. All of them had to clear the battlefield for the two giants.

Groudon roared. Kyogre answered. They collided, shaking the island. The sky changed color. Thick clouds gathered over the water, the light dimmed, wind swept across the rocks, lightning flashed, and the sea churned.

The worsening conditions made the human battle harder. Everyone had to fight while avoiding the two ancient Pokemon. Neither Groudon nor Kyogre had undergone Primal Reversion, but their attacks still struck everything nearby with enormous force.

Both Archie and Maxie saw an opportunity. Ethan held the orbs. Defeat him, and they could take what they wanted. Groudon and Kyogre were occupied with each other and might wear themselves down. Their ultimate dreams seemed suddenly close.

Archie drove his members into a fiercer attack on Ethan.

Maxie had fewer options. He had brought a small force and lost many of them to Groudon's beam. He could not make a frontal assault. He would have to outthink Ethan instead, a method that suited him well. Through the submarine's large monitor, he spotted Courtney on the island. An idea came to him.

...

Tyranitar, Scizor, Dragonitehold the line. Don't let them push you back! Metang, Milotic, Eevee, Blaziken, use your strongest attacks. No holding back!

Gardevoir, join them at the front. If you all hold, nobody can reach me. Gengar, stop taking it easy. There are too many of them for you to hide your strength now.

Raikou, Suicune, cover our flanks. Don't let any Pokemon slip around us!

Under Ethan's direction, his Pokemon and Shelly's worked together. Their defense held Team Aqua in front of them. Ethan had committed every Pokemon with him except Deoxys, which he kept back for an emergency.

He had expected a simple pursuit. He would have brought a stronger lineup if he had known the chase would become this chaotic. He had to manage with the team he had. Deoxys remained a powerful reserve. It might not win a duel against Groudon or Kyogre, but it gave Ethan room to act.

Shelly moved closer after her Pokemon repelled one of Matt's attacks. Archie's pushing harder. Can we really hold them?

She had rarely fought while outnumbered like this. Team Aqua and Team Magma usually brought the larger force. Even knowing Ethan's strength, she felt uneasy. With almost anyone else beside her, she would already have fled.

We have to, Ethan said. We could leave safely right now. But if we do, Groudon and Kyogre will exhaust each other, and the Teams will take them. We can't withdraw.

I know, but... She glanced toward Team Magma's submarine. Maxie had not acted in some time. The less he showed, the more dangerous whatever he was planning seemed.

Ethan understood. We can't spare anyone for him yet. Deal with Team Aqua first.

He also wondered why Courtney had not gone back to her own side. During a brief opening between commands, he looked around. Maxie and Tabitha were on the island again, escorting Courtney toward him at a slow pace.

How did they catch her? And when did Maxie leave the submarine?

They stopped some distance away. Maxie called, If you want her to live, hand over the Red Orb!

Ethan looked at Courtney before answering. She stood with her eyes lowered, expression empty. She showed no fear and no expectation that Ethan would trade the orb for her. She seemed to have given her fate to someone else.

She likely had not resisted when Maxie seized her. She felt guilty for leading Ethan here and revealing their destination. Even after risking her life to delay him, she did not want to be called a traitor.

Why do you think I'd give you the orb for her? Ethan asked, his expression unchanged.

Courtney lowered her head further. Shelly glanced at Ethan but said nothing.

Maxie studied him. I didn't expect that answer. I thought you were full of righteous principles.

Ethan shrugged. He was bargaining and would not reveal how much he wanted to save Courtney. One person's life matters, but so do many others. If keeping Groudon from undergoing Primal Reversion and falling into your hands requires a sacrifice, so be it.

Maxie had not expected him to say that. Perhaps Ethan was bluffing. You think I'll believe you? You were in contact with her long before this, weren't you? Your escape from the base was arranged. Otherwise, why would she defy my order and bring you here?

Maxie did not know Courtney had pressed the detonator and tried to die with Ethan. Nor did he know Ethan had pulled her from the collapse. He thought she had simply ignored her orders and defected.

Ethan did not correct him. Maxie might even be fishing for information, trying to find a weakness in Ethan's account. Both understood that the other was difficult to manipulate.

Explosions sounded behind Ethan. His Pokemon were still battling Team Aqua, while Groudon and Kyogre shook the island so violently that it seemed close to breaking apart. He had little time left to bargain.

But he would not simply hand over the orb. He held up its pouch and eyed Maxie. I might consider a trade. First tell me this: after it, would Courtney still be a member of Team Magma?

Chapter 710: You Tricked Me, Kid!

Maxie was pleased that Ethan would trade an orb for Courtney, though he kept his face still.

A traitor can't remain in Team Magma, he said. She's useless to me now. If her life buys the orb, I'll at least get something out of her.

He had unwittingly helped Ethan. Once Maxie had decided Courtney was a traitor, he could scarcely hide his disgust with her or say anything kind, even for the sake of bargaining.

Ethan turned to Courtney. You heard him. Your boss has said you're no longer in Team Magma. When I get you back, body and soul, you'll belong to me instead.

She raised her head and looked at him with complicated feelings. She had never expected him to trade an orb for her. Her life seemed insignificant beside all of Hoenn. She had held no hope. Now, after a swirl of thoughts, one simple feeling remained. She gave him a small smile and nodded, her eyes bright.

I understand.

Ethan faced Maxie again. I'll make the trade. How do I know you won't go back on your word once you have the orb?

Maxie snorted. You'll have to trust me.

No. Your word isn't enough. I need to feel safe making this exchange.

What do you propose?

A compromise. Have the heavy one bring Courtney to the middle and let her go. As she walks to me, I'll throw the orb to you.

Maxie considered it. The proposal was risky, but acceptable. Tabitha would stay close enough to seize Courtney again if anything went wrong. Maxie had no better option. Ethan was not simple to manipulate; if the terms favored Team Magma too obviously, he might refuse. Groudon and Kyogre were fighting, and the orb was within reach. Maxie could not let the chance pass.

Agreed. But don't try anything.

You'll get an orb.

Maxie gave Tabitha a signal. Tabitha led Courtney toward the center. At the same time, Ethan took the pouch holding an orb into view. Maxie watched every move. It looked like the pouch he had carried from the submarine, and the round shape inside was unmistakable. His tension eased. Perhaps Ethan meant to keep his word.

At the center, Tabitha released Courtney. She began walking toward Ethan. Ethan tossed the pouch to a spot a little way from Tabitha, who hurried over to collect it. Courtney reached Ethan while Tabitha was occupied.

I... she began.

Ethan held up a hand. This isn't finished. We can talk when we're away from here.

Tabitha did not open the pouch. He might have feared an ambush, or he might have been wary of Ethan's Pokemon. He felt the orb through the fabric, then ran back to Maxie.

Maxie took the pouch and smiled. The fool really gave up an orb for a woman. Ethan had turned a commander and laid an ambush, yet the orb had returned to Maxie's hands. As long as he kept it, he could find another chance to control Groudon and realize his dream. He shot Ethan a triumphant look and turned away.

Oh, Ethan said, feigning surprise. I think I mixed them up.

What? Maxie spun around.

Ethan held up a second pouch, smiled apologetically, and drew out a glowing red orb.

The Red Orb was still with Ethan. Maxie stared. Then what had Tabitha brought him?

He opened the pouch. Blue light shone across his face.

The Blue Orb? How did I get this? Nohow did Ethan get it?

Maxie's information was incomplete. He knew Team Aqua had stolen the Blue Orb, but not that Shelly now held it. He had missed the moment she handed a pouch to Ethan. He never imagined Ethan had both orbs, much less that he would trade away the blue one.

You tricked me! Maxie shouted.

Tricked you? I said I'd trade an orb. I never said which one.

Maxie opened his mouth, then stopped. Ethan had never named the Red Orb. Maxie had assumed it, because he did not know another orb was available.

What am I supposed to do with the Blue Orb? Capture Kyogre? I came for Groudon!

Ethan was not finished. He looked toward Archie, who was busy directing Team Aqua's battle and had missed the exchange.

Archie! Take a look at what Maxie has! Ethan called.

Archie glanced up and saw the Blue Orb in his rival's hand. Maxie! Why are you holding the Blue Orb?

Maxie had no useful answer. He could hardly confess that Ethan had played him. Besides, why should he explain himself to his sworn enemy? If nothing else, holding the Blue Orb meant Team Aqua could not control Kyogre. The thought made him feel a little better.

Ethan added fuel to the dispute. Careful, Archie. I don't have it anymore. Maxie might control Kyogre first and keep you from getting it at all.

The two organizations already hated each other. Archie could not simply ignore that warning. He understood Ethan well enough to believe that Ethan would hide the orb rather than use it to control Kyogre. Maxie was another matter. Archie could imagine him seizing Kyogre solely to thwart Team Aqua, then turning it against them.

He would not allow it. At a wave of his hand, Team Aqua changed targets and charged Maxie.

Maxie wanted to curse Ethan, but there was no time. He had to reach his submarine. With a full force, he would not have feared a fight against Team Aqua. Now he had only Tabitha and a few members operating the submarine. He and Tabitha fled toward it.

Shelly stared at Ethan. The change had happened so quickly that she had only just followed it. You really are devious. You handed Maxie that dangerous orb and made him Archie's problem. When did you switch them? I didn't even notice.

Ethan looked pleased with himself. When you gave me the Blue Orb. I expected another twist today, so I quietly swapped which pouch held which orb. But we can't leave the Blue Orb with Maxie. We still need to get it back.

He turned to Courtney. Can you fight?

Yes. She nodded.

Since Ethan had traded an orb for her, something in Courtney had shifted. She could face Team Aqua, and even Maxie, without the same turmoil.

Ethan looked at the two women beside him, one in blue and one in red. Once they had stood on opposite sides of a bitter rivalry. Now both would fight with him.

Good. Let's drive them all into the sea!

His Pokemon struck Team Aqua's flank. This time Ethan's group was attacking rather than defending. Team Aqua had to fight Maxie's group in front and Ethan's from behind. Its formation began to break.

Without Archie or Matt to lead them, the members left to guard the rear could not hold Ethan back. They gave ground. At the other end, Maxie fought while retreating toward his submarine, Archie close behind him.

Team Aqua's line was caught between two opponents, but Archie no longer cared about Ethan. He wanted the Blue Orb back.

Matt battled Tabitha. Both favored direct action, and they were closely matched. Archie took on Maxie.

Maxie could direct an organization brilliantly, but he could not overpower the larger Archie in a direct fight. As the struggle intensified, his prospects darkened. At this rate, Archie would follow him into the submarine even if he reached it. He could not lose his last means of escape.

Maxie changed course. Instead of retreating to the submarine, he led the pursuing Team Aqua members toward the center of the island, where Groudon and Kyogre were fighting. If you want the orb, let's see whether you dare follow. We may all die together.

Archie and Ethan noticed the turn. Neither stopped pursuing.

Archie knew his old rival. Maxie valued his own life. If real danger caught them, Archie doubted Maxie would keep running toward the two Legendary Pokemon. This was another calculated maneuver to make the pursuit hesitate. Archie would not fall for it.

At the island's center, Groudon and Kyogre were fighting with single-minded fury. They paid no attention to the human conflict. Each had been disturbed from sleep, and neither would stop until it brought the other down.

Maxie, Tabitha, and their pursuers drew closer to that battle.

Chapter 711: Take ThisPrecipice Blades!

Archie could be reckless, but even he knew sending ordinary members close to Groudon and Kyogre would be sending them to their deaths. He ordered them to stay back and delay Ethan. Archie and Matt continued the chase with their own Pokemon.

Ethan knew approaching the two ancient Pokemon was dangerous, too. He recalled the members of his team he did not need for this push. Gengar, Gardevoir, Dragonite, Raikou, and Suicune remained with him as he drove through the opposition.

Shelly and Courtney made no changes. Each had brought out only a few Pokemon. Courtney fought alongside three Mightyena rather than her usual Camerupt. A Fire-type Pokemon would have little chance against Team Aqua's many Water types.

The Mightyena formed a disciplined little pack. They were strong individually, but stronger together: when one attacked, the others guarded it. Mightyena naturally favored group action, followed a leader, and worked together to pursue prey. That made them attractive to commanders in both organizations.

Shelly's problem was different. On land, she could not use her strongest sea-dwelling Pokemon. She relied on Walrein and Crawdaunt, both capable partners. Team Aqua's members faced the same limitation. They too had left their favored fully aquatic Pokemon in the water and fought with those that could move ashore. Both sides lost some of their strength.

Archie had still been overconfident to think those members would stop Ethan. They had failed to break his defense with Archie and Matt commanding them. Without either leader, they stood even less chance. Ethan's team cut through their lines like a blade, with Shelly and Courtney following.

Raikou was especially difficult for Team Aqua. Its Electric attacks had a natural advantage against their Water types. Most Pokemon it struck went down on the first hit; few could endure a second. Explosions flashed among the members, their flames almost immediately doused by the rain.

He's too strong. We can't fight him! one member groaned.

Gardevoir defeated his Pokemon with Psychic. It flew several meters and landed on top of him. Pinned beneath it, the member could only watch Ethan's group pass.

And Lady Shelly is with him, said another injured member, clutching an arm. How are we supposed to attack her?

Idiot. Why are you still calling her Lady Shelly?

Because I respected her. She's why I joined Team Aqua.

Archie had expelled Shelly, and the whole organization had heard. Some who had admired her could not accept it. Was she being forced? Did she have a reason they did not know? They wished it were a false report. Seeing her fight beside Ethan ended that hope, yet many still could not bring themselves to attack her with all their strength.

...

At the island's center, Groudon and Kyogre unleashed their power. The ground trembled beneath them and threatened to break apart.

Lightning cracked overhead. Rain soaked Maxie's clothes. He glanced back. Archie was still closing in, clinging to the pursuit like a dog that would not let go. Maxie had run toward the ancient Pokemon expecting Archie to turn away, but had underestimated his courage and his obsession with the Blue Orb.

Maxie could understand it. If an easy chance to recover the Red Orb lay before him, he might pursue it just as fiercely.

He looked toward Kyogre and considered trying to capture it with the Blue Orb. He took several steps, but each attempt to move closer was stopped by flying volcanic rock or a wave of force. His human body could not withstand either. He had reached the limit of how far he could go.

Damn it. I have the orb, but I can't get near enough to use it.

Neither Groudon nor Kyogre had managed to defeat the other. They stopped almost together and gathered power. A dreadful pressure rose from both of them. Everyone nearby sensed that something was wrong.

Before anyone could act, enormous red and blue bursts of energy rose more than a hundred meters from the center of the island.

They collided. The explosion swept everything around them. The blast threw people and Pokemon away. The island beneath them took the worst of it. Volcanic rock melted or shattered under the force. Then another wave of energy expanded across the land, threatening to engulf it all.

Ethan pushed himself up and saw it coming. Go!

He recalled the Pokemon around him and sent out Dragonite again in the same breath. He climbed on and pulled Shelly and Courtney aboard, one on either side, after they recalled their own partners.

Dragonite shot toward the edge of the island. It was fast, but the blast wave caught it before it cleared the shore. Dragonite rolled, throwing all three people into the sea.

Splash!

The water was icy, but the heat vanished at once. Shelly surfaced first, swimming powerfully. Ethan followed, then remembered Courtney could not swim. He dived back and brought her up. She had held her breath and emerged gasping, but had not swallowed water this time.

Dragonite's smooth head appeared behind them. They looked back at the island. Most of it had disappeared. Its outer rim remained, but the raised volcanic rocks at the center were gone. A huge crater had taken their place, and seawater rushed into it through the broken ground.

Groudon and Kyogre stood inside, both wounded and breathing hard as they watched each other.

What was that? Shelly murmured.

Team Aqua and Team Magma had chased the two Pokemon since their organizations began, but much of what they knew came from old writings and stone tablets. They did not know every detail of their powers. The attacks they had just witnessed were unfamiliar.

Precipice Blades and Origin Pulse, Ethan said. Their signature moves.

Shelly and Courtney stared at the crater. Such power...

The moves were powerful, but Ethan was not stunned by the blast alone. Together, they had done damage comparable to Tri-Bird Assault from his three legendary birds. That comparison covered only a single use. His birds were exhausted after their combined attack and fought at a fraction of their strength afterward. Groudon and Kyogre had used their signature moves and were still ready to fight. Their individual power was far greater.

And this was before Primal Reversion. The same attacks would grow more terrifying in their primal forms.

After a while, the effects of the explosion faded. Some Team Aqua members farther away had reached the water in time. Many others floated motionless on the surface. Ethan could not tell whether they were alive.

He searched among them for Maxie and found nothing. Had Maxie been vaporized or sunk? Ethan was concerned about the Blue Orb still in Maxie's possession. Losing Maxie might rid Hoenn of a dangerous man, but losing the orb would cause other problems. Archie, Matt, and Tabitha were missing too. Ethan doubted all of them had died so easily. He expected at least some to reappear before long.

Courtney held onto Ethan's waist to stay afloat. Her hand brushed the pouch tied there. It was empty.

Where's the other orb? she asked.

Ethan looked down. The bottom of the pouch had been torn open. The Red Orb was gone.

He stared, then sighed. The blast must have ripped the fabric and thrown the orb free. How could he search for it now? The sea was beneath them, rain fell from dark clouds, and visibility was poor.

Shelly noticed the empty pouch and said nothing. It was terrible luck, but she could not blame Ethan. Had she carried it through that blast, she might have lost it too. They had finally brought the two orbs together, only to lose both within minutes.

At least neither Groudon nor Kyogre had fallen under anyone's control. They had fought and destroyed an island, but that was better than the disaster the Teams had intended.

For Ethan, the matter did not feel finished. I have a feeling this isn't over. The orbs are lost, but when we next see Archie and Maxie, I bet they'll have them.

Shelly frowned. Why do you say that?

A hunch. Call it a rule about villains. Ethan sighed. Next time, we won't be facing ordinary Groudon and Kyogre. They'll have undergone Primal Reversion. And I think we'll face Rayquaza as well.

Chapter 712: Groudon: You're All Right

Team Aqua's members fled in disorder. Not only their speedboats but also both organizations' submarines had been caught in the blast and sunk. Each side had suffered a severe loss. Most Team Aqua members could still ride their Water-type Pokemon and swim well enough to avoid drowning.

Ethan could spare them no attention. He watched Groudon and Kyogre. The orbs were gone, but Maxie and Archie had disappeared too. At least no one was left nearby to interfere with what he had to do.

What I said about the orbs is for later, he told Shelly and Courtney. We can watch for Maxie and Archie when they show up again. Right now, we have to stop Groudon and Kyogre before Rayquaza notices them. They can't keep fighting.

He had reason to worry. Long ago, Rayquaza had stopped a tremendous battle between these two, an event that had helped inspire the Draconid people's reverence for it. Neither Groudon nor Kyogre had undergone Primal Reversion today, so the damage was limited by comparison. But Rayquaza knew their presence. If it sensed them fighting, Ethan doubted it would ignore them.

Shelly agreed. Then this is yours to handle. We can't help much. You've kept Deoxys back all this time for exactly this moment, haven't you?

Her voice was teasing, but she was right. Deoxys had rested through the earlier fighting so it could act unexpectedly when it mattered. Ethan still wanted a better opening before sending it in.

He asked Dragonite to lift off from the water. He, Shelly, and Courtney climbed onto its back. Once they were safely in the air some distance from the island, Ethan took out Deoxys's Ultra Ball and waited.

Dragonite was strong, but carrying three adults made it less nimble. That weight had helped the blast wave throw it into the sea. Holding them aloft at a steady pace was no problem, though. It circled the broken island a few hundred meters up.

Groudon and Kyogre charged each other again. Their wounds and breathing showed that the earlier battle had cost them something, but not much. Left alone, they might fight through the night and into morning without settling anything.

As they collided, Ethan opened the Ultra Ball. Deoxys appeared in the air.

Its psychic senses had followed events even while it was inside the ball. It immediately looked toward the two ancient Pokemon.

See the blue one? Ethan said, nodding toward Kyogre. Focus on it. Help Groudon put it down.

Deoxys turned its head toward him. Courtney, seated in front of Ethan, looked back too. Shelly spoke from behind him. What did Kyogre do to you? I thought you wanted to stop the fight. Why help Groudon?

The easiest way to end a fight isn't to knock them both down, Ethan said. That would take too much effort and might make both of them attack us. Help one beat the other, and the fight ends.

Then why not help Kyogre? Shelly asked. It's a Water type and Groudon is a Ground type. Kyogre already has the advantage.

She did not say that, as a former Team Aqua member, she still felt closer to Kyogre. Courtney likely felt the same attachment to Groudon. Shelly would not press the point in front of her.

Ethan sighed theatrically. I thought you were clever.

What did you say? Shelly's eyebrows rose.

We're in the middle of the sea. Kyogre is called the embodiment of the ocean. If Groudon falls and Kyogre turns on us, it can control the water all around us. That's dangerous. We take Kyogre down first. And there's something more important.

He paused until both women were listening, then smiled. Groudon can't fly.

Shelly blinked. So?

If Kyogre loses and swims away, Groudon can't catch it. Then we leave too. Groudon can rage all it likes, but there'll be nobody left to fight. The battle is over.

Shelly had not expected that answer. It felt odd, yet she could not find a flaw in it. All right. That makes some sense. Groudon ought to thank you.

Below them, the two Pokemon exchanged several more blows. Ethan turned to Deoxys. Attack Forme.

Deoxys changed at once. Its body narrowed, four tentacle-like arms took shape, and three sharp points rose from its head. Without another order, it dived toward Kyogre.

The distance was six or seven hundred meters, but Deoxys crossed it in moments. Energy gathered as it flew. At close range, it fired into Kyogre's back.

Kyogre cried out in pain. Only after the blow did it realize it had been ambushed. Groudon noticed Deoxys at the same moment.

Deoxys had arrived quietly from a Poke Ball, without the earthquakes or tidal waves that announced its opponents. It had kept its distance until the dive, moved fast, and struck while they were occupied with each other. The attack caught Kyogre completely off guard.

Kyogre spun its great body toward the attacker. Deoxys was already watching for a counterattack and slipped aside. It followed with Psychic, striking Kyogre again. A target that large was difficult to miss.

Kyogre realized a simple charge would not catch such an agile opponent and began gathering power for a wider attack. Groudon saw its rival's exposed back and struck with a heavy claw. Kyogre fell from the air onto the water. The power it had gathered scattered before it could use it.

Groudon and Kyogre drew on immense internal energy, but they did not think of combat in the fixed names of moves that Trainers used. Instinct drove them to split earth, change weather, and release power in whatever form the moment demanded. People unfamiliar with them could seldom predict an attack by waiting for a named move.

Shelly and Courtney recognized some of what they saw. Other attacks were unlike anything they knew. They might have understood the difference better after watching Gengar fight with its playful, improvised methods.

Deoxys was an extraterrestrial Pokemon and did not rely on a fixed list of moves either. The energy sphere and barrier it had used before came from its free control of its power. Legendary Pokemon differed from ordinary Pokemon that lived among humans in mind as well as in body.

Before Kyogre could rise, Deoxys closed in again. Groudon suddenly attacked Deoxys instead. It dodged, but lost its chance to strike Kyogre. It remembered Ethan's order and did not retaliate against Groudon. It changed position and continued attacking Kyogre from an angle Groudon could not reach.

Kyogre was exasperated. Deoxys was not even half its size, yet it darted all around, hit hard, and evaded every blow. Groudon remained ready to attack from the other side. Kyogre could not deal with both at once. Why did this new Pokemon attack only Kyogre and show no interest in Groudon?

After a few minutes, frustration won. Kyogre roared, plunged into the sea, and swam away. A battle that might have continued until both ancient Pokemon were exhausted ended abruptly.

Groudon looked almost baffled. It wanted to pursue, but could never match Kyogre's swimming speed. It roared and turned toward Deoxys. Deoxys floated above it, stared coldly for a moment, then flew away too.

Groudon roared after the retreating figure. Deoxys did not turn back.

...

High in the sky, Ethan felt that Deoxys still wanted to fight when it returned to Dragonite's side. He looked down at the furious Groudon below.

Not satisfied? Do you want another round with it?

Deoxys made a sound Ethan could not interpret, but its meaning was clear enough. That brief clash had been little more than a warm-up. It had left only because Ethan asked. A Pokemon that had once challenged Rayquaza and gained the upper hand would recognize the strength of both Groudon and Kyogre.

Don't worry, Ethan said. We're leaving now so we can meet again. Next time, you'll get all the fighting you want.

Chapter 713: Time to Find Help

Night had fallen by the time Dragonite carried Ethan, Shelly, and Courtney down to an unfamiliar stretch of the Hoenn coast.

They had left the island after Kyogre's departure. More than an hour of flying had finally brought them back to the mainland.

Shelly jumped off first. Once Ethan and Courtney had climbed down, Ethan patted his panting Pokemon. Well done. You really worked hard today.

The journey had exhausted Dragonite. It had fought at Mt. Pyre, carried them to Team Magma's base, then flown them from the base to the island for another battle. Afterward, it had brought them back to shore. Between the fighting and the travel, it had barely had a chance to rest. Even Dragonite's stamina had its limits.

They had little choice. Team Magma's and Team Aqua's submarines had sunk, and the force of Precipice Blades and Origin Pulse had destroyed Shelly's submarine as well. Dragonite was their only way back to land.

It gave Ethan a broad, cheerful smile and a thumbs-up. Tired as it was, it was happy to have helped its Trainer.

Shelly dropped onto a nearby rock, rubbed her numb backside, and asked, What do we do now?

They had calmed this crisis, but she knew what Ethan had said was true. As long as Maxie and Archie remained free, their ambitions for the two ancient Legendary Pokemon would never disappear.

Ethan looked at the two women and thought for a moment. We need to watch their movements closely. Kyogre and Groudon are secondary. The real danger comes from Archie and Maxie. If we know what either of them plans to do next, we can step in before things get worse.

That's easier said than done. Shelly sighed. There are only three of us. We can't watch them across the whole sea.

Courtney lowered her head in silence, apparently considering the problem too.

It isn't as complicated as you think, Ethan said. Groudon and Kyogre might be hard to find, but we don't need to follow them. We only need to keep an eye on Maxie and Archie.

Shelly's expression turned thoughtful. She seemed to see where he was going. You mean...?

I think they're probably safe, and I expect the orbs will end up in their hands again, Ethan explained. So we prepare for the worst. Even with an orb, neither man can control and catch Groudon or Kyogre on his own. They'll need a lot of people. Watch the bases around here for sudden movements of personnel, and we should be able to find them.

That would save us some effort. Shelly's eyes brightened. We could work out their general plans by tracking their members. If we get detailed enough reports, we might even know every move Maxie and Archie make next.

She looked at Ethan with a small smile. You're quick, aren't you? You came up with that almost at once.

Courtney gazed at him just as intently.

Most people would still be celebrating. Ethan had thwarted Maxie's plot and driven off Kyogre. Even if he didn't boast about it, surely he deserved to feel pleased for a while.

Instead, he was already thinking ahead, frowning over the worst outcome and making plans to counter his opponents' next move. No wonder he had come so far. Few Trainers could match that composure.

Of course, Courtney was seeing him through a generous filter.

Was Ethan really that extraordinary? Perhaps he was, perhaps he wasn't. He had certainly dealt with more difficult incidents on his journey than most people encountered in a lifetime.

But ever since the exchange incident, Courtney had come completely over to his side. She admired him so much that she instinctively imagined him in an even better light.

That was what a filter could do. Ethan had no idea what she was thinking. Her gaze merely seemed familiar, as though he had seen someone look at him that way before.

Facing the women's very different expressions, he said seriously, I'll have to leave the next part to you two.

Shelly understood at once and laughed. So you want us to do the watching?

Yes. You're the only ones suited to it. Ethan sighed. No one knows Team Aqua and Team Magma better than you do. You must know which of their bases are hidden nearby.

Of course. Shelly nodded proudly. I remember all Team Aqua's secrets and deployments. I only left a few days ago. Even if they wanted to relocate, they couldn't do it overnight. Finding the nearest secret base will be easy.

Time was a strange thing. Shelly's resistance and pain had gradually given way to acceptance, changing how she thought and felt. People said time was the best medicine: eventually, even a deep hurt could ease.

She had plainly accepted her new identity and life. She still thought about Team Aqua now and then, but she saw herself as an outsider and could speak of it with some detachment.

Ethan nodded to Shelly and turned to Courtney. She nodded back without hesitation.

The same goes for me. A lot of Team Magma's members don't even know I've left. If I'm careful, I could turn some of them and make them my eyes inside the organization.

I can do that too, Shelly said before Ethan could answer. She glanced at Courtney. Plenty of my old followers are still in Team Aqua. If I ask, I'm sure they'll quietly watch for Archie.

Though Ethan's intervention had brought both women out of their organizations and made them teammates, they were still wary of each other. They had fought for years before he came along. Such hostility would not vanish in a few days.

Only Ethan standing between them kept the peace. Without him, they would probably go their separate ways in no time.

He sighed inwardly. Then it's settled. Each of you find people you can bring around. They don't have to leave their organizations. They only need to watch Maxie and Archie. Let me know as soon as you hear anything.

Understood, Shelly said. We're both doing as you ask. What will you be doing?

Me? Ethan shook his head. Saving the world is just a hobby. Challenging Gyms and the League is my real job. I'm going to keep traveling, of course.

How leisurely. Shelly folded her arms and rolled her eyes. At this rate, we'll end up working for you.

If that's how you see it, I can't stop you. Ethan gave her a long look, then smiled. You're free to give up. You can let Archie control Kyogre and put the whole world at risk.

Shelly opened her mouth but said nothing. She turned away rather than meet his eyes.

When he saw she had yielded, Ethan spoke frankly. Don't worry. My next task won't be easy either. I'm still a little short of the strength needed to stop Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre, and I might have to face Rayquaza too. Deoxys is the only one of my Pokemon that could fight at that level, and even then there's a lot of uncertainty. So I'm going to find help.

Oh? Courtney's interest stirred. Who are you going to ask? Have you found another Pokemon you want to catch?

Shelly stole a glance at him.

There are two, Ethan said openly. One is very powerful and promised to help if I ever ran into trouble. Unfortunately, it's all the way over in Kanto. There isn't time to make the trip.

Anyone who knew Ethan well would understand whom he meant. But as he said, going to Kanto and back would take too long.

And the other? Courtney asked.

Ethan raised his eyes to the star-filled sky and sighed. For the other, I'll have to go to Sky Pillar and see if there's even the slightest chance.

Sky Pillar? Courtney paused before remembering what the place was. The top of Sky Pillar was said to be Rayquaza's home.

But...

You know where Sky Pillar is? Shelly asked. As far as I know, it's only a legend. People have talked about it for years, but no one has ever found its location.

Ethan shrugged. I'll have to ask the Draconid people. They've always guarded that place, and as it happens, I have a small connection with one of them.

...

Under the stars, Ethan made his way toward Lilycove City alone. He would meet Misty there before setting out to look for Sky Pillar.

After their short rest, Shelly and Courtney had gone to carry out their assignments. If things went well, word of Archie and Maxie would reach him soon.

The sea breeze brushed against him, and he pulled his clothes tighter. After everything that had happened, he was hungry and tired.

To be honest, he had not traveled alone for a long time. He found himself missing the feeling.

Fortunately, they had landed close to Lilycove. He did not need to call on Dragonite again. Half an hour on foot brought the lights of the great city into view.

At nine that night, Ethan finally pushed open the doors of the Lilycove Pokemon Center.

Misty and Phoebe had heard he was coming and were waiting anxiously in the dining area. Both stood when they saw him.

To Ethan's surprise, Ash, May, Brock, and Max were there too.

Ethan! You're finally back! Misty hurried over. Up close, she saw how disheveled he was. His clothes were creased and his hair was a mess. He must have been through a great deal.

She went straight to his side, patiently straightened his clothes, and picked a tiny shell off his back.

Ethan patted her head, nodded to Phoebe, who looked as if she wanted to say something, then turned to Ash and the others. What are you doing here?

Ash scratched his head. We came with May for the Lilycove Contest. We ran into Misty, and she told us what happened. How did it go, Ethan?

Let me sit down first. Ethan sank onto a dining-room sofa and leaned back. Only then did he realize how thoroughly worn out he was; even his bones seemed ready to fall apart. The others were the only people left in the dining area. Is there anything to eat? I'm starving.

I'll ask Nurse Joy to make you dinner!

Misty hurried to the counter. She was so attentive that anyone who did not know them might have mistaken her for his girlfriend or little sister.

Ethan nodded and took a sip of the warm water May handed him. After soothing his dry throat, he told them what had happened since he left Mt. Pyre.

He left Shelly and Courtney out of it. He said only that Team Aqua had attacked while he was pursuing Maxie, that Groudon and Kyogre had then fought, and that both orbs had been lost in the battle.

Although she had prepared herself for bad news, Phoebe sighed when she heard it.

Chapter 714: Provoking Zinnia

I see...

Phoebe did not blame Ethan. One look at him told her he had done everything he could. If there was anyone to blame, it was herself. She had acted rashly, fallen for Maxie's trick, and set all the trouble that followed in motion.

She stood and bowed slightly to him. Thank you for everything you've done. Since things have turned out this way, there's no reason for me to stay. I'll be going.

Her bow did not come from a member of the Elite Four. It came from a granddaughter and a friend, genuinely grateful for his help.

Ethan thought more highly of her for it. His opinion of her improved again. It was no wonder she had become one of the Elite Four at her age. Apart from her occasional impulsiveness, he could find little fault with her character.

You're leaving? Misty had just returned with a tray and heard Phoebe's words. Now? It's late. Won't you stay the night?

Phoebe smiled as if the darkness outside did not concern her. It's all right. I'm used to traveling at night, and Ghost-type Pokemon like the nighttime best.

All right. Misty could tell she had made up her mind and did not press her. Where will you go?

She had known the girl her own age only a short time. But they had fought together, extinguished the fire on Mt. Pyre, and traveled to Lilycove side by side. They were hardly close friends, yet they could speak to each other as friends.

The orbs were stolen, Phoebe said without hesitation, but I still have to take my grandparents back to the mountain and help rebuild their home. They've lived there all their lives. Whether or not they need to guard the orbs, it's their home.

Misty set Ethan's tray before him and hugged Phoebe.

I hope we meet again someday.

So do I.

Ash and the others could only watch awkwardly. They barely knew Phoebe and had hardly spoken to her. After the two girls embraced, they joined Ethan and Misty in seeing her out.

When they returned to the dining area, the absence of a stranger made the atmosphere noticeably more relaxed.

Ash could not wait to tell Ethan what had happened on their travels. Ethan ate, nodding from time to time.

They had indeed come to Lilycove for May's Pokemon Contest, as Ash had said. It had ended that afternoon. May had won the Lilycove Contest and earned her third Ribbon.

Your third Ribbon already? Ethan stared at May in surprise. She was improving faster than he had expected.

May smiled shyly. Yes. After losing my first Contest in Slateport, I entered the Fallarbor, Verdanturf, Rubello, and Lilycove Contests. I was eliminated at Rubello, but I won the other three and got their Ribbons.

Congratulations. You're getting closer to becoming a top Pokemon Coordinator. Two more Ribbons and you can enter the Hoenn Grand Festival! It's a shame I arrived too late. I would have liked to see your performance at the Lilycove Contest.

May blushed and waved a hand. I'm working toward it! But don't worry about missing this one. There will be other chances.

She was a little embarrassed to hear a boy say that in front of everyone. And knowing what Ethan had accomplished, she felt recognized by his praise.

Me too! Ask me! Ash broke in, impatient now that May had finished her news. I've got six Badges already!

Six? Ethan raised his eyebrows. It was a little surprising, but it made sense. That's as many as I have. Where are you headed next?

Ash's journey did not involve taking on whole organizations as often as Ethan's, but it had plenty of surprises of its own. Somehow, Ash could find the right path even after arriving in the wrong place. He was earning Badges quickly.

I'm going to Mossdeep City to challenge the Mossdeep Gym, Ash said. What about you, Ethan?

Ethan shook his head. There's something important I need to do first. Besides, my next challenge is the Fortree Gym. Once I've finished there, I can head to Mossdeep.

We still can't travel together? Ash looked disappointed. That's too bad. I thought that if we went to Mossdeep together, we could stop by LaRousse City on the way.

LaRousse City?

The name was unfamiliar to Ethan. What sort of place is that? Is there something special about it?

Ash blinked. You haven't heard of it? It's...

He had barely begun to explain when Max interrupted him.

LaRousse City is famous! Max said, puffing out his chest. They call it the city of technology. It has moving walkways, block-shaped robots, a huge park, and busy shopping districts. Best of all, there's a Battle Tower where Trainers can battle!

Ash stood with his mouth open, awkwardly deprived of his explanation.

Max glanced at him and delivered one more blow. And Ash only heard about it this afternoon. The moment he found out about the Battle Tower, he wouldn't stop saying he wanted to see it.

With Max around, Ash could not keep even that small secret, much less show off his knowledge.

Come on, Ash complained. Couldn't you let me impress Ethan for once?

Max pushed up his glasses, unmoved. I was just stating the facts.

Their familiar bickering made everyone smile.

Amid the laughter, Ethan swallowed his food and thought about the city. Its name meant nothing to him, but the block-shaped robots and moving walkways suddenly rang a bell.

Wasn't that the city from the Deoxys movie? And speaking of Deoxys...

He had recently promised his own Deoxys that it could meet others of its kind during their travels. This might be his chance.

Is the city far from here? he asked.

Ash and Max looked startled by the sudden question. Brock took out a map, checked the location, and shook his head. Not very far. It's close to Lilycove, at the fork in the river on the peninsula to the southeast. Do you want to go?

Misty looked at Ethan with bright eyes. Max's description had interested her, and if they went with Ash's group, she could spend more time with May. May seemed to have the same thought; she watched Ethan hopefully.

He considered it for a while before answering. I can't decide yet. Let me make a call first.

A call? Ash and the others looked at one another. Did Ethan need someone else's permission to choose where he went? Whose?

Ethan rose, moved to a quiet corner, and called Zinnia. He did not need anyone's permission, of course. His plan had been to find her and ask her to take him to Sky Pillar.

But Ash and the others had given him another idea. He still intended to visit Sky Pillar. Could he make a trip to LaRousse City first?

Deoxys had traveled through space alone for so long that it longed for others of its kind. Perhaps his Deoxys could persuade the two Deoxys in LaRousse to help in the coming battle. Even if they were hard to approach or unwilling to help, letting his companion meet them would fulfill one of its wishes.

From that point of view, even a fruitless trip would be worthwhile.

To save time, however, Zinnia would have to come to him. He had no idea whether a phone call could persuade her to cross half of Hoenn. It was worth a try.

The phone rang for a while before she answered. Her voice was low. She did not sound sleepy, only dejected. Rayquaza's escape had clearly shaken her, and she still had not recovered.

Ethan came straight to the point and told her what he wanted. As he might have expected, she immediately refused when she heard he wanted to visit Sky Pillar.

I can't help you with that, Zinnia said firmly. The Draconid people have guarded Sky Pillar for generations. Only we and a few others who have been granted permission may enter. An outsider like you cannot go in.

Ethan told her about Groudon and Kyogre. She still refused. I'm sorry. I really can't take you there.

How stubborn could she be? Even an appeal to Hoenn's safety would not move her. Ethan thought for a moment and decided to provoke her.

Even if you won't tell me, I know where Sky Pillar is.

You know where it is? Zinnia laughed at the other end of the call.

She did not believe him. Few people had even heard the name Sky Pillar. Apart from the Draconid people and a handful of others, most knew nothing about it.

People with a particular interest in Groudon and Kyogre, such as Team Magma and Team Aqua, might find the name in old documents and learn that the tower was more than a legend. That was about as far as their knowledge went.

Ethan knowing the name did not surprise her. Claiming to know the exact location was nonsense. He must be trying to trick her into revealing it. Yes, that had to be it.

Then his next words made her eyes widen.

Sky Pillar is hidden on an uninhabited island near Sootopolis City.

Zinnia's heart pounded. She forced herself to stay calm. You've guessed wrong. It isn't there.

Ethan chuckled. It isn't? You don't have to hide it. I've actually been there before.

That part was true. Ethan had visited Sky Pillaronly in a game.

It was in the waters near the island that held Sootopolis City, just as he had said. In the game, he could follow a fixed route to the tower. This was the real world. Finding one empty island among the hundreds or thousands nearby would be far harder.

How did you...? Zinnia's voice rose before she caught herself. Hmph. Even if you've been there, it won't help. A barrier protects Sky Pillar. You couldn't possibly...

You mean the barrier the people of Sootopolis established and maintain? Ethan interrupted.

Damn it! He even knew about that? How was that possible? Had someone from Sootopolis told him?

The thought came to Zinnia at once. Who told you? she demanded.

Her sudden change in tone told Ethan his provocation had worked. He laughed softly. I already told you. I've been there. I found all this out myself.

Chapter 715: The City of Technology

The people of Sootopolis whom Zinnia and Ethan had mentioned were not the city's ordinary residents. They were the people who had lived in seclusion there before Sootopolis existed and had made a pact with the Draconid people.

Like the Draconids, they were guardians whose traditions had survived since ancient times, hidden from the wider world. The two groups existed alongside each other and protected the secrets of Rayquaza together.

There was one difference: the Draconids revered Rayquaza and wished to capture it, while the people of Sootopolis guarded the barrier.

Outsiders knew even less about the people of Sootopolis than they did about the Draconids. They were more mysterious still.

The only one Ethan knew by name was the Water Prince himself, Wallace. Very few people could know about that side of him. Perhaps even his niece Lisia had no idea.

If Ethan had not learned it from the games, how could he have guessed that a man who attracted attention everywhere he went was secretly a guardian?

Before Zinnia could recover from her surprise, he went on. That's not all I know. I even know what the top of Sky Pillar is called: the Dragonhark altar.

That put an end to Zinnia's suspicion that he was trying to draw information out of her. He knew far too much for an outsider. And she was certain the people of Sootopolis had not told him.

They only tended the barrier. They had never entered Sky Pillar and would not know about the Dragonhark altar inside it.

Then who had told him? Had he really been there?

Zinnia fell silent. After a while, Ethan asked, Do you believe me now?

She took a deep breath and forced herself to calm down. What exactly do you want?

What I said before. Ethan's tone did not change. I wanted to work with you and ask you to help me find Rayquaza. Clearly, that was wishful thinking. So I'll have to go to the top of the tower myself, find Rayquaza, and catch it.

Distraught, Zinnia missed the flaw in his claim. If reaching Sky Pillar were that easy for him, why had he gone to the trouble of calling her? She never thought to ask.
