That's impossible, she said grimly. Reaching the Dragonhark altar doesn't mean you'll see Rayquaza. It only answers the call of the Rainbow Meteorite, and that meteorite was lost long ago. You'll have made the trip for nothing.

She was right about the missing meteorite. Without it, even the Draconids could not summon Rayquaza from the altar. That was why, when Ethan caught Deoxys, Zinnia had tried so desperately to get close to Rayquaza. It might have been her only chance to see it.

Maybe, Ethan said lightly. Perhaps your people need the Rainbow Meteorite to see Rayquaza. But you're forgetting that I have Deoxys.

Zinnia understood at once. Calling Rayquaza was not the only way to see it. They could attract its attention. A Pokemon as powerful as Deoxys could surely do that, especially so close to Rayquaza at Sky Pillar.

Ethan's bluff began to shake her resolve. She did not want an outsider to enter Sky Pillar. Yet if Deoxys drew Rayquaza down to the Dragonhark altar, she might see it again. She could not miss such a chance.

I understand. Zinnia finally gave in. Where are you? I'll come to you.

A smile of triumph crept onto Ethan's face, though his voice remained steady. I'm in Lilycove City. How long will it take you to get here?

She considered it. I'm quite far away. I can't leave until tomorrow morning, and even then it'll take at least three days.

Three days. Ethan nodded. That was more than enough time for a round trip to LaRousse City.

All right. We'll meet in Lilycove in three days.

He ended the call and returned to Ash and the others. They were all looking at him. He nodded to them.

Looks like I have two days to relax after all.

...

Morning sunlight reached into the boys' dormitory at the Pokemon Center, and Ethan opened his eyes. He had not wanted to wake yet. Noise had done it for him.

The clock on the wall showed a little after six. The source of the racket was, predictably, Ash. He and Max were arguing about something, and Ash's loud voice carried across the room.

Ethan sighed. Children were children in any world. How could they have this much energy so early?

It reminded him of his first school outing when he was young. He had probably been just as excited.

He stared at the ceiling, his mind drifting to memories of Earth. He found himself missing home.

After a few more minutes in bed, he pulled himself up, dressed, washed, and went to join the others in the dining area. He had slept for more than eight hours, but he still felt drained.

Everyone else was ready. Their luggage sat at their feet, and they could leave at any moment.

You're so slow, Ethan! Misty, sitting beside May, made a face at him. Whenever we all stay at a Pokemon Center, you're the last to get up.

Ethan yawned widely, ignored her, and sat down to eat breakfast.

At least there was good news about the trip to LaRousse. They would not have to walk a long way. A light rail train ran straight from Lilycove, so he could rest while they traveled. Every bit of strength he recovered might let him last a few more minutes in the coming battle.

He finished breakfast at his own pace while the others watched expectantly without daring to hurry him. At last he picked up his backpack and waved an arm. Let's go!

They left the Pokemon Center and went to the light rail station downtown. The trains had only two cars, but so many visitors seemed to be heading to LaRousse that one departed every ten minutes.

They bought their tickets and boarded. They had barely taken their seats when the train pulled out.

At first they chatted idly. Once the train climbed onto an elevated bridge, everyone fell quiet and looked out the windows.

The broad windows gave them a view over much of Lilycove. From up here the city looked even more prosperous, and the people below were no larger than grains of rice. It was a new way to see the place.

Beyond Lilycove, the train picked up speed. In about half an hour it had passed through thick forest and reached the area around LaRousse.

The city stood on a large island in the middle of a river, with Lilycove behind it and the river mouth not far ahead. Its position made travel easy and had helped the city grow.

Before they reached the island, they could see dozens of wind turbines in the distance, their blades turning without pause. Beyond the rows of turbines rose the technological city.

Strangely shaped high-rises filled the view. A place known as the city of technology surely had industries to match.

Ash and Max pressed their faces against the window, as though they wanted to get off at once for a closer look. Ethan glanced out and turned away. The sight impressed him a little, but he had seen plenty of such things before. It no longer held his attention.

Max's repeated cries of Wow! rang in his ears. He was as noisy as a frog.

When the train finally stopped and the doors opened, Ash and Max rushed out. By the time Ethan and the others stepped onto the platform, the two boys were already on the escalator, almost out of the station.

Misty and May exchanged helpless smiles. Why are they in such a hurry?

Ash had always been like that. Max used to be more sensible, but after traveling with Ash for so long, he seemed to be picking up the same habits. Ash's enthusiasm was contagious.

Ethan and the others followed them down the escalator. Before they could leave the station, a floating Block Bot made of small green blocks approached.

Welcome to LaRousse City!

A smile appeared on its lowest block as a bright voice rang out. While it spoke, the blocks shifted, and the words Welcome appeared on its display.

This city really is high-tech! Max adjusted his glasses. What an amazing robot.

Misty and May nodded. Brock folded his arms and looked faintly disappointed. I'd rather have a pretty young lady welcoming us.

The robot floated closer and extended a camera. It took several photographs of their faces.

May was first. She had not expected to be photographed and flinched in surprise, twisting her face into an awkward expression. The robot captured it.

After photographing everyone, the robot made a few noises and dispensed several passport cards.

These are your city passports. You can use them to shop and travel. Please keep them safe!

Passports? Ash and the others accepted the cards with fresh curiosity. Everyone else's photo looked normal. May's showed her startled, contorted face. Ash and Max immediately laughed at it.

The robot turned and floated off to greet other visitors. May stared at it, then at the passport in her hand.

I want to take the photo again...

It was too late. With a sigh, she followed the others out of the station, where they finally got a proper look at the city.

Even the nearest trash can was electronic. It recognized different kinds of rubbish and opened separate compartments to sort them.

Wow, that's incredible... Max had lost count of how many times he had said something like it.

Ash was no longer paying attention to the trash can. He ran a few steps ahead and looked around. Where's that famous Battle Tower? Why can't I see it?

As he searched the skyline, Ash failed to watch his feet. He stepped onto a moving walkway and was carried away.

Only then did the others notice the walkways running across the ground in every direction. That was how people traveled around LaRousse.

Startled, Ash tried to run back toward Ethan and the others. The walkway moved so quickly that even pumping his arms and legs could not bring him closer. It carried him farther away.

His strange struggle drew attention. Several fashionably dressed girls nearby covered their mouths and giggled. When it came to embarrassing himself, Ash never disappointed.

Ethan was about to help when another group came toward Ash on a neighboring walkway, traveling in the opposite direction.

One boy among them apparently could not bear to watch. He tossed a Poke Ball and released a Blaziken. In a few leaps, it reached Ash, caught him, and lifted him off the walkway.

Whew... I'm saved. Ash wiped the sweat from his brow and looked gratefully at the boy. Thank you so much.

Don't thank me. The boy barely looked at him. With a cool wave of his hand, as if the rescue had been nothing at all, he added, I didn't save you for your sake. I just couldn't stand watching someone act so stupid.

Chapter 716: Ethan: Well, I'll Be!

What did you say?

Ash's gratitude vanished in an instant. He was furious. The boy who had rescued him merely stood with his hands in his pockets and looked back calmly.

A slightly heavyset boy beside him smiled at Ash. It's your first time here, isn't it? I heard you say you wanted to visit the Battle Tower. It isn't that way. Come with us.

He stepped onto a moving walkway going in the other direction.

Ethan took a closer look at the four newcomers.

The boy who had rescued Ash seemed fourteen or fifteen. He wore a gray shirt and trousers that looked rather old-fashioned, and his hair reached past his ears. With his fair skin, fine features, and composed expression, he looked like someone who fought with his head. In that respect, he was Ash's opposite.

The heavyset boy who had spoken was about the same age. He wore a red headband, a black shirt, and shorts, giving him a faintly hip-hop style.

The other two were younger girls dressed alike, and their faces looked nearly identical. Twins? Ethan had not met twins since arriving in this world.

They seemed about Max's age. Both wore tall hats and short skirts, with only the colors of their outfits to distinguish them. Ethan looked again and noticed their bright, innocent smiles.

Finally, he glanced at the first boy's Blaziken. Its coat and physique showed that it had been raised well, and its gaze was sharp. He wondered which was stronger, this one or his own Blaziken.

The four were clearly traveling together, much like Ethan's group.

Once Ash heard that they knew the way to the Battle Tower, he forgot the insult. He followed the twins onto the walkway. Ethan and the others exchanged looks and went after him.

The Battle Tower held little interest for Ethan. It offered battles, and he had more pressing business: finding the Deoxys hidden somewhere in LaRousse. But he had only just arrived and did not know where to look, so for now he followed the group.

Then the Ultra Ball at his waist stirred. His Deoxys had sensed another of its kind nearby. The city's technology filled its streets with electromagnetic fields, however, interfering with Deoxys's senses. It could feel the other's presence only faintly and could not tell which direction it came from.

Easy, Ethan murmured. This isn't the time to let you out. Wait a little longer, and you'll meet them soon.

Deoxys settled down inside its ball.

Ethan stepped onto the walkway at the back of the group. Ahead of him, Ash was already chatting with the boy who had insulted him as if nothing had happened.

That was one of Ash's admirable traits. A small unpleasant exchange passed, and he let it go. Ethan would not have been so forgiving. If someone treated him that way, he would write them off.

Ash looked at Blaziken, then addressed its Trainer. I'm Ash from Pallet Town. Are you going to the Battle Tower too? How about a battle with me?

The twins turned around. They spoke one after the other.

Our brother Rafe is really strong!

And so is his Blaziken!

Rafe turned to Ash and nodded. Ash, was it? Anyone can enter at the Battle Tower. If you challenge me there, I'll take you on.

The heavyset boy spoke up. You can't enter on your own. The Battle Tower holds Double Battles, so you'll need a teammate. Rafe's partner is me. Oh, I forgot to introduce myself. I'm Sid, and my partner Pokemon is Blastoise. It's strong too!

Double Battles? The format caught Ash off guard, but he did not look worried. I only need a teammate? I've got one. He's the best Trainer in the world!

The best Trainer? Sid asked, puzzled. Who?

Ash grinned at the two boys and pushed through the people on the walkway to reach Ethan.

Ethan! His eyes shone as he spoke quietly. Team up with me, okay? If we fight together, nobody will beat us. We could keep winning all day!

Ethan met Rafe's and Sid's gazes and shook his head at once. Ask someone else. I have something to take care of.

What? Ash had never expected him to refuse. They were Trainers at a Battle Tower. Wasn't battling the obvious thing to do? Disappointed but undeterred, he turned to Misty.

Hey, Misty. It's been ages since we battled side by side. Want to team up?

She refused too. I'm busy! May and I already decided to go shopping. You can't come somewhere like this and not look around.

Come on... After two refusals, Ash's face fell. He put his last hope in Brock. Brock, please. Team up with me.

Brock smiled at his pleading look. Have you forgotten? I'm not a Trainer anymore. Besides, there are plenty of beautiful older girls in the stands. How could I pass up the chance to sit with them?

Ash stared. He had asked all three of them, and none would join him. One was a Champion who had won in two regions, another a former Gym Leader, and the third had grown up in a Gym family. How could none of them be interested in a battle?

You guys! he complained. He glanced back at Rafe and Sid in embarrassment. They only smiled and did not seem to mind. Ash turned to his friends again. Just watch. I'll find a teammate without you!

May and Max were there too, but May was a Coordinator, and as for Max... Ash did not bother asking.

Just then the twins called out, We're here!

At the end of the walkway stood a tall, cone-shaped building on a small hill. Its glass exterior glittered in the sunlight and looked as modern as the rest of the city.

The walkway ended at the foot of the hill. They would have to walk the rest of the way.

It was a convenient way to travel, though Ethan did not care for it. He preferred the feel of solid ground under his feet. A short ride was fine; after a long one, his legs felt strange when he stepped off. Misty and May, on the other hand, seemed to like it.

Keep being this lazy, and you'll both turn into little piglets, he thought.

They climbed the winding stairs and entered the Battle Tower.

A spacious lobby greeted them. Elevators stood around its edges, and visitors filled the room. People were everywhere, and not all had come to watch battles.

Despite its name, the Battle Tower was almost a multipurpose center. It had shops, restaurants, a cinema, amusement facilities, and a library. Those were additions to its main attraction: a battle arena large enough for several thousand spectators.

Sid had explained the rules to Ash on the way. The moment they reached the lobby, Ash announced, I'm going to register! and vanished into the crowd.

Rafe and his companions went another way. They had booked their place in advance and could head straight for the arena. That left Ethan's group in the lobby.

Misty and May whispered together, then Misty smiled at the others. There's a while before the matches start. May and I are going to look around and come back for the battles.

I want to see the technology museum, Max said. I wonder what else they have here.

Brock scanned the lobby. Seeing no beautiful women, he shook his head. I'll go to the stands and save us some good seats.

All four looked at Ethan. He waved them on. Go ahead. I'll take a look around too.

Then we'll meet in the stands, Brock said.

They separated. Ethan left the lobby and took an elevator to the highest floor. From there he hoped to survey LaRousse and find where Deoxys was hiding.

His memory of the movie was hazy. He recalled a scientist on an Antarctic expedition finding a fallen meteorite and two Deoxys within it. One had a complete body; only the other's core remained. Rayquaza had descended, fought the complete Deoxys, and defeated it.

The scientist had taken the remaining core to LaRousse and spent years trying to revive it. Eventually the Deoxys Rayquaza had defeated came to the city in search of its companion. Its arrival caused an uproar and led to another battle with Rayquaza.

In a way, that would be a chance to catch Rayquaza without visiting Sky Pillar. But Ethan did not want an ordinary Rayquaza. He clearly remembered a Shiny black one at Sky Pillar.

He could not be sure he would meet it. Still, it was a chance to catch a Shiny Pokemon, something he had long dreamed of. Even if the odds were tiny, he had to try.

The elevator reached the top floor. Ethan stepped out and immediately spotted someone both familiar and unfamiliar.

He knew the boy from his appearances in the anime. In this world, however, they had met only once, and that meeting had not gone well.

Green hair, hands in his pockets, that same cool, cocky air. Ethan glanced at him, looked away, and started to walk past.

He had gone only a few steps when the boy turned and called after him. What are you doing here?

Ethan stopped and looked back, surprised that the boy had spoken to him at all.

It was Drew, the gifted Coordinator he had met once in Slateport City.

Instead of answering, Ethan asked, I could ask you the same thing. Why are you here?

What's so strange about that? Drew smiled faintly. I'm from this city. LaRousse is my home.

Ethan had not known that Drew came from LaRousse. Drew glanced to either side of him, found no one else there, and hesitated before asking, Where's the girl who's always with you?

May came to Ethan's mind. In the anime, she and Drew had begun as rivals. As they met more often, their relationship had softened. He had started paying attention to her, encouraging and helping her, even if he still pointed out her faults in his usual cold tone. Some viewers had thought they made a good pair.

Ethan gave a private, humorless laugh. Had Drew already fallen for her? Was he asking Ethan where May was?

He was about to tease the aloof boy when something felt wrong.

Wait. At the Pokemon Center yesterday, Ash and the others had said May had met Drew several times at Contests since Ethan last saw him. Drew must know May did not travel with Ethan.

So why ask him where she was?

Unless...

Ethan suddenly understood. Drew was not asking about May. He meant Misty!

But why? Had one slap from her during their last meeting left him unable to forget her?

Chapter 717: No Coordination

Ethan stared at Drew in astonishment. For a moment, he wondered if the boy actually enjoyed being hurt.

Had Misty's slap awakened some hidden side of him? Or was this going to turn into one of those ridiculous romances where a spoiled rich boy fell for the fierce girl who put him in his place?

Ethan raised an eyebrow to test his guess. You mean Misty?

Drew seemed to notice the look in his eyes. An awkward expression crossed his face. Of course I mean her. She slapped me last time. You think I'll let that go? I'm going to pay her back.

It was a plausible reason, yet it sounded to Ethan like an excuse. Once suspicion had taken root, it grew quickly. The more Drew explained, the more unusual his behavior seemed.

Give it up, Ethan said, watching him closely. Even if you see her again, I doubt you'll do anything to her. And some things... simply aren't going to happen.

The words carried two meanings. Drew's face changed. He was no fool; Ethan seemed to have guessed what was on his mind.

But how could he? Only in the past few days had Drew noticed that, night after night, he thought about the slap. Misty's face and every movement came back to him vividly. He was not even sure what those thoughts meant. How had Ethan seen through him?

Unwilling to talk any longer, Drew turned and entered the elevator without another word. Ethan watched until its doors closed.

He often said he thought of Misty as a little sister, but he knew he could be selfish. As long as they remained this close and their journey together continued, he would give no one else an opening, even if Misty herself had no interest in Drew.

Ethan shook off the thought and went to the floor-to-ceiling window. This was LaRousse's highest point. Most of the city spread out beneath him.

The city of technology had been laid out carefully. Residential, commercial, and office buildings were easy to tell apart. He scanned it several times but still could not pick out the research laboratory.

Where was the Deoxys core being kept?

He looked toward the far side of the island. A thick forest divided the city in two. He could make out the outline of the buildings beyond it, but not enough detail to identify them. Was the lab on the other side?

As he considered it, a voice message arrived from Misty. Ash's match was about to start.

Already? Ash must have found a teammate quickly. Since Ethan had made no progress with his search, he left the window and took the elevator down to the arena floor.

The battle arena occupied the broad middle section of the tower. Its circular field resembled a red-and-blue Poke Ball, with rings of spectator seats surrounding it.

The announcer was warming up the crowd when Ethan entered. His excited voice drew cheers from the stands.

Several matches took place here every day. As soon as enough competitors were ready, another battle could begin. Admission was free. A spectator could sit from morning until night and watch for as long as Trainers kept coming.

Ethan found the seat number Misty had sent. Brock's early arrival had paid off: he had secured places with an excellent view. They were neither too high nor too low, too close nor too far. Ethan could see the whole field without relying on the large screens overhead.

Misty, May, and Max were back, and the twins who had accompanied Rafe and Sid were sitting beside them.

When Misty noticed Ethan looking at the girls, she smiled. You don't know their names yet, do you? This is Audrey and this is Kathryn. Audrey, in orange, is the older sister. Kathryn, in pink, is the younger. They look alike, don't they?

Nice to meet you. I'm Ethan. He nodded to both girls and sat beside Misty. Then he told the group about seeing Drew.

Drew lives in LaRousse? May said in surprise. The others were taken aback too, but they soon turned their attention to the arena again.

It had all the flair of a high-tech city. Even the announcer, who also served as referee, flew around the arena on a small aircraft. Whatever the quality of the matches, the spectacle already outshone many other venueseven the Indigo and Silver Conferences.

Was that the appeal of a city built around technology?

The Battle Tower was also independent of the Pokemon League. Like the Whirl Cup, it was not run by the League or subject to its direction. LaRousse's wealth had equipped the arena with facilities many League competitions would envy.

Click. The lights over the stands went out, telling the audience the match was about to begin.

Our first match today is a team battle! the announcer called from above the field. Let's welcome both sides!

Under the spotlights, the floor opened and two platforms rose. On the red side stood Rafe and Sid. Opposite them were Ash and a handsome little boy who looked only seven or eight.

That's Ash's teammate? Misty blurted out. He's just a kid! He looks about Max's age.

What's wrong with that? Max adjusted his glasses and glanced at her. Kids can be strong. Ash chose him, so there must be something special about him. Just watch!

Oh? I'll be watching, then, Misty said with a smile.

If anyone could get the better of Max in an argument, it was Misty. He seemed a little afraid of her fierceness and did not talk back to her as freely as he did to Ash.

Ethan said nothing. He stroked his chin and studied the boy. Leave it to Ash to find the person at the heart of the story so quickly. His luck was remarkable.

The competitors' details appeared on a screen, and the announcer introduced them. On the red side are Rafe and Sid from a southern city! They've won several matches together and are a formidable pair. On the blue side are two first-time competitors today: Ash and our local LaRousse boy, Tory!

As usual, the announcer explained the rules. Each competitor sends out one Pokemon. Partners fight together until both Pokemon on one side are defeated. Now, please send out your Pokemon!

Matches here moved quickly. There were many entrants, and one pair could take the field as soon as another had finished. No screening trials or preliminaries stood in their way. If two people teamed up and were willing to battle, they would have an audience.

Skill levels varied, but the brisk pace and lack of delays made the matches exciting to watch.

Rafe and Sid released their Pokemon together: the Blaziken Ethan had seen earlier and the Blastoise Sid had mentioned.

Ash sent out Pikachu. Tory, however, made no move to release a Pokemon.

After more than ten seconds, the crowd began whispering. Even the announcer sounded puzzled. It seems Tory isn't sending out a Pokemon. Has something happened?

Max stared. What's going on? Why won't he send one out?

Brock frowned. Maybe he doesn't have a Pokemon.

He doesn't? Max echoed.

It sounded strange in a world where people and Pokemon lived so closely together. Even so, many people never owned a Pokemon, for all kinds of reasons. Could Tory be one of them? If so, why had he entered a battle?

Misty glanced at Max and teased him without mercy. So that's what makes Ash's teammate special. You were righthe's making quite an impression.

Max's face turned red. He stared at the boy, unable to understand why Ash had brought him onto the field.

Ash was talking to Tory, but they were too far away for Ethan's group to hear over the crowd.

When no second Pokemon appeared, the referee was nearly ready to declare a forfeit. At the last moment, Ash took out another of his own Poke Balls and handed it to Tory.

Tory hesitated, then opened it. Ash's Torkoal emerged.

It seemed to stretch the rule that each competitor use one Pokemon when Ash had supplied both. Still, they had avoided immediate disqualification, and the announcer, eager to get the match going, declared the start.

The spectators focused on the field. Rafe and Sid struck first, directing Blaziken and Blastoise into an attack.

Their teamwork was excellent. Blaziken leaped in and broke up Pikachu and Torkoal's formation. As Pikachu dodged, Blastoise caught it with Hydro Pump.

Blastoise followed with Bubble against Torkoal, then used Rapid Spin to knock it into the air. The first exchange had already cost Ash dearly.

No wonder Rafe and Sid had won so many matches. They were good.

Ash was no beginner now. He still had his mishaps, but after traveling through two regions he had become a regular contender for at least the top sixteen at major tournaments. If he was struggling this early, his opponents were capable Trainers.

Of course, he and Tory had no teamwork at all.

Ash tried to turn the match around, but Pikachu could not fight alone. Tory stood like a bystander, giving Torkoal no commands.

Even Max could see the problem. Why is he just standing there? Does he really know nothing about battling?

Misty stopped teasing him. She looked worriedly at Ethan. Is Ash going to lose?

Probably, Ethan said with a helpless shake of his head. Unless he changes what's happening, it's only a matter of time.

Ash directed Pikachu in a counterattack, but Torkoal, without guidance, sent out a burst of flame that hit Pikachu's tail instead of their opponents.

The crowd booed. They wanted a fast match, but not one where a team could not work together at all.

Ash finally took charge of both Pokemon himself. One Trainer could hardly match the attention of two, though, especially against Pokemon as strong as Blaziken and Blastoise.

He held on a little longer. Then Blaziken used Overheat. Its fierce flames struck Pikachu and Torkoal together, knocking both out.

May covered her mouth. They really lost...

Before the match, she and Misty had joked that Ash might be eliminated immediately. May had not expected a defeat this lopsided. He had barely managed a proper counterattack.

Pikachu and Torkoal are unable to battle! Rafe and Sid on the red side win! the announcer declared.

The one-sided match had not satisfied the crowd, but they still gave the winners a hearty round of cheers and applause.

Below, Ash gathered Pikachu and Torkoal into his arms. He looked dejected as the platform carried him and Tory back underground.

Ethan sighed and stood. The match is over. Let's go see them.

Ash had come here full of anticipation, only to lose badly within minutes. Instead of showing what he could do on this stage, he had fought an embarrassing match. Most people would be shaken. Fortunately, Ash was Ash. He would probably recover from the disappointment without anyone comforting him.

Chapter 718: Close Encounter of the Third Kind

Ethan and the others did not stay for the next match. They rose from their seats in the dark and left the arena through the passageway.

By the time they reached the competitors' side, they could see two people standing with Ash and Tory: a middle-aged man whose hair was the same color as Tory's, dressed in a neat, formal suit, and a pretty young woman.

As Ethan's group drew near, the man spoke to Tory with a note of excitement. Tory, you've finally decided to take part in a Pokemon battle?

Tory glanced at Ash and lowered his head. No... I only ended up there because of a misunderstanding!

He clenched his fists and ran away.

Ethan and the others reached Ash just as the man sighed and turned to leave. The young woman alone remained. She gave Ash an apologetic smile. I'm sorry you had to see that. Could you tell me what happened?

Ash looked back at Ethan's group, then nodded to her. Of course.

...

They gathered around a table at an outdoor cafe near the Battle Tower. The woman introduced herself first.

I'm Yuko, Professor Lund's assistant. He's the man you just saw, and Tory is his son.

Ethan had searched for the laboratory from the tower's top floor, only for its head researcher to appear right in front of him. Some people really were luckier than others.

He studied Yuko. She looked about twenty-seven or twenty-eight. Her makeup was neat, her hair was swept back from her forehead, and she wore a white top with black trousers. She had the capable air of a dependable assistant. A gentle smile and lively eyes softened that impression.

Brock went red at the sight of her. He pressed his hands to his cheeks and said dreamily, An assistant at your age? That's amazing! If you don't mind, Miss Yuko, I'd like to be your assistant too. You could teach me personally, hand in hand...

Max and Misty, seated on either side of him, each twisted one of his ears and stopped him before he could finish.

Stop right there! We don't need to hear about holding hands!

Many women would have been startled by Brock's shameless approach. Yuko simply kept smiling. She was too well-mannered to let her expression change or comment on it. Clearly, she had dealt with difficult situations before.

Her gaze did not linger on Brock. She sipped her coffee and turned to Ash. It seems Tory caused you trouble. I'm sorry.

Max asked the question that had been bothering him. What's wrong with him?

Yuko hesitated before answering. Tory doesn't dislike Pokemon. He's afraid to be near them. He went through something terrifying a few years ago. After that, his cheerful personality changed completely. Now even getting close to a Pokemon frightens him, let alone touching one. The Professor and I saw him in a battle on television and thought he might finally have recovered. But...

I see... Ash looked guilty. I didn't know. I pushed him into battling with me. I shouldn't have done that.

Misty turned to him. How did you meet? How did you end up on the same team?

Ash scratched his cheek awkwardly. Well, I only meant to ask him for directions. But when he saw Pikachu, he ran away without a word. I was curious, so I followed him. Somehow we ran right into the entrance for the arena, and the lift carried us onto the field.

That sounded like Ash. Most people would have asked somebody else after the first person fled. Only Ash would chase after him. It was a strange twist of fate that had brought Tory into his path.

Only you could do something like that, Max said. He was surprised, though perhaps he should not have been. But did they really let you onto the field so easily? Wasn't there any screening?

No. Ash shook his head. We went into the lift passage, and it took us straight up.

Yuko explained, That's because of the city passports you're carrying. Once you enter the competitors' passage, the system scans your information automatically. It's one of the Battle Tower's features. There's no need to go through a long registration process.

Oh, so that's why. Ash finally understood how simply following Tory had turned them into teammates.

He remembered how Tory had looked after the match. When will he get better?

Well... Yuko paused. We've tried counseling several times. The doctors say time alone won't heal this trauma. If he has the right experience, he may recover.

The right experience? Ash stood. Then I'll help him have one! If he and Pikachu become friends, maybe he'll stop being afraid.

He had already taken responsibility for helping Tory. He rubbed Pikachu's head, plainly confident that no one could resist his partner's charm for long. Without waiting for Yuko to agree, he ran off.

Oh! Yuko watched in surprise as the older boy vanished from sight. She had not expected such eagerness to help.

...

After they left the cafe, Max and Brock went looking for Ash and Tory, worried that Ash might get lost. May wanted to join them, but Misty drew her toward a nearby shopping center instead.

That left Ethan alone. Misty had invited him to shop with them, but he had declined.

You two enjoy yourselves. I'm going to walk around the park.

All right. See you later!

He waved to the girls, then watched Yuko disappear down another street. He called out Gengar.

I know, I know. Gengar shrugged before Ethan could speak. You want me to follow her, right? How many times is that now? Can't you give someone else the dirty work for once?

That's how important you are, Ethan said with a grin. None of my other Pokemon can fly through the sky and slip through the ground the way you can. Who else could do this job?

Then his tone grew serious. Be careful. I don't know what security the laboratory has. Stay hidden, and don't alert anyone.

Leave it to me. I'll handle it. Gengar patted its chest and silently followed Yuko.

Ethan waited until she was far enough away that she would not notice him, then set off in the same direction. He meant to try his luck at the laboratory now. If he could get inside, he might see the Deoxys core directly.

With Gengar ahead of him, there was no need to stay close behind Yuko. He walked at an easy pace, taking in LaRousse's sights and the particular feel of the city of technology.

He had not gone far when the Ultra Ball at his waist began shaking violently.

A moment later, a broad red aurora appeared in the sky. It came so suddenly and looked so out of place that within moments it seemed to cover the entire city.

Ethan looked up and understood at once. The other Deoxys had arrived.

His phone rang. As soon as he answered, Misty's voice came through. Ethan, is that...?

Yes, it's Deoxys, he said. Don't tell anyone yet. Stop shopping and find Ash and the others. Stay together. Something may happen soon.

What about you?

I'll act as things develop.

All right!

Ethan ended the call with a sigh. Deoxys had arrived before he could put most of his plans into motion. Still, he had come here hoping his Deoxys would meet the others. A little sooner or later would not change that.

People in the street were looking up. They were puzzled by an aurora appearing where it had no business being, but most treated it as strange weather and thought little more of it.

It vanished almost as quickly as it had come, lasting less than a dozen seconds. His Ultra Ball shook even harder once the light was gone.

Ethan found a quiet corner and released Deoxys and Gardevoir. Through Gardevoir's telepathy, he spoke to his Pokemon.

Can you sense where the other one is?

...Can't tell... the electromagnetic interference... too strong...

There was a quick way to contact the newcomer: have his own Deoxys send up an aurora. But that would be conspicuous and draw attention.

Professor Lund and Yuko, who had brought the Deoxys core to LaRousse, would probably realize as soon as they saw the red light that a Deoxys had come to the city.

Yet Ethan could not simply ignore it. In the movie, the searching Deoxys had attacked the entire city after failing to find its companion. He needed at least to calm it down.

His reasons for coming were simple: let his Pokemon meet the two Deoxys, stop the newcomer from attacking LaRousse, and prevent its later battle with Rayquaza from wrecking the city. After thinking it over, he decided to use the aurora to get its attention.

He would not send the signal from above the city. With Deoxys and Gardevoir's Teleport, he traveled to the broad forest outside LaRousse instead. Even if someone realized what was happening, they would not immediately find the person responsible.

In a flash, Ethan and his two Pokemon appeared among the trees. Once he was sure no one else was there, he nodded to Deoxys.

Go ahead.

Deoxys looked skyward. Blue light shot from its core, and an enormous blue aurora spread over the forest like a net.

Almost at the same moment, the red aurora reappeared above the city. The two fields of light lay side by side, answering each other, their colors crossing where they met.

As the red light flared, Ethan saw a figure flying toward them at tremendous speed. Gardevoir did not need to warn him. In less than half a minute, it landed opposite him.

A Deoxys identical to his own stood before him.

The two Pokemon gazed at each other. Together they rose into the air and slowly circled one another, like dancers tracing a great ring.

Chapter 719: Fearless Rayquaza

The two Deoxys made strange sounds Ethan could not understand. Gardevoir's telepathic link had been released for the moment, but the Pokemon appeared to be speaking amicably. Neither made a threatening move.

After a long exchange, they descended together and landed in front of him.

They looked identical, but Ethan could tell them apart. One regarded him with familiar, calm eyes. The other carried a cool, distant pressure. His own Deoxys nodded to him, and Ethan knew the first part of his plan had worked.

If he could persuade the wild Deoxys, he might avert the destruction it had caused in the movie. Then he could quietly help it find its companion.

He asked Gardevoir to connect him to the wild Deoxys through telepathy.

I know where your companion is, and I know it's safe. Please don't worry. Wait a little longer, and we'll find it without hurting anyone.

...I understand... My companion trusts you... I'll trust you too...

Ethan let out a breath. He had feared it might refuse to communicate, but the conversation had gone smoothly.

His Deoxys had also met another of its kind. It now knew it was not alone on this planet. That was Ethan's greatest reason for coming to LaRousse, and perhaps the best assurance that Deoxys would want to stay with him.

Then both Pokemon looked toward the distant sky and went on guard.

Ethan followed their gaze. A black speck was approaching fast. He understood at once.

Rayquaza was coming.

The auroras had attracted more than human attention. They had drawn the top predator from the ozone layer. Rayquaza held a grudge, and if Deoxys had hurt it before, it would want revenge.

So much for avoiding a confrontation.

Compared with Groudon and Kyogre's battle, the two Deoxys had done nothing dangerous. Their auroras carried no force. But viewed from the ozone layer, that display had been far more conspicuous than the battle, enough to catch Rayquaza's eye.

At least Ethan had thought to move out of the city. For now, LaRousse should be safe.

Within moments, Rayquaza reached the forest. The instant it spotted the Deoxys, it fired a blast of energy without hesitation. Both Deoxys rose into the air, dodged, and flew to meet it.

The attack missed them and kept descending toward the ground. Gardevoir reacted at once, wrapping Ethan in psychic power just as the scorching energy washed over him.

For a moment, he could see nothing but orange-yellow light. The psychic barrier kept him from being hurt, but the heat was nearly unbearable. A few seconds later, the attack passed.

Now Ethan was angry. Rayquaza clearly had no concern for whether the human below lived or died.

Then again, it lived high in the ozone layer, far above everyone else. With that great serpentine body, it seemed cold-blooded and indifferent to life. The Draconids worshiped it as a savior, but to Ethan it was a Pokemon that treated the whole planet as its territory. It had stopped Groudon and Kyogre's earlier battle only because their fight had disturbed it.

Rayquaza had seen two Deoxys waiting here and attacked anyway. It certainly had nerve. At a certain point, though, courage became stupidity.

Ethan had Gardevoir take him to a safer spot and settled in to watch.

From what he remembered of the movie and from their relative strength, Rayquaza had struggled against one Deoxys. What gave it confidence against two?

High above, the Deoxys moved in perfect accord, one before Rayquaza and one behind. They blocked its path and attacked together. Black beams shot from their cores. Rayquaza dodged the first but the second struck it, drawing a cry of pain.

The blow was still within the limits of what one of this planet's greatest predators could endure. Rayquaza twisted toward the Deoxys behind it and spat another burst of energy, which its target nimbly evaded.

Ethan had heard tales of two dragons playing with a pearl. Today he was watching two pearls toy with a dragon.

While the three Pokemon fought, Professor Lund and Yuko were scrambling in the LaRousse laboratory. They had noticed the first aurora over the city but thought little of it. In a world of Pokemon, unusual lights could have any number of causes.

It had been four years since their Antarctic expedition, when they saw Rayquaza fight Deoxys and brought the other Deoxys's core home. The scene had faded in their memories. They had not expected the Deoxys Rayquaza defeated to travel all this way in search of the core.

When blue light appeared over the forest and the red aurora answered it from the city, they understood. Deoxys had come. Its purpose was obvious: it wanted its companion back.

By rights, they ought to return the core. But they had spent four years pouring time, equipment, and effort into it, and their experiments were finally nearing completion. Letting go would be difficult.

Keeping it was dangerous too. A searching Deoxys could turn the city upside down.

Yuko immediately offered a suggestion for the residents' safety, but after considering it, Lund did not act on it. Instead, he called Officer Jenny by video and asked her to order a citywide evacuation.

An evacuation would affect hundreds of thousands of people. Any mistake would bring public criticism, so Jenny could not issue the order on one man's word alone. She needed to understand the threat.

Professor Lund, she said from a screen in the high-tech police station, why is Deoxys here? What is it looking for?

Lund would not reveal the core in his laboratory. What it's looking for isn't the immediate issue. Rayquaza may come after it. If those two fight near the city, we can't afford even a fraction of the damage they could cause.

Jenny could sense that he was withholding something. But this was no time to press him. If the Pokemon fought in LaRousse, the destruction could be catastrophic.

Understood. I'll issue the evacuation order now. Contact me at once if anything changes.

She ended the call and pressed a red button on her console. Across LaRousse, the city's robots sprang into action. Their screens changed from the green that signaled safety to yellow. They went from street to street and door to door, telling residents and visitors to evacuate. With the moving walkways, they directed people to the nearest shelters.

...

Elsewhere, Ash and the others had gathered in an enclosed park. Tory stood nearby, speaking quietly to a translucent, diamond-shaped figure that glowed cyan.

After leaving the cafe, Ash had found Tory there with surprising ease. He had seen the strange glowing figure beside him. Tory initially tried to hide it, but Ash's friendly persistence soon won him over. They became friends, and Tory introduced him to the figure.

Brock and Max arrived soon afterward. Misty and May followed. With the exception of Ethan, the group was together again.

They were laughing and talking when the evacuation alarm sounded. Misty alone understood what it might mean. The others looked around in confusion.

What's happening? Ash asked. He looked outside the park but saw only people evacuating.

Could it be connected to that aurora? Brock wondered. He had identified the most likely clue, though he could not be certain.

May looked at Misty. Misty had reacted strangely to the aurora, called Ethan, and then brought May straight to the others. She must know something.

Misty would normally have told her friends, but Tory was there. She shook her head slightly, asking May to stay quiet. May answered with a look. The two girls had become close enough to understand each other without speaking.

Max missed the exchange. He glanced at the people outside. Shouldn't we evacuate too?

Tory stood and pointed to a small gate at the other side of the park. I know a better place to shelter. That way leads to my father's laboratory. It's well protected.

But Ash shook his head. No. I'm going outside to see what's happening.

But the announcement says everyone has to take shelter, Tory protested.

That's exactly why we should look! Ash gave him a bright smile. We can't help if we don't know what's going on.

The idea shook Tory. He would never have thought of responding that way. But Ash and the others had already run out of the park. Tory gritted his teeth and followed.

Outside, people were evacuating faster, and a few frightened screams rose above the noise.

What was happening?

They looked across the river. Above the forest in the distance, a long green Pokemon twisted through the sky while two humanoid Pokemon attacked it. Explosions and bursts of fire flashed around them. The fighting seemed to be moving closer to LaRousse.

What Pokemon are those? Ash had never seen any of the three.

Max adjusted his glasses, eyes shining. I know! I read about the long green one. It's the Legendary Pokemon Rayquaza!

Rayquaza? Ash committed the name to memory and looked at the other two. Then who are those Pokemon?

Chapter 720: Single-Handedly

They're Deoxys. Misty could no longer keep the information to herself. They're Pokemon from outer space. They're incredibly strongevery bit as powerful as Rayquaza. They're rare Psychic-type Mythical Pokemon.

She did not say that Ethan owned one. She could not tell whether either of the Deoxys above the forest was his.

Deoxys? Mythical Pokemon? Ash repeated the name. He did not stop to wonder how Misty knew so much about them. Even he understood how rare they were. After seeing Ethan with so many Legendary Pokemon, Ash had envied him. If he could catch one now, perhaps he could close the gap between them.

Footsteps sounded behind him. He turned to see Rafe, Sid, and the twins hurrying toward them.

You? Ash said.

Rafe looked equally surprised. Are you going to that forest too?

What?

Don't pretend you don't know, Sid said with a grin. One look at that shape tells you the green one is Rayquaza, a Legendary Pokemon of Hoenn. And those two are fighting it and gaining the upper hand. They're powerful too. Who wouldn't want to catch Pokemon like that?

So we had the same idea! Ash remembered his defeat at the Battle Tower, and his competitive spirit flared. I'm the one who's going to catch them. I won't lose to you!

Then you'd better hurry, Rafe said. He glanced behind him. We're not the only ones after them. Some of those Trainers are well known at the Battle Tower. Keep standing here, and someone else will take your chance.

Ash and Sid noticed the others at last. More than twenty Trainers were rushing toward the river, ignoring the evacuation order. The two boys stopped talking and ran for the forest.

Brock, Max, Audrey, and Kathryn went after them. In a moment, only Misty, May, and Tory remained.

The glowing figure that had stayed beside Tory in the park had not followed him outside. It seemed unable to travel far from that place.

Tory had meant to lead everyone to the shelter at his father's laboratory. Instead, Ash had run toward the most dangerous place he could see. Tory hesitated. His fear of Pokemon urged him to stay back, but Ash had become his friend. He gritted his teeth and followed.

May looked at Misty. What's really happening?

She had stayed behind because Misty seemed to be keeping something to herself, and Ethan was missing. May could not shake the feeling that the two things were connected.

I'm not sure of everything, Misty said, watching the fight above the forest. But one of those Deoxys is definitely Ethan's. I don't know where the other came from or why they're fighting Rayquaza.

He didn't tell you?

You know what he's like. He's always involved in something big, and he keeps a lot of his plans to himself. There were other people around when he called, too. Anyway, let's go see what's happening.

...

Above the forest, Rayquaza's battle with the two Deoxys grew fiercer. Little by little, Rayquaza drew the fight toward LaRousse.

Ethan frowned. He had chosen the forest specifically to keep the city out of danger, yet the fight was moving toward it.

Through Gardevoir's telepathy, he asked his Deoxys to stop Rayquaza. It was a predator at the top of the food chain, though, and not so easily held back. The two Deoxys could defeat it together, but if Rayquaza wanted to move, they could not simply pin it in place.

Ethan saw what it was doing. The open sky above the forest favored the Deoxys. Rayquaza seemed to be heading for the city's crowded buildings, where it could maneuver among them and perhaps find a way to win.

It was clever from Rayquaza's perspective. For the people below, it would be a disaster.

Ethan stood on a tree branch with a view toward LaRousse. Something else surprised him: a crowd was coming this way from the city. Ash and his friends were among them, along with many other Trainers.

What were they doing here?

Pokemon began carrying the newcomers across the broad river between the city and forest. The excitement on their faces gave Ethan his answer. They were here to catch Rayquaza and the Deoxys, not to stop the battle.

Trust Trainers to react that way. Legendary Pokemon were fighting right outside a city. Anyone with a dream of catching one would want to try their luck, however impossible it seemed for an ordinary person.

For Ethan, they were a problem. With two Deoxys against Rayquaza, the outcome had looked nearly certain. Add a crowd of Trainers, and anything might happen.

He thought for a moment, watching Rayquaza edge toward the city, and had an idea. If the Trainers were so eager to meet a Legendary Pokemon, he would let them meet Rayquaza up close.

He gave his Deoxys an order through Gardevoir.

Steer the fight into those Trainers. Wherever the crowd is thickest, send Rayquaza there.

His Deoxys stopped attacking and concentrated on blocking Rayquaza's route. After several attempts, it turned the Pokemon away from the city and toward the Trainers crossing the river.

They had not expected that. Before setting out, they had watched the three Pokemon's course. Though the fight had been drifting cityward, its direction looked predictable. They had deliberately taken a wide route to avoid being caught beneath it, hoping to intercept the Pokemon from the far bank.

Why had the battle suddenly changed direction and accelerated toward them? A few quick-thinking Trainers sensed trouble and turned away. Most reacted too late. By the time they understood, Rayquaza was almost upon them.

Commanding a Pokemon from safety was one thing. Fighting with your own body inside the range of an opponent's attack was another. It tested both a Trainer's nerve and their survival.

Plenty of people could direct a battle calmly from behind the lines. Far fewer could keep their composure when an attack might kill them.

Boom!

Rayquaza fired another blast. It missed Deoxys and exploded against the river below. The shock wave and towering spray caught several Trainers riding Water-type Pokemon. People and Pokemon alike were thrown into the river before they could react.

Ash, Rafe, and Sid had been near the front and escaped that strike. They looked back at the others in the water, stunned.

What power! Sid sat astride his Blastoise and wiped river water from his face. That's what a Hoenn Legendary Pokemon can do? One missed attack threw up that much water and knocked so many people in. Are we really going to try to catch a monster like that?

Of course, Rafe said, his expression steady. It just removed most of our competition. We'll have more time to catch Rayquaza before they make it back to shore.

Even so, the middle of a wide river was a poor place to fight Rayquaza and two Deoxys.

The fallen Trainers had barely surfaced and had not yet climbed back onto their Pokemon when a second attack came. This time it came from one of the strange Pokemon fighting Rayquaza.

One Deoxys continued to engage Rayquaza. The other produced hundreds of copies of itself. They were not insubstantial illusions like Double Team. They seemed solid, and they attacked Pokemon and Trainers in the water and air without distinguishing between them.

That was the scene Misty and May found when they reached the riverbank. The copies were darker than the original Deoxys but could fly as it did. They used no named moves, striking at close range with their tentacle-like arms instead.

The attacks looked crude and full of openings, but they carried tremendous force. Smaller Pokemon could not match them.

May understood what she was seeing. Is Ethan trying to stop those people from catching Rayquaza?

Of course. Misty nodded. They've been told to evacuate, and they came here to interfere anyway. He has to stop them.

But some of them could get hurt. And what if they find out it was his Pokemon?

Oh, relax. Misty waved a hand. If you go looking for a Pokemon like Rayquaza, you should expect a few injuries. And how would they know? As long as Ethan stays out of sight, nobody will connect Deoxys to him.

May hesitated. Something about that did not sit quite right with her, but she accepted Misty's point for the moment.

Then her face changed. Waitwhere's Max?

They argued all the time, but he was her little brother. She scanned the bank in alarm and soon spotted him nearby with Brock, Tory, Audrey, and Kathryn.

Misty and May hurried over. The others had followed Ash to the river but had no Pokemon to carry them across, so they had stayed on the bank. That had spared them the attacks.

Max watched hundreds of copies fighting the Trainers. What an incredible Pokemon. It can make all those copies and hold off so many people by itself. I think it's the strongest Pokemon I've ever seen. Can a human really catch something like that?

And he thought this was impressive? Misty smiled to herself. If Max had seen Deoxys in that valley, holding out against Team Magma, Team Aqua, Rayquaza, and Ethan's strongest Pokemon all at once, he would know how powerful it truly was.

Chapter 721: Unstoppable!

The Trainers on the river and in the air had no choice but to fight the hundreds of Deoxys copies that came at them.

They soon discovered that, for all their numbers, the copies were fragile. Even a slight hit broke one apart into a fading shadow. That was a relief. The pressure on the Trainers eased at once.

If every copy had been as strong as the original, there would have been no point fighting. They might as well have fled. The technique looked terrifying, but its numbers came at the cost of durability.

The battle grew fierce. Ash, Rafe, and Sid were caught in it like everyone else.

Ethan's Deoxys had been with him only a short time and did not know Ash. It had been ordered to steer Rayquaza toward the Trainers and wear them down. Even if it had known Ash was Ethan's friend, it would have treated him like anyone else without special instructions.

Still, Deoxys was not trying to kill anyone. The Trainers had room to fight back. Ash and the others sent out Pokemon to counterattack and hurried toward the bank, knowing the river put them at a severe disadvantage.

The greater danger came from Rayquaza's fight with the wild Deoxys. Neither meant to strike the humans below, but the force spilling from their battle was more than many Trainers could bear.

Powerful attacks burst against the water, battering the Pokemon crossing it. Rayquaza's long, massive body swept through the sky and knocked Flying-type Pokemon down. Some Trainers finally understood that they lacked the strength even to approach such creatures.

The copies ignored Rayquaza and focused on the Trainers' Pokemon, adding to the confusion. Most of the crowd, however, had lost its caution at the sight of Legendary Pokemon. Even a one-in-ten-thousand chance of catching one kept them in the fight.

Cold river water and one defeat after another did not break their determination. If anything, their fixation on Rayquaza and the Deoxys grew stronger.

Amid the chaos, Ash, Rafe, and Sid fought their way across the river and reached the far bank first.

Whew, we're finally out. Sid climbed off Blastoise and wrung out his clothes. He looked back at the fight on the water. If we'd stayed in the river with those copies attacking and Rayquaza firing overhead, we might as well have been targets.

They're not quite copies, Rafe said. Ethan's first impression of him had been right: he thought carefully about what he saw. They move independently and can hit things. Splitting off pieces of itself is a better description.

Splitting? Sid sighed. Whatever you call them, what can we do about so many shadows?

He had a point. They could knock the creatures down one at a time, but there were too many to clear. To reach the Pokemon they wanted to catch, they first had to get past the split-off forms. It seemed like a deadlock.

You're right, Rafe admitted after a pause. We'll have to find a way to eliminate them before we get close.

He knew a simpler answer existed: bring a Pokemon strong enough to match Deoxys. But neither he, Sid, nor Ash had one.

Don't be so gloomy, Ash said with a grin. We made it ashore. That's the first step. If we keep trying, we'll find a way.

Sid agreed. Exactly! Why overthink it? Let's give it everything we've got.

Seeing that neither intended to back down, Rafe nodded. Then let's work together for now.

They were rivals in their hunt, but the opponent before them had put them on the same side.

From the forest, Ethan watched the Trainers fight harder instead of retreating. They seemed to be growing more determined with every attack. It gave him a headache, especially when he saw Ash at the edge of the trees.

Why couldn't Ash stay with Tory and help him get over his fear? Why did he have to join this mess?

Very well. If they would not leave, Ethan would raise the stakes. He fixed his gaze on the Trainers and sent another order to Deoxys.

Let them see what you can really do.

...

Pikachu, Thunderbolt! Corphish, Bubble Beam!

Blaziken, Flamethrower! Quagsire, Water Gun!

Blastoise, Hydro Pump! Magneton, Thunder Shock!

On the open ground before the forest, Ash, Rafe, and Sid directed their Pokemon against the Deoxys copies overhead. Their combined attacks broke apart more than a dozen. It barely changed the wider battle, but it cleared a patch of sky and made the space around them safer.

Then a figure flashed before their eyes. A Deoxys descended until it hovered only a meter off the ground in front of them.

Its colors differed sharply from the copies. This was the original.

What? Sid froze. Before he could react, Blastoise flew backward as if struck by an invisible force. It skimmed past him and slammed into a tree.

Thud! The trunk splintered. Blastoise crashed through several more thick trees before finally stopping. Its shell had protected it from the worst of the impact, and after struggling for a moment, it slowly got up.

How did it get here? Ash cried.

He had no time to move. The same unseen power hurled Pikachu into another tree. Pikachu! Ash could only watch as his partner struck the trunk and fell to the ground.

Rafe reacted faster. He snatched a Poke Ball from his belt and shouted to the other two, Don't just stand there! This is our chance. We have to bring it down together!

Ash and Sid knew the opportunity might not come again. They left their injured Pokemon for the moment and released everything else they had. Blue flashes filled the clearing, and more than a dozen Pokemon surrounded Deoxys.

Up close, the three Trainers could sense how unusual it was. Deoxys made a short, strange sound, like a signal none of them could understand. Its metallic, alien face showed no expression. It seemed cold and indifferent.

Everyone, attack! Sid called. His Pokemon rushed forward.

Deoxys raised both arms and released a pulse of power. Sid's Pokemon flew backward before they could touch it.

It's too strong! Sid stared as several of his Pokemon went down from that one blow.

Ash's and Rafe's Pokemon closed in from either side.

Swellow, Wing Attack! Snorunt, Icy Wind! Ash commanded.

Both moves struck toward Deoxys, but neither broke through its protective barrier. Rafe fared no better. His Pokemon failed to breach the defense and fell to Deoxys's counterattack.

His confidence took a heavy blow. He had expected a gap in strength, but not one this vast. They had barely begun, and it already felt impossible to cross. Could any human truly catch such a Pokemon?

A yellow shape flashed past him. Pikachu, hurt but back on its feet, ran low to the ground, leaped, and swung its shining tail at Deoxys.

What was it doing? Rafe had fought Pikachu at the Battle Tower earlier and remembered its poor performance. He expected this charge to end badly.

Instead, Pikachu's Iron Tail shattered Deoxys's energy barrier.

How could such a little Pokemon hold that much power? Why had it looked so weak in the tower?

Deoxys flung Pikachu aside with psychic force before it could cause any injury. But the broken barrier gave Rafe a moment of hope.

Now! Hit it with everything you have! he shouted.

The usually composed boy sounded fired up. His fallen Pokemon forced themselves upright despite the pain and launched their strongest attacks together. Five or six blasts of different colors converged on Deoxys.

Boom!

They struck almost at once, raising a cloud of smoke. It worked! Rafe's face brightened.

The smoke thinned. Deoxys still hovered in the same spot, unharmed. Its shape had changed: its body looked thicker, as though it wore protective armor.

Rafe's smile vanished. Why had it changed? His Pokemon had attacked with all their strength. Even a Legendary Pokemon ought to have felt that. Yet this one had not moved or suffered so much as a scratch.

What kind of monster was it?

As he stared, Deoxys changed back to its earlier form, raised its arms, and counterattacked. Rafe's face drained of color.

He had never encountered Deoxys before, but he understood now: it could take different forms. One excelled at attacking; another had extraordinary defense.

He did not have time to order a dodge. Black light flashed, and an explosion tore through the clearing, turning trees to ash and scouring the earth. His Pokemon fell, as did Ash's and Sid's.

After only two direct attacks, Deoxys had knocked out every Pokemon they had on the field.

You! Sid cried. The hopelessness was too much for him.

In desperation, he pulled out a Poke Ball and threw it at Deoxys. The time to make a capture attempt had clearly not come, but Rafe understood. With no Pokemon left able to fight, this was the only thing Sid could try.

Neither Rafe nor Ash expected it to work, yet both followed the ball with their eyes as it reached Deoxys.

Click. It dropped to the ground without reacting at all.

Huh? Ash and Sid stared. Had the Poke Ball broken?

Rafe was startled too. Then his face changed. Poke Balls rarely failed unless damaged. Even thrown at a healthy wild Pokemon, one should at least flash red.

There was only one explanation.

Run! he shouted at the others. Somebody has already caught this Pokemon! It has a Trainer!

Chapter 722: Too Bad I Wasn't There

Someone caught it? Sid exploded at the impossible news. How? Who could beat a monster like that?

After facing Deoxys himself, he understood the gulf between them. His Pokemon were like fireflies beside the moon. The difference was crushing. Other than Rayquaza, he could not imagine any Pokemon that might match it. Could a Trainer truly catch such a creature?

He would rather believe his Poke Ball was broken than accept Rafe's explanation. Yes, the ball had to be faulty.

Ash, meanwhile, thought of Ethan at once. In his limited experience, an Elite Four member like Lance might be able to defeat a Pokemon that strong. But if he had to name someone who could catch it, his first thought was Ethan. It could only be Ethan.

Ethan's powerful team and the many Legendary Pokemon he owned had left a deep impression on Ash. He alone seemed capable of capturing Deoxys. Could this one belong to him?

Ash looked at his own defeated Pokemon, then across the river at the Trainers under attack from the copies. He hesitated. Ethan wouldn't order his Pokemon to attack us, would he?

While Ash and Sid stood stunned, Rafe recalled his Pokemon and strode toward the river. Sid came to his senses and hurriedly recalled his team as well.

Seeing Ash still standing there, Sid shouted back as he ran. What are you waiting for? Get out of here!

Huh? Right! Ash recalled his other Pokemon, ran to Pikachu, and picked up his unconscious partner. Then he raced to the riverbank and jumped in.

Splash! The cold water cleared his head. Pikachu stirred and opened its eyes.

Pika...

Ash felt the knot in his chest loosen. He swam with one arm, holding Pikachu above the water with the other. Pikachu, you're awake...

Pika... it answered weakly.

Ash looked at it with concern. Why did you push yourself so hard? Pikachu did not have the strength to answer. Its eyes slowly closed again.

Hold on. I'll get you to a Pokemon Center. Ash held it close and swam after Rafe and Sid toward the city.

All three were dispirited. Only minutes earlier they had crossed the river on Water-type Pokemon, glad that the other Trainers were tangled up with the copies. Now their whole teams had lost, and they had to swim back on their own. It was a miserable reversal.

After defeating them, Deoxys swept over their heads toward the Trainers still fighting on the water. At first Ash, Rafe, and Sid flinched, afraid it meant to finish them off. It did not even glance down. Being ignored brought a different kind of defeat: they had never mattered to it.

The remaining Trainers had not seen the battle on the far bank. The copies kept them occupied, and they had no idea how badly the three boys had lost. Only when Deoxys appeared among them did someone finally notice it.

Fear was not their first reaction. They were delighted. They had struggled for so long to get past the copies and reach Rayquaza or either Deoxys. Now one of their targets had come to them.

Before they could act, Deoxys attacked.

Its strange voice sounded again. It brought both hands to the core in its chest and sent a tremendous beam of energy across everything around it.

Every Pokemon caught by the blast fell immediately. Those in the air and those above the water alike dropped into the river. In one attack, Deoxys had brought down more than half its opponents.

The Trainers stared as though the scene had stopped. Some did not even react when their own Pokemon hit the water.

Then a woman's scream broke the silence. Pelipper!

Her Pelipper had taken the blast without a chance to move and plunged into the river. It had taken her several seconds to grasp what she had seen. Her cry seemed to restart the world around them.

What kind of monster is that?

How can it be so strong?

Run!

The Trainers fell into chaos. Some jumped into the river after their Pokemon. Many more instinctively fled from Deoxys.

Misty's group watched from a safer stretch of bank. Apart from Ash, the others stood with wide eyes, worried for the people caught in the attack.

So that's Deoxys's power, Brock murmured. One attack beat so many Pokemon. He was so startled that even his usually narrow eyes opened wide.

Misty alone seemed unsurprised.

May glanced across the river and whispered in her ear, Will Ash and the others be all right?

They'll be fine. Misty checked that Brock and the others were too absorbed in the fight to hear them. Ethan knows what he's doing. He won't let this get out of hand. You saw it yourselfDeoxys had plenty of chances to hurt those Trainers badly and held back.

As they spoke, Deoxys attacked a second time. The remaining Trainers broke. It was less a retreat than a rout.

They had forgotten every thought of catching a Legendary Pokemon. After a single real exchange, they fled toward the city bank faster than they had come, as though wishing for another pair of legs.

Within moments, they were all ashore. Feeling safe for the moment, however, they stopped there to watch what happened next. They still had not learned their lesson.

Ethan had no patience for that. He gave Deoxys another order through telepathy. As it approached the bank, the Trainers scattered again and fled back into LaRousse. Even Misty's group withdrew to a safer position.

With the intruders gone, Ethan could give Rayquaza his full attention.

High above the river, the wild Deoxys and Rayquaza were still locked in a close fight. Both had taken some damage, but neither had a decisive advantage.

Once Ethan's Deoxys rejoined the battle, there was little doubt about the outcome. The two worked together until Rayquaza roared in anger, shot upward, and vanished into the clouds.

At last it was over. Ethan relaxed in the forest. He had only directed Deoxys through a few maneuvers, but the choices had taken a toll on his concentration. For now, the crisis had passed.

...

That night, Ethan entered the LaRousse Pokemon Center and found its dining room unexpectedly full.

Trainers sat eating in silence. Their troubled faces and occasional sighs betrayed their thoughts. For a room with so many people, the quiet was strange. It felt more like a library than a dining room.

Behind the counter, Nurse Joy hurried back and forth with treatment equipment.

Ethan spotted Ash's group in a corner, with Rafe and his companions at the next table. Ash's table was more at ease than the others, though they too spoke softly in deference to the mood.

Misty saw him and waved him over. He sat beside her.

Ethan, where did you go? Max asked at once.

For some reason, Max had started calling him by the same familiar form of address as Misty and Ash. He was the youngest of them, so Ethan thought nothing of it. The question drew every eye at the table, especially Ash's. Ash seemed to be testing a suspicion.

Where else? Ethan shrugged. I heard the evacuation order and went to a shelter with the people nearby. I only just got back.

Ash looked surprised. Simple as he was, he took the answer at face value. So whose Deoxys had that been?

Brock was less certain. Ethan's face gave nothing away, so he looked at Misty and May. Neither showed any sign of doubt either. That was odd. Did they know something?

Max pushed up his glasses and spoke as though Ethan had missed out terribly. That's too bad! Do you know what we saw by the river while you were hiding? Rayquaza and two Pokemon we'd never seen before! They were so strong. They beat Ash and...

Max, stop, May said quietly. Can't you read the room? Look at everyone's faces.

Max was clever, but still young and not always sensitive to other people's feelings. He finally noticed how grim the nearby Trainers looked and fell silent.

Ethan, however, had no such hesitation. He rubbed salt into the wound.

Oh, that fight! he said with a smile. I heard about it. The local television station broadcast it live, so the whole city knows why we evacuated. Everyone saw what happened.

He turned to Ash, still smiling. You lost badly. Too bad I wasn't there. If I had been, I definitely could have beaten that Pokemon!

Chapter 723: Revived at Last

Late that night, when most of the city was asleep, Ethan looked at Ash and the others sleeping soundly in their beds and quietly left the room.

The dormitory was still. He could just make out someone snoring somewhere.

He passed a yawning Trainer who had arrived to check in at this hour, pulled his clothes a little closer around himself, crossed the empty dining room, and slipped out the Pokemon Center's back door.

Gengar had been waiting outside for some time, peering about furtively.

After Ethan sent it to follow Yuko, he had been busy in the forest directing Deoxys against Rayquaza and the other Trainers. He had missed his chance to meet Gengar then. Once he returned to the Pokemon Center, dinner and a long chat with Ash's group kept him occupied. Only now, in the dead of night, could he get away to hear its report.

Gengar looked as though it had come to a secret rendezvous, and Ethan couldn't help laughing.

You're a Pokemon. Why do you look more like a spy now?

A spy? That sounds awful. Gengar gave a wicked chuckle. I'm a Pokemon agent with a one hundred percent success rate at tailing people!

Enough bragging. What did you find?

Gengar shrugged. I've had plenty of time to locate the laboratory and learn its layout. I found the Deoxys core you mentioned, too. But there are cameras everywhere. Anything visible will be spotted. I can get around them, but for anyone with a physical body, slipping in unnoticed would be nearly impossible.

What condition is the core in?

Gengar thought back over what it had seen. It's lying inside a sealed case, surrounded by equipment. I tried getting closer, but there's an alarm by it. I couldn't approach without setting it off, and I didn't want to alert them, so I came back.

Still only a core?

Ethan rubbed his chin. He remembered it regenerating into Deoxys in the latter half of the movie. Why was it still a core now?

Was it too early? Or was some other trigger missing?

Never mind. If he got the core to Deoxys, surely it would know how to restore its companion.

What about security? he asked.

I only saw a few people on patrol, and they didn't look particularly tough, Gengar answered at once. But like I said, cameras are everywhere. The moment you go in, they'll see you. Even if you take the core secretly, you'll trip the alarm.

Ethan trusted its assessment. If Gengar said the guards weren't much of a threat, they probably wouldn't endanger his plan. The cameras were another matter.

Professor Lund's laboratory was different from a Team Rocket facility or some other criminal organization's hideout. It was a lawful research center under official protection. Even the core was something Lund had found himself, making it his lawful property. Ethan couldn't simply invade the place in the open. He couldn't even let his own Pokemon be identified. Otherwise, the police would follow the clues straight to him.

That made this a new kind of challenge. He would have to rely on Pokemon no one had seen him useor Pokemon that didn't belong to him at all.

His mind made up, he told Gengar, Come on. Let's meet our new friend first.

...

Across the river from LaRousse City, in a forest on the far bank, Ethan climbed down from Dragonite into a small clearing.

Two Deoxys floated there, watching him in silence. The cool moonlight made them look even colder and more uncanny.

Luckily, this was the world of Pokemon, and one of them was his own partner. If he had found a sight like this in the wilderness back in his old world, he would have jumped out of his skin and thought he had wandered into a supernatural film.

He approached the wild Deoxys. I found your companion. Getting it out will be difficult, though, so I'll need your help.

Deoxys made a sound he couldn't understand. He hardly needed a translation to guess that it agreed.

His own Deoxys nodded when he looked its way. It seemed the two had become friends and could now get along peacefully. That was good news.

He had left his Deoxys here partly to give it time with one of its own kind, and partly to keep an eye on the wild one so it wouldn't leave or cause more trouble.

There was no time to waste. Ethan released Gardevoir and left her and Dragonite to protect his body. Then he turned to Gengar. All right. Let's do it. Pull my soul out.

He found a level patch of ground, lay down, and closed his eyes. Gengar came to his side, set a hand on his head, and pulled upward. For the second time since their experience at sea, Ethan's soul left his body.

He had been through it before, but seeing his own body lying there still felt strange. For an instant, it seemed unfamiliar, as though it belonged to someone else.

He shook off the feeling and urged Gengar on. Time's short. Let's go.

Only Ghost-type Pokemon could see him in this state, so Gengar would have to relay all his orders and directions. Gengar could also turn invisible. Neither it nor Ethan's soul had to fear the cameras.

As for the two Deoxys, Ethan had no intention of hiding them.

They only needed to avoid being seen before they reached the laboratory. Once inside, they could take the core. It didn't matter if anyone spotted them then. The whole city had watched them fight Rayquaza above the forest that day. People would assume they were acting on their own. Who would imagine a Trainer was directing them?

Under the moon, the two Deoxys streaked across the city toward the northern part of the island. In the darkness, no one noticed them arrive.

Professor Lund's laboratory stood beside lush flowerbeds. The building looked modern, but it had no sign and attracted little attention. Someone passing by without knowing what it was would never guess it housed a research center.

Careful, aren't you?

They landed by a small side door. Gengar and Ethan, still in his disembodied state, passed straight through the wall. The two Deoxys smashed the reinforced door and followed them inside.

The alarm sounded almost at once, its shrill call echoing through the quiet building.

This was a scientific facility in the middle of a city. Its designers seemed to have planned for petty thieves, not Pokemon breaking down doors. Even after the alarm had rung for some time, the guards were slow to arrive.

Two men carrying batons finally confronted Deoxys with a Pokemon each. They could do nothing to stop them. The Deoxys merely floated past, and both men and both Pokemon collapsed unconscious without even forcing the intruders to make a move.

They met no further resistance. Ethan knew the police must have been alerted, though. Perhaps they were already on their way.
