With Gengar leading, they went straight through the building. Within minutes they reached its central laboratory. The door looked thick and formidable, but Deoxys's power made short work of it.

Inside, beyond the core in its sealed case, two people were still sitting there: Professor Lund and his assistant, Yuko.

They hadn't left, even at this hour? Ethan hadn't expected that, but it made little difference. They were ordinary people. Whether they were present or absent would not change what happened next.

His part of the job was finished. Now it was up to Deoxys.

Professor Lund rose and faced the doorway.

You finally came.

He sounded calm, as though greeting an old friendor as though he had expected this all along.

Ethan kept his face still. He knew Lund wasn't speaking to him. The professor was addressing Deoxys. Humans and Pokemon other than Ghost types could not see Ethan's soul. He could dance right in front of Lund without being noticed.

Even so, Lund's perception astonished him. Two Deoxys had come in, yet the professor had picked out the one he had encountered four years ago. That was absurdly sharp.

The wild Deoxys paid him no attention. It flew straight to the middle of the laboratory and looked at the core.

Lund might have spoken as though they knew each other well, but as far as Deoxys was concerned, it had scarcely seen the man. At most, it had caught a glimpse of him four years ago. Why would it remember an unimportant human?

Lund seemed to expect no reply. He looked at the core he had spent four years trying to revive and said, When I saw you today, I knew you'd come here. I thought this day might arrive eventually. I just didn't expect it so soon.

Deoxys ignored him again. It swept out a hand, and the sealed case around the core shattered.

Lund's hands clenched so tightly that his knuckles whitened. Yuko gave him an anxious glance, looking as though she wanted to speak but could find no words.

He drew a deep breath. I've actually made a breakthrough in reviving it. I've mastered the technique. If I can replace a few more parts and have a little more time, I can

Before he could finish, Deoxys extended a hand. Energy flowed from its core to the other one. The core visibly began to grow, rapidly building a body around itself. Within a few seconds, a new Deoxys had taken shape.

Lund's unfinished sentence died on his lips. At last, he let out a helpless sigh.

Four years of work, surpassed in seconds. What had all that time, money, and effort been for? What was the point of working late in the laboratory night after night?

Ethan felt sorry for him. But effort did not always bring a reward. Lund had no malicious intent; he had simply wanted to restore Deoxys. Although its revival had happened differently from the movie, the result was the same. Years of painstaking work had come to nothing, a harsh outcome for the professor.

There was no other solution Ethan could see. The movie had ended much the same way, and he had no wish to change it.

As he reflected on that, the invisible Gengar drew close to his ear. It's getting late. We need to leave. If your soul stays away much longer, your body will be in trouble.

It was right. He had been away from his body both too far and too long. The work was done, and there was no reason to stay.

Ethan nodded. He took one last look at Lund's dejected face, sighed, and led the three Deoxys back the way they had come.

Only when they left the building did he see that the return trip might be less simple. The alarm had brought LaRousse's police to the laboratory. Worse, the city's defense system had activated. Countless smart blocks assembled into a huge robot that stood menacingly in their path.

It was only a slight complication.

Against three Deoxys, the officers and their Pokemon were routed at once. The robot, the ultimate defensive weapon of this city of technology, lasted barely a dozen seconds under their attacks before it broke into fragments scattered across the ground.

The defenders could only watch, helpless and frustrated, as the three Deoxys flew out of the city and disappeared above the forest.

Chapter 724: Keeping a Straight Face

Three Deoxys flashed through the night, the moonlight lending their bodies a faint silver sheen. In only a few minutes they left LaRousse City behind and landed in the forest clearing.

Everything was as Ethan had left it. No one had attacked the clearing, and no foolish wild Pokemon had wandered in. The only change was that Gardevoir had wrapped his body in psychic power to keep it warm through the night.

She really was thoughtful. It was a detail he hadn't considered himself, yet she had noticed it.

There was no time to dwell on that. He had gone a long way and stayed away a long time. His soul was starting to feel uncomfortable, as though its connection to his body had nearly broken. He hurried to lie above it, and in a moment of disorientation his soul slipped back inside.

When he opened his eyes and rose from the ground, his body felt warm. He didn't seem to have suffered any aftereffects.

Well done! he told Gardevoir with a smile.

Then he turned to the two wild Deoxys. He didn't know their sexes, or even whether Deoxys had sexes. What he did know was that this pair was unusual: they had come from the same meteorite.

Other Deoxys also traveled through space on meteorites, but usually there was only one in each. These two had shared a single rock. That was why the red-cored Deoxys had been so determined to find the blue-cored one in the movie.

The glowing blue presence Ash's group had encountered in the park was the blue-cored Deoxys's consciousness. Its body had been destroyed, leaving only its core, but its formidable psychic power let it move through a limited area around the park. Later, it had befriended Tory, who often withdrew there by himself.

All right, Ethan said. It's over now. You've found each other, and your companion has its body back. It's time for you to leave this place and start your own adventure.

The two couldn't speak his language, and their faces showed no change, but Ethan thought he saw a trace of gratitude in their eyes.

They turned together toward his Deoxys and made a strange sound. It answered them. The three alien Pokemon were communicating in their own way.

Ethan and the others couldn't understand them or read their expressions, so they could only guess what was being said. Gengar leaned toward his ear and whispered, I think they're asking your Deoxys to go with them.

They might be.

Fortunately, the exchange didn't last long. When it ended, Ethan's Deoxys remained beside him. He let out a breath.

He had caught it and helped fulfill its wish, but he hadn't known whether it would choose to leave with the others. An Ultra Ball could never hold a Pokemon of its power if it truly wanted to go. No one could stop it. The possibility had worried him all along.

Now it seemed to have made its choice. It had chosen him.

The heart-to-heart they had shared, and all the time they had spent together, had meant something. Deoxys really had accepted him.

As the wild pair prepared to depart, Ethan cleared his throat and told them he might need their help against a powerful enemy before long. Through Gardevoir's telepathy, he received an answer almost at once.

...We will...help you...

...

News of the nighttime disturbance, especially the defeat of the city's final defense system, spread by the next morning and frightened LaRousse's residents and visiting Trainers. The police responded quickly with an announcement: the Deoxys had entered the city by chance and had soon left. That calmed the immediate panic.

People kept talking about it over meals, though, and footage of the battle rapidly spread to other parts of Hoenn. The Trainers who had actually fought Deoxys and Rayquaza the day before were the exception. They said nothing, as if they wanted to forget the whole experience. The battle had left its mark on them.

With the Deoxys gone, the city of technology had become an ordinary city to Ethan. He didn't leave right away. Instead, he stayed with Ash's group and spent some peaceful time seeing what made LaRousse special.

After another half day, however, it was time for everyone to set out. Ethan had accomplished what he came for and gained plenty from the trip. Ash couldn't say the same.

He had promised Yuko he would help Tory overcome his fear of Pokemon. For the past two days, he had stayed with the boy whenever he could and tried everything he knew. But events hadn't unfolded as they had in the movie, and Ash never got the chance that might have changed things. In the end, Tory could tolerate Pokemon at a certain distance. He still couldn't bear them any closer.

Ash felt as though he had failed him. Ethan shook his head and offered what comfort he could. If you can't do more, you can't. Tory may just need time to grow older. I think he'll learn to manage it himself someday.

Ash was disappointed, but he knew he had done all he could.

At the harbor, they said goodbye to a reluctant Tory. Ethan and Misty watched Ash, May, Brock, and Max board a passenger ship and continue their journey. With the four of them gone, Ethan had no reason to remain either.

It was time to return to Lilycove City and wait for Zinnia. He gave Tory a polite nod. They didn't know each other well enough for much more. After a wave, he and Misty went to the light rail station and took a train away from LaRousse.

The view outside was much the same as it had been on their way in, but their mood had changed.

I miss having everyone around already, Misty said with a sigh. It's fun when we're all talking and laughing together. The time goes so quickly. Now it's just the two of us, and everything feels so quiet.

Ethan understood. Even he felt a sudden emptiness after all that noise and company. That's part of being Trainers. Traveling, challenging Gyms, catching Pokemonthat's what we have to do now. Someday, when we've retired and have time to spare, we can all gather like this whenever we want.

Retired? Misty covered her mouth with a laugh. You're already thinking about retirement at your age? Isn't that a little early?

Age has nothing to do with it. Ethan leaned back to make himself comfortable. If I get tired, I'll stop and rest. I don't mean right now, of course. First I'll challenge a few more regions and win a few more League tournaments.

That doesn't sound so far away. Misty's eyes shone as she looked at him. If you keep going at this pace, I'm sure you'll get there before long!

Then I hope you're right.

As they spoke, the train arrived back in Lilycove City. Ethan stepped off and took out his phone to ask Zinnia where she had reached. He found a message she had sent more than half an hour earlier.

He and Misty had only just boarded the train then. Between finding seats, looking out the window, and chatting, he hadn't noticed the notification. Zinnia's message said she was already in Lilycove, waiting in a forest outside the city.

That was fast. In less than two days, she had crossed most of Hoenn. She was plainly in a hurry. Even riding a Flying-type Pokemon, she must have traveled day and night with scarcely any rest.

I didn't expect her to be this eager, Ethan said. But we've rested enough. Let's go meet her.

They left the station without delay and headed out of Lilycove. From some distance away, they spotted Zinnia leaning against a large tree with her eyes closed. She looked as though she were dozing. She still wore the same outfit as before, but travel had left her dusty and her face a little drawn.

The sound of their footsteps made her open her eyes at once. Their earlier meetings had been reasonably friendly. Now the air between them felt strange, and they stood somewhere between allies and enemies.

Zinnia narrowed her eyes at Ethan for some time. Once he drew near, she said coldly, Follow me. She released Salamence and climbed onto its back.

That told him they had a long journey ahead. Ethan exchanged a glance with Misty, shrugged, and released Dragonite. They mounted together.

Zinnia was already airborne. Her Salamence flew southeast, and Dragonite followed at a distance. Misty sat in front of Ethan and looked back at him.

What did you do to her? she asked with a smile. She looks as though she's angry with you.

Ethan had taken Zinnia's call away from Misty and Ash's group. Misty had only learned afterward who had been on the phone, so she had no idea what they had said. Something unpleasant had clearly happened. Zinnia had helped them before, and although Misty found her odd and had mixed feelings about her, she didn't want Ethan to make an enemy of her.

What could I have done? I just made her angry with a few words. Ethan glanced at Zinnia ahead of them. She's too rigid. If she were more open to compromise, we could work together and both come away with something. There'd be no need for things to be like this.

He meant it. If Zinnia agreed to cooperate, Ethan would take the black Rayquaza at Sky Pillar, but he wouldn't leave her empty-handed. He intended to catch the ordinary Rayquaza they had encountered at LaRousse and give it to her in exchange. They would both end up with a Rayquaza.

Wasn't that what the Draconid people had sought for generations? Yet Zinnia's temperament had closed off that possibility. At least they weren't outright enemies yet. There was still some chance to change things.

The two Pokemon soon left the Hoenn mainland behind and flew toward Sootopolis Island. Flying was far faster than walking or sailing. Only a few hours later, the island came into view. Zinnia didn't land there. She used it as a landmark and turned southwest.

Countless small islands swept past beneath them. After almost another hour, a seemingly deserted island appeared ahead. Zinnia began to descend. Ethan signaled Dragonite to follow while he studied their destination.

It was a small island, no larger than two football fields put together. Apart from a few low hills and yellow sand covering the ground, it was bare.

Why bring us here?

He wondered, but gave no outward sign of it. The two Pokemon landed, their wings scattering sand. Ethan climbed down and looked around. Something was wrong.

The island was so desolate that there wasn't a single wild Pokemon nearby. He saw no bird Pokemon, not even a Water-type in the surrounding sea. That was far from normal.

The more unusual the place seemed, the more Ethan acted as though nothing concerned him. He kept his expression easy and gave away no hint of what he thought. Let Zinnia wonder what he knew.

It worked. Seeing him so calm, she felt some of her earlier doubts fade. Had this man really been to Sky Pillar before? Otherwise, how could he remain so composed at the sight of this place?

Chapter 725: Sky Pillar

Ethan followed Zinnia across the yellow sand toward the center of the island. He could see almost all of it at a glance, yet there was no Sky Pillar in sight. A tower that reached into the clouds should have been visible from far away. Where was it?

Zinnia soon gave him the answer. Between two weathered rocky hills, she took a small key-shaped ornament from inside her clothes and placed it in a carefully concealed recess in a stone statue. Light flared, and the view beyond the hills changed.

There was still yellow sand, but the cramped island opened into an immense desert, dozens of times larger than it had appeared from outside. At the far edge of his sight rose a huge stone tower that thrust toward the sky.

Sky Pillar.

So this was the barrier Zinnia had said the people of Sootopolis had put in place. It hid the island's true nature completely, making it look from outside like an unremarkable deserted island. Inside was another world. How had they created it? And how had they built a stone tower hundreds, perhaps a thousand, meters tall? It was astonishing.

Zinnia glanced at Ethan again. His expression hadn't changed, so she looked away. With protection like this, she truly couldn't understand how he could have found the place before.

One final trial remains, she said, looking ahead. The sand here can swallow your feet. The sun is fierce, and the winds are strong. Anyone acknowledged as worthy must cross the dunes on foot to reach the tower. It tests their resolve, and it is how we Draconid people honor our ancestors and Rayquaza

A shadow shot past her before she could finish. Ethan was already on Dragonite's back. In the blink of an eye, he had flown far ahead.

Zinnia stood speechless.

Misty covered her mouth, smiling at her. Looks like I'll have to walk there with you.

Zinnia had no answer to that either. She clenched her fists, watched Ethan recede into the distance, and finally let out a helpless sigh.

...

The dunes swept past beneath Dragonite. The entrance was at least five or six kilometers from Sky Pillar. That would be an easy distance on level ground, but trudging through this sand would be exhausting.

As for Zinnia's trial? He wasn't here because the Draconid people had chosen him. He had come to take Rayquaza. There was no reason to observe their customs or waste his strength on the walk.

Within minutes, he reached Sky Pillar. From below, it was even more magnificent. He tipped his head back, but its upper reaches disappeared into the white clouds.

Heavy stone formed its walls. After untold years, the exterior remained largely intact, marked by age but scarcely damaged. One great door was the tower's only entrance. Dozens of narrow windows on each level admitted light.

The Dragonhark altar lay at the very top. If he flew straight up, he might be able to draw Rayquaza there. First, though, he needed something else.

He patted Dragonite's neck and had it land beside the door. After jumping down onto solid ground, he looked back. Zinnia and Misty were nowhere in sight. Even after he had gone ahead, Zinnia was sticking to her people's tradition and crossing on foot. He hardly knew what to make of her stubbornness, but it gave him time.

He pushed open the heavy door and entered Sky Pillar.

Creak...

The great door, unopened for who knew how many years, swung aside. The ground floor was a broad hall, perhaps two or three hundred square meters. It was much more ruined inside than the tower's exterior suggested. Broken pillars lay everywhere, and murals covered the walls, though most were hard to make out. Wind had blown sand through the windows and buried parts of the floor. The weight of years was palpable.

Sunlight came through the small windows, keeping the hall brighter than he had expected. Yet the moment Ethan stepped inside, he sensed something strange he couldn't put into words. The air and walls felt as though an unusual power protected them. That made sense. Without something sustaining it, a building this old would surely have collapsed long ago.

He looked at the murals. Though they had no captions, their subject was clear: the ancient battle between Primal Kyogre and Primal Groudon, and Mega Rayquaza's intervention thousands of years ago. The Draconid people had preserved the event in stone as well as in oral tradition. Even if their history was interrupted, the murals could carry the legend forward.

Ethan took out his Poke Balls and released several of his Pokemon.

Spread out, he told them. Search every floor from here upward for a peculiar stone.

Gengar emerged as well. A stone? What does it look like?

I'm not entirely sure. I only know it's unusual and resembles a Key Stone.

A Key Stone? Gengar sounded startled. Here? Is it meant for Rayquaza? You told me Rayquaza doesn't need a Key Stone or a Mega Stone to Mega Evolve!

It doesn't. Ethan hesitated. That's why I don't know what this thing really is. But I know Rayquaza responds to it.

He found it puzzling himself. In theory, Rayquaza only needed to learn Dragon Ascent to Mega Evolve. Neither a Key Stone nor a Mega Stone was required. Yet he clearly remembered the official anime showing the black Rayquaza notice this stone, turn away from Zinnia, and react to it instead. Whatever it was, getting hold of it couldn't hurt.

Ethan clapped to bring his Pokemon's attention back to him. Let's move. We have to find it before Zinnia catches up.

They scattered through the tower, searching floor by floor. As he remembered it, the stone was round and about the size of a fist. Most of it looked like an ordinary pebble, but one face bore a mark like the distinctive part of a Mega Stone.

Each floor wasn't especially large, yet the search was slow. The first two levels held plenty of sand. Higher up, there was almost none, making it less likely that the stone had been buried. The real problem was the damage: broken columns, stairs, and reliefs had left countless fragments of similarly colored stone scattered around. They hid and confused anything that might be the one he wanted.

Some parts of the floor were cracked as well. A patch that looked solid could give way under a foot and send someone tumbling down with the stones. That slowed Ethan further. At least he remembered the stone was round, allowing him to dismiss many fragments at a glance.

Then an idea struck him. He took out a flashlight and swept its beam across the tower. The stone's polished face should reflect the light, and his Pokemon would notice even a brief glint.

It worked. As they reached the stairs between the seventh and eighth floors, the beam crossed a corner and a flash of reflected light appeared for an instant. Eevee's sharp eyes caught it.

Eevee called excitedly, scampered over, and brought back a round stone in its mouth. Ethan took it. Just as he remembered from the anime, a Key Stone-like pattern was faintly visible on one face, gleaming brightly in the flashlight beam.

He had actually found it.

Well done! Ethan laughed and stroked Eevee's head. With this, he could attract Rayquaza's attention. Perhaps it might even let Rayquaza Mega Evolve without Dragon Ascent someday.

He had barely put the stone in his bag and was about to call his Pokemon back when Misty's voice came from below.

Huh? Ethan, what are you doing?

He turned. Misty was climbing the stairs, looking baffled. Beside her, Zinnia watched him with open suspicion.

Ethan glanced at Zinnia and smiled. Nothing. Just looking at the murals.

Did looking at murals require him to release his Pokemon? His answer only made Zinnia more suspicious. She looked at the Pokemon around him. He had left her behind and reached the tower early; surely he had done something while she wasn't there. But she had arrived too late to catch him at it.

How infuriating. She had no idea what he was plotting. Since he plainly wasn't going to explain, she suppressed her unease, kept her face blank, and continued up the stairs.

Once she was halfway to the next floor, Ethan recalled all his Pokemon except Dragonite and followed. He fell into step beside Misty.

You walked the whole way? he asked.

Yes. The dunes really were hard to cross, and the wind was strong. I got sand in my eyes more than once.

Ethan glanced ahead and lowered his voice. Did Zinnia say anything to you?

No. She looked preoccupied. We didn't exchange a word the whole way. Misty couldn't hold back her own question. Why did you bring her along? Was it only so she could open that barrier?

She knew why Ethan had come, but to her, it made little sense. He had already had chances to catch Rayquaza before. Why come all the way here?

Ethan only smiled. Finding the island and opening the barrier were part of it. The main reason he had brought Zinnia, though, was luck.

Yes, luck. He was the only one who knew Zinnia had been the key to summoning the black Rayquaza in the anime. It was like drawing a rare prize in a game. Any Rayquaza might respond to a disturbance atop Sky Pillar, and he had already encountered Rayquaza twice. But would some other approach bring the exceptionally rare black one? Perhaps. Probably not.

He didn't dare gamble on his own luck. He had never even found a single Shiny Pokemon. Maybe they simply weren't meant for him.

Zinnia, on the other hand, had summoned that Rayquaza once in the anime. Even if it had been coincidence, he trusted her luck more than his own. That was why he had arranged for her to come. He sincerely hoped her extraordinary luck would hold and call the black Rayquaza again.

Chapter 726: Fair Competition

The three of them climbed in silence. After another ten minutes or more, their legs aching, they finally reached the top of Sky Pillar.

They emerged onto a high triangular platform. As they stepped onto it, four green flames suddenly sprang up in stone basins at its corners. The flames appeared without warning, eerie and mysterious, as though announcing something to the sky or lighting the way for someone.

This had to be Sky Pillar's most important place: the Dragonhark altar.

It didn't look like much of an altar to Ethan. Apart from its stone floor and a slightly raised set of steps, there was nothing here. He went to the edge and looked down. Thick clouds surrounded the tower, although there should not have been clouds this dense at its height. They looked almost manufactured, meant to hide the view. The Draconid people had been thorough in protecting this place.

They had reached their destination. It was time for the next step. Ethan and Zinnia turned toward one another.

After a long silence, Zinnia spoke first. I brought you here as promised. Will you tell me your plan now?

The journey and the long walk across the sand had given her time to calm down. She was beginning to suspect Ethan had deliberately made her angry before. But it was too late to dwell on that. He was already inside her people's sacred place, and their rules had been broken. She could hardly undo it now. Was she really going to make an enemy of him and drive him out?

What plan? Ethan shrugged. I'll summon Rayquaza and try to catch it. I was hoping you'd handle the summoning.

Me? She gave him a cool glance. Have you forgotten what I told you? Summoning Rayquaza requires the Rainbow Meteorite. It was lost long ago.

Surely that's not the only way. Ethan studied her, but didn't press the point yet. There's something I've been meaning to ask. You keep mentioning this meteorite. What does it look like?

Zinnia shook her head. I don't know exactly. It disappeared in my parents' time. I've only heard that it has a mysterious power: it attracts Rayquaza and can make it Mega Evolve into a stronger form.

It could make Rayquaza Mega Evolve too? That sounded remarkably like the round, Key Stone-like rock he had just found. Was the stone in his bag the Rainbow Meteorite?

Perhaps the Draconid people had searched for it outside the tower for decades while it had been here all along, hidden in plain sight. The idea was far-fetched, but possible. It would explain the stone's unusual shape, the Key Stone-like feature, and its power.

So you've never seen the Rainbow Meteorite yourself?

Zinnia didn't answer. That was answer enough. Losing her people's greatest treasure was hardly something she wanted to keep discussing with an outsider.

Ethan took the stone from his bag and held it out in front of her. She looked at it, surprised he would produce an ordinary-looking round rock now, but said nothing. Ethan watched her face closely. She seemed genuinely unmoved. She hadn't lied; she didn't recognize it.

Then he turned the stone to reveal the Key Stone-like mark. Zinnia's pupils contracted.

Wait. Is that...?

He caught the flash of surprise. Ethan tossed the stone lightly up and down. Her gaze followed every rise and fall.

Where did you get one of those? she asked.

You recognize it?

She hesitated, then nodded. From its shape, that's a Meteorite Key Stone.

A Meteorite Key Stone? So it wasn't the Rainbow Meteorite after all. Ethan was surprised to have guessed wrong, but it hardly mattered. He turned his attention to what she had identified.

Most Key Stones in this world were dug out of mountains. A very small number reached the planet aboard falling meteorites. Both kinds could enable a Pokemon to Mega Evolve, but Meteorite Key Stones supposedly held an unusual cosmic energy. So few had been found that scientists still did not understand what, if anything, made them different.

Rumor claimed that Pokemon Mega Evolved through a Meteorite Key Stone gained strength beyond what an ordinary Key Stone could provide, thanks to that cosmic energy. There was no evidence to support it. Still, Ethan thought a rumor like that might have some basis.

He smiled. Then perhaps I should replace my old Key Stone with this one.

His pleased expression made Zinnia ask again, Where exactly did you find it?

Didn't you just see me?

She remembered finding him on the stairs surrounded by Pokemon, all of them apparently searching for something. So that was it. But how had he known a Meteorite Key Stone was there? He had claimed to have visited Sky Pillar before. Had he seen it then?

She was curious, though the stone itself was of little importance to her. An ordinary Key Stone and a Meteorite Key Stone served much the same purpose in her plans.

Misty listened to them. She didn't follow every part of their conversation, but she knew Ethan had found something valuable, and she was sincerely happy for him.

Ethan, meanwhile, finally understood why this stone had drawn Rayquaza's attention in the anime. It must have been the cosmic energy inside it.

Let's set the stone aside, he said to Zinnia. I won't hide why I asked you to bring me here. I do need your help.

I've told you already. The Rainbow Meteorite is gone. I can't help you.

Are you sure? Ethan's eyes moved to the Key Stones bound around her right leg. You've prepared for this. Haven't you gathered a large number of them?

Zinnia's eyes widened. How... how do you know that?

It was her greatest secret. She was an exceptional talent among the Draconid people, stronger than others her age and relentlessly determined. After the failure involving Deoxys last time, she had searched desperately for a way to summon Rayquaza without the Rainbow Meteorite. At last she had thought of one: sacrifice a large number of Key Stones to draw Rayquaza's attention and bring it down.

The theory and her experiments suggested it could work. Only the real attempt remained. Yet she had developed the method privately and told no one. How could Ethan know? Could he foresee the future? Did he have an informant among the Draconid people? An informant might even explain his claim that he had been here before. But was that possible?

Ethan interrupted her spiraling thoughts. I won't ask for your help for nothing. You've been traveling in such a hurry these past few days that you probably haven't heard the latest news.

That much was true. Zinnia had spent most of her journey in the air, traveling day and night with only one thought: reaching Lilycove City and meeting him. She had paid little attention to anything else.

What are you getting at? she asked.

Ethan looked to Misty, who understood and explained. Yesterday, outside LaRousse City, two Deoxys fought Rayquaza and defeated it. Someone filmed the battle, and the video has spread online. It's caused quite a stir.

Rayquaza? Deoxys? Zinnia frowned at Ethan. What happened? Did you cause it?

She did not doubt Misty's account. A quick search would verify it, and she didn't think Ethan would invent a story like this.

Of course, he said. I'm telling you because I want you to know I can encounter Rayquaza, and I have the strength to defeat and catch one.

Zinnia didn't question that. She had seen enough when he captured Deoxys to understand what he could do. But why bring it up now? Was he simply boasting?

If you help summon Rayquaza this time, Ethan continued, I'll do my best to help you catch one as well. You and your people could fulfill the goal you've pursued your whole lives.

For an instant, Zinnia's heart leapt so fiercely she could barely contain herself. She took a deep breath and forced herself to think.

If catching one is so easy for you, she asked, why do you need my help?

Ethan looked up at the sky, trying to appear inscrutable. That doesn't matter. Will you accept the deal?

A deal... She considered it, then shook her head. I can summon and catch Rayquaza myself. I don't need your help. But I'll give you a fair chance to compete.

Ethan regarded her with surprise. She had turned down an easier opportunity and chosen to rely on herself. She must have considerable faith in her own strength. It suited him, though. It would save him the trouble of catching another Rayquaza for her.

What do you mean by a fair chance?

I'll summon Rayquaza. After that, which of us it chooses, and which of us it fights, will depend on our abilities.

Ethan nodded. There was some risk in that arrangement: he might lose his chance at the black Rayquaza, if it appeared. But with the Meteorite Key Stone in hand, he felt confident he could attract its attention.

And if he truly had no chance with Rayquaza, so be it. He had gone this long without a Shiny Pokemon. Missing one more would not ruin his life.

Agreed. Then please summon it.

Not yet. With the matter settled, Zinnia relaxed. She sat on the nearby stone steps. We need to wait until nightfall.

Nightfall? Ethan wondered whether there was some special reason.

Nothing complicated. My chances of successfully summoning Rayquaza are better at night.

That was all? He hadn't expected such an answer. Still, the more she relied on this kind of luck, the better he felt about their chances of drawing the black Rayquaza. Luck had its own rules, after all.

He looked at the sky. The sun was blazing overhead. It was only just past noon, at the hottest part of the day. They had a long wait ahead.

Chapter 727: Battling the Black Rayquaza

They waited from noon into afternoon, from afternoon into evening, and from evening deep into the night. They ate twice, and Ethan even groomed his Pokemon. At last, the moment Zinnia had been waiting for arrived.

Ethan stretched, recalled all his Pokemon except Gardevoir and Dragonite, and went to stand beside her.

Stars filled the sky. By chance, a meteor shower crossed it now, countless bright streaks trailing long tails through the darkness. The sight was magnificent.

It's beautiful... Misty murmured. Even during her travels, she had rarely seen anything like it. She might only be accompanying Ethan, but the climb up such a tall tower had been worth it for this view.

The meteors were beautiful, but Ethan and Zinnia had their attention elsewhere.

It's time, Zinnia said.

She took a deep breath, stood in the center of the altar, and raised her right hand toward the deep night sky. At once, the Key Stones wound around her leg shone green. The light ran up her calf and gathered along her arm. Ethan could not tell how she did it, but the green flames in the stone basins flared to more than a meter high. Her cloak and hair stirred without wind. When she opened her hand, several round Key Stones lay in her palm.

Green light enveloped them. Zinnia closed both hands around the stones, held them over her head, and called to the sky, Rayquaza!

This was the summoning method she had devised by combining a sacrifice of Key Stones with her people's secret arts. The green light in her hands burned like a beacon.

Almost immediately, a thick pillar of light plunged from the sky toward the Dragonhark altar. Something long and twisting moved within the green beam as it descended.

Roar!

A deafening cry came from inside. They could not yet see its source, but Ethan knew that roar. It belonged to Hoenn's Legendary Pokemon, Rayquaza.

The green pillar vanished, revealing a Shiny Rayquaza with a black body before them.

It had worked. Zinnia had summoned Rayquaza! Its color was strikingly different from an ordinary Rayquaza's, which only made her joy stronger. Her method really worked.

Ethan was delighted too. All the thought and time he had invested had paid off: she had called the black Rayquaza he wanted.

The green light slowly faded, its last traces making the black Rayquaza look even more imposing. Zinnia quickly opened her hand and presented the Key Stones, still faintly glowing, to it.

Rayquaza, please hear my wish! she called, hope and fervor in her voice.

Summoning Rayquaza was only the first step. What mattered was whom it would choose.

As soon as she finished speaking, the green light around Rayquaza disappeared. The glow around her Key Stones went out with it. Even the flames in the basins shrank into tiny flickers.

Zinnia stared from Rayquaza to the dull stones in her hand.

It didn't choose me? Why? I did everything...

The light seemed to leave her eyes as well. Then she noticed another glow behind her. She turned slowly.

Ethan's Meteorite Key Stone shone brightly in his hand, as though calling out to something. Rayquaza's attention had shifted to it. The Pokemon roared at him.

It's reacting to the Meteorite Key Stone? Zinnia said.

Ethan looked down at the stone and then up at her. It seems Rayquaza has chosen me.

She stared at him, eyes wide, her thoughts impossible to read. Ethan did not try to provoke her. He walked past and stopped before Rayquaza, leaving Zinnia to watch his retreating back.

The black Rayquaza regarded him from above. He met its gaze and liked it more the longer he looked. Its strength was no different from that of a green Rayquaza, but its black coloring was undeniably more striking. One glance was enough to remember it.

He would not risk delaying. Ethan took the Ultra Ball he had prepared.

It's up to you now. Go, Deoxys!

He threw the ball. It opened, and his Deoxys appeared before Rayquaza.

The black Rayquaza clearly had never encountered a Deoxys. It sensed the power in this unfamiliar Pokemon, though, and fixed it with a cold stare. Deoxys had the advantage of experience: it had faced Rayquaza's kind several times and knew what such an opponent could do. Few Rayquaza ever had a chance to fight a Deoxys. Against an equally strong foe it did not understand, this one could easily suffer for that lack of knowledge.

Both Pokemon prepared themselves, the tension between them rising. Rayquaza looked ready to attack when Zinnia finally broke her silence.

I...

Whatever it is, let's talk after the battle, Ethan said, cutting her off with a wave without looking back.

He didn't know what she wanted to say. Right now it didn't matter. The black Rayquaza was in front of him, and he needed to focus on it.

Zinnia hesitated, sighed, and stepped aside without another word. She had agreed to a fair contest before summoning Rayquaza. Unhappy as she was with the outcome, she had to let Ethan take his chance.

Ethan faced Rayquaza again. Let's see what you can do.

Deoxys, this battle is yours!

Deoxys moved. It placed a hand near its core and released the energy it had been gathering, sending a blast straight at Rayquaza. Rayquaza had been guarding against an attack; at nearly the same instant, it fired a powerful beam from its mouth. The two attacks collided.

Boom!

The resulting burst of energy blazed against the night, dazzling and dangerous.

That was the end of their opening test. They rushed at each other, and the fight at close and middle range began in earnest. The two Legendary Pokemon grappled, twisted, and chased each other above Sky Pillar so quickly they were almost impossible to follow. Gardevoir's telepathy let Ethan guide Deoxys throughout.

Ethan had commanded fierce battles before, but these two were different. Beyond a limited amount of guidance, he could do little to direct them. Much of what they could do was not tied to a fixed set of moves.

For a Trainer, that was both a blessing and a frustration. Pokemon this powerful could use their abilities freely, without being constrained by familiar moves. They could surprise an opponent in ways it could hardly defend against. On the other hand, Ethan could give only a broad plan of attack rather than precise instructions for every exchange. It left a Trainer in an awkward position.

He did not mind. If giving Deoxys room to act helped it defeat and capture Rayquaza, what did it matter? Nor was he merely a spectator. He might not dictate each movement, but his experience let him read some of Rayquaza's intentions and warn Deoxys in time.

After Deoxys missed one attack, Rayquaza abruptly twisted and lunged with its jaws open. The counterattack came at exactly the right moment, during a gap in Deoxys's offense. Against an evenly matched opponent, a bite from behind at that instant would be hard to avoid.

But Ethan had watched every movement. He caught Rayquaza's intention as soon as it turned and sent the warning through Gardevoir.

As though it had eyes in the back of its head, Deoxys used Teleport without even looking around. Rayquaza's jaws closed on empty air. Deoxys reappeared behind it and struck the would-be attacker with a sphere of energy.

Rayquaza cried out. Below, Misty raised a fist in delight.

Yes! Keep it up!

She had no stake in catching the Pokemon herself, but she was firmly on Ethan's side. Every advantage he gained thrilled her.

Zinnia's feelings were far less simple. Rayquaza had not chosen her, and part of her did not want Ethan to catch it. If he failed, they might be on equal footing again and she could have another chance.

Yet this was an extraordinary opportunity. She had summoned Rayquaza herself and could not bear to see it simply fly away, even if she was not the one to catch it. No human had ever succeeded in capturing a Rayquaza. Ethan was not one of the Draconid people, and their relationship had been strained, but his strength was undeniable. If anyone was to accomplish such a feat, she would rather it be a Trainer of his caliber than some unknown person.

Above them, the black Rayquaza grew angrier after being struck from behind. Its attacks became fiercer, wilder, and harder to predict.

Ethan knew it was pressing its offensive advantage, but he was not afraid. Deoxys was its equal in strength and had a Trainer supporting it. Rather than retreat, he ordered Deoxys to change from Normal Forme to Attack Forme and meet Rayquaza head-on.

The fight intensified at once. They clashed in the air, then crashed down onto the Dragonhark altar, forcing Ethan and the others to dodge out of their path. They fought back into the sky, vanished into the clouds, and finally emerged above the tower again. Every place they reached became part of the battlefield.

Each collision of their attacks exploded with a thunderous sound that echoed across the island. Fortunately, they were far from any settlement. Ethan did not have to worry about drawing a crowd or damaging anyone's property. He could let Deoxys fight with everything it had.

Neither Pokemon wanted to yield. Deoxys had Ethan's command and was determined to defeat the opponent he wanted to catch. Rayquaza had a fierce temper of its own. Having been summoned here, it had no intention of slinking away.

For both, only one thought remained: defeat the other at any cost.

Chapter 728: Caught!

Boom!

High above them, two terrifying bursts of energy collided. The shock wave swept every cloud from around Sky Pillar, clearing the sky for kilometers around the battlefield.

Even the tower trembled, the shaking particularly strong at its summit. For perhaps the first time since it had been built, the whole structure stood exposed, with nothing hiding it from view.

Thousands of years ago, the Draconid people had built Sky Pillar to be sturdy and protected it with a strange power. They must have expected battles here someday and wanted the tower to survive them. But they could hardly have imagined a Pokemon as strong as Rayquaza fighting against it.

Under the power of the two combatants, Sky Pillar stood like a lighthouse in a storm, enduring the thunder and wind while giving every impression that it might finally fail. The fight had pushed it past what it should have been able to withstand. Fortunately, the Dragonhark altar was not their main battlefield, so the tower took fewer direct hits.

Even so, Misty felt the floor shudder beneath her. She braced herself against a stone pillar and edged toward Dragonite. Being close to it made her feel a little safer. If the tower fell, Dragonite could rescue her at once.

Dragonite sensed her worry, turned with a smile, and gave her a thumbs-up.

Ethan and Zinnia barely noticed the shaking. Both stared at the battle above. It had reached its decisive point. Though the clash had been brief, its intensity had drained both Pokemon. Each had taken enough hits for its condition to deteriorate badly. They still attacked fiercely, but neither had the overwhelming presence it had shown at the start.

Ethan knew it was time to change tactics. Through Gardevoir's telepathy, he told Deoxys to shift from Attack Forme to Speed Forme. It stopped trading close-range blows with the black Rayquaza and began harrying it instead.

The change worked immediately. Rayquaza had grown used to its opponent's relentless offense. Deoxys's sudden burst of speed caught it unprepared, and for a time it could scarcely track where Deoxys went.

In Speed Forme, Deoxys's attacks were weaker, but only by the standards of Legendary Pokemon. They still struck hard enough to trouble a powerful attacker with limited defenses like Rayquaza. More importantly, Rayquaza had already lost too much stamina to adjust.

Whoosh! Whoosh! Whoosh!

Deoxys became little more than a blur. Under that constant pressure, the black Rayquaza began to lose ground. It roared and twisted its long body, seemingly trying to goad Deoxys into fighting it head-on again.

A wild Pokemon might have taken the bait. Ethan would not throw away the advantage he had worked to create. First, he had matched Rayquaza blow for blow with Deoxys in Attack Forme. Once Rayquaza was exhausted, Deoxys's speed let it stay beyond reach while landing hit after hit.

It sounded simple. Against a nearly equal opponent, guiding a battle to this point required a Trainer's full attention and careful choices. That was what a Trainer could offer: help a Pokemon perform beyond its usual limits, turn a balanced fight into an advantage, and make the impossible possible. It was one of the greatest differences between a wild Pokemon and one fighting beside a human.

Now it was time to finish the fight.

Deoxys made copies of itself and slipped past Rayquaza once more. The real Deoxys appeared behind it and struck with another powerful sphere of energy, hitting it squarely in the back.

The blast staggered Rayquaza. Pain crossed its face.

Zinnia's heart nearly leapt from her chest. Now! she shouted.

I know!

Ethan had seen the opening too. He pulled out the Ultra Ball he had prepared and hurled it skyward. Before all three of them, the spinning ball climbed more than ten meters and snapped open. Red light wrapped around the black Rayquaza and drew it inside.

Ethan's nerves tightened. He had caught many Legendary Pokemon, but Rayquaza stood near the top of the food chain. He could hardly remain calm at the prospect of catching oneespecially a black Shiny Rayquaza, the Pokemon he had dreamed of having.

The Ultra Ball fell onto the Dragonhark altar with a soft clack. It rolled several times, stopped, and shook violently. Rayquaza was making one last struggle inside.

But it was already injured. Even if it escaped, Deoxys would be waiting, along with Ethan's next Ultra Ball. The outcome felt inevitable.

Ultra Balls were one of the more expensive and prominent Poke Ball products. Like ordinary Poke Balls and Great Balls, they sometimes drew complaints about failed captures. That had more to do with how people used themand a measure of luckthan any lack of quality. Their success rate could be trusted.

This one gave Ethan reason to believe it. After several fierce shakes, the movement slowed. Each sway was smaller than the last. It might truly work.

Ethan's eyes brightened. Misty clenched both fists as if she could lend the ball her strength. Come on!

She knew there was much she had not seen or heard of, but she had never heard of anyone in her lifetime catching Rayquaza. This was no ordinary Pokemon. It was Hoenn's Legendary Rayquaza. Would Ethan be the first to accomplish it? Would she witness that moment?

They watched with hope while Zinnia looked on with mixed feelings. After only a few seconds more, the ball gave a final click, and its light went out.

Yes! Misty cried as soon as she saw the capture succeed.

She bounded over and threw her arms around Ethan's head. His face was pressed into her chest, and he felt its soft, still-developing curves. He pulled free so he could breathe again, looked at the Ultra Ball resting quietly on the altar, and laughed.

One ball. That was all it had taken. Perhaps there really was a reason Ultra Balls cost more.

He remembered how he had once needed his whole team to face Zapdos. Now Deoxys had beaten Rayquaza one-on-one. Rayquazahe had truly caught one! He had accomplished in this world something that had once been possible only in a game. Excitement surged through him.

He took a deep breath, eased out of Misty's embrace, and walked toward the ball.

Zinnia watched him pick it up. Her hands clenched into fists, then slowly loosened. The battle had shown her the power of top-tier Pokemon, a level beyond ordinary opponents and far beyond anything she could currently reach. If she had fought Rayquaza herself, even sending out her entire team might not have been enough. Ethan had defeated it with one Pokemon.

Monsters, she thought. Both Trainer and Pokemon.

Ethan knew nothing of her thoughts. The instant he held the Ultra Ball, his own emotions became surprisingly calm. It might have been his imagination, but the ball felt heavier now, as though he could sense the black Rayquaza's immense life force within it.

He did not release Rayquaza again. He put the ball straight into the pouch at his waist. At the same time, the Meteorite Key Stone he carried returned to normal. That gave him a bold idea, though testing it would have to wait for another opportunity.

Footsteps sounded beside him. Zinnia approached.

Guardian Rayquaza chose you, and you caught it. Congratulations.

The meteor shower had vanished sometime during the fight. By moonlight and the green flames around them, Ethan studied Zinnia's face. It was calm, revealing nothing.

Thank you, he said. You tried to tell me something before the battle. You can say it now.

It doesn't matter anymore. She glanced at the pouch, as if she could somehow see Rayquaza inside the ball. I wanted to tell you what I knew about its weaknesses. Clearly, you didn't need it.

Rayquaza's weaknesses? Ethan paused, then shook his head. The Draconid people might know something about its body, but its greatest vulnerability was simple enough: as a Dragon- and Flying-type, it was four times as weak to Ice-type attacks. Perhaps that was what she had meant to tell him. Most people knew too little about Rayquaza even to identify its types, much less plan around them.

Zinnia wasn't as stubborn as she had seemed. Once she knew she would not catch it herself, she had still meant to share what she knew rather than keep it to herself. Ethan's opinion of her improved. He had stopped her before she could speak, but the gesture still mattered.

And the Draconid people had spent thousands of years pursuing this goal without achieving it. How many of them had gone to their graves with that longing unfulfilled?

I understand how you feel, Ethan said after a moment. Well, I'm in a good mood today. Listen: the offer I made earlier still stands. When I can, I'll do my best to help you catch a Rayquaza and fulfill your people's wish.

Zinnia stared at him in disbelief. It took her a long time to find her voice. Why?

I told you. I'm happy today, and you didn't interfere with the battle. I appreciate that. Ethan changed tack. But perhaps you won't need my help. You just managed to summon Rayquaza on your own, without the Rainbow Meteorite.

Zinnia looked at the dull Key Stones scattered on the floor and sighed. It's not so easy. These weren't ordinary Key Stones. Our people spent years finding stones that reacted to Rayquaza. Each one took enormous effort to obtain. Now their energy is exhausted, and they're useless. Besides, the offering summoned Rayquaza, but that was all. It didn't choose me.

That's because you're too rigid, Ethan said. What does being chosen have to do with it? Beat Rayquaza with your own strength, throw a Poke Ball, and there you are. You've chosen it.

You don't understand. Zinnia sounded weary. This is our tradition. We aren't allowed to change it.

And that's why you still haven't caught a single Rayquaza.

His words struck hard. Ethan gave her one last look and beckoned Misty over. Once they were both on Dragonite, he looked down at Zinnia, much as Rayquaza had looked down on them earlier.

I've never let tradition decide everything for me. That's how I caught so many Legendary Pokemon in such a short time. I've said enough. I have other things to do. Think it over. When you're ready, contact meassuming I have time.

Dragonite spread its wings without waiting for an order and flew into the distance.

Ethan was gone, but his words continued to echo in Zinnia's mind.

That's why you still haven't caught a single Rayquaza.

The sentence struck like a hammer. Had they really followed their traditions too closely? Without the Rainbow Meteorite, they couldn't summon Rayquaza. Without being chosen, they couldn't carry on their role. Were those beliefs wrong?

No one was there to answer her. Zinnia stood motionless, watching Ethan disappear. Her heart pounded as his words and the image of him played over and over in her mind.

Chapter 729: Tate and Liza

Ethan and Misty left the island that held Sky Pillar on Dragonite. They flew through the night to a nearby island covered in green, pitched a tent, and rested there. The next morning, after recovering their strength and eating breakfast, they set off again.

Where next? After some thought, Ethan chose the Mossdeep Gym in Mossdeep City.

Neither Shelly nor Courtney had sent any news, so Archie and Maxie evidently had not begun to act. Ethan had prepared for them, but there was no reason to wait idly in the meantime. He could use the interval to challenge a Gym and win another Badge.

He had planned to go to Fortree City, but Mossdeep was closer to his current position at sea. Plans did not always survive a change in circumstances. It seemed he would be following Ash's route after all, although Ash had probably challenged Mossdeep Gym and left already.

Dragonite raced over the wide ocean. Flying close to the water put it in a playful mood. Without warning, it rolled sideways to show off, nearly throwing Ethan and Misty off its back.

You little... Ethan rapped it on the head. Dragonite barely felt the blow. It grinned, then settled down.

A school of Mantine leapt from the water and glided alongside them for a while before returning to the sea. The breeze on Ethan's face felt wonderful.

His mood was much lighter than it had been when he crossed these waters with Zinnia the day before. The sky seemed bluer, and even the sea looked clearer. Nothing around him had changed. Catching Rayquazaand a Shiny one at thathad changed the way he saw everything.

He felt kindly disposed toward everyone. If he saw a Team Rocket grunt fall over right now, he might even stop to help them up.

...

Mossdeep City lay on an island off the northeastern corner of Hoenn. Like Sootopolis City, it was separated from the mainland, but Mossdeep sat near the region's northeastern edge. It was less bustling than the larger cities. Its green hills, clear water, and coastal setting gave it a charm of its own.

Wailmer and Wailord lived nearby. People could stand on the shore and watch some of the largest Pokemon in the sea at close range.

The Mossdeep Space Center was another of the city's famous sights. Researchers there studied space and launched rockets, making it one of Hoenn's important scientific facilities. The Sunflora weather satellite and the crewed Ho-Oh III rocket had both launched from here. Above all, its researchers were interested in Pokemon hidden deep in space and still unknown to humanityPokemon like Ethan's Deoxys.

Its location was said to have been chosen for Mossdeep's mild weather. The surrounding sea was clear for much of the year. Strong winds, heavy rain, and other extreme conditions were rare, which made rocket launches easier.

None of that was Ethan's purpose in coming. He had one destination: Mossdeep Gym.

The city's official Gym was unusual. It had two Gym Leaders, a rarity even on a world scale: Liza and Tate, the Mystic Combination. They were twins, Liza the older sister and Tate the younger brother. Perhaps their youth and their exceptional ability had persuaded the League to let them run the Gym together.

Both specialized in Psychic-type Pokemon. They were even said to understand each other's thoughts without speaking and perhaps to read other people's minds. Psychic Gym Leaders seemed to have talents of their own. Sabrina did, and so did these twins. Even Phoebe, the Elite Four member Ethan had met recently, claimed she could converse with Ghost-type Pokemon.

Defeat the twins, and a challenger would earn the Mind Badge.

After landing on the island, Ethan did not go straight to the Gym. First he called Kennedy, the secretary at Devon Corporation. He wanted help cutting and polishing the Meteorite Key Stone he had found at Sky Pillar so that he could carry it like a normal Key Stone.

He had made up his mind the day he found it. Whether the rumored cosmic energy actually strengthened Mega Evolution or not, Meteorite Key Stone sounded far more impressive than an ordinary Key Stone. That alone was enough reason for him to make the switch.

Kennedy agreed readily, without even needing to ask Mr. Stone. Ethan had done Devon an enormous favor. This little job was nothing by comparison. A word to Kennedy's staff, and they would turn the stone into a beautifully finished piece.

Ethan thanked him and ended the call. He found a reputable courier, filled out the paperwork, and sent the stone to Kennedy. All he had to do now was wait. Within a few days, he expected to have a new Key Stone bracelet.

With that arranged, he and Misty finally headed for Mossdeep Gym. As they walked, they heard people all around them discussing the same recent event. Another rocket had launched successfully the previous morning. More than a day had passed, but the news remained a favorite topic at meals and in the streets.

That's a shame, Misty said, listening to the conversations. If we'd come a day earlier, we might have seen it launch. I've never watched a rocket take off in person. It must be spectacular.

Neither have I, in all twenty years of my life, Ethan said. It is a shame, but there'll be another chance. For me, what I gained yesterday would be worth missing rocket launches for the rest of my life.

Something occurred to him. We missed the launch, but Ash and the others probably didn't. I saw you talking to May earlier. Are they still here?

Misty shook her head. They beat the Gym yesterday and already left.

So we just missed each other.

Mossdeep Gym stood on the outskirts of the city. From outside, it looked more like a science museum than a Gym. Ethan was used to that. Gym Leaders' interests, other work, and ideas about design had given most Gyms strange appearances. He had seen much more unusual buildings than this one.

Inside, his impression held. The place felt like a large exhibition hall about rockets, space, and planets, filled with models and educational displays.

A woman working at the front desk stopped writing when they entered. Can I help you?

She looked about thirty-five, with thick, slightly wavy dark-blue hair and large round glasses. Her voice was gentle. She might have been an employee, but she also had the air of someone who belonged here.

Hello, Ethan said. I'd like to challenge the Gym. Are both Gym Leaders here?

Your timing is good. They just got back. Come, I'll take you to them.

She led Ethan and Misty deeper into the building and onto the battlefield. It was even more striking than the exhibits. The arena resembled the pitted surface of the moon. Darkness around it suggested the depths of space, while large planet models hung overhead and turned slowly, as if orbiting the field.

Ethan looked around with delight. No other Gym he had visited had felt quite so immersive, as though he had really stepped into outer space.

At one side of the arena, a boy and a girl in pale-blue martial arts outfits were practicing. They looked about ten years old, with similar fine features. Their hairstyles differed, and the girl had the slight beginnings of a figure, but otherwise they were difficult to tell apart.

These had to be Tate and Liza.

Liza, Tate, you have a challenger, the woman called.

They looked over together. Coming, Mom!

Mom? Ethan and Misty turned back to their guide. They had suspected she was more than an ordinary employee, but neither had expected her to be the Gym Leaders' mother. Looking closely, Ethan could see the family resemblance, especially in their dark-blue hair.

The girl came forward first and nodded to them. Hello. Welcome to Mossdeep Gym. I'm Liza, one of the Gym Leaders.

And I'm Tate, the other Gym Leader, the boy said.

I'm Ethan, your challenger.

I'm Misty. I'm traveling with him.

After those polite introductions, they moved straight to the match. Ethan and the twins took their places in the Trainer areas. Their mother went to the side of the field to referee.

My name is Rachel, she told Ethan. Before we begin, I need to explain this Gym's rules. First, the battlefield includes more than the ground in front of you. Those planets hanging from the ceiling are part of it too.

Ethan looked up at the models. Their size and position meant they could obstruct sight or block attacks. A Pokemon that could fly or jump high might even land on one and attack from above. The possibilities made this a truly three-dimensional battlefield. He would have to watch the air as carefully as the ground.

Rachel saw that he understood and continued. This is a Double Battle. Liza and Tate always use Solrock and Lunatone. You must send out two Pokemon at the same time. Neither side may switch Pokemon during the match. There is no time limit; the battle ends when one side's Pokemon can no longer fight.

With two Gym Leaders, Ethan had expected a Double Battle. He nodded to show he understood.

Then both sides, send out your Pokemon!

Liza and Tate released theirs almost simultaneously. As promised, they were Solrock and Lunatone, both Rock- and Psychic-types. Two flashes of blue light gave way to floating Pokemon shaped like the sun and moon.

Ethan studied them. He did not know either species particularly well. It wasn't that they were weak. They were simply obscure, had no evolutions, and looked unusual. Even when he played the games back on Earth, he caught them only to complete his Pokedex, never to use in battle.

Chapter 730: Sun and Moon Together

Misty knew little about the two Pokemon, so she took out her Pokedex in the stands and aimed it at Solrock first.

It looked like an orange meteorite, a round, uneven body with eight yellow stone spikes radiating from its sides and an eerie black pattern around its eyes. Its design might have drawn on the sun imagery of Renaissance art and mysticism, such as the Sun card in the tarot's Major Arcana.

The Pokedex responded at once. Solrock, the Meteorite Pokemon. Rock and Psychic type. Solrock is said to be a newly discovered Pokemon that fell from space, an embodiment of the sun that draws its power from sunlight. On clear days, Solrock gather in rows facing the sun to store solar energy, making them especially strong by day. They drift silently through the air, their expressions never changing, and can read an opponent's thoughts. By spinning, Solrock emit sunlight-like rays that temporarily blind their enemies.

Misty turned the Pokedex toward Lunatone. Its shape differed, resembling a brownish-yellow crescent moon, but it shared Solrock's strange meteorite-like appearance.

Lunatone, the Meteorite Pokemon. Rock and Psychic type. Lunatone were first found forty years ago at the site of a meteorite impact, leading some to believe they came from space, though that remains unproven. Research suggests the phases of the moon affect their condition and power. They become particularly active when bathed in a full moon's light. Their piercing red eyes inspire fear, and a stare can put an opponent to sleep.

Side by side, the two truly did look like the sun and moon. With the hanging planets above them, the battlefield had become a little solar system.

Ethan reached slowly for his Poke Balls. This would not be an easy fight. Tate and Liza had battled together for years and understood each other perfectly. He needed to choose his Pokemon with care.

After a moment's thought, he threw two balls. Go, Metang! Milotic!

Blue light flashed, and his Pokemon appeared opposite Solrock and Lunatone. On paper, both had useful type matchups against Rock- and Psychic-type opponents. Milotic's Water type and Metang's Steel and Psychic types appeared to give Ethan a considerable edge.

But battles were not decided on paper. The twins' Gym Pokemon would be strong and well practiced as a team, especially in this arena. Ethan's two Pokemon had evolved only recently and were still growing. They had never fought together in a Double Battle. Their lack of experience could easily outweigh their type advantage. Psychic-type Pokemon were troublesome in real combat, too.

He gave himself roughly even odds. That was only a prediction. Once the battle began, their performances would decide who held the advantage and who won.

Rachel saw that both sides were ready and signaled the start. Tate attacked first.

Solrock, Tackle!

Solrock crossed half the arena in a blink and bore down on Milotic. Ethan recognized the test. Tate had chosen a simple physical attack rather than a Psychic move, trying to gauge his opponent's strength. It might surprise a novice, but it was too direct to catch Ethan.

Milotic, Water Gun!

A long jet of water struck Solrock head-on, hurting it and stopping its charge. At nearly the same time, Lunatone came at Metang from another direction with Tackle. Ethan ordered Metang to meet it with Take Down rather than dodge.

Bang!

Take Down carried a measure of recoil for its user, but in this collision Metang was plainly the winner.

Ethan had won both exchanges of the opening round. Tate and Liza glanced at one another, caution showing in their eyes. This challenger was not ordinary.

They often opened Gym matches with these sudden charges. Their Pokemon had trained to deliver them with great speed and force, and few challengers could dodge or withstand them. Fewer still turned the exchange against them. The twins realized Ethan would be difficult and stopped holding back.

Lunatone, Ice Beam!

Solrock, Solar Beam!

Both Pokemon gathered power. Then two differently colored beams shot toward their targets. Lunatone's cold light and Solrock's brilliant orange-gold beam suited the moon-and-sun theme of the field perfectly.

Ethan gave two quick orders. Metang, Psychic! Milotic, Hydro Pump!

Four attacks met in the middle of the arena. The collision erupted with a roar. Heat from the explosion turned the water from Hydro Pump into steam, which spread across more than half the battlefield.

Neither side could see through it. Ethan kept his Pokemon back rather than send them blindly into the cloud. But when the steam thinned, Solrock and Lunatone were gone from the ground.

Where had they gone? Ethan was surprised only for an instant. He looked up and spotted them hiding behind one of the large planet models beneath the ceiling.

Of course. They had used the steam to take cover and prepare a surprise attack. He had found them in time.

Across the field, the twins were startled that he had discovered them so quickly. This was a favorite tactic of theirs. Challengers heard about the hanging planets before a match, but many still forgot to watch overhead once the fighting began. By the time they noticed the hidden Pokemon, it was too late. Ethan had looked up immediately. Had he been guarding against it all along?

With their position exposed, the ambush had lost its value. It became a straightforward exchange again. Their familiar opening tactics had all failed within the first moments of the match. Now Ethan could counterattack.

Metang, Flash Cannon!

The Steel-type ranged attack was powerful and especially effective against Rock-type Pokemon. Energy gathered in front of Metang's chest and burst toward the pair.

Solrock and Lunatone knew the arena so well that they slipped behind a planet without waiting for an order. They avoided the attack, but the Flash Cannon tore through their hiding place. It melted a great hole in the model, severing several support cables. The planet, seven or eight meters across, crashed onto the battlefield below.

The twins winced as though the blow had landed on them. Their Pokemon were exposed again. They looked at the model broken into pieces on the floor. Had Ethan hit it by accident, or had he deliberately taken away cover to limit where they could hide?

It had to be an accident... probably. They exchanged a glance, then focused on the battle.

Psychic! they called together.

At last, both of their Pokemon used their strongest Psychic-type attack. Ethan remained calm.

Metang, use Psychic to form a barrier in front of you!

Metang could not hold off both attacks for long by itself. That was not the whole plan.

Milotic, get behind Metang! Then use Surf!

Despite its name, Surf did not require a sea or a Pokemon riding across water. Even on dry ground, the move could summon a great wave that rolled toward the opponent.

The two invisible Psychic attacks struck Metang's barrier with a crackling hiss. Their force pushed it slowly backward. Then water spread rapidly outward from Milotic and changed the balance of the fight.

A wave crashed across the uneven battlefield. It swept up the fallen planet model and carried it toward Solrock and Lunatone. Tate and Liza could not ignore it. Surf was powerful, and Water-type attacks struck their Rock-type Pokemon with twice the usual effectiveness.

They abandoned the attack on Metang and ordered both Pokemon to rise into the air. That was exactly what Ethan had been waiting for.

A Twister sprang up from the water before the wave had subsided. Solrock and Lunatone failed to get clear and were caught inside. They were small and moved by levitating rather than with strong wings; they could not simply fly out of the vortex.

Metang began gathering energy and aimed into the heart of the Twister. It waited for the wind to stop and expose the trapped pair. Tate and Liza felt almost as though their own hearts were spinning with their Pokemon. Seeing Metang ready to fire made them more anxious still.

Fortunately, Solrock and Lunatone's meteorite-like bodies were tough. They endured the full force of the Twister. As its energy ran out and the wind weakened, they escaped, apparently without serious injury.

The twins had no time to relax. Metang had already locked onto them.

Dodge! they shouted together.

Metang fired as they spoke. Flash Cannon blazed across the field like a huge, glowing shell. Before the two Pokemon could get clear, it exploded between them.

Boom!

For an instant, the entire space-themed arena was bright as day.

Chapter 731: Off to Save the World?

The white light dazzled Tate, Liza, their mother Rachel, and Misty in the stands. All four raised their hands to shield their eyes. Seven or eight seconds passed before the glare from Flash Cannon faded enough for them to look at the arena.

Another hanging planet had been blasted from the ceiling. Solrock and Lunatone were covered in injuries. The pressure of Ethan's attack had not even given them time to put up a Light Screen. They looked ready to fall, but both were still conscious. Their meteorite-like bodies were remarkably hard. It was their physical structure, not their types, that had let them endure this much.

Tate and Liza frowned at Milotic and Metang. Ethan was strong. That was their clearest impression of him.

His Pokemon were not impossibly powerful. The twins could see they were still growing and were roughly equal to Solrock and Lunatone in raw strength. Ethan's tactics, commands, and eye for the battle were what made the difference. His Pokemon did not even seem particularly practiced as a pair, but they followed every order faithfully. Under his direction, together they performed far beyond what the twins had expected.

He was unlike any challenger they had faced, but the match was not over. They still had a chance to turn it around.

They called their battered Pokemon back to their half of the field and decided to attack from a distance. That would give Solrock and Lunatone time to react if Milotic used Surf or Twister again, instead of being trapped as they had been before.

It was a sensible plan. The trouble came from their coordination.

They were twins who had run the Gym together for years, supposedly able to understand each other's thoughts. But when they launched another attack, their Pokemon's moves collided with each other halfway across the arena. Neither came close to threatening Metang or Milotic.

The twins immediately began to argue.

You got in my way!

No, you got in mine!

Nonsense! You aimed from the wrong angle!

What are you talking about? I was supposed to attack Milotic, and you were covering Metang. You changed targets!

You never said that! We should each attack whichever one is closest!

Are you kidding? We agreed on this ages ago!

They went red in the face, arguing heedless of the ongoing match or their audience. Ethan and Misty stared. Rachel pressed a hand to her forehead and sighed.

Not again. Will you two stop? Isn't this embarrassing enough? You're in the middle of a Gym battle!

Their mother's sharp reminder quieted them for a moment. Then they ordered another attack, and once again their Pokemon's moves ran into each other.

Now Ethan understood. The twins had worked well together in the early part of the match. He had assumed their coordination would last. Instead, as the fight went against them, it fell apart. Their composure had gone with it. Rachel's reaction showed this was hardly the first time.

The stories about their bond were exaggerated. Once their familiar opening tactics failed, especially against a stronger challenger, Tate and Liza began to interfere with each other. In matches against inexperienced Trainers, the weakness might never show. Against someone like Ethan, it emerged quickly.

No wonder the Pokemon League had appointed them together. Psychic twins made an intriguing draw, and their talent surpassed that of most children their age. But they were still too young to run a large Gym individually. Together they had a better chance of handling skilled challengers.

Ethan had heard enough arguing. When the twins began bickering again, he sent Milotic and Metang forward. Focused on each other, Tate and Liza missed the movement in the arena. Their exhausted Pokemon were knocked down almost at once.

Rachel shook her head, looking weary, but raised her referee's flags.

Solrock and Lunatone are unable to battle! The winner of this Gym match is the challenger, Ethan!

Neither Ethan nor Misty felt much joy at the announcement. The match had promised far more than its abrupt ending delivered. The twins had fought well at first. Once they lost the advantage, their performance had collapsed. Ethan felt as though the battle had ended just when he was beginning to enjoy it.

Still, a win was a win. He had another Badge. Only one remained before the Ever Grande Conference, and then his journey through Hoenn would be nearly finished.

Tate and Liza finally noticed their unconscious Pokemon and stopped arguing. They stared in disbelief until Rachel cleared her throat. The reminder brought them back to their duties. They recalled Solrock and Lunatone and approached Ethan, their expressions complicated.

That was incredible, Liza said, admiration in her voice. Beside your Pokemon, ours hardly managed to work together. We barely had a chance to fight back.

You're one of the strongest challengers we've ever faced, Tate added. How did you get so good?

Ethan shook his head and answered with an almost maddening modesty. Travel more. See more. That's all.

The twins looked at each other. They had become Gym Leaders at ten, achieving something many Trainers never managed in a lifetime. From the start, they occupied a position most people could only hope to reach. And this man was telling them to go out and travel?

Ethan could tell they were not eager. As Gym Leaders, they were already respected and had work they could keep for years. Challengers came to their door every day, giving them opportunities to train without leaving home.

Yet Ethan believed they ought to spend their energetic youth seeing the wider world. They could return to run a Gym after gaining more experience, rather than spending their whole lives here. Of course, people wanted different things. Perhaps the stability of Gym life was exactly what the twins preferred.

It was not his business. They had met only today. He had answered their question, but it was not his place to lecture strangers.

His advice did not seem to reach them. They had expected a special training method from someone so capable. Travel? They walked around the Gym's neighborhood often enough, and that had not produced results.

Rachel opened her mouth as though she wanted to support Ethan's suggestion that they travel. She looked at her children and remained silent.

After a pause, Liza seemed to remember something. Tate, the Badge!

Oh! I nearly forgot too. Glad for something else to say, Tate took a Badge from inside his clothes and offered it to Ethan. This is our Mind Badge. It proves you've defeated us. Please accept it.

Ethan thanked him and examined it. The Badge was heart-shaped, pink across the top and yellow below, with a red cylinder at its center. It had a distinctly girlish look. Whoever had designed it must have expected it to appeal to girls.

After turning it in his hand for a moment, he placed it in his Badge case. Misty came down from the stands. They gave the twins a final nod and left the Gym.

...

The Mossdeep Gym had been a brief stop, and one of the easier Gyms Ethan had challenged. What came next would matter far more.

At last, Shelly called him. Almost at the same time, a message came from Courtney. Their contact could mean only one thing: Archie and Maxie were alive, and after all their preparation, they had begun to move again. Those old enemies had even chosen nearly the same time to act. Was this some special understanding between rival leaders?

Thick black clouds spread over Mossdeep City, seeming to cover the entire sky. People stopped what they were doing and looked up in surprise. Such weather was deeply unusual for residents accustomed to sun and mild winds.
