Ethan knew what it meant. As though the sky itself anticipated what was coming, the calm before the storm was ending. This would be the final confrontation. Archie, Maxie, Kyogre, and Groudoneverything would be settled in this crisis.

He would not go in unprepared. He took Misty to the Pokemon Center and adjusted his team. Several Pokemon that still needed training went to Cerise Park. He contacted Sabrina, Erika, and Chloe, and his strongest Pokemon returned from their care.

Misty felt the gravity of it too. She wanted to lighten Ethan's mood, but after opening her mouth several times, she could think of nothing to say.

Don't be nervous. Ethan slipped the returned Poke Balls into his pouch and smiled at her. Act as you usually do. Remember, I've got this.

By coincidence, the coordinates Shelly and Courtney had sent were different but both lay near Mossdeep, in the surrounding sea. That was good news: he could reach them in a few hours rather than spend days traveling.

Before leaving, he looked at Misty, who was still tense. Would you rather wait here for me?

No. She shook her head firmly and managed a bright smile. I'm a Water-type Trainer. The sea is my territory too. I can help.

That's the spirit. I wouldn't expect less from my traveling partner.

Ethan patted her head and released Dragonite. They climbed onto its back. It took off from outside the Pokemon Center and reached the sky above Mossdeep in a few wingbeats.

A passing Trainer flinched as Dragonite launched beside him. He was about to complain, but it had already carried the pair hundreds of meters up and vanished toward the dark clouds.

Honestly, he muttered after them. What's the rush? Off to save the world?

Chapter 732: As Long as I Stay Hidden

In an unnamed archipelago northeast of Mossdeep City, Ethan and Misty approached the edge of Hoenn. A dozen or so nautical miles farther out lay the open sea beyond the region.

Dragonite had carried them here in little more than an hour. Thick storm clouds still covered the sky. Ethan could not tell whether they were natural or caused by some strange power, but they made excellent cover. Beneath them, Dragonite was only a black speck. Even someone looking up would struggle to notice it.

Following the coordinates, Dragonite landed on one of the smaller islands. Ethan found Shelly again on a shallow stretch of shore. She was sitting atop the cabin of a submarine identical to the shark-shaped one that had sunk before. She leaned back with one leg crossed over the other, looking entirely at ease.

She acknowledged Ethan's arrival with a wave. He and Misty hopped down from Dragonite and went to her.

Ethan looked over the submarine. Wasn't your last one destroyed? Where did you get this?

I borrowed it from another Team Aqua base. Shelly stretched and climbed down. They keep these things in secret bases all over the place. Even they don't know how many they have. Find an unguarded base, and you can take one without anyone noticing. It's nothing remarkable.

She made it sound simple. Ethan knew it could not have been. Shelly had been Team Aqua's strategist and second-in-command. Even Archie or Matt would have had trouble locating an unguarded submarine so readily. Shelly knew the organization's logistics better than anyone. She was its brain, and she knew where everything was kept.

He did not need the details. Where's Archie?

Under their plan, Shelly had been tracking and watching him. Since she was here, Archie had to be nearby.

She studied Ethan before answering. You really did guess right. We planned for the possibility, but honestly, I never imagined Archie could have survived what happened to him.

Why not? Never underestimate anyone, especially someone that strong. Ethan glanced at her. If it had been me in his place, would you have assumed I was dead?

You're different. You're the most extraordinary person I've ever met. I know Archie. He isn't as fortunate as you.

Ethan understood her meaning: Archie did not command a collection of Legendary Pokemon that could save him. Pokemon power mattered, but survival also came down to the person. Archie was hardened and at home in the sea. Ethan had never believed a simple explosion or the water itself would kill him. His return had seemed almost inevitable.

There was no point arguing with Shelly. She already thought Ethan unique, and he was content to let her. It cost him nothing and added a little mystery to her view of him.

It doesn't matter now, he said. Courtney just contacted me. Maxie and Kyogre are coming this way too. They'll arrive before long. We need to get to work.

Maxie and Kyogre? Shelly frowned as she grasped the danger. How did they know Archie and Groudon were here? I thought we'd find Archie, deal with him, and then turn to Maxie. Now they're converging again. What timing.

Maybe the two Legendary Pokemon can sense each other. They've fought for so long that they probably know each other's presence. Kyogre found Groudon that way last time. Ethan patted the pouch at his waist. In any case, I'm better prepared now. I won't let them escape again, and we won't have to go looking for Maxie afterward.

I hope so. Shelly was less confident. Don't forget Maxie has the Blue Orb. I've heard Archie has obtained the Red Orb as well.

So Archie had gotten it after all. Neither leader had the orb Ethan himself wanted, but with those artifacts they might control the ancient Pokemon and trigger Primal Reversion. That made them dangerous.

All the more reason to hurry.

Shelly led Ethan and Misty across the shallows between islands to a larger one. It was more than twice the size of their landing spot, thick with forest and with a lake at its center. At the forest's edge, a Team Aqua grunt peered out at them. Shelly walked straight toward him.

The grunt relaxed visibly when he saw her. Then he noticed Ethan and grew tense again.

B-boss...

Shelly nodded. What's happening?

The leader's by the central lake. Groudon is there too.

Shelly and Courtney had each said they would recruit people inside their organizations to help. Shelly had clearly succeeded. No wonder she had been able to relax on the beach: she had already planted an informant near Archie.

The grunt guided them through the trees. At the lake, they hid behind several large trunks and looked across the water. Dozens of Team Aqua members were spread along the far shore. Beside them stood helicopters, speedboats, and a large landing craft. Archie and Matt were talking aboard the craft.

They brought plenty of equipment, Ethan said. Archie looks prepared. But where's Groudon?

The grunt checked Shelly's face. She nodded, and he answered. It's beneath the rock in the middle of the island. The leader has located it. They're about to begin.

They had arrived just in time. Shelly turned to Ethan and lowered her voice. What do you want to do?

Ethan rubbed his chin. You're the strategist. What would you suggest?

She first dismissed the grunt. That's all we need from you. Go back.

He understood they needed to talk privately. Of course. Please be careful from here on. He left without delay and ran back toward the shore.

Ethan watched him go. He seems to respect you more than Archie. How did you turn him?

After a pause, Shelly sighed. Only some Team Aqua members joined for that impossible ideal. Most just need a living.

A living? In a criminal organization? Her explanation sounded odd to Ethan, but he did not challenge it. He waited for her plan.

We have two options, Shelly said. First, we attack now, before Archie and his people know we're here. We could catch them completely off guard.

That sounds good, Misty said. They have no idea we're nearby. We'd get the most out of a surprise attack.

Ethan watched Team Aqua through the brush. It's the simplest and most effective answer. I have enough strength to hit them hard in a short time. But...

But it exposes us, Shelly finished. Team Magma will be on guard when it arrives. If Maxie doesn't want a direct fight, he may abandon the plan and leave with Kyogre.

Exactly. We could stop Archie before he controls Groudon, but if Maxie gets spooked and escapes, finding Team Magma and Kyogre again would take time. Other things might happen beyond our control. Courtney alone probably couldn't keep them here.

Misty understood at once. She had not thought that far ahead, but the risk was clear once they explained it.

Then...?

We watch and wait for Team Magma, Shelly said. Once the two sides clash, we move in and take advantage.

That works too, Misty said. They'd wear each other down and be too tangled together to escape. We could catch both sides at once.

Then she saw that Ethan and Shelly still looked troubled. What? Is there a problem with that plan too?

A serious one, Shelly said. By then both teams may have gained control of Kyogre and Groudon. If those Pokemon undergo Primal Reversion and fightand Ethan joins the battlethe scale of it could devastate these waters and even affect the mainland.

Misty's head ached. So the first plan is better after all?

Shelly looked to Ethan instead of answering. Misty followed her gaze. Whatever they decided, he would make the final call. They would carry out his choice even if the plan had flaws.

It may not be as complicated as we're making it, Ethan said. Think about their last attempt. Archie and Maxie failed because we interfered. They're trying again. Do you really think they haven't prepared for us?

You mean... Shelly seemed to see where he was going.

Just that. They may look determined to finish this, and each may have an ancient Pokemon. But they'll both be watching for me. Even if they fight each other, neither can commit completely while expecting me to appear.

Misty's eyes brightened. So they'll hold something back in case we show up. They might not even dare use Primal Reversion right away.

Exactly. The longer I stay out of sight, the less certain they'll feel.

Shelly saw the weakness in that. When do we enter, then? If they keep their strength in reserve, the moment we reveal ourselves they might join forces against us.

We'll see who has more patience. Ethan grinned. They can't remain at a stalemate forever. As long as we stay hidden, they'll keep fighting, even if they're only testing one another. Eventually one side will start losing and have to strike harder. That's when we move.

Chapter 733: Lying Low as the Stakes Rise

Once they had agreed on a plan, Ethan, Shelly, and Misty left the lakeshore and slipped up a small hill nearby. From there they could watch the lake from a safer position.

The view was excellent, and the hill stood well outside Team Aqua's working area. It was the best observation point on the island, somewhere they could conserve their strength and wait to see how events unfolded.

Team Aqua had patrols moving around the island to prevent interference. Shelly, however, had obtained their routes and numbers from her informant in advance. Knowing where to avoid them made the three much harder to find.

At the hilltop, Shelly hid half her body behind a tree and watched the lake through a monocular. Misty released Horsea. It went with Ethan's Gengar to gather information closer to the action, one traveling through the water and the other moving unseen through the ground.

Gengar could pass beneath the patrols without being seen. Horsea was common in the sea, so its presence around an island would attract little notice. Better still, Team Aqua and Team Magma were focused on Ethan and Shelly. Both teams knew what Pokemon those two owned, but had paid little attention to Misty. They did not know her team well enough to suspect Horsea was working for them.

Shelly and Misty had their tasks. Ethan leaned against a tree to save his strength. His part of the fighting would come later.

With trees and brush blocking his view of the lake, he could not watch it himself. He couldn't send another Pokemon to scout either. His gaze wanderedand came to rest on Shelly's back.

She had a slender, well-shaped figure. The cut of her outfit showed her lower back and the outer sides of her thighs. Her long black hair fell over her back, a little disheveled, and her lightly tanned skin lent her a wild beauty.

As if she had sensed him looking, Shelly lowered the monocular and turned sharply. Her eyes met his.

She gave him a cool, knowing smile. Even now, you're thinking about that? I thought you'd at least wait until we were alone. Planning to make a move on me already?

Ethan sighed. His eyes had landed on her almost by accident, yet she had caught him at once. Just his luck.

But what did she mean by waiting until they were alone? Had she already decided he had designs on her? Thankfully, Misty was too far away and busy with her own work to hear. Explaining this to her would have been difficult.

What are you talking about? Ethan looked away. I wasn't looking at you. I was looking at that dead piece of wood beside you. It's flowering even though the tree is dead. Strange, isn't it?

The change of subject was painfully obvious. Shelly glanced down at his trousers and smiled with unmistakable implication. She said nothing, but he felt she had said plenty. Ethan looked down too and instinctively shifted his stance.

His phone chimed, breaking the silence. He welcomed the interruption, took it out, and checked the message. Shelly snorted and turned back to the lake.

Or so he thought. She still had her back to him. Perhaps it was his imagination, but she seemed to arch it a little more now, her waist drawn in and her hips raised in a way that made her even more distracting.

Was she testing his patience? Did she know what she was inviting? Ethan shook his head and focused on the phone.

As expected, the message was from Courtney. Team Magma was nearby and would reach the island soon. They had arrived quickly.

Ethan put the phone away, went over to Shelly, and took the monocular from her hand. She rolled her eyes while he raised it toward the lake.

Archie and Matt had finished preparing. Team Aqua members spread out around a heap of rock. In Archie's hand was the Red Orb, the one blown away during their previous chaotic battle.

Fate had played a strange trick on both leaders. Archie wanted Kyogre, yet he stood before Groudon holding its Red Orb. Maxie wanted Groudon, but held the Blue Orb and had been following Kyogre instead. Each coveted the other's orb and ancient Pokemon. Neither dared abandon the one within reach and give the other an opening.

They're about to begin, Ethan said.

As if on cue, several excavators started digging into the rocks. Perhaps Groudon had not fallen fully asleep, or perhaps it had only been underground for a few days. Either way, Team Aqua soon woke it.

A violent tremor spread from beneath the island. Ethan felt it clearly on the hill, kilometers from its source. Even the sea grew rough. At the excavation site, Team Aqua members were thrown off their feet.

Then Groudon emerged. Magma rose first and spilled over the ground. Through that searing flow, the immense red Pokemon slowly climbed out of the earth.

Roar!

Its first cry carried a savage power Ethan could feel even from this distance. The Ultra Balls and Great Balls at his waist trembled faintly. His Pokemon sensed it too and were eager to act.

Not yet, he murmured to them. It isn't our turn.

When he looked back at the lake, Team Aqua was already fighting Groudon. Even without the monocular, he could tell how fierce the battle was. Archie and Matt led the attack while their grunts surged forward. Pokemon were knocked out by single hits, but the next wave kept coming.

They were in a hurry. They knew they had to secure Groudon before anyone interrupted. Its power was immense, but Team Aqua had numbers, and their Pokemon held some type advantage against a Ground-type opponent. Their attacks were having an effect.

At some point Misty had joined them. She watched anxiously. Could they actually catch Groudon?

That depends on how fast they are. Ethan tilted his chin toward the sea. Look. The third player has arrived.

A large ship of unusual design, red from end to end, was speeding toward the island. Ethan did not need to see an emblem to know it belonged to Team Magma. Its arrival drew Team Aqua's attention as well; their formation wavered for a moment. They had expected interference, perhaps, but not so soon.

Matt took a group toward the shore to meet them while Archie intensified the attack on Groudon. He held the Red Orb ready, apparently waiting for Groudon's strength to drop far enough for him to control it.

Ethan lowered the monocular. Both players are here. They'll clash soon. We can move a little closer.

Shelly and Misty nodded gravely and followed him toward the central lake. Gengar and Horsea met them along the way. Together they took cover in a dense thicket.

Archie and the remaining Team Aqua members were reaching a decisive moment against Groudon. Team Magma's ship had reached the island too. Ethan could make out Maxie and Tabitha standing near its bow.

Maxie stood with his hands behind his back and looked down at the battle, satisfaction flashing in his eyes.

Archie, stop wasting your strength! You're too late to catch Groudon. Kyogre is already mine. Hand over the orb while you still can!

Archie glanced back, his face dark, but gave no answer. He clenched his teeth and kept directing a fiercer assault on Groudon.

Maxie had no more patience for him. He waved a hand. A door opened at the front of his ship, and a Pokemon floated out, its eyes glowing red.

Kyogre! Misty whispered sharply from the thicket.

It was not as she remembered it. Kyogre moved on its own, but its red eyes made it plain that someone was controlling it. Archie had apparently thought Maxie was bluffing. Instead, his rival had gained control of Kyogre first.

Even Ethan was surprised. Courtney had not mentioned it. Perhaps her information was incomplete, or perhaps Team Magma had subdued Kyogre only moments ago. Either way, they controlled it now. The timing was earlier than Ethan expected, but he had prepared for the possibility. As long as Kyogre had not undergone Primal Reversion, matters were not yet at their worst.

Shelly was no longer content to wait. We should act, she said. They're both here now. They can't simply vanish. If Archie gains control of Groudon as well, this will be much harder to contain.

Ethan thought it over and nodded. Plans never quite survive events. But wait a little longer. Once the two sides are fighting each other, we move.

While they spoke, Maxie sent Kyogre over the island. Matt saw the Pokemon Team Aqua had dreamed of commanding in someone else's control and felt the pressure mount. He had to buy Archie enough time to take Groudon. Only then could they stand against Team Magma.

Matt led his grunts into Kyogre's path and sent out their Pokemon. They could not hold it. Kyogre surged forward, and its great body broke through them at once.

Damn it! Archie glared at Maxie, then turned back to assess Groudon.

After Shelly's betrayal in the Seafloor Cavern, he had reconsidered whether an orb could safely control an ancient Pokemon. Reports from his people had confirmed her concern: trying too soon might fail and drive the Pokemon into a frenzy, even turning it against its would-be master.

He had studied the problem and found what he believed was a safer method. First wear the Pokemon down to a certain threshold; then use the orb. That should give him a much better chance of controlling it.

Groudon was almost at that point. Almost. And now, at the worst possible moment, that arrogant man with glasses had come to interfere. Archie could hardly contain his anger.

Chapter 734: Primal Reversion

Archie turned toward Maxie and fought to keep his anger from showing. Don't get too pleased with yourself! Have you forgotten? That man is nearby. Are you going to let him profit while we fight?

Ethan, hidden in the brush, felt a jolt. That man could only mean him. But how did Archie know he was nearby? Had their hiding place been discovered?

After a moment, he decided Archie was bluffing. He wanted to make Maxie hesitate and buy himself enough time to gain control of Groudon. Archie could act decisively, but subtle schemes were not his strength.

Maxie was not fooled. How surprising. Even a brute like you can think of a trick now and then. He looked down at Archie with contempt. Do you really expect that to frighten me? I already control Kyogre, and I can trigger its Primal Reversion whenever I wish. Once Groudon is mine too, what can he do with a single Deoxys?

He plainly expected Ethan to interfere eventually. In Maxie's mind, though, everything would be settled by the time Ethan arrived. With both ancient Pokemon under his command, who could oppose him? Even Rayquaza would have to retreat from the two of them attacking together.

Archie had not expected Maxie to dismiss the warning so completely. Kyogre was closing in, and Matt and the other Team Aqua members could not stop it. Archie's eyes hardened.

They think I'm helpless? If I can't have it, neither can anyone else!

He turned and used the Red Orb on Groudon before it had been sufficiently weakened.

You fool! Maxie shouted, his eyes widening.

Controlling Kyogre had taught him how dangerous it was to use an orb rashly on an ancient Pokemon still at full strength. Archie was willing to drag everyone down with him.

Kyogre, stop him! Maxie raised the Blue Orb, trying to send Kyogre forward. He was too late. Archie's Red Orb flashed, and a streak of red light struck Groudon in the center of the lake.

Wrapped in the light, Groudon roared at the sky. Its body began to change.

No! Maxie cried.

Archie laughed wildly. Groudon grew from just over three meters tall to more than five, a massive figure nearly two stories high. Orange-yellow, magma-like light spread across its skin as though it wore molten rock. Marks shaped like the Greek letter omega appeared on its arms and knees. Its presence pressed down on everyone nearby.

There was no mistaking it. Groudon had undergone Primal Reversion.

So that's... Primal Reversion? Misty stared from the brush. Is that what it looks like when it evolves?

It isn't evolution, Ethan said, frowning. Primal Reversion restores an ancient Pokemon's original form. This is what Groudon really looked like when the world first came into being, in that age of chaos before land and sky took shape.

Its original form...

Their fear had come true. Primal Groudon was out of control. The orb could not command it. Hot, chaotic fury consumed its thoughts until it wanted only to destroy everything around it.

The Team Aqua members surrounding it were the first to suffer. Its attacks had grown far more powerful. Gaining a Fire type made it more vulnerable to Water-type attacks, but it could now knock out entire groups of Pokemon before they could use those attacks.

It roared. The whole island shook violently, great cracks opened across the ground, and magma erupted in fountains more than ten meters high. The molten rock had a source. Groudon slept along volcanic networks, which was why its emergence from underground so often brought a flood of magma with it.

The eruptions added to the chaos, but Primal Groudon's overwhelming force caused most of Team Aqua's losses. A single Fissure took out a broad swath of their Pokemon. It did not continue hunting down every grunt, however. Its attention shifted to Kyogre.

They had been enemies for thousands of years. Groudon's fixation on Kyogre seemed etched into its very DNA. Even in its confused rage, Kyogre remained its chief target.

The violent shaking reached the three in the brush. Ethan lost his balance and fell onto Shelly, pinning her beneath him. The feel of her body startled him. Their position was awkwardly intimate, much like moments he had shared with Sabrina and Erika. He tried to get up at once.

He knew how sharp Shelly's tongue could be. Earlier she had caught him merely looking at her. What would she say about this?

In his haste, he fumbled and put a hand on her chest. Worse, out of habit, he gave an unconscious squeeze.

Oh no.

Realization hit a moment later. His face changed. To his surprise, Shelly said nothing at first. Only when his hand remained where it was did she ask in a voice of bland expectation, How much longer are you planning to hold on?

What? Oh. Sorry...

Ethan pulled away, stood, and faced the battlefield as though nothing had happened. Shelly got up and straightened her clothes.

Enjoy that?

Cough! Cough...

He should have known she would say something. Avoiding her amused face, he fixed his attention on the lake.

Primal Groudon and Kyogre had begun to fight. Kyogre held a type advantage, but Groudon's primal power seemed to make that advantage irrelevant. At their first exchange, its heavy punch knocked Kyogre down from the air.

Misty had fallen in a different direction. She had not seen the embarrassing encounter. She rubbed her dizzy head as she got up, looked toward the lake, and caught sight of the blow.

It knocked Kyogre down with one hit? she cried. Ethan, we have to move now!

Not yet. He reached for his Poke Balls but kept his voice patient. They've only just begun fighting. If we reveal ourselves now, Maxie may cut his losses and escape. Let him trigger Kyogre's Primal Reversion too. Once both are consumed by their fight, neither side will be able to leave easily. Then we go in.

They did not have to wait long. Maxie had little choice. His team could not withstand Primal Groudon, and he would not give up this opportunity. He raised the orb and called on Kyogre's primal power to oppose it.

Blue light blazed around Kyogre. Its body swelled to nearly twice its former size, almost ten meters long. It became partly translucent, with a faint yellow glow from within. Marks resembling the Greek letter alpha appeared on its forehead and wing-like fins.

Primal Kyogre had appeared on the island beside Primal Groudon. After countless years, the ancient rivals stood before the world again in their legendary forms.

Unlike Groudon, Kyogre still obeyed Maxie. It did not attack indiscriminately. Its focus remained on Primal Groudon alone.

Maxie stood at the bow of his ship with the Blue Orb in his hand and looked down at the two Pokemon. Pride and triumph swelled in him. Who else in the world commanded power like this? With Primal Kyogre, he had reached the very top. If he gained Primal Groudon as well, no opponent could stand against him. He could achieve his greatest ambitionand perhaps go further still.

Boom!

The two primal Pokemon collided. It was only a direct impact, yet the weather changed at once. Lightning flashed and thunder rolled through an already clouded sky. A visible shock wave rushed outward. The island looked ready to break apart, and the surrounding sea formed more than a dozen small whirlpools.

This was the terrifying strength of primal Pokemon. Power like this was intoxicating.

Do I really command it? Maxie thought.

He began to smile, then froze. A figure burst from an unremarkable thicket across the lake. It moved so fast that it reached Primal Kyogre before he understood what was happening and struck it with a powerful attack.

What?

The attack had caught him completely off guard. An instant later, he recognized the intruder.

Deoxys! he snarled.

He had expected Ethan to meddle eventually. He had not expected an attack at this precise moment from this hiding place. If Deoxys was here, Ethan had to be here too. Maxie looked toward the thicket and saw one man and two women emerge.

Ethan. Maxie's eyes blazed with anger. How did this man keep appearing at the most critical moment?

Archie was startled to see him too, then burst into laughter. He laughed until he was short of breath.

I see! You were hiding here all along. I thought we'd kept this operation secret, but you found out anyway. You even slipped onto the island without anyone noticing. What a failure on my part!

His gaze fell on Shelly beside Ethan. He did not need to ask. She had surely helped bring him here.

Shelly met Archie's complicated look without a flicker of discomfort. The past was behind her. She had a new life and someone new to rely on. At last, she had left the shadow of Team Aqua behind.

Chapter 735: You Really Don't Hold Back

Archie looked away from Shelly and turned to Maxie. His position had only grown worse, yet the helpless anger he had felt a moment ago had given way to a certain spiteful pleasure.

A nearby explosion had injured him badly enough that he spat blood. Still, he looked up at Maxie with a mocking smile and called, Well, Maxie? How do you feel now? What are you going to do?

Maxie hated the smug look on Archie's face. He also saw Ethan nearby, ready to act. Archie did not need to spell out his meaning. With Primal Groudon out of control, Archie no longer had much to lose. The pressure was now on Maxie.

Why was Archie so pleased? Was he dazed from his injuries? Ethan was their common enemy. Did Archie truly hate Maxie so much more?

Maxie had no time to puzzle over it. Primal Kyogre should be stronger than Deoxys alone. But Primal Groudon was already fighting it, and Ethan owned other Legendary Pokemon besides Deoxys. That combination was dangerous.

Before Ethan appeared, Maxie had spoken boldly, seemingly without fear. With Ethan actually in front of him, he felt enormous pressure despite controlling Primal Kyogre. At least he was not alone.

On Maxie's order, Team Magma grunts poured from the ship. Shouting wildly, they leapt onto the island and rushed inland. They had reason to fight hard. Team Magma was stronger than it had ever been. It was missing one commander, but gaining an ancient Pokemon more than made up for that loss.

They had had chances to capture Groudon before. Every grunt knew this was the closest they had come to realizing their goal. The one flaw was that they controlled Kyogre rather than Groudon. If those positions were reversed, they would not need to be here at all.

Still, if they seized Groudon now, Maxie and Team Magma could make their dream real.

Ethan, Shelly, and Misty released more Pokemon as the grunts charged. Shelly and Misty brought out their Water-type teams. Ethan had deliberately changed his lineup for this operation.

Deoxys was already in the fight. The black Rayquaza remained in its Ultra Ball, not yet ready to appear. Ethan released five other Legendary Pokemon: Zapdos, Articuno, Moltres, Suicune, and Raikou.

Spread apart, the five could form a net around every Pokemon on the field except Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre. Brought together, they could strike like a fist powerful enough to trouble even those two ancient Pokemon.

Gardevoir and Dragonite also emerged to protect the three Trainers alongside Gengar. Ethan kept his other regular Pokemon in reserve. They were strong enough to matter, but he wanted an answer to any unexpected turn. Long experience had taught him to keep something back, even near the end.

The arrival of so many Pokemon changed the battle immediately. Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre continued to treat each other as their greatest threat. Under Ethan's telepathic direction, Deoxys ignored Groudon and attacked Kyogre alone.

As in their previous battle, concentrating on one ancient Pokemon rather than dividing their strength was the key. Kyogre was Ethan's target again. This time, though, it had undergone Primal Reversion. Its abilities had grown considerably, and Deoxys's attacks were less effective.

Deoxys had been able to contend with Kyogre and Groudon before. Their primal forms were on another level. Maxie felt a little relief. As he had thought, Deoxys could not defeat a primal ancient Pokemon by itself. Perhaps only the Mega Rayquaza of legend could threaten them now.

Then he looked at the rest of the battlefield, and his relief vanished.

Team Magma and Ethan's forces had engaged, but so had the remnants of Team Aqua. Some of Archie's grunts had slipped away when the situation turned grim. Many more, angry at Team Magma for ruining their chance to secure Groudon, attacked Maxie's people. They hated Team Magma more than they hated Ethan.

Ethan had no such divided feelings. Both leaders were his enemies. He did not intend to spare either of them.

Deoxys, change to Attack Forme!

He sent the order in his mind, then gave his five Legendary Pokemon their assignments through Gardevoir's telepathy. Zapdos, Articuno, and Moltres swept across the sky toward Maxie's ship. On the ground, Raikou and Suicune broke through the grunts toward Archie.

Capture the leaders first. More importantly, take the orbs from their hands.

Maxie saw what Ethan intended. The three Legendary birds crossed the battlefield at speed.

Stop them! he shouted.

Tabitha and the elite grunts guarding him released their Pokemon. None dared hold back. Their defense lasted a single exchange. The birds scattered their Pokemon and left many unconscious.

Cold sweat ran down Maxie's face as Zapdos, Articuno, and Moltres closed in. He had made a mistake. He had counted on Primal Kyogre's might without recognizing that Ethan did not need to defeat it first. If Ethan captured him, the fight would be over.

Kyogre was strong enough to face the birds, but it could not protect Maxie from three directions at once, especially while it fought Groudon and Deoxys on the island. Even now, Maxie refused to give up.

He gripped the Blue Orb and urged Kyogre to return. With his other hand, he took several Poke Balls from his pocket and threw them. Blue flashes revealed his own Pokemon between him and the birds. Maxie was not Team Magma's strongest battler, but he was more capable than the elite grunts. Surely his team could buy him a little time.

He had underestimated the birds together. A commander or leader might have had some chance against one of them by sending an entire team. All three acting in concert were another matter.

They had fought under Ethan for a long time. Their individual power had grown, and so had their coordination. Ice, lightning, and fire poured forward, their attacks overlapping. Maxie's defenders fell almost at once.

The birds surrounded him in a triangle, leaving no way out. As he looked desperately from side to side, Zapdos darted its head forward. Its long, pointed beak caught the Blue Orb.

Maxie instinctively pulled the orb toward his chest. A human could not win a contest of strength with Zapdos. One sharp tug, and the orb was gone.

No!

For the first time in a long while, Maxie lost his composure completely. Primal Kyogre did not obey him personally. It obeyed the orb. Without it, he could no longer command Kyogre.

He reached for the stolen orb. Before he could touch it, enormous talons seized him and lifted him into the air. Moltres held him like prey, pinning his arms so he could not move. He could only cry out.

His thoughts went blank. He was the leader of Team Magma, a force that had shaken Hoenn. How had he been reduced to this?

On the island, Archie had no chance to laugh at his rival. Suicune and Raikou were coming for him. On the ground, grunts from both teams blocked their path, so they could not move as quickly as the three birds. But nothing in that crowd could hold them back for long.

Damn it... Is this the end? Archie pressed a hand to his aching chest and coughed more blood. He did not run. He leaned against a rock, too weak to move.

He was a strong man, but Groudon's shock wave had caught him at close range. His injuries were hidden beneath his clothes; inside, he was bleeding in several places. Even a small movement hurt badly.

Suicune and Raikou approached from either side. Then a roar sounded nearby. A huge, stumbling man rushed in front of Archie.

M-Matt? Archie stared at his back.

Team Aqua's commander was broader and more imposing than Archie himself, his bare torso usually making him look like a tower of dark iron. Now he was battered and covered in wounds. Even so, he stood between Archie and the two Legendary Pokemon.

Boss, I'll hold them off! Get out of here!

For all his faults, Archie inspired more devotion in his people than the cold Maxie did. Even now, someone was willing to risk himself for him.

It's no use. Archie shook his head. I can't walk. You should leave. Team Aqua can't lose everyone here.

Are you joking? Matt roared at Suicune and Raikou without turning around. How could I abandon you?

He charged at them. In the next instant, a heavy jet of water struck him and hurled him back. He landed beside Archie and lay still, unconscious from the impact.

Archie looked down at his loyal commander. Before he could say a word, two shadows fell over him. Suicune and Raikou stood close enough that he could feel the moisture around one and smell the sharp electric tang around the other.

Clack.

The Red Orb slipped from his fingers and rolled to Suicune's feet.

Heh... ha... Archie stopped looking at the Pokemon and raised his eyes to the clouded sky. You really don't hold back...

Chapter 736: Time to Show Off

Thud. Thud. Thud.

Moltres, Zapdos, and Raikou dropped Maxie, Archie, and Matt beside Ethan. The two seized orbs rolled to his feet. He picked them up before looking down at the captives.

Matt aside, the two leaders were in a sorry state. Archie had passed out from his injuries. Maxie was still conscious, but Moltres's rough flight had left him staring blankly, as though he could scarcely understand what had happened. His usually neat swept-back hair was a mess, his uniform torn, and his glasses gone.

You... Ethan began.

Gengar appeared with two long vines it had found somewhere and, in a blink, tied all three men securely. It certainly acted fast. Ethan appreciated that Gengar could see what needed doing without an order, though it had cut off whatever he might have said.

Never mind. The leaders had lost, and now they were captured. There was little to discuss with Maxie.

Ethan looked toward the battlefield. Team Aqua and Team Magma members saw their leaders taken prisoner and panicked. Their panic became a desperate resolve. Both sides stopped attacking each other and surged toward Ethan, determined to rescue their leaders.

Hold them back!

There was no time to relay individual orders by telepathy. At Ethan's gesture, his five Legendary Pokemon moved in front of him. Shelly and Misty directed their Water-type Pokemon to the flanks so no one could circle around.

Pokemon came in masses across the ground and through the air, a dark wave that looked frightening from a distance. Ordinary grunts and elite members alike might take some effort to defeat, but they could no longer threaten Ethan. His strongest lineup was with him now.

Zapdos and Raikou, the fastest of the five, struck first.

Zapdos, RaikouThunderbolt!

One attacked from the sky, the other from the ground. Electricity burst outward in all directions, flashing across the field. Most of Team Aqua's Water-type Pokemon fell almost instantly. Even from far away, the crackling current conveyed the power behind those attacks. Zapdos and Raikou might not have bodies as massive as Groudon's or Kyogre's, but their moves were formidable.

Suicune, along with Shelly's and Misty's Water-types, had to move around the edge of the electrical assault to avoid being caught in it. A few enemy Pokemon came through elsewhere, but their numbers were too small to change the fight.

Once the current subsided, the other Legendary Pokemon reached the front and engaged Team Magma's forces. Suicune cut into their Fire-type formation like a blade. Powerful Water-type attacks poured from its mouth, easily dropping any Fire-type that tried to block it. Mightyena and Crobat escaped that first charge, only to face Articuno and Moltres.

Seeing both enemy formations break, Shelly and Misty sent their own Pokemon forward. For practical purposes, Team Aqua and Team Magma had already lost. No ordinary force could withstand five Legendary Pokemon at once.

Then Ethan spotted a conspicuous figure slipping out of the chaos toward the shore. The broad body and bright Team Magma uniform gave him away: Tabitha.

He was running? With Maxie captured, Tabitha had decided not to be taken alongside him. He moved with surprising agility for his size, scrambling back onto Team Magma's ship. Several escape boats hung along its side. He headed straight for them.

Ethan had not spent all this time preparing only to let a commander escape. He could not catch every grunt, and he did not intend to try. The two leaders and their commanders were responsible for this. He would not let one slip away before his eyes.

He was about to send Dragonite after Tabitha when a tarpaulin on one of the boats flipped aside. A small, shapely woman in a hooded Team Magma uniform stood up. Her face was too far away to see clearly, but Ethan knew who it was: Courtney, who had remained out of sight until now.

Why was she hiding there?

Before he could think further, she kicked Tabitha in the stomach and sent him sprawling. She released a Pokemon and had him restrained before he could rise. The movements were smooth, fast, and so unexpected that Tabitha barely reacted.

She does have some sense, Shelly said. She sounded grudgingly impressed, then gave a dismissive snort. An ambush at Team Magma's escape route. Clever, perhaps, but it's only a small trick.

Even though Courtney was on their side now, Shelly could not quite bring herself to praise her old rival. Water and fire did not readily mix.

With the human fight settled, Ethan turned his attention back to the lake. That was where the true danger lay. Magma had nearly filled its once-clear water. The ground around the ancient Pokemon had broken apart. And this was still only the beginning of their battle.

As Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre fought, the upheaval spread. Storm clouds stretched for hundreds of miles and kept advancing. Lightning lit the sky and thunder shook it. Dozens of waterspouts rose from the sea into the clouds, with great whirlpools churning beneath them. Fiery meteors punched holes through the cloud cover and crashed into the island and ocean, throwing up earth and spray.

It looked like the end of the world.

Within half a minute, another violent shock split the large island into many pieces. Wind howled. Waves more than ten meters high swallowed whatever they could pull from the shore. No one could keep fighting in such conditions except the Pokemon that had caused them.

Ethan's group and the Pokemon of both teams stopped. The remaining grunts cared only about escaping. If they stayed, they would die here with their leaders.

Ethan, Shelly, and Misty had to carry Maxie, Archie, and Matt away from the shattered island. They returned to the smaller one where Ethan had met Shelly. Rain lashed their faces.

The water revived both leaders. They saw what their Pokemon had doneand then saw grunts struggling in the sea. Maxie showed little reaction. Archie turned pale.

Save them! he pleaded.

In this sea, even strong swimmers would likely die once they fell overboard. Ethan could not stand by and watch. He frowned. He might not be able to save many himself, but he had to try.

Then he spotted Courtney on Team Magma's ship. She had gathered several people and was already helping those in the water. That was a great relief. The ship and its crew could handle the immediate rescues, leaving Ethan free to focus on the two ancient Pokemon.

He held up the two orbs, both still glowing faintly, and turned to Shelly. How do I make these stop them?

Why ask me? I have no idea. She spread her hands. Try thinking at them?

Ethan actually tried. The Red Orb had long since lost any hold over Primal Groudon and did nothing. He worked at the Blue Orb for a while too. Perhaps Primal Kyogre was too far away, or perhaps the orb had stopped working, but it gave no response. He plainly did not know how to use it.

He could hardly turn around and ask Maxie. If the orbs would not solve this, he would have to use force, just as he had planned.

First he needed to contain the weather. If it kept spreading, the nearby islands and eventually the Hoenn mainland would suffer.

Ethan whistled. Zapdos, Articuno, and Moltres rose into the sky. Through Gardevoir's telepathy, he could still direct them from far below. He sent them to three points around the battlefield, forming a triangle that enclosed its center.

He intended to use something like a technique for fighting a wildfire. When flames spread outward, a controlled fire can burn toward them and create a barrier. He would have the birds' power drive against the expanding storm, form an opposing flow, and stop it from reaching farther.

Ordinary Pokemon could not do it. These three were not ordinary.

At Ethan's command, they beat their wings and released a torrent of energy. Fire. Ice. Lightning. Their powers surged from three directions into the vast weather front. The wind, clouds, waves, and falling fire seemed to strike an invisible wall. They could advance no farther.

The storm was a byproduct of the two ancient Pokemon's battle. Holding it back was within the birds' strength, so long as they kept up the effort.

Containment was not a lasting answer. The battle continued to produce more violent weather inside the triangle. If enough accumulated, its eventual release could be devastating. Ethan needed to stop the source quickly.

He drew a breath and looked around at the people with him. At last, the moment had come.

Watch closely. Time to show off.

Under the eyes of Shelly, Maxie, Archie, and Matt, Ethan put the orbs away and took out another Ultra Ball he had prepared.

Every gaze fixed on it. As far as they knew, Deoxys was the strongest Pokemon he owned, and it was already fighting the two primal Pokemon.

What could be inside this ball that he would bring out now? Did he have another Pokemon strong enough?

Chapter 737: The Great Battle

The answer came quickly.

Ethan tossed the Ultra Ball high. Blue light flashed, and a long, dragonlike Pokemon appeared in the sky, its body gleaming black as ink.

Shelly, Maxie, Archie, Matt, and Courtney aboard the ship all recognized it at a glance. So did the Team Magma and Team Aqua members who had fallen into the water. Their mouths hung open and their eyes widened in disbelief.

R-Rayquaza!?

It was impossible. Insane. How could this man have a Rayquazaand a black Shiny Rayquaza at that?

Everyone was stunned, but Maxie and Archie in particular felt as though everything they knew had been overturned. Ethan had only recently acquired Deoxys. How much time had passed since then? And now he had caught Rayquaza too? Were Legendary Pokemon just lying around for him to find?

Shelly was surprised as well, though she recovered sooner. When they had last parted, Ethan had said he would try his luck at Sky Pillar. She simply had not expected him to find the place and return with a black Rayquaza.

Rayquaza circled overhead and roared. The cry rang across the battlefield, drawing the attention of Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre at once.

It was not the Rayquaza they had encountered before, but they knew the species well enough to recognize that hateful presence. After a glance, however, both turned away. Like Deoxys, a Rayquaza that had not Mega Evolved was no equal to them in their current forms.

They had overlooked something. Deoxys and the black Rayquaza were on the same side. They shared an objective and had no reason to fight each other. More than that, they had a Trainer.

Having a Trainer meant more than ceasing to be wild. Under a Trainer's direction, Pokemon could act with far better judgment and make much more of their strength.

Until now, Ethan had been occupied with Team Aqua and Team Magma and had let Deoxys attack as it pleased. With both organizations routed, he could give the ancient Pokemon his full attention.

He recalled Raikou and Suicune, then signaled Shelly and Misty to call back their Pokemon too. Only when that was done did he look toward the distant battlefield.

The real fight was just beginning.

Deoxys, Rayquaza, attack Primal Kyogre together!

That's it. Deoxys, keep striking its belly. It's vulnerable there!

Rayquaza, leave Primal Groudon alone. Let's take down one opponent first!

Rayquaza, come back! I said to leave Groudon and go after Kyogre!

All four Pokemon clashed. Outwardly, Ethan looked composed, as though he had the whole battle under control. Apart from Gardevoir, no one knew how exhausting it was to direct themmostly because of Rayquaza.

He had caught it too recently. They had no dependable bond yet and had barely communicated. Rayquaza was fighting the two primal Pokemon because it sensed their power and, by nature, wanted to challenge them. It was hardly obeying Ethan.

Still, Rayquaza had entered a Poke Ball. Whether it had been hours or days, it was no longer a wild Pokemon. They would need time to get used to each other, but it had made no attempt to flee. It even seemed to understand that Deoxys was now its ally, rather than seeking revenge for its earlier defeat.

For now, Ethan was satisfied. He had never expected to direct Rayquaza as easily as his other Pokemon. He only needed it to unleash its strength.

Primal Reversion had greatly increased Kyogre's and Groudon's abilities, but neither could endure unlimited punishment. Rayquaza and Deoxys in Attack Forme were both exceptionally powerful attackers. If Rayquaza drew their attention and gave Deoxys room to land its blows, it would have done everything Ethan needed.

That was exactly what happened. Groudon and Kyogre might have dismissed Rayquaza at first, but its relentless attacks were impossible to ignore. After another fierce hit, Primal Kyogre turned to face it.

That was Ethan's opening. With Kyogre's back exposed, he ordered Deoxys to gather power for a heavy strike.

Primal Groudon went after Deoxys at that very moment. Deoxys had to dodge, losing its chance to attack.

He could not relax for an instant.

Unlike Kyogre, Groudon had been hastily controlled with an orb by Archie. The attempt had failed and driven it into a frenzy. It had lost all restraint. In its confused mind, whoever stood before it was a target.

When Kyogre went after Rayquaza, Deoxys naturally became Groudon's first choice.

So it would not be simple. Ethan could accept the missed opportunity. A fight of this intensity required patience. If he waited without rushing, another opening would come.

For now, he had Deoxys Teleport to Kyogre's far side, putting Kyogre between it and Groudon. Groudon promptly switched targets and attacked Kyogre again.

That was what a Trainer could do. Ethan's wider view let him choose a position that protected Deoxys and turned Groudon against its old rival. A wild Pokemon might have dodged Groudon's charge, but it would not necessarily have placed Kyogre in its path. Now Kyogre faced enemies on three sides.

Kyo!

Groudon's blow struck, and Kyogre cried out in pain. The scene stirred a bitter memory. Just days ago, it had faced the same three-sided assault and eventually fled in defeat. Was it happening again already?

Agitated, Kyogre drew on a tremendous reserve of power. Energy began to gather in its mouth. At almost the same moment, as though sensing its intent, Groudon started building power too.

Oh no! Shelly cried from afar. Origin Pulse and Precipice Blades!

She had seen Kyogre and Groudon use their signature moves against each other before. The resulting explosion had left her deeply wary of both attacks. And they had been in their ordinary forms then. Now both had undergone Primal Reversion. The impact would be far worse. Worse still, the moves were unmistakable; there was no mistaking what was coming.

Archie and Maxie had witnessed that previous collision too. Their faces changed as they realized they were once again within range. Ordering such a move against someone else was one thing. Being helpless in its path was quite another. Neither wanted to be obliterated by it.

Ethan understood the danger as well. Even if Deoxys and Rayquaza stopped one of them, the other would still release its attack. They would have to get clear.

He ordered Deoxys and Rayquaza away through Gardevoir's telepathy, then said to Shelly and Misty, I don't think we're safe here. Let's move back.

Neither objected. Taking the three prisoners with them, they hurried toward the far side of the small island. Ethan also warned the three Legendary birds in the sky to brace themselves.

The birds were outside the attacks' direct range. Their task was to stop the blast wave afterward, keeping it from devastating the surrounding sea and land. It might not put them in danger, but it would hardly be easy.

After running a few steps, Ethan glanced back. Deoxys had Teleported beyond the attacks' range. The black Rayquaza, however, was still weaving around Groudon and Kyogre, attacking them.

It really did not know when to stop. Perhaps it had no idea what was coming. Perhaps it did, but believed it could withstand the blow. Either way, this lesson might make it more willing to listen.

Only seconds later, Groudon and Kyogre were ready. They unleashed their moves almost together. Two torrents of energy, far larger and brighter than those of their last encounter, surged from opposite sides and collided at the center.

BOOM!

Red and blue pillars shot into the sky. The explosion was so loud it hurt their ears. Before they could make out the scene, a powerful shock wave reached them and knocked Maxie and the other prisoners sprawling.

Gardevoir raised a psychic barrier around Ethan, Shelly, and Misty. They were nearly a kilometer from the blast, yet the barrier lasted only seven or eight seconds before the shock wave shattered it. The wind knocked all three to the ground. Fortunately, the barrier had absorbed most of the force, and they escaped with nothing worse than a fall.

They rose and looked toward the battlefield. The energy of Precipice Blades and Origin Pulse had not fully faded. It swelled outward like a mushroom cloud.

Ethan searched for his Pokemon. Deoxys had escaped the blast with Teleport, and even the shock wave could not break through its defenses. It appeared unharmed.

The black Rayquaza was nowhere in sight. Ethan scanned the area again and again, but could not tell where the blast had thrown it. He trusted a Legendary Pokemon at the top of the food chain to survive. It might be badly shaken and injured, but he did not believe its life was in danger.

Unable to find it for the moment, he turned his eyes skyward. The shock wave had reached the three Legendary birds, which strained with all their strength to hold it back. Inside their triangle, enormous waves churned. Beyond it, the sea remained comparatively calm.

But they could not hold on much longer. Their defenses might give way at any moment.

Chapter 738: The Curtain Falls

Ethan decided to let the birds stop resisting. They had held back the worst of the shock wave. What remained would lose strength crossing the wide sea before it reached the Hoenn mainland. At worst it might arrive as a severe storm. Cities and villages could still suffer damage, but human society could withstand it.

He had done enough. Now he needed to focus entirely on Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre.

It was time for them to experience the three birds' combined strength.

The birds had used Tri-Bird Assault when Ethan caught Deoxys. Deoxys had blocked it with both a barrier and its Defense Forme, yet the attack had destroyed half its body. Only its rapid regeneration had made it appear unharmed afterward.

He wanted to see how Groudon and Kyogre would take it.

They were too far away for Gardevoir to pass on his orders directly. Ethan found another way: he sent the instructions to Deoxys by telepathy and had Deoxys relay them to the birds. Before long, contact was restored.

At his command, Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres beat their wings and climbed above the clouds. They drew together and began gathering power.

The collision of Precipice Blades and Origin Pulse had finally subsided. Its shock waves were still spreading, but Groudon and Kyogre had resumed fighting at the center. Both bore fresh wounds. Their moves had canceled each other out, but the explosion had hurt them all the same.

As for Rayquaza, Ethan searched the battlefield again. The once-verdant large island had been all but wiped away. Broken branches and other debris floated on the water and steadily sank. Rayquaza was nowhere to be seen.

The blast must have driven it beneath the sea. Ethan doubted its life was in danger, but at such close range, the explosion might have knocked it unconscious. It could take some time to recover.

If only it had listened to him. He shook his head. There was no time to look for it now.

Ethan raised his eyes to the clouds above the battle. The explosion had scattered much of them along with everything below. Sunlight had broken through, and the extreme weather had vanished. That respite lasted only a moment.

Under the three birds' power, thick clouds formed again. Lightning flashed and thunder followed. The sky over the sea darkened once more.

Groudon and Kyogre noticed none of it. Intent on each other, they collided at close quarters and kept fighting, oblivious to what was building overhead.

Go on. Keep fighting. Now it's your turn to take an attack from me.

The birds' dance continued above the clouds. After a few minutes, they had gathered enough power. A tremendous peal of thunder sounded, and at their direction a column of energy poured from the sky like a waterfall toward Groudon and Kyogre.

Only then did the two primal Pokemon sense something wrong. They looked up as the torrent descended around them. It was too late to dodge; in their confusion, neither even seemed capable of reacting to the danger. They could only take the blow.

Within moments, the energy swallowed them both. Ethan and the others could no longer see either Pokemon. All that remained before them was the dazzling column and the harsh hum of its power as it poured down.

Maxie, Archie, and Matt had never seen Tri-Bird Assault before. Their mouths hung open. If they had not witnessed it themselves, they would never have believed Pokemon other than Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre could produce an attack this strong.

That man truly was a monster.

The torrent stopped in less than half a minute. The birds had already spent part of their strength holding back the explosion, so they could not sustain this attack as long as they had before. It was enough.

As the light cleared, everyone looked toward the center of the battlefield. Both ancient Pokemon lay on the ruined island. After a long pause, Primal Kyogre stirred and slowly lifted itself from the ground. It was covered in wounds, but it could still move.

It had actually endured the attack. Its exceptional special defense and stamina had surely helped.

Primal Groudon did not rise. It remained where it had fallen. The glow along its body faded, and it reverted from its primal state to its ordinary form.

Groudon had given out first. Kyogre had been the one surrounded and attacked earlier, and both had suffered from the collision of their signature moves. Groudon had started with more strength, yet it was the one that fell. Its hard hide gave it formidable physical defense, but that could not protect it from this torrent of energy.

Ethan let out a breath. The birds could use Tri-Bird Assault only once in this fight. If it had accomplished little, he would have needed another plan. Instead, it had knocked Groudon out and left Kyogre badly injured. The situation had turned in their favor.

He called the weakened birds back and was about to send Deoxys in to finish the fight when the sea beside the battlefield burst open. His black Rayquaza surged out of the water.

It was covered in wounds, much like Primal Kyogre. The blast from Precipice Blades and Origin Pulse had injured it badly. Even so, Rayquaza charged at Kyogre without hesitation.

Ethan stopped Deoxys and let Rayquaza have its chance.

By now, the outcome was nearly settled. Ethan had prepared other options for this battle. He had even made an arrangement with the two Deoxys he had met in LaRousse: if his Deoxys produced an aurora, they would come to help. It appeared he would not need to call them.

Once Groudon and Kyogre failed to withstand Tri-Bird Assault, their defeat became all but certain. The one still standing might turn its attacks entirely on Ethan's Pokemon, but it no longer had the strength to change the battle.

Then there was the unconscious Groudon.

Ethan studied it for a long time, torn over what to do, before looking away. Was Groudon strong? Of course. It belonged among the most powerful Pokemon in the world, especially after Primal Reversion.

Did he want to catch it? The thought tempted him a little. Only a little.

There were Pokemon he liked far more. His feelings toward Groudon and Kyogre were lukewarm, and he did not need to catch every powerful Pokemon he encountered. Keeping one of these two with him might bring more trouble than it was worth. Better to let them sleep undisturbed in hidden places and allow their legends to live on.

Rayquaza and Primal Kyogre were fighting again. Though both were badly injured, the difference in strength soon put Rayquaza on the defensive.

Then the balance changed. As Kyogre's remaining strength fell, its Primal Reversion ended. Its body visibly shrank back to its usual size, and the -shaped markings vanished within seconds.

Look! Misty said, brightening. It doesn't have enough energy left to keep its primal form!

Ethan hurriedly took the two orbs from his bag. Their glow had returned to normal. The connection between them and the ancient Pokemon had plainly broken.

The orbs were only a trigger. They could induce Primal Reversion and make Groudon and Kyogre stronger, but they did not supply the energy to sustain it. That energy came from the Pokemon themselves, and the stronger form consumed it at a tremendous rate. Once their reserves fell below a certain point, they reverted.

With Kyogre back in its ordinary form, the fight turned again. It was no match for the black Rayquaza now. After being pushed back for so long, Rayquaza finally gained the upper hand and pressed its attack.

Kyogre seemed to lose much of its fighting spirit along with its primal form. Unable to withstand Rayquaza's assault, it turned and fled. This was the second time it had left a battle in defeat.

Rayquaza tried to pursue it. Ethan called it back through telepathy. Still unaccustomed to being a Trainer's Pokemon, Rayquaza did stop chasing Kyogre, but it did not return. It darted back and forth over the sea, as though proclaiming itself the battle's true victor.

Ethan had no patience for that behavior. He gave Gardevoir the Ultra Ball. She Teleported within range and recalled Rayquaza herself.

As Gardevoir returned, several dark shapes crossed the sky. Ethan looked up. The three Legendary birds folded their wings and landed beside him.

It's finally over, Shelly said, surveying the devastation. What do we do now?

Ethan looked across the battlefield. Kyogre had gone so far that it was barely a dark speck in the distance. Groudon lay where it had fallen, showing no sign of waking.

Farther out, Courtney's ship sat beyond the battle zone. She had rescued most of the teammates who had fallen into the water, but the ship had taken damage from being so close. It seemed to have lost power and remained motionless.

Ethan recalled the birds, glanced at Maxie and Archie, and answered Shelly. First we'll wake Groudon and get it away from here. I notified the International Police on our way here, so they should arrive soon. We'll hand these people over when they do, explain what happened with you and Courtney, and then I'll return the two orbs. That should settle everything.

Yes. It was over. Maxie and Archie were both in custody. Their commanders had either left their organizations or been captured. Even without a wider pursuit, Team Aqua and Team Magma would fall apart sooner or later.

After all these years, Shelly had never expected it to end this way. Yet now that the moment had come, she felt strangely uncertain.

What am I supposed to do next?

Chapter 739: It's All Over

Just as Ethan had predicted, several International Police patrol boats appeared on the horizon about half an hour later, speeding toward them.

After receiving Shelly's and Courtney's messages, he had contacted Anabel before coming here. Her patrol boat had spent a long time at sea, but it had finally arrived.

They never seemed to be there when he needed help most, yet the International Police never missed the aftermath. Late, but here at last. Fortunately, Anabel had remained offshore nearby. Had she gone ashore, she could not have reached them so quickly.

While they waited, Ethan had Misty's Water-type Pokemon spray Groudon with clean water to wake it. Groudon proved sensible enough. When it opened its eyes, its old rival was gone and several formidable opponents were watching it closely. Without hesitation, it dragged its wounded body toward the sea and kept walking. Before their eyes, the water swallowed it completely.

Too heavy to swim on the surface, it could only hold its breath and leave along the seabed. The sight hardly suited the dignity of an ancient Legendary Pokemon. But then, as Ethan had observed more than once, Groudon could not fly.

With both ancient Pokemon gone, the crisis was truly over. Now came the cleanup.

There was little left on the battlefield to clear. Ethan and the others recalled the Pokemon they no longer needed, keeping only Dragonite and Gengar out to guard the prisoners.

Courtney left Team Magma's ship in a speedboat, bringing the captive Tabitha with her. Most of the Team Magma and Team Aqua members she had pulled from the water took the remaining speedboats and lifeboats and fled when they saw the patrol boats. Only a few with serious injuries could not be moved.

After a battle like that, the escapees were too shaken to think of rescuing their leaders. Their leaders? Their own lives mattered more.

Ethan made no effort to stop them. They were minor members. With both leaders and their commanders captured, what could the rest accomplish? At worst they might cause local disturbances, and Officer Jennys across Hoenn could deal with that without calling in the International Police.

The engine grew louder. Courtney reached the little island, brought Tabitha ashore, and marched him toward them.

Well done. Ethan sent Gengar to meet her. Gengar tied Tabitha up beside Maxie and the others. Ethan then turned to Courtney. I wondered where you'd gone. Setting an ambush along the escape route caught him completely off guard. Thanks to you, we've got both leaders and all their commanders.

Shelly rolled her eyes and pursed her lips, looking almost jealous, but for once she did not argue with Courtney. She had to admit that without Courtney's kick, Tabitha might have escaped. That would have spoiled an otherwise complete victory.

She did not look at Courtney, but two men beside her stared at the former commander with open hatred: Maxie and Tabitha. Maxie had abandoned Courtney first, yet she had undeniably turned against Team Magma, joined Ethan, and helped bring them down. A traitor, as far as they were concerned. They wanted to tear her apart. Bound and defeated, they could do nothing but curse her silently.

Courtney paid them no attention. After everything that had happened, she had fallen for Ethan just as Shelly had. His praise brought a faint smile to her lips and a new brightness to her eyes.

That only made Shelly more jealous. Courtney had fallen for him quickly.

A rhythmic roar sounded overhead. A helicopter crossed the sea and descended onto the island. Its door opened, and Anabel jumped out.

Well, well. She looked Ethan over in amazement. You've made a spectacle of yourself again.

The birds had stopped most of the escaping energy, but some had become wind, cloud, and rain that spread across the surrounding sea and coastal areas. Hurricanes and enormous waves had struck the islands. The patrol boats approaching the battlefield had pitched violently in the storm.

I didn't cause this. Ethan nodded toward Maxie and the other prisoners and shrugged. They did. I was merely passing by, happened to recover the orbs, happened to catch them, and happened to resolve the whole thing.

That is quite a lot of things to happen by chance. Anabel smiled at his joke. Whatever you call it, thank you. You spared Hoenn's people a terrible crisis and brought the leaders of Team Magma and Team Aqua to justice. Everyone can see what you've done. We won't forget it.

It's nothing. I like testing myself in situations like this and growing stronger. Personally, I'd welcome more of them. He paused, then added with a half-smile, Though a more tangible reward would be nice.

He meant it as a small joke. To his surprise, Anabel nodded.

There is a reward.

Really? Ethan stared at her. There actually is?

Of course. The higher-ups have decided to give you the honorary title of Special Investigator of the International Police. You'll receive a cash award as well.

Special Investigator? And cash?

His eyes lit up. The title meant little to him. It was honorary; it would neither change his life nor give him license to do as he pleased. The money, thoughthat was welcome. He had no idea how much it would be, but he was pleased to get any at all.

Maxie's and Archie's faces darkened. They knew exactly why Ethan was receiving an award, and it had come at their expense. Their fury accomplished nothing.

The decision was made some time ago, Anabel continued. You know how slow approvals can be in a department like ours. It's nearly finished now, and you should receive everything soon.

How much money?

She kept that to herself. You'll find out when it arrives. I can tell you it won't be less than the prize money you won at a League Conference.

That was vague. The Indigo and Silver Conferences took place on the same landmass and split the field between them. Competition at each had been thinner, and their prizes smaller. He had heard the Ever Grande Conference paid generously, but which one did she mean?

Even at the lower end, it would be two or three million. A sum like that for nothing more than what he had already done was excellent news.

So I wasn't working for free after all, he said with a grin. But a title and a reward? It sounds as though you're trying to tie me to the International Police.

Is that strange? Anabel asked frankly. A Trainer as strong as you, with sound principles, is exactly the kind of partner we want. For the stability of every region, of course we'd make an effort to keep your cooperation.

Strong, yes. Ethan could agree with that. Sound principles? His outlook on life and his values were fine. His views on romance, though...

Ahem. Best not to dwell on that.

It was a funny coincidence. Professor Cerise had made him a special investigator for the laboratory, and now the International Police wanted to give him the same title. He really seemed destined for the name, though he had never set out to investigate anything. One event had simply led to another.

Those are the official thanks, Anabel said. For my personal thanks, how about I treat you to dinner once this is all settled?

Shelly, Courtney, and Misty all looked at her at once. Each gaze held at least a little hostility. Ethan felt the weight of their stares and hurriedly waved a hand.

I don't have much time right now. Some other day.

Anabel knew how busy he was, with Gyms to challenge and the Ever Grande Conference approaching. She did not press him. All right. Let me know when you can.

While they talked, a patrol boat came alongside the damaged Team Magma ship. Police officers boarded in a stream, secured the vessel, and moved the injured Team Aqua and Team Magma members onto their boat.

After their conversation, Anabel took Ethan and the others aboard a patrol boat, escorting Maxie and his fellow prisoners with them. There was a great deal of work ahead: questioning and detaining the members of both organizations, for a start.

At Ethan's request, Shelly and Courtney received special immunity from the International Police. They were classified as informants. Once they had given a full account of what had happened, they would face no further penalty. It was the best outcome they could have hoped for.

There was one condition. They had spent years in their organizations and taken part in their activities. To make certain they had truly left that life behind, and to ensure their treatment did not look entirely without consequence, they would remain under a guardian's supervision for one year.

The person assigned to supervise them was, naturally, Ethan.

It was mostly a formality. He would keep traveling, not watch them every hour. Anabel knew that perfectly well. She had used her authority to give them a workable arrangement, even if her superiors might object to it.

The International Police wanted to maintain their good relationship with Ethan. Provided a request did not go too far or violate a principle she had to uphold, Anabel would do what she could for him. This decision showed how much she valued him.

Everything proceeded in order. The whole affair seemed settled at last.

While Shelly and Courtney gave their statements in an interview room aboard the boat, Ethan and Misty leaned against the deck railing and looked into the distance. The dark clouds had cleared. Even the sea appeared calm again.

If several islands marked on the map had not been shattered and sunk beneath the water, a person might never have guessed that such a battle had taken place here.

It's finally over, Misty said, smiling as the sea breeze stirred her bangs. Now we can focus on traveling and getting ready for the Ever Grande Conference.

Yes. Team Aqua and Team Magma won't be springing up in our path anymore. Ethan sighed. One more Badge and I can enter the Conference. That went fast.

Misty's mood turned wistful. Their journey through Hoenn really was nearing its end. After the Ever Grande Conference, she would have to return to Cerulean City and take over the Gym.

But I haven't spent enough time with Ethan yet.

She hated the thought of leaving.

Ethan did not know what was on her mind. He said nothing more, and the two of them quietly watched the view.

Some time later, two sets of soft footsteps approached. Shelly and Courtney joined them at the railing.

Ethan smiled at their expressions. You both look all right. How did it go? Is everything settled?

Chapter 740: Meeting Bea for the Third Time

It is, Shelly said with a long sigh. She leaned on the railing beside them and watched the white clouds on the horizon. Thanks to you, we're both in the clear. They no longer classify us as members of Team Aqua and Team Magma. We're officially your informants now. We've cut ties with those organizations completely.

Ethan looked to Courtney. She nodded; she had received the same treatment.

Did Anabel say what will happen to Maxie and Archie?

What else? They'll go back to the mainland and stand trial. I expect they'll spend the rest of their lives locked up with other serious offenders.

Ethan was not surprised. There was no death penalty in this world. A life sentence, leaving them to grow old alone in a small cell, was the harshest punishment they could receive.

Good. What will you two do next?

Shelly gave him a half-smile. What can we do? That woman just put us under your supervision. We're still under observation. Officially and privately, it seems we're tied to your side.

No one's restricting your freedom, Ethan said. The supervision is mostly a formality. I'm going to keep traveling; I can't have you with me all the time. Anabel knows that. It's probably why she made me your supervisor.

He thought a moment. Actually, do what I suggested before. Both of you should go to Kanto. I have an investment there, and a group of people who've had trouble fitting into ordinary society have gathered around it. You'd fit in. More than that, I'd like your help keeping an eye on them.

His expression and tone told Shelly and Courtney there was more to the request.

Are they causing trouble? Courtney asked quietly.

Not yet, Ethan said with a shrug. The investment started small, and I didn't pay it much attention. But the group keeps growing. I worry they'll use my name to make trouble. I'd feel better if the two of you watched them for me.

I see. Courtney agreed at once. If that's what you want, I'll go to Kanto.

Shelly rolled her eyes at being beaten to the answer. As you command, Mr. Supervisor.

Are you making fun of me? Ethan glared at her. This is a necessary step toward clearing your names.

Don't like the title? Shelly drew out the question and gave him a mischievous look. Then I suppose I'll call you Boss. Or would you rather we call you Master?

Ethan nearly choked. Shelly really was bold. No wonder she had risen to the second-highest position in an organization like Team Aqua. She knew how to say something outrageous without blinking.

But this was not a joke to make in front of Misty. Even Boss sounded wrong. Anyone who heard it might think he had set up another organization like Team Aqua or Team Magma.

Then he remembered that the bikers already called him that, and the name had spread. He sighed. They could call him whatever they liked.

...

The patrol boats were taking Archie and Maxie back to headquarters, away from Ethan's route. When they passed Muscle Island, Ethan and Misty disembarked. They would see whether they could transfer to a ship bound for the Hoenn mainland.

Shelly and Courtney would accompany Anabel to the International Police's Hoenn headquarters first. Once they completed the final paperwork, they could leave from there and fly to Kanto.

After saying goodbye, Ethan and Misty stood on Muscle Island's pier and waved to them. They watched the patrol boat until it vanished, then turned to look around. Leaving the boat here had been a last-minute decision. They knew nothing about the island.

It was small, but distinctive. A ring of forest surrounded a modest town. At the island's center, two connected rock formations looked like an arm flexing its muscles.

What surprised them was the port. No ships were docked there, and there was not a person in sight.

That's strange, Misty said, looking around. Where is everyone?

Ethan checked the time. It was only about three or four in the afternoon, too early for dinner. Even if people were eating, surely someone would still be out on the streets.

The empty streets were not really a problem for them. The empty harbor was. How would they get back to mainland Hoenn? Would he have to ride Dragonite again? It would be fast, but sitting in one position for hours while the sea wind battered him was uncomfortable. His body had had enough of it.

Let's find someone to ask. Given the island's size and location, ships may not come often. We might have to stay here tonight.

They left the harbor and walked through town. It was not entirely deserted. Through a general store's window, they saw an elderly woman struggling to arrange the goods. They had just started toward her when a chorus of shouts rose from a nearby forest park.

It sounded like a crowd exercising, voices ringing out in a vigorous rhythm. Curious, Ethan and Misty exchanged a look and headed for the park instead.
