Past several thick trees, they came upon a clearing where thirty or forty men and women were training. The youngest were in their mid-teens, the oldest in their forties. All wore sports clothes, though some had taken off their shirts, and others wore hats or sunglasses. They did squats, threw punches, climbed, and lifted weights. Every one of them looked athletic.

That's... Misty stared. Quite a sight.

Seeing so many people exercise together was startling. The whole park seemed thick with sweat and raw enthusiasm, almost too much for either of them.

Then Ethan noticed someone familiar in a corner of the clearing: a gray-haired girl in a black-and-white athletic top and shorts, working through the exercises with the rest.

Wait. Isn't that Bea?

Misty followed his gaze. It is! What is she doing here, training with all these people?

Let's ask.

They circled the edge of the park and approached Bea. She was so focused on her workout that she did not notice them until Misty greeted her. Bea turned in surprise.

You two?

She plainly had not expected to meet Ethan and Misty here again.

Good to see you again, Bea, Misty said. What are you doing here?

Training my muscles with everyone so I can grow stronger.

Your muscles? Ethan glanced around, puzzled. I understand the idea, but will this actually make you stronger? Is it doing anything for you?

Bea was strong enough to contend physically with Pokemon. Her reputation as a once-in-a-century talent in Galar was well deserved. The others in the park, however, were doing fairly basic exercises. With Bea's conditioning, even twice this difficulty would probably bring little improvement.

She had not considered that. The man in charge told me that if I followed his method, I would definitely get stronger.

That was all it took to convince her? Ethan and Misty exchanged another look.

Is it possible, Misty asked carefully, that he misled you?

Bea looked at her in obvious confusion.

Does the man even know how strong you already are? Ethan asked.

Bea tilted her head. What do you mean?

For all her dedication to training and her position as a Fighting-type Gym Leader, she seemed innocent about other people and their intentions.

I mean he might not understand your abilities. He saw how young you are and assumed you're an ordinary beginner. This routine is probably just wasting your time.

Bea thought that through in earnest. I see. That explains why I haven't noticed any changes in my body.

Ethan and Misty stared at her. She was only realizing that now?

At that moment, a young man came over from the other side of the clearing, perhaps because their conversation had interrupted Bea's training. He looked about twenty-seven or twenty-eight, with tanned skin, a lean muscular build, a sleeveless athletic shirt, and short reddish-brown hair. He had an open, good-looking face.

He glanced at Bea, then at Ethan and Misty. Good afternoon. Is this your first time on the island?

He gave them a brilliant smile. His teeth were so white that they almost seemed to flash. This must be the man Bea had mentioned. At least he seemed friendly and straightforward.

It is, Ethan said. We hoped to take a ship back to mainland Hoenn, but there aren't any at the harbor. Why is town so empty? And where did all the boats go?

Oh, that. A warning went out that the waters around here would be dangerous for the next few days. Most people took the boats to larger cities this morning to wait it out. Didn't you receive the warning before you came?

Dangerous waters. Ethan understood: the warning must have been about Groudon and Kyogre. Even this town's emptiness was a consequence of their battle. The storm they had raised had finally blown back into his own plans.

If the town evacuated, Misty asked, why did all of you stay?

The man waved a hand. A few waves and a storm can't break our spirit. Trainers should toughen themselves in extreme weather!

They were a determined group. Many Trainers these days sheltered in a Pokemon Center at the first hint of rain, unwilling to endure any discomfort. These people still welcomed a challenge.

Unfortunately for them, the storm they had been waiting for would never come. Ethan had already ended it.

Even with the warning lifted, the town's boats would not return until its residents did. No ship was likely to call today. Ethan and Misty would have to spend the night.

The man looked them over. You're Trainers too, aren't you? Why not join us? The secret to winning Pokemon battles lies in a Trainer's muscles. Without a body honed through hard work, you can't win!

Only a Fighting-type Trainer would say that. The group's physiques and exercises made it clear that Fighting types were their specialty. No wonder Bea had joined them.

Ethan could not agree with the man's claim. Surely Pokemon battles depended first on the Pokemon. A Trainer mattered too, but building muscles while neglecting tactics would only get a person so far. He saw no point in arguing with this crowd.

Thanks, but we'll pass. He smiled. We're friends of Bea's. We saw her here and just came over to say hello.

Chapter 741: A Double Battle with Bea

If you're friends, why not join us for some muscle training? The man grinned at Ethan and Misty again. Ah, I forgot to introduce myself. I'm Rocky. I started this training ground and run it, and I'm the strongest Trainer on the island. If you want to be as strong as I am and reach the heights of Pokemon battling, you have to train your muscles without giving up!

Rocky was clearly confident in his abilities. Perhaps that was how he had gathered such a crowd.

But the strongest Trainer on this island? Its only settlement was a small town, with few residents and probably fewer Trainers. Visitors might rarely stay here at all. Ethan could not imagine proudly introducing himself with such a limited title.

He would not have mentioned it even if it were true of him. That was not because winning two regional tournaments had made him look down on ordinary Trainers. There were simply too many little islands and towns in the world. If each had someone claiming to be its strongest Trainer, the claim meant very little.

And Rocky was inviting others to become as strong as he was. Even Ethan would not say something like that.

Sorry, Ethan said, shaking his head. Traveling over mountains and across seas tires me out enough. I don't want to spend more energy on exercises like these. Besides, I think sound tactics and developing your Pokemon are the only way to reach the top of Pokemon battling.

It was the opposite of Rocky's view. Ethan normally had the manners not to say such a thing to a man's face. But Rocky had apparently drawn Bea into basic exercises without understanding how strong she already was. He was wasting her time while insisting that his own narrow approach was the answer. His hearty smile did not make Ethan like him any better.

Rocky frowned. Oh? He looked Ethan up and down. You've got it completely wrong. An excellent physique is crucial to Pokemon battling. It can even be the key to victory.

There's no point arguing, Ethan said with a shrug. I can't change your mind, and you can't change mine.

Rocky had evidently not expected to disagree so sharply with a visitor. You come to Muscle Island and say that? You don't know our traditions. Fine. If you think your method is better, let's settle it the way Trainers do. We'll battle and see which approach works.

A battle? Well... Ethan hesitated.

Rocky took his hesitation for fear. What, don't you dare? Was all that talk? Maybe you're simply afraid of hard work.

Ordinarily, I'd battle you ten times if you liked, Ethan said with a sigh. My Pokemon are in an unusual situation right now, though. This isn't a good time.

It was no excuse. He had just fought Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre and had not adjusted his lineup. The seven Legendary Pokemon with himDeoxys, the black Rayquaza, Zapdos, Articuno, Moltres, Suicune, and Raikouwere hardly fair choices against Rocky.

His other Pokemon were Gardevoir, Gengar, Dragonite, and two reserves he had kept with him: his giant red Gyarados and Crystal Steelix. Those twelve were all he currently carried. Which one could he use without making the battle feel like bullying?

If he had to name the weakest, it would be Dragonite. Even then, he feared Rocky might come away from a battle with it permanently shaken.

The people exercising nearby heard the exchange and gathered around. Rocky explained what the visitor had said. At once the crowd united in outrage at Ethan's strange ideas.

Hey, kid! You're good-looking, but what a weakling!

Only someone strong in body can reach the top of Pokemon battling!

That's right! Hard muscle training makes you the strongest!

Female Machamp rules!

Ethan sighed at the jeers. He had had enough of these people, with muscles where their brains should be. They were rude and would not listen. Now he had little choice but to battle. He had intended to give Rocky some dignity, as a visitor merely passing through. That courtesy was losing its appeal.

Then let thunder break through the darkness.

He reached for Gardevoir's Poke Ball, ready to teach them a lesson. Before he could draw it, Bea stepped in front of him.

They had become friends after sheltering together from the rain in a cave on Dewford Island. Bea might know little of social niceties, but she would not stand aside while a friend faced a hostile crowd. Besides, she knew Ethan had objected to Rocky's training because of her. She could not leave him to handle the trouble alone.

She looked Ethan in the eye. I'll take this battle for you.

She had seen him hesitate and assumed something was wrong with his Pokemon. She knew from watching his Gym battle on Dewford Island that he was strong and not afraid to fight. Why else would he hold back? Perhaps his Pokemon had been badly injured and he had not had time to treat them. It was the only explanation she could think of.

Ethan and Rocky both turned to her. Ethan was surprised that she had stepped forward. Rocky was surprised for another reason: this pretty, short-haired girl was a Fighting-type specialist like him, yet she was taking the side of someone he considered an outsider to their training.

He studied her for a moment, then glanced pointedly at Ethan. Anyone can battle me. But I wouldn't hide behind a woman.

The taunt did not trouble Ethan. Misty was furious on his behalf. She knew why he had hesitated: his Pokemon were too strong. Any one of his Legendary Pokemon would cause a sensation merely by appearing, and Rocky had mistaken his restraint for cowardice.

She glared at Rocky. Ethan, do it. Teach him a lesson!

Ethan reached for a Poke Ball. At this point, he could only show them the difference between their abilities. His movement convinced Bea even more firmly that something was wrong with his Pokemon.

No. Let me handle it, she insisted.

It's all right. I can

Leave it to me.

Watching them argue over who would face him, Rocky felt they were looking down on him. He held up a hand. Enough. If both of you want to fight, we'll make it a Double Battle!

Ethan and Bea exchanged a glance and nodded, as though they had reached an agreement without words.

All right, Ethan said. Two against two.

The onlookers quickly cleared a space, abandoning their workouts to watch. Ethan and Bea took one side. Rocky chose a woman in her twenties with a red band tied around her head as his partner, and they went to the other.

Go on!

Rocky, beat that rude man!

Show him what we can do!

Let him feel the power of muscles!

The crowd shouted for Rocky. Misty answered from among them. She was only one person, but she cupped her hands around her mouth and called with all her strength.

Go, Ethan!

Once everyone was in place, Rocky set the rules. We're only here to decide who wins. No need for anything complicated. Each Trainer sends out one Pokemon. Defeat both opposing Pokemon, and you win.

Ethan and Bea nodded. A man acting as referee blew his whistle, and all four Trainers threw their Poke Balls. Blue light flashed, revealing four Pokemon in the clearing.

Rocky's choice surprised Ethan. Despite all his talk of muscles, he had sent out a Walrein rather than a Fighting-type. His partner fit Ethan's expectations better: she had a Hitmonchan.

For all the time they spent training their bodies, this group did not restrict themselves to Fighting-type Pokemon.

Bea sent out her signature Machamp. She was taking the match seriously. Ethan chose Gardevoir. In an ordinary battle, both Pokemon would be among their Trainers' strongest partners.

With all four ready, the referee signaled the start.

Before the battle, Ethan had wondered whether this group's physical training gave them some unusual way to fight. He soon found he had imagined too much. Rocky and his partner stood in place like any other Trainers. They neither moved with their Pokemon nor used their own bodies for anything. They merely looked more energetic.

Had all that tireless exercise accomplished nothing more than that? Ethan wondered, but the battle was underway.

At the four Trainers' commands, their Pokemon engaged. Bea and the other woman naturally matched their Fighting-types against each other. Both ordered them forward to settle the fight at close range. Ethan and Rocky took a more direct approach: their Pokemon attacked from where they stood.

Machamp ran toward the center of the field, swinging all four arms at Hitmonchan. Hitmonchan answered with both gloved fists. Just before their punches met, something hissed past them.

Gardevoir's invisible psychic force collided with Walrein's thick stream of water beside the fighters. The water burst into spray and drenched them both.

Chapter 742: A Black Terror

Amid the spray, Machamp and Hitmonchan met in a flurry of fists. One attacked, the other guarded or dodged, then answered with its own blow. In a dozen seconds they threw nearly a hundred punches.

But two fists were no match for four arms. Hitmonchan punched so fast its gloves blurred, yet Machamp soon gained the upper hand. There was a hard difference in strength. A Gym Leader's ace was not going to go easy on the Pokemon of a Trainer from a remote island.

It was a fight on entirely different levels.

Gardevoir and Walrein's contest proved just as one-sided after their first probing exchange. Not just anyone could stand against one of Ethan's strongest regular partners.

Gardevoir seldom fought these days and could almost be overlooked. But it had been with Ethan longer than any of his other Pokemon, growing steadily stronger all the while. His mutated giant red Gyarados might surpass it, as might Gengar, who had lived for thousands of years. Apart from those two, no one in his usual lineup could beat it.

Under ordinary circumstances, if Rocky had formally challenged Ethan, his Walrein would never even have faced Gardevoir.

After scattering Walrein's Water Gun, Gardevoir used Psychic again. An invisible force wrapped around the Pokemon and lifted its entire body into the air.

The interval between Gardevoir's two psychic attacks was so short, and both moves so fast, that Rocky had no time to react. Before he understood what had happened, Walrein was trapped.

How could Gardevoir attack again that quickly?

Walrein, break free!

Rocky frowned. But Gardevoir's control of psychic power had long since become masterful. Walrein could not simply struggle out. Gardevoir pressed its hands down. Psychic force squeezed Walrein, then hurled it to the ground. It landed heavily on Hitmonchan, which Machamp had just knocked backward.

Thud!

The two Pokemon lay in a heap. The crowd's cheers for Rocky died away. Everyone stared, too shocked to speak. No one had expected this. The girl who had trained beside them for days and the young man who had only just arrived were dominating the island's strongest Trainer.

Only Misty's excited voice broke the silence. Go, Ethan! Go, Bea!

Walrein and Hitmonchan had both taken a hard hit. Their limbs were tangled, and they struggled to get up. Machamp strode toward them.

Walrein, pull yourself together! Get up! Rocky shouted.

His Pokemon needed no warning. Both could see Machamp coming. Their frantic attempts to rise only got in each other's way. They were experienced enough to recover from the confusion, though, and managed to stand before Machamp reached them.

Hitmonchan had barely raised its fists when Machamp's punches fell like a storm.

Thud, thud, thud!

Caught off guard, Hitmonchan took a dozen more blows. Machamp seized an opening, lifted it high with Seismic Toss, and slammed it back to the ground.

Walrein, meanwhile, fired a chilling, pale-blue Aurora Beam at Gardevoir. That was not enough to catch it. Gardevoir Teleported aside, appeared on Walrein's other flank, and struck with another direct Psychic. Walrein fell.

It was an overwhelming victory. Ethan and Bea had held nothing back and given their opponents no chance to recover.

For Ethan, Rocky was no harder to beat than an ordinary Team Aqua or Team Magma member. He was not Ash, and Gardevoir was not Pikachu. Its strength did not reset or fluctuate wildly so that a weaker opponent could fight it on even terms. Once Ethan had sent out one of his aces, he would press that advantage and leave the other side no opening.

What? Rocky could hardly believe how easily Walrein had fallen. This had barely resembled a Double Battle. His side had lost almost as soon as the Pokemon engaged. They had done no meaningful damage, and after only two or three hits, both had gone down.

Walrein had balanced abilities and excellent stamina. Since when had it been so fragile? Or was the gulf between them so wide that it only seemed weak?

Before Rocky could absorb the sight, something flashed at the edge of his vision. He turned to see his partner's Hitmonchan fly backward and land flat on its back. They had been completely defeated in just a few exchanges.

The crowd erupted. None of them had expected their island's strongest Trainer to lose like this. Rocky stared for a long moment before he grasped how far above him Ethan stood.

So strong. Why had Ethan been reluctant to battle if he had a Pokemon like that? And why was Bea, who had seemed so ordinary during training, just as impressive?

Rocky could not make sense of it. He knew that even if they fought again, he would lose. The thought left him dispirited.

I lost, he admitted. He recalled Walrein. You're strong. Stronger than anyone I've met. But that doesn't prove your method is better than ours. Even after losing to you, we'll keep training our muscles.

Ethan merely shrugged. He had no urge to gloat or resume their argument. How these people trained was their own business. Rocky had challenged him, and he had answered with overwhelming strength.

Gardevoir had never been threatened. The fight had not helped it improve. It had scarcely counted as a warm-up. That was not Ethan boasting; these were simply the Pokemon he had with him. Had he chosen Eevee, Metang, or Milotic instead, he might still have won, but not so effortlessly.

Rocky had been unlucky to challenge him at this particular moment. Ethan saw no reason to say more. He waved to the group and left with Bea and Misty.

To him, it was a minor interruption. After tonight, Rocky would probably disappear into the depths of his memory. Perhaps Ethan would recall the battle only when he thought back on meeting Bea again.

...

At sea off Sootopolis Island, the International Police patrol boat continued southwest. It had sailed for hours since Ethan and Misty disembarked. Its destination was not Sootopolis City but Slateport City, on the southern coast of the Hoenn mainland, where the International Police had their regional headquarters.

Shelly had spent hours sitting idly in the cabin. Before night fell, she went out onto the deck for some air. As soon as she emerged, she spotted Courtney leaning against the railing and gazing toward the horizon. Shelly clicked her tongue, then walked over and looked out to sea beside her.

They were both aboard a police vessel. Their names had been cleared, but Shelly still felt more at ease near a former member of an organization like her own than among officers she had once had to avoid. Courtney glanced at her and said nothing.

They stood together in an awkward but strangely companionable silence. Shelly lost track of time. The cool sea wind began to bite through her clothes. She looked at Courtney's windproof cloak, gave a small huff, and pulled her own clothing tighter.

She was about to go back inside when a rainbow caught her eye. It was beautiful, its colors touched with gold in the evening light.

Yet Shelly frowned. A rainbow at dusk? There had been no rain, nor could she see any mist in the air. Why would one appear out of nowhere?

Then it changed. A gap opened in the curved rainbow like a doorway, revealing a deep black space behind it, dark as a star-filled sky. Something Shelly had never seen before emerged from the opening.

A Pokemon, she supposed.

It was tall and bizarre. Its body seemed made of black crystal, gleaming with an uncanny dark light, like living armor shaped around a monster. It had no wings, yet floated in the sky. Three claws tipped each huge hand, and a three-sided crystal projection rose from each hand's back, fading from white to black. Its legs were thin, especially below the knees. Jagged edges lined its sides, and an enormous four-sided pyramidal tail extended behind it. Spikes that shone black jutted from its helmetlike head.

One look was enough to chill Shelly to the bone.

Alarm rang through her. She had never seen this frightening creature, and it was still far away, yet she felt certain it had come for their ship.

In the next instant, it vanished. When it reappeared, it was directly above the patrol boat.

Look out!

Shelly searched for someone to warn, but apart from Courtney, no one was nearby. Most of the officers were in the dining room.

The strange Pokemon made its move. It barely seemed to stir, but an invisible force stopped the entire patrol boat dead. The engines kept driving against whatever held it. The hull shuddered as if it had struck a solid object, and a shrill, grinding sound of twisting metal rose from below.

The sudden jolt threw everyone aboard off their feet. Shelly, accustomed to years at sea, caught the railing as she fell and quickly stood again. She looked up at the Pokemon, her face grim.

A Psychic-type. It had to be. In Shelly's judgment, no other kind of Pokemon could hold a patrol boat this large in place. That made it all the more dangerous.

Where had it come from? Why attack this ship?

There was no time to puzzle it out. Alarms rang across the water. After their first moment of confusion, the trained International Police officers regrouped and rushed onto the deck fully armed.

Hurried footsteps sounded beside Shelly. Anabel staggered out, still dizzy from being knocked down. She gripped the railing and stared at the black Pokemon overhead.

What... what is that?

Chapter 743: Making a Rival for Herself

Seeing Anabel's astonishment, Shelly wanted to say that if even the International Police did not know what the creature was, the rest of them certainly could not.

One thing seemed clear: this unknown Pokemon was at least in Groudon and Kyogre's class, perhaps stronger. Its extraordinary shape and the pressure it gave off made that plain. A single glance was enough to tell anyone it was no ordinary Pokemon.

Anabel did not know what it wanted, but it had attacked a police boat. That made it an enemy. Worse, its intent felt unmistakably hostile. Recovering from her surprise, she organized the officers around her to fight back.

Poke Balls flashed across the deck. A large group of Arcanine appeared and, at their officers' orders, sent a mass of flames into the sky. The volley looked formidable. As the fire reached the creature, however, it passed straight through its body and sped on without hitting anything.

It was like punching a shadow. The attack met no resistance, not even a ripple.

How is that possible?

The officers stared in disbelief. None understood why they could not touch it.

Shelly was the first to grasp what they were seeing. It's a projection! Its real body isn't here. We can't hit it!

Anabel's brow tightened. A projection? What kind of Pokemon could damage a ship like this using only a projection? How terrifying would the real creature be? And what did it want?

No one could answer her. The Pokemon soon showed them its purpose.

Two shafts of black light shot from its hands into the ship. Moments later, they emerged carrying Archie and Maxie, wrapped in darkness, out of the cabin where the men had been held.

Anabel had not imagined the prisoners were its target. Their flailing and bewildered faces showed that Archie and Maxie knew no more than she did. Even the normally composed Maxie looked wildly around him.

Before the watching officers, the two men rose higher and higher. They reached the creature, and all three vanished into the black opening overhead.

The attack ended as quickly as it had begun. Anabel and her officers had had no means of stopping it. They could only watch the prisoners disappear. Even after the sky returned to normal, the officers stood on deck for some time before they could take in what had happened.

Two dangerous criminals already in custody had been rescued by an unknown Pokemon. They had thought the affair was over. Why had another problem appeared now?

Anabel sighed, her head already aching. Shelly looked at her with some sympathy. After Maxie and Archie were captured, Shelly's and Courtney's past offenses had been cleared. The case no longer involved them. Once they left Hoenn, they would not even need to fear retaliation from their old organizations. For Anabel, however, the trouble was beginning again.

We should contact Ethan, Shelly suggested after a moment. He needs to know. And he might be the only one who can tell us what that Pokemon was.

...

When Ethan received the news, he had just arrived with Bea and Misty at an inn in the small town. The town was too small to have a Pokemon Center, and most of its residents had evacuated and not yet returned. The three had searched for some time before finding this hot spring inn at the foot of a mountain.

That search made Ethan admire Bea all the more. Before they came, she had been eating and sleeping near the park in the forest, exposed to the weather with only a simple tent. She had stripped her life down to the bare necessities for the sake of training. No wonder her body was so strong.

The innkeeper was an elderly woman. She said she had lived through all manner of storms and saw no reason to evacuate. If she died, she would die with her house. She grumbled that young people could not bear a little bad weather and only knew how to build muscles that were no use to them.

Following her running commentary, Ethan and the others entered a guest room and sat down in its Japanese-style sitting area. The woman went to prepare dinner. With no outsider nearby, Ethan finally told Bea and Misty what he had learned.

They were attacked? Misty's eyes widened. I thought it was all over. Are there other Legendary Pokemon in Hoenn besides Rayquaza, Groudon, and Kyogre?

From Anabel's and Shelly's descriptions, Ethan already knew the attacker's identity. It isn't from Hoenn. In a sense, it isn't even a Pokemon of this world.

You know what it is?

Ethan nodded and sighed. It's connected to the creatures called Ultra Beastsbeings from another dimension. More precisely, it's one of the Legendary Cosmic Pokemon. They come from the same place as Ultra Beasts, but they're much stronger and aren't counted among ordinary Ultra Beasts anymore. Ultra Beasts don't naturally belong in this world. Most arrive through wormholes called Ultra Wormholes. They're dangerous, especially when someone puts their power to use. The damage can be catastrophic.

Ultra Beasts? Ultra Wormholes? Legendary Cosmic Pokemon? Misty had never heard any of these terms. Her understanding of the world had shifted yet again.

Bea was equally lost. She did not interrupt. Instead she quietly turned over the unfamiliar information, trying to guess what Ethan and Misty had experienced.

So one of those Legendary Cosmic Pokemon attacked Anabel? Misty asked.

Yes. The one known as the Plunderer of LightNecrozma.

The Plunderer of Light. Misty could not imagine how powerful a Pokemon must be to earn a name like that.

But I don't understand, she said. Why would it rescue Archie and Maxie?

To an outsider, the two men and Necrozma had no apparent connection. Why would such a powerful creature save humans who must seem insignificant to it?

Ethan saw one possible answer in its sudden appearance. Team Rainbow Rocket was already beginning to form.

Led by Giovanni, Team Rainbow Rocket would surpass Team Rocket, Team Magma, Team Aqua, and the other criminal organizations across the regions. It would gather their leaders under one banner. Their immense ambition and malice would resonate with the power spilling from Necrozmathe power to open Ultra Wormholes. Under Giovanni's influence, they would be summoned to Alola and become Team Rainbow Rocket.

Its goal was simple: to rule every world.

With the Aether Foundation's knowledge of other worlds, Team Rainbow Rocket would build a powerful army of Ultra Beasts. Its ordinary members would be extraordinarily strong, and each leader would gain at least one Legendary Pokemon. In wealth and fighting strength, the organization would stand at the world's summit. If no one stopped it, conquering the world might be only a matter of time.

Of course, the stronger the enemy, the greater the resistance it would face. By assembling leaders from every region, Giovanni would also draw opposition from them all.

But that was supposed to be a story for much later, in Alola. Why were there signs of it already? The timing was far too early.

Had Ethan's actions caused a butterfly effect? Team Rocket had suffered a heavy blow, and Team Magma and Team Aqua were on the verge of collapse. Had those changes altered the future?

That explanation did not quite fit. Even if Giovanni had conceived the idea, where would he get the power before reaching Alola? How would he contact Necrozma?

Another possibility struck Ethan: someone in the future was trying to change the present.

In a world of Pokemon, changing time was not impossible. Someone might have reached back through time and brought these events forward. Otherwise, why would Necrozma appear here and take Archie and Maxie specifically? Whoever was behind it must be gathering strength for something.

Whatever the answer, the thought set alarm bells ringing. His enemies were moving. The future looked more dangerous than before.

At least Ethan's own strength continued to grow. If this was connected to him, perhaps his future opponents feared him enough to act early. It was only a guess, but he wanted to believe it.

He shook his head and kept the speculation to himself. Sharing it with Bea and Misty would only trouble them; it would do nothing to help right now.

Ethan changed the subject. The heavy mood gradually lifted. The three were no longer strangers and had shared experiences to draw on, so their conversation wandered easily from one topic to another.

Misty picked out some of the most exciting things she and Ethan had done recently. Bea, never one for many words, gave them a brief account of her own travels. All three learned more about one another.

For the first time, Bea heard that Ethan had won two regional League Conferences, helped the International Police deal heavy blows to three criminal organizations, and even saved the world without anyone noticing.

Misty grew animated as she spoke and stood up at one point in her excitement. Bea did not think she was lying. She had spent enough time with them to have a sense of their characters. Even so, the accounts sounded almost impossible. Bea stared at Ethan, struggling to connect these feats with the handsome man sitting before her.

So that's who he is. He's remarkable.

She remembered offering to fight for him earlier that day. In hindsight, the offer was almost funny.

Misty looked down and caught Bea's expression, the brightness in her eyes. She abruptly regretted how much she had said and sat back on the tatami. She had seen that look too many times.

Everything she had told Bea was true. That was precisely the problem. Why had she gone on about Ethan's virtues to another woman?

What an idiot I am. I've found myself another rival.

Chapter 744: The Wrong Person

Dinner was finally ready around seven that evening. The elderly innkeeper, who was also the cook, filled more than half the square table with a generous meal.

Muscle Island was far from the mainland, with fewer vegetables available, so most of the dishes were seafood. Perhaps Ethan had paid well. Whatever the reason, the woman's decades of cooking experience showed in every plate. Fresh seafood, enticing colors, careful presentationeven familiar ingredients smelled so good that the three guests wanted to taste them at once.

Misty did not wait. She stole a bite before the meal began and gave the cook an enthusiastic thumbs-up.

Mm! It's delicious!

Bea stared at the crowded table, plainly surprised by its size. Ethan smiled. Help yourself.

She hesitated. Do you usually eat this much?

Of course not. Most days we keep things simple. When we meet a friend, though, we sometimes have a feast. It's become a habit.

Bea finally picked up her utensils. Rather than the seafood, her eyes went to the desserts. Ethan and Misty exchanged a surprised look.

Anyone who saw how Bea dressed and knew she specialized in Fighting-type Pokemon might assume she followed a strict training diet, avoiding sugar and fat in favor of protein. Instead, she loved sweets and ate them without restraint. The pleasure on her face after each bite left no doubt.

Ethan and Misty let her enjoy them and turned to their own plates. After a tiring day, a fine meal was an excellent reward.

Neither Bea nor Misty drank alcohol. Ethan poured for himself and had several cups of sake. The food called for something to accompany it, and he had reason to celebrate. Necrozma had taken Maxie and Archie, but Ethan had stopped Groudon and Kyogre. Team Aqua and Team Magma on the Hoenn mainland would be swept away regardless.

The meal lasted until nine. They ate and talked, with Misty doing most of the talking, and all three enjoyed themselves.

After washing up, it was time to sleep. Standing in the bedroom together, however, they found the mood had grown a little delicate.

The old Japanese-style inn was small, with only one guest room. There were no beds. The guests would lay bedding on the tatami and sleep on the floor.

That would not normally have been a problem. Ethan and Bea, however, had not grown close enough for sharing a room to feel entirely natural. They had once sheltered from rain together in a cave and sat together wearing little more than their clothes, but that had been an emergency. Travelers made allowances when they had to.

Here, in a quiet, comfortable room, it felt different. Misty's presence kept things from being too awkward, yet Ethan found himself thinking of them as ordinary people rather than Trainers roughing it outdoors.

While he worried, Bea knelt and spread out her bedding. There was not a hint of embarrassment on her face. Ethan realized he had been the only one fretting. Bea was direct by nature. They were friends, all three would be present, and their bedding would not even touch. Once the light went out, what did it matter?

Her calm helped him relax. It was not merely that he was less decisive than Bea. He already had several women in his life and had to consider how things might look. He also owed Bea respect for her reputation.

Misty laid her bedding beside Bea's. Ethan spread his a little farther away. The sake was beginning to catch up with him. He yawned, slipped under his covers, and fell asleep within seconds.

Misty and Bea were not so quick to sleep. They had eaten too much, and their unsettled stomachs kept them awake. After the light went out, Misty drew Bea into another conversation.

Crack!

A great roll of thunder sounded overhead. Heavy rain began to drum on the roof and pour into the courtyard.

Rain? Misty turned toward the window in the dim light. I like falling asleep to it. It's been stuffy all evening. Maybe this will cool things down.

She wished Bea good night and had barely closed her eyes when something cold touched her face. Her good mood vanished.

What? Is the roof leaking?

She sat up and held out a hand. Several drops fell into her palm. Bea sat up too. Even in the dark, her movements made it clear that water was falling on her bedding as well.

Misty sighed and switched on the light. A wide patch of ceiling above them was wet, and water dripped steadily from it.

What do we do?

The two girls, both in their nightclothes, looked at each other helplessly. Ethan was still sound asleep, and the roof above him was dry. The old inn had evidently needed repairs; tonight's downpour had found the weak spot. There was no one to fix it now.

They looked at the open floor on either side of Ethan. We'll have to move.

Without waking him, they rolled up their bedding and carried it over. Where exactly to put it was another question, particularly for Bea.

Misty had slept beside Ethan many times, in tents and elsewhere. She was used to it. Bea would be much closer to him than before. Would she be able to sleep? They could wake Ethan and ask him to move, but neither wanted to disturb him while he slept so deeply.

After a moment's hesitation, Bea laid out her bedding beside Ethan's. Misty felt a vague unease, then reasoned that they would still be under separate covers. Ethan was asleep anyway. What could happen? She settled on his other side.

Rain continued to fall outside. The light went out, leaving the room dark again.

Bea lay stiffly on her back, listening to the water rush past the window. She could not settle. Her body felt tense, and her heart beat faster than usual. For all her composure, she was lying beside a man. She could hardly be indifferent.

Her regular schedule eventually caught up with her. After some time, her breathing slowed, and she fell asleep.

The rain did not let up. Its steady patter filled the quiet room, along with the faint sound of three people breathing.

Much later, Ethan woke in a haze. He was thirsty.

Perhaps the innkeeper's homemade sake had been stronger than it tasted. Even after sleeping, his head swam. He noticed nothing unusual around him. In the dim light, he climbed out of his warm bedding, found a cup of water on the table, drank, and crawled back.

He changed position to go to sleep again and sensed someone in front of him. Half opening his eyes, he made out a person lying with her back to him. The figure beneath the covers was a woman, with short hair.

Erika? What's she doing here? Am I dreaming?

The room was too dark for him to notice the difference in hair color. Sleep and drink muddled his thoughts, and he did not question why Erika would be beside him.

Missing her, he left his own covers and drew the woman into his arms. He buried his face in her hair and reached for her without thinking.

Then the touch made him pause. He knew Erika intimately. She always smelled faintly of flowers, her body was soft, and her figure was unmistakable.

This woman felt different. He touched her again, unable to believe it. She was smaller. Her scent was soap and shampoo, not flowers. And beneath his hand, he felt firm abdominal muscles. Her whole body was taut, like someone who trained every day.

Trained?

The thought struck him like a bolt of lightning. He snatched his hand away, retreated to his own bedding, and finally saw who was beside him. It was Bea, not Erika.

What had he done? Ethan looked at his hand, then at Bea, cold sweat forming on his forehead. If she noticed, she would think he had touched her deliberately. How could he explain it?

But why was she beside him? She had spread her bedding on the other side of the room. Had he returned to the wrong place after getting water?

He started to rise and find his own bedding, then noticed Misty lying on his other side. He was in the right place. Both girls had moved while he slept.

A soft dripping sound came from elsewhere in the room. He understood. The roof had leaked over their original bedding.

His heart pounded. He waited, watching Bea. She neither woke nor turned on him. He let out a silent breath. She must have slept through it. Thank goodness. He really had touched her; if she knew, he would have no way to defend himself.

He resolved to act as though nothing had happened. Quietly, he turned toward Misty and lay down again.

At least there was no danger of mistaking Misty for Erika. Misty had none of Erika's curves, and Ethan would never pursue her while she was underage. Even if he accidentally touched her, their closeness meant she was unlikely to hold it against him.

Bea still had not stirred. Reassured, he closed his eyes.

What Ethan did not know was that Bea had awakened the moment he buried his face in her hair. She was facing away, so he had not seen her eyes snap open. She had felt his hand slip beneath her covers and into her clothes.

No man had ever touched her that way. Shock left her unable to think or even breathe for a moment. By the time she understood what had happened, Ethan had already let go and pulled away.

That surprised her too. She remained still. He had been close enough for her to smell the sake on his breath. He must have been confused in his sleep.

He probably mistook me for his girlfriend.

Bea had learned at dinner that Ethan had a girlfriend. Misty had made a point of mentioning it. Her reason, to an outsider, was obvious: she wanted Bea to know Ethan was already involved with someone, and to prevent anything from developing between them.

For all Misty's calculations, she had not imagined Ethan would skip straight past that warning in his half-asleep state and reach for Bea.

Chapter 745: Partings, an Investigation, and Expectations

The next morning, Misty pestered Ethan awake. When he opened his bleary eyes, she was already washed and dressed, kneeling beside him and tickling his cheek with a strand of her hair. It itched, though pleasantly.

Ethan, you really can't hold your liquor, she said, covering a laugh. You only had a few cups last night, and you slept this late!

You have no idea, Misty.

It was seven twenty. He had slept a little later than usual, but sake was hardly the reason. He had spent half the night turning over what had happened with Bea and had barely slept until dawn. He could not tell Misty that.

Bea's and Misty's bedding had already been folded and put away. Misty was here, but Bea was not. The rain had stopped sometime in the night. A faint smell of food drifted in from outside; breakfast must be ready.

Ethan washed and dressed, then followed Misty into the courtyard. A middle-aged man in work clothes was on the roof, repairing something under the elderly innkeeper's direction.

Bea was practicing martial arts in the courtyard. Each punch and kick seemed to cut audibly through the air. A sheen of sweat covered her skin. She must have been training for some time.

Such dedication. Ethan wished he had her persistence, but he was at least half lazy. Given the chance, he would rather spend a little longer in bed.

Misty was still looking up at the repairman. You don't know this yet, but it rained hard last night. The roof leaked over our room. Bea and I nearly got soaked!

Really? Ethan did his best to look unaware. I slept so deeply I didn't even hear the rain.

Hearing his voice, Bea glanced toward him. Her punch stopped. After two or three seconds, she resumed training as though nothing had happened.

The greeting Ethan had been about to give caught in his throat. Guilty as he felt, he noticed that pause at once. Had she realized what happened? Of course it was possible. Bea had not been drinking. How could she fail to notice him touching her in the night? But if she had noticed, why had she not stopped or scolded him? Perhaps he was imagining things. Then again, why had she paused just now?

Misty's gaze moved suspiciously between them. Something about the atmosphere felt wrong. Had anything happened while she slept? Surely not. She had been beside them and heard nothing, and she herself had woken Ethan that morning.

They were probably embarrassed, she decided. It was one thing to sleep near each other in the dark and another to open their eyes and see each other's faces.

...

After a cold shower, Bea came into the sitting room. Ethan and Misty were already waiting at the table. They began breakfast once she sat down.

As on the previous night, the food was delicious. The dishes looked simple, but simple ingredients tested a cook's skill all the more.

Neither Ethan nor Bea spoke. Misty finally broke the silence. Bea, where will you go next?

After a night's rest, it was time to travel again. Trainers rarely stayed in one place for long; another unknown adventure always waited. Ethan and Misty had one last Gym to challenge. Bea, now that she knew this island's exercises offered her little, would look elsewhere for training.

I think I'll leave Hoenn, Bea said without looking up. I've challenged all the well-known Fighting-type Trainers here. It's time to visit another region.

Ethan felt relief. He could no longer face her with the ease he had before. Some time apart might let the embarrassment fade. By their next meeting, perhaps they could both forget it.

So soon? Misty sounded disappointed. After the evening together, she felt closer to Bea. I thought you'd at least stay for the Ever Grande Conference. Now you won't get to watch Ethan win another title!

Hey, Ethan cut in. Don't talk as though I've already been named Champion. Hoenn isn't like Kanto or Johto. There are plenty of strong Trainers here. I can promise I'll do my best not to lose through carelessness, but winning won't be easy.

After breakfast, they packed and left the inn for the harbor. The evacuated residents had begun returning overnight. The town looked far livelier than it had when Ethan and Misty arrived; its streets were no longer empty.

They watched Bea board a ferry heading in another direction. Ethan and Misty then boarded their own ship. As the horn sounded and the ferry eased away from the pier, they stood by the rail, each lost in thought.

At that same moment, uninvited visitors reached the sea southeast of Mossdeep Island.

A helicopter bearing the TV Mauville logo flew toward the place where Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre had fought. In the back sat the reporting duo Ethan had met at the park in Mauville City. They craned their necks to see the water below.

Ty, the cameraman, searched for a while before turning to Gabby. Are you sure this is the place? Weren't there several islands? I can only see a few shoals.

You idiot. Those shoals were the islands, Gabby said. Something flattened them.

The helicopter landed on a relatively even stretch of exposed ground, and they climbed out. Ty checked a satellite map but could not match the place around him to the islands marked there.

Remind me why we came all this way? he asked.

Were you listening at all? Gabby sighed. If we want to get back into the studio and move up at the station, we need a big story and the truth behind it. Come on, investigate. It took me a lot of work to get someone to fly us here. I don't intend to leave empty-handed.

As reporters, they had heard more than most people. The extreme weather that had affected much of Hoenn had spread from this area. They were certain the official explanationunusual air pressure and tectonic movementwas not the truth. Someone or some Pokemon had fought here and affected the entire region.

What Pokemon could wield enough power to do that? The obvious answers were Groudon and Kyogre.

Short on time, they began searching for evidence. They found fragments of a ship, uniforms lost by Team Aqua and Team Magma members, marks left by the battle, and even an International Police armband.

The clues pointed to a hidden fight involving both criminal organizations, with the International Police involved as well. Gabby grew excited. Publishing the truth would cause a sensation. If the police had concealed it, there must be an extraordinary story to uncover. The reporter who broke it would surely gain recognition at the station, a promotion, and better pay.

They photographed the scene, collected and secured the evidence, and searched on for something more decisive. What they had found showed that a battle had occurred and that Team Aqua and Team Magma were connected to it. It did not prove Groudon and Kyogre had been present or caused the weather.

They worked slowly through the site, overlooking no corner. For a long time they found nothing else. At the place where Ethan had stood, however, they noticed footprints and a patch of ground that remained unusually intact, as though some power had protected it.

After studying the traces, Gabby's eyes brightened. Someone was directing Pokemon against Team Aqua and Team Magma. Maybeand this is a guessthis person even fought Groudon and Kyogre!

That's hard to believe, Ty said. Who could possibly be strong enough to battle two Legendary Pokemon? One of the Elite Four?

The Elite Four... Gabby considered it. She knew little about battles, but she knew they were among Hoenn's strongest Trainers. Perhaps. Based on the route and what we've heard, Drake seems the likeliest to have come here.

Ty thought she might be right, yet something troubled him. He looked toward the remains of the island erased by Precipice Blades and Origin Pulse. Comparing them with the earlier satellite map, he could picture the large island that had stood there. Now it had vanished entirely.

What kind of power could wipe an island away? Could even one of the Elite Four stop a battle on that scale?

He said nothing. They bent to their search again, hoping for conclusive evidence, but found none. They had come too late. After more than a day of wind and rain, seawater had washed away most of the traces.

They had arrived full of expectation. Hours later, they left without the proof they needed.

...

After nearly a full day at sea, Ethan and Misty's ferry from Muscle Island docked at Lilycove City. It was much slower than flying, but comfortable and leisurely. They were in no hurry and had enjoyed the journey.

Ethan had barely disembarked when Kennedy called. The Meteorite Key Stone Ethan had found at Sky Pillar was ready.

Devon Corporation had worked quickly. Kennedy had gathered the necessary specialists before the stone even reached the company's headquarters. As soon as it arrived, they took it to the workshop and worked through the night. The job was finished in little more than a day.

Ethan looked forward to seeing it. If the stories were true and the Meteorite Key Stone held energy from space, might his Pokemon grow stronger through Mega Evolution than other Trainers' Pokemon did?

That was only a guess. He did not yet know whether the stone was truly special, whether it differed at all from an ordinary Key Stone, or whether it would even affect ordinary Pokemon. He would find out when he had it in his hands.

Chapter 746: The Final Gym

Ethan asked Kennedy to mail the Meteorite Key Stone directly to Ever Grande City. He and Misty rested another night in Lilycove City before setting out for Fortree City.

At the Pokemon Center, Ethan took the chance to change his lineup. He transferred Articuno, Zapdos, Moltres, Raikou, and Suicune to Sabrina. Deoxys and the black Rayquaza were now the only Legendary Pokemon he kept with him. He sent his red Gyarados and Crystal Steelix to Cerise Park and brought back the team he had been training.

With Scizor, Eevee, Milotic, and Metang in hand again, Ethan finally felt like an ordinary Trainer. No sudden criminal organization to confront, no Hoenn legends to worry about. He could challenge a Gym at his own pace and focus on training his Pokemon. Wasn't that what a Trainer's life was supposed to be?

Before leaving Lilycove, he called Phoebe and arranged to meet her in Fortree. He still had the Blue Orb and Red Orb. It was time to return them.

Why not take them to Mt. Pyre himself? It was out of his way. Besides, after all the help he had given Phoebe, asking her to come to him was hardly unreasonable.

Ethan and Misty headed west from Lilycove. The day was mild, with a light breeze. They had no need to hurry. Relaxed for the first time in a while, they could enjoy the scenery and notice things they had passed over before. It was a rare pleasure after weeks of tense travel.

After more than half a day, they passed a Safari Zone, a protected habitat where wild Pokemon lived and bred. The law and the Pokemon League protected it, but visitors who paid the fee could use the provided Safari Balls to catch Pokemon without battling.

For anyone who disliked fighting, it could be an ideal place to catch a partnerif luck was on their side. Safari Balls did not have a high success rate, and a bad day could make it dismal. That was why the supposedly easier chance did not draw every Trainer.

Ethan had no Pokemon he wanted to catch there. He and Misty went straight past its entrance.

As they left the reserve behind, Misty could not resist teasing Ash. You'd pass it by because you know there's nothing there you want. If Ash came this way, he'd definitely go in for a look!

After traveling with Ash through two regions, she knew him well. He could never pass up a place like this.

You're right, Ethan said with a smile. He loves finding something to get excited about. Besides, this is on the way from Verdanturf Town to Lilycove City. He must have passed it after challenging the Verdanturf Gym. I'd bet he already went inside.

They followed the road north. After walking another few hours and stopping for lunch, they came past a high mountain range. Ethan glanced across the nearly empty road and spotted someone he had met before.

Is that...?

Misty followed his surprised gaze. A man of about twenty-four or twenty-five, with light blue hair and a well-cut black suit, walked ahead of them. He looked every inch a refined young gentleman.

Do you know him? she asked.

You don't recognize him? Oh, you haven't met. Ethan explained, That's Steven, Mr. Stone's son. His father runs Devon Corporation.

So that's Steven. Misty had heard the name from Ethan and Mr. Stone, even if she had never seen the man. What's he doing here?

Ethan wondered too, until he looked at the surrounding mountains. What did Steven enjoy most? Searching for rare stones. It was a running joke about him, but also true. Something unusual in this area must have attracted him.

Steven was about to enter a cave when he turned, as though he had sensed their gaze. He spotted Ethan and Misty, paused in surprise, then changed direction and walked over. His eyes briefly rested on Misty before he greeted Ethan with a smile.

I didn't expect to run into you here.

A coincidence, Ethan said. If you're here, does that mean there's a special stone nearby?

Steven shared his father's well-known interest in stones, so the guess did not trouble him. That's right. He moved aside to show the cave entrance. I heard a Trainer exploring there discovered a hidden passage into its deeper levels. I thought there might be rarer stones inside.

That sounded like Steven. A wealthy young man could afford to travel wherever his hobby led him.

A secret cave in these mountains, though... Ethan touched his chin. Do you mean the Scorched Slab?

Steven looked at him in surprise. You know about it? You're not even from Hoenn, yet you know a place that obscure.

Ethan had not foreseen anything. He remembered the cave from a game he had played. The details were hazy, but he recalled a rare Heatran somewhere in its depths.

Heatran was a Legendary Pokemon, and some considered it powerful. Ethan found it ugly. It held no appeal for him, even if one truly lived there.

I heard the name by chance, he said, waving the subject away. I travel a lot and hear things. Something reminds me of one of them now and then. I don't actually know more than the name.

Steven accepted that. Then he seemed to remember something else. Kennedy told me you helped my father again recently.

It took Ethan a moment to realize he meant the meteorite. I wouldn't call it a favor. We helped each other. Without Mr. Stone's information, I couldn't have caught a powerful Pokemon I wanted.

Deoxys? Steven smiled. A pity I wasn't there. If I'd known, perhaps I'd have caught it myself.

Ethan had doubts. Steven specialized in Steel-type Pokemon; would he even have tried to catch Deoxys? And if he had gone, he would also have faced Courtney's Team Magma members, Shelly's Team Aqua members, and Rayquaza's arrival. Could he have overcome all of them and caught Deoxys, as Ethan had? Even a former Champion might not have managed it so easily.

They had met by chance and both had places to go. After a short conversation, they said goodbye. Misty watched Steven disappear into the cave and offered her impression.

He seems genuinely pleasant, she said after a moment. Polite, easy to talk to, without any of the arrogance you might expect from a wealthy heir. He's confident in his strength too, and I get the feeling he hates losing.

That's a good reading of him, Ethan said. Steven really is impressive. There's a reason he's so popular in Hoenn.

The encounter soon slipped from their minds. They left the mountains and traveled for another day. By the following evening, they could just make out the lights of Fortree City ahead, though they still had some distance to go.

Fortree was known as a city in the trees, at play with nature. It lay in northern Hoenn at the foot of a long mountain range. The city was not large, but dense forest wrapped around it. Trees hid even its taller buildings. From a distance, it was hard to tell where the forest ended and the city began.

Tree houses stood throughout Fortree, built among tall, straight trunks and linked by hanging bridges. It lacked the bustle of a metropolis, but the green canopy and birdsong gave it a charm of its own. Most residents walked. Cars were rare, and roads rarer still.

Frequent heavy rain made the trees grow taller here than elsewhere. People said the residents were unusually healthy and long-lived. Wild Bug-type Pokemon often flew past the tree houses.

It was late when Ethan and Misty arrived, so they went straight to the Pokemon Center. At dinner, Misty heard that Fortree's annual Feather Carnival had taken place only a few days earlier. The sky-themed celebration drew the whole city together. She sighed at what they had missed.

I wish we could have gone.

She was a lively ten-year-old girl. Of course a festival would appeal to her.

We couldn't help being delayed, Ethan said. You'll have time to enjoy yourself at the Ever Grande Conference. That will be more exciting than any carnival.

...

The Fortree Gym stood on the outskirts and was the only building in the city that was not built in the trees. It resembled a four-sided step pyramid, like those of the Maya, rising hundreds of meters. Without a Flying-type Pokemon to carry a challenger, reaching the battlefield at the top meant climbing a long, exhausting staircase.

Two stone Pokemon statues flanked its entrance. Each stood more than ten meters tall, wings spread and head raised as if calling to the sky. Looking up at them from below was imposing.

After a night's rest, Ethan felt full of energy. The next morning, he officially came to challenge the Fortree Gym.

He and Misty walked down a long passage toward the entrance. A man who was clearly a staff member came out to meet them, smiling.

Here to challenge the Gym?

We are, Misty said before Ethan could answer. But you came out as if you were expecting us. How did you know we were here?

He gestured proudly at the building behind him. This is the tallest structure in Fortree. From inside, we've got eyes as sharp as a hawk's. We notice anyone who walks up this passage. Come inWinona, our Gym Leader, has been waiting for you!

Chapter 747: Battling Winona

The three of them did not enter the Gym itself. They followed the long staircase up the outside of the pyramid toward its summit.

It had looked high from the ground. Climbing it revealed just how high: the equivalent of at least twenty-six or twenty-seven ordinary floors. After the long passage they had already walked, the ascent was exhausting. Misty was panting before they were halfway up.

It's so tall... She wiped her forehead. Why didn't they put in an elevator? I can understand wanting to test challengers, but they could think about those of us who just came along to watch.

The staff member seemed accustomed to the climb. He was not even breathing hard. We're a Flying-type Gym, he said with a smile. You can ride a Flying-type Pokemon straight to the top. Still, I think taking the stairs occasionally is good for you.

Steep and long as they were, the stairs finally ended. At the top, Ethan and Misty stopped at the sight before them.

From the tallest building in Fortree, they could see the entire city. Below lay a sea of green. Trees hid almost everything except the tallest structures, which rose above the canopy. Having climbed so far, they felt a curious satisfaction in looking out over it.

It is beautiful, Ethan said. Worth the climb.

He turned toward the rest of the summit. A standard battlefield occupied the top of the Gym. Its floor was covered with a thick layer of earth, deep enough for a Ground-type Pokemon to use Dig. On either side stood a lift that could raise a Trainer into the air to direct a battle.

At the far end, a woman in her twenties watched him. She wore a flight suit and a helmet with goggles. Her long hair was grayish purple, and years of flying had given her a fit, shapely figure. She was attractive in a quiet way.

This must be Winona.

Welcome to the Fortree Gym, she said when their eyes met. I'm Winona, its Gym Leader.

Known as a bird Pokemon Trainer who soared around the world, Winona specialized in avian Pokemon and could read the wind. She believed living in harmony with nature was the best way to live, which was why she had chosen Fortree for her Gym. Like Wallace, she valued elegance and spectacle in battle. People respected both her grace and her strength.

I'm Ethan.

And I'm Misty.

They kept the introductions brief. Winona knew why they had come. Misty went to the spectator area, while the staff member guided Ethan to a Trainer's platform. Winona took the opposite side. Both lifts rose, carrying them more than ten meters above the battlefield.

So that was this Gym's specialty. Directing a battle from the air suited a Flying-type Leader. Anyone afraid of heights might have trouble, especially with the whole arena already atop a tower. Ethan often flew above the clouds on his Pokemon. This platform was low by comparison.

The staff member moved to a raised place near the center of the field to referee. The Fortree Gym battle between Leader Winona and challenger Ethan will now begin. Each side may use three Pokemon. The battle ends when all Pokemon on one side are unable to battle. Only the challenger may switch Pokemon freely.

The rules were ordinary enough. Despite the aerial arena, there were no unusual battle requirements.

Once Ethan was ready, Winona threw a Poke Ball. An Altaria appeared before him.

He was not surprised. Altaria was her signature Pokemon and one of her strongest. It was the first Pokemon many people associated with Winona.

Sending it out before she knew her challenger's strength told Ethan she did not hold back. She took every Gym match seriously. He welcomed that, but a novice Trainer might face a long struggle here, perhaps failing repeatedly. Some Gym Leaders preferred to guide beginners with a gentler team. Others fought in earnest from the start. Each approach had its advantages; overcoming a hard Gym could bring tremendous growth.

As for his answer to Altaria, Ethan did not deliberate. He took a Poke Ball from his belt and threw it onto the field. Blue light flashed, and Winona saw his choice.

Metang? She nodded appreciatively. Steel-type attacks won't be especially effective against Altaria, but its Flying- and Dragon-type moves won't do much to Metang either. A sound choice.

She was confident enough to assess his Pokemon aloud.

Altaria circled high above the field. Metang floated about a meter from the ground. Despite the distance between them, both fixed on each other, ready to fight. Pokemon could sense an opponent's presence and gauge its strength more directly than their Trainers could. Altaria's eyes were alert and expressive. Metang, with its cold, stony heart, showed little emotion.

The referee signaled the start.

Winona opened aggressively. Altaria dove straight toward Metang. It was the quickest way to close the distance, but a direct approach made it easier to hit. She must trust Altaria's speed.

Ethan wanted to test that speed. He ordered Metang to attack. An invisible wave of Confusion shot toward Altaria. With a slight shift of its wings, Altaria changed course, arced around the attack, and swept toward Metang from the side.

It was fast. No wonder Winona had chosen that approach.

Ethan had suspected as much. Still, Altaria had reached Metang before it could attack again. With the bird moving so quickly, Metang could not dodge either.

Now! Peck! Winona called.

Peck? Ethan was taken aback. With such an opening, why use a basic move?

Then he saw what made Winona's Peck different. Altaria's short beak flashed. In a few seconds, it struck Metang dozens of times, as quickly as a bird pecking at scattered grain. The beak blurred, and the repeated ringing of metal filled the arena.

Each Peck was weak, but so many blows together could do real damage. Ethan had to admire the training behind it. Altaria had earned its place as Winona's signature Pokemon.

Even so, as Winona had said, Altaria's attacks did only half their usual damage against Metang. Metang's sturdy defenses reduced their effect further. The assault looked alarming but achieved little.

As I thought, Winona said, shaking her head. That move has surprised and beaten many challengers. I expected this result against a Pokemon that resists it, though.

Ethan heard the disappointment in her voice. He had not chosen Metang simply to exploit her typing. Only a few Pokemon on his current team needed training, and he had to send them out in some order.

The instant Altaria finished, Metang countered. It swung its two heavy claws with Metal Claw. Altaria had committed to close combat knowing the risks; it spread its wings and slipped away as the claws rose. A Flying-type Pokemon's agility served it well.

Ethan had not counted on Metal Claw connecting. As soon as Altaria climbed, he had Metang attack from range with Confusion.

Altaria kept its distance now. It dodged the psychic attacks and answered with Dragon Breath and Dragon Pulse. Firing while moving brought mistakes, though. It landed one Dragon Breath, but Metang found an opening of its own.

One lapse was enough. Confusion struck Altaria and held it, drawing it lower toward Metang while dealing damage.

Altaria, break free! Winona ordered.

It could not muscle its way out. Winona quickly found another approach. Though Altaria could not move, it could open its beak. At her command, it fired Dragon Pulse into the ground below. The impact pushed it upward, and the blast threw up a cloud of smoke and a wave of air. The disruption broke Metang's hold.

Altaria had no time to relax. Above you! Winona shouted.

Altaria looked up. Metang had already rushed toward it, both claws gleaming as they swung. With no time to dodge, Altaria wrapped itself in its fluffy plumage and braced for the hit.

Ethan had recognized Winona's plan as soon as she called for Dragon Pulse. He had anticipated the escape and ordered Metang to use Agility, closing the distance before striking with Metal Claw again.

He had not expected Altaria's instant response: Cotton Guard. Only a few Pokemon with thick plumage could use the move. It sharply raised Altaria's defenses, an effective answer to a close-range strike.

Impressive. Winona had not even called for Cotton Guard. Altaria had reacted on its own instinct. Ethan had admired its training once already; now it had earned that admiration again.

Chapter 748: Making the Battlefield Favorable

Cotton Guard stopped Metang's Metal Claw. It also left Altaria tucked into its plumage, unable to move or counterattack.

Ethan took the opening. Metang used Psychic, dealing damage while an invisible force lifted Altaria high into the air.

Winona hesitated, then ordered Altaria to remain in its defensive posture. Most Trainers who lifted an opponent that high would slam it to the ground for a second hit. Cotton Guard could not protect Altaria from Psychic, but its cushioning would lessen the impact when it fell. Better to prepare now than react too late.

Her sensible prediction worked against her. Altaria hung in the air like a large, fluffy ball. Metang made no move to throw it down. Instead, it kept applying Psychic. After several seconds, Winona realized Ethan might never have intended to drop it at all.

Another seven or eight seconds passed with Altaria suspended in pain. She could not let it continue. Winona abandoned her plan and ordered Altaria to escape as it had before.

Ethan noticed the first movement. It was too late to start struggling now.

At the instant Altaria released Cotton Guard, he gave the command. Metang finally sent it plummeting toward the ground.

Winona could only watch. Altaria could not raise Cotton Guard again quickly enough, nor could it fire Dragon Pulse at the ground to push itself free as it had earlier. Ethan had waited for precisely this moment. She had to admit that his patience and timing were excellent. His perception alone set him apart from an ordinary Trainer.

Altaria struck the earth with a crash. Its plumage offered some protection, but the fall from that height, added to the damage it had already taken, knocked it unconscious.

The referee raised his flag. Altaria is unable to battle! Metang wins the first round!

As he spoke, white light enveloped Metang. Everyone at the arena recognized an evolution.

For Ethan, it was welcome news. Metang had traveled with him for some time and fought in many individual and group battles. Today, it finally evolved. Aside from Eevee, every Pokemon he currently owned had now reached its final form. His team had grown stronger again.

The glow faded, revealing a more imposing Pokemon: Metagross.

It looked almost as though two Metang had been joined. Its blue-green body resembled a spacecraft or lander, with four thick legs extending from its sides. It had red eyes and a striking silver X across its face.

Misty was delighted for Ethan, but she did not know much about Metagross. She pointed her Pokedex at it.

Beep. Metagross, the Iron Leg Pokemon. Steel and Psychic type. Research suggests its four brains connect into a complex neural network, making it more intelligent than a supercomputer. By processing information in parallel, the brains can complete calculations almost instantly. It analyzes opponents and defeats them with this computing power. Metagross can fold its four legs and float or fly. In addition to psychic power, it possesses tremendous physical strength. It can seize prey with all four legs and pin it with its claws. At temperatures below freezing, its magnetic force grows stronger, so Metagross living on snowy mountains are especially active.

Across the field, Winona could not share Ethan's pleasure. His Pokemon had evolved after beating hers. She shook her head, recalled Altaria, and took out her second Poke Ball.

A Pelipper appeared over the field. Ethan noticed it and returned his attention to the match. He kept Metagross out. It had taken little damage and could still fight. More importantly, it had only just evolved. This battle would help it learn the feel of its new body and abilities.

Winona was not surprised. Metagross had been strong even before evolving. It would be troublesome. At least the matchup had shifted in her favor: Pelipper was Water/Flying, so Metagross's Steel-type attacks would do only half their usual damage against it.

Both Pokemon moved into position. At the referee's signal, the second round began.

Pelipper was no weaker than Altaria. With less need to fear Steel-type moves, it concentrated on avoiding Metagross's psychic attacks. It flew in unpredictable directions, used Water Gun to keep its distance, and struck whenever Metagross left an opening.

Ethan offered almost no instructions. Having won the first round, he did not consider this one's outcome crucial. He wanted to see what Metagross could do without his direction and get a measure of its new strength.

The two Pokemon traded attacks for a while. Pelipper's best tactic seemed to be alternating long-range Hydro Pump with close-range Steel Wing. Moving between near and far attacks gave Metagross trouble.

But the Pokedex had been right about its intelligence. After taking only two hits, Metagross appeared to recognize the pattern. When Pelipper tried it again, Metagross seized the bird with several of its powerful claws.

Winona startled. Was she about to watch the previous round repeat itself? Pelipper, get free!

Pelipper could not break Metagross's grip. At first it could beat its wings and struggle. Metagross's claws did not budge. It even tried to catch Metagross in its huge beak, but Metagross was far too large to fit.

As Pelipper tired, the claws tightened. After a long struggle, its eyes rolled back and it fainted in Metagross's hold. Metagross's red eyes still gleamed. It did not let go until its opponent was completely unconscious.

The referee inspected Pelipper and raised his flag with a faint shake of his head. Pelipper is unable to battle! Metagross wins!

Metagross had won again without much difficulty, though it had taken some damage across the two rounds. It could probably fight once more, but a third round might leave it and its opponent both badly hurt. Ethan had seen what he wanted to see, so he recalled it.

Impressive, Winona said. Two losses in a row, both decisive, left her no choice but to acknowledge it. You've raised MetangMetagross, I should sayexceptionally well. My Pokemon barely had a chance to fight back.

Even an inexperienced spectator could have seen it. Winona knew Ethan was no ordinary challenger.

Your Altaria and Pelipper are strong too, Ethan replied. Against most challengers, they'd be difficult opponents.

Winona's expression eased. Then this is the last round. Let's see if I can win one back.

Her attitude had changed over the two battles. She now regarded Ethan with the respect due a strong opponent.

She threw her third Poke Ball. A Shiny Swellow appeared high in the air.

Wow! Misty cried from the stands. It's turquoise! I've never seen a Swellow that color. It's beautiful!

Compared with an ordinary dark-blue Swellow, its fresh coloring was certainly unusual. Whether it was prettier was a matter of taste. Its fierce gaze and sharp talons, however, were unmistakable.

After a moment's thought, Ethan chose Milotic.

He would have enjoyed meeting Winona in an aerial battle with Flying-type Pokemon, if he had another partner that needed training. Dragonite was the only Flying-type he carried, and it was too strong for this match to help it improve.

His regular team was still small. They had all grown into powerful partners, but gaps in type coverage sometimes limited his choices. His journey was not even halfway over, though. He would have more chances to expand it.

Milotic emerged onto the field. Pelipper's Water Guns and Hydro Pumps had already turned the earth muddy. That suited Milotic's scaled body, making it easier for the Pokemon to move. Neither Milotic nor Swellow had a clear type advantage, which made this round seem fairer than the last two.

Nature was another matter. A bird might seem to have an advantage over a snakelike creature in the food chain, but strength could overturn the roles of predator and prey. There was no simple rule for this match.

Swellow circled above while Milotic coiled on the ground. Both watched the other eagerly. The arrangement resembled the previous rounds, but these Pokemon would fight in their own ways.

The referee signaled the third round. At Ethan's order, Milotic attacked first. It sent a stream of water sweeping across the sky.

The blue arc traced a long line, but Swellow was too fast to hit so easily. It made a few circuits overhead, staying ahead of the water with room to spare.

Ethan had not expected a hit. The water fell across the arena, soaking the earth. Puddles began to form. Winona saw his intention at once and frowned.

He was reshaping the battlefield to favor Milotic.

Chapter 749: All Eight Badges

As the earth grew muddier, Milotic moved across it more easily. Its smooth scales helped it slide through the wet ground and pick up speed. It twisted away from each of Swellow's dives with increasing ease.

Swellow, meanwhile, dared not fly too close to the mud or attempt another close-range strike. It might coat its feathers and slow it down. The bird had strength to spare, but fewer ways to use it.

Winona's opinion of Ethan rose another step. His willingness to change the battlefield showed rare creativity. It reminded her of Ash, the challenger who had visited some time ago. Were the two alike?

Swellow could still attack from a distance. It sent an Air Slash toward Milotic. Milotic answered with Water Gun, but the cutting air broke through the stream and continued toward it. Milotic slid aside across the wet ground without panic.

They traded attacks, neither finding a reliable way to defeat the other. For a time, the battle stalled.

Swellow, Aerial Ace! Winona called, changing tactics first.

Swellow wheeled through the sky, gathering speed. Ethan watched closely. Aerial Ace used swift movement to throw an opponent off before the decisive slash. Ordinarily, it was an attack that would land. He needed to make the situation anything but ordinary.

Milotic, Twister!

A spiraling wind rose from the field, lifting muddy water into the air and flinging it in every direction. The battlefield became harder to read. Swellow lost sight of Milotic behind the twisting column, while the turbulent air and flying mud disrupted its path.

Winona had chosen Swellow for her final round because it was skilled and experienced. It had the patience of an aerial hunter. If the Twister blocked its attack, it could wait for the wind to fade.

That was the right choice. After only a dozen seconds, the Twister weakened. Before it had fully vanished, Swellow seized its chance. It dove at great speed, made a sharp right-angle turn, and struck Milotic with Aerial Ace.

Milotic stumbled and fell backward. By the time it rose to retaliate, Swellow was high above it again.

Ethan saw the wound, but remained calm. Milotic, Recover.
