Milotic gave a soft cry. Pale light surrounded it, and most of the injury healed. The battle seemed to have returned to where it began.

Still, Milotic had spent more energy on Twister and Recover than Swellow had used for its attack. Winona saw a possible path to victory.

Good! Swellow, let's do that again!

The first Twister had failed to stop Swellow. Ethan knew it would be difficult to fight this bird by the same means. Yet when Winona prepared to repeat her tactic, another idea came to him. He ordered Milotic to use Twister again.

The same spiraling wind rose from the field. Misty frowned from the stands, and Winona did too. Why repeat something that had not worked? Was Ethan out of ideas, or hoping a second attempt would succeed?

He gave them their answer. As soon as the Twister formed, Milotic plunged into it. The wind swept it upward within seconds. As it began to fall, it twisted its body, changed direction in midair, and dropped toward Swellow.

Winona understood. Swellow had avoided close combat, so Ethan was carrying Milotic to it. But she thought the plan too simple. The air was a Flying-type Pokemon's domain. Without the wet earth beneath it, Milotic could not maneuver. It would be an easy target.

Swellow, show it what you can do!

Swellow spread its wings and charged. Ethan smiled. Winona had taken the bait.

Now, MiloticSurf!

Winona, Misty, the referee, and even Swellow froze in surprise. Milotic alone obeyed without hesitation. A great wave formed beneath it in midair and crashed down with Milotic toward Swellow.

The wave spread like an enormous net. Swellow was too close. It had time only to look up before the water struck, knocked it out of the sky, and drove it to the ground.

Milotic, Swellow, and the wave landed together. Swellow, once so proud in flight, looked like a drenched bird now. Its soaked feathers clung to its body.

What? Winona's expression changed.

Milotic was already slithering toward Swellow. Swellow, get away! she called.

Swellow beat its wings desperately. Water flew from them, but after a dozen strokes it could not rise even a meter. Milotic reached it.

Aqua Tail!

Water wrapped around Milotic's tail. It lashed Swellow with a sharp smack, knocking it off balance. Milotic gave it no chance to recover. It closed in, coiled its tail tightly around the bird, and squeezed until Swellow fainted.

Swellow is unable to battle! The winner of this Gym battle is the challenger, Ethan!

The referee's raised flag ended the match. Winona had been defeated by a constricting hold more than once today.

You win, she said. That was excellent strategy. I had a chance in the last round, but you outplayed me.

You were strong too. Without that last idea, I might not have beaten you.

They had made a good impression on each other, and exchanged a few more compliments after the match. Misty came down from the stands and sighed at the display. Adults could make even a finished battle complicated.

Winona took a shining Badge from her clothes and placed it in Ethan's hand. Here. The Feather Badge, proof that you've defeated me.

Ethan thanked her and examined it. Misty leaned in beside him. The Badge resembled a silver-white wing, simple and clean in its design. Ethan liked it.

As he placed it in his Badge case, Winona spotted the seven others inside. You've collected all eight? I'm honored that mine was the last.

Trainers usually chose a Gym route by distance, but many still tried easier Gyms first and saved harder ones for later. Leaders knew that, and few liked being considered the weakest, first stop. Winona was pleased to be Ethan's final challenge.

Erika had told Ethan something about Gym Leaders' feelings on the subject. He could guess why Winona was smiling.

They said goodbye and left the Fortree Gym. With all eight Badges collected, Ethan's journey through Hoenn was nearing its endbut the Ever Grande Conference still awaited him. Afterward, he might visit the Battle Frontier. He had plenty left to do.

Once they were clear of the Gym, Misty asked eagerly, Where next? Straight to Ever Grande City?

It's too early. There's at least another half month. Ethan shook his head. But you've reminded me: we can verify my eligibility at the Pokemon Center now.

They followed a leafy path back into Fortree and went to the Pokemon Center. Nurse Joy was at the counter. Ethan explained what he needed.

Of course. Let me check your Badges.

He handed over the case. Nurse Joy confirmed all eight, entered something into the computer, and returned it.

You're registered in advance. When the Conference begins, you'll still need to confirm your participation in person at the venue.

Ethan had followed the same process at the Silver Conference and had no objection. Thank you.

They left the Center without stopping to rest. Ethan had planned to find a lively city where he and Misty could relax while he finished training for the Conference. They had barely stepped outside when a call from May disrupted that plan.

What? It's starting already? Misty exclaimed.

Ethan stood about a meter away, yet he could hear her clearly over the phone. The Hoenn Grand Festival was about to begin. May had earned her five Ribbons and was on her way to the host city. She had called to invite Misty to join her there.

Misty hesitated and looked back at Ethan. He nodded.

Absolutely! she told May, laughing. Ethan just got his eighth Badge, so we've got time. Let's meet there!

She ended the call and started off at once. Ethan raised a hand to stop her.

Why are you so excited? You're not competing. And haven't you forgotten something?

Forgotten what? Misty looked confused. We've got our bags. Nurse Joy returned your Badge case. What else is there?

Ethan shook the two pouches hanging behind him. Misty saw them move and stuck out her tongue.

Oh! The orbs. We still have to give them back to Phoebe.

As she said Phoebe's name, someone dropped from the tree canopy above and landed in front of her.

Ah! Misty jumped. Then she recognized Phoebe. What timing.

If this world had the saying about Cao Cao arriving the moment his name was spoken, Misty would certainly have used it.

Chapter 750: Lisia's Lucky Day

Phoebe looked much as she had when Ethan and Misty last saw her. A few days had changed nothing.

Phoebe, you startled me! Misty said, pressing a hand to her chest.

They had been through a great deal together and had traveled side by side for more than a day. The surprise made Misty forget to speak formally to a member of the Elite Four. Phoebe felt more like an ordinary friend now.

Phoebe rubbed her nose and grinned. Like a Ghost-type Pokemon, I come and go without a trace!

Ethan had not expected her to appear just then. He removed the two pouches from behind him and handed them over.

Keep them safe. Don't let anyone take them again.

Phoebe accepted the pouches and bowed deeply. Anabel told me what happened, Ethan. Thank you so much. I'll guard them properly this time, I promise. And without ambitious people like Maxie and Archie around, I don't think anyone will come after them again.

Ethan and Misty exchanged a look. Phoebe clearly did not know that Necrozma had taken Maxie and Archie. Anabel must have kept the news quiet to prevent panic, even withholding it from a member of the Elite Four.

That was understandable, though Ethan saw little reason to fear another immediate attempt on the orbs. The two men might have escaped custody, but they were hardly free to act as they pleased. And if Necrozma chose to help them seize Groudon and Kyogre, no hiding place for the orbs would stop it.

Anabel had not told Phoebe. Ethan and Misty did not tell her either.

How are your grandparents? Ethan asked.

They're settled, Phoebe said with a smile. The League is building a new house for them where the old one stood. It isn't finished yet, but they should soon be able to live quietly again.

Ethan nodded. With that, their business here was done. They could continue their journey without worrying about the orbs.

They talked a little longer, declined Phoebe's invitation to a meal, and waved goodbye. Phoebe watched them leave, gripping the two pouches tightly and holding on to her gratitude.

...

The Hoenn Grand Festival was held in Slateport City. Ethan and Misty knew the city well. On an earlier visit, they had toured the Oceanic Museum, met Drew, and watched May compete in her first Contest. Returning felt like revisiting an old stop on their journey.

After two days of travel, they reached Slateport. Ash and his friends had already been there for some time. Rather than staying in the city, they had moved into the Grand Festival's competitors' village.

The Pokemon League treated Contests almost as seriously as its battling tournaments. It had built a splendid venue, along with a Pokemon Center, dormitories, dining halls, and training facilities. The complex stood beside Slateport's waterfront, divided between a harbor and the competition area. From above, the latter formed a pentagon. Tall buildings and open-air spaces surrounded a grand five-sided arena at its center.

Crowds had filled the grounds already. Contests might not quite rival League tournaments in popularity, but the anticipation here came close.

At the dormitory, Misty and May grabbed each other's hands and talked excitedly.

May! You really did it!

I know. Honestly, I didn't think I'd win five Ribbons and make it to the Grand Festival!

You worked for them!

While the girls celebrated, Ethan looked toward Ash. Ash happened to look back.

You've got all eight Badges too? Ethan asked.

Of course! Ash's eyes shone with the same excitement as May's. I can't wait for the Conference!

Neither can I. The Ever Grande Conference should be something.

A thought seemed to strike Ash. Ethan, now that you've got your Badges, can we all travel together for the next few weeks?

Unless something comes up. Why?

Yes! Ash jumped. That means more big meals!

Ethan stared at him. That was what he had been so eager to ask? Ash really did love food.

Yet the request also showed how close Ash felt to him. He would not speak so freely to just any friend. Ethan had become both a rival Ash wanted to catch up with and someone he could rely on.

Ethan also met May's mother, Caroline. He had expected her to attend such an important event and cheer for her daughter. May was a little disappointed that her father, Norman, could not leave his Gym. He would watch her on television from home.

In May's room at the elaborately decorated dormitory, Ethan learned the Festival's schedule. It had a preliminary round and a main competition. Tomorrow, 247 registered Coordinators would perform on the Appeal Stage. Sixty-four would advance, then compete for the final victory.

It sounded much like a League tournament. With the preliminary round only a day away, May was understandably nervous. After they talked for a while, Misty suggested one last practice session. Everyone except Ethan went to the nearby outdoor training field.

Ethan was only here to watch. He was glad of the free time. As the others hurried away, he headed toward the snack street beside the venue to browse.

When he competed, he had to prepare seriously. It was pleasant to experience a tournament without that pressure.

Snack streets sold much the same foods and trinkets wherever he went. The pleasure lay in the bustle. Ordinary treats and goods became tempting among the crowds and bright stalls.

He let Gardevoir out and bought a few snacks he liked. Together they moved slowly with the flow of people.

It had been a long time since Ethan and Gardevoir had spent time alone. Their telepathic connection meant they needed few words to understand one another, but that did not make these quiet moments any less valuable.

Gardevoir was not unheard of in Hoenn, yet Ethan's stood out in bearing and appearance. Passersby kept turning to admire it. One stranger even approached and asked Ethan to trade Gardevoir away. Ethan had no patience for someone who would make such a presumptuous request. He waved the person off and continued.

A little farther along, he saw three familiar figures. Despite their disguises, he recognized Jessie, James, and Meowth at once. Wherever Ash went, they were rarely far behind. They had drawn a crowd and were calling out around some stall, apparently promoting a new scheme.

Ethan did not care to find out. He was about to pass when all three seemed to sense him and turned at once. Their eyes met his. They shivered and went rigid.

Ethan looked away and walked past with Gardevoir. His pace was unremarkable, but to Team Rocket's trio, every footstep sounded as though it landed on their hearts.

They did not move until he had vanished into the crowd.

Jessie's back was soaked with sweat. Still frozen in place, she whispered, H-he's gone, right?

There was no one in the world they feared more.

I think so. James breathed out, then glanced at Meowth. Hey, did you wet yourself?

That's sweat! Sweat! Meowth wanted to swipe at him, but Ethan might still be close enough to return. That was too close. I never expected to see him here!

I thought he was going to finish us, Jessie said, recovering slowly. Just being near him is terrifying.

James hesitated. Have you noticed? This isn't the first time he's ignored us. He never seems to go out of his way to bother us.

Wouldn't it be more accurate to say he doesn't consider us worth noticing? Meowth ventured.

Because we're no threat to him, Jessie said, showing a rare flash of insight. Then she smiled. Fine by me! As long as we don't start trouble with him, we'll be safe. We can keep our attention on the twerp and Pikachu.

That's true!

They laughed together. Their fear faded as quickly as it had come, and they returned to their work.

Outside the snack street, Ethan found a bench. He laid out the small trinkets he had bought and divided them into groups. His visit had not been aimless. Since he had found gifts here, he wanted to send some home. Sabrina, Erika, and Chloe, who kept helping care for his Pokemon, all deserved thanks.

He was sorting the last of them before finding a delivery service when a petite girl stopped in front of him. She wore a cap, sunglasses, and a face mask.

Hehe. I knew it was you!

The mask muffled her voice, but it sounded familiar. Ethan studied her hair, figure, and rather bold, showy short skirt.

Lisia? What are you doing here?

It was the young Contest idol he had met in Sootopolis. She had wrapped herself up as though desperate not to be recognized, though Ethan had identified her quickly enough.

Lisia took off her mask and gave him a broad smile. They invited me for the Festival. I got bored in my room, so I came out in disguise for a walk. And then I found you! I'm so lucky!

She looked from side to side. Misty was nowhere nearby. Where's the girl who's always with you?

Ethan knew they did not get along particularly well. She's practicing with her friends at the training field.

Lisia's smile grew brighter. She boldly slipped both hands around Ethan's arm and held it close. Wonderful! Then let me keep you company while we look around.

Ethan felt her press against him and tried to free his arm, but she held on too tightly. He let it be, privately glad Misty was elsewhere. If she saw this, she and Lisia might argue for hours.

Sorry. I just finished browsing and was about to go back and rest.

He meant it as a refusal. Lisia turned it into an invitation. That's perfect! I've been out for ages and I'm tired too. Let's go back to the dormitories together!

Chapter 751: Misty: Someone Stole My Man!?

Ethan was certain Lisia had not been out for long.

Yet she had announced that she was tired and wanted to return to the dormitories with him. Her reason was obvious.

But...

He glanced at the hands clasped firmly around his arm. If he went back like this and Misty saw them, the scene would explode.

On the other hand, if he did not go back, was he supposed to keep walking around with her?

In truth, Ethan thought highly of Lisia. She was cheerful, lively, pretty, and an idol. She had a great deal going for her. He was hardly the sort of person who could not appreciate his good fortune.

If he had been alone, he would gladly have let a girl like her accompany him. The trouble was that there was already someone at his side. If the two of them met now, it would be like Mars crashing into Earth.

And he could not bring himself to turn Lisia down.

What a headache...

After turning it over in his mind, he started slowly toward the dormitories with her. He would think of a way out as they walked.

Lisia had no idea Ethan regarded her as a complication. She had slipped out to relax, and unexpectedly running into him had been a wonderful surprise.

He had left a deep impression on her. He was handsome, his Pokemon were powerful, he was famous, and beneath his composure he had a sense of humor. He matched everything she had imagined in an ideal partner.

If only that girl called Misty were not always with him.

Still, Misty was not here now. With no one to get in the way, Lisia could finally spend some proper time with Ethan!

Her good mood made her talkative. Watching the steady stream of visitors, she sighed. That's the inconvenient thing about being an idol. Wherever I go, I cause a commotion. I can't even enjoy a quiet walk. But you haven't disguised yourself at all, Ethan, and nobody recognizes you on the street. I guess people in Hoenn don't know you yet. I'm sure you'll be the most popular person here after the Ever Grande Conference!

She was right that fame made ordinary outings difficult. If Ethan had his way, people would still fail to recognize him after the Conference. That was unlikely, but he would be leaving Hoenn around then anyway, so it would not affect him much.

Something in Lisia's remark gave him an idea.

He glanced at Gardevoir. Understanding immediately, it used telepathy to speak to Gengar in his shadow.

A moment later, Gengar slipped out unseen and rose into the air a short distance away. It puffed out its cheeks and blew. A powerful gust swept over Ethan and Lisia.

The sudden wind snatched the cap from Lisia's head. She had already taken off her sunglasses and mask to talk to Ethan, leaving her unmistakable face in full view.

A chubby little boy happened to pass them. The flying cap caught his eye, and his gaze fell on Lisia's face. After half a second of stunned silence, delight and disbelief lit up his expression. He pointed at her and shouted, Ah! It's Lisia!

His cry set off an uproar. Lisia jumped, and everyone nearby turned to look.

She was one of the most popular Contest idols around. Anyone who followed Pokemon Contests knew her name. At first the passersby seemed doubtful, but once they saw that it really was her, excitement swept through the crowd.

Lisia!

Wow, she's so cute!

My whole family are fans! Could you give me an autograph?

Lisia stood frozen, still wondering where the wind had come from and how it had blown off her cap. Only when people surged toward her did she come to her senses. She released Ethan's arm, put on a stiff smile, and waved.

H-hello, everyone...

Within moments, fans had surrounded her. When she looked for Ethan, he had disappeared into the crowd.

By the time Ethan squeezed free, he was a good distance away. He glanced back. More people were hurrying toward the commotion, many without even knowing what had happened.

Gengar floated beside him, doubled over laughing. You really are wicked! What a rotten idea!

I had to get away somehow. Ethan shot it a look. Enough laughing. Go back and protect Lisia. The staff responsible for keeping order will probably arrive soon, but make absolutely sure she's safe until they do.

Don't worry! Gengar thumped its chest. Leave it to me!

Ethan watched it go. Lisia would not escape the crowd quickly, so he decided to find Misty first. Once Lisia was free, she was bound to come looking for him at the competitors' village. He could warn Misty in advance and perhaps keep her from getting too angry when Lisia appeared.

He left the snack street and followed the direction Misty and the others had taken. After checking two outdoor training fields, he finally found them at the third.

They had company. One of the two newcomers he knew, and the other he did not.

Drew was the first to catch his eye. Hands in his pockets, he stood in front of Misty with a deliberately cool pose. Misty did not so much as glance at him.

On May's other side stood a rather peculiar man with purple hair, a pointed green hat, and green clothes.

Ethan could not tell what they had been discussing. But as he approached, both men looked at him and then left at the same time, heading in different directions. That puzzled him. Drew's departure made sense, but what about the purple-haired man?

Misty waved Ethan over. He joined her and watched the stranger walk away. Who was that?

His name's Harley, Max answered. He's odd. He often refers to himself the way a woman would, and he's always tricking people with underhanded methods!

So that was Harley. Ethan remembered him vaguely from the anime, though he had never paid him much attention. Max's tone made it clear he did not like the man.

What did he and Drew want? Ethan asked.

Max shook his head. Drew came to make his usual big talk. Harley had a disagreement with my sister before, and he came to apologize. But I don't think it's that simple. Who knows what he's up to?

Whatever his plans are, just be careful around him.

Ethan did not dwell on it. He was about to ask May how practice was going when a girl's voice rang out behind him.

Ethan! I knew you'd be here!

His heart sank. He turned, and there was Lisia, hurrying toward him. Gengar followed beside her with a mischievous grin.

Lisia!? Misty's eyes widened at the sight of her. What are you doing here?

Oh? Lisia feigned surprise. You didn't know? Ethan and I were walking around together for quite a while. If we hadn't been interrupted, we'd still be together now!

Misty's anger flared instantly. Lisia rushed up and wrapped herself around Ethan's arm again. Gritting her teeth, Misty seized his other arm and tried to pull him away.

Ash, May, Max, and Brock exchanged bewildered looks. They had never seen Misty so angry.

Who is she? Ash asked. Why is she fighting Misty over Ethan?

I don't know. May shook her head. Misty's never mentioned her to me.

Lisia... Lisia... Brock rubbed his chin. Then recognition dawned. Oh! It's her!

The other three turned to him. You've heard of her?

Brock took the Grand Festival booklet from his pocket, flipped through a dozen or so pages, and read aloud: ...During the Festival, we've also invited Contest idol Lisia to perform...

A Contest idol? The others looked even more surprised.

Brock closed the booklet. I looked her up earlier. She's a Coordinator herself, and I think her fans call her Lissi. She's very popular in Hoenn and other regions too.

Now that you mention it, I think I've heard her name on television, May said. And since becoming a Coordinator, I've learned how hard it is. For her to become a Contest idol at this age, she must be amazing.

Ash frowned. Then how does Misty know her? And why do they seem so...?

He stopped short of saying they seemed to hate each other. Lisia was close enough to hear.

Meanwhile, Ethan was almost dizzy from being shaken back and forth. Where had these two girls found so much strength? It felt as though they might tear him in half. When neither showed any sign of stopping, he pulled them toward each other and wrenched his arms free.

Stop pulling! You're going to tear my arms off. If you've got something to say, settle it with words!

Misty and Lisia let him go and turned to face each other instead. Ethan rubbed his arms, stepped back, and finally breathed out.

Gengar drifted over. Ethan frowned and whispered, How did she find us?

I brought her, of course.

What!?

Gengar grinned. You told me to protect her. You didn't say what to do afterward! Once she realized I was your Pokemon, she kept pestering me to find you. I couldn't get away, so I brought her here. Besides, I wanted to see what would happen when those two girls got together again. It's every bit as good as I hoped!

You...

Ethan shook his head. He had accounted for everything except Gengar's love of a spectacle.

They could not stay at the training field. Misty and Lisia showed no sign of stopping, and Ethan did not want to draw an audience. He took them back toward the dormitories.

May was too worried about Misty to continue practicing. She followed with Ash, Max, and Brock.

They had barely reached the dormitory entrance when Lisia's manager, having discovered her absence, came out looking for her.

Lisia! The manager hurried up, visibly anxious, and held out a phone. Where have you been? Do you know someone photographed you arm in arm with a man? It's already online! People are saying your relationship has been exposed!

Ethan and the others leaned in. The photograph showed him with Lisia on the snack street, at the moment she had been recognized, her hands still around his arm.

Someone had taken the picture and posted it in no time at all. They had been quick to spot what would make news.

Lisia only smiled, apparently unconcerned. Misty, by contrast, swayed and nearly fell. She had left Ethan alone only long enough to help May practice, and all this had happened?

Someone had stolen her man!

Chapter 752: May's Road Through the Grand Festival

Misty was still fuming when she returned to the dorm room she shared with May.

She was not angry with Ethan. She was angry at herself for letting Lisia find an opening while she was away. Misty dropped onto her bed and brooded, leaving May unsure how to comfort her.

Um... May chose her words carefully. Today was an accident. None of us knew Lisia would be here, so you can't blame yourself for letting your guard down. Look on the bright side: she'll leave after the Grand Festival. Then you won't have to see her again.

Misty's feelings for Ethan were no secret. Everyone around them could see it, even bookish Max. But May's words only made her look more dejected.

There are things you don't know, Misty said helplessly. When my journey in Hoenn ends, I have to go back to the Cerulean Gym. Ethan will go on to Sinnoh, and Lisia has performances there too. I'm worried...

She did not finish. May understood: Misty feared Lisia would take Ethan from her. May wanted to reassure her, but what could she say? With Misty far away, neither of them could know what would happen. Comfort offered against the unknown would mean little.

Misty leaned against the wall, looked up at the ceiling, and sighed. If only I could keep traveling with him...

...

Ladies and gentlemen! Here in Slateport City, the event every Coordinator dreams of has finally arrived: the Pokemon Contest Grand Festival!

Vivian stood at the center of the open-air arena, microphone in hand, announcing the start of the annual Festival. She wore a long red gown. Her blond hair, blue eyes, sweet appearance, and stirring voice added their own brightness to the occasion. One of the most popular Contest hosts, she was a familiar presence at ordinary Contests and major celebrations alike.

The arena could hold tens of thousands of spectators. This was the first day of competition. As the booklet had explained, 247 Coordinators would compete in the preliminary round for 64 places in the next stage.

Ethan sat in a front row with Misty, Ash, and the others, holding popcorn and enjoying the show at close range. Because May's turn was later, she sat with them for the moment too.

Watching the entrants gave them a sense of the field's strength. Several faces were familiar. Ethan had seen only one previous Contest and knew few Coordinators, so the first one he recognized was Robert.

Robert had beaten Drew to win the Slateport Contest. He was the second entrant to take the stage today, and he was as elegant as ever. His Milotic gave a splendid appeal and earned 98 points, an exceptionally high score. The audience cheered. May looked uneasy.

He's just as impressive as before, Ethan said. Ninety-eight is almost a perfect score. Unless something unexpected happens, Robert will probably reach the final rounds. He may be your biggest obstacle to winning.

May nodded. Compared with him, she knew she was still inexperienced in every respect. Even so, she believed in herself. She had earned five Ribbons, proof that she could hold her own against anyone here.

Four more Coordinators followed Robert. All performed well. Each had won five Ribbons, after all; none could be dismissed. They might not match Robert, but their appeals were exciting in their own ways.

Then it was Drew's turn. His partner was Roselia again. It showered the stage with petals and shone in the spotlight, winning Drew 95 points. So far, only Robert and Drew had reached scores that high.

May swallowed. The pressure was building.

Don't be nervous, Ethan told her from the next seat. Forget their scores and show everything you can do. If you give it your all, this will help you grow, whatever the final result.

He knew from his prior-life knowledge that May would not win this Grand Festival. He wanted to soften the blow in case her hopes rose too high. His words helped her settle a little.

May looked at the man who had won tournaments in two regions. Were you nervous the first time you entered a Pokemon League tournament?

You've picked the wrong person to compare yourself with, Ash said, laughing before Ethan could answer. I've never seen Ethan look nervous!

Ethan rubbed his nose. Ash was right that May should not use him as her standard. He had felt nervous in tournaments, but never as visibly as she did. It was not the opponents or even reaching the final that unsettled him. It was the prospect of a championship within his graspand the joy of a victory that close.

The others chuckled. May realized she had asked the wrong person, smiled ruefully, and turned back to the stage.

More than a dozen entrants later, the peculiar man Ethan had met yesterday stepped up. Harley's Pokemon was Cacturne, a green, humanoid cactus with dark green protrusions that made it look somewhat like a scarecrow. Harley's own outfit suddenly made sense: he and his Pokemon had dressed to match.

Cacturne performed a swift appeal with Bullet Seed. Harley received 84 points. That fell short of Robert's and Drew's scores, but it was respectable and seemed enough to advance.

At that point the staff called May backstage to prepare. She took a deep breath and stood.

Go, sis! Max called.

Show them your very best, May!

Ethan and the others offered their encouragement. May gave them a small smile and headed down the competitors' passage.

Misty watched her go with a worried frown. Why do her steps look so heavy?

She'll be fine, Ash said. May's really good. Trust her.

Ash and his friends traveled with May and had seen far more of her performances than Ethan or Misty had. If they were confident, the others could afford to be too.

Several more entrants performed before May's turn finally came. She wore her usual outfit, but a faint smile rested on her face as she walked calmly to the center of the stage. She had come a long way since her first Contest.

That was why Ethan believed so strongly in traveling widely. Seeing more of the world and experiencing new things helped a person grow. Keeping someone confined to a comfortable, familiar place when they were old enough to travel would only hold them back.

Next, please enjoy an appeal by Coordinator May! Vivian announced.

May spun gracefully and released Beautifly. The Pokemon beat its wings, scattering powder across the stage. In the sunlight it glittered like golden rain. The entrance alone drew approving applause. It was not the loudest response of the day, but the audience appreciated what it saw.

In a competition this important, every point mattered. Coordinators trusted their strongest partners rather than risk an unfamiliar Pokemon and a mistake that could eliminate them. It was much like a League tournament in that respect: different in nature, but demanding the same care.

May and Beautifly continued. Beautifly danced through the air, casting wave after wave of powder until the stage seemed caught in an endless golden shower. Then it used Silver Wind, bringing the appeal to its peak. At the finish, it landed on May's arm, and the two struck a pose together.

Applause rose again. Ethan and his companions clapped while turning their eyes to the large screen for the score.

The judges at this Grand Festival were different from the usual panel of Nurse Joy, Mr. Sukizo, and Mr. Contesta. Two women and a man with greater expertise in this kind of assessment had taken their places. They held less prominent positions, but had sharper eyes and a more neutral perspective. The audience trusted their scoring.

After conferring, the three awarded May a total of 88 points.

Nearly ninety! The score showed the judges' approval and put May ahead of many competitors, including Harley. Based on the performances so far, a place in the next round seemed secure.

Ethan and the others relaxed. May's mother, Caroline, let out an especially long breath. She had been more nervous than anyone and wanted her daughter to shine on this stage.

As May left the arena, the group rose to meet her backstage. Each entrant had only a minute or two for an appeal, but with entrances and exits, all 247 performances would take close to nine hours. It was a test of endurance for the judges, and spectators came and went throughout the day. Most people chose to watch the entrants who interested them. With May finished, Ethan's group had no reason to stay until the end; they could check the list of qualifiers after the preliminaries concluded.

They met May coming toward them on a path outside the arena. Caroline, Misty, Ash, and the others praised her until she grew embarrassed.

Just then Harley appeared from nowhere and came up behind May, smiling broadly.

That was wonderful! he said with an exaggerated flourish. His tone was flattering, yet there was something hard to place beneath it. It looks like you'll have no trouble reaching the main competition!

May jumped. Since he had come to congratulate her, she answered politely. You did well too, Harley. Your score was high. I'm sure you'll make it through.

Oh, no. He waved both hands, still smiling. Your Silver Wind was the truly impressive part! I hope you'll keep using it in the matches ahead!

At the mention of Silver Wind, May thanked him earnestly. I really do owe you for suggesting it. I'll keep using it!

It's a promise, then. See you!

Harley hurried away again. May and the others were about to move on without giving the exchange another thought when Ethan spoke.

May, keep your distance from that man.

She blinked. Huh? Why?

He seems sly. That advice sounds helpful, but I suspect he's plotting something. He kept bringing up Silver Wind. There's more to it than he lets on.

Exactly! Ethan sees it too! Max nodded vigorously. I told my sister Harley was bad news and we shouldn't trust him. Now that Ethan's saying it, I know I'm right!

May might dismiss advice from Max, but she could not ignore Ethan's warning.

I understand. She nodded seriously. Don't worry. I'll be careful around him.

Chapter 753: Just Like in a Romance Drama

At five o'clock that afternoon, the intense first day of preliminaries came to an end. After totaling every contestant's score, the organizers announced the top 64.

The Coordinators waited tensely. Those who had performed well expected to advance, while those whose appeals had gone badly still looked up at the big screen, hoping for a lucky place in the next round. Many had a rough idea of where their scores put them, but with so many entrants, no one could be certain until the official results appeared.

The Festival came only once a year. Honor, reputation, and prize money were at stake. Anyone eliminated today would have to wait until next year to try again.

Now, let's reveal the results! Vivian cried.

The big screen changed, displaying 64 names and portraits in order. Robert had the highest score. Surprisingly, Drew was not second. That place belonged to a woman with long, dark blue hair. Ethan and his friends had not expected her, but there had been three points between Robert and Drew, and the field was full of talent. Someone surpassing Drew was hardly impossible.

Their eyes swept down the list. May's portrait appeared at number 48.

She was delighted and deeply relieved. She had expected to advance, but only seeing her name there finally let her relax.

A feast! A feast! Ash shouted. May made it to the main competition! We have to celebrate properly!

As the others cheered, Ethan checked the rest of the list. He did not recognize most of the entrants, but Harley's portrait appeared near the bottom. He had advanced too. Whatever Ethan thought of the man's character, Harley was capable. If he put less effort into scheming against people, he might do even better. But that habit seemed rooted so deeply in him that Ethan doubted he would get much farther without changing it.

That evening, the group enjoyed the feast Ash had demanded. Caroline paid for it, both to celebrate her daughter's place in the main competition and to thank Ash, Brock, and the others for looking after May and Max on their journey.

Ash did not mind who paid as long as the food was good. He and Pikachu devoured it as though they had not eaten for days. Everyone but Caroline was used to the sight. If anything, they appreciated how openly Ash enjoyed himself.

The first day of the Grand Festival ended in that easy, friendly atmosphere.

The schedule allowed one day of rest after the preliminaries. The main competition would begin on the third day, giving May more time to prepare.

But the next morning, just as they finished breakfast in the dining hall, Harley appeared again.

Good morning, May!

He wore such a bright smile that, however little they liked him, May and the others could hardly ignore his greeting.

Good morning, Harley, May answered.

Harley approached with an overfamiliar air and an affected smile. You're going to practice, aren't you? So am I! Would you mind practicing together?

May repeated the refusal Ethan had helped her prepare the day before. I'm sorry. I've already made plans with my friends. We're going somewhere farther away today, so I can't practice with you.

Harley paused. This was the first time May had refused him. After their earlier encounters, he knew she was kindhearted and easily embarrassed. That was why his little schemes usually worked on her. But this answer did not sound like her at all.

He was surprised, but kept smiling. Don't say that. We're both Coordinators, and we've both reached the main competition. Shouldn't we help each other? Besides, aren't we friends?

Harley was like a burr that would not come loose. Ethan did not know how he had first met May or what had happened between them, but she could not seem to shake him. Harley was right about one thing: unlike Misty, May struggled to refuse people. If she were alone, she would not know what to do.

Fortunately, even without Caroline beside her, she had someone else to rely on. May said nothing to Harley and turned to Ethan with a helpless look.

Ethan sighed inwardly. He had hoped May could handle this herself, but Harley was more than she could manage for now. Ethan stepped in front of her and faced him.

It was the first time they had properly confronted one another. Harley studied Ethan's face, then met his eyes and felt an abrupt, oppressive pressure.

Didn't you hear her say she has plans? Ethan asked coldly. Leave while you still can. You seem to care about your reputation, so don't make me throw you out. I won't be this polite the next time I ask.

His words were much harsher than May's. Harley's expression changed. Behind Ethan, Misty loosened her clenched fists. It was probably fortunate Ethan had stepped in first. Given her temper, she might already have unleashed the full force of her anger on someone this persistent.

Harley looked Ethan up and down, frowning. Who are you?

You don't know who he is? Ash cleared his throat, ready to list Ethan's titles, but Ethan raised a hand to stop him.

Who I am is none of your concern, Ethan said. All you need to know is that you're not welcome here.

It was blunt, and being dismissed like rubbish in front of everyone was more than Harley could bear.

What did you say? His voice rose. Who do you think you are, talking to me like that?

I'll say it once. Ethan remained cool. If you keep bothering May, don't expect me to be courteous.

Harley wanted to lash out and teach this stranger a lesson. But he had spent so long laying the groundwork to make May lose the competition. He could not throw that work away now. Absolutely not.

He drew a breath, forced down his anger, and turned to May with an ingratiating tone. May, you don't feel that way, do you? We're friends, aren't we?

Well...

May had not expected Ethan to be so direct. Now Harley appealed to her, and she could not find an answer. He was clearly trying to make her speak for him.

Harley assumed the man who had appeared at May's side was a recent acquaintance. Otherwise, why had he never seen him at any of her previous Contests? Harley had known May through several of them. Surely she would choose his side.

May looked torn. It was not that she could not choose between Ethan and Harley. She wanted to refuse Harley, but could not say it to his face. Ethan stepped in again.

This is ridiculous, he told Harley. You're an adult. Can't you stop picking on a young girl and act like a man? Drop the affected smile, and stop putting on that feminine way of speaking.

That finally struck Harley's temper. Misty, Ash, and Brock exchanged glances too. They had rarely seen Ethan so confrontational. His words were harsh, but after Harley's behavior, hearing them was satisfying.

Harley could not stand such mockery. May had once merely failed to warm to his Cacturne and called it frightening, and he had held that against her ever since. Ethan had now insulted him to his face.

He could deceive and sabotage May, but looking at Ethan, he wanted to drive the man's head into the floor and make him pay for his rudeness.

I see. Harley took a deep breath. The artificial smile vanished. Outwardly he looked composed, but rage boiled inside him. You're determined to oppose me. Fine. If you're looking for trouble, I'll give it to you.

That was what Ethan had been waiting for. Words alone would not make Harley go away. From the moment he stepped forward, Ethan had expected they would have to battle.

At least you've chosen a man's way to settle this. Ethan pointed a thumb behind him and smiled. Come to the battle field out back. I'd like to see what someone like you can do.

Harley followed him out of the dining hall without a word, his face dark. Ash, Max, and Brock could not stay seated either and hurried after them.

May opened her mouth as she watched them go, but Misty stopped her.

Leave it to Ethan. Misty gave her a brilliant smile. Two men fighting over a girlit's just like a romance drama! And with someone like Ethan involved, it's an experience not everyone gets.

What are you talking about? May's face turned bright red. Still, Misty's words made her think that letting Ethan handle Harley might be better than enduring his constant attention herself.

Ethan led Harley from the dormitory hall toward a nearby outdoor battle field. It was a little after seven in the morning. With no matches today and the hour still early, few spectators or passersby were about. Even the competing Coordinators had not come out yet. The whole area looked empty and quiet.

After following Ethan for several dozen meters, Harley's stare grew more venomous. A vicious idea took hold. Seeing no one nearby, he released Cacturne and kept walking behind Ethan. Ethan gave no sign that he had noticed. Harley flashed his Pokemon a look, ordering it to attack from behind.

Its target was not another Pokemon. It was Ethan himself.

Trainers and Coordinators shared an unwritten rule: in a Pokemon battle, official or private, they did not attack the opposing Trainer unless defending themselves. No law enforced it, but breaking that boundary would earn widespread condemnation. Most people respected it. Harley clearly did not.

Cacturne swung its spiked arm at the back of Ethan's head.

Just then Ash and the others emerged from the dormitory hall and saw what was happening. Ethan had no Pokemon beside him, and Cacturne's strike was almost upon him. Their faces changed.

Ethan! Look out! Ash shouted.

He was too far away. Even if Pikachu raced to Ethan now, it would not arrive in time.

Chapter 754: Miserable Is the Only Word for It

Excitement gleamed in Harley's eyes. He could already picture Cacturne knocking Ethan down.

Then something unbelievable happened.

Cacturne had reached Ethan's back and brought its raised arm down. But a dark shape sprang from beneath Ethan's feet, putting itself between them like a wall. It lifted both hands, and a wave of black energy hurled Cacturne backward.

Harley's expression froze. It took him two seconds to understand what he had seen. Why was Ethan unharmed while Cacturne had been sent flying?

He looked again. The figure that had emerged from the shadow was a Gengar. Why had a Gengar been hiding in the man's shadow in the first place?

Keh-heh-heh-heh! Gengar lowered its arms and grinned at Harley. I've seen what passes for your cunning. Pretty pathetic. And trying a trick like that in front of me? You have a lot to learn!

Hearing it speak stunned Harley all over again. A Gengar that could speak human language? There were Pokemon like that in the world?

After a moment, he remembered to check on Cacturne. The blast had flung it dozens of meters into a wall. Cracks spread across the masonry, and Cacturne lay unconscious beneath them.

Sweat soaked Harley's back. He knew his own Pokemon better than anyone. Cacturne was his strongest and most trusted partner. It had ambushed a man from behind and still been defeated in a single blow. The gap between the two Pokemon had to be enormous.

That could not be right. Harley would rather believe Gengar had struck a vulnerable spot by chance than accept that it was so powerful.

Ash and the others finally relaxed.

That scared me. Ash breathed out. I forgot Gengar was there! With it guarding Ethan, nobody's going to hurt him.

Ethan had only paused. He glanced back at Cacturne, then at Harley's shifting expression, shook his head, and continued toward the battle field without a word.

Knowing what kind of man Harley was, the ambush had not surprised him. He had even suspected Harley might try it and felt no need for extra precautions. Harley could have brought several more Pokemon and still could not have reached Ethan under Gengar's watch.

Ethan's silent dismissal enraged Harley further, but it also cleared his head. His strongest Pokemon had fallen in one hit. What was he supposed to use now?

He watched Ethan walk away, mind racing. The failed ambush had put him in a humiliating position of his own making. Ash, May, and the others had come outside, so he could not try another cheap trick. Nor could he slip off unnoticed with Ethan ahead of him and the group behind. Uneasy, he followed them to the nearby outdoor battle field.

Ethan went straight to one of the Trainer's positions. He was here now; Harley could decide whether he dared accept the challenge.

Harley wanted to teach Ethan a lesson, yet Gengar's display left him wondering what he had gotten into. Still, he had come this far. He clenched his teeth and took the opposite position.

With his hands in his pockets and his eyes half-lidded, Ethan said, Come on. One battle or a full series, I don't care. Show me what you can do.

Harley's blood boiled. Ethan managed to hit a sore spot with even a casual remark. No wonder Harley had disliked him on sight.

He had to try, however little confidence he felt. Big words, Harley scoffed. I was about to say the same. Let's see whether you're as good at battling as you are at talking.

He paused and held up five fingers. If we're doing this, make it five against five. We each use a different Pokemon in every round, win or lose. After all five battles, whoever has more wins takes the match.

Harley was quick to scheme. He did not know the tale of Tian Ji's horse race, but he had arrived at a similar strategy. Whether Gengar had truly overwhelmed Cacturne or merely landed a lucky blow, it was plainly strong. Harley assumed it was Ethan's best Pokemon.

He could sacrifice his weakest Pokemon against Gengar, taking it out of the remaining rounds, then use his other partners to win the rest. He would lose one battle but win the series. The plan sounded excellent in his head.

It depended, of course, on his other Pokemon being stronger than Ethan's. Harley knew nothing about Ethan's team, and Ash's group had no intention of enlightening him.

Confident in his supposed advantage, Harley took out a Poke Ball. He did not release his Pokemon or name a first pick. He merely held the ball and waited for Ethan to show his hand.

Ethan saw through the little tactic. He shook his head, unwilling to bother arguing, and took a Poke Ball from his belt pouch. It made no difference how many rounds they played. His Pokemon's strength gave him every reason for confidence. Schemes could accomplish little against an overwhelming opponent.

Go, Ethan! Ash called.

You can do it, Ethan! May added.

The cheers darkened Harley's mood. Then Ethan's ball opened in a flash of blue light, revealing an Eevee.

Harley's mouth curled into a smile. Eevee was ordinary enough, often encountered in the wild, and this one had not even evolved. To him that meant weakness. He had traveled a long time without meeting a single Eevee that impressed him.

Surely Gengar really was this man's strongest Pokemon. Now Harley knew what to do. He threw his own Poke Ball, releasing Wigglytuff.

As Jigglypuff's evolution, Wigglytuff was twice as tall and considerably stronger. It was no longer quite as round, but its large eyes, soft pink-and-white fur, short limbs, and long ears still made it look harmlessly cute. A thin film of tears always covered its eyes. Beneath that gentle appearance, a Normal- and Fairy-type Wigglytuff could surprise anyone who underestimated it.

Ethan knew the species well and would not have let his guard down even if he had not. Harley's Wigglytuff, though, looked unusually sly. Its eyes and expression were fierce. It seemed to take after its Trainer.

The Pokemon moved to their respective sides of the field. With everyone watching, Harley made no further underhanded move. He believed an evolved Wigglytuff would beat an unevolved Eevee easily. Win the first round, and the advantage would be his.

There was no referee. Once both Pokemon were ready, they rushed together without waiting for a formal signal.

Almost at once, Harley realized something was wrong. Eevee looked like any other of its kind, yet it was far harder to deal with. Neither Wigglytuff's Body Slam nor its Double Slap could land. Eevee struck back with Tackle and Quick Attack, driving Wigglytuff steadily backward until it was panting.

Harley had underestimated Eevee badly. Worse, the first battle was slipping away from him.

Wigglytuff, what are you doing? he shouted. Stop playing around! Use Sing!

Despite its name, Sing was no cheering song. It could lull an opponent to sleep and turn a battle around in an instant.

Wigglytuff knew it was in trouble. It swung a hand to force Eevee back, leaped to a safer distance, and opened its mouth.

A spray of sand struck its face before it could sing a note. Sand filled its mouth, silenced the song, and stung its eyes. Harley had been naive to expect such an easy chance to put Ethan's Pokemon to sleep.

Eevee had interrupted Sing with Sand Attack. At Ethan's command, it took advantage of Wigglytuff's blinded state and struck with Take Down. Wigglytuff's eyes rolled upward, and its body flew back to land at Harley's feet. It was out.

Harley stared with his mouth open. For a long moment, he could not believe it.

I... I lost?

He had expected a certain victory. Instead, he had been on the defensive from the start and lost quickly without any real chance to fight back.

Ash and the others exchanged looks.

Um... Max hesitated. Does Harley know who he's battling?

I don't think so, Ash said, scratching his head. I haven't told him.

Neither have I, Brock said.

May shook her head. I haven't mentioned it either.

Max pushed up his glasses, an excited glint reflecting off them. So he thinks Ethan is just an ordinary Trainer?

Looks that way, Ash said. Should we tell him?

Why would we? Misty snorted. Harley seemed so sure of himself. I want to see how he feels after all five battles.

A Coordinator already fought at a disadvantage against a Trainer who specialized in battles. Harley's opponent was a man who had crushed challengers on the League tournament stage. After Harley's scheming and harassment, no one in the group felt much sympathy for him.

And now he could not even fight back. Miserable was the only word for it.

Chapter 755: A Hasty Retreat

Harley opened his mouth, then closed it without a word.

Perhaps Ethan had done what Harley himself had done: sent out one of his strongest Pokemon first to steal an unexpected early win. If so, the man was devious.

Harley told himself to stay calm. He drew a deep breath, recalled Wigglytuff, and took out his second Poke Ball.

Well played, he said, unable to resist a sneer. That little trick won you the first round. You won't be so lucky again!

Ethan stared at him. What trick?

Since Feebas, Beldum, and Torchic had evolved, Eevee really was the weakest Pokemon he currently carried. If Harley could not even beat Eevee, perhaps he ought to examine his own team rather than blame Ethan. What a strange way to think.

Ethan shook his head. Under Harley's rules, even a winning Pokemon could not fight again, so he recalled Eevee and took out a second ball.

Harley once again waited without showing his Pokemon. Ethan was used to it by now. If Harley volunteered to go first, that would be more suspicious.

Blue light flashed, and Milotic appeared on Ethan's side of the field.

Harley hesitated. Milotic was rare in his experience. Robert had used one to great effect in the preliminaries, and Harley had seen perhaps one or two others during years of travel. He could count every Milotic he had encountered on one hand.

Anyone who knew the species knew it evolved from Feebas and became remarkably beautiful. Even so, few Trainers seemed to raise one. Harley had seen too little of them to judge their strength precisely, but he was sure Milotic was formidable.

He considered the ball in his hand, looked at Ethan, put it back in his pouch, and selected a different one.

Changing his choice after Ethan had revealed Milotic was shameless. Max protested loudly, and Misty booed him. Harley ignored them. Only winning mattered.

He opened the new ball. Manectric appeared before Milotic.

Misty booed even louder. Ash, Brock, and May frowned. Harley had deliberately chosen an Electric-type to face Ethan's Water-type and seemed perfectly pleased with himself. Still, Ethan did not object, so the others let it go.

Ethan truly did not care. An Electric-type might make the fight harder, but it was still a fight. Before the Ever Grande Conference, he welcomed chances for his Pokemon to practice against unfavorable type matchups. Rehearsing them now would keep them from losing their heads when such a battle mattered.

Besides, he understood Harley well enough by now. Complaining about the switch would achieve nothing; Harley would only mock him. Defeating his Pokemon would make the point better.

Both sides ready, the second round began.

The type advantage did demand some caution. An Electric-type attack could hurt Milotic badly, though a twofold weakness alone would not decide the match. It was better to prevent Manectric from landing a hit at all.

Milotic did not immediately flood the field with Water-type moves, which could make the surroundings unpredictable. First it used Safeguard, protecting itself from paralysis even if an Electric attack connected. Then it sent a Twister at Manectric, both damaging it and obscuring Milotic's position.

Manectric darted about to escape the swirling wind. Once released, the Twister followed a predictable path. Thanks to Manectric's speed, it took only one hit before escaping the affected area.

It had barely cleared the wind when a powerful Hydro Pump met it head-on.

Milotic had held back its Water-type attacks only until the right opening. Taken by surprise, Manectric caught the blast full in the face and flew backward, almost beyond the boundary line.

Knowing Harley, Ethan doubted he would stop fighting over a line anyway. But the blow visibly unsettled him. They had only just started, and already the battle looked like the first round.

Manectric, what are you doing? Shock it! Harley yelled.

Landing an attack was not as simple as saying so. On an open field, a Pokemon's condition, distance, position, timing, and state of mind all mattered. This was no turn-based game with an opponent waiting to be struck. Ethan had used Twister's interference to set up Hydro Pump; Manectric could not simply fire a bolt and expect it to connect.

Still, it answered its Trainer's urging and attacked with everything it had. Spark, Discharge, Thunder FangMilotic dodged several moves, but one Electric attack did land.

That was where Ethan's preparation paid off. Safeguard kept Milotic from being paralyzed, allowing it to press on.

With Manectric close, Milotic drove it back with Aqua Tail. Before it could use Discharge again, Milotic launched Surf.

A huge wave rose before Milotic and crashed down, burying Manectric in spray and carrying it across the field.

Like many Fire-types, some land-dwelling Electric-types handled a soaking badly. Wet fur could slow them and interfere with their attacks. Manectric, a doglike Pokemon with a golden triangle of fur atop its head, was particularly troubled by the water.

Some dogs were strong swimmers, but even a paddling Manectric could not break free of a wave this large. It tumbled helplessly through the water until the surge reached the opposite Trainer's position and began to lose force.

Manectric washed up at Harley's feet. Above it was his dark, shifting expression.

Get up and fight!

Manectric had plainly crossed the boundary. Harley did not care. This was a personal dispute, not a formal match, and he had no intention of stopping over a rule like that.

Ethan had expected as much. Milotic rode the tail of its own wave and arrived behind Manectric before it could rise. In front of Harley, it whipped Manectric across the face with another Aqua Tail. The sharp crack rang out. Manectric fell unconscious.

Harley flinched as though the blow had landed on him. He stared at Milotic standing so close, his chest tight and his stomach turning.

Gengar had not even entered the match, yet he had lost twice. Both defeats had been decisive. He finally understood that none of his Pokemon could beat Ethan's. He had challenged someone far beyond him.

What was the point of continuing? Milotic's last strike had knocked all the fight out of him. He wanted only to leave this humiliating place.

I... I just remembered something I have to do. We'll call today's battle a draw for now. I'm leaving!

Before anyone could respond, Harley recalled Manectric, threw out that dry excuse, and hurried away. He walked as though a monster were about to devour him from behind, picking up speed until he vanished from sight.

He... just left? Ash and the others stared after him, then looked at one another in disbelief.

They had expected Harley to lose. They knew the gulf between the two men. They had not expected him to abandon the match halfway through. He had proposed five rounds, and only two were over. There were still three chancesthough, realistically, none would have helped him.

Had he lost all five, he might never have been able to hold his head up around them again. By leaving before the end, he could insist, as he already had, that the match was a draw. No one could force him to admit otherwise. He was unlikely to challenge Ethan again, though.

Let him go, Ethan said. He recalled Milotic, stroked its head in praise, and turned to the others. The match didn't finish, but I doubt he'll bother May anymore. That's what I wanted. And those battles weren't much practice for my Pokemon anyway.

The others agreed that the result was enough. Only Misty remained indignant.

He got off too easily! You should've beaten every Pokemon he has and shown him exactly how strong you are!

She was firmly on Ethan's side and could not stand hearing anyone speak badly of him. Harley's harassment of May only made her dislike him more. Two quick defeats did not satisfy her.

Don't worry, Ethan said with a smile. There are Contests in plenty of places. We'll probably see him again, and when we do, we can be the ones to give him trouble.

He said it lightly because he knew how far ahead of Harley he stood. Without that confidence, he could not have approached the battle so calmly. Harley's words were not worth getting angry over; they were on different levels altogether.

Ethan had grown rather self-assured. Given his achievements, perhaps that was understandable. Only Elite Four members and regional Champions could truly be compared with him now.

Both rounds together had taken less than five minutes. Ethan had not even worked off breakfast. The group chatted and laughed as they returned to the dormitory, soon putting Harley and the entire incident out of their minds.

At the entrance, they split up again. May needed to practice for tomorrow's main competition. Ethan and Ash did not want to waste the day either. Since they were together, they decided to find a quiet spot and prepare for the approaching Ever Grande Conference.

Max and Brock went with May, their traveling companion. Misty looked back and forth between May and Ethan, then stayed beside Ethan.

He and Ash were only going to train, not battle each other. The practice would likely be dull. Misty would not take any chances, though. Lisia had already stolen a march on her once. This time, Misty intended to keep Ethan in sight.

It would not happen again!

Chapter 756: May's Mishap

A dazzling fireworks display opened the Grand Festival's main competition. As the crowd cheered, special guest Lisia took the stage and sang CharmLove, warming up the audience before the matches began.

Ladies and gentlemen! Once Lisia had left, Vivian walked to center stage in a pink dress. Her voice was as sweet and clear as ever. Smiling, she waved to the stands. The main competition of the Pokemon Contest Grand Festival, every Coordinator's dream, is finally beginning! These Coordinators earned five Ribbons in Contests across the region, then placed among the top 64 on the preliminary Appeal Stage. Now they'll face each other in spectacular competition for the title of Top Coordinator. And the winner will receive this brilliant Ribbon Cup behind me!

The preliminaries had been modest by comparison. This was a full-scale event before the arena crowd, broadcast live on television and online to homes across Hoenn. The main competition was the Festival's true beginning. Even people who chose not to watch would hear how popular it was.

Now, let me introduce our judges! Vivian gestured behind her.

The panel had grown for the main competition, another sign of how seriously the organizers took it. Five judges sat there: Mr. Sukizo, president of the Pokemon Fan Club; Mr. Contesta, head of the Contest committee; and three Nurse Joys. Ethan had found it odd not to see Sukizo and Contesta in the preliminaries. Given their positions, it made sense that they had been reserved for the main event.

The three Nurse Joys looked identical, down to their clothes. Standing side by side, they made an impressive sight. They were neither twins nor triplets, but members of one enormous family. Perhaps only Brock could tell them apart. Ethan wondered where the organizers had found them, and how they distinguished them. Were the slightly different colors of their hats enough?

Each judge greeted the audience. Some ardent Lisia fans sat beside Ethan, still enthralled by her lively song. They shouted so loudly he could not hear a word from the panel. Presumably the judges wished the Festival well.

May was not in the stands with them today. She waited in the preparation room with the other contestants.

Under the rules, each Coordinator needed two Pokemon over the course of the main competition. The first round was another appeal: one Pokemon per contestant, with three minutes to perform. The judges would score the acts, with each judge awarding up to twenty points. Only the top 32 would advance to the next round of Contest battles.

With both appeals and battles, the format offered something for viewers of all ages. That variety was one reason Contests were so popular. Some girls and older spectators even preferred the Grand Festival to a League tournament.

The day before, Ethan and Ash had done basic training. Ash had focused on the accuracy of his Pokemon's moves. Ethan had taken a more hands-off approach and let his Pokemon join Ash's group to experience a different training style. They had gained something from it.

Ash had wanted a private battle with Ethan, but Ethan refused. Save the main attraction for the Ever Grande Conference, he had said. Why enjoy it early?

That had persuaded Ash. He stopped asking and looked forward to their eventual meeting even more.

Misty, meanwhile, felt she had wasted the entire day guarding Ethan. Lisia had not appeared once, even by bedtime. Misty was pleased, but frustrated too. A persistent rival she could confront. Lisia's unpredictable appearances were harder to defend against. Misty never knew when or where she might strike again.

Vivian was still speaking. At last, she raised her voice. Now, please welcome our 64 Coordinators to the Appeal Stage!

Applause and cheers filled the arena. Ethan waved his light stick gently. Amid that sea of excitement, the first round began.

A boy in his teens ran to center stage, leaped high, and released Ninetales. It breathed flames as soon as it appeared, producing a striking opening appeal that drew applause.

Going first was difficult. The audience had not yet settled into the show, and many minds were still elsewhere. Even an excellent act could lose some of its effect. The boy handled the pressure and gave the Festival a strong start.

Unexpectedly, Harley came out second. He emerged from the competitors' passage smiling, blowing kisses and waving to the stands. Nothing in his manner recalled his humiliating retreat the previous day. That defeat had done nothing to shake his composure; in one respect, his resilience was formidable.

Perhaps Gengar had hurt Cacturne too badly for it to recover overnight. Harley had brought a Banette instead.

Banette greeted the arena with a chilling laugh and a frightening expression. The air seemed to grow colder. The audience went quiet. People whispered to one another, wondering what Harley meant to do.

He soon showed them. At his command, Banette conjured a ring of Will-O-Wisps and then used Thunder, calling a powerful bolt down onto its own body. It kept laughing within the golden lightning. The glare made its grin more eerie still.

As Vivian exclaimed, it was a dark, unsettling performance with an explosive impact. The crowd stared in astonishment.

The act had little to do with conventional beauty, yet its strange style expanded their idea of what an appeal could be. Harley earned a high score: 89 points, just one short of the next ten-point mark.

That... Ash stared for a while before managing, I've never seen an appeal like that.

Neither have I, Ethan said. It's an unusual direction, but it works. In a way, Harley's personality suits this style. I have to give him credit.

Though of course Harley would put his creativity into something unsettling.

More than a dozen Coordinators followed. Their performances varied. Strong acts scored over eighty, and one entrant with a Ledyba even reached ninety. Others landed in the seventies; the lowest earned only 72, all but ending that contestant's run even before everyone had performed.

It was both splendid and unforgiving. Whatever each entrant's result, the atmosphere in the arena grew steadily livelier.

Soon it was May's turn. Her pretty, cheerful appearance earned an immediate round of applause. Instead of Beautifly, she released Skitty, which came out full of energy and used Assist at once. To everyone's surprise, it produced Silver Wind.

White light shone around Skitty's paws. A spiraling wind thick with glittering scales swept upward from them.

Assist, sometimes called Cat's Paw, was a Normal-type move available to only a few feline Pokemon. It borrowed a move at random from one of the user's teammates. Regardless of the borrowed move's type or how unsuitable the user's body might seem, a strange power let it perform the move once.

That unpredictability made Assist a clever technique in battle, but also a risky one. A borrowed move might create trouble for its user. This time, Skitty had drawn Silver Wind from May's Beautifly. A cat performing a Bug-type move was surprising enough; the sparkling scales drifting overhead made the sight especially delightful.

May looked pleased and ordered Assist again. Skitty borrowed Bulbasaur's Razor Leaf, sending a wind full of leaves across the stage.

Whether that was her plan from the start or she had been encouraged by her luck, May kept using Assist. Combusken's Flamethrower, Bulbasaur's Vine Whip, Beautifly's String Shot and Gustone little cat performed move after move that was not its own. The audience loved it. May and Skitty worked in perfect step, giving them an exciting appeal.

But Assist's uncertainty could work against them.

On the next use, Skitty produced Solar Beam, a powerful Grass-type attack. It should have been a chance for an especially brilliant display. Instead, as the move began, Skitty froze. May's commands stopped too.

The big screen caught even a moment's hesitation. Their pause was far longer than a moment. The audience frowned, wondering what had happened. Ethan and Misty were just as puzzled.

Why isn't she continuing? Misty asked.

Well... Brock hesitated. As far as I know, none of May's current Pokemon can use Solar Beam.

He did not need to finish. Ethan understood. A move neither May nor Skitty expected had broken the rhythm of the act, and any mistake was magnified on a stage like this. But if none of May's partners knew Solar Beam, how had Skitty borrowed it?

There was no time to consider that question. May recovered from her confusion and ordered Assist again. This time Skitty used Petal Dance. Pink petals filled the air, drawing the audience back into the performance and easing the effect of the earlier pause.

Then another problem appeared. Skitty's eyes turned into spirals, and it staggered around the stage as though drunk.

Ethan recognized the side effect of Petal Dance at once: the move could leave its user confused. One accident had followed another before May could recover from the first.

Most spectators could not tell. They thought Skitty was spinning about on purpose, showing off its playful sense of humor. Laughter spread through the stands at the adorable Pokemon's antics.

Only Ethan and the others who knew what they were seeing understood how alarmed May must be. Fortunately, she had grown a great deal. Her face betrayed none of her panic, and in a moment she thought of a way to save the act.

Chapter 757: May's Request

Before the watching crowd, Skitty began slapping its own face with Double Slap. Each blow sounded painful.

Most spectators could not understand it and assumed this was another strange part of the act. Those who recognized Skitty's condition saw what May was doing: using the sting of the blows to break its confusion. It worked.

The performance was nearly over. At May's command, Skitty gathered itself and sprang high into the air, spinning as it rose. It used Blizzard, shaping a spiral of icy wind beneath it. Before the wind died, dozens of sharp, smooth icicles joined into a giant crystal.

Sunlight caught the structure and made it sparkle like a diamond. Its pure, transparent beauty drew gasps. It was a fine ending, and the audience's cheers and applause showed their appreciation.

Most importantly, Blizzard was Skitty's own move, not one borrowed through Assist. It landed gracefully on the crystal's peak and held its finishing pose.

Ethan and his companions looked up at the large screen. The numbers flickered, then settled on 79 points.

Seventy-nine. A dangerous score, though understandable. May's opening and finish had been strong, but the judges could hardly have missed her two obvious mistakes. Without that impressive ice crystal at the end, her score might have been lower.

May was disappointed on the stage. In the stands, Caroline and Max looked sorry for her.

That score isn't encouraging, Max sighed.

Ethan nodded. May's fate now depended on the others. If enough remaining Coordinators performed well, they would push her below the cutoff. She could only hope some of them scored lower.

Two more contestants performed. Then came one of the Festival's three leading favorites: Drew, who had placed third in the preliminaries.

He walked slowly onto the stage to loud cheers. Like May, his looks immediately won him admirers; young women in the crowd called out for him. Objectively, Drew had an impressive appearance, bearing, and Pokemon team. He was young too. If he and May had not clashed when they first met, they might have become friends.

Their relationship had eased somewhat as they traveled and met again. They no longer treated each other as enemies on sight, but an ordinary conversation was still difficult.

Drew used Masquerain this time. It had a bright blue body and four diamond-shaped wings. Its long, droplet-shaped head resembled a large nose, and paired with the eye-like markings on its wings, it gave the impression of an odd face.

Masquerain opened with Hidden Power. Light shone through its wings, creating a brilliant display overhead. Drew lowered his head, half-closed his eyes, and raised his right hand with practiced elegance. At that signal, Masquerain scattered the light across the entire arena.

Points of light drifted down. While the audience admired them, Masquerain filled the field with enormous bubbles, then used Silver Wind to send them floating away in a waterfall of wind and shimmering spheres.

It was magnificent. The audience applauded fiercely; some people rose to their feet. The visual impact even surpassed May's ice crystal. From the strength of the response, Drew's score would surely be high.

The numbers flashed and stopped at an astonishing result: 100 points. A perfect score.

There it is! Vivian cried. Our first perfect score of this Grand Festival!

Drew had earned it. His presentation and Masquerain's movements had been flawless, fluid, and beautiful. He had shown off his Pokemon's appeal to the fullest. He had performed even better than in the preliminaries.

The contrast with May was clear. Her appeal had been colorful, but it relied mostly on moves borrowed from other Pokemon rather than displaying Skitty's own strengths. That departed from the Festival's purpose and was the main reason her score had been so low. She still had room to grow.

Ethan leaned back and watched a stray bubble drift toward him. Drew's performance would affect May, but it also put tremendous pressure on everyone scheduled to follow him. Those contestants had drawn an unlucky position.

Of course, a strong competitor would face that pressure and turn it into drive.

Drew left the stage gracefully. More than a dozen Coordinators followed, many clearly shaken by his perfect score. Mistakes multiplied. Some could not even perform at their usual level and received low marks. Inadvertently, Drew had helped May's chances.

Then Robert, the favorite to win the entire Festival, appeared. He was one of those competitors who became stronger under pressure. After Drew's triumph, Robert gave an equally spectacular performance and earned another perfect 100.

Stunned silence gave way to a roar of delight. One perfect score at a Festival would have been remarkable. Two in the same round left the audience amazed.

The contestants who remained seemed to crumble under the weight of both performances. No one stood out before the round ended, much less achieved another high score.

Wow... Max scratched his head, relieved for his sister. Good thing May went on before those two. She might actually make the next round.

The turn in her fortunes had come quickly, but they still needed the official rankings before they could celebrate.

At last, Vivian made the announcement. The Coordinators who passed the first round and will advance to the Contest battles are...

The large screen changed to a list of portraits, revealing the qualifiers one by one. Robert was first, and Drew had moved past the woman who placed ahead of him in the preliminaries to take second. Both had scored 100 this round, so their earlier rankings appeared to break the tie. Robert had performed better in the preliminaries, after all.

Other strong entrants followed. The woman who had outranked Drew yesterday, however, did not appear. The random order had placed her after Robert. Seeing both his and Drew's perfect performances had shaken her so badly that she gave a poor appeal and a low score. Despite her excellent preliminaries, she was eliminatedperhaps the unluckiest competitor in the Festival.

Harley's portrait appeared soon enough. His 89 points were well above the scores of many shaken contestants.

The list kept filling. In the competitors' waiting room, the mood grew heavier with each name. May's palms turned damp. When places 29, 30, and 31 passed without her portrait, her heart seemed to leap into her throat.

Then number 32 appeared. It was her own smiling face. She clenched her fist in excitement. With 79 points and help from other contestants' mistakes, she had narrowly reached the next round.

Misty and Max rejoiced in the stands. Caroline was so happy she secretly wiped tears from her eyes. No one wanted to see May succeed more than her mother.

After the qualifiers came the pairings for tomorrow's Contest battles. This draw was part of each day's proceedings, but the matchups had to be settled now.

The screen changed again, showing two frames with portraits cycling at random. The first two pairs were chosen. On the third draw, the portraits slowed and stopped on May and Harley.

Oh? Misty raised her eyebrows. That's interesting. Did the organizers do it on purpose? Do they know about May and Harley?

Of course not. Ethan laughed and shook his head. It's coincidence. With only 32 entrants and sixteen pairings, they had a fair chance of drawing each other.

...

Knock, knock, knock.
