After dinner, Ethan showered and was getting ready for bed in a bath towel when someone knocked at his door. Curious, he opened it and found May outside.

Etha May began, then saw his wet hair, bare chest, and towel. Her face flushed.

Ethan was embarrassed too. He tightened the towel and gave her an apologetic smile. I thought you were Misty.

Misty? Did he mean he would be comfortable answering the door like this for her?

May seemed lost in thought. What brings you here so late? Ethan asked.

She gathered herself. Um... would you teach me how to battle?

Ethan blinked. She wanted him to teach her? She had Ash and Misty nearby. Why come to him?

He glanced outside. Darkness had fallen, with the moon and stars high overhead. It was not very late, but few people were walking around the dormitories.

Of course. Wait a moment while I get dressed.

When he came out, May was waiting. She had not invited anyone else, and Ethan did not suggest it. He followed her quietly downstairs and toward the nearby outdoor battle field. Far off, the snack street was still bright and noisy, a sharp contrast with the quiet around them.

Neither spoke until they reached the closest field. Then Ethan could not hold back his curiosity. Why ask me when Ash and Misty are right here?

They had known each other for a long time, yet this was the first time they had been alone together. It felt a little strange.

May lowered her head, looking shy. Because you're the strongest person I know.

Ethan had not expected such high praise. Did she even rate him above her father? He rubbed his nose. Being complimented to his face by a pretty girl was gratifying, and stirred another feeling he could not quite name.

You don't need to be so formal with me, he said with a smile. You're friends with Misty and Ash. Call me Ethan, like they do.

Chapter 758: May's Special Training

Ethan... May tried the less formal name quietly. There was nothing unusual about it, yet she felt a little shy. Perhaps it sounded too intimate. Still, the change made them feel a step closer.

She remembered the sweet, genuine smile Misty wore whenever she addressed him that way. An odd feeling came over her.

Ethan noticed her embarrassment and smiled. All right. How would you like to train?

May quickly focused. The other day, you beat Harley. Could you tell me how you did it?

Ethan thought back over the match. There was no useful insight to offer. His Pokemon had simply overwhelmed Harley's.

Well... Harley wasn't much of a challenge for me, he said after a moment. I didn't find anything about him particularly difficult.

May looked disappointed. People truly were different. To her, Harley was a troublesome opponent. To Ethan, he had been no obstacle at all.

Waitshe was already calling him Ethan in her thoughts? She had only just started. It must be because she had heard Misty and Ash say his name so often.

Ethan saw her expression. I may not have advice tailored to beating Harley, he said, but I can help you get stronger.

Huh? What do you mean?

He took a Poke Ball from his pouch and released Gardevoir, then called Gengar out of his shadow.

We still have tonight. I can help train your Pokemon so they're stronger for tomorrow's match.

R-really? May's excitement was unmistakable. Gardevoir and Gengar were among Ethan's strongest Pokemon. Training against them would surely benefit her partners.

Of course. This is a rare opportunity. I don't offer personal training very often.

He was not boasting. His choice showed how much he cared about May's progress. Eevee and Milotic alone had defeated Harley, yet he had brought out Gardevoir and Gengar to teach her. Harley's pride would have suffered if he knew.

Thank you so much! May bowed deeply. I'll work hard!

That's the spirit. Ethan nodded approvingly. We don't have much time, so let's begin.

Yes!

May released Beautifly and Bulbasaur. Ethan looked at them. These are the two you plan to use against Harley tomorrow?

I think so. Her confidence faltered. Is there a problem with that?

None. Bulbasaur can attack from the ground while Beautifly attacks from the air. Together, they can pressure an opponent from two directions. It's a good combination.

May let out a relieved breath. I'm glad. I was worried you wouldn't like my choice.

Choose the team you want, May. Don't let anyone else decide for you, including me. Ethan shook his head. You made the top 32. You're already a Coordinator people know about, and you need to trust your own judgment. In a Contest battle, what matters is showing off your Pokemon's strengths. Any partners you can do that with are valid choices.

I... I understand.

The four Pokemon were ready. Ethan motioned for May to attack whenever she wished.

She prepared to give the command, but one more look at Gardevoir and Gengar made her swallow. Gengar grinned, and Gardevoir wore a gentle smile. Both seemed friendly. Yet May could feel an enormous pressure from them. She knew how powerful they were. The feeling was no trick of her nerves.

Relax, Ethan said. The battle hasn't started, and you're already wavering. Look at your Pokemon. They're eager to begin.

Huh?

May looked at Beautifly and Bulbasaur. They could sense the power facing them too, but neither shrank back. Their eyes burned with fighting spirit.

Beautifly, Bulbasaur... Their determination steadied her own.

Good. Remember that feeling, Ethan said. There's nothing to fear. Go all out with the partners you trust most. Even if you lose, you won't regret giving everything you had.

May took a deep breath and nodded. Ethan, here I come!

...

Bang! Bang!

Beautifly and Bulbasaur flew backward and collided. The moment they landed, they struggled to their feet again.

After more than an hour of training, both were battered and breathing hard. Their stamina and resolve were near their limits. Gardevoir and Gengar, on the other hand, seemed as fresh as when they had started.

They're so strong, May thought for what felt like the hundredth time. Watching them battle had never shown her just how formidable they were. Only facing them herself made it clear.

Beautifly and Bulbasaur had attacked without pause. They had not injured their opponents or even tired them out. Gardevoir and Gengar had held back, defending most of the time and avoiding vulnerable spots when they counterattacked, yet May's team was still in disarray. Only their precise control had allowed the training to last this long.

Beautifly, Bulbasaur, how are you? Can you keep going? May watched anxiously. Both Pokemon nodded, and she drew breath to order another attack.

Someone spoke before she could.

So this is where you two disappeared to! Sneaking off for a date?

May turned. Misty, Ash, Brock, and Max had arrived. Of course the voice belonged to Misty.

A d-date? Ethan and I only came here to train!

Ethan? All four caught the change in how May addressed him and glanced at one another. Misty had meant it as a joke, but her teasing had revealed something interesting. For May's sake, none of them said so aloud.

Ethan worried Misty might embarrass her further and changed the subject. What brought you all out here?

We came to see what you were doing, Misty said, spreading her hands. May was gone from our room for ages. We worried something had happened to heror that Harley had attacked her before the match. Then we knocked on your door and found you missing too. We came looking and caught you two secretly battling.

Secretly? May's ears reddened at the suggestive word.

Ash, oblivious to the mood, saw her battered Pokemon facing Ethan's. How did the training go?

Misty, Brock, and Max turned to Ethan. So did May. She could not judge her own progress. She had attacked throughout the session and failed throughout it. Was that good or bad?

Not bad, Ethan said. To learn how to hit, first you have to learn how to take a hit. They stayed on their feet this long, so their endurance has improved. Their attacks are more coordinated too. I think they'll do fine tomorrow.

May brightened at his approval. The others were pleased for her as well.

That's great! Ash said. If Ethan says they'll be fine, they will!

Ethan's confidence also came from his prior-life knowledge. In the anime, May had beaten Harley. With this extra training, her chances should be better still.

He added a warning. That's assuming a normal match. Don't underestimate him. Against someone who relies on tricks like Harley, carelessness is your greatest enemy.

I won't let my guard down. May nodded firmly. Then, still eager, she said, I feel like I need more work, though. Ethan, can we keep going?

He shook his head. That's enough for tonight. It's past ten. Rest is part of training. Take Beautifly and Bulbasaur to Nurse Joy so they can recover. If you spend all their strength tonight and they're exhausted tomorrow, it will all have been for nothing.

Only then did May realize how late it was. She had barely noticed the time pass. She wanted to continue, but trusted Ethan's judgment and agreed at once.

Thank you for everything tonight, Ethan. I promise I'll win tomorrow. I won't let you down!

...

The Grand Festival arena was packed again. The crowd was even more excited than the day before. Two fierce matches had already warmed them up, and they were eager for the next.

May and Harley entered to a roar of cheers. Given their earlier friction and Harley's clash with Ethan, there was no friendliness left between them. This match would settle matters on the stage.

As in an ordinary Contest, the battle had a five-minute limit. Within that time, each Coordinator had to combine the beauty of their own presentation with their Pokemon's moves and win more points.

Without pleasantries or even a word to each other, May and Harley released their teams. May chose the partners she had settled on the night before: Bulbasaur and Beautifly. Harley sent out Cacturne and Banette.

One was Grass- and Dark-type, the other Ghost-type. The pair suited Harley's sinister, unpleasant manner. On type matchups alone, May held an advantage against Cacturne with both of her Pokemon. But knocking an opponent out was not the sole way to win. The visual appeal of their moves counted heavily too.

That complicated things. After Ethan's training, Beautifly and Bulbasaur might have won an ordinary battle with ease. This, however, was the Grand Festival.

Vivian saw that both sides were ready and raised her microphone. The third Contest battle: May versus Harley! Begin!

Chapter 759: May's Battle

As Vivian declared the match open, the timer at the edge of the field began to count down.

5:00... 4:59... 4:58...

Harley gave the first commands. Banette used Screech, followed by Cacturne's Bullet Seed. The attacks swept toward Bulbasaur and Beautifly before May could issue an order, forcing her to defend.

Last night's training paid off immediately. Her Pokemon had spent so long avoiding Gardevoir and Gengar that they calmly evaded both attacks. Harley's opening failed.

Bulbasaur struck back. Two vines shot from its bulb and caught Cacturne and Banette around the ankles. Harley told them to dodge, but the vines were too fast. Before they could break free, Beautifly sent a Silver Wind into them. The strong gust hit both for a solid blow.

May kept the combination going. Bulbasaur spun like a top, flinging the two bound Pokemon into the air. As they whirled, Beautifly struck them with a second Silver Wind. The wind accelerated their spin, and they crashed heavily to the ground.

The crowd cheered. Spectators admired the stylish combination, and the judges nodded approvingly. A large portion of Harley's yellow point bar vanished. May had scored first.

Yes! Misty cheered from the stands. Keep this up and she'll beat Harley for sure!

Caroline was pleased too, but puzzled. How did May improve so much in one night?

Max hurried to explain Ethan's training session. Caroline looked at Ethan with gratitude. Thank you for taking care of May.

Several people sat between them. Ethan leaned forward and waved the thanks away. May has talent, and she worked hard for this. I only helped a little.

As the adults spoke politely about May, Misty fell thoughtful. She seemed to be seriously considering something.

The battle continued. Less than four minutes remained. Cacturne and Banette staggered to their feet, still dizzy from their spin and unable to locate their opponents properly.

Ethan had taught May to press an advantage. As Harley shouted for his Pokemon to recover, a storm of petals swept around them. Petal Dance dealt damage, and another section of Harley's point bar disappeared.

The match was going entirely May's way. That was not necessarily because Beautifly and Bulbasaur were stronger than Cacturne and Banette. Her attacks flowed so smoothly from one to the next that Harley could find no opening. Interrupt her rhythm once, and he might stop the assault. But May had yet to make a single mistake, leaving him to watch his Pokemon take hit after hit.

He did try to counter. Once Cacturne endured the petals long enough, Harley ordered Pin Missile. Needles shot into the swirling flowers and shredded some into fragments that drifted down.

It bought only a moment. Even a cactus covered in spines could not shoot down every petal. While Cacturne was occupied, May launched her finishing combination.

Bulbasaur used Razor Leaf. Beautifly used Silver Wind. Wind lent speed to the leaves, and the leaves gave the wind force. The intertwined attacks struck Cacturne and Banette in an instant. Neither could withstand them. Both fell on their backs, unable to battle.

Harley's face flushed and paled by turns. He stood frozen, unable to accept the result. But Vivian's voice rang through the arena.

Harley's points have fallen to zero! May advances to the next round!

Applause rose from the stands. Ash, Misty, and their friends clapped and cheered. Seeing May defeat Harley fairly on the stage was satisfying after everything he had done.

Ethan glanced at the clock. It had stopped at 2:27. He could not remember how long May's match with Harley had taken in the anime, but surely it had not ended this quickly or easily. Their training had made a difference. He felt a small glow of pride. Perhaps, when he stopped traveling, he could make a living teaching new Trainers.

May celebrated with her two Pokemon. Harley recalled his own, plainly bitter. He glared at her once and left. Unlike his private battle with Ethan, this loss had happened before an entire arena. He could not pretend it had ended otherwise.

May soon led Beautifly and Bulbasaur backstage to rest. Victory was worth celebrating, but she had more matches today. After this round, the final sixteen would be paired again, then reduced to eight and four. The champion would be decided today as well. There was no time for her to rejoin her friends; she needed to recover and prepare.

Other pairs followed her onto the field, including Drew and Robert. Both performed steadily, beat their opponents by wide margins, and advanced.

Just over an hour later, May returned to face a plump Coordinator named Anthony. Ethan had never met him. Ash and his friends had helped Anthony recover Ribbons stolen by Team Rocket on the day of the preliminaries, and had become friendly with him. May had not helped with that incident and had only met him a few times. In any case, even friends had to compete seriously here.

Anthony was roughly as capable as Harley, with the strength to reach the top eight. Unfortunately for him, May had momentum. She maintained the form she had shown against Harley, using Combusken and Bulbasaur to defeat his Swalot and Pinsir.

Anthony gave her a difficult match, though. He hid Pinsir inside Swalot's mouth and used the two together in an unusual combination that troubled May for a time. She held firm, then seized the instant Pinsir emerged from Swalot's mouth to overcome them both.

The timer showed 0:37 remaining. It had been one of the closest matches so far. May's point bar had fallen by nearly half. But a win was a win, and she had reached the top eight.

For a newcomer, it was an excellent achievement. At a Festival of this scale, May had already surpassed Ash's result at his first Indigo League tournament. She deserved to celebrateand unlike Ash in that tournament, she still had a chance to push on toward the title.

Drew and Robert battled again soon after and advanced to the top eight as expected. The competition was now much fiercer. None of the eight remaining Coordinators was weak, and the next draw might decide who had a path to the final. A gentler matchup could carry someone forward; drawing Robert might end a run immediately.

Contestants and spectators alike held their breath as the portraits spun across the large screen. The four quarterfinal pairings appeared.

May's opponent was Drew.

Everyone with Ethan was startled. They knew the shrinking field made a meeting likely, but had not expected it already. May had just fought Harley, and now she had drawn the other person with whom she had a difficult history.

Ethan alone was unsurprised. The anime had paired them here too. It felt like a fated encounter. Just as Gary had been Ash's early rival in Kanto, Drew was May's. They seemed bound to meet.

May was backstage, so they could not see her reaction. It was easy to imagine her mixed feelings.

The quarterfinals began after a short break. At least May was not in the first match. She had a few more minutes for her Pokemon to recover and to plan against Drew. It was not much. Once the first pair finished, May took the stage.

Even on the big screen, her expression looked heavier than in any earlier match. The confidence she had carried against Harley and Anthony was gone. She pressed her lips together, grave and tense.

Max swallowed. May looks really nervous. I've never seen her like that.

Of course she is, Ethan said. She's facing Drew. He's consistently performed better than she has. At a moment like this, anyone would feel the pressure.

At Vivian's signal, both Coordinators released their teams. May chose Skitty and Combusken. Drew sent out Roselia and Flygon.

Ethan frowned. He did not know May's reasoning. Skitty and Combusken were not at a clear type disadvantage, but Bulbasaur and Beautifly had trained together the previous night. The coordination they had developed might have served her better.

Did she have another plan? Or were Bulbasaur and Beautifly too tired after their earlier matches, leaving her no choice?

Chapter 760: The Grand Festival Ends

After thinking it over, Ethan guessed May had chosen Grass- and Fire-type Pokemon to make a combination stronger than either could manage alone. Whatever her plan, the teams were set. He could only hope she performed well.

Vivian gave the signal. The timer started, and so did the match.

Drew attacked first. Ethan noticed a pattern. May had also been a beat slow to act against Harley and Anthony, surrendering the initiative and leaving herself to defend and counterattack. It was a poor habit. An early attack could score the first points and put the other Coordinator on the defensive. May had not had enough time to polish away habits like this. Another region of travel would teach her a great deal.

Roselia used Petal Dance. Flygon darted through the shower of petals and flew at Combusken and Skitty. May reacted calmly despite going second. She ordered Skitty to use Assist, which borrowed Combusken's Fire Spin. Flames caught the petals and dispersed them. Combusken then leaped with Sky Uppercut, forcing Flygon to pull back. Its jump fell a little short, though, and the punch missed.

May and her friends in the stands all winced at the missed opportunity. Drew was untroubled and prepared another attack.

This time Flygon used Flamethrower while Roselia used Solar Beam. The two powerful moves rushed toward May's team. There was little time to dodge. May ordered Combusken to answer with Fire Spin.

On its own, Fire Spin should not have been strong enough to hold back both attacks. Yet when the moves met, they formed a larger whirlpool of flame and light. Its regular rotation resisted Flamethrower and Solar Beam, preventing either from advancing. The crowd watched in astonishment.

Drew was surprised too. In his brief hesitation, May called out again. Combusken poured more fire into the spinning column, which threw the incoming attacks back toward their owners. Flygon and Roselia were hit by the rebound. An explosion filled the field with smoke, and a large section of Drew's yellow point bar disappeared.

Yes! Ash punched the air. May got the first big hit! Maybe she really can beat Drew!

Misty and the others were delighted too. A few more exchanges like that could carry May into the semifinals.

Ethan hated to dampen their excitement, but he said, May and her Pokemon are doing well. I still think Drew will win.

What? Ash stared at him. But May's performing better!

She just sent their moves back at them, Misty added.

The others could not see why Ethan sounded certain. Brock thought for a moment. Do you mean Drew hasn't been fighting seriously yet?

Ethan nodded. Brock's level head served him well when he was not distracted by an attractive woman.

Look at Drew's face. He's been composed from the beginning. He's not underestimating May or acting out of arrogance. He's testing her without feeling pressed.

That doesn't mean she'll lose, Ash objected.

No. But look at his Pokemon. They took that counterattack and still haven't panicked. They seem ready for more.

Ash and the others studied Roselia and Flygon. Ethan was right. Neither appeared badly hurt, and both still looked eager to fight.

Drew sees May as a worthy rival, Ethan continued. He wants to know how much she's grown. I think that was his test. Now he'll give her everything he has.

It was the sort of observation a champion made. As Ethan finished speaking, the match changed. Drew's attacks came faster.

May could not adjust at once and fell behind. Time ticked away. Flygon and Roselia attacked repeatedly, while Combusken and Skitty defended and seized what chances they could to counter. The struggle remained fierce, but the balance was shifting toward Drew.

Even spectators who could not follow every exchange saw May's yellow point bar shrinking toward the edge. Ash and the others grew quiet.

0:45... 0:44...

May's Pokemon did not yet look exhausted, but her point bar had only one segment left. Drew still had nearly half of his. One more hit might eliminate her.

May knew it. When Drew ordered Flygon to use Flamethrower again, she launched a final counterattack.

The flames shot straight at Skitty and Combusken. Combusken leaped into them. Wrapped in fire, it rose beneath Flygon and delivered a Sky Uppercut. The punch scattered the flames and struck Flygon hard in the face. The audience answered with applause and cheers.

It was a brilliant move, but May could not turn the match around. As Flygon landed, Drew countered at once. Roselia released Stun Spore, paralyzing Combusken and Skitty. Flygon followed with Steel Wing.

Bang!

Unable to dodge, both of May's Pokemon were knocked backward. Her point bar reached zero. The clock stopped at 0:03.

Only three seconds had remained in the five-minute match. Even without Drew's final attack, however, May would have lost on points when time expired.

The crowd cheered Drew's victory and applauded May too. She had given them a wonderful battle despite losing. After a brief moment of disappointment, May comforted her Pokemon, stood, and bowed to the spectators still calling for her.

Ethan and his friends rose from their seats and went to the competitors' exit. They met May as she came off the stage.

You were amazing, May! Max said.

You did so well!

Caroline, Misty, Ash, and Brock joined in. None seemed disappointed that she had been eliminated; they were sincerely proud of her. Ethan stood at the back of the group and applauded quietly.

Reaching the top eight was an excellent result. May had started among 247 Coordinators, all of whom had earned five Ribbons. This was her first event on such a scale, and she had advanced farther than most. She had even outdone Ash's result at his first Indigo League tournamentbut Ethan decided not to bring that up.

They left the arena together and ate lunch at a nearby restaurant, watching the remaining matches on television. Drew defeated another opponent to reach the final, where Robert awaited him. One of them would win the Grand Festival.

Ash sipped his juice. Who do you think will win?

Robert, one friend answered.

I think Robert too. He's so strong.

Ash had not expected such agreement. Really? I thought some of you would say Drew!

Drew's excellent, Brock said, but Robert is a little stronger. I don't think the outcome is much in doubt.

Ash turned to Ethan, hoping for a different answer. Robert, Ethan said. They've already given my reasons.

The television proved them right. Drew fought with everything he had, but Robert's Milotic and Claydol seemed a level above his team. With more than two minutes left, Drew's point bar had fallen to its final segment while Robert still held most of his. The result was almost certain.

Drew refused to give up. He fought until the clock ran out, his two Pokemon collapsing only at the very end. Amid a roar of cheers, Robert became the Grand Festival champion.

May watched Drew's disappointed face and clenched her fists. Drew had beaten her convincingly, only to lose to Robert in much the same way. The gap between them felt like a chain she could see but could not yet cross.

The group stayed with the broadcast through Robert's award presentation and the Festival's closing. As at the opening, there was a performance. To Misty's displeasure, the singer was Lisia.

Misty watched her charm the crowd. Gradually, her gaze hardened. She had made a decision.

...

At eight that evening, an enormous outdoor party filled the Grand Festival plaza. The closing banquet was a Festival tradition, held to thank every contestant for their hard work and celebrate the new champion. Only after everyone had eaten and enjoyed themselves would the event truly be over.

The food was served buffet-style and was so good that Ash and the others had wandered off in different directions. May sat at a long table and finished the last bite on her plate. She was about to take a walk when Misty came over.

May, will you walk with me?

May paused. There was something unusual in her friend's voice. Had something happened? She did not ask. She stood and nodded.

Of course.

Chapter 761: Misty's Once-in-a-Lifetime Request

Misty and May left the party and followed a stone path to the shore. Dim streetlights stretched their shadows long across the ground. Behind them, more fireworks rose and lit the night sky. Waves broke against the rocks with a steady rush.

May could not keep her concern to herself any longer. What's wrong today? You seem unhappy.

Misty stopped and faced her seriously. May, what will you do after the Grand Festival?

May did not know why she was asking. I haven't decided exactly, she said after a moment, but I think I'll keep working toward becoming a better Coordinator.

Misty looked as though that was the answer she had expected. Why do you ask? May said.

Could you do me a favor? Misty's solemn voice made May's smile fade.

We're friends. Whatever it is, tell me.

Misty took a deep breath, as if she were entrusting May with a dream of her own. After the Ever Grande Conference, will you keep traveling with Ethan in my place?

W-what!? May could hardly believe her ears. You want me to travel with Ethan? Why?

Misty turned toward the sea, looking forlorn. Night hid the water from view; only the sound of the waves reached them.

I don't have much choice. When the Conference ends, I have to return to Kanto and take over the Cerulean Gym. You know how popular Ethan is. People like Lisia are always finding ways to get close to him. I can't stop worrying.

May understood at once. Misty wanted her to keep an eye on Ethan.

Well... but...

May instinctively felt it was inappropriate. She and Ethan were good friends, nothing more. Watching him on Misty's behalf and keeping other girls away went beyond the place a friend ought to claim in his life. Traveling with him normally would be one thing; going with that purpose was another. What if Ethan misunderstood her? What if he came to dislike her?

Her better judgment told her to refuse. Yet when she met Misty's earnest, hopeful gaze, the words would not come.

Misty knew what troubled her. Still, May was the only person she could ask. Without Misty there, she could all too easily picture what would happen the next time Ethan met Lisia. She could not bear to watch Lisia take him away.

May, this is my once-in-a-lifetime request. You're my best friend. Please say yes.

May held her gaze for a long while. At last she nodded. All right. I'll travel with Ethan, and I'll look out for you.

Relief flooded Misty's face. She smiled again. Thank you, May! I knew I could count on you!

By the time they returned arm in arm, the party had ended. Ethan and the others were waiting for them, surprised to see the two girls so close together.

May, Max asked, where did you go? What took so long?

Misty lifted her chin before May could answer. I'm not telling you!

What's with the secrecy? Ash muttered. It's probably just girl talk. I don't want to hear it anyway.

At the words girl talk, May glanced guiltily at Ethan. He caught the look and wondered why she was watching him. Had they really been talking about him?

...

They had spent several days in Slateport City. With the Grand Festival over, it was time to leave for Ever Grande City.

Ever Grande lay to the east of Hoenn's mainland, a scenic coastal town on a large island covered in flowers. Its greatest claim to fame was the Ever Grande Conference and the Hoenn Pokemon League, both held there. Like Silver Town, it had grown and prospered around a major tournament.

Flying from Slateport would have been quickest, but Ethan was the only one in the group who could easily afford it. The others were young, and there was no need to spend the money. A passenger ship sailed directly to Ever Grande. It would take longer, but the Conference was still more than ten days away.

When they gathered at the docks the next morning, Jessie and James appeared disguised as salespeople, apparently preparing some new trick for Ash. They spotted Ethan with him, startled, and scurried off. Ash and his friends failed to recognize the pair and wondered why the salespeople had run away.

Ethan only shook his head. He had become a monster in Team Rocket's eyes.

After about two days at sea, they reached Ever Grande City. The excitement was palpable as soon as they disembarked. Visitors and competitors had arrived in great numbers despite the days remaining before the opening ceremony. Even Ethan and Ash felt their nerves tighten. The Conference was finally close.

The city occupied little land, but its modern buildings rose high and stood close together. In that respect, it could hold its own against much larger cities.

Ethan and Ash needed to confirm their eligibility at the registration center. At May's suggestion, Misty and the others headed instead to the Ever Grande Noodle Nosh, a ramen shop she was eager to visit. May said its ramen ranked among the three best bowls in Hoenn. That was enough to interest the group.

Ethan remembered that May loved food. Food enthusiast was the polite phrase. If a person or Pokemon stole something from her plate, though, her anger could transform her. Good food mattered that much to her.

Ash wanted to join the ramen outing, but registration came first. He watched the others leave, humming happily, then trudged after Ethan toward the Conference grounds.

The venue stood in the hills beyond the city, arranged around a lake. Facilities occupied the shore and connected by walkways to the central arena, forming a web of paths across the water. The grounds were broad, and people crowded nearly every part of them. Ethan and Ash wondered why so many had come early.

They went straight to registration. Entries remained open until just before the opening ceremony, but most Trainers registered well ahead of that deadline unless something delayed them.

Ethan had entered in advance at the Fortree Pokemon Center, so he only needed to verify his qualifications. He waited while Ash registered, then they accepted Conference guidebooks from Nurse Joy.

Despite the name, the booklets offered little help with battling beyond the schedule. Most pages covered food and restaurants. May would probably appreciate them.

Like the Indigo League and Silver Conference, this tournament would have a ceremonial flame relay. Nurse Joy told them it was happening today. Ash forgot all about ramen and wanted to see it at once. Ethan was curious too. He sent Misty a message, and the two left registration for the relay route.

Before they reached the venue gate, they saw a short elderly man step out of a black car. Ethan recognized him. Ash was already hurrying over.

President Goodshow! It's been a long time!

Charles Goodshow turned at the sound of Ash's voice and spotted Ethan behind him. Ash! Ethan! Are you entering the Ever Grande Conference too?

That's right! Ash said.

Ethan came up beside him. Good to see you again, President Goodshow.

Goodshow nodded. I'm glad you're both here. I'm sure you'll give us splendid matches. Ethan, I expect you're aiming for another championship?

Who isn't? Ethan smiled. I'll give it my best. Whatever result that brings, I'll accept it.

It was a careful answer. He had made his ambition clear without saying anything that would annoy the other competitors if repeated. Goodshow gave him a knowing look.

Then I wish you both good results. I have business to attend to, so I'll leave you here.

They knew how busy he was. After saying goodbye, they watched him go and continued toward the flame relay.

Goodshow entered an office building at the venue and went to a small conference room. Smoke hung in the air. Every organizer responsible for the tournament had gathered, smoking in gloomy silence. They rose when he arrived.

Sit down. Goodshow took the chair at the head of the table. His usual jovial manner vanished. Tell me. What are we going to do?

Almost everyone looked past him at the screen on the wall. It showed Ethan lifting the trophy at the previous Silver Conference. Silence gave way to uneasy discussion.

So he really entered Ever Grande?

With his strength, won't he win the whole thing again?

I heard he challenged Hoenn's Gyms with a different team. Will he still be as strong as before?

Who knows? But if he wins with that team too, we might as well hand him the trophy from now on and forget running the tournament!

None of it answered Goodshow's question. He rapped the table, silencing the room. I asked for solutions, not complaints.

The officials looked at one another. At last one spoke timidly. There isn't much we can do. We can't forbid him from competing.

Arguments broke out at once.

Of course not! We've never barred someone like that since the tournaments began!

Our credibility would collapse if people found out!

Then what can stop him?

Only one man remained silent, smoking with a faintly mocking smile. He was John, the live broadcast director at both the Indigo League and the Silver Conference.

John looked around the table and sneered inwardly. No one here understood ratings and audience demand better than he did. Keep Ethan out? John would be the first to object. Even Goodshow's wish to find a way to prevent another title was misguided.

These officials talked endlessly about the tournament's development. They overlooked ratings and reputation. A competitor like Ethan drew viewers by himself. Those viewers made the broadcastand the Conferencea success. Let the others rack their brains; they would find no sensible way to stop him.

John shook his head, stubbed out his cigarette, crossed one leg over the other, and looked back up at the photograph.

It really was a good picture of Ethan: confidence, a little rebelliousness, and just a hint of arrogance. He seemed to be looking down on everyone in the room.

Chapter 762: The Preliminary Round

When Ethan and Ash reached the flame relay route, they were surprised to find Misty, May, and the others already there. They had only just finished their ramen when Ethan messaged them. How had they arrived first?

Misty grinned at their faces. Didn't expect us? You thought you could leave us behind and watch the relay yourselves? No chance! We weren't going to miss this.

At the ramen shop, the group had happened to meet one of the torch runners, who traveled with a hat-wearing Meowth. After Ethan's message came, they decided to follow the runner to the relay. They had been closer to the route than Ethan and Ash, so they arrived ahead of them.

Now that they were all there, they watched the ceremony together. It had been underway for some time, and several runners had already carried the flame. The best viewing spots were taken, leaving the group to watch from a distance beside the road.

According to the story, the flame had been taken from Moltres. To most people, that made it sacred and mysterious. To Ethan, Moltres was a Pokemon he could see every day.

Misty smiled throughout the relay. Ethan found that curious. She had seemed troubled for days, but her usual cheer had returned after the Grand Festival party. He did not know what had happened, only that he was glad to see her happy again. Perhaps May had cheered her up. He ought to thank May when he had the chance.

Back in Ever Grande City, Ash and his friends went to check into the dormitory. Ethan parted from them and visited a delivery company. Kennedy's package had arrived: the Meteorite Key Stone. Ethan had eagerly awaited it, wanting to see how it differed from an ordinary Key Stone.

Its appearance disappointed him. Finished and polished, it looked almost exactly like any other Key Stone. No one could have guessed its origin by sight alone. He would have to test it through a Pokemon's Mega Evolution and judge whether it made any difference.

Ethan put it away and went to the police station. The reward promised by the International Police had finally arrived too. A bespectacled senior official, formal and scholarly in manner, presented it instead of Anabel or Looker. After photographs and speeches, Ethan received the money.

Five million, with no tax deducted. It was far more than he had earned for winning either the Indigo League or the Silver Conference, and it gave his bank account a welcome boost.

The award also included a certificate naming him a Special Investigator of the International Police. He now had a measure of official standing. When confronting dangerous organizations in other regions, he could do so with recognized authority.

The Ever Grande Conference had not even begun, and he had already gained a great deal.

When Ethan returned to the competitors' dormitory, Ash had just finished contacting Professor Oak and his mother, Delia. It was only natural to tell the two people most important to him that he had arrived. Ethan hesitated, then sent word to Sabrina, Erika, and the Cerise family too.

They were pleased, but work and distance would keep them away. They would watch on television. Ethan did not mind. If Sabrina and Erika both arrived in person, that might cause more trouble than their absence. The Cerise family would have been no problem, of course.

Afterward, the group went to the Pokemon transfer machine. Ash had decided to challenge the Conference with his current team. Ethan had other plans. His Hoenn Pokemon had grown strong, but they might not be enough to win the title alone. The partners who had traveled with him through two earlier regions deserved a chance to compete too.

He sent several Legendary Pokemon away and brought back Tyranitar, Scizor, Venusaur, Jolteon, and Blastoise. Alongside Dragonite, Eevee, Milotic, Metagross, and Blaziken, they formed his Conference roster.

Crystal Steelix and his enormous red Gyarados remained at Cerise Park. Both were so powerful that Ethan excluded them without hesitation.

Now he had to devote the remaining days to intensive training and getting his team into its best condition. However close he and Ash were, they were competitors. They would train separately until they met in the tournament, keeping their tactics and true strength private.

...

Time raced by. Before they knew it, the preliminary round had arrived.

Unlike the Grand Festival, the Ever Grande Conference had three stages: a preliminary round, preliminary tournaments, and the main competition. More than six hundred Trainers had entered. Reducing that field to the 256 who would reach the main competition promised fierce competition.

The first stage used one-on-one battles, one Pokemon per Trainer. That format made upsets possible. When opponents were closely matched, an unfortunate type matchup could mean immediate elimination.

After ten days of training apart, Ethan and Ash met again. They had stayed in the same dormitory building, yet rarely crossed paths. Ash had seen Misty now and then, but this was his first sight of Ethan in all that time. Ethan had left early and returned late each day, spending nearly every waking hour outside meals at the training grounds. No one knew what he had done there.

Ash was curious about the results, but Ethan did not volunteer any details, and Ash did not ask.

Be careful, Ethan said with a smile. Don't get eliminated before you even reach the main competition.

That's not happening! Ash clenched his fist. Just watch. I'll make it through!

You never know, Misty teased. What if your first preliminary opponent is Ethan? You'd be on your way home straight away.

Don't jinx me! Ash sputtered. Misty, keep your mouth shut!

The preliminary matches took place not in the large arena on the lake, but in fifteen matching venues around the outer grounds. Each so-called small venue held three thousand spectators. With all fifteen in use at once, the scale was impressive.

Enthusiastic crowds nearly filled them to bursting. The Ever Grande Conference needed no advertising; its name alone drew attention across Hoenn. Even the preliminaries attracted viewers in droves.

Ethan was assigned to Venue A4. Misty accompanied him there while Ash went to his own venue. Most entrants had reached this point by earning eight Badges, though some had qualified through other routes. Their skills varied widely, making the preliminaries unpredictable.

Ethan was in A4's third match. While waiting, he watched two battles that were not especially strong.

The first pitted two young boys against each other. They looked about Ash's age, but seemed fresh from a Trainer school. Their theoretical knowledge was good. Their Pokemon, however, fought by the book, trading rigid attacks and defenses as though reciting a lesson.

The spectators showed little interest. Misty yawned. Perhaps only the boys themselves believed they were engaged in a thrilling, evenly matched contest. After nearly seven minutes, the red-haired boy eked out a win. The audience gave him polite, thin applause. Oblivious, he beamed and waved back.

The second match was more engaging. Two middle-aged men dressed like office workers threw themselves into directing their Pokemon, sweating and gesturing so vigorously they seemed to work harder than their partners. Their Pokemon met at close range, exchanging solid blows. Whatever the Trainers lacked in polish, the fight was livelier than the first.

The older man lost. He was not eliminated yet, however. With so many entrants to reduce to 256, some would need an extra match while others received byes. His strong showing earned him another chance. Only a second defeat would end his run.

Then it was Ethan's turn. He demonstrated what an overwhelming difference in level looked like.

He used Eevee, and that was enough. From the referee's start signal to the flag marking the finish, the match lasted 42 seconds. Ethan's opponent never landed a single hit before Eevee's relentless attacks brought its Pokemon down.

The audience stared for a beat, then erupted. Some spectators had only just opened their bags of chips. They looked up after putting the first bite in their mouths and found the battle already over. This was nothing like the two matches before it.

For many in Hoenn, it was their first look at the handsome man in the Trainer's box, one hand in his pocket and a calm smile on his face.

His opponent looked from its fallen Pokemon to the referee's flag, mouth open. More than a year of work, and it was over almost before it began. The battle would leave a mark on that Trainer.

Ethan left the field to the crowd's cheers and lightly slapped Misty's raised palm.

That was fast, she said with a laugh. I expected an easy win, but I didn't think the other Trainer would last less than a minute.

Eevee did well. Ethan smiled down at it. It gave the other Pokemon no opening. I should be through to the next round. I wonder how Ash is doing.

Want to see? His match was scheduled later. It probably hasn't started.

Of course. Let's go.

On their way to Ash's venue, they spotted Team Rocket's trio again. Since Ethan had begun traveling with Ash, he saw Jessie, James, and Meowth far more often.

This time they were not causing trouble. Dressed as vendors with small boxes hanging from their necks, they sold rice crackers, milk candies, juice, and boxed meals. They knew how to earn money from a crowd. When they were not trying to steal Pikachu, they showed business sense and worked hard, even if Jessie complained. It was a pity they kept choosing the wrong path.

Ethan and Misty reached Ash's venue as he emerged from the competitors' passage. His match was about to start. May and the others were in the stands, with two unfamiliar people beside them.

Chapter 763: Who Is This Man?

Ash had chosen his most trusted partner, Pikachu, for the preliminary match. His opponent wore a white martial arts uniform and a red headband. That outfit practically announced a Fighting-type Pokemon. Sure enough, a Hitmonlee stood before him.

Ash had made a good choice: Pikachu was not at a type disadvantage. Then again, Ash might not have cared even if it were. His reputation for battling against unfavorable matchups was well earned.

Ethan and Misty arrived just as the match began. Hitmonlee rushed at Pikachu, trying to fight up close. It swept one leg across the field, but Pikachu leaped high and brought an Iron Tail down on its round head. Hitmonlee struck the ground.

That first exchange said a great deal. Pikachu had taken the initiative, and Ethan doubted this would be a hard fight for Ash.

He was right. Hitmonlee rose and attacked with High Jump Kick. Pikachu avoided it with Quick Attack, then used another Iron Tail to knock Hitmonlee out. It had won without a single Electric-type move.

Ash had grown tremendously. Ethan could no longer think of him as the careless, clumsy child who had started traveling so long ago. Ash had become a difficult opponent.

After the match, they met outside the competitors' passage. Ash's friends introduced the two people with them.

One was a stocky boy with orange hair tied in a ponytail. He wore traditional clothes and spoke in a rustic style, referring to himself with a rough, folksy pronoun. He looked intimidating but was actually rather absentminded. His name was Morrison.

Ash had met him during his recent travels. They had much in common: both fought with spirit and refused to give up. They competed over nearly everything, becoming friends and rivals at once.

Even without the introduction, Ethan knew something about Morrison from the anime. He was one of Ash's Hoenn rivals. He was capable, but fate would pair him with Ash at this Conference, where he would lose and finish in the top sixteen.

The other newcomer was an older man, perhaps two or three years older than Ethan, whose performance at this Conference would outshine nearly everyone else's. Tyson was the torch runner with the hat-wearing Meowth whom May's group had met at the ramen shop and the relay.

Ethan knew his future in the anime: Tyson would win the Ever Grande Conference. That made him Ethan's most serious expected rival here.

He did not know either man personally, so he greeted them with a polite nod.

All the preliminary matches finished within the day, narrowing the field to 256. At sunset, the qualifiers gathered in the main arena for the opening ceremony. Before contestants and spectators, the ceremonial flame reached the raised platform and lit the cauldron. Only then did the Ever Grande Conference truly begin.

After a rest day, the preliminary tournaments began. First came the draw.

All 256 contestants assembled in a hall, giving Ethan his first look at many potential opponents. Besides Morrison and Tyson, he recognized quite a few faces from his travels. Their presence here was a surprise.

The room was crowded and noisy even though everyone spoke quietly. Nearly four hundred others had already been eliminated. Had they all been packed in here too, there would scarcely have been room to breathe.

Nurse Joy explained the rules again. Unlike the opening preliminaries, this stage consisted of three Double Battles per contestant. A Trainer had to win all three to advance; one loss meant elimination. The 32 winners would enter the final tournament, where full six-on-six battles would decide the champion.

Most had read the guidebook, though a few had not learned the format until now. Everyone who had reached this stage was eager to see what came next.

The draw appeared on the big screen. All 256 portraits flashed into place at once. Ethan searched for his own, but Ash called out first.

Found it! I'm in Arena C this afternoon!

Morrison seemed determined to be louder. I've got Arena E this morning!

They were competing even over who could announce a schedule more forcefully. Ethan shook his head and looked back at the screen. He found his portrait at the lower right. His first match was fourth in the afternoon at Arena F.

He had not been drawn against Ash. That was good newsnot because he feared Ash, but because he did not want to send his friend home early. As for Ash beating him? Ethan smiled to himself.

Then he checked his opponent and found another familiar face. Anthony, the man who had operated an unofficial Gym and claimed to own the world's strongest Pokemon, had entered. His supposed marvel had been a Pelipper carrying several Poke Balls in its mouth.

Across the hall, Anthony saw Ethan's portrait too. He remembered the man who had beaten him and tightened his fists, eager for a rematch. Wait and see. I'll show you how much I've grown since then. I'll avenge that loss!

They were not truly enemies, but Anthony wanted to settle the score. He also had to defeat Ethan to reach his second match. Either way, he could not afford to lose.

As the group left for the dining hall, a woman stepped into Ethan's path. He was startled for a moment, then recognized her and sighed. Alexa had interviewed him at both the Indigo League and the Silver Conference. She was dressed as a reporter again, with her equipment-laden Gogoat at her side.

We meet again. She smiled. I came early just to get the first interview with you.

It's been a while, Alexa, Ethan said with a wry smile. You give me too much credit. I'm not going anywhere. There was no need to rush.

Alexa planted a hand on her hip. You're a sought-after story. Hoenn hasn't recognized you yet because people here don't know what you can do. Once you advance, reporters will be queuing up. I'd rather get here before them.

May and Max knew Ethan had won two regional tournaments. Even they were surprised a reporter had traveled to Hoenn specifically for him. Tyson and Morrison were more stunned. They had never heard Ethan's name before today. Why would a journalist seek him out when the preliminary tournaments had not even begun?

Why was no one interviewing them?

Tyson had some fame in Hoenn and had been selected as a torch runner. Surely that made him a better subject. Both men quietly adjusted their clothes and posture, hoping to draw Alexa's eye. She never looked away from Ethan. Their hopes sank.

Hurried footsteps approached. A woman with a microphone and a man carrying a camera ran toward them, breathing hard.

Morrison and Tyson brightened. At last, reporters for them! They prepared to greet the pair. The two ran straight past without a glance and stopped in front of Ethan.

What?

Morrison and Tyson could only stare. The man was taller, better-looking, and in better shape than they were, but what else set him apart?

Ethan recognized the newcomers: the TV Mauville reporter and her cameraman whom he had met in Mauville Park. He tried to recall their names.

You're... Emma and Ida, right?

Gabby and Ty, they corrected with embarrassed smiles.

Ah. Sorry. Ethan had remembered both names wrong.

It's fine, Gabby said. She glanced warily at Alexa, who was studying her with interest. Ethan, do you remember promising me an exclusive interview?

Ethan searched his memory. He had wanted to escape their persistence in Mauville and had put them off until the Ever Grande Conference. They had remembered and come to collect on the promise.

Now both Alexa and Gabby wanted an interview. Ethan looked between them, unsure whose request to accept first. Alexa understood why Gabby was here, and her expression grew serious. Coming early had been the right decision. Hoenn's reporters were already beginning to notice Ethan.

Morrison finally turned to Ash. Who is he? Why do all these reporters want him?

Tyson quietly leaned closer to hear.

Him... Ash looked toward the sky, complicated feelings in his voice. His name is Ethan. He's the person I've spent my life trying to surpass.

That only confused Morrison and Tyson further. They had spent enough time with Ash to know how direct he usually was. Why answer with a riddle now? Apart from the man's name, they still knew nothing.

But Ash's words and the reporters' attention made one thing clear: Ethan had to be formidable. For the first time, both men studied him seriously.

Chapter 764: Toying with His Opponent

Ethan finally put both interviews off until later. He had only cleared the first preliminary stage, and the preliminary tournaments had yet to begin. An interview now would be premature. He ought at least to reach the final tournament before talking about his prospects. Boasting too early could put viewers off and make him look conceited.

Alexa and Gabby saw that his mind was made up and reluctantly let the matter rest. Alexa had interviewed him twice and understood his manner. Gabby was less at ease. Ethan had won in two regions and was a leading contender here. Getting the first, perhaps exclusive, interview with him might decide whether she could return to her station. She glanced at Alexa with fresh determination.

...

With their opponents known, the competitors began preparing for their matches. Ash, Morrison, and Tyson studied the people they might face and considered which Pokemon to use. Ethan alone seemed to have nothing to do.

He had spent more than ten days training privately. Every adjustment and preparation he could make was done. His Pokemon were in top condition. Their strength gave him confidence against anyone drawn across from him.

The early matches were already underway. Morrison's was scheduled first among the group, so Ash and the others went to cheer him on. Ethan barely knew Morrison or Tyson and felt no urge to cultivate a friendship. He took Misty and walked unhurriedly toward his own arena.

He was confident enough not to scout these potential opponents. Their unknown teams might add a little difficulty and make the Conference more interesting.

Cheers rang out from distant arenas. Outside, spectators unable to buy tickets gathered in small groups before enormous screens to follow the action.

The preliminary tournaments used larger venues in the inner ring instead of the fifteen outer arenas from the first stage. There were five of these, labeled A through E, each seating ten thousand people. Television crews had begun broadcasting the matches too. Coverage was not yet as extensive as it would be for the final tournament, but plenty of viewers watched at home or online. The Ever Grande Conference was steadily drawing all of Hoenn into its excitement.

Ethan watched several matches from the stands. His turn came in the second-to-last match of the afternoon.

As Alexa had said, the Hoenn crowd did not recognize him. His entrance caused no special stir, though some women applauded and cheered more loudly when they saw his handsome face. That small difference made Anthony envious as he entered from the other side. Why was the applause for him so thin? And why were his own cheering supporters all men?

Ladies and gentlemen, the announcer called, next is the ninth match in Arena F! In red, Ethan! In green, Anthony! Let's see what they can show us!

At the referee's signal, both Trainers threw their Poke Balls. This was a Double Battle, testing how well each pair could work together. Ethan had no concerns on that score.

Blue light flashed, and Milotic and Metagross appeared. The stands grew louder. Both species were difficult to raise and rarely seen compared with more common Pokemon. Seeing them together was a novelty.

Anthony's team looked more ordinary, but he had brought his two strongest partners. One was Pelipper, the same Pokemon that had once carried Poke Balls in its mouth while he claimed it was the world's strongest. The other was Magneton, evolved from a Magnemite that had also hidden in Pelipper's beak during that earlier deception.

Water and Electric moves gave Anthony a broad range of attacks when the pair worked together, despite the poor matchup between their own types. He had planned carefully. Ethan had beaten him with Dragonite before; Anthony had brought Magneton partly to counter it. Ethan had not sent Dragonite out, but Magneton still held a type advantage over Milotic. Anthony felt he had guessed well enough. Today he would settle the score.

The referee started the match. Anthony's hopes faltered in the first exchanges.

A type advantage mattered only if he could land his attacks. Milotic and Metagross gave him no easy chance. Pelipper's Water Gun and Hydro Pump met stronger attacks from Milotic. Its Air Slash and Wing Attack could not break through Milotic's defense either, and Milotic's counters left Pelipper injured.

Anthony tried to send Magneton against Milotic instead, but Metagross kept it occupied and battered it badly. His attacks seemed to land on padding: every advantage he expected was blunted before he could use it. An old, unhappy memory returned. Ethan was not even using Dragonite, yet the battle felt like their first meeting, when he had been defeated so easily.

He had traveled too far, earned eight Badges, and reached this stage to suffer the same fate again. Anthony shoved the thought aside and tried everything he could imagine. Shouting from his position, he ordered his Pokemon to cross paths and exchange opponents. This time the switch workedbut the battle did not improve.

Milotic's ranged attacks kept Magneton away. Streams of water stopped its electrical attacks from doing meaningful damage. Pelipper fared no better against Metagross. Both of Anthony's Pokemon were now at a clear disadvantage. He had no answer left.

Ethan's expression never changed. He stood calmly, issuing an occasional order. His team was simply stronger. Anthony had traveled, but not through as many battles or experiences as Ethan and his Pokemon. Ethan's keen eye and sense of timing let him read Anthony's plans and counter them. The gap between the Trainers compounded the gap between their Pokemon.

He did not finish the match immediately. He wanted Milotic and Metagross to spend more time battling in the Conference atmosphere. He did something similar at nearly every tournament, helping newer team members grow accustomed to competing before a large crowd.

Unfortunately for Anthony, that meant a longer ordeal. Milotic and Metagross defended and countered only enough to keep him under pressure. They did not rush to knock his Pokemon out. Under nearly ten thousand watching eyes, Ethan's pair gradually settled in. Milotic moved more fluidly, and Metagross hovered more steadily. The crowd no longer seemed to affect them; they could fight at their normal level.

That mattered. Many Trainers and Pokemon lost some of their ability to nerves on a stage like this. Anyone who overcame that fear already held an advantage over much of the field. Ethan's older partners had passed that hurdle long ago, but the Pokemon he had caught in Hoenn still needed experience. That was why he was willing to let the match continue.

Anthony's condition moved in the opposite direction. His spirits sank, and his Pokemon's coordination fell apart. Next to Ethan's increasingly smooth pair, Pelipper and Magneton looked clumsy together. Everyone could see that Anthony would lose.

In a corner of the stands, Gabby and Ty kept their camera rolling. Their outdoor family program had no access to the official camera area, so they had bought tickets and filmed like ordinary spectators.

He's incredible, Ty said. He's playing with that opponent. The man can't do anything.

Gabby was no battling expert, but she had a reporter's eye. She nodded, excitement brightening her face. If he performs like this in every match, the championship is only a matter of time.

She grew more determined. After failing to find the Pokemon behind Hoenn's changing weather during their trip off Mossdeep's coast, Ethan had become her greatestand perhaps onlychance to regain her place at the station. She could not let another reporter get his exclusive interview first, even if she had to use a few tricks.

Ethan knew nothing of Gabby's thoughts. He saw that Anthony had lost the will to fight and judged the practice sufficient. With a wave, he ordered Milotic and Metagross to finish. Both opposing Pokemon went down, and the arena erupted in cheers.

Fans loved a close, exciting contest, but an overwhelming victory could be just as thrilling. They had watched Anthony's resistance fail against Ethan's strength and followed every exchange from Ethan's side. His win brought a flood of applause.

Chapter 765: Different Expectations

When Ethan left the arena after his match, he ran into Ash and the others hurrying toward it.

Misty was still talking animatedly beside him about the excitement she had seen in the stands. In the middle of her story, Ethan stopped. She looked up in surprise and saw Ash's group approaching.

Huh? Your match is over already? Ash asked, disappointed. What a shame! We came as fast as we could to watch, but we're still too late.

Morrison and Tyson looked disappointed too. They had already marked Ethan as a difficult opponent and hoped to see what he could do.

There was no helping it. Ethan's match had been scheduled late, and he had spent a long time in the arena, but the venues were far apart. They could not cross from one to another in a few minutes.

Ethan waved a hand and smiled. You didn't miss much. It was an ordinary battle. You can see how long it took me to come out.

As he spoke, a solitary figure emerged from the competitors' passage and trudged away.

Ash watched him go. That's Anthony, isn't it? He was your opponent, Ethan. What happened to him?

Anthony looked as though he had been through some terrible ordeal. All the energy had gone out of him.

Max pushed up his glasses. Isn't it obvious? Mr. Ethan beat the fight right out of him!

What? Really? Ash scratched his head. I've battled Anthony too. He used underhanded tricks to beat a lot of challengers, but he's still strong. What kind of battle would leave him like that?

That only made Morrison and Tyson more curious.

Misty had learned over their long travels that some things were best left unsaid in front of others. Before Ethan could answer, she smiled at them. It wasn't anything special. The battle just dragged on. Anthony couldn't stand the atmosphere, and it got to him.

Morrison and Tyson had questions, but accepted her explanation. They had felt the pressure of this stage themselves. It was nothing like an ordinary battle or a Gym challenge, and it had affected their Pokemon badly. They could perform at barely more than half their usual strength.

Fortunately, most of the competitors faced the same problem. With nearly everyone struggling, it had not seemed unfair.

Ethan asked how their matches had gone. As expected, all of them had advanced.

Ash had made it through by a narrower margin. Perhaps his opponent had been unusually strong, or perhaps he had chosen a poor pairing. Each side had lost a Pokemon in a clash that left both badly hurt. Corphish's fine performance and sheer persistence had finally carried Ash to a hard-fought victory.

May and the others worried that he might fall before the final tournament. Ethan was more confident. He knew Ash better than they did, and he was certain Ash would make the top thirty-two.

That certainty did not come from having watched the anime. Ethan could sense it in Ash himself: the makings of an excellent Trainer.

At the end of the first round, half of the 256 competitors were out. The remaining 128 were matched again within their respective groups for the second round.

Ethan's next opponent, also assigned to Arena F, was a Trainer named Vito.

At first the name meant nothing to Ethan. Then he saw the family accompanying Vito and heard Ash explain who they were. Vito belonged to the Winstrate family, whose string of victories had made them fairly well known in Hoenn.

The family's grandmother, father, mother, son, and daughter all loved Pokemon battles. They would challenge passing Trainers and prove so persistent that they would hardly let anyone leave without battling the whole family. Over time, their habit had earned them a measure of local fame.

Vito was the strongest of the five.

Ash had encountered the family during his travels, but Vito had not been home then. Ash had heard that he was away training for the Ever Grande Conference. Now Ethan had drawn him as an opponent. What a coincidence.

Ash's story stirred Ethan's memory. The Winstrates had appeared in the anime and in the games. To a player, though, the five were not especially strong. With a few extra levels, they were easy to defeat and good for experience points.

How would the strongest of them perform in this real world?

...

After a night's rest, Ethan arrived early at Arena F the next morning. His match was the first of the day, which finally gave Ash, Tyson, and Morrison the chance to watch him together.

With half the competitors gone, the day's schedule held half as many matches. The competitors' dormitories were growing quieter, while the stands grew fuller and the atmosphere more heated. Even for the morning's first match, the seats were packed.

Some spectators had never seen Ethan battle. Others had watched him the day before and come back early, drawn either by his appearance or by his strength. He was beginning to attract attention at the Ever Grande Conference.

To the crowd's cheers, Ethan and Vito entered the battlefield from opposite sides.

Vito was about twenty-four or twenty-five, with green hair tied in a ponytail. He was of average build and pleasant enough to look at. His manner seemed gentle, even a little hesitant, rather than forceful. Ethan would not underestimate a member of the Winstrate family on that account.

While Ethan studied Vito, Vito studied him. Though he had come to compete at Ever Grande, he was the odd one out in his family: battling did not interest him as much as other ways of living.

Ethan was plainly better-looking than he was, and Vito found himself taking to him. Compared with a heavily muscled Trainer who looked rough, a handsome man ought to be more civilized. Perhaps the battle would be gentler too...?

Cheers for both competitors rose from the stands. At the referee's signal, Ethan and Vito took out their Poke Balls. Blue light flashed as their Pokemon appeared.

Vito sent out Alakazam and Swellow. Ethan answered with Blaziken and Eevee.

Yesterday, Ethan had helped Metagross and Milotic adjust to the crowd. Today it was these two Pokemon's turn. His newer partners needed time in the arena, and even the older ones would rotate in to recover the feel of competition. He intended to give them all a chance.

The battle began, and both Trainers issued their commands.

Alakazam's Psychic type and Swellow's Flying and Normal types each posed a threat to Blaziken. Once again, Ethan's opening matchup was slightly unfavorable. Two such starts in a row might have frustrated another Trainer. Ethan barely gave it a thought.

If Vito relaxed because of his type advantage, even for a moment, he would soon be the one in trouble.

Swellow climbed high, searching for an opening. Alakazam floated cross-legged and raised both spoons toward Blaziken and Eevee.

Unlike Anthony the day before, Vito did not attack at once. He seemed poised to unleash a storm of attacks at the first mistake.

Ethan acted as if he had noticed nothing. At his order, Blaziken sent Flamethrower across the field, while Eevee ran around the flank toward Alakazam.

In the stands, Tyson and Morrison sat up almost together, holding their breath as they waited to see Ethan's strength. Ash watched just as closely. He wanted to see what these Pokemon could doand whether the gap between himself and Ethan had widened or narrowed.

May and Max had never watched Ethan battle in person either. May knew his strength mostly from Ash's stories, while Max had seen only a little of him in televised recordings. Now they could judge for themselves whether he was as formidable as they had heard.

For a moment, everyone, whether they cared about Ethan or not, focused on the battle.

Blaziken's flames reached Alakazam. It calmly lifted a spoon, forming an invisible barrier before it. The fire struck hard but could not break through.

Eevee raced in from the side. Vito and Swellow both saw it. Without waiting for an order, Swellow dived to intercept. Alakazam raised its other spoon and aimed it at Eevee.

Swellow's outstretched talons drew so close they seemed about to touch Eevee. At the same instant, Alakazam's psychic power swept toward it. One attack came from above, the other from the ground. The two Pokemon had caught Eevee between them.

Their teamwork needed no instruction from Vito. Compared with Anthony's pair yesterday, they were on another level. From experience, Vito could already picture Eevee falling to their combined assault.

Then Eevee turned sharply away from Swellow's dive. It burst forward with Quick Attack, slipping past Alakazam's invisible Confusion and slamming into the Psychic-type Pokemon.

Beautiful!

The announcer cried out without thinking, and the crowd erupted. Who would have expected such a reaction from an Eevee that looked so ordinary?

There was more. The impact broke Alakazam's concentration. Its barrier shattered, and the remaining flames of Blaziken's Flamethrower poured through and scorched it. One move from Eevee had reversed the exchange.

Tyson and Morrison each had their own thoughts, but both were astonished by Eevee. Its performance alone suggested that Ethan really was as capable as they had heard.

Ash exchanged a look with Pikachu. What Eevee had done looked simple: dodge, then strike. In truth, the timing had to be exact. A second too early or too late, and it would not have escaped Swellow, much less Alakazam's unseen psychic attack.

Ash had seen that kind of agility only in his own Pikachu, after three regions of hard travel. Eevee had been on the road for much less time. How had its reactions become so sharp already?

Chapter 766: Not Tempting Enough

One brilliant exchange could not decide a whole battle. Eevee had performed beautifully, and Blaziken had followed its lead, but Swellow and Alakazam still held type advantages over Blaziken. The fight had only begun. Vito did not let the setback trouble him.

What did need attention was Eevee's position. It had closed in on Alakazam, denying the Psychic-type Pokemon the safe distance it needed to attack. Most Psychic types had few effective options at close range unless they were among the rare ones skilled at physical combat. Alakazam needed space again.

For it, gaining that space took only a Teleport. At Vito's signal, Alakazam vanished and appeared on the far side of the field.

It had barely reappeared when another torrent of flame swept over it.

What?!

Everyone stared. The announcer blurted, Ethan predicted Alakazam's next move and had Blaziken attack in advance! But how did he know where it would appear?

It seemed almost impossible. The battlefield was an open rectangle, neither enormous nor small. Picking the exact place where Alakazam would reappear was unlikely enough; launching an attack there with such confidence was something few Trainers would dare. If Ethan had guessed wrong, he would have sent his flames into empty space and looked ridiculous.

The announcer and the crowd were astonished. The competitors watching from the stands imagined themselves in Vito's place and were just as amazed. This was one Trainer outplaying another.

Prediction itself was nothing miraculous. Any Trainer with experience had anticipated an opponent's move once or twice. But this was no cornered Pokemon with limited ways out. On an open field, Ethan had guessed both that Alakazam would Teleport and exactly where it would emerge. Then he had acted without a moment's hesitation. The certainty of his decision alone put him beyond most Trainers.

No one was more shocked than Vito. He had ordered Alakazam to Teleport at once, choosing its destination on the spur of the moment. He had only just made the decision himself. How could Ethan have known?

That was beyond merely impressive.

Alakazam cried out from inside the flames, snapping Vito back to the battle. He hurriedly called for Swellow to beat its wings and blow the fire out. As it did, Eevee closed in again and struck Alakazam with Swift.

Anyone could see that Ethan was concentrating on Alakazam. Swellow stayed high in the air, where it could evade most attacks; defeating the Pokemon closer to the ground first made sense.

Alakazam had barely escaped the flames when Swift hit it. Worse, the fire had burned it. Dark red marks covered its body, and it looked both hurt and miserable.

Vito regretted sending out Swellow. A different Pokemon on the ground might have screened Alakazam or shared the pressure, sparing it this string of attacks. Regret came too late. One more hit like that and Alakazam would be the first to fall.

He kept Swellow closer to Alakazam now, ordering it to guard its partner rather than range high and far. The change protected Alakazam for the moment, but it robbed Swellow of its mobility and handed Ethan the initiative.

Vito had little choice. The burn was hampering Alakazam's use of its psychic powers. He needed to buy time until it passed.

For some reason, Ethan did not press the attack. Vito finally had a chance to breathe.

In the stands, Ash and the others could not understand why Ethan was letting the opportunity go.

Why isn't he attacking? Ash frowned. That was a perfect chance. If he waits until Alakazam gets over the burn, won't all that work be wasted?

The others were puzzled too. Tyson nodded. He's missed the best moment. I'd keep up the pressure and knock Alakazam out in one go.

Did he fail to seize it? Morrison asked. Or didn't he react in time?

Misty trusted Ethan so completely that she assumed he had a reason. Of the others, only Brock had an inkling of what it might be.

He looked at Blaziken and Eevee, whose movements had grown more fluid as the match continued. Then he looked around at the cheering crowd. Perhaps Ethan was using the battle to settle his Pokemon into the atmosphere of the Conference.

No wonder he had won in two regions. He was thinking further ahead than most people.

Brock hesitated, then kept the thought to himself. This was something the younger Trainers needed to recognize on their own. If Ash, Tyson, and Morrison saw it, they might use these early, less intense matches to help their own Pokemon adjust. If they did not, perhaps they had not yet reached that point in their understanding.

They watched for some time without grasping Ethan's purpose. Brock shook his head. It was hardly a disaster; many Pokemon could perform wonderfully on this stage without such preparation. Still, Ethan's decision showed that he considered things other Trainers overlooked. Settling his Pokemon early would not make him champion by itself, but it could improve his results. It gave him a stronger foundation and a higher ceiling.

Once Blaziken and Eevee had grown comfortable with the Conference atmosphere and warmed up fully, Ethan decided it was time to end the match.

At his command, both Pokemon suddenly quickened their attacks. Vito was caught off guard.

From the stands, spectators had thought Ethan was missing chances to finish the fight. On the field, Vito had felt no such ease. He knew only how troublesome Eevee and Blaziken were, and how hard he had to work to hold them back.

You could not appreciate their strength until you faced them. Their speed, their reactions, and the power of their moves ranked among the best Vito had seen from Pokemon of their kinds. Holding them off had already taken everything he had. Now that they had changed pace, the pressure doubled.

Alakazam, only just recovering from its burn, broke first. Eevee struck it with Quick Attack and knocked it to the ground.

Swellow fared a little better in the air, but not for long. Blaziken leaped high and drove it down with Double Kick. Eevee was waiting on the ground and landed another blow. Swellow fell as its partner had.

The referee raised a colored flag to signal Ethan's victory.

Only then did the spectators fully realize that the match was over. Eevee's opening display had drawn cheers, but the middle of the battle had settled into a quiet stretch with little to excite them. Just when they expected the match to fade out after its strong start, it had ended in a sudden burst of action lasting little more than ten seconds.

The abrupt finish took them by surprise. Scattered applause began only after a pause, then spread through the arena.

Morrison and Tyson came away with a different opinion of Ethan. At first, both had thought him an exceptionally dangerous opponent. After watching him pass up so many chances, they judged him indecisive. That eased their worry. If that was truly his weakness, each felt confident he could beat Ethan when they met.

With his second-round win, Ethan needed only one more victory to reach the final tournament.

Since Morrison and Tyson had come to watch his match, Ethan returned the courtesy by watching one of Tyson's. Tyson revealed little, easily defeating his opponent with his hat-wearing Meowth and Sceptile.

The win earned Tyson more support from the crowd. He was presentable, strong, and, above all, a Trainer from Hoenn. That last fact alone won him favor. At a Hoenn tournament, many spectators naturally wanted a local competitor to become champion.
