Morrison's match ran at the same time as Ash's, so Ethan went to watch Ash instead. Perhaps because his previous match had been so difficult, Ash fought beyond his usual level and overwhelmed his opponent. Their impressive performances kept the spotlight from settling too firmly on Ethan.

That gave Gabby an opening.

After the day's matches ended, she slipped into the competitors' dormitories alone at eight that evening. She had already learned Ethan's room number. Finding the hallway empty, she hurried to his door and knocked.

Ethan was still awake, reviewing the day's match and considering what he needed to improve. He assumed the visitor was Misty. When he opened the door and saw Gabby instead, his brows rose, and he immediately grew wary.

Given a choice, he wanted nothing to do with these self-styled uncrowned kings of the press.

Gabby noticed that he was alone and smiled. Sorry to disturb you, Mr. Ethan. Is this a convenient time for an interview?

Perhaps to help her plan succeed, she had dressed carefully despite the late hour. Her makeup was immaculate, and she wore perfume that seemed to drift toward him whenever she moved.

Ty, the cameraman usually at her side, was nowhere to be seen. Ethan grew more suspicious.

Didn't I tell you I'd wait until I reached the final tournament? I still have another match tomorrow. You're early.

Gabby smiled wider. A little early, maybe, but I think it's worth it. Aren't you going to invite me in?

The implication was plain. Ethan finally understood and glanced down at her. Her outfit was daring: a low neckline revealed a glimpse of her chest, and a short skirt left her legs bare. She had come dressed to tempt him.

So that was her plan. Seduction?

Gabby took a step toward the room. Ethan stayed in the doorway and did not let her pass.

He was not blind to the invitation. He simply could not afford to be careless around reporters. A gift that fell into your lap might be a carefully laid trap.

Perhaps Gabby really meant to trade intimacy for an interview and a better position at work. But she might also be carrying a hidden camera, ready to record whatever happened next. If those images got out, his reputation could collapse. To keep them private, he might have to submit to her demands.

He could be wrong about her. Yet what if he was right? Reporters knew how to use such material, and some would even use their own looks to get it. Ethan would not take the risk, however small the chance.

Of course, the main reasonhe cleared his throatwas that Gabby simply was not tempting enough.

Ethan admitted he was hardly iron-willed when it came to women. What had happened with Maya, and his time with Erika, had shown him how easily he could be drawn in. But the temptation had to be strong enough.

Consider the women in his life: Sabrina, Erika, and Maya of the Whirl Islands. Every one of them was beautiful. They had standing, looks, strength, and status, and each was devoted to him.

Beside them, Gabby's appearance held no attraction for him. An ordinary man might find her beautiful, but Ethan felt no interest at all.

Chapter 767: An Unexpected Draw

Ethan did not want Gabby inside his room. But she had dressed for this visit and made up her mind. A few words at the door were not going to send her away.

They could hardly keep pushing back and forth in the hallway, either. Anyone who saw them might think he had called for some kind of private service. If a photograph got out, he would never be able to explain it.

Fortunately, Misty and May came down the hall at that moment, laughing together. They saw the two of them at the door.

Misty eyed the woman warily. Miss Gabby? What are you doing here?

Gabby knew Misty traveled with Ethan, but dismissed her as a girl too young to understand what was happening. She waved a hand and smiled. I just came to visit Mr. Ethan. Aren't you two asleep yet? Staying up late is a girl's worst enemy, you know.

She seemed to think that would send them away. Misty was not so easily fooled. As she drew closer, she caught Gabby's perfume and took in her clothes. Her intentions were plain.

Misty abandoned her plan to return to the girls' room. She took May by the hand and led her straight into Ethan's.

Gabby froze. Those two had gone inside? Then what was she supposed to do? Ethan had let them pass without a word, which made it even harder to believe.

She stared at him. Did he prefer little girls? Both of them at once? No wonder he had kept her out. Apparently a mature woman was not to his taste. What a strange appetite.

Inside, Misty released May's hand, went to the table, poured herself a glass of water, and drank it in one go. May sat stiffly on the bed, glancing around with curiosity and embarrassment.

She had never entered a man's room before. When she had come to Ethan for special training, she had stayed at the doorway. Now she was inside, sitting where he had clearly lain down, and her heart was beating faster.

So this was Ethan's room.

His clothes were neatly set out where he had taken them off. His belongings and a glass he had drunk from were close at hand. The room was clean and tidy, yet everything in it seemed to carry some trace of him.

Misty, by contrast, was as comfortable as if she were in her own room. She picked things up and used them without hesitation. May felt a little envious. It was not Misty's relationship with Ethan she envied; she simply wished she had an older brother she loved and could depend on. Instead, she had a younger brother who never listened to her.

Misty came over with a canned drink, handed it to May, and dropped onto the bed beside her.

You saw that, didn't you? she said with a snort. That reporter practically poured perfume over herself. She looked ready to throw herself at Ethan. There'll only be more people like her. We have to keep watch.

Even if you say that...

May forced a weak smile. If things were already like this, how was she supposed to prevent it in the future? Agreeing so impulsively that day might have been a mistake. It was too late to take it back now.

Bang.

The door shut heavily. Ethan joined them and shook his head. She's finally gone. Good thing you arrived when you did. I don't know how I would have got out of that otherwise.

Wouldn't you have liked it? Misty rolled her eyes. A beautiful woman comes to your door. Isn't that exactly what you want?

You little troublemaker! Ethan put an arm around her neck and rapped her on the head for teasing him.

May watched them tussle, a feeling she could not name rising in her chest. Would she and Ethan be like that one day?

...

On the third day of the preliminary tournament, Ethan faced his final qualifying opponent before noon. After two rounds, only sixty-four of the Ever Grande competitors remained. Empty beds filled the dormitories, and there were far fewer matches each day.

The weaker and less fortunate Trainers had been steadily eliminated. Those left behind were stronger. Ethan's opponent looked ordinary and was not someone he had encountered during his travels, but he was no weakling. Against someone else, he might well have advanced.

Unfortunately for him, he had drawn Ethan. He had drawn the strongest person in the field. Ethan had yet to make a dazzling show of himself, but at this point no other competitor was likely to get past him either.

Ash, Tyson, and Morrison all had matches at the same time, so Misty was once again the only one cheering Ethan on. Her voice alone could drown out the other supporters. She had no intention of losing on enthusiasm.

For this battle Ethan sent out Metagross and Eevee. Both had already competed, but they were among the less powerful members of his team and could use more practice. They had not fought together in his earlier matches, either. Ethan was curious to see how well this new pairing would work.

Their opponents were Sandslash and Farfetch'd. Sandslash's Ground type gave it an edge over the Steel-type Metagross, while Metagross resisted Farfetch'd's Flying-type moves. The overall matchup was difficult to call. Each pair's performance would decide it.

The opposing Trainer had clearly watched Ethan's previous two matches. Knowing Eevee and Metagross would be difficult to handle, he ordered an all-out attack from the start. That suited Ethan perfectly.

He had already helped Eevee and Metagross adjust to the stage, so he did not need to spend this match doing it again. He ordered them forward. All four Pokemon met in a head-on clash, and Ethan won.

It was a victory of raw strength. Their Trainers' orders mattered, but in close combat the Pokemon had to rely on their own reactions and condition. Eevee and Metagross, already settled into the tournament, surpassed Farfetch'd and Sandslash on both counts.

The crowd loved the change of pace. After Ethan's earlier matches, they had taken him for a Trainer who liked to draw battles out. Now they saw that he could attack fast and meet an opponent head-on.

His match ended quickly, while the others were still fighting. Ethan did not go to watch them. He took Misty straight to the main stadium. This had been the last preliminary round, and the Trainers who advanced would gather there for the next draw.

The winners arrived one after another. Ash, Tyson, and Morrison advanced as expected. By the time they reached the stadium, all thirty-two entrants in the final tournament were present.

Standing in the middle of the field, Ethan looked around. Six hundred Trainers had begun the Conference; now only thirty-two remained. The gathering space felt enormous. Many people he had met on his travels had left the stage disappointed.

Others had reason to celebrate. The remaining Trainers wore small smiles and waved to the spectators in the stands. Even the lowest finish among them would be a place in the top thirty-two. For most people, that was an honor they could accept with pride. Strength and luck had both been necessary to stand here out of six hundred entrants.

Now that the main tournament was about to begin, cameras filled the stadium. The sparse press presence from earlier rounds had given way to the full glare of the Ever Grande Conference. Flashbulbs went off so often that the draw looked like a press event. Even as the light stung their eyes, the competitors kept smiling and showed the cameras their best side.

Portraits began rolling across the big screen. Unlike the earlier rounds, the final tournament would use full six-on-six battles. Trainers would have room to use their complete teams rather than see their hopes ended by one bad exchange. They could fight freely and show the audience more of what they could do.

After a dozen seconds, the portraits stopped. Ash and Morrison quickly found their opponents. Then they saw the pairing for Ethan and Tyson and turned to them in surprise.

Ethan and Tyson would face each other in the round of thirty-two.

Ethan looked away from the screen, untroubled. Ash and the others knew he and Tyson had met only a few days ago, but even a passing acquaintance could make a hard-fought match feel uncomfortable. Both were strong, too. To Ash, Ethan was the best Trainer in the world; Tyson's performances had marked him as another contender for the championship. One of them would have to leave early.

That was a pity, but it was as far as the others' thoughts went.

Ethan knew more. In the anime's timeline, Tyson was the winner of this Ever Grande Conference. Ethan had not expected to meet him in the very first round of the final tournament. What an interesting draw.

He did not mind. An opponent was an opponent, whether they met now or later. The only thing he regretted was what the early pairing meant for Tyson. A Trainer who might otherwise have had the strength to reach the runner-up spot would now have his result fixed in the top thirty-two, missing a chance to make his name.

As for the possibility that Ethan might lose to him, the thought did not even occur to him.

If it happened, Ethan would hardly be the only one unable to accept it. The Legendary Pokemon he had beaten, and the opponents he had defeated in other regions, would be just as bewildered. By now, people who had lost to him wanted him to go further too. Losing to a champion seemed understandable and far less embarrassing.

Ethan glanced at Tyson among the competitors. Tyson looked back, his eyes bright with fighting spirit. Ethan answered with a small smile.

Come on, then. Show me what you can do.

...

After they left the stadium, Ash suggested celebrating their success, and everyone agreed. Ethan treated the group to a feast at a nearby restaurant.

Morrison heard there would be good food and shamelessly joined them. Ethan did not object. Morrison was Ash's friend, and that was reason enough to include him.

Tyson went to a restaurant on his own, perhaps wanting to keep some distance before tomorrow's match. Ethan did not press him. They hardly knew each other.

After the meal, Ethan finally agreed to speak with Alexa and Gabby at a nearby cafe. He had put the interviews off as long as he reasonably could. The world ran on relationships as well as Pokemon battles. Alexa had interviewed him twice already; he was not going to turn her down now.

As for Gabby, her attempt the night before had failed. Ethan worried she might resent him and write something spiteful, or try to charm her way in again, so he agreed to her interview too.

There was a further reason to choose her. Anyone willing to go so far for a promotion was fiercely ambitious. If Ethan could not make her a friend, he had no wish to make her an enemy. He was not afraid of trouble, but avoiding needless trouble was better.

More reporters would pursue him as he advanced. Since an interview was inevitable, he could let Gabby have the opportunity and make it known that she had his exclusive Hoenn interview. That would satisfy her and give him an answer for everyone else. One decision could solve both problems.

Chapter 768: You Have No Idea How Strong He Is

While Ethan was giving his interviews, Tyson was on the outdoor training ground at the other end of the competitors' dormitories. He was putting his hat-wearing Meowth and the rest of his team through their final practice before facing Ethan.

No matter how much he trained, one problem refused to go away: his Pokemon's condition.

They prepared thoroughly in private and practiced every day. Yet the moment they entered an arena, it was as if an invisible shackle fell over them. They could not use their full strength. Their jumps, runs, and moves became unsteady. More troubling was their state of mind. Tyson felt a little nervous himself, and that nervousness was enough to make his Pokemon's movements slightly awkward.

It was hard to avoid under the eyes of tens of thousands of spectators, with everyone's attention fixed on the battle. Perhaps they would need a few more matches to grow accustomed to it.

His thoughts returned to tomorrow's opponent. Tyson had watched only one of Ethan's matches, but Ethan's Pokemon had seemed untouched by that pressure. Ethan himself had looked composed, as though such crowds were nothing new to him. That puzzled Tyson and made him wary.

Even so, Ethan's commands had seemed indecisive. His Pokemon had performed well, but he had let chances to win slip by and dragged out a match he could have ended much earlier. Tomorrow might be difficult, Tyson thought, but he would win.

He turned his attention back to training. Before he could speak to his Meowth, it bristled, bared its claws, and stared toward the entrance.

Tyson looked around in alarm. Another Meowth stood beneath a tree, watching them. He recognized it at once: the Meowth that traveled with Team Rocket's trio.

Since meeting Ash, Tyson had encountered the trio several times. He had no reason to be friendly with people who so often did wrong. Their shared interest in Meowth had given them something to talk aboutbut really, it was the two Meowth that had anything in common.

Why was this one here? Before Tyson could ask, his own Meowth went over and said something to it.

Team Rocket's Meowth glanced at Tyson and the Meowth in the hat, then turned away, leaving them to look at its back.

I came to warn you, meow. Don't underestimate that man!

What do you mean? Tyson asked. Is he that strong?

Meowth did not turn around. It lifted its eyes to the night sky and spoke gravely. You can't even imagine how strong he is. Team Rocket is the strongest organization in the world, and even we couldn't beat him. And those Pokemon he hasn't shown yet? One look at any of them would make you shake. You can't stand against them!

Tyson was bewildered. Was Ethan really so powerful? Trembling at the mere sight of a Pokemon sounded absurd. Ethan was a man, not some spirit or god.

He understood that Meowth meant well, but dismissed the warning as an exaggeration. He was about to point out that he was strong too when, in the blink of an eye, Meowth vanished.

Tyson's words stuck in his throat. That strange departure made him take the warning a little more seriously. Could Ethan truly be as formidable as Meowth claimed? Tyson could see no sign of it. Still, caution cost nothing. He decided to raise Ethan one level in his estimate.

...

On the roof of an office building at the Ever Grande Conference, Pokemon League president Charles Goodshow stood with his hands behind his back and watched the night sky.

Footsteps approached. Without turning, he seemed to know who had come.

Beautiful night, isn't it?

It is. John, the live broadcast director, came to stand beside him with a half-smoked cigarette in his mouth. But I like the view ahead of us even more.

Goodshow lowered his gaze. The main stadium glowed in the distance, and beyond it the food stalls bustled beneath the lights.

After a long silence, he asked, You disagree with my decision too?

Only the League's senior officials knew what he meant. In the final tournament draw, they had used unusual means to target one competitor: Ethan.

He had won championships in Kanto and Johto and crossed the sea to pursue another in Hoenn. Goodshow had intervened to make that third title harder to win. The League had arranged for the strongest remaining entrants to face Ethan instead of eliminating one another in other matches. If one of them beat him early, they would avoid the embarrassment of one Trainer collecting every Conference title.

John blew out a ring of smoke and shook his head. I don't know. The investors and the board care about ratings. Give them those, and they won't mind who wins. The audience likes a star they can follow, too. And if Ethan really is strong enough to win again, putting more strong opponents in his path won't stop him. He'll beat them, reach the final, and take the title.

Goodshow was silent again. At last he sighed. Do you think I don't know that? But how can we leave it untested? One man taking every championship can't be healthy for the League. I can't watch it happen while I'm president.

Stubborn old man, John thought. He decided to try once more.

I see it differently. He dropped his cigarette and crushed it under his shoe. One Trainer winning every Conference wouldn't harm the League. It could give everyone a standard to aim for. A Grand Slam champion who stands apart from the field would inspire other Trainers to work harder and find ways to surpass him. The League wouldn't sink into decline because of him.

Goodshow was getting old and could be set in his ways, but he was not shortsighted. He had held the presidency for years. He had simply never faced a challenger as strong as Ethan, and now he could not tell which course would serve the League best.

John's argument affected him. Goodshow was not entirely convinced, but he had to admit it made sense. If events unfolded that way, the future might look very different.

After a third long silence, he shook his head. Perhaps. But we've already interfered with this draw. Let's see what happens. If Ethan defeats everyone we put in front of him and wins anyway, he'll have proved he's someone worth holding up as an example. Then we'll consider what you've said. For now, let's deal with the tournament before us.

...

Nine the next morning. The Ever Grande Conference's main stadium.

The final tournament had moved into the Conference's largest venue. Although this was only the opening round, all eighty thousand seats were filled. The smaller arenas' atmosphere could not compare. A single burst of applause from a crowd this size seemed to shake the earth. For the competitors, it was another challenge to their composure.

Ethan walked calmly from the competitors' passage into the cheers and faced Tyson across the field. One match had already been held here, warming up the crowd. Theirs was the second of the day.

They stood on a raised platform. A cover concealed the battlefield between them until it was time to begin.

As announced earlier, the final tournament used full six-on-six battles. Trainers could switch Pokemon during a match. A wheel would select one of four fieldsgrass, rock, water, or iceat random. After either side lost three Pokemon, there would be a brief break and a second field would be chosen for the rest of the battle.

The format was much like the Indigo and Silver Conferences Ethan had already competed in.

The announcer briefly introduced both Trainers, then called out, They're ready! Let's see which field they'll fight on in the first half!

A large wheel appeared on the stadium screen, marked with symbols for the four fields. It spun rapidly, slowed after a dozen seconds, and stopped with its pointer on a water drop.

The Water Field! Ethan and Tyson will battle on the Water Field for the first half!

Water. Ethan gave the choice some thought. Fewer of his Pokemon could fight comfortably there than on the other three fields. It limited his options somewhat. He was not worried. He trusted his team to win.

The cover in front of them opened. Gears turned beneath the platform, and a pool rose into view. A dozen or so rocks broke the surface of the water.

Under the eyes of the crowd, Ethan and Tyson each took out a first Poke Ball.

Before either released a Pokemon, Ash and the others began guessing in the stands.

Who do you think will win? Morrison asked.

Ethan, of course, Misty answered at once. I don't care how strong Tyson is. He won't beat Ethan.

Morrison dismissed her answer. He did not know she was a Trainer from a Gym family. To him, she was just a pretty girl traveling with Ethan, and her opinion carried little weight.

He turned to Ash, only to hear the same prediction.

I say Ethan too, Ash said. He's the strongest Trainer I've ever met. No one has ever beaten him in a six-on-six battle!

My pick is Ethan as well, Brock said with a smile. In fact, I don't think anyone here can beat him.

Come on. Morrison shook his head. Why does everyone choose him? Tyson has looked stronger so far. I think he'll win, though it won't be easy. It might come down to their last few Pokemon.

As they argued, the two Trainers made their opening choices. Tyson sent out Sceptile.

Ethan was mildly surprised. Tyson had given up the field advantage to start with a Grass-type starter. Then again, perhaps he expected Ethan to use a Water type and had chosen Sceptile to counter it. It was a clever predictionand a correct one.

Ethan opened his Poke Ball. Blue light flashed, and Blastoise appeared in the water.

Ash, Misty, and the others nodded knowingly. Blastoise? Then Ethan's got this.

Morrison was even more confused. Hold on. Yes, it's the Water Field, and Blastoise is a Water type, but Sceptile has the type advantage. Why are you so sure Blastoise will win?

Ash grinned. Because you have no idea how strong Ethan's Blastoise really is. Watch it fight, and you'll understand why we said that.

Huh?

Morrison could not imagine what kind of strength would make all of them disregard a type advantage and believe so firmly that Ethan would win.

Chapter 769: Another Sure Win?

True to its name, Sceptile might have been modeled on a lizard and a crested dinosaur. The Hoenn Grass-type starter was green across most of its body, with a broad tail like a mass of leaves and sharp, blade-like leaves growing from its wrists. The round seeds on its back held nutrients that could bring trees to life in an instant.

Pokemon researchers had observed Sceptile tending the trees in forests and basking in the sun to regulate its body temperature. It was especially capable in rainforests, where it could race through the jungle, leap between branches, and pounce on an enemy from above or behind, finishing the attack with the leaves on its arms.

It was a powerful species and a favorite of many new Trainers. No wonder Hoenn's Pokemon Professors recommended it as one of the region's starter Pokemon.

Ethan had faced Sceptile before, but Tyson's looked stronger than any he had encountered. He wanted to see what it could do against Blastoise.

Whatever happened, Ethan had great faith in the Blastoise he had caught near the start of his journey. It had not competed for a long time and faced a type disadvantage, but it was strong and had fought in two Conferences already. Ethan trusted it to win.

Once both Pokemon were ready, the referee gave the signal. The match that would decide which Trainer reached the top sixteen was underway. Their friends and the crowd were watching closely, and the Pokemon League had its own special interest in the result.

The referee's flag fell. At their Trainers' commands, both Pokemon moved at once.

Sceptile was a Grass type built for close combat. It bounded over several rocks and closed rapidly on Blastoise.

Tyson expected Blastoise to dive beneath the water to avoid that approach. Instead, it floated where it was and fired a Water-type attack. A powerful Hydro Pump burst from one of its cannons, aimed at the spot where Sceptile was about to land.

Tyson had traveled long enough to know how to fight a Water type, and Sceptile began to dodge without waiting for an order. It had scarcely moved when the Hydro Pump struck.

Huh?

Tyson stared. Blastoise's aim was unusually good. It had predicted the landing point of his swiftly moving Sceptile and hit it squarely.

Whether Ethan was as strong as Team Rocket's Meowth had claimed, Tyson could not yet say. His Pokemon's fundamentals, at least, were solid. Sceptile resisted Water-type moves, so the hit did limited damage. Even so, the force of the stream stopped its advance. Sceptile flipped in the air and landed on a rock below.

Tyson had been braced for a difficult match, so the surprise did not shake him for long. He ordered Sceptile forward again. Its type advantage meant little from a distance; with few ranged attacks to use here, it needed to get close. This time Tyson was prepared. Blastoise could not possibly catch Sceptile the same way again.

Sceptile sprang toward another rock. Blastoise fired Hydro Pump once more.

In midair, Sceptile changed tactics and used Double Team. Four images split away from it, evading the water and confusing its target.

Before Tyson could relax, Ethan said calmly, Blastoise, hit the one on the far left.

Tyson's heart jumped. He studied the images. Even he could not tell which one was the real Sceptile. Had Ethan worked it out? How could a person see through something the Pokemon could not?

Blastoise fired another Hydro Pump from its other cannon. The stream crossed the short distance in a heartbeat and struck the Sceptile on the far left, knocking it straight into the water.

What?! the announcer cried. Blastoise found the real Sceptile! How? Was that luck, or did Ethan see something the rest of us missed?

Ash and the others were stunned too. Morrison, who had doubted Ethan earlier, could not deny what he had seen. That's incredible. How did he tell? They all looked exactly the same! I couldn't have done that.

None of his companions could answer the question.

That's why I said no one here can beat Ethan, Ash said. He sighed, but a fire burned in his eyes as he clenched a fist. Everyone who faces him notices how strong his Pokemon are. Hardly anyone realizes that Ethan himself is the hardest part of facing him.

Brock nodded. It's Ethan's mind and his commands that make his Pokemon seem so unbeatable.

Listening to them, Morrison studied Ethan again. The man seemed more complex, and more mysterious, than he had a few minutes earlier.

May was even more affected. Before she learned much about battles, Ethan's two Conference titles had told her he was strong, but she had never known what that strength meant. After becoming a Coordinator and competing in the Grand Festival, she could appreciate it. This handsome man with the gentle smile was far stronger than even Robert, the Grand Festival champion.

The battle continued. Sceptile had fallen into the pool with its Double Team broken. Ethan gave it no chance to climb out. Blastoise dived and swam after it.

The mood in the stadium tightened. Even spectators who rarely watched battles knew the danger of a land Pokemon trapped in the water with a Water type. Some of the more timid ones closed their eyes.

Underwater cameras showed Blastoise as a massive shadow. Despite its size, it was closing on Sceptile at remarkable speed. Sceptile flailed briefly, righted itself, and swam toward the nearest rock. It could not match Blastoise in the water. Within moments, its pursuer was behind it.

Sceptile! Behind you! Tyson shouted.

Sceptile saw the rock almost within reach. It felt the surge of water at its back and had time only to turn before Blastoise's round head slammed into it.

Bang!

Blastoise drove Sceptile toward the bottom of the pool. Sceptile was not a Water type, but it did not fear water. It had taken a breath before going under. Instead of rushing to the surface, it raised both arms and watched carefully for the next attack.

What came was no ordinary strike. A huge shell spun toward it, sending ripples through the water.

Sceptile might have blocked another Pokemon with its leaf-bladed arms. How was it supposed to stop a spinning shell? Even touching it looked painful. The water kept Tyson's commands from reaching it, so it had to respond on its own. There was no time to escape.

Sceptile released a stream of bubbles, adjusted its angle, and crossed its arms. It used X-Scissor against the oncoming shell. Two slashes cut through the water and struck it, but had no effect.

Before Sceptile could try another move, the shell hit it full on.

Tyson waited anxiously for Sceptile to surface. With his Pokemon underwater, he could follow the fight only on the big screen, like the crowd. Seeing Blastoise use Withdraw and drive its shell into Sceptile again made his heart sink.

He looked across the field. Ethan's expression had not changed. He showed no pleasure at gaining the advantage. That composure made him especially difficult to face. Tyson would get no opening from overconfidence or carelessness.

At least Sceptile was still standing. It used the impact to push itself up and out of the water, landing back on a rock. But it was covered in injuries, and much of its strength was gone.

It had not touched Blastoise once. If Tyson changed nothing, defeat was almost certain. He was not too stubborn to act, nor too concerned about looking weak before the crowd. He raised his Poke Ball and recalled Sceptile.

Cheers broke out in the stands. Misty's voice was the loudest. Though she was far away, Ethan thought he could hear her.

Strength earned respect. There had been no knockout, but Tyson's decision to switch first showed that he had lost the opening exchange. Some spectators wished the round had lasted longer; most were pleased with what they had seen.

In the main grandstand, Goodshow sighed as he watched Tyson retreat. It could be a tactical adjustment, nothing more. Still, he sensed a pattern he did not like. Was this heading toward the very outcome he feared?

Amid the spectators' different reactions, Tyson sent out his second Pokemon. Blue light flashed, and Metagross appeared on one of the rocks.

Ethan raised his brows. They shared a Pokemon species. He had not intended to use his own Metagross today; otherwise, he could have watched two of them face each other.

He recalled Blastoise and took out his second Poke Ball. Dragonite appeared in the sky.

In the stands, Ash nodded again. Dragonite. Ethan's got this round too.

That Dragonite really is strong, Brock agreed.

Morrison glanced at them. Why did they declare Ethan the winner no matter which Pokemon he sent out? Did they think so little of Tyson? Or did they honestly believe every Pokemon Ethan owned was that powerful?

Raising a whole team to ace level took more than training. It required countless real battles. Most Trainers poured all their effort into one or two aces, a few solid mainstays, and a handful of weaker Pokemon. That was the best ninety-nine percent of them could hope to achieve.

Blastoise had looked like an ace. If Dragonite was just as strong, Ethan had shown his best cards in the first two exchanges. What would he do later? Tyson's strongest Pokemon was his Meowth. If Tyson kept that ace fresh until Ethan's best were exhausted, how would Ethan answer?

Ash and the others seemed entirely unconcerned. Morrison grew more confused. Had they missed the problem, or was he overthinking it? Did Ethan have more Pokemon he had not seen?

As he wondered, the second exchange began and drew his attention back to the field.

Chapter 770: A Burning Fist Just for You

Dragonite flew above the pool while Metagross hovered over a rock. Despite fighting on the Water Field, neither Trainer had chosen a Water-type Pokemon. That was unusual in a match this important. Most competitors seized every advantage the field offered.

Tyson had not used a Water type from the start, so his choice was less surprising. Ethan, though, had just watched his uninjured Blastoise perform brilliantly on this very field. Why switch it out?

Only Ash and the others who had known Ethan since Kanto recognized the habit. Unless he had a particular reason to do otherwise, Ethan changed Pokemon after each battle.

There were benefits and costs. Rotating gave every member of his team practical experience. It also exposed his lineup early, robbing him of the element of surprise. A Trainer needed immense confidence in his Pokemon to fight that way, and Ethan had always been such a Trainer.

Metagross and Dragonite were already exchanging attacks. Like Blastoise before it, Metagross opened from a distance. It used Confusion, trying to defeat Dragonite before it could cross the field.

Dragonite was no Sceptile. It had an answer. Calmly, it used Twister. Wind and water rose together, forming a waterspout in the middle of the pool. Hidden from Metagross behind the churning column, Dragonite plunged into the water.

Only then did many spectators remember that Dragonite loved water. It often lived beside it. Even its earlier forms, Dratini and Dragonair, spent much of each day in it. Dragonite could fly above the field and swim beneath it. Apart from lacking pure Water-type attacks such as Water Gun and Hydro Pump, it could use this arena almost like a Water Pokemon.

The crowd's oversight was understandable. Dragonite was rare, and its earlier forms rarer still. Most people knew the species only from videos or glimpses of other tournaments. Experienced Trainers such as Tyson and Ash had faced Dragonite during their travels and knew more about how it fought.

With Dragonite out of sight, Tyson would not send Metagross into the pool after it. He ordered Metagross higher, away from the waterspout and the surface, guarding against an attack from below.

But Dragonite did not come from below. It burst straight out of the waterspout, both fists burning, and closed on Metagross in the blink of an eye.

Tyson and Metagross had fixed their attention on the water. Neither expected Dragonite to emerge from the spinning column. Now its speed decided the exchange. The dozen or so meters between them vanished. Droplets from the waterspout spattered Metagross's body; it barely had time to move its eyes before a flaming fist struck.

Bang!

Fire was strong against Steel. With Dragonite's momentum behind it, Fire Punch dealt a heavy blow. Flames streamed beyond Metagross and burned for a moment in the air behind it.

The crowd gasped. The sight of Dragonite bursting through the water with a burning fist aimed straight at its opponent was hard to ignore. Dragonite could use moves of many types, even if it did not specialize in all of them. That versatility had put a close-range Fire-type moveFire Punchat its disposal.

Metagross's body glowed red from the heat. It lost its balance and slammed into a rock.

After a stunned pause, the announcer found his voice. What a creative attack! We thought Ethan used Twister to block Metagross's Confusion. Instead, Dragonite hid inside the waterspout and struck from the last direction Tyson expected!

In the stands, Morrison swallowed. He had not expected that either. Dragonite might have made the Twister itself, but entering it after it formed would still hurt. What sort of madman planned an attack like that?

Ash, on the other hand, hardly looked surprised. Morrison's understanding of Ethan shifted again. Ethan did not fight by fixed rules. Two exchanges into the match, Morrison had gone from favoring Tyson to doubting his own prediction.

Tyson had more than surprise to contend with. He gave a wry smile. Now he understood Team Rocket's Meowth a little better. He had raised his guard, but he had still underestimated Ethan.

From the opposite side of the field, Ethan's strength and the strength of his Pokemon were impossible to miss. Their defense offered no opening, and Ethan's unexpected attacks left Tyson little room to answer. He had never felt so thoroughly outmatched. Where had Ethan trained Pokemon that could both attack and defend this well? How did he command them so precisely?

The ease Tyson usually felt against other Trainers had vanished. Facing Ethan, he felt inexperienced, almost like a beginner. For a moment, he had the absurd impression that he had already lost, though they had barely begun.

He drew a deep breath and forced himself to settle down. An unusually bad start had made him nervous, and that was magnifying the pressure. Ethan was the strongest Trainer Tyson had met on his journey, but Tyson was strong too. He had beaten plenty of opponents. His most trusted Pokemon had not even taken the field yet. There was still a way back.

Besides, like Morrison, Tyson could not believe every Pokemon Ethan brought would be this strong. Even the Elite Four could not guarantee that all their Pokemon were trained to the same exceptional level. Surely an ordinary Trainer could not.

Metagross rose from the broken rock. Fire Punch had hurt it, but it still had plenty of strength. Better yet, the blow had not burned it. Tyson's eyes hardened. This battle had only just begun. All six of his Pokemon were still available. He would give everything he had, as if this were the final.

Across the field, Ethan knew nothing of Tyson's thoughts. But he saw the change. Tyson had been serious before; now his gaze was sharper and his bearing stronger. Dragonite's punch seemed to have shaken him fully awake. Perhaps he understood the danger and meant to fight at a hundred and twenty percent.

Ethan merely smiled.

Tyson pressed the attack. Under his commands, Metagross struck back fiercely and gave Dragonite real trouble. Dragonite answered in kind. They fought in the air, crashed among the rocks, and rose from the shattered stone to clash overhead again. Both took injuries, and the audience loved every moment.

This was what a main-tournament battle ought to look like. Yet it seemed almost too good for a round-of-thirty-two match. It felt more like a final. Other competitors watched open-mouthed, impressedand relieved that they had not drawn either of these two.

The broadcast ratings climbed as the fight went on. John, the live director, ought to have been delighted. Instead, worry outweighed his satisfaction. He looked toward the small old man standing with his hands behind his back on a distant platform.

If the first round already offered a match of this quality, what would Goodshow do later? Suppose Ethan won and then faced opponents weaker than Tyson in successive rounds. Would the declining competition turn viewers and the press against the tournament? John sighed. The old president had led the League to its peak and possessed far more strength than his appearance suggested. John hoped he truly had a plan.

On the field, the battle raged on. Its shock waves churned the pool. Fortunately, both Pokemon could fight above the water. Had they needed the rocks underfoot, the footing across the Water Field might have collapsed. Even so, water surged out of the pool, changing the field's appearance.

The two Pokemon looked evenly matched, but the balance could change in an instant.

Tyson let his guard slip for a moment. Ethan seized it. At his command, Dragonite grabbed Metagross and dragged it beneath the water.

There, Metagross could barely resist. Its psychic power seemed useless underwater. Though it could normally hover, its dense, heavy body could not lift itself back to the surface.

Dragonite was at ease. It released Metagross, swam around behind it, and delivered a point-blank Thunder Punch. Metagross went limp.

The underwater cameras showed the exchange, but the water made it hard for spectators to tell whether Metagross was truly finished. They got their answer when Dragonite burst through the surface and tossed the unconscious Pokemon out of the battlefield.

The stadium erupted. The referee raised a colored flag and called, Metagross is unable to battle! Dragonite wins this round!

Moments earlier, the Pokemon had seemed to be trading blows evenly. No one had expected the result to come so suddenly. After their surprise, the spectators gave them thunderous applause.

Tyson could only shake his head. He had done everything he could. After a poor start, Metagross had fought back and appeared to match Dragonite. It was the best Tyson had seen it perform since he caught it.

Even that had not been enough. With Metagross underwater at the end, the pool had kept Tyson from recalling it; he could only watch it fall. Worse, looking closely now, he saw that Dragonite bore few marks. Their apparent equality had been his own wishful thinking.

It was almost unbelievable.

Chapter 771: A Confident Man Indeed

Tyson recalled his unconscious Metagross and considered his next choice. He was reaching for a Poke Ball when Ethan recalled Dragonite too.

Huh? Ethan was switching again?

For the second time in this match, Ethan had withdrawn a Pokemon while he held the advantage. Tyson did not know why, but after a moment's hesitation he returned the ball in his hand to his belt and chose another.

His first choice had been his best answer to Dragonite among the Pokemon he had brought. With Dragonite gone, there was no point planning around it. He had to prepare for an unknown opponent instead.

At the referee's signal, they released their Pokemon together. Two flashes of blue light revealed the teams for the third exchange: Ethan's Scizor and Tyson's Shiftry.

Ash and his friends knew Scizor well. They gave it a glance, then turned their attention to Shiftry.

Most of its body was brown. A long, thick white mane hid much of its face. It had pointed ears, a narrow nose, a wide mouth with tightly set teeth, and cloudy yellow eyes. It looked rather like a little old man with long white hair and wooden sandals.

Ash took out his Pokedex and aimed it at the unfamiliar Pokemon. Misty, May, and the others leaned in to hear.

Shiftry, the Wicked Pokemon. Grass and Dark type. A mysterious Pokemon said to live quietly deep in forests undisturbed by outsiders. One legend claims it was once a bird Pokemon whose beak and wings were taken away as divine punishment for wrongdoing. It can read an opponent's thoughts and move first. Said to appear on cold winds, it has long been feared as a guardian of the forest.

Before Ash put the Pokedex away, Morrison asked cautiously, You're not going to tell me Ethan's certain to win this one too, are you?

To Morrison's surprise, Ash shook his head. I don't know. Ethan's Scizor is strong, but that description makes Shiftry sound strong too. I can't say which one will win.

A Pokemon said to have received divine punishment certainly sounded mysterious and dangerous. The others nodded. Then Misty snorted.

Ethan's Pokemon will win, of course.

Everyone turned to her. No one in the stadium believed in Ethan more unconditionally than Misty did. She ignored their looks and lifted her chin.

If one of the Pokemon he's caught recently lost, I'd believe it. But a partner that's traveled with him for so long? I don't believe that.

Her argument sounded reasonable enough that everyone looked back at Ash. He reddened. On the rare occasion he offered an opinion, Misty had contradicted him in front of them all. She had given him no room to save face. Then again, this was Misty.

Still, with Morrison watching, Ash wanted to stand his ground. Scizor isn't one of Ethan's very first Pokemon. It can't be as strong as Blastoise. I think Shiftry has a better chance in this round.

Brock rubbed his chin. He wanted to back Ash up, if only to help him win an argument with Misty for once, but he could not. Scizor is Bug and Steel. Shiftry is Grass and Dark. Bug-type moves will hit Shiftry for four times the usual damage, while Shiftry's attacks face resistance. This matchup is rough for Shiftry.

Huh? Ash's face changed. He had forgotten about type matchups. He usually charged straight into battle without worrying much about them, and he had made the same mistake while judging this fight.

Well... I mean... He searched for another reason to favor Shiftry, but Ethan rarely lost even with a disadvantage, let alone an advantage like this. Across from him, Morrison waggled his eyebrows. Ash could hardly retreat now.

May sighed at the little spectacle unfolding beside her. Early in her travels, she had struggled with this sort of bickering. These days she could tune it out. She and Max turned back to the field.

The third exchange had begun. Ethan's strength was clear to the spectators, but Tyson's earlier performance had impressed them too. Even if Tyson was weaker, they expected him to force Ethan to fight hard. Perhaps this round would be as close as the last until a sudden decisive moment.

They were wrong.

Ethan gave them a lesson in how thoroughly a type advantage could decide a battle.

Shiftry lived up to both its name and its Wicked Pokemon classification. It fought with tricks and feints, making constant small movements to mislead Scizor. Even without Tyson's commands, it tried one deception after another.

Ethan saw through most of them. Scizor followed his orders without wavering, ignoring even openings that looked easy to exploit. Its stubborn discipline robbed Shiftry's tricks of their effect. If Scizor refused every bait, what could Shiftry do?

A few close-range tricks escaped Ethan's notice. They happened too quickly, too subtly, or outside his line of sight. Yet even when they worked, they did little damage against Scizor's steel body.

Under Scizor's attacks, Shiftry fled from one cluster of rocks to another across the pool. The crowd was startled. Tyson looked nothing like the Trainer who had fought Dragonite so fiercely. Only Tyson knew how little room he had to act.

Blastoise and Dragonite had been difficult enough. Scizor was worsenot necessarily because it was stronger than they were, but because Shiftry could not get through its defense. The type matchup had left Tyson with no answer. Like Ethan in the first two exchanges, he had gambled on a pairing and lost.

I should have kept the first Poke Ball I chose, he thought.

With his team already reduced, another switch hardly seemed practical. If he exposed yet another Pokemon and it still could not beat Scizor, he would gain nothing. At the very least, Shiftry needed to take Scizor down with it.

Tyson glanced at the pool and made his decision. He abandoned his evasive approach and ordered Shiftry to close in, hoping to knock Scizor into the water. If that worked, Scizor's weight might trap it in the pool as Metagross had been trapped. Even if Shiftry fainted too, Tyson could accept the trade.

It was the only plan he could see. He had to try.

Ethan quickly recognized the change. It could reverse the battle if Tyson pulled it off, but Ethan was not about to give him that chance. As Shiftry approached, it would have to endure Scizor's attacks.

Shiftry tried several times. It never managed to knock Scizor into the pool and came close to being knocked out itself. Tyson's heart sank further. The idea had sounded much easier than it was.

He was about to tell Shiftry to be more careful when Scizor found an opening first. As they passed each other again, Scizor ignored Shiftry's attack and struck it squarely with X-Scissor. Shiftry flew into the water.

Splash.

It sank for a moment. When it surfaced, its eyes had rolled back and it lay motionless.

The referee raised a flag. Shiftry is unable to battle! Scizor wins!

The applause was subdued. Dragonite and Metagross had raised the crowd's hopes for another thrilling exchange. Instead they had watched a plain, one-sided victory. Many felt Tyson should have done better.

They had not stood where Tyson stood. They could not feel how helpless Ethan made him. He was like a mountain across Tyson's path. Tyson had prepared himself after the previous loss, but this battle flattened his spirits again.

Another defeat. This time he had barely fought back at all.

He wanted to blame the type disadvantage. Ethan, though, had won the first two exchanges despite unfavorable matchups. The excuse rang hollow. Tyson had simply been outmatched.

It was also true that most of Tyson's Pokemon fought best on land. The Water Field limited them. If only he could change it now. But the field would not change until either side had lost three Pokemon. Beating three of Ethan's Pokemon looked extraordinarily difficult, and Tyson could not bear the thought of losing one more of his own.

After recalling Shiftry, he sent Sceptile out again. It was the only Pokemon he could use to search for an opening.

He watched Ethan withdraw Scizor and reach for yet another Poke Ball. His heart rose into his throat. Blastoise was the opponent he least wanted to see again. When a different Pokemon appeared in the blue light, he exhaledthen tensed once more.

He had not known much about Ethan before this match, but he understood one thing now: this man had tremendous confidence in himself. What other Trainer would recall a Pokemon after an easy win, then send out a new one without regard for the opponent's type?

Now Sceptile was standing on the field, and Ethan had chosen Jolteon.

Anyone with even a little battle knowledge knew that Grass types resisted Electric-type attacks. Jolteon's moves would do only half their usual damage. Tyson could not see a reason to choose it over other Pokemon except Ethan's confidence.

Perhaps Sceptile's body would still be wet from its earlier fall into the pool, allowing an Electric attack to produce an unexpected effect. But Ethan did not look as though he was relying on that. He had made his choice regardless of whether Tyson sent Sceptile back into the water.

Chapter 772: A Killer Move

Jolteon and Sceptile began their battle.

As Tyson had suspected, Ethan had not chosen Jolteon for some special strategy. He looked as though he had reached into his belt pouch at random and sent out whichever Pokemon's ball his hand found, regardless of whether it suited the matchup. Even he could not predict his next choice, much less anyone else.

Almost no other Trainer at the Ever Grande Conference would dare fight that way. Random choice could hand an opponent a type advantage and make a difficult battle worse. Ethan's willingness to do it showed how little he feared such disadvantages. He trusted his Pokemon's strength.

In the main grandstand, Goodshow watched helplessly. He had arranged for Ethan to face one of the strongest performers from the preliminary tournament, yet Tyson could not even make Ethan take the matchup seriously. The round of thirty-two was unlikely to stop him. Goodshow could only hope Tyson forced Ethan to reveal more of his team so later opponents would know what to expect and perhaps find a weakness.

On the field, Sceptile went straight on the offensive. It had already fought through half a match and was warmed up; the rest had restored much of its energy.

Jolteon, however, had been with Ethan since early in his travels and had distinguished itself at both the Indigo and Silver Conferences. In strength, composure, and experience, it surpassed Sceptile. A few leaps across the rocks were enough to find its rhythm. After several probing attacks, it took the advantage.

It needed no Electric-type moves. Its Normal-type attacks could trouble Sceptile, and Pin Missile gave it a Bug-type move that struck Grass types hard.

Its speed was Tyson's greatest problem. Sceptile's powerful legs let it cross the rocks easily, but Jolteon was quicker and lighter. Four paws gave it surer footing, and Sceptile could rarely catch up.

The two Pokemon darted back and forth across the Water Field, first ahead, then behind, then left and right. They touched down on almost every cluster of rocks. To the naked eye, they were little more than passing shadows; the audience needed the screen's slow-motion replays to follow them.

That could not last. Their attacks cracked the rocks and sent pieces sinking into the pool. As their room to move shrank, the battle grew more intense. At last, both Pokemon were forced into a direct exchange on a single flat rockthe only foothold left.

Now that they could no longer run, the audience could finally see Sceptile's desperate struggle. Jolteon was superior in too many ways. However much rest Sceptile had received, it was being driven to the brink.

Tyson gripped a Poke Ball. He thought for two seconds, then decided not to recall Sceptile. That instant of distraction was enough for the battle to reach its end.

Jolteon fired Pin Missile. Sceptile, covered in injuries, had nowhere to dodge the dense swarm of sharp needles. It tried to answer with Leaf Storm, but Pin Missile came first. The needles were short-ranged, yet they launched with such speed that Sceptile was struck again and again before the storm of leaves could fully form.

Sceptile gritted its teeth and tried to hold on. Jolteon's shape flashed before it. By the time Sceptile lifted its head, Jolteon was already lunging with Quick Attack.

The hit caught Sceptile squarely. It fell and lost consciousness.

Sceptile is unable to battle! Jolteon wins! the referee announced.

Applause came from the stands, though it was not especially enthusiastic. After Metagross and Dragonite's brief, thrilling contest, Tyson's later Pokemon had spent most of their time under pressure. The crowd could see the gap between him and Ethan. It was also clear that his team had not been comfortable on the Water Field.

With Tyson's third Pokemon defeated, at least the field would change. Perhaps he would fare better on new ground.

Ethan did not look at Tyson's expression. He recalled Jolteon, left his command position, and went to the nearby rest room. Under the final tournament rules, the fall of a third Pokemon on either side brought a brief intermission. Spectators could visit the facilities; Trainers could rest and plan their next moves.

For Ethan, there was little to plan. Facing Tyson had been no more difficult than facing Harrison in Johto. Tyson's performance in these rounds had even fallen short of Harrison's.

Of course, Ethan had used longtime partners. Milotic and Metagross, which he had caught more recently, would have had a harder time. But they had fought in the preliminaries, and his rotation now favored the older members of the team. Tyson had been unlucky to meet him in this round. If they had met one round later, Ethan might have needed to work much harder.

Tyson still had his formidable Meowth. Ethan hoped it would give him a better surprise.

Elsewhere in the stands, Team Rocket's Meowth stopped in the middle of selling rice crackers and drinks. The trio were in disguise, and it looked toward Tyson's side of the battlefield.

Jessie noticed first. What's wrong, Meowth? Don't just stand there. This is our chance to make a fortune! Get moving!

I know, meow. Meowth looked at Tyson once more, shook its head, and followed Jessie away. They were the same species and had lived somewhat similar lives. It had said what it could the night before. Against that man, warnings would do little good.

While the Trainers took their break, the roulette wheel appeared on the stadium screen again. The Water Field symbol was gone, leaving rock, grass, and ice. The pointer spun, slowed, and came to rest on grass.

Tyson breathed more easily. The Water Field had kept his Pokemon from fighting at their best. Now they could finally move freely.

The intermission passed quickly. At the referee's signal, the Trainers returned to their positions with new Poke Balls. The entire Water Field descended. Gears rumbled, and a Grass Field rose in its place, covered with thick grass, small hills, and several trees.

Tyson was more urgent than before. He released his Pokemon as soon as the field locked into place. Blue light flashed, and Donphan appeared.

Ethan could see Tyson's determination to recover from his losses. Three of his Pokemon were down without a single knockout in return. Ethan would have been anxious in his place too.

He smiled and threw his own Poke Ball. A roar shook the field before the crowd saw what had emerged.

Ethan has sent out Tyranitar! the announcer called. Good news for Tyson! Donphan's Ground type has an advantage against the Rock-type Tyranitar. This could be his chance to pull a round back!

Tyson heard him. He disliked the suggestion that only a favorable type matchup gave him a chance, but the announcer was right about one thing: this was an opportunity. Donphan had the type advantage, and the open Grass Field suited it. Tyson could not imagine losing this exchange.

His smile disappeared a moment later.

Both Pokemon reached their starting positions, but before the referee could begin, Donphan looked into Tyranitar's cold eyes. The force of its presence made Donphan step back in fear.

What?! Tyson frowned. The announcer cried out too. An unexpected development! Tyranitar's sheer presence has frightened Donphan. What will that mean for this battle?

After Ethan's gigantic red Gyarados and Crystal Steelix, Tyranitar was his third ferocious-looking Pokemon. It had not yet reached the heights of those two, but an ordinary Pokemon could still be shaken by it. It needed no Intimidate Ability. Its fierce face and gaze were enough to inspire fear.

Donphan, stay calm! Don't let it scare you!

Tyson had to encourage his Pokemon before the fight even started. Fortunately, Donphan's long travels had given it some nerve. The sight had merely caught it off guard, and Tyson's voice helped it recover.

Better now than in the middle of the match. Ethan would surely have attacked if Donphan had faltered then. Tyson took what comfort he could, though the incident left a shadow over his hopes.

Once both Pokemon were ready again, the referee raised the flag to begin the first exchange of the second half.

Donphan, Sandstorm! Tyson ordered.

Yellow sand rolled across more than half the field. Ethan lost sight of Tyranitar inside it. So did the audience, the referee, and even the cameras.

From the other side, Tyson gave his next command. Donphan, use Rollout!

This was clearly a combination he trusted. Sandstorm cut off the opposing Trainer's view and made effective orders difficult. Donphan could then roll through the obscured field and crash into its target before the other side knew where the attack was coming from. Against many Trainers, it might work.

Yet Sandstorm was a Rock-type move, and Tyranitar was part Rock type. The blowing sand also hid the battle from Tyson. If Rollout failed, he would not know what was happening inside his own cover.

Most of all, Tyranitar could keep fighting and tearing apart whatever stood before it without Ethan's guidance. With its towering body and heavy armor, how much damage could a rolling Donphan really do? Tyson had considered that risk, but his order was given. He could only trust his Pokemon now.

Donphan curled into a wheel and charged into the sandstorm like a runaway tire.

Chapter 773: At Least One Knockout

As soon as Donphan rolled into the sandstorm, the crowd lost sight of both Pokemon. Even the cameras showed nothing but dense yellow sand. The wind howled, and the storm showed no sign of fading.

Under that noise, people could hear Donphan rolling and feel the ground shake. They had to imagine what was happening inside.

Tyson knew how this combination usually worked. Donphan ought to be striking Tyranitar about now. A tremendous crash rang out, like two trucks colliding, followed by Tyranitar's roar. The Pokemon had met.

It worked! Tyson felt a flash of relief. Then the sound of rolling stopped.

Why had Donphan stopped? Why could he hear only Tyranitar?

Before he could work it out, Tyranitar roared again. Something heavy slammed against the ground, then took blow after blow. A faint cry of pain reached Tyson through the wind. It sounded like Donphan.

He stared into the sand, but could see nothing. From his raised command platform, he could look over the storm toward Ethan. Ethan stood calmly with one hand in his pocket. He showed none of the panic a Trainer might feel at losing sight of his Pokemon and the ability to command it. He seemed unconcerned about the battle hidden in the sand.

Either Ethan had faced such a situation before or he trusted Tyranitar to win without his help. In either case, Tyson's tried-and-tested combination had failed.

The sandstorm would not stop just because he wanted it to. It had to run its course. Until then, Tyson was the one left worrying about what he could not see. What if Donphan fell first? He would have trapped his own Pokemon.

Donphan, get out of there! he shouted.

He needed Donphan back in sight so he could assess the damage and give a useful order. Abandoning the sandstorm and the surprise attack was worth that. But no Donphan emerged. Tyranitar's roars only sounded more frightening.

Something had gone wrong insideperhaps from the very start. Tyson could not even recall Donphan, since he could neither see nor locate it through the sand.

Fortunately, the storm did not last much longer. The sand began to settle, and visibility slowly returned. A tall figure stood at its center, chest rising and falling. A smaller shape lay motionless before it.

Had the battle already been decided? So quickly? Everyone watched without blinking until the last of the sand cleared.

The standing Pokemon was Tyranitar. Its eyes were red, as though it had only just emerged from a wild, confused state. Donphan lay unfolded on its back, soft belly exposed in a deep pit. Marks of tremendous force scarred both its body and the ground around it.

The announcer stared, then cried, Tyranitar must have used Superpower to stop Donphan's Rollout, then hit it with Thrash! Those cries we heard were Donphan's!

Anyone who understood battles could see how Donphan had lost. It was still hard to believe such a sturdy Pokemon had been beaten so thoroughly, so fast.

Experienced Trainers felt sorry for Tyson. Donphan had borne the full force of Thrash, a powerful Normal-type move that sent its user into a frenzy of destruction. Living things and objects alike could be smashed in its path. The sandstorm had kept Tyranitar's attention fixed on the one opponent directly before it. Donphan had taken every blow.

In effect, Tyson had delivered Donphan to Tyranitar himself. Without the sandstorm, Donphan could probably have dodged a wild attack like that. A Pokemon using Thrash was hardly going to pursue it with perfect judgment.

Tyson knew that too, and his face darkened. It was not that he had never considered the risk. He had not expected Tyranitar to choose Thrash without a Trainer's command. Most Pokemon, unable to see in a sandstorm, would at least guard themselves. If Tyranitar had misjudged the moment and missed Donphan, the resulting confusion could have left it helpless before a counterattack.

Tyranitar had taken that chance. Its attack had also been strong enough to knock out Donphan, a Pokemon with excellent defense and stamina. Tyson had lost without seeing the battle, while Ethan had won without giving a single order.

Only now did Tyson clearly feel how far apart they were. He had seen and heard warnings before, but being forced this far made the difference impossible to dismiss. He had never battled an Elite Four member, only watched recordings. Yet a thought rose unbidden: perhaps even the Elite Four were no more formidable than this man.

Tyson startled himself. Ethan was a tournament entrant, just as he was. How could he rival or surpass the Elite Four? Surely that could not be right.

He shook the thought away and looked at Donphan's exposed belly. Tyranitar's Superpower must have overturned it, leaving its soft underside open to Thrash. Bad luck, Tyson told himself.

What he failed to see was the risk built into his own tactic. Rollout inside Sandstorm could overwhelm a small Pokemon. Against a Rock-type powerhouse like Tyranitar, it was a poor gamble. Repeating it would likely have ended the same way.

Ethan was surprised too. Donphan had fallen so easily that it felt as if the fight had ended before it began. Then he realized that his own Pokemon might simply be that strong.

They had fought Legendary Pokemon and clashed repeatedly with Team Rocket, Team Aqua, and Team Magma. Each battle had helped them grow. Ordinary competitors no longer felt particularly threatening when Ethan returned to them.

That was one reason he often left his old partners in care when he entered a new region and caught new Pokemon there. If every Conference match was as easy as this one, the tournament would feel like a formality.

He could see why the League appointed some talented young Trainers as Gym Leaders or members of the Elite Four. They were too strong to find much challenge in a Conference, so the League gave them a role and standing instead.

Would someone from the League ask him to become an Elite Four member one day?

Ethan smiled at the thought and recalled Tyranitar. Tyson still stood across the field, lost in thought. Ethan took out a new Poke Ball and released his next Pokemon without waiting to see Tyson's choice. Venusaur appeared before him.

Tyson came back to himself and felt a sting of humiliation. He had lost, yet Ethan was the one to show his next Pokemon first. Was Ethan so sure he could win even after giving away that advantage?

Then Tyson gave a bitter smile. What did it matter? The previous exchanges had already shown him that Ethan was beyond him. Even if his last two Pokemon each won a round, he would still have to beat four more of Ethan's to take the match. Could he honestly imagine doing that?

His Ever Grande Conference journey would probably end here, in the first round of the final tournament. He had arrived full of hope, only to meet an opponent like this. He could not accept leaving without a single victory.

At least one. He had to beat at least one of Ethan's Pokemon so the result would not look quite so dreadful.

Tyson chose his most trusted and strongest partner: Meowth. It had performed well in the preliminaries, though those short matches had not left a strong impression on the crowd. Its hat, boots, and upright stance drew attention now.

Team Rocket's Meowth stopped selling rice crackers once more and fixed its eyes on the other Meowth. It no longer cared about making money. It wanted to see whether this fellow Pokemon, whose fate seemed so like its own, could help Tyson knock out even one of Ethan's partners.

Go on, meow.

Ethan studied the Meowth carefully. Ash had told him its story. It had lost a fight with a Persian for leadership of its group and been badly injured. Tyson found it by chance and nursed it back to health. The hat and boots had first been part of its treatment, then became its trademark as it stayed with Tyson.

Perhaps the injuries or the memory of that fight ran deep. Like Ash's Pikachu, this Meowth refused to evolve. It had remained a Meowth and become Tyson's strongest Pokemon.

Ethan had expected Tyson to save his ace for the end. Sending it out now showed how desperate the battle had become. Tyson had no choice but to stake everything on it early.

Chapter 774: A Battle in the Spotlight

Venusaur and Meowth took their places on opposite halves of the Grass Field.

Apart from Ethan, Tyson, and those who knew them well, such as Ash and Morrison, no one realized that this hat-wearing Meowth was Tyson's strongest Pokemonand his last hope. The crowd noticed its almost human outfit without sensing the danger beneath it.

Ethan studied Meowth more carefully than he ever had before. He had dealt with Team Rocket's Meowth many times, but its comic presence had led him to overlook the species. This Meowth made the familiar Pokemon seem strange again.

Its shape resembled a small housecat or a beckoning cat. Most Meowth walked on four legs, though a few learned to walk like people through sheer determination. Pale yellow fur covered most of its body, turning brown at the end of its tail and on its hind paws. Its oval face held large eyes and a wide mouth but no visible nose. A bright gold coin gleamed on its forehead.

Meowth could sleep through the day and become energetic after sunset. They moved silently on careful paws and washed their faces often to keep the coins on their foreheads clean. They loved shiny things, especially coins, which they hid when they found them. Around garbage dumps, they were even known to fight Murkrow over glittering objects.

Meowth and Venusaur had no type advantage over one another. Of all Ethan and Tyson's exchanges, this was the fairest matchup yet.

Tyson's earlier losses had not shaken Meowth. It wore a confident smile and raised one sharp claw toward Venusaur.

The referee lifted the flag and began the round. Before Tyson could give an order, Meowth charged, its claws glinting. It meant to settle the fight at close range.

Ethan did not fear close combat, but he would not give up Venusaur's reach and let Meowth approach freely. Venusaur, Razor Leaf.

A dozen or more sharp leaves spun toward Meowth. It twisted its body and slipped past most of them. Those it could not avoid, it sliced apart with its claws. By the time the leaves had passed, it had reached the middle of the field.

Vine Whip, Ethan ordered.

Two long vines emerged from the flower on Venusaur's back and lashed at Meowth. Unlike a volley of leaves, the vines were part of Venusaur's body and could change direction at will. Their reach was shorter, but they were harder to evade.

The vines cracked through the air. Meowth jumped over the first strike. Before it landed, the vines sprang up from where they had hit the ground and curled toward it again.

Meowth's eyes narrowed. It twisted sharply in midair and escaped, only for the vines to turn and pursue it once more. It could not dodge a third time. Calmly, it slashed ahead with both claws and cut the vines apart.

That stopped the attack, but it stopped Meowth's advance too. It landed where it was, unable to close the remaining distance.

The exchange took only moments. Neither Pokemon had gained much, yet the crowd leaned forward. Meowth had clearly earned its place in this match, and the battle promised to be worth watching.

From his command position, Tyson was impressed by how Venusaur had kept his ace away. He called, Meowth, try again! Meowth had reached halfway across the field; it was a promising start.

Meowth raised its claws and rushed forward. Ethan answered at nearly the same instant.

Venusaur, Sleep Powder!

A thick cloud of green powder poured from the flower on Venusaur's back, spreading around it. In the sunlight the cloud glowed an ominous green. Meowth knew better than to let a sleeping powder settle on it.

Instead of retreating, it accelerated. Before the powder could fall, it sprinted right up to Venusaur and lifted a claw. Eyes widened across the stadium. Tyson had found one of his few openings in the match.

Even Ethan had not expected such determination. Meowth had risked being put to sleep to get close. None of Tyson's other Pokemon had shown that kind of nerve. This was an ace.

Venusaur's vines snapped out again. At this distance, though, Vine Whip was less useful. The vines needed room to extend and turn. Tyson had driven Meowth in close for precisely that reason.

Meowth slipped past the vines and raked Venusaur with both claws.

Slash! Slash!

The crowd cheered. The announcer joined them. Meowth has hit Venusaur! That blow shouldoh. Without a type advantage, it hasn't done much damage. And the Sleep Powder is falling now. How will Meowth get out?

Many spectators had begun favoring Tyson. Ethan looked too strong, they wanted a closer match, and Tyson was a local Hoenn competitor. His first clean hit excited them almost as much as it excited him.

Ash and Morrison clenched their fists along with the crowd. Misty looked at them in distaste, crossed her legs and arms, and leaned back in her seat. It was just two scratches. The battle's barely begun. What is everyone so excited about?

Her companions realized they had annoyed her. They sat up straight and pretended nothing had happened.

On the field, Meowth faced the danger the announcer had spotted. No matter how fast it was, it could not simply run clear while Sleep Powder fell around it. Its small body and hat kept the powder from landing on it immediately, but green particles drifted ever closer. The whole stadium watched to see what it would do.

A flash of electricity burst from Meowth and cracked through the air.

Thunderbolt! the announcer cried. This Meowth knows Thunderbolt!

The discharge ignited the surrounding Sleep Powder and burned it away. The current spread farther, but the Pokemon it ought to have struck was gone.

Where was Venusaur?

When the glare faded, the crowd saw it well beyond the electric attack's reach. Supported by its vines, Venusaur had pulled itself backward in an instant, reopening the distance between them.

How had it known to move? Had Ethan anticipated Thunderbolt?

Tyson was the most startled of all. Thunderbolt was one of Meowth's hidden strengths. It had used the move only once in the preliminaries, and Ethan had not watched that match. Had Ash or someone else told him?

Ethan read the question on Tyson's face. No one had warned him. He had seen Tyson's Meowth in the anime long ago, but could not remember exactly what it could do. As far as he recalled, it was simply an unusually strong Meowth.

He had judged from its behavior. Meowth had seen Sleep Powder and rushed closer anyway. It must have had some way to protect itself. Ethan did not need to know what that way was to see that Venusaur should keep its distance. While everyone watched Meowth, he had ordered Venusaur back. That was how it escaped Thunderbolt.

Tyson, however, assumed Ethan had learned the move in advanceeither from a recording of his earlier match or from someone who had seen it.

As Tyson searched for an explanation, Ethan attacked. Meowth was strong, but Venusaur had traveled with Ethan since it was a Bulbasaur. It had grown and evolved beside him and helped him win Conference titles. It had worked as hard as any Pokemon on his team.

A hat-wearing Meowth was not going to intimidate it. Even a Persian in that hat would have been another opponent to face.

A huge seed shot from Venusaur's flower toward Meowth. Meowth dodged the seed itself. Then it exploded, and the blast engulfed it.

That's bad news, the announcer said. Seed Bomb fires a large seed with a hard shell. Meowth avoided the direct hit but couldn't escape the explosion.

Meowth burst from the smoke and leaped to safe ground, breathing hard. It had run from the center of the blast, but the explosion covered a wide area. It had still been caught. Fortunately, the distance spared it a critical wound.

Burn marks stung its body and slowed it, yet its resolve to help Tyson win was greater than the pain.

Tyson exhaled when he saw Meowth escape. He blamed himself for losing focus. Had he noticed Venusaur's attack sooner, he might have spared Meowth those injuries. Regret would not help it now. He fixed his attention on the battle.

Meowth was still fighting with everything it had. Tyson would do no less.

Chapter 775: Into the Top Sixteen

Meowth! The battle isn't over. Let's go! Tyson called.

Meowth answered at once and rushed toward Venusaur again. Venusaur had drawn back, and even that modest gap would not be easy to cross.

Two vines whipped toward Meowth before it had gone far. This time it did not try to dodge them outright. It used Double Team, sending images of itself at Venusaur from several angles.

Tyson watched anxiously. Ethan had seen through Sceptile's Double Team at the start of the match. Would he find the real Meowth too? After everything else Ethan had done, Tyson would hardly be surprised if he did.

The vines swept through several images without hitting the real one.

Yes! Tyson punched the air.

Ethan could not identify the real Pokemon every time. Distance, size, movement, and the surroundings all mattered. He had to study the differences between the images. Meowth was small, and the move had happened in a blink. One glance was not enough.

Tyson's relief did not last. Once Venusaur cleared the first images, its vines swept back across those remaining and struck the real Meowth from behind. A sharp crack rang out. Meowth was driven to the ground like a ball with the air knocked out of it.

Many spectators winced for Tyson. Those vines are too fast, the announcer said. Seed Bomb injured Meowth earlier and slowed it down. Before that, it might have escaped.

Meowth lay still for a moment, then forced itself up and advanced once more. The crowd cheered its persistence. Tyson saw the welt across its back and knew it was fighting through pain.

Come on, Meowth. You have to beat Venusaur.

Ethan watched in silence. After that blow, Meowth seemed to draw on some last reserve. Its speed returned to what it had been at the start, and its reactions sharpened. It blocked the vines and shredded Venusaur's Razor Leaf with its claws.

Ethan realized what its Ability must be: Technician. It strengthened lower-powered moves, making simple attacks more effective. The force in Meowth's claws as they stopped the vines and tore apart the leaves made the Ability clear. No wonder it had improved so much in the relatively short time since Tyson caught it. Technician suited it perfectly.

Even with that surge, Ethan was not afraid. At his command, Venusaur attacked in earnest. The two Pokemon traded moves in what looked like the deciding exchange of the round.
