Meowth revealed another of its specialties: Iron Tail. Its tail struck with the hardness of steel, knocking Venusaur's vines aside and freeing its claws for other attacks.

Meowth was using everything it had. Venusaur still looked composed. When it began fighting at full strength, Meowth could no longer keep up.

Venusaur caught it with a sudden Take Down, upsetting its rhythm. It hid a powerful Power Whip among its other vine attacks, staggering Meowth again. Then, while Meowth was dazed and unable to defend itself, Venusaur finished charging Solar Beam. The concentrated blast struck and knocked Meowth to the ground.

S-so strong... Morrison stared. They were trading blows a moment ago. How did Meowth lose so suddenly?

Because Ethan started fighting seriously, Misty said with a snort. He gave Tyson's Meowth time to show what it could do, so everyone could see Tyson wasn't weak. If it had been a stranger, Ethan would have ended it sooner.

Living alongside Ethan had taught Misty how he thought. She was right.

Ethan did not know Tyson well, but they had spent several days together. Beating him at full force from the first instant would have been like slapping him in public. Battles were not the only thing that mattered; people had to live with one another afterward. Tyson was already going to be eliminated. Letting him display his strength for a while cost Ethan nothing.

The referee raised a flag. Meowth is unable to battle! Venusaur wins this round!

Tyson came out of his daze at the announcement. He looked at his unconscious partner for a long moment, then shook his head with a helpless smile. Even Meowth had not managed to defeat one of Ethan's Pokemon.

Ethan was astonishingly strong. Tyson had been beaten so thoroughly that he could not argue with the result. He had already felt the distance between them and prepared himself for the loss. Now that it had come, he could accept it. But whatever fighting spirit he had left seemed to go with Meowth.

For his final Pokemon, Tyson sent out Hariyama. Ethan considered the two remaining members of his selected team, Gengar and Gardevoir. Then he chose neither and brought Tyranitar back.

Hariyama's Fighting type had a fourfold advantage over Tyranitar's Rock and Dark types. Anyone watching could see that Ethan was giving Tyson an opening. He had made the choice before the crowd and the cameras without concern.

Tyson no longer had the heart to take advantage. Hariyama fell before Tyranitar in a brief, one-sided finish. Ethan had won all six rounds without losing a Pokemon.

Congratulations to Ethan for reaching the top sixteen! the announcer called. And let's applaud Tyson as he leaves us. Thank you for a memorable match!

Both Trainers recalled their Pokemon and met at the center of the field to shake hands.

I lost, Tyson said, rueful but sincere. You're incredibly strong. You've shown me how much there is beyond what I know.

You're strong too, Ethan said with a smile. Without me here, you could have won this year's Ever Grande Conference.

Tyson took it for polite encouragement. He smiled bitterly, shook his head, and let it pass.

After they parted, Ethan waved to the stands and left through the competitors' passage. Misty, Ash, and the others were waiting. They gathered around him, applauding and offering congratulations.

Congratulations, Ethan!

You were amazing! I didn't think you'd beat Tyson so easily!

Where is Tyson? someone asked. Hasn't he come out yet?

He's already gone, Ethan told them. He's setting off on another journey right away. There wasn't time to tell you himself, so he asked me to apologize.

They exchanged startled looks. The six-to-zero loss had affected him that badly? Apart from Ash, most of them would have struggled to accept such a result. Going somewhere quiet to recover before continuing his travels was understandable. They respected his decision and said no more.

Ethan turned to Ash. I've made the top sixteen. You're next. Don't stumble now.

Don't worry! Ash clenched a fist and grinned. I'm not the Trainer I used to be. Just watch. I'll be in the top sixteen soon too!

Ash's match was that afternoon. His opponent was Katie, a Trainer from Lilycove City. She had impressed everyone during the preliminaries. However confident Ash sounded, his friends expected a difficult battle.

At noon they shared a hearty meal at a nearby restaurant, both to celebrate Ethan's win and to send Ash into his match in good spirits.

...

The sacred flame still burned brightly. At two in the afternoon, the Ever Grande Conference's main stadium filled with noise.

As the announcer introduced the competitors, Ethan, Misty, May, and the others made their way through the crowd to their reserved seats. They had spent time cheering Ash on in the competitors' passage, so he had already entered the arena when they reached the stands. They had missed the long warm-up and arrived just as the battle was about to begin.

Ethan sat down, set aside his popcorn, and looked up at Katie on the big screen. She was a beautiful woman in her twenties with long green hair. Standing with her arms folded, she looked calm.

Paper rustled beside him. Brock had produced a small notebook and was flipping through it. Without lifting his head, he recited, I keep notes on every beautiful older woman. The people of Lilycove call Miss Katie the Cool Beauty. She loves music, plays the clarinet, and enjoys spicy foodespecially spaghetti with Tamato Berries...

Stop! Misty cut him off. Where do you even find all that? And why is it all trivia? What about her battles? What types does she use? Which Pokemon is her ace?

Of course I didn't write that down. Brock smiled. It's my hobby notebook. I record what interests me. By the way, she's one of the three most beautiful women in this Conference.

That was Brock for you. Ethan could only admire the effort. These details must have been harder to gather than information about Katie's Pokemon. When a beautiful woman was involved, nothing could stop Brock.

Ethan looked at Katie again. She was certainly striking. If she was only in Brock's top three, what did the other two look like? He was curious in a purely appreciative way, of course. Nothing more.

The wheel settled on the Rock Field for Ash and Katie's first half. Gears raised a battlefield crowded with rocks of different sizes. At the referee's signal, both Trainers released their opening Pokemon.

Ash chose Torkoal. Katie chose Venomoth.

Torkoal's Fire type should have given it the advantage against the Bug and Poison-type Venomoth. Yet Ethan and Ash's close friends exchanged uneasy smiles. They had noticed a strange pattern: when Ash faced a bad type matchup, he struggled but sometimes won. When the matchup favored him, he often lost.

Perhaps it was only chance. Even so, seeing this pairing gave them a bad feeling.

Chapter 776: Ash's Battle

With the crowd cheering and their friends worried, Ash and Katie's match began.

Watching a great tournament from the stands was nothing like competing in one. Under the spotlights, tens of thousands of eyes followed two Trainers and two Pokemon. The crowd's mood rose with every fine move and fell with every mistake. Its cheers rolled around Ethan, and he felt his own excitement grow.

This was the atmosphere of the Ever Grande Conference. This was the world's favorite sport. Under its lights, every action seemed larger, every movement more vivid. Even an ordinary move could draw cheers. A remarkable performance could make a Trainer known everywhere. A newcomer might grow through the experience and, with enough luck, leave as a star.

Torkoal and Venomoth had already begun fighting. Ethan ate some popcorn, leaned back, and watched.

Katie shared her Chinese name with Tate of the Mossdeep Gym. Leaving their Pokemon's strength aside, the poised woman on the field made a far more striking impression than the younger Gym Leader. She had earned eight Badges and reached the final tournament, so her battling skill would be no small matter either.

Katie opened with Venomoth's Stun Spore. Torkoal withdrew into its shell to avoid the powder. Katie seemed to have expected that: she ordered Venomoth to use Disable, preventing Torkoal from using Withdraw again.

It was a clever move. A turtle Pokemon relied on its shell for defense and sometimes for attack. Disable sealed the last move its target had used, taking away one of Torkoal's most valuable options.

Ash did not appear concerned. He ordered Flamethrower. Venomoth dodged the flames, and Katie immediately recalled it.

The crowd was confused. Why switch Pokemon so soon after the match began? Ethan understood. Katie was a measured Trainer who gathered information before committing herself. She had led with a Flying Pokemon to probe Ash's lineup. Now she had seen Torkoal and could choose a better matchup.

Blue light flashed. Golduck appeared before Torkoal, just as Ethan expected.

Ash recovered from his surprise and ordered Torkoal to attack before Golduck had settled in. Golduck reacted first. Its Water Gun struck Torkoal and lifted it into the air. Then Golduck ran beneath its landing point and used Fury Swipes the moment it came down.

Claws raked Torkoal again and again. In a few seconds, it had taken dozens of hits. Golduck's final swipe sent it tumbling back beside Ash. Its eyes had turned to spirals. The referee raised the flag and announced the first result.

Max and Morrison exchanged uneasy looks. She's strong, Max said. Is Ash going to lose? Katie had defeated his first Pokemon with alarming ease.

One loss doesn't decide a match, Ethan said calmly. Katie's style gives Ash trouble, but he'll adjust. It may still be a rough fight. Unless something unexpected happens, I think he'll win.

His steady voice settled their nerves. Ethan had no proof he could offer, but they trusted the judgment of a two-time Conference champion.

On the big screen, Ash looked more nervous now. Sweat ran down his forehead. To recover a round and gain a type advantage, he sent out Pikachu against Golduck.

Katie gave him no such chance. She recalled Golduck in front of him and sent out Dugtrio instead. She understood type matchups very well.

Misty glanced at Ethan. Doesn't she fight like you did at the Indigo Conference?

A little. Ethan remembered how he had once needed to plan carefully around type advantages because his Pokemon were not yet overwhelmingly strong. By the Silver Conference he relied on that less. Now he could often ignore matchups entirely. Travel had changed him. Katie fought much as he had in those earlier days.

Type advantage, however, did not always settle a battle with Ash. Dugtrio's Ground type threatened Pikachu and ignored Electric attacks. Its three dark heads crowded together in the center of the field, a formidable answer to an Electric Pokemon. But Pikachu had beaten Ground types in memorable ways before. Ash had earned his reputation for winning against bad matchups.

Katie knew none of that, or did not think it mattered. She smiled confidently. Ash did not retreat either.

At the start of the round, he sent Pikachu forward with Quick Attack. Katie ordered Dugtrio to use Dig. It vanished underground, leaving Pikachu to stop and watch for its return.

Dugtrio did not surface. From below, it used Sand Tomb. The center of the Rock Field collapsed into a widening pit of flowing sand. It reached Pikachu and pulled it in. With the ground slipping beneath its feet, Pikachu could not escape with Quick Attack. Ash told it to use Thunderbolt instead.

The Electric attack did nothing to Dugtrio. Murmurs passed through the stands. Max and the others sighed. Ash could devise wonderfully inventive tactics, then make a basic mistake as if he had forgotten how types worked.

Katie smiled faintly. She ordered Dugtrio to use Double-Edge through the sand. Ash, equally rashly, told Pikachu to meet it with Iron Tail.

The collision exploded. Smoke filled the pit, and Pikachu shot high out of the Sand Tomb toward Ash. For a moment Max and the others were relieved: at least it had escaped.

Ethan narrowed his eyes. Pikachu's posture was wrong. He shook his head. The master of winning bad matchups seemed to have gone missing for now.

What's wrong? Misty asked.

Before Ethan could answer, Pikachu hit the ground beside Ash and lay motionless. Its eyes were open, but it could no longer move.

What? Max stared. Pikachu lost?

They had known Pikachu could lose. They had not expected it to fall so quickly or so completely.

Ash rushed, Ethan said. If he'd focused on escaping Sand Tomb before trying to fight Dugtrio head-on, he could have worked his way back into the round.

The others agreed, though they knew that a patient retreat was hardly Ash's style. Temperament shaped the way a Trainer fought. With Katie winning two rounds using Dugtrio and Golduck, Ash was in a dangerous position. Ethan's confidence kept his friends from giving up hope.

Ash lifted Pikachu and set it beside him. Then he sent out his third Pokemon: Glalie.

Ethan had never fought or watched Ash's Glalie in person, but he knew its strength from the anime and from Max's accounts. Even without Pikachu and Torkoal, Ash could still turn the match around.

Katie left Dugtrio in. Perhaps she had no clear counter to Glalie, or perhaps she had another plan.

She tried to repeat her underground tactic. As soon as Dugtrio used Dig, Glalie drove a Headbutt into the ground. The impact forced Dugtrio back out. While it was stunned, Glalie hit it with Ice Beam.

Ice was strong against Ground. Together with Headbutt, the attack knocked Dugtrio out almost at once. The crowd was shocked, and Katie was too. Glalie had hit too hard for her to switch Dugtrio away. She should have changed Pokemon before the round began. Two easy victories had made her careless, and now she had paid for it.

Cheers filled the stadium. After watching Katie defeat two of Ash's Pokemon so easily, some spectators had written him off. Glalie's immediate win gave them a contest again. Not everyone wanted the one-sided victories Ethan had delivered; a match that swung back and forth was exciting too.

At last, a win, Max said. He and the others exhaled. They had believed Ethan's prediction, but two losses had tested that belief. Now they could see a path back.

Katie recalled Dugtrio and sent out Misdreavus. Neither Pokemon had a type advantage over the other. A Trainer could bring only six Pokemon, after all; no team could cover every matchup.

Glalie had taken no damage in the previous round, and Misdreavus was fresh. Ash opened with Ice Beam. Katie ordered Misdreavus to advance straight through the attack toward Glalie.

The crowd could not understand her choice. Ethan saw it and guessed her plan at once.

So that's what she's doing. She's decisive enough to be ruthless.

Chapter 777: Max: I Think I Jinxed It

Misdreavus came straight through Ice Beam, from the front of the attack to the back. Its body was covered in wounds, but it did not slow. It kept charging at Glalie.

That only confirmed Katie's plan for Ethan. It was painfully obvious.

Ash still had not worked out her strategy. He clearly did not know what made a Ghost-type Pokemon so dangerous. All he saw was a rare opening, and he did not hesitate to order Glalie to use Headbutt.

Glalie rushed forward at full speed and slammed into Misdreavus. Misdreavus made no attempt to dodge.

Bang! Even from the stands, they could hear the impact.

The blow threw Misdreavus backward. Just before it fell, a purple light flashed in its eyes. Anyone who was not watching closely could have missed it. The light vanished, Misdreavus hit the ground, and its eyes rolled back. It was unable to battle.

Ash thought he had been handed an easy win. He raised his right fist and cheered, delighted to have pulled back another round.

The next moment, purple light flew out of Misdreavus's eyes and into Glalie's. Pain crossed the floating Pokemon's face. It dropped from the air and lay still, also unable to battle.

What?! Ash stared, unable to understand what had happened. The announcer's voice rang across the field.

Misdreavus is unable to battle! Glalie is also unable to battle! This round is a draw!

In the stands, May looked just as lost. She had never seen anything like it. Why did Glalie fall too? Misdreavus had already lost.

Max pushed up his glasses. Was that Destiny Bond? he asked, sounding uncertain.

He knew the move from studying Pokemon, but recognizing one in a real battle was harder. Several moves had similar looking effects. A brief flash of light was not much to go on.

Yes, it was Destiny Bond, Ethan said with a nod. It's a Ghost-type move that takes the opponent down with its user. If an opponent's attack directly knocks out the Pokemon that used it, the attacker faints as well. It's a way to force a one-for-one trade.

It's that powerful? May asked. Then couldn't you use it to take down any opponent?

It has serious limits, Ethan said. Using it twice in a row fails. It also fails if the opponent doesn't attack soon enough. An experienced Trainer may spot what you're trying to do. Still, against an opponent you can't otherwise beat, it can turn a battle around.

No one had tried Destiny Bond against Ethan, but a Trainer's intentions could sometimes be plain to see. Katie's had been. If she had used it against him, he would not have given Misdreavus the opening. Against Ash's style of battling, it had caught him by surprise.

Only a skilled Ghost-type specialist could use Destiny Bond with real finesse. Yet against someone like that, Ethan would already be on guard. For all its power, pulling it off was far from easy.

Brock rubbed his chin. Why would Katie use it here? Maybe she wanted to change the pace, but trading one Pokemon for one doesn't gain her much.

The exchange had certainly startled the crowd and given them plenty to talk about. Whether it had improved Katie's position was another question.

She must have her reasons, Ethan said. Maybe none of her remaining Pokemon had a reliable way to beat Glalie, so she chose the safer trade. Or perhaps she thought Glalie was Ash's ace and wanted it gone quickly.

He could only guess. Katie alone knew what she had been thinking.

With Ash's third Pokemon down, the match reached its intermission. Katie still held a lead of one Pokemon.

Ethan reached for more popcorn and found the bag empty. When he turned, May was tossing the last kernels into her mouth one by one. She tilted her head at his look, apparently unaware she had eaten his popcorn.

Well, fine. She could have it.

The short break passed quickly. While the Trainers rested, the field wheel settled on the Water Field for the second half.

That was good news for Ash. His Corphish was strong, and the water would give it room to show what it could do. As soon as the match resumed, he sent Corphish out. Katie answered with Golduck, which had performed so well earlier.

The two Pokemon attacked at once. They fought evenly at first, but Katie soon read Ash's straightforward approach. Golduck caught Corphish with Confusion and held it helpless in midair. Golduck threw it into the pool, only for Corphish to seize its chance, burst out of the water behind Golduck, and land a heavy blow.

The battle began to shift Ash's way. When they met at close range again, Corphish clamped Golduck's claw in its pincers and hurled it away. It immediately gathered a Bubble Beam and fired, defeating Golduck.

It had been one of the few rounds in this match that went back and forth instead of favoring one side throughout. Corphish had simply performed a little better, earning Ash the win.

They're finally tied, Max said, letting out a long breath. Now they're back at the starting line.

There's more to it than that, Ethan said. Ash fights on momentum. Once he gets a win, it's much easier for him to find his rhythm.

Corphish was still waving its pincers triumphantly. Katie's expression barely changed, but Ethan could see a hint of urgency in it.

She sent Venomoth back out. Ash recalled Corphish and brought out Swellow, turning the round into an aerial battle.

People jokingly called it Bug Swellow: whenever it appeared, it was bound to take down at least one Pokemon. The nickname said plenty about its strength. Ash had even chosen a favorable matchup this time, sending a Flying type against Venomoth's Bug type. Such a deliberate type advantage was unusual for him.

Ash finally showed the skill everyone expected of him. Venomoth used Disable again and sealed one of Swellow's moves, but Swellow's greater strength and relentless attacks carried it to a comfortable victory.

Three down for Ash, four for Katie. Ash had won another round.

On the big screen, Katie's brows drew together. The Cool Beauty of Lilycove City looked far less cool than her reputation suggested.

Ash now had the initiative and showed no sign of switching. Katie took out her fifth Poke Ball. A Scizor appeared in front of Swellow.

Scizor? May asked. It's a Bug type too, like Venomoth. Is it really a good choice against a Flying type like Swellow?

Flying is strong against Bug, Ethan said, nodding before shaking his head. But Scizor is also a Steel type. Flying-type attacks don't do much to Steel.

May studied its body again. It really did look like steel. A bird Pokemon would probably hurt its beak pecking at that armor.

When the round began, both Pokemon used Quick Attack and charged. They clashed five or six times in a matter of moments, neither gaining an edge. They changed moves and traded attack for defense. Even after a prolonged battle of Double Teams, they remained evenly matched.

At last, Swellow caught the briefest opening and struck with Aerial Ace, defeating Scizor.

Bug Swellow had lived up to its name again. Its strength had brought Ash two wins.

Ethan smiled. If Ash kept growing like this, his talent with Flying-type Pokemon might one day make him an excellent Flying-type master. And what would that make Ethan?

As a Scizor Trainer himself, he could see that Katie's Scizor was quite strong, even if it did not match his own. It could have beaten Swellow. It had ended its Double Team first, though, and that small mistake had cost it the round.

The score stood at three to five. Katie was on the edge of elimination. One more loss would end her tournament.

Under the eyes of the whole stadium, she solemnly sent out her final Pokemon. Blue light flashed, and a Walrein appeared in the pool. It lifted its head and roared.

That's quite an entrance. Ethan raised his brows and smiled at the others. I'd say Walrein is Katie's ace.

Her ace? May asked.

Yes, Misty said. As a Water-type Trainer, she agreed with Ethan. Look at its condition and its muscles. You can feel how strong it is.

With both of them saying so, Max and the others had no reason to doubt it.

Ace or not, Ash still has Swellow and two other Pokemon, Max said with a grin. He can wear Walrein down if he has to. There's nothing to worry about.

...

Corphish is unable to battle! Walrein wins!

As the announcer called the result, Max stared from the stands, his mouth hanging wide enough to fit two eggs.

He had just said Ash could not lose. Now Walrein had defeated Swellow and Corphish one after the other. For a moment, Max wondered if he had jinxed them. How else had such a promising position turned so suddenly?

Ash looked grim too. It was hard for anyone to stay calm after the same opponent knocked out two of their Pokemon in succession.

He had not expected Walrein to be this strong. It had beaten Swellow and Corphish with startling ease. Both had used some energy in earlier rounds, but defeating them back to back still showed how powerful Katie's ace was.

Worse, Walrein had built up its own momentum and was almost unhurt.

Ash had one Pokemon left. He could still give the last round everything he had. He gritted his teeth and threw his final Poke Ball.

Chapter 778: An Arrangement of Fate

Under the crowd's gaze, Ash's final Pokemon appeared: Grovyle.

Both Trainers had only one Pokemon left. Whoever won this last round would advance to the next stage and join the final sixteen.

Even Max and the others were tense. They stood with their fists clenched and called out to Ash.

Come on, Ash!

Don't lose!

As their friends cheered, May quietly asked, Brother Ethan, do you think Ash can make it through?

It was not that she lacked faith in him. At this point, a single mistake could send him out of the tournament. Nobody could know the winner until the last moment.

Watching Ethan battle felt entirely different. They never worried that he would lose. They only wondered how much of his strength an opponent might force him to show. Ash's matches could make them anxious even when he had the advantage, as though defeat might come at any moment.

Trust him, Ethan said with a light smile. Ash is the kind of Trainer who handles pressure best when it matters most. Give him a match where he's comfortably ahead, and he may not know what to do with it. Put him in a hard fight like this, and you'll see what he can really do.

May looked toward the Trainer's area. Ash's face was serious. Thinking over the way he fought, she nodded.

Somehow, calling him Brother Ethan lately had made May feel closer to him. No matter how nervous she felt, hearing his voice now seemed to calm her. It was strange.

On the field, Grovyle and Walrein had begun their fight.

Walrein was an Ice and Water type, while Grovyle was a Grass type. Each could strike the other's weakness for double damage. That mutual threat promised a fast battle.

Grovyle had not yet evolved into Sceptile, but it was arguably Ash's strongest Pokemon at present. People jokingly called it the number one member of his team. Sending it out last showed how much confidence Ash had in it.

Two aces were facing each other. It was bound to be a fine match. Ethan sat up straighter.

Come on, Ash. Show me how much you've grown.

Walrein opened with Ice Beam. Grovyle dodged and countered with Leaf Blade, but Walrein dived into the water. Grovyle's attack missed, and its target disappeared beneath the surface.

Walrein used the field to its advantage, surfacing to attack and then vanishing again. For a while, Grovyle could hardly return a blow. Ash soon found an opening, though. He used the patches of water frozen by Walrein's own Ice Beams to jolt it out of the pool.

Walrein had used so many Ice-type attacks that the whole surface was becoming a hard sheet of ice. It had trapped itself above the water and could no longer dive away. Grovyle had more chances to attack.

The ice slowed Grovyle somewhat, but it was still fast enough to close the distance. With Quick Attack it suddenly accelerated and struck Walrein in the neck before it could react.

Walrein fell heavily. Then it revealed its own surprise. It sprang back up and, imitating Grovyle's movement, charged at tremendous speed and slammed its head into Grovyle. Caught off guard, Grovyle stumbled back more than a dozen steps before regaining its footing.

The spectators realized what they had seen. Mimic was a Normal-type move that let a Pokemon copy the last move its opponent had used and make it its own for the battle. Even a move outside its usual strengths could become a sudden weapon.

Walrein now had Quick Attack, at least temporarily. In a way, it had made up for its lack of speed.

After a moment's surprise, Ash stopped trying to outpace it. He ordered Grovyle into a close-range fight. Katie told Walrein to meet it head-on.

That was exactly what Ash wanted. As the two drew close, Grovyle abruptly sprang backward and fired Bullet Seed. The attack struck Walrein.

Max and the others gaped. Ash had used a feint! He had fooled Katie, the announcer, and the audience alike. It had looked as though Grovyle would settle the round at close range. Instead, it had drawn Walrein into an attack. Ash really had grown.

Grovyle could attack from a distance and hold its own up close. Though unevolved, it was performing almost as well as Tyson's Sceptile. Once it evolved, it would surely become stronger still.

The successful strike gave Grovyle the initiative. It pressed its advantage and controlled the pace. In their final exchange, it dodged Walrein's Quick Attack by the narrowest margin and struck a vital spot with Leaf Blade. Walrein fell.

The match was decided. The referee announced the result at once. Walrein is unable to battle! Grovyle wins! The winner of this match is Ash!

The match had swung back and forth, with several excellent rounds. The crowd had enjoyed every turn and now gave Ash a roaring cheer. Max and the others stood, shouting something toward him.

Their voices vanished beneath the noise. Even someone sitting beside them could barely make out their words, let alone Ash down on the field.

Ethan remained seated, but he applauded quietly. He had seen real progress from Ash. His basic style had not changed, yet his Pokemon were stronger and he had added some strategy to his instincts. He had come a long way since the beginning of his journey.

That made Ash more dangerous, though to Ethan he was still a little inexperienced.

When Ash disappeared into the competitors' tunnel, Ethan and the others left the stands to meet him outside. They had barely approached when Ash waved at them with a broad grin.

Congratulations, Ash! Max and May hurried forward. You're through to the next round too!

That was a good battle, Ethan said. You've grown a lot.

Ash's grin stretched nearly from ear to ear. Heh, of course! I'm pretty good. How could I go out in this round?

Misty gave his boasting no mercy. Listen to you. If I hadn't watched the match, I'd think you beat her easily. You only just scraped through in the final round.

Ash had long since learned to fear Misty's sharp tongue. Apart from Ethan and May, she could be just as cutting with anyone. His smile stiffened, and his pride faltered.

All right. Ethan rubbed Misty's head. You two can stop bickering. Katie was strong. Against someone other than Ash, she might well have advanced.

Ash brightened instantly and shot Misty a triumphant look. See? Even Ethan says Katie was strong. Beating her proves I'm stronger!

Misty had not truly meant to pick a fight, especially on a happy day like this. After traveling with Ash for so long, teasing him had become a habit. Seeing him back to his old self, she smiled at the corners of her eyes, snorted, and turned away.

Another match passed after Ash's. Morrison's match came in the final time slot of the day. He won by a wide margin, easily defeating his opponent, and Ash watched his rival with envy.

Ash had struggled to overcome Katie. Watching Morrison win so comfortably made him feel as though he had been outdone.

By the end of the first day's matches, Ash and Morrison had both advanced. Tyson alone had been eliminated by Ethan. With the two friends still in the tournament, the prospect of a battle between them seemed more real.

That evening, Ash suggested celebrating the three of them reaching the final sixteen together. May enthusiastically agreed. They found the highest-rated pizza restaurant they could and sat down to a feast.

Its most popular dish was an authentic pizza baked in a stone oven. The crust was crisp, the cheese melted in their mouths, and the toppings included roasted meats, seafood, and fruit. Everyone ate their fill.

Ash and Morrison even turned dinner into another contest, each determined to eat more than the other. Ash's appetite was no match for Morrison's enormous stomach, though. He lost by a narrow margin, sighed in frustration, and, with his belly stretched full, declared he would beat Morrison next time.

While they ate and laughed, the draw for the final sixteen was released.

When the notice arrived, nobody felt like eating any longer. Ethan paid the bill, and they hurried back to the competitors' hall. The trip took long enough that, by the time they arrived, the big screen already showed every pairing.

Ash and Morrison looked up. Both froze, then turned toward each other. Their portraits stood side by side in the first pairing of the first row.

They had just shared a meal. Tomorrow they would have to decide which of them was stronger on the battlefield. Their faces went still, their eyes full of complicated feelings.

They had known that as the field narrowed they might eventually meet. Neither had expected it so soon. One would win; the other would leave the tournament with regrets.

Ethan looked away from them and searched for his own pairing. He found his portrait in the last group of the second row. His opponent was a young woman with a ponytail and thick black-rimmed glasses.

He tried to recall her matches. With so few competitors left, he had some impression of nearly all of them. In the round of thirty-two, this woman had fought with a ferocity completely at odds with her unremarkable appearance. She had crushed her opponent in a one-sided match.

Interesting. Ethan rubbed his chin thoughtfully.

He had drawn Tyson in the first round, then the strongest of the remaining competitors in the second. Was he going to face the strongest Trainer in the final eight as well? He did not dwell on it. Perhaps his luck was simply like that.

Even if he had known the Pokemon League had arranged the draw deliberately, he would only have laughed. Against overwhelming strength, such little tricks were useless.

He turned back toward Ash and Morrison just as Morrison ran through the doors. Ash stood stunned for a moment, then chased after him. May and the others watched in confusion.

They... May began.

Leave them be, Ethan said with a wave. It's a quarrel between two boys. They can work it out themselves. Let's return to the dormitory and wait.

As Ethan saw it, Ash and Morrison were friends as well as rivals. They had to face each other tomorrow. If they wanted to preserve their friendship through the battle, only they could speak honestly with each other. Nobody else could do it for them.

May and the others understood. They nodded, left the boys alone, and followed Ethan back to the dormitory.

After they were gone, Goodshow stood behind a glass window on the hall's second floor. He watched Ethan's retreating figure in silence for a long time.

Yes, he had arranged this opponent too. He had chosen the strongest Trainer left in the field.

Ethan was already among the final sixteen, and that was dangerous. If Goodshow could not stop him in the next round, Ethan might reach the final eight, or even the final four. Then everything Goodshow wanted and hoped for might truly fail.

Chapter 779: Watching the Match

It was the same stadium, but the atmosphere for the round of sixteen felt livelier than it had in the round of thirty-two. The number of seats and spectators had not changed. The crowd was simply more excited, cheering louder for battles that promised to be fiercer.

The whole Ever Grande Conference was caught up in the celebration. Promotional portraits of the competitors had appeared at bus stops and department stores in Hoenn's major cities. Even employees at some large companies were quietly neglecting their work to watch the annual event.

It drew more attention than the Grand Festival, which had ended only recently. Now it seemed to have the entire region watching.

At 8:30 that morning, with everyone looking on, Ash and Morrison opened the day's schedule.

Whatever the two had discussed the night before, they stood solemnly in their Trainer's areas. Morrison in particular looked nothing like his usual carefree self. He was tense and conflicted. One glance showed he was still fighting with himself.

The rules were the same as in the previous round. The announcer introduced both Trainers, then the wheel chose the field for the first half. It stopped on the Ice Field. A rectangular field covered in thick ice rose into place at the center of the stadium. Everything was ready. The battle began.

Ethan and the others sat among the spectators. Wanting to watch in comfort this time, and hoping to keep May from eating all his snacks again, Ethan had brought a large supply. He also waved over the stiff-backed Team Rocket trio and bought drinks from them at a price so low it was practically a giveaway. Fully prepared, he settled in to watch.

Ash's first Pokemon was Corphish. After hesitating for a long while, Morrison sent out Girafarig.

Others might think Morrison had struggled to choose a Pokemon. Ethan and his friends knew he was struggling with how to face Ash at all. It was hard to see such a cheerful boy brought to this state. It showed how much he valued their friendship.

Ash had already faced Gary and Richie in fateful matches, and he had fought Ethan as a friend. He was used to meeting people he cared about in competition. Of the two, he seemed calmer.

As for the Pokemon, Girafarig was a Normal and Psychic type, while Corphish was a pure Water type. Neither had a type advantage or a clear edge from the field. On paper, this should have been an even match.

But Morrison seemed to have lost all composure. He commanded Girafarig like a complete beginner, choosing moves without a plan and making basic mistakes. Its performance was a mess. The crowd was baffled. How could a Trainer this amateurish have reached the final sixteen?

This won't work, Max said, shaking his head. He did not know Morrison very well, but he could see the problem. If he keeps fighting like that, he's bound to lose.

Ethan took a sip of his drink. Does Morrison's condition look familiar to you? he asked Misty and Brock.

They turned to him. You mean...?

It's like Ash when he faced Richie at the Indigo Conference.

The name took them back to Kanto: another boy in a cap, with a Pikachu on his shoulder and a steadier temperament than Ash's. Morrison was in much the same state Ash had been then. He could not show his usual skill, and he barely seemed willing to fight.

It was almost fitting for someone so often called a heavier version of Ash to stumble over the same problem.

Only Morrison can bring himself back, Ethan said. Though I doubt Ash will stand by and do nothing.

They turned back to the field. Corphish was weaving around the ice pillars and rocks, running circles around Girafarig. Morrison could not settle himself enough to give useful orders, and Girafarig grew even less steady. After evading several attempted counterattacks, Corphish knocked it out with Crabhammer.

Ash had won the first round. He did not look pleased. He watched Morrison with a troubled expression.

Morrison did not recall Girafarig or send out a second Pokemon. The referee frowned and raised a flag to warn him. It was a bad sign. If the referee raised the flag again and Morrison still failed to act, he would be judged to have forfeited and disqualified.

Boos rose from the stands. This was the annual Ever Grande Conference, already down to the final sixteen. Was this really the match they had come to see? Dissatisfaction spread quickly, and Max and the others began to worry about Morrison.

What is he doing? Max scratched his head as he heard the crowd turn. Why is this so hard for him? Ash has already decided to fight with everything he's got.

Ethan shook his head. The choice was simple enough to understand: victory or friendship. Only boys as earnest as Ash and Morrison could get so caught in it that they could no longer move. It showed how much Morrison cared about his friend, but as a Trainer, he was falling short.

In Morrison's place, Ethan would apologize and then battle at full strength. To him, that was the greatest respect one could show a friend.

Morrison remained motionless. The referee raised the colored flag again. Morrison has lost the will to battle, so

Ash interrupted before the referee could finish. Ethan's group was too far away to hear what he said. They saw him call out to Morrison with fierce emotion. Morrison gritted his teeth and finally took out his second Poke Ball.

It held Growlithe. By type, that was hardly a wise choice. Morrison had already lost a round, and Ash's Water-type Corphish was still on the field. Sending out a Fire type seemed to deepen his disadvantage.

Perhaps Growlithe could make something of the Ice Field. Then again, if it melted the ice and exposed water, that might help Corphish even more. Morrison's choice was hard to fathom. Had his emotions clouded his judgment so badly that he had sent out the wrong Pokemon?

With the crowd still wondering, the second round began. Ash kept Corphish in and ordered an immediate, forceful attack, as though he hoped to wake Morrison up.

The earlier exchange had helped. Morrison's condition improved somewhat. He still could not bring himself to attack Ash's Pokemon directly, but at least his commands now made sense.

It was nowhere near enough. Corphish had the type advantage, and Morrison remained hesitant. Ash took a second easy win. The spectators grew angrier. What kind of battle was this? Their boos drowned out almost everything else.

Even Ethan grew impatient. He understood Morrison's feelings, but people had come to watch a match, not to watch one competitor flinch from fighting. Morrison was wasting time and the enthusiasm of everyone across Hoenn who had made room in their day to watch.

Some had traveled a long way to sit in these stands. Others had stolen a few minutes to follow the broadcast. One poor round could be forgiven. Failing to recover for a second was another matter. Youth, innocence, inexperience, and devotion to friendship were not enough to excuse it.

Across the field, Ash called something to Morrison again. Morrison's expression shifted visibly: first flushed with embarrassment, then angry, and finally pained.

Holding his fallen Growlithe, he murmured something to it. Then he seemed to find new energy and shouted aloud. At this distance, perhaps only Ash and the referee could hear his words. But in an instant, Morrison's old spirit seemed to return.

Finally, he's back to normal. Ethan gave a huge yawn and snorted.

Ash and Morrison might have moved each other with their friendship, but it had not moved everyone else. Now that the match was about to become a real battle again, Ethan felt a little interested.

Morrison looked lively once more. He recalled Growlithe and, without waiting for the referee, promptly took out his third Poke Ball. Blue light flashed. Swampert appeared before Corphish.

Ash did not recall Corphish, though it had already fought two rounds and spent considerable energy. For one thing, Corphish had knocked out two Pokemon without taking damage and still had momentum. For another, Ash did not want to take advantage of Morrison's earlier hesitation.

At the signal, both Pokemon charged, trading attacks at long, middle, and close range. Hydro Pump met Bubble Beam. Mud Shot met Aqua Jet. Focus Punch met Crabhammer.

Their direct exchange was as clear and exciting as any the crowd could have wished for. In only a few minutes, they attacked and counterattacked without either gaining the upper hand. Their blows shattered ice rocks into fragments and cracked the frozen surface. Nearly half the field was reshaped by the fight.

At last, Focus Punch and Crabhammer met again. The collision erupted, and both moves struck their targets. Corphish and Swampert fell together.

The referee looked them over and raised the flags. Corphish and Swampert are both unable to battle! This round is a draw!

Audiences could be fickle. They had booed Morrison for his hesitation; one fine round was enough to change their minds. They cheered both Pokemon with all their strength, as though they had forgotten their irritation.

Morrison had lost three Pokemon, so the match entered its intermission. Max and the others decided to visit Ash in the rest area and encourage him. Ethan stayed in his seat. He could not be bothered to move or to watch the two boys promise each other they would fight seriously.

The break passed quickly. When the Trainers returned, the second-half field had been chosen: the Grass Field.

Ash sent out his first partner, Pikachu. By coincidence, Morrison sent out Steelix.

That was both good news and bad news. At its best, Pikachu could show astonishing power against Pokemon with a type advantage over it. It was as if Ash's talent for winning bad matchups suddenly switched on, and Pikachu might knock one out in moments.

The bad news was that it did not happen often. In this round, Pikachu ran and attacked, trying to find an opening, but it could not draw on all that hidden potential. When it traded Iron Tails with Steelix, Steelix struck it down. Pikachu was unable to battle.

Since the main tournament began, Pikachu had lost twice in a row to Pokemon with favorable types against it: Katie's Dugtrio, then Morrison's Steelix. It was surprising, yet it made a certain kind of sense.

Pikachu's reputation for being able to match almost anyone, and lose to almost anyone, had not come from nowhere.

Chapter 780: Growing Stronger with Every Battle

With Pikachu's defeat, the score stood at three to two. Morrison had recovered some ground, but the two rounds he had practically given away at the start still left him in danger.

Ash had four Pokemon that had yet to appear. Morrison would have to approach every remaining round carefully. He could not afford another easy loss.

Ash carried Pikachu back, returned to his Trainer's area, and sent out Torkoal.

As a Fire type, Torkoal had an advantage over Steelix. Morrison did not switch. He let Steelix face it, brimming with energy despite the poor matchup. He looked like a different person from the boy who had fought the first two rounds.

As soon as the round began, he ordered Steelix to trade attacks with Torkoal. Dragon Breath collided with Flamethrower. The flames proved stronger, pushing through the Dragon Breath and striking Steelix.

Fire did double damage to Steelix, and it cried out in pain. Ash seized the chance and told Torkoal to press its advantage. But when Torkoal breathed fire again, Steelix reacted and answered with another Dragon Breath.

This time Flamethrower did not break through. The moves exploded against each other, filling the air with flame and smoke.

Steelix used the cover to Dig underground. Unsure where it would emerge, Torkoal hurriedly used Withdraw. Steelix burst up directly beneath it and launched it high into the air.

As Torkoal fell, it accidentally flipped onto its back. Steelix took the opening and hit it with Dragon Breath. Torkoal was unable to battle.

The referee raised a flag. Torkoal is unable to battle! Steelix wins!

That made two victories in a row. Steelix had beaten Torkoal despite the type disadvantage, knocking out a second opponent. From another point of view, Torkoal's Conference performance was as consistent as ever.

Morrison is fighting better and better, Brock said as he watched Torkoal fall. The others nodded. Morrison had plainly set aside his conflict. He no longer hesitated when he attacked, and his old cheerful energy had returned.

He is, Ethan agreed. He's fired up now. Ash may be the one in trouble.

Once Morrison recovered, he had won two straight rounds and erased the lead Ash had gained. Without the two victories he had handed Ash earlier, Ash might already have been far behind. Morrison was every bit as capable a Trainer as Ash. If Ash could not bring out his Pokemon's full potential, one misstep might end his tournament.

Both now had three Pokemon left. After a moment's thought, Ash sent out Grovyle.

Grass-type attacks would not do full damage to Steelix, so the matchup did not seem ideal. But this was Ash's Grovyle: powerful, coolheaded, and entirely unruffled.

Like Ash before him, Morrison chose not to switch. Perhaps he had forgotten he could. Steelix had already fought two rounds and was looking tired, yet Morrison sent it against Grovyle all the same.

As expected, Grovyle won. It dodged Steelix's Dig with agile steps. Then, against an incoming Dragon Breath, it created a moment the crowd would remember.

Grovyle leaped high, crossed its arms before its head, and used Leaf Blade to split the Dragon Breath. It drove forward until it reached Steelix's massive head and struck with all its force.

Boom! Steelix's enormous body crashed down, shaking the entire Grass Field. The big screen showed that it had fainted.

Ash's number one Pokemon had earned its reputation. The whole sequence looked impressive. Steelix is unable to battle! Grovyle wins!

The score was tied again. Once Ash and Morrison had begun fighting in earnest, every round had been exciting. The audience was finally seeing the strength expected of Trainers in the final eight. It was a shame one of these two would have to fall in the round of sixteen.

Watching the field, Ethan reached for the snacks on the seat beside him. His hand found nothing. He tried another bag and found that empty too.

Huh? He looked down. All that remained of the snacks he had bought were a few empty wrappers. Had he eaten them that quickly?

He turned to May. Her cheeks were puffed out, and she was still chewing like a little squirrel. There was no question who had eaten them.

But when had she managed it? She was fast. He had bought so much food, and she had not left a bite.

By the time Ethan looked back to the field, Ash and Morrison were fighting again. Morrison had sent out Gligar, a purple, scorpion-like Pokemon with wings on its back.

The insides of Gligar's wings were blue. Two pointed fangs protruded from its mouth. Large pincers tipped its forelimbs, and a fearsome stinger sat at the end of its tail.

Gligar were said to nest on steep cliffs. They could glide silently through the air as though sliding over the ground, then hop back to their nests after landing. Clinging to rock walls, they caught the wind with the membranes on their limbs. When they spotted prey, they spread their wings and swooped down, gliding toward it. Their large claws and talons seized a victim's face. They would cling to it, startle it into panic, and then strike with their poisonous stingers.

Ethan knew Gligar from the anime and games, but this was the first time he had seen a Trainer use one since coming to this world. He studied it with interest.

Grovyle remained Ash's Pokemon. The two moved quickly and fought evenly at first. Grovyle used the thick grass to its advantage. When Gligar skimmed low over the ground, Grovyle leaped onto its back, hoping to attack from above.

Gligar reacted at once. It carried Grovyle high into the air and threw it off. Grovyle could neither maneuver nor dodge up there. Gligar seized its neck and drove it violently into the ground.

The impact knocked Grovyle unconscious. It was unable to battle. The whole exchange had taken only a few minutes.

The fast attack brought both Trainers fully into the excitement of the match. The referee had scarcely raised a flag before Ash recalled Grovyle and, without hesitation, sent out Swellow.

The Pokemon took their contest into the sky. Trainers and Pokemon alike refused to yield. They tangled and chased each other, accumulating wounds but never stopping their attacks.

After a final clash at very close range, both Pokemon dropped from the air and hit the ground. Neither could battle. They had taken each other out.

The crowd loved the sheer force of it. Seeing both fall together brought a roar of delight. They seemed to have forgotten Morrison's poor start entirely. Now they eagerly awaited the next round.

The crowd's energy swept up Ash and Morrison. Both looked even more excited. Yet each had only one Pokemon left and one chance remaining. Reason kept telling them to calm down.

Max and the others clenched their fists in the stands. At this point, none of them could say who would win.

May hesitated, then leaned toward Ethan. Brother Ethan, who do you think will win?

Somewhere along the way, the others had begun to treat Ethan as though he knew everything. If he named a winner, it almost felt as if that person would win.

Honestly, even with his memories of the anime, Ethan could not call this match with confidence. Katie had been different. Morrison and Ash were almost evenly matched. Indeed, Morrison had given away two rounds and still forced Ash into a final showdown. Judging by today's battle alone, Morrison might be stronger.

He had almost fought a six-on-four match.

But a battle did not produce the same result every time simply because the Pokemon, Trainers, and field were the same. A single thought or a moment's distraction could change the outcome. Ethan did not know whether his presence in this world had altered how this match would end.

After thinking it over, he chose to trust Ash.

If Morrison had fought this way from the beginning, Ash would probably have lost by now, Ethan said. But there are no second chances for the start of a match. A Trainer's state of mind is part of their strength. They're tied now, and at a moment like this, I think Ash will still win.

May nodded. She thought so too. Brock, Max, and Misty probably all hoped Ash would win as well. They had met Morrison only a few times. Ash was their friend and traveling companion. They could hardly help favoring him.

Both Trainers sent out their final Pokemon. Ash chose Glalie, which had fought so well in the previous round. Morrison chose Metang.

This was their last exchange. The winner would advance. After the last two rounds, the crowd was eager to see what these Trainers would show them next. The stadium grew quiet as everyone watched.

Ice-type Glalie faced a Steel and Psychic type, a difficult matchup. But with Ash cornered again, perhaps his knack for overcoming bad type matchups would emerge.

Metang and its evolution, Metagross, had appeared surprisingly often in this year's Ever Grande Conference, though they were seldom seen in ordinary matches.

A brief pause seemed to have cooled Ash and Morrison down. The instant the round began, though, both eagerly ordered their Pokemon forward. How could they truly be calm in a match this important?

Metang met Glalie head-on. Its larger, sturdier body won the collision. Ash did not lose heart. If Glalie could not overpower Metang up close, it could attack from a distance. He ordered Ice Beam.

Metang used Confusion to bend the beam back. It curved through the air and struck Glalie itself. While Glalie reeled, Metang closed in and hit it with Take Down.

Metang had the advantage after their first exchange, just as most spectators had expected. Then Ash showed another sign of his growth.

To the crowd's confusion, he ordered Glalie to use Ice Beam again. Morrison gave Metang the same command as before. Confusion reflected the beam back toward Glalie.

Morrison did not know that this was exactly what Ash had been waiting for. As Ice Beam returned, Glalie used Icy Wind. A frost-laden gale burst from its mouth and turned the beam around once more, speeding it up and strengthening the attack. A moment later, both moves struck Metang together.

Chapter 781: The Finishing Hold

The reversal caught Morrison completely by surprise. He had never expected Ash to combine two moves, increase their power, and turn Ice Beam back on Metang. When Ash came up with an idea, it could be almost impossible to prepare for.

The two Ice-type attacks froze Metang where it hovered. Its body temperature was so low that the ice held it in place, and frost and snow coated its surface. Ash would not waste the opening. Glalie charged in with Headbutt and struck it squarely.

The blow toppled Metang and did considerable damage, though it also broke Metang free of the ice. Morrison saw it recover and immediately counterattacked.

Metang flew toward Glalie at high speed and landed a Meteor Mash from close range, taking back some of the ground it had lost. Ash refused to give way. He sent Glalie into a close-quarters fight.

The two Pokemon tangled, colliding head-on and trading blows like brawlers. Everyone knew the decisive exchange was close. The spectators gave the field their full attention.

Metang came in with another Meteor Mash, while Glalie charged with Headbutt. Just before they collided, Glalie shifted its course. Metang's fist missed, and Glalie struck it instead. Metang tipped backward and fell in front of Glalie.

It's over, Ethan said softly.

As he spoke, the referee raised a flag. Metang is unable to battle! Glalie wins! The winner of this match is Ash!

Ethan and the others stood with the rest of the crowd and applauded Ash. He had earned this victory the hard way.

Both he and Morrison were strong Trainers. If bad luck had not paired them against each other, each might have reached at least the final four. Fate had put them in the same group instead.

After the result, Ash and Morrison walked together and shook hands. Ethan could not hear what they said, and there was no need to recount it. When they left the field, they came up to the stands and joined his group to watch the other matches.

With Morrison present, the others kept their comments gentle. They congratulated Ash and offered Morrison a few words of comfort. Perhaps he had settled things with Ash, because he waved their concern away.

You don't need to console me, he said. I'm disappointed I lost, but I didn't get my head straight in time. Ash beat me fair and square. We agreed he'll keep fighting for both of us now!

There was no bitterness in his expression. He was his usual openhearted, easygoing self. Unlike Tyson, who had left as soon as Ethan eliminated him, Morrison stayed to enjoy the rest of the tournament. That was one of the better things about people like him.

Three more matches followed Ash and Morrison's. The competitors varied in ability. They had bright moments, but the battles were less exciting. The audience did not mind. So long as nothing strange interrupted the matches and the Trainers kept fighting, they were happy to watch.

At the noon break, Ethan's group left the stadium. They ate a simple lunch nearby and chatted about the strengths and weaknesses of the other competitors. Ash even offered a solemn assessment of several of them. After eating, they wandered around outside the stadium. At last, at three in the afternoon, Ethan's match arrived.

Good luck, Brother Ethan!

You can do it!

The Trainers in this Conference are strong, Ash called. Watch out for an upset!

They were gathered outside the competitors' tunnel to wish Ethan luck. At Ash's teasing, Misty made a face at him. Brother Ethan isn't as inconsistent as you. You nearly lost! Just watch. He'll beat his opponent in no time.

All right. Wait for the good news. Ethan smiled, waved, and walked into the tunnel, leaving them with a confident view of his back.

...

To the sound of cheering, Ethan emerged onto the field and took his place in the Trainer's area. Across from him stood the young woman with glasses. Their eyes met across the field, and they gave each other polite nods.

Her name was Shizuko. It sounded gentle, entirely unlike her fierce battling style. Though they had entered together, the crowd cheered noticeably louder for her.

The difference came from their earlier matches. Ethan had faced Tyson, arguably the strongest Trainer left apart from him. But Ethan had won so decisively that the audience had seen little of a contest. They knew both Trainers were strong without getting a clear sense of just how strong.

Shizuko was different. She had dispatched her opponent with startling force and efficiency. A young woman with a quiet appearance and a violent battling style was memorable. She had become more popular with the crowd, and many people betting on the match favored her.

The screen selected the Rock Field for the first half. At the referee's signal, both Trainers threw their opening Poke Balls. Ethan sent out Blaziken. Shizuko chose Primeape.

Primeape was a fitting partner for someone with her fiery temperament. With both Pokemon ready, the battle began at once.

Primeape bounded toward Blaziken, restless and furious, much like its Trainer. Blaziken, a Pokemon with a fiery fighting spirit, charged to meet it. Before they reached the middle of the field, Blaziken used Flamethrower without slowing its stride.

Primeape had been eager for a close-range fight. Blaziken had looked ready to give it one. Primeape did not expect a sudden blast of fire and was engulfed before it could prepare. While the flames still covered it, Blaziken accelerated and drove a high kick into it.

The match had barely started, and Primeape had already taken two attacks. Max laughed in the stands.

Ethan uses more strategy than Ash does after all!

What do you mean? Ash pouted. Didn't you see me thinking things through earlier? I don't just rush in anymore!

Thinking and strategy aren't quite the same, Misty said with a grin. Max means you still have a long way to go before you catch up with Ethan.

Come on! Ash muttered, his face hot with annoyance. Just watch the match.

Primeape got up and finally closed with Blaziken. Both were Fighting types, and their close-range exchange was more exciting than most. Shizuko's Primeape was strong. It used Low Kick, Karate Chop, Cross Chop, and even the Normal-type Scratch with practiced skill and boundless drive. Its fighting ability could stand beside that of Pokemon from a Fighting-type Gym.

Blaziken was not as specialized in pure Fighting techniques. It gained little advantage up close, though it could hold Primeape off without falling behind.

That was where the Trainer mattered. Ethan saw that a close-range contest alone would not win it. He changed tactics and had Blaziken use its fire. Blaze Kick punished Primeape when it got close; Flamethrower struck when it backed away.

Blaziken took control of the pace. After several fiery attacks, Primeape fell. A cheer broke out. It was not overwhelming, but the audience plainly approved of what they had seen.

The referee raised a flag. Primeape is unable to battle! Blaziken wins!

In the opposite Trainer's area, Shizuko frowned. She had studied recordings of Ethan and knew he was a formidable opponent. She was confident in her own strength too. She had believed she could beat him.

Despite a difficult opening, Primeape had seemed to hold the upper hand through much of the round. Shizuko had thought she would win. Then Ethan changed the pace, and everything turned against her in a matter of moments.

Looking back, she felt as though she might have found a way to turn it around. At the same time, perhaps she never had one. The uncertainty bothered her.

She kept the thought to herself and took out her second Poke Ball. Blue light flashed. Dodrio stood before Blaziken.

Ethan studied the three-headed, flightless bird and felt he understood Shizuko's tastes a little better. Primeape and Dodrio were both volatile Pokemon, well suited to her aggressive style. Or perhaps working with them had shaped that style.

He kept Blaziken in against the three-headed bird. In the stands, Ash and the others were surprised.

Ethan isn't switching Pokemon?

That's unusual for him, someone said.

Maybe he wants to give the Pokemon he caught in Hoenn more experience, Brock suggested, rubbing his chin. His other partners are already extremely strong, and he's given them all a chance to battle. It would be like him to focus on the newer ones now.

The others nodded. Few Trainers would use a final-sixteen match to train a Pokemon. Ash and Morrison certainly would not dare. Then again, Blaziken and Ethan's other Hoenn partners were already strong enough to contend for the championship. Calling this training was only relative to the strength of his older team. Anyone who mistook these Pokemon for weak would be a fool.

Blaziken and Dodrio began. Dodrio fought much like Primeape, rushing into range before attacking fiercely. It was faster, and its three heads gave it more ways to strike. After facing Primeape, however, Blaziken was ready for this style.

It did not need a Fire-type move. Using only Fighting techniques, Blaziken subdued Dodrio and gave the crowd a moment to remember.

Each of its claws seized one of Dodrio's outer heads. It pressed its right foot down on the middle head, holding all three in a finishing pin. Dodrio could not move.

Shizuko saw the danger and reached for her Poke Ball to recall it. Before she could lift her hand, Blaziken tightened its claws and foot. Dodrio fainted in its grip.

Camera flashes burst from every angle, preserving the sight. Two to zero. Blaziken alone had put Shizuko in a dangerous position.

Many spectators were stunned by Ethan's strength. Those who had bet on Shizuko were especially nervous. They had expected the more aggressive-looking Trainer to dominate; instead, she was the one being pushed back.

At least she still had four Pokemon she had not sent out. The rest of the match remained uncertain.

Chapter 782: Toyed With

Shizuko took out her third Poke Ball and sent out Houndoom.

After so many encounters with Team Magma and Team Aqua, Ethan knew Houndoom well enough to fight one with his eyes closed. He glanced at Blaziken. It was still in good condition and gave him a nod. Smiling, he left it on the field.

In the stands, Misty laughed. Looks like Ethan wants Blaziken to take down three in a row!

Ash and Morrison sat up. Sweeping three opponents was difficult, especially here. They had just fought their own match and knew how strong the Trainers in this round were. A sweep demanded the right field, favorable matchups, a Pokemon in good condition, and exceptional strength. It could happen in an early qualifier. Against stronger opponents later in the tournament, the challenge grew much greater.

Ash and Morrison had each knocked out two Pokemon with one of their own. Because their abilities were so close, neither had managed three.

Shizuko did not know if Ethan intended a sweep, but she felt slighted. Blaziken had already beaten two of her Pokemon. Did he think it could simply stay in and defeat another? Her anger rose, and her manner grew fiercer. When the round began, Ethan heard it in her louder commands.

A Pokemon battle was not decided by which Trainer sounded more imposing. It came down to the Pokemon's strength and condition.

Houndoom used the Rock Field's uneven terrain to circle Blaziken and search for a blind spot. Blaziken simply jumped onto a rock. From above, it could see Houndoom wherever it moved. The ambush was over before it began.

Shizuko changed tactics and had Houndoom attack from below. Blaziken's powerful kicks turned those approaches away, landing several blows of their own. She tried matching fire with fire instead. Flames heated the rocks red and split them apart, but they still could not overcome Blaziken.

Only then did Shizuko understand how difficult Ethan was to fight. It always felt as though she might win, yet every route was closed. She was being suppressed at every turn.

Houndoom could not break through and was in danger of falling. Shizuko took a deep breath, calmed herself, and hurriedly recalled it.

Ethan raised his brows as Houndoom vanished. From the way she battled, he had expected Shizuko to keep attacking until the bitter end. She knew when to switch after all. It was the right choice. If a Pokemon could not win, changing the lineup in time was better than waiting one move too long and regretting a knockout.

Shizuko opened another Poke Ball. Claydol appeared before Blaziken.

Many spectators, and even many Trainers, were unfamiliar with it. Claydol was a Ground and Psychic type that resembled a black figure molded from mud or clay. It stood about one and a half meters tall, with short limbs, many eyes, and mysterious markings across its dark body. It floated in midair, an eerie sight.

It was said to be a mysterious Pokemon born from clay dolls made by a flourishing ancient civilization twenty thousand years ago. According to one account, strange rays had brought those dolls to life. Another story held that ancient people had shaped them in imitation of something that fell from the sky.

Claydol moved by floating with psychic power and even slept while hovering. Its two detached arms flew under its mental control and could fire beams. Water would dissolve its body, so in rain it wrapped itself in psychic energy for protection.

Its types gave it a strong advantage over Blaziken. Ethan was skilled at fighting poor matchups, though, and did not recall his partner. Houndoom had taken a little more of Blaziken's stamina, but as long as it still wanted to fight, Ethan would trust it.

In the stands, Ash and Morrison disagreed about whether Blaziken could complete a three-Pokemon sweep now that it faced a type disadvantage.

That won't be easy, Morrison said, folding his arms. Blaziken has fought nearly three rounds already. Now it has to face something strong against it. It must be tired, however powerful it is. I don't think it can do it.

Ash privately agreed, but this was Ethan's Blaziken. He hesitated. I don't think Ethan can beat this one either. This... this...

Claydol, Max supplied, pushing up his glasses.

Right! Claydol. That's what I was about to say! Ash looked awkward and quickly went on. Ethan would be fine against another opponent, but Shizuko reached the main tournament. She's strong too. She won't give him the opening.

Misty snorted at their confident analysis and did not bother arguing. Did they really think Ethan fought at their level? How naive.

While the referee prepared the round, Ethan considered his approach. Ash and Morrison were right about one thing: Blaziken was tired, and this matchup was awkward. Its strength and fighting spirit had not faded, but it had fought many exchanges. Ethan's job was to turn that disadvantage into an opportunity.

The referee waved the flag. Ethan attacked first. Sitting back under pressure would only invite damage; he needed to seek an opening himself.

At his command, Blaziken ran through the Rock Field's complicated terrain, weaving among the stones as Houndoom had done. It gave Claydol no easy chance to catch it with Confusion.

Shizuko copied the answer Ethan had used against Houndoom. She sent Claydol higher into the air to attack from above.

But Blaziken was not Houndoom.

It fired Flamethrower into the sky. Flames engulfed Claydol and blocked Shizuko's view. At the same time, Blaziken sprang up level with Claydol and drove a kick into the center of the blaze.

Unable to see what lay beyond the fire, Shizuko chose caution. Rather than order a blind Teleport, she had Claydol shield itself with Confusion. A barrier seemed safer than appearing somewhere else only to be struck by Blaziken from an unseen direction. It could hold off the flames while she watched for the next move.

That was precisely the choice Ethan had hoped she would make. Claydol raised its psychic defense just before Flamethrower wrapped around it. Fire burned against the barrier but could advance no farther. The blast came quickly and faded quickly too. As it covered Claydol, its trailing flames were already dying away.

Shizuko looked to the place where Blaziken had fired and saw no sign of it. Where had it gone? She searched the open field and behind the rocks. Nothing.

Oh no. She looked up. Blaziken burst out of the flames and kicked Claydol's barrier.

The shield was strong enough to stop Flamethrower, but it was not unbreakable. After bearing the fire, it shattered under Blaziken's airborne kick. The kick continued through and hit Claydol itself.

Caught by surprise, Claydol flew backward. It lost its balance and crashed heavily to the ground. The force of the blow was plain to see. The spectators cheered. This was more like the spectacle they had wanted after the quieter opening rounds.

Amid the applause, Shizuko's face reddened. Ethan had predicted her thinking. She had been careless. Her careful defense had been broken by one brutal kick. Fortunately, it was a Fighting-type strike. Though strong enough to break the barrier, it dealt only half damage to Claydol itself.

Even so, the pressure on her grew. Blaziken could perform like this against a Pokemon that should counter it. How was she supposed to guard against every trick?

The battle had to continue. If Claydol could not beat Blaziken, Shizuko would be in real trouble. She ordered it to attack as soon as it recovered.

Psychic attacks came in quick succession. Despite its earlier success, Blaziken had to give ground and hide behind a rock. Claydol's type advantage began to show. It floated toward Blaziken's shelter, changing its attack angles and forcing it farther back into Ethan's half of the field. Soon Blaziken was near the boundary, with little room left to retreat.

Shizuko did not relax. She grew more cautious. And, just as she feared, Blaziken counterattacked when Claydol next used Confusion.

A hot Flamethrower swept over the space before Claydol. Remembering the last trick, Shizuko immediately ordered Teleport. Claydol moved back to a safe distance, preventing Blaziken from launching another attack from inside the flames.

It returned to Shizuko's half of the field. The fire died out. Blaziken did not follow. Puzzled, she looked down and found it standing exactly where it had been. It had done nothing else.

She had been fooled.

Before she could dwell on the mistake, Blaziken leaped back toward the middle of the field. It reclaimed all the ground Claydol had just forced it to surrender. One false attack had erased her progress and reset the battle.

What a frightening man.

Shizuko prepared to order Claydol forward again and drive Blaziken back to the boundary. This time she resolved not to retreat from another Flamethrower, even if Claydol had to take the hit. She would knock Blaziken out.

Ethan began his counterattack before she could speak.

As Blaziken's stamina fell, it seemed to find another reserve of power. Its steps quickened, and it ran toward Claydol faster than others of its kind.

The change in pace put Shizuko on alert. Ethan had beaten her first two Pokemon by changing the rhythm of the fight. Whatever Blaziken planned, she could not let it succeed.

Stop it! she shouted.

Claydol tried to catch Blaziken with Confusion. It had to aim, release the psychic force, and wait for it to reach the target. Blaziken was already gone by the time each attack arrived. Several tries missed. Claydol changed methods and used a Rock-type move to block its path.

Stones formed in the air and hurtled toward Blaziken.

Chapter 783: Like a Fish in Water

The stones were part of Rock Tomb, a move commonly used by Rock- and Ground-type Pokemon. Dozens of huge rocks fell around Blaziken and drove into the ground.

Shizuko had underestimated its speed. Blaziken easily dodged the first stones. As more fell, it had less room to move, but then it accelerated sharply. A few leaps carried it out of Rock Tomb's reach. It sprinted forward, jumped high, and slammed into Claydol with Quick Attack.

With the running start behind it, Blaziken reached its top speed. It was almost a streak of lightning. Claydol had no time to react before the hit landed.

Oh no. The thought had barely formed in Shizuko's mind when the attack succeeded. Blaziken was too fast for her to respond, let alone give a command. She had guarded against so much, yet it had found an opening.

Blaziken knocked Claydol to the ground again. This time it was close enough to prevent it from rising. Fire wound around Blaziken's claws, and it struck with Fire Punch.

Claydol shuddered in pain. Ethan ran through the moves it might know and narrowed his eyes. It looked as if Claydol meant to take Blaziken down with it. Don't give it the chance! he shouted.

Flames covered Blaziken's right leg. Before Claydol could carry out whatever it intended, Blaze Kick knocked it out.

The referee raised a flag. Claydol is unable to battle! Blaziken wins!

Ethan had won three rounds, bringing the match to intermission. He walked to the rest area to the sound of cheering. In the stands, Ash and the others applauded and marveled at him.

I can't believe Ethan really took down three with one Pokemon, Ash said. He admired Ethan sincerely, and the sight made him want to battle him again.

He's frightening, Morrison agreed. We're all among the final sixteen, and he beat three Pokemon with just one. If he keeps this up, he could win the whole tournament.

Actually, you're both counting wrong, Brock said. Ash turned to him in confusion.

Strictly speaking, Blaziken would have taken down four, Brock explained. If Shizuko hadn't recalled Houndoom at the last moment, it was only a few exchanges away from losing too.

Ash and Morrison realized he was right, which made the feat even more startling. Who could take down four opponents at this Conference with a Pokemon that was not even their ace? Only a Trainer far stronger than the rest of them.

In the rest area, Ethan leaned back in a chair and closed his eyes to conserve his energy. He had not been chasing a three- or four-Pokemon sweep. He had long since stopped needing a showy result to prove his strength or draw attention.

He had kept Blaziken out because most of his other Pokemon had already taken a turn in the Conference. His older partners had enjoyed the tournament atmosphere again, and none of the remaining opponents appeared as difficult as Tyson. He could now give his newer Pokemon experience.

More than anything, Blaziken's condition and determination had persuaded him to leave it in. But four rounds had drained much of its stamina and focus. The intermission had also broken its momentum. Ethan did not plan to send it out in the three rounds remaining after the break.

The rest period ended quickly. Before the match resumed, the field wheel spun as usual for the second half. Its pointer stopped on a frost symbol. Ethan and Shizuko would battle on the Ice Field.

Ice Field. Ethan rubbed his chin. Articuno was his only Ice-type Pokemon, so he could not draw on a type-based field advantage with the others. Blaziken might have melted the ice and created an unexpected opportunity, but after four rounds it was in no condition to return.

Who should he send out? Still considering it, he went back to the Trainer's area when called.

Both Trainers took their positions, and the referee waved the flag. Like Ethan, Shizuko did not immediately choose a Poke Ball. Her solemn face suggested that she too was struggling over her lineup.

Their concerns were different. Ethan had several newer Pokemon he could use and was weighing which suited the field best. Shizuko needed one that could withstand his attacks and perhaps win back a point.

Ethan chose first. At the referee's urging, Shizuko took out a Poke Ball too. Two flashes of blue light revealed their choices.

Shizuko had not brought back Houndoom. She sent out Piloswine, apparently leaving Houndoom in its ball to rest longer.

Ethan was not surprised. Piloswine might look heavy and clumsy, but it fought with the same headlong aggression as Primeape. In appearance it resembled a mix of a yak and a wild boar. Its Ice- and Ground-type body was covered in long brown hair, even over its face. Only its snout and two long tusks showed through.

That thick, long coat protected it from the cold. Its legs were short, but its broad, rough hooves kept it from slipping in snow. With hair obscuring its eyes, it often charged about blindly. Its sensitive nose still told it what was nearby. It was highly alert to sound, and its keen sense of smell could find mushrooms buried beneath frozen ground.
