That was why Ethan had compared it to Primeape. Both could attack with such relentless force that, once they caught an opponent, they would keep battering it. Ethan also knew that Piloswine had earned much of Shizuko's reputation at this Conference. It might not officially be her ace, but its strength was not far off.

Ethan's choice was Milotic. Fire for the first half, water for the second. That seemed fair enough. More to the point, Milotic had a favorable matchup against Piloswine on both offense and defense. Before the round began, the balance already leaned his way.

Shizuko's expression darkened. After so much thought, she had chosen a Pokemon that happened to be weak against his. Her bad position had become worse. She could only hope Milotic would be easier to handle than Blaziken.

To the crowd's cheers, the battle began. Three losses had not changed Shizuko's style. She ordered Piloswine to attack first.

Piloswine drove its four heavy hooves over the ice and charged with Take Down. Its approach shook the whole field. It could use ranged moves, but trading those attacks with Milotic would favor the Water type. Shizuko preferred to close in and win at short range. If Piloswine could reach Milotic, its weaker close-combat ability ought to leave it vulnerable despite its type advantage.

Ethan understood the plan. It was the best way to beat his Milotic. But reaching it would not be so simple.

Milotic fired a powerful Hydro Pump straight at Piloswine. Shizuko frowned and ordered it to change course. Against Water Gun she might have let Piloswine push through. Hydro Pump was far stronger. Even with its considerable stamina, Piloswine could not endure many hits from a move strong against it.

The detour left it farther from Milotic. Ethan smiled faintly. The blast had only grazed Piloswine's shaggy coat, but it had achieved what he wanted. He waved a hand, and Milotic fired another Hydro Pump.

Shizuko had to redirect Piloswine again. It covered more ground, but it was fast enough to reach Milotic's vicinity in spite of the delays.

Then Milotic slipped behind a large block of ice and vanished. Shizuko had Piloswine charge straight through rather than waste time going around. The solid block exploded into countless shards under its impact. Ice chips filled the air, but Milotic was nowhere to be seen.

What? Where had it gone?

Shizuko's first thought was that it had dug beneath the ice. Milotic was not Steelix, though. It could not use Dig. She scanned the field and found it gliding across the ice at an astonishing speed.

How was that possible? Only two or three seconds had passed since it hid behind the block, yet it had traveled more than twenty meters. Was it as fast as Blaziken?

Looking more closely, Shizuko saw a shallow sheet of water beneath Milotic's body. There was not much of it, but on the smooth ice it let Milotic move almost as though it were swimming. When had it put the water there?

The answer came to her at once: those two Hydro Pumps. So that was it. Ethan had planned this from the beginning.

Across the field, Ethan saw understanding dawn on her face and smiled.

The Ice Field was different from the Rock and Grass Fields. Water spilled across it would not soak into the ground, nor would it freeze immediately. For a while it stayed on the surface, making a broad, slippery film.

Most Pokemon would struggle to move on wetter ice. A Water type could use it to move smoothly, like a fish in water. If Ethan had no Ice-type Pokemon to exploit the field, he would turn it into a Water Field instead.

Hydro Pump's volume had made the plan possible. Water Gun would not have spread enough water. Piloswine might also have forced its way through the weaker attack, ruining the setup. Each part of the plan supported the next. That was why Ethan had chosen Hydro Pump.

Chapter 784: A Message to All of Hoenn!

In moments, Milotic followed the water across the ice into Shizuko's half of the field. All the effort she had put into closing the distance had been wasted. Worse, with the water still there, the same thing would happen again.

How had Ethan thought of it? Shizuko had to deal with the water first.

At her command, Piloswine drew a deep breath and blew Icy Wind over the puddles. The shallow water froze into a thin layer of ice at once.

An effective response! the announcer cried. However much water Milotic spreads, Piloswine can freeze it immediately! That isn't good news for Milotic. What will Ethan do now?

Ethan saw Shizuko relax a little and smiled. Did she think she had found the answer? It would not be that simple.

Milotic, use Rain Dance!

Milotic lifted its head and called to the sky. Clouds gathered across what had been a clear blue morning. A few low rumbles of thunder sounded, and rain began to fall steadily over the entire Ice Field. Rain Dance had taken effect.

Ethan looked back at Shizuko. Let's see how you answer this.

She stared up at the unending rain, her brows knotted. What could she do? She could clear the sky or wait for Rain Dance to end, but she had no way to stop the weather now. Piloswine could use Icy Wind until it wore itself thin and still fail to keep up.

Blizzard might disrupt the rain clouds for a while. Its effect would not last as long as Rain Dance, though. Once it ended, the rain would return, and nothing would have changed.

Fighting Milotic on this field was a poor choice. With a helpless shake of her head, Shizuko recalled Piloswine.

Shizuko has chosen to withdraw, the announcer said regretfully. She had a chance to close in on Milotic, but the rain has put an end to that plan. Who will she send out next? Ah, it's Swampert!

Swampert was the last of Shizuko's Pokemon that the crowd had yet to see. Bringing it out now suggested it was her first partner and perhaps her strongest.

Many Trainers saved their strongest Pokemon for the second half. They could conceal their strength, study the opponent, and choose a favorable matchup. Their ace could also steady the team and turn the match around when things went wrong.

Objectively, Shizuko had switched at the right time. Piloswine had barely been on the field and had taken no damage. If she had waited until it was as battered as Houndoom, she might have acted too late. Taking a hard lesson early had made her quicker to adapt.

Ethan did not switch. Milotic remained out to face Swampert, drawing Ash and the others' attention again.

Ethan isn't changing Pokemon this time either?

Is he trying for another three-Pokemon sweep?

Two Pokemon, each knocking out three opponents in a single match? That would take extraordinary confidence.

You're reading too much into it, Misty said before they could get carried away. Ethan is giving his Pokemon battle experience. He hasn't set a target for how many opponents each one has to beat.

Ash gave an embarrassed smile and sat up straight rather than argue with her.

Milotic and Swampert began to fight. Both were Water types, but Swampert was also a Ground type. Water-type attacks would be resisted, so it could use Ground moves to strike Milotic instead. How those moves would work on ice was another question.

The rain showed no sign of stopping. Spectators closest to the field even felt it dampen their clothes. Beneath the steady, moderate shower, the Pokemon skipped any cautious opening and went straight into a fierce exchange.

Both knew Water-type attacks would have limited effect and chose other moves. Swampert found mud somewhere and repeatedly hurled it with Mud Shot. Milotic answered with Twister, blowing the mud away.

When its ranged attacks failed, Swampert used all four limbs to run at Milotic for a close fight. Ethan had no reason to fear it. He did not counterattack at once, though. Milotic acted as if it could not match Swampert up close and slipped around the ice blocks, giving Shizuko that impression.

Once she grew less careful, Ethan gave the order. Milotic's Dragon Tail whipped into Swampert.

Smack! The heavy blow drove Swampert back several steps. Shizuko startled and stopped sending it so close. Privately, she cursed Ethan's cunning. He had this much strength and still used a little trick like that.

Ethan could not hear her thoughts. He only regretted that Swampert had become more cautious. If Shizuko had kept attacking as recklessly as she had in the first two rounds, he could have won easily. Now it would take more work.

As Swampert's attacks grew less aggressive, Milotic pressed forward. The balance of offense and defense shifted in a moment. Its smooth scales and long body made it more agile than Swampert on the rainy, slippery ice. Its attacks came from more varied angles and were harder to avoid.

Swampert still had two arms, an advantage over Milotic in a close fight. But that advantage did not last.

Milotic dodged an Iron Tail, slid in like a snake, and caught Swampert at the right moment. Its long body coiled tightly around it with Wrap. As Milotic squeezed, Swampert's face reddened.

Oh no! Shizuko cried. She had been so careful, yet Ethan had found an opening again. Swampert, break free!

That was easier said than done. Swampert stood a meter and a half tall. Ethan's fully grown Milotic measured 6.2 meters when its snake-like body was stretched out. Its length gave it an advantage. Swampert might have had greater raw strength, but Milotic had bound its arms and legs together, leaving it no room to use them.

Swampert kept struggling. At last it pulled one arm free and tried to push Milotic away. Rain slicked Milotic's already smooth scales. No matter how Swampert tried, its hand could find no grip.

Time passed. Its strength drained away under the pressure, until it felt as though the bones throughout its body might be crushed.

Swampert! Shizuko saw that leaving it there meant certain defeat. She raised its Poke Ball to recall it. Red light flashed toward Swampert, but Milotic shifted and blocked the beam with its back. The light could not reach Swampert, so the recall failed.

Shizuko's face changed. Ethan lowered his gaze. It's over. Milotic, finish it.

Milotic lifted its tail over Swampert. Realizing what was coming, Swampert struggled harder. It even spat water at the tail, hoping to knock it away. But a Water-type attack would do little to another Water type, and Milotic simply twisted aside.

Violet light spread across its tail. In one smooth movement, Milotic loosened its coils and brought the tail down with Dragon Tail.

Smack! Swampert had no time to react. The blow landed squarely on its head and knocked it unconscious.

Swampert is unable to battle! Milotic wins!

As the referee raised the flag, Shizuko felt cold all over. Her strongest Pokemon had fallen. What hope did she have now? Her two remaining Pokemon both had poor matchups against Milotic.

The rest went as she feared. She sent Piloswine out again, then Houndoom. Milotic defeated both with ease. Shizuko lost so completely that she never even saw Ethan's third Pokemon.

The defeat shook her. For a moment she doubted whether she had deserved a place in the main tournament at all, or whether she was truly as strong as people had said.

Ethan, by contrast, stood amid a tremendous roar from the crowd. With two Pokemon, each taking down three opponents, he had sent all of Hoenn a message about who was strongest at the Ever Grande Conference. He had not set out to make that statement, but the result spoke for him.

Seeded favorites and dark horses alike had fallen easily before him. Only now did the crowd fully grasp what kind of Trainer Ethan was.

He had drawn less attention before because his victories looked almost too simple, with none of the dramatic swings that helped an audience judge a contest. By beating a highly regarded competitor from the previous round even more easily, he finally made everyone look at him.

He had the image and the skill. Opinion shifted at once. Calls for him to take the championship rose louder than ever.

Judging by his performance and control of the tournament, people no longer wondered whether he could win. They wondered who his final opponent would be and how he would defeat them. They had seen enough of the remaining Trainers to know their abilities. None seemed his equal. None even appeared capable of threatening him.

The main tournament had run for only two rounds, and only a few quarterfinalists had been decided. Yet across those rounds, Ethan had used eight Pokemon. Every one of them had overpowered its opponents without a single loss. Other Trainers' matches looked pale beside his. He was the only competitor still unbeaten, and he seemed far ahead of the field.

Unless he placed a bet and manipulated the result himself, or performed disastrously in the final rounds, the crowd could not imagine anyone defeating him.

Ethan waved calmly to the cheering spectators and walked into the competitors' tunnel.

From the same spot behind the same window, Goodshow watched him go. The old man's face seemed to have aged another decade.

John drew on his cigarette and stepped beside him with a bitter smile. Public opinion has turned. We can't stop his rise now. It looks as though the championship is his.

Goodshow said nothing. After a pause, John asked, What will you do? Keep arranging the strongest possible opponents for him?

Only a helpless sigh answered him.

Chapter 785: Ethan Advances, Ash Is Eliminated

Ethan left the competitors' tunnel and immediately spotted Ash and the others waiting outside. They applauded as he appeared. Misty had even found a bouquet of flowers to give him.

What's all this? Ethan laughed helplessly. You're making such a fuss, you'd think I'd already won the championship.

Max was at an age when he could not keep his excitement to himself, even with Ash and Morrison standing beside him. Ethan, you were amazing! Nobody could touch you! Two Pokemon, and each one beat three opponents! You should have seen the stands when you won. The crowd practically exploded!

Ash and Morrison looked uncomfortable. Nobody could touch you included them. They knew Ethan might be stronger, but Max did not have to say it in front of them. Morrison was already out, but Ash had reached the final eight and might still face Ethan. Max sounded certain Ash would lose.

Even so, they could not deny Ethan's performance. Neither of them could have achieved that result in his place.

You're exaggerating, Ethan said with a wave and a smile. I wouldn't call myself unbeatable. But at this Conference, I don't think anyone can stop me from taking the title.

Ash and Morrison fell silent. Was that any different from what Max had said? They had expected a little humility. Instead, Ethan had agreed with him.

Morrison glanced at Ash. He had been eliminated and could do nothing about Ethan's confidence; perhaps Ash would challenge it. But Ash only clenched his fists and, unusually for him, said nothing.

Why was he letting that pass? Morrison knew Ash fairly well, but he did not understand what Ethan meant to him.

Had another Trainer announced that he would win the Conference in front of Ash, Ash would have argued. Ethan was both a rival and someone Ash trusted deeply. The impression Ethan had made over their long acquaintance was so strong that Ash believed anyone capable of beating him and taking the championship would have to be Ethan. In his mind, it ought to be Ethan.

By the end of the day, all eight quarterfinalists had been decided. Beyond Ethan and Ash, there were six Trainers the group had neither met on their travels nor had a chance to get to know here.

Though all eight had reached the same stage, they received very different treatment. Reporters swarmed Ethan like sharks catching the scent of blood. Cameras crowded toward his face. The other seven could not find a single interviewer. Ash was standing right beside Ethan, yet the reporters ignored him and pushed him aside.

That's frightening, May said. They were only at the final eight. Why had everyone rushed him already?

Misty and Brock were used to it. They had seen this at both the Silver and Indigo Conferences. It's their job, Misty said with a shrug. Of course they can smell a story. Wait until you see what happens after a final. That's frightening.

At the center of the crowd, Ethan felt the reporters' eager attention more sharply than anyone. He was prepared. He announced that he had already promised exclusive interviews to Lumiose Publishing House and TV Mauville, declined every other request, and let tournament security escort him away.

Those interviews could serve as his shield. TV Mauville's staff could deal with the disappointed reporters from here.

...

The next round's pairings appeared that evening. Every competitor except Ethan felt the weight of the moment. Nobody wanted to become the stepping-stone for someone so strong. Eight Trainers would be divided into four pairs, and one unlucky person had to face him. Even those who avoided him now might meet him in the following round. The danger could only be delayed.

They had reached the final eight, yet some felt as worried about elimination as they had in the qualifiers.

The hall that had once been packed with competitors now held only a handful. Ethan and Ash stood together. The others kept their distance from one another, wary of potential opponents and perhaps afraid of revealing too much.

At precisely seven o'clock, the big screen updated. The tension was so sharp that everyone seemed afraid to breathe. Even Ash swallowed hard and clasped his hands. May, Max, and their friends caught the mood. Morrison was sweating as though he himself had a match ahead.

The display changed to show the pairings. Before Ethan could read it, someone cheered from across the hall. Beside him, Ash's shoulders relaxed, and he let out a long breath.

Ethan looked up. His portrait stood first in the top row. Opposite it was a man not yet twenty, with spiky hair and upturned eyes. Across the hall, the man scratched his head. His face crumpled, and he silently cursed his luck. Why did he have to draw Ethan?

Ethan found Ash's pairing next. Ash would face a blue-haired girl. That result would be interesting to watch.

Back on Earth, some viewers of the anime had said that Ash's loss to Tyson was forced by the plot and that, without Tyson, he would certainly have reached the final four. Ethan had defeated Tyson himself. Now that Ash faced someone else, Ethan would see whether Ash's present strength could carry him through.

...

Sableye is down! Metagross wins! The winner of this match is Ethan!

The announcer's call rose over the cheers of the audience and the applause of Ethan's friends. Ethan had won another clean six-to-zero match. In the day's opening battle, he had again looked untouchable.

He had used four Pokemon. In the first two rounds, he sent out Gardevoir and Gengar and let them have a turn. Both won with ease, giving their opponents almost no chance to answer. Gardevoir simply overpowered its opponent, even through a type disadvantage.

Gengar was more merciless. It toyed with its opponent until the poor Pokemon was exhausted. It even blocked the opposing Trainer's Poke Ball with its power before ending the fight, looking thoroughly satisfied.

Eevee and Metagross handled the remaining four rounds, winning two apiece. Neither produced another three-Pokemon sweep, and they were less showy than Blaziken and Milotic had been, but both performed well.

Overall, today's opponent was at most as strong as Shizuko. He had caused Ethan little trouble. Ethan was through to the final four.

The match had been one-sided, yet the crowd enjoyed it. Calls for Ethan to take the championship only grew louder. He needed to defeat just two more opponents to lift the Ever Grande Conference trophy.

There were four matches scheduled that day. Ash's was next. After his own match, Ethan went directly to the stands and took Ash's seat rather than leave the stadium.

Ash's face was tense and heavy with thought. This was different from how he had felt against Morrison. He had reached the final eight before and challenged for a place in the final four before, but he had never made it. Now he had another chance, and that carried its own pressure.

Win, and he would set a new personal record. Lose, and he would repeat the old result.

From his Trainer's area, Ash looked up at the ceremonial flame. Its light seemed to kindle a fire in his own eyes.

Wait for me, Ethan. I'll beat my opponent and come challenge you.

...

Pikachu is down! The score is now four to five, and Ash is in trouble! All he has left is a badly worn Grovyle. Can he turn this around?

Sweat ran down Ash's cheek beneath the announcer's ringing voice. Pikachu had failed to win again, leaving him in a desperate position. He carried Pikachu back, gritted his teeth, and threw his last Poke Ball. Grovyle appeared, panting.

The announcer was right about its condition. Its strength was nearly spent, and wounds covered its body. It looked as though it might fall without another attack. But it was Ash's last Pokemon.

This opponent had been too difficult. In strength and performance, she held a slight edge over Ash. It felt like facing Morrison at his best, perhaps an even harder fight.

Ash had been under pressure throughout. Glalie and Swellow had each traded themselves for one of her Pokemon. Pikachu, Torkoal, and Corphish had achieved nothing and been knocked out in succession.

Only Grovyle had turned the tide for a while. It had fought far beyond its usual limits, giving perhaps two hundred percent to defeat two Pokemon despite taking severe damage. That had brought the score to where it stood now. With Pikachu down after only one round of rest for Grovyle, it had to return, exhausted, and somehow seek one more win for Ash.

This is bad, Brock said. His eyes were wide, but he could see no route back for Ash.

It is, Ethan agreed, shaking his head. If Grovyle were fresh, perhaps Ash could win. In this condition, one hit might finish it, and his opponent still has two Pokemon she hasn't revealed. Even I can't see a way out.

A Tackle, or even a resisted Water Gun, could be enough. What could Grovyle do with so little left? It had already given everything. If its teammates had been stronger, if Pikachu had fought better, perhaps Ash would not be here. But there was no changing those rounds now.

Ethan had thought Ash might surpass his old result without Tyson in the tournament. It seemed too early for him. Against Morrison, he had barely won even after Morrison gave away two rounds. Against someone still harder to beat, Ash had done well to get this far, but he remained a little inexperienced. His lineup was not strong enough either.

With the Ash of his Kalos, Alola, or Galar years, Ethan thought, this match would have ended in a wide victory. He shook his head and looked back to the field.

Ash's opponent sent out her next Pokemon. Blue light flashed, and Typhlosion appeared before Grovyle.

Everyone who cared about Ash felt their hopes sink. Ash's own eyes dimmed. His last Pokemon could scarcely stand, and now it faced a Fire type strong against it. Ash had not lost his will to fight. He simply understood that he had no way to turn this around.

The referee lowered the flags, and the round began. No miracle came. Typhlosion breathed fire. Grovyle could not even dodge before the flames covered it.

So Ash had lost after all. Ethan shook his head again, sorry for him. When the fire cleared, Grovyle lay motionless. Ash's journey through the Ever Grande Conference was over.

Chapter 786: The Final

Ethan and the others left the stands and waited by the competitors' tunnel. At last Ash came out, his shoulders low and his steps heavy.

Seeing his face, Max and May swallowed the words of encouragement they had prepared. He looked too downhearted for any of it.

Ethan was about to speak when Misty strode past him. Though she was only ten, she walked with the force of someone much older. Everyone turned toward her. With a stern face, she raised her right hand and swung it at Ash's cheek.

What? The others stared. Ash froze in shock, too startled even to dodge.

Misty's palm stopped a few centimeters from his face. She had not struck him after all.

M-Misty, what are you doing? Ash asked. With her temper, he had thought she might really slap him.

There, she said, narrowing her eyes. You can make another expression. I thought you'd left your spirit on the field.

Ash flushed. I... I was just...

Just what? You lost. Why wear that miserable face? So you were eliminated. Your skills weren't enough this time. If that's the problem, work harder and try again!

Perhaps a sharp remedy was what he needed. Under Misty's blunt words, Ash's face went from embarrassed red to angry purple and then back to normal. His gloom faded with it. Max and the others breathed easier. May even gave Misty a quiet thumbs-up. Only Misty would have dared to do that.

She's right, Ash. Cheer up, Morrison added. Remember how you talked to me yesterday? Why are you the one falling apart now?

Ash stared for a moment. He was behaving exactly as Morrison had after his own loss. If Morrison could recover, why couldn't he? Ash let his disappointment and frustration go with a sigh. Light returned to his eyes, and he nodded to them.

You're right. One defeat doesn't decide everything. My journey is only beginning! Next time, I won't stop at the final eight.

That's the Ash we know, Max said with a grin.

...

With Ash eliminated, Ethan was the only one of their group still in the tournament. Calling him a lone seedling hardly fit. He was more like a great tree, sturdy and towering, sweeping aside opponents as he dominated the Ever Grande Conference.

Next came the semifinal. By coincidence, Ethan drew the blue-haired young woman who had eliminated Ash. He avenged his friend with another easy six-to-zero win. He seemed unstoppable.

Ash's feelings were complicated. He had given everything and failed to beat her. Against Ethan, she could not knock out even one Pokemon. The gap between him and Ethan was dispiritingly wide. They had not fought each other since the Silver Conference, but he could see how much more he still needed to improve.

Having won the semifinal, Ethan was first through to the final. He waited to see who would emerge from the other match.

The two Trainers there fought under a peculiar strain. Both wanted to win, advance, and claim the greater honor. Both dreaded what advancing meant: facing Ethan. Would they reach the final only to be easily beaten in front of everyone? Yet neither could bear to fall one step short. They fought with that conflict hanging over them.

In the end, a Trainer named Hua proved a little stronger and reached the final. He had earned a place opposite Ethan, though his feelings about it were mixed.

When spectators compared their performances, most shook their heads. The gap looked too large. Nearly everyone expected Ethan to win the title easily. Only the most reckless gamblers would stake everything on Hua.

The semifinals were followed by a rest day. Under the Conference's arrangements, Ethan and Hua each filmed promotional material for the final. Publicity spread across Hoenn. The Pokemon League wanted even remote towns, isolated islands, and sparsely inhabited deserts to hear the news and have a reliable signal to watch.

Online support matched the opinion in the stadium: ninety-seven percent for Ethan and three for Hua. Ethan led by 152.78 million votes. In image, presence, and strength, the two scarcely seemed comparable. It might have been the most lopsided show of support in Ever Grande Conference history.

The public seemed to agree on one thing: Ethan winning would be the natural result.

After a busy half day, Ethan began receiving calls. Sabrina, Erika, Maya, Professor Cerise's family, and people calling from Kalos all contacted him. So did Anabel, Looker, Lance, Clair, Lisia, and many others close to him, whether by phone or message.

Some could not cross the sea to Hoenn because of work or distance. Others had their own reasons for missing the final in person. They all wished him well and would follow the match on television.

Their blessings and reminders warmed Ethan. This was what it felt like to have people care about him. Without noticing how it happened, he had made so many friends in this worldand girlfriends too.

He had formed ties here that mattered deeply. If he were ever offered a return to his old world, he would hate to leave. He thought he would refuse. Too much of his life was here now for him to let go.

...

After a night's rest, Ethan's strength and focus had returned. The final battle arrived.

Salutes thundered. Balloons and streamers rose from the stands. Before the match, Pokemon League President Goodshow spoke beside the ceremonial flame. He thanked the staff, then the Trainers for their efforts. The announcer stirred up the crowd, and at last the finalists entered through opposite tunnels under thousands of eyes.

Ethan waved to the cheering spectators as he walked calmly to his Trainer's area. Hua looked far more nervous. It was his first final, and the cheers for Ethan were overwhelming. He had prepared himself as well as he could, but everything beyond the field seemed against him.

He knew the crowd thought he could not beat Ethan. He ought to use their doubt as fuel, to prove them wrong... but even he suspected he was no match for this man. He could only give it everything he had.

The announcer gave both finalists a grand introduction. The field wheel began to turn. Hua watched tensely; Ethan barely reacted. The first-half field was the Grass Field.

It was a fairly even setting. Fish and jellyfish Pokemon could not fight there, but most others had room to show their strength. For Hua, that was welcome news.

At the referee's signal, both Trainers took out Poke Balls. The cheering climbed to its peak. Hua made no move to throw his, so Ethan sent his out first.

Blue light flashed. Blaziken appeared, and the crowd shouted itself hoarse for the Pokemon that had swept three opponents in the previous round.

Hua's face fell. He remembered what Blaziken had done to Shizuko. He had not been on the receiving end, but putting himself in her place was enough to make him feel trapped. While studying the recording, he had tried several tactical simulations with both Shizuko's team and his own. None had changed the outcome.

Was he about to experience the same thing? What a way to start the final.

At least he had expected Blaziken might lead. The Poke Ball in his hand held a Pokemon it could not counter easily. He threw it, and his partner appeared.

It's Slowbro! the announcer cried. Hua has opened with a Slowbro he hasn't shown in any previous match! He's kept a surprise for the final!

So that was his plan. Ethan smiled. Slowbro was a Water and Psychic type. Both Blaziken's Fire- and Fighting-type attacks would deal only half damage. As a type matchup, it was a sound choice. Hua had brought a Water type onto a Grass Field because he had correctly guessed Ethan would open with Blaziken.

Whatever Hua's chances, that preparation was worthy of a finalist. Ethan was measuring him by his own standards. By ordinary standards, Hua was very strong. If Ash had faced him, Ethan would have given Ash only about a forty percent chance to win. Yet Hua still stood opposite Ethan feeling that victory was distant.

Slowbro's appearance made the match more interesting. As Slowpoke's other evolution alongside Slowking, it might look vacant and slow, but it was no easy opponent. Its Water and Psychic types gave it many ways to attack.

Slowbro was pink and walked on two legs. Its head resembled Slowpoke's, and a cream-colored stripe crossed its belly. A spiral-shelled Shellder clung to its tail. Its appearance suggested several real animals: an otter, a hippopotamus, even a platypus.

Standing upright, it had longer limbs than Slowpoke. Slowpoke evolved into Slowbro when a Shellder bit its tail while it was hunting in the sea. The sweet taste seeping from the tail entranced Shellder. Greedy for more of that flavor, it refused to let go and even changed its shell into a spiral shape as it kept feeding.

According to observations, if the Shellder fell off during a fierce battle, or if the tail was severed and the Shellder came away, Slowbro would revert to Slowpoke.

Slowbro's reactions were sluggish, but that could also help it. Toxins from the Shellder on its tail dulled its sense of pain. It could be struck and only slowly realize what had happened. That delay might let it keep fighting a little longer.

It sounded like a minor trait. In the right moment, those extra seconds could turn a battle around.

Chapter 787: A Champion's Chant Across the Stadium

Blaziken and Slowbro began their battle. Hua went all out from the start, hoping to take control immediately. If he could suppress Blaziken before it found its rhythm, perhaps he could avoid the fate of Ethan's earlier opponents.

Hua had set himself a modest goal. If he could survive the first round without losing, he would count the final as a victory in his own mind. Ethan would no longer be unbeaten, and Hua could feel that he had earned his place here, even if he eventually lost.

He had a plan. Ethan had no intention of giving him that opening. Ethan had not set out to win the Conference without losing a Pokemon, but after coming this far against opponents who had not seriously threatened him, he saw no reason to let the chance go. Why not finish as well as he could? No one in the last several Ever Grande Conferences had won the title without losing a round. Perhaps he could be the first in years.

With their different aims, the Trainers ordered their Pokemon forward. Hua did not hold anything back for later. Slowbro fired Confusion and Water Gun in an unbroken barrage, determined to bring Blaziken down.

The type advantage made even Blaziken withdraw from those attacks for the moment. It was a direct, effective plan, and Ethan had no immediate way through. Invisible psychic force and long streams of water swept across the Grass Field. Blaziken ran swiftly among the thick grass, dodging them.

Seeing it forced to move, Hua grew more excited. Few Trainers had managed to put Ethan under pressure in this Conference. Even a temporary advantage gave Hua hope of winning the first round.

Then he began to notice the problem. Blaziken was too fast and could keep running for too long. Its legs moved so quickly it seemed to fly across the grass. Slowbro had not hit it once, while each failed attack drained Slowbro's stamina and energy.

The tall weeds hid Blaziken's orange-red form as it flashed past. Slowbro's small eyes lost track of it more than once. Without Hua's warnings, Blaziken might already have come up behind it. Hua realized the round would not be as easy as he had hoped.

Ethan saw that moment of hesitation.

He was bold but attentive, patient enough to read an entire battle and quick to catch a small opening. Once Hua gave him one, Ethan acted at once. Blaziken ducked under another Water Gun without slowing, then sprang high out of the grass toward Slowbro.

No! Hua saw the sudden change. Slowbro's ranged attacks and type advantage had held Blaziken back, but its close-range fighting was weak. Letting Blaziken reach it could be disastrous.

Don't let it close in! Use Psychic!

It was a sensible order. Psychic could hurt Blaziken and push it away to restore the distance. But Blaziken's leap was a feint. Halfway across, it dropped suddenly back into the grass. Psychic passed through the space it had occupied and vanished harmlessly.

As soon as it landed, Blaziken used Quick Attack. It raced low over the ground toward Slowbro, faster than before. The leap had drawn out Hua's defense and made him aim at an attack from the air. This was Ethan's real change of pace.

Hua's mistake had consequences. Only a second or two had passed, but that was enough in a battle. He could not give Slowbro a new order in time.

Blaziken's legs blurred. It was not usually known as one of the fastest Pokemon, but natural talent and Ethan's training had given it remarkable speed. It might not match the very fastest, yet ordinary Pokemon could hardly keep up with its footwork. It crossed more than ten meters in a blink.

Before Slowbro could react, Blaziken reached its round pink face. It lowered its head, raised a shoulder, and drove into that face with the force of Quick Attack.

Bang! Quick Attack was not a Fighting-type move, and Blaziken's speed made the impact severe. Slowbro rolled backward for more than ten meters before stopping just short of the boundary.

Slowbro! Hua cried. The blow had happened too quickly for him to respond. At least his Pokemon had not gone out of bounds.

Slowbro still lay there, staring blankly, while Blaziken turned and charged again. Get up! Hua shouted.

Slowbro's sluggishness was showing its other side. It lay motionless, a huge question mark almost visible over its head. It seemed not to know how it had ended up on the ground.

Don't just lie there! Blaziken is right behind you! Hua called, growing frantic.

That delayed response could be a double-edged sword. At times, it let Slowbro keep fighting after a hit and create a comeback. Now it held Slowbro back. Most Pokemon would already be on their feet. Hua could shout all he liked; Slowbro was still trying to understand what had happened.

Blaziken did not give it time to recover. Fire and Fighting moves were resisted, but they were not its only weapons. Its sharp claws were part of its body and useful weapons in their own right.

Blaziken reached Slowbro and raked its back with one claw. Then it used Slash, striking a vulnerable spot precisely.

Slowbro's face suddenly twisted with pain. The pain did not come from the fresh claw marks. The earlier shoulder blow had finally registered in its brain. It rolled on the ground, too distressed to get up and fight back.

Ethan would not miss the chance. First he had Blaziken position itself between Slowbro and Hua, preventing a recall beam from reaching it. Then another Slash struck Slowbro's head and finished the round.

Slowbro is unable to battle! Blaziken wins!

The referee raised the flag. Hua's hope of taking even one round from Ethan had failed. The crowd cheered.

Ash applauded too. Ethan is incredible at finding an opening. Hua made one small mistake, and Ethan beat him for it.

And Blaziken did it without relying on Fire or Fighting moves, Max added, adjusting his glasses. It's so fast, too.

Brock smiled. More than raw power, look at its speed compared with other Blaziken. It was quick to begin with, and Ethan's training has developed that strength. It's becoming a fast attacker. That's why its speed has stood out so much in these recent matches.

Fast attacker. May quietly remembered the phrase, though it had little to do with being a Coordinator. It made her think of her own Combusken. Lately she had felt it nearing a breakthrough. Soon it might evolve into Blaziken, and she could not help looking forward to what kind of Pokemon it would become. Might it have a talent for speed like Ethan's?

Since becoming a Coordinator, May had recognized many gaps in her skills. Appeals were a matter of ideas and cooperation with her Pokemon. The bigger challenge was battling. She traveled with Ash, but she could neither imitate his style nor learn much from it.

Combusken was her first Pokemon. With Ethan's Blaziken as an example, May had hopes for it. She had seen enough of Ethan's battles to know how strong he was. Traveling with him might improve her own battling as well. She could help Misty keep an eye on Ethan and gain something for herself too.

On the field, Hua recalled Slowbro with reluctance. It was the surprise he had prepared for Blaziken and had abilities it never got to use. The loss drained his spirits. Looking up, he saw that Ethan was not switching Pokemon either. He sighed. Why was the thing he feared most happening again?

Whether he had lost his nerve or decided that struggling would change nothing, Hua fought the second round without the drive he had shown in the first. He still ordered attacks, but Ethan could feel the difference.

Hua sent out Tauros. Without Slowbro's type advantage to protect it, Tauros met Blaziken's fire. Flames burst from Blaziken's mouth and, soon after the opening exchange, stray blasts ignited the surrounding grass. Fire spread quickly across the field.

Tauros was caught with nowhere to flee. When the flames died, it lay on the ground, blackened. Spectators nearby could even smell scorched beef.

Its chest still rose and fell faintly. At least its life was not in danger. Hua caught himself thinking that and stopped. Why at least again? He had worried about the same thing in the previous round.

Tauros had fallen easily, but Hua did get one piece of good news: Ethan recalled Blaziken afterward. There would be no second three-Pokemon sweep from it.

Hua felt relieved, then ashamed of that relief. He had come to fight for the championship. Why did a simple switch by his opponent feel like an achievement? He felt pathetic.

Nobody else saw him as a fool. Most spectators had expected this result before the final began. What they were seeing only confirmed it.

Champion!

Champion!

Champion!

The second round had barely ended, and the third Pokemon had yet to appear, but voices rolled through the stadium like a rising wave. At first the chants were uneven. Within seconds, they found one rhythm and echoed above the field.

Chapter 788: Champion

In the rounds that followed, Ethan gave Milotic, Metagross, and Eevee a turn in the final.

Objectively, Hua was a capable Trainer. He might have been somewhat weaker than Tyson, but not by much. He could never have fought his way to the final otherwise.

On another day, without bringing in partners such as Jolteon and Tyranitar, Ethan would have needed more time to beat him with the Pokemon he had used here. But Hua had lost his nerve. His attacks weakened, his defense fell apart, and in that state he could not threaten Ethan.

It was a pity. Hua had reached the final without the confidence to match. He had let fear put him behind before the battle began, and the weight of the occasion had badly affected his performance.

Steven or Ash would not have been shaken this much in his place. Not everyone had their temperament, though. Hua was an ordinary Trainer in his first final. Drawing Ethan might have been the worst luck of his life.

Champion!

Champion!

Champion!

Gardevoir came out last as Ethan's safety net and defeated the final opponent with ease. The championship battle was over.

We have a new Ever Grande Conference champion! the announcer shouted. He had to strain his voice to rise above the stadium. Nearly hoarse, he cried, Ethan defeats Hua six to zero! Let's congratulate the champion who dominated his way here and set a record: Ethan!

The stands erupted again. The sound seemed to swallow everything else, until all Ethan could hear was the roar of the crowd.

This was what it meant to be the public's choice. Ethan had fought flawlessly, commanding his matches so completely that he had won over the audience as well as his opponents. Their cheers answered him.

Standing in his Trainer's area, Ethan felt his ears ring. He had won two Conferences before. Apart from Tyson, he had faced few strong opponents this time, and many battles had felt one-sided. Still, the sight before him stirred him deeply.

No wonder so many Trainers pursued a championship their whole lives. Being praised by thousands like this was intoxicating.

Hua came over with admiration on his face and held out a hand. Congratulations. You deserve this championship. I lost, and I have no complaints.

He meant it. Losing to someone else would have left him full of regret, wishing he had performed better. Against Ethan, the gap was so large that frustration gave way to reluctant respect.

Ethan shook his hand. You're strong too. You didn't win this time, but I believe you can reach your goal in the next Conference.

Hua had been unlucky and lucky at once. Meeting Ethan in the final had given him no real chance to compete and made him one of the most thoroughly beaten finalists. Yet without Ethan eliminating Tyson, Hua would not have reached the final at all. Ethan had opened the way for him and then closed it himself.

After a brief exchange, Hua stepped back and joined the applause. Ethan waved to the audience for more than a minute before they went to the podium together.

There Ethan met Pokemon League President Goodshow again. The old man's face was complicated. Congratulations on winning another Conference.

If anyone in the stadium had hoped Ethan would fail, it was Goodshow. Ethan heard the lack of warmth in his voice and smiled. Thank you. Don't worry. I'll keep working hard and try to win the next region's Conference too!

The words struck Goodshow like a knife. His smile froze. That was precisely what he least wanted to hear. Ethan planned to enter another region's tournament?

Goodshow forced an awkward smile. He would not reveal his feelings on the podium. He moved on to Hua and the third-place Trainer, whose placing had been decided the day before, shook their hands, and offered encouragement.

When Goodshow stepped aside, the three Trainers accepted trophies from the ceremony attendants in turn and waved to the audience before the ceremonial flame. Salutes boomed. Streamers and balloons filled the air. The whole stadium was wrapped in celebration.

At last Ethan posed for a photograph with his entire championship team. The Ever Grande Conference had officially ended.

It was finally over. From his first steps on Hoenn soil to this moment, this journey had reached its conclusion.

Ethan left through the competitors' tunnel and found reporters waiting backstage. They surrounded him in layers and gave him no chance to slip away. This time he could not avoid them. He answered several questions, and only when they were satisfied did he escape to the rest area.

Ash and the others greeted him with more congratulations.

Ethan, congratulations on your third Conference trophy!

Congratulations, Champion!

Misty returned his phone. It had hardly stopped ringing since his victory. In little more than ten minutes, messages had poured in from nearly everyone who could contact him. There were too many to answer now. He could thank them that evening.

For the moment, there was a familiar tradition to observe after a championship: a celebratory meal. Ash had been looking forward to it more than anyone. Ever since Ethan entered the rest area, he had been asking when they could go eat.

...

The Conference ended, but its excitement lingered. People kept discussing the matches that had stayed with them. Ethan and his friends had other plans.

Trainers did not stay still. After one night of celebration, Ethan and Ash gathered their things and prepared to set out again. Their destination was the Battle Frontier in Kanto.

The Battle Frontier consisted of seven private battle facilities outside the Pokemon League's control, gathered within one region. They were rather like privately run Gyms. Each facility had its own leader, a Frontier Brain. Defeating one earned a Frontier Symbol, and a challenger needed the first six Symbols before qualifying to face the seventh facility.

Private did not mean amateur. The facilities were well equipped, and every Frontier Brain was formidable. Some had exceptionally rare Pokemon and were stronger than most Gym Leaders, perhaps even comparable to the Elite Four. The Battle Frontier was less famous than the Pokemon League, but it was a powerful group.

Ash had learned about it from Ethan and was instantly interested. He had already planned to return to Kanto. Now he wanted to challenge the Frontier as soon as possible.

Ethan was in no hurry to enter another region after the Ever Grande Conference. The Frontier gave him a reason to revisit Kanto, and he could escort Misty home along the way.

Only Max needed to leave the group and return to his family's home in Petalburg City. He hated parting from Ash and Brock, but after traveling for so long, he knew he had to see his parents. When he turned to May, however, his sister avoided his eyes.

Um... May rubbed her cheek awkwardly. You'll have to go home without me. I need to visit Kanto too.

What? Max stared. You're going to Kanto?

May and Misty had kept their agreement quiet. The others were not particularly observant either. Apart from the two girls, nobody knew May had agreed to travel with Ethan next. Even her brother was learning only now that she would not go home with him.

Ethan, Ash, and Brock were surprised too, but none pressed her. They had seen May and Misty's friendship grow. If Misty was going home, it seemed natural that May might want to visit her there.

Max could not accept that his sister was leaving him to return alone. What do you need to do in Kanto?

May glanced guiltily at Misty and searched for an excuse. Misty pulled her behind her and lifted her chin at Max.

It's between girls. Why do you need every detail?

Max could challenge his sister, but he had no courage to argue with Misty. Still, he could hardly believe he would be going home by himself.

But Mom and Dadwill they even agree?

Misty cut him off with a wave. That's for us to handle. I'll explain it to your parents myself. Don't worry. I'll bring your sister back to you safe and sound.

Max looked at May one last time. She gave him an apologetic smile. He could only sigh.

Early the next morning, they went to the harbor at Ever Grande City. Ethan's group had originally planned to take Max home first and sail for Kanto from Petalburg. Morrison offered to handle that part instead.

You all go straight from here. I'll take Max home.

Are you sure? May asked, embarrassed.

Of course! Morrison laughed. I'm glad I met you all and glad we're friends. I can't go with you to Kanto, but I can do this one last thing for you.

Ash and the others were moved. Even Ethan thought Ash had made a truly good friend.

Max was less enthusiastic. He and Morrison did not have much to talk about, and he imagined a dull journey back to Petalburg. He wanted to refuse, but Morrison meant well and May seemed to have accepted. Max sighed again.

They watched Morrison and Max board their ship first. Max looked back with the expression of someone abandoned. Then Ethan, a smiling Misty, Ash, May, and Brock boarded an ocean liner bound for Kanto.

...

Hooooonk!

On a calm blue sea, a large liner that had crossed from Hoenn sounded its long horn and eased toward port.

It was Ethan's ship. After several days at sea, they had reached Kanto that morning. The harbor ahead belonged to a city Ethan knew well: Vermilion City.

When he had first arrived in Kanto from Kalos, Vermilion City had been his first stop. Now, after so much time, he had returned by sea again.

His thoughts were different. Back then, all he could think about was Pokemon. Now he wondered about Sabrina and Erika. They were both important women in his life. After so long apart, of course he missed them.

Yet the closer the ship came to shore, the more nervous he felt about being home again.

Ash and the others did not know what was on Ethan's mind. They stood beside him at the deck railing, watching the approaching harbor with complicated feelings of their own.

We're finally back, Ash said. Kanto was home. He returned after each regional journey to rest and begin again. He had reached only the final eight this time, but he had grown. That was something to be glad about.

Chapter 789: Back to Cerise Park

When the group disembarked in Vermilion City, it was time to part. For some of them the separation would last only a few days. Brock and Misty, though, had finished their journey and might stay home much longer.

Ash and Brock left first. They waved goodbye to Ethan and followed the road northwest. Each needed to see family. Ash had his mother to visit; Brock had his own household to return to. Even traveling together at the start, they would part along the way. It made the farewell a little sad.

Ethan wanted to see Sabrina and Erika at once, but he had arrived in Vermilion City. How could he leave without visiting Professor Cerise? His Pokemon were staying there too. He had to see his partners.

Misty and May came with him. Misty was back in Kanto, yet she had no intention of immediately returning to the Cerulean Gym. She said she wanted to visit Ethan's Pokemon and brought May along toward Cerise Laboratory.

Seeing the two girls whispering together behind him, Ethan suspected they had another reason. He did not think much of it. They would be parting soon, he assumed, and perhaps Misty simply wanted more time with him.

Misty had something else in mind. Out of Ethan's hearing, she leaned toward May. We'll meet Chloe Cerise soon. Be careful. She looks like a good girl, but she isn't simple. She's someone you'll have to watch out for later.

Someone to watch out for? Isn't that a little... May stopped herself. Misty seemed to see a rival behind every tree.

May knew Ethan was handsome, kind, attentive to her feelings, strong in battle, and much like the Trainer she aspired to become. He was exactly her type. But did Misty really think so many girls would fall for him? Wasn't she overestimating his appeal?

Well, May had to admit that he had begun to attract her too. She kept the thought to herself. She knew how much Ethan mattered to Misty, and Misty was becoming prickly with their own separation approaching. There was no reason to provoke her.

Ethan had not told Professor Cerise or Chloe he was coming. He wanted to surprise them. He took out a few souvenirs he had brought from Hoenn, bought more at a nearby gift shop, divided everything into parcels, and carried them into the laboratory grounds.

He had lived there for some time, and he still had a room of his own. Entering the English-style courtyard, he looked around and felt how familiar it all was.

Misty had visited before, but she had spent her time at the battle field behind the building. This was her first visit through the main entrance. She and May stopped whispering and looked around with curiosity. The enormous domed park behind the laboratory caught their attention even more than the building itself.

Brother Ethan, May asked, is this where your Pokemon stay?

Yes. Ethan nodded. This is where I received my Pokedex and officially began as a Trainer. My whole journey started here.

The beginning of Ethan's journey. May looked toward Cerise Park again. After hearing his words, the laboratory seemed almost mysterious, as if it had acquired a different light.

The three followed the stone path to the laboratory's front door. Ethan had just raised a hand to knock when light footsteps approached inside. The door opened.

A girl with long reddish-purple hair braided down her back stood there, carrying a bamboo basket full of Berries. She had been about to go out. Looking up, she found a boy and two girls on her doorstep.

It was Chloe. Ethan opened his mouth to greet her, but she blinked and shut the door again.

He stared. What was that about?

Before he could knock, the door opened once more. Chloe looked at him, blinked again, and closed it a second time. Ethan understood: she thought she was seeing things and was checking to make sure he was real.

Did she think she was still dreaming? It was not unreasonable. He had not warned her he was back in Kanto, and now he was standing outside her home.

He was about to call her name when she seemed to accept what she had seen. With a delighted cry, she flung the door open for a third time.

Brother Ethan! You're back?

One sentence and her delighted expression put Misty on alert. Chloe was not like Lisia, though. Misty might count her as a rival, but she could still talk to her normally. They would not clash as openly as Misty and Lisia did.

I'm back. Ethan smiled at Chloe. What were you doing just now? Didn't you trust your own eyes?

Chloe blushed and smiled sweetly. Of course I didn't. You came back without saying a word. Who would have expected you?

I wanted to surprise you. Ethan introduced the others. You've met Misty. This is May, a friend we met while traveling in Hoenn. She came to see Kanto with Misty. May, this is Chloe Cerise, Professor Cerise's daughter.

Hello.

Hello.

It's been a while, Chloe, Misty added.

May and Chloe shook hands. Despite Misty's warning, May liked her at once. Chloe looked as gentle as she sounded. It was hard to see her as an enemy. Chloe seemed to take to May just as readily.

Perhaps it was a matter of temperament. Misty and Lisia had disliked each other at first sight. May and Chloe felt none of that.

Ethan glanced at Chloe's basket. Were you going somewhere?

I was. Seeing him had put a bounce in her voice. It's Saturday and I have the day off, so I was going to give your Pokemon some extra Berries in Cerise Park.

The answer moved Ethan. While he had traveled, Chloe had been quietly looking after his Pokemon. A simple thank-you could not repay that care.

You've worked hard for them, he said. Unsure how else to express it, he handed her a gift. I picked up some souvenirs while I was in Hoenn. I hope you like them.

To Ethan it was a small gesture. To Chloe, the thought alone brought warmth. Thank you. She accepted the parcel and smiled at him again.

Ethan looked past her. Are the Professor, Ren, and Parker here?

Chloe nodded. They are. Would you like me to tell them you've come?

No, thanks. Ethan gestured toward Misty and May. Neither of them has seen Cerise Park properly. Why don't you show them around? I'll go in and see the Professor.

He nodded to the two girls and went into the laboratory with his remaining gifts. Chloe turned to them with a smile. Come with me.

Basket in hand, she led the way. Misty and May exchanged a glance and followed.

The park gate was only a minute's walk away. Through the enormous glass, May saw no Pokemon at all. Why is it so empty? I thought Trainers kept their Pokemon here.

Chloe used her access card to open the gate. The park hasn't officially opened to everyone yet, she explained. Only Ethan's Pokemon live here for now, and there weren't that many to begin with. He took several to the Ever Grande Conference, so only a few are left.

Inside, a long gravel path stretched before them. Small lawns lay on either side, with low hills and dense forest beyond.

After a few steps, Chloe left the path and led them through a little stand of trees to a thick patch of flowers. She pushed the branches aside. There was Ethan's Venusaur, dozing among the blooms.

It felt strange. Only days earlier they had watched Venusaur fight at the Conference. Ethan had then sent it and several other old partners back here. Seeing it in the flowers now was almost like watching it cross space in an instant.

Chloe set down her basket, took several green Berries from its full supply, and placed them before Venusaur. Wepear Berries are its favorite, she told the girls. They're sweet and crisp. Would you like one?

Misty and May shook their heads together. At Chloe's voice, Venusaur opened its eyes, looked at her, and nodded with a smile. It opened its mouth and swallowed the Berries.

Chloe brushed soil from herself, picked up the basket, and guided them farther into the park. Only then did Misty and May begin to spot the Pokemon tucked away around them.

Scizor was practicing with its blade-like arms against a tree trunk. Tyranitar rested in a pile of rocks. Jolteon chased butterflies through the forest. Blastoise soaked in the water. Crystal Steelix poked its head from a cave. Chloe seemed to know where each would be, and they came to her willingly when she approached.

The sight left Misty with an uneasy, complicated feeling. While she had been away, another girl had cared this well for Ethan's Pokemon.

They finally reached the park's largest lake. Misty's pace slowed as she recognized where they were. What is it? May asked.

Before Misty could answer, the lake exploded upward. A huge red Pokemon rose from the water.

May understood at once why Misty had stopped. She too went rigid. Its fierce appearance and enormous cold eyes made her breath catch and her heart race. The sudden arrival was frightening.

It was Ethan's gigantic red Gyarados, the unquestioned ruler of the park. It had the largest lake to itself. Even Ethan's other Pokemon, Venusaur and Blastoise included, preferred to keep their distance from this place.

Neither Misty nor May dared move closer. This was May's first time seeing it. She had heard scattered descriptions from Misty and Ash, but nothing had prepared her for its size. She had never imagined a Gyarados could be so enormous or intimidating. And could Gyarados really be red?

Chloe walked to the lakeshore without concern and threw all the remaining Berries from the basket toward Gyarados. It swallowed them, turned, and sank back beneath the water.

Chloe gathered up the empty basket. Seeing the other girls' faces, she smiled. It looks frightening, but it's obedient. As long as nobody attacks it first, it would never start a fight.

May hesitated. Aren't you afraid of it?

Afraid? Chloe shook her head. They're Ethan's Pokemon. They would never hurt me. What is there to fear?

Chapter 790: An Encounter

While Misty, May, and Chloe explored Cerise Park, Ethan went into the laboratory.

He knew the layout well enough to find his way without help. He passed through the halls and went straight to the work area.

Professor Cerise, Ren, and Parker were gathered around several instruments, deep in discussion. None of them noticed him arrive. Ethan stopped and looked around.

Quite a bit had changed since his last visit. Equipment had been moved, and there were more machines than before. The laboratory was becoming more complete with every passing month. The sight left him oddly wistful. He had not been gone that long, yet it felt as if an era had passed.

Rather than interrupt their animated discussion, he stood and waited. Ren happened to glance his way. Her eyes lit up.

Huh? Ethan? When did you get back?

She had been the first to notice. At her voice, Professor Cerise and Parker turned. Surprise and delight spread across both their faces.

Ethan?

Our champion's come home!

The three set aside their work and came over. Professor, Ren, Parker. It's good to see you again. Ethan hurried to hand them the gifts he had brought. These are just a little something for you. Please take them.

Being a champion in three regions had not gone to his head. He treated them as he always had. A few titles would not make him act like someone else.

Though they had not seen him in some time, the Professor and his assistants felt no distance between them. He had come back as the same Ethan they knew.

I watched every match of yours I could, Parker said with a smile as he set his gift aside. You were as strong as ever, just like at the Silver and Indigo Conferences. None of them could stand up to you!

He pointed toward his desk. Ethan followed the gesture and spotted a figurine of himself.

Good grief. They were making those already?

Parker was more than a supportive friend. He truly enjoyed watching Ethan battle. Of the three researchers, he was the only one with a serious interest in Pokemon battles. If footage of one of Ethan's matches was available online, Parker had almost certainly seen it. Having watched his strength grow, he never worried much that Ethan would lose. What better experience could a fan ask for? Every match was a pleasure to watch.

That's right, Ren said teasingly. He even took time off work to watch your final. Afterward he said, That's it? He was disappointed your opponent went down so easily.

Parker readily admitted it, right in front of his boss. I wasn't wrong! Compared with the Silver and Indigo Conferences, this opponent was much weaker. It didn't feel like a final. It felt like a round-of-sixteen match!

Well, of course it had. Ethan had eliminated the strongest opponent earlier, and even Hua had lost heart and failed to show his true strength.

To be fair, though, the average Trainer at the Ever Grande Conference had been a little stronger than at the Silver or Indigo Conferences. It was only the strongest contenders who had fallen short.

Professor Cerise kept smiling through the exchange, though his eyelid twitched a few times when he heard Parker had been watching matches on the job. He said nothing about it. Once the greetings were done, he asked Ethan, What brings you back this time? Did you just come to visit?

Not entirely. I have another reason. Ethan told them he planned to challenge the Battle Frontier.

The Battle Frontier? Professor Cerise stroked his chin. I've heard of it. If I remember correctly, there's a facility near Vermilion City...

He went to a computer and worked for a moment. A map of Kanto appeared on the large screen, marked with several locations. As he had said, one facility lay between Vermilion and Saffron City. Five others were marked as well; only the seventh facility's location was hidden.

This map is a huge help. Ethan photographed it with his phone. Thank you, Professor. It'll save me a lot of wandering.

...

When Ethan left the laboratory and entered Cerise Park, he found the three girls resting on a stretch of level grass. His Pokemon were nearby, as were Misty's and May's, all playing happily together. The girls stood when they saw him.

Are we leaving? Misty asked at once.

It was not that she was eager to go home. Being around Chloe had begun to weigh on her. Every time Chloe mentioned something about Brother Ethan that Misty herself did not know, she felt another prickle of irritation.

Ethan shook his head. I'm afraid we'll have to leave tomorrow. Professor Cerise invited me to dinner at his house tonight and asked me to bring all of you. I couldn't turn him down, so we'll stay another day.

Their reactions could not have been more different. Misty looked disappointed, May did not seem to mind, and Chloe was delighted.

Ethan took in their expressions, shook his head helplessly, and let it go. He went deeper into the park, released the Pokemon he had been carrying so they could roam freely, and visited his other partners who lived here.

He had only recently parted from most of them, so those visits were brief. He spent longer with the gigantic red Gyarados and Crystal Steelix, whom he had not seen in quite some time.

Clouds drifted overhead. Sunlight poured through the dome's glass and fell across the trees, casting long shadows. Ethan lay back on the grass and gazed up lazily.

It had been a long time since he had enjoyed an afternoon like this. No Gym battle to plan, no road to cover. He could simply be with his Pokemon and listen to the clear voices of the three girls talking nearby. The respite might be temporary, but he felt utterly at ease.

Now this was living.

It was still morning, though, with most of the day to go before dinner. He could not bring himself to spend all of it lying here. Then he remembered Misa, Masha, and the biker gang out on the edge of Vermilion City. Shelly and Courtney had been here from Hoenn for almost a month too. How were they getting on? He ought to go see them.

Ethan got up, brushed the dirt from his clothes, and told the girls he was heading out. Misty rose immediately.

I'm coming with you, she said. I'm bored here, and it's been ages since I've seen Shelly and Courtney. I'd like to see how they're doing.

Ethan saw through that at once. Misty had met the two women, but she was hardly close to them. She just did not want to stay in the park.

As soon as Misty spoke, May and Chloe stood as well.

I'll come too.

Me too.

So much for going alone and giving the girls more time to get acquainted. Now all three were coming, including Chloe.

Ethan left the other Pokemon in the park. He recalled only Gardevoir to her Poke Ball and called Gengar back into his shadow. Then he set off with the girls toward the outskirts of Vermilion City.

They had not gone far when he spotted a familiar dark-skinned boy approaching, one hand in his pocket. It was Chloe's childhood friend, Goh. Ethan did not particularly dislike him, but he had to wonder: why did they run into each other every time he came back?

Goh was heading toward Cerise Park with a mysterious smile and a spring in his step. When he drew near enough to recognize Ethan, the smile vanished. Of all the people he could have met, it had to be him.

Goh was asking himself much the same question. Why was this man always here whenever he came to see Chloe? And he had no desire to see Ethan's Pokemon either. That awful Gengar and terrifying red Gyarados had each left him with memories he would never forget.

He wanted to pretend he had seen nothing and walk straight past. Chloe was there, though. He could not ignore her.

Ch-Chloe. What a coincidence... Goh forced out a greeting, trying to look normal.

Goh? Chloe looked surprised. Where are you going?

I... I was just taking a walk around here. Anyway, I should go. See you when school starts. Bye!

Goh kept glancing at Ethan as he spoke, then hurried away as if fleeing a monster. Ethan watched him go and turned his attention elsewhere. Goh did not want anything to do with him, and the feeling was mutual.

No matter how often they met, they remained strangers. Their temperaments and beliefs simply did not fit. Even if Goh eventually traveled the world with Ash, Ethan doubted the two of them would become friends.

The encounter was a small interruption. Ethan put it out of his mind as soon as they left. They crossed the busy city and found the bikers' base on its outskirts.

Calling it a base made it sound grander than it was. It consisted of a motorcycle repair shop and a bar.

After Ethan invested in them, the gang had banded together and learned to run a business. Once a group of people down on their luck, they had begun to make something of themselves. Business was picking up too.

Rows of motorcycles stood outside the bar and inside the repair shop. At the very least, the bikes showed how far the gang had come. They had traded up from their bicycles and become bikers in earnest.

Several members were at work in the shop. When they saw Ethan, delight broke across their faces, and they gathered around him.

Boss!

Boss!

Ethan had never agreed to be their boss, but they had decided he was anyway. He had grown used to it. One of them ran ahead into the bar to tell the others, while the rest ushered Ethan inside as though he were a star.

Masha and Misa had already heard the news. They emerged from different rooms with a crowd of bikers and surrounded him so eagerly that Misty, May, and Chloe were pushed aside.

Boss! Masha's eyes shone. You finally had time to visit! When did you get back to Kanto?

That can wait! Misa shoved her younger brother aside with her hip. We watched you win the championship on TV. You were incredible, Boss!

The brother and sister were not the only ones talking. Everyone had something to say, and the bar filled with noise. Ethan spoke up to calm them.

Easy, easy. Don't scare my friends.

He called the girls over. Once the crowd made room, he finally had a chance to look around the bar. It resembled the American country bars he had seen on television: bottles behind the counter, a dartboard on the wall, and a pool table. The one unusual feature was the collection of Ethan posters covering the place.

It was a strange feeling. Other bars might display photographs of beautiful women. This one had photographs of him, stared at every day by a gang of men. Without knowing the story, a visitor might wonder about the gang's tastes.

A handful of other customers were there as well. They watched him curiously.

Knowing this was no place for a private conversation, Ethan caught Misa's eye. She understood, sent the gang on their way, and led him and the girls into a room that looked much like a meeting room.

When the door closed behind them, the whole world seemed to fall quiet at once.

Chapter 791: Seeing Courtney and Shelly Again

The meeting room was reasonably tidy. Ethan took a seat and turned to Misa and Masha.

How have you been?

Very well, thanks to you. Misa smiled. The bar makes a profit every day, though the repair shop is still our main business and our biggest source of income. I think we'll earn back the initial investment soon.

Ethan understood that teaching people how to earn a living was better than simply giving them money. He had only meant to find something useful for a gang that spent its days drifting about. He had not expected the business to give them a new start.

They talked for a while, and he got a clearer picture of how everyone was doing. Then he changed the subject. By the way, where are Shelly and Courtney? I thought they'd come here too.

The two big sisters don't usually come to the bar, Masha said. They're in the warehouses not far behind us.

Big sisters? They had been here less than a month, yet Shelly and Courtney had already earned the bikers' respect. Then again, they had been senior officers in Hoenn's two largest organizations. Handling a bicycle gang would hardly be difficult for them.

In that case, take me over to see how they're doing.

Misa and Masha led everyone out the bar's back door, along an overgrown passage, and up to two warehouses. One was red and the other blue.

Shelly and Courtney had not come to Kanto alone. When they accepted Ethan's arrangement, each brought members of her organization who wished to follow her. They also took most of Team Aqua's and Team Magma's remaining supplies and equipment. With that much support, they had established themselves quickly.

Some bikers might have underestimated them for being women, or for being beautiful. But with their people and equipment behind them, the gang had learned to follow their directions. The newcomers had practically taken over the place.

That was what Ethan had wanted. Shelly and Courtney could keep the bikers in line and stop them from causing trouble.

The warehouses were far more heavily guarded than the bikers' base. The sentries noticed Ethan's group as soon as they approached. With a glance around, Ethan even picked out a lookout hidden farther back.

The precautions made sense, but these people had been pardoned. They had spent so long as villains that they could not shake their habits. Even if the guards were only keeping out thieves and curious strangers, the arrangements were remarkably thorough and professional.

Everyone from Team Aqua and Team Magma knew Ethan's face. Those who had come to Kanto also knew they owed their pardons from the International Police to him. No one stopped him. As at the bar, someone hurried off to notify Shelly and Courtney, while the others welcomed him inside with complicated expressions.

Few of them could look at Ethan without feeling something. He had single-handedly broken up their organizations and captured their leaders. He had also enabled the ordinary members to walk away free. To them he was both savior and destroyer, someone they respected and feared in equal measure.

Up close, Ethan saw that the warehouses resembled the secret base where Shelly had once hidden in Hoenn. Both looked ordinary outside, but their interiors had been converted into bases. The red warehouse naturally belonged to Courtney and the former Team Magma members. Shelly and her former Team Aqua members occupied the blue one.

The bases stood side by side but were clearly separate. They looked peaceful enough, yet the relationship between the two groups remained as uneasy as the relationship between their commanders. That they could live this close without a fight was already a testament to Shelly and Courtney's restraint.

Ethan was still deciding which warehouse to visit first when the two women came out with their people to meet him. Both smiled when they saw him. Then each glanced at the other, and both smiles disappeared. It would be a long time before they truly made peace.

Shelly spoke first. I didn't expect to see you here. I thought you'd head straight for another region after the Ever Grande Conference.

Ethan heard the light teasing in her voice and smiled. How could I? I asked you both to come here. Of course I had to check on you before I left.

Courtney said nothing, but the look she gave him made it clear she was happy he had come.

Choosing a warehouse was another matter. Going with Shelly would upset Courtney; choosing Courtney would upset Shelly. Ethan hesitated, then decided that if he chose neither, he could make no mistake. He stayed where he was and talked to them outside.

After only a minute or two, both women invited him in. In the end he chose Shelly's warehouse. That did not mean he valued her more. Shelly's temperament simply made her harder to placate. Courtney was less likely to take offense and easier to soothe.

Shelly shot Courtney a triumphant glance. Courtney was annoyed, but she and her people followed them in.

Inside, Ethan found much the same layout as the warehouse base he had seen in Hoenn, minus the submarine and with more rooms for the members. Not bad. He looked around and nodded. He had not expected them to establish a base so quickly. It was still rudimentary, but at least their lives here were taking shape.

Your friends helped a great deal. Shelly glanced at Misa and Masha. We couldn't have settled in so fast without them.

Oh, it was nothing, the siblings said, smiling ingratiatingly. We only ran errands and did some heavy lifting.

That was more or less true. The bikers knew the area, had numbers, and could supply muscle. Shelly still did not trust them with certain work. But they had helped, and she remembered even small favors.

Misty, May, and Chloe had fallen quiet as soon as they entered the bikers' bar. They had followed Ethan without speaking. Now they looked around the warehouse curiously, staying close behind him like three little attendants.

After a tour, Ethan sat on a sofa and asked Shelly and Courtney, What are your plans from here?

What plans could we have? Shelly sat opposite him and leaned back. We're settled, more or less. Once we've adjusted, we'll need to take on work to support ourselves.

Take on work? Ethan asked.

Of course. People like us aren't going to find ordinary jobs and sit quietly at a desk. In a few days, I'll start looking for contracts to catch Pokemon for other people. Legal business.

Catching Pokemon for clients? Ethan rubbed his chin and nodded. It's close to what you used to do. At least your skills and experience won't go to waste.

He turned to Courtney to hear her plan. Instead, she asked, Which region are you traveling to next?

I came back to challenge the Battle Frontier. After that, I'll travel through Sinnoh.

Sinnoh. Courtney nodded. Going by your past journeys, you'll probably come into conflict with another organization there. If that happens, let me come and help you.

Shelly stared at her in shock. So that was her move! Shelly had been thinking about how to put down roots here, while Courtney had already thought of following Ethan into another region. Why had that not occurred to her? She could not afford to underestimate this woman.

While Ethan considered the offer, Shelly hurried to add, I'm going too!
