Honestly, Ethan had never thought that far ahead. He had been focused on settling the two women in Kanto, not on what might happen when he encountered other organizations elsewhere.

As his travels continued, further clashes were likely. His Pokemon made him confident he could face those groups, but sometimes he lacked enough people to get things done. Nor could he place his full trust in the International Police. Having capable people he knew well at his side would help.

Misa and Masha could hardly sit still as he weighed the idea. Boss! Count us in too!

You? Shelly shot the siblings a dismissive look before Ethan could answer. This isn't a street fight. You two are barely even delinquents. You're far too green. Unless you're prepared to risk your lives, you'll only get in the way, whether we're facing Legendary Pokemon or a regional organization.

Misa and Masha swallowed. Her grave tone frightened them, but neither backed down. Before they could reply, Ethan raised a hand.

Shelly's right. It's too dangerous for you at present. If the day comes when you can handle yourselves independently, I'll consider bringing you in.

Hearing it from Ethan disappointed them, but they nodded obediently. We understand, Boss. You can always count on us to support you. Even if we can't fight beside you, we'll keep this place running well!

That's more like it. Shelly nodded and acknowledged their strengths. Fighting isn't your strong suit, but you're good at repairs. Most of the people who came with us are field operatives. We're short of ground support, and you can fill that gap.

Being praised by Shelly filled the siblings with pride. They felt as if they had finally earned her approval. Both thumped their chests. Don't worry, Big Sister! We can only repair simple motorcycles and machinery for now, but we'll work twice as hard. We won't let you down!

Shelly had won them over with a few words. She had lifted their spirits, given them a useful role, and put their skills to work. She had been one of Team Aqua's leading minds for good reason.

Ethan had begun to form a plan. Since you both want to help, and I could use that help, why don't you lead a special operations team? Each of you can select a few people from those you brought here.

A special operations team? Shelly and Courtney nodded together. They exchanged a look, then turned away with blank faces.

Who's in command? Shelly asked.

Here they went again. Neither was willing to yield to the other, and Ethan could already feel a headache coming on. Still, he had to settle it. He sighed and told Shelly, You can command the team for now. But don't make major decisions alone. Discuss them with Courtney, and if you can't resolve a disagreement, contact me.

Shelly gave Courtney one more satisfied look before nodding to Ethan. Understood. I know when to put serious matters first. What about personnel and equipment? Any requirements?

Ethan thought for a moment. We don't need a large team. Keep it under ten people if you can. As for equipment, prioritize mobility. I want you able to reach wherever you're needed quickly.

Mobility... Shelly nodded. Then I'll have to return to Hoenn. Team Aqua has another secret base, and there's a submarine there that would suit us. The International Police never seized it. We can use it to get around.

So Shelly had kept something back after all. Ethan distinctly remembered her telling Anabel, aboard the marine police ship, that she had disclosed every Team Aqua secret. Apparently she still had a hidden asset.

Neither she nor Courtney was easy to deal with. Fortunately, they were on his side now. He no longer had to worry about either of them scheming against him.

Chapter 792: Scott

They discussed a few more details. By dusk, Ethan finally left with Misty, May, and Chloe.

Shelly and Courtney still had people to choose for their team and preparations to make before setting out. That would take time, but Ethan was not leaving for Sinnoh immediately. They had room to get everything in order.

Outside the warehouses, Ethan turned to those who had come to see him off and nodded. Until next time, then.

Boss... Misa and Masha looked at him with tears in their eyes. They had only spent a few hours together, and neither wanted him to go. They knew he had important things to do and could not stay with them forever. They could only say goodbye.

Shelly and Courtney took the parting more calmly. They expected to meet him in Sinnoh soon, and now they had work to occupy them.

Shelly waved lazily. See you in Sinnoh.

Courtney nodded with solemn purpose. I'll be waiting for you there.

Ethan smiled at them once more and walked away with the three girls. Shelly and Courtney watched until he disappeared. Then they glanced at each other and went back into their separate warehouses, leaving only Misa and Masha in the open yard.

Masha looked toward the road Ethan had taken, then toward the warehouses. Sis, do you think Big Sister Shelly and Big Sister Courtney both like the Boss?

Isn't it obvious? Misa snorted. Neither of them is an ordinary woman. Only someone like the Boss could attract them. Just watch. When they reach Sinnoh, all they'll need is the right opportunity, and they'll offer themselves to him!

Masha scratched his head and turned to his sister. What about you?

Me? Misa gazed after Ethan, stars in her eyes. Isn't that obvious too? Of course I feel the same!

...

After leaving the outskirts, Ethan did not return to Cerise Laboratory. He headed for Chloe's house. He knew the way and walked ahead of the others.

May, a few steps behind, leaned toward Misty and asked quietly, Who were all those people?

Chloe pricked up her ears too. She knew the bikers, but she had no idea who lived in the warehouses or where they had come from.

Seeing Chloe's curiosity, Misty straightened a little and cleared her throat. You know Brother Ethan doesn't just challenge Gyms when he travels. He helps the International Police with their cases too. Those two women used to be officers in criminal organizations. After he defeated them, they agreed to work for him.

May had spent her journey with Ash. Most of what she knew about Ethan's travels had come from Misty's stories. She had no idea that his adventures had been even more dangerous than Ash's. The International Police, criminal organizationsit all sounded thrilling. Ethan seemed more impressive than ever.

Out of the corner of her eye, Misty saw that Chloe wanted to hear more as well. Delighted, she chose some of Ethan's most exciting encounters with Shelly and Courtney and told both girls about them.

Ethan listened to the chatter behind him, his own exploits growing more glorious with each retelling. He could not help feeling a little pleased. At that moment, nothing was more satisfying than having three beautiful girls praise him.

They were still talking when they reached Chloe's house. The conversation had eased the tension between Misty and Chloe. Misty was not truly petty; despite her feelings where Brother Ethan was concerned, she liked Chloe as a person.

Ethan climbed the steps and rang the bell. The door opened almost at once. Chloe's younger brother, the cool-looking Souta, stood on the other side.

You really came! he cried. Delight and excitement shone in his eyes.

Souta had not changed much. He was still open and enthusiastic, and handsome too. Ethan could easily imagine him being popular with his classmates. He remembered that Souta had called himself a fan at their first meeting and had asked for an autograph. His enthusiasm plainly had not faded.

Professor Cerise and his wife stood behind Souta, both smiling. The Professor had told Yoshino that Ethan was coming and had left the laboratory early. In truth, he had reached home only a few minutes ahead of his guest.

Aunt Yoshino, Souta. It's good to see you again. Ethan handed them the gifts he had prepared. Misty and May stepped forward to greet them too.

It's nice to meet you. I'm Misty.

And I'm May.

The girls were on their best behavior. Yoshino took to them immediately and welcomed everyone in with a warm smile.

They had arrived early, and Yoshino still had much to prepare. She brought them into the living room, made tea, and asked her husband and children to entertain the guests before hurrying to the kitchen.

Souta was so excited that he seemed to have an endless supply of questions. He kept Ethan talking about his travels, his championship victory, and everything in between.

Ethan answered each question patiently at first. Souta's enthusiasm eventually became more than he could keep up with. Fortunately, he had someone to help. He glanced at Misty, and she understood at once.

Misty happily took over. She knew how to praise Ethan without revealing anything private about him. Before the whole room, she picked out some of their more exciting Hoenn adventures and brought them to life.

Everyone listened closely. Souta was especially appreciative; each delighted That's amazing! gave Misty a fresh glow of satisfaction. Praising Ethan made her happy tooperhaps even happier than praising herself.

After they had finished a round of tea, the doorbell rang again. Souta went to answer it and returned with Ren and Parker. Now everyone had arrived. When Yoshino finished cooking, Ren helped her set the table, and the warm family dinner began.

...

After spending the night at Cerise Laboratory, Ethan, Misty, and May set out early the next morning. They left Vermilion City and headed north toward the nearest Battle Frontier facility.

It was called the Battle Arena. Ethan knew little about it. He had only caught a few glimpses of it in the anime and had never looked into it closely. That did not matter much. He only needed to defeat its Frontier Brain and earn proof of victory.

The Battle Arena stood near a village on the plains outside Saffron City. Following the location on Professor Cerise's map, the three walked for much of the day before reaching the area.

Before entering the village, Ethan stopped and gazed toward Saffron City for a long while. Sabrina was there, so close that another stretch of road might bring him into her arms. His longing almost overwhelmed him. He wanted to go to her at once.

But reason held him back. This was not the time to rush. At the very least, he would finish his challenge at the Battle Arena first. Ethan pushed his yearning aside, let out a long breath, and looked over the village.

Though it lay in the countryside, farmhouses stood close together amid lovely scenery. The air was fresh, and the place felt restful. The area was outside the Pokemon League's jurisdiction, yet the League seemed to have built a Pokemon Center here for Trainers visiting the nearby Battle Arena. It had landscaped the surrounding grounds as well.

Ethan went straight to the Center with Misty and May. Inside, they found a large, lavishly furnished space. A few other Trainers were eating dinner there. As always, Nurse Joy ran the front desk.

They checked in and were about to head for the dining room when a slightly stout man in sunglasses and a blue casual shirt approached them with a smile.

Excuse me. Are all three of you Trainers?

Ethan turned and gave him a puzzled look. And you are...?

Allow me to introduce myself. My name is Scott. You certainly look like Trainers, so may I ask what brings you here?

Scott. If Ethan remembered correctly, this was the owner of Kanto's Battle Frontier, the man who financed all its Frontier Brains. What a coincidence to meet him here.

Before Ethan could reply, Scott took off his sunglasses and studied Ethan's face. Wait... Have we met somewhere? You look familiar.

Ethan had never met him. There was only one reason Scott might recognize him. A moment later, Scott gasped.

Ah! I've got it! You're that cham

Ethan interrupted him with a small cough. There were not many Trainers in the Center, but he still did not want to draw attention.

I am, he said quietly. Please keep your voice down. I don't want to disturb anyone.

Scott realized his surprise had gotten the better of him and laughed. Sorry! I simply never expected to see you here. You caught me off guard.

I'm surprised too. Ethan smiled and revealed that he knew who Scott was. I didn't expect to find the owner of the Battle Frontier in a place like this.

Scott looked even more astonished. You know me?

Ethan would hardly tell him about watching the anime. He gave Scott a mysterious smile. Is that so strange? A wealthy man who owns the Battle Frontier is bound to attract attention.

He was making it up. Scott kept a low profile and rarely appeared in public. If he were truly that famous, far more people would recognize him. Scott seemed to understand that Ethan was merely being polite and smiled.

So you've come to challenge the Battle Frontier, Mr. Ethan?

Of course. We arrived a little later than I hoped, so it looks like I'll have to challenge it tomorrow.

That's wonderful! Scott's eyes brightened. The Frontier Brain at this Battle Arena is Miss Greta, and she's very strong. Watching a champion like you battle her should be quite a spectacle. I wouldn't miss it for anything!

Greta. Her name brought a fleeting, rather silly thought to Ethan's mind. He tried to recall what he knew of this Frontier Brain. She had appeared so little in the anime that he could remember neither her appearance nor her Pokemon.

It was no great concern. Whatever partners she used, he was confident he could win if he stayed alert.

After chatting with Scott a while longer, Ethan agreed to go to the Battle Arena with him the next day. He watched Scott leave, then took Misty and May into the dining room.

Once Scott was out of earshot, Misty let out a breath and laughed. When he first walked up to us, I thought he was a talent scout. I never would have guessed he was the man behind the Battle Frontier. He doesn't look the part at all!

...

The night passed quietly. After breakfast the next morning, the three spent a little more time at the Pokemon Center. When it was time to leave, they went outside.

A red sports car came roaring up and stopped at the entrance. Scott was at the wheel.

Hop in! It's not far, but let me drive you to the Battle Arena.

Ethan had not expected Scott's promise to go with them to mean this. Then again, perhaps there was a reason Scott was so stout.

They climbed in. After a little over five minutes along a winding country road, the car entered a small forest. A Japanese-style building appeared among the trees ahead.

So that was the Battle Arena? Ethan had imagined something like a Roman arena. This looked more like a temple. As they drew closer, he heard many voices calling out in the rhythm of training.

Scott smiled as he drove. Miss Greta isn't only the Frontier Brain of the Battle Arena. She's an excellent karate master, and she's full of energy. Once you meet her, I'm sure you'll be friends in no time!

Chapter 793: A Fourth Encounter with Bea

Ethan, Misty, and May got out of the car and entered the Battle Arena with Scott.

Just beyond the gate, men and women in blue training clothes stood in two neat lines on an open-air practice ground, throwing punches again and again. A blonde woman led them from a raised platform. She wore a tight blue outfit beneath a black martial arts uniform.

She had to be Greta, the Arena's Frontier Brain. Ethan and the others did not want to interrupt the class, so they went around the side and waited quietly some distance behind her.

From closer up, Ethan studied her. She looked only seventeen or eighteen, with pleasant features and a long, toned build that spoke of years of exercise. Her blonde hair had straight bangs, with each side curling up like a fist. It was an unusual choice of hairstyle, though the longer he looked, the more it seemed to suit her.

Scott leaned close and said softly, There she isMiss Greta. Don't let her youth fool you. She's a rare talent in karate! I went to a great deal of trouble to persuade her to come here.

He sounded proud to have recruited her as a Frontier Brain. Finding someone so capable had not been easy, nor had convincing her to accept the post. Building an Arena of this size had also demanded a great deal of money and effort from him.

Ethan did not yet know how strong Greta was, either at karate or at Pokemon battles. But there were at least thirty students training under her. So many people would hardly have sought her instruction if she had nothing to teach.

As Ethan's group looked around and waited for the morning practice to end, someone else entered through the gate. Ethan did not notice until Misty gave a startled exclamation.

It's Bea!

Bea? The first memory that came to Ethan was the night he had reached out in his sleep and touched the wrong person. He turned quickly. Bea had arrived at the practice ground with a backpack over one shoulder and a grave look on her face.

It really was her. What was she doing in Kanto, and why had she come here at the same time? Wherever Fighting-type Trainers gathered, it seemed Bea was bound to appear.

Perhaps her presence was simply too strong, or perhaps Greta recognized a fellow martial artist. Unlike Ethan's group, Bea caught Greta's attention immediately. Greta stopped her movements and watched the newcomer with a serious expression.

Her students noticed the change in her. They stopped practicing and followed her gaze. Some looked puzzled, others surprised or curious, and a few openly admired Bea. Most could not understand why their teacher seemed so wary of her.

Only the two women knew what they had sensed: each recognized the bearing of a skilled fighter in the other.

Bea ignored the many eyes on her and walked steadily up to Greta. She gave a formal karate bow. Are you the Frontier Brain here? I've come to challenge you.

Straight to the point, as ever. Greta took in Bea's clothes, her practiced bow, and the strength she carried herself with. She returned the bow.

That's right. I'm Greta, the Frontier Brain of this Arena! Folding her arms, she looked Bea up and down and answered in an energetic voice, I accept your challenge!

Wait a moment! Ethan called.

His voice drew everyone's attention. Only then did Greta, Bea, and the students realize another group was standing nearby.

Who are you? Greta asked in surprise. Then she spotted Scott beside them. Mr. Scott? When did you get here?

Bea was just as stunned to see Ethan. She had never imagined she would run into him here. The memory of that night rose in her mind at once, and her heart gave an involuntary jolt.

Scott laughed and led the group over. I came for a reason, of course. Let me introduce you. This gentleman is no ordinary challenger. He's Ethan Vale, champion of the most recent Indigo Conference and Silver Conference, and now of this year's Ever Grande Conference too! He's here to challenge your Battle Arena.

Scott traveled the world regularly, so it was no surprise that he knew about Ethan's three championships. Greta, however, was taken aback. She knew Ethan had won the Indigo Conference in Kanto, even if she knew less about what had happened in Johto and Hoenn. She had never expected a champion in three regions to come and challenge her.

Was he treating her as a diversion? On second thought, he was probably here to train his Pokemon.

Ethan nodded to Greta, then looked at Bea. It's been a while, Bea.

Nearly a month had passed since they parted. He had not expected to see her again so soon, let alone here. Misty stepped forward too. It's good to see you again, Bea!

Bea nodded to Misty, then met Ethan's eyes. Her feelings were more complicated than she could hide. After weeks of training, she had thought she had put that incident behind her and could face him calmly. Seeing him again stirred her emotions like a stone dropped into still water.

Scott and Greta watched the exchange in surprise. You know each other?

Of all the coincidences, both challengers had arrived together and turned out to be acquainted. At least that would spare everyone a dispute over who went first.

Greta waved to her students. Raise the wheel!

A section of the ground beside them split apart, and a huge wheel rose from beneath it. It had three colored sections, each marked with a different number of dots from one to three.

Bea and Ethan stared at it. Greta explained with a smile, The rules here are simple. A one means a one-on-one elimination match, a two means two-on-two, and a three means three-on-three. Which of you wants to challenge me first?

Ethan and Bea looked at each other. Bea hesitated, ready to let him take the first match, but Ethan gestured for her to go ahead.

Ladies first.

He had spoken before she could. Bea was not one to make a fuss over it. She nodded and stepped up to the wheel.

A long lever protruded from its edge. Bea pulled it hard, sending the wheel spinning. It slowed and finally stopped with its pointer on a yellow section marked by three black dots. She would fight Greta in three rounds.

Good, Greta said. A three-on-three elimination match. The first to defeat all of the other Trainer's Pokemon wins!

With the number of rounds decided, everyone moved to prepare for battle. Ethan was not up yet. He followed the students into the Battle Arena's main hall with Misty and May.

The students knelt around the edges. Ethan and the girls copied them, kneeling in the area reserved for guests. In most respects, this place resembled an ordinary Gym. Apart from the wheel, Ethan had seen little to explain what made a Battle Frontier facility different or why it was called part of a frontier. Perhaps he would understand later.

Greta and Bea took positions on opposite sides of the hall. An older student stepped forward to referee.

As the one accepting the challenge, Greta released her Pokemon first. She tossed three Poke Balls at once. Blue light flashed, and three Pokemon appeared outside the battle area: Hariyama, Medicham, and Hitmonchan.

All three were Fighting types, fitting Greta perfectly. It looked even more like a Gym now.

Bea released her Pokemon as well. Three more flashes revealed Grapploct, Hawlucha, and Pangoro, facing Greta's team across the hall. They too were Fighting types. This would be a clash between two teams built around the same specialty.

Bea's partners opened the eyes of the Kanto spectators. Pokemon from distant regions were still a novelty here. These three looked especially fierce, each with an intimidating expression that made the students worry for Greta.

Greta herself did not recognize them well. As a Frontier Brain, she had studied Pokemon from other regions, but reading about a species was different from facing it in battle. Few Pokemon from so far away reached Kanto. The unfamiliarity made her less certain of what to expect.

It was a limit of living in one region. Then again, Kanto Pokemon might seem just as unusual to Trainers elsewhere.

Although both teams had been revealed, this was no simultaneous three-on-three battle. Each Pokemon would enter in turn, and each bout would have its own winner. The reveal seemed designed to put both Trainers' options in plain sight. Ethan was not sure what purpose that served, but it was at least one difference from an ordinary Gym challenge.

Without further talk, the two women chose their first Pokemon. Greta sent Hariyama into the battle area. Bea chose Pangoro. Both were Fighting types that preferred strength over finesse. Their opening clash promised to be fierce.

Ethan had seen Bea's Pangoro fight before and knew how formidable it was. Scott had also told him that Hariyama was Greta's ace and the partner she used most often. This might be the decisive bout of the entire match.

At the referee's signal, the battle began. The two Pokemon charged with heavy strides and met in the center.

It was a contest of raw power. They traded crushing blows, neither willing to give ground. Even a heavy hit could not make either take a step back. There were no intricate exchanges of technique, but this had its own appeal. The force of it set the audience's blood racing.

The students clenched their fists. With every shift in the struggle, they cheered or shouted encouragement. Every collision held their attention.

No matter how fierce, the contest could not last forever. Greta was an excellent TrainerScott would never have recruited her otherwisebut she had met a formidable opponent.

Bea was an official Pokemon League Gym Leader. She traveled widely to train and challenge others, and her strength could not be dismissed. She was no match for an Elite Four member, perhaps, but she was more than capable of facing a Frontier Brain.

In the end, Pangoro's greater resolve and strength won out. It brought Hariyama down first and took the opening round.

Chapter 794: Karate

Hariyama's defeat gave Bea the first round. Ethan, Misty, and May applauded from the side, and even Scott clapped with a smile.

As the man behind the Battle Frontier, Scott was happy to see either a Frontier Brain win or a challenger succeed. What mattered to him was a fine performance that showed the spirit of the Frontier.

While Ethan applauded, Bea stole a quick glance at him as though it meant nothing, then put her attention back on the match. No one, Ethan included, noticed.

Greta was disappointed, but she accepted the result. The first bout had been a straightforward contest of strength. Her Hariyama had lost because Pangoro was stronger, and there was nothing to argue about.

She recalled Hariyama, considered her remaining partners, and sent out Medicham for the second round.

Medicham was a humanoid Pokemon. Its head, legs, and lips were bright red with pale yellow spots; the rest of its body was white. It had a slender upper body, a fuller lower half, and long arms. The coloring made it look a little like a yoga practitioner or a Latin dancer.

After difficult yoga training, a Medicham could use its developed psychic power to predict an opponent's movements. It often went without food for long periods while meditating. By concentrating deeply, it could perceive an opponent's aura. Some accounts even claimed meditation raised its inner energy, sharpened its sixth sense, and let it blend into mountains and fields until its presence vanished.

As a Psychic- and Fighting-type Pokemon, Medicham fought with more technique than Hariyama. It could evade attacks with graceful, dance-like motions, then strike hard when it saw an opening.

Bea studied it, thought for a moment, and withdrew Pangoro. She sent Hawlucha into the battle area instead.

It was a questionable choice. Pangoro's Dark typing would have made it immune to Medicham's Psychic-type attacks. By replacing it, Bea had given up that advantage.

Still, Pangoro had taken damage in the first bout and lost stamina. No one knew whether it could finish another full round. Resting it would leave Bea a reserve for later. And unlike her other remaining partner, Grapploct, Hawlucha at least had the Flying type to help it fight back against Medicham.

At the referee's signal, the second round began. Knowing the matchup was unfavorable, Hawlucha attacked first.

Despite the hawk in its name and the cape-like feathers on its body, Hawlucha did not truly fly. It was light enough to leap high and use its wing-like cape to adjust its position, hanging in the air for a moment. That made its attacks hard to predict.

Medicham's flexibility served it well, though. With broad, supple movements, it slipped past Hawlucha's varied attacks. Hawlucha raised its two talons and lunged again, only to miss. It was visibly growing impatient.

Greta seized the opening. Fighters like her and Bea were quick to spot the smallest mistake. In an instant, Medicham used psychic power to make Hawlucha seize up, followed with a Fighting-type strike, and brought it down with surprising ease.

It was not simply a matter of overall strength. Medicham's pliant body had answered Hawlucha's forceful attacks perfectly, and its Psychic typing gave it another edge. The score was tied at one apiece.

Greta's students cheered. Ethan and the others watched Bea's calm face and knew the match was far from over.

She soon proved that all her travels and training had not been wasted. For the third round, Bea kept Pangoro in reserve and sent out Grapploct. Though it too faced an unfavorable type matchup, its four upper tentacles gave Medicham's flexible body nowhere to escape. Grapploct caught it, held it fast, and tightened its grip until Medicham fainted.

That put Bea ahead two to one. She was not finished. When her rested Pangoro returned to face Hitmonchan, it overwhelmed the Pokemon reputed to punch faster than a bullet.

One blow shattered Hitmonchan's hopes of winning. A second shattered Greta's hope of a comeback. With a long bamboo leaf between its teeth, Pangoro was a fearsome sight.

Bea won the match three to one, and made it look almost easy.

The students scratched their heads, unable to hide their disappointment. Ethan's group, by contrast, applauded quietly.

I lost. Greta shook her head ruefully and faced Bea. You've trained your Pokemon exceptionally well. I couldn't match you.

Though she was a Frontier Brain, Greta did not cling to her pride as some Gym Leaders might. She could admit defeat without making excuses. Unfortunately for her, Bea was not the best person to receive a gracious compliment.

Bea nodded once. I lost one round. That proves I still haven't trained enough.

Greta had no idea how to answer. If one lost round meant Bea lacked training, what did three lost rounds say about her? What would it say about the students she taught?

Bea's stiff delivery gave Greta a sense of her character. She shook her head and let it pass. Going over to Bea, she took a round, golden coin-like Symbol from inside her clothing.

This is the Guts Symbol, awarded for defeating the Battle Arena. Please accept it.

Bea thanked her, placed the Symbol in her backpack, then stepped aside and looked toward Ethan. He rose with Misty and May and approached Greta.

Congratulations, he told Bea first. That was an excellent battle. He turned to Greta, but before he could issue his own challenge, she shook her head.

I'm sorry. I'd like to battle you now, but you've just seen all my Pokemon go down. I can't fight you until they've recovered.

Huh? Misty blurted out. Are those the only Pokemon you have, Greta?

Of course not. Greta smiled. I have plenty of others. But if I'm battling a champion, I want to use my strongest team. As you saw...

So Hariyama and Medicham were among her best. Ethan wanted to face them at full strength too. With both injured, he would have to wait.

All right. I'll wait.

Greta looked relieved. Many Gym Leaders and Frontier Brains would welcome a serious battle against someone of Ethan's caliber. Win or lose, it would be valuable training for their Pokemon. She did not want to miss the chance.

Having settled that, Greta turned back to Bea. May I ask you something? You're a skilled karate practitioner, aren't you? Would you be willing to spar with me, without our Pokemon?

Every eye in the hall returned to the two women. A karate match between them would be a rare sight.

Bea paused in surprise, then nodded slightly. Yes.

Greta gave her Poke Balls to a student to take for treatment, straightened her clothes, and faced Bea. Her presence suddenly grew fierce. Ethan led Misty and May back to their places, clearing the floor. Scott even took off his sunglasses and fixed his eyes on the match. The students hardly dared breathe.

Bea met Greta's gaze without flinching. Her own fighting spirit rose. The two women gave low cries together and took their stances.

They circled and tested each other, searching for an opening while guarding against an attack. The tension filled the hall before either had thrown a strike.

Ethan knew nothing of karate or its finer terms. He was an outsider watching for the spectacle. In the time it took him to blink, Greta stepped forward and struck with both hands. Bea blocked and counterattacked. It happened so fast that after a second or two, they had already exchanged blows and separated again.

To Ethan, it looked even. The students' startled cries suggested Bea had gained the better of that exchange.

Misty leaned toward him. Brother Ethan, can you tell what's happening?

He shook his head. I've never studied it. I don't even know the rules. Let's just enjoy watching. We'll know the result when it's over.

Anyone could recognize an obvious advantage. In a brief exchange like that, though, who had landed a strike or earned a point was beyond him. It was the kind of moment that separated experts from beginners and those who only knew a little. Ethan did not need to be an expert to appreciate it.

Having gauged each other's skill in the first exchange, Greta and Bea stopped probing. They launched into a fierce contest, hands and bare feet flashing through a succession of short, violent clashes. They looked every bit as formidable as the Pokemon they had just commanded.

Ethan and the girls were engrossed. Even Greta's students stared; they could rarely have seen a karate match fought at this level. Then, without warning, the women stepped back at the same time and bowed to each other.

Was that it? Ethan could not tell who had won. Greta supplied the answer with a smile.

People have called me a rare talent in Kanto, and I thought I was quite good. Today I met someone better. Thank you for holding back at the end.

Talents seemed to be everywhere these days. Greta was a rare talent in Kanto; Bea had been called a once-in-a-century talent in Galar. The word was beginning to feel overused. Still, if Greta was thanking Bea for holding back, Bea must have come out ahead. Perhaps that extra century really did make a difference.

You're too kind, Bea said. You took my attacks. I would call it a draw.

Come on. Greta held out both hands, showing everyone her reddened palms. Look at these. That last kick was so strong that even blocking it with both hands felt as though the bones might break. If we'd kept going, my hands would have swollen first. I lost.

Now everyone understood. The exchange had looked even, but Greta's body had been the first to reach its limit. Her students stared at Bea in fresh amazement. She looked about Greta's age, yet she had even greater strength. Where had this formidable woman come from?

And Greta had lost at karate as well as in the Pokemon battle. In every contest today, the challenger had surpassed her.

Chapter 795: How Strong Could He Be?

In a lounge at the Battle Arena, Ethan, Misty, and May sat across from Bea. No one else was there. Greta and Scott had both stayed away, apparently understanding that the old friends would appreciate time to talk.

Tea and a plate of fruit stood on the table. The room was small but comfortably furnished. Ethan and Misty were already friends with Bea and felt at ease. May was meeting her for the first time. Once the introductions were done, though, May simply lowered her head, swung her legs, and quietly ate the fruit one forkful after another.

Bea glanced away from May's stomach, which somehow stayed flat no matter how much she ate, and looked at Ethan. After a moment's hesitation, she said, I haven't congratulated you yet. Congratulations on winning the Ever Grande Conference.

It wasn't such a big deal. Ethan waved a hand and smiled. The tournament went smoothly. Winning felt like the natural conclusion. Besides, congratulations don't have a deadline. You're not too late.

Misty brightened at once. You should have seen him, Bea! From the qualifying rounds through the main tournament, Brother Ethan won by huge margins. The other Trainers couldn't keep up with him at all!

Bea almost said something, then kept quiet. Although she had left Hoenn, she had watched every one of Ethan's matches on television. She was embarrassed to admit it.

Ordinarily, she paid little attention to other people's affairs and devoted herself to training. Yet during the tournament, she had found herself stopping her practice whenever Ethan had a match. Each time, she went to a Pokemon Center to watch the broadcast.

She had been unsettled lately. The memory of that night kept intruding on her thoughts, making it hard to concentrate on training. She understood little about romance, but she knew something had changed in her state of mind.

She had come to the Battle Arena hoping to recover the feeling of a good fight and push those distracting thoughts aside. Instead, as if fate had arranged it, she had met Ethan again. She could hardly have expected that. Far from clearing her mind, the meeting had left her even more confused.

At least no one else knew.

With Misty leading the conversation, they covered everything from Ethan's championship victory to Bea's recent travels. The atmosphere in the lounge grew easy and cheerful.

At noon, Greta and Scott came in and invited them to lunch. By the time they finished eating, Greta's Pokemon had completed their treatment and recovered their strength. Everyone gathered at the battle arena again.

In the meantime, the students had looked into both visitors. Scott had already introduced Ethan as the winner of the Indigo, Silver, and Ever Grande Conferences. An online search revealed that Bea was no ordinary challenger either: she was an official Gym Leader in Galar.

The students might not have known much about Galar, but they knew what a Gym Leader was. No wonder Greta had lost. Her earlier match had been more than a challenge from an unknown Trainer; it had been a contest between a Gym Leader and a Frontier Brain. An official Gym Leader had proved herself the better fighter.

Ethan and Greta returned to the wheel in the open-air practice ground, surrounded by the others. Greta folded her arms. You know the rules. Go ahead and spin it.

Ethan nodded and gave the lever a casual pull. The wheel spun, slowed, and stopped with the pointer on a red section marked with two dots.

Two. He would use two Pokemon. It was a good enough result. He would not get three rounds, but he could at least face Greta's two strongest partners.

The group went back to the battle hall. Ethan and Greta took their places in the Trainer areas, facing each other across the field.

Unlike Bea, Ethan projected no fierce presence. He simply stood there, looking like an unusually handsome Trainer. Nothing more. Yet no one in the hall dared underestimate him.

They took his easy smile for the composure of someone who had no need to show his strength. Once the battle began, they knew he would show no mercy.

As before, Greta released her Pokemon first. Two flashes of blue light revealed Hariyama and Medicham, both of which had fought well against Bea. Ethan had expected them after waiting for their treatment. He released the two partners he had already chosen: Blaziken and Scizor.

Since the Ever Grande Conference, the Pokemon Ethan had caught in Hoenn, including Blaziken and Milotic, had received plenty of training. Their tournament experience had raised their strength another step.

If he kept traveling with them alone, ordinary battles and ordinary Pokemon would offer them little room to grow. Only unusually strong Gym Leaders and Trainers could still test them properly. He would need to catch some new Pokemon.

That explained why Ash started building a new team whenever he reached a new region. As a Pokemon grew stronger, wild opponents and everyday incidents no longer helped it improve as much.

Ethan made finding new partners a priority, then brought his thoughts back to the field. Bea's match had shown that Greta's two Pokemon were capable and could still give his partners useful practice. But he would have to act on his new plan soon.

Greta sent Hariyama out first. Ethan looked it over and marveled again at the world's technology. Only hours ago, Pangoro had knocked it out. After treatment and rest, it stood before him lively and ready to battle. The efficiency was remarkable.

Ethan lifted his chin slightly. Blaziken strode into the battle area with firm steps.

The Ever Grande Conference had changed Blaziken in ways visible beyond its improved strength. Its movements were steadier, its expression calmer. It had battled from the qualifiers all the way to the final, before enormous crowds. Experiences like that had made it grow.

It was one reason Ethan's Pokemon stood above so many others. Having reached the summit once, they knew what the view from it looked like.

The students stirred at Blaziken's entrance. Earlier they had known little about this particular partner, but during Ethan's break they had hurried through footage of his Ever Grande matches. They had seen how strong Blaziken was and watched its spectacular three-Pokemon sweep. Now it was standing in front of them.

They were excited, though not simply because they feared for Greta. Facing a three-time conference winner, they had moved past taking offense whenever their teacher lost. Seeing Ethan and one of his championship Pokemon battle was enough. Win or lose, they would have something to talk about for days.

Greta had not studied the footage herself, but the students' reaction and Blaziken's bearing told her this Pokemon was special. She glanced at Bea. Blaziken gave her much the same impression as Bea's partners: it would be difficult to handle. Perhaps that was why Ethan had won three conferences.

Scott watched Blaziken without blinking. We haven't even started, and you can already feel how strong it is. No wonder Mr. Ethan has accomplished so much!

He turned to Misty. He didn't have this Blaziken at the Silver Conference, did he? He caught it in Hoenn?

That's right.

Impressive, Scott said. If a newer partner is this strong, I can't imagine how powerful the Pokemon he caught earlier must be by now.

How powerful? Misty considered it seriously and found she did not know the answer herself. Gardevoir, Gengar, the gigantic red Gyarados, and Crystal Steelix came to mind. She doubted any of them would lose even to an Elite Four member's ace.

And Brother Ethan's strongest partners had never been the ones he displayed at conferences. There were the three Legendary birds and two Legendary beasts. Then there were Deoxys and the black Rayquaza, whose power and capacity for destruction she had seen with her own eyes. They could only be described as disasters.

When Misty did not answer, Scott merely smiled. He assumed she might not know much about Ethan's older Pokemon. Besides, if those Pokemon no longer traveled, surely their strength had stopped growing.

The same older student stepped in as referee. At his signal, the match began.

Blaziken surged toward Hariyama. It used no fire. It seemed intent on testing the larger Pokemon at close range, which suited Greta perfectly.

At her command, Hariyama braced itself. It raised its thick palms and watched Blaziken's every movement.

The gap between them vanished in a few seconds. Just before reaching Hariyama, Blaziken accelerated again. Its orange form became a blur.

Block it! Greta shouted.

Hariyama swung both huge hands. Neither it nor Greta had judged Blaziken's speed correctly. In a flash, Blaziken seemed to disappear from directly ahead. It appeared at Hariyama's side, leaped, and drove a powerful kick into its body.

So fast! Greta had barely time to gasp before Hariyama staggered backward.

Its height, bulk, and toughness kept it standing, but the kick had done real damage. One strike was enough to put Greta on alert.

She was a skilled karate fighter as well as a top Pokemon Trainer. From either perspective, she could appreciate the precision of that kick, and she now understood Blaziken's strength more clearly.

Frowning, she ordered Hariyama forward again. The two Pokemon fell into a close-range struggle. Unlike the clash with Bea's Pangoro, this was strength against speed.

Hariyama had the clear advantage in raw power. Blaziken was faster and dared not meet every blow head-on. Yet whenever Blaziken slipped around behind it, Hariyama could not afford a moment's carelessness.

After several exchanges, keeping up with Blaziken was becoming harder for Greta. She looked across the field. Ethan stood as calmly as before, giving only the occasional short, precise command. He looked as though the entire battle was under control.

The contrast frustrated her. They had only just begun, and the outcome was not settled. Why did he look so certain he would win? Yet she could not deny what was happening. She had tried everything she could think of, and Hariyama still had no answer to Blaziken's speed.

Chapter 796: Defeated, and Thanking Him for It

Hariyama's Arm Thrust missed again. Its Force Palm had not touched Blaziken either. Through all their exchanges, it had landed only one Vital Throw, hurling Blaziken hard onto the floor. Blaziken had immediately got up and escaped.

Greta could only sigh to herself. This was difficultfar too difficult. With Blaziken moving so fast, how was Hariyama supposed to catch it?

That did not necessarily mean Blaziken was stronger. Its speed simply left Hariyama's great power with nowhere to go. Against a strength-based opponent like Bea's Pangoro, Hariyama would at least have had a chance to answer each attack.

There was one hopeful thought. Moving at this pace would drain Blaziken's stamina quickly. If Hariyama could endure until it had to slow down, it could finally strike back.

But if Greta could see that, so could Ethan. He had no intention of letting the battle last that long. Blaziken might be a Fighting type, but Ethan had never planned to defeat a pure Fighting type by relying on Fighting moves alone. Fire remained Blaziken's best weapon.

Blaziken evaded another attack and slipped behind Hariyama. It clenched both claws. Flames sprang up around its fists, and it swung them hard.

Fire Punch!

An orange blur swept past. Both fists struck Hariyama in quick succession. With a roar, flames burst from the blows and spread across its back. The pain made Hariyama stagger again.

When the visible flames died away, Hariyama was still suffering from a burn. That was the worst possible news for Greta's plan to prolong the fight. Blaziken could afford to wait. Hariyama could not. Every movement and every punch now brought fresh pain from the burn.

Ethan saw that it was time to finish the round. At his command, fire engulfed Blaziken's body. It used Flare Blitz, charging like a blazing ball toward Hariyama.

For the first time, Blaziken attacked straight from the front. Greta would have preferred it to stay as far away as possible. She wanted Hariyama to dodge, but it could not match Blaziken's speed. The burn tormented it as well. It managed two steps before pain stopped it.

Flare Blitz drove Blaziken to its highest speed yet. It slammed into Hariyama's chest. Blaziken took damage from the collision too, but the attack brought Hariyama down. Its huge body fell backward and struck the floor with a thunderous crash.

Hariyama had spent the round almost helpless. Their different fighting styles had left it absorbing blows while landing very few of its own.

Ethan would have liked to beat Hariyama in a direct contest of strength, but he had no Pokemon that was solely a Fighting type and suited to that kind of struggle. He had chosen a fast, evasive approach instead. Whatever the method, a win was a win.

I can't believe it... A student rubbed his eyes. Master Greta's Hariyama was beaten just like that?

The Arena's students knew how strong it was. Hariyama had defeated countless challengers. Even Bea's Pangoro had needed a long fight to overcome it and had taken considerable damage. Watching this round, the students had felt only helplessness. Blaziken had given it no opening at all.

So this was what a championship-winning Trainer could do? Bea had fought in a completely different style. Still, Blaziken's performance showed its own strength. Another Trainer's Pokemon might have tried the same tactics and been knocked out before succeeding.

Greta shook her head without making excuses and recalled Hariyama. Ethan called Blaziken back as well. This was a two-on-two elimination match, and both teams had already been revealed. He was not going to make Blaziken fight both rounds. Scizor deserved a turn.

With a wave from Ethan, Scizor buzzed its wings and sprang into the center of the field before Greta could send out her second Pokemon. His eagerness suited her. She did not get an opportunity to face an opponent like Ethan every day.

She no longer felt like someone merely defending the Arena from a challenger. She wanted to learn from fighting him. The Blaziken round had exposed weaknesses in her Hariyama. What might this Scizor teach her?

At Greta's signal, Medicham entered the battle area.

The matchup was unfavorable for it. Medicham's Fighting and Psychic types faced Scizor's Bug and Steel types. Still, Scizor's advantage did not look overwhelming at first glance. No one doubted its ability, though. It had traveled with Ethan since Johto and performed well at the Conferences.

The students fell silent and watched intently. The older student refereeing signaled for the second round to begin.

This time Medicham attacked first. Its Fighting and Psychic moves might not do much damage to Scizor, but Greta was not about to stand still. Type matchups were not absolute. Battles had been turned around countless times through composure, experience, and quick decisions.

At Greta's direction, Medicham charged and prepared a Focus Punch. She clearly wanted to test Scizor at close range. Fighting-type Trainers could be stubborn about their specialty; unless forced otherwise, they preferred not to rely on attacks of other types.

White light wrapped Medicham's fist. It ran up to Scizor, leaped high, and drove the punch downward.

Scizor, block it!

Their speeds were comparable. Ethan did not try to evade. Unlike Hariyama, Medicham was not built around raw power, and Scizor had excellent defense and a favorable type matchup. There was little reason for another evasive battle.

Scizor used Metal Claw, slashing upward to meet the descending fist.

Greta was a Frontier Brain for a reason. Even after her battle with Bea, she still had a trick she had not shown. Just before the two attacks met, Medicham's figure flickered and vanished from Scizor's sight. It reappeared behind Scizor and struck from the rear.

Focus Punch landed with a heavy metallic thud, making Scizor stumble. It was a startling blow. Scizor stood about six feet tall, weighed well over two hundred pounds, and had a steel-hard body. To make it lose its footing, Medicham's punch had to carry exceptional force. It had shown nothing like this against Bea.

Even so, the unfavorable type matchup blunted the result. The surprise blow had landed, but it had done less than Greta hoped. Ethan had also seen the resilience of Frontier Brains and Gym Leaders again. At their level, anyone could produce a brilliant move when given the chance.

He was surprised, but not worried. The same trick would not catch him twice.

Greta tried it again, ordering another Focus Punch. Medicham leaped toward Scizor just as before. When it vanished and reappeared, a bright sheen flashed across Scizor's body.

Iron Defense.

The second Focus Punch hit with a deeper clang, as though Medicham had struck a thick iron door. Scizor stood perfectly still and took the blow outright. Medicham pulled its fist back in pain.

Greta winced as she watched it clutch its hand. Between Scizor's natural defense, Iron Defense, and the resistance from its typing, its body had become dauntingly hard.

Then Scizor counterattacked. Its huge pincers snapped forward in a series of punches as fast as bullets. Medicham rallied, dodging and blocking, but its flexible body could avoid only so many. One lapse was enough. Bullet Punch struck again and again, more than a dozen blows in the blink of an eye, leaving Medicham reeling.

Anyone who knew Ethan's battles recognized the danger. Once he found an opening, the outcome was usually settled. His eye for weaknesses was formidable. Without a decisive move to reverse the situation, an opponent could only endure the finish.

Scizor followed Bullet Punch with Metal Claw, then drove Medicham to the floor with Iron Head. Medicham tried one last counterattack, but Scizor evaded it with Double Team. Its chance to recover was gone.

Another Metal Claw landed hard and knocked Medicham unconscious. The challenge was over.

Medicham is unable to battle! Scizor wins! the referee announced.

Misty and the others applauded, and Greta's students joined them with equal enthusiasm. They were Arena pupils and might have mourned their teacher's defeat against anyone else. By now, Ethan had won them over completely.

Even Bea's beauty and skill had not earned quite this response from them. Ethan was a champion, and that changed how they saw the match. Besides, the Battle Arena stood in Kanto, and Ethan had won the Indigo Conference. From a regional point of view, he belonged to their side as much as Greta did. They could cheer for either of them without betraying anyone.

Greta recalled Medicham and approached Ethan, applauding. Against Bea, she had felt she might win a round or two. Against Ethan, she had never seen even the smallest path to victory.

He was far too strong. It was not merely the strength of his Pokemon. Under his direction, Trainer and Pokemon moved together, each supporting the other. Greta could find no weakness in them, while every tiny error she made seemed to grow the instant he noticed it.

Was this the skill of a man who had won three regional conferences? How had he achieved it? Greta had the unsettling feeling that even an Elite Four member might look as fragile as she had against him.

That was eye-opening, she said. Those two aren't even your strongest Pokemon, are they? You beat my best partners so easily with a team below your full strength. I hardly know how to describe you.

Describe me normally. Ethan smiled. My Pokemon are the strong ones. Their own hard work brought them here. I'm just an ordinary person. How am I any different from the rest of you?

It was the sort of thing a champion could say: humble on the surface, yet impossible to separate from the strength he had just displayed.

With a wry smile, Greta took another coin-like golden Symbol from her clothing and placed it in Ethan's hand.

The Guts Symbol of the Battle Arena. It's proof that you defeated me. Please accept it. And thank you, truly. You showed me how much more there is to learn. From now on, I'll train even harder.

Chapter 797: Seeing Sabrina Again

At dusk, Ethan's group stood outside the Battle Arena. Greta had offered to host them for dinner, but Ethan, Misty, May, and Bea politely declined. With Scott accompanying them, they said goodbye.

Greta wished Ethan could stay longer. Every extra day might bring another chance to spar with him and improve. But he had achieved what he came for, and he could not spend more time here. For one thing, he was eager to reach Saffron City. For another...

I'd better not, Ethan said. He looked past Greta at her students and smiled. If I stay much longer, my hand might go numb.

After the match, he had tried to leave, only to be surrounded by students asking for photographs and autographs. It had taken him a long time to satisfy them. Who knew what they might ask for next if he stayed? The joke made them smile sheepishly.

Finally Greta and all her students bowed together in the manner of karate practitioners. Have a safe journey! they called.

Ethan waved. The group climbed into Scott's red sports car and drove away from the Battle Arena.

...

The car stopped smoothly in the open space outside the same Pokemon Center. Ethan and the others got out and waved to Scott.

This is far enough, Ethan said. We can handle the rest of the way ourselves. Thank you for everything.

I should be thanking you, Scott said with a smile. Strong challengers like you push the Frontier Brains to improve. That makes my Battle Frontier stronger!

He paused, then asked, Which facility will you challenge next, Mr. Ethan?

I haven't settled on one, but probably the Battle Factory near Mt. Moon. Why?

Scott's eyes lit up. What a coincidence! I'm heading that way too. It seems I'll get to see you battle again.

Scott was more of a battle enthusiast than Ethan had realized. Then again, without that passion, he would never have built a Battle Frontier this large.

I'll see you there, then.

Until next time!

They watched Scott's car disappear, then went into the Pokemon Center.

Ethan wanted to reach Saffron City before dark. But Misty and May were traveling with him, and he had to consider their stamina and comfort. They would spend the night here and leave in the morning.

After checking in, they put away their luggage. About fifteen minutes later, all four met in the dining room and ordered dinner. Ethan and Misty turned their attention to Bea.

Where are you going next? Misty asked her.

By now everyone understood that Bea sought out Fighting-type Gyms and renowned Fighting-type Trainers. She challenged one, then traveled on to the next. She glanced at Ethan before answering.

I've heard Bruno of Kanto's Elite Four is near Mt. Silver. I plan to challenge him.

Bruno? Misty exclaimed. You're challenging a member of the Elite Four?

Ethan looked at Bea in surprise. May listened closely too. She did not know Kanto's Elite Four well, but surely they were about as strong as Hoenn's. For this beautiful older girl to challenge one took courage. Then May remembered Bea's battle at the Arena and that she was an official Gym Leader. Perhaps it was not so unreasonable.

Have you thought it through? Ethan asked. I don't know Bruno well, and I've never met him, but I know he's strong. Make sure you're prepared.

He was not trying to discourage Bea. Bruno was formidable even among the Elite Four, and some called him a human Pokemon. Anyone who rushed into a challenge against him without enough preparation or strength could be soundly defeated.

Bea nodded. I'll give it everything I have.

Her decision was made. Ethan and Misty told her what little they knew about Bruno, hoping it would help her understand the opponent she had yet to meet. Most of their information was secondhand. Ethan did remember which Pokemon were considered Bruno's strongest, though, and offered a few warnings and thoughts on them.

Bea watched him help her for a long moment before quietly looking away.

Chansey arrived pushing a cart with their dinner. Once the plates were on the table, Ethan noticed how many desserts Bea and May had ordered. May loved all good food. Bea had a particular weakness for sweets. In this, at least, the two were alike.

...

They rested at the Pokemon Center overnight. Early the next morning, Ethan, Misty, and May said goodbye to Bea.

Ethan offered her his hand. You're heading for Mt. Silver, and much of that area is in Johto. We really don't know when we'll meet again. Good luck with your challenge.

We'll be rooting for you, Misty said with a smile. Tell us how it goes!

Bea looked at Ethan's hand, then took it and nodded. Thank you.

She swung her shoulder bag into place and set out west with determined steps, leaving them a striking view of her back.

Misty watched her solitary figure grow distant and sighed.

What's wrong? Ethan asked.

Bea's amazing. She travels and trains all over the world by herself. I couldn't do that.

It's part of her training. Ethan watched Bea go. But even birds return to their nests. Her home is in Galar, and she's a Gym Leader there, so I'm sure she goes back often. Maybe traveling between her Gym duties helps her relax too.

After parting from Bea, Ethan could finally set off for Saffron City. He grew quiet on the road. Misty and May's voices filled the air, but he rarely joined them. As the city drew nearer, his pace quickened. He could hardly wait to get home.

The distance was short enough that they reached Saffron City's outskirts by noon.

At the Saffron Gym, a challenge was about to begin. The challenger was a novice Trainer from Cerulean City, traveling to collect badges. His opponent was to be Sabrina, the beautiful Psychic-type Gym Leader.

The young Trainer was already waiting on the battlefield. Sabrina was walking there through a long corridor with her father when she abruptly stopped.

Hm? Her father looked at her. What is it?

Sabrina turned toward the south. He followed her gaze, but there was only a wall. Before he could ask again, she turned without a word and headed for the exit.

Sabrina! Where are you going? Your challenger is waiting!

She did not look back or explain. Her father could neither stop her nor call her back. He sighed, took out his own Poke Balls, and went to the battlefield alone.

What could have made Sabrina abandon a Gym match so suddenly? It was unlike her. And yet he had a vague feeling something similar had happened before.

Ethan arrived at the Saffron Gym alone. He looked up at the Pokemon League sign above it, feeling excited, uncertain, and a little nervous.

How was Sabrina? Had her feelings for him changed? Would she greet him as she had before?

He raised his head. The Gym doors opened, and Sabrina stood at the top of the steps, smiling down at him. The moment their eyes met, Ethan's mind went still. For that instant, neither saw anyone else.

He had only begun to lift a hand when Sabrina vanished from the steps. His vision blurred. Before he understood what had happened, her warm, fragrant body was in his arms. Her long black hair swept against his face.

Ethan held her tightly, and she held him just as tightly.

Sabrina. I'm here... he whispered.

She kissed him before he could say more. He answered her eagerness with his own. A long while passed before they drew apart.

Sabrina leaned back, and Ethan finally had a chance to look at her. Her black hair still fell softly to her shoulders. Her eyes, her expression, and her familiar bearing had not changed. She was still Sabrina.

As the first rush of emotion ebbed, Ethan remembered where they were. The Gym stood beside a street. Pedestrians passed by, and Trainers came to challenge it. Before anyone noticed them, he patted Sabrina's back.

Let's go inside. If we stay out here, we'll end up in today's headlines.

Sabrina did not care whether anyone saw them, but she had no objection when Ethan asked. She led him inside. At his insistent urging, they went straight to her room.

His longing for her was nearly overflowing. He needed another way to express it. Sabrina was his lover, and with her he held nothing back.

...

Meanwhile, in the Saffron Gym's battle hall, Sabrina's father finally defeated the novice challenger after three difficult rounds. He gave the disappointed young Trainer a few encouraging words and watched him leave. Then he shook his head and returned to the Gym's inner rooms.

He had not battled in some time and felt rusty, but he had managed to defend the badge. Young Trainers were getting stronger. This one had nearly beaten him.

He looked at his watch and frowned. Where had Sabrina gone? Why was she still not back?

Growing concerned, he went to the front entrance and looked outside. He saw no sign of her. A few students who practiced psychic abilities at the Gym happened to come in, and he stopped them.

Have you seen Sabrina?

Miss Sabrina isn't in the Gym? They shook their heads. Sorry, we didn't see her on our way back. Could she have returned already?

No. If she had, she'd have come to the battlefield. Something must have delayed her. He sighed. Well, if the Gym Leader isn't here, we can't accept any more challenges today. Put up the closed sign. The Gym will take the rest of the day off.

After giving the instructions, he decided not to worry further and left. Unlike Sabrina, he did not live at the Gym. He had a home nearby. Though their relationship as father and daughter had improved lately, they had long lived apart.

With Sabrina missing and these new Trainers becoming harder for him to handle, a day off sounded welcome. Normal business could resume when she returned. Hands behind his back, he went down the steps toward the street.

He had taken only a few steps when he faintly heard a woman's breath coming in short gasps. The sound seemed to come from a window on the side of Sabrina's bedroom. He almost laughed at himself.

Listen to that. It had been so long since he last battled that he was hearing things. Sabrina had gone out; how could there be a woman's voice in her room? Especially a voice like that?

He shook his head, thought no more of it, and walked away humming as he glanced up at the bright sky.

Chapter 798: Gengar's Little Joke

A battle was unfolding inside the Saffron Gym, though it was taking place in Sabrina's room rather than on the battlefield.

Ethan performed admirably. Over the course of more than an hour, he defeated Sabrina so thoroughly that she could only beg him to stop. They had gone three rounds, with only a few minutes of rest between them. By the end, Sabrina was overheated and lay breathing hard, unable to get up.

Evidently Ethan's Pokemon were not the only ones who could put on an impressive performance in battle.

He lay on the bed, gazed at the unfamiliar ceiling, and stretched. Youth really was his greatest advantage. He had energy to spare.

He drew an exhausted Sabrina into his arms and breathed in the scent of her hair. For the moment, he felt completely content. The desperate longing and passion of their reunion had settled into a quiet warmth.

One concern came to him. In the heat of the moment, he had forgotten to ask whether she was in a safe part of her cycle, and he had not prepared a condom. He glanced at Sabrina, lying peacefully beside him like a tame cat, and could not bring himself to spoil the moment by asking now.

He would ask later. And even if there were consequences? They had already chosen each other. They were still young, though, and it would be early for them to become parents. For now, he wanted to enjoy the tenderness of being together again.

...

That afternoon, Ethan showered and came out of Sabrina's room feeling refreshed. The world seemed brighter. His legs and lower back were tired, however, and he had no wish to fight another battle any time soon.

Fortunately, he had had the foresight to send Misty and May to explore nearby before entering Saffron City. With those two around, he and Sabrina could hardly have enjoyed even a quiet embrace, let alone time alone together.

He checked the time. Misty and May had agreed to meet him at the Gym, but they had not returned yet. He decided to wander around while he waited. Sabrina needed to wash carefully after all the exertion before she came out to see anyone.

Ethan strolled through the Gym. He realized he had never properly explored it. Besides serving as an official Pokemon League Gym for challengers, it was also a center for studying psychic abilities. The lessons were Sabrina's principal income apart from League funding.

It reminded him of Erika's flower and perfume shops, and of Roxanne's work as a teacher. Different as their businesses were, each Gym Leader had a way to earn money beyond the Gym. Of course, some pursued pleasure more than business. Brawly of Dewford, for instance, spent much of every day surfing.

Several rooms opened off the first-floor hall. In one, men and women dressed in white sat at desks with spoons in their hands. They tried to bend the spoons with psychic power or guess what was on the other side of cards.

Not everyone had a talent for psychic abilities. Some stared until their eyes ached without making a spoon move at all. Their occasional correct guesses about the cards seemed more like luck.

With nothing else to do, Ethan opened the door and went in. No one noticed him at first. Only when he reached a table and picked up a spoon did the man across from him look up.

Who are you? The man studied him. I haven't seen you here before. You're not one of us, are you?

No. I'm visiting the Gym Leader. I had some time free, so I thought I'd look around.

Visiting Miss Sabrina? The man looked doubtful. He did not believe some stranger could casually come to see the famously distant psychic Gym Leader. Still, he let it pass. You're welcome to look, but don't handle our equipment.

Ethan glanced at the table. You mean the spoons?

Of course. Psychic ability is something you're born with. Without the talent, you can train all you like and never reach it.

Ethan looked around. Everyone here seemed to be a beginner; no one had shown much power. Curious, he asked, You've been training here a while, haven't you? What can you do now?

The question was sincere, but the man smiled proudly. Since you want to know, I'll show you.

He took a spoon, fixed his eyes on it, and shouted as his entire body strained. Veins stood out on him. Under the pressure of an unseen force, the spoon slowly bent until it formed a right angle.

The man exhaled and looked at Ethan with unmistakable pride. See? That's my psychic power. Someone without the gift could never do it.

Leaving Pokemon aside, the gap between this class and Sabrina was enormous. Even Tate and Liza at the Mossdeep Gym were far beyond them. Perhaps with psychic abilities, talent really did set a hard limit. Years of practice could accomplish something, but it could hardly turn a beginner into Sabrina.

Ethan gave a polite little clap. He was about to speak when the man grinned. That took me three years to learn. What do you think? Want to try?

I'll pass. I know myself. I have no talent for this, and I've never practiced.

He started to leave. His shadow shifted beneath his feet. A lock of hair beside his temple moved, as though something invisible had brushed against it. Two seconds later, Ethan shook his head helplessly and looked back at the man.

All right. I'll give it a try.

You really will? The man had only wanted to impress him. He had not expected this young stranger to try it himself. Well, it would teach him the difference between a psychic student and an ordinary person.

He placed a fresh spoon on the table, eager to see Ethan's expression when he failed.

Ethan held out his hand. He made no show of concentrating. To the man's shock, the spoon flew straight from the table into Ethan's palm.

What?

The man's eyes bulged. Worse was to come. With Ethan still apparently doing nothing, the spoon in his hand twisted itself into a tight spiral.

I... I... I... The man could barely form a word.

His reaction brought the others over. When they heard that Ethan had supposedly never used psychic power before, yet had twisted a spoon like that, they gaped.

How is that possible?

He must be joking. We've practiced for so long...

A prodigy!

They crowded around Ethan, all talking at once. Before they could question him further, Sabrina's voice came from the doorway.

I wondered where you'd gone. So this is where you were.

Ethan waved to the students, smiled, and went to meet her. They walked out side by side. The sight shocked the students even more than the spoon trick.

Did I see that right? one whispered. Miss Sabrina spoke to him. And they left together?

The man who had challenged Ethan remembered his claim to be visiting Sabrina. He had been telling the truth. But who was he? How could Sabrina treat a man with such warmth? Both surprises had overturned everything the student thought he knew.

Outside the room, Sabrina laughed softly. I didn't know you felt like playing tricks on my students.

It wasn't me. Ethan spread his hands. It was Gengar.

Gengar appeared in midair beside him with a wicked grin. The flying spoon and its twisted shape had been its work.

Heh. I only wanted to tease them a little, Gengar said. He questioned my Trainer first. I had to show him what we could do.

That wasn't showing him. That was making a fool of him. Ethan sighed, then remembered something. Sabrina, I sent that Jigglypuff I caughtthe one that puts people to sleepto stay here. How is it doing?

I'm glad you still remember it. Sabrina smiled. You never asked about it when we talked. I thought you'd forgotten.

It was true. Ethan had not checked on Jigglypuff once since catching it and sending it here. He had not caught it because he wanted another partner, though. He had wanted to spare the world a menace. A Jigglypuff carrying a microphone could create a disaster wherever it went.

I left it with you because I knew you could keep it under control. Where is it now?

Probably wandering around the city. I hid its microphone, then let it roam. It used to sneak back at night to steal the microphone. After I turned it into a doll a few times, it settled down.

Ethan nodded. Sabrina had not confined Jigglypuff, only taken away its weapon. Until it recovered the microphone, it should remain quiet. Taking the microphone back from Sabrina would be difficult for it.

Still, be careful, he said. It might find another one somewhere.

The Gym doors opened as he spoke. Misty and May came in.

Good, it isn't closed after all. Misty exhaled in relief when she saw Ethan. There was a sign outside saying the Gym was closed today. I thought no one was here. I'm glad we came in to check.

Closed? Sabrina tilted her head. Perhaps her father had put up the sign. She said nothing about it.

Hello, Sabrina. It's good to see you again. Misty brought May forward. This is a friend we met in Hoenn. She came with us to visit Kanto.

Misty had evidently told May that Sabrina mattered to Ethan. May greeted her a little stiffly. Hello, Sabrina.

Sabrina nodded a greeting to both girls. Ethan turned to them. Where did you go all this time?

Misty brightened and held up a flyer. Brother Ethan, look what we found! Saffron City is holding a Pokemon Contest in a few days. We can't miss a chance like this!

Ethan looked at May. Do you want to enter?

I do. May nodded firmly, hope in her eyes. I want to see how a Kanto Contest differs from the ones in Hoenn!

Chapter 799: News from Johto

Kanto had Pokemon Contests too. They differed a little from the Contests in other regions, but the idea was much the same. Ethan and Misty had never had reason to look into them before. Now they were traveling with May, a Coordinator, and that had changed.

Ethan took the flyer from Misty. The Contest would be held in a forest park within Saffron City, not far from the Gym. It was a sizable event, but it would not begin for several days. There was time to challenge another one or two Frontier facilities before returning.

He needed to ask May what she wanted. Will you come with us to the next facility, or would you rather stay here for now?

I'll travel with you, May answered without hesitation.

You don't need time to prepare? Ethan gestured toward Sabrina. If you want to stay, you can stay with her. You won't need to worry about food or a room, and there's space here for training.

Really, it's all right. May shook her head. I'd rather keep traveling with you. Misty will help me practice along the way.

Ethan let the matter rest. He had made the offer for May's sake, but pressing it might make her think he wanted to send her away. Traveling would be good for her too. She would see more than she could by training in one place, even if she had less time to prepare specifically for the Contest.

That evening, the four of them ate dinner at a Western-style restaurant. Ethan explained to Sabrina why he had returned to Kanto.

She was disappointed to hear he would leave the next day. She knew he had goals he wanted to pursue and did not try to stop him. Besides, he would return in a few days for May's Contest. Knowing they would see each other again soon eased the parting.

They went back to the Saffron Gym that night. With another separation ahead, Ethan and Sabrina spent more time together. After the afternoon they had already shared, it tested his stamina. Even an iron-bodied man might have struggled with so many rounds in so few hours. Fortunately, the oysters he had ordered at dinner seemed to help when he needed them.

Still, Misty looked concerned when she saw the shadows under his eyes the next morning. Ethan waved her worry away with a smile. A little exhaustion was nothing beside being apart from Sabrina for so long.

After breakfast, they said goodbye outside the Gym. Sabrina stood on the steps, a little tired herself but glowing. Ethan smiled up at her.

You don't need to walk us any farther. You're a Gym Leaderwhat would people think if they saw? Don't worry. I'll be back in a few days.

Sabrina nodded. Ethan waved once more and left with Misty and May. She watched him go.

Not long after leaving the Gym, the three passed a middle-aged man walking toward it. They had gone a few steps beyond him when Misty hesitated.

Why did that man look familiar?

Did he? Ethan raised an eyebrow. He thought back but did not remember meeting the man.

I've got it! He's Sabrina's father. I met him when I came with Ash to challenge the Saffron Gym.

Sabrina's father? Ethan looked back. The man was indeed heading toward the Gym. Surprised, Ethan shook his head. Never mind. Let's keep moving.

...

Celadon City was the nearest city to Saffron. Ethan knew very well who was there, but he did not dare go to see Erika yet. He had only just reunited with Sabrina. He needed a little time before he could face Erika with a clear mind.

There was another reason too: his staminaand his aching lower backwould not allow it.

Instead, he chose the second Frontier facility near the area south of Lavender Town as their destination.

Misty could have left the group by now and gone home to Cerulean City. Perhaps she was reluctant to part, or perhaps she did not miss her three sisters quite enough yet. She had shown no inclination to go. Ethan did not suggest it either. He had traveled with her for so long that he was used to having her beside him. He would miss her if she left.

They took the main road east out of Saffron City. As they walked, Misty told May about the strange and funny things she and Ash had encountered in this area. Her stories stirred Ethan's memories of his own early travels.

He felt a strong nostalgia. Kanto really had been his starting region, the place where he took his first steps as a Trainer and met so many people and Pokemon.

After a little more than half a day, they reached Lavender Town. The town was famous for ghostly incidents and as a resting place for departed Pokemon. Like Mt. Pyre in Hoenn, its Pokemon Tower was where people held funerals and memorials.

None of the three wanted to linger. They stopped for lunch, then planned to continue while there was still daylight. Ethan's phone rang.

To his surprise, the caller was Miki, eldest of Ecruteak City's five Kimono Sisters. Why would she be calling him?

Hello, Miss Miki. Is something wrong?

Well... Her voice came through the phone, with faint voices of her younger sisters behind her. Are you planning to visit Johto any time soon, Mr. Ethan?

Johto? Ethan raised an eyebrow. Has something happened?

Nothing like that. Miki sounded a little embarrassed. Your Eevee has been away from us for a long time, and we miss it. We hoped it might come back to visit.

So that was it. Eevee had spent a long time with the sisters, longer than it had with Ethan. To them, it was family. Since they had entrusted it to him, he ought to bring it back when they asked.

The timing works out well, Ethan said after a moment. I've just returned to Kanto. Once I finish what I'm doing here, I'll make time to come over.
