Really? That's wonderful! We'll look forward to seeing you.

They exchanged a few more words and hung up. Ethan had barely lowered his phone when it rang again. At first he thought Miki had forgotten something, but the screen showed a different caller: Liza of Charicific Valley.

What was happening today? Why was everyone calling him at once? There was only one likely reason Liza would contact him, so he answered immediately.

Mr. Ethan, she began, are you free any time soon?

What's happened? Is something wrong with my Charizard?

She heard the concern in his voice and laughed. It's good news. Your Charizard has trained hard and is preparing to challenge the strongest Charizard in the valley. If it wins, it'll be the strongest here. You're its Trainer; I thought you'd want to see that.

What? His Charizard was ready to challenge the valley's strongest? Had it grown that much? Ethan was thrilled. Now he had every reason to go to Johto.

Will it happen in the next few days? Because...

Liza cut him off. You're busy right now, aren't you? Don't worry. I called to let you know in advance. Charizard doesn't have to challenge it this week. It can wait until you have time to be there.

It was unusually thoughtful of Liza to arrange things that way. It gave Ethan enough time to plan his travels. He thanked her and ended the call.

He felt newly energized. Once Charizard finished this challenge, it could return to his team. Eevee's visit to the sisters might also provide the occasion for it to evolve. Either event could make his team much stronger.

...

The three left Lavender Town and traveled north. Their next destination was called the Battle Dome. The name sounded grand, but Ethan assumed that, in the end, it would be much like a Gym and offer little unusual.

Misty was disappointed. Between Battle Arena and Battle Dome, she had expected the buildings to match their names or at least serve some special purpose. Apparently she had expected too much.

By evening, after a full day's travel, they reached their destination. They were too tired to inspect the Dome. They found rooms at a Pokemon Center and soaked in hot baths, washing away the day's fatigue.

The next morning they approached the facility refreshedand discovered that it was anything but ordinary. The Battle Dome was far grander than the Battle Arena. Hundreds of people streamed through its entrance, making the area bustle. Ethan spotted reporters in the crowd and helicopters circling overhead.

This is quite a production, Misty said in surprise. Why are so many people here? Is there an event?

I don't know. Let's ask someone.

They moved through the crowd and soon learned the reason. A Frontier match was being held today featuring Tucker, the Battle Dome's superstar. Tucker was also its Frontier Brain.

So it's just a battle, Misty said. I thought there was some other event to draw a crowd this large.

At least we can see how popular Tucker is. Ethan shook his head. Come on. Let's go in.

The Dome's interior surprised them again. Nearly every seat was filled. Men and women of every age had come, though groups of young women were the most noticeable. Ethan and the girls were increasingly curious about the man they were waiting to see.

They found their seats. Soon the lights dimmed and the large screen played a promotional video for the challenger. As it ended, a young female Trainer stepped onto the stage.

A second screen lit up on the opposite side. An announcer's voice rang through the Dome.

A Pokemon battle blooms like a fleeting flower! People of the Battle Dome, revel in dazzling moves and the art of ingenious tactics! The Dome's superstarTuckerhas arrived!

Spotlights flashed and petals fell. A man in a black cloak descended into a Trainer's area. Suspended as though on wires, he swept in a circuit above the arena before landing.

The crowd reached a new pitch. Shrill screams from his female fans filled Ethan's ears.

He's incredibly popular! Misty covered her ears. May nearly buried her head against Misty to escape the noise.

Ethan could not hear Misty over the cheering. He kept his eyes on the cloaked man, curious to see what kind of person this Frontier Brain was.

Tucker landed and swept his cloak aside, revealing himself. In a strong voice, he called, Beautiful people, welcome to the Battle Dome!

Chapter 800: Returning to a Familiar Place

The large screen finally gave Ethan a clear look at Tucker. He was ordinary-looking, hardly anyone Ethan would call handsome. His bright purple and pale white outfit made him resemble a huge dragonfly, and shiny purple boots completed the strange effect.

What Ethan found hardest to accept was the man's long reddish-purple hair. Tucker had tied it into two tails, with the hair at his temples swept out to the sides. It looked like a great windmill. On a man around thirty, the whole ensemble was well beyond Ethan's taste.

Ugly, he thought. Bizarre. Still, Tucker had a right to dress as he liked. People pursued beauty in different ways, and Tucker clearly enjoyed drawing eyes with elaborate clothes and presentation.

He must also be strong. That went without saying. He was said to be skilled at performing for his fans and engaging with them, which helped explain his popularity.

Once Tucker had finished showing himself off, the match finally moved toward the battle. A referee who also served as host stepped onto a mobile, hovering commentary platform. It rose above the field, making Ethan and the girls take another look at the Dome's technology.

Neither the Indigo nor the Silver Conference had possessed a floating commentary stand like this. Scott and Tucker had plainly poured money and effort into the Battle Dome. The investment was paying off. The packed, enthusiastic crowd grew wilder under the lights and special effects.

The host explained the rules. Ethan listened closely enough to learn that Battle Dome matches were Double Battles. A side lost when both its Pokemon were unable to battle. It was another change from the Battle Arena.

As the Frontier Brain, Tucker released his Pokemon first. Two flashes of blue light revealed Swampert and Arcanine.

Sending out two Pokemon should have been ordinary. Tucker's exaggerated movements, the host's commentary, and the lights turned it into a performance.

Ah! Arcanine, the swift runner of fire! Swampert, ruler of water and earth! These are the two opponents our challenger faces today! Tucker has brought us a fusion of blazing heat and icy cool!

The Pokemon cried out on cue, and the cheers surged again.

He really knows how to put on a show, Misty murmured as the audience chanted Tucker's name.

May's eyes glinted. She seemed to be taking inspiration from the entrance. Misty noticed at once and hurried to stop her.

Wait! Don't copy him. Stick with your own style.

The young woman challenging Tucker released her own two Pokemon. Having seen Swampert and Arcanine first, she chose a team with favorable type matchups. That gave her confidence, but a Frontier Brain was still a Frontier Brain. After barely a dozen exchanges, Tucker defeated her easily.

The crowd's cheering reached its loudest point yet. Short as the battle had been, Ethan had seen enough to judge Tucker's ability. He was good. Among official Gym Leaders, Ethan would place him around the lower middle.

Tucker was especially fond of using his Pokemon together, with tactics that gave him the initiative. Their cooperation let him recover even when he faced an unfavorable type matchup. That was the main reason he had won so comfortably. But Ethan had seen the approach now. It would be less effective against him.

Tucker gave another victory performance. Only when he had finally finished did the crowd, still hungry for more, begin to leave.

Ethan took Misty and May to a member of staff to register for a challenge. The process presented a few complications. Whether Tucker needed time to gather spectators, advertise, and arrange the show, or was simply busy, the earliest available match was the next morning. The staff also required a list of the challenger's past achievements.

The reason was plain. Tucker's every appearance was meant to draw attention. What could produce more excitement than a superstar beating a celebrated opponent?

Ethan considered giving a made-up identity to avoid a fuss. Then he remembered that many spectators might have watched him battle. A false name could cause confusion. He registered as himself.

As soon as the staff member entered Ethan's name, his tournament record filled the computer screen. The man stared, mouth open.

Indigo Conference champion. Silver Conference champion. Ever Grande Conference champion. Honorable Trainer of the Orange League. Sea Hero of the Whirl Islands.

There were so many titles they almost blurred together. Was this really someone he should be handling at an ordinary registration desk?

Several seconds passed before he remembered to stand. M-Mr. Ethan. Your registration is complete. Under our rules, your match is scheduled for nine tomorrow morning. Please make sure you're here on time.

That was what reputation could do. Ethan hardly had to say anything. A champion with those accomplishments was coming to challenge the Dome; how could any staff member treat it casually?

The man watched Ethan leave, then let out a breath. Without wasting another moment, he hurried upstairs to Tucker's lounge.

Inside, Tucker was posing before a large mirror while his manager organized something nearby. The manager frowned at the staff member's hasty entrance. What's happened?

Still out of breath, the man told them who had registered.

Ethan?

Both Tucker and his manager followed international news as part of their work. They knew about Ethan's victories in three regions. Even so, hearing that he had come to the Battle Dome shocked them.

Are you certain? Tucker asked. It's really him?

Absolutely. I checked the records. His face matches too. There's no mistake.

The manager thought for a moment and sighed. Ethan... I've watched his battles. He has ambitious plans. He used different Pokemon in all three conference finals. It looks as if he's trying to raise every one of his partners to championship strength. Why come here now? Does he have some other purpose?

He glanced at Tucker for a reaction and found his eyes shining.

What an opportunity! Tucker laughed. Once the news spreads, tomorrow's tickets will sell out. The crowd will go mad for me!

The manager frowned. But he's extremely strong. Are you sure you can handle him? If you lose...

Win or lose, we benefit. Tucker turned to him, eyes bright. Publicize the match. If he beats me, he's a three-time champion, so no one will blame me. But if I win...

He let the thought hang. The manager understood.

You think you can beat him?

How will we know unless I try? Tucker said confidently. I'm the Battle Dome's superstar. If I hadn't promised Scott I'd run this facility, winning the Indigo Conference would have been easy for me. Ethan wouldn't have had his chance!

The manager seemed encouraged. He turned to the staff member. Publish this immediately. Make sure every spectator knows. Call the reporters too. I want this match advertised everywhereideally, all of Kanto should hear about it before tomorrow.

But... The staff member hesitated. Isn't that difficult on such short notice?

I'll double your pay this month.

Understood. I'll get it done!

...

Unaware of what the Dome was planning, Ethan and the girls checked into a nearby Pokemon Center. Their match would not happen until the next day, so they had to stay another night.

The pause suited May. She needed time to adjust her plans and practice for the Contest. Ethan did not have to help. Misty was already working through ideas with her. The two girls talked animatedly, heads together, leaving Ethan little chance to join in. He went to find something to do on his own.

The Center stood on a low hill, overlooking a wide stretch of countryside. Clouds drifted slowly overhead. They were far from Kanto's busy central cities, in a sparsely settled region of forests and plains. From here, the main road continued toward Cerulean City if one turned west farther on.

Cerulean City. No wonder Misty had grown chattier as they came closer, while her expression grew more downcast. Once they reached her hometown, she would be home. And going home meant leaving Ethan.

She was young enough that every thought showed on her face. No one had to guess what was troubling her. But there was little to be done. She could not travel the world with him forever. Everyone eventually had to return to their own life.

Ethan stood on the grass and looked into the distance for a while. Then another thought came to him. If Cerulean City was close, so was that other place.

He had time free. Why not go see it?

Ethan let Misty and May know where he was going, released Dragonite, and climbed onto its back. Dragonite rose through the clouds and raced toward Cerulean Cave.

There was only one reason for Ethan to make such a detour: Mewtwo.

Dragonite, his second flying mount, pushed its speed to the limit. The landscape flashed past beneath the clouds. A little more than an hour later, after skirting Cerulean City, Ethan spotted Nugget Bridge in the distance.

That brought back memories. On his first visit to the bridge, five Trainers had blocked his way. Were they still there after all this time? It made no difference. He had not come to see them.

Dragonite landed by the riverbank near the bridge. Following his memory of the route, Ethan soon found the entrance to Cerulean Cave.

He did not know whether Mewtwo still lived here. He did not know where else to look for it, either. He hoped it had stayed.

He recalled Dragonite, released Gardevoir, and called Gengar out. With both partners beside him, he entered the cave.

The path beneath his feet felt familiar and strange at once. Everything looked much as it had when he first came here.

Wild Pokemon began peering out before he had gone far. They sensed the power coming from Gardevoir and Gengar and wisely kept their distance. Even territorial Pokemon that lived in groups stayed in their nests, pretending they had seen nothing.

Ethan was only halfway through the cave when two Ultra Balls at his waist began shaking violently.

Chapter 801: Mewtwo, I'm Back!

Ethan gently steadied the two Ultra Balls at his waist and continued deeper into Cerulean Cave with Gardevoir and Gengar.

The cave was dim. Its floor was wet and slippery, and underground water blocked the way in places. With Gardevoir and Gengar beside him, none of it posed much of a problem. His long travels had also made him more agile. He could climb over smooth boulders with care and edge along narrow, steep paths by gripping the stone beside him. Only at the broad underground lake did he ask Gardevoir to teleport him across so his clothes would stay dry.

After another half hour, he reached the cave's deepest chamber. The narrow passage opened into a wide, circular space. Crystals scattered throughout the chamber caught and reflected a faint light, bathing it in a soft glow.

Mewtwo sat cross-legged on a flat stone at the far end.

It was still here. Its appearance had not changed, but Ethan had grown stronger since their last meeting. This time he could feel the oppressive power Mewtwo kept hidden within itself.

As though it sensed him enter, Mewtwo slowly opened its eyes.

I knew it was you the moment you stepped into the cave.

Its voice was as calm as Ethan remembered, reaching his mind directly through telepathy. He was not surprised it had noticed him. Deoxys and Rayquaza had sensed Mewtwo from inside their Ultra Balls; Mewtwo could surely sense them in return.

It's been a long time, Mewtwo. Ethan smiled as if greeting an old friend. I wasn't sure I'd find you here. After all this time, you're still using the cave as your hideout.

Mewtwo floated off its stone and came slowly toward him. Its gaze passed over Gardevoir and Gengar, then settled on Ethan's belt.

Your Pokemon have grown considerably stronger since we last met. Why have you come this time?

Its presence sharpened. A wave of air swept out beneath it, stirring Ethan's hair and blowing grit into the air. He had to keep dust from his eyes.

Only two sentences in, and Mewtwo was already putting on pressure. Ethan complained to himself, but he could hardly blame it.

Imagine sitting peacefully at home when someone walked in unannounced, came straight to your bedroom, brought two bodyguards, and kept two more powerful companions hidden at his waist. Anyone would be on guard. The fact that Mewtwo had spoken to Ethan first showed it remembered their connection. A stranger might already have been attacked.

It also showed how wary Mewtwo had become of Ethan's growing strength. It remembered that on his last visit, Ethan had tested it with the Psychic-type Pokemon beside him. Now he had returned with even stronger partners. His purpose was obvious.

Ethan did not hide it. He took the two Ultra Balls from his belt.

I met two new partners on this journey. They're both strong, and they heard you were strong too. They want to test themselves against you, so I've taken the liberty of visiting.

Stopping by to test Mewtwo was becoming a habit whenever Ethan returned to Kanto. His words were polite, but Mewtwo understood. He wanted a battle. If Ethan won, he would walk away unharmed. If Mewtwo lost, the man would likely throw a Poke Ball without hesitation and try to catch it.

Mewtwo was used to such challenges. It understood what it meant to exist as a Pokemon, and, more than anything, it did not fear a fight.

It was Mewtwo, a being made to surpass Mew. Did Ethan think a couple of stray Pokemon could defeat it? How naive.

Mewtwo did not say yes outright. Its rising power was answer enough. Strange force filled the chamber until even the air seemed solid.

It was Mewtwo, all right. It had felt Deoxys and the black Rayquaza and was not intimidated in the least.

When Ethan saw it was ready, he pointed upward. There's too little room here. Let's take this outside.

Without waiting for its agreement, he had Gardevoir teleport him out of Cerulean Cave.

...

Ethan, Gardevoir, and Gengar appeared in a clearing and landed steadily. Before entering the cave, Ethan had asked Gardevoir to mark this spot so it could bring them back in an instant. The preparation made it plain that he had planned to challenge Mewtwo all along.

Mewtwo appeared moments later. Ethan did not begin the battle there. He released Dragonite, climbed aboard, and flew north until they reached a remote forest lake.

Mewtwo followed. When Ethan stopped, it hovered over the water.

Is this the battlefield you've chosen?

Yes. Ethan looked around. We won't have to worry about people seeing us. Even if the battle causes a commotion and someone comes looking later, they won't discover your cave from this far away. We won't have to destroy the vegetation around it either. Thoughtful of me, wasn't it?

Mewtwo ignored his self-satisfaction. Disorder had followed it since the day it was created. If people noticed it, so what? It had never cared much for human opinion. Coldness was part of its nature.

Under Mewtwo's gaze, Ethan took out both Ultra Balls. He tossed them lightly in his hand but released only the black Rayquaza first. He wanted to see what a single Rayquaza could do against Mewtwo.

The sky darkened at once. Clouds spread overhead until the forest and lake lay beneath a lid of black. Wind began to rise. Rayquaza had not even appeared, and already the weather was changing around it.

The Ultra Ball opened. Blue light flashed. With a deafening clap of thunder, a huge, winding dragon emerged. It roared and climbed toward the clouds.

Mewtwo watched calmly from the air as the black Rayquaza vanished into the cloud cover. Then Rayquaza came down again and fixed its immense head toward Mewtwo.

The two faced each other, one enormous and the other small by comparison. Rayquaza's presence was overwhelming even as it hovered still. Mewtwo answered with a surge of power of its own. Against the dark sky, its pale body stood out sharply.

Mewtwo was small only beside Rayquaza. At nearly two meters tall, it was larger than most adult humans.

They studied each other. Rayquaza looked wary; Mewtwo's expression scarcely changed.

I've seen this species in the upper atmosphere. Rayquaza, isn't it? An ancient Pokemon and a Legendary Pokemon. It has quite a collection of titles. I didn't expect you to catch one in so little time.

It seemed to be acknowledging Ethan's progress, but its tone suggested it was unimpressed. Power gave Mewtwo confidence. It had not fought Rayquaza yet, but it was certain it would not lose.

Ethan let its ancient-sounding pride pass. Mewtwo had been created only a few years ago, but it possessed the strength to justify its words. He knew that well enough. He even suspected his Rayquaza would lose if they fought one-on-one.

Rayquaza was formidable too. Both were Legendary Pokemon. Only a battle could show how this meeting would end.

Ethan waved a hand. High overhead, the black Rayquaza opened its mouth and fired a deadly beam at Mewtwo.

Mewtwo's gaze sharpened. It formed a psychic shield before itself and caught the entire blast.

With a heavy roar, the beam struck the shield. It slowly dispersed without breaking through. Mewtwo might dismiss its opponent in words, but it was taking the battle seriously. It would not leave itself exposed to a hit like that.

It must have felt the force packed into Rayquaza's attack. Otherwise it would not have put up so strong a barrier.

Watching from Dragonite's back beyond the field, Ethan could only smile and shake his head. Rayquaza belonged among the world's mightiest Pokemon, especially as an attacker. Few could defeat it at all, and none could safely ignore a direct hit.

If Mewtwo had treated it as lightly as its words suggested, it would have paid for the mistake. But Mewtwo was experienced and clever. Its actions were more cautious than its voice, and it gave Rayquaza no easy opening.

Its own attacks were dangerous, even in its present form, and not far behind Rayquaza's. More importantly, Mewtwo was far faster. Rayquaza would have to guard against every opening it gave away.

The probing exchange was over. They fought in earnest, and the battle grew fierce at once.

Soon Ethan could hardly follow Mewtwo with his eyes. A pale streak moved constantly before the black Rayquaza, which twisted its great body to meet it. Attacks flew without pause. Ethan recognized some; others he could not even name.

Missed attacks struck the lake below, sending up one explosion after another. The surrounding forest shuddered, whole stands of trees rolling in waves beneath the force of the fight.

Ethan patted Dragonite, and it carried him farther from the field. Even there, the shock waves made it beat its wings hard to hold steady. They retreated again.

From this distance, Ethan was only a spectator. That was fine. He had not planned to direct Rayquaza closely today. At this level, his commands would mostly concern the timing of attacks and evasions. The actual clash depended on the Pokemon themselves.

This might be the first time even Mewtwo had faced a Pokemon this powerful. Rayquaza had its own challenges, but Mewtwo too would have to learn whether it could adapt and bring out all its strength.

Wind drove the clouds into thicker masses. Thunder cracked. Then torrential rain fell over the battlefield. Ethan was glad he had moved away before it soaked him. From a dry vantage, he could watch and even think through what each Pokemon was doing.

They were among the world's strongest. Their battles could change the weather, alter the terrain, and send wild Pokemon fleeing. Yet neither was without weaknesses.

From a Trainer's point of view, both Mewtwo and the black Rayquaza still fought much like wild Pokemon. They drew on overwhelming power and instinct, but had not yet developed the disciplined habits or refined control that came from training within a team. For all their ferocity, they wasted effort at times.

That was why a trained Pokemon could sometimes defeat a wild Pokemon of similar type and strength. If Mewtwo and Rayquaza ever truly learned to fight as partners with Trainers, both could become stronger still.

That was a distant prospect. Ethan had not caught Mewtwo. Rayquaza was gradually accepting that it belonged to a human Trainer, but it would take time before he could direct it as freely as he directed the three Legendary birds.

Chapter 802: That Day Will Come Soon

The black Rayquaza crashed into the lake. Mewtwo followed it under the surface. They fought through the water, churning it into chaos, then rose back into the sky. Water poured through breaks torn along the shore and flooded nearly half the surrounding forest.

They had been fighting for only seven or eight minutes, but Ethan could already judge the balance between them. Unfortunately, Rayquaza did not seem able to beat Mewtwo.

Its huge body brought no advantage. Against Pokemon of similar size, Rayquaza could use its bulk without giving ground. Against a human-shaped opponent like Mewtwo, that length became a burden. It could not guard its head and tail at once. Mewtwo was faster already, and Rayquaza's size offered even more openings to exploit.

More importantly, Mewtwo had overwhelming power and a formidable mind. It could move things at a distance, control the weather, shape objects with thought, turn back time, alter memories, and influence minds. It was not confined to trading one move for another. It found creative, unexpected ways to hurt Rayquaza.

Both Pokemon belonged among the world's strongest, yet Mewtwo looked more comfortable and held the advantage. Being called the strongest Pokemon created by human hands was no empty boast.

Ethan sighed. Psychic power was as outrageous as ever. Its uses went far beyond the cold figures in a Pokedex. In the real world, it often seemed stronger than anything else.

When Ethan caught the black Rayquaza, and later when Deoxys fought another Rayquaza in LaRousse City, Deoxys had at times suppressed its opponent despite having a weaker body. That alone showed what psychic power could accomplish. Mewtwo had a body to rival Rayquaza's as well.

After learning Rayquaza's style, Mewtwo drew fully on its own strength. It pressed its advantage with increasing ease.

That did not mean Rayquaza would fall quickly. For now Mewtwo was only ahead. To defeat Rayquaza, it would have to show still more.

Ethan, however, had not come here for a one-on-one battle. Having seen that Rayquaza alone could not presently beat Mewtwo, he threw his second Ultra Ball.

How had he built his reputation in the first place? He had always been good at overwhelming an opponent with numbers.

Blue light flashed, and Deoxys appeared beside him. Mewtwo noticed it immediately. It said nothing about facing two opponents at once. It had sensed both powerful Pokemon when Ethan entered the cave and had watched him bring out two Ultra Balls. It could hardly have believed he intended to use only one.

And Mewtwo's confidence came from its own strength. Let them both come.

Deoxys flew straight toward it. From inside its Ultra Ball, it had already used its abilities to watch the battle. It was eager to join in, and Ethan had now given it permission.

Its arrival changed the match at once. Deoxys was a Psychic-type Pokemon too, difficult for Mewtwo to handle even without Rayquaza waiting beside them. Under pressure from both, Mewtwo made more mistakes and took more hits. It had to fight seriously, and within moments it was on the defensive.

Yet Mewtwo did not retreat. It stood against two Legendary Pokemon at once, despite the turn in their favor.

All three clashed in the air. The battle grew fiercer, the weather more violent. Thick black clouds spread rapidly outward.

Kyogre and Groudon were not the only Pokemon whose battles could change the world around them. If Mewtwo, Rayquaza, and Deoxys fought without restraint, they too could cause enormous damage to the surrounding land. That was an important reason Ethan had chosen this remote place.

Fortunately, they all understood this was not a fight to the death. Each held back to some degree. Even so, they could not fully contain the energy spilling from their attacks.

Gengar rose from Ethan's shadow and hovered beside him. Watching the distant battle, it hesitated. With this much going on, won't people notice?

Gengar's fortunes were bound to Ethan's, and it thought about the problem from its Trainer's point of view. People discovering Deoxys and Rayquaza would matter little; Ethan had already caught them. If outsiders found Mewtwo, though, it would face endless pursuit and harassment. That would make Ethan's hopes of someday catching it much less certain.

Ethan shared the concern. Don't worry. The battle will be over soon.

You're not planning to catch Mewtwo right now, are you?

He shook his head. Not yet. There still has to be an opening. I think it will come soon.

Gengar wanted to know what he meant, but Ethan offered nothing more, so it kept the question to itself.

Overhead, the three Pokemon drifted closer to Ethan again. This time he did not retreat. He called to Deoxys from afar, Let's raise the difficulty! Use Attack Forme!

A human voice was small amid a clash like this, but Deoxys heard him. Its body shifted into Attack Forme.

At first Mewtwo did not seem concerned. Then they exchanged blows again, and Deoxys caught it unprepared. The alien-looking Pokemon had become a greater threat. Mewtwo's position worsened.

It gathered powerful spheres of energy in both hands. It drove Rayquaza away, only to be struck by Deoxys. Against either Pokemon alone, Mewtwo had no fear and believed it could win. Against the two together, even it struggled.

That was an achievement in itself. How many Pokemon could have held out against opponents of this caliber?

Ethan checked the time. Then, without warning, he recalled both of his Pokemon into their Ultra Balls.

Mewtwo was caught off guard. One moment it was deep in battle; the next, its opponents were gone. It hovered motionless.

Why?

It looked toward Ethan. If he had continued, he might truly have captured Mewtwo this time. Why stop now? What was he thinking?

Someone from Ethan's old world might have recognized the tactic. Ethan was drawing Mewtwo in by stepping back just when it expected him to press forward.

Of course he wanted to catch it. Mewtwo had been one of his favorite Pokemon even before he came to this world. But he did not merely want to possess it. He wanted Mewtwo to accept him willingly as its Trainer.

A Pokemon with Mewtwo's intelligence would not truly be bound by a Poke Ball alone. Unless it recognized Ethan of its own accord, he could never work with it as naturally as he did with his other partners. That was why he kept making these elaborate visits and withdrawing before a final capture.

Mewtwo did not know any of that. From its perspective, Ethan was growing stronger and more mysterious each time they met. It was also beginning to regard him more and more as an equal.

No special reason, Ethan said with a smile. I told you I came to spar. We've done that, so it's time to stop.

An interesting man. Mewtwo's eyes changed slightly. Its opinion of him rose again.

Actually, Ethan added, I came to ask for your help with something.

Perhaps Ethan's choice to stop had altered Mewtwo's view of him. It did not think to refuse at once. Instead it asked, curious, You want my help? With those two Pokemon, what could you possibly be unable to do?

It was a fair question. In this world, powerful Pokemon made a powerful Trainer. Someone of Ethan's standing could receive the finest welcome from organizations and officials alike. Money, influence, and admiration were well within his reach.

Mewtwo was clever enough to guess a moment later. You want me to help you face some troublesome Pokemon.

Yes and no. Ethan smiled mysteriously. Don't worry. It won't be difficult for you.

Then couldn't those Pokemon of yours handle it easily?

That involves something private. Those two are strong, but they're also my hidden trump cards. There are situations where I can't let them appear. That's when I'd need your help.

He did not wait for Mewtwo to agree. He patted Dragonite's shoulder, and it carried him away, leaving Mewtwo with his departing silhouette.

His voice reached it one last time. Wait for word from me. That day will come soon!

...

At dusk, while Misty waited anxiously, Dragonite brought Ethan back to the Pokemon Center where they were staying. She let out a long breath when she saw him.

She had not feared for his safety. Few Pokemon in the world could hurt him now. She had worried that something might delay him until he missed tomorrow's match.

Where did you go, Brother Ethan?

Nowhere special. I looked around nearby. Ethan did not tell her about Mewtwo. Instead he turned to May. How is your practice going?

We've settled on the basic structure of my performance, May said with a smile. It still needs a few details. And now that I'm in Kanto, I'd like to catch some Pokemon from here.

Kanto Pokemon. Ethan remembered the ones May had obtained here in the anime. If he wanted her to have the chance to follow that course, they would need to visit Professor Oak's laboratory first. Fortunately, it lay along their route and would not disrupt the plan.

Brother Ethan, Misty asked, did you hear what happened near Cerulean City while you were out?

Cerulean City? What happened?

The news said there was extreme weather nearby. They think some Pokemon were fighting there!

So that was all. It was the battle he had just watched. He had not expected it to make the news. Moving the fight away from Cerulean Cave had been wise. If it had happened near the city, crowds of Trainers might have rushed in. At this distance, no one had disturbed them.

Who knows? Maybe a Legendary Pokemon appeared.

Misty's memories of Mewtwo had been erased. Until she truly met it again, Ethan saw no reason to explain. His suggestion turned the girls' thoughts toward Legendary Pokemon. They began wondering aloud what could appear in Kanto besides the three Legendary birds.

They had not talked long before Misty remembered something else. Oh, Brother Ethan! You haven't heard, have you? Tomorrow's battle between you and Tucker is all over Kanto!

Chapter 803: You Put on Your Show

Huh? Ethan stared at Misty. All of Kanto knows? What do you mean?

Misty held up her phone and told him about the reports she had seen throughout the day.

I don't know what happened, but the television news and radio have been full of stories about your battle with Tucker tomorrow. My phone keeps sending me alerts too. It's only been half a day, and I've already seen hundreds of posts!

Misty did not understand it, but Ethan immediately had an idea.

Hundreds of posts? Had someone paid to push the story?

He could guess who. Tucker had seen Ethan register for a challenge and recognized the value of his titles. Now he wanted to use them to raise his own profile.

That was quite an ambition.

He had turned an ordinary challenge into a public spectacle, as though letting the opportunity pass would cost him millions. He had not even asked Ethan whether he agreed.

People like that existed in every world.

Of course, Ethan might be wrong. Perhaps Tucker was not behind it. But the possibility seemed remote. Tucker stood to gain the most from the match, and Ethan could think of no one else with a reason to arrange this.

It was a gamble, though. Was Tucker sure he could handle all this attention?

Ethan could roughly see his plan. Win or lose tomorrow, Tucker would become better known.

Winning, of course, was out of the question.

Now that Tucker had put the match before all of Kanto, Ethan could not afford to lose. He would fight with everything he had. As long as he performed steadily, a Frontier Brain had no chance of taking a point from him. Even one of the Elite Four would struggle.

Tucker probably understood that much. He would try to win, but he must have prepared another outcome.

Lose gracefully, then collect the popularity the broadcast brought him.

If Tucker had discussed it with Ethan beforehand, Ethan might well have helped him. He could train his Pokemon, win the Symbol, and let Tucker benefit from the occasion too. Even if they never became friends, there was no need for bad blood.

But now...

Ethan gave a quiet, humorless chuckle. He had made up his mind. He would use this match to show people that they could not exploit him at will.

...

After a night's rest, Ethan, Misty, and May finished breakfast and left the Pokemon Center for the Battle Dome.

When they had returned to their rooms the previous night, all three had seen the flood of stories about the match. Even Ethan had found them while checking his phone before bed.

An unseen hand seemed to be guiding the coverage, portraying Tucker as someone who could stand on equal footing with Ethan. Many people who knew nothing of either Trainer's actual strength took the promotion at face value. They expected a magnificent Pokemon battle and followed the news eagerly.

Some who lived close enough had even bought tickets overnight to watch in person. More than a dozen television stations were bringing equipment to broadcast the match across Kanto.

Naturally, Ethan's friends heard about it too. He received call after call that evening. Even Erika learned from the news that he had returned to Kanto. She was delighted, but she also complained that he had given her no warning.

What could he say? He had planned to appear in Celadon City unexpectedly and surprise her. Tucker's publicity had spoiled that plan and left Ethan in an awkward position.

It only deepened his irritation. Tucker's unilateral decision had thrown his own plans into disarray.

They could see the crowd long before they reached the Battle Dome. The line stretched for nearly a kilometer. People were clearly eager for the match.

Among them stood fans carrying banners for Tucker. Most were young women. They chatted and laughed as they waited, waving their fan merchandise and looking forward to his appearance.

Tucker certainly knew how to cultivate a following.

Ethan pulled his hat lower and started past the line. His phone rang. The caller was a member of the Battle Dome's staff.

No one wanted today's match to go ahead more badly than Tucker's people. They had agreed on nine o'clock, but before eight, someone was already calling to ask where Ethan was and urge him to attend.

When he hung up, Ethan sighed. Each new intrusion made Tucker and his staff harder to bear. They seemed to have no sense of boundaries.

At least there were plenty of Ethan's supporters in the line as well. He had won the Indigo Conference through battle after battle before a vast audience. Time had passed, but people still remembered his performances. Some admired his skill; others admired his looks. His fans were numerous, and as more arrived, they threatened to outnumber Tucker's.

Casual viewers could follow the match on television or online. The people who had traveled hundreds of miles to be here were mostly devoted fans of one Trainer or the other.

Ethan had never tried to cultivate fans, or even paid much attention to them. That did not mean they were not there.

Following the staff member's earlier directions, he led Misty and May through a side entrance, avoiding the crowd. They went straight to the challenger's lounge to wait for the match. It was their last chance to make any adjustments.

Misty looked around with interest. The Battle Dome was well equipped, and the lounge alone showed how much money had gone into it. There was even a Poke Ball transfer machine in one corner, like the ones at Pokemon Centers.

After exploring the room, she dropped onto the sofa and stretched. This place isn't bad. Brother Ethan, what Pokemon are you going to use against that man?

Ethan's reaction had soured both girls on Tucker. Misty would not even use his name.

Ethan laughed softly. Tucker has planned everything so carefully and arranged such a grand show. I wouldn't want to disappoint him. I'll help see his performance through to the end.

Misty and May heard the mockery in his voice. Both leaned forward eagerly.

So...?

Tucker thinks he gains something whether he wins or loses. But he's overlooked one thing. There's a world of difference between losing with dignity and fleeing in humiliation.

As the girls watched, a Poke Ball floated out of Ethan's belt pouch and settled in his hand. Gengar rose from his shadow and gave them a mischievous grin.

If Tucker is so sure we're on the same level, I'll show him what despair really feels like. He'll pay for what he's done.

...

Ladies and gentlemen! Thank you for waiting!

At nine o'clock, the hovering commentary platform appeared above the field, and the host's excited voice rang through the Dome.

As you all know, today's Battle Dome challenge is one everyone has been waiting for! Defending the Dome is none other than our own superstar, Tucker! And his challenger needs no introduction either: Ethan Vale, champion of the Indigo Conference, the Silver Conference, and this year's Ever Grande Conference!

The crowd roared. Cameras swung toward the field.

After letting the reaction build, the host continued, Both Trainers stand among Kanto's finest in strength and popularity! Now that they've met, which one will prevail? Before we find out, let's enjoy some highlights from their greatest battles!

The arena lights dimmed. One large screen showed Ethan's best moments from the Conferences. When his montage ended, the opposite screen played highlights of Tucker's performances in the Battle Dome.

Set to driving music, the editing was impressive. It could stir anyone's excitement. Tucker's footage even looked more spectacular than Ethan's.

The Dome's staff had clearly worked hard to present Tucker as Ethan's equal. Though he was a Frontier Brain, the publicity placed him on the same level as a champion of three Conferences.

The audience did not know any better. They expected a close, thrilling contest and responded enthusiastically.

After the montage, spotlights converged on a rising platform. Ethan slowly came into view. He faced the cheers with a calm, easy expression and offered the crowd a small wave. Their response was deafening.

Tucker's entrance was far more elaborate. Colored lights flashed across the field. Petals rained from above. Dressed in his flamboyant costume, Tucker sailed into the arena on a swing.

He swung back and forth a dozen times, then leaped down and landed neatly in the center of the field. As the spotlights found him, he bent at the waist and gave the crowd a dazzling smile and a deep bow, like a star taking the stage.

The entrance had been carefully designed, and it drew thunderous applause.

But when Tucker straightened and looked at Ethan for the first time, he found the man's expression unchanged. His entrance had made no impression at all.

Tucker frowned, displeased. He considered Ethan a rival of comparable stature. Why was Ethan so cold toward him?

He had planned to speak with Ethan in front of the crowd and make them look like worthy opponents who admired each other. That plan was falling apart. Something in Ethan's gaze even struck him as hostile.

Tucker felt more uncomfortable, but he dismissed the concern. To him, Ethan was a useful prop. If he would not cooperate, Tucker could still make use of him in the battle. He would at least say what the occasion required.

Ethan, he called warmly, welcome to the Battle Dome! I look forward to seeing a performance worthy of the Tactics Symbol today!

The Tactics Symbol was the prize for defeating him. Ethan merely gave a slight nod. He did not answer.

Tucker had been rebuffed again.

Ethan knew his silence might seem rude, even arrogant. At this point, he did not care.

You want to build a stage and put on a show? Then perform alone. You put on your show; I'll fight my battle. I came for the Symbol. If you expect me to play along, keep dreaming.

Tucker's staff had not expected such a cold response either. They had never met Ethan. Even if he did not share Tucker's love of showmanship, they had assumed a champion would at least exchange a few polite words.

Instead, Tucker was left talking by himself. How could that look like a clash between two great rivals? He looked more like a clown performing for a man who barely acknowledged him. It was almost as if Ethan did not take any of them seriously.

Chapter 804: A Humiliating Lesson

Tucker could tell that Ethan seemed hostile, but he did not consider why. Nor did he take it seriously.

After all, Tucker had publicized the match without even informing Ethan. He was self-important enough to make that decision and unlikely to consider anyone else's feelings. In his own mind, he had done nothing wrong.

Protesting to someone like that would accomplish nothing. He might even take it as weakness. Ethan had chosen to answer him in battle.

Still, Ethan's refusal to engage gave Tucker the uneasy feeling that the occasion was slipping out of his control. He studied Ethan while maintaining his smile. This must be your first visit to the Battle Dome. Why don't I explain the rules?

The rules were beside the point. With a huge crowd and television cameras watching, Tucker wanted another chance to display his charm and promote the Dome.

He was only halfway through his sentence when Ethan raised a hand to stop him.

No need, Ethan said evenly. I checked them beforehand. Unless you've changed the rules especially for me, let's begin.

It was a blunt response in front of so many people. Tucker's expression flickered. With the crowd and cameras on him, all he could do was give a short laugh and look hard at Ethan.

Arrogant, wasn't he? Let's see if he could keep that attitude once the battle began.

The host sensed the awkwardness and quickly took over before the audience noticed. Our challenger has clearly done his homework! That's how well known the Battle Dome is. Now let's see what theme Mr. Tucker has chosen for today's match!

As Ethan had seen the previous day, Tucker always sent out his two Pokemon first, regardless of his opponent's strength or team. He would then give the pair a dramatic theme to make his approach look special. The gimmick might work against an ordinary Trainer, but using it against Ethan showed too much confidence.

Before the watching crowd, Tucker tossed two Poke Balls. Twin flashes of blue light revealed Salamence and Charizard.

Fire and dragon soaring through the sky! Today's theme is the Roar of Twin Dragons!

Tucker struck a stylish pose. His fans shrieked at the sight of his Pokemon. They knew Salamence and Charizard were his two strongest partners. Both looked larger and stronger than the Pokemon he had used yesterday.

If Tucker had brought out his best, his supporters expected a spectacular match. Perhaps he could even bring the champion down.

They had always seen Tucker as immensely powerful. In their minds, only his commitment to the Dome had kept him from challenging the Indigo Conference himself. Had he entered it, the championship would surely have been his. Now they were eager to see how he would defeat Ethan.

Tucker!

Go, Tucker! Show him what you can do!

From the opposite Trainer's area, Ethan heard the shouting and looked at Tucker's Pokemon. He had only one thought: Finally, the opening act is over.

Of all the opponents he had faced, whether in official Gyms or private venues, Tucker had the most drawn-out introduction. He had turned an ordinary battle into a time-consuming spectacle. At least they could finally get to the point.

Ethan had already decided on his pair. He would use them no matter what Tucker sent out.

A Poke Ball floated from his pouch and opened by itself. Gardevoir appeared in a flash of blue light. At the same time, Gengar rose from the shadow at Ethan's feet with a wicked chuckle and hovered beside her.

Anyone familiar with Ethan's team knew what it meant when he chose these two. Either the opponent was dangerous enough to demand his full attention, or Ethan had grown so fed up that he wanted to end the battle without mercy.

Tucker fell into the second category.

He had no idea what he was facing. He was still considering the type matchup. Salamence was Dragon/Flying; Charizard was Fire/Flying. Against Gengar and Gardevoir, the only significant issue he saw was that Dragon-type moves would not affect a Fairy type.

Otherwise, it seemed like a fair contest. Neither of his Pokemon would suffer much from a type disadvantage. They could show what they could do. Tucker believed that put him on even footing with Ethan, and victory no longer looked difficult.

Of everyone in the Dome, only Misty understood what Tucker was about to face.

Watching the screen from her seat in the lounge, she smiled at May. Brother Ethan really is fed up with him. This is just a regular challenge, and he actually sent out Gardevoir and Gengar!

May knew Ethan was strong and had watched him become champion. But she had seen little of these two Pokemon. She understood they were his true aces, yet he rarely called on them.

Are they really that strong? she asked.

Of course. Misty fixed her eyes on the screen. Watch. This won't take long.

...

At the referee's signal, the battle began. On Tucker's command, Charizard and Salamence charged at Ethan's Pokemon.

Ethan lowered his gaze. In a voice barely loud enough for himself to hear, he said, Don't let them live.

Gardevoir and Gengar both received the order. Gardevoir's mind was linked to Ethan's. If he felt insulted, she felt it too, and she would not allow it. Gengar was a Ghost-type that delighted in playing tricks on others. It certainly would not stand by while someone mistreated its Trainer.

Neither had any reason to hold back.

Tucker had barely sent his Pokemon forward. He was still smiling when two blurs flashed across the field. In the next instant, Charizard and Salamence fell at his feet.

What?

His smile froze. He looked down. Both Pokemon were struggling to rise.

How was that possible? The battle had just begun. They had only just taken flight. How had they been thrown back already?

The spectators were just as confused. They turned to one another, asking what had happened. The host reacted first and ordered the footage replayed on the big screens.

Only in slow motion could anyone see it. Charizard and Salamence had rushed toward their opponents. Almost simultaneously, Gardevoir and Gengar had raised their hands. Their powers struck Tucker's Pokemon like two enormous invisible hammers, hurling them backward even faster than they had charged.

It had all happened in a flash. Only the high-speed cameras had captured it clearly.

Once they saw the replay, the audience understood. But new questions replaced their confusion. This was not the fight they had imagined. Hadn't they been promised an evenly matched contest? How had Tucker's Pokemon been sent flying by a single blow?

Even his fans stood stunned. Their cheering stopped.

Tucker's face changed color. He had never imagined his best Pokemon could be repelled so easily. These were his aces. When had anyone knocked them down with a single attack?

Fortunately for him, they were injured but could still fight. Even so, fear crept in. He might have underestimated this young man. Sweat gathered on his forehead.

He wanted to tell his Pokemon to be careful, but Ethan gave him no chance.

As soon as Charizard and Salamence struggled to their feet, Gardevoir and Gengar attacked again. With effortless movements, they knocked both Pokemon to the ground.

It was over.

The battle had lasted only a dozen or so seconds. Tucker's Pokemon had not managed an attack. Gengar and Gardevoir had defeated them with ease.

Even so, Ethan thought their performance deserved applause. Tucker's aces could certainly take more punishment than the Pokemon fielded by Team Magma and Team Aqua. Gardevoir and Gengar had needed two attacks to finish them.

The fallen Charizard and Salamence drew a roar of disbelief from the crowd. What kind of battle had that been? It had ended almost as soon as it began. Was that all a Frontier Brain could do? Even a fight against wild Pokemon might have lasted longer.

Shock gave way to suspicion. Ignoring Tucker's wide eyes and ashen face, the spectators began shouting. The publicity he had sought was turning against him.

His image changed completely in an instant.

For Ethan, the match had served its purpose. Tucker had wanted attention, and Ethan had given it to him. Tucker had hoped to show his face to all of Kanto; Ethan had exposed him to ridicule instead.

Tucker had assumed any outcome would bring him more followers. Ethan had answered with a humiliating defeat. Everyone watching across Kanto had seen how easily Tucker fell. They would remember him, and this match, as a joke.

That was the consequence of using Ethan for his own ends.

Ethan recalled his Pokemon, gave Tucker one cool glance, and walked back toward the lounge without another word.

Ordinarily, Tucker would present him with the Symbol after losing. In this situation, Ethan doubted the man was in any mood to do it. Tucker's immediate problem was finding some way to salvage the disastrous broadcast.

You love to perform, don't you? Then let's see whether you can turn the audience's opinion around this time.

The staff could bring Ethan his Symbol later.

He opened the lounge door and found Misty smiling at him.

Well? Feeling better?

She knew exactly why Ethan had treated Tucker that way. She felt no sympathy for him. He had brought it on himself.

A little, Ethan said with a shake of his head. It was a small punishment. But I didn't expect his Pokemon to go down so easily. I thought we'd have a few more exchanges.

That's because your Gardevoir and Gengar are too strong, Misty said, laughing. Don't forget who you are now. You're the champion of three regions. How could people like him stand against your strongest Pokemon?

That was Misty. Few others would have said it quite that way. It was one reason Ethan liked traveling with her. She made the journey easy, pleasant, and fun, and she knew how to help her companions when someone had upset them.

Unfortunately, with the Battle Dome challenge behind them, their next destination was Cerulean City.

Chapter 805: May Joins the Team

Ethan, Misty, and May waited in the lounge for more than an hour. Neither Tucker nor any of his staff appeared. They might as well have been forgotten.

Misty was growing impatient when the door finally opened. The staff member who had registered Ethan's challenge entered with an apologetic expression and a gleaming gold Symbol in his hand.

I'm sorry to keep you waiting, Mr. Vale. This is the Battle Dome's Tactics Symbol. It's yours now.

Ethan was not surprised that a staff member had brought the award instead of Tucker. If he had lost so badly, he would hardly want to face his opponent either. Tucker also had a serious public relations crisis to manage.

Ethan accepted the Symbol without comment, but Misty was not ready to let Tucker off. We've been traveling a long time, and this is the first time a Gym Leader hasn't handed over the prize himself. Mr. Tucker must be very busy right now.

Her sarcasm rubbed salt in Tucker's wounds. Fortunately for him, he was not there to hear it. The staff member looked uncomfortable, but he would not be passing it on.

You're joking, miss. His smile was stiff. We're not a Pokemon Gym, so our customs are a little different. It's getting late, and I won't disturb you any longer. Excuse me.

He shut the door without waiting for Misty to answer and hurried away. The moment it closed, Misty burst out laughing.

Serves him right! He tried to use Brother Ethan, and this is what he gets. I'd like to see how he keeps calling himself a Frontier Brain after that!

May scratched her cheek. She thought Tucker had behaved badly too, but she was less fiery than Misty. To her, the matter seemed settled. There was no need to keep after him.

Ethan examined the Tactics Symbol. He had worked so hard to earn it, after all, and it was proof that he had beaten Tucker.

Apart from a shape resembling the letter H on its face, it looked much like any other badge. It seemed to be made of solid gold, though. The Battle Dome and its image-conscious Frontier Brain certainly had money to spare.

With their purpose accomplished, the three collected their belongings and left. The Battle Dome would be little more than a minor episode in their journey, hardly worth dwelling on.

They headed west along the main road and reached Cerulean City that evening. Misty had not wanted to face her return home, but once they entered the city, she said little about it.

There was no reason to stay at a Pokemon Center when her home was here. She led Ethan and May straight to the Cerulean Gym.

The Gym looked much as Ethan remembered. Even the enormous picture of a Seel was still there. But parts of the outer wall and roof had begun to deteriorate, giving the building a neglected air.

After seeing Gyms across several regions, Ethan had to admit that Cerulean's was small and outdated by comparison. Once Misty took charge, she might need to renovate the entire place.

May saw it differently. She looked around with excitement. So this is your home? Wow, what a beautiful Gym! It looks like an aquarium. Do they put on shows inside?

Misty fell silent.

She did not blame May for the question. She blamed her three sisters for turning a perfectly good Gym into a place that visitors mistook for an amusement attraction.

What upset Misty most was Cerulean Gym's reputation throughout Kanto as the weakest official Gym. She often wanted to argue against it, but remembering her sisters' battling ability left her with little to say.

Just come inside, she said with a sigh.

Ethan and May followed her in. Perhaps because evening was approaching, there were no challengers or spectators for the water ballet. The great interior felt empty and cool.

Daisy! I'm home! Misty called.

No one answered. She led them deeper into the Gym.

For Ethan, returning here brought back his first Gym challenge and the later visit when he had helped with a performance. So much had happened since then, yet both visits felt like they had taken place only days ago.

Thinking of the performance also brought back the kiss he had shared with Misty's second sister, Violet.

They kept walking until voices reached them near the pool. Daisy, Violet, and Lily were practicing there, surrounded by Pokemon.

Whatever their skill as Gym battlers, the three had earned their reputation as the Cerulean sisters. They were beautiful and graceful, and their long, strong legs caught the eye. Many spectators came to their shows as much to see them as to watch the water ballet.

They gave the Gym's battles less attention, but no one could doubt their passion for the performances. Even after the day's shows ended, they often practiced late into the evening.

Nothing's changed, Misty said, spreading her hands with a helpless sigh. Then she cleared her throat.

Daisy, Violet, and Lily turned together. Their faces lit up when they saw her.

Misty!

Mist!

You little brat! You finally decided to come home!

They grumbled, but they were sisters who had been apart for a long time. Of course they had missed her. Their delight lasted less than a minute before Violet and Lily started scolding her.

You stayed away so long this time! We've had to run the Gym and keep up our performances. Do you know how exhausting that's been?

Exactly! You're not leaving again, whatever you say!

Misty's smile froze. She had not expected her second and third sisters to change their tune so quickly.

Daisy, the eldest, noticed their visitors. She smiled at Ethan. Mr. Vale, thank you for taking care of her.

Violet and Lily seemed to notice Ethan only then. Like two mermaids, they sprang from the water, climbed onto the poolside, and crowded around him.

Lily's eyes shone with curiosity. Nothing happened between you two on the road, did it?

Violet nudged Ethan with her elbow and grinned. She didn't try anything improper with you?

That's enough! Misty cried, embarrassed and flustered. What are you talking about? I'd never do that!

May had heard about Misty's sisters before, but meeting them showed her just how bold and lively they were. So these were Misty's sisters. Compared with them, May was far too gentle with her own brother, Max.

Perhaps to stop them teasing her in front of Ethan and May, Misty hurriedly pulled May over to introduce everyone.

This is May, my friend from Hoenn. May, these are my sisters. First, this one with the long blond hair who looks so gentle is Daisy, my eldest sister.

Daisy gave May a warm smile. Welcome to Kanto. Thank you for keeping Misty company on the journey.

Oh, you don't need to thank me, May replied quickly. Compared with the other two, Daisy seemed poised and caring, just as May would expect of an older sister.

Misty pointed to Violet. This is my second sister. She may be pretty, but she bullies me all the time, and she can be rather willful. Be careful around her.

Honestly! Violet put her hands on her hips. Is that any way to describe your sister? Then she turned to May with a fresh smile. Welcome to Cerulean Gym!

Ah... thank you. May hardly knew what to say.

Finally, Misty indicated Lily. And this is my third sister. She looks sweet, like a princess, but she loves taking my things!

Don't listen to her, Lily said cheerfully. She never looks after them, so I put them away for her.

Once they had all exchanged greetings, Misty began declaring how hungry she was. Daisy had no choice but to leave Violet and Lily with their guests while she made dinner.

Perhaps being home had let Misty relax completely. Ethan could even hear a hint of childish pleading in her voice. For all her complaints, she loved her family.

Dinner did not take long. As they ate together, Misty excitedly recounted the things she had seen and done on the journey. She could hardly get the words out fast enough. Ethan could hear how much she wanted to share her happiness with her sisters.

Daisy listened to her adventures, then turned to Ethan with a serious expression. You really have gone to a great deal of trouble for her. Thank you.

It's the other way around, Ethan said, waving off the thanks. Misty looked after me throughout our time in Hoenn. My journey wouldn't have gone so smoothly without her.

Misty knew he was being polite, but his words still moved her. Her eyes grew damp.

Brother Ethan...

...

That night, after a comfortable hot bath, Ethan was getting ready for bed when someone knocked on his door. At this hour, he thought he knew who it must be. He closed his robe, rose, and opened it.

Misty stood outside, just as he expected. To his surprise, May stood beside her.

Why had they come together? Misty visiting alone would have made sense. She was home now, and they would part the next day. She might want a private conversation before then. But why was May here? Had they met in the hallway, or planned this together?

While he wondered, Misty led May inside without ceremony. Unlike Misty, May was blushing.

What brings you both here? Ethan asked.

Misty sat on the edge of his bed. Before answering, she looked at May. May blushed more deeply. She opened her mouth twice but could not get the words out.

Misty sighed and turned to Ethan. All right, I'll say it. Brother Ethan, May wants to travel with you in the next region!

What? Ethan raised his eyebrows.

Misty and May had kept their discussions quiet. Ethan had assumed May had come to Kanto only to look around with Misty. Where had this idea of traveling with him come from?

He looked at May, but she lowered her head rather than meet his eyes. She gave a silent nod.

Well... Ethan hesitated. Why bring this up so suddenly?

As he remembered it, May had gone to Johto alone after the Ever Grande Conference to enter its Pokemon Contests. Instead she had come to Kanto with Misty, and now she wanted to travel with him. He could hardly help being surprised.

What's strange about it? Misty said with a smile. May's a Coordinator. Of course she needs to travel, grow stronger, and enter Contests in different places. And what better way to learn than traveling beside a champion?

There was sense in that. Still, they had given him no hint beforehand. They had simply come to his room and asked. He had had no time to prepare for it.

But he had no reason to refuse. Once Misty left the group, Ethan would be traveling through the next region alone. May's company would spare him that loneliness.

He looked at May again. This time she met his gaze, and he saw the determination in her eyes.

All right. Ethan gave her a gentle smile and nodded. Welcome to the team, May. Officially.

Chapter 806: Seeing Erika Again

After spending the night at Cerulean Gym, Ethan and May said goodbye to Daisy, Misty, and the others early the next morning.

Misty and May faced each other, reluctant to part. Both had a great deal on their minds.

Misty... May began, then fell silent.

Keep your chin up. Misty seemed to have come to terms with their parting. Though she hated to see May go, she smiled. Next time we meet, you'd better be a great Coordinator. I'll watch all your Contests on television, so don't go losing to everyone else!

May could be sentimental, but she was optimistic at heart. Encouraged by Misty, she nodded firmly.

Don't worry. I'll become a top Coordinator!

Take care.

They clasped hands tightly. They did not need to say more.

Then Misty turned to Ethan. One look at the face she loved and the tenderness in his eyes nearly brought her to tears. She took a deep breath and steadied herself. Her eyes were still red as she took something from her belt pouch and held it out.

Brother Ethan... Her voice trembled. I can't keep traveling with you. I prepared this earlier, and I want you to have it. When you see it, I hope you'll think of me.

Ethan looked down. It was a fishing lure shaped like Misty.

When had she made it? He had not noticed a thing. In the anime, Misty had given Ash a lure like this. Now she was giving one to Ethan. It was cute, though he wondered whether it could actually attract Water-type Pokemon. For that matter, he seldom found time to fish.

Whatever its practical value, it was a gift from Misty. He accepted it with care.

Thank you.

Ethan nodded to the three Cerulean sisters, then waved to Misty one last time and set off with May.

Misty watched them until they disappeared into the distance. Even then, she did not look away.

Daisy, Violet, and Lily exchanged glances. Violet finally teased her. You can stop looking. They've gone too far to come back just because you stare after them.

She expected Misty to argue as usual. Instead, Misty wiped the corner of her eye and turned with a bright smile.

What are you talking about? I was thinking about how to run the Gym. I've decided to make Cerulean Gym the strongest in Kanto!

Her sisters stared for a moment, then shook their heads and laughed.

Honestly, Misty... Still, this is good. With you here, we can concentrate on our water ballet!

Yes! Finally, someone to share the work!

...

Not long after they left the Gym, May hesitantly asked, Brother Ethan, where are we going next?

She had felt comfortable when Misty was with them. Now that it was just her and Ethan, her heart beat faster. She was nervous and unsure how to act around him.

Fortunately, Ethan was as gentle with her as ever. I was going to visit Professor Oak's laboratory, but my plans have changed. I need to go to Celadon City first.

May knew who lived there. She had met Erika near the beginning of the Hoenn journey and liked her very much, so she had no objection.

Ethan had planned to challenge the Battle Dome, take Misty home to Cerulean, visit Professor Oak, and only then go to Celadon. Tucker's campaign had told everyone about the challenge, however, forcing Ethan to see Erika sooner. He suspected the visit would demand plenty of his strength and energy.

To reach Celadon from Cerulean, they had to pass through Saffron City. Together with the roads they had already traveled, the route formed a rough rectangle. It involved some backtracking, but they were moving quickly and had lost little time. When Ethan called Ash the previous night, Ash had only just returned to Pallet Town.

Ethan already had two Frontier Symbols and was moving faster than Ash. Pallet Town was simply farther from the place where their ship had docked.

They passed through Saffron City without lingering. Ethan met Sabrina, and the three had lunch together before he and May hurried on. The Saffron Contest was drawing closer. If May did not want to miss it, they needed to keep moving.

At first, traveling alone together felt rather quiet. May was friendly, cheerful, and sweet, but she was not especially talkative. Neither was Ethan. Their first stretch on the road was subdued. Once they knew each other better, he was sure they would find plenty to discuss.

They continued west. Kanto's large cities were mostly clustered in its center. The land here was relatively flat, with dense forests but few mountains. When they tired, they rested for a while, then set out again.

May got to see a side of Kanto she had not known. Overall, though, Kanto, Johto, and Hoenn were not so different in appearance.

Will Sinnoh be like this too, Brother Ethan? she asked.

Big cities look much the same wherever you go, Ethan said, glancing up at the sky. Tall buildings, busy people. You notice the differences between regions in remote mountains, by lakes, and in places people visit on holiday.

May looked disappointed, so he quickly added, Sinnoh is a large island in its own right. It has plenty of distinctive scenery worth seeing. Mt. Coronet and its many lakes are beautiful. And the snow-covered north makes an impression you won't forget.

May pictured the places he described. That sounds wonderful. You hardly ever see snow in Hoenn. She smiled. You know so much about Sinnoh, Brother Ethan.

Ethan waved the praise away. Only from what I've read. I haven't seen it for myself. I'm looking forward to setting foot in Sinnoh just as much as you are.

The conversation eased the awkwardness between them. May began asking him questions from time to time, and he answered each one. Ethan knew a great deal, and even without battling, May felt her understanding of the world growing. Traveling with him felt quite different from traveling with Ash.

...

The road from Saffron to Celadon was shorter than the one from Cerulean to Saffron. They could see the city's outline before dark.

They did encounter a few Trainers along the way. None recognized Ethan. They simply met his eyes on the roadside and instinctively wanted a battle, as Trainers often did. Ordinarily he might have accepted, but he was in a hurry and declined each challenge.

Once inside Celadon City, he and May headed directly to the Gym.

This visit would be different from the brief meeting with Sabrina. Erika had already heard that Ethan was coming, so he could no longer surprise her. She had contacted him several times on the road to ask where he was. Now she was waiting at the Gym with a generous dinner prepared.

Like a wife waiting for her husband to come home, Ethan thought.

Celadon Gym had changed beyond recognition. A fire had destroyed most of it before Erika first joined Ethan on his travels. After a long reconstruction, it was finally complete.

If the address had changed, he might not have recognized it at all.

The old Gym had resembled a greenhouse shaped like a Gloom. The new one was a vast, modern facility. Its scale and equipment had been transformed, though it retained the Vileplume-like steel solar panels on its roof. Rising in the center of the city, it looked like an enormous conservatory.

Even from the entrance, the building was imposing. It drew the eye away from the tall commercial towers around it.

Ethan stood before the doors for a while. Then, with an uneasy heart, he entered.

The building had changed, but the staff had not. The same lively young women worked there. They recognized him immediately and stayed at a distance, whispering excitedly among themselves.

They knew how Erika had been when she returned from her travels. None believed she had come back without falling for someone. Erika had tried to conceal it at first, but how could she? Ethan's Pokemon had appeared at the Gym. Erika watched his matches and spoke to him on the phone. The staff had seen it all.

And now, knowing he would arrive today, Erika had been restless from morning onward. What more proof did they need?

Still, none of them would say it aloud. Erika treated them well, but she was their Gym Leader and owned a perfume shop. They could keep their deductions to themselves. Besides, Ethan was a champion in three regions. Any rumor about him could become enormous news. They would gossip only in private.

Someone had to receive the visitors, however. One of the older staff members stepped forward with a smile.

May I help you?

She knew perfectly well why he was there. Ethan saw the barely hidden amusement on their faces and shook his head.

I'm here to see Erika. Is she in?

Of course. Please follow me.

She led Ethan and May through the Gym's great greenhouse to a Japanese-style room. She asked them to wait outside while she went in to announce their arrival.

May tilted her head as she watched the woman go. She knew about Ethan and Erika, but she did not understand why they needed such formalities.

Ethan noticed her confusion. Celadon is different from other places. You've seen how grand the Gym is and how many people come and go. Here, Erika is a Gym Leader first and our friend second. Until we've made our relationship public, we have to follow the Gym's usual procedures.

May nodded, though she only partly understood. She had not seen Sabrina leap into Ethan's arms outside the Saffron Gym and took his explanation at face value. Adults sometimes had obligations that children like her and Ash did not have to worry about.

At that moment, the room's door opened. Erika emerged beside the staff member, dressed beautifully for the occasion. She smiled at Ethan and gave a small bow.

As Ethan had said, they had to behave normally before others while their relationship remained private, no matter how intimate they were when alone. That also suited Erika's character. Even if she and Ethan married one day, she would remain poised and reserved in public. She would never disregard onlookers as readily as Sabrina did.

You're here, Erika said.

Ethan met her tender gaze and nodded. Yes. I came to see you.

They needed no embrace or kiss. A glance and a few simple words were enough to carry all the love between them.

Chapter 807: A Pokemon to Remember Their Love

The young woman who had shown them to Erika's room discreetly took her leave. Before going, she glanced at May, as though she hoped to take this cheerful third wheel along and leave Ethan and Erika alone.

May, however, was staring at the lavish dinner laid out in the room. The smell alone had her mouth watering. If Ethan announced that it was time to eat, she looked ready to dive in.

The staff member shook her head with an amused smile and left by herself.

Erika looked toward May, and Ethan explained, May is traveling with me from today onward. Once we've finished what we need to do in Kanto and Johto, we'll go to Sinnoh together.

Erika had already heard about the arrangement over the phone. Ethan said it again so they could acknowledge it openly.

Then I hope you'll look after him, Erika told May gently.

Oh, no... May waved her hands. You're too kind, Miss Erika. I should be thanking him. I'm the one learning from Brother Ethan!

We needn't keep thanking one another. Erika stepped aside and gestured toward the meal. We're all among friends. Let's eat before everything gets cold.

May had been waiting to hear that. She wanted to start immediately, but growing up in a Gym had taught her manners. She followed Ethan and Erika into the dining room and waited for them to take their seats.

She meant to sit beside Ethan, only to find Erika had already taken that place. After a moment's surprise, May sat opposite him. A seat was a seat. She picked up her chopsticks.

It would become the decision she regretted most that day.

The feast was delicious, but May also had to sit through an entire meal of open affection. Erika showed just how attentive she could be. She placed food on Ethan's plate, poured his wine, peeled shrimp for him, and even wiped his mouth with a napkin.

Suddenly May's dinner did not taste quite as good. She could remember her mother, Caroline, fussing over her that way only when May had been very young.

Erika and Sabrina were entirely different kinds of women.

After the meal, the staff member returned and escorted May toward a guest room. May looked back once. Ethan, a little tipsy, was walking in another direction with Erika supporting him.

Wasn't that Erika's room? Was Brother Ethan not staying in a guest room?

She caught herself. That was a naive thought. Misty had not needed to tell her that both Erika and Sabrina were romantically involved with Ethan. She could see it for herself. It was startling, and it did not seem entirely proper, yet with someone as remarkable as Ethan, she could understand how it had happened.

May had learned more than most girls her age from her family and her travels. She did not know exactly what Ethan and Erika would do, but she understood they would share a bed, as her parents did.

The thought made her heart race and her ears grow hot. She looked away, pushed it from her mind, and followed the staff member with her head lowered.

...

May could not sleep that night. She did not usually struggle in an unfamiliar bed, but she was in a strange place without anyone she knew nearby. She had eaten so much, and her mind kept wandering.

For the first part of the night she thought about the upcoming Saffron Contest. Around midnight her thoughts turned to the journey to Sinnoh. Later, she could think of little but the relationship among Ethan, Erika, and Sabrina.

Did Erika and Sabrina know about each other? If they did, had they both accepted the arrangement? If they did not, was Ethan deceiving them both?

Misty had asked her to watch out for Lisia and other girls. Surely Erika and Sabrina were not the girls she meant?

May worried over it all night. Just as she finally grew sleepy, rain began tapping against the window. The sound woke her fully again.

Ethan did not sleep much that night either. In his case, he scarcely had time. May's mind kept working; Ethan's body did. It was the ox that tired from plowing, while the field only grew more fertile.

Muffled breathing carried through the Gym's lodging area for much of the night. Fortunately, the young women who worked there had gone home after their shifts, so no one noticed. Even so, Erika kept her voice down as much as she could, perhaps afraid May might hear something unsuitable for her.

...

Ethan woke late the next morning. The clock showed that it was past ten, an unusually long sleep for him. When he tried to rise, his eyelids felt heavy and his body seemed drained.
