Erika was already gone. Her bedding had been folded neatly. Ethan stared out the window at a flowerpot full of rainwater and sat there for a long while before his head began to clear.

He dressed. They had been occupied as soon as they entered the room the previous night, so only now did he look around properly. It was unmistakably Erika's bedroom: elegant Japanese furnishings, calligraphy and paintings, and carefully placed vases. It suited a refined young woman from a distinguished family.

After taking it in, he went out. He met May in the room where they had eaten dinner. Each noticed the other's dark circles and tired face.

Ethan knew why he looked that way. What had happened to May? Had she been awake all night too and only just got up?

Before he could ask, Erika entered carrying their breakfast. She looked radiant.

You're awake? She smiled warmly and set the food before them. You were both sleeping so soundly that I didn't want to disturb you. You must be hungry. Come and eat.

In one respect, Erika was formidable. They had been together until late, yet she looked refreshed and lovelier than ever, while Ethan felt as if she had drained the strength from his bones.

They had arrived only the previous evening. Ethan could hardly leave immediately after spending a single exhausting night here. He would stay another day, and perhaps recover some energy.

Provided he did not exhaust himself again. Somehow, that seemed unlikely.

After breakfast, Ethan let his Pokemon out in the Gym's greenhouse to roam. With nothing else to do, he found a reclining chair and settled in.

Erika still had the Gym and her perfume shop to run. One challenger came to battle her. Ethan watched briefly. Erika held back, and the challenger left happily with a badge. Ethan lost interest and returned to the greenhouse to enjoy his quiet day.

May had no such rest. Her thoughts from the night before had given her new ideas for her performance, and she was practicing under the eyes of several young women from the staff.

They were curious about Ethan but could hardly question him directly with Erika nearby. Instead they gathered around May, asking for stories and hoping to learn more through her.

They had chosen the wrong person. May had not shared Ethan's most extraordinary adventures. Apart from what she had seen at the Conferences, she knew most of his exploits only from Misty's accounts.

Nor did May enjoy boasting. She understood that some matters were private. She answered harmless questions briefly and pretended not to know when a question crossed that line.

Even so, her account of Ethan's Ever Grande Conference battles impressed the women.

He sounds amazing, said a green-haired girl. I should have watched with Erika when she was following his matches in secret.

There's still time, another said with a laugh. He's going to Sinnoh, isn't he? We can watch the Sinnoh Conference with Erika.

The women chattered and laughed. May wanted to ask for a little peace so she could practice, but she could not find an opening.

Then their questions shifted to her.

Wait, did you say you came eighth in the Hoenn Grand Festival?

I didn't place eighth, May said quietly. I made it to the top eight.

That's still wonderful. Few newcomers do so well in a major competition their first time.

What do you mean, few? Ethan entered a Conference for the first time and won the championship!

Erika certainly knows how to choose a man!

May sighed as the women returned to gossip. She finally understood the saying that three women could put on a play. Here, there were six or seven. Once they began talking, every subject ended in more teasing and laughter.

Something small and green flickered through the trees on the far side of the greenhouse. It caught May's eye.

What's that? she asked without thinking.

What?

The staff stopped talking and followed her gaze. They saw only plants, but they seemed to know what she meant.

Oh, that... The woman who had escorted Ethan and May the previous evening smiled. It's our little secret. Erika asked us not to tell outsiders, but you came with Ethan, so you're different. Hasn't he told you?

May was even more puzzled. Told me what?

The women laughed again. Only when May grew visibly frustrated did the woman lower her voice.

What you saw was Celebi, a Mythical Pokemon.

Celebi?

May had traveled across an entire region. She was no longer a beginner, and she had spent plenty of time with her Pokedex. She certainly knew of Mythical Pokemon. What she could not understand was why Celebi was here, or why the staff seemed so accustomed to seeing it.

You really don't know, one of the women said. Ethan caught that Celebi.

It's Brother Ethan's Pokemon?

May had only just begun traveling with him. She had not seen his battles with Team Magma and Team Aqua, and Misty had mentioned Deoxys only once when May first saw it. She had no idea he had other Mythical or Legendary Pokemon. This revelation stunned her.

There was more. Do you know why Celebi stays here? another woman asked. Before May could guess, she went on. Because Celebi is the Pokemon that marks the love between Ethan and Erika!

May had heard of a keepsake exchanged between lovers. She had never heard of a Pokemon serving that purpose, though the meaning was clear enough.

It was hard to believe. This was a Mythical Pokemon. Had Ethan really given one away just like that?

Chapter 808: May Thought She Had It Figured Out

May practiced amid the chatter for more than an hour. When the lunch break finally came, she ate and returned to the greenhouse alone.

Since its reconstruction, Celadon Gym's greenhouse had grown to several thousand square meters. It was divided into sections of different sizes and filled with lush plants and Grass-type Pokemon.

Oddish, Gloom, Vileplume, Bellsprout, Weepinbell, Victreebel... Erika had also brought back Grass-type Pokemon from Johto and Hoenn. They lived together peacefully, sometimes peeking out of the vegetation as they went about their leisurely lives.

May was looking for someone else. She walked slowly through the greenhouse, searching the trees and shrubs for Celebi. The glimpse she had caught earlier had made her want to meet it.

It was a Mythical Pokemon, a rare creature most people would never see in their lives. Celebi was here in the Gym. This might be her only chance to look at it closely.

Besides, it was Brother Ethan's Pokemon. It would not flee in fright or attack her. She could approach without worrying about danger.

The dense greenery and winding paths made the search difficult. May walked for a long time without seeing Celebi again, but she would not give up. Determined to find it, she pushed into the deepest part of the greenhouse.

The going grew harder. Thick trees crowded around her, their foliage limiting her view to a meter or two. The air even seemed thin. After only a dozen or so meters, she felt as though she could barely breathe.

She stumbled and caught a trunk to keep from falling. A few steps later, she rounded a tree blocking her way and found a small clearing. The air felt a little easier to breathe.

May was about to sit and rest when she spotted a small green Pokemon flitting above a bed of flowers.

Celebi!

Her energy returned at once. She hurried closer and finally got a good look at the Mythical Pokemon. It resembled a little green onion with transparent wings on its back, large blue eyes, and two short antennae. It was adorable.

May approached carefully. Celebi noticed her. Perhaps it was used to spending time with Erika and the staff, or perhaps it had grown comfortable around people since being caught. It showed no fear. Instead it circled May with interest, studying the unfamiliar girl.

Hello, May said with a smile. I'm a friend of Brother Ethan's. It's nice to meet you.

Bi~

Celebi tilted its head, looking puzzled.

Before May could say more, Ethan spoke from behind her. You gave it the wrong name. He came to her side and looked at Celebi. I caught it, but we haven't built much of a bond yet. If you want to get close to it, you'd do better to mention Erika.

Huh? But isn't it your Pokemon?

It is. Ethan smiled. I left it with Erika soon after catching it. You know what Erika and I mean to each other. Celebi belongs to me, strictly speaking, but it's also a Pokemon we share.

Now May understood why the staff called Celebi a token of Ethan and Erika's love.

Are you going to leave it here permanently?

We'll see. The main reason I left it here was so it could keep Erika company while I'm away. Celebi is Grass-type as well as Psychic-type, so it suits her.

Celebi had not seen Ethan in a long time, but it recognized the Trainer who had caught it and spent some time with it. It flew around him. Up close, Ethan noticed it seemed a little rounder. Erika had clearly taken good care of it.

He smiled at a memory. It's a little glutton, just like you. I caught it with a cup of instant noodles.

Instant noodles? May gaped. A Mythical Pokemon that so many people dreamed of meeting, caught with a cup of noodles?

That's what comes of loving food, Ethan said lightly. Then he sighed. I promised to take it around the world and let it taste food from everywhere. It doesn't look as though I can do that anytime soon.

Why not? Why can't it travel with you? Don't you have that... that other Pokemon?

May did not finish, but Ethan knew she meant Deoxys. Misty had told him she had revealed that secret to May. Since May would be traveling with him now, she would learn about his hidden partners over time anyway. There was little reason to conceal everything from her.

Their circumstances are different, he explained. Deoxys was born to fight. Under my training, battle has become its main purpose. Celebi is capable in a fight too, but it's more peaceful and less driven to compete. I never know when I'll have to face a powerful enemy. With room for only a limited number of Pokemon on hand, I can't always bring Celebi, however strong it is.

May saw what he meant.

When my travels end, I'll keep my promise and take Celebi around the world, Ethan added. For now, it can stay with Erika a while longer.

After a quiet day at Celadon Gym, the three had dinner. Ethan and Erika went back to her room and spent another demanding night together. This time Ethan saved some strength, allowing him to rise early the next morning.

They had already stayed an extra day. Today they had to set out.

Erika understood. Though she hated to see him go, she prepared his things with loving care.

I packed lunches for you. There should be enough to last until you reach Pallet Town.

She handed him the parcel at the Gym entrance. This time she seemed less concerned about onlookers. She straightened his clothes and gave him a few gentle reminders.

Ethan was moved. He drew her into his arms, breathing in her perfume and the scent of her hair.

Go back inside, he murmured near her ear. You don't need to see me off any farther. I'll come back when my Sinnoh journey is over.

A day or two together could not ease the longing caused by a long separation. Yet Erika knew his ambitions. He wanted to challenge the world, and she supported him despite how much she missed him. She looked forward to their next reunion, and to a time when he would no longer need to travel.

I'll wait for you.

With the Gym staff watching, Ethan kissed Erika lightly. He waved goodbye, then left with May without looking back.

He could not settle into a comfortable life yet. Coming to this world had given him an extraordinary opportunity, and he meant to make something of it. Erika and Sabrina were both accomplished, beautiful Gym Leaders. He wanted to keep growing into someone worthy of them.

Champion of three regions? That was nowhere near enough. He intended to become the strongest in the world.

...

From Celadon Gym, Ethan and May headed west toward Pallet Town. Their destination was Professor Oak's laboratory.

May assumed they were simply going to meet Ash. Ethan had another purpose: he wanted her to receive the Squirtle that, in the anime, had belonged to her.

Now that May was traveling with him, he had a responsibility toward her. He knew little about being a Coordinator. Apart from battle training and sharing what he knew of the world, he could offer only so much guidance. At the very least, he would see that she did not miss out on the Pokemon she was meant to have.

The Battle Factory near Mt. Moon was also not far from Pallet Town, so the trip would serve his Frontier challenge as well.

With a destination in mind, the road felt easier. After half a day's travel, they reached the long bridge across the sea where Team Rocket had once ambushed Ethan. The sight brought back many memories. This time, to save time, he and May flew over it on Dragonite instead of crossing on foot.

May had never ridden with Ethan before. She sat behind him, watching the sea flash past below. The flight excited her, but their closeness made her heart beat a little faster. When Dragonite turned with the air currents, she found herself pressed against Ethan's broad back. Her cheeks warmed.

At her age, thoughts and feelings could rush in without warning. She was beginning to discover what it meant to like someone. She had spent most of her time with boys like Ash and Max. Ethan was the first mature man she had come to know this closely. Everything she had witnessed over the last few days had unsettled her, stirring unfamiliar emotions.

In some ways, she was going through what Misty once had. She might even be starting down the same path.

When Dragonite landed, Ethan helped May down and noticed her flushed face. He assumed the cold wind had caused it.

Pallet Town was closer now that they had crossed the bridge, though they would not reach it immediately.

Brother Ethan... May hesitated. Why don't we ride Dragonite all the way? Wouldn't that be faster?

Misty had asked him the same question once. Looking at May, Ethan seemed for a moment to see Misty standing there instead. Then the illusion faded, leaving the cheerful girl before him.

He pointed to the streams, trees, and stones beside the road. What do you feel?

Huh? May was confused for a moment, then thought she understood. I feel nature. Do you mean that riding Dragonite is only a way to travel, and we'd miss what we can learn from all this?

You're thinking too hard. Ethan laughed. I mean that when we walk, we can enjoy the scenery along the way. From the sky, we see clouds and the ground racing past.

May stared at him. She had considered her answer so carefully, only for the reason to be that simple. She pressed a hand to her forehead, but she had also discovered his playful side.

They walked on. Just as Ethan was about to suggest a break and something to eat, May's phone rang. It was Max.

Why is Max calling me? she wondered.

As soon as she answered, her brother's excited voice came through. Where are you, sis? Bet you don't know this! I'm visiting Professor Oak's lab with Professor Birch right now!

Chapter 809: A Reunion, a New Partner, and a Departure

Pallet Town. Professor Oak's laboratory.

Ethan and May arrived the following morning, dusty from the road. After Max's call, they had traveled as quickly as they could, but they still had to camp outside for a night. Even then, Ethan had not flown the rest of the way on Dragonite. Unless there was no other choice, he seemed determined to travel under his own power.

May was used to sleeping outdoors after her journey with Ash. She did not find it hard. She even thought this way of traveling was good for her.

Only one thing made her shy: instead of sleeping separately in sleeping bags as she had with Ash and their friends, she and Ethan had shared a tent. Being alone in one tent with him felt awkward. Still, it was warmer than sleeping in the open, and they did not have to worry about sudden wind or rain. She had been too nervous to sleep at first, but once she drifted off later in the night, she rested almost as well as she would have at an inn.

They climbed the slope and steps to the laboratory. Ethan knocked on the door. Hurried footsteps sounded inside, and Max opened it with a broad grin.

May! Mr. Vale! You're finally here!

May put her hands on her hips. What's going on? Why are you here?

Max had not explained much on the phone the previous day. Now she meant to get an answer.

Heh. Max rubbed his nose, looking pleased with himself. If you can come to Kanto, why can't I? You didn't bring me, so I came with Professor Birch!

Someone else appeared from another room: Tracey Sketchit, whom Ethan had not seen in a long time. After traveling through the Orange Islands with Ash, Tracey had stayed at Professor Oak's laboratory and become one of his trusted assistants.

Tracey and Max looked unexpectedly well matched standing together. Tracey was a Pokemon Watcher, and Max might be suited to following the same path.

It's good to see you again, Mr. Vale, Tracey said with a smile. Congratulations on winning in Hoenn. I watched your matches on television. They were exciting!

Ethan chatted with him and introduced May. Tracey then explained how Max had come to be there.

Once Max returned home, he had felt increasingly left out. Ash and Brock had gone back to Kanto, and even May had followed Misty there. The group of four had scattered, leaving him alone. He talked at length with Norman and Caroline, but they would not let a young boy cross the sea to Kanto by himself.

Then Professor Birch happened to visit. When Max learned that Birch was going to Professor Oak's laboratory, he seized the chance to accompany him.

So that's what happened. May shook her head. Honestly, I can't get away from you anywhere. If I'd known you were going to insist on coming, I might as well have brought you myself.

I wouldn't have gone with you, Max retorted, turning his head. Not with that scary girl around. Where is she, anyway?

He meant Misty. Oddly enough, Max was unafraid of his own older sister, but Misty inspired both respect and fear in him.

May covered her mouth to hide a laugh. She's gone home to take over her Gym. It's just Brother Ethan and me traveling together now.

Max brightened and seemed about to say something, but May added, Of course, we'll video call her almost every day. You can see her whenever you like!

His face fell. Any thought of joining them vanished.

I don't want to see her.

In the anime, Max had got along reasonably well with Misty. They had met only a few times there. On this journey, he had seen far more of her headstrong side, including the time she slapped Drew. She had left an unforgettable impression on him and shown him just how frightening an older girl could be.

Ash and Professor Oak joined them from another part of the laboratory. After the greetings, Ash grinned at Ethan.

You took your time getting here, Brother Ethan. I would've set out yesterday if I hadn't known you were coming! Have you started the Battle Frontier challenge?

Started? Ethan drew two gleaming Symbols from his pocket and held them up. While you were resting at home, I earned two of them.

What? Ash stared. Already?

He had only been home for two days since returning from Vermilion City. How had Ethan moved so quickly?

Ethan shook his head. Don't worry. I rushed because I need to go to Johto for a few days. You might have all your Symbols by the time I get back.

Ash relaxed. He was not really trying to beat Ethan for speed; he just did not want to fall too far behind. Ethan was the Trainer he hoped to catch up with.

After they talked a while longer, Ethan turned to Professor Oak. He had not forgotten why he had come.

Professor, could you give May one of the Kanto starter Pokemon?

Everyone but Oak looked surprised. Even May had not expected Ethan to ask for a Pokemon on her behalf.

Brother Ethan, I...

He gave her a reassuring look, and she swallowed the rest of her words.

A Kanto starter? Oak nodded readily. Of course. Giving Pokemon to new Trainers is part of my job. May has traveled already, but she has only just come to Kanto. On new ground, she's a newcomer in a way.

Max considered that, then smiled. Professor, does that make Mr. Vale a newcomer whenever he reaches a new region? A beginner who's won three regional championships sounds terrifying!

Everyone laughed. Ash joined in at first, but his smile gradually faded. When would he reach Ethan's level?

Oak led them to the research room where the starter Poke Balls were kept. May could choose whichever she liked.

They had barely entered when a small blue, turtle-like Pokemon rushed out of the room and collided with May's leg. Professor Birch came hurrying after it, out of breath.

It was Squirtle, one of Kanto's three starters. It had been running too fast to see where it was going. The collision knocked it onto its back, and its rounded shell made it hard to right itself. It flailed in alarm.

May bent down and picked it up. Then she looked at Birch. Professor Birch, what happened?

May? When did you arrive? He caught his breath. I was observing the three starters, and this Squirtle suddenly ran off.

Again? Tracey sighed. How many times has it done that this month? Something must have frightened it. It's timid and bolts at the slightest disturbance. We've been trying to help it overcome that habit, but so far nothing's worked.

May looked down. Squirtle was pressed against her chest, with two large tears at the corners of its eyes. It looked pitiful. She kept holding it as they followed the others inside.

Three Poke Balls sat on a device in the center of the research room. Two were closed; the third was open. Squirtle had evidently come from that one.

There's also a Charmander and a Bulbasaur, Oak told May. Counting the Squirtle in your arms, which would you like?

Well... May tried to set Squirtle down so she could consider the choice. It would not let go. When Max offered to help, Squirtle pulled its head into its shell.

It seems to like May, Ash observed.

Everyone could see that. At the very least, Squirtle felt safe in her arms.

What should I do? May asked helplessly.

Why not choose Squirtle? Ethan said. You need to choose one, and it doesn't want to leave you. Take it with you. Personally, I think it's a good choice.

May considered his words. She had only just met Squirtle, so she could not yet know whether it was the right partner for her. But Ethan had brought her here and asked for a starter. She did not believe he had done either thing without a reason. Perhaps he knew something she did not.

His encouraging look settled it. She nodded. All right. I'll choose Squirtle!

Ethan felt a small sense of satisfaction. With his help, May had met the Squirtle she had obtained in the anime. He could have taken her to catch a stronger Pokemon or one better suited to her, but he did not want his presence to keep these two from finding each other.

Now that she had chosen it, that concern was gone. He had achieved what he came for. Still, they had only just arrived, so he could hardly leave before sharing a meal.

Their visit made the laboratory livelier. At noon, Ash's mother Delia prepared a generous lunch for everyone. Over the meal, Ethan mentioned that he intended to set off afterward.

Ash responded immediately. Right! It's time to get moving. Pikachu and I are ready for our next adventure! Seeing Ethan's two Frontier Symbols had left him eager to begin his own challenge.

I'm going too! Max stood up.

To everyone's surprise, he chose to travel with Ash rather than with his sister. Ash was taken aback for a moment, then nodded happily. Max had been part of his Hoenn group, and it would be good to have him along again.

Delia looked from one boy to the other with concern. Neither of you is very good at looking after yourselves. Will you really manage on your own?

A voice came from outside the room. Then count me in!

Ash turned. Brock was coming through the door with his pack on his back.

Brock! Ash leaped up and hurried to meet him. What are you doing here?

Coming along on your next adventure, of course. Brock wore his familiar expression, but the smile was clear in his voice. Looks like I arrived at just the right time.

Chapter 810: Cleffa and Articuno

That afternoon, Ethan and the others stood outside Professor Oak's laboratory to say goodbye to Oak, Professor Birch, Delia, and Tracey.

Ash had hurried home to pack after lunch and had just returned to join them.

Take care, Oak said first. I wish you every success with your challenges. Birch and Tracey offered encouragement too, while Delia quietly gave Ash one reminder after another.

Okay, Mom, I know. I'll take care of myself. Don't worry. Ash seemed embarrassed to be the only one treated like a child in front of everyone. After assuring her again, he hurried over to Ethan and the others.

Then we're off, Ethan said to Oak. May, Ash, Max, and Brock waved goodbye as well. They left the laboratory together and walked out of Pallet Town, disappearing from their friends' view.

...

They were all heading for the Battle Factory near Mt. Moon, so Ethan and Ash's groups traveled together for now. The conversation and laughter made the road livelier.

Even so, they kept a clear division between their two parties. Ethan and Ash walked side by side at the front, each leading his own group. May and Max followed behind them. The siblings talked quietly, but May stayed closer to Ethan while Max stayed nearer to Ash. May had already settled into her new role as Ethan's traveling partner.

Brock brought up the rear behind Max, carrying his pack, enjoying the scenery, and keeping an eye on everyone.

With so much to discuss, time passed quickly. By the time they felt tired and thirsty, Mt. Moon was not far away.

Ethan looked back and saw sweat on Max's forehead. The boy was struggling to keep up, so Ethan called a halt.

Let's rest here and have something to eat. If we start again soon, we should reach Mt. Moon before dark and camp there.

As the oldest among them, Ethan naturally took charge. Neither Ash nor Brock objected. Following his lead seemed entirely normal to them. He had earned their trust through his strength and reliability.

Now Brock could show his skills. While the others gathered firewood and water, set up a table, and laid out the utensils, he tied on an apron and set to work. With the Pokemon helping, he soon served everyone a meal.

Let's eat.

Ethan tasted the rich vegetable soup and gave Brock a thumbs-up. This is excellent! Just as good as I remember.

Brock was a remarkable cook. Of the people Ethan knew, perhaps only Erika could match him. Brock smiled bashfully at the praise. Ash and the others had eaten his food throughout their travels, so they simply enjoyed it as they always did. They had grown accustomed to eating well.

Ethan remembered something and turned to May. I should warn you: I can only make simple meals. If you travel with me, you'll have to put up with rougher food on the road.

May's face fell. Along with shopping and dressing up, she loved good food. She hated the thought of giving that up during a journey. But she had made her choice.

It's fine, she said with a rueful smile. I'll eat whatever we can make on the road. But when we reach a city, I'm having a feast!

Everyone laughed. May's love of food was no secret.

As they ate, the grass nearby rustled. A wild pink Pokemon with a star-shaped outline emerged.

Huh? Max stared. Why is there a Cleffa here?

It was indeed a Cleffa, the youngest stage of the Clefairy and Clefable line. Its pink body, tiny black eyes, brown pointed ears, small mouth, and curl of hair on its forehead made it rather cute, though not everyone would agree.

Max had reason to wonder. Cleffa usually appeared at night. They rarely strayed far from places where meteors had fallen and generally lived in mountains. This was flat land, and evening had only just begun.

Then again, Mt. Moon was close. Cleffa, Clefairy, and Clefable lived there. Perhaps this one had wandered away while playing and followed the smell of dinner.

For a rare wild Pokemon, that was risky. Another group of Trainers might have reached for their Poke Balls at once. Fortunately, Ethan and Ash's friends had no interest in catching it.

Sensing no hostility, Cleffa hopped closer. It inspected one Pokemon, then another, pestering Ash's and May's partners with its curiosity until they seemed both amused and at a loss.

It's friendly enough, Max observed. It doesn't seem lost.

Maybe it's hungry?

May rose and approached it, hoping for a closer look. Cleffa was comfortable with the Pokemon but wary of humans. It darted behind May's Munchlax, and she stopped where she was.

The other Pokemon greeted it warmly. Cleffa soon relaxed and began playing with them.

For Ethan and the others, the encounter was a small interruption. In the original anime story, Team Rocket's trio had attacked Ash's group after Cleffa appeared. With Ethan here, the three did not dare show themselves. Without their interference, nothing more came of it.

They prepared some food for Cleffa too. After dinner, the group set off again. In barely half an hour, the little Pokemon seemed to know them all.

The sun sank, and darkness began to spread. They had traveled only half a day from Pallet Town and had just eaten, so everyone still had energy. Rather than camp there, they kept walking toward Mt. Moon.

At the mountain's foot, before they entered the rocky slopes, a Clefairy and a Clefable came looking for Cleffa. Their anxious expressions made it clear they were its family.

The group returned Cleffa to them and started to leave, but Cleffa stopped them. At first they could not understand what it wanted. Then they realized it was inviting them into Mt. Moon.

They had not expected that. After a brief discussion, they agreed that spending the night inside the mountain might be better than camping outdoors.

Following Cleffa along a winding path, they climbed halfway up and entered a cave. Deep inside lay an enormous round meteorite beneath a shaft of moonlight. Groups of Clefairy and Clefable danced around it, their celebration both joyful and mysterious.

For Ash and Brock, this was a return visit. They had come here near the start of their first journey. Everything seemed to have changed, and yet nothing had. They were no longer inexperienced beginners. They had grown through success and failure. Still, they were traveling and pursuing the same dreams.

May and Max had never seen the place and looked around in wonder. Ethan was glad finally to see it with his own eyes as well.

...

They rested in the cave that night and set out again early the next morning. Beyond Mt. Moon, the Battle Factory was closer, though they first had to cross a vast forest.

Without Ethan, Ash's group would almost certainly have got lost. With him, there was little danger of it. He read the map accurately and, when a path divided, sent Dragonite above the trees to check their direction. They kept to the right route.

It made the journey less unpredictable. It was also a major reason Ethan could travel so much faster than Ash.

They were nearly out of the forest when something cold touched Max's face. He looked up and saw a large blue bird with long, beautiful tail feathers gliding high above them. Snowflakes drifted down from it.

Look! There's a beautiful Pokemon in the sky!

The others followed his pointing finger. Ash and Brock stared at the bird, then turned almost at once toward Ethan.

Why are you looking at me? Ethan asked, puzzled.

Brother Ethan... Ash hesitated. Is that...?

Yes, Ethan said. It's Articuno.

Articuno? May and Max exclaimed. Delighted, they pulled out their Pokedexes and aimed them at the sky.

While the siblings watched the bird, Ash and Brock kept their eyes on Ethan. He understood the question in their expressions and shook his head.

Don't jump to conclusions. This has nothing to do with me. There isn't just one Articuno in the world. There are even Articuno with a different form in Galar. Meeting one on a journey isn't so strange.

Ash and Brock had seen Ethan's Articuno in unforgettable battles: the clash of the Legendary birds at Shamouti Island in the Orange Islands and the battle between the Legendary birds and beasts at Johto's crystal tower. No wonder they thought of his Pokemon first. But this Articuno clearly did not belong to him.

It was gone in little more than ten seconds. May and Max had been so absorbed in watching it that they missed the conversation. They kept gazing after it, remembering that brief, beautiful sight.

Too bad it flew away, Max said. Still, seeing a Legendary Pokemon this beautiful right after arriving in Kanto makes the trip worthwhile!

That was hardly the whole story. The man standing beside Max had an Articuno of his own, along with the other two Legendary birds. Ash wanted to tell him, but Ethan only smiled. Ash held his tongue. Ethan could reveal it himself when he wished.

It really was beautiful, May agreed. Then she frowned. But why would Articuno be here? There aren't any snowy mountains or ice fields nearby.

Chapter 811: The Battle Factory

After leaving the forest, the group stopped for a late breakfast at a Pokemon Center near its edge. Nurse Joy gave them the Battle Factory's exact location, and they set out again.

Beyond a short canyon, an enormous steel building rose before them. It looked every bit like a factory.

So that's why they call it the Battle Factory, Max said, gazing up at it. I thought it was just a name. It really looks like one! What do they make here? Surely they didn't build a factory just to match the name.

Who knows? Ethan said. We'll find out inside.

They were about to enter when a man's voice called from overhead. Mr. Vale! Ash! I've been waiting for you!

They looked up. Scott, in a blue shirt, was smiling and waving from an outdoor walkway on the second floor.

Mr. Scott! Ash waved back. I didn't expect to see you here!

May looked puzzled. You know him too?

Of course. On my way home from the ship, I passed through Viridian Gym. I met Mr. Scott there and battled Agatha from the Elite Four! That's when he explained the Battle Frontier to me again.

You battled an Elite Four member? May, Max, and Brock had not heard about that part of Ash's trip. They crowded around him with questions.

How strong was Agatha?

Did you beat her?

Ash scratched his cheek and gave an embarrassed laugh. Well... she beat me completely. Her Pokemon were incredibly strong.

While they spoke, Scott hurried down the stairs and reached them a little out of breath. He greeted Ash, then turned apologetically to Ethan.

Mr. Vale, I'm sorry about what happened at the Battle Dome.

Scott owned the Battle Frontier, so he knew exactly what had happened. The match had attracted so much attention that the internet was still arguing about it. People mocked Tucker for promoting himself as Ethan's equal when he had proved so weak. He had become a public joke.

Scott had little power to prevent it. He had recruited the Frontier Brains because of their abilities, and each had a different temperament. He relied on them to build the Frontier's reputation and could hardly afford to alienate them. Even if he had wanted to stop Tucker, he might not have been able to.

Ethan understood. He had no intention of blaming Scott. The matter was over, and until Scott brought it up, he had nearly put Tucker out of his mind.

Don't worry, he said. That was Tucker's decision, not yours or the other Frontier Brains'. I don't hold it against you. It's behind us, isn't it?

Yes, yes. It's behind us, Scott said quickly.

The exchange made little sense to Ash and Max. They quietly asked Brock, but he knew only that Ethan's match with Tucker had caused a stir across Kanto. He had not been there and knew nothing of what lay behind it.

After a few more words, Scott led them toward the factory entrance. Before they reached it, an engine roared on the other side of the doors. The doors burst open, and a strange red, six-wheeled armored vehicle shot out.

The machine was angular and rugged, with rows of huge exhaust pipes pouring black smoke from its rear. It circled wildly across the open space. Its brakes seemed to have failed. A man's alarmed voice could be heard from inside.

Not again, Scott sighed. It's out of control. He turned to the group. Could you help stop it?

Leave it to us!

Ash, May, and Brock eagerly released their Pokemon. Ethan stayed back, certain they could handle it.

Three flashes of blue light revealed Ash's Grovyle, May's Combusken, and Brock's Mudkip. The three Hoenn starters, one of each type, had come together here in an unexpected way. With Pikachu's help, they stopped the runaway machine.

Perhaps damaged it until it stopped would have been more accurate. Even a tough armored vehicle could not withstand several Pokemon attacking at once. Fortunately, only one or two wheels and some related parts were broken, and stopping it prevented worse destruction.

The vehicle's hatch opened. A man in a red cap, black sleeveless shirt, dark trousers, and a long vest climbed down from the roof.

Thanks to you, I made it out! He wiped sweat from his forehead. This wild horse won't listen to its owner. Really, thank you!

Then he saw the damaged tires and wheel fittings, and his face fell. Oh, that's bad. It took me so much work to build this masterpiece. Looks like another major repair.

It's only a car, Scott said with a smile, beckoning him over. Let me introduce

Only a car? the man burst out. He pointed proudly at the machine. This is the Noland J-9, a supermachine I built myself! It runs on steam. Isn't that stylish?

Ash and the others exchanged doubtful glances. Neither its shape nor its colors looked particularly stylish to them.

Max muttered, So it's a steam car. Haven't those been obsolete for ages? Clean energy and controlled nuclear power are where the future is going.

The man heard him. What do you know? he cried, throwing back his head. Steam is a man's dream! A rugged supermachine like this is what a real man should drive!

The discussion was running away from them. Scott cut in. Enough about the car. Remember the Trainer I told you about yesterday? He's here.

The man grew serious at once. He stepped closer and studied the visitors, finally fixing his gaze on Ethan.

You're the champion?

I am.

At this distance, Ethan could see him clearly. He had brown hair, sparse facial hair, and slight lines around his mouth. He looked at least thirty-five. His muscular arms suited someone who worked on machines, while his clothes made him seem younger than he probably was.

The man laughed. It really is you! I've waited a long time for this. Oh, I haven't introduced myself. I'm Noland, the Frontier Brain in charge of the Battle Factory.

Ethan had guessed. So had May, Max, and Brock. A man driving out of the Factory was likely connected to it. Only Ash seemed to realize who he was when Noland said it aloud.

Ash and the others introduced themselves. Noland looked at Ethan with bright anticipation.

Ever since I heard you were coming, I've been waiting to battle you!

Then we'll have our match, Ethan said, meeting his gaze. That's why I'm here.

Noland was not merely being polite. He genuinely wanted to test himself against Ethan.

Scott grinned. If you want to face this champion, you'd better give it everything you've got. He beat Tucker in only two attacks.

I'm nothing like that performer, Noland said confidently. My Pokemon are strong!

Me too! Ash called. I came to challenge the Battle Factory. You can't battle only Brother Ethan!

I haven't forgotten you. Noland turned to Ash with a hearty smile. Scott told me about the spirit you showed against Agatha at Viridian Gym. I'll give you my best too.

Noland took them inside the Battle Factory, but instead of leading them straight to the battlefield, he brought them to a grassy area. A young man was feeding a large number of Pokemon there. He looked up at their approach.

Master, who are they?

Noland introduced them. This is Sergio, my first apprentice. He helps me around the Factory. Sergio, these Trainers have come to challenge me. The one in the middle is Ethan Vale, champion in three regions.

You're Mr. Vale? Sergio hurried over, excited. Ever since Scott told us you might come, Master has been waiting for this day. We're glad you're finally here!

His words made Noland's anticipation clear. Ash felt a small pang of envy. He had come to challenge Noland too, yet Ethan received all the attention. Then he remembered Ethan's strength and achievements. Of course Noland would be eager to face him. Ash respected Ethan as much as anyone.

After Sergio had greeted them, Noland gestured toward the Pokemon. These are my partners. I usually let challengers choose freely which one they'd like to face. But for you two, I've prepared a special Pokemon.

Which one? Ash asked eagerly.

I'll keep that a secret until the battle. Noland smiled.

Ethan had already guessed and could not resist spoiling the surprise. Articuno, isn't it?

What? Noland and Sergio stared at him. Articuno was the Factory's greatest secret. How could Ethan know?

Noland glanced instinctively at Scott, then remembered that even Scott did not know. He could not have told Ethan.

Ash and the others were stunned too. Brother Ethan, Ash asked, are you saying the Articuno we saw earlier belongs to Mr. Noland?

Chapter 812: Ethan Has an Articuno Too?

There was no point keeping the secret now that Ethan had guessed it.

Yes, there's an Articuno here, Noland admitted. But it isn't exactly mine. We're good friends. He looked at the others. How did you know?

Ash quickly told him about the bird they had seen over the forest.

So that's what happened. Noland shook his head with a rueful smile. It sneaked out to play again. I wanted to surprise you when the battle began. Looks like that plan's gone.

Would they really have been that surprised? May glanced from side to side. Ash, Max, and Brock stood to her right; Ethan stood to her left. Every one of them had encountered Legendary Pokemon before.

Ethan had Celebi and Deoxys. Ash frequently met Legendary Pokemon too and sometimes befriended them. Compared with ordinary Trainers, their group had seen many rare Pokemon. Learning that an Articuno lived here might startle them briefly, but it was unlikely to leave them speechless.

Even so, having an Articuno willing to stay at the Factory was remarkable, whether Noland had caught it or not. Legendary Pokemon were rare even among Elite Four members, champions, Gym Leaders, and Frontier Brains.

Noland explained how the bird had come to be here. Not long ago, he had been flying one of his homemade aircraft at night when he encountered an injured Articuno. He helped it, and they became friends. Since then, Articuno had visited the Factory from time to time.

It sounded like a simple incident that might happen anywhere. Perhaps friendships built in such ordinary ways were the most genuine.

I see, Brock said, stroking his chin. Since stepping away from Gym work, he had begun thinking more and more like a Pokemon Breeder. He understood the bond Noland described. Then another thought occurred to him. If you haven't caught Articuno, does that mean it's still a wild Pokemon?

Sergio understood his concern. Don't worry. We've kept its presence strictly secret. We never show it to ordinary challengers. Today is the first time we've told visitors.

I can confirm that! Scott laughed. If you hadn't come, I might still have no idea it was here.

He did not sound offended. He was praising how well Noland had protected the secret.

We'll keep quiet too, Ethan said for the group. None of us will spread the news.

I trust you, Noland told Ethan with a broad smile. You're a champion, after all.

After a little more conversation, Noland led them to the Factory's battlefield. It occupied a vast, mostly empty workshop. Steel beams and pipes lined the space. The dim lights and metallic smell suited the name Battle Factory.

They had already settled on Articuno as Noland's Pokemon. He had no other partner that could match it, so each challenge would be a one-on-one battle. The first Pokemon to win would decide the match.

Beforehand, both Ethan and Ash used the Factory's transfer machine to adjust their teams.

This would be Ethan's first official battle against a Legendary Pokemon. Ash, too, looked unusually serious.

Ethan met Ash's eyes. This time he did not offer Ash the first match. He indicated that he would go ahead.

Ash did not mind. They were friends, and both would have a turn. He was curious which Pokemon Ethan would choose against Articuno.

Noland and Ethan took their places on opposite sides of the field. May, Ash, Max, Brock, and Scott went to the viewing area. Sergio stood beside the field as referee.

Noland gave a sharp whistle. A beautiful blue bird flew out of a side passage and circled overhead. Snowflakes drifted from its wings across the battlefield.

It was the Articuno they had seen above the forest. After several beats of its wings, it descended onto Noland's half of the field. May and Max finally had a close view of it.

It's beautiful, Max said, wide-eyed.

May's thoughts went to Pokemon Contests. Imagine using Articuno in a Contest. Everyone would be watching it...

She was thinking like a Coordinator even here. After admiring Articuno, the spectators all turned to Ethan. What would he send out against it?

Ethan did not release a Pokemon at once. He took three Ultra Balls from his pouch and held them in his palm.

Mr. Noland, he said with a smile, I'd like you to choose your opponent from these three.

Noland raised his brows. I've heard of a defender letting a challenger choose which Pokemon to face, but never the other way around. If you're offering me three choices, I assume all three are powerful?

You could say that. Ethan nodded lightly. They're not my strongest, but each is on the same level as your Articuno.

Noland's eyes narrowed. On the same level? Did Ethan mean strength, or something else? Were all three Ultra Balls holding Legendary Pokemon?

The possibility startled him. It sounded impossible. Then again, this was a man who had won championships in three regions. Who knew what partners he kept in reserve?

May, Max, and Scott had much the same thought. Only Ash and Brock exchanged a look of recognition.

So he's going to use one of those Pokemon against Articuno? Brock swallowed.

Looks that way. Ash frowned. I've never seen Brother Ethan use them in an official match.

What are you talking about? Max demanded. Does Mr. Vale have a Legendary Pokemon too?

Brock let out a breath and gave him a wry smile. Watch. You'll know soon enough.

Their evasive answers only made Max and Scott more impatient. May knew a little more about Ethan. Could he be planning to use Deoxys? But there were three Ultra Balls. What was in the other two?

Noland made his choice. He pointed to the ball at the far right of Ethan's hand. They all look alike. I'll trust my instincts and pick that one.

Ethan glanced down. A tiny snowflake was engraved on its surface. Of all three balls, Noland had chosen this one.

What a fateful choice.

Ethan put the other two away and tossed the selected Ultra Ball into the air. Blue light flashed. Another magnificent blue bird appeared above the field.

Everyone except Ash and Brock gasped. The feathers, the imposing body, the familiar shapeit was unmistakably an Articuno.

Ethan had one too?

Mr. Vale has an Articuno? Scott cried.

Snowflakes drifted down as Ethan's Articuno circled the workshop, then landed on his side. The two birds faced each other across the field.

The spectators looked back and forth, rubbed their eyes, and finally accepted what they were seeing. May, Max, and Scott were still astonished.

Max turned to Ash and Brock. You knew from the start that Mr. Vale had an Articuno?

That's not all, Brock said with a smile. You saw the three Ultra Balls. This one held Articuno. The other two...

The other two? Max's eyes widened.

Across the field, Noland asked the same question. I never expected you to have an Articuno of your own. What was in the other two balls?

Ethan smiled. I told you. They're on the same level as Articuno.

He had not named them, but in Kanto the answer was obvious.

So that's it, Noland said with a rueful nod. Incredible. You've brought all three together.

Max was impatient for confirmation. Do they mean...?

Yes, Brock said. The other two Legendary birds of Kanto: Moltres and Zapdos.

May, Max, and Scott looked at Ethan anew. They had a much clearer sense of the Pokemon he commanded and the strength behind his achievements.

On the field, the Articuno studied one another. Their fighting spirit rose. They were the same size and carried themselves with the same proud bearing. The only visible difference was the clear, glittering collar worn by one of them.

Sharing a species did not make them affectionate. Each recognized a formidable opponent in the other. Their strength, temperament, and Legendary pride all drove them to settle which was superior.

With both sides ready, Sergio raised his flags. The Battle Frontier match between Ethan Vale and Factory Head Noland begins now!

Gears turned overhead. The ceiling shuddered and slowly drew back, revealing the open sky.

As everyone looked up, Scott proudly explained, This is one of the Battle Factory's best features. For an aerial battle, the roof opens so both Pokemon have room to fly. For a water battle, the field can quickly fill and become a pool. Whatever Pokemon you bring, we can provide a suitable battlefield.

He had every reason to be proud. The Factory was his investment and part of his Battle Frontier. The challengers' amazement gave him immense satisfaction. It was one of the main reasons he had built the Frontier in the first place.

Chapter 813: A Duel Between Two Articuno

Clack!

The gears stopped. The Battle Factory's roof had opened completely, revealing a clear blue sky and the sun high above. Warm light and fresh air poured in, changing the atmosphere of the field.

Without waiting for orders, both Articuno spread their wings and flew out of the building into the open sky.

The Trainer areas were on raised platforms. Ethan could stay where he was, see the whole battlefield, and call commands to his Articuno.

With both sides ready, Sergio raised his hand again. Battle, begin!

Ethan and Noland called their first moves at the same instant.

Articuno, use Blizzard!

Articuno, Steel Wing!

Ethan wanted to control the field and test his opponent. Noland sent his bird straight in with a Steel-type move that was strong against Ice types.

Their choices reflected their temperaments. Ethan usually fought methodically. He tested an opponent before pressing his attack, leaving fewer openings and waiting for the chance to strike decisively. Strategy, together with the strength of his Pokemon, had brought him so many victories.

Noland's rugged, forthright manner led him to attack directly. As Blizzard formed, his Articuno hardened its wings like steel and plunged into the storm. Snow swallowed both birds, hiding them from view.

With the Pokemon out of sight, some of the tension in the viewing area eased. Max had been clenching his fists ever since the battle started. He relaxed his hands and turned to the others.

Who do you think will win?

This was a battle between Legendary Pokemon. Encounters with them were rare enough; watching two fight was thrilling.

Scott, nearest to Max, shook his head. Hard to say. They're both Articuno. Either could win.

Ash hesitated too. Maybe it depends on which one fights better?

Brock smiled with more certainty. I think Mr. Vale's Articuno will win.

Why? the others asked.

They were the same species, with much the same moves and type. Leaving their Trainers' commands aside, their strengths ought to be close. Why was Brock so sure?

Remember, Brock told Ash, who knew Ethan's bird best. Noland's Articuno has only been here a short time and rarely battles other Trainers. Ethan caught his long ago, and it's faced many powerful opponents. That experience matters.

Brock kept one more thought to himself. Ethan's Articuno wore a collar that seemed to increase its power. That could only improve its chances.

Ash remembered its battles at Shamouti Island and the crystal tower. It had fought other Legendary Pokemon, the birds and the beasts, under tremendous pressure. Those were only the matches Ash had witnessed. Ethan must have used it in others during his travels.

In experience and strength, Ethan's Articuno probably had the advantage. Ethan's commands would add to it.

A cry rang from inside the Blizzard. One of the birds had been struck, but the storm concealed which one. Explosions and flashes of light showed that a fierce fight was underway, yet no one could see its course. Snow drifted down over the spectators.

Everyone looked up, waiting for the birds to emerge. Ethan remained calm. Noland looked more anxious. With neither Pokemon visible, their Trainers could do little; the birds had to rely on themselves.

The Blizzard was fierce but short-lived. After two or three minutes, it dissipated. Snowflakes falling into the warmer air quickly turned to water.

At last they could see both Pokemon. To the crowd's surprise, Noland's Articuno, the one that had charged into the storm, bore several small wounds. They were little more than scratches and did not hamper its movement, but they showed that it had come off worse inside the Blizzard.

Brock's prediction appeared sound. In a direct contest of strength, Ethan's Articuno had the edge.

Noland saw it too. He had no easy answer, but he could at least keep his bird out of another storm that blocked his view. Now that the sky was clear, he could direct the battle again.

He ordered Articuno forward. Its setback had not broken his aggressive rhythm. The two birds fought high above the field, one giving chase and then the other. Ice-type moves met in the air, scattering crystalline snow.

Ash and his friends barely noticed the beautiful flakes. They watched each exchange, their attention fixed on the two Articuno.

They were Legendary Pokemon indeed. They had only just begun, and neither had used its full strength, yet the weather was already changing. Ice energy leaked into the air. Their attacks altered the surrounding atmosphere. Dark clouds gathered across what had been a sunny sky, blocking the light.

The temperature dropped abruptly. Even from the viewing area, the others felt the chill.

So this is Articuno's power, Max murmured. They've darkened the whole sky.

May and Max had never watched a battle of this scale so closely. The moves were familiar, yet whether because of the birds' power or the awe surrounding Legendary Pokemon, the fight felt very different from an ordinary match.

Ash pulled down the brim of his cap. You haven't seen anything yet. The real battle's only beginning.

He was right. Ethan had spent these exchanges measuring Noland's Articuno. Now he knew its strength, and it was time to finish the match.

The rhythm changed in an instant. Ethan's bearing sharpened. At his command, his Articuno turned and drove forward like an unsheathed blade, cold power gathering around it.

Noland did not know Ethan's fighting style. The sudden shift caught him off guard, and his Articuno took a heavy blow before he could adjust.

He stared in alarm. He had only just grown used to the earlier pace and was looking for his own opening. Ethan had acted first.

Noland reacted quickly, ordering his bird to pull away before it took more damage. He frowned at its labored breathing. He needed a way to recover, but Ethan's Articuno was already closing in again.

Left with little choice, Noland copied Ethan's earlier move. He called for Blizzard to buy time, blunt the attack, and let his Articuno regroup.

At that moment, it was a good decision. Thick clouds now covered the sky. As Noland's bird drew on its power, it created a Blizzard larger and stronger than the first.

Snow-laden winds swept over the entire Factory. They blew through the open roof and down into the building, striking Ash and the others in the face.

They wore only light clothes. At such close range, the bitter cold was unbearable. Huddling and shivering, they fled farther back, found towels to wrap around themselves, and crowded together for warmth.

May glanced at Ethan. He was still standing on the Trainer's platform, exposed to the wind. She grabbed another towel and ran back toward him.

She need not have worried. When she struggled through the storm to his side, she found a barrier surrounding him. The wind could not reach it.

Huh?

Gengar rose from Ethan's shadow with a grin. You made that trip for nothing, little girl.

Of course Gengar was protecting him. With Gengar there, May thought, even a falling meteor would have trouble reaching Ethan. She felt foolish for forgetting it.

Embarrassed, she looked at Ethan. His attention remained on the battle. She was about to leave when he spoke without turning.

Stay. Come stand beside me and watch the battle from here.

May stopped. Had she heard correctly? Did he want her beside him to spare her the Blizzard, or was there another reason?

She stepped closer. Ethan turned to her with a smile.

You're a Coordinator now, and battling is an important part of that. I don't know much about teaching Contests. But as we travel together, I hope you'll watch my battles from my point of view and find something you can learn for yourself.

From his point of view? May's heart beat faster. She was not quite sure how she felt, but she nodded and took her place beside him on the Trainer's platform.

This was not a League tournament. It was a formal challenge, but its rules were less rigid, and the two sides already knew each other. Even if Noland had seen May joining Ethan, he was unlikely to object. In any case, he was occupied by the Blizzard and had no time to look over.

Visibility inside the storm was almost nonexistent. Once May was beside him, Ethan looked up again. He could make out only two blue shapes, like ice crystals, circling and darting in and out of the snow. He could not tell which was his Articuno and which was Noland's.

They would have to wait for the Blizzard to end. Judging by the heavy clouds, this storm would last much longer than Ethan's first one.

He could neither direct his Pokemon nor follow the fight. Now it came down to which Articuno could defeat the other unaided in those harsh conditions.

Chapter 814: Old Habits

The Blizzard grew stronger, with no sign of easing. The temperature inside the battlefield fell and kept falling. Snow soon lay across the floor in a layer that was neither thin nor especially deep. Even Noland on the opposite platform was lost from sight.

Under Gengar's protection, May breathed into her hands. She pulled the towel tighter around herself and moved a few steps closer to Ethan, but she could still feel the cold.

She glanced at his clothes and wondered whether she should offer him the towel. Before she could speak, both Articuno dived out of the storm and returned to the battlefield below.

The Blizzard continued. With the birds closer, however, the shock waves of their attacks and the gusts from their wings scattered some of the snow around them. It was not their intention, but the movement let the spectators follow them again.

Ethan could see Noland across the field too. He had to admire the man. Despite the cold and with no Pokemon shielding him, Noland stood straight as ever, seemingly unconcerned by the storm.

People born in this world really were hardier than someone from Earth, Ethan thought. Then he remembered how much longer he could now stay underwater than an ordinary person. Perhaps this world was gradually changing him too.

He returned his attention to the battle.

Noland's Articuno had picked up more wounds inside the Blizzard. Ethan's bird had not escaped unharmed either. Fresh scratches marked its body. The two had clearly fought hard while hidden.

Most of the battle had taken place out of sight, but everyone could tell that the deciding moment was approaching.

With their Pokemon visible again, Ethan and Noland both ordered an all-out attack. Standing beside Ethan, May could hear his commands and see his decisions more clearly. She concentrated, trying to imagine how he saw the fight.

Noland noticed her beside him. He glanced over and said nothing, just as Ethan had expected. Perhaps he had no attention to spare. His Articuno was panting; Ethan's still had more energy. Noland knew he was at a disadvantage and had to make a final push.

Articuno, use Ice Beam! he called.

Using an Ice-type move against another Articuno was hardly ideal. But Steel Wing and the few other moves of different types his Articuno knew had not achieved much. Ice attacks were what it did best. Ethan's bird had no obvious way around their shared typing either.

That was why Noland had not panicked, despite being behind. Still, with his Articuno tiring, the next exchange might decide the match.

Ethan gave a faint smile and called for Ice Beam too.

Two identical blue-white streams of energy shot from the birds' beaks, racing toward each other.

Boom!

The beams collided and burst into brilliant light. The explosion drove the Blizzard outward, leaving a round pocket of clear air. Its shock wave crossed the Trainer platforms, struck Ash and the others in the stands, and kept spreading before finally weakening.

May cried out. The wind whipped her hair and almost took her bandanna. She ducked behind Ethan to keep her footing. The force of the Legendary Pokemon's attack was frightening.

The two Ice Beams were still pressing against each other. Then Ethan's Articuno gained ground. Its beam broke through Noland's and struck his bird.

Ash stared. Why did Brother Ethan's Articuno win when they used the same move?

Max and Scott had no answer. Brock did. Because of its collar.

They looked at the ornament around Ethan's Articuno's neck.

What does it do? Ash asked.

If I'm right, it's made of Never-Melt Ice, Brock said. Wearing it greatly strengthens Ice-type moves. That's why Ethan's Articuno won the exchange.

Ash frowned. Isn't that cheating? If it's wearing something like that, how is this fair?

I wouldn't say that, Brock replied. Farfetch'd has its leek, Marowak its bone, Machoke its gold belt, and Grovyle the twig it carries in its mouth. Those are all items too. The Pokemon League allows them, as long as they aren't excessive.

Ash opened his mouth. A twig or belt seemed more like decoration than something that made a move stronger. Then he considered Farfetch'd without its leek, or Marowak without its bone. Both would lose a great deal of fighting ability. Perhaps Never-Melt Ice was not so different. Even so, he felt Ethan had gained an unfair edge.

Scott saw his expression. Look at it another way. Ethan obtained that Never-Melt Ice through his own ability. Why should using something he earned be unfair?

Ash still looked ready to argue, but Scott went on. In the end, a battle is decided by its result. A Trainer might win a Conference match through extraordinary luck, or because an opponent withdraws. Either way, a win is a win. People remember the winner.

That was more complicated than Ash was ready to accept. Scott did not expect him to agree immediately. He only wanted Ash to understand that Pokemon battles were not always as simple as they seemed.

On the field, Noland's Articuno cried out and fell toward the ground. Ice-type attacks dealt only half damage to an Ice-type Pokemon, but Articuno's power was formidable, and the Never-Melt Ice had strengthened the beam. Even reduced, the impact hurt.

Before Noland's bird could rise, Ethan's swooped down. It landed on top of its opponent and raked it with both claws.

Perhaps fighting fierce Legendary Pokemon had awakened something wild in Ethan's Articuno. It could use powerful moves, yet it also relished a raw physical struggle.

Noland's Articuno had never faced an attack like this. Weaker Pokemon usually yielded to its command of ice. Only an opponent of equal standing could force it into such a position.

It tried to claw back, but pinned underneath the other bird, it could do little. Feathers scattered across the ground. Its long tail, once so graceful, stood out in disarray. The elegant Legendary Pokemon looked more like a bedraggled hen.

Almost by instinct, it used Sheer Cold in a desperate counterattack. Ethan's Articuno spread its wings and answered with an even stronger Sheer Cold.

The two bursts of freezing power erupted together. Ice seized everything around them and raced outward, forming sharp spines like the petals of a giant frozen flower.

Watch out! Gengar cried. It raised a barrier around Ethan and May. Across the field, Noland released another Pokemon to shield himself.

The ice kept reaching toward the spectator area. Pikachu blasted the advancing spines apart with electricity before they struck Ash and the others.

When the freezing power finally stopped spreading, the battlefield had become a world of glistening crystals and falling snow. At its center, where the two Articuno lay, a solid mass of ice hid everything from view.

Crack. Crack.

The great ice flower shattered. An Articuno wearing a necklace burst free and climbed into the air. It spread its wings and called triumphantly to the sky.

The other Articuno lay motionless on the ground.

Was it over? Sergio hurried in from wherever he had taken shelter. One look at Noland's bird was enough.

Articuno is unable to battle! Mr. Vale wins this challenge!

Noland stood still for a moment, then shook his head. He had lost completely. Ethan's Articuno held the advantage in both strength and experience. There was nothing to dispute.

With the fight over, Noland suddenly felt the cold. He began shivering. He told Sergio to get emergency care for Articuno, then clambered over the icy ridges toward Ethan.

May promptly handed him her towel. He wrapped it around himself several times, stamped his feet, and let out a long breath.

I can feel my toes again. He looked up at the Articuno still circling overhead, then at Ethan. Your ordinary Pokemon are strong, but even your Legendary Pokemon can fight like that. I don't know how you train them.

Ethan gave the same answer he always did: plenty of experience in battle.

His Articuno landed beside him. At about 1.7 meters tall, it stood only a head shorter than Ethan. It began arranging its feathers as though it had not just fought a fierce match.

Ethan stroked its still-cold body. Then he, May, and Noland headed back toward the stands.

On the way, Ethan asked May quietly, Well? Did you learn anything?

May did not know what to say. She had barely been able to see the battle. Ethan's commands had been brief, yet his Articuno understood each one. The match was on a different level from the battles she usually knew.

Ethan noticed her discomfort and patted her head. The moment his hand touched her hair, he realized what he had done.

He had grown so used to doing that with Misty that he had mistaken May for her. Old habits were hard to break.

He lowered his hand without showing his surprise. It's all right if nothing comes to mind yet. These things take time. After we've traveled together longer, you'll gradually start to see more.

I... I understand.

He had spoken naturally, but May lowered her head, blushing. His hand had rested on her hair for only a moment. Even so, her cheeks had turned pink.

Chapter 815: Just as I Expected!

Ash and the others came over to meet Ethan. Before anyone could congratulate him, Max sneezed.

Noland looked at the boy, then back at the frozen battlefield. He gave Ash an apologetic smile. Cleanup will take a while, and Articuno is hurt. I'm afraid it'll be afternoon before I can battle you.

That's fine! Ash said. I'd wait as long as it takes for a match with Articuno. After watching you and Brother Ethan fight, I'm more fired up than ever!

Nothing excited Ash more than Pokemon battles. Even food, sleep, and catching new Pokemon came second.

As they left the battlefield, the air grew noticeably warmer, though the continuing Blizzard kept it from feeling comfortable.

Noland had a solution. He called out his Magmar and had it use Sunny Day. The storm soon dispersed, clear weather returned, and warm sunlight fell across the Factory again.

While Ethan and the others rested, Noland and Sergio gathered a large group of Fire-type Pokemon to clear the field. The Pokemon melted the snow and ice quickly. Articuno's recovery would take longer.

The Factory had its own treatment equipment, so they did not need a Pokemon Center. But wounds and spent strength could not be healed instantly.

Ash could barely sit still. He had already decided which Pokemon would face Articuno, and waiting only made him more restless. The others watched him pace the lounge with amusement.

Seriously, Max said, spreading his hands. Aren't you tired? Sit down and rest. At this rate, you'll be worn out before the battle even starts.

Ash wanted to sit, but his excitement would not let him.

From the sofa, Ethan asked, though he thought he knew the answer, Who are you planning to use?

Everyone looked at Ash. He grinned and held up a Poke Ball.

This guy, of course. I had it sent over from Liza especially for this match!

May and Max did not know which Pokemon he meant. Brock nodded. I see. With its type and its strength, that's probably your best choice.

Max was puzzled, but he had a more pressing question. He edged toward Ethan.

Um, Mr. Vale... could I spend a little time with your Articuno?

So that was why Max had kept glancing at him. Seeing Ethan's Articuno had made the boy eager to meet it. Ethan laughed.

Of course. It can take you for a flight, if you like. Just keep yourself warm.

He took out the Ultra Ball marked with a snowflake and released Articuno. Blue light flashed, and the lounge grew colder at once. Goosebumps rose on everyone's exposed skin.

No one paid the chill much attention. They were too busy admiring the beautiful blue bird. At such close range, the lights of the lounge seemed to give its feathers a faint glow.

Even Ash, who had met and befriended many Legendary Pokemon, felt a thrill. Those had been wild Pokemon. Ethan had actually caught this one. Ash envied him, though he did not begrudge him the achievement.

Ethan gave Articuno a few instructions and helped Max onto its back. Pikachu leaped nimbly into Max's lap. At Ethan's word, Articuno flew out through an open window and climbed into the blue sky.

It was not an especially large Articuno, but a small boy and Pikachu were easy for it to carry.

May and Ash hurried outside. By the time they reached the grass, Articuno had vanished into the clouds.

That Pikachu, Ash said, shaking his head with affectionate exasperation. It went off to have fun and left me behind!

Brock joined them. They talked on the lawn for perhaps fifteen minutes before Max's jubilant shouts announced Articuno's return. It emerged from the distant clouds and landed gently before Ethan. Max and Pikachu hopped down, both grinning.

How was it? Ethan asked.

Amazing! Max said. Articuno flies so fast! It took us through the clouds and over a lake and a forest, but the ride was smooth the whole time. Right, Pikachu?

Pika!

The only thing... Max scratched his head. My backside got a little cold.

Everyone laughed.

By afternoon, with the Factory's Pokemon helping, the battlefield was fully restored. Noland's Articuno had healed and recovered its strength. When Sergio brought the news, Ash's eyes lit up.

My turn at last! I've been waiting forever!

Then make sure you win, Ethan said with a smile. We'll watch you from the stands.

I will! Ash thumped his chest. I'll beat it!

The field looked as though the morning's blizzard had never happened. The Fire-type Pokemon had even dried the water left by the melting ice. Their work was impressive.

Noland was waiting on his Trainer's platform. He folded his arms as Ash approached. Come on, Ash! Show me what you can do!

At Noland's call, Articuno appeared again and settled on the field. The roof remained open for its flight. Time had passed, and though it was still day, the sun was sinking westward.

Ash took out his Poke Ball. I'm counting on you. Go, Charizard!

Charizard emerged with a roar and fixed a fierce gaze on Articuno. Ash had brought it from Liza at Charicific Valley specifically for this battle.

Ethan and Brock studied it at once. Charizard looks well, Brock said. Stronger, too. It must have trained hard in the valley. I wonder how much it has improved.

Ethan agreed. He thought of his own Charizard, which was also training there. He had kept in touch with Liza by occasional messages every few weeks and knew a little of the valley's hierarchy.

A wild Charizard currently held the top position. Ethan's was preparing to challenge it. Ash's belonged to the tier below. Ethan's Charizard had arrived stronger and trained just as diligently. Seeing the power Ash's now carried made Ethan still more eager to visit Charicific Valley. How far had his own partner come? Surely it was stronger than Ash's by now.

While Ash and Noland spoke, Ethan and the others joined Scott in the stands. May and Max cupped their hands around their mouths and cheered for Ash.

Charizard and Articuno faced each other across the field.

Articuno had already lost once today. Its opponent then had been another Pokemon of its own standing, but a defeat was a defeat. Its Legendary pride would not accept a second loss.

Ash and Charizard had reasons they could not afford to lose either. Charizard had trained for a long time in the valley, and its Fire type gave it the advantage. Ethan had beaten Articuno already. Ash would not let himself fall here while chasing the Trainer he looked up to.

Sergio signaled the start. As in Ethan's match, both Pokemon took flight at once, rising out of the open-roofed arena.

Ash struck first. Charizard, Flamethrower!

Charizard turned in midair and sent a stream of blazing fire toward Articuno. Noland had expected a Fire attack and ordered Ice Beam in response. He had underestimated the strength of Charizard's flames.

The moment the moves met, the heat overwhelmed and melted the icy beam. The fire continued on and struck Articuno, driving it down into the ground amid a cloud of dust.

Even a Legendary Pokemon needed a moment to recover from a Fire-type attack.

Well done, Charizard! Ash's eyes shone. Just as I expected! You can stand up to Articuno!

The spectators wore different expressions, but they were thinking the same thing: Ash was getting ahead of himself again.

One successful attack did not settle a battle that had barely begun. Articuno rose and charged. Ash tried Flamethrower again, but Articuno used Agility. Its speed surged, and it dodged the flames easily.

Then it approached Charizard from another direction and used Mist. A dense cloud enveloped them both.

The spectators could not see inside. A heavy impact sounded, and Charizard shot out of the fog and crashed to the ground.

Charizard! Ash cried, clenching his fists.

It was the very tactic Ethan had used against Noland earlier. Ash had watched that match and ought to have been ready for it, yet Noland had caught him by surprise.

Fortunately, Charizard had been knocked down rather than badly hurt. It shook its head and got back to its feet.

Articuno dived again. Ash ordered Charizard to use Dragon Breath repeatedly to keep it back. Blue-green energy streamed from Charizard's mouth. With Agility's added speed, Articuno avoided the first attacks.

But Charizard had traveled and fought for years, then trained for a long time in Charicific Valley. It did not panic when Articuno evaded it. Several breaths forced Articuno toward one position. Charizard then fired a faster, stronger Dragon Breath straight into its belly.

Chapter 816: A Bright Future Ahead

Dragon Breath struck Articuno, sending it falling from the sky. Ash quickly ordered Charizard to close in and grab it. Articuno recovered just as Charizard reached it, turning sharply away from both claws.

Ash had not expected that. Articuno had only just taken a direct hit, yet it had already regained control. Watching Ethan's match had not shown him how tough a Legendary Pokemon truly was. He had to battle one himself to feel its extraordinary endurance. There was a reason Ethan's Articuno had needed so long to defeat it.

While Ash was still surprised, Noland called a counterattack. Ice Beam struck Charizard. The Fire-type weathered it and flew at Articuno again.

This time Articuno dodged Charizard's Flamethrower, closed the distance, and hit it with Steel Wing. Charizard could not shrug that blow off as it had Ice Beam. It plunged from the sky and struck the ground hard.

Max frowned. Why does it suddenly look like Charizard can't beat Articuno?

It can, Ethan said, shaking his head. Noland has worked out Ash's pattern. He's relied on Flamethrower since the start. He also tried to set up Seismic Toss, but he couldn't land it. If Ash keeps counting on Charizard's type advantage without changing his approach, the match will get harder for him.

So he's in danger?

He is, Ethan said with a small smile. But he's Ash. Charizard has the favorable type and plenty of strength. This is a setback, and he'll find another way. Let's watch.

They trusted Ethan's judgment, but Ash would have to change the fight himself. Noland gave him little time.

Charizard had barely risen when Articuno flew overhead. At Noland's command, Water-type energy gathered in its beak. A large sphere of water shot toward Charizard.

Ethan recognized Water Pulse. Water and ice were closely related, but an Ice-type Pokemon without Water typing could not normally use Water attacks unless it had learned them. No one had expected Articuno to know this move, much less keep it hidden until now.

It caught Ash off guard. Charizard could not dodge. The Water Pulse struck it squarely, turning the type advantage against him and paying back the earlier Fire attack.

Ash's early confidence had vanished. He watched Charizard with a tight frown.

This is bad, Brock said. I didn't know Articuno had a Water move. Ash will have to be more careful about getting close.

Noland kept a good surprise in reserve, Ethan said. If he'd used Water Pulse against my Articuno, Ash would have known to expect it. He waited until Charizard was already struggling, then struck hard. For someone who acts so rugged, he's a careful tactician.

Max and the others began to see why Noland was a Frontier Brain. Against Ethan, he had appeared outmatched. That did not make him weak. Ash could lose if he gave Noland an opening.

On the field, Charizard was badly hurt. Its body showed the damage from Water Pulse, but it could still fight.

Noland pressed his advantage. Ash ordered Charizard back into the air to avoid the next attack. The roles had reversed. Ash often seemed to suffer most when he began with a favorable type matchup. He did sometimes win such battles, but rarely without putting everyone through a scare.

Charizard tried to keep its distance. One lapse let Articuno catch it in a combination of Ice Beam and Water Pulse. Shards of ice struck across its body. Charizard raised its wings in time to block the worst of them.

Ash... May, Max, and Brock watched anxiously.
