Max was about to ask Ethan what Ash could do when the scene stirred a memory. Hadn't he watched Ash face a similar reversal at the Ever Grande Conference? Ash had escaped that trouble in the end. Max kept his question to himself and waited.

Charizard's wings had been frostbitten. Its movements slowed. Noland ordered Articuno to repeat the attack.

Ice Beam came first, then Water Pulse. The moves met in the air, creating a spray of hard ice that shot at Charizard.

Ash called for Flamethrower, but the fire could not melt the flying shards quickly enough. They passed through the flames and battered Charizard. It staggered in midair, nearly falling again.

Noland saw his chance to end the match. Articuno, let's finish this! Climb fast and get above Charizard!

Articuno accelerated upward. Noland thought victory was close. Ash, who had been waiting for an opening, moved at last.

Charizard, get above Articuno! Use Overheat!

Charizard's body blazed red. Heat surged through its frost-stiffened wings, restoring their movement. Like a great ball of fire, it climbed rapidly past Articuno and took the higher position.

It must have learned Overheat during its training in Charicific Valley. Ash had kept the move back for a reason. Overheat was enormously powerful, but the effort sharply reduced the user's special attacking strength afterward. Repeated use made each later attack weaker. Its timing mattered. It was best used to win in one stroke.

Ash had judged that the match had reached that point. Noland saw his intention. He smiled and met the challenge rather than retreating.

Charizard attacked from above with Overheat. Articuno rose to meet it with Water Pulse. A blazing column of fire and a dense water sphere collided. Light flashed, steam erupted, and an explosion shook the air.

Water Pulse could not match Overheat's raw power. But Water had the advantage against Fire, making the clash far less straightforward than their strength alone suggested.

Ash watched for the outcome and missed Noland's small smile. Articuno shot out of the steam, its wings gleaming with Steel-type energy. It slashed Charizard heavily as it passed.

Charizard was near its limit. Steel Wing had not knocked it out, but Articuno turned for another pass, both wings shining again.

Everyone could see Noland meant this to be the last blow. With so little strength left, Charizard would fall if it landed. Ash had spent his hidden move. He could only call, Block it!

He was putting his trust in Charizard. Hurt, exhausted, and forced onto the defensive, it seemed moments from defeat.

But Charizard had once surpassed even Pikachu as Ash's unquestioned ace. It had defeated one of Ethan's Pokemon at the Silver Conference. It had earned that reputation.

As Articuno came in, Charizard raised both claws and caught its wings by sheer force. It stopped the Steel Wing attack.

Noland had not expected that. Ash's eyes lit up.

Now! Seismic Toss!

Charizard held Articuno fast. Drawing on its last reserves, it carried the bird into a spiraling dive. They fell faster and faster, straight toward the ground.

Boom!

They struck in an instant. Dust burst across the field, and the impact shook the spectator area. Max and the others grabbed the railing, but none took their eyes from the settling cloud.

When the dust cleared, Charizard lay motionless. Articuno was struggling to its feet.

What? Max cried. Ash lost? But that move

The result seemed impossible. Then, before he could finish, Articuno collapsed. Charizard slowly pushed itself upright.

It... Max stared.

Charizard looked down at the unconscious Articuno and roared toward the sky, proclaiming its victory over a Legendary Pokemon.

We did it! Ash and Pikachu jumped with joy before Sergio had even called the result.

Ash had defeated Articuno. He had scarcely dared imagine accomplishing that before. This victory showed how far he had grown from the inexperienced boy he had once been.

Sergio announced the outcome and took Articuno for treatment. He and Noland exchanged a rueful look. Noland went to meet Ash as Ethan and the others came down from the stands.

My first day battling with Articuno, and I've lost twice, Noland said with a sigh. You're both stronger than I expected.

Ethan's Articuno had beaten his more comfortably, as one might expect of a three-region champion. Ash surprised him most. The boy had enjoyed a type advantage, but defeating a Legendary Pokemon one-on-one was still a remarkable feat.

Noland accepted both losses without complaint. These two Trainers had bright futures ahead of them.

Chapter 817: A Few Words May Will Remember

After the three of them exchanged a few compliments, Sergio returned. Noland took two badges from the gift box he carried and handed one each to Ethan and Ash.

Please accept these. They're Knowledge Symbols, proof that you defeated me.

Ethan and Ash thanked him and took their Symbols.

Like the two Ethan had already collected, each was made of solid gold. It was a little larger than a bottle cap and heavier than it looked, with three diamond shapes stamped into its gleaming face.

Ethan already had two Symbols and remained calm. This was Ash's first, won against an exceptionally strong opponent. He could hardly contain his excitement. He held it high and struck a victory pose for May and the others.

I got the Knowledge Symbol!

May, Max, Brock, and Scott applauded. They chose to overlook how smug he looked.

Evening had come without anyone noticing. Ethan and Ash had accomplished what they came for, and it was time to leave. Articuno departed first.

Its visible injuries had been treated. After two battles in succession, Noland's Articuno seemed satisfied. Whether it had recovered its strength or not, it nodded to Noland, gave a high cry, and flew into the distant sky.

Articuno was fond of Noland, and the Battle Factory was somewhere it liked to visit. Noland was its friend. But this was not its home. It might return from time to time, yet it would never live here for long.

That was for the best. A wild Pokemon was free. By staying away most of the time, Articuno also made it harder for outsiders to connect it to the Battle Factory and discover where to find it.

Only after it vanished from sight did Ethan and the others say goodbye to Noland, Scott, and Sergio.

Where will you two challenge next? Scott asked.

Ethan and Ash exchanged a look. The nearest Frontier facility for Ash was the Battle Arena. Ethan had already challenged it and would ordinarily go somewhere else. But May's Saffron City Contest was about to begin. Ethan needed to take her there in time.

We're heading to Saffron City, Ethan said.

Saffron City? Scott looked puzzled. Mr. Vale, wasn't the Battle Arena your first challenge? Why go back there?

When Ethan explained that May was entering the Contest, Scott understood.

I see. He smiled at May. If I get the chance, I'll come and cheer for you.

May knew it was a polite offer. She smiled back. Thank you.

It was getting late, so the group said their farewells and set off. Scott and Noland watched them go.

Looks like those two might conquer the whole Battle Frontier, Scott said. As its owner, he could not help feeling moved by the arrival of such powerful challengers.

Noland glanced at him. He had little doubt that Ethan would keep winning, but he had not expected Scott to rate Ash so highly. Beating Articuno proved the boy was strong. Still, Noland was hardly the strongest Frontier Brain. Wasn't it too early to predict that much?

While they spoke, Team Rocket's trio lay bored on the Battle Factory roof, watching Ethan's party disappear into the distance.

Say... James chewed on a blade of grass. Was it really all right for us to lie here the whole time?

Exactly! Jessie complained. Articuno flew away, and the twerp and Pikachu left too. We didn't do a thing! What happened to giving Articuno and Pikachu to the Boss?

You two idiots! Meowth stared at them. How were we supposed to pull anything off with that man around? We have to wait until he and the twerp split up before we make our move, meow!

But... James looked toward the sky. Articuno's already gone. Haven't we missed our chance with it?

Meowth waved that aside. So what? I'd rather do nothing than run into that man, meow!

...

It was nearly dark when they left the Battle Factory, so instead of pushing on, the travelers spent the night at a Pokemon Center. Once Charizard's injuries were healed, Ash sent it back to Liza in Charicific Valley.

Charizard had done what Ash had called it here to do. Its priority now was to continue training in the valley until it could become as strong as Ethan's Charizard. Every extra second away meant another second of training lost. Ash said nothing about that comparison, but he had it in mind.

The night passed quietly. After breakfast the next morning, they resumed their journey to Saffron City.

At Ash's suggestion, they took a mountain route instead of the road they had traveled before. It looked shorter on a map, but it was no real shortcut. The level road would have been faster and easier.

They had already walked those roads many times, though, and repeating the same route would add little to their travels. That was why Ash chose the difficult mountain path. To him, travel was more fun when it tested you.

Ash went wherever the mood took him, with little advance planning. It made his journeys full of surprises and considerably more tiring. Sure enough, they had scarcely entered the mountains when, well before noon, he dropped onto a bare boulder in exhaustion.

Ethan, May, and Max were less tired than he was. It was rare to see someone with Ash's seemingly boundless energy worn out. Perhaps his first Symbol had made him so excited that he had spent too much strength on the climb.

They had no choice but to rest. Mountains stretched all around them, with no trees or other vegetation in sight, only exposed rock.

Ash and the others let out their Pokemon and set up camp with practiced ease. Some looked for firewood and water while the rest arranged the cookware. Everyone knew what to do, leaving Ethan with nothing to prepare. He took charge of watching the Pokemon instead.

Ash's Pikachu, Swellow, Grovyle, Corphish, and Phanpy; May's Combusken, Squirtle, and Munchlax; Brock's Forretress; and Ethan's Eevee gathered together to play. They made a cheerful, noisy crowd.

Ethan finished brushing Eevee's fur with a wooden comb. Then he leaned against a rock and found himself watching May's Munchlax for some time.

May noticed when she returned with water. She handed the bucket to Brock, who was cooking, then sat beside Ethan and looked at Munchlax too.

What is it, Ethan? Is something wrong with my Munchlax?

Of course not. Ethan laughed and shook his head. Seeing it just makes me wonder when I'll catch a Snorlax or Munchlax of my own.

Oh? You like Munchlax too?

I do. They're strong and adorable. Apart from eating and sleeping a lot, what is there to complain about?

May had never realized he liked this sort of Pokemon. In her mind, Ethan's Pokemon were all extraordinarily powerful, while she could hardly imagine describing her Munchlax that way.

That reminds me, Ethan said. Misty told me you'd learned a Pokeblock recipe?

May blushed. Pokeblocks were colorful, square treats made from blended Berries. They could fill a Pokemon's stomach and provide nutrients it needed, rather like vitamins. That sounded excellent in principle. May's Pokeblocks were another matter.

Well... She hesitated, embarrassed. Mine might taste a little off. Munchlax doesn't mind, but the other Pokemon don't seem to like them much.

May was putting it gently. Ethan knew her Pokeblocks were a catastrophe. What she made was painful to behold, with an effect to rival the dreadful meal Misty had once cooked when Brock fell ill during her travels with Ash. May's might even have been worse.

She called her creation May's Delicious, but neither Brock nor Max could stomach it. Every Pokemon the group had with them had taken a single bite and immediately fainted from the taste. That was how potent it was.

Only May's Munchlax, perhaps because it would eat anything, had finished its share and looked quite happy afterward.

May and her friend Misty had more in common than their cooking. Both had also had bicycles damaged by Pikachu. Still, their food did have one admirer. Jessie had tasted both Misty's cooking and May's Pokeblocks and found them delicious.

Jessie had an extraordinary talent of her own. Either her tastes were unique, or she really was a human-shaped Pokemon.

What's wrong with that? Ethan said, choosing not to mention how bad the Pokeblocks truly were. He smiled encouragingly. People improve. How can you succeed without failing along the way? I'm sure more and more Pokemon will come to love your Pokeblocks.

Those few words moved May deeply. She felt that Ethan believed in her, and in her heart she grew closer to him.

After a short rest, they set out again. For Ash and the others, the trip proved unusually smooth, apart from the hard walking. In a little over half a day, they crossed the mountains and a stretch of forest and reached Saffron City.

Ethan's presence was the reason. Team Rocket's trio dared neither approach nor cause trouble. With no one blocking the way, reaching the city was simply a matter of time.

They went straight to the Saffron Contest Hall. It shared the city's name with Saffron Gym, but the two stood in different places.

The Contest Hall occupied the center of a huge park within the city. Broad lawns, leafy woods, and a clear lake made the grounds beautiful and inviting. The hall itself was a grand, domed building.

Before they even entered the park, they saw a huge billboard outside its gates. It advertised this year's Saffron Contest. Several sleek, brightly colored Pokemon with carefully groomed coats posed around a giant Ribbon medal. Against its golden border, the Ribbon shone brilliantly.

A Pokemon Contest... Ash looked from the billboard to May and grinned. It's your turn to show us what you can do!

May smiled with confidence and was about to answer when she caught sight of someone familiar.

Huh? She pointed. Isn't that Drew?

Chapter 818: Are They Twins?

Following May's pointing finger, Ethan and the others turned and saw a familiar figure. It really was Drew.

It is him!

Ash, Max, and Brock had mixed feelings about seeing him. Drew was not exactly a friend, but he was no enemy either. He was a rival with whom they had a peculiar relationship. Apart from their surprise that he had come to compete in Kanto too, they had little to say.

For May, though, the presence of a strong opponent who had beaten her before added a great deal of pressure.

Perhaps Drew heard her voice, or perhaps he simply sensed someone watching. He turned halfway and spotted the group. He made no move to greet them. After searching their faces and failing to find the person he wanted, he frowned and walked away without a word.

May claimed she did not mind, but his arrival weighed on her all the same.

They entered the park and headed for the Contest Hall. Before they reached it, they saw a crowd going inside one after another.

That's strange, May said. The Contest isn't until tomorrow. Why is everyone going in today?

Probably a rehearsal. Ethan gave a lazy yawn. Events this big usually have one. You ought to go take a look.

May thought he was right. She hurried ahead and joined the crowd, while Ethan and the others followed at an easier pace.

Ethan, Ash asked curiously, with a chance like this, don't you want to enter a Contest yourself?

He sounded rather excited. Ethan glanced at him and saw the interest in his eyes. He remembered that Ash really would enter a Contest someday and smiled.

Sounds more like you want to enter. Contests are a whole new stage for me. Maybe I'll try one another day, but I'll pass for now. Ethan patted Ash's shoulder. You, though? I think you'd be a hit. Dress up the way you did before, give Pikachu a nice makeover, and you'd be famous in no time. Right, Ashley?

Even Ash understood that Ethan was teasing him.

Oh, come on! He stood there, punching the air like a Primeape while Ethan walked away laughing. I'm never dressing up as a girl again!

Ash had never wanted to remember how Jessie and James tricked him into dressing as a girl so he could challenge Erika at the Celadon Gym. Ethan's reminder left him mortified.

Max did not know the story, but he recognized an embarrassing secret when he heard one. He also remembered Ash dressing as a woman for the grand ball at Faraway Lake during their Hoenn travels. He pressed Brock for an explanation, then laughed without sparing Ash's feelings.

Ashley! Ashley!

Stop calling me that!

Still bickering, they entered the Contest Hall.

Inside, workers were putting the finishing touches on the venue. Some worked on the stage design, others on the lighting. The Coordinators who had come in were studying the stage amid the bustle, no doubt imagining how they would perform on it tomorrow.

It resembled a vast theater. The facilities were not especially new, but the stage was enormous, with plenty of room for a performance.

They found May in the crowd. She was examining the venue too, perhaps deciding which Pokemon would suit it best. They did not disturb her. Ethan and the others turned toward the stage instead.

A fashionable woman stood at its center, drawing their attention. She wore a sunhat, a blue midriff-baring top, a short skirt, and white stockings. Her dark blond hair fell in broad waves. She was quite pretty, and the beauty mark beneath one eye looked particularly familiar.

Huh? Max said. Doesn't she look like the woman who hosted the Hoenn Contests? What's she doing here?

Ash scratched his cheek. I think her name was... was...

Vivian! Brock supplied at once, then frowned. But something's different. She's every bit as beautiful as Vivian, and they look almost identical. Vivian's beauty mark is under her left eye, though, while this woman's is under her right. Their clothes and the way they carry themselves are different too. Could they be twins?

Ethan drew a sharp breath. Brock's eye for women was frightening. One glance, and he had guessed the truth.

The woman was not Vivian, who was still in Hoenn. She was Vivian's younger twin sister, Lilian. Ethan knew that because he had watched the anime. Brock had worked it out by observation alone. Then again, he was the man who could tell one Nurse Joy or Officer Jenny from another. Perhaps he never forgot a pretty woman he had met.

The stage lights converged on Lilian. At the director's signal, she took out a Poke Ball and released an Espeon to begin the rehearsal.

Espeon performed move after move. Its graceful motions and dazzling techniques captured everyone's attention. Its fine bearing and flawless execution showed how carefully it had been trained. A woman trusted to judge performances clearly knew what she was doing.

Then something unexpected happened.

May must have lost track of her Pokemon, or perhaps it had been drawn in by the show. Her Squirtle slipped away, ran straight onto the stage, and sent bubbles floating everywhere.

May rushed after it in alarm. Ethan and the others hurried over too, afraid something might go wrong. Squirtle had already interrupted the performance. Fortunately this was only a rehearsal; in the actual Contest, the consequences could have been much worse.

May knew it. She jumped onto the stage, anxious to retrieve Squirtle. Before she could reach it, Lilian picked it up.

You can't do that, Squirtle. Lilian smiled gently at it, then handed it to May. You're welcome to look around, but you can't let your Pokemon run onto the stage.

Up close, her voice sounded quite different from Vivian's. Lilian spoke more steadily, as suited her manner, while her older sister was much more lively onstage.

I'm so sorry, May said. This is its first trip away from home. I should have kept a closer eye on it.

Squirtle was unhappy in May's arms. It squirmed and struggled to get free. Lilian noticed, crouched down, and smiled at it.

Your Squirtle seems full of enthusiasm, and it clearly likes the stage. Why not let it give a proper performance here tomorrow?

Lilian was easy to approach. Rather than getting angry over the interruption, she patiently encouraged Squirtle. That generosity put her ahead of many others in her profession.

It's a little too soon for that. May smiled awkwardly. I've only had Squirtle for a few days. It needs to practice before it goes onstage. I'm sorry we interrupted your rehearsal, Miss Vivian. We'll get out of your way.

Vivian? Lilian stopped short.

May grew uncertain at her reaction. You are Miss Vivian, aren't you? You hosted the Contests in Hoenn. We met several times there! Don't you remember me? I'm May, from Petalburg City.

Oh, I see! Lilian smiled in understanding. The Vivian you mean is my older sister. I'm her younger sister.

May had been apart from Ethan and the others when they noticed the resemblance. Only now did she learn that the woman who looked so much like Vivian was her twin.

Seeing May's astonishment, Lilian sighed. I suppose someone from Hoenn would confuse us. She's my sister, but really, dressing in those frilly, puffy dresses at her age? She's trying far too hard to look young. I have much better taste in clothes and style. Her tone brightened. I haven't introduced myself! I'm Lilian, the host of the Kanto Pokemon Contests. It's a pleasure to meet you!

It sounded as though Lilian and Vivian did not get along especially well. That was their business. Lilian still had work to do, so after greeting May, she returned to the rehearsal.

May inspected the stage and learned the rules and precautions from the staff. Then she and the others left the hall for the Pokemon Center beside it in the park.

May, Ash, Max, and Brock would stay there tonight and wait for tomorrow's Contest. Ethan, however, had a better place in mind.

After seeing them into the Pokemon Center lobby, he waved. I'll be going. I'll see you before the Contest starts tomorrow. May, I'm looking forward to your performance.

I know, May said. I'll do my best!

Ethan walked away without looking back. Ash scratched his head and turned to May. Where's Ethan going? Aren't you traveling together? Isn't he going to help you practice?

Probably to see Sabrina, May said. She was not concerned that Ethan would miss her training. Letting her watch his battles up close had already taught her a great deal. Choosing her Pokemon, planning her style, and deciding how to perform were things she needed to do for herself. Ethan could not make those choices for her. Max, Ash, and Brock were plenty of company.

Besides, May understood the nature of Ethan and Sabrina's relationship. She had no intention of getting in the way of their reunion.

Ash was briefly surprised, then nodded. He had witnessed Ethan's complicated relationships with Sabrina and Erika. He understood little about romance, but he knew both women were Ethan's partners. Of course Ethan could go to see either of them.

Brock alone watched Ethan disappear and shed tears of envy. Ethan's luck in love was something he could never hope to match.

May had guessed correctly. Ethan was going to meet Sabrina. This was his last stop in Saffron City before leaving Kanto again. He had only one more chance to spend time with her; who knew how long it would be before he returned? Even if tonight left him tired, it would be worth it.

He did not boldly stay at the Saffron Gym this time. It was too conspicuous. Coming and going there so often would draw attention, to say nothing of Sabrina's father being there to interrupt them.

Ethan called Sabrina and invited her out. They browsed a nearby mall, watched a movie, and finished with a romantic candlelit dinner. Then they went to a hotel for couples and spent a wonderful night together.

There was no need to recount all the intimacy and exertion that followed. When Ethan rejoined May and the others at the contestants' dormitory the next morning, everyone could see both happiness and fatigue on his face.

Chapter 819: You've Heard of Me?

Ethan arrived with time to spare before the Contest. He could ask May and the others how things were going.

How are your preparations?

He looked at May. She showed little sign of nerves. Her travels through Hoenn had helped her grow. She was nothing like the girl who had entered her first Slateport Contest. Travel really did teach people a great deal.

Everything's ready, May said with an easy smile. I still feel I could have done more, but I'll show everyone the best I can do.

Confidence is a good thing. Give it your best.

Ash suddenly spoke up. Ethan, guess who we saw yesterday.

It was surely someone Ethan knew, but he had no clue who. He saw no point in wasting effort guessing. Who?

Ash was poor at keeping a secret anyway. Harley!

He's come to Kanto too? Ethan was not especially surprised. As he recalled from the anime, Harley had appeared in Kanto. First Drew yesterday, and now Harley. What's drawing all these people from Hoenn here? Did he say anything?

Not much, Ash said. But he's helping out at the Pokemon Center.

Helping? Ethan seemed indifferent, though he asked, Does he work here?

Max answered. He said Nurse Joy helped him before, and he's ashamed of his past. That's why he's helping here. He said he wants to take a new step forward.

He's talking nonsense, Ethan said with a snort. He hasn't changed. Don't believe him, at least not yet.

Really? Ash hesitated. Yesterday he told us the Kanto Contest rules are different from Hoenn's, and Nurse Joy confirmed it. She said he's been working hard here, too.

So? He told you the truth about that. It doesn't mean he's kindhearted or has turned over a new leaf. He can give you a little piece of common knowledge to earn your trust, then use it for whatever he's planning.

Ash trusted Ethan far more than he trusted Harley. He knew Ethan would not lie to him and accepted his judgment without reservation. So we need to watch out for Harley?

Don't worry. He's on my blacklist. I'll stay with May, and whatever scheme he tries, it won't work.

May, Ash, and the others relaxed once Ethan promised to step in. May was particularly touched that he would protect her. To them, Ethan was the strongest person they knew. Harley would get nowhere against him, even if he brought several accomplices. Nor would his tricks fool Ethan.

By the way, Ethan asked May, have you registered yet?

I was just about to go over and do it.

Just about to? Ethan raised an eyebrow and glanced at the clock. It's after eight already. Doesn't registration close soon?

No, it closes at eleven. We have hours left.

Eleven? Ethan frowned. Isn't that when the Contest starts? Why would registration close at the exact moment it begins? Where did you hear that?

Harley told us, Ash said. Then realization struck. Wait. You mean he lied to us?

Honestly... Ethan sighed at them. How many times will you let him fool you? There's a whole group of you, and no one thought to check? Why would you take his word for something like that? You're even more gullible than Team Rocket.

His words were harsh, and they flushed with embarrassment. Brock felt it especially keenly. He was the oldest and usually the steadiest, yet he had been there for all of it and still let Harley deceive them again.

Seeing their uneasy faces, Ethan shook his head. I'm not trying to blame you. Just be more careful with someone like Harley. We can talk about it later. Let's go register.

May and the others realized that was urgent. They hurried out of the Pokemon Center toward the Saffron Contest registration desk. A little more than ten minutes later, they arrived breathless.

The registration hall was empty except for one staff member behind the counter. May's heart sank. She stepped forward quickly, handed over her Contest pass, and asked about the deadline.

Registration closes at ten. You still have more than an hour, the staff member said with a smile. Then she returned May's pass apologetically. But this pass is for Hoenn. It can't be used here. Please exchange it as soon as you can.

What?

May had feared a problem with the deadline, but she had never imagined her pass would be invalid too. She was at a loss. Ethan spoke patiently with the staff member and learned that a Kanto pass could be issued at the Pokemon Center.

It was a simple fix, but it meant another round trip. They hurried back to the Center, exchanged May's pass, and returned. This time her registration went through.

When they finished, it was already nine fifteen. There was still some time, though far less than they had thought.

If Ethan had not urged them to come early, they would have trusted Harley's eleven o'clock deadline and missed the Contest entirely. Harley had not changed at all. His diligent work for Nurse Joy had only been a way to fool May again.

Harley's awful! Ash punched the air. He lied to us! I won't let him off next time I see him.

As though summoned by the words, Harley walked through the registration hall doors, humming a tune. He had registered already and had no reason to return. But after misleading May yesterday, he wanted to see her face when she failed to enter. He had timed his visit for that.

Instead, he found May standing by the counter. His expression changed at once. Hadn't he told her registration closed at eleven? Why was she here so early?

His eyes fell on the man beside her. Realizing Ethan might be responsible, Harley glared with deep resentment. The last person he wanted to meet had appeared after all. Ever since losing their previous match, he had tried to avoid Ethan. Now they were face to face again, and Ethan looked more confident than ever. Harley's envy only deepened.

Then Ethan spoke, nearly making him choke with anger.

Well, if it isn't the man I beat. Come to finish the battle we left unfinished last time? Ethan asked with a smile.

Harley's face darkened. He was about to answer with something sharp when May, Ash, and Max marched up to confront him.

You actually dared show your face here? You liar!

Wait... Though they had caught him, Harley spread his hands and feigned confusion. What are you talking about? Why would I lie to you?

You're still denying it? Max demanded. You deliberately told us the wrong registration deadline! And you said May's pass would be fine!

Harley's mind raced. Did I? Then I must have remembered wrong. Please believe me. This wasn't my fault...

He kept explaining, but May and the others no longer believed him. Still, as long as he insisted it was an honest mistake, Ash and the rest had no way to prove otherwise. They glared at him and left the registration hall.

Once they were gone, Harley's face darkened again. He had not expected May to escape his trap. His plan was ruined, and the same trick would be harder to use in the future.

Damn it. It was all that man's fault. Harley cursed Ethan under his breath.

There was no point in staying. He headed for the doors, still lost in thought, and collided with another group entering the hall.

The impact caught him unprepared. He fell hard on his backside, and his distinctive green leaf-shaped hat tumbled to the floor.

You He opened his mouth to shout, but a woman on the other side beat him to it, louder and ruder than he had intended.

What's wrong with you? Watch where you're going!

Harley looked up. The speaker was a purple-haired woman in a long red dress and oversized butterfly glasses. Beside her stood a man dressed like an assistant and a Meowth in a suit and bow tie. What an odd group, dressed so extravagantly.

He studied them as he got to his feet. Are you here for the Contest too?

Of course! The woman lifted her chin and looked down her nose at him. Don't you know who I am? The great and mysterious messenger of love and beauty, the fairy known as Jessibella!

A fairy? Jessibella? Harley had only just come from Hoenn and knew none of Kanto's Coordinators. But she said the name with such confidence that he assumed she must be formidable, perhaps even famous.

His manner changed instantly. So it's you! I've heard so much about you. Even all the way over in Hoenn, your name reached me.

Huh? His answer bewildered Jessibella.

She pulled her two companions aside and whispered where Harley could not hear. What's with him? He's heard of me?

They were, of course, Jessie, James, and Meowth in disguise. They had come so Jessie could indulge her dream of being a Pokemon Coordinator.

I don't know, James said with a frown. Maybe he really thinks you're famous?

How could anyone be that stupid? Meowth said in disbelief. Maybe he's mistaken you for someone else.

Even better! Jessie feared little. Her eyes shone with excitement. He looks like a Coordinator. We can use him.

Are you sure? James hesitated. Won't he figure it out? And doesn't he look familiar? Haven't we met him somewhere?

Jessie was no longer listening. She left James and Meowth and faced Harley with a radiant smile.

How lovely that you know my name. You must be an accomplished Coordinator yourself.

Harley eyed the trio. One moment they had been whispering together; the next they were beaming at him. Something felt off. He dismissed the feeling, having no idea how unreliable the woman before him truly was.

Besides, an ugly plan had already formed in his mind: he could use her to strike at May.

Chapter 820: The Fairy Jessibella

More than accomplished, Harley said with a smile. I placed very highly at the Hoenn Grand Festival!

That was only half true. He had entered the Grand Festival, but he had been eliminated in the top thirty-two. It was hardly a lofty finish. Lying came so naturally to him, however, that nothing in his voice gave him away. He sounded every bit as confident as Jessie, and she and her companions did not doubt him.

Oh? Then you're not bad, Jessie said, surprised that he might be so skilled. She laughed. Still, you've got a long way to go before you can compare with the fairy Jessibella!

Naturally, naturally. Harley rubbed his hands together, all flattery. I heard your name even in Hoenn! You're entering the Saffron Contest too, aren't you?

Of course. Jessie smiled smugly. A little Contest like this is nothing to me. If I enter, first place is as good as mine!

Few people could boast with Jessie's utter certainty. Because she seemed to believe every word, Harley believed her too. The apparent entourage of assistants only strengthened his impression that she was a formidable Coordinator.

How impressive! Let me congratulate you on your victory in advance.

After a dozen more compliments, Jessie was so pleased with herself that she had forgotten the limits of her actual ability. Harley made himself seem humble. Simpleminded Jessie took it as proof that he was captivated by her charm and had become a fan.

Once he had laid the groundwork, Harley raised his real purpose.

Well... He looked troubled. If you wouldn't mind, could you help me with a small problem?

A small problem? Jessie agreed without thinking. Of course! Do you want my autograph?

Harley froze. He nearly said no, but an autograph would make him look more like a genuine fan and help his plan. He forced himself to nod.

Yes, exactly. Though the autograph is only part of it. I really do need Miss Jessibella's help with something.

He searched his pockets for something she could sign. Finding nothing else, he reluctantly handed her his Kanto Contest pass.

Jessie produced a pen from somewhere and scrawled her name across it in large letters. Her handwriting twisted and lurched without the slightest grace. Could a person really write so badly? Was she actually a celebrity?

Harley's eyebrow twitched. He could not say that to her face. He pretended delight and carefully tucked the pass away.

Thank you so much. I'll treasure it!

At least Jessie remembered that he had asked for help. She tossed the pen to James, then turned to Harley with a broad smile. Now, what does the great Jessibella need to do for you?

Excitement glinted in Harley's eyes. He had been waiting for this.

It's simple, he said, trying not to laugh. A nasty little girl has been giving me trouble. She bullies me all the time. If you meet her in the Contest, could you teach her a lesson for me?

A girl in the Contest? Jessie had not expected that request, but she waved it off. Don't worry. That's just the sort of thing we're best at She coughed. I mean, leave it to me!

...

After leaving the registration hall, Ethan and the others went straight to the Saffron Contest Hall to wait with May.

The Contest had not begun, but spectators were already arriving. Within a few minutes, the seats were full. The competitors' waiting room was growing crowded too. It was becoming difficult to talk or do much else there, so Ash, Max, and Brock gave May their last good wishes and went to the stands. Ethan stayed with her.

He had promised to prevent Harley from interfering again. Yet Harley never came near May as the opening drew closer. Neither did Drew, whom they had seen yesterday.

Drew's absence meant little, but Harley's was unusual. Ethan did not believe for a moment that he had given up. Suspecting another scheme, he became more careful. He checked the schedule, May's clothes and props, and even her Poke Balls himself.

Such attentive care moved May. Her gratitude kept growing, though she said nothing and held the feeling quietly in her heart. Some people could change a person's feelings without being noticed. Ethan was more like sunlight: she could see and feel the warmth of everything he did for her.

She watched him go back and forth, checking each detail. Her heart settled, and her last trace of nervousness faded. When Ethan returned, she gave him a big smile.

He looked baffled. What is it? What's making you so happy?

Nothing. May shook her head lightly. I just think you'd be well suited to entering a Pokemon Contest.

Counting Ash, that made two people who had suggested it. Ethan wondered what it was about him that made them say so. Was it only because he had beautiful Pokemon like Articuno and Milotic?

Because I've learned the whole process? he asked with a smile. Trainers and Coordinators have a lot in common, but they're still different paths. I've been a Trainer a long time, and I've achieved a little success. Starting over as a novice Coordinator would feel strange.

May understood his meaning. As a champion, he was reluctant to enter a Contest as a beginner. Pokemon Contests were not decided solely by battling strength. Judges made subjective calls, which brought uncertainty. Winning would be wonderful, but losing might embarrass him.

May thought he was worrying too much. Performances and battles were different things. A loss in one did not diminish what he had achieved in the other. Yet she only smiled sweetly and did not press him. Ethan had his own reasons. If he did not want to enter, she would not bring it up again.

There was nothing wrong with concentrating on battles, either. He could give that path his full attention and climb still higher.

As they talked, the Saffron Contest began. Like the other competitors in the waiting room, Ethan and May turned to the large screen on the wall.

Brilliant lights swept the stage. Lilian, the host they had met yesterday, stepped into the spotlight and took command of the hall.

She waved to the audience and spoke over lively music. It's showtime! Pokemon and Coordinators are here to mix love and dreams into one spectacular performance! Let's bring the Saffron Contest to life! I'm your host, Lilian. Come along and enjoy it with me!

Under the spotlights, Lilian looked even more dazzling than she had the day before. Her youthful energy and lovely face caught everyone's attention.

A wave of cheers rose from the stands. The audience seemed eager for this rare Saffron Contest.

The camera operator thoughtfully swept the crowd, showing their reactions on the screen. By coincidence, Ethan spotted Brock the moment the camera passed him. He stood out like a firefly in the dark.

Brock was not making his usual extravagant gestures or staring with hearts in his eyes. Even so, his lovestruck, fidgeting manner set him apart from the people around him.

I feel like... May scratched her cheek awkwardly. Brock is being a little...

Embarrassing? Ethan laughed. I agree. Falling for someone so openly, no matter where he is, takes a confidence I could never match. Though I have to admit, his taste is good.

They were only joking, not trying to hurt Brock. They would have said the same thing to his face. That was the ease of traveling together.

Lilian introduced the Contest's prize: a gleaming Saffron Ribbon. Its elaborate shape resembled a shield topped with a crown. Every competitor looked at it longingly. The Ribbon was an honor and a ticket to a greater stage.

Once she had explained the rules, Lilian introduced the judges. Ethan might have expected a different panel now that the stage had moved from Hoenn to Kanto. Instead, he recognized every face.

There was Mr. Contesta, head of the Pokemon Contest Committee; Mr. Sukizo, president of the Pokemon Fan Club; and Nurse Joy.

This Nurse Joy might be from Saffron rather than Hoenn. Brock was probably the only one who could tell which Joy she was.

Seeing familiar judges eased May's mind. She knew Contesta's and Sukizo's preferences after so many Contests and could plan her performance accordingly. A new panel would have been harder to read.

There was a drawback too. Familiar judges made competitors less nervous, but those judges had seen their acts many times. Without something striking or original, it would be harder to earn a high score. Familiarity cut both ways.

After introducing all three, Lilian stirred the audience into another round of cheers. The first round of judging finally began.

To Ethan's surprise, Harley was the first performer.

So that's why he wasn't in the waiting room, Ethan said, shaking his head. He didn't have time to make trouble.

Harley's unusual outfit drew immediate attention and applause as he came onstage. The cheers filled the hall.

The Saffron audience seemed more enthusiastic than those at the Hoenn Contests. Perhaps they simply enjoyed performances more, or perhaps Lilian was particularly good at exciting a crowd. Either way, Harley received a warm welcome as the first act.

At center stage, he released his partner. Even in a new region, he had chosen the same Pokemon: Cacturne.

Harley's character left much to be desired, and he never missed a chance to target May. But he had skill and a clever mind. His stage performances rarely went wrong. Working in step with Cacturne, he gave Kanto's audience a fine show.

For the finale, Cacturne used Needle Arm to pierce the Cotton Spore drifting above the stage. It made a striking finish and earned Harley a very high score in the first round.

Chapter 821: The Saffron Contest

Harley's unexpectedly strong performance put some pressure on May. Pressure could also be a source of motivation. Seeing a rival do so well might draw out her own potential.

Harley had given the Saffron Contest an impressive opening. The other competitors performed in turn, but perhaps his act had shaken their confidence. Most earned relatively low scores.

Ash and the others had never imagined Harley would lead the field. It was only the first round, yet his score made clear that he had come prepared.

Competitors took the stage, performed, and left. As time passed, the atmosphere in the hall grew more excited. Most of the first round was over, and fewer and fewer people remained to perform.

May had drawn the final slot, for better or worse. It gave her more time to prepare, but watching so many other acts could increase her nerves. Fortunately, she had steadied herself, and Ethan was beside her. She felt a little nervous, as anyone would, but it would not affect her performance.

When another competitor left the stage, a purple-haired woman in a red dress and butterfly glasses walked out.

Lilian introduced her as the fairy Jessibella. Ethan recognized her at once: Jessie of Team Rocket. He was briefly surprised that she had entered, then remembered Jessie's nature and found it entirely plausible.

He had no intention of stopping her. He liked Team Rocket's trio well enough. He could enjoy the spectacle and see what Jessie had planned.

Jessie released a Pokemon to begin her act. It was not one of her own, but James's Cacnea.

James had caught Cacnea in a forest near Rustboro City in Hoenn. It had traveled with the trio for a long time. Less than half a meter tall, it resembled a round cactus or a green jack-o'-lantern. A golden flower like a crown sat on its head. It had thick arms and a body covered in spines. Its silly appearance did not suggest great power, but it evolved into Cacturne, Harley's signature Pokemon.

Ethan did not know the species especially well. Still, one look at Cacnea's shape gave him an idea of its abilities.

Jessie and Cacnea faced one another. The audience waited to see what dazzling move they would perform. Then the two ran together and embraced.

The crowd stared. That was it? It was such a simple action. And Cacnea's spines looked sharp, yet Jessie had hugged it without hesitation, taking every prick. It was an unprecedented sort of performance. People winced in sympathy and wondered what she meant by it.

Lilian suddenly cried out, tears streaming down her face. How moving! This is love! Love and peace! Their bittersweet embrace has touched our hearts!

With that explanation, the spectators realized the hug might carry a depth of feeling they had missed. They supplied their own interpretations, and soon many were in tears like Lilian. A spotlight fell on Jessie and Cacnea, adding to the mood.

Even May, Ash, and the others seemed to feel the bond between person and Pokemon. They clenched their fists, moved by the scene.

Ethan might have been the only person in the hall who remained expressionless. Wasn't Jessie simply stuck on Cacnea's spines? How had everyone imagined so much more? Even the three judges were smiling and applauding.

He could not understand it. Lilian, Contesta, Sukizo, and Nurse Joy were all professionals. Surely they could see the predicament Jessie was in. Why were they responding this way?

Then Ethan saw what he had been missing, and why he had resisted the idea of entering a Contest himself. He approached things rationally. That served him well in Pokemon battles: he exposed few weaknesses, spotted his opponent's quickly, and used them to win.

A Contest demanded something more emotional. A Coordinator and Pokemon could create beauty together, an elusive feeling visible onstage but hard to put into words. That was what Ethan lacked. Perhaps the judges, Lilian, the crowd, and even May and Ash had genuinely felt something in Jessie's awkward, motionless act.

Jessie's accidental performance had succeeded beyond anyone's expectations. Was she a rare natural talent after all?

Her act was not finished. Whether she had grown used to the spines or was simply enduring them, she moved to the next part.

Still embracing Jessie, Cacnea used Pin Missile. It guided the sharp needles into the air, where they collided and burst. Hot, rainbow-colored light showered down like stars, surrounding Jessie and Cacnea. For a moment, Jessie really did look like the fairy whose name she had taken.

Gasps rose from the stands.

Amazing... May murmured beside Ethan. She studied the screen. Looks like Harley isn't the only difficult opponent. This woman is one too.

Ethan said nothing. May had not recognized Jessibella at all. She genuinely believed Jessie was a formidable Coordinator. Ethan hesitated, then decided not to tell her the truth. Given Team Rocket's usual standards, they would eventually reveal themselves without his help. For now, the extra pressure might bring out more of May's potential.

Jessie earned an extremely high score for her first-round performance. It was even higher than Harley's, putting her in first place.

Ethan looked up at the ceiling. The result surprised him, yet somehow it made sense. When Jessie took something seriously, she really could be impressive.

There was one small incident as she left. After being pierced by Cacnea's spines twice at close range, Jessie could not move at all. Lilian called for the medical staff, who carried her off on a stretcher.

That did nothing to change her score. If anything, the spectators saw it as further proof of her dedication, and their applause grew louder.

After Jessie, it was finally time for the last competitor in the first round: May.

Good luck, Ethan told her in the waiting room. I know you can do it. Just show them what you've practiced.

Don't worry. I'll do my best!

May gave him a sweet smile, rose, put aside her doubts, and walked steadily down the competitors' passage. Soon she appeared onstage.

Seeing her relaxed, confident face on the screen, Ethan focused on the performance ahead. In truth, he knew surprisingly little about his own traveling companion's plans. He did not even know which Pokemon she would use or how she had arranged her act. Leaving her to go on a date the night before the Contest had hardly made him a reliable companion.

But he and Sabrina rarely had time together. When she was so close, how could he avoid seeing her? He would have to make up for neglecting May during their later travels.

May had not complained in the slightest. That only made Ethan feel more guilty. It was why he had been so attentive to every detail earlier.

Lilian briefly introduced May and her Contest record. Then May's performance began.

Squirtle had come onstage with her, but May did not risk an untested act in the first round. She threw a Poke Ball and sent out Combusken.

She plainly wanted Squirtle to grow comfortable with Contest performances, even though it would not perform today. Ethan was struck again by how much May had grown.

Combusken spun and landed steadily at center stage. May pulled off her bandanna and tossed it into the air. Combusken used Fire Spin, followed by Sky Uppercut. The rising heat carried the bandanna high. Combusken leaped into the flames, sprang upward, and struck the spread-out cloth with another Sky Uppercut, sending it neatly back onto May's head.

May and Combusken jumped together to the center of the stage and finished with a graceful bow. The act was over.

Ethan rubbed his chin. It had shown Combusken's speed, skill, and strength, but it was more exciting than beautiful. The overall effect felt a little plain.

Combusken was a Fire and Fighting Pokemon. May had chosen a cool, energetic style rather than a delicate one. Still, Ethan could sense Ash's influence in her act. There was nothing inherently wrong with it, but a performance built only on impressive moves could struggle to earn top marks. It might also limit May's growth as a Coordinator.

Even so, the audience enjoyed it, and the judges gave her a respectable score. Ethan estimated that she was above most of the field. She should make the next round.

Moments after her performance, the screen announced the eight competitors who had advanced. May had made it in seventh place, safely above the cutoff. Jessie and Harley had taken the top two spots and advanced as well.

For May, seventh was progress. At least she had no longer qualified in last place; she had climbed a rung. The eliminated competitors had to accept their disappointment. Those who advanced had little time to celebrate before their next matches.

As in Hoenn, the second round was a series of Contest Battles. But Kanto had one important rule difference: competitors could use different Pokemon for the performance and battle rounds. One Pokemon could specialize in stage appeals while another focused on combat, improving both displays and making the battles more intense. The audience welcomed that prospect.

Shall we keep going? Lilian returned to the center of the stage with a bright smile and pointed toward the screen. First, let's see the opening matchups for the second round!

Chapter 822: How Far May Has Come

The matchups for the eight remaining competitors appeared on the screen. Ethan immediately found May's name.

The draw had put her in the first battle, and her opponent was Harley. What a twist of fate. Harley had placed second in the performance round, while May had placed next to last among the qualifiers. On paper, the pairing favored him.

But Ethan, Ash, and the others did not consider May the weaker of the two. They were confident she would win. Facing Harley early had its advantages: she could send him home and be rid of him. For Harley, it was a chance for revenge.

He hated both Ethan and May and wanted them out of his way. He would have liked to save his confrontation with May for later, but defeating her now would keep him happy for days. Both Coordinators were determined to teach the other a lesson.

Ethan paid little attention to the other matchups, Jessie's included. He saw no other competitor as dangerous as Harley. If May beat him, she would likely win the Saffron Contest. This match might decide everything.

After a short break, the second round began. Before the expectant crowd, May and Harley returned to the stage.

Lilian explained the rules. You have five minutes. Show off your Pokemon's moves beautifully while reducing your opponent's score. That's the key to victory! Both Coordinators are ready, so let's see what they'll do in our first battle!

The five-minute countdown started. May and Harley released their Pokemon at the same moment.

To Ethan's surprise, May chose Squirtle, which she had caught only recently. It was a risk. But unlike the appeal round, this battle did not require a precisely rehearsed routine with its Trainer. Squirtle needed to show what it could do. May had also kept it beside her during the earlier performance. Evidently she had considered using it here all along rather than choosing on impulse.

Harley had changed Pokemon too. Instead of Cacturne, he sent out an Ariados. Allowing different partners for the two rounds gave Kanto Coordinators more flexibility than they had in Hoenn and promised a wider range of performances.

Neither Pokemon had even settled into place before Harley ordered an attack. Ariados shot a long strand of silk at the ceiling and swung toward Squirtle. In an instant, it was right in front of Squirtle, using Scary Face.

Startled by Ariados's sudden appearance and its frightening expression, Squirtle rolled backward twice and came to a stop by May's feet.

It had been with May only a short time. Its courage was still developing, and such a reaction was understandable. May did not panic. She encouraged Squirtle back to its feet and ordered Ice Beam.

Ethan had not expected a newly caught Squirtle to know the move. May must have spent considerable effort training it when he was not around. Unfortunately, Squirtle could not yet control that much energy freely. The force of its own Ice Beam sent it flying backward. Off balance, it fired far past Ariados.

Harley laughed at the attempt, but he did not waste his opening. Ariados used Spider Web to bind Squirtle and haul it toward the ceiling.

Wrapped tight like prey, Squirtle could only squirm as Ariados drew it closer. The spider's threatening presence made it more frightened. No blow had landed, yet Squirtle's Contest score dropped on the screen. A Contest Battle measured more than physical damage.

Whether Harley wanted to humiliate May or show off, he delayed his next attack. He had Ariados spray silk all around the stage, building a huge web. Then Ariados tossed Squirtle onto it like a ball of yarn, pulled it up, and tossed it again. It repeated the game several times. Squirtle could not break free, and its score fell further.

Ethan understood what Harley was doing. He wanted May to look helpless and foolish. But his arrogance would cost him. May was no longer the inexperienced girl he had once been able to torment.

When Harley finally grew tired of playing and sent Ariados in to finish Squirtle, May gave her command. Squirtle fired another Ice Beam. This time the web held its body steady. The beam struck Ariados squarely. Its recoil also tore Squirtle loose, breaking through layer after layer of silk and sending it back to the stage.

Ariados froze solid where it stood. The cold raced along its silk and turned the entire web into ice. The battle had reversed in an instant.

Harley's face changed. He had been so pleased with himself that he had never considered this possibility. Ariados's score plunged. Ice Beam had hurt it, and the judges clearly appreciated the spectacular effect it had created.

May seized the opportunity. Before Ariados could break free, she ordered Bubble. Countless bubbles struck the spider, shattering the ice on its body and dealing more damage.

Ariados thawed. Harley was about to order a counterattack when he saw that the silk beneath its feet remained frozen solid. Ariados could not move properly.

Squirtle leaped onto the web, took a running start, and used Tackle. It knocked Ariados to the floor below. The impact and fall together left the spider unconscious.

What? Harley stared. His Ariados had gone from complete control of the match to defeat in moments. Worse, he had lost to May in his very first battle of the second round. The humiliation stung, but his anger could not change the result.

All three judges' screens showed a large red X. Lilian announced, Ariados is unable to battle! Squirtle turned a hopeless position into a victory. The winner is May!

The audience erupted. Ash and the others cheered until they were nearly hoarse, their delight a sharp contrast to Harley's dark expression. He had deceived them only yesterday. May's victory was a satisfying answer.

May jumped for joy and hugged Squirtle. Without so much as a glance at the furious Harley, she turned and left the stage. Her confident departure made his face grow darker still. He wanted to say something cutting, but she was already gone.

Ethan greeted her with applause when she returned to the competitors' lounge.

That was a great battle, he said. I didn't know Squirtle had learned Ice Beam. And you beat Harley! That's worth celebrating.

Hehe... May smiled. No one was happier about advancing past Harley than she was.

...

Elsewhere, Harley came down from the stage intending to leave the Saffron Contest Hall and its painful memories behind. Instead, he met Jessie, James, and Meowth on their way to the stage.

Then he remembered he still had a way to get back at May. The woman calling herself the fairy Jessibella might prove useful.

Miss Jessibella! he said, putting on an ingratiating smile. Did you see the awful girl I just battled? She's the one who's been tormenting me!

Jessie stared at him blankly. What? I was getting my injuries treated. I didn't see your match. Did someone beat you?

Cacnea's spines had injured her during the first round. The medical staff had treated her quickly and carefully after carrying her offstage, but she had only just returned. She had missed May and Harley's battle entirely.

Harley's smile stiffened. It doesn't matter that you missed it. I nearly won, but that nasty girl used a trick and got lucky. I've lost my chance now. You have to avenge me!

Remembering their friendly conversation, Jessie did not question him. She patted her chest and promised, Don't worry! No one can beat the fairy Jessibella. She's just some little girl. I'll get revenge for you!

Harley was delighted. He lavished more praise on Jessie until she was floating with pride, then took his leave.

Once he was gone, James and Meowth exchanged uneasy looks. Didn't he seem to be up to something?

Who cares? Jessie said. For once, her reasoning was sound. We want to win the Saffron Contest. We'll have to beat anyone in our way. Getting revenge for him is just a bonus.

James and Meowth began to imagine victory too. Jessie's first-place score in the appeal round had astonished them. If she kept this up, they might honestly win something for once.

Full of hope, they sent Jessie onto the stage.

With Harley eliminated, there were few competitors who could challenge either May or Jessie. Jessie combined real ability with a touch of luck and swept past two opponents in succession. She and May reached the final battle.

It was an unprecedented showing for Jessie. Ethan found himself reconsidering her talent for performance. If she gave up being a villain and truly pursued life as a Coordinator, perhaps she could reach heights most people never would.

Chapter 823: What Are You Two Doing Up Here?

Ladies and gentlemen, the Saffron Pokemon Contest has reached its final battle! After round upon round of competition, two Coordinators will now face each other for the Saffron Ribbon. Please welcome May and the fairy Jessibella!

At Lilian's introduction, May and Jessie returned to the stage amid the crowd's cheers. Both had performed better with each successive match. Their exciting battles had won over the audience, and the hall rang with applause.

For Jessie especially, this was a rare moment of public admiration. She held her head high, smiling and waving to the spectators. She could hardly have looked more pleased with herself.

Then she looked across at her opponent and jumped. It was the girl who had traveled with the twerp in Hoenn!

Wait. How had that girl ended up here?

Careless as ever, Jessie had not paid attention to the identities of the other entrants, even as they took the same stage. She only recognized May when they came face to face in the final.

In the stands, James and Meowth sighed at her reaction.

Jessie finally noticed who she's up against, meow.

Yeah, James said, spreading his hands. That girl's no pushover. Jessie won't beat her easily.

It's not the girl I'm worried about. Meowth searched the audience. You saw her traveling with that man last time. If she's here, then...

He did not finish, but sweat broke out on James's forehead. You mean that man is nearby?

He has to be, meow. Even the Boss finds him troublesome. I don't want him noticing us.

What do we do? James asked.

Meowth thought for a moment, then snapped his claws. Plan B, meow!

Plan B? Since when do we have a Plan B?

Since now, meow!

That's a little sudden. What is Plan B?

Rather than answer, Meowth asked, Have you forgotten what we're here for?

James blinked innocently. To help Jessie enter the Contest?

Idiot! Meowth scratched James across the face in frustration. We're here to capture Pokemon for the Boss, meow!

James fell with a cry, then scrambled up again. Holding his face, he said, Oh, that. Of course I knew.

The final battle had begun. May had chosen Squirtle again. Jessie had sent out Wobbuffet, the trio's unofficial fourth member.

In the second round, Jessie had won her battles by using Wobbuffet's Counter and Mirror Coat to send her opponents' attacks back at them. The method was simple, but it had defeated two competitors. Both had helped her by stubbornly attacking head-on.

May had apparently studied those matches. She did not rush into an attack. Instead, Squirtle kept moving, searching for an opening in Wobbuffet's defenses.

Meowth watched the field intently. Jessie will probably lose if this keeps up. We should get ready now, meow.

Ready for what? James asked.

See that man? Meowth pointed with one claw.

James looked toward a shadowed part of the hall. Harley, whom they had met earlier, leaned against a pillar and watched the battle.

Him? What about him?

Meowth grinned. He wants Jessie to get revenge for him. We ought to collect a fee, meow.

James's eyes lit up. You mean...?

Exactly. He placed second in the first round, so his Pokemon must be strong. We can take them to the Boss.

In the corner, Harley stood with his arms crossed, glaring at May. He had lost through carelessness. If he had finished Squirtle promptly, the battle might have gone differently. He regretted his mistake, but the result was settled.

Jessibella was his last hope of seeing May humbled. Come on, then, he thought. Show me what you can do. Don't disappoint me.

A sly smile crossed his face. Then a man and a Pokemon appeared before him.

He focused and recognized Jessibella's assistant and companion. You two? What do you want?

James rubbed his hands together and smiled awkwardly. Well, you've seen how troublesome that girl is. The great Jessibella might need some of your strength to beat her.

Harley frowned more deeply. My strength? What do you mean?

Your Pokemon, of course! Meowth said.

But the battle has started. She can't change Pokemon now. And I've been eliminated. How could I lend her mine?

James gave him a brilliant smile. We have a special technique for summoning Pokemon to help during a battle. It's Jessibella's signature move. It can turn a match into two against oneor even more!

Oh? Harley's eyes brightened.

He had never dealt with Team Rocket before. He did not know these two were Pokemon thieves and still believed Jessibella was a famous Coordinator. He had no reason to suspect them. Besides, Harley often used tricks himself, so the proposed technique did not trouble him.

Still, he asked cautiously, Why do you need my Pokemon?

We wouldn't bother you if we had a choice, James said. Jessibella didn't bring many Pokemon on this trip.

Harley hesitated. Jessibella seemed famous, had two assistants, and had topped the first-round rankings. Surely someone like that would not deceive him.

All right. Which Pokemon do you need?

James and Meowth could barely contain their delight, but they kept smiling calmly. If possible, could we borrow Cacturne, which you used in the appeal round, and Ariados, which you used for battle?

Without further argument, Harley took out two Poke Balls and handed them over. James and Meowth exchanged gleeful looks, then carefully composed themselves.

With your Pokemon, Jessibella is certain to win, James said gravely. Thank you. We'll leave you to enjoy the match. Look forward to the good news!

Before Harley could answer, they hurried away. He assumed the Contest's tight schedule required them to move fast and turned back toward the stage.

The battle was going badly for Jessibella. Squirtle was avoiding a direct attack on Wobbuffet and wearing down its score by other means. No wonder her assistants had come to him.

Harley narrowed his eyes at May. With my help, he thought, you'll be humiliated.

After deceiving May so many times, Harley had been deceived by Team Rocket. They had no intention of helping Jessie defeat May. They simply wanted his Pokemon, while he foolishly believed his own scheme had succeeded. Even a clever trickster could fall for someone else's trick.

As Harley waited, the final battle entered its last minute. May continued directing Squirtle around Wobbuffet, trying different ways to attack.

She still had not recognized Jessie, but watching Wobbuffet's two earlier battles had taught her how it fought. It could not launch an attack of its own. That was typical of Wobbuffet. The purple-haired woman's familiar voice and manner nagged at May, but she had not connected the clues.

Squirtle could not easily defeat Wobbuffet outright. Its steady pressure had, however, reduced Wobbuffet's Contest score to a dangerous level. Squirtle's score had barely fallen. If the clock ran out, May would win even without knocking Wobbuffet out.

Jessie was growing frantic. No matter what she ordered, Wobbuffet stood there looking blank and harmless. It had no way to take points from Squirtle without first receiving an attack.

Harley was getting anxious too. He kept waiting for Jessibella to use the technique her assistants had described. She made no such move. What was she doing? There was almost no time left.

At that moment, every light in the Saffron Contest Hall went out. Darkness swallowed the room. The battle stopped, and spectators looked around in confusion, talking among themselves.

Huh? Lilian's voice echoed through her microphone. What's going on?

A spotlight suddenly came on, illuminating Jessie in the middle of the stage.

Jessie looked around, just as puzzled as everyone else. Two figures leaped to her side. Music started up from somewhere.

Under the light, the crowd saw a man in a white uniform and a Meowth standing upright beside Jessibella. James and Meowth had shed their disguises.

The audience had no idea what this interruption meant. Neither did Jessie. She stared at her partners. What are you doing here?

Meowth ignored her and laughed toward the stands. I heard someone ask, What's going on?

James leaned back against him and raised a fist. From beyond the far horizon!

Almost by reflex, Jessie tore off her disguise, jumped beside James, and leaned against him. From the other side of the great thunderbolt!

A voice is calling us!

Thanks for waiting, meow!

The brave, blooming flowers of evil!

The lovely, tough villains!

Jessie!

James!

And Meowth, that's me! Meow!

Wherever Team Rocket goes

The world!

The universe!

Waits for us!

Wobbuffet!

Only after finishing the entire routine did Jessie come to her senses. She turned on her partners. I'm asking you! What are you two doing up here?

Chapter 824: Already Over

Jessie. James turned to her with a bright smile. Don't you understand? The operation is over!

Operation? Jessie stared at him. What operation? What's over?

Why, the James drew out the word, then swept an arm dramatically. Several grappling lines dropped from the ceiling in front of them. great Pokemon snatching operation!

Pokemon snatching? Jessie looked bewildered. Since when was that the plan? And my battle isn't even finished!

As she spoke, the last seconds of the five-minute clock ran out. Wobbuffet was still standing, but its Contest score was far below Squirtle's. By the rules, Jessie had lost.

No! Three red Xs appeared on the judges' displays. Tears streamed down Jessie's face as she reached toward the prize. My Saffron Ribbon!

Lilian had caught on by then. At first, she, the judges, and much of the audience had assumed this was an unscheduled part of the show. The director's alarmed denial in her earpiece told her otherwise.

You she began, ready to stop them. Then several children ran onto the stage. Lilian recognized May's companions from yesterday's rehearsal. Why were they up there too?

Ash reached Team Rocket first. What are you doing here? he demanded.

Twerp, Meowth said, this has nothing to do with you. Stay out of it, meow!

While he spoke, Meowth scanned the audience for the man they feared. The disruption had gone on long enough for Ethan to appear, but there was still no sign of him. Meowth breathed a little easier. He dared not wait any longer.

He flipped several smoke bombs into his paws and hurled them down. They burst with sharp pops, spreading thick white smoke across the stage.

Even Harley now understood that he had been tricked. He leaped onto the stage and plunged into the smoke. Team Rocket were already rising on their cables.

Wait! Jessibella! Give me back my Pokemon!

Meowth only laughed. You were stupid enough to hand them over, meow! Don't blame us!

He pressed a switch. A tremendous blast tore a hole through the hall's heavy roof. Cold air rushed inside, blowing everyone's hair about. James and Meowth laughed wildly as the cables carried the trio up through the opening and out of sight.

The gust scattered the smoke. It also blew something from Harley's pocket, sent it spinning through the air, and slapped it against his face. He pulled it away. It was his Kanto Contest pass, bearing Jessie's ugly autograph.

Damn it! he shouted. He wanted to throw it away, but he still needed the pass. He stuffed it back into his pocket and ran for the exit.

He hated those swindlers. So much for the fairy Jessibella! He had trusted her to avenge him and had handed over his Pokemon. It was humiliating. When he caught the trio, he would tear them apart.

At the doors, Harley looked back and shot May a hateful glare. Somehow this was all her fault. Next time they met, he would make her pay.

May could only stare after him. She had no idea what had happened. Why did it feel as though she was being blamed for it? Ash, Lilian, and the spectators were similarly confused.

One moment Jessibella had been battling; the next, she was gone. Who were the people with her? Why had Harley chased them? It had all happened too quickly for anyone to piece together.

Lilian recovered first, a professional to the end. She smiled toward the crowd. It seems we've had an unexpected interruption. But the clock has run out, and under Contest rules, the winner of the Saffron Contest is May! Let's congratulate her!

The lights came back on. Staff hurried onto the stage to clear away pieces of the damaged roof. The odd finish did not keep the spectators from standing and cheering for May.

The final battle had not been especially exciting or beautiful, but a win was a win. May lifted Squirtle high and waved to the crowd, smiling. Her excitement at earning the Ribbon was plain to see.

Once the stage was clean, Mr. Contesta personally presented her with the Saffron Ribbon. May had won her first Ribbon since arriving in Kanto.

That evening, Ethan treated the group to a generous dinner in celebration. Afterward, it was time to move on. This Ribbon was only a beginning. To enter the Kanto Grand Festival, May still needed four more.

Perhaps May's victory spurred Ash on. Perhaps he felt behind Ethan, having earned only one Frontier Symbol. Either way, he did not linger in Saffron City. With Max and Brock, he set out after dark for the nearby Battle Arena.

Ethan thought Ash was rushing. Given the strange turns Ash's journeys often took, setting off into the night might cost him time rather than save it. But it was Ash's journey to choose. Ethan and May had an adventure of their own, and he had no need to interfere.

After seeing the three off, Ethan and May returned to the Saffron Gym. Ethan spent more time alone with Sabrina. They rested there one final night. Then he left her warm company and set out with May again.

Their next destination was the Battle Palace, on an island in the Kanto sea near Cinnabar Island. The facility stood on Metallica Island. Ethan knew little about the island beyond its position among the islands along a sea route. He had chosen it next so that later Frontier challenges could follow a sensible route without unnecessary backtracking.

Ash might walk until he got lost. Ethan preferred to make a rough plan before leaving. Neither way of traveling was inherently better; they simply suited different people.

The following morning, Ethan kissed Sabrina goodbye. Her reluctance to see him leave showed in her eyes. After breakfast, he and May packed and headed for the nearest port city.

The first part of their route overlapped with Ash's. Only farther along would the roads branch in different directions. If Ash had stayed one more night in Saffron, they could have traveled together a little longer.

Then again, too many people traveling together made an adventure feel more like a picnic and offered fewer chances to learn. Perhaps Ash had been wise to go ahead.

...

The sky was clear and the sun bright. It was a fine day to travel.

Outside Saffron City, Ethan and May walked side by side along a riverbank levee, then crossed a broad stretch of grassland toward the sea. The soft grass underfoot smelled fresh. A light breeze made the walk comfortable.

May glanced across the fields and stopped. A farm stood in the distance.

Look, Ethan! She pointed to it with a smile. Isn't that farm beautiful? I used to imagine living quietly in a place like that. It must feel wonderful.

Ethan nodded absently. A moment later, something came back to him, and he stopped too. Would you like to see it?

Huh? May clearly wanted to, but she hesitated. Could we? Aren't we in a hurry?

A journey doesn't end in a day. It's good to take a break sometimes, and we can spare the time. Ethan smiled. If you'd like to visit, we can ask the farmer whether we may have a look around.

Really? That would be great!

When he nodded, May eagerly hopped down from the levee and started toward the farm. She had taken only a few steps when two Voltorb appeared from nowhere and fired electricity at her.

May had not seen them. She cried out and watched the two flashes race toward her. They struck something like an invisible wall and dispersed in midair.

She turned and saw Ethan's Gardevoir lowering an arm. He had released it without her noticing. It must have saved her.

But why had Ethan brought Gardevoir out at just that moment? Had he seen the danger beforehand?

May could not have guessed that the scene had reminded Ethan of an anime episode, prompting him to prepare. Without him, the Voltorb would have given her a painful shock. He had recognized the risk in time to prevent it.

Still shaken, May put a hand to her chest and backed away from the Voltorb. Why did they attack me?

They probably took you for an intruder, Ethan said. We're close to the farm, and you were walking toward it. They may be guarding the property.

That's right! a girl's voice called nearby.

The grass rustled, and a young girl emerged. She held a broom and wore denim overalls. Freckles dotted her face, and her untidy red hair was tied in pigtails. She looked Ethan and May over.

Who are you? Why are you coming onto my family's farm?

May glanced down and realized she was already standing on someone else's grass. Oh, I'm sorry. I didn't notice

Before she could finish, the girl recognized her face. She gave a surprised cry and ran over, stopping directly in front of May.

Are you the one who won the Saffron Contest yesterday?

Huh? May was surprised to be recognized so soon. Yes, that's me.

I knew it! The girl cheered, her cheeks flushing with excitement. I saw your performance and your battles on television. You were amazing!

The commotion drew a man and a woman out of the farmhouse. They looked toward the group.

Nicolette, what's going on? Do we have visitors?

Chapter 825: A Battle with the Egg Farmer

Inside the farmhouse, Ethan sat with May in a warm living room. He raised his cup of tea and took a sip. May nibbled a cookie from the table.

Across from them sat the family who owned the farm. The freckled girl with pigtails they had met outside was Nicolette. The middle-aged couple beside her were her father, Christopher, and her mother, Jeannie. They looked like a close, happy family.

Despite their age and the work of managing a large farm, Christopher and Jeannie did not look weathered by years outdoors. They seemed younger than they were. Their home was warm, tidy, and well kept. The family appeared to be doing well.

We haven't introduced ourselves, Ethan said, setting down his tea. I'm Ethan Vale, a Trainer traveling through Kanto. Sorry to turn up uninvited.

And I'm May, May said quickly. I'm a Pokemon Coordinator and Ethan's traveling companion. I want to become a Top Coordinator!

A Top Coordinator! Christopher and Jeannie exchanged a look, then smiled at their daughter. Nicolette wants to be one too, but...

Ethan and May followed their gaze.

But what? May asked. Anyone can become a Coordinator, can't they? Do you disapprove?

Of course not, Christopher said. We've often encouraged her to travel as a Coordinator and gather experience. It's just...

Nicolette lowered her head, looking embarrassed and ashamed.
