Ethan knew how this sort of encounter would unfold if Ash were here. The family would reveal its trouble, and Ash would step in to solve it. May had once traveled with Ash; almost instinctively, she asked, Just what? Has something happened?

Nicolette's situation is complicated, Jeannie said with a sigh. We couldn't explain it in a few words.

She seemed reluctant to say more, so May changed the subject. What kind of farm is this?

You may have seen part of it on your way in, Christopher said. People entrust us with their Pokemon Eggs, and we care for them until they hatch.

Pokemon Eggs? May knew Pokemon hatched from Eggs, but she had never seen one herself.

That's right, Jeannie said with a smile. Would you like a tour?

May looked at Ethan. When he nodded, she smiled eagerly at their hosts. Yes, please! I've never seen a Pokemon Egg. I'd love to look.

Christopher and Jeannie had farm work to do, so they asked Nicolette to show the visitors around. Nicolette was happy to have a legitimate excuse to escape her chores for a while.

She led Ethan and May out of the farmhouse. May fell a few steps behind and gave Ethan a questioning look. She had not traveled with him for long, but she knew he rarely spent time on such small detours. Why had he agreed to visit this farm?

She had a vague feeling that there was more to it, much like when they had visited Professor Oak's Laboratory. She had no evidence, yet it felt almost as though Ethan knew something in advance. On that earlier visit, she had received Squirtle. Could something similar happen here? Her heart beat a little faster.

The farm had an unusual layout. Four large storage buildings stood around a central tower, arranged like the blades of a windmill. The farmhouse was at their base. Perhaps the plan made it easier to oversee everything.

Nicolette led them into one of the storage buildings. Two long rows of shelves were filled with Pokemon Eggs.

The Eggs varied in size, color, and pattern. There were so many designs that May could not begin to tell what species they held. The sight was astonishing.

Wow! So many Eggs!

It was Ethan's first time seeing so many together too. He was impressed.

Nicolette rubbed her nose and smiled proudly. Pretty amazing, isn't it? People have entrusted all of these to us. We take very good care of every Egg.

Ethan approached a pink Egg with a pale ring around it. The room was warm, evidently for the Eggs' development. Each one had a numbered label for tracking and rested on a soft pad so it would not roll. Their shells were clean and smooth, as though wiped regularly. The family did seem attentive.

What kind of Pokemon will hatch from them? he asked.

Nicolette thought for a moment. Pichu, Vulpix, Growlithe, Machop, Ponyta, Tauros... all sorts!

Most appeared to be Eggs of common Kanto Pokemon. Ethan supposed that made sense. Owners of rare Eggs would usually raise them themselves unless they lacked the time or ability.

May stopped at another shelf. It also held Eggs, though fewer than the others. Why aren't there as many over here?

Those belong to us, Nicolette said with a shrug. For one reason or another, some people abandoned the Eggs they left here, so we're raising them. Actually, you've come at a good time. Have you ever seen a Pokemon hatch? One of these Eggs should hatch soon. Would you like to stay and watch?

Before May could answer, Ethan nodded. If you don't mind, we'd love to.

That settled May's suspicion. Ethan had some reason for bringing her here.

She was right. He had not stopped at the farm on a whim. In the anime story, May would receive her second Pokemon since coming to Kanto here. Ethan wanted to make sure she had that chance, which was why he was willing to spend time at the farm.

Even if May had guessed that he had a purpose, he could never tell her what he knew. He would keep it to himself.

Outside the storage building, Nicolette turned toward May with a determined look. May, let's have a battle!

Huh? May stared at the girl, who was about her own age. Why all of a sudden?

Because of what my parents said inside. I want to prove I don't have to leave home to train. I can stay here and still become a great Coordinator!

I suppose you could train here, May said, scratching her cheek. Why not tell your parents how you feel?

I want to. Nicolette hesitated and blushed. But they won't accept it. They think I have to travel to learn about the world. If I battle you, I can show them what I can do.

Show your strength? May nodded. So you want one battle?

Yes! Nicolette nodded hard. You just won the Saffron Contest. If I can even tie with you, my parents will have to acknowledge my ability.

May saw her confidence but was uncertain. She returned to Ethan and asked quietly, What should I do?

The family had offered them tea and cookies and given them a tour. It felt awkward to battle their daughter as guests. Winning might seem rude; losing might be just as unhelpful.

Go ahead and battle seriously, Ethan said. She's overconfident. If you don't beat her, she may think winning a Contest is easy. I don't agree that she can learn everything by staying home. Helping her see that would do her parents a favor.

I understand.

Ethan's advice decided the matter for May. She stepped back toward Nicolette and reached for a Poke Ball, then hesitated. Ethan wanted her to win, but how hard should she fight? Should she use Combusken at full strength, or give Nicolette more time against Squirtle? She decided to let Nicolette choose.

May took out three Poke Balls and released all three of her Pokemon. Combusken, Squirtle, and Munchlax appeared before Nicolette.

What's this? Nicolette asked.

These are all the Pokemon I have with me, May said, spreading her hands. You want to battle, and I'm not sure which to use. You can pick my opponent for me.

Another Coordinator might have taken that as an insult. Nicolette had never even left home to compete. She did not think of it that way and instead studied the three Pokemon carefully.

She had seen Combusken and Squirtle perform at the Saffron Contest. Battling either seemed risky. That left Munchlax. It sat drowsily, looking as though it had barely woken up. Nicolette pointed.

I choose Munchlax!

May had not expected that. Nicolette claimed she wanted to prove her strength, yet she had selected the least battle-tested of May's Pokemon. Perhaps she did not know Munchlax had never fought. But her careful choice and expression suggested she had picked it precisely because it looked weak.

My Munchlax... May began.

Nicolette was already releasing her own Pokemon. A Vileplume appeared before Munchlax. Perhaps afraid May would change her mind, Nicolette ordered an attack before Combusken and Squirtle had even moved away.

Vileplume, show them a beautiful Petal Dance!

Vileplume lowered itself, aimed the flower on its head, and sent out a cloud of pink petals. They struck Munchlax instantly. Munchlax had not even tried to dodge.

Vileplume was fully evolved and used the move with accuracy. Whatever Nicolette lacked in travel experience, her Pokemon had some strength.

The attack left Munchlax dazed. Worse, it became confused and began hopping about wildly. Perhaps because of that confusion, it raised both arms and used Metronome without being told.

Metronome could call up almost any known move at random. Even the Pokemon using it could not know what would happen. With luck, it might unleash a powerful attack. With bad luck, it might hurt itself. It was unpredictable and risky, especially when Munchlax was already confused.

Nicolette swallowed and grew cautious despite her early success. Come on, she thought. Show me the strength of the Saffron Contest winner.

Chapter 826: Back on the Expected Path

Under Nicolette's wary gaze, Munchlax's Metronome produced Splash. Its round body bounced up and down on the grass like a Magikarp stranded on a riverbank.

So the famous moment had happened after all. May looked embarrassed. Nicolette's guarded expression froze. After all that caution, Munchlax had used a move that did nothing. She felt foolish for treating it as a dangerous opponent.

Then she recognized her chance. Vileplume, use Stun Spore now!

Orange powder poured from Vileplume's flower and settled over Munchlax. Still bouncing helplessly, it could not dodge. Now it was confused and paralyzed, trembling where it stood. May watched anxiously. She wanted to help it pull itself together, but she had no idea how.

Nicolette pressed the advantage. Vileplume, Bullet Seed!

It was a sound tactic against most Pokemon. Munchlax, unfortunately for Nicolette, did not behave like most Pokemon.

Vileplume fired a rapid stream of seeds. They struck Munchlax in a steady barrage, bursting in small explosions and raising a cloud of smoke.

Nicolette grinned. Ha! So much for the Saffron Contest winner. You're nothing special!

That angered May. Until now, she had treated the battle as a friendly test. Nicolette's taunt made her take it seriously.

What did you say? May glared at her, then called into the smoke. Munchlax, get up! The real battle is just starting. Show her what you've got!

Perhaps Munchlax sensed her anger. Two sharp, shining eyes appeared in the smoke. Munchlax burst out with a glowing fist, accelerated across the dozen or so meters between them, and slammed into Vileplume.

The blow was immense. Vileplume cried out and flew backward, landing hard some distance away.

What? Nicolette turned to check on it. Even May was astonished by the move Munchlax had used.

Was that...?

Focus Punch, Ethan said with a smile. It looks as though your Munchlax learned it without your knowing.

The surprise was welcome. That punch had brought Munchlax into the fight and answered Nicolette's insult.

Great job! May gave Vileplume no time to recover. Finish it with Solar Beam!

Ethan shook his head. A Grass-type move against a Grass and Poison Pokemon: May really had picked up some of Ash's habits.

Munchlax obeyed without question. It gathered energy and fired a long beam from its mouth toward Vileplume. The Pokemon had only just risen. It ducked instinctively, and the beam passed over its head, brushing the flower's petals before striking a small hill in the distance.

Only a little of the attack had touched Vileplume, but that was enough. Its eyes rolled back and it collapsed.

No way! Nicolette cried. It barely grazed Vileplume, and it still went down? A Contest winner really is different!

Her attitude had changed completely. She had the cause wrong, though. She thought Solar Beam had decided the match. The decisive blow had been Munchlax's earlier, accelerating Focus Punch.

May had won without the battle slipping away from her. She and Nicolette recalled their Pokemon. When they turned toward Ethan, they saw Christopher and Jeannie watching from nearby. They had witnessed the battle.

Nicolette had hoped to prove herself to her parents, only to lose so plainly. She lowered her head in shame. Beside Ethan, May received his praise and smiled brightly, making the contrast harder for Nicolette to bear.

Then Ethan spoke to her. I think traveling and seeing more of the world will teach you more than training at home. May is only a year or two older than you, but her experience has made her stronger.

Nicolette looked up. Though she argued against leaving, she was not as opposed to travel as she claimed. Part of her even wanted to go. She stayed because she loved her home and her parents. Her room, the shelves full of Eggs, the lovely farm, and all the familiar things around her gave her reasons not to leave.

She admired May's life as a Coordinator and wanted to prove she could match her. Losing had shown her the gap between them. Ethan's words made the thought of travel more appealing, though she would not admit it aloud.

Are you a Coordinator too? she asked him. She wanted to know who was advising her before deciding what to say back.

No, Ethan said, making no effort to boast. I'm just a Trainer.

May did not like the way Nicolette had asked. Ethan isn't an ordinary Trainer. He won the last Indigo League Conference!

What? Nicolette knew what a championship meant, even though she had never watched a League battle. She stared at Ethan. You? Is that true? You're not making it up?

Ethan had not expected May to bring up his old victory. He understood that she did not want Nicolette to look down on him, so he nodded.

May's telling the truth. But we aren't listing our accomplishments to impress you. We want you to know that going out into the world lets you see more of it and keep improving.

Ethan would not ordinarily have said so much to a girl he had just met. He had a reason: he wanted May to receive the Egg he knew she could gain here. If they helped Nicolette's parents persuade their daughter to travel, the family might thank them with a gift.

He could have tried to buy the Egg instead. That would have been a mere transaction. May would have had no part in earning it and less reason to treasure it. Better to let her help someone and receive it in return.

A Contest winner's example might not have been enough to sway Nicolette. Hearing from a League champion as well shook her resolve. Ethan then let Gardevoir give a small demonstration, restoring the patch of hillside that Munchlax's Solar Beam had damaged. Nicolette was stunned.

Could traveling really make someone that capable?

That afternoon, after the farm work was finished, Nicolette and her parents sat down to tea with Ethan and May again. May told Nicolette stories of the places she had seen and the things she had experienced since becoming a Coordinator. At last, Nicolette made up her mind.

Thank you, she said, looking solemnly at Ethan and May. I've decided to be brave and travel.

Christopher and Jeannie looked at each other in surprise and relief. Their daughter had finally overcome the fear that had held her back. They were about to thank the visitors when a red warning light came on.

It's time! Nicolette rose first. Remember when I told you one of the Pokemon Eggs was about to hatch? It's happening now!

The family hurried outside. Ethan and May, curious to see a hatching, followed them to the tower surrounded by the storage buildings.

An orange-red Egg marked with swirling patterns rocked gently on a strange machine. Several beams of white light shone on it. From its color and markings, Ethan guessed it held a Vulpix. The Egg began to flash. It would hatch any moment.

We arrived just in time, May said. She stepped closer to study it.

Ethan had seen Pokemon hatch often in the anime, but never in person. He found the sight fascinating too.

Before long, the Egg changed. A bright light flashed, and its entire shape transformed into a Vulpix. May had expected the Pokemon to break through a shell. To her surprise, no shell remained at all.

Nicolette set to work caring for the newborn. She dried it with a towel, examined it, and fed it milk, moving through each task with ease. Young as she was, she had plenty of practice looking after newly hatched Pokemon.

More than half an hour passed. Ethan and May had been guests for a long time and ought to be going.

Christopher and Jeannie had still made no offer of a gift. Without Team Rocket causing trouble here, there had been no dramatic incident to make them especially grateful. Ethan hesitated, wondering whether to raise the matter himself. Then Nicolette approached May with an Egg under a transparent cover.

May, please accept this Pokemon Egg.

Huh? May glanced back at Ethan. Can I really take it?

Of course. Nicolette smiled. You and Ethan helped me decide to leave home and become a real Coordinator. You liked the Eggs so much that I wanted to thank you with one.

Ethan studied its color and pattern. It was an Eevee Egg. He nodded to himself. Their visit had been worthwhile.

In the anime, May had received Eevee, her second new Pokemon in Kanto, from this farm. Even without Ash here, Ethan had helped bring events back to their expected course.

Chapter 827: Eevee: Huh?

May accepted the Eevee Egg from Nicolette, still a little embarrassed by the generous gift.

She did not know what Pokemon would hatch from it. Ethan and Nicolette's family kept the secret, smiling and telling her she would find out when it hatched. The mystery gave May something to look forward to.

Ethan was relieved too. As far as he knew, in May's travels through Kanto, Johto, and later Sinnoh, Squirtle and Eevee would be the only Pokemon she added to her team. With his help, she had now received both. They could travel freely without his needing to worry about missing either opportunity.

That did not mean May would never catch another Pokemon. If they met one that suited her, Ethan would point it out and help even if she did not ask. For now, that was a question for another day.

They thanked the family and left the farm while it was still early afternoon. Their intended port was not far away. After crossing a broad plain and passing a pond, they saw it within a little over an hour: Silver Town.

The town was small but surprisingly lively. Its position between Saffron and Vermilion Cities, with the sea close by, helped its economy. At the same time, many young people had been drawn away to larger places. With fewer residents, growth was difficult.

Ethan was about to head for the docks and buy two boat tickets when he overheard important news: the Silver Town Contest would be held tomorrow.

Huh? They have a Contest here too? May asked, astonished. Silver Town was less than a day's walk from Saffron City. She had not expected another event so close by.

There are exceptions, Ethan said with a smile. I don't know every detail of the Contest circuit, but smaller places hold Contests too. Where else would Harley and all the other Coordinators earn their Ribbons? If only a few big cities hosted them, hardly anyone could collect five in a year. The Grand Festival wouldn't have enough entrants.

Oh, I see. May nodded.

Her lack of experience was understandable. Like Misty had been at her age, she was only ten. Some things did not occur to her until someone explained them.

It did mean a busy schedule for Mr. Contesta and Mr. Sukizo, the Contest judges. They must have barely finished one event before traveling to the next. Lilian, the beautiful host, would be just as busy.

However the schedule worked, May would not pass up the chance to compete. She needed more Ribbons for the Kanto Grand Festival.

They entered the town. Its Contest Hall stood at one edge of it, modest in size. A tall flight of steps and a sloping stretch of grass led up to the many-angled entrance.

May had learned from her close call in Saffron. Though there was plenty of time, she registered at once. Without Harley or Team Rocket interfering, nothing unexpected happened.

After registering and looking over the venue, they checked in at a nearby Pokemon Center. May hurried to the outdoor training ground behind it to rehearse. This time Ethan had time to watch.

He let his own Pokemon out and sat on a bench beside the field, grooming them while looking up now and then to see how May was doing.

May had changed her plan. Squirtle would perform in the first round, and Combusken would battle in the second. The division made good sense. It gave each Pokemon a role, helped both develop, and kept either from feeling overlooked.

May could design and rehearse Squirtle's appeal on her own. Combusken, however, needed a practice opponent, and her small team offered few choices. Ethan saw her hesitate to ask.

He laughed and pointed to his Pokemon. Pick whichever one you like to practice with Combusken.

May was delighted, but a look at the Pokemon around him made her frown. There were only five: Gardevoir, Gengar, Eevee, Dragonite, and Blaziken. She could not decide which to choose, so she turned to Combusken.

You pick, she told it softly. Be careful, though. Ethan's Pokemon are all strong. Don't push yourself too hard.

Combusken nodded and studied the candidates. Gardevoir and Gengar looked friendly enough, yet both gave it a frightening feeling. Gengar in particular seemed to have mischief in its eyes. Combusken looked away almost immediately.

Dragonite wore a kindly smile and even offered Combusken a thumbs-up, as though volunteering. Its powerful presence was unmistakable. Combusken knew it was no match and passed it by too.

That left Blaziken and Eevee. The instant Combusken met Blaziken's gaze, it felt a sharp pressure, almost like a blade. Facing the fully evolved form of its own species, it hardly dared breathe. It hurriedly turned away.

Only Eevee remained. It lay harmlessly on Ethan's lap while he brushed its fur. Combusken gave a small cry, choosing it.

Eevee? Ethan smiled. A sensible choice.

May's Combusken was strong by ordinary standards, but it was far behind most of Ethan's Pokemon. Eevee, being unevolved and so cute, at least looked less intimidating.

Ethan lifted his hands away. Go on, Eevee. Help Combusken practice.

Eevee called back, sprang off his lap, and approached Combusken eagerly.

May wondered how the match would go. Would Ethan's Eevee win easily, or might Combusken have a chance? Combusken was more developed physically, and that could make a difference even against a capable Eevee.

She wanted to watch, but Squirtle's rehearsal mattered more. She gave Combusken a few last instructions and turned to the appeal she was planning. Her first task tomorrow was to pass the performance round. Only then would Combusken get to battle. Helping Squirtle make the strongest possible showing had to come first.

At the start, May managed to watch both Pokemon. As she and Squirtle settled into practice, she could no longer spare the attention. One quick glance showed Combusken and Eevee trading blows without an obvious winner. She returned to Squirtle.

Ethan watched their match closely. Combusken had traveled through a region with May and fought in many battles. It was far from weak. But Eevee trained primarily for combat and had the edge in experience.

Combusken had greater striking power, and their speed was comparable. On those measures it ought to have the advantage. Yet Eevee was already controlling the rhythm, despite the even-looking exchanges. May could not see it yet. Ethan knew Combusken would eventually lose unless something changed.

Defeating Combusken was not the purpose of this practice. It was meant to help Combusken grow.

Combusken, Ethan called, don't chase Eevee. Move toward your twelve o'clock. That's where it'll land.

Combusken hesitated for an instant, then followed his instruction. Pokemon rarely took orders from someone other than their Trainer. But Combusken knew May trusted Ethan, knew his skill, and knew it could not beat Eevee unaided.

Instead of pursuing Eevee, it moved to intercept. A moment later Eevee landed exactly where Ethan had predicted. Combusken instinctively used Double Kick, sending it flying.

Eevee slid backward a long way before it stopped. Once it was safe, it did not attack. It turned to stare at its own Trainer, looking thoroughly confused. Whose side was he on?

Ethan smiled back. What are you looking at? Never seen such a handsome Trainer?

Eevee was about to protest when Combusken came running. It had to turn back and fight. Its brief advantage did not change the overall match; before long, Eevee was gaining the upper hand again.

Now, use Ember! Ethan called.

Combusken had been preparing Scratch. This time it did not hesitate at all. It abandoned the claw attack and sent flames toward Eevee. Eevee had quietly readied a defensive counter and was startled. It leaped away several times to escape the fire.

From a safe distance, Eevee complained to Ethan again. He merely spread his hands. Why are you looking at me? Don't let things outside the battle distract you. Carefulit's coming again.

Eevee turned. Combusken was already charging at it, so it had to resume the fight. Now wary of another instruction from Ethan, Eevee fought cautiously. It no longer moved with its earlier ease. Combusken found openings and recovered from its disadvantage. The practice ended in a draw.

Eevee ran to Ethan and protested at length.

All right, all right. Ethan soothed it with a smile. I gave Combusken a few pointers because I know you're stronger. Remember, this wasn't about deciding a winner. We're helping it improve.

Eevee understood that, but being undermined by its own Trainer had made it feel attacked from both sides. Still, as Ethan said, their practice had only begun. It would have another chance to settle the score.

Chapter 828: Like Watching a Film Whose Ending You Know

After their first match, Eevee and Combusken fought three more practice rounds. By the time May finished working with Squirtle and looked over, both Pokemon were panting and marked with scrapes. They had spent a great deal of energy.

Ethan offered only the occasional hint during those three rounds. Combusken did not win a single one, and its new ambition to beat Eevee began to fade. There was a real difference in their strength. Combusken had managed to avoid being knocked out in all three only because Ethan guided it at critical moments.

The matches were still worthwhile. Fighting Eevee improved Combusken's control of its moves and its ability to respond to an opponent. It had grown.

May wiped her forehead and came over. How did the training go?

Combusken improved quickly. Give it a few more days like this and it could enter a Pokemon League tournament, Ethan said. How did things go with Squirtle?

Great! May gave him a thumbs-up. You'll see tomorrow.

They wanted Squirtle and Combusken in good condition for the Contest. At dusk they took all the Pokemon back to the Center, had Combusken's injuries treated, fed everyone a hearty meal, washed and brushed them, and finally sent them to rest.

By the time they finished, it was fully dark. Ethan and May sat on a bench in the corridor, looking up at the Pokemon Center ceiling without speaking.

May was exhausted. She had been responsible for every little task and now did not want to move a finger. Ethan saw how tired she was and let her rest in silence.

After a long while, she stretched and smiled. I never noticed how much work it is when I have to prepare for a Contest on my own.

Ethan understood. At her earlier Contests, Max and Brock had helped. They had shared jobs she scarcely needed to think about. Now that they were gone, everything fell to May. Other Coordinators dealt with that routinely. She had simply been well looked after until now.

Ethan was about to answer, but May spoke first. It's all right. I'll keep trying. I'm a little overwhelmed now, but before long I'll know how to handle everything.

He looked at her in surprise, then smiled. She was still the cheerful, optimistic girl he knew. These difficulties had not discouraged her. She looked forward to learning. It was one of the reasons she had been so loved in the anime.

I believe you, he said. I believe you'll become a Top Coordinator one day.

There was no trace of a joke in his voice. May stared at him, wondering why he believed in her so firmly. Everyone could voice a dream. How many people truly achieved theirs?

...

The Silver Town Contest began on schedule at ten the next morning. The small hall was full. Though the crowd was smaller than at a city Contest, its enthusiasm was just as strong.

As expected, Lilian hosted again, with Mr. Contesta, Mr. Sukizo, and Nurse Joy judging. The only likely change was that this Nurse Joy belonged to the Silver Town Pokemon Center rather than Saffron's. She looked and dressed exactly like the other Joy, and her judging standards seemed the same.

After Lilian introduced the judges and explained the rules, the competitors came in. There were only a dozen or so, May included, and Ethan recognized no one. It appeared to be a modest field. If May performed as well as she could, she had a good chance of winning.

Cheers greeted the start of the Contest. A few seconds before it began, however, a middle-aged man dressed like an office worker hurried in with a briefcase. He tripped on his way up to the stage, drawing good-natured laughter from the audience.

Ethan did not laugh. He frowned, remembering something. So it was him. The scene was familiar from the anime. This small-town Contest had appeared there after all. As he recalled, May had won it. He had even less reason to worry now.

With everyone present, the performance round began. The first few entrants finished their acts to applause. May was fourth.

She brought out Squirtle, just as she had rehearsed. The instant it emerged from its Poke Ball, before it could land, Squirtle drew its head and limbs into its shell. It spun through the air, firing Ice Beam as it turned. Faster and faster it spun, becoming a dazzling top.

When Squirtle finally landed and bowed to the crowd, countless clear ice crystals fell around it. They glittered beneath the lights. The audience cheered for the entrance.

May had more planned. Squirtle released a cloud of bubbles and formed one enormous bubble at the center. It jumped onto the giant bubble and struck it with Ice Beam. The burst became a great flower-shaped formation of ice spikes across the stage. Squirtle landed steadily atop it.

In the front row, Ethan applauded with the other spectators. May and Squirtle were better than they had been before. Squirtle had joined her recently, yet May had helped it find confidence. It no longer feared the stage and could show its skill with openness and flair. Both had grown quickly. May really was made to be a Coordinator.

An act like that would easily carry her into the second round.

After May came the office worker who had nearly arrived late. Lilian had introduced him as Jeremy. He was about forty, short and a little heavyset, with an honest face. In his ordinary gray suit, he looked like any unremarkable man one might pass on a street or train.

Silver Town was small, and Jeremy was local. Many spectators knew him and saw him regularly. Recalling his fall, they chuckled kindly and waited to see what he would do.

The stage lights dimmed. To a burst of electric guitar, a man strode out with hair stiff as a broom, dark sunglasses, a leather jacket, leather gloves, leather pants, leather shoes, and an electric guitar in hand. He looked like a rebellious rocker.

Who was he? That seemed to be everyone's question. Only Ethan, the director, and Lilian knew: this was Jeremy, transformed. His whole manner differed so much from the mild office worker's that he seemed like another man. When the audience realized it, jaws dropped.

He had more surprises in store. Jeremy released Butterfree and launched into rapid guitar playing. Butterfree used Poison Powder, then Stun Spore. Great purple and orange clouds spread across the stage. It used Whirlwind to scatter them farther, then Safeguard. Rainbow light appeared in an instant, turning the powders into something like brilliantly colored clouds.

The display stunned the spectators. Butterfree's beauty showed through the combination of moves.

Then an interruption came. A woman and a boy appeared below the stage and stopped Jeremy's performance. His wife and son tried to keep him from pursuing his dream. With May's help, Jeremy spoke honestly from the heart. The crowd, already moved by his act, rose and applauded. In the end, his family gave him their support.

It was a small incident, yet it made the otherwise ordinary Contest feel more meaningful.

Jeremy and his family left the stage to the audience's encouragement. The Contest resumed, and the remaining entrants performed. May and Jeremy were among four Coordinators who advanced to the battle round.

Large city Contests often sent eight people through. With fewer entrants at a small-town event, four was enough. There would be fewer battles, though no less excitement.

The matchups appeared on the big screen. As though the anime's story had a hand in the draw, May and Jeremy did not face each other immediately. Both beat their separate opponents with little trouble and met in the final.

To Ethan, the outcome seemed to hold little mystery. He knew what May and Combusken could do, especially after yesterday's practice. It felt like watching a film whose ending he already knew.

For everyone else, it was a gripping match. May and Jeremy each recognized the other as a serious opponent.

May sent out Combusken. Jeremy brought out a Venusaur larger than most of its kind. Both Pokemon had performed well in their previous battles. Combusken had the type advantage, giving May an apparent edge.

But a Contest Battle was about more than type matchups. How beautifully a move was used mattered too, leaving room for surprises. Jeremy's huge Venusaur had imposing strength and could not be dismissed.

Still, Ethan knew how the match would end. Venusaur showed its power at the start. Its Vine Whip broke apart Combusken's Fire Spin despite the unfavorable typing. It even used the formidable Grass-type move Frenzy Plant, pushing Combusken into a dangerous position.

After yesterday's training, though, Combusken was harder to corner. With May urging and directing it, it fought back. It set the plants covering the stage alight and finished Venusaur with Sky Uppercut.

May had won without the desperate reversal Ethan remembered from the anime. Combusken had answered Venusaur more calmly. It had never beaten Eevee during their later practice rounds, but the experience and lessons from those bouts were real. They helped it defeat Venusaur and earn May another Ribbon.

The victory brought less applause than Ethan expected. The audience was not lacking in enthusiasm. After Jeremy's moving reconciliation with his family, many had hoped to see him win and fulfill his dream.

Competitions could be cruel that way. Jeremy had a reason to want the victory. May had her own determination not to lose.

Chapter 829: A Surprising Outdoor Battlefield

May won the Silver Town Contest and earned her second Ribbon in Kanto.

When Ethan had traveled with Sabrina, Erika, or Misty, his own adventure had always come first. His companions had arranged their journeys around him. With May beside him, he would have to make time for Contests like this one. On the face of it, that took time away from his travels.

In truth, he was glad to take part as a spectator. Watching from a different perspective gave him fresh insights, helped him grow, and let him learn things from the Coordinators that he might never have encountered otherwise.

He had no role to play in the Contest, but that made it both a rest and a chance to relax. There was value in balancing effort with leisure.

As for Jeremy, the man May had defeated, he changed back into the honest-looking office worker after the Contest and left the hall with a faintly lonely air.

He had not won or quite fulfilled his dream, but at least he had gained his family's acceptance. That was a great deal in itself. Perhaps they would meet him again at another Contest someday.

That could wait. With May's victory behind them, it was time to continue their journey.

They had bought their tickets the day before, so they did not return to the Pokemon Center after leaving the Contest hall. They waited at the docks, boarded a small passenger ship, and set off from the Kanto mainland.

As planned, they were bound for Metallica Island, not far from Cinnabar Island and home to the Battle Palace. The voyage would take much longer than a few hours through the complicated sea routes.

The three-deck ship pulled slowly away from the pier. A little over an hour after leaving Silver Town, they could make out Vermilion City in the distance. The ship did not stop there. As the sun went down, it left the coastal waters for the open sea.

Out there, the view was much the same. The water was bluer and the air saltier and more damp. Instead of a long mainland coastline, there were islands scattered around them.

The novelty of being at sea soon wore off. Passengers stopped staring at the unchanging water and found other things to do.

Even on a ship this small, a Pokemon battle was inevitable. Two boys who could not yet have been ten were directing their Pokemon across the deck, enjoying themselves immensely. Their unpolished match drew a few adults over to watch.

Ethan had no interest in looking. He lay back in a deck chair and enjoyed the last sea breeze before sunset. May sat beside him, studying a map and chatting with him now and then.

A school of Arrokuda swam up from somewhere in the surrounding sea and leaped alongside the ship. Then someone suddenly shouted, It's Lugia!

The cry drew most of the passengers to the rail. They looked out over the water and did indeed catch a glimpse of a silver shape passing beneath the surface. It was partly submerged; though it looked like Lugia, no one could be sure what it was.

That was enough to excite them. Marveling at their luck, the tourists took out their phones to film it.

May went over for a look too. When she returned, Ethan was still lying in his chair, his eyes closed and his expression unmoved. She could not help smiling.

Ethan, she asked quietly as she sat down, did you ever see Lugia while you were traveling through Kanto and Johto?

Of course. I've seen more than one. His tone did not change, as though a Legendary Pokemon like Lugia could no longer interest him. It's just a big water bird. Once you've seen enough of them, there's nothing particularly special about it.

He was showing off now, even if he made it sound casual. Then again, he had the experience to back it up.

A strong wind rose after dark, churning the waves and rocking the little ship. The weather made it easy to wonder whether the vessel could withstand it. For a frequent traveler like Ethan, though, the motion only helped him sleep.

They spent the night aboard and reached their destination early the next morning.

From a distance, Metallica Island looked like an ordinary large island covered in greenery. Ethan did not know where its name came from. Did it have rich metal deposits? Or did it have many Pokemon with bodies as hard as metal?

He had found no explanation on the map. It hardly mattered. He had come to challenge the Battle Frontier, not investigate the island's name.

They disembarked at a tiny town. Their ship sailed away almost as soon as they left the dock. With its noisy horn gone, the surroundings fell so quiet that it felt as if they stood inside an isolated primeval forest.

Perhaps few people came here apart from the occasional challenger. Even the town seemed deserted. Ethan and May stopped briefly at the Pokemon Center outside it, then followed their map toward the mysterious Battle Palace.

The walk was less peaceful than they expected. Dense forest covered nearly the entire island and sheltered all kinds of wild Pokemon. With so little human disturbance, the Pokemon were fiercely territorial. Ethan and May were attacked several times despite merely passing through.

The Beedrill were especially numerous and aggressive. They harried the pair for a long stretch of the path. In the end, Ethan brought out Scizor and Dragonite to escort them, and only then did they reach the Battle Palace without further trouble.

Palace was hardly the best word for it. It looked more like a ruin.

An imposing tower of neatly stacked stone rose among the trees, built in a style that seemed foreign to the region. Moss covered its steps, blocks, walls, and stonework. Parts had crumbled. There was no telling how many years it had stood here or why anyone had built it in this forest.

Scott clearly had not paid to build this place. Perhaps its history had something to do with the Frontier Brain who lived here.

Ethan and May had only just climbed the steps when an old man came out of the ruins. He looked to be in his seventies or eighties, with a round bald head, white eyebrows and beard, a bare chest, unusual tattoos on his arms, and a staff in his hand.

More challengers have come to my door. Welcome.

Despite his age, the man was full of vigor. He moved easily and spoke in a strong, ringing voice. Sunlight even flashed off his bald head.

His distinctive appearance let Ethan recognize him at once: Spenser, the Frontier Brain of the Battle Palace. Ethan knew his name, but little else. He did not know which Pokemon Spenser used or how he liked to battle.

You must be Mr. Spenser, Ethan said. Since the Frontier Brain had already guessed their purpose, he went straight to it. My name is Ethan. As you said, I've come to challenge the Battle Palace.

There is only one reason people cross the sea and brave the waves to get here. Spenser smiled. I am Spenser. Whenever I see a young trainer like you, with sharp eyes and so much spirit, I'm glad to know the next generation of Pokemon Trainers is in good hands.

Even from those few words, Ethan could feel an elder's concern for someone younger. It fit the impression Spenser gave him: a wise, generous old man.

Spenser glanced up at the bright sky. I can see confidence in your eyes, and that's good. I'll meet your challenge with everything I have. But on such a fine day, why battle indoors? Would you like to have our match outside?

There it was. Although Spenser phrased it as a question, his tone made his preference plain. Ethan remembered the outdoor battle from the anime. It was the true test of the Battle Palace.

That suited him. He had been worried the challenge would be too easy. An interesting new kind of match appealed to him far more than a dull indoor battle.

Of course, Ethan said without hesitation. The air here is wonderful, and you can really feel the natural world around you. I'd like to breathe more of it.

Spenser smiled at his agreement. Staff in hand, he led them away from the Palace.

At first May assumed outside meant a clearing near the building. But Spenser kept walking, and she began to wonder where he was taking them.

After more than ten minutes she quickened her steps to walk beside Ethan. Where do you think he's taking us? she whispered.

Who knows? Ethan shrugged, then joked, At least he won't take me off the island.

They crossed a stretch of forest. The ground began to climb sharply, and before May quite realized it, they were ascending a modest mountain.

At the summit, the landscape opened around them. They could finally see the whole Battle Palace, though the trees and vegetation hid most of it and left only its outline visible.

May stopped to catch her breath and took in the hilltop. It looked as if someone, or some Pokemon, had sliced away half the mountain with tremendous force. The flat top had been made into a simple battle arena. A cool sea breeze reached them there, lending the air a chill despite the sunshine.

So this was what Spenser meant by an outdoor battle. They had certainly come a long way for it.

May was impressed by the old man's stamina. She and Ethan were young and used to traveling, yet the climb had left her breathless. Spenser was far older and had reached the top without even looking winded.

Then he gave her a still greater surprise. Spenser pointed first at the ground beneath them, then toward a distant coastline, and finally to a winding river on the other side.

This arena is where our battle begins, he told Ethan. From that coast to the river, the entire forest is our outdoor battlefield.

What? May blurted out. All of it?

It was hard to blame her. The area Spenser had marked with two casual gestures was enormous. By her estimate, it covered at least a third of Metallica Island.

Yes, all of it. Spenser nodded to May, then turned an approving gaze on Ethan.

The young man had remained calm from the moment they met. Even after seeing the full extent of the battlefield, his expression had not changed. Compared with earlier challengers, his composure was remarkable.

Ethan did not know the impression he had made. He simply studied the boundaries Spenser had indicated, fixed them in his memory, and nodded.

A larger arena and more complicated terrain were nothing to be alarmed about. When he had battled Legendary Pokemon, the sky and the earth themselves had been the battlefield. Why should this scale shock him?

With the battlefield explained, Spenser set out the rules. We will have a three-on-three elimination battle. Defeat all three of my Pokemon and you win. You may switch your Pokemon freely during the match and choose whichever lineup best serves you.

May still had a question. Since Ethan said nothing, she asked, Um, Grandpa Spenser, with a battlefield this large, won't we lose sight of the Pokemon as they fight? How will anyone decide the result?

Spenser laughed and beckoned. A small flying robot appeared before May, hovering in the air.

Don't worry. This is the Battle Palace's referee robot. Its camera will let us follow the Pokemon and see how they're doing wherever they go!

Chapter 830: Three-on-Three Survival Battle

May had not expected a place as ancient-looking as the Battle Palace to have such advanced technology. Still, the referee robot would make things convenient.

If that's how we watch the battle, she asked, how do we give our Pokemon commands?

Spenser stroked his long beard with a chuckle. We don't. In a forest this vast, they must win without their Trainers directing them. Their own abilities will decide the battle!

No commands? The Pokemon would fight as they pleased?

Ethan touched his chin. Why did that sound so familiar? Wait. Wasn't that exactly what he was good at?

With May's questions answered, Spenser was about to head for the Trainers' area on the other side of the arena. Ethan stopped him.

One moment, Mr. Spenser.

Spenser turned. What is it?

It's rare to find a battlefield this large. Could we change the rules a little? Ethan asked with a smile.

Spenser and May both looked at him in surprise. Change the rules? Did Ethan think the challenge was too difficult? May could hardly believe that.

Of course, Spenser said. What did you have in mind?

Ethan glanced at the broad expanse below the mountain. On such a large, complicated battlefield, sending out only one Pokemon apiece would be dull. Why play three separate rounds? Let's send out all three at once and let them fight throughout the forest. Whichever side still has Pokemon standing at the end wins the challenge.

Some people would have recognized the idea immediately: the famous survival format. The teams would battle across difficult terrain until one side was left standing. It suited this setting perfectly.

Spenser blinked in surprise. But that means committing everything at once. You'd have no chance to change your lineup.

All the better. Ethan spread his hands. It would test the Pokemon both individually and as a team. Isn't that fitting for a battle in the wild?

Spenser considered the proposal, then nodded. If you've thought it through, I have no objection.

With the rules settled, they took their places in the opposing Trainers' areas.

As the Frontier Brain, Spenser released his Pokemon first. He drew three Poke Balls from his clothes and threw them together. Blue light flashed, and Shiftry, Claydol, and Venusaur appeared on the arena.

Only a moment later, Ethan threw his own three Poke Balls. Scizor, Metagross, and Dragonite emerged.

Dragonite and Scizor had long been mainstays of Ethan's teams in Johto and Hoenn. They might not have reached the very pinnacle of strength, but they could compete at the level of League champions. Metagross had grown quickly too and was still improving. By sending all three out together, Ethan made clear his determination to win this forest battle.

Metagross remained as cold and impassive as a stone. Dragonite and Scizor, however, took on a fiercer air the instant they appeared and glared at their opponents.

Shiftry and Venusaur glared back. Even so, beside Dragonite's enormous eyes and comically intense expression, they seemed to lose something in the contest of intimidation.

The flying referee robot moved to the center of the arena. Once both sides were ready, its starting light changed from red to green.

All six Pokemon moved at once.

With so many combatants and so much ground to cover, there was little use calculating type advantages now.

None of the Pokemon was particularly fast, but Dragonite had wings. It reached Spenser's side of the arena first, dodged two lashes of Venusaur's Vine Whip, and swooped low into Shiftry, knocking it toward the cliff.

Shiftry managed to grab Dragonite as it was sent flying. Instead of tumbling over the edge, it was carried with Dragonite out above the distant forest.

Scizor and Venusaur clashed next. Neither Razor Leaf nor Vine Whip could get past Scizor's huge pincers. The closer Scizor came, the more trouble Venusaur was in.

Claydol moved to help, but Metagross struck with psychic power before it could intervene. Claydol had to deal with its own opponent.

As promised, neither Trainer interfered. Ethan, Spenser, and May could only watch.

They did not all watch in the same way. Ethan stood with his hands in his pockets, calmly observing as if the battle had nothing to do with him. May and Spenser followed it with fierce concentration.

Ethan had asked May to watch from his point of view and see what she could learn. She kept her eyes wide, unwilling to miss a detail that might help her in her own battles.

Spenser had never presided over a battle quite like this one. Six Pokemon were fighting across an enormous arena. Energetic as he was, it was difficult for a man his age to keep up with all of them at once.

Ethan watched with easy trust. May and Spenser watched with tension.

With no boundary to keep it on the hilltop, Venusaur chose not to stand and struggle against Scizor. It turned and ran down the mountain into the forest. That was its own territory; a Grass-type Pokemon could draw more strength from fighting among the trees.

Scizor pursued it without hesitation.

Only two or three minutes after the start, Metagross and Claydol were the last Pokemon left in the starting arena. Before long, their own fight carried them off the summit too.

Ethan, May, and Spenser stood alone. From the forest below came the occasional sound of battle.

Now the referee robot came into its own. It flew down into the trees, and a separate screen beside the Trainers showed the view from its camera.

There was only one robot. It could not follow every fight, so the screen showed only Metagross and Claydol, the last pair to leave the hilltop. At least the three spectators could focus on one contest.

Onscreen, the two Pokemon floated among the trees, weaving through the forest and trading attacks as they went.

Metagross was Steel and Psychic type; Claydol was Ground and Psychic type. Neither pairing gave an obvious overall advantage. Either could win on paper. In a real battle, though, their condition, composure, and experience mattered more than a calculation of types.

Spenser's Claydol was strong. So was Ethan's Metagross, hardened by Pokemon League competition. Without either Trainer directing them, they fought to a standstill. Of the three clashes taking place across the forest, this was the closest.

Ethan could not see Dragonite or Scizor. But explosions from their moves rang through the trees, followed now and then by the crash of falling trunks. He was confident both of his Pokemon had the upper hand. He knew what they could do.

Then an explosion thundered across almost the entire island. They turned to see a brilliant light flare in one part of the forest, bathing a great stretch of trees in green.

None of the three was new to battling. They could guess what had happened.

Was that two moves colliding? May asked.

Probably Venusaur's Solar Beam meeting Scizor's X-Scissor, Ethan said.

Solar Beam and X-Scissor? May knew both moves, and knew how far apart their raw power was. That Scizor could use X-Scissor to cancel a Solar Beam astonished her. Bug-type moves were strong against Grass types, but the matchup alone could not account for what she had seen. Scizor's own strength was unmistakable.

Spenser's eyes widened slightly too. He looked at Ethan again. He did not follow news from elsewhere closely and knew nothing of the young man's past. He could still sense the tremendous power of Ethan's Pokemon.

What a remarkable young Trainer. No wonder he had been confident enough to send all three Pokemon out at once and leave them to fight without orders. The challengers Spenser had met before seemed to be on another level entirely.

The area where the light had flared fell silent. One Pokemon must have been defeated. Most likely it was Spenser's Venusaur.

It had happened quickly. Only a dozen or so minutes had passed. In an ordinary arena, that might have been a fight of average length. On this sprawling battlefield, with all the travel through difficult terrain, it felt as though the battle had barely begun.

Before Spenser could reflect further, another great blast sounded. The three looked toward the coast, where Dragonite and Shiftry had been fighting.

That clash had been every bit as fierce as Scizor's. A wide swath of trees had fallen, and spray rose from the sea. Then, just as before, the noise stopped after the explosion. From the hilltop, no one could see what had happened.

Ethan expected Dragonite had won. He was not underestimating Spenser's Pokemon. He simply knew that Dragonite and Scizor had earned his trust.

May's delight showed on her face. Spenser quietly looked away and returned his attention to the screen. Metagross and Claydol were now the only pair still fighting.

Perhaps their struggle was too loud, or perhaps they had crossed into another Pokemon's territory. In the midst of their battle, a swarm of Beedrill burst from the trees and attacked both of them indiscriminately.

The interruption took all three spectators by surprise. Spenser shook his head with a rueful smile.

Well, that's unfortunate. The wild Pokemon here are very territorial. Usually they're an obstacle for challengers. Today I've brought the trouble on myself, and my own Pokemon is their target. There's some irony in that.

Ethan could picture how it normally worked. Beedrill lived throughout the forest and attacked intruders, adding another unpredictable hazard to an already complicated battlefield. Today three fights were taking place at once, with explosions powerful enough to anger the swarms. They had come out to find whoever was responsible, regardless of whose territory the fighters were in.

The battle had become more difficult. Individually, the Beedrill were not especially strong, but there were enough of them to make the swarm alarming.

Metagross and Claydol might have looked more like stone and clay than ordinary animals or people, but they were not foolish. Neither stayed to face so many Beedrill. Both broke away and fled back along the route they had taken through the forest.

Chapter 831: I Think I Can Beat You

More Beedrill kept joining the swarm. Before long, there were two or three hundred of them. Even from a distance, the hum of their wings was audible.

According to a study someone had once done on the dangers people most dreaded encountering in the wild, a Beedrill swarm ranked near the top. These cold, aggressive forest hunters lived in colonies and could be deadly to a new Trainer or an ordinary traveler who wandered into their territory.

Metagross and Claydol were being pursued, but Ethan, May, and Spenser held to the rule they had agreed on. None of them interfered or offered help. They watched to see what would happen.

Either Pokemon could have driven off the Beedrill easily if it had been free to concentrate on them. Instead, each had to watch for attacks from its opponent while avoiding being surrounded. The danger multiplied.

Even so, they were not merely fleeing. They struck back as they retreated. The situation was unfavorable, but neither seemed in immediate peril.

The fight drew closer to the hill. The buzz of Beedrill wings grew clearer. Ethan and Spenser kept their composure, while May grew visibly tense.

She could not face a threat like this without concern. She knew Ethan was beside her and would take care of it if things went wrong, but she still measured her own abilities against the swarm. Combusken, Squirtle, and Munchlax together could not have held off so many Beedrill. If Ethan had not been there, she would have hidden until they passed.

On the screen, Beedrill fell now and then, but their numbers scarcely seemed to diminish. Then a disturbance broke out on both sides of the pursuing swarm. The referee robot swung its camera around.

Dragonite and Scizor had arrived. They must have heard the battle and hurried over. Their presence also confirmed what Ethan had expected: each had won its own fight.

With those two powerful Pokemon joining in, the situation changed at once. Beedrill fell in great numbers. The rest saw the danger and fled; in moments, the swarm was gone. It had arrived quickly and departed faster still.

Only the unconscious Beedrill on the ground and the damaged trees showed that a battle had taken place.

With the swarm gone, Metagross and Claydol stopped retreating and faced each other again. Dragonite and Scizor approached, and Claydol grew uneasy. It could feel how much stronger these Pokemon were than the wild Beedrill. Metagross alone had matched it; two more opponents would be overwhelming.

Dragonite and Scizor had no interest in ganging up on it. They stopped a short distance away and left enough room for the other two to continue their battle.

Spenser looked at Ethan with fresh respect. When the young man proposed a three-on-three free-for-all, Spenser had assumed he meant to concentrate his forces on one of Spenser's Pokemon, gain a numbers advantage, and win from there.

Apparently, that had never been the plan. Ethan simply found three separate one-on-one matches too troublesome and preferred to send everyone out at once. Dragonite and Scizor's refusal to attack Claydol made that clear. The younger generation could be formidable indeed.

Seeing that they were only blocking its escape routes, Claydol put Dragonite and Scizor out of mind and focused entirely on Metagross.

Claydol was one of Spenser's main partners and had been with him for years. Metagross had performed impressively at the Ever Grande Conference but had not made Ethan's first-string team. Ethan judged them to be on much the same level, and their battle bore that out.

They resumed fighting as evenly as before. No contest could remain tied forever, though. Both fired Hyper Beam, and the two blasts met in the forest. When the explosion cleared, the result was plain on the screen: Metagross and Claydol lay amid the debris, both battered and unconscious. They had knocked each other out.

It was a surprise, yet it made sense. Ethan's Pokemon were powerful in their own right, but his judgment and commands were a major reason they won so often. Without his guidance, Metagross had to rely on its own considerable abilities. Holding Spenser's Claydol to a draw was a good result.

Ethan was satisfied. May shook her head slightly, disappointed that Metagross had not managed a clear victory. Spenser had his own regret that Claydol could not stay standing. At least it had defeated an opponent; he had not lost all three without an answer.

Well, I managed to take one of your Pokemon down, Spenser said lightly. Perhaps this old man hasn't lost his touch!

He had nearly suffered a complete defeat, but his spirits were as good as ever.

More than that, Ethan said with a smile. Your Pokemon is truly strong. Mine had to give everything it had just to reach a draw with Claydol. I still have work to do.

Spenser laughed. Many challengers had fallen to his Claydol, and he knew its strength better than anyone. Dragonite and Scizor had plainly been stronger than Metagross. If one of his main partners had only tied with a Pokemon outside Ethan's leading lineup, Spenser understood the difference between them. If Ethan kept improving, even that less favored Pokemon might become more than Spenser could handle.

The referee robot began retrieving Spenser's fallen Pokemon. He had given it their Poke Balls at the start of the match. It recalled Claydol first, then flew off to find Shiftry and Venusaur.

Dragonite picked up the unconscious Metagross. With Scizor beside it, it headed back toward the starting arena.

After a few more words with Ethan, Spenser placed a gleaming gold Symbol in his hand.

Please accept this. It's the Battle Palace's Spirits Symbol, proof that you defeated me.

Like Ethan's earlier Symbols, it was made of gold. Its design was rather plain: a square block marked with grooves.

...

Ethan and May returned from the Battle Palace to the quiet town on Metallica Island. The challenge had gone more smoothly than they expected. It was only noon.

Ethan had barely felt involved. He had watched the whole contest while his Pokemon fought on their own, and they had earned him another Frontier Symbol. Of all the Battle Frontier facilities he had challenged, this one had been the easiest for him.

That did not mean it would be easy for anyone else. Defeating Spenser's Pokemon without giving a single command would be difficult for most Trainers. Ethan's team had often fought independently and had been trained by that experience. Ash or another challenger might have struggled badly.

A win was a win, and the journey had been worthwhile. He had seen spectacular scenery too. Now it was time for their next destination.

Metallica Island's remoteness presented a problem. When Ethan asked at the little dock, he learned that the next passenger ship would not arrive for three days. Getting here had been easy; leaving was another matter.

He brought out his second flying mount. Dragonite appeared before him and May again. It had just fought a battle, but the difference in strength had kept it from taking any injuries. Its time resting in its Poke Ball had restored its energy as well.

Thanks for helping us again, May said with a smile. Ethan helped her onto Dragonite's back, then climbed up behind her. Once they were both settled, Dragonite beat its small wings and rose high into the sky.

The breeze felt pleasant, and May narrowed her eyes in contentment. As Dragonite leveled out, she looked back. Metallica Island was shrinking beneath them and soon fell far behind.

It had been some time since Ethan last traveled through the air. He had had two flying mounts on his journey. The first was Charizard, now far away in the Charicific Valley. The second was Dragonite beneath him.

They flew differently. Charizard felt powerful and steady when carrying Ethan, though it could not match Dragonite's speed. Dragonite was livelier, rising and dipping as it pleased and often skimming the water. Neither was a better flyer; each had its own style.

Their next destination was near Fuchsia City, not terribly far from Metallica Island. Dragonite was much faster than a ship, but by the time dusk approached they still had not reached the mainland. They landed on a nearby island to find somewhere to spend the night.

Fortunately, this island was larger and more prosperous than Metallica Island, perhaps because it lay closer to the mainland. It had less forest and more mountains. Its town was bigger, with more people, cleaner streets, and a lively air.

Dragonite came down in the town. Ethan and May asked some residents where they were. The island was Potpourri Island, and the town was Wisteria Town, one of the largest settlements in the surrounding waters.

They also heard that a Pokemon Orienteering competition would be held the following morning. It was an occasional event in which a person and a Pokemon partnered up and raced through five locations around the island. The first team to reach the finish would win a Teamwork Medal and a prize of Potpourri Island's famous fruit.

An orienteering race? Local fruit? The mention of food immediately caught May's interest.

Their timing was fortunate. If the Palace challenge had taken longer, they would not have reached Potpourri Island on the eve of the race, and they would have missed it altogether.

They followed the streets to the Pokemon Center outside town. Adults and children alike were talking about tomorrow's competition, making May even more eager to enter.

At dinner, she finally said it aloud. Ethan, let's take part in the orienteering race tomorrow!

Ethan chuckled. Is it the medal you're after, or that local fruit?

May gave a sheepish grin, but admitted it freely. I want both! I heard this isn't a test of battling strength. It's just a race across the island. That means I have a chance to beat you!

Chapter 832: A Pokemon Marathon

Ethan shook his head, amused and a little helpless at May's declaration.

So you want to compete against me, he said with a smile. I wasn't planning to enter, but if you're challenging me, let's see how we do. Beating me won't be easy. Tomorrow I'll show you that experience counts for something!

They laughed and talked over dinner, imagining what the next day's race might be like. Then Ethan's phone rang. He checked the screen and saw a name he had not expected: Anabel.

Why would she call now? Several possibilities crossed his mind, and then he began to suspect the reason. He gestured to May, got up, and went to an empty corner before answering.

Anabel's familiar voice came through. Without much small talk, she asked, I hear you've returned to Kanto and started challenging its Battle Frontier?

Those people had sharp noses for news. Ethan was not surprised she knew what he was doing. Perhaps he had even told her himself before; he could not remember after so long.

That's right. I've already won several Symbols, he said. Is something wrong?

Anabel took a breath. Her voice turned solemn. What I'm about to tell you may sound unbelievable, but please trust me. Every word of it is true.

The more seriously she spoke, the more certain Ethan became of his guess.

Don't worry. I've seen plenty of unbelievable things. Tell me.

As he spoke, he glanced across the room. May was sitting where he had left her, happily absorbed in her meal. He smiled to himself.

There's a Battle Tower in Kanto's Battle Frontier, Anabel began. Its Frontier Brain is also named Anabel. In a sense, she and I are the same person.

She paused, perhaps listening for a reaction. Ethan offered only attentive silence. His lack of surprise impressed her, and she went on.

I don't mean that I secretly run the Battle Tower while working for the International Police. In one sense that description comes close, but the truth is that there are two of us in this world.

To someone who knew nothing of the matter, her explanation would have sounded contradictory. Ethan had known about it for some time.

So there are two Anabels living in the same world, he said.

Yes. Now she sounded more surprised than he did. Doesn't that shock you?

This Pokemon world is full of mysteries. I've seen too many to be startled by one more. You might not know this, but I'm something of a miracle myself.

He had spoken the truth as if it were a joke, the surest way to make it unbelievable. Anabel assumed he meant the things he had accomplished on his journey or the Legendary Pokemon he had caught. She paid the remark little attention.

She had no idea that Ethan, like her, had come from another worldone he thought of as much more real.

I see. That puts me at ease. Anabel exhaled. A few years ago, I passed through a strange space called an Ultra Wormhole and came here from another world. I became what the International Police call a Faller, and I lost my memories of the past. Later I joined the International Police and eventually reached my present position. That's why I said the Anabel here and I seem to be one person, yet strictly speaking we aren't.

A Faller was the International Police's term for a person carrying energy from Ultra Space. Passing through an Ultra Wormhole left that energy on a traveler. Ultra Beasts sensed it and pursued such people, attacking them. Once the International Police learned of this, they recruited Fallers to serve as bait in hunts for Ultra Beasts.

Anabel was one of those people. But her skill and record had carried her far beyond that role. Her achievements grew, she rose through the ranks, and she eventually became a regional leader.

When she first joined, she had worked under Looker. Her diligence earned her a promotion until she became his superior instead. The reversal had bothered Looker for a long time. Whenever it came up, he sighed over it.

Looker's feelings aside, crossing worlds was Anabel's greatest secret, bound up with classified matters such as the Ultra Wormholes. If she could tell Ethan now, the International Police must hold him in high regard. It also meant she had a pressing reason.

Let me guess, Ethan said. You're telling me because you want me to keep it secret when I reach the Battle Tower.

Exactly. Anabel laughed a little. You're easy to work with. As I said, my arrival here is highly classified even within the International Police. The Anabel of this world knows nothing about it. When you meet her, please act as though you've never met me. Don't make her suspicious.

Why not tell her? Ethan asked.

It's complicated. Anabel gave a rueful laugh. Suppose someone identical to you appeared one day and said they'd come from another dimension, or from a world a few years in the future. How would you feel?

Uncomfortable, I think. Ethan tried to put himself in that position. We might have the same name and face, perhaps even similar memories. Living alongside someone who looked like my reflection and knew all my secrets would be unsettling. Sooner or later, it would cause trouble.

That's it. Anabel sighed. More than anything, learning about me could irreversibly disrupt the life of the woman I used to beor rather, the version of me in this parallel world. We have to keep it from her and deal with the Ultra Wormhole incident as quickly as we can.

Ethan did not press her further. I understand. When I meet the Anabel at the Battle Tower, I won't give her any reason to think I know you.

He ended the call and returned to May. She tactfully did not ask who had called or why he had been away so long. Instead, she picked up their earlier conversation and talked eagerly about tomorrow's race.

...

The event's full name was Pokemon Orienteering. Each contestant would team up with a Pokemon and visit five designated places on the island. Whoever completed the route in the shortest time would win.

Similar races were held from time to time in Kanto and other regions. Their spectacle and unpredictability had made them popular, almost a third major form of competition beside Pokemon League tournaments and Contests. Ethan thought of them as a Pokemon version of the marathons held on Earth.

There was no single organizer for all these events, so the prizes varied. On Potpourri Island, the main award was a Pokemon Teamwork Medal, accompanied by a great quantity of the island's famous fruit.

The fruit sounded like a modest extra, but it was the finest harvest the island produced at this time of year. Plump and delicious, it was a special prize that money could not buy. It represented the island's abundant harvest, too. Many locals entered for the fruit rather than the medal. May was not the only food lover drawn to it.

After breakfast the next morning, Ethan and May left the Pokemon Center and stepped onto the grass outside. Nearly a hundred people had gathered: contestants, their friends and families, and even more spectators.

Ceremonial salutes fired into the air, bursting into clouds of smoke. A short distance ahead stood a red arch marked START. It served as both the beginning and the finish of the race.

They had registered the night before. Now they slipped into the group of contestants like any other entrants.

Nurse Joy handed a map and a compass to each of them. When she had finished, she addressed the crowd.

Everyone, please listen! The map shows five locations, each with a stamp. To complete the race, visit all five, stamp your map at each one, and return here. The fastest contestant wins this year's Pokemon Orienteering competition. You may use only your map and compass. Anyone caught using another aid or riding a Pokemon will be disqualified!

The crowd called back in acknowledgment. Ethan looked over his opponents. Men and women of every age had entered. The youngest appeared several years younger than May, while the oldest looked about as old as Spenser. Ethan wondered if all of them could really finish the course.

The entrants released their partner Pokemon. Flashes of blue light appeared all around. Ethan and May opened their Poke Balls too.

Unlike in the anime, May did not have an Eevee yet. The Egg she had received at the farm had not hatched. She chose Squirtle as her partner instead. Ethan brought out his own Eevee.

Among the other entrants were Oddish, Machop, Growlithe, Bellsprout, and many more. Most were young or inexperienced Pokemon, and evolved ones were rare. This really was a casual sport with a low barrier to entry, open to nearly anyone.

Once everyone was ready, the contestants gathered at the starting line. Spectators on either side of the course cheered them on. Ethan even spotted one or two television crews filming the scene.

A sharp whistle sounded. The race began.

People and Pokemon surged forward together. In the packed group, Ethan and May could not pass anyone or run at full speed. They kept an even pace with the crowd.

Fortunately, there was no fixed route. A little more than a hundred meters beyond the start, several paths branched away. The contestants could choose among them according to their own judgment.

The crowd split in several directions. In moments, more than half the people who had blocked Ethan and May's way were gone.

Ethan had studied the map as soon as Nurse Joy gave it to him and worked out a reasonably good route. He took the path on the far right without hesitation. May followed as though that were the obvious thing to do.

When he looked at her, she grinned. What? Is it strange? I said I was going to beat you. Of course I have to take the same route to race you!

Ethan knew she simply did not want to choose a route for herself, but he let it pass with a smile. He and Eevee gradually picked up speed.

Now the benefits of all his time on the road began to show. Young and fit, Ethan passed the runners ahead one after another and soon reached the leading group on their path.

May did not fall behind. She and Squirtle stayed half a step back, keeping close on his heels.

Chapter 833: Keeping Every Happy Memory

Neither Ethan nor May had entered a race like this before. It did not take long for them to realize that keeping up their present speed would be unwise.

The problem was not how quickly they were tiring. The path itself had grown difficult. After the paved stretch near the start, a narrow trail wound through the forest, overgrown with weeds and scattered with stones that could trip an unwary runner.

They had no choice but to slow from a fast run to a jog. Their Pokemon had energy to spare. Eevee and Squirtle even found time to play as they ran, though it was mostly the restless Eevee pestering Squirtle.

Otherwise, the race went smoothly. Their first destination was Lunatone Rock, on the eastern side of the island. According to the map, it stood on a high, rocky hill with a lookout over the whole island. A great stone statue of Lunatone marked the checkpoint.

At the foot of the hill, the slope steepened. Ethan and May finally pulled away from the other contestants on their route. Their years of travel showed: accompanied by Eevee and Squirtle, they climbed nimbly and soon left the runners behind.

At the summit they found the statue, several meters high. Ethan could not tell how old it was. Wind and sun had worn the stone until, from a distance, its surface really did resemble the face of the moon.

The stamp sat on a platform beside it. Short on time, they gave the view below only a quick glance, went to the platform, and marked both maps with the Lunatone stamp.

That was their first checkpoint complete. They took another path down the hill, and May glanced at Ethan with a smile.

Looks like we're tied so far.

His long legs helped him cover ground, but May took quicker steps. Each had an advantage, and she had kept pace with him all the way.

Don't get ahead of yourself, Ethan said. That was only the first checkpoint. The race has barely begun.

True. I wonder how everyone on the other routes is doing. If they finish ahead of us, that won't be good.

Unlike in the anime, Ash and his friends were not among the entrants, and the Team Rocket trio were not around to cause trouble. That seemed to remove some strong opponents and distractions. But Ethan and May were visitors. Local contestants might know shortcuts and trail conditions they did not. They still had to give the race their best effort.

They hurried downhill without stopping and headed straight for Rainbow Falls. It was the checkpoint farthest from the Pokemon Center, but from Lunatone Rock it lay conveniently along their route.

A waterfall poured from the mountains into a pool below. A lovely rainbow shone within the falling water and never seemed to fade, like a bridge made of color.

Remoraid were firing Water Gun to form arches of spray. Ethan and May ran beneath them to a platform at the foot of the falls, found the stamp, and put their second mark on their maps.

They encountered several other contestants there. Ethan could not tell which routes they had taken. Everyone looked hurried, and each team departed in a different direction. At least they all followed the rules; no one tried to hide the stamp. Perhaps the cameras installed somewhere around the course helped discourage that.

On another day, Ethan and May would have stopped to admire the waterfall. Today they left almost at once for the next checkpoint: a cape overlooking the sea.

To reach it, they followed the riverbank. Ahead lay a lookout facing the ocean, with two upright pillars of rock nearby. The stamp platform stood at one side of the lookout. They marked their maps with its Kingler design.

The cape was another beautiful sight, but they had no time to linger. They set off for the fourth checkpoint.

By now May's youth and shorter experience of traveling were catching up with her. After running so far, her energy was failing and her pace slowed visibly.

Ethan realized she was no longer beside him. He looked back. She followed in silence with her head down, sweat on her forehead and at her temples. She could not keep this pace much longer.

He slowed at once. When she caught up, he ran beside her again.

May looked up, surprised. She bit her lip. Why are you slowing down? This is your chance to get ahead of me.

How could I leave you here on your own? Ethan smiled. Winning a race and a pile of fruit matters less than the person I'm traveling with.

He had put friendship before competition in a single sentence. May was deeply touched, and her cheeks flushed.

From then on, she no longer cared about beating Ethan to the finish. She stayed beside him with a lighter, happier heart.
