For the rest of the course, he helped her over fallen logs and narrow crossings. They waded slowly through water together. When they grew hungry, they paused for energy bars. Though May was tired, Ethan's help kept her from falling farther behind.

There was a saying that work felt easier when a man and woman did it together. May did not know the phrase, but she felt its truth. With Ethan beside her, the race began to feel more like an outing in the wild. Her weariness seemed to lift, leaving her full of energy again.

In that mood they reached the fourth checkpoint, a giant tree three hundred years old. It was the tallest in the surrounding forest, its spreading branches thick with leaves and full of the presence of living nature. Beneath it they found the stamp and marked their maps.

Only one checkpoint remained. So far, everything had gone well. They knew nothing of the runners on the other routes, but no one on their own path had overtaken them. Even if they were not the fastest, they ought to be near the front.

Then they spotted Nurse Joy in the forest. Apparently she was competing too. She had helped organize and officiate the race, and now she was taking part in it herself.

They passed at a distance without calling out and continued toward the final checkpoint: a rope suspension bridge.

It spanned a deep river gorge. To reach the stamp, contestants had to slide down a long rope to the ground below, cross the hanging bridge, and reach a high stone pillar standing amid the river. The height and distance would be daunting to anyone afraid of heights.

Ethan and May were not troubled by it. They slid down the rope, landed lightly, and ran across the creaking, swaying bridge. At the pillar they pressed the fifth and final stamp onto their maps.

We did it! May lifted her right hand and jumped with delight.

Ethan watched her celebrate, smiling fondly. It's a little early to celebrate. Let's get back to the finish.

May stuck out her tongue in embarrassment. They could not let up at the last moment. She quieted down and followed him toward the Pokemon Center.

From some distance away, they could see a red ribbon stretched across the starting line. Crowds stood on both sides, apparently cheering for their return.

We might actually be first. That's lucky, Ethan said.

He had entered for fun, but a victory would make the day even more satisfying. May heard him and quietly eased her pace until she was half a step behind. She had wanted to compete with him before the race; now she was willing to give him the win.

Ethan reached back and drew her level with him.

What are you doing? he asked with a smile. Why hold back when we're almost there?

May understood. He wanted them to cross the line together, and the thought touched her even more.

Before, her feelings for Ethan had been a hazy admiration for his handsome face and his strength. Now his gentleness and consideration had won her over, much as they had won Misty over. They had not traveled together long, yet May was already falling for him.

She stopped hesitating and let him pull her along. With Eevee and Squirtle at their sides, Ethan and May broke the finish ribbon together.

A new record! Nurse Joy cried from beside the course. Somehow she had appeared there ahead of them. Three hours and twenty-four minutes! Since the Potpourri Island race began, no one has ever finished in under three and a half hours. And these two crossed at exactly the same time! Congratulations to both of you!

The spectators erupted in cheers. It might have been the first time they had seen two people finish together, and they studied the pair with curiosity.

May's face shone with happiness. She had hoped they would finish near the front. Breaking a record as well was a wonderful surprise. Surely no one could beat her and Ethan as a team.

She was pleased about the medals, too. It would be another honor to add to her Contest achievements, though the award was not what she cared about most. The plump, fragrant fruit was far more tempting.

May caught herself just before she began to drool.

A staff member came over to inspect their maps. After confirming all five stamps, he nodded to Nurse Joy. She smiled even more broadly, guided Ethan and May aside to rest, and returned to the finish to wait for the remaining contestants.

For Ethan and May, the race was over. It had added a bright memory to their long journey. For everyone else, it was still underway.

They waited more than two hours while the other teams gradually returned. Around noon, the oldest contestant reached the Pokemon Center with help from the staff. The Potpourri Island Pokemon Orienteering competition was finally complete.

Applause from Nurse Joy, the spectators, and the other entrants greeted Ethan and May as they stood together on the winners' podium. The event was held often enough that there were plenty of medals in storage, even though it had never produced two winners at once.

The fine fruit was another matter. It now had to be divided between two winners, and there did not seem to be enough to make two generous prizes. Fortunately, the winners were traveling together. Nurse Joy did not have to worry about how to divide the bounty between strangers.

She hung a gold Pokemon Teamwork Medal around each of their necks, then had the fruit brought over. Finally came the group photograph.

Eevee and Squirtle stood at either side. Ethan and May leaned close together, medals shining, and smiled toward the camera. With a click, the moment was captured.

The picture was printed almost immediately. May accepted it and studied the two of them, smiling so brightly and standing so close. They looked like a couple, she thought, even with their difference in age and height.

Her face reddened again. She gazed at the picture for a long while, smiling foolishly to herself, then carefully slipped it between the pages of the notebook she carried with her.

May's change of heart had reached its conclusion. Ethan had gained another devoted admirer.

Chapter 834: It Depends on What Munchlax Learned

In the open yard behind the Potpourri Island Pokemon Center, their Pokemon helped carry over the crates of fine fruit they had won in the orienteering race. After a quick wash, Ethan, May, and all their Pokemon sat in a circle and began a feast.

Some fruit looked like pineapples, some like apples, melons, pears, or grapes. They resembled familiar varieties, but there were differences Ethan could not name.

He picked up a pear-shaped fruit and took a small bite. It was sweet and so juicy it nearly overflowed. He could not think of a grand description for it. It was simply delicious. No wonder the island reserved fruit this good for its prizes.

May held a different fruit in each hand, biting first one and then the other. Happiness was written all over her face. She really did love food. They had worked hard and broken a record to win this meal; perhaps that made it taste even better.

Ethan finished his fruit and reached for another. His hand found an empty crate. He turned and discovered May's Munchlax sitting beside him. Somehow, in the short time they had been eating, it had emptied two large boxes by itself.

The contrast with his Gardevoir was striking. She ate in small, graceful bites, while Munchlax had swept through the fruit like a storm. Between May and her Pokemon, Ethan was surrounded by eager eaters.

He did not mind. He had only wanted to taste the fruit. His companions and their Pokemon mattered far more than whether he got another piece. He leaned back and watched them enjoy themselves.

There was no Team Rocket, Team Magma, or Team Aqua to fight now, and no mighty Legendary Pokemon looming over them. Their journey held only the Battle Frontier and Contests. Compared with the upheavals they had lived through, it might seem quiet. Ethan did not find it dull. These gentler days gave his life variety and let him gather strength for battles yet to come.

No one could fight constantly, however tough they were. This was closer to the everyday life of most ordinary Trainers. In a way, Ethan had returned to how his journey began.

...

After leaving the Pokemon Center, Ethan and May remained on Potpourri Island and visited its town, Wisteria Town, again. The orienteering race was not the only event taking place here. The Wisteria Town Contest would be held the next day.

It was excellent news for May. Another win would bring her closer to the Kanto Grand Festival. But her good mood lasted only until they reached the Contest hall. There she spotted a rival she could not stand: Harley.

Like the Silver Town Contest venue, Wisteria's hall was no great arena. It was a three-story building with a rounded base set on a lawn. A street of food stalls stood outside. At its entrance, they saw Harley.

He wore his familiar outfit and his usual sly smile. Ethan could not tell whether Harley had recovered the Pokemon the Team Rocket trio had tricked away from him, but he looked well enough. Ethan guessed he had, or he would hardly be here.

Harley saw May and instinctively took a few steps toward her, ready to taunt her or try another trick. Then he noticed Ethan at her side and stopped.

He had almost forgotten that May was no longer traveling with those easily fooled children. She was with this infuriating man now. After being thwarted by Ethan several times, Harley did not dare approach so casually. He resented Ethan and feared him too.

Harley glared at them from a distance and turned away. Privately, he resolved to make May lose badly today.

He had gone, but the sight of him weighed on May. She disliked admitting it, yet Harley was a strong Coordinator. His schemes were hard to anticipate, and his stage performances were strange and changeable. Apart from Drew, he was the most dangerous rival she had met. She could not treat him lightly. This Contest would be harder than the one in Silver Town.

You'll have to be careful, Ethan said. With me here, Harley won't get away with any underhanded schemes. But he's still an excellent performer. If you battle him, keep your guard up.

I know.

The unexpected encounter had spoiled May's desire to stroll around. After looking over the arena inside the hall, she and Ethan went to a nearby open space to plan her performance.

Ethan sat on a bench holding May's Egg. Which Pokemon will you use this time?

May had left her other Pokemon in Hoenn. For now, she had only Combusken, Squirtle, and Munchlax, along with the Egg that had not yet hatched. Her choices were limited. Combusken and Squirtle had already taken part in Contests. Naturally, she looked toward Munchlax.

Munchlax? Ethan followed her gaze and nodded. Good idea. It's time Munchlax got some experience and shared the work. To be safe, let's practice the way we did last time. I'll lend you one of my Pokemon.

He took Eevee's Poke Ball from his pouch and released it. May had considered using Combusken and Squirtle to train with Munchlax, but having Ethan's Eevee as a practice partner was even better.

With little time to spare, May took the Pokemon to the open ground and began training.

Watching her, Ethan suddenly felt as though he were playing a game in which he had to raise and guide a character. That character was May. He wondered how far she could grow in the end.

...

The next day, the Wisteria Town Contest began. The host and the judges were the same familiar faces. They were professionals, but seeing them at every Contest could make a spectator wonder whether anyone else ever filled those roles.

Ethan took a seat in the audience and watched from start to finish. The first few Coordinators performed well enough to open the event on a good note. Then May's turn came.

She chose Squirtle, not Munchlax, for the first-round appeal. Squirtle's confidence and strength had grown through its recent training, and it was becoming more accomplished onstage.

Squirtle combined Rapid Spin and Bubble Beam to create a splendid spiral of bubbles. It finished with Ice Beam, shattering the bubbles into a great fountain of ice. The polished display earned May a high score.

Ethan was impressed. Squirtle did not make a single mistake. May's talent was becoming more obvious with every performance. Before longperhaps by the end of the Kanto Grand Festivalshe could truly be a first-rate Coordinator.

After May left the stage, the excitement she had created seemed to lift the next few entrants. They performed better than expected and won applause, though none reached her level. Then Harley came out, and the atmosphere changed.

He used Ariados again, one of his most frequent choices. So he had recovered his Pokemon after all. Whatever the Team Rocket trio had tried, they evidently had not come out ahead against Harley.

Ariados wove a web like the one it had used against May before. That did not mean Harley had run out of ideas. Ariados climbed to the top and plunged down like a bungee jumper. With Scary Face, it became a terrifying, bandaged-looking spider, only the two dark spots on its back showing like eyes staring ahead.

Harley's style was as eerie as ever. Its distinctiveness still won applause and appreciation from most of the audience.

Several more Coordinators performed after him. Perhaps his act had left the hall in too strange a mood: their performances faltered, and the crowd's response grew cool. Ethan shook his head. As in a Pokemon battle, an outstanding Contest performance could make ordinary entrants look weaker and affect the audience watching them.

When the three judges finished scoring, the screen displayed the eight Coordinators advancing to the second round. May's portrait was first. She had earned the highest score in the appeal round.

It was a delightful result. May had once barely advanced in last place; now she was the leading Coordinator in the first round. Ethan had not witnessed every step of her growth, but he had accompanied her through several important moments. Seeing this achievement moved him.

The eight qualifiers were paired for the battle round. Unlike at the Saffron Contest, May and Harley were placed in separate brackets. Each defeated their other opponents and reached the final.

Another meeting that felt destined. It was no great surprise, though. Both were now far stronger than most entrants, and neither had faced another rival who could stop them. The final would show which of them was better.

They sent out their Pokemon. As agreed the day before, May used Munchlax in the battle round. Harley chose Octillery.

Munchlax had already appeared in May's earlier matches that round. It had battled splendidly, defeating its opponents with little difficulty and carrying her to the final.

Ethan had not seen Harley's Octillery in any previous battle or performance. Harley had probably caught it recently. Even so, he had clearly devoted care to its training; on its first Contest stage, it had performed extremely well.

Two Pokemon making their Contest debuts had both reached the final. What would happen when they met? Lilian presented the matchup as a mystery for the audience. Ethan, however, remembered the anime and the outcome it had shown.

Ordinarily, May's Munchlax would lose to Harley's Octillery. This time Ethan had intervened. During their practice battle the day before, without calling May's attention to it, he had made a point of training Munchlax to interrupt Rest.

Rest was Octillery's specialty. In the anime, it had recovered a great deal of health with the move, turned the battle around at a crucial moment, and defeated Munchlax.

Ethan could not guarantee that Munchlax had learned enough from one session. At least it would be less likely to freeze in confusion when Octillery tried Rest. Beyond that, the outcome depended on Munchlax's own judgment and talent.

With Ethan watching expectantly, the decisive battle began.

Chapter 835: How Did I Get Here?

Octillery was Remoraid's evolved form, but almost its entire body was red. People said it resembled the red octopuses of the eastern Pacific or the giant Pacific octopus. Others thought its shape and coloring might have been inspired by an octopus-shaped sausage.

Along with its soft body, it had a pair of rather vacant-looking eyes and a long, protruding mouth. An octopus also needed tentacles. Most of Octillery's extended behind it, while two longer ones reached forward. Each bore two round yellow suckers.

Ethan had spent time studying the Pokedex and had battled Octillery before. He knew they usually sheltered behind rocks or in caves on the seabed. They liked to squeeze into holes, dens, and even jars. They could spit ink to attack, steal other Pokemon's nests, and use their tough heads as weapons. Once their suckered tentacles caught an opponent, they could hold it fast, batter it with headbutts, and finish it when it could no longer move.

Their most famous weapon was the black ink they fired from their mouths to blind an opponent. Some people even used that ink in cooking. Ethan had no idea how it tasted; few people ate it.

Octillery could shoot water from its mouth just as Remoraid could. Even so, the two looked so unlike each other that people had long doubted Octillery evolved from Remoraid, preferring to believe it had always looked this way.

May had probably never battled one, and she knew little about it. That did not stop her from opening with a fierce attack.

Munchlax gathered its energy into its right hand for Focus Punch. Its fist shone like a lamp, and its round body charged toward Octillery with heavy strides.

Harley smiled faintly, unruffled, and gave his order. Octillery sprang high, landed squarely on Munchlax, and wrapped several tentacles around its head, locking it in a hold.

Munchlax tried to shake it loose but could not. With its sight blocked, it staggered like a drunk. It tried to swing its glowing fist upward and knock Octillery off, but Octillery was too slippery to hit. The display showing Munchlax's Contest points lost a small segment.

Octillery was not finished. Still clinging to Munchlax, it puffed up its long mouth and fired Octazooka straight at its head from point-blank range.

Boom!

The direct blow struck a sensitive spot and sent Munchlax falling backward. Even the audience heard the explosion. When it hit the floor, its Contest points dropped again.

The match had barely begun, yet Munchlax was already at a disadvantage May had never imagined. Ethan watched from the stands without changing expression. Harley was no easy opponent, and May had never faced a Pokemon quite like this one. Ethan had known the battle would be hard.

Harley had clearly trained Octillery well. Its performance suggested he had kept it as a surprise weapon.

May seemed to understand the danger. When Munchlax got up, she did not send it close again. She ordered Solar Beam, hoping to strike from a distance.

Harley gave another small smile. At his command, Octillery spat several Sludge Bombs. They hit Munchlax before it could fire, splattering over its mouth. Solar Beam was forced back and burst against Munchlax itself.

Harley did not miss the chance to mock May. From his seat, Ethan could not hear the words, but they were unlikely to be kind.

Ethan looked at May again. Octillery had shown how powerful and difficult it was, and Harley was trying to rattle her as well. What would she do now?

He had helped Munchlax train yesterday, but strength could not be built in a single afternoon. They had practiced a response to Rest. May still had to find a chance to use itand survive until then.

After the two setbacks, May was shaken. She steadied herself quickly and told Munchlax to use Metronome.

It was a gamble on an unknown move, relying entirely on luck. Yet it might be her only way out of this position.

Harley's arrogance surfaced again. He stood with a hand on his hip and watched coldly. To him, Metronome was a desperate, dangerous choice that might hurt its user as easily as help. May must have run out of ideas.

Munchlax finished the move while everyone watched. A soft white light faded. Apart from Munchlax's rather stylish motions, nothing happened.

Confused murmurs spread through the stands. What had Metronome selected? Why was there no visible effect? Harley burst out laughing.

While he was still mocking May, a thick beam of energy suddenly dropped from above. Electricity crackled loudly as it engulfed Octillery, leaving it scorched in an instant.

Now the crowd understood. Metronome had worked, calling down a powerful Electric-type attack. Against Octillery, the hit was devastating. It wiped away the advantage Harley had built, putting the Pokemon back on nearly equal footing. May's gamble had paid off.

Harley ordered Octillery to use Rest.

Rest was a Psychic-type move. Used on oneself, it could restore all lost energy; used against a target, it could put that Pokemon to sleep. As a means of recovery, it was formidable. Provided its user was not knocked out while the move took effect, its energy could return in an instant and its other ailments could disappear as well.

Ethan smiled in the stands. Just as in the anime, Octillery had turned to Rest. Powerful as the move looked, it had a weakness. Ethan had prepared Munchlax to exploit it. Now he would see what it had learned.

May did not know what Ethan had practiced. During yesterday's training, most of her attention had been on Squirtle's appeal. She had not seen him concentrate on countering Rest. When Octillery went to sleep, she responded in her own way and ordered Munchlax to attack.

Munchlax hurried forward on its short legs and used Tackle against the apparently motionless Octillery.

Thump!

It put its full weight into the collision. But Octillery had anchored several tentacles firmly to the floor. For all the force of the hit, it did not budge.

May was surprised but did not give up. She ordered Focus Punch. Munchlax's white-glowing fist drove upward into Octillery's chin. Again, its grip on the floor kept the blow from having the effect May wanted.

Rest was nearly complete. Two attacks had failed, and May grew anxious. If Octillery woke with its strength fully restored, Munchlax, already worn down, would almost certainly lose.

What could she do? Ideas flashed through her mind and were discarded just as quickly.

Then something changed in the arena. With no new command from May, Munchlax looked at the sleeping Octillery and remembered its practice with Ethan the previous day.

Almost on instinct, it bent down and pried Octillery's tentacles off the floor, one by one. It gathered Octillery in its arms and carried it toward the edge of the stage.

Oh? Lilian exclaimed. Munchlax has picked up Octillery! What is it trying to do?

May and Harley were just as puzzled. Then Munchlax reached the boundary, lifted Octillery high, and threw it out of the arena.

Harley's face changed. May's lit up. The audience gasped together, then broke into laughter.

There was no need to fight through all the energy Rest might restore. There was no complicated counter to work out. Once Octillery landed out of bounds, it would be disqualified, however healthy it became. That was Ethan's simple and effective answer.

Octillery, wake up! Harley shouted in panic.

But Rest needed a little longer to finish. Until it did, Harley could not rouse Octillery, and Octillery could not simply choose to abandon the move halfway through without a special method.

It fell lower and lower. Harley watched helplessly as it landed beneath the stage with a thud.

A white flash crossed Octillery's body, and it opened its eyes. Rest had succeeded. Its energy and condition were as good as when the battle began. Yet it was staring up at Munchlax from an unfamiliar place.

How did I get here? Wasn't I on the stage? How did one nap put me down below it?

The audience laughed again at its bewildered expression. No one had expected a Contest final to end like this.

May was the most delighted of all. When she had run out of ideas, Munchlax had found an answer on its own. She had never imagined it would do that.

At the judges' table, the three judges exchanged looks, checked the remaining time and Contest points, and shook their heads with wry smiles. Neither the clock nor either Pokemon's points had run out. But the rule was clear: leaving the arena decided the match.

Octillery is out of bounds! Munchlax wins! Lilian announced brightly. Congratulations to May, the winner of the Wisteria Town Contest!

Harley's expression could not have been darker. He had expected Octillery to finish recovering in another moment and then win. Instead, Munchlax had simply thrown it off the stage.

It was nothing like May's usual battle style. He remembered the brief surprise on her face when Munchlax picked Octillery up. An idea occurred to him, and he turned toward the audience.

There were so many people in the stands, yet his eyes found one handsome young man almost at once. Ethan had his head tipped slightly back and was looking at Harley with the faintest mocking glint in his eyes.

Chapter 836: A Pokemon Ranger

Ethan would not have bothered to mock Harley. The contempt Harley thought he saw was all in his own mind. Ethan had not even been looking at him.

Ethan had scarcely been concerned by men like Maxie and Archie. Harley was not even an opponent to him. That judgment was dismissive, but Ethan considered it fair.

Harley might be a dangerous rival for May. Against Ethan, he was not as strong as the elite members of the criminal organizations Ethan had fought. On those sprawling battlefields, his Pokemon might have fallen to a single move from one of Ethan's main partners, just as an ordinary grunt's would. Harley's only extra weapon was a collection of underhanded schemes, and those were easy to see through.

Why would Ethan go out of his way to taunt someone like that? If Harley ever became a threat to him, perhaps Ethan would spare him another glance. It was an arrogant view, and Ethan did not pretend otherwise.

May's Wisteria Contest victory brought her another step closer to her goal. Beating Harley again had also strengthened her confidence, which would help her grow.

Ethan left the hall before her and waited by the rear entrance, leaning against a wall. He watched the spectators drift out through the front doors, still talking about the match.

May emerged holding her Ribbon. Her face lit up when she saw him. She had worked out that Munchlax's decision to throw Octillery out of bounds must have come from Ethan's training. Now she wanted to thank him.

You earned half of this Ribbon with me, she said. If you hadn't taught Munchlax that trick, I don't know what I would've done.

It was true. In the last moments of the battle, May's mind had gone blank. If Munchlax had not acted on its training, she would have lost.

That just shows you've still got room to improve, Ethan said. As for me, I only did what I should have. It wasn't a big deal. He tossed her backpack to her and smiled. We've won, and that's worth celebrating, but our journey isn't over. Time to get moving.

May answered with a broad smile. Right!

...

Both islands had small towns, but the quiet settlement on Metallica Island could not compare with Wisteria Town in size, population, or prosperity. At its dock, Ethan and May easily found a ship back to the Kanto mainland. They would not need another bumpy ride on Dragonite.

Their next destination was the peninsula where Fuchsia City stood. It was close enough that the crossing took only a little more than half a day. Ethan's next Frontier challenge, the Battle Pike, lay near Fuchsia.

They disembarked at a port town as evening approached. Rather than press on in the dark, they checked into its Pokemon Center.

While they were arranging their room, a familiar-sounding woman called from the dining area. You there, handsome. Want to join me?

Her voice had a mature warmth to it. Ethan was sure he had heard it before. He turned and found a red-haired woman with glasses and a ponytail sitting at a table, waving to him. He recognized her at once: Lorelei, one of Kanto's Elite Four.

He had not expected to meet her here. With a curious May beside him, Ethan crossed to her table and sat opposite her without waiting for an invitation.

What a coincidence, he said. I never thought I'd run into you here.

It is a coincidence. I didn't expect you back in Kanto, Lorelei said with a smile. What brings you here?

She studied him as they spoke. It had been a long time since they had met, and he seemed to carry himself differently now.

Ethan told her he had returned to challenge the Battle Frontier. Her surprise was plain.

You've already won League Conferences in three regions. I didn't think you'd come back to challenge a place like that.

What's wrong with it? Ethan heard the faint dismissal in her voice and laughed. Don't underestimate the Frontier Brains. Some are exceptionally capable, and their Pokemon can be dangerous. If you went in thinking otherwise, one of them might even beat you.

He noticed May looking at Lorelei with curiosity and introduced them.

This is May, my current traveling partner. She's a Coordinator. May, this is Lorelei, a member of the Kanto Elite Four.

The Elite Four? May stared. The elegant woman in front of her looked only in her twenties. But age was not the reason for May's surprise; Phoebe of Hoenn's Elite Four was younger still.

May was amazed to encounter someone of Lorelei's standing in an ordinary Pokemon Center, casually greeting Ethan like an old friend. Then she remembered that Ethan had won three regional League Conferences. It was hardly strange for him to know members of the Elite Four.

A Coordinator? Lorelei looked May over kindly. I was about your age when I first set out. Seeing you reminds me of myself then. Keep working at it. Your dream follows a different path from mine, but it isn't an easy one, especially for someone so young.

Women seemed to win people's affection more readily than men, especially women with Lorelei's presence and standing. A single encouraging remark from her won May over at once.

Then Lorelei remembered something and turned back to Ethan. You were the one who told a man named Drake to challenge me, weren't you?

Drake? For a moment Ethan could not place the name.

Don't play dumb, Lorelei said with a huff. The head Trainer of the Orange League.

Oh, him! Ethan finally remembered the man celebrated throughout the Orange Islands as their strongest Trainer. Had Ethan told him to challenge Lorelei? Perhaps he had.

Did he win? Ethan asked.

Of course not. Lorelei smiled. I gave him a thorough lesson. He lost badly.

She did not describe the match, but Ethan could imagine it. Sounds rather painful for him.

Neither of them considered Drake worth discussing for long, and the conversation moved on. Lorelei had stopped here only by chance. She was on her way to an event in Cerulean City and had decided to stay the night when it grew late.

It was a rare meeting. They were also closer in standing now and had more to talk about, so the conversation lasted until late. In the morning, they exchanged brief farewells and went their separate ways.

Fuchsia City stood on a peninsula, though the city itself was not on the coast. From the port town, Ethan and May headed northeast. At a forest, they left the main road and took what looked like a shortcut through the trees.

Before long, something felt wrong.

Ethan... May held her Eevee Egg as she walked beside him. Doesn't this forest seem a little...

Too quiet? Ethan scanned the trees and nodded. In a forest this large, we should hear something. Be careful. Something has happened here.

May grew alert and watched their surroundings as they went deeper. The trees thickened around them.

Suddenly a woman leaped out and blocked their path. A Plusle jumped down from her shoulder and copied her, stretching its little arms across the trail.

Please stop! the woman called. This area is closed. You two mustn't go any farther!

Ethan had almost thought they were being ambushed. So much for that excitement. But why would a wild forest be closed? He had heard nothing about it.

He looked the woman over. She appeared a year or two younger than him, petite and attractive, with red eyes and a teal ponytail that sprang upward. Her orange and white uniform covered a black one-piece suit. The combination made her look energetic and, Ethan thought, a little alluring.

She seemed familiar. Then he realized he had seen her in the anime, though never in person. He had a guess about who she was.

Closed? he asked. What do you mean?

It's a forest in the wild, May added. Why can't we go in?

The woman kept her voice calm. The situation inside is complicated. I can't explain it in a sentence or two. Something serious has happened. This area won't reopen to ordinary Trainers until we Pokemon Rangers have dealt with it.

Ethan spotted the insignia on her armband and nodded to himself. He had guessed right: she was a Pokemon Ranger.

Then perhaps we've come at the right time. Ethan opened his wallet and showed her the credential the International Police had given him recently. I'm not an ordinary Trainer. I'm a Special Investigator of the International Police. Maybe I can help.

A Special Investigator?

Even May glanced at the credential, wondering when Ethan had gained another title. The Ranger's eyes widened. She took the card, examined it carefully, and confirmed it was real.

Forgive me, she said, handing it back. I didn't expect to meet someone from the International Police here. In that case, please come with me.

Ethan had thought the credential was merely an honorary award he might never use. It had proved useful sooner than he expected. Association with the International Police could open doors.

He and May followed the woman into the forest. As they walked, she introduced herself.

I'm Solana. The Ranger Union sent me here to handle a special incident.

After so much travel, Ethan had finally met a member of the Pokemon Rangers. Their purpose and the Ranger Union's were easy enough to understand: they protected nature and Pokemon.

Rangers were elusive. An ordinary Trainer might rarely see one unless they ventured into an area where the environment had been seriously damaged. The organization worked across regions. Instead of relying on Poke Balls for their work, Rangers used Capture Stylers to connect with Pokemon, forming temporary partnerships and borrowing their strength to help people and protect the natural world.

They handled accidents and natural disasters, often without recognition. It was a distinctive and admirable profession, balanced between everyday duty and danger.

Ethan introduced himself and May. I'm Ethan Vale. Besides being a Special Investigator, I'm a traveling Trainer. This is my companion May.

Ethan? Solana frowned. She felt she had heard the name somewhere, but she paid little attention to news from the wider world and could not place it.

Where had she heard it?

Chapter 837: This Is My Real Job!

Ethan had not expected to meet a Pokemon Ranger here. Travel was tiring, but it let him visit new places, meet new people, and encounter something unexpected each day. That freshness was the reason he loved it.

Solana led Ethan and May along the forest trail for some time. They pushed through dense brush into the forest's depths, where the way ahead was completely blocked.

Huge thorny vines twisted across the path. Some were as thick as pipes, and each seemed hundreds of meters long. They had swallowed a broad stretch of the forest.

There are so many thorns, May said. They look out of place, too. Ms. Solana, what happened here?

Solana hesitated. Then she remembered Ethan's International Police credential and decided to tell them. Celebi is behind this.

Celebi? May stared at her, then immediately looked at Ethan. He calmly looked back as if to ask why she was watching him.

May knew there was more than one Celebi in the world, so meeting one anywhere was possible. She also knew Ethan's Celebi was with Erika and could not be here. Her glance had been instinctive. She stuck out her tongue at him. Solana missed the silent exchange.

At the wall of thorns, she took out a red and black handheld device that looked rather like a folding phone. She aimed its camera at a few wild Pokemon peeking out nearby. Information appeared on the screen almost immediately.

What's that? May stepped closer to look.

Our Capture Styler, Solana said as she operated it. It launches and controls a Capture Disc. That lets us connect with wild Pokemon and become temporary partners. It also has phone and transmission functions, and a built-in Pokemon database. Professor Hastings invented it. It's indispensable to a Ranger.

A Capture Styler? A Capture Disc? Professor Hastings? The unfamiliar names opened up a whole field May had never seen or heard about.

What are you doing with it now? she asked.

Finding a Pokemon that can handle these vines.

Solana scanned several Caterpie, Venonat, and Metapod. She studied their information, shook her head, and turned the device toward a group of Linoone. Their details filled the screen.

Ethan took a look. Unlike a standard Pokedex, the Styler did not read its results aloud. Its data seemed fuller and more specialized, though. It showed each Pokemon's height and condition, along with its moves and Ability. If every Pokedex could do that, Trainers would be able to choose Pokemon to catch far more deliberately. What remarkable technology.

They know Slash? Solana's eyes brightened. You'll do!

The Styler changed shape in her hand, becoming something like a pistol. She aimed at the Linoone and fired. No bullet came out; instead, a small object like a spinning top shot toward them.

As it spun, an antenna extended from the Styler. Solana waved the device, guiding the Capture Disc in loops around the Pokemon. Trails of light followed it and enclosed the Linoone.

Is that the Capture Disc? May asked, as curious as ever.

It is. The Styler guides the disc around a wild Pokemon. The light trail carries a Ranger's feelings to it. When our hearts connect, the capture is complete, and the Pokemon is willing to help us as a temporary partner.

Solana made it sound simple, but Ethan knew there was more to the device. Its light line could be broken by a Pokemon's attack or another blow. The Styler would take damage and lose energy. If its energy fell to zero during a capture, the disc could even explode.

Those problems were uncommon. The part that truly troubled him was that a Capture Styler could also capture someone else's Pokemon. Ranger technology could override the hold of a Poke Ball and take its occupant. If that capability became widely known and spread beyond the Rangers, it could threaten the balance of the world.

No wonder the Rangers kept it secret. For now, at least, the organization was using its tools to protect Pokemon and nature. Ethan did not know what the future might bring.

Solana had no idea he knew their deepest secret. She concentrated on the Linoone, moving her hand faster and faster. The circling light quickened and finally entered the Pokemon.

Their expressions changed at once. Their wary, curious looks became clearer and more open, as though they understood something new. Whatever the bond truly was, the difference in them was plain.

Capture complete! Solana smiled. She had done this many times before. Plusle, use Helping Hand!

Helping Hand strengthened the moves of the Pokemon it aided. Plusle hopped in front of the Linoone, chattered to them, and made a few encouraging gestures.

Now, use Slash! Solana called.

The Linoone obeyed as readily as a Trainer's own Pokemon. They charged the thorns together and slashed open a path through the wall.

May's eyes shone. She went to Ethan and whispered, Look! The Styler really is amazing. She didn't have to catch those Pokemon in Poke Balls to get their help.

It is. Do you want one? Ethan teased. You could become a Ranger. Then wild Pokemon could help you too.

Don't be silly! My dream is to become a Top Coordinator. I'm not changing it. May waved the idea away, then frowned. But why doesn't Ms. Solana use her own Pokemon? With that Styler, she can get help so easily. Does she only have Plusle?

Who knows? Ethan shrugged. Maybe there's a reason we don't know, or some unusual Ranger rule.

While they spoke, the Linoone's claws widened the gap until it reached farther into the forest. Solana beckoned Ethan and May after her and entered the dark passage first.

As they walked, she explained where the thorns had come from.

They appeared suddenly last night. They blocked the paths, upset the local ecosystem, and frightened many wild Pokemon away. We came as soon as we received the report. We've confirmed the cause: Celebi.

Ethan remembered the first time he had met Celebi in the Mysterious Forest. If a Celebi had made these thorns, it had probably done so instinctively after something hurt it. Whatever had happened last night might have been much like that earlier incident.

So that's why you've closed the forest, he said. A Mythical Pokemon is involved.

Solana had been watching them as they walked. Neither had shown much surprise at Celebi's name, and that impressed her. Perhaps they had dealt with Mythical or Legendary Pokemon before.

Yes. We've received several earlier reports of thorns growing abnormally wherever Celebi appeared. We're still investigating why it happens, but something must have happened to Celebi in each case.

Then the immediate priority is finding this Celebi, Ethan said.

Exactly. Solana sighed. That hasn't been easy. We searched carefully after arriving but found no trace of it. We're beginning to wonder if it has already left the forest.

We? May asked. I thought you were alone.

A figure leaped down in front of them as soon as she said it.

Who said she was alone? I'm right here!

The newcomer landed steadily. He was a black-haired young man about Solana's age, dressed in a similar Ranger uniform with a red headband. A Minun stood on his shoulder where Solana carried Plusle.

Honestly, jumping down from that height again... Solana rubbed her forehead. This is Lunick, my partner on this assignment.

Plusle and Minun made the pair look like more than ordinary teammates to Ethan.

Hello, Lunick said to the two travelers. If Solana brought you this far, I assume you have permission from headquarters. I won't question it. Let's work together.

Like Solana, he made a good first impression. Seeing two Rangers here, Ethan understood that the Celebi incident must be difficult even for them.

Rangers might sound numerous because their work spanned regions and included protecting both nature and Pokemon. In fact, their ranks were small and selective. Away from headquarters, a region might have only a handful. Sending two to this one forest showed how seriously they took a Mythical Pokemon.

Ethan and May introduced themselves. Unlike Solana, Lunick recognized Ethan's name immediately.

Wait! You're Ethan Vale, the one who won League Conferences in three regions?

Lunick followed events beyond Ranger work more closely than Solana did. Anyone traveling through Kanto, Johto, or Hoenn who kept up with news was likely to have heard of Ethan.

Ethan smiled. Unless there's another person with my name, yes.

Lunick's eyes lit up. I haven't watched your matches, but I've heard about you. They say you're an incredible Trainer.

Hold on. Solana was thoroughly confused now. Aren't you a Special Investigator of the International Police? When did you become a League champion too?

I told you I travel as a Trainer. Ethan laughed. The International Police role is a side job. Being a Pokemon Trainer is my real one!

Chapter 838: Ethan's Method

Only now did Solana realize how much the man in front of her had accomplished. It made little difference to her. She rarely followed news from outside the Ranger Union. Learning he had won three League Conferences told her he was capable, but it did not change how she treated him.

Solana and Lunick were the only Rangers here. With everyone together, they shared all they knew. They stopped to rest while Ethan listened, then he touched his chin.

So since this began last night, you haven't found Celebi, but you have found ashes scattered through the forest?

Yes, Lunick said. Wood ash, as if trees had burned down. But there hasn't been a forest fire here recently. We can't explain where it came from.

Given what Celebi can do, it may have brought the ash with it while traveling through time, Ethan said. As the Trainer of a Celebi, he felt qualified to offer an opinion. That would explain its appearance. Did you follow the traces to look for Celebi?

The Rangers exchanged a look. Solana answered. We came this morning and noticed the ash. We searched around it, but the thorns and vines have changed the terrain. Some places are covered completely. There isn't a clear trail to follow. Celebi is small, too. If it decided to hide, finding it would be difficult.

She was right. Celebi could slip into any hollow tree. In a forest this large, finding it without startling it would be like hunting for a needle in a haystack.

Then there are two approaches left, Ethan said, glancing at the Capture Stylers on their belts. You could recruit more wild Pokemon to help search. Given enough time, they might find it. Or...

Or what? Solana asked.

Find a way to draw it out.

Both Rangers frowned and shook their heads.

I don't think that will work, Solana said with a sigh. Celebi is peaceful and likes forests, but it's naturally timid. Especially in its present condition, even wild Pokemon wouldn't be able to lure it out.

It was not impossible, Ethan thought. They simply lacked the right Pokemon. A Pokemon important enough to catch Celebi's attention, or one carrying a familiar presence, could draw it out. Another Celebi, for example.

Neither Ranger could provide that. Ethan could. He could even use Solana's Styler to have his Celebi sent from Celadon Gym. But he did not want to reveal his own Celebi to two people he had only just met, even if they were Rangers trying to heal this forest.

It was a private secret. Unless there was a good reason, he would not tell outsiders. The women who tended the greenhouse at Celadon Gym were a different matter; they had to care for Celebi there.

Still, Ethan would not leave the wild Celebi to suffer. The Rangers had found no other danger, but what if Celebi itself was badly hurt? Every delay could reduce its chance of survival. Ethan loved Pokemon too much to ignore that possibility.

He needed a way to help while keeping his own secret.

After a moment's thought, he decided. I can help you, but you must agree to one condition.

Both Rangers looked at him. We'd be glad of your help, Lunick said. What's the condition?

Ethan's voice was calm and firm. When I search for Celebi using my method, you must leave the forest. And you must not watch.

What? The demand caught them both off guard.

Why? Solana asked, her brow furrowing. Do you have a way to find it? For a moment she wondered whether Ethan wanted them gone so he could secretly capture Celebi.

I can't promise success, but there's a good chance, Ethan said, leaning back. You may keep trying your own way instead. I'll continue my journey and leave this to you. It isn't my assignment. I only stopped because a Celebi might be in danger.

He had made the choice clear. If they wanted his help, they would have to let him take charge of the search and follow his directions. If they could not trust him, he would leave them to their work.

May felt the tension between them and held her breath. Solana considered the demand, then shook her head.

No. This is a Ranger matter. Even if you work with the International Police, you can't simply

I understand, Lunick interrupted. He stopped her and turned to Ethan with a serious nod. I'd rather trust you than waste more time searching without a direction.

Solana stared at her partner. Lunick...

It's all right. Trust me. He gave her a reassuring look, then smiled at Ethan. A man who has won three regional League Conferences and works with the International Police must have methods of his own.

Solana hesitated again. In the end, she trusted Lunick and said nothing more, leaving the decision to him.

We'll do as you ask, Mr. Vale, Lunick said. We'll watch the forest perimeter and won't look in.

Ethan showed no change of expression. Then he added, I'll need you to leave one Capture Styler with me.

That sounded like pushing his luck. Lunick paused, but something seemed to click. He nodded. Take mine.

There was more respect in his voice now. Ethan regarded the younger man more highly as well. Lunick was outgoing and good-humored, but he could make a firm decision. Perhaps he had guessed that Ethan needed the Styler to transfer a Pokemon here and understood that Ethan was serious.

Rangers were not chosen lightly.

If things go as expected, this should be resolved soon, Ethan told him. And I'll return your Styler intact.

Lunick handed it over and left a way to contact him. Then he and Solana headed toward the edge of the forest.

They walked more than a hundred meters before looking back. Ethan and May had vanished from sight, and they were too far away to be overheard. Solana turned to Lunick.

Are you sure about this? We left him in charge and gave him important equipment. He won't even let us watch. I don't like walking away from something so secretive.

Do we have a better choice? Lunick asked as he walked. We've spent all day trying. We searched from the air with Flying Pokemon and underground with Dugtrio. Every attempt failed. I'd rather give this man one chance than keep wandering without a plan. Three League victories don't come from nowhere. He may surprise us.

As soon as they had gone, Ethan examined the Styler. A short time spent trying its controls was enough for him to understand the functions he needed. He asked May to stand watch in case the Rangers came back, then called Erika.

He had decided to bring his Celebi here and ask for its help after all. In the film about Celebi's journey through time, a group of Celebi from other times had revived one that had died. Ethan trusted that his own Celebi could help an injured member of its kind.

Erika answered quickly. Once Ethan explained, she went to the greenhouse to find Celebi.

When everything was ready, Ethan judged that Solana and Lunick had gone far enough. He changed the Styler's configuration and pressed its transfer button. A GS Ball appeared before him.

It was curious. According to Kurt, Professor Oak, and Professor Ivy, the GS Ball's materials had once prevented it from being sent through a transfer machine. After Ethan caught Celebi in it, the ball seemed to behave normally and could be transferred. He did not understand why. He had never mentioned the change to the professors, keeping it a secret until now.

May glanced over from where she stood guard and saw the unusual ball. So that was Celebi's Poke Ball. It certainly looked different.

Ethan picked it up and pressed its button. Blue light flashed, and an onion-headed creature appeared before him. Celebi, of course.

It immediately sensed how different the forest air was from the greenhouse and flew about with delight. Ethan called it back, mindful of the time, and explained what had happened.

Celebi understood him well. It recognized the seriousness of the situation, gave a soft cry, and flew up over the treetops.

Green light shone from its body. The glow spread rapidly across the forest, and the invasive vines and thorns began to vanish beneath it.

That light did more than clear the forest. It seemed to carry a message between Celebi.

Within half a minute, another Celebi came flying unsteadily from deeper among the trees. It approached Ethan's Celebi. As he had hoped, even hurt, it had sensed its own kind and come out to meet it.

Guided by Ethan's Celebi, the wild one descended in front of him. He examined it at once. Scratches and scrapes covered its body, but they were shallow. It had no obvious life-threatening wound. Its listlessness seemed more likely to come from exhaustion. Food, water, and rest ought to help.

May!

She ran over with the first-aid kit. The wild Celebi shrank back from them at first. Ethan's Celebi reassured it, and it finally accepted their help. Compared with most Celebi, this one even seemed a little bolder.

They cleaned its wounds, applied medicine, and dressed the scrapes. May had done such work many times on the road. Her gentle face helped the wild Celebi relax and accept her care.

When the treatment was done, Ethan produced his other reliable remedy: instant noodles. The smell made the wild Celebi's mouth water. Whatever caution it had left disappeared.

Chapter 839: A Woman Who Likes Narrow Eyes

At the edge of the forest, Solana and Lunick saw the green light sweep across the trees as soon as Ethan's Celebi released it. They had been walking for only seven or eight minutes and had not gone very far.

It's Celebi! He really found it! Solana recognized the Mythical Pokemon's power. She turned back at once, but Lunick caught her arm.

Wait. Ethan told us to stay away until he called.

What are we waiting for? she asked. If he's found Celebi, he's done what he promised. Every minute we delay, it might fly awayor it might be weak and waiting for our help.

Lunick hesitated. She had a point. Solana was not trying to break her word lightly. Their priorities differed from Ethan's. They had been sent by Ranger headquarters to find Celebi and restore the forest. The vines and thorns had vanished, and Celebi had appeared. Why wait?

But we did promise him... Lunick said.

Maybe he forgot to contact us. Besides, this is Celebi. Aren't you worried that he sent us away so he could catch it for himself?

The secrecy of Ethan's request invited that suspicion. Lunick did not think Ethan would exploit an injured Pokemon, but he finally gave in.

All right. We'll go back quietly. But we observe from a distance first. We can't charge up to him, and we absolutely mustn't offend him.

I know, Solana said, rolling her eyes. I'm not reckless. I only want a quick look.

They hurried back along the trail.

...

After several bowls of noodles, the wild Celebi was plainly feeling better. It had grown fond of the man who had fed it and became bolder, even alighting on Ethan's palm.

It looks much better. Do you think it's out of danger? May smiled and reached over to stroke it. Its body felt odd: soft, yet textured almost like grass.

Your treatment helped a great deal, Ethan said. All that traveling with Ash and the others wasn't wasted. You're good at tending Pokemon now.

May smiled shyly. I learned most of it by watching Brock.

Gengar suddenly poked its head out of Ethan's shadow. The wild Celebi startled and flew a little higher. Gengar ignored its reaction and frowned at Ethan.

I sense someone coming. I think those two are back.

Ethan showed no surprise. Solana and Lunick did not know him well enough to trust him fully, and he did not know them well enough to trust them either. That was why he had asked May to stand watch. He had not expected them to return quite so soon, though. They must have turned back the moment they saw Celebi's light.

It no longer mattered. The treatment was finished.

Ethan recalled his Celebi into the GS Ball, and Gengar slipped back into his shadow. Barely ten seconds later, he heard faint footsteps among the nearby trees.

Ethan... May sounded worried. She did not know how they should handle this.

Stay where you are, he said, giving her a reassuring look. Act normally. And use that Styler to signal them.

May took Lunick's Capture Styler and used the method he had shown them to contact him. A receiving beep sounded close by. It was loud enough for Ethan and May to hear, and it left the Rangers hiding there thoroughly embarrassed.

There was no point concealing themselves now. Solana and Lunick came out of the trees.

Um... Neither could find a good explanation.

Ethan did not bother to wait for one. He opened his hands. Startled again by their sudden arrival, the wild Celebi rose into the sky and flew away.

Celebi! Solana called after it, but a few beats of its wings carried it out of sight.

Ethan had deliberately allowed it to leave. That was not how he described it.

If only you'd arrived a little later, he said with a rueful shake of his head. We've treated its injuries, but we hadn't built enough trust yet. Now it's flown away.

May hid a smile. Ethan himself had told her to contact them; now he was complaining they had come too early. It was an excuse meant to tease them.

Solana and Lunick could tell as well. That made the encounter more awkward.

I'm sorry, Lunick said at last. When we saw the green light, we knew you'd found Celebi. We worried something might happen and came back on our own. Please don't hold it against us.

Hold it against you? Ethan's tone gave little away. I would have stepped in to help Celebi whether you were here or not. As for what you did... He sighed. Never mind. I'm used to it.

He said no more. He gathered the litter from the ground, shouldered his bag, and walked away.

May returned the Styler to Lunick, nodded to both Rangers, then hurried after Ethan. Solana and Lunick watched them disappear into the forest. For a while neither spoke.

Lunick finally patted Solana's shoulder with a wry smile. We've left him with a poor impression of us. Don't dwell on it. The matter here is settled, and we still have a long report to write.

...

Meeting Solana, Lunick, and the wild Celebi had been a brief interruption to the journey. Ethan and May put it behind them as they left the forest. Only May kept wondering where the Celebi would go next.

They reached Fuchsia City without further trouble. Night was approaching, so they did not go straight to the Battle Pike outside town. They stayed at the city's Pokemon Center first.

After dinner, May asked Nurse Joy to examine her Egg. Several days had passed since the family at the breeding farm had given it to her. They had said it would hatch soon, and May wanted to make sure her travels had not harmed it.

Nurse Joy checked it carefully. Everything looks fine, she said with a smile. You've cared for it well. The shell is clean and smooth, with no cracks, and everything inside appears normal. It should hatch into a healthy Pokemon.

May let out a breath. That's a relief. I've been worried that all this traveling might be bad for it.

Keep a close watch on it anyway, Nurse Joy said. I expect it to hatch within the next day or two.

That soon? May's eyes brightened. I understand. I'll take good care of it!

...

After a night's rest, they set out for the Battle Pike the next morning. It stood on a hill not far outside Fuchsia City, with the sea visible from its grounds.

The facility's shape was striking. A gigantic Seviper seemed to be sprawled across the building. From a distance it looked almost alive, and a little unnerving. Its unusual design spoke to the Frontier Brain's particular taste.

Ethan and May followed a long stone path to the structure and knocked on its great doors. Before long, three young women in their twenties came out. Their brightly dyed hair and clothes gave them the look of a rough street gang.

Seriously? A challenger this early? Can't we get any sleep? one complained, rubbing her head.

That's your hangover, not the challenger's fault, another said.

Only because you kept pouring me drinks!

The woman in front had blond hair, a long white coat over a red crop top, and an exposed midriff. Her voice was husky, perhaps from smoking, and she had a peculiar rolling way of speaking. The other two wore different outfits but had much the same style and manner. Faint smells of tobacco and alcohol drifted out behind them.

May, unused to women like these and put off by their argument, took a step back.

Before Ethan could speak, all three noticed his face and brightened.

Well, where did this handsome one come from?

We've never had a challenger this good-looking!

They began appraising and teasing him right in front of him. Ethan disliked dealing with people like this. If he answered, they might take the invitation to crowd him. If he ignored them, they might only try harder.

A steadier woman's voice came from inside and rescued him. You're making too much noise. What's going on?

A tall woman with long black hair stepped through the doorway. She seemed about twenty-seven or twenty-eight and stood a head above the other three. Her narrow eyes and single eyelids gave her a sharp, cool look. Ethan recognized the Frontier Brain of this facility: Pike Queen Lucy.

They had never met in person, but he knew a good deal about her from the anime. What he remembered best was her taste in Pokemonand in people.

Lucy favored serpentine Pokemon. She also liked narrow-eyed faces. In the anime, Brock's declaration of love had genuinely moved her. At home, she kept Abra, Snorlax, Cyndaquil, Swinub, Makuhita, and Skitty, all with the same narrow-eyed look. Brock happened to share it. Few mature women in the anime had returned his affection, which made Lucy especially memorable to Ethan.

He wondered whether she had met Brock yet.

Once Lucy appeared, the three women who had teased Ethan quieted down. Ethan stepped up and explained why he had come.

His introduction was unnecessary. Lucy recognized him and knew from the other Frontier Brains that he was challenging their facilities. She folded her arms and smiled.

Greta told me about you. I thought it'd take you a few more days to get here, but you're already at my door. The other Frontier Brains didn't keep you busy for long, did they?

Chapter 840: Expect the Unexpected

Anyone who followed current events, especially in Kanto and Johto, had probably heard Ethan's name. The Pokemon Leagues drew enormous attention. Even if someone else had won, people would still know the champion's name.

Lucy and the three women worked in Pokemon battling. Of course they had watched the tournaments that drew the eyes of an entire continent. But months had passed, and their attention had been on the Pokemon rather than their Trainers. Like many people, they had forgotten what Ethan looked like and had failed to recognize him at once.

Now that Lucy had identified him, the three women finally understood.

Oh! So it's you!

I watched the battle where you won the championship. You were incredible!

Hey, Mr. Champion, how about an autograph? Right here on my chest. Do you have a pen? If not, your finger will do!

They really did say whatever came to mind.

At the discovery that he was the champion, their eyes lit up again. They crowded around him more boldly than before and even pushed May aside. Trainers arrived to challenge the Pike all the time, but a champion at their door was a rare sight.

Hearing the commotion, several more women dressed much like them came out of the facility. They gathered around Ethan and inspected him as though he were a rare Pokemon.

It reminded him of Erika and the Celadon Gym. Both places had a female Leader and female staff who liked to gossip together. The chatter could get noisy. The women here, though, were far less restrained.

Some men might enjoy being surrounded by women, but Ethan neither liked the attention nor took pleasure in the praise. He would have preferred it if Lucy had never recognized him and had treated him like an ordinary challenger.

There was little he could do about it. Fame and achievements beyond most people's reach came at a price. He had faced this before, more than once, and would face it again. Someone who enjoyed the attention might see it differently, but Ethan did not.

Lucy was a Frontier Brain, and she had no intention of letting her underlings carry on. One sharp order sent every woman surrounding Ethan back to her place.

Ethan's opinion of her rose. These women were hardly meek or obedient by nature. Whatever their usual relationship with Lucy, the fact that they obeyed a single command when it mattered showed how well she led them. She deserved her title.

With that settled, Lucy and the others led Ethan and May into the Battle Pike.

Beyond the doors stretched a vast chamber that resembled the inside of a pipe. Ethan looked around and saw how the facility had earned its name.

The battle arena stood at its center. Instead of a plain field built around one type of terrain, it combined shrubs, soil, a winding stretch of water, more than a dozen platforms above the pool, and small islands. Pokemon could battle on land, in water, or in the air. It felt more like a real patch of wilderness than the bare arenas he was used to.

Of all the Frontier facilities Ethan had visited, this was the most varied battlefield.

He and Lucy climbed the high steps to the Trainer positions on opposite sides of the arena. From there they faced each other across the field.

Lucy might have had a gentle-sounding name, but her bearing was that of a boss. Merely standing there, she was impossible to dismiss.

A woman with short blue-green hair and a matching strapless top stepped onto the referee's platform.

The Frontier battle between Indigo League Champion Ethan Vale and Pike Queen Lucy is about to begin! Each Trainer may use two Pokemon. The first to win two rounds wins the match. Trainers, send out your Pokemon!

Lucy was called the Pike Queen because of her strength, not merely because she ran the facility or because of her looks and bearing. Challenger after challenger had come through her doors, and she had won far more often than she had lost. Her skill let her rule this place like a queen.

There was no doubting her ability. Facing a League champion like Ethan, however, she still felt considerable pressure.

He stood there doing nothing, making no unnecessary movements. He almost seemed to leave himself open everywhere. Yet Lucy felt a suffocating force coming from him.

The faint resignation he had shown when her women surrounded him had vanished the instant he took his place as a Trainer. A flash of confidence appeared in his eyes, and the pressure he gave off made everyone take notice.

So this is a champion?

Nothis was a man who held the championship titles of three regions. He was nothing like her previous challengers.

Lucy kept her expression composed despite the difficulty she felt ahead. She calmly took a Poke Ball from her coat. Almost at the same moment, Ethan took one out as well. When they released their Pokemon, everyone watching saw the first choices of the match.

By sheer coincidence, two identical Milotic appeared in the water before their respective Trainers.

Neither had expected the other to choose the same Pokemon.

Huh? They both sent out Milotic? The women watching could hardly believe it.

With so many kinds of Pokemon, matching choices were uncommon but hardly impossible. For both Trainers to send out a rare Milotic in this particular match, though, was an extraordinary coincidence.

Ethan and Lucy were just as surprised as the spectators.

Lucy meant to give an opponent like him her full effort. Alongside her signature ace, Seviper, Milotic was one of her main Pokemon. It was a natural choice for an opening round in which she could test him.

Ethan, meanwhile, had been concentrating on training his own Milotic. With water covering more than half the field, sending it out made perfect sense to him.

Each had a reason. The result was this unexpected mirror match.

I didn't realize you had a Milotic too. Lucy sounded as steady as ever despite her surprise. Good. Same Pokemon, same type. This is the perfect way to measure our skill. Now show me what you can do.

Seeing was better than hearing about it. Ethan had won three regional tournaments and enjoyed a formidable reputation, but Lucy had seen those victories only on screens. She would have to face him herself to learn whether he lived up to it.

More than anything, she wanted to battle him and discover the difference between them.

The two Milotic swam to their starting positions. Under the lights, with ripples reflecting around them, both Pokemon looked exceptionally beautiful.

Once they were ready, the referee raised her hand.

Begin!

Both Pokemon moved as her call ended. In near-perfect unison, they opened their mouths and fired Hydro Pump at each other. The two torrents crossed the arena, collided in midair, and burst into a shower of spray.

Identical moves had canceled each other out. But neither Trainer had ordered that exchange. It was an instinctive test at the start of the battle; now they took command.

Milotic, use Twister!

The order came from Lucy, not Ethan.

That caught him off guard. Twister was one of his favorite moves whenever he battled with a Water-type Pokemon, and he often combined it with other techniques. This time someone was using it against him.

But because he knew Twister so well, he knew how to answer it.

Milotic, use Twister too!

Two spiraling winds rose one after the other. They grew larger as they swept toward the middle of the arena. Although they spun in different directions, their power was evenly matched. Instead of crashing apart as the Trainers might have expected, the two Twisters merged into an even greater vortex.

The larger vortex pulled harder. Pool water, loose shrubs, and stones tore free and whirled upward. A murky waterspout took shape, blocking each Trainer's view of the other side.

Here the difference in their styles became clear. Lucy had used Twister as a straightforward attack. After launching it, she waited for her opponent to expose an opening.

More than ten seconds later, she stared in astonishment as Ethan's Milotic rode the rising water into the air, then dropped rapidly from above. Its Iron Tail struck her Milotic with full force.

Smack!

Lucys Milotic had not anticipated an attack from the sky. The blow landed cleanly and sent it plunging into the pool.

Milotic!

The cry came from the women watching, not from Lucy. They all sprang to their feet.

They had stood by Lucy since the Battle Pike opened. When had they ever seen her Milotic put at such a disadvantage right at the start? This was the Pike Queen's second-strongest main Pokemon, surpassed only by her ace Seviper. It was no ordinary Trainer's casual choice.

The descending Iron Tail had caught it completely off guard. Yet wasn't that proof of Ethan's more inventive approach?

Fortunately for Lucy's Milotic, the water absorbed some of the impact. The hit still hurt, but after a few seconds beneath the surface, it burst out in a spray and drove its head toward Ethan's Milotic.

The counterattack missed. Even so, the sight of Milotic back in action let Lucy's supporters breathe again.

Her Milotic pressed on without a pause.

That's better. The women settled back into their seats, their brows relaxing. Now she's got it back to the boss's usual style. Attack, attack, and keep attacking. Nobody can stand up to that!

Ethan was too far away to hear them, but May caught every word.

She knew the title Pike Queen meant Lucy was strong. She still disagreed completely with what the women were saying. There were no absolutes in a Pokemon battle.

Nobody can stand up to her attacks? That's because you haven't met Ethan yet!

May was not like Misty, who acted as though she were the world's biggest Ethan fan and believed him unbeatable. Still, she knew he had faced many difficult opponents since becoming a Trainer and had yet to lose an official match. An attack that supposedly no one could withstand would not be enough to stop him.

She kept the thought to herself. That was more her way than arguing with strangers.

And the battle proved her right.

Lucy's Milotic kept attacking with Iron Tail and Tackle and even tried Wrap. Apart from its Water-type moves, it used nearly everything it knew. Under Ethan's direction, his Milotic answered each attack.

Ethan's sharper reading of the battle let him defend and counterattack. He broke Lucy's rhythm, then had his Milotic land another Iron Tail before hers could react.

The women in the stands fell silent again. May felt a private satisfaction and cast them a faintly triumphant glance.

See? There is no such thing as an attack nobody can withstand. Now you know what Ethan can do.

Chapter 841: The Pike Queen

By now, Lucy knew how difficult Ethan's Milotic was to fight. Compared with her own, it performed exceptionally well on both offense and defense. It left her few openings. Even when she gave the battle her full attention, keeping up was hard; the slightest lapse let it catch her out.

Then again, this Milotic had competed in regional tournaments and come through battles of the highest intensity. Its ability should not have surprised her.

What troubled her more was the man behind it. His precise judgments and his steady style, daring when it needed to be, were the real problem. Under his direction, Milotic fought beyond its usual limits. It was as though he had given it another pair of eyes and another mind. He showed exactly what a Trainer could contribute.

Before Lucy realized it, her Milotic had fallen behind. Same species, same type, even many of the same movesyet Ethan kept finding small advantages in the details. By the time she noticed how they were adding up, it was too late to undo them.

Most Trainers in that position would gamble on a bolder strategy to recover. Lucy was no exception. She knew that if the battle continued as it was, she would lose.

Milotic! Dive into the water!

Her Milotic plunged beneath the surface without hesitation.

Ethan stared for a moment, then understood. Lucy had realized she could not win while he could direct every exchange. By hiding her Pokemon underwater, she meant to cut off his line of sight and break that connection, leaving the two Milotic to settle it between themselves.

It was a good idea. Unfortunately for her, as Greta had found out before, Ethan's Pokemon excelled at fighting without instructions. Lucy had chosen the wrong way to challenge him.

His Milotic dived in after hers. Soon the surface settled, leaving only widening rings of ripples. Then bubbles rose from the bottom, the water churned, and waves spread toward the banks. The two Pokemon were plainly fighting beneath the pool.

Without underwater cameras or a large screen, nobody could tell exactly what was happening. Lucy likely hoped her Milotic's familiarity with the arena would help it find an opening. Against an ordinary Trainer, denying them a view of the battle might have worked. For Ethan's Pokemon, independence was an advantage.

In the stands, Lucy's supporters clenched their fists and watched the water intently. Which Milotic would come out on top? Would they surface in a dead heat and continue the fight?

They did not have long to wait.

Water burst upward. One Milotic emerged with its tail wrapped tightly around the other and hauled it onto the bank. It tightened its coils. The captive struggled a few times, then went completely limp.

At first glance, the two looked alike. But the women who spent every day with Lucy's Milotic knew the little differences. They recognized the unconscious one immediately: it was Lucy's.

The boss's Milotic lost?

I can't believe it. It looked so easy for him...

So the champion's Pokemon really is stronger?

As they sighed, May's eyebrows lifted. That's what I thought. There is no such thing as an attack nobody can withstand. Ethan is as amazing as ever!

Ethan did not know what anyone in the stands was thinking. All his attention was on his Pokemon. A closer look showed small wounds on his Milotic's body. The underwater fight had been fierce and dangerous.

The victory might have looked effortless from outside the pool, but it had been nothing of the sort. The two Milotic were closely matched. His had fought a little better, but it could never have overwhelmed Lucy's through strength alone. If he had to put numbers on it, he would have called the balance 5.3 to 4.7.

Lucy had suffered for her final choice. It had not been a foolish order; she simply did not know how Ethan usually battled. His Pokemon often took part in sprawling free-for-alls where he could not direct each of them. They had learned to make their own decisions. Had Lucy known that, she would never have sent her Milotic underwater to fight on its own.

After this loss, she had clearly realized it. It was not too late to adjust.

Lucy recalled her unconscious Milotic and took out a second Poke Ball. Blue light flashed, and her ace, Seviper, appeared before the cheering women.

You can do it, boss!

Seviper, show him what you've got!

Ordinary staff might have held back out of consideration for the challenger rather than cheering so loudly for their Leader. These women had no such reservations. Their shouts echoed throughout the Battle Pike.

Ethan paid them no attention. He did not even glance their way. This was hardly enough to rattle him, and his one-round lead gave him no particular pleasure either. He recalled his Milotic and studied Seviper.

When he thought of that species, Jessie's Seviper came to mind first. It was strong, full of character, and one of her most recognizable Pokemon. But the Team Rocket trio never dared cause trouble in front of him, so she had not shown it to Ethan once since catching it.

He still knew plenty about Seviper. It resembled a venomous snake, perhaps a black pit viper. Its body was mostly black, with a golden lower jaw, gold armor on its head and back, and six small gold projections along its belly that helped it crawl. Its fangs were sharp and red; its tail was shaped like a blade.

Seviper honed that tail blade against rocks, making it razor-sharp and coating it with potent venom. It hid in grass, struck approaching prey with its poisonous fangs, then slashed with its tail to cut and poison the victim. It was a dangerous, cold-blooded hunter.

Lucy clearly liked battling with serpent-shaped Pokemon. Milotic and Seviper were only the ones she had shown so far; Steelix and Gyarados shared that long, snakelike build. She seemed as fond of them as she was of the narrow-eyed Pokemon she kept at home.

What should Ethan use against her ace?

After putting away Milotic's Ball, he weighed Blaziken against Eevee for a moment, then sent Eevee out.

It was not that he had no other Pokemon to train. Tyranitar, Metagross, or Scizor could all have matched up well against Seviper. But he did not want to choose one of them. He knew how troublesome Lucy's supporters could be. If he sent out a Pokemon that countered Seviper and won, they would never let him hear the end of it. He would rather avoid inviting that trouble. Eevee was his choice.

His calculations did not stop at the edge of the arena.

Because water covered more than half the unusual field, neither Pokemon could take the usual central starting position. They stood instead on small patches of open ground toward the sides of their respective halves. The slight shift in position made little difference.

Once both Pokemon were ready, the referee waved her hand again. The second round began.

Despite her first loss, Lucy attacked as aggressively as before. Seviper raced toward Eevee and snapped at it. Eevee sprang away, but Seviper immediately swung its bladed tail at the spot where Eevee would land.

Eevee reacted in time and jumped again, escaping the slash. The assault was not over. A snake's powerful muscles let it surge forward in an instant, and Seviper lunged with its fangs.
