Another Pokemon might have been caught at such close range. Ethan's Eevee was lively and quick to react. At the last possible moment, it avoided the venom-sheened fangs, kicked off with both hind legs, and struck Seviper on the head.

Ah, so close! Several disappointed cries rose from the stands.

The women knew that little sequence was one of Seviper's signature tactics, unimpressive as it might look. Once its fangs landed and the venom entered its opponent's body, Seviper gained a commanding advantage. Comebacks after that were rare. Eevee had escaped, and now that it knew what to expect, the combination would be even harder to land.

They did not realize that Ethan had thought That was close as well. He was good at reading the field and noticing details, but this was his first fight against Lucy's Seviper. He could not have anticipated that sequence. Eevee's quick reactions had saved it from a dangerous hit. It had grown a great deal.

With Seviper's opening attack over, Eevee went on the offensive. It could not move as fast as Seviper, but its small body gave it nimble footwork and it was an excellent jumper. It circled the snake and harried it from every side.

Seviper's fangs made approaching too closely dangerous, however. Eevee kept trying to find a safe opening and achieved little. The fight settled into a stalemate.

Lucy's eyes narrowed. She gave another decisive order, and almost before her words ended, Seviper's tail flashed toward Eevee. The bladelike tip moved so fast it whistled through the air.

Eevee, dodge!

Eevee had been watching the tail and leaped backward, but the strike was too fast. It hit the ground and sent an explosion of soil and debris outward, knocking Eevee into the nearby pool.

Splash!

Eevee panicked at first, paddling wildly like a little dog. Once it adjusted, it began swimming for the far bank.

Lucy saw her chance. Seviper was no water snake, but it went into the pool without hesitation and swam after Eevee.

The situation had turned dangerous. Eevee was agile on land; in the water it could barely fight at all. At their present speeds and distances, Seviper would catch it before it reached the shore. Then Eevee would be at its mercy.

Ethan frowned and swept his gaze over the pool. An answer came to him.

Eevee, get onto that log beside you!

The enormous vortex in the first round had torn shrubs and small trees out of the ground. Some had blown beyond the arena, but many still floated in the pool. Now that debris offered Eevee a way out.

Chapter 842: It's Time for Eevee to Evolve

At Ethan's command, Eevee changed course. Instead of swimming for the bank, it headed for a floating log nearby.

Water churned behind it. Eevee did not need to look back to know Seviper was closing in; it could almost feel the venomous snake's cold breath.

Fortunately, the log was close enough. Eevee clambered onto it just before Seviper caught up. Without stopping to shake the water from its fur, it ran along the wood and leaped. Seviper's tail slashed at it as it sailed over the broad stretch of pool, but Eevee landed safely on the far bank.

Lucy silently cursed the missed opportunity. It had escaped after all.

She knew, though, that surviving two close calls was no accident. Eevee's ability to get through Seviper's assault unharmed was real. Its species was physically weaker than Seviper, yet it had managed to fight on even terms. That said plenty about its strength.

She had already been surprised by Ethan many times. He had done it again. If only he had narrow eyes too...

The battle drew her attention back. Now that Eevee had reached land, the situation had reversed. If Seviper came ashore where it was, Eevee would be waiting to harry it. But retreating across the pool or taking the long way around did not suit Lucy's style.

Fortunately, she had another tactic.

At her order, Seviper stayed afloat instead of coming ashore. It opened its mouth, and a torrent of fire roared across the water toward Eevee.

Ethan had not expected Lucy's Seviper to know Flamethrower. Or rather, he had seen it use the move in the anime and forgotten. It hardly mattered. On open ground, with that much distance between them, Eevee could easily dodge.

Just as he was about to give the order, a thought stopped him. Lucy was a Frontier Brain, the Pike Queen. She must know a straightforward Flamethrower could not hit Eevee so easily. Why use it?

He understood almost at once. The flames raced over the pool toward the bank. Lucy did not expect a direct hit, though she would welcome one. The fire was chiefly a screen. Seviper was already swimming toward shore behind it, intending to climb out while Eevee's view was blocked.

But the flames blocked Lucy's view too. She watched Seviper near the bank and raise its head above the edge. Just when she thought it would get ashore, Eevee appeared beside it.

What?

How had Eevee gotten there? Shouldn't Flamethrower have driven it away?

Before Lucy could think it through, Eevee used Take Down and knocked Seviper back into the pool.

He saw through it.

Lucy had treated Ethan as her most difficult opponent, yet she had still underestimated him. Flamethrower could have attacked Eevee and covered Seviper's landing at the same time. Once Ethan recognized the plan and moved Eevee to the bank, the screen worked against Lucy. Seviper had lost sight of Eevee behind its own flames and failed to notice where it had gone.

Splash!

Seviper fell back into the water. Before it could recover, Eevee struck it with Swift, adding another wound.

Lucy could no longer risk approaching Eevee head-on. Her first two attacks had achieved something and made it seem as though she controlled the fight. She had felt the slightest relaxationnot even enough to call carelessnessonly for Ethan to seize back the initiative. Until the battle was truly over, she could not let down her guard.

He had earned his championships. Even a Pokemon that was not one of his main battlers could hold its own against her Seviper. She could not underestimate either of them.

At Lucy's command, Seviper dived, surfaced farther away, and climbed safely onto the bank. Eevee used the pause to shake the remaining water out of its fur. Flamethrower had already evaporated most of it, so the dampness no longer hindered its movement.

They faced each other again. Neither attacked first.

The battle had moved beyond its opening and middle stages. Everyone sensed that the deciding exchange could come at any moment, perhaps with the next move, and watched even more closely.

To Lucy, May, and the women in the stands, either Pokemon still seemed capable of winning. Neither held a clear advantage. Ethan saw it differently. Seviper had shown nearly every tactic it possessed. Unless Lucy had some entirely new move in reserve, what he had already seen no longer posed much of a threat.

It was time to decide the matchon his terms.

At his command, Eevee began its real counterattack. Ethan focused completely. Eevee accelerated and darted in with Quick Attack again and again. Seviper repeated its earlier moves, but they had lost their effect. Ethan read each one, and Eevee's agile footwork carried it out of danger. It found opening after opening and kept landing blows.

The pressure on Lucy rose sharply. Even May and the women watching were startled.

What happened? one of Lucy's supporters asked. It's like we're watching a different person. The boss's Seviper can't fight back at all.

Weren't they trading blows just a moment ago?

May wondered the same thing. She had watched Ethan battle at the Ever Grande Conference and had seen him fight others during their travels. He usually gave her the impression that he won almost effortlessly as a match went on. She had never seen him take on this sharp, relentless style. It was an unfamiliar side of him.

Those were only impressions from the sidelines. Lucy and Seviper felt the change directly.

Lucy could not understand it. She had seemed to have a real chance a moment before. Now Seviper could barely defend itself. Its attacks missed; its movements could not carry it away from Eevee's strikes. Its strength drained rapidly, and it could not organize an effective counterattack. It could only endure.

What had happened? Had she somehow triggered a switch?

She tried several times to change the pattern, but nothing helped. Even when another Quick Attack knocked Seviper down for good, Lucy could scarcely believe it.

We've lost? Weren't we ahead earlier?

The referee announced the result. Only then did Lucy come back to herself and look at Ethan with mixed feelings. So this was what he could really do.

Ethan let out a long breath when he saw he had won. That had not been easy. How long had it been since he had needed to concentrate so hard?

Lucy's Seviper was formidable, but Eevee itself was another reason the match had been so demanding. As Ethan had already noticed, its body was beginning to struggle against opponents this strong. The problem was neither a lack of experience nor poor execution. Its small, adorable form imposed a limit.

Not every Pokemon was Ash's Pikachu, capable of battling Legendary Pokemon one day and losing to a beginner the next. For most Pokemon, their stage of evolution affected both the strength they could bring to a fight and the limit of their potential.

Eevee had done more than enough. But its evolution had become urgent.

Lucy recalled her unconscious Seviper and came over, her expression still complicated. Ethan had seen that look on defeated opponents more times than he could count.

You're incredibly strong, she said. I lost this battle fair and square.

He had heard those words countless times too. Still, praise from the Pike Queen pleased him.

You're giving me too much credit. Your Seviper fought well. It nearly brought down Eevee more than once.

Lucy did not take the polite remark at face value. Nearly winning was still only a hypothetical. Eevee had not fallen. And had she truly had the chance to bring it down?

May and the other women joined them. Lucy's supporters surrounded Ethan and studied him as though he were some remarkable creature. This time his clear victory over their boss had subdued them. They did not dare tease him so freely, though their looks were full of amazement and admiration.

Lucy was not talkative. She had lost, and there was no more to say. She took a medal from her coat and placed it in Ethan's hand.

Please accept my Luck Symbol. It's proof that you defeated me.

Ethan thanked her and carefully put the gleaming gold Symbol into its case.

He had now conquered the Battle Factory, Battle Arena, Battle Dome, Battle Palace, and Battle Pike. Five Frontier Symbols were his. If he defeated the Battle Tower, he would have all six he needed to challenge the last Frontier facility: the Battle Pyramid.

Time had passed quickly. His journey through Kanto's Battle Frontier was nearing its end.

Ethan and May said goodbye and left. By the time they came out of the Battle Pike, evening was close. They returned to Fuchsia City rather than traveling on. After a night at the Pokemon Center and time for their Pokemon to recover, they set off again.

Their next destination was the Battle Tower in southeastern Kanto. There Ethan would meet the Anabel who lived in this world.

Honestly, if the Anabel of the International Police had not warned him in advance, he would have had no idea how to act around the Battle Tower's Anabel.

He would have to pretend he did not know her. That much was certain: he had never met this Anabel. But he knew that face. Treating her like a stranger, keeping any familiarity out of his voice, meeting her eyes without betraying himselfhis acting would soon be put to the test.

...

The Battle Tower was a long way from Fuchsia City. Reaching it meant crossing half of Kanto, a journey that could not be finished in a day. They had three options.

The easiest and quickest was to fly, either on an airplane or on Dragonite. That was also the option Ethan least wanted. The other choices were a ship or the road.

He discussed it with May, and with his suggestion and her agreement, they chose to walk. The distance was considerable, but they would arrive eventually. More important, they would not miss the stories and scenery along the way.

They followed the main road out of Fuchsia City, left the peninsula behind, and walked for most of the day. After lunch, they finally reached the Kanto mainland.

Then the Egg in May's hands began to hatch.

Nurse Joy's estimate had been right. Ethan and May watched expectantly as the shell cracked open and a newborn Eevee came into the world.

Chapter 843: Red Lightning

It had not happened quite as suddenly as it seemed. May was still chatting with Ethan as they walked a mountain path, the Egg cradled in her arms, when she felt it tremble. She thought at first that her grip had slipped on the uneven trail. Then came a faint cracking sound.

Ethan, look! Her eyes lit up as she glanced down. I think the Egg is about to hatch!

It certainly looks that way. One glance told Ethan something was changing. He looked around them. They were halfway up a mountain, with no town ahead or village behind. Forest stretched in every direction, and there was no sign of anyone for miles, let alone a Pokemon Center.

We'll have to welcome the little one ourselves. It's getting dark, so let's camp here tonight.

A Pokemon Egg usually needed no help to hatch. Still, neither of them had done this before, and Ethan wanted to be as careful as he could in case something went wrong. He let several Pokemon out, set up their tent and a simple camp, and prepared hot food and water.

When everything was ready, Ethan, May, and the Pokemon gathered around the fire. Every eye turned toward the Egg. Gengar had slipped out of Ethan's shadow at some point and was watching with interest too.

What? Ethan asked with a smile. You've lived all these years and never seen a Pokemon hatch?

I haven't. Gengar shook its head. Its face held an unusually thoughtful expression. I've even forgotten what it was like when I was born.

The answer brought a weight to the camp. Ethan looked around. His Pokemon had lowered their heads, as if the Egg had made each of them think of its own beginnings.

Who remembered the moment they were born? Beyond that, how many of Ethan's Pokemon had ever known their parents? Someone had given him Gardevoir. Dragonite had been abandoned. Crystal Steelix had always been alone. There were many more such stories.

And Ethan himself was no different. Coming to this world had severed every tie he had on Earthto his parents, relatives, and friends. He was adrift here without roots. He could not go back.

Let's not dwell on that. He gave a rueful shake of his head. We're together now. That makes us a family. Whatever happens next, we'll face it together.

They were bound closely by the Poke Balls and the lives they shared. They might not have been born into one family, but they had become one. With each other beside them, none had to be alone.

May listened quietly. She had parents and a younger brother, so she could not fully know what it felt like to be cut loose from everyone. The sadness in the circle still touched her.

Then the Egg moved again, drawing everyone's attention. A few soft cracks sounded. Before their eyes, its shape changed: the Egg itself transformed into an Eevee. Not a single piece of shell remained.

It was remarkable. The newborn Eevee was smaller than the ones they might meet in the wild, as anyone would expect of a baby. Yet as a Pokemon, it was already developed enough to move, see, hear, and cry. Apart from being more fragile, it looked much like any other Eevee.

It's an Eevee! That's wonderful! May had not known what was inside the Egg, and she was delighted. Eevee was popular and adorable. She liked it on sight.

There was another reason to be happy. As with her Combusken and Ethan's Blaziken, they now had another Pokemon line in common. She hoped to learn from Ethan's Eevee and grow as a Trainer herself.

The baby looked curiously at the people and Pokemon around the fire. Before it could take everything in, a large, fluffy, foxlike head appeared at its side. Ethan's Eevee sniffed its new relative, tail wagging excitedly.

Except for May, no one was happier to see an Eevee hatch. The other Pokemon came close too, each eager to examine and welcome the newcomer. They all gave the new life their warmest care.

May set out the food and water she had prepared. Let me introduce myself. I'm May, she said with a tilted smile. Welcome to the family.

...

Eevee's arrival added to May's team and kept her smiling for a long time. After a night's rest on the mountainside, though, it was time to travel on. Ethan and May set out the next morning, now with a lively little Eevee at May's side.

Seeing how eager it was to explore, Ethan released his own Eevee to guide the newborn and let it discover the countryside. They went along at an easy pace and eventually reached a large city called Commerce City.

Ethan had never visited it and had not even heard its name. That was a gap in his own knowledge, he realized when he saw the many tall buildings. The city looked more prosperous than Viridian or Pewter. Without an official Gym of its own, however, it had little fame among traveling Trainers.

May's first concern on arriving was to ask whether Commerce City held a Pokemon Contest. She soon received good news and bad. It did host one, and its scale and popularity were second only to the Saffron Contest. Unfortunately, the Commerce City Contest had ended two weeks earlier.

May could only laugh ruefully. They had reached the city too late.

Before she could dwell on her disappointment, she heard another piece of local news: the legend of Red Lightning.

People said a strange figure draped from head to toe in a red cloak was attacking Trainers around town. It moved like lightning and could even use Pokemon moves. That was how it had earned its name. It challenged Trainers it met on the street whether they agreed or not. When it won, it covered their Pokemon in graffiti. It had beaten so many that people were growing uneasy.

May told Ethan. He rubbed his chin. A stranger who can use Pokemon moves and only draws on the Pokemon it defeats? Sounds like a Pokemon in disguise.

Red Lightning. Had that character appeared in the anime? Ethan could not remember at all.

I don't think so, May said with a frown. People say it can talk. If that's true...

She had been about to say it could not be a Pokemon. Then she remembered Gengar, and Team Rocket's Meowth. Another talking Pokemon was hardly impossible.

We should be careful, whoever it is, she said. We're Trainers too. It would be troublesome if it decided to target us.

To her surprise, Ethan laughed. Wouldn't that be convenient? Human or Pokemon, it's already caused enough trouble. If we run into it, we'll stop it.

May had thought of Red Lightning as an urban legend. She had briefly forgotten that the man beside her was more legendary than the tale itself. Commerce City was enormous, anyway. The chances of meeting this figure were slim. There was no reason to worry.

Just as she reached that conclusion, a sudden laugh sounded above them while they crossed a park. Both looked up. A figure entirely wrapped in a red cloak stood in a large tree, staring down at them.

A red cloak... Could it be May began.

Heh, heh, heh. The figure looked down on them, and a deep man's voice issued from beneath the cloak. So you've heard my name. That's right. I am Red Lightning!

It extended a red pincer and pointed at Ethan's Eevee. You and I will battle!

Without waiting to see whether Eevee agreed, it jumped down in front of them.

At this range Ethan could make out the red-cloaked figure. His guess had been right: the theatrical stranger was a Scizor. He owned one himself, so the body shape and the portion of its head that showed were easy for him to recognize.

There was something unusual about its left eye. It was a different color, as though the Scizor had mismatched eyesor someone had fitted something over it. Whatever the reason, the cloak did look impressive. Ethan almost wanted one for his own Scizor.

May was still uncertain. You want to battle Eevee? Does that mean you're a Pokemon?

Scizor's humanlike shape, its concealing cloak, and the popularity of Pokemon masks made it hard for her to be sure. Her lack of experience did not help.

Red Lightning gave no answer. It raised its right pincer and attacked. Hot energy gathered there, then a Hyper Beam shot toward Ethan's Eevee.

The beam's path also included Ethan and May. Ethan's brows drew together.

Keeping Trainers out of an attack was an accepted rule of Pokemon battles. A Pokemon living with people in a city, able to understand their speech, could hardly be ignorant of it. They had only just met and had no quarrel. This attack was deliberate.

Ethan's opinion of Red Lightning turned sharply against it. He no longer felt any need to handle the matter gently.

Good. Since we've met, we'll put an end to your troublemaking today. He stared coldly at the Scizor and paid no heed to the approaching beam. He knew someone would act the moment a Trainer was threatened.

A huge ball of dark energy flew from the shadow at his feet and struck the Hyper Beam with perfect aim.

Boom!

The attacks collided in an explosion. Gengar appeared in front of Ethan and May and used its power to shield them from the blast. Across the park, Red Lightning crossed its great pincers to block the shock wave, but the red cloak blew away.

May finally saw what stood beneath it. Scizor! It really is a Pokemon!

Now that its disguise was gone, she noticed an odd device hanging at its neck. It looked like a speaker.

Looks like we've uncovered Red Lightning's real identity, Ethan said.

As the smoke cleared, he walked forward and picked up an object that resembled a false eye. He tossed it lightly in his hand. It had been covering Scizor's left eye and had fallen off in the blast, landing near him.

A camera, he said, and a speaker under your neck. So you aren't a talking Pokemon at all. The so-called Red Lightning is just a puppet someone is controlling.

Chapter 844: A Spoiled Child

Whoever was controlling Scizor had probably never expected its disguise to be exposed so quickly. They could not have expected someone to stop its Hyper Beam so easily, either.

Surprised or not, Scizor kept attacking. It changed targets from the Eevee it had picked out to the ominous-looking Gengar in front of it.

Red Lightning rushed in and swung both great pincers at Gengar. Its fists struck as fast as bullets, dozens of blows in the space of moments. Gengar remained calm. Wearing an insolent grin and letting out its familiar cackling laugh, it vanished and reappeared, easily avoiding the assault.

Scizor abruptly changed its rhythm, slipping a Metal Claw into its string of Bullet Punches to alter the angle of attack. Gengar slipped past that too, almost casually.

Red Lightning had ability. It could never have defeated so many Trainers or caused such a stir otherwise. Against Gengar, though, it could do nothing.

It could be as strong and fierce as it liked. Unless it was an exceptionally powerful Legendary Pokemon, had broken past its body's limits, or had allies to gang up on Gengar, Ethan's two-thousand-year-old partner would put it down. Gengar's moves hit hard, but raw power was not its greatest weapon. Its endlessly varied ways of attacking were almost impossible to guard against. Treating it like an ordinary Pokemon was a sure way to suffer.

Red Lightning had never learned that lesson. Perhaps it had met no worthy opponent before. It fought bravely, but its pincers could not touch even Gengar's shadow. Gengar toyed with it until its body was covered in wounds.

At last Gengar turned toward Ethan. What should I do with this one? Give it a thorough beating or catch it?

Ethan considered it. Scizor was acting on someone's orders. Punishing the Pokemon alone would solve nothing; they needed the person behind it. He gave Gengar a look, and his partner understood.

Gengar formed two Shadow Balls and sent them at Scizor one after the other. While Scizor concentrated on blocking them, Gengar disappeared. It reappeared behind its opponent.

Perhaps it was a Bug-type's instincts that warned Scizor. It felt danger at once. Each pincer smashed a Shadow Ball apart; then Scizor spun and slashed downward with its right claw. It was too late to stop what came next.

A wave of Dark Pulse swept through its guard and struck its body. Scizor crouched in pain, trembling from head to foot as though the blow had become unbearable.

The person controlling it was shocked. Scizor! What's wrong? They had not expected a single hit to leave it almost unable to battle.

Ethan listened for anything revealing in the voice. All he could hear was something like a man in his thirties or forties, and the sound had plainly been synthesized electronically. It gave him no other clue.

Whoever was speaking had evidently realized they had found a dangerous opponent. They did not want to lose Scizor here. As soon as it could stand again, the voice ordered it to retreat. Scizor leaped into the treetop and glided away.

Scizor is flying? May stared. How? It has wings, but I thought it couldn't fly!

It can't. Ethan raised a palm to feel the air. It's the wind. The buildings make drafts all through this city. Scizor is using them to glide over long distances, so it looks as if it's flying. See? It just landed and jumped again.

Before May could reply, Ethan signaled Gengar once more. Grinning, Gengar rose into the air and followed the fleeing Scizor.

Come on. Once Gengar was out of sight, Ethan sent out Gardevoir to guard them. Let's find out what's really behind thisand meet the person in charge.

With Gengar tracking Scizor, there was no risk of losing it and no need to hurry. Ethan and May walked under Gardevoir's guidance. At its current strength, Gardevoir could pinpoint Gengar anywhere in the city, even among crowds and complicated streets. Gengar was cooperating, of course. If it chose to hide its presence, even a Legendary Pokemon would struggle to detect it.

They passed through several narrow streets and came onto a main road leading toward the center of Commerce City. Scizor's refuge had to be somewhere ahead.

Ethan had not expected that, but it made sense. Red Lightning operated throughout the city. A place in the center offered quick routes in every direction.

Still, something puzzled him. The attacks had been going on for some time. How had Officer Jenny and the other Trainers failed to find anything? A red-cloaked figure stood out, even here, and so many assaults should have left traces. Were Scizor and its controller that good at hiding, or was there another reason?

It no longer mattered much. Red Lightning had come after him. Whatever sort of urban legend it had become, Ethan meant to put an end to it today.

People and cars grew more numerous as they entered the city center. Passersby stared curiously at Gardevoir, a Pokemon unfamiliar to many in Kanto. Ethan and May slowed down. Any conspicuous move under so many eyes would attract more attention and complicate what they planned to do.

He began to understand a little of what Officer Jenny and her colleagues might have been dealing with. Perhaps they too had reason to be cautious.

The crowds soon fell behind them. They turned into another alley and could move freely again. Gardevoir stopped and pointed toward the top of the tallest building nearby. At that moment Gengar floated down from above.

You took your time, it said quietly. Red Lightning's nest is up there. I have to say, rich people live well.

Ethan did not understand the remark until Gardevoir used Teleport to take him and May to the roof.

On top of a building nearly thirty stories tall stood an entire estate. Its main house was a huge three-story villa with a tower. A fountain, lawns, and landscaped gardens spread out before it. The estate occupied the whole rooftop.

This really is how rich people live, May said, staring. I've only seen houses like this on television.

Ethan was impressed by the owner's wealth too. Surely they owned the building; who else could build an estate on its roof?

So that's how they stayed hidden, he said. Up here, ordinary people would have trouble spotting them. Even the police might hesitate to act if they suspected the owner. And attacking Trainers only to draw faces on their Pokemonthat sounds like the whim of someone with too much money. The person behind it might even be a child.

Gengar stared at him. How did you know it really is a child? I followed Scizor up here and saw it talking to a little girl.

A girl? Ethan nodded. I expected a boy, but that doesn't matter. I guessed from the pranks. Who but a child would spend their time drawing on Pokemon's faces?

There was no reason to hide now. Ethan led May and their Pokemon openly toward the house. After the trouble its owner had caused across the city, she could be the one to worry.

They were noticed almost at once. As they reached the villa's entrance, a little girl appeared with the same Scizor.

She looked younger than May. Her brown hair was tied into two ponytails, and she wore a red dress. She was pretty and carried herself with the confidence of a child raised in a wealthy home. That confidence faltered visibly when she saw them.

You followed me here? How did you find this place?

Her voice sounded nothing like the synthesized man's voice from Scizor's speaker, but the tone was familiar. Ethan knew she had been controlling Red Lightning.

Was it supposed to be difficult? he asked. You just hadn't met a capable Trainer before. Picking on beginners proves nothing.

Whether it was his tone or the discovery of her hiding place, the girl grew angry. What? You don't like my pranks?

Pranks? Ethan shook his head. I haven't seen all of them, but people in this city have suffered because of you. More Pokemon than I can count have needed treatment at the Pokemon Center after your attacks. You went far beyond a prank. And you tried to hit me a few minutes ago. Would calling that deliberate harm be unfair?

Her face flushed, whether from fear or anger Ethan could not tell. This is none of your business! You came into my home without permission. I won't let you get away with that! Red Lightning, defeat them!

Scizor stepped in front of her again. Gengar had driven it off once, but it stood bravely now to protect its Traineror perhaps its owner.

Someone else came running toward them. Please, wait!

Ethan turned. An elderly man dressed as a butler hurried up, breathless. Without even taking time to recover, he addressed Ethan.

Sir, please wait. When Ethan did not attack, the man exhaled and bowed. Please forgive Miss Luna's rash behavior. I know these pranks have gone too far. Could you be generous and let the matter rest?

Ethan raised an eyebrow. So you knew she was attacking Pokemon around the city?

Well... The butler hesitated at his tone. The master and mistress know nothing of it. I alone knew that Miss Luna

Stop talking. I don't need you meddling in my affairs! Luna interrupted.

May could hold back no longer. Why are you doing this?

Luna lifted her chin. Because it's fun, of course!

May stared. That's...that's your only reason?

Of course. How many times do I have to say it? Nobody gets to tell me what to do. Now you've invaded my home, so be ready for what happens next. Red Lightning, use Hyper Beam!

Chapter 845: Perhaps a Different Approach

Ethan understood the situation now. Luna was a spoiled child who cared only about amusing herself and easing her loneliness, without considering anyone else.

She treated attacks on Trainers, and battles forced on people who did not want them, as an exciting game. The butler had not told her parents; he had hidden the truth. Unable to stop her himself, he had let it continue. He had not helped her attack anyone, but his silence made him complicit. If Luna went on like this, she would eventually cause a disaster.

Before he arrived, Ethan might have had no place involving himself in her affairs. Scizor had attacked him too, however. Now the matter concerned him directly.

Scizor gathered another Hyper Beam and fired toward him. This time Gengar did not intervene. Gardevoir used its psychic power to halt the attack.

Luna saw a chance. She was furious with Ethan for meddling, but wary of the Gengar that had already defeated Red Lightning. Seeing another Pokemon take its place gave her some relief.

She was young, but no fool. Red Lightning had beaten many Trainers in this large city, showing her all sorts of Pokemon. Her wealthy upbringing also gave her access to plenty of information. She knew what Gardevoir was. Scizor's Steel typing gave it an advantage against Gardevoir on both offense and defense. She did not know why Ethan had set aside Gengar, but she would seize the opportunity.

Red Lightning, use Agility!

Scizor rushed toward Gardevoir. Luna imagined it dodging Gardevoir's Confusion, closing the distance, and keeping the Psychic-type pinned down. Then victory would belong to Red Lightning.

She trusted her Pokemon. After all its victories in the city, she knew how strong it was. The Trainers she had met before had failed against it, and she expected this irritating man to fail too.

Reality disagreed. Scizor had covered barely half the distance when Gardevoir raised its right hand. It predicted exactly where Scizor would step. Psychic force hit like an invisible wall and hurled it backward.

Red Lightning! Luna cried, stunned.

Scizor got up at once and charged again. This time it knew a direct approach would not work. It used Double Team. Five copies appeared alongside the real Scizor, and six identical red figures lunged at Gardevoir.

Luna smiled. She had seen this many times. A weak opponent fell to Hyper Beam. A stronger one might resist that, but Agility and Double Team let Red Lightning close in and defeat it. So many Trainers had lost to this combination. Surely it would work again.

Gardevoir lifted its other hand. Both hands moved, and a second surge of psychic force struck. The real Scizor flew backward, while all five copies vanished at once.

What? Luna's face changed again. Since meeting Ethan, she had gone from delight to alarm to anger and back several times. Now even Red Lightning's familiar combination had been broken.

Scizor stood again, but did not rush forward. It fired Swift from a safer distance. Gardevoir formed an invisible barrier before itself, and every star struck that barrier instead. Scizor's attack achieved nothing.

Luna's heart sank. Her Pokemon looked like a small child being toyed with by an adult. Could the gap between Red Lightning and this Gardevoir really be so wide?

She was intelligent despite her age. A child who could direct one Scizor to victory against so many Trainers had talent and had grown through repeated battles. Both her command and Red Lightning's strength exceeded what most children her age could manage, even surpassing plenty of ordinary Trainers. She knew it, which was why she had acted so fearlessly.

Now the skill she prized was failing before Ethan, and the confidence she had built over so long was breaking with it.

As she searched for something to do, the butler stepped in Ethan's way again.

Stop! His voice was stern. Sir, leave this property at once. You're trespassing. If you refuse, I'll inform the master and mistress and hold you responsible. Perhaps you don't know that they are famous inventors and influential people in this city.

The old butler was loyal to his employers, but he was hardly being reasonable. Did he think a threat would frighten Ethan? Luna's parents were inventors; so what? Their devotion to work had plainly left them little time to supervise their daughter.

Ethan shook his head. He did not care to argue. He took his Special Investigator of the International Police credentials from his wallet and held them up.

Read this. I didn't come here at random. I followed the person responsible for the attacks.

He had not wanted to invoke that position, but this was the second time a situation like this had forced his hand. An official title was undeniably useful where a private citizen might be turned away.

Despite his poor eyesight, the butler could read the credentials. He stiffened. An International Police Special Investigator? And Ethan was calling Miss Luna responsible for a crime?

This had gone beyond what he could manage. He took out his phone to call her parents, but he was too late.

Without waiting for another order, Gardevoir subdued Scizor, held Luna with its psychic power, and used Teleport to take them both away. Before the butler could cry out, Ethan released Dragonite and left with May. A moment later, the rooftop estate was empty except for the butler, frantic with worry.

...

Gardevoir appeared outside the Commerce City police station with Luna and Scizor. Seconds later, Ethan and May arrived on Dragonite.

He had noticed the station on the way to Luna's villa and asked Gardevoir to remember its location for this purpose. The officers came out in surprise at the group's arrival. Ethan told them what had happened.

They were astonished. Red Lightning, the figure that had thrown all of Commerce City into turmoil, was a Scizor. The person directing it was a girl of only eight or nine.

They took Luna and Scizor inside, contacted their superiors, and notified her parents. Once the handover was complete, Ethan left the matter with them.

He had no wish to be hard-hearted toward a little girl. But what she had done was too serious for a simple apology to erase. Even if he forgave her attack on him, would all the Trainers she had hurt forgive her?

The graffiti was trivial. The injuries were not. How many Pokemon had their worried Trainers rushed to the Pokemon Center after Scizor defeated them? That was why Ethan had taken matters this far. Luna needed to learn that her actions had consequences.

What the police did next, how her parents apologized to the Trainers, and whether Luna came to understand her wrongdoing were no longer his decisions. He did not even want to follow the case. He had done his part.

Outside the station, May seemed about to speak, then held back. Ethan glanced at her and sighed softly.

You think I handled it badly?

She shook her head, hesitated, then nodded. I think there must be a better way. Maybe...we didn't need to take her to the police. If someone explained it to her first, she might learn to do the right thing.

She was still a little naive. Ethan smiled without arguing. Maybe. But I think people trained to handle this should take it from here. We're travelers. We can judge what happened without deciding what sort of person she is. A child doesn't get a pass for wrongdoing because she's young or rich.

May still looked uncertain, so he continued. Think about what would have happened if she hadn't met us today. How many more people would she and Scizor have attacked? And we're traveling. We don't have the time or means to guide her through everything she needs to learn.

May nodded. He had persuaded her to some extent, though she still had reservations.

Ethan looked up at the blue sky. We aren't trying to punish her. We want the attacks to end and the people she hurt to receive an answer.

...

They left Commerce City and continued toward the Battle Tower. After camping for the night, they arrived around noon the next day in a small town called Gardenia Town. At last, May had found the Pokemon Contest she had been hoping for.

Something else surprised her even more. Outside the town's Pokemon Center, she and Ethan ran into Ash and his friends again.

It was quite a coincidence. May had left Ash's group, so they had no particular reason to stop and watch Contests anymore. Yet here they were. To Ash and his companions, however, their meeting did not seem so unexpected.

See? Ash said proudly to Brock and Max at the Pokemon Center doors. I told you I had a feeling we'd meet Ethan and May here. I was right!

He hurried over to Ethan. How many Symbols have you got?

Five. One more at the Battle Tower, then I can challenge the last facility. What about you?

Heh, heh. Ash opened his Symbol case to show Ethan. I've got four! Metallica Island is next!

Their routes had crossed. After Ash challenged the facility on Metallica Island, he would still need to make a long detour to the Battle Tower for his final Symbol.

Even so, Ash was moving fast. He still got lost and caught up in incidents along the road, but without May traveling with him, he no longer stopped for her Contests. That alone had made his journey smoother and quicker.

Chapter 846: Brock's Coordinator Debut

After so long apart, they had plenty to catch up on. As usual when they met again, Ethan treated everyone to a generous meal at a good restaurant. Brock's cooking was delicious, but gathering around a table to eat, drink, and talk had a different pleasure of its own.

Ash, Brock, and Max met May's new Eevee there. They played with it and congratulated her. Then they learned she intended to use the recently hatched Pokemon for her appeal in the first round of the Gardenia Contest. The three exchanged uneasy looks.

Isn't that risky? Brock asked after a pause. Eevee only hatched a few days ago. Would entering it in a Contest already be too much?

He had a point. May had only recently taken first place in an appeal round before advancing to the Contest Battle stage. Her run of wins looked promising, but she had achieved it without facing a formidable rival. Against someone like Drew, she would have a much harder fight.

To Ash and the others, this seemed the time for May to consolidate what she had learned rather than introduce an untested Pokemon. Eevee lacked experience and had never taken part in anything like a Contest. That would place even more pressure on May's own ability as a Coordinator.

May had thought about it. It'll be all right. I've shown Eevee lots of recordings during our breaks these past few days, and we've practiced a lot. We work well together. As long as we don't make a major mistake, I think we'll get through the appeal.

They still looked worried. Ethan spoke up. May has made her decision. Let's trust her. Besides, this is a small-town Contest. There won't be as many entrants, and probably no especially troublesome opponents. She has a good chance.

With Ethan supporting her, the other three let the matter rest.

After lunch, they went to inspect the venue. Like the Silver Town Contest that had brought them across the office worker, the Gardenia Contest was modest in scale. Its hall sat amid a stretch of lawn. From a distance it looked like half a Poke Ball set facedown on the grass, right down to the round shape and similar colors. There were not many contestants, and the stands held only a few thousand seats.

They helped May register, then came outside to the lawn. The Contest was tomorrow, so Coordinators were practicing all around them with their Pokemon: Bellsprout, Ninetales, Sentret, Koffing, and many others.

There was plenty of activity, but Ethan saw no familiar face among them. It appeared to be an ordinary small Contest without a particularly dangerous rival. May felt a little more confident.

She was about to practice with Eevee on the grass when she met a girl coming the other way with a Raticate.

The girl was about May's age and height. She wore a sleeveless green dress, and her sea-green hair was tied in a side ponytail. Pretty and rather sweet-looking, she seemed anxious now, glancing about as if she were lost.

Hello, she asked May timidly. Could you tell me where to register for the Contest?

May pointed to a small door beside the hall's main entrance. Over there.

Oh, thank you so much! The girl brightened. She was close in age to Luna, the wealthy child they had met the day before in Commerce City, but her manners could hardly have been more different.

As the girl started away, May called after her. Um...is this your first Pokemon Contest?

Yes! She nodded eagerly. The Gardenia Contest will be my very first!

A new Coordinator. Seeing her brought back May's own early days. Perhaps she had looked just as uncertain then.

I'm May. I'm entering too. If there's anything you don't understand, you can ask me.

That would be wonderful! I'm Mollie. It's nice to meet you.

After another grateful nod, Mollie went briskly to register. May knew time was short and took Eevee onto the grass to practice.

Ethan and the others left her to it and sat on a nearby bench to watch. Ash could not sit still for long. After only a few minutes he jumped up.

Ethan, just waiting here is boring. Since we have the chance, want to battle?

Ethan had nothing else to do and was about to agree when a woman approached them. She walked straight toward Brock, drawing every eye.

She seemed to be in her late twenties. Long, smooth hair fell past an orange T-shirt; she wore a fitted red skirt and black stockings. Her composed appearance concealed a lively warmth.

Oh my...how wonderful! So charming!

She stood before Brock, looking him over with obvious enthusiasm and murmuring praise. Even Brock grew shy under that attention. His face turned crimson, and he trembled with excitement.

Was this finally his chance? She was beautiful, and a little older than him, exactly the kind of woman who caught his eye. Hearts practically appeared in his eyes.

You're too kind! Compared with you, my charm is nothing!

The woman did not seem to hear him. She leaned closer and reached outto lift the Bonsly he had been holding.

This Bonsly is absolutely perfect!

Brock's smile froze. Only then did everyone realize she had been admiring his Pokemon, not him. It was an awkward misunderstanding. Ethan could almost hear Brock's heart breaking.

...

They later gathered beneath a sun umbrella: Ethan, May, Ash, Brock, Max, and the woman, each with a hot drink at the table. She still held Brock's Bonsly.

Ethan had only just met it, but Ash had mentioned it during lunch. Brock had caught Bonsly by chance a few days earlier while traveling past a ninja school. Though it had been with him only a short time, his careful attention had left it in excellent condition. This woman had noticed immediately.

I'm sorry about earlier, she said with a smile. My name is Yuma. I'm a Pokemon Breeder. It's a pleasure to meet you.

The others were surprised to meet another Breeder. Brock seized on the connection. Miss Yuma, I'm a Breeder too! What a coincidence!

Yuma smiled. I could tell as soon as I saw you. She looked down at Bonsly with admiration. Its sheen and its condition make it clear. You care for it differently from the Trainers and Coordinators here. That's something a Breeder can do.

You can tell all that just by looking? Ash asked.

Of course. Breeders concentrate on managing Pokemon's health. Trainers and Coordinators focus more on strengthening their bodies and moves. That affects their diets and even how their Pokeblocks are mixed. I can see the difference at a glance.

Her explanation showed her expertise. Ash, May, and Max were impressed. Ethan had to acknowledge it too. He had talent for battling, but May knew more about appeals, and Yuma clearly knew more about caring for Pokemon. Each field demanded its own skill.

Delighted to meet a fellow Breeder, and a beautiful one at that, Brock brought out his other Pokemon. Marshtomp and Forretress appeared in two flashes of blue light.

They're beautiful! Yuma examined them and praised them freely. Brock showed her the Pokemon food he had prepared as well. After tasting it, she was even more impressed.

Amazing. She looked at him with shining eyes. I didn't expect to meet such an accomplished Breeder here. Would you consider entering the Contest?

Brock? In a Pokemon Contest? The suggestion surprised them all. Why would a Breeder ask another Breeder to compete as a Coordinator?

Me? Brock asked.

Yuma smiled at their puzzled faces. You might not guess it now, but I used to be a Coordinator. I even competed in a Grand Festivaland won.

Winning a Grand Festival was the Coordinator's equivalent of a League championship. It was no small feat. Ash and the others exclaimed again. May was especially startled: the woman who had introduced herself as a Breeder had once been a top Coordinator.

Breeding and Coordinating do share a great deal, Brock said. But why do you want me in this Contest?

My Breeder's skills helped me win that Grand Festival, Yuma explained. I believe it's my job now to pass what I learned on to the next generation of newcomers.

They understood. Yuma had recognized Brock's skill from the way he cared for his Pokemon and wanted him to bring that skill into a Contest, just as she had.

Before Brock could answer, May stood. Miss Yuma, please teach me those techniques!

I'm sorry. Yuma shook her head. I want to train a complete beginner. You're already a capable Coordinator in your own right.

May was disappointed to be turned down, but praise from a Grand Festival winner still pleased her. Yuma looked back to Brock. He had made up his mind.

I understand. His face took on a determined expression. Then he clasped Yuma's hand with a broad smile. If that's what you wish, Miss Yuma, I'll do it!

Before she could add another word, he let go and dashed off toward registration. Ethan laughed to himself at Yuma's astonished face. She could hardly have expected to meet a Breeder with Brock's peculiar personality. Perhaps she was already wondering whether events had escaped her control.

Brock raced back almost immediately and proudly waved his Contest Pass in front of her. He had been fast enough to give her no chance to reconsider.

Ethan could no longer hold in his laughter. He turned to May. Looks like Brock is making his Coordinator debut here. You've gained a troublesome opponent.

Chapter 847: May Versus Brock

May had not expected things to turn out this way. Brock was not finished surprising her. Fired up by his decision to compete, he challenged her directly.

You'd better be ready, May! The brilliant Miss Yuma has personally vouched for me. I'll be the biggest obstacle between you and the Gardenia Ribbon!

May had thought the Contest would have no strong rivals. Now a friend was entering to compete against her. Brock was a formidable opponent. If he passed the appeal round, his years as a Gym Leader would make him difficult for most Coordinators to beat.

But May was not afraid. Yuma could teach Brock; May had Ethan beside her. In appeals or battles, she intended to win.

She smiled. I'm looking forward to it. Just be careful you don't go out in the first round.

Same to you. Brock folded his arms and smiled confidently through his narrow eyes. You and Eevee are the ones who need to be careful.

Once he had committed to entering, Brock seemed transformed. He went off with Yuma for private training. Ash and Max followed, curious to see what sort of special methods she had. Ash forgot all about his proposed battle with Ethan.

That left Ethan and May together again. Brock's challenge had stirred May's determination, and she returned to practice with renewed energy. Ethan could only shake his head and recline on the bench, waiting to see what would happen.

...

It's performance time!

At Lillian's familiar opening cry, the Gardenia Contest began amid the audience's cheers. Ethan sat in the stands with Ash and Max. With two friends competing, they had stayed out of the contestants' waiting room rather than favor either one. They would simply watch and cheer for both May and Brock.

Lillian explained the rules, introduced the same three familiar judges, and welcomed the first Coordinator to the stage.

To Ethan's surprise, it was Mollie, the girl who had asked May for directions on the lawn. She carried a long wooden stick, whose purpose was not yet clear. Despite being a newcomer onstage for the first time before so many people, she showed no nerves. She walked out gracefully and bowed.

Then she released the Raticate they had seen with her. Mollie threw the stick high. Raticate sprang after it and caught it between its two large front teeth. In moments it had gnawed the wood to pieces. The simple performance showed off Raticate's particular charm, and the crowd cheered.

She doesn't perform like a beginner, Ethan said after Mollie finished. Plenty of people who've entered several Contests couldn't stay that calm and composed. Give her a few years, and I think she'll be one of the top Coordinators.

Ash and Max were startled to hear him praise someone so strongly, but they could see why. Mollie received a good score. She bowed once more before leaving the stage, as poised and polite as ever.

Several other contestants followed with competent, unremarkable appeals. Then it was May's turn.

As planned, her partner was Eevee. She used a ball as a prop, creating an interplay between herself, the ball, and her Pokemon. There were no dazzling moves. Instead, the routine brought out Eevee's grace and skill. May had clearly planned it with care. She and Eevee made no major mistakes, earned another high score, and safely advanced to the battle round.

Brock performed last. After seeing everyone else's appeals, he could not help feeling nervous. His partner was Bonsly, the Pokemon Yuma had admired.

Bonsly began with Fake Tears. Streams poured from its eyes like little fountains, making the audience laugh. Then the mood changed. Brock and Bonsly tossed and caught baseballs together, displaying the Pokemon's dexterity and cuteness.

Like May, Brock had chosen not to rely on flashy moves. His performance drew its appeal from his Pokemon's own character. The audience applauded warmly.

When all the scores appeared, Ethan looked up and saw that May, Brock, and Mollie had all advanced to the Contest Battle stage. Working with a new Pokemon, May placed third in the appeals. That was lower than her recent best, but still a solid result. Brock placed sixth and Mollie eighthstrong debuts for two newcomers.

The draw for the next round brought less welcome news for Brock and Mollie: they would face each other first. Only one of the new Coordinators could advance.

During the interval, Ash, Max, and Yuma went backstage to encourage May and Brock. Ethan stayed in his seat. As before, watching this Contest felt rather like watching a film whose ending he already knew. He would leave the preparations to the others.

The break passed quickly. Ash and the others returned to the stands, and the Contest Battles began. Brock and Mollie were first.

Brock sent out Marshtomp. When Mollie released her Pokemon, a startled murmur spread through the audience. She had an Absol.

The Dark-type Pokemon was a four-legged creature with something of a fox or a graceful large cat about it. White fur covered its body, red eyes looked out beneath a curved horn, and long fur fell across its face in a shape like a hooked jewel.

Its appearance was striking, but that was not the chief reason people reacted. Some might mistake it for a Mythical Pokemon on first sight, although Absol was simply uncommon rather than exceptionally rare. What made people wary was an old rumor.

Absol could sense changes in the sky and earth that warned of disasters. It came down from the mountains when danger approached. Over time, people came to call it the Disaster Pokemon. In more superstitious times, they had blamed it for the catastrophes it tried to warn them about and driven it away.

In truth, its ominous appearance concealed a gentle nature. It sometimes even protected fields without the farmers knowing. It had been misunderstood.

Still, for a beginning Coordinator to own an Absol was remarkable. Unfortunately for Mollie, her first Contest Battle was against Brock, a former Pewter Gym Leader.

He might lose his composure around a beautiful older woman, but the young girl opposite him saw an entirely different side. Brock would give her no mercy in battle.

Mollie had Absol attack immediately. Perhaps she had only recently caught it, for it had few strong moves at its disposal. It relied on Scratch, Razor Wind, and Quick Attack. Marshtomp had not reached its final evolution either and knew no overwhelming technique, but Brock's experience and judgment created a gap between the two teams.

Mud Shot was enough to shut down Absol's speed. Brock finished with Water Gun, and Absol fell. The Pokemon had exchanged fewer than three rounds of attacks before the result was decided.

Mollie left the stage with Absol, visibly disappointed. Facing an opponent that strong in her first Contest Battle could easily shake her confidence. Ethan sympathized, but Brock could not be expected to hold back. Giving his full effort was a responsibility to himself and his Pokemon. This was a competition, not a Gym challenge. Taking it easy on Mollie here would have been a mistake.

The audience applauded both of them. Other pairs battled, but Ethan's earlier judgment held: apart from May and Brock, nobody in this Gardenia Contest looked especially difficult. May's Munchlax performed well, and she and Brock met in the final.

Brock had kept his word. He was May's greatest obstacle to the Ribbon.

The final paired Munchlax against Marshtomp. Max looked from one end of the stage to the other, then spread his hands. One side is my sister, and the other is Brock. I don't know who to cheer for.

Ash had an easy answer. Cheer for both of them!

With the audience waiting and their friends watching, the final began. May attacked aggressively from the outset, sending Munchlax at Marshtomp again and again.

Brock knew how difficult she could be. He ordered Protect to block as many attacks as possible while he searched for an opening. He had been a Gym Leader, and he had traveled with May for a long time. He spotted a weakness quickly.

Between Munchlax's attacks, Marshtomp used Mud Shot. The spray coated Munchlax and turned a broad patch of ground beneath it slick. Munchlax lost its footing and fell hard.

Marshtomp slid over the mud to close in. Its unusual hands and feet made the wet ground an aid rather than an obstacle; it moved faster across it. Munchlax struggled upright, slipped again, and fell. Marshtomp drove its head into Munchlax.

But as Marshtomp tried to pull away, Munchlax grabbed hold of it.

Brock had not expected that. He had avoided Water Gun because it would wash away the mud. His plan had been to beat Munchlax while it could not stand steadily. Somehow it had seized a chance anyway. May and her Pokemon truly had grown.

There was no time to admire them. Brock tried to get Marshtomp free, but Munchlax clung on as though to a lifeline. Marshtomp pulled and Munchlax held tight until both of them slid off the muddy patch onto dry ground.

There Munchlax released it on its own. Brock felt no relief. His attack had failed, and at such close range Munchlax now had the advantage.

Ash turned toward Ethan. Who do you think will win?

May, Ethan said without hesitation.

Why my sister? Max asked.

Ethan laughed. Isn't it obvious? It has nothing to do with their strength or how they're doing. May is my traveling companion. Of course I want her to win.

Chapter 848: The Tomboy

Ethan's words were a little unfair to Brock, but Ash and Max did not argue. He was free to cheer for whomever he liked. Brock was a friend, yet Ethan had never traveled with him; May was his traveling companion. Different relationships brought different loyalties.

Ash and Max had traveled with both contestants, and Max was May's brother besides. They were the ones who found it hard to choose a side.

Onstage, the battle continued. After the last exchange, Brock finally managed to put some distance between Marshtomp and Munchlax. He tried Mud Shot again to hamper Munchlax's movement, but May was ready.

Munchlax, Solar Beam!

A surge of energy interrupted Mud Shot and struck Marshtomp hard. It had to scramble away.

Both finalists were plainly stronger than the earlier contestants. They traded attacks and counterattacks on nearly equal terms, thrilling the audience. The match felt less like a graceful Contest Battle and more like a straight fight between Trainers. No one minded. A good battle was a good battle.

Even the best battle had to end. May's Munchlax found an opening, closed in on Marshtomp, and defeated it with Focus Punch. The Gardenia Ribbon was hers.

Brock shook his head ruefully. He regretted not going farther, but May was his friend and former companion. He applauded and congratulated her sincerely. Traveling beside Ethan had clearly helped her grow.

May accepted her fourth Ribbon amid the crowd's cheers. One more would qualify her for the Grand Festival coming soon. She and Ethan were now at roughly the same stage in their respective journeys, which meant neither would have to hold the other up for long.

Brock did not seem discouraged by his defeat. Yuma had become his mentor, and the prospect of spending time with such a beautiful woman made him happy. During the interval, she had even come backstage and invited him to travel with her afterward. He was still thinking it over; leaving Ash and Max would be hard. But from his point of view, things were going well.

Then they left the Contest Hall. Outside, Brock saw Yuma standing with Mollie.

His heart dropped.

Yuma smiled faintly as he approached. Brock, after that match I can see you're already an excellent Coordinator. I have nothing more to teach you.

His hopes sank. Miss Yuma, what do you mean?

She looked toward Mollie. This was her first Contest too. I've decided to become her mentor.

What? Brock felt as if the sky had fallen. He made one last attempt. But I... I think I still

Yuma shook her head before he could finish. Keep working hard, Brock. I hope we meet again at a Grand Festival one day.

She left with Mollie without giving him another chance to speak. Brock took the second blow like a man made of glass. In the evening light, Ethan could almost imagine him shattering across the ground.

It was a little pitiful. Ethan shook his head. He could have seen this coming. Brock's endless, eager infatuation with women might have been more than Yuma wanted to handle. More than that, Brock's ability left her little pleasure in teaching him.

Why had she approached him? She wanted to show a beginning Coordinator how a Breeder's skills could help in a Contest. Brock had entered his first and placed second. He hardly resembled a beginner. What was there for her to teach?

Ash patted Brock's shoulder with a mischievous smile. Come on, don't lose heart. Better luck next time.

Next time? Brock's expression crumpled. He shouted at the sky, There won't be a next time! I'm never becoming a Coordinator again!

His Coordinator debut ended on a bitter memory. Still, Brock had been turned down by women many times before. He would survive this too.

...

After a night in Gardenia Town, the two groups said goodbye in the morning and set out for their separate destinations. Ash, Brock, and Max headed for Ash's next Frontier facility. Ethan and May continued toward the Battle Tower.

It was not far from Gardenia Town. Ethan remembered seeing a Battle Tower in LaRousse City, Hoennthe technological city where he had encountered wild Deoxys and Rayquaza and later battled its block-shaped robots. That tower belonged to Hoenn's Frontier facilities, however, and had nothing to do with Kanto. He had passed by without challenging it.

Kanto's Battle Tower stood at the far eastern edge of the mainland, alone in a broad forest, distant from towns and people. After more than a day's travel, Ethan and May reached the forest.

Its remoteness made the tower hard to find. There was no road or trail underfoot and no landmark to guide them. They soon lost their bearings among the trees.

Fortunately, Ethan was not Ash. He did not keep wandering at random. He found the forest's only lake and followed the water. That led them easily toward the tower. Long before they reached it, they could see a building more than twenty stories high through gaps in the foliage.

That's the Battle Tower? May asked, looking up.

It is. Ethan smiled. Surprised? Did you expect a tower shape?

A little. She stuck out her tongue. The Battle Factory, Battle Dome, and Battle Palace didn't look quite the way their names suggested either, so I was prepared. I just didn't expect a building this...

Luxurious?

Yes. She examined what looked more like an expensive office building. Why build it so grandly in an empty forest? It doesn't fit the surroundings at all.

As they drew nearer, they heard a voice ahead. They assumed it belonged to a wild Pokemon until they went around several large trees and found a short, purple-haired youth muttering beneath one of them.

The youth was only a little taller than May, with delicate features and an apparent age somewhere in the teens. Hearing their footsteps, the figure started and turned around with a small cry. The voice was androgynous. With those boyish clothes and build, most people would have taken the stranger for a boy.

Ethan knew better the moment he saw her. She was Anabel, the Frontier Brain of the Battle Towerthe Salon Maiden.

Her face, voice, and figure all made it easy to mistake her for a boy. Ash and his friends had done so in the anime, not realizing their error until someone corrected them. Even Ethan found it hard to imagine that this tomboy would one day become the more feminine Anabel he knew in the International Police. A resemblance around her eyes was almost all that linked them at first glance.

Sorry. Did we startle you? May asked. She knew none of that and had never met this Anabel.

It's all right. Anabel put a hand against her chest and studied them. What brings you here?

Remembering the International Police Anabel's request, Ethan showed no hint of recognition. He smiled and explained that he had come to challenge the Battle Tower.

I thought so. Anabel smiled back. People rarely come here for anything else, but I always ask. Oh, I forgot to introduce myself. I'm Anabel, the Frontier Brain of that tower.

You're the Frontier Brain? May was astonished. She had pictured an imposing adult when she heard about the Battle Tower's ruler, not this delicate-looking boy. Ethan had given her no warning to expect otherwise.

Anabel led them toward the tower. She explained why she had been in the forest: she was patrolling the surrounding land. She considered herself its guardian. When no challengers came, she spent much of her time checking the forest's condition and looking for wild Pokemon that might need help.

From directly below, the building seemed taller still. A green-haired man with the look of a ninja came out as they reached its doors.

Back early today, Anabel? he greeted her. Then he noticed Ethan and May. More challengers? It feels as though there've been more of them lately. That must keep you busy.

Anabel waved a hand. It's my job.

Their easy exchange sounded like ordinary workplace conversation. It made it even harder for May to connect the youth beside her with the grand title of Frontier Brain.

Inside, they entered a bright hall. This was the Battle Tower's arena. At first glance it looked like a normal indoor venue, almost a basketball court, complete with a wooden floor.

Ethan could not understand that choice. The flooring might survive a light match, but a single Pokemon using Dig could tear holes through it in minutes. Had the people who built these Gyms and Frontier facilities never considered that? Were they rich enough not to care, able to repair any damage, or secretly in business with a flooring supplier?

If he ever ran a Gym, he would never choose a battlefield floor like this.

May headed to the seats. Ethan and Anabel took the Trainer positions at opposite sides of the arena.

The Frontier battle between challenger Ethan Vale and Battle Tower Brain Anabel will now begin! Each side may use three Pokemon. Only the challenger may switch Pokemon during the battle!

The rules sounded much like those of an ordinary Gym match. In a sense, that was an awkward weakness of the Battle Frontier. Its facilities were less conveniently placed and less famous than official Gyms. Beyond the exceptional strength of some Frontier Brains, they offered little to distinguish themselves. No wonder Scott, who owned the whole enterprise, traveled around recruiting challengers and spreading the word.

Anabel had already taken out her Poke Ball. She threw it firmly, blue light flashed, and Alakazam appeared before Ethan.

Whatever the difference in appearance between this tomboy and the Anabel of the International Police, their choice of Pokemon, at least, was much the same.

Chapter 849: I Admit I Took a Gamble

Anabel was a difficult opponent, both now and in her later life with the International Police. In the anime, Ash had lost to her once, trained specifically for a rematch, and only beaten her on his second visit. That alone said a great deal about her strength.

The young Anabel had another remarkable ability. Since childhood she had sensed what Pokemon were thinking. She could communicate with wild Pokemon, almost converse with them, and sometimes reach a state of complete harmony with them. In theory it was closer to unusually keen empathy than psychic power, but people still considered her a psychic.

Scott had said that when Anabel became excited during a battle, she could even convey her thoughts directly to her Pokemon. She could guide them without speaking, as if by telepathy. In those moments, Scott considered her the strongest Frontier Brain in some respects. That was his judgment; everyone had their own view of who deserved the top place.

Whatever the ranking, Anabel belonged among the strongest Frontier Brains. Ethan had never sensed that ability in the International Police Anabel. Perhaps passing through the Ultra Wormhole and losing her memories had cost her this gift as well.

He studied the Alakazam across the arena and took out the Poke Ball he had prepared. Blue light flashed, and Dragonite appeared.

Ethan had decided on Dragonite before arriving. It was a normal part of rotating his team; he would have chosen it even if Anabel had sent out someone else. At his level, type matchups were no longer the only concern. His Pokemon could fight through unfavorable situations. Giving each of them time to battle and keeping the team developing evenly mattered more to him.

Dragonite and Alakazam had no direct type advantage over each other. That made the match seem comparatively even.

The green-haired referee saw both Pokemon ready and signaled the start.

Dragonite beat its wings and rose into the air, looking for a chance to strike from above. Anabel directed Alakazam to defend and counter, meeting movement with stillness. The two styles made for a compelling battle.

Dragonite tested it with Wing Attack. Alakazam fired Psybeam, hoping both to hurt Dragonite and disturb its condition, but Dragonite was too fast for the beam to land. Alakazam then used Teleport to avoid the incoming wing.

One exchange was enough for both Trainers to recognize a serious opponent. Ethan had expected it and knew roughly how skilled Anabel was. She, meanwhile, was startled by Dragonite's reactions. This challenge would be hard.

Dragonite attacked again, much more fiercely this time. Alakazam's psychic power struck repeatedly. The force was invisible, making it harder to evade than most moves, but Dragonite's experience in the air let it slip away again and again.

Alakazam was experienced too. It was one of Anabel's main Pokemon, and its close bond with her sharpened their coordination. As it learned Dragonite's flight patterns, maneuvering around its attacks grew steadily harder.

Ethan changed course. Ranged attacks were no longer working, so he told Dragonite to close in and keep Alakazam occupied at close quarters. He did not expect Alakazam to be capable there too.

Most Psychic-type Pokemon would try to open the distance once an opponent got close, avoiding direct contact and wearing the foe down. Alakazam, with its slight frame, looked especially vulnerable to that kind of pressure. Yet as Dragonite came in for the attack, Alakazam answered with Focus Punch and drove it back.

Ethan's eyebrows rose. May looked equally startled from the stands. It was the opposite of the Alakazam they had expected. A less capable Trainer could have charged straight into that trap and lost the battle.

For Ethan and Dragonite, it was a surprise, not a defeat. Once Dragonite recovered, its own close-range ability began to win out. That difference lay in the Pokemon's bodies as much as their experience. Learning a physical move did not give Alakazam the strength to match a Dragonite built for fighting up close.

Focus Punch was Fighting-type, too, and Dragonite's Flying typing reduced the damage it took. Alakazam prolonged the fight with Recover, restoring much of its strength, but it ultimately fell to Dragonite's Thunder Punch.

Alakazam is unable to battle! The first round goes to challenger Ethan Vale and Dragonite!

Anabel shook her head ruefully. She had made no obvious mistake, Alakazam had performed well, and she had even brought their thoughts into harmony. Yet she had lost in a way that seemed almost ordinary.

The difference in raw strength was plain to her. She had been a Frontier Brain long enough to recognize it. Still, she had not expected one of her main Pokemon to be beaten like that. Since becoming a Trainer, she had never met anyone who left her feeling so helpless.

Who is he?

She looked Ethan over. The longer she studied him, the more familiar his face seemed. She lived far from cities and rarely met new people, though, and could not recall where she might have seen him. If she had encountered a Trainer this strong before, surely she would remember.

There was no time to solve that mystery. She recalled Alakazam and chose her second Pokemon: Metagross.

Ethan thought for a moment. Dragonite was still in good condition, but he returned it and sent out his own Metagross. Of the Pokemon he had brought, it was relatively less powerful. This was a chance to measure it against a first-rate Trainer's Metagross.

Anabel had not expected a mirror match. You have a Metagross too. She examined Ethan's Pokemon and nodded appreciatively. It's strong, and the metal on its body has a fine sheen. You've raised it well.

Ethan returned the compliment. As they spoke, both Metagross took their positions. The referee signaled the second round.

Same species, same evolutionary stage, and much the same collection of moves: individual ability and the Trainers' decisions would settle this one.

Ethan could tell Anabel's Metagross was powerful, another of her main Pokemon like Alakazam. His own did not yet match Dragonite. Anabel also had her silent way of communicating orders. Despite the apparent symmetry, he was the one at a disadvantage.

That made him focus harder. He had chosen this battle for his Metagross precisely because the opponent would push it.

Both Pokemon moved forward at the start. When they reached a suitable distance, they attacked almost together. Each opened with Psychic. Two invisible forces collided in midair and burst apart. The explosion raised no smoke, but sparks crackled like electricity.

Under that spray of sparks, both moved again. Their Trainers' different styles now showed in their choices.

Anabel's Metagross came in fast. Like her Alakazam, it was clearly suited to close-range fighting. Ethan's Metagross had not trained for that specifically, but its body was built for it. There was no reason to retreat from a direct clash. What mattered was how each Trainer handled it.

Ethan kept one precaution in mind. Rather than send his Metagross forward at once, he ordered Iron Defense.

As he spoke, Anabel's Metagross accelerated and slammed toward his with Take Down.

Her bond with her Pokemon was useful. She could send instructions straight to its mind without speaking, saving precious time and allowing instant changes in a fast battle. In that sense she could act almost as another Pokemon on the field.

But the speed had a drawback. If an opponent anticipated the order after it had been given and the Pokemon had acted, changing it could be too late. Anabel had only just conveyed Take Down when she saw Iron Defense and realized the danger. Her Metagross was already committed to the charge.

How did he know? she wondered. Who uses Iron Defense before the opponent has even attacked?

Her Metagross hit Ethan's with a clang that echoed through the hall. Take Down was powerful, but it also injured the user through recoil. Iron Defense had sharply raised Ethan's Metagross's resistance. Anabel's blow did less damage to its target than the collision dealt back to her own Pokemon.

Yes! May shouted from the stands. Ethan's prediction had been brilliant, as though he had seen straight through Anabel's plan.

He had no time to celebrate. While her Metagross felt the recoil, Ethan ordered Tackle. His Metagross struck and drove it away. Anabel's Pokemon had taken two hits in quick successionan unfortunate opening. At least the second blow carried it out of reach before Ethan could follow up further.

Once it was safe, Anabel breathed again. Dragonite's victory over Alakazam had shown her a gap in Pokemon strength. This exchange showed her a gap between Trainers.

Ethan eased his own tension when she withdrew. Iron Defense had involved some prediction, certainly. But even if he had guessed wrong, Anabel's Metagross would have attacked sooner or later. Using the move early would not have been wasted.

As it turned out, he had guessed correctly. Anabel was very strong. Compared with the Anabel he knew from her International Police years, however, she was still young and inexperienced.

Chapter 850: Which One Is the Shadow?

Ethan had won a useful early advantage, but Anabel's Metagross was still a little stronger than his. That was only natural. It was one of her main partners and had spent a long time beside her, battling a stream of challengers at the Tower. Its strength had been tested and refined constantly.

Ethan's Metagross had fought its share of battles, but it was still developing. Compared with most Trainers' Pokemon it was excellent; compared with the partner of a truly accomplished Metagross user, it fell slightly short. More time and experience would close that gap. There was no way to rush it.

Ethan knew this, which was why he took the round so seriously. After the poor opening, Anabel grew more cautious. Her steady, carefully measured attacks made the fight harder. She was the Battle Tower's Frontier Brain for good reason.

The Metagross clashed again and again. Anabel's pushed Ethan's to the brink more than once, only for his direction to help it recover lost ground. In the end, they were evenly matched. Both fired Hyper Beam in a final exchange, and both fell.

The green-haired referee raised his hand. Both Metagross are unable to battle! This round is a draw!

Anabel and Ethan saw the result differently. She found it frustrating. Her Metagross was stronger, and her silent communication with it gave her another advantage. By every measure, she should have won. Ethan's command had dragged the round to a tie anyway.
