For Ethan, it was a fine outcome. His relatively less powerful Metagross had taken one of Anabel's main Pokemon out with it. The experience would strengthen its confidence and skill. The effort had cost Ethan some mental energy, but a good meal and rest would restore that. If it helped him win, it was worth spending.

The tally now stood at two to one in his favor. Anabel felt a pressure she had not known in years. She had been behind before, but usually when she was holding back or had not chosen her strongest team. Today she was fighting in earnest, yet Ethan had driven her to this point. It reminded her of her first journey as a Trainer, when she had been too weak to answer a formidable opponent.

She had thought those days were behind her. Now that helpless feeling had returned. She shivered; excitement and tension prickled her arms. She wanted to defeat the man facing her, while knowing how wide the gap between them might be.

Anabel recalled her unconscious Metagross and took a deep breath. She tried several times to calm herself, but could not quiet the heat rising within her. The desire to overcome this opponent came from somewhere too deep for that.

Ethan recalled his Metagross as well. He did not share her turmoil, but he had learned how difficult she was and could sense her determination. He had put her under tremendous pressure.

He took out his third Poke Ball. Almost at the same moment, Anabel released her last Pokemon. Blue light flashed, and Scizor and Espeon appeared on the field.

May sat straighter in the stands. She knew Ethan's Scizor well. The Espeon across from it drew her attention.

Espeon resembled a small cat, less than a meter tall and light on its feet. Purple fur with a velvet sheen covered its body, its eyes were purple, and a red gem rested on its forehead. Its design suggested a legendary two-tailed cat as well as the features of a fennec fox.

People said Espeon had developed its power to foresee danger in order to protect itself. It was fiercely loyal to a Trainer it trusted, and that protective instinct sharpened its ability to predict what lay ahead. The short, fine fur all over its body sensed tiny movements in the air. From those changes it could anticipate the weather and an opponent's actions; the tips of its forked tail moved subtly when it was reading an opponent.

It was less suited to battling at night. In sunlight, the red gem on its forehead glowed as it stored psychic power, which Espeon could then release through the gem. Once that power was exhausted, the gem's color faded.

It was an elegant Pokemon, and understandably popular. May's interest went beyond that. She was already thinking about how her newly hatched Eevee might evolve one day.

What did Ethan call thinking ahead? Planning before the need arose? Preparing for rain before it fell? Whatever the phrase was, there was no harm in considering it early. Espeon was one possibility she liked, but the other evolutions appealed to her too. Seeing one battle would help her decide.

The final selections had been made blind. Ethan had not known Anabel would send Espeon. Seeing his Bug/Steel-type Scizor face her Psychic-type made him feel a little sorry for her. Already behind, she now had an unfavorable type matchup. Anabel's face showed a trace of bitterness when she saw it.

Determination soon replaced that look. Ethan nodded to himself. She was young, but she would not give up. She deserved her place at the Battle Tower.

For a moment he considered switching Scizor for Dragonite. As the challenger, he was allowed to do so. But Anabel had decided to fight through the disadvantage. Changing his Pokemon now, even with good intentions, would seem disrespectful. He kept Scizor in.

Anabel stood at the edge of defeat. Normally, losing a challenge would be no disaster. A Frontier Brain was there not merely to guard a facility, but to test Trainers and award a Symbol when one earned it, spreading the Battle Frontier's reputation. Today was different. She had brought out all her main Pokemon and treated Ethan as a formidable opponent. Losing on those terms could shake her confidence.

Then again, a battle this demanding might teach her something and help her grow. What she gained or lost would depend on how she understood it afterward.

Scizor and Espeon took their positions. After two rounds of powerful moves, the wooden floor had begun to break. Splinters and raised boards marked the arena, though Ethan had not even brought out one of his heavier Pokemon. The damage might affect this final round.

The third round begins now! the referee called with another sweep of his arm.

Anabel's three Pokemon all had Psychic typing, yet the first two had also been capable at close quarters. Ethan was ready for Espeon to fight that way too. It was one reason he had chosen Scizor blindly. Bug and Steel typing made it less vulnerable against Psychic opponents, and Scizor excelled up close.

Both Pokemon moved at the signal. Like Metagross in the previous round, Espeon opened with Psychic. Ethan had anticipated it. At almost the same instant, Scizor used Double Team. The move let it avoid the invisible attack, then sent several red figures rushing toward Espeon together.

Which one was real? Anabel's eye for detail would be tested.

She watched closely and picked correctly. At a silent command from her, Espeon fired Psychic at the figure on the far right.

Ethan saw that she had found the original. He ordered Quick Attack. Scizor accelerated and escaped the strike. The rush had brought it close to Espeon, however.

At the sight of Scizor's gleaming pincers, Anabel kept her composure. She did not have Espeon trade blows. It used Agility, ran clear, and opened a safe distance. Scizor's attack struck nothing.

Ethan understood the plan: use Espeon's speed to stay out of reach and wear Scizor down bit by bit. He could see what Anabel was doing, yet had no easy answer. The speed difference was too great. Espeon was the second-fastest of Eevee's evolutions, behind Jolteon but far ahead of most Pokemon. Scizor, sheathed in heavy-looking steel, could not simply chase it down.

From safety, Espeon used Psychic again. Ethan had Scizor dodge while he searched for a way through. Psychic attacks did only half damage to its Steel typing, but evasion could not continue forever. If Anabel and Espeon stayed patient, they could still exhaust Scizor.

He needed a more forceful tactic. Ethan made his choice.

Scizor used Double Team to avoid another Psychic. Including the original, six red figures charged Espeon at once.

Anabel was surprised he had repeated the same maneuver. Perhaps, she thought, her evasive strategy had left him with no other option. She did not let that assumption make her careless. Once more she studied the figures for the real Scizor.

Recognizing a Double Team once often made it easier the next time. A Trainer learned how the Pokemon moved, and success gave them confidence. Anabel watched for a few moments and concluded that the far-right figure was the original again.

She silently ordered Espeon to attack.

Just as it began, she caught a movement from the far-left figure. Her heart jolted. Was that the original? Had Ethan deliberately shown her a false pattern the first time?

With no time to think further, Anabel sent another urgent command, redirecting Espeon toward the figure on the far left. Its invisible Psychic power struck almost instantly.

The figure shattered. It had been a copy.

Anabel had guessed wrong. If that was only a shadow, where was the real Scizor now?

Chapter 851: Haven't We Met Somewhere?

Confused, Anabel looked again at the far-right figure, the one her first instinct had marked as Scizor. It had vanished under Espeon's first Psychic attack too.

What? That one was wrong as well?

She had been certain she saw through the move. How could both of her guesses have failed? There was no time to work it out. The four remaining red figures were nearly upon Espeon, too close for it to run clear.

Acting on instinct, Espeon struck at the two in the middle. Like Anabel, it chose wrong. They had tested four of the six figures without finding the real Scizor.

Now the danger was immediate. Both Anabel and Espeon knew that if Scizor reached close range, escaping would be difficult and fighting it directly would be worse. Everything they had gained with Espeon's speed would disappear.

They had chosen to spend those first moments attacking rather than opening more distance. If their guesses had succeeded, the choice would have kept Espeon safe. Because they had failed, a heavy price followed.

Of the two figures left, the one on the left reached Espeon and raised both pincers. Scizor used X-Scissor.

Espeon, dodge! Anabel cried through their bond.

Espeon did not know Teleport. At this range its speed was no use. The Bug-type move struck before it could escape.

Everyone could see the real Scizor now. Knowing its identity after the hit did little good.

Like Anabel's Alakazam and Metagross, Espeon could fight an opponent that came close. It used Iron Tail, Take Down, and Quick Attack to hold its ground against most foes. None of those moves worked nearly as well against Ethan's Scizor, and the type matchup was against it.

After only a few more exchanges, Scizor's rapid attacks drained Espeon's remaining strength. It sank to the floor and could not rise.

Espeon is unable to battle! The winner is challenger Ethan Vale!

The green-haired referee shook his head, disappointed for Anabel, but raised his hand impartially. Apart from the draw between the two Metagross, Ethan had won this challenge by a wide margin. It had to sting for her.

Anabel recalled Espeon and hurried over to Ethan. Instead of congratulating him, she asked the question that had been troubling her.

Mr. Vale, how did you do that with the copies? I thought I could see the real one. Why was I wrong so many times?

That misjudgment had turned a manageable situation into a collapse. May joined them, looking just as curious. Ethan smiled. He waited for Scizor to reach his side, patted its shoulder, and answered.

It's simple. I had Scizor use Double Team twice.

Twice? May and Anabel asked together.

The instant you saw through the first set, it used Double Team again over the original copies and changed its position.

You can do that? Anabel stared at him. No wonder her successive guesses had failed.

The idea sounded straightforward, but she knew how demanding it was. A Pokemon needed great command of Double Team to cover the first set without exposing the trick. During the battle she had sensed that something was off, but she had not thought of a second use of the move. Scizor had concealed it exceptionally well.

Why tell her the method? Wasn't he worried about revealing a secret?

Then she considered it further. With enough practice, many Pokemon that knew Double Team might be able to use it twice. That was theory. Doing it mid-battle, at precisely the moment an opponent recognized the original, without letting a capable Trainer notice, was much harder. Too early or too late, and the trick failed. The Trainer had to read the situation sharply enough to choose the right instant. Simply knowing the principle would not let most people reproduce it.

The explanation left Anabel even more impressed with Ethan.

That was an excellent battle, she said. There was no dejection in her voice, only a little excitement. I've never faced a Trainer as strong as you. Losing is frustrating, but I learned a great deal. I'd love to battle you again someday.

Ethan nodded to himself. Even a decisive loss had not broken her confidence. She had taken the experience and grown more eager to fight. Anabel was not easily defeated in spirit.

Before he could answer, she spoke again. Mr. Vale, may I ask you something?

What is it?

She hesitated. Have we met somewhere before? You look...familiar.

Ethan's heart jumped. Had she noticed? He had told May nothing about the two Anabels and had been careful not to act as if he knew this one. Where had that feeling come from? Was it her ability to sense others through her bond with Pokemon?

This was why he disliked dealing with Trainers who specialized in Ghost or Psychic types. Ordinary Trainers were one thing, but Gym Leaders, Frontier Brains, and Elite Four members of those specialties often possessed unusual abilities themselves. A careless word around them could give away a secret.

Still, this Anabel and the Anabel of the International Police were separate people here. However closely related they were, they shared no memories. Why should Ethan seem familiar to her?

While he searched for an answer, May laughed.

Of course he looks familiar, she told Anabel. Ethan won the Indigo League. You probably saw him on television.

May knew nothing of Ethan's real worry, but she had given him an escape.

The Indigo League champion? Anabel looked surprised. It made sense: she must have seen his face on a broadcast. So that's why...

She accepted the explanation, though a faint feeling that something was still off remained. She chose not to pursue it. Instead she took a gold-colored Symbol from her pocket and handed it to Ethan.

Mr. Vale, this is my Ability Symbol. It's proof that you defeated me. Please accept it.

It looked almost like a gold coin or a bottle cap. Ethan accepted it carefully and put it in his Symbol case. Seeing all six places filled, Anabel nodded in understanding.

So you've collected six Symbols. You'll be challenging Mr. Brandon next.

Brandon was the Frontier Brain of the Battle Pyramid, the seventh and final facility. Challengers needed all six earlier Symbols before they could learn its location and seek him out. As the final test, Brandon was widely regarded as the strongest of the seven Frontier Brains.

Yes. The time's gone quickly, Ethan said. Will you tell me where the Pyramid is, or should I ask Scott?

Scott will tell you. Anabel smiled. Even if I wanted to, I don't know its exact location. The Frontier Brains know of one another, of course, but we look after different areas and don't often meet. I know even less about the Battle Pyramid.

That was mostly true, though not absolute. Some Frontier Brains were friends despite their infrequent contact. Lucy, for example, had heard from Greta that Ethan was traveling between the facilities.

Ethan waved goodbye to Anabel and left the forest with May. At the nearest Pokemon Center, they entrusted the Pokemon that had battled to Nurse Joy. Then they went to the dining area. While they waited for dinner, Ethan called Scott.

He answered quickly and guessed the reason before Ethan spoke. Mr. Vale, a call from you now must mean you've collected all six Frontier Symbols.

I have. I'm calling to ask where the final facility is.

Scott sounded wistful. Already? I still remember the first time we met. I didn't think you'd finish this quickly. Well, I've sent its location to your phone. Take a look!

Ethan thanked him and ended the call. As he went to open the message, he noticed May staring at him.

What? Is there something on my face?

She shook her head. I don't understand why every challenger has to ask for the Battle Pyramid's address after getting six Symbols. Isn't it always in the same place?

That's exactly it. Ethan smiled. It may be built like a pyramid, but it isn't fixed in one place. It moves.

Moves? Does it have wheels underneath, like a camper? Or does it travel by sea?

Neither. It's more extravagant than that. He pointed upward.

May understood and gasped. It's in the sky?

Yes. Brandon fitted the entire Pyramid with a flight system. He can move it wherever he wants. That's why challengers have to get its current position from Scott. Ethan opened the message and turned his phone toward her. Right now it's near Viridian City. By tomorrow it could be somewhere else.

Viridian City... May sighed. Then we'd better hurry there. We're at the eastern edge of Kanto. That's a long way to walk.

That works out well. Ethan put his phone away and slid her dinner toward her. You still need one more Ribbon for the Grand Festival. The Festival itself is on our way back, so we can handle both things along the route. Besides, as I said, the Pyramid moves every day. By the time we're done with the Festival, it might turn up right in front of us.

Chapter 852: Then Let's Trick Him Again!

Leaving the forest that held the Battle Tower behind, Ethan and May traveled out of eastern Kanto. Several days on the road were uneventful without being dull, and by the time they reached the central part of the region, both were covered in travel dust.

Compared with the rural landscapes elsewhere, this area was far more prosperous. Tall buildings, bridges, and parks were everywhere. Saffron, Vermilion, CeladonKanto's major cities were concentrated here.

They did not pass through the cluster of cities, though. Instead, they turned north. After more than half a day's walk, around their lunch break on the fourth day, they arrived in a place called Mulberry City.

Mulberry was called a town in the directions they had heard, but it was large enough to feel like a small city. Streets and rivers crisscrossed it, high-rises stood above the crowds, and people streamed past in every direction.

It had not been on their route. A few Trainers who had challenged Ethan in the wild had told them that a Pokemon Contest would soon be held here, so they had made the detour.

With the Grand Festival approaching, fewer and fewer towns still had Contests scheduled. That meant little to Coordinators who had collected five Ribbons years ago. For May, who had begun collecting Kanto Ribbons partway through her journey, and for newcomers or Coordinators who had lost several times, the deadline was pressing.

At the Pokemon Center, Nurse Joy told them that the upcoming Mulberry Contest was the last remaining Contest where a Coordinator could earn a Ribbon before the Grand Festival. May could only be grateful they had come.

She patted her still-developing chest and let out a long breath. I'm so glad we got here early. If we'd been two days later, I really would have missed the Grand Festival!

You would have...

Once that final opportunity passed, May would have to wait until the following year to challenge the Kanto Grand Festival. She would surely be stronger and better prepared by then, but she would no longer even be in Kanto. She would miss a chance to grow at a crucial point in her journey, and returning a year later would not feel the same.

After a short rest at the Pokemon Center, they went straight to the Contest Hall. It stood in the middle of Mulberry, a familiar half-dome of blue and white that looked unremarkable beside other venues.

The crowd outside was another matter. Perhaps the city's size and population helped account for it, but there were nearly a hundred Coordinators and their Pokemon gathered there. Apart from major venues such as the Saffron Contest Hall, Ethan had never seen so many entrants in one place.

That was only part of the reason. Coordinators who, like May, still needed one more Ribbon had crossed the length of Kanto to enter. With one glance around the crowd, May spotted several opponents she had met before.

Everyone who had yet to collect five Ribbons wanted one last chance to reach the Grand Festival. However many of them entered, only one would leave with the Ribbon.

There really are a lot of people... May said.

They worked their way through the crowd, registered at the service desk, and took a look at the stage so May could get familiar with it. Then they left the hall.

They had not gone far when they saw that persistent figure again: Harley.

May muttered, Seriously, why is he everywhere we go?

As if he had sensed her gaze, Harley spotted them at once. This time, instead of avoiding them, he strode openly up to the pair.

Well, it's been a long time, you two. His pleasant mask was gone. He narrowed his eyes at May and spoke with open mockery. If you're here, collecting Ribbons can't have gone well. What, after all this time, you still haven't got five?

Harley traveled alone and could devote himself to entering Contests wherever he found them. May had fewer opportunities and competed less often.

What's it to you? She rolled her eyes. You're here too, aren't you? That puts us in the same position.

After spending so much time with Misty, May was beginning to sound a little like her.

The same position? Harley gave a smug smile and pulled open one side of his coat. Five glittering Ribbons hung inside. I collected mine ages ago. I only came today to watch you make a fool of yourself!

How he had been so certain May would enter the Mulberry Contest was anyone's guess. Coming here simply to gloat, though, was entirely in character.

May was about to answer when Ethan stepped forward. Harley recoiled as if he'd been startled by an arrow and took a step back.

W-what do you want?

He hated reacting that way in front of a crowd. It made him look timid. But his earlier defeat had left him so frightened of Ethan that he feared the man might start a fight at the slightest provocation.

Ethan merely gave him a cool glance. Without saying a word, he led May away.

Harley froze, then flushed red. Ethan had dismissed him without even bothering to respond. He opened his mouth several times, but anger did not make him brave enough to call after them. All he could do was clench his fists and watch Ethan's back recede.

He dared to provoke May because he knew her temperament. Outside a Contest battle, she would not do anything to him. Ethan was different. When Ethan decided to act, he really acted.

That lack of restraint, combined with Ethan's strength, was why Harley could only swallow his anger. He had deceived May time after time, but after his crushing defeat and humiliating departure from their last battle, he could not manage a single boast in Ethan's presence.

That did not mean he intended to leave things alone. Their feud had become irreconcilable. Apart from Contests, finding some way to get back at Ethan occupied Harley's thoughts more than anything else.

Then his eyes happened to settle on another group he could not stand.

It was Team Rocketthe three who had posed as Jessibella and her attendants at the Saffron Contest and tricked him.

After James and Meowth had conned Harley out of his Pokemon, he had chased them a long way before finally getting both Pokemon back. He had given all three a beating for it, too.

The encounter had taught him who they were. Jessie, James, and Meowth belonged to Team Rocket, a criminal organization. They habitually opposed Ash and were hostile toward his friends. That included May and Ethan.

In that case... Harley's eyes shifted. He already had an idea.

Replacing his dark expression with a smile, he walked over to the trio. Jessie was still dressed as Jessibella, apparently unwilling to give up her dream of winning a Contest. James and Meowth followed her, again dressed as her manager and assistant.

The three had just come from the registration desk when they met him face-to-face.

You!?

Recognizing the man who had punished them last time, Team Rocket jumped and immediately turned to leave. They had only taken a few steps when Harley called out.

Wait.

What do you want? Jessie turned back and glared at him. I've got a Contest to enter. I don't have time to stand here talking to you!

That's right, meow! Meowth added. We haven't tricked you out of any Pokemon this time!

You've misunderstood. Harley smiled. I'm here to help you.

Help us? Jessie frowned. What do you mean?

Harley took out two Poke Balls and waved them before the trio. I'll lend you my Pokemon, just like last time, so you can win the Contest.

What!?

Jessie, James, and Meowth exchanged bewildered looks. What was he plotting?

You'll lend us your Pokemon? James asked. Why would you do that? What's in it for you?

Harley answered with a question of his own. You and that boy Ash are sworn enemies, aren't you?

That's right! Fire seemed to spring into Jessie's eyes at the mention of Ash. We're going to get that twerp's Pikachu, and we'll teach the twerp a lesson too!

Then his friends are your enemies as well?

Of course!

There you have it. Harley smiled. We share an enemy, which makes us friends. My target is that girl May. Oh, and Ethan too.

Ethan!?

All three felt their hearts sink. Ethan was nowhere in sight, yet even hearing his name sent a chill through them. Harley wanted to pick a fight with him? Was the man tired of living?

They kept those thoughts to themselves. Even so, James said, haven't you forgotten that we stole your Pokemon last time? After that, you'd still lend them to us?

I haven't forgotten. Harley was still angry about it, but he kept his voice as steady as he could. I'm willing to make a concession to defeat our common enemies. To make sure this goes smoothly, though, lending you my Pokemon comes with a condition.

A condition? James grew wary. What condition?

Harley spread his hands. To prevent another unfortunate incident like last time, one of you stays with me as a hostage.

A hostage? The three looked at one another, then put their heads together right in front of Harley and began whispering.

He was close enough to hear them breathe and strained to catch a word, but their plotting remained inaudible. He frowned and was about to interrupt when they broke apart and turned to him with broad smiles.

Rubbing his hands, James asked, So which of us would you like to keep as your hostage?

Harley suspected they had something up their sleeves. Even so, he was confident he could keep these simple-minded fools under control and let the whispering pass. He looked from one to another and finally fixed his gaze on Meowth.

That Meowth.

Of the two people and one Pokemon, Jessie had to compete and could hardly be left behind. James, being human, might find some clever way to cause trouble. To Harley, Meowth was the safest and most suitable hostage.

A talking Pokemon was exceedingly rare. Meowth might not be the only one in the world, but he was valuable enough that Jessie and James would never abandon him. Keeping him would prevent a repeat of their last trick.

What Harley did not know was that Meowth was exactly the one they had hoped he would choose. When he was not looking, all three wore the same sly grin and exchanged another glance.

Harley intended to use Jessie to stop May and get at Ethan. Team Rocket intended to use this opportunity to swindle Harley again.

As for going up against Ethan? What a joke!

To them, Ethan had become practically invincible. He was a champion in three regions, commanded Legendary Pokemon, and even their boss Giovanni preferred not to provoke him.

They also knew that Ethan saw them as too weak to pose a threat. As long as they behaved themselves around him, he would leave them alone even if they met face-to-face. Why would the three of them ruin such a favorable arrangement?

Only fools would do that.

Harley wanted to send them to their deaths? Then they had no reason to hold back from tricking him again.

Chapter 853: What Is She Up to This Time?

Harley took out two Poke Balls and handed his Cacturne and Banette to Jessie. At the same time, Jessie and James handed Meowth over to him.

Not that they had to hand Meowth over. He walked up to Harley of his own accord, smiling.

Although the exchange had gone smoothly, Harley was not about to let his guard down. These people had tricked him before. To keep Meowth from slipping away, he found a length of rope, tied him up tightly, and held on to the other end.

With that done, both sides nodded in satisfaction.

I'll be looking forward to your performance tomorrow morning, Harley said.

Leave it to us! I promise I'll beat that little girl!

Jessie thumped her chest in assurance. Harley clearly had confidence in his Pokemon as well. He waved goodbye and led Meowth away on the rope without further hesitation.

Jessie and James watched him go. With two Poke Balls in hand, they looked at each other and burst out laughing.

We didn't do a thing, and he gave us two Pokemon, Jessie said with a wicked chuckle. Today really is our lucky day!

It sure is, James said. They're that fool's main Pokemon, too. I never thought getting them would be so easy. What a bargain! Oh, but what about Meowth?

Don't worry. We worked that out with him already. He'll find a chance to escape on his own!

Are we still entering the Contest?

Of course. Jessie spread her mouth in her familiar, enormous grin. With an opportunity like this, I'll use his Pokemon to win the Contest first. Then we'll run off with both of them and deliver them to the boss!

While Harley and Team Rocket carried out their bargain, Ethan and May had left the front of the Mulberry Contest Hall for a broad open space nearby. They had registered and inspected the stage. Now it was time for some focused practice.

Unfortunately, the open space was packed with Coordinators training alongside their Pokemon. There was no room for the two of them. They walked much farther before finding an unoccupied spot.

Perhaps the number of entrants had put pressure on May. This time she chose not to perform with a newer partner such as Eevee or Squirtle. Instead, she brought out Combusken. Her first Pokemon was still the one she trusted most.

Ethan found a chair and sat down to watch her practice. Before long, he shook his head helplessly.

Her nerves were getting the better of her. The crowded field and her encounter with Harley had unsettled her so much that she kept making mistakes while working with Combuskenmistakes she normally would not make.

If this was how she performed in private, what would happen in tomorrow's Contest?

Let's stop for a moment...

He beckoned May over. She knew perfectly well that her state of mind was the problem and gave him an embarrassed smile.

Relax. Don't let the other entrants get to you. Ethan could do little beyond helping her look at things differently. Think about it. If they were that strong, they'd already have five Ribbons, like Harley. The fact that they're entering this Contest means they haven't been able to win enough. And if you make it through the first round of judging, I don't think any of them can beat you in a battle.

Ethan knew how to comfort her. Ash and the others would probably have cheered May on, but he offered another way to see the field. His words made her pause and think.

He had a point. A few entrants, like her, might have missed earlier Contests for reasons of their own. Most of the others had entered those Contests and been eliminated. If they had lost before, why should she be afraid of them?

Once she understood that, May felt noticeably calmer. Even her hands and legs stopped shaking so much.

Thanks, Ethan. I'm feeling a lot better now.

She took a deep breath and returned to the grass with Combusken. This time their practice went smoothly. There were no more mistakes; she seemed to have found the form she had shown at earlier Contests.

...

They became so absorbed in practice that the hours slipped by. When May finally looked up, the sky had gone completely dark.

After a good night's rest at the Pokemon Center, they returned the next morning for the Mulberry Contest. Spectators poured into the hall from every direction, and Ethan joined the stream of people heading to the stands.

Lilian was hosting as usual, and the judges were the same three familiar faces. Barring a surprise, the Grand Festival might well use the same team. No one minded. The host and judges were skilled, respected, and popular. Seeing different people in their places might have felt strange.

Lilian's energetic introduction ended, and the Contest began. Only then did the full size of the field become clear. As Ethan had thought, the number of entrants rivaled a major city Contest, even if the hall itself was smaller.

Their skill varied just as widely. Not everyone had a realistic chance of winning. Some Coordinators traveled from Contest to Contest and could go a whole year without earning a single Ribbon. Yet the dream seemed close enough to reach, even as it kept slipping away, and countless people continued to enter.

Since this was the last Contest before the Grand Festival, the contrast was especially sharp. The best entrants showed real skill and earned high scores. At the other end, repeated mistakes made some performances almost comical.

One Coordinator after another stepped onstage and left again. Whatever their results, they brought the audience to life.

Then it was May's turn.

As in practice, Combusken was her partner for the appeal. Perhaps she had truly settled her nerves, because she performed even better than usual. Her stage presence had plainly reached another level.

During the disc-catching portion, Combusken caught every disc perfectly and showed off its coordination. Then it used Fire Spin to create a huge storm of flames on the stage, displaying the move's beauty as well as its power. For the finale, Combusken sprang up out of the fire and made a magnificent exit.

The hall erupted in applause. The audience was amazed by Combusken's dazzling performance and gave May their loudest cheers.

Harley, sitting in the stands, looked nothing like the excited spectators. His face had gone dark. He had never expected May to be in such good form today.

That appeal would have earned a high score even at the Grand Festival. Compared with the entrants before her, she had raised the standard by half a level.

Damn it! He clenched his fists.

How could this happen? Wasn't a setting like this supposed to make her nervous? Why had she performed better instead?

All he could do now was put his hopes in Jessie. Perhaps she could use his Pokemon for an even stronger appeal and outshine May.

Something else bothered him. When he had spoken with Team Rocket earlier, he had discussed tactics with Jessie and James. James had thumped his chest and promised to interfere during May's performance. Yet nothing had happened. Had they forgotten Harley was holding a hostage?

Harley frowned, unable to make sense of it.

In a warehouse not far from the hall, the answer was taking shape.

Meowth was tied hand and foot to a pillar. Harley's Ariados hung quietly in a web opposite him, keeping watch.

Ever since Harley had bound him and brought him here the day before, Meowth had been deciding when to escape. The timing mattered enormously to their plan.

If he escaped too early, Harley would notice and go looking for Jessie and James. They would never get away with Cacturne and Banette. If he waited too long, Harley would realize Jessie was not following his plan to target May and Ethan, and would come after them anyway.

Whether Meowth could escape was another question entirely. As the slyest and cleverest member of the trio, he thought Harley had badly underestimated him.

He kept a placid expression for Ariados's benefit. Behind his back, though, the claws on his bound paws extended to sharp points.

A burst of cheering came from the distant Contest Hall. Meowth knew his chance had arrived. He whistled toward the outside of the warehouse, and within moments there was a sound at the door.

Ariados climbed down from its web almost at once and watched the entrance warily. The door opened, and a blue, harmless-looking Wobbuffet poked half its body inside.

Wobbuffet!

It gave Ariados an apologetic smile, as vacant-looking as ever, and rubbed its smooth head. It made no other move.

Ariados was puzzled. Something felt wrong. As it prepared to drive this unexpected visitor away, it heard a sudden rush of air behind it.

It whipped around. The talking Meowth had somehow freed himself from the rope and was already right in front of it, claws raised.

Meowth's steps had been so light and his movements so careful that Ariados had noticed him too late. His claws knocked it down before it could react. He did not press the attack. The moment Ariados fell, he and Wobbuffet bolted from the warehouse.

By the time Ariados recovered and chased them outside, they had vanished.

Harley knew nothing of what had happened in the warehouse. He was still waiting to see what Jessie could do with his Pokemon.

After May's appeal, more than a dozen Coordinators took their turns. At last Jessie came onstage. Harley straightened in his seat and held his breath.

You've waited long enough! Welcome to the fabulous stage of the world's greatest idol, Jessibella!

Jessie waved grandly to the audience. Her butterfly mask, shawl, red gown, and white gloves completed her Jessibella costume and gave her the bearing of a queen.

Her appearance alone stood out from Coordinators who had come in their everyday clothes. The spectators' eyes lit up. Most had never heard of Jessibella, but looking at her now, they could almost believe she was a world-famous idol.

Harley himself had believed it the first time he saw her. The convincing costume and Jessie's boundless confidence had sold him on the act.

Only Ethan applauded mildly, his face blank amid the cheering crowd. He was not trying to make a point or look mysterious. Knowing who Jessie really was, he found her appearance here equal parts exasperating and absurd.

Ash was nowhere nearby. How had she turned up anyway? Did a Contest stage draw her more strongly than Pikachu, enough for her to stop chasing Ash for a while?

Regardless of how Jessie competed, she was bound to cause some sort of trouble before the end. The Contest had been unpredictable already; her arrival added another complication.

Even so, Ethan kept clapping. He had to admit Jessie had a talent for the stage.

What surprised him more was the Pokemon she released. It was not one of her own. It was Harley's Cacturne.

Ethan had no trouble recognizing it. He knew Jessie and Harley well enough, and with both of them here, it was hard not to suspect they were plotting something together. Jessie's goal was easy to guess: win this Contest and claim the final Ribbon.

Harley's goal could only be one personMay.

Chapter 854: The Show Begins

Jessie and Cacturne began their appeal. Cacturne opened with Needle Arm and Cut, using precise strokes to carve a long white radish into the shape of a tower.

In a way, it resembled May's disc-catching routine with Combusken. Both displays showed what their Pokemon could do with skill and control. Cacturne earned a round of applause.

With her opening safely behind her, Jessie moved to the next part. Cacturne used Cotton Spore to send countless spores into the air. They floated like dandelion seeds until it swept across them with Bullet Seed, bursting them into still finer tufts. The soft white flecks drifted down like snow, turning the stage into a dreamlike scene.

Harley's Cacturne was certainly strong, with ability worthy of a top Grand Festival entrant. Jessie's ideas and direction were excellent too. The two worked remarkably well together. Cacturne showed no discomfort at performing for a different Trainer.

Jessie really did have a gift for this. Her appeal earned the second-highest score so far, just behind May's.

The first round was not even half over, but May and Jessie had outperformed the rest of the field so thoroughly that it was hard to imagine later entrants scoring above them. Both had effectively secured places in the next round already.

That was good news for them and added even more pressure for everyone else. More than a hundred Coordinators now had only six remaining places to compete for.

May no longer had to worry about that. When even the crowd favorite Jessibella failed to surpass her score, she let out a relieved breath. All she had wanted was to get safely through the appeal round.

Traveling with Ethan had taught her something of his approach. Her style had begun to resemble his, and her Pokemon were steadily growing stronger. Once she reached the battle stage, her experience and her Pokemon's strength made her much harder to eliminate.

The Contest continued at a lively pace. With so many entrants, the appeal round took an unusually long time, stretching into the afternoon. Eventually everyone had performed, and eight Coordinators advanced.

When the big screen displayed the results, Ethan saw May at the top, just as expected. Jessie had fallen to fourth place but had qualified too.

Jessie's score had been high when she finished. Other Coordinators had given strong appeals afterward and, despite the pressure, pushed her down the rankings. Her position hardly mattered. Reaching the battle stage was what counted.

There was little time left, so the second round began after only a short break. May and Jessie landed on opposite sides of the bracket. If both kept winning, they would not meet until the final.

From what Ethan had seen, a final between them seemed likely.

He slipped away to use the restroom. By the time he returned, the first battle had started. Neither May nor Jessie was in it; the opening match was between two other Coordinators. That was why he had felt free to leave. May took the stage only after their match ended.

Her opponent was a handsome young man with a mature air. He sent out Skarmory. May chose Squirtle.

Squirtle was still in its first evolutionary stage. Professor Oak had given it to May after she came to Kanto, and it remained a little timid. Yet it had grown remarkably fast. Against a formidable opponent with a stronger body, it did not retreat. At May's command, it withdrew into its shell to avoid Skarmory's attack, then countered with Rapid Spin and gained the advantage.

If Brock had been watching, he would have recognized how much May's battle style had come to resemble Ethan's: steady and unhurried. It had once shared something with Ash's style, but that likeness had all but disappeared.

No style was inherently better; the question was which Trainer it suited. For May, the change had helped considerably. She no longer fought with Ash's impulsiveness.

Of course, anyone who had reached the second round from a field of more than a hundred was no weakling. The young man had underestimated Squirtle and paid for it, but once he adjusted, he gradually steadied the battle.

May had changed too. Squirtle looked harmless, yet it was much stronger than an ordinary Pokemon of its age. Alongside Bubble and Water Gun, it could use Ice Beam. As Skarmory swept past, Squirtle froze one of its wings. Unable to keep its balance, Skarmory crashed onto the stage.

Squirtle took advantage of the opening. Smaller and more agile, it moved around its opponent and brought Skarmory down for good.

Ethan applauded with the rest of the audience. As a Trainer who spent every day with May, he could see her progress clearly. He knew she was taking cues from him and beginning to follow a similar path.

Still, her growth was nothing like it had been in the animated story he remembered. He could not say what kind of Trainer she would eventually become. A female version of himself, perhaps?

One thing was certain: having May travel with him and watching her change had taught Ethan how satisfying it could be to guide someone else. It was a different feeling from raising Pokemon.

He suddenly understood why Yuma, the former top Coordinator who now worked as a Pokemon Breeder, had offered to coach Brock and Mollie at the last Contest. Seeing May grow stronger little by little filled him with a satisfaction he could hardly match.

Jessie took the stage after May. For the battle round, she again used one of Harley's Pokemon rather than her own: Banette. The two groups had clearly made an arrangement.

Ethan did not interfere. He preferred to watch what happened. The Team Rocket trio was too afraid of him to try anything against him directly. Whatever Harley had talked them into, Ethan expected Harley to be the one who suffered for it.

That was not blind arrogance. Ethan knew his own strength, and he knew the trio.

Onstage, Jessie and Banette were working together as smoothly as Jessie and Cacturne had. Banette obeyed her without resistance. Harley had probably spoken to his Pokemon beforehand, but Jessie, like James, also had a natural ease with Pokemon.

Banette was strong enough that Jessie barely had to direct it. Truthfully, detailed battle commands were not her strength. Relying on its own understanding of the fight, Banette defeated its opponent with ease.

Like May, Jessie followed that victory with more wins. Both reached the final, where they would at last face one another.

By then the sky had darkened. The spectators were tired, but they roused themselves and waited eagerly for the last match of the Mulberry Contest. After this, anyone wanting to see another Contest Battle would have to wait for the Grand Festival. They did not want to miss the final.

Now, let's welcome our two finalists to the stage!

Lilian sounded as lively as ever, despite having hosted the Contest all day. A spotlight fell on one entrance. May walked out waving to the cheering audience.

First is May, who has traveled all the way from Hoenn! She has four Ribbons so far. Will she collect her fifth today and secure a place in the Grand Festival? Let's watch and find out!

The spotlight swung to the other entrance, and Jessie emerged at an unhurried pace, smiling.

And now, with her magnificent costume, the dazzling Jessibella! Will she earn her first Ribbon in today's Contest? Let's look forward to her performance!

Only then did Ethan realize Jessie still had not won a single Ribbon. After all this time, that was almost hard to believe.

If Jessie stopped hounding Ash and seriously entered Contests in one place, she might have collected five Ribbons by now. On the other hand, would she still be Jessie if she gave up chasing Ash and Pikachu? She had chosen her own path and had to live with what it cost her dream.

May and Jessie took their positions and threw their Poke Balls. Squirtle and Banette appeared onstage once more. Both had fought several matches already, but Pokeblocks and brief rests had helped them recover. Neither had taken much damage, and both looked ready.

Lilian saw that they were prepared and gave the signal. The final battle of Kanto's last Contest before the Grand Festival began.

Harley sat up straight in the stands. At last! Excitement flashed in his eyes. He had waited so long for this moment.

Why else had he entrusted Cacturne and Banette, his two strongest Pokemon, to Jessie? If she used them to defeat May here, May would be eliminated. Harley would get his revenge.

He clenched his fists, imagining it already. In his mind, his Pokemon were stronger than May's. His earlier loss had been nothing but bad luck, and he was certain they would win if given another chance.

One thing still troubled him. James had yet to do anything to hinder May. Their plan was that, once Jessie had Harley's Pokemon, James would disrupt May's performance as well. Why had there been no sign of him?

Harley felt uneasy. What if James had gone to rescue Meowth? But he could not leave now, at the most important moment of the Contest.

Then he spotted James peering out from the entrance to the contestants' passage. Harley relaxed. As long as James was here, he had not gone to free Meowth, and their cooperation could continue. May had merely faced fewer obstacles than Harley had planned.

Onstage, Banette moved the instant Lilian announced the start, without waiting for Jessie to command it. Electricity formed in its hand and struck Squirtle before May could react.

The timing was perfect. Banette had quietly gathered energy before the battle began. As soon as Lilian finished speaking, it released the attack and caught May and Squirtle off guard.

Harley could not be accused of breaking the rules. Banette had used the move only after Lilian's signal. Before then it had neither moved nor visibly changed. It had found a loophole, nothing more.

The Electric-type attack hit the Water-type Squirtle hard. May's point bar on the screen shrank a little. Squirtle was not so easily beaten, though. It rose almost at once, determination burning in its eyes, and fired an Ice Beam from its mouth, catching Banette by surprise in return.

Chapter 855: Harley: Not Again!

Ice Beam froze Banette inside a block of ice. It soon broke free from within and spat several clusters of blue flame toward Squirtle.

Will-O-Wisp could melt ice, and its ghostly appearance and name might make it seem like a Ghost-type move. It was Fire-type, though, and would do little to a Water-type Pokemon like Squirtle. Even so, May did not want to lose points. She had Squirtle use Withdraw, then Rapid Spin away from the flames.

Contest Battles were not decided simply by which Pokemon fell. Beautifully executed attacks that struck an opponent affected the score. Even a weak hit reduced a Coordinator's point bar. The losses might look small, but they could add up.

Jessie ordered Banette to use Thunder Shock again, hoping its type advantage would bring Squirtle down. Golden electricity formed around Banette and shot toward its opponent. Squirtle countered with Bubble. The bubbles poured from its mouth and collided with the current in midair.

To everyone's surprise, the Water-type attack overpowered the electricity. It drove the current back, then carried on to strike Banette.

What!?

Jessie stared from the stage. Harley's expression changed in the stands. Had May's Squirtle really become this strong? Electric-type moves had the advantage against Water types. How had Bubble pushed one back?

His confidence faltered.

Jessie, meanwhile, showed her own peculiar talent. After Banette was hit, she scolded and berated it. The abuse from its temporary Trainer made Banette furious. Jessie seized on that anger and ordered Frustration.

Banette rushed Squirtle and attacked in a frenzy of punches, kicks, and headbutts.

Frustration was a Normal-type move that almost any Pokemon could learn. It let a Pokemon pour its dissatisfaction into an all-out attack. With little thought for technique, it used whatever could strikehands, feet, knees, head, or tail. The weaker its bond with its Trainer, the stronger the move became.

Many Trainers and Pokemon would never use it. Jessie and Banette had no bond to speak of, and Banette was only on loan, so neither hesitated.

Squirtle was caught off guard and took several hits. The attack did damage, but its wild flailing had little of the beauty a Contest rewarded. May's point bar fell only a little.

After her first moment of alarm, May regained her composure. Squirtle withdrew into its shell, avoiding Banette's reckless blows. Then it used Rapid Spin to knock Banette away, breaking the attack and hurting it in return.

It was a sensible response, though a fairly standard one for a Pokemon with a shell.

At a distance again, Banette used Will-O-Wisp to force Squirtle out. The spinning shell was a difficult target. The ghostly flames swept past without touching it.

Jessie changed tactics and tried Thunder Shock. Squirtle's shell was ricocheting unpredictably across the stage, too fast for the electricity to catch.

At one moment the spinning shell flew above Banette. May saw her chance and gave a command. Powerful jets of water burst from the shell as it spun, and Squirtle crashed into Banette.

A Normal-type attack alone could not harm a Ghost-type Pokemon. The added water changed the spinning shell's impact, and Banette felt it. The move was far more spectacular than its own Frustration. Jessie's point bar dropped sharply.

Harley watched in growing distress. The scores on the screen plainly favored May, and the clock was running down.

Jessie had clever ideas, but to him her battle commands lacked any strategy. She seemed to know only how to keep attacking. Harley was certain he would never have handled Banette so poorly himself. Now he could only hope that Banette and its unreliable temporary Trainer somehow turned things around.

Come on. Try harder!

His hopes went unanswered. Since beginning to travel with Ethan, May had changed more than her style. Watching him battle had broadened the way she thought. She had not been tempered by many great battles, but she now fought more like an experienced Trainer, gave commands more easily, and recognized an opponent's weaknesses.

After several intense minutes, she spotted another opening. Squirtle used Bubble once more. Jessie ordered Banette to dodge the stream, unaware that the bubbles were bait.

While Banette concentrated on avoiding them, Squirtle fired an unexpected Ice Beam and froze it in a block of ice again. This time May did not let it escape. Squirtle followed immediately with Water Gun, striking the block and sending it off the stage.

As it happened, Banette broke free just as Water Gun landed. The stream hit Banette directly, carrying it and the shattered ice out of bounds and into Jessie.

Banette was not knocked unconscious, but it had left the stage, and Jessie's point bar was empty. The match had turned in an instant.

Jessie stamped her feet in fury. In the stands, Harley slammed a fist against his seat. What was wrong with her? He had lent her his Pokemon and given her the perfect chance, and she had still lost to May!

Before Lilian could announce the result, every light above the stage went out. Darkness filled the hall.

The audience was confused. Harley, though, had a dreadful sense that he had seen this before.

Two spotlights came on and converged on Jessie. Music sounded from somewhere, and James, now wearing his Team Rocket uniform, leaped onto the stage and stood back-to-back with her.

Jessie threw aside her costume pieces in one swift change and stood in her familiar Team Rocket uniform. They had even put roses between their teeth, striking extravagant poses.

I heard someone ask, What's going on?

Then let us tell you!

From beyond the far horizon!

From the other side of the great thunderbolt!

A voice is calling us!

Thanks for waiting, meow!

The brave, blooming flowers of evil!

The lovely, tough villains!

Jessie!

James!

And Meowth, that's me! Meow!

Wherever Team Rocket goes

The world!

The universe!

Waits for us!

Wobbuffet!

All three members of Team Rocket stood exposed before the entire Mulberry Contest Hall.

Unlike her appearance at the Saffron Contest, Jessie showed no shock or sadness over her defeat. She laughed loudly instead.

It's a little disappointing that I didn't win, but that's all right. The mission's accomplished. Sogoodbye!

She recalled Banette into its Poke Ball. James pressed a detonator, blasting a large hole in the roof. Bits of masonry fell, and the audience felt the cool night wind. The trio caught a rope, climbed up through the hole in moments, and disappeared.

Harley stared, open-mouthed. The scene and their exit were so familiar that it felt as though the Saffron Contest was happening again. The memory stung.

He could not understand how Meowth was here. Hadn't he locked Meowth in the warehouse? And how had these three made off with his Pokemon again?

A gust of night air made him shiver and jolted him back to himself.

Cacturne! Banette!

This betrayal hurt worse than the last one. Harley felt as if a knife had gone through his heart. He had trusted them, and they had fooled him all over again.

He did not even stop to glare at May. He sprinted for the hall doors and set off after Team Rocket once more.

After he left, the staff restored the lights. The spectators looked from the empty stage to the hole in the roof, unable to make sense of what had happened.

Lilian had witnessed the Saffron Contest incident, though, and quickly drew their attention back to the result.

It seems Jessie chose a rather unusual way to leave after her loss, she said lightly. Unexpected, perhaps, but certainly as flashy as her name! And now the result is clear. Let's congratulate May, the winner of this year's Mulberry Contest!

Cheers and applause filled the hall. May waved to the crowd, smiling brightly. The match had taken an unexpected turn, but she had won her fifth Ribbon. At last she had qualified for the approaching Grand Festival, just in time.

...

After the awards ceremony, May left through the contestants' passage and found Ethan waiting outside. She carried her new Ribbon and a booklet. Holding both up for him to see, she could hardly hide her excitement.

Congratulations, Ethan said. You keep getting better. If you perform like that at the Grand Festival, you might even win it.

I've learned a lot from traveling with you, May said with a smile. When I battled Jessie just now, I imagined I was you. I kept asking myself how you'd fight Banette. Before I knew it, I'd won!

Ethan felt both pleased and proud. May saw him as an example to follow; perhaps the path he had taken was a good one after all.

But something still feels strange, May added.

Strange? What do you mean?

Team Rocket, of course. When I traveled with Ash, those three were always causing trouble. This time they didn't interfere with us or wreck anything. Even after losing, they just slunk away. That's not like them!

It was new to May, but Ethan was used to it. And had the trio really done nothing? Harley was probably running himself ragged chasing them across town. He had schemed against May for so long, only to be played by Team Rocket twice.

Wherever the two sides ended up, Ethan was sure they would fight again. Villains had a way of making each other suffer.

He shook his head and looked at the booklet in May's hand. What's that?

A guide to the Grand Festival. Mr. Contesta gave it to me at the awards ceremony.

I see. Ethan nodded. With that in hand, you're officially a Grand Festival contender now.

Chapter 856: The Aurora Incident

Only two things remained for Ethan and May to do in Kanto: Ethan's final Battle Frontier challenge and May's eagerly awaited Grand Festival.

Neither would be easy. Brandon, known as the Pyramid King, was regarded as the strongest Frontier Brain. His powerful Pokemon had defeated countless confident challengers. The Grand Festival would be full of strong Coordinators too. Every one of them had earned five Ribbons and would be a difficult opponent.

Ethan had so many powerful Pokemon that losing seemed impossible. May's challenge was less certain. If she could break through to even the semifinals, it would be a huge step in her growth.

It was late, so they spent the night in Mulberry City. The number of visiting Trainers meant they could not get a room at the Pokemon Center. With no other choice, Ethan endured the front desk worker's scrutinizing look and took May to a hotel next door, where they booked one room.

May was a little shy about it, but she made no objection. She slept soundly in the soft, comfortable bed and woke at dawn feeling as if all the fatigue of the past few days had vanished.

They set out from Mulberry and headed west again. Kanto's Grand Festival would be held on the Indigo Plateau, rather than in one of the region's large cities. That changed the order of their plans.

Ethan had intended to accompany May to the Grand Festival before challenging the Battle Pyramid. Once he learned where the Festival would take place, he decided to find the Pyramid first instead.

He opened the live map Scott had sent him. As expected, the Battle Pyramid had moved again. It had left Viridian City and was now near Pewter City.

Pewter is Brock's hometown, isn't it? May asked.

That's right. He used to lead the Gym there. His father is filling in as Gym Leader now.

Walking beside Ethan, May hopped over a small puddle without turning her head. Do you think Brock will ever go back to the Gym? He's a Pokemon Breeder now. That isn't really the same as being a Trainer, is it?

Ethan thought of the animated story's later Sun and Moon era, when Brock was still a Gym Leader and had become much stronger. He shook his head.

I'm sure he'll go back. Being a Breeder doesn't stop him from training Pokemon. A Gym Leader has status, a salary, and allowances, too. Why would he give that up easily?

They had walked well beyond Mulberry by then and reached a plain. After crossing it and rounding a low hill, a wide landscape opened before them. Snow-covered mountains stretched across the distance. Below them lay a vast forest and a blue lake reflecting the clear light. The view was beautiful enough to make them stop and breathe it in.

What an amazing view! May said.

They stayed to admire it for a long time, and both took out their phones to keep a picture of the scene. More than a dozen Altaria happened to fly overhead, adding to its beauty.

Then two bands of aurora suddenly appeared in the sky, one cyan and one red. They were lovely, but their arrival was jarring.

Huh? An aurora? May stared. Something about it was familiar. Why would there be an aurora here? And why did it appear so suddenly?

As soon as she spoke, she remembered where she had seen something like it. It was just like... She turned quickly to Ethan, who nodded.

Yes. It's an aurora from Deoxys.

Deoxys? There's one here too?

It isn't so strange. Including mine, I've met three Deoxys, and that was all in Hoenn. They don't stay within regional borders. They fly wherever they want, so finding one in Kanto isn't much of a surprise. Since we've seen it, let's go and find out what's happening.

May had no objection. Wherever Ethan decided to go, she was happy to follow. They set off down the slope toward the forested hills beneath the aurora.

The Altaria that had just flown overhead seemed to lose their bearings in its light. They had been moving steadily in one direction. Whether the aurora frightened them or a magnetic disturbance confused them, they began flying erratically and soon scattered.

There was no time to worry about them. Ethan and May made their way briskly down the slope and into the forest.

May took out a compass to check their direction. Its needle spun wildly. Alarmed, she looked at her phone and found that it had lost its signal as well.

The magnetic disturbance here is serious, Ethan said with a frown. He took a Poke Ball from the pouch at his waist, only to find that it would not open.

May tried her own Poke Balls. None of them would release the Pokemon inside. They won't open! Ethan, what do we do?

Without their Pokemon, most Trainers were little different from ordinary people when danger struck. They were not people with extraordinary abilities like Bruno or Bea, nor psychic users like Sabrina.

Someone else might have panicked. A Poke Ball that could not be opened from the outside, though, was a small problem for Ethan.

Gardevoir.

At his quiet call, the first Poke Ball in the pouch at his left hip opened at once. A flash of blue light appeared, and his Gardevoir emerged on its own.

That was one of the advantages of having a Psychic-type Pokemon. Gardevoir was not the only one that could do it, either. If Ethan wished, powerful partners such as Deoxys, Rayquaza, the three legendary birds, the two legendary beasts, and even his enormous red Gyarados could leave their Poke Balls by themselves.

Once Gardevoir appeared, Gengar rose from the shadow at Ethan's feet. With both Pokemon beside them, the two could handle most unexpected dangers.

May relaxed at the sight. Having Pokemon close gave them the confidence to face a wild Pokemon if one appeared, rather than having no option but to run.

The forest was large, and they had no clues to follow. They wandered in search of the aurora's source. At least a broad path ran between the trees, so they were unlikely to lose their way.

The deeper they went, the more something felt wrong. May looked around and lowered her voice. Ethan, isn't it a little too...quiet?

She was right. There was no sound from wild Pokemon. Even the wind seemed to have gone still under the strange magnetic field. It reminded Ethan of the forest where they had met Celebi.

Something's ahead, Gengar said suddenly.

Ethan glanced at Gengar and Gardevoir. Both were looking toward the trees ahead, but neither seemed especially wary. Whatever they had noticed was probably not dangerous.

He was about to send Gengar to investigate when a figure jumped down from a large tree and landed in front of them. It was Solana, the Pokemon Ranger they had met before.

What was she doing here? Ethan had only just been thinking of their last encounter with Celebi, and now she had appeared again. Then again, Rangers patrolled nearby. They reached a disturbance as quickly as firefighters reached a blaze.

You two? Solana looked surprised to see Ethan and May. Then she grew awkward, evidently remembering how badly their previous meeting had ended.

May did not dwell on that. Solana, why are you here?

To May, an aurora made by Deoxys hardly seemed like an incident. It had caused no obvious disaster; it was simply something a Pokemon could do. Why would the Rangers be involved?

Solana looked grateful for the friendly question. Whether May meant to or not, she had given Solana an easy way past the awkwardness.

There's a severe geomagnetic anomaly in this area. It's disrupting our equipment, so Ranger headquarters sent me to investigate.

A geomagnetic anomaly. Just as Ethan had thought. May looked behind Solana but saw no sign of Lunick. Where's your partner?

Lunick? He has other work to do, so he isn't with me. What brought you two here?

May glanced at Ethan. He still did not seem inclined to speak. We were passing through. We saw the aurora and came to have a look. That's how we happened to meet you.

Passing through? Solana was not quite convinced. They had been nearby when Celebi appeared, and now they were here for this aurora. She had not known Ethan long, but she doubted it was all coincidence. Was there something the Rangers had missed?

The Ranger Union had a strong intelligence network, but it knew little about Deoxys. Solana did not recognize the two-colored aurora as one of its distinctive signals. She was about to learn.

The sky twisted. A moment later, a Deoxys emerged from the distortion.

Deoxys!? Solana cried. She had not expected to encounter one here, but she recognized it immediately.

It looked toward Ethan from a distance. He could hardly make out its features, yet he had the distinct feeling it bore him no hostility. Then he understood: it must be one of the two Deoxys he had met in LaRousse City.

What a coincidence. The Deoxys seemed to have appeared merely to show itself. After that brief glimpse, it vanished again.

For Solana, even a moment was enough to change her understanding of the situation. I see. The geomagnetic anomaly must have something to do with Deoxys. It wouldn't have appeared here otherwise.

She turned to Ethan, her expression serious. Mr. Vale, this involves a Mythical Pokemon again. To be safe, would you please help me?

Worried he might recall their last disagreement, she added quickly, I promise nothing like last time will happen. If you give me an instruction, I'll carry it out.

Ethan considered her earnest request. He had nothing against Pokemon Rangers; in fact, he admired their work. Solana's conduct the last time had simply made him feel she had gone back on her word.

Now that she was willing to acknowledge it, he had no wish to keep their relationship strained. He would likely deal with Rangers again, and he could hardly stand aside when a Deoxys he knew was involved.

Don't count on me for too much, he said. But if you really need my help, I won't refuse to get involved.

He suspected there would be little danger or fighting here, as long as Rayquaza did not intrude.

Solana let out a quiet breath of relief. After the Celebi incident, she had looked into Ethan's backgroundnot out of suspicion, but curiosity. Strangely, there was no record of his earlier life, as though he had appeared from nowhere.

That mattered less to her than the almost legendary career he had built since becoming a Trainer. She was deeply curious about him. If she could, she wanted to know him better and repair the poor impression she had left with him before.

Chapter 857: Solana's Gesture of Goodwill

Solana led them along a forest path to a Pokemon Center among the trees. It was unlike the Centers in busy towns, looking more like a research facility. That made sense. A Center in a remote forest would do more research than tend to the Pokemon of passing Trainers. Otherwise, why build it somewhere so quiet?

One thing had not changed: the person in charge was a familiar-looking Nurse Joy. Seeing her face made the place feel welcoming.

Solana asked as soon as they met, Nurse Joy, is the system working any better?

She must have spoken to this Joy before, whether in person or by phone. Otherwise she would not have known so much about the Center's trouble.

No. We still can't use it. Joy sighed. None of the equipment will turn on, and the power has stopped. We've switched to backup power, but that won't last much longer if this continues.

Whether or not Deoxys had caused it, the damage from the geomagnetic anomaly was plain to see. Solana told Joy about the Deoxys they had just seen.

Oh! Joy looked startled, then thoughtful. So the anomaly that began last week was caused by it?

That seems likely. Solana nodded and stepped aside to introduce Ethan and May. But even if Deoxys is involved, Mr. Vale is here. I'm sure we'll be able to resolve this.

Joy looked at Ethan in surprise. Ethan gave Solana an equally surprised glance. Was he imagining it? They had met only recently, yet she seemed far more admiring of him now than she had then. It felt almost unreal. Still, it was a welcome change.

I'll help as much as I can, he said. He turned to Joy. Can you tell us exactly what happened?

Joy thought back. It started about a week ago. The magnetic field suddenly became abnormal, our equipment began failing, and we couldn't carry out our work. We contacted Ranger headquarters, and Solana came afterward.

Solana nodded. Headquarters assigned me to investigate the cause, but I hadn't found any clues. We only learned Deoxys was involved a moment ago.

Ethan understood. The two were saying much the same thing. Neither Joy nor Solana knew more than the outline, and perhaps not much more than he did.

Before reaching the Center, he had assumed Deoxys had arrived by chance and produced the aurora. The week-long disturbance suggested there might be more to it. He rubbed his chin and considered the possibilities.

Nurse Joy, has a meteorite ever fallen near here?

A meteorite? Joy blinked. You think that's connected to the magnetic anomaly? There was one nearby, but that was ten years ago!

Just as I thought. Ethan owned a Deoxys and knew a great deal about the species. The mention of an old meteorite gave him a likely explanation.

He signaled to Solana and May. They understood, smiled politely at Joy, and followed him into the adjoining dining room.

Mr. Vale, do you already have an idea? Solana asked as soon as they sat down.

Yes. It has to do with that meteorite. The room was empty apart from the three of them, so Ethan spoke openly.

But Nurse Joy said it fell ten years ago, Solana said. Why would it disrupt the magnetic field only now?

The meteorite arrived ten years ago. Something inside it may have awakened only recently.

Solana was quick to follow his reasoning. Are you saying a Deoxys was inside?

Rather than answer directly, Ethan asked, How much do you know about Deoxys?

She thought for a moment. I know one appeared in LaRousse City. According to a report from Professor Lund that Ranger headquarters obtained, Deoxys traveled across space with a meteorite before reaching Earth. It seems to be a Pokemon associated with meteorites.

That's close enough, though calling it a Pokemon born alongside meteorites isn't quite right. Deoxys does travel through space with them. That's why we saw one here.

His certainty convinced Solana that he was probably right. Even so, one question troubled her.

Mr. Vale, how do you know all this? Even a League Champion or an International Police officer shouldn't understand Deoxys this well.

She was not trying to pry. It simply seemed unbelievable. The Rangers had worked hard to obtain even one of Professor Lund's reports. It was kept at headquarters, where only senior Rangers had access to its contents. Yet Ethan apparently knew more than they didperhaps even more than Lund, who had studied Deoxys for years.

How could that be?

Ethan weighed how to answer. Should he conceal the truth or reveal something about himself? Then he thought it over. His enemies already knew about many of his Pokemon. Telling an organization like the Rangers would do little harm and might help them understand what he could contribute.

He took an Ultra Ball from his waist pouch and set it quietly in front of Solana.

She blinked at it. What about this Ultra Ball?

Ethan smiled, speaking as if it were nothing remarkable. There's a Deoxys inside.

For a second Solana was still. Then she realized what he had said.

What!? She shot to her feet and stared at the ball. Her cry was so loud that Joy looked over from the other side of the Center.

You're too loud... Ethan had expected surprise, but even he was startled by her reaction.

Solana sat down quickly. Then she leaned toward the Ultra Ball with the wide-eyed curiosity of a child.

There's really a Deoxys in there? She tried to lower her voice, though the astonishment still came through. How did you do it? I mean, how did you meet it and catch it? That's incredible. It's such a rare Mythical Pokemon. I'd never even seen one in person before today!

Ethan put the Ultra Ball away. How I caught it is personal, so I'd rather not say. He shrugged. I told you for one reason: Professor Lund has studied Deoxys for years, but a Trainer who lives with one can understand it in ways no one else can.

If Misty had been here, she might have applauded his display of confidence with both hands. May, however, looked at him with much the same quiet admiration as Solana.

No matter how many times she heard it, May still found it astonishing that the man beside her owned so many Legendary and Mythical Pokemon.

Solana steadied herself, but her estimation of Ethan rose higher still. She now understood how he had found Celebi so easily before. Perhaps that kind of thing was easy for someone like him. If someone told her he had a Celebi of his own, she would hardly be surprised.

I'll find out where that meteorite fell, she said, rising from the table.

While Solana investigated, Ethan and May ordered food and filled their stomachs. She soon returned with a document in her hand and several additional pieces of equipment.

To end the disturbance and its effect on local equipment as soon as possible, they wasted no more time. They left the Pokemon Center and headed deeper into the mountains.

Ethan was reminded of Hoenn. He had once accepted a request from Devon Corporation and gone to deal with a meteorite and a Deoxys there. After all this time, he seemed to be facing a similar incident again.

The three followed Solana into the higher hills. Dense forest gave way to rocky ground, and the path climbed steadily. Soon they reached the foot of the mountains.

Solana did not lead them up the slope. She stopped before a cave beneath a cliff. Its opening was more than twice a person's height. Ethan could not tell whether it had formed naturally or been dug out. Cold air streamed from it, and the interior vanished into darkness.

It's in there. Solana checked her document against her Capture Styler before turning to the others. If the records are right, the meteorite is somewhere inside the cave.

Inside? May asked. Didn't it fall from the sky? How did it end up in a cave?

It did fall from the sky. It struck the ground above this cave, broke through the roof, and landed inside.

That's quite a coincidence.

While they spoke, Ethan studied the Capture Styler in Solana's hand. Isn't that affected by the magnetic disturbance?

Every electronic device they had tried on the way here, from phones and Pokedexes to Poke Balls, had failed. Even Solana's Plusle seemed drained, lying listlessly on her shoulder. Yet the Capture Styler still worked. They were closer to the meteorite now, where the disturbance ought to be stronger.

Solana looked a little proud. Rangers work in extreme places and weather all the time. The Capture Styler was designed with conditions like these in mind. Magnetic disturbances were one of the problems its designers tested for. After a lot of redesigning and trials, they made a device that could keep operating here.

She raised another device for them to see. And this one detects geomagnetic activity. It still works too.

Ethan nodded. Whatever the Ranger Union's size, he had to admire its technology.

I didn't realize your equipment was so useful. If ordinary Trainers had one, we wouldn't have to worry about getting lost anywhere.

He meant it as an idle observation. Solana heard it differently and made a mental note, though she said nothing.

They followed her into the cave. Rangers really were confident in their skills. They traveled the world with a Capture Styler, often without Poke Balls or powerful Pokemon of their own. Wild Pokemon were not necessarily a danger to them; almost any one they met could become an ally.

Their flashlight beams reached far down the dark passage, giving them a narrow path of light. May stayed close behind Ethan, carefully watching the ground and the black spaces around her.

She was afraid of the dark, as many people were. More than the darkness itself, she feared something dangerous might leap out and attack.

Fortunately, perhaps because of the geomagnetic anomaly or the power of Deoxys, they walked for a long time without anything happening.

Chapter 858: Both Home and Prison

They walked through the dark cave for more than ten minutes. Ethan guessed they must be well inside the mountain by now. Several hundred steps later, light began to appear ahead.

They emerged into a circular chamber. At its center, a silver meteorite pitted with round hollows lay embedded in the ground. Sunlight fell through a great opening in the ceiling and struck its surface, giving the stone a cold, mysterious glow.

Is that the meteorite with Deoxys inside? May asked. She went closer and realized how enormous it was. Even the part above ground rose three or four meters high.

Then another question occurred to her. If a meteorite this big hit Earth, shouldn't it have caused far more damage than this?

She had a point. A stone that size falling from space should have devastated the surrounding area, not merely punched a small hole through the mountain.

Perhaps Rayquaza had something to do with it, Ethan said. He did not know, but he could make a guess. Rayquaza lives in the ozone layer and treats this planet as its territory. It wouldn't stand by while a meteorite destroyed it. One or more Rayquaza might have intercepted the stone and slowed it. That might also explain why the Deoxys inside took ten years to awaken.

That could be right. Solana consulted the documents in her hand. The records say there was a violent explosion when it fell, but nothing more. There was no other disaster, so people assumed it was a small meteorite and paid little attention. Even this cave was reported only after local villagers found it by chance, and the report attracted hardly any interest.

The area was remote. Few people had reason to come here, let alone search for a meteorite.

May looked around. Then where is Deoxys hiding?
