Solana swept the chamber with her geomagnetic detector. The readings pointed to this place as the source, but she could not locate Deoxys itself.

This is where a specialist comes in, Ethan said.

He had no reason to keep his own Deoxys hidden now. He took its Ultra Ball from his pouch. Come out, Deoxys.

At his quiet call, the ball opened from within. Blue light flashed, and the strange, almost alien-looking Mythical Pokemon appeared before May and Solana.

So this is Deoxys? They stared at it from close range. Neither saw it quite as Ethan did. Its mysterious appearance inspired awe, but also a touch of fear. Like the meteorite beside it, the creature had come from space, and its alien shape made their skin prickle.

Deoxys paid them no attention. It floated toward the meteorite. At once the chamber shook. Solana's geomagnetic detector blared, and even her Capture Styler briefly stopped working.

The disturbance is getting stronger... Something is about to come out.

Solana nearly lost her footing. May caught her, and they held each other upright.

The space above the meteorite twisted, much as the sky beneath the aurora had. Another Deoxys appeared before them.

To an outsider it looked identical to Ethan's in size, markings, and form. Ethan, as its Trainer, could sense the differences between them.

Perhaps the presence of another of its kind reassured the newcomer. It made no threatening move and began communicating with Ethan's Deoxys. Soon a message reached him through his partner.

It...feels...pain...

Deoxys was speaking into Ethan's mind. Because it was an alien life-form with an alien way of expressing itself, however, its telepathy was never as precise or clear as Gardevoir's. Sometimes he had to guess what it meant.

He knew the wild Deoxys was in pain, but could not make out the cause from his partner's halting message. Fortunately, there was a more direct way to address the problem.

My Deoxys says the wild one is suffering, Ethan told May and Solana. We need to get it away from here.

Shouldn't that be easy? May asked cautiously. Your Deoxys can talk to it. Couldn't it ask the wild one to leave?

That's what worries me. If it could leave so easily, it would have gone already. I suspect the magnetic disturbance is keeping it here.

But we saw it in the sky earlier. How did it get out then?

I think that was a double, Ethan said, following his hunch. It may have sent a copy outside to make the aurora, hoping another Deoxys would see it and come to help.

It was only his analysis, but May thought he was probably right. She sighed. It's a shame our Poke Balls still won't work. If we could put it in one, this would be much simpler.

Solana had followed their discussion. All we need is to bring Deoxys away from here? Leave that to me!

She changed her Capture Styler into its working configuration, as she had when they first met, and launched a Capture Disc toward the wild Deoxys. She hoped to form a temporary bond with it, communicate directly, and enlist its help.

The idea was sound. She had overlooked both its power and its reluctance.

White capture lines curled around Deoxys. Solana thought she had succeeded, but a sphere of energy suddenly expanded from its body and tore through every line.

What? How did it do that? Her eyes widened. In all her time as a Ranger, she had never seen a Pokemon break free of the capture lines that way.

May teased her gently. I suppose it doesn't want to be your friend.

The failure robbed Solana of her earlier confidence. Embarrassed, she stepped back. It was obvious she could not handle this on her own.

She scratched her cheek and gave an awkward smile. I...have another thought. I'll ask headquarters if they know anything that could help.

Ethan turned from her to the wild Deoxys. He was certain now that he had never met this one. Its glance from the sky had not meant it recognized him. It must have sensed the presence of his Deoxys.

He would need to use his own method to free it. Can you move the meteorite out of here? he asked his partner.

It was a blunt solution. If the geomagnetic anomaly kept the wild Deoxys near its meteorite, they could move the meteorite itself. Whatever the precise cause, perhaps taking the stone elsewhere would remove the constraint.

His Deoxys nodded without speaking. It rose above the meteorite and lifted both hands. An invisible force wrapped around the huge stone, which began to shake violently.

Ethan could not judge its weight without knowing its density, but it had to weigh at least a dozen tons. An ordinary Pokemon might have no way to move something so massive. This was Deoxys, one of the world's most powerful Psychic-type Pokemon.

The meteorite slowly rose, exposing fresh earth beneath it. Deoxys guided it through the gap overhead and flew out beside it.

Once it was gone, Ethan turned to May and Solana. Come closer. We should get out of here too.

Solana wondered how he intended to bring them out. Before she could ask, another ball at his waist opened on its own, and the Gardevoir she had met earlier appeared.

So that's how...

The view before Solana changed abruptly, and she felt a moment of softness beneath her feet. When she found her bearings, the three of them stood outside the mountain under blue sky and white clouds, on yielding grass. They had arrived in the blink of an eye.

Teleport really is convenient, she murmured. Then she looked up and saw Deoxys flying toward them with the enormous meteorite.

Ethan gestured behind them. Let's go. We're still within the disturbed area. We need to get farther away.

They retraced their route out of the hills, stopping only when they had gone a long way. Deoxys set the meteorite down with a heavy boom that shook the ground.

Strangely, the strong geomagnetic anomaly persisted despite the distance. Ordinary devices and Poke Balls still would not work.

Ethan... May looked puzzled. We took the meteorite out of the cave and brought it all this way. Why is the magnetic disturbance still here?

Then there's only one likely explanation. Ethan shifted his gaze from her to the stone behind them. The anomaly may not be affecting the meteorite. The meteorite itself may be causing the anomaly.

At that moment, Solana received a response from headquarters. I think I know what's behind this, she said with a rueful smile. Have you heard of the solar wind?

Solar wind? May shook her head, then noticed Ethan nodding. He seemed to know everything. What is it? A kind of wind on the Sun?

Not really wind, Solana explained. It's a supersonic stream of charged plasma particles released from the Sun's upper atmosphere. Because it blows outward and reaches planets like ours, we call it the solar wind.

May waited for her to continue.

Headquarters says sunspots are growing larger right now, strengthening the solar wind. Its wave pattern exactly matches the geomagnetic anomaly here. So the solar wind appears to be involved. After what we just saw, though, I think it's affecting this meteorite in particular, and the meteorite is producing the local disturbance.

All three looked at the stone.

Ethan rubbed his chin. Every clue leads back to it. The meteorite must be the source.

May finally understood what had happened. No wonder moving away from the cave didn't help. The meteorite brought Deoxys to Earth, but now it's trapping it too?

That seems to be it, Solana said. She turned to Ethan. Mr. Vale, what should we do next?

What else can we do? If this stone is a prison, we'll have to break it and free Deoxys.

Huh? May hesitated. Do we really have to? Isn't there another way? This meteorite is...its home too.

Chapter 859: No Longer the Same

Apart from breaking the meteorite, I don't think the three of us have a better solution. Ethan smiled at May's concern for Deoxys. The stone has no use to it now. It can't ride it back into space, and staying with it is hurting it. Given the choice, Deoxys would probably destroy the meteorite itself.

He had his Deoxys ask the wild one. It agreed. The only reason it had not destroyed the stone already was that the geomagnetic anomaly weakened its powers. Trapped inside the meteorite, it could not break free without help from outside.

With that settled, Ethan led May and Solana back to a safer distance and signaled to his Deoxys. It rose high into the air and began gathering energy.

The wild Deoxys returned inside the meteorite. It changed to Defense Forme and used the power it could still summon to raise a barrier before itself, ready to withstand the blast.

Ethan's Deoxys was ready too. An energy sphere swelled before it until it was nearly two meters across. It pushed the enormous ball toward the meteorite.

The sphere struck almost at once. A blinding white flash filled Ethan's vision. Before he even felt the force of the explosion, an immense boom sounded in his ears. The shock wave followed.

They were more than fifty meters away, but Ethan had underestimated the blastor, more precisely, what happened when the meteorite exploded.

Its unusual material burst into a spray of brilliant colors. Fragments flew in every direction, tearing up the surrounding ground. Gardevoir reacted in time, wrapping Ethan, May, and Solana in psychic power to protect them from the shards.

The shock wave still swept over them. Wind whipped their hair and clothes, made it hard to open their eyes, and nearly knocked them off their feet. Fortunately, no one was hurt.

When the blast passed, they looked ahead. The meteorite was gone. In its place lay an enormous crater.

The wild Deoxys stood inside it in Defense Forme, beginning to stretch. Its barrier had broken at some point, and its body bore scrapes, but none seemed life-threatening. The wounds were already healing. In the short time they watched, most had closed.

Ethan kicked a meteorite fragment away from his feet and nodded. That worked.

It certainly did. Solana surveyed the area. The meteorite was gone, but so was the landscape as it had been. The crater looked like a chunk scooped out of level ground. Still, freeing Deoxys was worth it.

Remembering the original problem, she hurriedly took out her geomagnetic detector. She checked the readings and broke into a delighted smile.

The anomaly's gone!

Ethan checked his phone. Its signal had returned. May took out a Poke Ball and released Eevee.

Everything works again. That's wonderful!

The rescued Deoxys approached Ethan's partner. Multicolored ripples spread from both of their chests, each pattern shining into the other's body.

What are they doing? May asked.

It's how they communicate, Ethan said, still watching them. The wild one is probably thanking mine.

After a short exchange, the wild Deoxys shot into the sky and vanished. Its departure was sudden and decisive.

Huh? It just left?

Why wouldn't it? Ethan shook his head. It said goodbye and thanked my Deoxys. Now it wants to get away from the place that held it captive.

After all they had done, the incident seemed to end almost abruptly. In truth, that was what they had wanted. Ethan already had a Deoxys and did not need to catch another.

The effort had not been wasted. They had freed a trapped Mythical Pokemon, resolved the geomagnetic anomaly, and helped the Rangers. Most of all, Ethan's Deoxys had met another of its kind. Ethan had promised to help it find more companions, and this encounter honored that promise.

Solana thanked Ethan and May for their help. The three also exchanged contact information.

She wanted to accompany them back to the Pokemon Center, but Ethan declined. Let's part here. This took quite a while, and we need to continue our journey.

They had both come away with a better opinion of the other. Solana admired Ethan more than before, and he had begun to appreciate her in turn.

Where are you going next? she asked.

After their earlier disagreement, she would never have asked so easily. Now it felt natural. May briefly explained their plans.

The Battle Pyramid and the Grand Festival? Solana spent much of each year in the wild, but she was not ignorant of major competitions. She knew both Ethan and May had reached decisive points in their journeys. Then I wish you both success. Where will you go once those are over?

May turned to Ethan. If nothing changes, he said, we'll probably travel through Sinnoh next.

Sinnoh? Solana was surprised, then smiled. What a coincidence. I'm being assigned there next. It looks like we'll have a chance to meet again.

Really? Ethan smiled too. Then perhaps we'll see each other there.

...

Two days of travel later, Ethan and May finally reached Pewter City. For some reason, the Battle Pyramid had stayed near the city throughout those two days instead of moving again. Ethan did not know why it had stopped, but he was glad. They would not have to waste more time and effort chasing it elsewhere.

The map showed it somewhere outside the city. After such a long journey, though, they could afford a short rest before the challenge. The Pyramid did not seem about to fly away. They headed for Pewter's Pokemon Center first.

Ethan had been here before. It had been a long time, and he had forgotten some of the streets, but as he walked, old memories returned.

He guided May through an alley and onto the street where the Pewter Gym stood. He pointed ahead.

Brock's Gym and home are just up there. I remember the front looking like a little house built beneath a rockalmost one huge boulder. It was distinctive. When you went around it, though, the rock was only decoration. The building looked more like a warehouse. See, it's just like

He stopped. The entrance that should have looked like stone was now covered in bright colors, as if someone had painted all over it. Flags, streamers, and strings of lights hung from the front. It was spectacularly gaudy.

Was this really the Pewter Gym he remembered? May was astonished too.

This is Brock's Gym? It's so colorful. It doesn't match how I picture him at all.

Other Gyms had changed over time as well, including the Celadon and Cerulean Gyms. That in itself was not surprising. Ethan was taken aback by how completely the Pewter Gym's style had changed since Brock led it.

His parents must have wanted it this way. It doesn't suit Brock's serious face, but it does fit the passion underneath, Ethan said.

May covered her mouth as she laughed. Now I want to know what Brock would think if he saw his home like this.

They stopped to look a little longer, then continued down the street. It was someone else's family matter, and Brock was not here to explain. They could ask him when they next met.

Pewter was a small northern city, far from Kanto's bustling center, but its streets were lively enough. Shops lined both sides of the road. Pedestrians, vehicles, and Trainers traveling with their Pokemon moved among them.

Ethan and May walked side by side, talking and laughing. As they passed a woman with dark purple bobbed hair and glasses, Ethan suddenly felt that something was wrong.

He frowned, stopped, and looked back. The woman turned at almost the same moment, their gazes crossing over the crowd.

May noticed his reaction and looked too. The woman appeared to be in her twenties and otherwise unremarkable. She wore a dark red trench coat and oval black-framed glasses, giving her the look of an office worker.

What's wrong? Do you know her?

Ethan did not answer immediately. He studied the woman. He was certain he had never met her, yet she felt strangely familiar. Who could she be?

While he tried to place her, she turned away without showing any alarm and went on as though nothing had happened. Even after she disappeared, he could not think of where he might have seen her. He let it go.

I can't remember. It probably isn't important. Let's keep going.

Once they had left, the woman peered out from a shadowed alley nearby. Seeing that Ethan was truly gone, she let out a long breath.

A large man in ordinary clothes, with an eye patch, came up beside her. He frowned at her expression.

Miss Matori, what's wrong?

The bob-haired woman was Matori, Giovanni's secretarythe melon-rind glasses Jessie liked to call her. The man beside her was Gozu, captain of the Matori Matrix, Team Rocket's special unit under her command.

Matori's low, measured voice suited her composed appearance. I just saw that man.

That man? Gozu's face changed. Within Team Rocket, only one person needed no name when spoken of that way: Ethan Vale, the threat that weighed on all of them. Did he recognize you?

No. Matori shook her head. But even though we'd never met, he seemed to sense something about me.

How could he? You've never appeared before him. Even the International Police's files contain nothing about you. What could he have noticed?

I don't know. That's what bothers me. She sighed. Fortunately he only suspected something. If he'd known who I was, we'd be in serious trouble.

Gozu had faced Ethan before. The encounter had left a deep impression, and he knew how difficult the man was to deal with. Since then, Ethan had caught even more powerful Pokemon. Facing him again, Gozu felt helpless.

It was not that Team Rocket had failed to prepare. Ethan had simply grown too strong. Even the whole organization could no longer do much against him. Gozu hated admitting it, but he knew the gulf between them.

Why is he here? he asked. Could he have discovered we're in the city?

Impossible. No information about our presence has leaked. Matori shook her head, then added cautiously, Still, we should report this to Boss Giovanni and let him decide what to do.

Chapter 860: The Samurai Boy Is Still the Same

While Matori returned to Team Rocket's secret base to seek Giovanni's instructions, leaving the entire organization on alert, Ethan and May knew nothing of it. They checked in at the Pokemon Center and washed away the dust and fatigue of the road. Before dark, Ethan took May to the Pewter Museum of Science. It was a chance to walk off dinner and broaden her horizons, though she did not seem very interested.

They stayed one night. After breakfast, they left Pewter City for the forest nearby.

Mountains surrounded Pewter to the northwest, north, and northeast. They were bare and rocky rather than green, their dark gray slopes matching the city's name. Forest covered their lower reaches, lending the foothills a more lively appearance.

Ethan and May walked a long way north among the trees. The sun had climbed high, but the Battle Pyramid was nowhere in sight.

Ethan, are you sure it's here? May asked. We've walked for ages. It hasn't flown off again, has it?

Ethan checked the map Scott had sent him and shook his head. It's still where it was before. If the map is right, we'll reach it in another ten or twenty minutes.

As he spoke, something rustled in the bushes ahead. May thought a wild Pokemon was about to appear. Her eyes brightened, and she gestured to Eevee. It understood and leaped into the undergrowth.

May did not mean to catch anything. Combusken, Munchlax, Squirtle, and Eevee were still growing, but the four of them were enough to take her through the Grand Festival. She saw a playful encounter with a wild Pokemon as a chance for Eevee to practice.

Eevee vanished into the bushes. The leaves shook, and then a frightened boy shouted from inside.

Oh. That wasn't a Pokemon!

May hurried forward, alarmed that she had scared someone. Before she reached him, an older boy in samurai armor stumbled out of the bushes and fell to the ground. Eevee sprang out behind him.

I really did frighten him... she murmured. She was about to apologize when Ethan spoke.

You?

The armored boy looked up and recognized him. You're...that Trainer from before?

It was the Samurai boy Ethan had met during his first journey through Kanto. He looked just as he had then, wearing the same armor and carrying the same bug-catching net on his back.

May was relieved that they knew each other. Perhaps the mistake would be less awkward to settle.

I'm sorry, she said with an apologetic smile. I didn't mean to scare you. Are you all right?

Of course. A little thing like that doesn't bother me. Samurai got to his feet and brushed the dirt off his armor. Next time you send a Pokemon into the bushes, look first. You might frighten someone.

He sounded so composed that Ethan might have believed himif he had not heard the shout a moment ago.

The last time Ethan saw him, he and Chloe had been on their way to the Indigo League. They had met Samurai and the ninja Aya in Viridian Forest. After so long, the boy was apparently still wandering Kanto's woods. He might as well have grown roots in the forest and merely moved from one patch to another.

What was his name again? Ethan could not remember asking. Since the boy had never offered it, he saw no reason to ask now.

Samurai turned to him. I've been training ever since you beat me. This time I'm going to settle the score!

How long had it been since someone challenged Ethan so boldly? His thoughts drifted back to the start of his journey. Time had passed quickly.

May leaned toward him and whispered, Why does he sound so angry with you? What did you do?

It had been so long that Ethan could not recall every detail of their meeting. They had certainly battled. Probably nothing much. Maybe I beat him a little too thoroughly.

A memory stirred, and he smiled. Do you remember what I told you back then? he asked Samurai.

Of course! You Trainers from Pallet Town are a difficult bunch. I met several more after you, and every one of them beat me. Samurai drew himself up. But that's in the past! I've trained since then. I'm not the boy you defeated before!

Ethan remembered now. After beating Samurai, he had played a trick on the Trainers from Pallet Town by encouraging the boy to challenge them. Samurai had done exactly that and, just as in the animated story, had suffered one defeat after another. Even against Ash, he had managed little more than a draw.

May looked puzzled. She leaned close again. Since when are you from Pallet Town?

It was a little joke I made back then, Ethan whispered. I didn't expect him to take it seriously.

The exchange was brief, but Samurai felt slighted. Hey! What are you two talking about? He pulled a Poke Ball from his clothes and released his Pokemon. Send yours out! Today you'll find out what a crushing defeat feels like!

A flash of blue light revealed a Butterfree.

It looked different now, but Ethan was sure this was the Caterpie Samurai had owned before, the one that had become a Metapod and traded Harden after Harden with Ash's Metapod in the forest. Its evolution showed at least some progress.

Then again, the boy was badly out of touch. If he watched Pokemon tournaments, he would know what Ethan had accomplished. Someone who knew Ethan had won the Indigo League would hardly challenge him with such confidence. Perhaps ignorance made him fearlessor perhaps he had that much faith in his own growth.

Ethan looked into his waist pouch, sighed, and raised his head. I beat you once already. If you want another battle with me, you'll have to beat my assistant first.

Assistant? Samurai followed Ethan's gaze to May. This girl? He did not especially want to battle her, but he could see no way around it. Fine. I'll beat her and then I'll beat you!

May had no idea when she had become Ethan's assistant, but she understood what he wanted. She stepped in front of him beside Eevee.

That's right. You can't challenge Ethan just because you feel like it. Beat me first!

Eevee gave an excited cry and jumped toward Butterfree. Since hatching, it had played and tussled daily with Ethan's Eevee. May's partner was just as mischievous, energetic, and curious, and its battle style was growing similar too.

Ethan offered one warning. Watch out for Butterfree's powder moves.

May nodded and focused on the fight. They were in the wild with no referee. As soon as both Pokemon were ready, the battle began.

At their Trainers' commands, Eevee and Butterfree moved almost together. Butterfree flapped its wings and sent a strong Gust toward Eevee. Eevee slipped behind a large tree and avoided it easily.

The wind shook the tree and set its leaves rustling. Bushes shuddered as well. With whole stretches of forest in motion, Butterfree could no longer see clearly where Eevee had gone.

Samurai caught a glimpse of movement off to one side. He turned in time to see Eevee spring onto a tree trunk, launch itself upward, and slam into Butterfree.

Butterfree! Look out!

His warning came too late. Eevee struck, and Butterfree reeled in midair.

Samurai had expected Butterfree's height to give it the advantage over a Pokemon on the ground. Instead, the complicated forest terrain had helped Eevee hide from its sight. Without Butterfree flapping, the Gust died away.

That first exchange told him the pretty girl was no easy opponent. She was more capable than the Trainers he usually met wandering through the forest.

Samurai had spent years here and seen many Trainers and tactics, though. He did not panic. Once Butterfree steadied itself, he attacked again.

Butterfree shot a white thread of silk toward Eevee. It moved so quickly that it caught Eevee's ankle just as it landed from its leap.

May had an answer ready. Calmly, she led Eevee to a nearby tree. Eevee circled the trunk several times, winding the silk around it, then pulled hard. Anchored by the tree, it dragged Butterfree down toward the ground. Samurai had to order Butterfree to break the thread.

Ethan found a rock and sat down to watch. Samurai's first two attacks had achieved nothing. There was a gap between his battle sense and May's.

It was not a matter of how many Trainers he had faced. A good Trainer read a complicated battlefield and adapted to danger instead of trading attacks mechanically. Samurai still lacked that flexibility. His years in the forest exposed him to new Pokemon and opponents, but his habits limited what he learned. Without entering tournaments or watching high-level battles, genuine growth would be difficult.

Unless something changed, May would beat him soon. The battle unfolded as Ethan expected.

Once May understood Butterfree's strength and habits, she settled into a counterattacking rhythm. Trees and bushes gave Eevee cover for both defense and quick movement, letting it evade Butterfree's attacks while creeping closer.

Butterfree finally released Stun Spore. Eevee used Sand Attack to scatter much of the powder. It darted through the gap it had opened and struck Butterfree with Quick Attack, knocking it out.

Butterfree fell with a thud directly in front of Samurai.

Damn it... He clenched his fists at the sight of his unconscious partner. He had not expected to lose even to this girl. How could he get revenge on Ethan now?

Well? Ethan smiled. My assistant is pretty good, isn't she?

Samurai reddened, unwilling to accept it. I was careless. I want another battle!

Another one? Ethan raised an eyebrow and looked at May. She nodded. He turned back with a smile. All right. That's fine with us.

Delighted, Samurai took out the Poke Ball holding his strongest partner. He had saved this Pokemon to challenge Ethan, but after losing one match, he had to win one back first.

Chapter 861: I Have a Feeling We'll Meet Him Again

A flash of blue light revealed a Heracross whose entire body was purple. Its color was so different from an ordinary Heracross's that Ethan and May recognized it at once as a Shiny Pokemon.

That was unexpected. Ethan had not imagined a Bug Catcher who rarely left the forest would own a Shiny Pokemon. Then again, perhaps that was precisely why he had found one. He devoted his time to searching deep among the trees for Bug-type Pokemon.

So your Shiny Heracross is your strongest partner? Ethan asked.

May did not underestimate it. She recalled Eevee and took out Combusken's Poke Ball. Samurai was a useful opponent for practice, but that did not mean she wanted to lose through carelessness.

Another flash of blue light brought out her first partner. Combusken's Fire-type moves gave it an advantage over Heracross. May clearly had no intention of handing Samurai an opportunity. In that respect, her style was growing more like Ethan's all the time. She was almost a smaller, female version of him.

Ethan shifted on his seat and called one more warning. Be careful with fire. We're in a forest. One mistake could start a disaster.

I know, May said.

Both Trainers and Pokemon were ready. The battle began.

Despite the unfavorable matchup, the Shiny Heracross went straight on the attack. That aggression suited its species. Lowering its great horn, it charged Combusken with Horn Attack.

Combusken did not try to meet the heavy blow head-on. It leaped high over Heracross and landed behind it, avoiding the attack and leaving its opponent's back exposed.

May's temperament kept her from getting carried away by a contest of strength. She preferred to find an opening rather than force a clash, and that caution showed in the way she fought.

Heracross plowed through two trees before it stopped. Its horn was formidable, especially with Horn Attack behind it. A direct hit could have badly injured Combusken. But now its unguarded back offered the perfect chance to strike.

Combusken ran forward without waiting for May to tell it and used Double Kick.

Samurai had improved since their last meeting, though, and Heracross was his strongest Pokemon. He stayed calm. At his command, Heracross beat the thin wings on its back and flew a short distance. It soon landed again, but the movement was enough to avoid Combusken's kick.

Heh. Did you think I wouldn't be ready? Samurai said smugly. Now you'll see what my Heracross can do!

Heracross attacked again, this time with Pin Missile. Wave after wave of sharp needles whistled through the air toward Combusken. Samurai plainly wanted to finish the fight quickly.

He still underestimated May. She might have spent fewer years battling other Trainers, but her ability to adapt was on another level. She had not won so many Contests by accident.

Combusken, Quick Attack!

At her command, Combusken ran in a zigzag. It was not moving at extraordinary speed, but it was fast enough to slip past every volley of needles.

Damn it... Sweat gathered beneath Samurai's armor. He had fought strong Trainers in the forest before, yet this girl felt strangely harder to handle. Against both Butterfree and Heracross, he could not bring his strength to bear. Moves that usually worked against passing Trainers had failed him again and again.

The more that happened, the more anxious he grew. At this rate he would never challenge Ethan. He could not even beat May. He wanted to change the course of the battle, but she gave him no chance.

May admitted to herself that Heracross's short flight had surprised her. Her experience in Trainer battles was still limited. Now that she had seen the trick once, though, she would be ready if Samurai tried it again.

It was her turn to attack. Combusken used the momentum of Quick Attack to close on Heracross. It kept running, apparently ready to settle things with a close-range Fighting-type move.

Heracross was part Fighting type too. Under Samurai's direction, it planted its feet and waited. Why should it fear another Fighting-type Pokemon?

What reached it was not a Fighting-type move. Just before impact, flames flared around Combusken's body, and it slammed into Heracross.

It was Flame Charge.

May had taken Ethan's warning to heart. She did not dare use Ember or Flamethrower freely among the trees. Flame Charge kept the fire close to Combusken's body, where she could control it.

The feint caught Samurai unprepared. He could only watch Combusken strike like a ball of fire. Fire was strong against Bug types, and even a sturdy Heracross cried out in pain.

Combusken did not let up. It followed with a string of Peck attacks, using the Flying-type move to bring the Shiny Heracross down.

How... Samurai's legs weakened at the sight of his fallen Pokemon. He sank to his knees, unable to accept the result.

He had lost again. The second time he met Ethan, he and the ninja Aya had tried to overwhelm him together in Viridian Forest. Their fight had ended before a final result, but Samurai knew he had been losing then too. He had trained for so long and beaten many passing Trainers, yet he had lost to Ethan's side just as easily upon meeting him again.

This time he had not even fought Ethan. Ethan's supposed assistant had beaten him first. It was infuriating.

Then another thought occurred to him. The pretty girl traveling with Ethan last time had been beautiful, but now he was accompanied by a different pretty girl. What a womanizer! And, if Samurai was honest with himself, how enviable.

I lost today. He got up and faced Ethan, fists clenched. But next time we meet, I'll beat you! Then I'll draw all over your face and make you see what it's like to be left sleeping outside!

Draw on his face?

The remark finally brought back what had happened before. Ethan spread his hands. That wasn't me. Remember the Jigglypuff we met? It drew on everyone. I got caught by it too...

He stopped. He had since caught that Jigglypuff. It was his Pokemon now. Did that make its mischief his responsibility after all?

Perhaps Samurai was not entirely wrong. Ethan sighed inwardly. Somehow the blame had all landed on him. No wonder the boy held such a grudge. Still, there was no chance he would admit to it now.

Samurai recalled his Pokemon and left, still seething. Once he had disappeared among the trees, May returned to Ethan with a laugh.

It sounds as if the two of you have quite a misunderstanding.

We do. Ethan shook his head. It's more than I can explain in one sentence. I'll tell you when we have time. Besides, I have a feeling that if we come back to Kanto, we'll run into him again.

...

After the interruption, they gathered themselves and continued deeper into the forest. In a little more than ten minutes, they saw the tip of a pyramid above the trees. Both quickened their pace.

Several hundred meters later, they rounded a stand of large trees and finally saw the Battle Pyramid in full. Its shape matched its name: a great pointed pyramid. It was dark rather than stone-colored, made of joined panels that looked like metal plating or solar cells. The whole structure had a technological air.

It rose fifty or sixty meters high and was too broad for Ethan to judge at a glance. The massive building looked magnificent and utterly out of place in the forest.

That's the Battle Pyramid? May gasped. It's enormous!

Ethan nodded. It was hard to imagine a building this size flying from place to place. He had no idea how Brandon had managed it.

What caught Ethan's attention more, though, were the ancient ruins beside it. Broken walls stood amid vines and moss. They looked centuries old. Wind and sun had worn the writing on their pillars and stones until it was almost illegible.

May noticed the ruins too and frowned. She was about to say something when the ground suddenly split beneath them. A hole opened, and both stepped into empty air before they could react.

May had no time even to scream. Something caught her falling body. When her eyes adjusted to the darkness, she saw Gengar holding her and Ethan suspended with an uncanny power.

You two are impossible, Gengar said with an exaggerated sigh. Falling into a trap like that? Careless.

It started to float them back toward the opening, but Ethan stopped it.

It isn't a trap. He looked down, then up. Part of the ruins' underground structure gave way under our feet. It's been here too long. Take us down, Gengar.

Ruins? Interested now, Gengar lowered them gently to the bottom. Within seven or eight seconds, Ethan and May were standing safely on solid ground.

Without help, a fall from that height might have left them scratched and bruised. The loose earth that fell with them would at least have cushioned the landing, so it probably would not have been deadly.

Once he was sure there was no other hidden danger, Ethan looked around. They were in a passage belonging to the ruins. Stone slabs covered the floor, murals marked both walls, and Pokemon statues stood at intervals. Like the broken structures aboveground, everything showed its age.

Then Ethan noticed an electric lamp farther down the passage. He and May looked at each other.

Is someone down here? May whispered. Could an ancient Pokemon have survived all this time?

You're getting carried away. Ethan shook his head. The Battle Pyramid has been here for days, right beside the ruins. I'd guess its Frontier Brain is investigating them.

So we might meet him down here?

Who knows? It seems likely.

They followed the passage toward the light. At a fork, they chose one route and kept walking. To guard against mechanisms or other hazards, Ethan released Gardevoir. With it and Gengar beside them, they could handle an emergency.

As they walked, Ethan took photographs of the writing and pictures on the walls. He could not read the inscriptions, but he could preserve them and send them to Professor Cerise. Cerise might have no use for them himself, yet he could pass them to other researchers. That way, Ethan could at least help someone study the ancient ruins.

Chapter 862: The Underground Ruins

Murals of ancient Pokemon covered the passage walls. Ethan recognized some of them, but others were unfamiliar. He took a few quick photographs of the murals and statues as he and May walked on. They passed several obvious traps, carefully avoiding the mechanisms rather than touching them.

What do you think this place was? May asked, looking around. It even has traps. Could it be a tomb?

Something like that. Underground ruins tend to be either tombs or hiding places. Until we find a distinctive feature or whatever secret was kept here, we can't be sure what this one was for.

Perhaps they had chosen the right direction. After another hundred or so steps, a wide bend, an underground crossroads, and several dozen more meters, they reached a strange, broad door with a few recesses in its surface.

May frowned at it. That door looks different from the rest of the ruins. Do you think it's the room with the secret you mentioned?

There's an easy way to find out. We go inside.

Remembering the traps they had passed, Ethan kept his distance and signaled to Gengar. For once it did not grumble. Apparently it was curious about the other side too. It slipped into the wall and vanished.

Ethan and May waited quietly. Barely a dozen seconds later, Gengar emerged again.

The door has a trick to it, it said with a grin. Good thing you didn't go straight through. As soon as the first person passes it, it slams shut and locks. Only a switch nearby can open it again.

Without waiting for Ethan's reply, Gengar went to a stone pillar, pulled out a loose brick, and pressed the switch hidden behind it.

Stone scraped against stone. With a series of harsh clicks, the door opened and revealed a dark space beyond.

Having a Ghost-type Pokemon made this sort of exploration easier. Gengar could find mechanisms that would defeat most people, and even follow concealed passages through solid ground to places no human or ordinary Pokemon could reach.

Just as Ethan and May prepared to enter, hurried footsteps sounded behind them. Someone was running down the corridor, getting closer. They stopped and turned in surprise.

A few breaths later, a middle-aged man appeared, panting from his run. He seemed equally surprised to find them. Who are you?

Ethan looked him over before answering. The man was in his forties, wearing olive-green expedition clothes. His grayish hair was a little long and untidy, his complexion pale, his gaze sharp, and his mouth set in a stern line.

Ethan was fairly sure who he was, but asked anyway. Who are you?

The man studied them closely. I'm Brandon. How did you get into these ruins?

So this was the final Frontier Brain: the Pyramid King of the Battle Pyramid. Of all people, he was the one Ethan would expect to find here.

Brandon? May stared, then turned to Ethan. Then he's the

Brandon's eyes narrowed before she could finish. You know me?

Of course, Ethan said. We came to challenge you. We were nearly at the Battle Pyramid when the ground collapsed beneath us and dropped us into the ruins.

I see. Brandon folded his arms. Then you've defeated the other six Frontier Brains and earned their Symbols.

His gaze passed over their shoulders to the open door. Visitors aren't allowed in this area. Even if you entered by accident, you should leave as soon as possible.

Ethan did not move. We've lost our way. Mr. Brandon, what is this place?

Brandon hesitated, deciding whether to tell them. They were already standing in the ruins, though, so there was little point in concealing it.

These are the ruins of Pokelantis. It was a mysterious ancient kingdom. I learned it existed only when I found references to it in old documents.

Pokelantis? Ethan and May exchanged a look. Neither had heard of such a country.

Few people have. According to legend, the empire of Pokelantis tried to control Ho-Oh and conquer the world. It angered Ho-Oh, which destroyed the entire kingdom and erased it from history in a single night.

Brandon walked to their side and looked into the dark room without entering. The story says the king escaped. Seeking revenge, he used a strange power to seal Ho-Oh in a stone orb and hid it somewhere. It may still be hidden to this day.

The King of Pokelantis. Ho-Oh. A stone orb. Those words suggested something extraordinary, especially with Ho-Oh involved.

Thinking of Ho-Oh reminded Ethan of Johto, where it had stopped him from catching the three legendary beasts. He had encountered it himself, which was enough to know this part of the legend could not be true. If Ho-Oh had been sealed in ancient times, who had he seen? What would become of Johto's stories about the three beasts? The tale had plainly been exaggerated.

He rubbed his chin. So the room ahead is where the orb is supposed to be?

Possibly. I've searched for information about this kingdom for years. I discovered these ruins only a few days ago and have been examining them bit by bit. Your arrival disrupted that plan. Whether the orb is actually in this room remains to be seen.

Ethan remembered that Brandon was not only a Frontier Brain but an adventurer and archaeologist.

Brandon went through the doorway first. Ethan and May followed with Gardevoir and Gengar.

The instant they entered, braziers along both walls lit on their own, one after another, illuminating the room to its far end. There, a gigantic statue several meters high sat on a stone throne, holding a ring-topped staff.

The firelight revealed an elderly man in a cloak and rounded hat, with wrinkles covering his face. Perhaps it was only the shifting light, but the statue looked sinister. A cold draft stirred from an unseen crack or corner.

All three stared.

Is that the King of Pokelantis? May asked cautiously. She kept her voice low, as though speaking too loudly might wake something.

Neither man answered. They had noticed a second, smaller stone throne beneath the statue. No one sat there. At first it seemed unremarkable, except for the stone orb resting on its seat. It resembled a Poke Ball.

May followed their gazes and saw it too. The orb was slightly larger than a modern Poke Ball and earth-yellow all over. A band of carved markings ran around its middle, with a square black-purple gem set into it like a switch.

There really is a stone orb! Could Ho-Oh be inside?

May was astonished. Then she remembered Misty telling her that she and Ethan had met Ho-Oh. The orb could not hold it. Why, then, had the orb been placed in such a prominent spot?

All three approached, but no one reached out to touch it. Brandon silently approved of their caution. Neither visitor had tried to seize a rare artifact on sight.

From my research and eyewitness accounts, Ho-Oh is still active somewhere in the world, he said. So the orb doesn't contain Ho-Oh. Something else may be inside.

Ethan knew as much, but he was still curious. Should we open it and see?

He was beginning to recall the story tied to these ruins. The orb held the king's spirit, if he remembered correctly. In the animated story, it had possessed Ash and controlled him for quite some time.

Brandon shook his head. Curiosity is useful, but we don't know what's inside. We don't even know whether it could still be alive after thousands of years. Until we understand it, we shouldn't touch it carelessly.

That was the difference between an archaeologist and a tomb robber. Another person might already have picked up the orb and opened it. Brandon could resist the temptation.

Ethan wanted to meet a soul from thousands of years ago and hear how it spoke and thought, but he did not want some strange being possessing him. Since neither man moved closer, May certainly would not.

The orb seemed to grow impatient. It began to rock gently on the throne, though no one had touched it.

Perhaps the presence of living people had awakened the king's spirit. Unable to lure anyone near, it shook the orb to draw their attention. Ethan and Brandon were too wary to take the bait. If anything, the movement made them more cautious.

Gengar floated to Ethan's side, frowning. Be careful. I sense something familiar in there, and I don't like it. It's almost like...a ghost.

Ethan nodded. Brandon glanced over in surprise, then looked away. Even he was not used to hearing a Gengar speak.

The orb rocked harder. With no one coming close, however, its invitation was useless.

Perhaps it could wait no longer after thousands of years, or perhaps it feared losing this rare chance at a host. Black light flashed from the stone orb, and it opened on its own.

A hazy, dark figure floated out and rose into the air. It was too dense and shadowed for Ethan to see its features. He could only make out the shape of an old man, rather like the statue behind it. This was probably the king's spirit.

The figure circled the room as if choosing a target. When it reached the space above Ethan, it suddenly dived toward him. Between middle-aged Brandon and young May, the spirit apparently preferred the body of a young man.

Ethan frowned. He had kept his distance, and it still chose him. What rotten luck.

He did not have to act. Gengar, a Ghost-type Pokemon and an expert at dealing with spirits, moved in front of its Trainer.

Heh heh heh. I won't let an old thing like you take over my Trainer!

Gengar thrust both hands forward. Dark energy struck the king's spirit, which shrieked as if badly hurt and flew backward.

Chapter 863: The Stone Poke Ball

What could a disembodied human soul do against a Ghost-type Pokemon?

It might wield some dark energy and have existed for countless years, but the answer was still nothing. Next to a Ghost-type Pokemon, the power of a human soul was like a newborn child: helpless in its grasp.

Gengar's shove sent the King of Pokelantis's spirit flying backward like a kite with a broken string. It traveled a long way before it finally stopped.

Who are you? Why have you trespassed in my bedchamber?

When one could not seize the initiative, one could at least claim the moral high ground.

His surprise attack had failed, and the blow had taught him that these intruders would be hard to handle. The king changed tactics, trying to hold them in place with words.

That might have worked on reckless explorers. Ethan and Brandon were not going to fall for it. His ancient manner of speech did sound strange to their ears, though.

Who are you? Brandon asked instead of answering.

Heh heh heh... The spirit laughed with imperious self-importance. I am the ruler of the world! The King of Pokelantis!

Brandon frowned and turned to Ethan and May. Then the legend was wrong. It wasn't Ho-Oh sealed in that stone orb. It was the King of Pokelantis himself!

You have heard my name? The spirit shook violently. Excellent. Offer me your Pokemon, and this time my empire shall conquer the entire world!

Several black rays flashed from him like tentacles, shooting toward the Poke Balls at Ethan's, May's, and Brandon's waists.

Unable to possess anyone, he seemed to have decided to steal their Pokemon instead. The ghostly tendrils got only halfway before Gengar waved a hand and stopped them again.

No matter how fiercely the king threatened them, he could achieve nothing with Gengar in front of him. It was a natural mismatch, and he had no way around it.

I see. Brandon watched the defeated tendrils withdraw into the spirit and gave a cold snort. He had pieced the affair together. What was sealed back then was your own ambition! The legend is false. You spread it yourself so people would think Ho-Oh was inside. When an unsuspecting, greedy explorer touched the orb, you could take over their body and live again!

That was exactly the King of Pokelantis's scheme. Brandon glanced toward the stone orb sitting quietly on the throne.

We have to seal him again. The mechanism must be inside that orb. If we can get hold of it, perhaps we'll find a way to contain him.

Ethan shook his head. There's no need to go to all that trouble.

When Brandon looked at him, Ethan shrugged. If we seal him in the orb again, what changes? He got out on his own just now. Or the next adventurer who finds it might touch it, and he'll try to steal that person's body. We'd be right back where we started.

May's eyes brightened. Then we could hide it! Somewhere nobody would ever find it!

It's not that simple. These ruins were well hidden, and we still found them. Throw the orb into the sea or bury it deep underground, and someone will eventually come across it. There's no place that's truly safe. Hiding it would only make him wait another few hundred or thousand years.

May hesitated. Then you mean...?

Brandon glanced at Ethan. He means to destroy the King of Pokelantis's soul completely.

Destroy his soul? May's eyes widened. But he was human. Wouldn't that be...?

She was neither naive nor given to misplaced pity. Even so, the king had a human soul. If Ethan destroyed it, wouldn't that amount to killing a person?

It was understandable that the thought troubled her. She had spent so long traveling with Ash. Whatever trouble they encountered, their adventures usually ended with everyone safe and happy. This was different.

And could it cause problems for Ethan? She would never tell anyone, of course, but Brandon was there too. If word spread, what would the law say? What would people think?

Ethan had no idea how much May had considered in that brief moment, or how concerned she was for him.

He's lived long enough, Ethan said calmly. Surviving as a soul for all this time goes against the natural order. A harmless spirit would be one thing. But he's still ambitious, and he refuses to rest. We might as well help him on his way before he can hurt anyone else.

Brandon was a Frontier Brain as well as a levelheaded explorer who understood the larger stakes. After a moment's thought, he agreed.

You're right. We can't leave him like this. What do you intend to do?

Leave it to the Pokemon best qualified for the job. Ethan pointed ahead. Gengar, he's yours.

Heh heh heh! All I have to do is make him disappear? Got it!

Gengar laughed so loudly that it looked more like the villain than the King of Pokelantis.

As it drew closer with a wicked grin, the king suddenly panicked. A bodiless soul could sense, deep within itself, why a Ghost-type Pokemon was dangerous to it.

He turned and tried to slip through the wall. But how could he escape a Gengar that had lived for more than two thousand years?

A terrifying pull caught his spirit and dragged it backward. No matter how he struggled, he could not resist it.

No!

He flew toward Gengar. Looking back, he found the talking Pokemon right beside him, its mouth wide open.

Gengar did not intend to eat the King of Pokelantis. It was no man-eating Pokemon, even if the man was only a soul. Besides, an evil old creature like this looked too filthy and unappetizing. Gengar would worry about getting a stomachache. Its open mouth was merely a way to draw him close.

What are you doing to me? the king demanded.

Then, to his horror, Gengar seized him with both hands. He had no body, yet pain tore through him all the same.

Gengar gave a sharp pull. The ancient emperor who had hoped to revive himself and resume his conquest screamed as his soul was ripped apart. It dissolved into the air.

May's eyelids twitched. Unable to watch, she turned her head away, but she said nothing. She knew the spirit was wicked, full of obsession and resentment, and could not be allowed to remain.

Fragments of the King of Pokelantis's soul vanished in scattered bursts of black light. He was gone from the world completely.

Gengar dusted off its hands and returned to Ethan's side. Now he won't hurt anyone else.

Ethan shook his head. His mood had grown a little heavy, but he did not regret the decision. I suppose the legend of the King of Pokelantis ends today.

You've done a good thing, Brandon said evenly, though he studied Ethan again.

The young man before him was calm and observant, bold without being careless, decisive enough to do what he believed necessary. This was no ordinary Trainer.

Though they had only just met, Brandon knew that someone with such resolve was not a minor figure. I haven't asked your names.

Ethan, who barely knew Brandon, had no idea he had made such an impression.

We forgot to introduce ourselves. I'm Ethan Vale, a Trainer. This is May, my traveling companion and a Coordinator.

May gave Brandon another small smile.

Ethan Vale... Brandon felt he had heard the name somewhere before.

He nodded. That's settled for now. Since you came to challenge me, let's go to the battlefield.

Brandon led the way out. After a few steps, he realized Ethan had not followed and turned back.

Ethan pointed at the stone orb on the throne and smiled. The orb isn't doing anything now. Mind if I take it?

He phrased it as a question, but hardly sounded as if he meant to wait for permission. Gardevoir raised a hand, and the next moment the orb rested securely in Ethan's palm. Brandon would not have had time to stop her even if he had tried.

He looked at Ethan again without expression, gave no answer, and turned to leave. Ethan took that as tacit consent. And even if Brandon objected, he had no intention of handing over something already in his possession.

He shrugged at May, and the two followed Brandon down a passage on the other side of the chamber.

Brandon had been exploring these ruins for days. He seemed to know every passage and trap in their first section. With him leading, Ethan and May had no need to worry about a wrong turn or a hidden mechanism. Within minutes, they reached the exit.

Along the way, Ethan examined the orb. He had already seen its appearance and had no need to study the markings again. It really was made of stone, cold and heavy in his hand. It felt as though it weighed at least a pound and a half, a world apart from a light modern Poke Ball. He could almost use it as a thrown weapon.

Imagine producing it in the middle of a battle and hurling it without warning. He could split the opposing Trainer's head open! That would be a victory on and off the battlefield, devastating his opponent in both mind and body.

He was only joking with himself. If he actually did that, Officer Jenny would probably put out a worldwide warrant for him the very next day.

May leaned over and took the orb to turn it in her hands. It's heavy! Is this really a Poke Ball from thousands of years ago? Apart from the material, it doesn't look that different from a modern one.

She was right: other than its material, the two kinds of ball seemed much alike. Ethan still refused to underestimate it.

It could hold a human soul, and according to the legend, it could capture Ho-Oh. He did not know why the king had failed to catch Ho-Oh and ended up sealing his own spirit inside instead. But if any part of the legend was reliable, this stone ball might be on the level of a Master Ball even now.

Whatever, Ethan said with a smile. You can never have too many Poke Balls. I'm sure I'll find a use for it someday. When the time comes, we'll learn what it's capable of.

They followed Brandon through a hidden, half-open stone doorway and emerged aboveground.

Sunlight struck their eyes. After so long in the dim ruins, they had to stand still for a while before the sting faded and they could see properly again.

The Battle Pyramid stood a few dozen meters ahead. From this close, its height was even more impressive. To think that a structure so enormous could fly high into the sky and travel for long periods was astonishing.

At its entrance Ethan saw someone whose presence surprised him, though it made sense: Scott, the owner of the entire Battle Frontier.

Scott broke into a broad smile as soon as Ethan appeared. Well, Mr. Vale, you've kept me waiting! I came as soon as I sent you the location because I didn't want to miss this spectacular battle. I never expected you to take so long to arrive!

Chapter 864: Returning to Familiar Ground

A few days earlier, as soon as Scott had told Ethan where the Battle Pyramid was, he had set out for it himself.

Scott came to watch even when an ordinary challenger reached the final facility. This time, a man with League titles from three regions was about to battle the strongest of the Frontier Brains. The match promised to be spectacular. How could he miss it?

He had been a long way off when he sent the location. To make certain he arrived in time, he had hurried all the way hereonly to wait several days for Ethan.

If he'd known, he would not have rushed so much. At least Ethan had finally arrived.

But something was odd. Scott looked from Brandon to Ethan and back again. How did you two end up together? Did you already know each other?

No. We happened to meet by chance. Ethan shook his head and told Scott what had just happened in the underground ruins. Scott stood stunned for a while after hearing the story.

An ambitious King of Pokelantis? What a shame I wasn't there. I'd have liked to see what a human soul actually looks like.

May covered her mouth with a laugh. Mr. Scott, you're lucky you weren't there. If you had been in that room, he might have possessed you!

True! Scott laughed. There aren't many men as handsome as me. I'm sure the King of Pokelantis would have wanted my body!

After the brief joke, Brandon and Scott led Ethan and May into the Battle Pyramid. They passed through a doorway built in the same style as the pyramid and went straight to the battle hall on the first floor.

The hall was much plainer than the exterior. It contained a standard battlefield and nothing else, not even a table or chair. What it did have was space: even when the pyramid was airborne, there was plenty of room to battle.

A young man came to greet them. He looked about Ethan's age, though his face was somewhat boyish. He wore a headband and expedition clothes, and had an open, cheerful manner.

Master, why are you back so early today? Then he noticed Ethan and May behind Brandon. Have challengers arrived?

Scott introduced him before Brandon could answer. Mr. Vale, this is Samuel, Brandon's apprentice and assistant. He referees matches here at the Battle Pyramid. He's a friendly fellow; I'm sure you'll get along. Samuel, this is Ethan Vale, the man I've been telling you about these past few days.

This is him? Samuel's eyes lit up. He hurried over and looked Ethan up and down, curious about a man who seemed to be his own age.

You're Ethan Vale? The one who won League tournaments in three regions? Wonderful! Ever since Mr. Scott told me about you, I've been looking forward to your arrival. After all these days, you're finally here!

Brandon's expression cleared as he listened. No wonder Ethan's name had sounded familiar. He was the man Scott and Samuel had been discussing all week.

Three regional League championships? This would be no ordinary challenger. Perhaps he would even make Brandon fight seriously for the first time in a while.

Ethan did not pretend to be modest. He chatted with Samuel for a moment, gracious and at ease. There was no point in playing down his achievements when everyone already knew them. A Champion should carry himself with some confidence.

Brandon had already gone to the Trainer's position on one side of the field. Ethan gave the others a small wave and walked to his own position. Samuel hurried to the referee's area.

He was about to explain the usual rules when Brandon raised a hand to stop him. Samuel looked at him, puzzled. Brandon kept his eyes on Ethan.

A Champion has come to challenge me. We needn't use the ordinary rules. Ethan, how would you like to battle?

He's letting me choose the rules? That suited Ethan perfectly.

He smiled. I've heard you have three rather unusual Pokemon, Mr. Brandon. I came to see them for myself.

Brandon raised an eyebrow. He knew precisely which three Ethan meant. But he had never shown them to outsiders. How did Ethan know?

You know which Pokemon I have?

Not all of them, Ethan replied. I don't know the rest of your team. But I have heard a little about those three.

Scott was lost. What three Pokemon? What are you two talking about? The more I listen, the less I understand. Did Brandon have a secret even Scott knew nothing about?

May, by contrast, stayed calm. Before coming here Ethan had told her a little about Brandon, including some of the Pokemon he might use. She even knew which of Ethan's Pokemon he intended to send against them.

Seeing that his master did not mean to keep the matter hidden, Samuel turned to Scott. Mr. Scott, how much do you know about the legendary giants?

The legendary giants? Scott frowned. The eternal Pokemon from the old stories? I think they're a group of Legendary Pokemon from Hoenn: Regirock, Regice, and Registeel. I've heard they came from rock, icebergs, and magma, though I don't know if that's true.

There are more than those three, Ethan said. Far away in Galar are Regidrago and Regieleki. They're legendary giants too. Most people around here don't know about them, so they group Regirock, Regice, and Registeel together as the three Regis.

I see. I certainly haven't heard of the other two. Scott nodded, then realization struck him. He stared at Brandon. Wait. Don't tell me you have those three Pokemon?

Samuel nodded, then quickly shook his head. Master has caught members of the three Regis, but not all three. He has two of them.

Two? Ethan frowned. What did that mean? Brandon had only two? Had Ethan come too early?

That's right. Master has caught Regirock and Registeel. We haven't caught Regice yet, but we have some leads. I believe we'll complete the trio before long!

Ethan sighed inwardly. He really had arrived too soon.

Brandon, who had been quiet for a while, asked, How did you know I was collecting the three Regis?

Ethan invented a reason on the spot. I happened to hear someone mention a powerful explorer traveling around in a mobile pyramid, looking for the three Regis. I thought it might be you.

Whether Brandon believed him was Brandon's business.

Still, this was a disappointment. I thought you'd have all three by now, Ethan said, shaking his head. I wanted to test myself against them. It seems I can't have the battle I came for yet.

Brandon, Scott, and Samuel understood the implication. Ethan knew Legendary Pokemon were involved, yet spoke with such confidence. Either he had complete faith in the strength of his own Pokemon, or he had caught Legendary Pokemon of a comparable caliber.

After a moment's thought, Ethan looked at Brandon. You have a lead on Regice, so perhaps it won't take long. I'm willing to wait.

What? Scott and Samuel stared at him. Was he saying there would be no match today?

Then Brandon laughed. Interest lit his eyes, and his reserved manner fell away. You've given me an intriguing challenge. I accept it. If you want to face all three Regis, I'll grant your wish. I'll contact you as soon as I've caught the last one!

Scott and Samuel had waited days for this match and never imagined it would end like this. Had they waited for nothing? Yet the thought of seeing all three Regis battle Ethan soon made the extra delay seem worthwhile.

For Ethan, the journey had not been wasted. He had issued his challenge. However strong Brandon's other Pokemon were, they could not be as rare as the three Regis. Defeating all three together would mean much more to him. He was willing to wait for that chance.

They exchanged contact details. Ethan said nothing more and did not linger. He and May left the Battle Pyramid.

Scott and Samuel watched until the pair disappeared from sight.

He really just walked away... one of them said.

And he wants to fight all three Regis. He's certainly confident, said the other.

Even Brandon folded his arms and nodded. He is an interesting man.

...

From the Battle Pyramid, Ethan and May retraced their route toward Pewter City. After making the long trip here, neither had expected to leave without a battle. Still, waiting would make for a more exciting match.

After all, Ash had challenged Brandon three times in the animated story before earning his last Frontier Symbol. A little complication in Ethan's own journey was nothing to worry about.

Where do we go next? May asked.

The Grand Festival and the Battle Pyramid would both have to wait. Suddenly, they had no immediate destination.

Since we can't battle Brandon soon, let's change plans. We'll go to Indigo Plateau first and decide what to do from there. Johto isn't far away, so before the Grand Festival begins or Brandon catches Regice, I can take care of a few things there.

Johto... May nodded. She had no objection. As long as she had enough time to practice before the Grand Festival, it mattered little where she spent the intervening days.

Indigo Plateau was not far from Pewter City. Beyond the mountains northwest of town lay its broad expanse.

They returned to the city, ate a filling meal, replenished their travel supplies, and headed west into the rising and falling mountains.

They did not hurry. After several days of travel, they reached Indigo Plateau. They spent more than another day crossing it before finally arriving at the city where the Grand Festival would be held.

From high ground, Ethan looked down at the familiar city and felt a surge of memories. This was where he had won his first regional League title. After so much time, he had come back again.

This time, though, he was not here to claim another trophy. He had come as May's companion for the Grand Festival.

The Grand Festival and the Pokemon League Conference were held in the same city. They even shared many facilities and buildings. Only their main venues and dates differed.

It's so big and beautiful! May said, her excitement growing as she thought of the competition ahead. Ethan, is this where you won the Indigo League?

It is. This was the first step toward my dream. Ethan was moved too, though he found himself recalling all the little things that had happened during his earlier visit.

They stood there for a while, then gathered themselves and descended into the city.

The Grand Festival was still more than ten days away. There was no special atmosphere in the streets yet. Apart from the residents, Ethan and May did not see a single Coordinator.

But they had not come to stay. Ethan accompanied May to the registration office so she could sign up early. Then they left the city and continued west.

Johto lay ahead. Ethan had at least four things he needed to do there. Most important of all was a trip to the Charicific Valley, where he would watch his Charizard challenge for the summit.

Chapter 865: Challenging the Summit!

The Charicific Valley lay between Violet City and Azalea Town. Ethan had been there before, so he knew the way.

This time, though, they knew the date of the Grand Festival, and the journey was long. Ethan still had other business in Johto, and May needed enough time to train. They could not spend too many days on the road. After discussing it, they decided to ride Dragonite and reach the valley as quickly as possible.

Travel felt different the moment they climbed onto Dragonite. It spread its wings and carried them off the ground.

White clouds and blue sky stretched above them; mountains and forests passed below. The air was cold enough that May, sitting behind Ethan, instinctively leaned closer to him.

Compared with their usual journeys on foot, this was simply a way to cover distance. They could not take in nature at close range or meet new people and encounter unexpected things. Speed was its only practical advantage.

Still, soaring above the land gave them another kind of pleasure. From up here, they could take in sky and earth at a glance. Mountain ranges that seemed impossible to cross on foot slipped swiftly beneath them.

Hours in the air grew monotonous, and the cold wind made conversation difficult. Fortunately, after flying for most of the day, they reached the Charicific Valley before sunset.

Beyond several mountains, Ethan recognized the Charizard-shaped peak and the long river lined with Charizard statues.

Without needing a direction, Dragonite descended and followed the river upstream.

Ethan could not quite name how he felt about returning. But knowing his Charizard was close filled him with anticipation.

Behind him, Dragonite had slowed and the wind was no longer so fierce. May finally had a chance to speak. She looked around in surprise.

So this is the Charicific Valley? It's magnificent. Ethan, who put all those Charizard statues in the river? And that mountain aheadwas it carved into the shape of a Charizard, or did it form naturally?

You'll have to ask the woman who lives here. I think she'd be happy to answer.

Dragonite carried them to the great doorway in the Charizard-shaped mountain. It did not land there. Instead, it flew straight over the entrance and came down in the valley beyond.

The doorway was for first-time visitors and Trainers who had wandered here by accident. Ethan was an old acquaintance; he could simply fly over the mountain.

Beyond it lay the Charicific Valley itself. May finally saw what the place was really like.

Nearly a hundred Charizard were scattered among the rocky slopes. Some ate Berries, others rested, and many more gathered in pairs to play and spar. Orange figures stood out everywhere she looked.

There are so many Charizard...

Dragonite's arrival caught their attention. In an instant, every Charizard turned toward the newcomers. Liza, who managed the valley from a nearby cottage, noticed them too.

She came out with her female Charizard, Charla, and waved to Ethan. You finally made it!

Ethan was about to answer when an orange blur crossed his vision. A moment later, a tall, powerful Charizard stood beside him.

Time had passed. Its body had changed, and so had something in the way it carried itself. Ethan recognized his Charizard immediately.

Charizard!

He threw his arms around it, and Charizard hugged him so hard it lifted him off the ground. Both of them were overjoyed to be together again.

When Charizard set him down, Ethan stepped back and looked it over from head to toe. You've grown stronger. Your eyes are sharper too. You've really come a long way!

Charizard bared its teeth in a grin.

Liza had reached them by then. You're a few days later than I expected, but you aren't too late. She looked at May. And who is this?

May smiled openly. I'm May. I'm traveling with Ethan now.

Liza did not ask where Erika, who had accompanied Ethan on his last visit, had gone. She merely gave him a knowing look. Evidently she had taken May for his new girlfriend. He's quite the flirt, isn't he?

After they exchanged greetings, Liza invited them into her cottage.

The wooden floor creaked beneath their feet. Water was heating over the fireplace. Once Ethan and May had settled at a small table, Liza brought them a pot of steaming tea.

Ethan's Charizard and Charla came inside too. They were too large to sit at the table and settled on the open floor before the fireplace.

Ethan happened to glance their way. Charla kept casting flirtatious looks at his Charizard and teasing it with her tail. His Charizard sat aloof, barely acknowledging her.

Well, now. His Charizard had not only grown stronger here. It had won a female Charizard's heart. He wondered whether Liza had noticed.

Liza set several plates of snacks in front of them. You made it today, but it's getting late. Why not stay the night? Tomorrow morning your Charizard can challenge the strongest one in the valley.

Ethan looked at his Charizard. It was already watching him. He turned back to Liza and nodded. We'd be glad to stay.

Of course! Liza waved away his formality. I bought plenty of ingredients today. I'll cook you something so good you'll jump out of your seats! It's rare that I get visitors, and I want to hear all about your adventures outside the valley.

They drank tea, ate snacks, and talked beside the crackling fire. Ethan and May shared amusing stories from their travels, while Liza told them what Ethan's Charizard had been doing in the valley.

Liza was lively, cheerful, and easy to talk to. Their conversation went on until the windows had gone black with night. Only then did they realize how late it was.

Oh! Is it that late? Give me a moment and I'll make dinner.

She declined their offers to help, tied on an apron, and went into the kitchen. Before long, a tempting smell drifted out, along with the sounds of something simmering.

Dinner would take a while. Ethan finally had time to speak with his Charizard. Words alone could not tell him how much it had grown, though. After a few moments, he asked May to stay inside and went out into the darkness with Charizard.

May did not ask what they were going to do. She had a good idea. Ethan would have Charizard demonstrate its skills so he could judge its progress himself.

She began talking to Charla, only to watch the female Charizard follow them outside too.

So much for company. May spent a while alone in the cottage, then let out her Combusken and Eevee to keep her entertained.

That was the scene Liza found when she carried a pot of soup out of the kitchen. She set it on the table. Hm? Where are Ethan and the Charizard?

They went out for something. They'll be back soon.

Out? As a Trainer herself, Liza could guess why Ethan had taken his Charizard outside. She said no more, though she wondered why Charla had followed them.

At that moment the door opened. Ethan came back in with both Charizard.

Oh, am I the last one? He laughed when he saw May helping Liza set the table. Looks like I got back at just the right time.

May and Liza could see the pleased smile on his face. He was clearly satisfied with Charizard's growth.

After washing his hands, Ethan let his other Pokemon out, and everyone ate dinner together.

Liza had not exaggerated her skill as a cook. The meal was simple, with a pot of hearty seasonal soup as its main dish, but making such an ordinary dish taste this good showed real talent. Ethan and May praised it freely. They did not quite jump out of their seats, but May went back for enough extra helpings that her stomach rounded a little.

...

They spent the night at Liza's cottage. After washing up and eating breakfast the next morning, they headed toward the deepest part of the valley.

Many wild Charizard lived here, but they had their own territories. The broad clearing beyond the entrance belonged to them all and served as their main gathering place. Other parts of the valley were restricted, and not every Charizard could venture into them.

The strongest Charizard lived in one of those places. It had claimed the valley's highest and most comfortable spot. Today, Ethan's Charizard meant to take both its position and its title.

Perhaps Ethan and May's arrival had told the others what was coming. Perhaps the Charizard had expected this challenge for some time. As the group and its two Charizard walked deeper into the valley, Charizard streamed out from all sides and followed.

Everyone seemed to know that something important was about to happen. Tension filled the air. May had no part in the battle and would only watch, yet the mood made her nervous too.

They crossed the wide valley, climbed a small hill, and went up a long flight of steps to its highest point.

There, an enormous, exceptionally powerful Charizard reclined with its eyes almost closed, as though half asleep. Its bearing alone marked it as the valley's strongest.

Is that the one? May whispered, as if afraid to wake it. It doesn't look easy to beat.

Did I ever say my Charizard would be easy to beat? Ethan smiled. We won't know which one is stronger until they fight.

The wild Charizard were already forming a ring around them. Low growls rose from the crowd. They were excited, but restrained; none stepped forward. They all understood the importance of this challenge.

One Charizard among them caught Ethan's eye. It was no larger or smaller than the others, but while they were eager, it stayed half hidden in the crowd. It watched Ethan's Charizard with envy and frustration.

Ethan turned to Liza. That's Ash's Charizard, isn't it? He sounded certain despite phrasing it as a question.

Liza followed his gaze. Yes, that's Ash's. It's fiercely competitive. Seeing yours challenge for the top first must be hard for it.

Before Ethan could reply, she added, One more thing. This is a matter of Charizard honor. No one else may interfere in the battlenot even a Trainer.

Her meaning was clear. The two Pokemon would decide the outcome by their own strength and skill.

Ethan had not intended to interfere anyway. He had come to witness this moment with his own eyes.

Chapter 866: Who Will Be King of the Charizard?

The strongest Charizard in the Charicific Valley slowly opened its eyes.

It rose to its full, imposing height. Only then did Ethan see several large scars across its chest. They were marks of past battles, proof of how many formidable opponents it had faced and defeated.

When its gaze settled on Ethan's Charizard, a fierce pressure seemed to burst from it. No one became the valley's strongest without earning the title.

Ethan's Charizard did not retreat under that threatening stare. It stepped forward and returned the look just as fiercely. Its own presence grew steadily stronger until it matched the wild Charizard's.

They stood face-to-face, neither intimidated, neither willing to yield. A tense, combative hush fell over the platform.

It's been a long time since I felt an atmosphere like this, Liza said with a smile. They look evenly matched.

Ethan looked at his Charizard instead of answering her. Go on. I'll be here to see you win!

Charizard nodded and strode toward the valley's champion.

The two stopped opposite each other, ready to fight. Ethan, Liza, and May stepped back to give them room. Even Gengar floated out of Ethan's shadow, folded its arms, and settled in to watch.

All around them, the watching Charizard fell silent.

The two opponents said something to each other. Gengar translated for the people beside it.

Just insults. You're no match for me, I'll beat you, that sort of thing. Your Charizard isn't very clever, if you ask me. I'd swear at the other one until it got angry enough to lose its head. Then winning would be easy!
