Ethan gave Gengar a sidelong look. Just watch quietly.

A light breeze lifted a leaf from the ground. At that instant, both Charizard moved.

The valley's champion spread its wings and shot into the sky. It ruled this place, and it preferred to fight from above. Like a lord looking down on a challenger, it could use its aerial skill to defeat opponents.

Challengers usually had no choice but to follow. That gave the champion room to exploit its greater speed, pull ahead, and seize the initiative.

This challenger, however, was different. A Pokemon trained under a human had learned a more systematic way to fight.

Instead of rising after its opponent and falling into its rhythm, Ethan's Charizard breathed fire. A huge fireball roared toward the path the wild Charizard was about to take.

Fire was not especially effective against another Fire-type Pokemon. Everyone knew that. But a direct hit was not the point.

Climbing with its head raised, the wild Charizard did not notice the fireball at first. Its keen senses and agility saved it at the last moment: it tilted aside and easily avoided the attack. At their level, a long-range strike was unlikely to land cleanly.

Boom.

The fireball exploded beside it. The blast missed its body, but thick smoke spread out and swallowed it, hiding its view.

When the wild Charizard burst through the smoke into the open air, Ethan's Charizard had vanished. It looked around in surprise.

Ethan's Charizard shot out of the haze and slammed headfirst into the wild one's lower belly before it could react.

Yes! Gengar shouted.

Beautiful! May cried at the same moment.

From below, they had seen the whole move. Ethan's Charizard had followed its fireball upward, using the burst of flame and smoke to mask its approach.

No Trainer was giving it commands, but tactics learned through training had become part of the way it fought. That was the difference between it and a wild Pokemon. It had gained the advantage in their first exchange.

The unexpected hit told the valley's champion that this challenger was dangerous. Its usual way of defeating opponents had failed.

With a roar, it righted itself in the air and charged at Ethan's Charizard.

The champion was fast. A few beats of its wings brought it close enough to grapple in midair, and its powerful body gave it the advantage in a contest of strength. Its flames were surely formidable too, though it had yet to show them.

In raw speed, power, and physique, the larger wild Charizard surpassed Ethan's. But those advantages only went so far. It lacked the same refinement of technique.

Ethan's Charizard met it with the structured methods and varied experience of a trained battler.

They fought in the air, beating at each other with wings and claws. Dragon-type energy and flames flashed between them.

Then Ethan's Charizard caught an opening. It seized the wild Charizard from behind, locked its arms around it, and drove it toward the ground with Seismic Toss.

The wild Charizard struggled, but its strength did not exceed Ethan's by enough to break free in time.

Before the watching crowd, it struck the earth with a thunderous crash. Most of its body plunged into the soil, leaving a great crater in the platform.

Ethan's Charizard flapped away and landed nearby. It had hurt its opponent twice, but the fight had not been as easy as it looked. Making those openings and keeping up the intense aerial struggle had cost it energy. Its chest rose and fell with heavy breaths.

Dust from the impact hid the wild Charizard from view.

May watched the cloud, but nothing emerged. That looked painful. Could the throw have beaten it?

Not so easily, Ethan said. If that were enough, it wouldn't be the strongest Charizard here.

As if to prove him right, a large shape appeared within the dust. Its eyes glowed red as it walked steadily toward them.

When it stepped clear, May gasped. What? It doesn't even have a scratch?

It's smart. Ethan narrowed his eyes. Just before it hit, it used Dragon Breath against the ground. It broke up the hard surface and softened the impact, even though it couldn't escape the hold.

So all that effort was for nothing? May asked.

Not quite, Liza said. It reduced the damage; it didn't avoid it. It fell from a great height. Look closely beneath its old scars. Do you see the new scrapes?

May studied the Charizard again. Faint abrasions did mark its body. She had missed them among the older scars. Ethan's Charizard had achieved something after all.

The wild Charizard roared and sprang forward, flying low over the ground as it drove straight at its challenger.

Ethan had seen enough by now to understand how it fought. It relied on its formidable body and the most direct kind of attack. That could overwhelm an ordinary Trainer's Pokemon. Against his Charizard, it was less certain.

His Charizard exhaled black smoke. A thick Smokescreen covered it just as the wild one rushed inside.

Both disappeared from sight. Flashes of flame pierced the smoke, and Charizard cries rose from withinsome furious, some pained. Their voices were too similar for anyone outside to tell which one had the upper hand.

As the smoke thinned, the two Charizard came back into view. Both were breathing hard, standing about three meters apart and watching each other.

Another draw. By every means available, Ethan's Charizard had checked the superior close-range fighter and kept the contest even.

Liza watched with open admiration. Your Charizard is remarkable. I haven't seen one push our strongest this hard in a long time.

She was right about the valley's champion. Outside this place, it would be far stronger than even Lance's Charizard. To Ethan, its sheer physical strength nearly rivaled the Charizard of Leon, Galar's strongest Champion.

Now Ethan understood why Ash's Charizard had remained here so long after Ash declared it would become the strongest. With an opponent like this guarding the top, it was no wonder Ash's Charizard had yet to claim that place.

Today, though, Ethan believed the title would change hands.

Go on, Charizard. Show it what you can do!

Ethan did not speak aloud, but his Charizard seemed to feel his fighting spirit. An even fiercer presence burst from it.

Strangely, Ethan felt something in return. He seemed to sense Charizard's blood, its lungs, the fire in its eyes, every breath it took.

And with that came its fierce desire to defeat the opponent before it. The bond between them felt closer than ever.

Before Ethan could think further, his Charizard abandoned the tactics and careful technique it had used until now. It flew straight toward the wild Charizard and initiated a close-range fight.

The champion did not know why its challenger had grown still more determined. But a direct clash suited it perfectly, and it flew to meet the attack.

Now the struggle for the valley's honor truly began.

Claws struck flesh. Fists hit bodies. The two traded savage blows without holding back. Neither was trying to take the other's life, but every strike showed the ruthless force of a primal fight.

May had never seen Pokemon battle this way. She had imagined battles as an exchange of named moves and counters. This looked brutal.

The sight shook her ten-year-old understanding of the world. Pokemon did not always live peacefully with one another. This world, too, had its struggles between the strong and the weak.

Even so, she frowned and kept watching closely. This was the most important battle of Ethan's Charizard's life so far. She also knew she could learn something from the two Pokemon before her.

Chapter 867: Entei Again!

The two Charizard grappled on the ground, surged into the sky, and crashed back down. They smashed several Charizard statues and wrecked most of the rocks and trees on the platform. Even the watching Charizard retreated to avoid being caught in the fight.

It had become that fierce.

The opponents were tangled together and moving too quickly for anyone to tell which was which, let alone who had the advantage. However long the struggle continued, it would eventually have a winner.

One Charizard suddenly whipped its tail around. With a sharp crack, the other flew backward and struck a boulder.

Before the fallen Charizard could rise, its opponent swooped down and planted a foot hard on its stomach.

Raargh!

The Charizard on the ground cried out. It could endure no more. Its eyes rolled back, and it lost consciousness.

ROAR!

The standing Charizard threw back its head and bellowed toward the sky, announcing its victory to the whole valley. It looked every bit a conqueror.

Only now could the spectators see who had won. As Ethan had hoped, it was his Charizard.

Yes! It won! May cheered. Gengar let out a long whistle.

Both crowded around Ethan with smiling faces and congratulations. He nodded to them, then looked at Charizard.

That wasn't easy.

Fresh wounds stood out on its body. It had worked hard for this victory. Yet without a Trainer directing the fight, it had defeated the valley's strongest Charizard by its own strength. Ethan could see how far it had grown.

Well done. He met Charizard's eyes and smiled with pride.

At once the wild Charizard around them raised their heads and roared in chorus. Their cries seemed both a celebration and a proclamation that a new king had been born. The sound echoed throughout the Charicific Valley.

In the crowd, Ash's Charizard cast one envious look at Ethan's. It clenched its claws, turned with renewed determination, and walked away.

It was proud and ambitious too. How could it be content to watch another Charizard reach the top first? There was nothing it could do about today's result, but it could turn its envy and frustration into a reason to train harder.

After accepting the crowd's cheers, Ethan's Charizard walked over and stopped before its Trainer. May hurriedly took a healing spray from her bag and treated its wounds.

Neither Ethan nor Charizard cared much about ruling the valley. Charizard was not going to stay. But defeating the valley's strongest had been the proof it needed that it was ready to leave.

With its departure, Ethan would gain another exceptionally powerful partner alongside his red Gyarados.

Liza approached, applauding. Congratulations! You really did it!

As the valley's caretaker, she had watched Ethan's Charizard grow throughout its time here. She was delighted by the result.

I suppose you'll be off on new adventures together. Heretake this as a gift to celebrate the win. She drew a blue-green stone from her clothes and offered it to Ethan.

He had never seen this particular stone in person, but recognized it immediately. It was a Mega Stone: Charizardite X. He had not expected Liza to own one, much less give it to him.

When he did not reach for it, she smiled. Take it. I happened to find it while traveling in another region. I hear it lets a Charizard evolve further into a new form.

Ethan raised his eyebrows. It's so valuable. Why don't you keep it?

I'm not trying to become the strongest Trainer. And living out here, I have no use for it. It will do far more good in your hands than mine.

Then thank you. Ethan accepted the Charizardite X.

Earlier, in the Dragon Holy Land, he had received Charizardite Y from Clair's Dragon Tamers. Now, unexpectedly, he owned both of Charizard's Mega Stones.

He could choose between its X and Y forms whenever the time came. Whichever form he wanted, he would have the stone for it. That was a thrilling thought.

Thinking of transformation reminded Ethan of the strange feeling he had experienced during the battle.

Could it have been a sign of something like the Bond Phenomenon?

If so, perhaps his Charizard might gain a third form, one belonging to Ethan alonean Ethan Charizard alongside Mega Charizard X and Y. He found himself looking forward to the possibility.

He would have to study that feeling when he had time. If a bond transformation was possible, he wanted to discover how to bring it about.

Now it was time to say goodbye.

Despite its long stay, Charizard had made no friends in the valley. It had devoted itself entirely to training. Nothing held it here, and there was no one it needed to visit before leaving.

Only Charla watched its departure with obvious reluctance. Her pleading looks went unanswered by Ethan's Charizard.

It cared more about growing stronger than romance, much like its Trainer. It could not read Charla's feelings at all.

Well, a heart free of distractions made for a faster blade. On the other hand, if it had noticed her interest at any point during its long stay, there might have been a whole brood of little Charmander by now.

Ethan thanked Liza again for looking after Charizard. He and May waved goodbye, climbed onto Charizard's back, and flew away.

...

Charizard's trial was over, and it had returned to Ethan's team. The change made his roster much stronger.

He had little reason to send it into an ordinary Gym match or a tournament round against lesser opponents. In the wild, though, when he faced Legendary Pokemon or a dangerous organization, he now had another powerful card to play.

Ethan expected to save that card for some major battle in the future. Instead, he found a suitable opportunity soon after leaving the Charicific Valley.

Their next destination was Ecruteak City. Ethan wanted to take his Eevee back to visit the Kimono Sisters and talk with them about how it might evolve.

Before that, he also meant to visit the Whirl Islands. Sea Priestess Maya was there, and he had shared an intimate night with her. Now that he was back in Johto and not too far away, failing to see her would feel callous.

He could swear he was not going merely because he wanted her body. All right, that was part of itbut only a little. More than anything, he did not want to be a man who forgot someone after what they had shared. He owed her consideration.

Charizard carried them over the mountains and soon beyond the valley's borders. They flew west for most of the day.

As they neared Goldenrod City, Charizard sensed something unusual in a dry valley below. It slowed suddenly and dropped lower. Ethan looked around, puzzled, until Charizard shifted a wing to direct his attention to one spot.

There he saw a familiar shape.

It was a large, four-legged Pokemon more than two meters tall, with orange-red fur and a powerful body. Red, six-pointed markings spread over its cheeks, a golden three-lobed crest rose from its brow, and a pale trail of smoke drifted behind its back.

What's that Pokemon? May asked. It looks so cool!

Cool? Ethan gave a sharp snort. Of course it does. That's Entei, one of Johto's famous Legendary Pokemon.

There was no mistake. The figure Charizard had spotted was Entei.

It lay resting beside a hot spring in the valley, unaware that anyone had found it. Ethan could not let this chance pass.

He did not yet know whether this was the same Entei he had met before. But he had Raikou and Suicune, and missing the last of the three Legendary beasts had long bothered him. This time he would not let anythingor anyoneinterrupt his attempt.

Behind him, May stared in shock. That's Entei? She had never expected to come across a Legendary Pokemon here. She reached for her Pokedex to learn more.

Before she could use it, Charizard abruptly dived straight toward Entei.

Is Ethan going to catch it? May wondered. He seemed to have made up his mind as soon as he saw it. He had not even said a word, yet Charizard was already carrying them down.

Did they understand each other that well? Or had Ethan clashed with Entei before? The way he had recognized it immediatelyand the edge in his voicemade May suspect the latter.

Below them, Entei's eyes snapped open. It looked up and saw Charizard dropping from the sky. It stood at once, gathering itself to face the intruder.

Then its gaze shifted to the humans riding on Charizard's back. Recognition struck. Without another moment's hesitation, Entei turned and ran.

That told Ethan everything. It really is you!

Another Entei might have stood its ground when someone entered its valley. This one had fought Ethan before and lost. It knew what he could do, and its immediate flight had given it away.

It looked nothing like the majestic Entei of legend. Trainers who had grown up admiring tales of it would be stunned to see it fleeing like this.

But escape would not be so easy. Charizard landed, and Ethan slid from its back. He helped May down, then pointed after Entei. Charizard shot away like an arrow.

It had taken part in the last battle against this Entei. Loyal to Ethan, it understood what finding the beast again meant. That was why it had recognized the familiar presence during the flight and descended on its own.

Trainer and Pokemon wanted the same thing: having found Entei, they would not let it slip away.

Charizard accelerated and soon closed the gap. Entei weaved between great rocks and through the valley's uneven terrain, trying to shake its pursuer. Charizard had too much experience to fall for such simple evasions.

From above, it could see farther and fly a more direct course. No matter how sharply Entei turned, the distance between them continued to shrink.

Perhaps Entei realized it could not get away. As if preparing to leap forward again, it suddenly twisted back and lunged at Charizard with its jaws open.

Charizard had been ready for a counterattack. The moment Entei turned, it folded its wings and dropped lower, slipping easily beneath the bite.

Chapter 868: Mega Charizard X!

Charizard and Entei were locked in battle.

A few dozen seconds later, Ethan arrived with May, who was breathing hard from the run. Seeing that Charizard had caught Entei, Ethan wasted no time. He drew several Poke Balls and released more of his partners.

Gardevoir, Dragonite, Tyranitar, and Scizor appeared in flashes of blue light. At his direction, they spread out to surround Entei from several sides and block its escape.

Ethan did not intend for them to join the fight. Their job was to stand guard.

He turned his attention back to Charizard and Entei.

May caught her breath. Ethan, are you trying to catch this Entei?

Yes. I met it while traveling through Johto before, but it got away. This time, I'm catching it no matter what.

With Charizard?

Of course. Ethan smiled. Charizard has just finished training at the valley. Its first match back should be against an evenly matched opponent, and Entei fits perfectly.

But... May hesitated. It just fought the strongest Charizard in the valley. I treated its wounds, but it hasn't recovered its energy. Then it carried us for hours, while Entei was resting here. Can it really win like this?

Don't worry. Ethan took out the Charizardite X Liza had given him and a Mega Ring set with his Meteorite Key Stone. He held them up and smiled at her. If Charizard gets stronger, its fatigue won't stop it.

May remembered Liza saying the strange stone could make Charizard evolve into a more powerful form. So that was Ethan's plan. She did not know how he would bring about such a change, but he looked certain of himself.

She said nothing more. Instead, she stepped aside and scanned Entei with her Pokedex. Its entry taught her a little about the Legendary Pokemon, but she was even more eager to see the new form Ethan and Liza had mentioned.

In the valley, Charizard and Entei continued to fight. Within minutes, they had torn up the ground around them.

Entei remembered how dangerous Ethan was. Trapped and fighting for a way out, it held nothing back. As it drew upon its power, Ethan and May felt the temperature rise steadily. The air itself seemed to smell of flame.

The sky darkened. Thick clouds gathered over the valley in moments. Legendary Pokemon seemed to bring changes to the heavens whenever Ethan fought them.

Under Entei's full assault, Charizard began to give ground.

Its strength had grown by leaps and bounds in the Charicific Valley. It could face Entei alone. But May was right: after its battle with the valley's strongest Charizard and the long flight here, it was exhausted. It did not have the energy to win a prolonged fight as it was.

Ethan whistled for it to return.

Charizard beat its wings, broke away from Entei, and leaped backward. It floated a few meters before landing firmly beside Ethan.

Even after their short exchange, sweat showed on its body. Entei, by contrast, still looked full of energy.

Neither Pokemon had taken an obvious wound. Their power was close enough that the mismatch was one of stamina, at least for now.

Ethan went to Charizard and tied Charizardite X around its neck. Then he fastened the Mega Ring around his own wrist.

He took his time, treating each step with care. Entei watched from a distance. Instinct told it this was bad news, even if it had no idea what the human was doing.

Entei wanted to run. The Pokemon stationed on every side made it hesitate. They had not fought it yet, but each one felt dangerous.

Once the stone and ring were in place, Ethan and Charizard looked toward Entei together.

Go on! Show it what you can do. Let it feel your new power! Ethan shouted the last words.

He tapped the Key Stone on his Mega Ring twice. The Key Stone and Charizard's Mega Stone lit up together, scattering rainbow-colored light.

May and Entei stared as the flame at the tip of Charizard's tail changed from orange to blue.

A wave of air burst from Charizard as its body transformed. Its orange skin turned black and its wings dark blue. The underside from its jaw to the tip of its tail became sky blue. Blue clawlike points grew from its shoulders, two finlike spikes appeared behind its neck, and the tips of its horns sharpened and turned blue.

Its shape had not changed beyond recognition, but the colors, fierce eyes, and two streams of blue flame spilling from its mouth made it look magnificent and intimidating.

ROAR!

In its new form, Charizard bellowed at Entei. The sound rang through the whole valley, and even the clouds overhead seemed to part before it.

Mega Charizard had arrived.

Even Gengar came out to stare. May's eyes widened at the fierce, striking form. This...this is what Charizard becomes?

Yes. Ethan smiled. Mega Charizard X.

Charizard took a moment to grow accustomed to its transformed body. Then it spread its wings and charged before Entei could collect itself.

Entei did not want to fight such a formidable-looking opponent, but it had no way out. It braced itself.

The gap between them vanished. Entei had been on guard, yet the newly empowered Charizard still found an opening.

Other Trainers' Mega Charizard were powerful enough. Ethan's Charizard had already undergone an enormous improvement before Mega Evolving. In this form, its strength was frightening.

Entei had expected a change, but it had underestimated how much stronger Charizard would become. From their first exchange it felt pressure on every front. Mega Evolution had narrowed, perhaps even erased, the advantage of a Legendary Pokemon.

Charizard's type had changed from Fire and Flying to Fire and Dragon as well, making its close-range attacks still more threatening.

The two grappled again. From above, Charizard repeatedly struck with Dragon Claw, Dragon Tail, and Dragon Breath, pressing its advantage.

Entei was solely Fire-type. Its flames did reduced damage to Charizard, limiting its options. It still had some general-purpose Normal-type and Dark-type moves, so it was not helpless.

Charizard swept a claw wreathed in draconic flame toward it. Entei ducked beneath the strike and sprang up to bite Charizard's belly. Charizard twisted aside, dodging in turn, and the fight continued.

When Entei tried to evade again, Charizard's tail struck its body and sent it stumbling back several steps.

Entei steadied its breathing and studied its opponent warily. It was one of Ho-Oh's guardians, a Legendary Pokemon. When had a battle last forced it into such an undignified position?

And it was facing an ordinary Pokemon, not another Legendary one. Entei had never expected to be pushed so hard.

But it would not simply surrender. With a roar, it summoned every reserve of strength and lunged again. It fought as if drawing on one hundred and twenty percent of its power.

At the height of that surge, Entei unleashed its strongest counterattack. A thick, dazzling column of energy shot from its mouth toward Charizard flying low overhead.

This did not look like any conventional named move. It was neither an ordinary Normal-type nor Fire-type attack. It resembled the raw instinctive power that Rayquaza or Deoxys might use. Entei had truly been driven into a corner.

Charizard refused to give way. It raised both claws. Blue flames flared from its mouth and tail, then ignited around its hands. Instead of retreating, it charged straight at the beam.

At the point of impact, Charizard swung its claws. It stopped the column of energy head-on. With another slash, it shattered the attack.

Ethan watched without changing expression. His strategy had been simple: give Charizard enough strength to overcome the disadvantage of its fatigue.

It was working. Charizard had Entei on the defensive.

That did not make Entei weak. Its strength as a Legendary Pokemon was plain to see. Mega Evolution had simply made Ethan's Charizard stronger still.

Ethan thought back to the start of his journey. He had grown into a Trainer who could face a Legendary Pokemon with a partner that was not one itself. Time had passed quickly.

On the field, Charizard beat its wings and surged forward through the fading remnants of the beam.

Entei was still releasing energy. By the time it saw Charizard coming, it could not dodge. Two slashes knocked it to the ground. Before it could rise, a scorching Dragon Breath struck it.

Now's your chance! May cried.

Ethan knew it too. The battle had reached its turning point. He pulled a Great Ball from his pouch and threw it toward Entei.

The ball arced through the air and opened before it reached the fallen Pokemon. Red light streamed out and enveloped Entei.

Entei did not want to be captured, but Dragon Breath still blocked its vision and wracked its body. It failed to see the ball until the attack cleared and the red light had already closed around it.

It was too late to resist. Entei vanished into the Great Ball before it could even roar.

Click. The ball landed on the ground and began to shake violently.

Ethan, May, and all of his Pokemon watched it. Charizard watched too, but quietly gathered its strength. If Entei escaped, it would strike again before the beast could react.

The Great Ball gave it no chance.

Human technology could be unreliable at times, but sometimes it managed to do its job. With a soft click, the ball's light went dark and its shaking stopped.

After Raikou and Suicune, Ethan had now caught Entei. All three of Johto's Legendary beasts were finally his.

Chapter 869: It's Been a Long Time, Sea Priestess

With all three Legendary beasts in his care, Ethan's team had become far stronger. It was a surprise he could never have expected before coming back to Johto.

He was still looking at Entei's Great Ball when May hurried over, picked it up, and carried it to him as carefully as if it were a precious treasure.

Her caution was understandable. While traveling with Ash, she had glimpsed Legendary Pokemon a few times, but usually from a distance. Even when she met one, she had approached it warily. This was different. Ethan had caught Entei by his own strength, and now she was holding its Poke Ball in her hands.

Ethan smiled at her expression and remembered himself when he first caught Zapdos. He had probably looked much the same.

Beside them, a flash of light swept over Charizard. When it faded, Charizard had returned to its usual form. May watched in fascination.

I thought it would stay like that, she said, a little disappointed. Does it have to evolve all over again for every battle?

Yes. Ethan called his other Pokemon back from their positions around the valley. Mega Evolution isn't permanent. It makes a Pokemon stronger by temporarily bringing out hidden power, but it needs both a Key Stone and a Mega Stone. It can't maintain that form indefinitely. Knowing when to use it and when to let it end matters.

His Pokemon gathered around him and looked at the Great Ball in his hand. Gengar seemed about to say something, but it and Gardevoir turned toward the same part of the valley.

Human footsteps, Gengar said quietly. Coming this way fast.

That was hardly surprising. People traveled through all kinds of places, especially Trainers who liked exploring mountains and caves. Ethan had expected the chance of an interruption from the moment he decided to catch Entei. One reason for stationing Pokemon around the fight had been to keep strangers from interfering before the capture was over.

At least whoever this was had waited until Entei was safely caught.

Ethan recalled several of his Pokemon, put Entei's Great Ball in his pouch, and was about to leave with May on Charizard when two voices carried toward them.

Hurry! The battle sounds came from this direction. Those had to be two rare Pokemon!

But it's quiet now. What if they've already gone?

Then we'd better hurry even more!

Ethan paused. One of the voices sounded familiar. Had he met its owner before? He slowed his steps and waited.

The answer soon came around a great rock in the valley: a teenage boy and girl.

The girl was pretty, with pale blue hair tied into two long pigtails that curled upward at improbable angles. Her fitted top and shorts suited her bright, energetic bearing.

The boy wore a cap backward, a red sweatshirt, and yellow shorts. A lock of hair stuck defiantly through a gap in the cap.

They all recognized one another at once.

You two? Ethan said.

Mr. Vale? the pair exclaimed.

His memory caught up. Jimmy and Marina?

They were the two Trainers Ethan had met while traveling through Johto. They had shared an adventure and met again at the Silver Conference. They were hardly strangers.

It's us! Jimmy said excitedly. It's been ages. I never thought we'd run into you here!

Neither did I, Marina said. Mr. Vale, what brings you here?

Ethan shook his head. I was about to ask you the same thing. Why are you two in this valley?

The weather changed, and we heard a battle, Jimmy said. Of course we came to see what was happening.

He glanced around at the battered ground. Wait. Were you the one fighting here?

I was. Ethan gave an answer that was true, if incomplete. I found a fairly rare Pokemon and caught it.

Entei certainly qualified as fairly rare.

Oh... Jimmy's excitement visibly faded. He had clearly come hoping to find the battlers, only to discover that someone else had reached them first.

Where's your other friend? Ethan asked. The one from your hometown. His name was...?

Vincent? Marina laughed softly. He's traveling on his own somewhere else. You've met him plenty of times, Mr. Vale. How can you still forget his name?

It was strange. Ethan had met countless people on his journey, old friends and new faces alike. Yet the name of that round-faced boy never seemed to stay in his memory.

Jimmy and Marina turned their attention to May. And who is this?

I'm May, she said with an easy smile. I'm traveling with Ethan, and I'm a Coordinator.

A Coordinator? Jimmy instinctively looked at Marina.

What a coincidence, Marina said, smiling. I switched paths recently. I'm a Coordinator now too!

Really? May brightened. That is a coincidence.

Since becoming a Coordinator, May had met many others, from friendly rivals to people as spiteful as Harley. The more she spoke with fellow Coordinators, the more she learned. Meeting a friend of Ethan's made the conversation easier still.

With midday approaching, the four found a clean, open place nearby and sat on the rocks. Ethan and Jimmy prepared lunch while May and Marina talked about Contests.

May soon discovered that although Marina had entered the field only recently, she regularly placed first in the preliminary judging and had already won several Ribbons. She had striking insights into the stage and the Coordinator's craft as well.

It was astonishing. Marina looked about May's age, yet she already knew so much and performed so well.

Ethan noticed May's admiring look and smiled to himself as he worked on lunch. She could not know that Marina would one day win a Grand Festival and become one of Johto's leading Coordinators. Someone destined for that achievement naturally had her own way of seeing the art.

Once the food was ready, they spread out a picnic cloth and ate a hot, practical meal in the valley. It was not particularly tasty, but Ethan had done what he could. In the kitchen, his greatest success was cooking something thoroughly enough that no one would go hungry.

Marina raised her eyebrows a little at the first bite. Jimmy and May, on the other hand, ate with evident enjoyment.

Running into the pair had been a pleasant interruption. After lunch and a little more conversation, May and Marina exchanged contact details. Then the two groups said goodbye and continued toward their separate destinations.

Neither Ethan nor May mentioned meeting and catching Entei. They shared only a few stories from the road.

Once Jimmy and Marina had gone, Ethan and May climbed onto Charizard again and flew toward the Whirl Islands. They would have preferred to walk and explore, but the time before the Grand Festival was slipping away. Another unexpected delay might come at any point, so they needed to leave room for it.

Fortunately, the rest of the flight passed without incident. After many hours in the air, they sighted the Whirl Islands in the distance as night fell.

Ethan felt a trace of uncertainty, as he had when returning to Kanto. He had been away a long time and had not contacted Maya. What if her feelings toward him had changed? Would this trip have been for nothing?

Then he dismissed the thought. If he lacked even this much confidence in himself, that would be a poor showing. He held League titles from three regions and traveled with so many Legendary Pokemon. Surely he could face one conversation.

He gently pressed his feet against Charizard's sides. It accelerated toward Blue Point Isle, where Maya lived.

...

Night covered the sea. Thin clouds veiled the moon and softened its light.

At the Temple of the Sea on Blue Point Isle, Maya had finished her duties for the day. The beautiful, graceful Sea Priestess stood on the broad terrace outside her room, gazing west across the water.

Far beyond her sight, people said, lay the Hoenn mainland.

For some time she had come here every night before bed to look in that direction. She had never explained why, but her attendants knew what occupied her thoughts. Her Sea Hero was somewhere across the sea.

A cool wind swept over the terrace, and Maya drew her long dress closer around herself.

She had stood there long enough. As she turned toward her room, the clouds began to drift away from the moon. A black speck appeared against its light.

Maya stopped and looked up. Was it a bird Pokemon?

The speck grew larger as it approached. It was no bird. A dragonlike Pokemon was flying toward the temple, with someone apparently riding on its back. It seemed to be coming straight for her.

Her heartbeat quickened. She suspected who it might be, but the dim light kept her from seeing clearly.

A minute or two later, the approaching Pokemon entered the glow from her room. It was a Charizard. And the figure riding it was her Sea Hero.

Had the God of the Sea finally answered her prayers?

Maya's heart settled. She resumed the composed bearing of the priestess everyone knew.

Charizard's wings stirred the air as it landed on the terrace.

From its back, Ethan looked down at the beautiful woman before him. Without her scepter, some of the distance of her sacred office seemed to fall away. She looked simply like a woman, as she had that night.

He found the answer he hoped for in her eyes.

Ethan swung down onto the terrace and smiled. It's been a long time, Sea Priestess.

Maya smiled back. She was about to speak when another figurea young girlclimbed down from Charizard's back.

Chapter 870: Seeing Maya Again

An attendant led May to a lounge on her own.

May wanted to ask where Ethan was going and why they had been separated. Before she could, several more attendants arrived with plates of plump fruit and tempting desserts. Her attention went straight to the food.

Miss May, please rest here for a while. We're preparing a guest room for you. Once it's ready, you can take a bath and settle in for the night.

May nodded, then realized what the attendant had said. Oh! Yes...all right.

After the attendants left, she tried some fruit and then helped herself to a dessert. She ate contentedly for a while.

May loved snacks, but even the best food lost its hold on her after she had tasted it. Where had Ethan gone? Why hadn't he come back? Could something have happened to him?

Alone in an unfamiliar building among strangers, it was easy for a young girl to imagine trouble.

When they had landed on the terrace, Ethan had introduced May to the beautiful older woman. Then he and Maya had gone off together, leaving an attendant to bring May here. A long time had passed since then.

May looked outside. It was already past ten. Curious and worried, she set down what she was eating and slipped out of the lounge before the attendants returned.

A long corridor stretched outside. Whether because it was late or because this part of the temple was usually quiet, she saw no one. She could not even hear footsteps. Only the faint sound of waves reached her through the windows.

The silence in such a large building unsettled her.

Maya hasn't locked Ethan up, has she?

The priestess was beautiful and dignified. She had looked close to Ethan, much as Erika did, and May doubted she meant him harm. But Ethan had several women in his life. If Maya found out, she might be furious.

Could she already know? The thought made May increasingly uneasy.

She understood that Ethan's relationships could be seen as playing with several women's feelings. If they became public, he might at least be scolded and, at worst, lose his reputation. Maya was a Sea Priestess with standing and influence. An argument with her could be especially serious.

I should at least explain things for him.

May looked both ways, worked out the route back, and headed deeper into the Temple of the Sea.

The building's layout was complicated, perhaps to give it a solemn atmosphere. She nearly lost her way several times. The night was dark, and much of the corridor was lit by candles instead of electric lights. It made her uncomfortableand a little afraid.

She did not release a Pokemon. That might draw the attendants' attention. Gathering her courage, she went on alone.

For a temple this large, the lack of guards surprised her. It did allow her to reach Maya's room without being stopped.

May stood before the closed door. Beyond it was Maya's bedchamber and the terrace where they had landed. Ethan had gone inside and had not reappeared.

What were they doing? Was Maya reprimanding him? Were they getting along?

There were no windows on either side. May tried pushing the door. It would not open; it seemed to be bolted from within. She managed to shift it only enough to make a tiny gap.

Through that gap, she heard a woman making broken, unfamiliar sounds.

May recognized Maya's voice, but it sounded strangeat moments pained, at others impossible to place. It rose, sharpened, fell, and softened.

May had never heard sounds like that before. Even so, her face turned bright red.

Wh-what is that?

She had an inkling. The thought made her heart race and her mouth go dry. Almost without meaning to, she leaned toward the gap and opened her eyes wide.

Just as she put her eye to it, footsteps sounded from farther down the corridor.

May started and quickly stepped back. A few seconds later, the attendant from the lounge came into view.

The woman looked surprised to find May there. Her gaze flicked to the narrow gap in Maya's door.

Miss May, she said smoothly, what are you doing here? I was coming to find you.

May's ears burned. She wanted to sink through the floor. I... I was just feeling cooped up, so I went for a walk.

The attendant smiled. She clearly saw through the excuse, but did not say so.

Voices in the corridor seemed to reach the people inside the room. The sounds beyond the door stopped abruptly.

The attendant noticed too. She gestured down the corridor. Your room is ready, Miss May. Please come with me.

May could scarcely remember following her. Only when she stood in a bright, warm, comfortable guest room and heard the attendant say good night and close the door did she come back to herself. Her heart was still pounding.

...

May did not see Ethan again until the next morning.

She sat at a long table in a spacious dining hall, eating breakfast. When she happened to look up, Ethan was coming through a side door, looking thoroughly refreshed.

She opened her mouth to greet him, then thought better of it. She lowered her head and took a spoonful of porridge.

Ethan did not notice her embarrassment. But as he came closer, he saw the dark circles beneath her eyes. What's wrong? Didn't you sleep well?

May felt a rush of shame. Keeping her face as calm as she could, she gave a small nod. I guess I'm not used to the bed. I didn't fall asleep until dawn.

That was not the real reason. After what had happened the night before, she had bathed and lain awake for hours with one thought circling in her head.

She had glanced through the door only briefly, yet she had seen enough to know she should not have looked. In the moonlight, two figures had been on the bed. She could not see exactly what they were doing, but Ethan had been bare-skinned and above Maya.

The glimpse had shaken her. She had turned over in bed for ages and even had a strange dream when she finally slept.

She could tell Ethan none of that. It was something she meant to keep buried.

To stop him noticing her discomfort, she asked, Where's Maya? I haven't seen her.

Her cheeks warmed again. Did the question reveal that she knew Ethan and Maya had spent the night together? Fortunately, Ethan did not read that much into it.

She left just after dawn. There was an important ceremony she had to conduct. He sat down. Let's eat quickly. Afterward I'll show you some of the well-known places around here.

May's attention shifted. Once they finished breakfast, they left the temple and visited Inland City down the mountain. Then they went to the Whirl Stadium, where the Whirl Cup had been held.

See this place? Ethan said, pointing toward the battlefield. This is where I knocked out Ash and Misty and earned the title of Sea Hero.

Show-off.

May was glad he had brought her to see the island and its sights. Still, something puzzled her. They had been in such a hurry that they had flown here on Charizard. Why did he suddenly have time for a leisurely tour?

The answer arrived soon enough.

From the stadium they traveled to Bluefinland, a town on the other side of the island. Residents were streaming from every direction toward its square. May overheard their conversations: Sea Priestess Maya would hold a ceremony there today to bestow the God of the Sea's blessing.

Oh, so that's why we're sightseeing. Ethan had brought her along because he wanted to attend Maya's ceremony. May shook her head helplessly.

In the midst of the ceremony, Maya stood with her scepter in hand. She looked sacred and untouchable, carrying all the dignity of her office. The people around her praised her and bowed in reverence.

Yet May could not keep the image from the previous night out of her mind: Maya on the bed beneath Ethan.

Wonderful. Now I can't forget it. She sighed in frustration.

After the ceremony, Ethan and May met up with Maya and returned to the Temple of the Sea.

What happened next was even more trying for May. Ethan and Maya shut themselves in a room again and did not appear for the rest of the day. May ate dinner by herself.

At least she had her own Pokemon and Ethan's for company, so she was not lonely.

She next saw him at breakfast the following morning. This time, to her relief, Ethan was finally ready to leave with her. Otherwise, every night in bed might have brought back that glimpse through Maya's door.

Maya came to see them off in person. Ethan and May climbed onto Charizard and nodded goodbye. With a few beats of its wings, Charizard rose from the Temple of the Sea and flew into the sky.

It was fast. When May looked back, the temple was already far away. Even so, she had the distinct feeling that Maya was still standing there, watching them go.

...

Charizard carried them north from the Whirl Islands. Their next destination was Ecruteak City, where they would visit the Kimono Sisters.

Ethan's Eevee had spent an entire regional journey waiting to evolve. It was ready, but Ethan had not settled on a form for it. Perhaps talking with the five sisters in Ecruteak would help him finally make a choice.

Charizard's shadow skimmed over the sea. The sunshine seemed perfect for travel. Ethan and May both thought so at first.

Half an hour later, the weather changed. Wind rose, then strengthened. The clouds grew dark. An unbroken bank of storm clouds appeared on the horizon, lightning flashing within it, while the sea below turned rough.

A storm! Ethan called back to May.

She leaned around his arm to look ahead. Her brow tightened. Can we fly through it?

Ethan shook his head. Charizard could make it alone. We couldn't. Even if lightning missed us, the cold rain and wind would be too much.

The wind grew stronger. May had to shout for him to hear her. Then what do we do?

Chapter 871: Snowman Snorlax

Ethan scanned the sea below for an island where they could shelter from the storm.

They had flown too far from the Whirl Islands. Blue water stretched in every direction, with no land, island, or coral reef in sight. There was nowhere to hide from the storm, not even a place to land.

Ethan! Look over there!

May's sharp eyes had picked out a small dark speck on the sea beneath the storm.

Ethan looked closely. It was a little boat adrift on the water. It was not large, but it would be more than enough to keep off the wind and rainprovided it could withstand the storm without sinking.

He patted Charizard's neck. Understanding, Charizard descended toward the vessel.

It was only a little over ten meters long, with a single wheelhouse that looked flimsy against the sea.

As they drew nearer, Ethan saw it was neither a fishing boat nor a passenger or sightseeing vessel. Apart from a winch, the deck was empty, and a long antenna rose above the wheelhouse. It looked like a privately owned research boat.

Waves and strong winds rocked it, but for now it seemed secure.

Whatever kind of boat it was, it was their only choice. The storm was almost upon them. Ethan thought he could already smell rain in the wind.

Charizard dropped to wheelhouse height and flew just above the sea. Ethan turned to look inside.

A light was on. A red-haired woman was busy at the controls.

Rather than jump aboard and startle her, Ethan waved from Charizard's back.

Perhaps Charizard's orange form stood out over the water, or perhaps his wave caught her eye. Either way, the woman soon noticed him and May. She looked startled, then opened the door and hurried out.

Excuse me! Ethan raised his voice over the wind. Could we come aboard to shelter from the storm?

The small vessel might not be entirely safe, but it would at least spare them a soaking and keep them out of the lightning.

The woman did not hesitate. She waved them over. Hurry, get on!

With her permission, Ethan jumped onto the deck and helped May down after him. Once they were steady, he recalled Charizard into its Poke Ball.

The woman ushered them into the wheelhouse. Only then did Ethan get a good look at her.

She seemed to be twenty-five or twenty-six. Her long, fiery red hair was tied in a casual ponytail, and she had fair skin and a pretty face. Perhaps for comfort during long stretches at sea, she wore only a white tank top above the waist. It gave her a brisk, capable air.

As soon as she shut the door, the wind's roar softened. They could still feel the boat rocking, but at least they were out of the weather.

The woman returned to the controls. Without looking back, she asked, You two are Trainers, aren't you?

That's right. Thank you for letting us aboard. Otherwise we'd have had to face the storm out there. Ethan nodded, then he and May introduced themselves.

People ought to help one another when they're away from home. I'm sure anyone else would have done the same. She smiled. I'm Luka. You could call me a researcher of sorts.

Like the color of her hair, Luka had a warm, lively manner.

A researcher of sorts? May asked. Why only of sorts? What do you study, Miss Luka?

Steering toward the edge of the storm, Luka laughed. Just the Pokemon living around here. I don't have a doctorate or anything, so of sorts seems right.

There were many independent researchers like Luka. They had no official funding, titles, or positions. What they did have was a boundless love of Pokemon and the determination to devote themselves to studying them.

While they spoke, the storm reached them.

The world around the boat suddenly darkened. Rain poured down, enormous waves rolled past, and lightning flashed through the sky, briefly illuminating everything.

With the storm all around them, no one felt like talking. They fell silent and watched through the windows, their moods rising and falling with the waves.

Ethan was not worried for his own safety. He had received the sea's blessing, and he had so many Pokemon with him. What could a storm do to him? He simply did not want himself and May left drenched and miserable.

In fact, his presence aboard might protect Luka. If the boat capsized, he could help her. That was the worst case, though, and he hoped the vessel would come through intact.

Under Luka's hand, the little boat skirted the storm's center and headed for its edge, tossing like a leaf on the sea.

Her skill at the helm found them a comparatively safe route. It took considerable effort to navigate the wind and towering waves, but she brought them out without mishap.

Luka really was an old hand at the wheelno, a seasoned captain. It helped that she had altered course before the storm reached them. Without that head start, the passage would never have gone so smoothly.

At last the clouds parted and the sky above them cleared again.

There was one problem.

Ethan checked the map on his phone and shook his head. They had avoided the storm, but their course had shifted. He could no longer tell where they had drifted from the waters near the Whirl Islands.

Reaching Ecruteak City would take a longer route now.

While he studied the map, May suddenly cried out, Ethan! Lookan iceberg!

An iceberg? Before Ethan could answer, Luka shook her head. You must have seen something else. There have never been icebergs in these waters. It's too warm, and the climate isn't right for them. Waitthat really is an iceberg!

She had turned her head in the middle of her objection and seen it herself. Ethan looked up too.

A huge, uneven mass of ice was drifting slowly toward them. There was no mistaking it.

Incredible, Luka said. I've sailed these waters for years, and I've never seen an iceberg here.

Maybe the storm carried it in, Ethan suggested. He had no better explanation.

Then they noticed shapes moving across the ice.

They were too far away to make out clearly, but their silhouettes did not look human. They seemed to be large Pokemon. All three grew curious.

Should we go and see? May asked.

Luka answered by turning the wheel. The boat headed straight for the iceberg.

A few minutes later, they could see its whole shape. It was not one solid mountain of ice. Several smaller bergs were joined to a flat expanse, where groups of snow-white Snorlax were frolicking and playing.

Apart from their color, they appeared no different from ordinary Snorlax in size or any other feature. Against the ice, though, they were a remarkable sight.

White Snorlax? May exclaimed. Are they all Shiny Pokemon?

Luka hesitated, then shook her head. They certainly look different, but I thought Shiny Snorlax were blue. I've never heard of a white one, much less a whole group of them.

May turned to Ethan. Do you know what's going on?

He thought for a moment. I remember a legend from somewhere in Johto. They say that if you build a snowman on the coldest night of the year, it will come to life as a Snowman Snorlax.

May drew a sharp breath. Really? She looked back at the Snorlax. Their white bodies did resemble snowmen. So all of these used to be snowmen that came alive?

Silly. Ethan tapped her on the head. It's a folk tale. Surely you know that can't be true. These Snowman Snorlax are probably a group with an unusual coloration that people haven't fully studied yet.

May held her head and stuck out her tongue. I suppose so.

By then the boat had reached the iceberg. Luka cut the engine, went out on deck, and looped a rope around a protruding block of ice to secure the vessel.

When she was finished, the three of them climbed onto the ice. The Snowman Snorlax did not seem surprised by their arrival. They only watched the newcomers curiously.

Luka took out her camera and snapped more than a dozen photographs. Then she turned to Ethan and May. Sorry, you two. I'm going to stay here for quite a while and study these Snowman Snorlax. Feel free to go on without me.

For an independent Pokemon researcher, finding a place like this was an extraordinary chance. She intended to spend several days observing the Pokemon's behavior and habits in this nearly untouched refuge.

She did not mean to reveal its location, but she wanted to satisfy her own curiosity.

Seeing Luka prepare to make camp, Ethan and May thanked her again and headed off on their own. They had met by chance; now it was time to part.

They left the shore and walked toward the iceberg's interior. Snowman Snorlax were everywhere. Ethan estimated there were more than a hundred.

That alone was astonishing. Snorlax had enormous appetites; a whole small island might be needed to feed just one. The amount of food this many would eat in a day was almost beyond reckoning.

May, who had a Munchlax of her own, found it especially hard to believe.

Where are we going, Ethan?

Ethan took a Poke Ball from his belt pouch and smiled. Now that we've found Snowman Snorlax, I can't pass up the chance.

You're going to catch one?

Of course. I've always liked Snorlax, and these are especially rare. I've never even seen one before. How could I let the chance go?

Ethan had not expected two surprises so soon after returning to Johto. First Entei a few days ago, and now Snowman Snorlax. Both were unexpected discoveries.

May felt a little envious. A Snowman Snorlax...

Her own Munchlax was adorable, but these Pokemon were so rare. If she caught one, it would hardly need to perform in a Pokemon Contest. A few small movements onstage might be enough to earn high marks.

But she already had a Munchlax.

They walked slowly among the Snowman Snorlax while Ethan searched for one to catch.

He was not the Trainer who had just set out on his journey anymore. As one of the world's strongest Trainers, he no longer caught every Pokemon that interested him. With so many to choose from in a single group, he needed to consider his choice carefully.

He kept walking and looking until they reached an ice forest near the center of the berg. There he finally found a suitable one.

Beneath an ice tree sat a Snowman Snorlax larger and fatter than the others, steadily tossing white fruit into its mouth. From its bearing, if it was not the group's leader, it was at least a dominant Pokemon.

Chapter 872: Truly Strong

Ethan, what do you mean by a Totem Pokemon? May asked.

It's not a term people use around here, Ethan explained. It comes from the distant Alola region. It describes a Pokemon much larger than others of its speciesone you can tell is different at a glance.

I see. May nodded, then asked, Does that mean Totem Pokemon are especially strong?

Ethan shook his head, then nodded.

Apart from their size, people haven't found any difference in their anatomy or moves compared with ordinary Pokemon. In that sense, they're the same. But a larger body can also mean a stronger build and greater physical power. So they probably do have an advantage over others of their kind.

He was not entirely certain of that. Did they really have an advantage?

In the games, numbers determined strength, and Totem Pokemon had the same base stats as ordinary members of their species. But this was a real world. Surely a larger body would bring better physical capabilities.

Still, it was only a guess. He would have to catch one and observe it to know for sure.

Despite choosing his target, Ethan did not make a move. May watched him in puzzlement. He was hardly indecisive. Why was he hesitating now?

What are you thinking about? she asked.

Ethan sighed and gave her a wry smile. Snorlax already eat an enormous amount. If I catch a Totem Snorlax this big, how much food will it go through every day?

So that was it. May glanced back at the Snowman Snorlax.

It must eat more than an ordinary Snorlax, judging by its size. But don't forget my special Pokeblocks. Snorlax love them, and they provide lots of energy!

Even with Pokeblocks, Ethan was unsure how much it would take to feed that enormous body. He would have to find an expert to improve the recipe someday.

There was no point dwelling on it now. He looked up at the Totem Snowman Snorlax again.

Its body looked as though it were covered in snow. It hardly seemed possible that such a strange Snorlax was simply a Normal type. Ethan suspected it might have the Ice type too.

The Snorlax kept tossing white fruit into its mouth, apparently oblivious to the two intruders in front of it. Ethan threw the Poke Ball he was holding onto the ice before it.

Whatever its type, that would not matter against overwhelming strength.

A flash of blue light released his Gardevoir in front of the Snorlax. She had not had a proper battle in a long time. Ethan chose her both to make sure of the result and to let her stretch her abilities and keep her edge.

Gardevoir took a few slow steps forward. Elegant as her movements were, the power she radiated put the Snowman Snorlax on alert. It was impossible to ignore.

The Snorlax lowered its fruit and stared at her with a vacant expression.

Its face was smeared with fruit juice, and its eyes looked half asleep. For a Totem Pokemon, it had remarkably little dignity. One might have thought it had grown so large simply by sitting still and eating all day.

Ethan knew better than to underestimate it. Ash's Snorlax and May's Munchlax were both powerful. Plenty of Trainers had paid dearly for assuming that a lumbering-looking Pokemon could not fight.

Gardevoir approached until she stood before the Snorlax. It scratched its broad belly, then rose to its feet. It might not enjoy fighting, but it would not back down from someone who had come looking for a battle.

The other Snowman Snorlax in the distance seemed not to notice. Even if one of them had, it would likely have tilted its head, watched for a moment, and gone back to what it was doing. That was simply their nature.

Without a word from Ethan, Gardevoir attacked. She raised an arm, and a wave of psychic force surged from her palm toward the Snorlax.

It could not see the psychic power, but it clearly sensed something dangerous coming. With a sweep of its arm, it hurled a branch laden with fruit and snow into the air.

Whether by chance or design, the branch struck the incoming force. It burst apart, scattering snow, bits of fruit, and splinters. The falling debris briefly screened the two Pokemon from each other.

Then came a rapid, pounding rhythm of footsteps. The Snowman Snorlax was charging at Gardevoir!

Its feet moved so fast they almost blurred. In an instant it closed the distance, balled up a huge fist, and punched at her face.

For a species known for its slow pace, its speed was astonishing. It overturned every expectation.

Then Ethan remembered the Snorlax Ash had caught on the Seven Grapefruit Islands. Driven by its appetite for delicious grapefruit, it had taught itself the butterfly stroke and could swim faster than a motorboat.

In a large population, one or two exceptional individuals were bound to turn up. This Totem Snowman Snorlax was remarkable for more than its size. Ethan's interest deepened.

Fast as it was, though, speed alone would not be enough to land a hit on Gardevoir.

Its fist came within a dozen centimeters of her face. It looked certain to connect a moment later, but in battle that small gap could be impossible to cross.

A surge of psychic power expanded outward from Gardevoir. The three-meter-tall Snorlax, heavy as it was, flew backward under the force. After little more than a meter, its weight brought it crashing down.

Thud!

It struck the ice hard enough to leave a hollow. Yet as it fell, it twisted and sprang straight back to its feet.

What an agile fat Pokemon.

Ethan and May appeared to have the same thought. Gone was the drowsy look the Snorlax had worn over its fruit. Once the battle began, its expression had turned serious.

It closed in again and swung another punch at Gardevoir. This one was faster, and a cloud of cold air coiled around its fist. It looked far more dangerous.

Ice Punch. Ethan had been right that it could at least use Ice-type moves, though that did not prove it was an Ice type itself.

At this distance the blow was harder to evade, but Gardevoir had no trouble. She used Teleport, disappearing from the Snorlax's path and reappearing some distance away.

She looked at its broad back and began to raise her hand. Before she could attack, the Snorlax's sharp battle instincts showed themselves again.

It whipped around and fired an Ice Beam from its mouth straight at her. The response was decisive and precisely aimed, coming almost the instant she appeared.

The Snorlax plainly had considerable experience. Ethan was delighted. A Pokemon already this strong and seasoned would need far less time to develop after capture. With some training and guidance, it could become a top-level fighter.

What a surprise, Ethan said with a chuckle. Then he shook his head. But I think it still underestimates you. Gardevoir, show it what you can do!

Gardevoir did not dodge. She raised one arm toward the Ice Beam, and a huge ball of psychic energy formed in front of her. It shot forward to meet the attack.

So much power was packed into the ball that it seemed almost solid. It held together against the Ice Beam, parted the cold stream, and struck the Snowman Snorlax. The impact sent it staggering backward and down.

It rubbed its head and got back to its feet almost at once.

May drew in a breath. That looked painful. How can it take a hit like that and stand right back up? Just how tough is it?

Very tough, Ethan agreed. But Snorlax are known for their stamina and special defense. It could probably take several more.

As they spoke, Gardevoir attacked again and landed another hit. The Snorlax staggered, then tried to counter with its remarkable speed, only for Gardevoir to evade it easily.

Her effortless performance might have made the Snowman Snorlax look less formidable than it was. Strength, however, was relative. Even Ethan's Milotic, Metagross, or Eevee would have had a difficult fight against it. An ordinary Trainer's Pokemon might not have been its match at all.

It could hit hard, endure punishment, move quickly, and fight with experience. Fortunately for Ethan, it had never been trained by a human. Otherwise it would be even harder to defeat.

He really had found a treasure.

On the battlefield, the Snowman Snorlax seemed to realize it was in danger. It prepared one last attempt.

It raised both hands toward the sky. Clouds gathered over what had been a clear day, and a fierce wind brought snow with it.

Blizzard! May cried.

The snowfall thickened until it stung their eyes. The wind made it difficult to stand. Ethan and May retreated several dozen paces and sheltered behind a few ice trees.

If the weather was this violent at the edge of the fight, it was worse where Gardevoir stood.

They could no longer see the battlefield, but Ethan remained aware of her condition through their telepathic bond. The snow battered Gardevoir like driving rain.

She formed a psychic shield around herself, keeping both the snow and wind at bay.

Whoosh! Crackle!

The Blizzard pounded against the shield. Beyond it, Gardevoir could see less than a meter. Even her senses could not locate the Snowman Snorlax. The wind and snow drowned out its running footsteps too.

Ethan and Gardevoir both knew this would be its final strike. Where it would come from, they could only wait to find out.

They did not have to wait long.

A few seconds later, a huge, round figure appeared behind Gardevoir in the snow. The Snorlax rushed close, leaped high, and brought a fist down toward her from above.

As before, blue-white frost swirled around the punch. Its power was impossible to dismiss.

Just as the fist was about to land, Gardevoir spun around.

Chapter 873: Ethan's Twenty-Sixth Pokemon

The Snowman Snorlax had not expected Gardevoir to find it then. The Blizzard had robbed her of sight and hearing, yet she still knew where it was. It had never encountered anything like this, and the discovery came at the worst possible moment.

Its opponent was even more troublesome than it had realized. There was no time to change course, so it drove its Ice Punch toward Gardevoir's face with all its strength. This was the closest it had come to landing a blow in the entire fight. It would not retreat now, even though she had seen it.

For an instant, everything seemed to slow. Wind roared, snow fell thickly, and the Snorlax's fist crept toward Gardevoir.

Only then did it see the strange, pale red light shining in her eyes. It had never fought an opponent like her and did not understand what that light meant. It only felt that those eyes saw through everything it might do.

Ethan could not see through the Blizzard, but his senses were linked to Gardevoir's by telepathy. It was almost as though he stood beside her. He could see the Snowman Snorlax too.

Future Sight. Now.

He gave the command silently. At once, an overwhelming force unlike anything Gardevoir had shown so far erupted before her and struck the Snorlax.

Boom!

A shock wave burst outward from the Snorlax. Then came a violent explosion. Snow already on the ground, flakes still falling, and even the driving wind were swept away. In less than a second, the Blizzard across the battlefield vanished.

With her view restored, May looked toward the center of the field. The Snowman Snorlax had been flung several meters into the air. It fell heavily onto the ice.

Thud!

May had no idea what had happened. Gardevoir stood unharmed, the faint red glow fading from her eyes, while the Snorlax lay where it had landed.

What just happened? May asked. What was wrong with Gardevoir's eyes?

She used Future Sight.

Future Sight?

May had little experience with Psychic-type Pokemon. She had never even heard of this move. Its name sounded impressive, though. Could it really let Gardevoir see the future?

Ethan seemed to read her thoughts. It's an advanced Psychic-type move. Despite its name, it doesn't actually predict events. It marks an opponent for an attack that lands later. When that delayed effect is triggered, it deals a great deal of damage.

May understood. So even when the Blizzard hid it, the mark let Gardevoir know where the Snorlax was?

Exactly.

The Snorlax did not rise. It appeared to be completely unconscious. Knowing the fight was over, Ethan took an empty Poke Ball from his belt pouch and threw it.

The ball arced over the Snorlax and snapped open. Red light drew the fallen Pokemon inside. The ball did not shake once before confirming the capture.

May ran over, picked it up, and brought it back to Ethan. He took it and bounced it lightly in his hand, delighted.

With the Snowman Snorlax and Entei, whom he had caught a few days earlier, Ethan now had twenty-six Pokemon.

Collectorsand even some ordinary Trainershad more. But twenty-six Pokemon acquired over three regions was a respectable number. Except for Jigglypuff, every one of his Pokemon was formidable. He had both quality and quantity.

And, from a certain point of view, even Jigglypuff was frighteningly powerful.

Well, we've done what we came to do. It's time to leave.

Ethan put away the ball and recalled Gardevoir. Then he released Charizard, and he and May climbed onto its back. He glanced one last time toward Luka's camp, but she was nowhere in sight.

They did not linger. Charizard beat its wings and rose away from the iceberg.

Ethan checked the map and fixed their direction. Charizard flew northwest. Within a matter of seconds, the strange iceberg and its surrounding waters were far behind them.

At that moment, Luka looked up from the camp she was pitching elsewhere on the ice. She spotted their retreating figures, smiled, and waved.

...

Ecruteak City was an old city in northern Johto.

It stood among the forests between Mt. Mortar and the great plain. Everywhere were white walls, blue roof tiles, and connected courtyards. There were no high rises, only century-old houses that gave the city a quiet elegance.

Even many of the people on its streets wore traditional kimonos and walked at an unhurried pace.

After a day's travel and a night spent outdoors, Ethan and May arrived the following afternoon.

Charizard landed on a low hill beyond the city. Between red blossoms and green leaves, they could see much of Ecruteak. The Burned Tower and Bell Tower were visible on the far side.

May had never visited a large city built in this style. She stood taking in the view for some time. Ethan was already partway down the hill before he turned and beckoned her to follow.

Ethan had come for one purpose: to bring his Eevee back for a visit.

But he could not simply appear at the Kimono Sisters' door without warning. That was why he had asked Charizard to land outside the city. He took out his phone and called Miki, the eldest sister.

Someone answered promptly, but it was her manager.

Mr. Vale? I'm sorry, Miss Miki and the others are performing onstage right now. The show will end soon. I'll ask her to call you back as soon as she comes offstage.

Ethan had been right to call first. The five sisters had busy schedules every day. Without warning, it was hard to find a time to see them. They often performed in the evenings as well. Their programs changed from show to show; the legend of the three legendary beasts that Ethan had watched on his last visit had not been performed in a long while.

He relayed the message to May. She shook her head in disappointment.

What a shame. If their show had only just started, I could have watched it too. I guess I'll have to wait until next time.

They came down the hill and walked into the city, heading toward the sisters' home. May looked around as they went.

Everything looks so old-fashioned, she said with wonder.

Ethan nodded and told her about Bell Tower, Burned Tower, Ho-Oh, and the three legendary beasts.

They were about halfway to the house when Miki called back.

Mr. Vale? I'm sorry my sisters and I were performing when you called. You're almost at our home already? Wonderful! We've missed Eevee too. I understand. Please wait a little while. We'll get ready and come straight back.

He could hear her sisters chattering and occasionally interrupting in the background. They seemed surprised and excited that he had come.

When the call ended, May covered her mouth and laughed. I didn't know you were so popular with them.

What can I say? Ethan smiled and shrugged. Someone as outstanding as me is a rare find.

He had visited once before and could roughly remember the way. Following his memory, he led May through the streets.

As they reached the sisters' expansive compound, two expensive sedans stopped at its gate. The doors opened, and all five Kimono Sisters stepped out. They had not even had time to change out of their elaborate costumes.

May stared at them. Those are the Kimono Sisters? They're all so beautiful! And those kimonos look expensive. They're gorgeous!

Hearing the envy in her voice, Ethan shook his head. Don't let the costumes fool you. Once they take off the makeup and change clothes, you'll find that they're...still beautiful.

May rolled her eyes at the little joke. Ethan laughed. When you have a chance to dress up like that, you'll look just as beautiful. Come on, let's catch them before they go inside.

They crossed at the crosswalk. The sisters soon noticed them.

Sayo, the youngest, had been looking around ever since she heard Ethan was coming. She was the first to spot them. Sisters! Look! It's Mr. Vale!

The other four turned together. Their different temperaments showed in their reactions.

Miki, the eldest, Kuni, the second, and Sayo walked over to greet Ethan. Zuki, the third sister who had challenged him to a battle on his first visit, stayed where she was. Perhaps she was naturally reserved, or perhaps she still felt dissatisfied about that encounter. Naoko, the shy fourth sister, remained beside her. The two watched from a distance.

Ethan greeted them all with May at his side. Miss Miki, Miss Kuni, Miss Zuki, Miss Naoko, Miss Sayoit's good to see you again.

May nodded to them. It's nice to meet you. I'm May, Ethan's traveling companion.

Traveling companion?

The sisters exchanged glances. None of them spoiled the mood by asking where Erika had gone.

Ethan released Eevee. The moment it saw the five women, it cried out with delight and bounded toward them.

Eevee!

It's so good to see you again!

You hardly seem to have changed at all!

Four of the sisters crouched at once, stroking Eevee and looking it over with obvious joy. Zuki gave it a glance, then turned her attention back to Ethan.

Mr. Vale, I heard you won another League championship in Hoenn?

Her cool tone made the atmosphere awkward. Ethan met her gaze without flinching.

That's right. And there's more. This time I'm back to challenge the Battle Frontier. I've already beaten six of the Frontier Brains. One more victory and I'll have another honor to add to my record.

Miki sensed the tension and quickly rose. She gave Zuki a look, warning her to be quiet, then smiled at Ethan.

You must be tired after such a long journey. I'll see to your rooms and dinner. Later, you must tell us how Eevee has been doing.

At their invitation, Ethan and May entered the courtyard.

As on his first visit, the sisters' wealth impressed Ethan. There was a pond crossed by a small bridge, with a pavilion and other buildings along its banks. Covered walkways joined the large, Japanese-style house beneath its blue tiled roofs. Cherry trees grew in a corner of the grounds. Every detail showed the sisters' resources and taste.

Miki brought the two guests to a sitting room and made tea. Then she excused herself to remove her makeup and change clothes with her sisters.

For Eevee, this really was a homecoming. It ran about, exploring surroundings both familiar and a little strange after so much time away.

May released her own Eevee to keep Ethan's company. After watching them roam, she took a sip of tea and asked, How did you get to know Sayo and her sisters?

Her curiosity was understandable. Ethan was a Trainer; the five women were famous stage performers. It was hard to imagine how their paths had crossed.

Ethan's thoughts drifted back to their first meeting. He gave May a brief account of Eevee running wild in the Ecruteak Dance Theater and the events that followed.

As he spoke, he also remembered Erika traveling at his side back then. It felt as if it had been only yesterday.

Chapter 874: Zuki

While Ethan and May talked in the sitting room, the five sisters gathered in their dressing room. They chatted as they removed their makeup and changed clothes.

After showing the guests in, Miki, the eldest, had gone to give instructions in the kitchen. She returned to find the youngest, Sayo, struggling with her costume. Miki smiled, sat behind her, and helped her out of it before attending to her own clothes.

Farther into the room, beyond Naoko, sat Kuni and Zuki. Those two were closest in age, with many shared interests, and were especially close to each other.

Kuni wiped off her lipstick and glanced at Zuki, who was removing her makeup. She seemed to want to say something, but held back.

Zuki noticed. What is it? Why do you keep staring at me?

I should be asking you that, Kuni said quietly. Don't think I missed the look on your face earlier. Is it because of Ethan?

Zuki's eyes shifted. Don't make things up. You know me. I'm always like this.

Oh, come on. Kuni gave a little laugh. I know what you're usually like. When have you ever paid a man any attention? Most of them leave you completely unmoved. Yet whenever you see Ethan, you seem to go out of your way to challenge him.

Zuki stared at her sister. Was that really true?

Thinking back, she had behaved the same way when she first met Ethan. Even now, before anything had happened between them, she felt something she could not put into words.

I have nothing against him. I just

Kuni shook her head, cutting her off. I know what sort of person you are. You're proud, and you're the best Pokemon battler among us. You think women shouldn't lose to men. You dreamed of becoming a Trainer when you were little, but in the end you had to choose the stage. There are some things we can't change, Zuki. We can only accept them.

Zuki fell silent. She had never thought seriously about some of those things before. Hearing Kuni say them aloud struck a nerve.

By then Miki had finished helping Sayo. She had not heard the conversation. Sayo, Naoko, would you two go and keep our guests company?

The two youngest sisters left together. As Miki began removing her own makeup, she looked toward Kuni and Zuki. Don't take too long. We shouldn't keep them waiting.

Kuni and Zuki focused on getting ready. Once Kuni had finished, she went to join Miki. As she passed Zuki, she leaned close to her ear.

Don't overthink it. For now, at least try to be kinder to Ethan.

She patted Zuki's shoulder and left with their eldest sister.

Alone in the dressing room, Zuki stopped what she was doing and looked at herself in the mirror.

People generally agreed that she and Kuni were the most beautiful of the five sisters. Close in age and somewhat alike in appearance, they were both reserved, but their beauty differed. Kuni had a thoughtful, cultured air; Zuki was cooler and more striking. In truth, none of the five lacked beauty.

Zuki studied her reflection and sighed. Kuni was right: she was too proud. For years, no man had managed to catch her interest.

As far as she was concerned, the men she met were nothing special. Yet one after another would come back from some short journey with a few Pokemon and parade them in front of her. It was infuriating. If she had been free to travel and become a Trainer, she was certain they would be no match for her.
