But, as Kuni had said, she had chosen to be a performer.

Her gaze traveled from her face down over her figure, and she sighed again. She was no longer particularly young. It was not simply vanity that had kept her alone: of all the men she had met, she had found none worthy of her.

She had met rising politicians, business leaders, renowned authorities on Pokemon, and young actorsplenty of men considered successful.

Only...

For an instant, the mirror seemed to show Ethan in place of her reflection.

She had to admit that his appearance suited her tastes. He was still a man, of course, but he did not repel her. Quite the opposite: she liked him.

Unlike the other Trainers she had met, Ethan had achievements she could respect. He had won the League tournaments in Kanto, Johto, and Hoenn. Few could do that. In fact, no one had managed it since the Leagues began. And as he continued traveling, he would surely earn still more honors.

He shone so brightly that she felt both jealousy and envy.

She envied his accomplishments, the freedom he had as a man, and the strength of his Pokemon. She even envied the woman named Erika who had traveled beside him.

Why couldn't she be the one at Ethan's side?

That was exactly what Zuki thought. She was convinced that only someone as exceptional as Ethan was worthy of her.

She did not believe herself less beautiful than Erika. She was taller, and her bearing was every bit as fine. Was the only difference that Erika had met him first?

Deep down, Zuki knew why she kept picking fights with Ethan. She was too proud and stubborn to admit it, even though there were better ways: she wanted him to notice her.

So far, it did not seem to have worked.

After staring into the mirror for a long while, Zuki shook her head helplessly. Her eyes dropped to the drawer in her dressing table. She frowned and pulled it open.

Among her usual perfumes was a small pink bottle. She moved the others aside and took it out.

The bottle held something unusual. Years ago, when she and Kuni had first begun performing, she had acquired it to make herself more alluring. It was not perfume, but a liquid containing an aphrodisiac. Mixed in a small amount with perfume, it was supposed to make men's hearts race and draw their attention to her.

She had been short of confidence before her debut, and Kuni had suggested the trick. Zuki had used it only once. It worked as promised, but the men's leering looks had disgusted her so much that she hid it away and never touched it again.

Holding the bottle, her eyes flickered.

Perhaps now...

...

In the sitting room, Ethan and May watched the two Eevee chase each other. They had barely taken a couple of sips of tea when Gengar emerged from Ethan's shadow.

It yawned, glanced around, and looked surprised. This place seems familiar. Haven't we been here before?

Of course, Ethan said with a smile. It's the Kimono Sisters' home. We were guests here once. Don't you remember?

Oh, this place! Gengar nodded. Since it had been here before, it saw no reason to stay put. It told Ethan it was going to explore the old house.

Be careful, Ethan called after it. Don't cause trouble!

I know, I know. Stop nagging. Gengar rolled its eyes.

It turned and almost collided with Naoko and Sayo, who were entering with plates of tea cakes. Letting out a wicked cackle, it pulled a frightening face at them. Both girls recoiled in alarm, and Gengar went off laughing.

That Gengar... Ethan shook his head. There's no stopping it.

Naoko and Sayo set down the plates and sat opposite Ethan and May. They had changed into everyday clothes. Ethan smiled and nodded to them.

Only a little over a year separated the two younger sisters. Both were in their teens and slightly older than May. Sayo, though the youngest, had a composed manner and eyes much like Miki's. Ethan thought their personalities might be alike too.

Naoko's features were a little more mature, but a trace of sadness lingered in her expression. Her timid, darting gaze made her seem especially vulnerable. Both were already lovely, and Ethan imagined they would grow into beauties like their older sisters.

Naoko bowed lightly. Mr. Vale, Miss May, please wait a little longer. Our sisters will be out soon.

You're both so pretty, May said without thinking.

Close up, she found them even more striking without their stage makeup than they had been in costume.

Naoko and Sayo smiled. You're the pretty one, Miss May.

Ethan watched the three exchange courtesies and shook his head. Come on, you're friends and close in age. You don't need to be so formal with one another.

The three looked at each other and laughed. The mood grew easier, and they began chatting.

May told them stories from her travels and explained that she was a Pokemon Coordinator working toward the Grand Festival. Naoko and Sayo listened with envy. They offered to give her advice on her stage performances.

May was thrilled. They were not much older than she was, but they were already professional performers with a popular show. Their advice might give her new ideas and a fresh style.

I'd love that. Thank you!

She took them by the hands and led them out to the lawn. Eager to begin, she released her other Pokemon and practiced under the sisters' eyes. Naoko and Sayo lived up to their offer and gave her several pointers.

Ethan leaned against the low table with his cheek in his hand. He was happy for May. Here, time itself seemed to slow.

How peaceful.

When he retired, he would like to find a place like this, drink tea, admire flowers, and watch the clouds drift by.

Footsteps approached. Miki, Kuni, and Zuki appeared along the covered walkway. They stopped outside the sitting room to watch May practice. Only after some time did they come in and kneel on the tatami across the low table from Ethan.

If I'm not mistaken, Miki said, Miss May is a Coordinator?

A good eye, Ethan replied. She is. She's traveling with me so she can enter Pokemon Contests in different places.

I thought so. She has a very steady stage presence. I'm sure she'll do well.

Kuni refilled Ethan's tea. I imagine this visit has something to do with Eevee?

Miki and Kuni were observant. They had even guessed his reason for coming. Then again, it showed how well they knew his Eevee.

That's right. Eevee reached the point where it could evolve a while ago. It shows signs of changing at any time, but since we haven't decided what it should become, it's been holding back.

I thought as much. Miki and Kuni looked toward Eevee, then turned back to him. What do you think would be best for its evolution, Mr. Vale? We said before that Eevee is your Pokemon now. Doesn't that mean your opinion should carry the most weight?

Chapter 875: The Aphrodisiac

I've thought about it, of course, Ethan said with a light laugh. But I believe we should see this through together. Eevee came to me from you. In the end, what it evolves into ought to depend on what you and Eevee think.

Miki and Kuni had not expected that answer.

They knew Ethan pursued the highest honors a Trainer could earn. Eevee was his Pokemon now, and its evolution and the abilities it gained would matter greatly to him. Yet he had brought it back to consult them.

It surprised and touched them. He was showing the sisters, and Eevee itself, the utmost respect.

If that's how you feel, Miki said, then we really should discuss it carefully.

Kuni nodded. She was about to ask Zuki, the sister with the most experience in battle, for her opinion. It might also ease the tension between Zuki and Ethan. But Zuki was gazing out the door, lost in thought. She did not seem to be following the conversation at all.

Honestly. I told her to act normally. What's she doing now?

With Ethan sitting in front of them, Kuni could say nothing. She looked away in resignation.

At that moment, a maid announced that dinner was ready. They stood, called to May and the younger sisters outside, and went together to the dining room. Their footsteps creaked along the wooden floor of the covered walkway.

Ethan washed his hands outside the room, then followed the others into another space furnished in a traditional Japanese style.

A long, low table stood on the tatami, laden with colorful dishes. The sight alone made him hungry. He recognized some of the food; other dishes were entirely new to him. Every one looked and smelled delicious.

Please sit down, Mr. Vale.

As the eldest sister and head of the household, Miki took the host's place. Ethan sat to her left, Kuni opposite him, and the others settled around the table.

To his surprise, May paid little attention to the feast. She was still bent toward Naoko and Sayo, talking with them about their earlier practice.

It was remarkable how quickly they had grown close. Ethan listened for a moment and smiled. May had clearly gained a great deal from the sisters' advice.

Once everyone was seated, the meal began. Guided by Miki and Kuni, and enlivened by May and Sayo, the conversation was warm and cheerful. They talked about the sisters' performances, then about Ethan and May's travels.

Adventures like theirs were exciting however many times the sisters heard about them. They also fed the five women's longing to experience a journey for themselves.

During dinner, Miki told the others that Eevee was ready to choose an evolution. In practice, it was mainly news to the two youngest sisters. Everyone joined the discussion eagerly.

Jolteon! Sayo suggested first. Electric attacks are so strong!

Miki sighed. Sayo, have you forgotten? Mr. Vale already has a Jolteon. We even met it before.

Sayo stuck out her tongue. Oh! I forgot.

Naoko laughed. Just because you have a Jolteon, Sayo, doesn't mean someone else's Eevee has to become one too.

I know!

They considered other possibilities. Espeon, Vaporeon, and Flareon each had supporters, but none satisfied everyone. The more they talked, the less certain they became.

Time passed as they ate and discussed Eevee. Several bottles of sake had been set out. Miki and Kuni kept pouring for Ethan, and he returned their toasts. Before long, the bottle in front of him was empty.

Ethan had only an average tolerance for alcohol. The sake was mild and the bottle small, but he was beginning to feel a little lightheaded. He was still all right.

Miki moved to fetch another bottle. Zuki rose before she could.

I remember some good sake in the cellar. I'll bring it up.

Without looking at anyone, she walked straight out.

Everyone except May, who did not know Zuki well, was surprised. Even without knowing the history between her and Ethan, a person could tell they did not get along. Why would Zuki volunteer to bring him more sake?

Was she trying to make peace? The others assumed she had found a way to do it. Kuni even thought their conversation in the dressing room might have helped.

Then she felt a prickle of unease. She knew her sister too well. If Zuki wanted to improve matters, she would not have looked so distant in the sitting room or at dinner. And she had left with a grave expression.

Excuse me, Kuni said quietly. I need to use the restroom.

She left the dining room and hurried toward the kitchen and wine cellar. Zuki was nowhere to be found, even when Kuni went all the way inside.

That made her more certain her sister had something in mind. Worried Zuki would worsen her relationship with Ethan, Kuni went looking for her.

She found her at her bedroom.

The light was on and the door half open. Kuni approached and saw Zuki standing at a table. An uncorked bottle of sake stood before her. In her hand was a small pink bottle.

It had been years, but Kuni recognized it at once. It was the aphrodisiac they had bought together when Zuki was younger.

What is she doing?

Alarmed, Kuni pushed through the door. Zuki!

Zuki turned, startled by her voice. She did not stop what she was doing. She poured the liquid from the pink bottle into the sake.

Why are you here? she asked.

Her face was expressionless. She put the pink bottle aside, corked the sake, and gave it a gentle shake to mix the liquids. Her tone and movements were as casual as if she were doing nothing of consequence.

Kuni knew better. She hurried into the room. What are you doing?

Nothing. Just adding a little fragrance to the sake.

Don't lie to me. I know what that is. Kuni stepped close and lowered her voice. Who are you planning to give that bottle to?

She knew the answer. Zuki would never harm her family. That left only Ethan.

That's none of your concern.

Zuki did not look at her. She scratched a small mark on the sake bottle's cork, then took several identical bottles from a cupboard and set them together.

Kuni grabbed her sister and drew her aside. What are you trying to do? Have you lost your mind?

Backed against the wall, Zuki had to face her. I have a plan. Stay out of it.

Her stubborn, serious expression only troubled Kuni more. Do you even understand what that stuff is?

Of course. Zuki smiled faintly. Once Ethan drinks it, he'll be at my mercy.

You fool! Kuni scolded her. It isn't that simple. It's an aphrodisiac. How can you give it to someone else, especially a man? You could end up hurt yourself. And once you do this, our relationship with Ethan could be ruined for good.

You're making it too complicated. Zuki gave a derisive smile. I know what I'm doing. If he gets to have me, why would he turn against us?

Kuni staggered back, as if she no longer knew her sister.

If he gets to have her? Was that really what Zuki intended?

You...you... She could scarcely speak.

She had thought Zuki meant to play a cruel prank: make Ethan lose his composure in front of her and embarrass him. She had never imagined her sister intended to involve herself physically.

Only now did Kuni understand that she had misread everything. Zuki had not challenged Ethan because she disliked him. She liked himenough to try to obtain him this way.

How could that be? Was this truly the proud sister Kuni knew?

Yet Kuni had to admit that an exceptional man could draw women's attention just as a beautiful woman could draw men's. Someone like Ethan might be one of a kind. Still, surely no man was worth going this far for.

You really are mad, she murmured. What if one of us drinks that sake by mistake?

Don't worry. I marked the bottle. There won't be a mistake.

Kuni could not persuade her. What if this gets out of hand? What if you lose control of it?

Lose control? Zuki snorted. Once a man has had a taste, why would he give it up? After the first time, there'll be a second without any prompting. And if I have something I can use against him, he won't be able to get away without the story becoming public.

There was no reasoning with her. Kuni heard resolve in every word. Zuki had thought this through; it was no passing whim. That made it even more frightening.

Kuni felt she had to stop her. But with Zuki's temperament, how could she change her mind? She had a strong feeling things would not unfold as Zuki expected, and the thought filled her with dread.

Kuni was right. Events were already moving away from Zuki's plan.

While the sisters argued, half of Gengar's head rose slowly from the floor. The table hid it from them. Neither noticed their uninvited observer.

Gengar had seen Zuki pour the liquid into the sake and heard every word they had said. It had spotted her leaving dinner while it was wandering the house in search of interesting things. Curious, it had followed her here.

Now, listening to them argue about drugging Ethan, Gengar grinned silently. So this human woman had a scheme of her own.

It did not think Ethan stood to lose much. Even without the aphrodisiac, its Trainer was forever getting close to women. If it had been another kind of trouble, Gengar might have stepped in. But this?

Heh. What's one more? Or perhaps two...

An idea struck it. Gengar snatched the pink bottle from the table. With a tug of psychic power, it loosened the corks of the other sake bottles.

Eager to see what chaos would follow, it poured the remaining liquid from the pink bottle evenly among them. It closed each bottle again and tucked the now-empty pink one away.

The sisters had noticed nothing. Gengar's grin widened.

The show's about to start. You think you'll have the last laugh? Let's see how this really turns out.

Thoroughly pleased with its prank, Gengar sank back through the floor and vanished as quietly as it had come. Neither Kuni nor Zuki knew it had been there.

The two were still arguing over the marked bottle. Kuni could not talk her sister out of the reckless plan.

At last she tried another approach. Don't forget Erika. Anyone can see there's something between her and Ethan. She may even be his girlfriend now.

When the sisters had first met Erika, she and Ethan had not yet become a couple. Even then, a woman choosing to travel everywhere with a man suggested something. After all this time, Kuni was sure their relationship had grown closer.

So what? Zuki did not seem concerned. She only got there before me. I want him, and I intend to have him.

Before Kuni could say more, Zuki moved past her and gathered up all the sake bottles from the table.

She turned back, determination in her eyes. My mind is made up. Stop me if you want. But we've been away too long. We need to return before they start wondering where we are.

Chapter 876: The End of Dinner

Zuki and Kuni returned to the dining room, each lost in her own troubled thoughts.

Though they had argued in Zuki's room, they had not been away long. No one at the table suspected anything. The others assumed the sisters had met outside and come back together.

Zuki placed the bottle with the marked cork in front of Ethan. She set the other bottles before Miki, Kuni, and herself.

Her expression did not change, and her hands never faltered. She did it all as naturally as she might have poured tea. She had clearly made up her mind.

Kuni watched in alarm, even more nervous than Zuki seemed to be.

It was too late for regrets. All she could do was hope that Zuki got what she wanted. If she did end up with Ethan, it might benefit their whole family. His looks and strength aside, his achievements would raise the sisters' standing.

Yet Kuni knew what Zuki was doing was wrong. It was unfair to Ethan and to Erika. Still, she had been unable to stop her sister. For now, she could only watch and hope nothing went awry.

She also braced herself to clean up any mess. Whatever happened, Zuki was her sister. Even if Miki and Ethan condemned them afterward, Kuni would stand beside her.

No one could see her thoughts.

Ethan thanked Zuki as he accepted the sake. If she was making an effort to reconcile, he ought to respond kindly.

But she went back to her seat without a word or a change of expression, leaving him puzzled. She really did seem unlike herself today. Then again, she was often distant. He let it go and uncorked the bottle.

At once, the mild fragrance of sake mingled with a strange, pleasant scent that drifted through the dining room.

That smells wonderful, Ethan said. For some reason, his heart began to race as soon as he breathed it in.

Everyone else smelled it too. It does, Miki agreed, then glanced at Zuki in confusion. Do we have sake this fragrant in the house?

The bottle looked ordinary, yet its scent was remarkable. Kuni glanced at Zuki as well.

Did she add too much of that liquid? Will someone notice?

Zuki did not meet her eyes. It was her first time adding it to a drink, and she had no way to judge the dose. She had used her best guess and added a little extra to make sure it worked. Now she too worried Ethan might grow suspicious.

Fortunately, no one thought the sake had been tampered with. Its fragrance had caught everyone's attention. Even Naoko and Sayo, who never drank, sniffed the air and looked over curiously.

It smells lovely, Sayo said, her eyes bright. Miki, could we try a little?

No! Kuni answered before Miki could. You're not old enough to drink.

Her sharp tone startled the two younger sisters. Kuni realized she had overreacted. Ordinarily, a little sake might have been all right. Tonight, the bottle in front of Ethan made it dangerous. If anyone mixed up the bottles or drank from his by mistake, there would be trouble.

Why not? Miki said. We're celebrating our guests' visit. The girls are growing up, and sooner or later they'll attend gatherings where people drink. A small taste won't hurt.

Kuni reconsidered. If she kept objecting, she might draw attention to herself.

All right. One cup each, no more. I'll pour it.

She took the bottle before her, removed its cork, and poured a cup for Naoko and one for Sayo.

For a moment she thought the fragrance had grown stronger when she opened it, as though it hovered right before her face. She dismissed the feeling. The dosed bottle was still in front of Ethan. Surely the smell had simply spread through the room.

By now she could no longer tell where the scent came from. It seemed to fill the very air.

Is it really that potent?

Even without drinking from the marked bottle, Kuni's mouth felt dry and her heart beat faster. She glanced around. Her sisters all seemed at least a little flushed.

We can't stay in a room full of this smell. Dinner needs to end soon.

Naoko and Sayo knew nothing of her worries. Delighted, they accepted their cups and set them carefully in front of themselves.

They had secretly tasted alcohol a few times before, but even the mildest drinks had seemed sharp. This sake smelled far more inviting.

May saw them receive a cup and looked hopefully at Ethan. She did not ask, but her meaning was clear.

Ethan shook his head. You're the youngest here. Stick with juice. You can try sake in a few years.

May knew he meant well, and she was too young. She was not greatly disappointed, though the scent did make her curious.

Miki and Zuki uncorked their own bottles. The mixture of sake and the sweet scent grew stronger still. No one could have said which bottle it came from.

Faces warmed across the room. Hearts quickened. Even their thoughts seemed less firmly under their control.

That dulled attention, combined with the sake Miki, Kuni, and Zuki had already drunk, kept them from noticing what they normally might have. Their preoccupations did not help.

Zuki watched; Kuni held her breath. The group raised their cups together. Naoko and Sayo each took a cautious sip. Ethan, Miki, Kuni, and Zuki drained theirs.

The cups were small, holding only a large mouthful. Ethan could ordinarily manage a dozen or so without difficulty. Yet after this one, the sake tasted strange.

It was less like ordinary sake than a sweet flower wine steeped with rose petals. It was pleasant enough, even delicious.

The others did not notice as muchat least not yet.

In her room, Zuki had shaken the marked bottle after adding the aphrodisiac, mixing it thoroughly through the sake and releasing its fragrance. Gengar had skipped that step with the other bottles. Much of their added liquid had settled near the bottom.

For now, the sake Miki and the others poured contained little of it. The effect would grow stronger as they emptied their bottles.

They drank a few more cups. Ethan was visibly losing his composure. His gaze had grown unfocused, his cheeks were red, and he breathed heavily. He looked drunk.

Miki had two rosy patches on her cheeks as well, though no one noticed. She laughed at him. Are you already tipsy, Mr. Vale? Your tolerance isn't very good. We haven't had many cups at all.

She poured herself another drink and swallowed it. Her condition was becoming more like Ethan's. The same was true of Kuni and Zuki.

All three sisters were accustomed to entertaining guests and could usually drink far more than Ethan. But the lower they got in their bottles, the more their thoughts slowed. The sake tasted odd, yet they could no longer examine why.

Zuki and Kuni had kept their eyes on Ethan. Both saw that something was wrong with him, and both knew he was not merely drunk. The aphrodisiac must be working.

I'll take him to his room, Zuki said.

She poured the last of her bottle into her cup. Perhaps to steady her nerves and keep herself from backing out, she swallowed all of it, then rose to help Ethan.

Everyone looked at her. Kuni was the most anxious of them all. The crucial moment had arrived, and she watched Zuki without blinking, afraid something would go wrong.

Miki was the eldest and normally the most attentive. She ought to have realized how strange it was for Zuki to volunteer to escort Ethan. But the drug was beginning to cloud her mind too. Though less affected than Ethan, she felt too hazy to think it through.

Naoko and Sayo exchanged a look. Things were unfolding in a way neither had expected. Still, their older sisters said nothing, so they stayed quiet.

May did not know Zuki well enough to find the offer odd. She was amused instead by Ethan's apparently poor tolerance. He could not even keep up with Miki and her sisters. He might as well have drunk juice with May.

Under their eyes, Zuki reached Ethan and helped him rise from the tatami.

It was the first time the two had been so close. The aphrodisiac had left him confused and aroused, but it had not taken away his ability to move. As soon as she supported him, he stood.

Zuki looked at his face and quickly turned her eyes away. Even without the drug, her own heart was pounding. She had made her decision, but of course she was nervous. She had never been this close to a man.

She felt his rapid heartbeat and his breathing. She saw the growing heat and fascination in his gaze. It embarrassed her.

Men had looked at her that way during performances before, and those looks had disgusted her. From Ethan, it felt different. That was the chief reason she had gone to such lengths, even chosen such a scheme, to claim him.

Some things have to be won for yourself.

Supporting Ethan, Zuki led him out of the dining room. They disappeared into the night.

With two people gone, the table fell quieter. Dinner was drawing to a close.

Kuni drank a few more cups with Miki. Several minutes later, May had finished eating, and Naoko and Sayo had emptied their cups. At last the meal ended.

Kuni's face was red too. Suppressing the restless feeling in her chest, she turned to the younger sisters. You two should share a room with Miss May tonight.

All three girls were pleased. They had become good friends through their afternoon's practice and had plenty more to talk about. A shared room would give them time together.

We'll go ahead, then, Sayo said.

Naoko and Sayo, both flushed, left with May.

Once the three were gone, Kuni hesitated. She could not stop worrying about Zuki and Ethan. Miki, I'll leave the rest to you. I'm going to see how Zuki is doing.

Miki swallowed the last of her sake and waved her on.

Kuni rose, but heat rushed into her face. Her heart was thudding, and she could not keep her balance.

Strange. Am I drunk too?

She did not dwell on it. She steadied herself against the doorframe, then stumbled out along the covered walkway toward Zuki's room.

Chapter 877: Sisters

Zuki supported Ethan as they left the dining room and headed for her bedroom.

He could still walk, but only with her help. Supporting a grown man was hard work. Fortunately, Zuki was tall enough to manage.

The effort made her blood pump faster. Whether from that or something else, she felt that something was wrong with her too.

When the cool night air touched her skin, she realized how hot she felt all over. It was almost as if the aphrodisiac had affected her as well.

Did I breathe too much of that scent?

It was the only explanation she could think of. She shook her head, trying to clear her mind, and guided Ethan along the covered walkway.

Inside her room, she settled him on a chair while she spread bedding on the tatami. Then she helped him onto the futon.

By now the drug had taken hold of Ethan. He reached for her and leaned in close. Zuki shivered at the unexpected touch. Her thoughts blurred, and she nearly lost control of herself.

What's happening?

She had thought she had only caught the scent, but she was clearly feeling its effects. In a way, it strengthened her resolve.

First, though, she had one important task.

Pulling herself away from Ethan, she went to a cabinet and took out a camera she had prepared in advance. She adjusted it, switched it on, and set it on a stand aimed at the bedding. Only then did she breathe out.

It was her last resort: evidence she could use against Ethan afterward. If she recorded him with her while he was under the drug's influence, she believed he would have no way to deny what happened. To keep it from becoming public, he would have to accept her.

She sensed movement behind her. When she turned, Ethan was already there, reaching to embrace her. She did not step away.

He pulled her close and kissed her insistently, tugging roughly at her clothes. The tension she had been holding in suddenly gave way. Desire rose through her until she could barely think.

She held him in return, answering his kisses. They fell onto the bedding together and rolled into each other's arms.

Her last clear memory was of everything around her seeming pink, and a fierce heat within her that demanded release.

...

Kuni had not gone far from the dining room before she stumbled and had to brace herself against a wall. She drew several ragged breaths before her racing heart calmed.

The relief did not last. Heat kept pressing against her reason. Her legs trembled, and Ethan's face appeared in her mind unbidden.

Part of it came from feelings she had not acknowledged. The drug stirred them further.

Startled by the image of him, Kuni broke into a cold sweat. It cleared her head a little.

Why am I thinking of Ethan?

She tried to push him out of her thoughts, but could not. The image remained, joined by a strong longing she did not want to name.

Her heart thudding, she gritted her teeth and moved slowly along the wall toward Zuki's room.

Like Zuki, Kuni assumed the fragrance in the dining room had caused her condition. She was worried about her sister, though, and forced herself onward despite how unsteady she felt.

As she reached the part of the house where Zuki's room lay, she heard strange sounds from a distance.

She had never heard them in person, but she understood what they were. They were unrestrained sounds of pleasure, and whoever made them seemed wholly caught up in it.

She really did it?

Zuki had been bold enough to carry out her plan. Yet could that voice truly be hers? The tone matched, but Kuni could scarcely imagine her cool, aloof sister sounding like that.

Almost without deciding to, Kuni went closer. At Zuki's door, she slid it open a crack. The light inside showed her everything.

She swallowed. The sight overwhelmed her, leaving her mind blank. At this distance, Zuki's voice reached her without anything to muffle it. What remained of Kuni's reason warned her to leave immediately.

When she came back to herself, she found she had already stepped into the room.

Wait. When did I come in?

Ethan and Zuki were too absorbed in each other to notice her. Kuni was relieved for a moment.

I have to leave.

But her legs carried her toward the bedding instead. They finally gave way, and she sank down beside the couple with a small sound.

As she pushed herself up and looked ahead, Ethan met her eyes. The heat in his gaze was enough to break what control she had left. Like Zuki before her, Kuni felt her thoughts disappear into the moment.

...

Miki finished clearing the table and stepped outside the dining room. The house was quiet. She assumed her sisters had all gone to bed.

She looked up. The moon was full, though drifting clouds covered most of it, leaving only a slender portion visible.

Like Kuni, Miki was near the limit of what she could bear. Her skin burned, her thoughts were muddled, and her limbs felt weak. The world seemed tinged pink.

There was no man beside her, no familiar scent to stir her further, so she could still hold on to some controlbut only just. She had even washed her face with cold water several times.

She knew nothing of the drug. She could not understand why she felt this way. Had her tolerance for sake really become so poor? She had never reacted like this before. Worse, she found herself thinking about a man.

Ethan.

What am I thinking? Miki laughed at herself. She was several years older than him. Many men preferred someone their own age or younger. Kuni and Zuki were closer to Ethan's age and might suit him better.

But he appeared to have a girlfriend already. If he had not, Miki might have tried to introduce him to one of her sisters. A connection like that would be good for their family.

She did not know how closely her thoughts resembled Kuni's.

Simply thinking about Ethan brought back the longing she had briefly suppressed, stronger than before. She shook her head, trying to drive him from her mind. It did no good.

She needed to get to bed. With a sigh, she leaned against the wall and made her way toward her room.

As she passed near Zuki's room, she heard unusual sounds. They drew her toward the door. By the time she fully realized where she was, she stood before it.

The door was open. Miki stared at the scene inside, understanding at last what she had heard.

Both Kuni and Zuki were there with Ethan. How had this happened? Was she dreaming?

She could not look away. Her mouth went dry, and something long held down seemed to surge up inside her, threatening to sweep away her thoughts.

Almost without willing it, she moved slowly toward the three of them. Her awareness blurred.

...

The full moon cast a silvery light over Ecruteak City.

In the sisters' guest room, Sayo rubbed her eyes and sat up. The clock on the wall showed that it was past two in the morning. She had tossed and turned for hours without falling asleep.

She usually slept well. What was wrong tonight?

She turned and saw Naoko lying awake, her eyes bright in the dim room.

You can't sleep either?

No, Naoko said softly. My heart keeps beating too fast.

Sayo felt the same. Across the room, May was sleeping soundly, though sprawled in a way that was hardly ladylike.

Could it be the sake? Sayo whispered.

Probably, Naoko said with a wry smile. We shouldn't have been so eager to taste it.

They had drunk the dosed sake too, but only one small cup each, poured from near the top of a bottle where Gengar's added liquid had not fully mixed. Of everyone who drank, they had received the least. It had only made their hearts race and kept them awake.

Who knew it would have such a strong aftereffect? Still, it had a faint rose scent, and it tasted good. Sayo wriggled under her blanket and spoke sweetly. Naoko...

Naoko sighed. You need to use the bathroom again, don't you?

Her younger sister had two small habits she had never grown out of. She disliked sleeping alone and, despite being a teenager, still shared a room with Naoko. She also woke at night to use the bathroom and was afraid of the dark, so she always asked Naoko to go with her.

Naoko could hardly refuse her sister.

They left the light off to avoid waking May. Each put on an outer layer, and they slipped out of the bedroom, one after the other.

For all its space and elegance, the large house had its inconveniences. The bathroom was a long walk down the corridor from their room.

Their footsteps echoed in the quiet passage. Tonight, however, they were not the only sounds.

Naoko stopped and listened. Sayo...do you hear something strange?

I do. Sayo grew nervous. What is that? Could it be a ghost?

It doesn't sound like one. I think it's coming from Zuki's room.

Zuki's room? But why would she still be awake?

Curious, the sisters exchanged a glance and turned toward Zuki's door.

As they drew closer, they made out several women's cries and moans. Neither had heard anything like it before, but both understood at once.

They stopped, blushing and at a loss for what to do.

Is that...Zuki? Sayo asked, her face burning.

Yes. Naoko faltered. But I think I hear Miki and Kuni too.

What are they doing?

The question escaped Sayo before she thought it through. There was only one man in the house tonight: Mr. Vale. But how could that be possible?

The sounds continued. The sisters stood listening for a while, embarrassed and uneasy. At last they edged toward the door. Since it was happening right beside them, they felt they had to see what was going on.

Chapter 878: Afterward

Two heads appeared at the open doorway. Naoko and Sayo peered into the roomand saw a sight they would remember for the rest of their lives.

They could only stare in shock. They had never imagined this side of their three older sisters. All three of them, at the same time, with one man. Had they truly been so carried away that they had not even closed the door?

The younger sisters stood rooted to the spot, their faces growing redder. The scents from the room only made it harder to think.

Sayo heard heavy breathing beside her and turned. Naoko looked dazed and was beginning to lose awareness of her surroundings. Sayo realized they could not stay there.

She pulled the door shut, putting it between them and the room.

Bang!

The noise did not interrupt anyone inside, but it startled Naoko back to herself. She looked at her own hands and blushed deeply, mortified by how the drug and the scene had affected her.

I... I... She could not finish.

Sayo was in no mood to tease her. She took Naoko's hand and led her back toward their bedroom. The bathroom could wait.

Neither spoke as they hurried along the corridor. Only when they were back in familiar surroundings did they breathe freely again.

May was still fast asleep, unaware of anything happening in the house. She had merely shifted into another untidy sleeping position.

Naoko and Sayo slipped under their now-cool blankets and pulled them over their heads. An uneasy silence filled the room. Sleep was even further away than before.

They tossed and turned until almost dawn, when both finally dozed. What they had witnessed followed them into their dreams. They woke embarrassed and avoided each other's eyes, unaware that the other had slept just as poorly.

Between the three older sisters and these two, Ethan had kept all five Kimono Sisters from a restful night.

Only May slept well. When she woke, the weariness of their journey had vanished. She felt refreshed and full of energy.

Good morning! she said brightly.

She was already dressed and had folded her bedding neatly by the time Naoko and Sayo rose. For a moment, her cheerful manner reminded them of Ethan.

You're up early, Miss May, Naoko said, rubbing her eyes and forcing herself to sound alert.

Early? May glanced at the clock. It was past seven. Then she remembered that stage performers sometimes worked late into the night. Perhaps their schedules were irregular.

She looked more closely at the sisters. Both seemed exhausted, with dark circles beneath their eyes.

Did you sleep badly? I hope I didn't keep you awake.

Naoko and Sayo exchanged a look.

No, it wasn't you, Naoko said quickly. It was just... She struggled to find an explanation.

Sayo supplied one. We had some sake last night, and it made it hard to sleep.

Naoko flushed. That's right.

I see. May accepted it. Even Ethan had seemed drunk last night, so it was easy to believe the sisters might have had trouble sleeping.

That reminded her of him. He ought to be awake by now. Would he look as worn out as these two after his drinking?

When Naoko and Sayo had dressed, the three left the bedroom.

Their room lay deep within the house. Any route to the dining room, washstand, or bathroom took them past Zuki's room. The two sisters walked nervously, afraid of what they might see.

Everything was quiet as they approached. But the door they had closed during the night stood open again.

They looked inside. Ethan was asleep under a blanket on disordered bedding. No one else was there.

Naoko and Sayo were relieved. At least they had not found anyone else.

May, however, was puzzled. Is this the guest room where Ethan stayed? It looks more like a woman's room.

From its furnishings, it clearly was. There was a strange smell toonot exactly unpleasant, but hard to identify.

Naoko and Sayo were once again at a loss for an answer. Fortunately, May assumed the guest rooms might all be decorated this way.

Ethan was still asleep. Thinking he must be suffering from all the sake, she let him rest and went with the sisters to wash up.

Once they were ready, the three entered the dining room. Miki, Kuni, and Zuki were nowhere to be seen. Where had they gone?

...

A little earlier, around the time Naoko and Sayo woke, the three older sisters had been sitting together in Miki's room without a word.

Before them stood a camera. They had just finished watching its recording. Zuki had meant to capture something she could use against Ethan. Instead, it showed all three sisters going to him in turn and what followed.

It was painful to watch and harder still to remember. Silence weighed on the room.

They had changed into fresh clothes, but marks on their necks and their exhausted, strangely radiant faces revealed how they had spent the night.

At length, Miki sighed and looked at her sisters. That was quite a spectacle. Now tell me: what happened?

Her voice was hoarse, whether from the night itself or simple thirst.

None of them had lost their memory. The night returned in fragments, but they remembered being with Ethan until dawn. Only when the feverish feeling finally subsided had they collapsed from exhaustion. They woke almost immediately in shock, confusion giving way to alarm.

All three had fled the room, trembling, weak, and sore. Not even Zuki had dared stay.

Kuni glanced at Zuki. Miki's flat question left no room to avoid an answer.

Zuki told the whole story: how she had mixed the liquid into the sake, how Kuni had tried to stop her, and how she had given Ethan the marked bottle.

That's everything, she said with a sigh. I didn't judge the amount properly. That must be why the scent affected all of us.

Even now, she did not realize the sake the three sisters had drunk had been dosed too. She thought only the fragrance had affected them.

Miki said nothing for a long time. Her silence pained Zuki. This was her fault. She had dragged both older sisters into it.

I'm sorry I involved you.

Miki and Kuni looked at her. Zuki rarely apologized. They were surprised to hear her admit fault, even though what she had done plainly demanded an apology.

And it had done more than merely involve them. Miki bore marks left by both of her sisters as well as by Ethan, and she had left marks on them too.

What happened filled them with embarrassment, anger, regret, and helplessness. Yet neither Miki nor Kuni could bring herself to hate Ethan. Zuki had set it in motion. He, too, had been drugged.

They even found themselves thinking that, if it had to happen, at least it had been with Ethan. Both recognized his good qualities. They would have been distraught if it had been some other man.

Then again, Zuki would never have attempted anything like this with anyone else. Ethan was a victim of her scheme, but he was also the reason she had devised it.

What do we do now? Kuni asked. Her body trembled from sheer exhaustion after the long night. Miki and Zuki felt just as worn out.

Zuki fell silent. Her plan had gone completely out of control, and both her sisters were entangled in it. If only she had been involved, she might have known what to do. Now she had no idea.

The room fell quiet again as all three considered their options.

How much do you think he'll remember? Kuni asked hesitantly.

Probably as much as we do, Miki said after a moment. He drank directly from the marked bottle, but the drug doesn't erase memories. He'll remember.

That was a difficult prospect. They fell silent once more.

Finally Miki made her decision. We should tell him the truth. It's the best choice we have. If we're honest and ask his forgiveness, perhaps we can put this behind us as quickly as possible. That would be best for both sides.

She turned to Zuki. Don't worry. After all three of us have been with him, I hope he'll accept you.

Kuni glanced at Zuki. Seeing her nod, she sighed. I suppose that's all we can do.

...

No one disturbed Ethan, and he slept until late morning.

When he finally sat up, he stared around the unfamiliar room. His head was still foggy. His body ached and felt drained.

The bedding beneath him was damp. Sweat and other fluids marked the tatami nearby, along with a few spots of blood that had not been cleaned away. Torn scraps of clothing lay farther off. He had nothing on, and his skin felt sticky.

Where am I? How did I get here? What happened?

Then fragments of the previous night came back to him.

I...with all three sisters?

As he sat there in disbelief, Gengar passed through the wall and appeared before him.

Chapter 879: I Have Other Women in My Life

Oh, you're awake. Gengar greeted Ethan with a grin, then glanced down. You know, that isn't very decent. I'm your Pokemon, so you don't have to worry too much about appearances around me, but couldn't you put on some pants? Even a cloth would do.

The reminder brought Ethan fully back to himself. His clothes lay some distance away, untouched by the mess around the bedding. Relieved, he hurried to dress, putting aside the fact that his skin still felt dirty.

The clothes were clean enough, though they had picked up a peculiar smell. The floor was worse. It stuck to his feet with every step, and each movement left his body aching. Then his stomach growled.

His surroundings and his condition were both miserable. The rich dinner he had eaten must have been used up during the night. No wonder he was starving.

Before washing and finding food, though, he needed to understand what had happened. Even if he had behaved recklessly after drinking, how had it gone on so long? And why had Miki, Kuni, and Zuki all come to him? Something was wrong.

Gengar moved closer, looking him up and down with a series of amused clicks of its tongue.

Humans really can't handle drugs well. Such a small amount, and you were all overwhelmed.

Drugs? What drugs? Ethan stared at it. Gengar clearly knew something. And where were you last night? Why are you only back now?

Wandering around here, Gengar said with a shrug. Lucky for you I was. Otherwise, you might really have suffered.

It told him what it had seen: Zuki putting an aphrodisiac in his sake, and Gengar adding the rest to her sisters' bottles.

Ethan stood speechless. Zuki had tried to drug him, and Gengar had responded by drugging the others too? What sort of turn had events taken?

It took him a while to absorb it. So that was why last night had happened. The person who had made it worse was his own Pokemon.

He rubbed his aching head. You found out and didn't warn me or stop her. Instead, you helped her along?

Of course. Gengar grinned. She was determined to have you. I couldn't bear to spoil her plans. Besides, I didn't see how it could hurt you. I wanted to see what would happen. I didn't expect the eldest sister to get involved too, but stillthree of them. Not bad!

Not bad? My back feels as if it's breaking.

Ethan sighed. Did you think my life wasn't complicated enough?

Gengar looked genuinely puzzled. Why is this a complication? You already have plenty of women. You seem to like being close to them. I thought you'd be happy with more.

That left Ethan speechless. Was that truly how Gengar saw him?

Once he understood the cause, guilt began to settle over him. He felt he had taken advantage of all three sisters, however little control any of them had had. His gaze dropped to three faint spots of blood on the floor.

What a mess.

But why had Zuki tried to drug him in the first place? Had she meant to use the incident against him?

He questioned Gengar again. It recounted the conversation it had overheard between Zuki and Kuni. Only then did Ethan learn that Zuki liked him.

She likes me?

He thought back over her behavior. How was he supposed to have guessed? Who tried to attract someone by constantly picking fights with him?

Then he remembered Zuki's proud, guarded temperament. In that light, he could understand it. Understanding did not tell him what to do now.

Thinking only made him hungrier. His skin still felt sticky. Since he had no solution, he left the room, showered, and changed into clean clothes. Then he headed for the dining room.

Whatever awaited him there, he needed to eat first.

Halfway along the covered walkway, he saw May practicing with Naoko and Sayo in the distance. May was too focused to notice him. The younger sisters did, and their faces instantly turned red. They turned their backs without even greeting him.

Ethan stared. Why were they embarrassed? He had done nothing with them.

Unless they know what happened last night?

He was right, though he did not know it. He shook his head and kept going.

After a few steps, he met Kuni coming the other way. Both stopped. The awkwardness between them was unmistakable.

Kuni looked more unsettled than Ethan. Facing him again made it difficult for her to stay calm, and her legs felt weak. She drew a breath and forced herself to speak.

You're...awake? She tried to steady her voice, but it trembled.

Ethan scratched his head, unsure what to say. He could hardly ask how her body felt.

At least she had not met him with anger or accusations. Perhaps there was still a way to talk this through.

Before he could respond, Kuni said, I was going to wake you. We've prepared lunch in the dining room. Please come with me.

She turned and led the way. Ethan did not yet know what the sisters intended, but he had to face them honestly.

A dozen steps brought them to the dining room. Miki and Zuki were already inside. Both looked up when Ethan appeared, then lowered their eyes shyly.

The table held a generous lunch, every bit as fine as the previous night's dinner. Kuni joined her sisters on one side. The atmosphere was heavy. Ethan sat opposite them without hesitation.

Perhaps it was his imagination, but even after a night of airing and a thorough cleaning, he thought he could still catch a faint trace of yesterday's scent.

Mr. Vale... Miki spoke first. Do you remember what happened last night?

Ethan nodded.

Miki and Kuni exchanged rueful looks. Zuki, by contrast, seemed to grow calmer.

Miki took a breath. You must have questions. Let me explain.

She recounted everything she knew. From the sisters' point of view, there was no Gengar and no secret addition to their bottles. They believed the fragrance from Ethan's sake had affected them and led to what followed.

Ethan could hear their distress. He felt sorry for them. After a moment's hesitation, though, he decided not to reveal what Gengar had done. He thought it better that they not know. He acted as though this was the first time he had heard the story.

I see. No wonder last night...

Color rose in Miki's and Kuni's faces.

Let's treat last night as if it never happened, Miki interrupted, plainly unwilling to discuss its details. Then she met his eyes. But I have one request concerning Zuki.

Here it comes.

Ethan had known their calm invitation and elaborate meal were leading somewhere. Now they had reached the point.

You understand why Zuki did this, Miki said. She came up with an extreme plan because she wanted you to accept her.

Ethan looked at Zuki. She met his gaze steadily.

I'm not worth doing all this for, he said. You must know I already have someone.

Erika, Zuki said, with a look that suggested she had expected as much.

Well... Ethan scratched his head. Not only Erika. There are others.

What? All three sisters stared at him.

You have other women besides Erika? Kuni exclaimed, her voice suddenly much louder.

You don't need to shout, Ethan said with an embarrassed smile. Relationships...sometimes they take unexpected turns.

Zuki glared. Does Erika know?

He nodded. She came into my life after someone else.

The three women were astonished. They had met Erika and knew her as a traditional, reserved woman. Had she become involved with Ethan while knowing he was already with someone? Who was this other woman?

You're quite the flirt, Zuki said coldly.

Ethan gave a bitter smile. That's why I said I'm not worth what you did.

What's the use of saying that now? She glared again. It's too late. Or do you plan to have your fun and walk away?

Her words stung. He had enjoyed parts of the night, but it still felt unreal, clouded by the drug. A reckless thought crossed his mind, and he immediately kept it to himself.

Miki and Kuni exchanged uneasy glances. The news of Ethan's other relationships had upset what they had expected from this conversation.

Zuki was angry, but her decision did not waver. You clearly aren't going to leave them. Fine. I still want to be with you.

Ahem! Ethan coughed, startled by her directness. She knew what she wanted, said it, and acted on it. That was Zuki. She had hardly given him room to refuse.

He tried anyway. This could affect your reputation and your future happiness. Shouldn't you think it over more care

Zuki narrowed her eyes, cutting him off. Do you object?

Her force of will was unmistakable. Ethan yielded. ...All right. I don't.

Zuki nodded in satisfaction and smiled. Then congratulations. You have another woman in your life, and a home in Johto too.

Miki and Kuni had not expected her to embrace a relationship with Ethan despite knowing he had other women. Yet that was Zuki's nature: once she chose a course, she threw herself into it.

If they were in her position, perhaps they would have accepted it too. What else could they do? Pretend the night had never happened?

Zuki looked radiant, and Ethan wore a helpless smile. Watching them, Miki and Kuni felt a pang of sadness. Zuki had gained what she wanted. What had the two of them gained? They had lost something precious.

Even so, they loved their sister. If Zuki could be happy, that was a comfort.

Miki took several bottles of sake from the side and set them before the group.

This is happy news, and it settles something we've all worried about. We should celebrate with a few drinks. She saw Ethan eyeing the bottles nervously and laughed. Don't worry. No one has put anything in the sake this time.

Chapter 880: A Second Time

Miki's teasing caught Ethan out, and he felt embarrassed. To change the subject, he asked, Where are Naoko and the others? Shouldn't we invite them to eat with us?

Miki saw through the question, but answered without pointing it out. They're helping May practice. They'll eat on their own later.

In fact, she had deliberately sent Naoko, Sayo, and May away before lunch. She did not want the younger girls to hear the awkward conversation ahead or be caught in an argument if it went badly. In that respect, she had taken care to protect them.

What Miki could not know was that her two youngest sisters had already seen what happened between Ethan and the older three the night before.

Ethan nodded and pulled the cork from his sake bottle.

After last night, he had no desire to drink again soon. An identical bottle was enough to make him uneasy. But if a toast would ease the atmosphere and help them move past what had happened, he could manage one.

He poured himself a full cup. Thankfully, the strange fragrance was gone. He began to relax.

Zuki rose with her cup, came around the table, and sat beside him. A faint blush colored her face, and her eyes held a softness he had never seen from her before.

She poured her own cup from Ethan's bottle and raised it toward him.

Please drink with me, she said. I hope you'll look after me for the rest of our lives.

Zuki and her sisters had grown up surrounded by old customs. Like Erika, each retained something of a traditional, devoted woman's manner. Once she chose someone, Zuki could be gentle and attentive without giving up her own character. She had been raised to regard that sort of loyalty as natural.

Ethan was still adjusting to her change in manner and to the idea of Zuki as his partner. But he had given his answer. He would not take it back.

Her words touched him most of all. She was entrusting her life to him.

He lifted his cup, touched it to hers, and drank. Zuki emptied her cup too. Her face remained cool and beautiful, but her gaze grew softer as she refilled Ethan's cup.

She looked like a considerate wife.

Ethan raised his drink again. Across the table, Miki and Kuni wore complicated expressions. With a quiet sigh, he offered them a toast as well. Both drank with him, though the gesture only sharpened their sadness. They were sisters, yet the night had left each of them with a very different future.

A few cups whetted Ethan's appetite. He stopped standing on ceremony and began eating in earnest.

Lunch was much quieter than dinner had been. Everyone had private thoughts, and the meal passed in a subdued calm.

By the time Ethan had eaten his fill, he had finished another bottle of sake. Then his heart began to race again. His thoughts turned hazy, just as they had the previous night.

He stiffened. What? They said there was nothing in this sake!

He looked up. Miki, Kuni, and Zuki were flushed and their eyes had begun to lose focus too.

They felt it as well. Miki struggled to keep herself upright and her thoughts clear. What's...happening? There was no scent this time. Why...

She turned toward Zuki, plainly suspecting her sister had dosed the sake again. But Zuki was as bewildered as the rest of them. She had done nothing. There was no reason to do anything now. How could this be happening?

Kuni could no longer speak. She sat breathing heavily, her face growing redder as her gaze settled on Ethan.

The mood from the previous night filled the room again. What little reason they had left warned them that matters were about to go badly. Would it happen all over again?

None of them knew the answer lay in the bottles from last night.

While Zuki and Kuni argued in Zuki's room, Gengar had poured most of the remaining aphrodisiac into all the other sake bottles. Zuki had brought the bottles to dinner, but Ethan was affected and left with her before every bottle had been opened or emptied. Miki and Kuni had finished only the bottles in front of them. Several dosed bottles remained.

Because no one suspected those bottles, they had been set out for lunch and served again.

Why was there no scent now? Overnight, the fragrance had dissipated in the sake, leaving the drug's effect. The mixture had become harder to detect, and all four had drunk from it.

Unfortunately, none of them knew that. Within moments, the effect had fully taken hold.

Miki forced herself to look at the others. Zuki had slumped against Ethan. Certain of her feelings this time, she held his waist without reserve and kissed him.

Kuni was moving toward him too.

Miki's thoughts blurred further. The memory of the previous night broke what remained of her resistance. She knew Ethan was with Zuki now, but her own feelings drew her toward him alongside Kuni.

What followed echoed the night before, though now all four were together from the beginning, and the room was different.

...

Outside in the courtyard, Naoko and Sayo continued helping May with her performance practice.

May valued the rare opportunity and worked hard. Under their guidance, her steps and stage presence took on a more practiced form. She was no longer moving like someone who had learned everything on the road. The sisters' advice was an important step in her development as a Coordinator.

Even determined practice had its limits. May was soon sweating and exhausted. She sat down on the wooden veranda to catch her breath. Her Pokemon flopped down nearby, equally unwilling to move.

Naoko and Sayo exchanged pleased smiles. They were happy to see her progress.

It's getting late, one of them said. Let's take a break and have lunch.

At the mention of food, May's stomach growled. She had spent the whole morning dancing and jumping through routines. She had burned a great deal of energy, and the food here was especially good.

They tidied up and headed toward the dining room.

On the way, Naoko remembered that Miki had specifically asked them to come late so the older sisters could speak privately with Ethan. Surely their discussion was over by now. What had they needed to talk about so secretly?

Only a few dozen steps later, they reached the corridor outside the dining room. Naoko heard something and stopped.

Wait. Why does that sound familiar?

The voices rose and fell without being muffled. She could hear them even from here. She recognized the sounds she and Sayo had heard outside Zuki's room the night before.

Naoko's face flamed. Had this been what Miki and the others meant to discuss with Ethan? In broad daylight?

Sayo and May heard it too. Both stopped, blushing.

Sayo had seen enough the previous night to know. The memory had distracted her even during May's practice, so she recognized the sounds at once.

May understood them as well. Not long ago, at the Temple of the Sea, she had caught a glimpse of Ethan and Maya through a door. She knew what the voices meant.

They sounded like Miki, Kuni, and Zuki. Ethan was the only man in the house. May could draw her own conclusion, but it made no sense to her. When had Ethan become involved with all three women? Last night they had seemed like polite acquaintances.

Had their relationship changed that quickly? Or had there been something between them all along that she had failed to notice?

The three young women stood with different thoughts, none daring to take another step.

Um... Sayo's heart raced. I'm...not that hungry after all. Maybe we should eat later.

Yes, May said with an awkward smile. We could practice some more.

Naoko had already turned back. Sayo and May followed her without another word.

The journey back was nothing like their cheerful walk to lunch. They all knew what they had heard, but no one mentioned it.

They sat along the veranda wall and stared into the courtyard. Practice was out of the question. None felt like it, and May was still hungry.

They stayed there for a long while as the sun shifted overhead. May's stomach growled again, breaking the silence. She stuck out her tongue in embarrassment when the sisters looked at her.

Only then did they notice that all three were sitting in exactly the same posture. They exchanged a smile, and the tension eased a little.

Why don't we find something in the kitchen? Sayo suggested.

Naoko and May agreed. They found enough food there to fill their stomachs, but afterward they were unsure what to do.

Perhaps they imagined it, or perhaps the people inside had forgotten themselves completely, but they thought they could still hear the dining room from the kitchen. When would it end?

Once May had recovered her energy, she returned to practice, giving them something else to focus on. Yet all three were distracted. May kept making mistakes, and Naoko and Sayo could not give the work their full attention. Their progress slowed.

...

Ethan wished he could have a cigarette. There was none nearby, and he did not smoke anyway.

Once the drug's effect had passed, he sat up and checked the time. It was after seven. The light outside was fading, and night would soon fall.

Compared with the previous night, he thought he had fared better. This time it had lasted only three or four hours. He had not fallen asleep afterward, nor had he lost himself quite so completely. Perhaps his body had built a little resistance. His memories were clearer too.

He was still exhausted, especially after the night before. At least he had eaten a great deal at lunch and could keep going.

Beside him, Miki, Kuni, and Zuki dressed in silence, their faces flushed. Their hair was loose and disordered. None seemed able to find anything to say.

Miki and Kuni looked as though they wanted to speak. In the end, they said nothing. They bowed to Ethan and left the room on unsteady feet.

Chapter 881: Defining Their Relationship

That evening, more than two hours after they had parted, Ethan sat across from Miki, Kuni, and Zuki in his guest room. The three sisters had bathed again.

This time, even Miki had nothing to say. What could she say? The boundary she had tried to draw earlier had fallen apart in the face of what they had done.

Ethan looked at the three women. Zuki met his eyes without flinching. Miki and Kuni looked down, shy and embarrassed. All three still wore a blush from the afternoon and seemed much more subdued than usual.

Ethan sighed to himself. He had made another mistake, but he would take responsibility for it.

I think we need to talk about what we are to each other now.

Miki and Kuni grew even more self-conscious. Though both were older than he was, neither spoke. They waited for him to continue, with a hope they were reluctant to admit.

Ethan paused. None of us intended for things to happen this way. But I won't run from what happened. You may think I'm greedy for even saying this. Still, if you want me toand unless your hearts belong to someone elseI will take responsibility for both of you.

He had not said it outright, but they understood. He was offering to be with all three sisters.

It sounded like something from an anime or novel. If another man had said it to Miki, she might have slapped him. Now the circumstances were different.

She and Kuni remembered their own actions and Ethan's during the night and the afternoon. Those hours would remain with them for the rest of their lives. They could not simply pretend nothing had happened, leave him with Zuki, and step aside.

To their minds, his willingness to accept them both was the best outcome left.

Still, Miki and Kuni did not answer immediately. They turned to Zuki. Whatever they wanted, she should have a say. Only a short time had passed, but Ethan had already acknowledged Zuki as his partner.

Zuki understood her sisters' looks. She loved them, and her own actions had started all this. That was why she had sat quietly through the conversation. Ordinarily, she might never have tolerated sharing his attention.

She smiled at them. Wouldn't this be good? We sisters can stay together, without worrying that we'll have to part someday.

Her words made Miki and Kuni think of how close the three sisters themselves had been during those two encounters. The memories embarrassed them, though the drug had been responsible for much of it.

Zuki had given her answer. Miki and Kuni exchanged a look and saw that they agreed.

Miki smiled ruefully. We've already been with you. I don't think either of us can treat that lightly. If you'll have us, we'd like to stay at your side. We won't ask you for any particular status.

It was an old-fashioned way to see themselves. Ethan found it both moving and sad. Plenty of people would regard a sexual encounter as no reason to commit to a life together. These women spoke of lifelong loyalty. Their conservatism could be stubborn, but it meant they did not make promises casually.

By a bewildering turn of events, all three beautiful sisters had chosen him. He knew he would owe them more than words in return.

He had come to Ecruteak to discuss Eevee's evolution. They had not settled that question, yet he had gained three partners instead. That was a weighty obligation, one he might spend a lifetime honoring.

It also gave him a place in Johto where he could feel at home. The Temple of the Sea was a place he could visit, but it did not give him the same sense of belonging.

Once they had defined the relationship, Miki and Kuni relaxed a little. Beneath their lingering embarrassment, both felt glad. Whatever else had happened, they believed they had followed their hearts.

Then Kuni remembered something and cried out. Oh! Weren't we supposed to perform tonight?

Oh no! Miki and Zuki looked at the clock.

The five sisters were busy performers, taking the stage nearly every day or every other day. The upheaval in their household had made them forget tonight's scheduled show entirely.

What do we do? Kuni grimaced. There's no time to do our makeup, change into costumes, and reach the Ecruteak Dance Theater. And...

She glanced at the marks visible on Miki's and Zuki's necks. Even with makeup, they could hardly appear before an audience looking like this.

Miki looked at Ethan and gave a helpless smile. We'll have to call our manager and cancel tonight's performance.

I suppose so, Kuni said with a sigh. We've never canceled a show since our debut. That streak ends today, and the audience already inside will have to leave.

It can't be helped, Miki said. We have something important to settle here. We could announce that we're ill and take a few days off. Once things are calmerand Ethan has gone back to travelingwe can perform again.

The way she said Ethan's name sounded natural and intimate. Kuni and Zuki considered the proposal, then nodded. These past two days had changed the course of their lives. They could hardly return to the stage before finding their footing.

That's best, Kuni agreed. Then she frowned. But if we forgot a performance, surely Naoko and Sayo didn't. Why haven't they reminded us?

Her sisters' expressions changed. Where were the younger two?

A possibility occurred to all three at once. Perhaps Naoko and Sayo had seen what happened in the dining room that afternoon. It had been broad daylight, after all. If so, of course they had stayed away.

The thought made the older sisters burn with embarrassment. If the younger girls had witnessed them, they hardly knew how to face them.

...

After the afternoon's exertion, Ethan washed and went to bed early. This time he slept alone in an actual guest room.

He and Miki, Kuni, and Zuki had agreed on their relationship, but it would take time to grow comfortable living as a family. More immediately, he was exhausted. His body needed rest.

He slept soundly until someone opened his door the following morning. Slowly, he opened his eyes.

Zuki stood there, neatly dressed, come to wake him. She wore light makeup and a subtle fragrance.

You look beautiful today, Ethan said before he could stop himself.

He was not given to sweet talk with other women. Zuki was different now.

Her lips curved at praise from the man she liked, though she still gave him a pointed look. She could change for someone she cared about without ceasing to be herself. That proud spirit was part of what made her appealing.

Get up. Everyone's waiting for you at breakfast.

Ethan dressed and washed while she waited. Then they went side by side to the dining room.

There he saw May, Naoko, and Sayo at close range for the first time in what felt like ages. So much had happened in two days. He had glimpsed them from across the courtyard before lunch yesterday, but sharing a room again felt different.

The others reacted to his arrival in their own ways.

Miki greeted him with a nod, a shy smile, and a faint blush. She seemed to have accepted what had happened. Kuni looked much the same, though she was more embarrassed and quickly turned her eyes away.

May, Naoko, and Sayo tried to act as though they knew nothing. Their darting eyes and tense expressions betrayed them.

Ethan cleared his throat and sat beside Miki, in the place a man heading the household might take.

The meaning was plain to Naoko and Sayo. They looked at Miki. She made no objection; she had even set out Ethan's bowl and chopsticks in advance. Their older sisters' relationship with him had changed profoundly.

Naoko and Sayo exchanged a glance. Would they have to call him their brother-in-law now? Their eldest sister's? Their second sister's? Their third sister's? It was hard to untangle.

Everyone's here, Miki said softly. Let's eat.

Thank you for the meal!

Breakfast was unusually quiet. They ate slowly, with only the sounds of chopsticks touching plates and people chewing. After the last two days, the stillness was welcome. They needed time to adjust to one another.

For a moment, it felt like sitting with a real family. Some awkwardness remained, but Ethan thought that would ease with time.

May liked the atmosphere too. She was used to following Ethan from place to place, and Miki, Kuni, and Zuki all treated her warmly.

After breakfast, Miki and Kuni cleared the dishes. They returned, and everyone sat together around the table to talk.

Miki asked the question on their minds. Ethan, how long do you plan to stay?

Using only his given name still felt a little awkward to her. She was older than he was, they were not married, and she did not want to speak to him too intimately in front of Naoko and Sayo. She settled on Ethan. He would not have minded any name spoken with affection.

He thought for a moment as the five sisters watched him.

You know I have two things ahead of me: my battle with Brandon and May's Grand Festival. Brandon hasn't contacted me yet, so there's no need to rush to him. The Grand Festival is still some time away, and May can practice well here. I'd like to stay a few more days.

Miki and the others breathed easier. None wanted him to leave so soon. Now that their relationships had changed, the older sisters would have liked him to remain for good, though they knew that was impossible.

May smiled as well. Naoko and Sayo had helped her improve quickly, and she could feel the difference. She also loved the food here.

Ethan looked around the table. Seeing Miki, Kuni, and Zuki so pleased that he would stay a little longer moved him. Their feelings for him were real.

He took three Great Balls from his belt pouch. One was marked with a flame, one with a water drop, and one with a lightning bolt. He set them on the table and looked at the three older sisters.

There's something I need to tell you too.

Chapter 882: A Place for the Three Legendary Beasts

Ethan's serious tone startled Miki, Kuni, and Zuki. They looked at the three Great Balls on the table.

Why have you brought out Poke Balls all of a sudden? Zuki asked.

Ethan glanced at Naoko and Sayo and hesitated.

The five were sisters who lived together. Now that he had defined his relationship with the three older women, the younger two would learn about it sooner or later. Some things could not be hidden in this house. He decided it was better to speak openly from the beginning.

He looked back at Miki, Kuni, and Zuki.

Since we're together now, there are things I should arrange. I want to give you some peace of mind, so you won't be left worrying when I travel again.

The three older sisters barely reacted. Naoko and Sayo, however, felt a jolt. They had suspected the truth, but hearing it from Ethan still startled them. All three of their sisters were with him.

One man with three partners was not a relationship the law would recognize. Was this really going to work?

Neither younger sister objected. They kept silent, marveling that Ethan had won over three women who had always held others to such high standards. Their feelings of envy were harder to explain.

Ethan caught their complicated looks. They know. How much had they seen? Surely they had not witnessed everything.

He glanced at May. She sat staring down at the table, pretending the subject had nothing to do with her. After Sabrina, Erika, Maya, and now the three sisters, perhaps she had grown used to his tangled relationships.

Miki, Kuni, and Zuki were still studying the Great Balls. One of them laughed lightly. What are these? Don't tell me you've brought us Pokemon as gifts.

May thought of something, particularly when she saw the ball marked with a flame. Ethan, are you going to...?

The older sisters caught her alarm. Perhaps the balls held something more significant than they had guessed.

Ethan smiled. It's a remarkable coincidence. There are three of you and three Pokemon. This city is where their legend began. The Burned Tower, the Bell Towerit almost feels as if our meeting was meant to happen.

Three Pokemon, an old legend, and Ecruteak's towers. The sisters could think of only one possibility.

Zuki looked at the balls. Are those...?

Yes, Ethan said. They hold Entei, Raikou, and Suicunethe three legendary beasts.

Silence fell. Every face showed disbelief. No one knew what to say. Even May had not known Ethan had Raikou and Suicune.

He has those two as well as Entei? And the three legendary birds? There were Deoxys and Celebi too. How many Pokemon don't I know about?

Ethan looked around the table. You don't believe me?

It's not that, Miki said with a strained smile. It's simply astonishing.

He spoke with complete seriousness, yet the claim was hard to grasp. For most people, legendary Pokemon remained distant figures in stories. Not everyone encountered them as often as Ethan or Ash did.

Rather than explain further, Ethan picked up the Great Ball marked with a water drop. He aimed it toward the open courtyard and pressed its button.

Blue light shot through the dining room and out into the yard. As it faded, Suicune appeared.

The Pokemon's long, elegant form seemed part leopard, part deer, part mythical beast. It carried a noble air, as if a veil of moisture surrounded it.

Ethan knew Suicune well, and May was surprised only so much. The five sisters could no longer stay composed. Miki, Kuni, and Zuki held their surprise in their expressions, but Naoko and Sayo sprang to their feet.

They had grown up in Johto hearing stories of the three legendary beasts. Their own performances retold those legends. The beasts meant more to them than they did to most people.

It really is Suicune, Miki murmured. Minutes earlier she could not have imagined meeting it this way.

I can hardly believe my eyes, Kuni said.

Suicune looked around, found a comfortable place in the courtyard, and lay down. Its calm behavior finally helped the sisters accept that Ethan truly had it.

They turned to the two remaining Great Balls. If this one held Suicune, the others must hold Raikou and Entei.

Miki shook her head and gave Ethan a searching look. You keep finding ways to surprise us. How did you come to have all three?

It seems we've chosen an extraordinary man, Kuni said with a smile.

Three regional League titles and all three legendary beasts were feats most people could not hope to achieve. Zuki felt more certain than ever of her choice. He was every bit the man she had seen in him.

Ethan pushed the Great Ball marked with a flame toward Miki.

She looked up at him.

Miki, you have a Flareon. You must be fond of Fire-type Pokemon. Entei represents fire, so I thought it would suit you.

No, no. She hurriedly shook her head. I couldn't possibly accept it.

Before they knew what the balls held, the sisters could joke about Pokemon gifts. Now they knew they held legendary Pokemon. They could hardly treat them as presents.

Ethan picked up Entei's ball and placed it firmly in her hand.

Don't worry. We're family now. There's no need to keep score over what's yours and what's mine. I'm not giving Entei away. I'd like its mistress to look after it and let it keep you company while I'm gone. If I need it, I'll call it back.

The sisters understood. So long as they remained together, they could share in caring for his Pokemon. If that changed someday, the beasts would return to him.

I understand. Miki closed her fingers around the ball. I'll take good care of it.
