Be careful, Ethan added. I only caught Entei recently. We haven't had time to build a deep bond, and it might not always listen.

Leave it to me, she said with a smile.

Ethan picked up Suicune's now-empty Great Ball and handed it to Kuni.

You have a Vaporeon, so Suicune suits you. Will you look after it for me? It's gentle, and it's been with me the longest. I think the two of you will get along.

I...all right.

Miki's acceptance made it easier for Kuni. She gave Ethan a warm smile, took the ball, and looked toward Suicune in the courtyard with delight.

Finally, Ethan offered Raikou's Great Ball to Zuki. She took it without ceremony or even a thank-you, though the smile at the corners of her eyes gave her away.

Ethan knew her temperament and was not offended. It's a pity your Eevee evolved into Umbreon, so their types don't match. But you and Raikou both have fiery tempers. I think you'll get along.

Hmph. You're the one with a fiery temper.

The three balls were now in the sisters' hands. For the time being, Entei, Suicune, and Raikou would remain in Ecruteak. Ethan would call them back whenever he needed them.

Miki, Kuni, and Zuki looked at the Great Balls they held. The responsibility felt heavy, and the moment almost unreal.

Naoko and Sayo watched Ethan hopefully, as if waiting for something from him too. But he had no other Pokemon to place in their care.

As for you two, he said apologetically, we'll have to see about that another time.

Their disappointment was plain. They understood why he had entrusted valuable Pokemon to the sisters who were now his partners, yet they could not help feeling envious. Neither was quite sure what she envied most.

Ethan cleared his throat and brought everyone's attention back to him.

These are the three legendary beasts, he told Miki, Kuni, and Zuki. I know what they mean to people in Johto. Please keep them out of public view. And don't neglect their training while they're here. I'd like them to learn to work together, perhaps even develop a coordinated technique.

After catching Entei, Ethan had considered using the three beasts against Brandon's three Regis. But Entei was new to him. It would take time for the three to work as a team; for now, a lack of coordination might become a weakness. His three legendary birds were a more reliable choice for the coming battle.

Leaving the beasts here offered them a chance to learn to cooperate.

The three sisters nodded. A Trainer at Ethan's level faced challenges ordinary Trainers did not. Pokemon as powerful as the legendary beasts might be needed, and they could not afford to let the trio grow idle.

I'll buy a Poke Ball transfer machine in the next few days, Miki said. Whenever you need them, we'll send the three beasts to you at once.

Then she frowned, as if remembering something. Before Ethan could ask, she laughed.

With all the excitement, I nearly forgot. Zuki, don't you have the Clear Bell our family has passed down for generations?

The Clear Bell?

Ethan suddenly realized there was something he had overlooked.

Zuki smiled too. It's been sitting in storage so long it must be covered in dust. I might have forgotten it myself. She turned to Ethan. You don't know our family's history yet, do you? Perhaps there really was fate in our meeting. You became our partner and entrusted the three beasts to us. As it happens, we have something of our own to offer you in return.

Chapter 883: Taking Turns

Zuki left the dining room. A long while later, she returned carrying a finely made box.

Everyone looked at it. It had plainly been cleaned and looked almost new. Zuki opened it under their gaze.

A bell about the size of a fist rested on a soft lining. Its shape was ordinary enough, but its material was not. Despite its earthy yellow color, it was partly transparent.

Is that the Clear Bell? Sayo asked.

Apart from Miki, Kuni, and Zuki, no one had seen it before. Even Naoko and Sayo, familiar with their family's history, had not known the bell was kept in their home.

Zuki nodded and began to tell Ethan and May a story from long ago.

Seven hundred years earlier, the people of Ecruteak had built two towers, one to the east and one to the west, as monuments to friendship between humans and Pokemon. Both commanded magnificent views. The eastern tower called Pokemon to wakefulness, while the western tower brought them sleep. Ho-Oh and Lugia lived atop them.

Then, a hundred and fifty years ago, lightning struck the western tower. It burned for three days and nights. Rain finally put out the fire, but little of the building remained. Three unknown Pokemon died in the blaze. Ho-Oh descended and used a mysterious power to restore them to life.

That was the familiar story of the three legendary beasts. Zuki had more to tell.

Our ancestors built the towers, she said. For generations, our family served as guardians and attendants of Ho-Oh and Lugia. But after the fire, everything changed. People feared Pokemon that could control life and death. Some wanted to subdue them by force; others wanted that power for themselves. Ho-Oh, Lugia, and the three beasts left Ecruteak and disappeared.

She continued, With both Pokemon gone and one tower destroyed, our family lost heart. Our ancestors left the towers and moved to this estate. We've lived here ever since.

Zuki took the Clear Bell from its box and placed it before Ethan.

We no longer serve Ho-Oh and Lugia as our ancestors did, but we've kept this bell. We hoped it might one day call Ho-Oh back.

Yet I've never heard a story of Ho-Oh returning to Ecruteak, Ethan said, touching his chin. So no one in your family has managed to summon it?

Kuni nodded ruefully. They've tried countless times over a hundred and fifty years. Ho-Oh never answered. Eventually our family grew tired of trying. By our generation, no one made the attempt. That's why the bell was left in storage.

It also explained why Naoko and Sayo had not known the family possessed it.

I had no idea your family had such a history. Ethan picked up the bell and turned it in his hands. Is this what you meant when you said you could offer me something in return?

The three older sisters exchanged a look. Miki answered.

After so many failures, our family came to believe the bell needed something more to draw Ho-Oh's attention. You've brought the three legendary beasts. They have a connection to Ho-Oh. That connection may be what was missing.

Ethan understood. With Entei, Raikou, and Suicune here, the sisters hoped the Clear Bell could summon Ho-Oh.

He set the bell back on the table and smiled. Why do you think I want to meet Ho-Oh?

The women stared at him.

It's Ho-Oh, Zuki said. Don't you want to catch it?

The three sisters' perspective had changed quickly. Before becoming close to Ethan, they would have scorned anyone who spoke of capturing Ho-Oh. Such a person would have seemed arrogant and unworthy of the legendary Pokemon.

Now they were encouraging Ethan to do it. Others might not be capable, but surely their partner was.

Catch Ho-Oh? Ethan shook his head.

If he fought it in earnest, could he capture it? He thought he probably could. Apart from Pokemon on Arceus's level, and a few with unusual forms or Mega Evolution, very little in this world could withstand Rayquaza and Deoxys together. He had other powerful Pokemon waiting besides.

But did he need Ho-Oh?

It was undeniably strong. Its power to restore life, its golden appearance, and its rarity made it a dream for many Trainers. Ethan saw the appeal.

He also saw the trouble. If word of its capture spread, Pokemon hunters and criminal organizations would target him. Ordinary Trainers would crowd around him to challenge him or seize it. Travel would become a struggle.

And Ho-Oh had lived for thousands of years. A Pokemon with its own ways would hardly sit quietly in a Poke Ball or willingly submit to a human. Even if captured, it might come out on its own and resume roaming the world.

That did not mean Ethan would refuse a truly excellent opportunity. At present, though, he saw no need to pursue it.

The sisters were surprised by his indifference.

You aren't interested in Ho-Oh? Miki asked.

It's more complicated than that. Ethan gave a short snort and told them how Ho-Oh had interfered when he first tried to catch the three beasts.

Only then did the sisters learn he had already crossed paths with it.

So we don't need to summon Ho-Oh? Kuni asked.

Why not? Ethan grinned. Ho-Oh and I still have unfinished business. It escaped last time. If we have a chance to meet again, I won't waste it. I don't plan to catch it now, but I do want to show it what I can do.

The sisters laughed. He could hold a grudge even against Ho-Oh. For all his strength, there was something boyish about his determination to fight it.

His answer also eased their minds. They had suggested capturing Ho-Oh for Ethan's sake, but it was a symbol of Johto. If possible, they would rather see it remain free.

Let's try summoning it after midnight, Miki said. Most people will be asleep. There'll be less chance of drawing a crowd. And we'd love to see Ho-Oh for ourselves.

With the time settled, they talked eagerly about the plan. After a while, Miki, Kuni, and Zuki each left to spend time with the legendary beast entrusted to her.

May took Naoko and Sayo back to her performance practice. In moments, Ethan was alone in the room.

He shook his head, drank a few more cups of tea, and watched the courtyard for a while. At last he stretched and returned to his guest room. After the last two days' exertion and a full breakfast, he was sleepy again. A nap would help him prepare for the meeting with Ho-Oh after midnight.

He had just spread his bedding when the sliding door opened. Miki came in.

Weren't you getting to know Entei? he asked, surprised. Why are you here?

Miki closed the door behind her and sat beside him, a faint blush on her cheeks.

I fed it. Flareon is keeping it company now. Entei still seems wary of me, but I think time will help it trust me.

That's good. These things take time.

Ethan did not ask why she had come. Their relationship had changed abruptly, and they hardly knew each other as partners. She probably wanted a private conversation. It would be strange to share a life with him without knowing where he came from, who his family was, or what his past had been like.

They began to talk. Miki asked about his life without making him feel interrogated, guiding the conversation naturally toward what she wanted to know. Ethan admired her tact.

He learned about her interests, preferences, and the years that had brought her here. Their understanding of each other deepened.

As they talked beside the bedding, Ethan found himself drawn to her. They were partners now, and he reached for her hand. Miki let him hold it. He drew her into his arms and kissed her.

It was the first time he had kissed Miki while fully clearheaded. She closed her eyes shyly and returned the kiss.

They lay down together.

...

Afterward, Ethan was no longer sleepy. He dressed, folded the bedding, and watched Miki leave with a shy face and unsteady steps.

I couldn't resist.

He shook his head at himself. Since accepting the three sisters as partners, his self-restraint seemed to be failing him.

What should he do now?

He heard another set of light footsteps outside. At first he thought Miki had forgotten something. These steps sounded softer. A moment later, Kuni slid the door open and came in, looking shy.

Ethan stared. The two sisters had missed each other by perfect timing.

There was little doubt why Kuni had come. Like Miki, she wanted time alone to know him better. Ethan spoke with her and shared much of what he had just told Miki.

Before long, their conversation led them back to the bedding. Ethan was young and had had a few minutes to rest. Compared with the last two days, that felt like plenty.

The poor bedding had barely been folded before he spread it again. The room looked much as it had earlier, though the woman beside him was different.

...

Kuni left on unsteady feet. Ethan was more awake than ever. He dressed again and folded the bedding once more.

He had only just finished when the door opened for a third time. Zuki stood there.

Before stepping inside, she sniffed the air. What is that smell? It's strong. She understood immediately and gave a sharp little snort. My sisters were here before me, weren't they? And you had a fine time with both.

Ethan could only shrug.

Despite her words, Zuki came in. Like Miki and Kuni, she closed the sliding door behind her.

Chapter 884: May in a Kimono

Ethan did eventually fall asleep. When he woke again, evening had come and Zuki was gone.

He stared at the clear impression she had left beside him, then shook his head with a helpless smile. He had spent time with all three sisters again. This time they had come to him one by one, but the outcome was much the same.

There was one difference: they had all chosen it freely and with clear minds. That changed how it felt to him.

Still, Zuki could have woken him before leaving. Perhaps she had thought he was sleeping too soundly.

May arrived outside the door just then to call him to dinner. The disordered bedding and lingering scent in the room seemed to tell her what had happened. She stood outside, blushing, and called softly without coming in.

I heard you, Ethan answered.

He stretched, dressed, and followed her toward the dining room. On the way he asked how her practice was going.

I've improved a lot, May said confidently. I'm sure I'll do better at the Grand Festival!

Her confidence made Ethan look forward to seeing her perform. She might not win the whole competition, but after this training, she was bound to leave an impression.

In the dining room, Miki, Kuni, and Zuki greeted him. Miki and Kuni gave him gentle smiles. All three still looked a little flushed, and Ethan felt a private sense of satisfaction.

Then he noticed their clothes. They wore formal kimonos, hair ornaments, and light makeup. Naoko and Sayo were dressed the same way.

Why are you all dressed up? Do you have a performance tonight?

Idiot. Zuki put a hand to her forehead. We're summoning Ho-Oh tonight. Remember?

Ho-Oh? What does that have to do with your clothes?

Zuki, just tell him, Miki said, stepping in before her sister could tease him further. She turned to Ethan. Our family traditionally wore ceremonial dress when making offerings or calling to the legendary Pokemon. We no longer perform those rites, but we're going to summon Ho-Oh tonight. It feels right to honor the custom.

I see. Ethan nodded. I have to say, you all look beautiful in kimonos, however many times I see you wear them.

All five sisters blushed. Miki, Kuni, and Zuki were still new to their relationship with him; praise from Ethan carried weight. Naoko and Sayo kept stealing shy glances at him too.

Ethan noticed May sitting quietly off to one side in her everyday clothes. He remembered how much she had admired the sisters' costumes when they first arrived.

Do you have a kimono that would fit May? he asked. Why don't you help her dress for tonight too?

Me? May looked up, startled. Then warmth spread through her. Ethan had remembered what she had said about the kimonos.

Of course, Kuni said, looking her over. You're about Naoko's size. We still have a kimono she wore a couple of years ago. Come with me.

May blushed at being measured in front of Ethan, but she followed Kuni happily. Naoko and Sayo went along too, curious to see her dressed and made up.

The dining room grew quieter. Ethan ate and talked with Miki and Zuki. Before long, the others returned.

May looked transformed. The hair at the back of her head was gathered with a pretty clip. She wore light makeup and an orange kimono that reached her ankles. It had few ornaments or patterns, giving it a simple elegance that suited her.

Ta-da! Sayo clapped. Look who we have here!

May turned once in front of Ethan, a little self-conscious, then looked at him expectantly.

He applauded. You look lovely, May. It suits you.

He meant it. The outfit lent her a more composed air. Miki and Zuki nodded in approval too and told her how pretty she looked. May beamed at the compliments and sat down to eat.

Everyone was comfortable enough together now to enjoy dinner. By the time they finished, it was past eight. Night covered the city, the moon hung at an angle in the sky, and a murmur of activity had risen outside.

Midnight was still hours away. Ethan appeared calm, but everyone else was restless. To most people, a legendary Pokemon was something from a tale; Ho-Oh, so rare and so important to Johto, felt more distant still. The thought that they might summon it tonight made sitting still difficult.

They talked to pass the time. By a little after ten, Ethan could see they were too distracted to stay inside. He led them out into the city early.

Ecruteak was an appealing place to live. Its old buildings gave it a sense of history, and life moved at a slower pace. At night there were no bright clubs or dazzling signs. Instead, a busy pedestrian street filled with small vendors and their stalls.

Usually the Kimono Sisters hesitated to go out even this late. Almost everyone in Ecruteak knew them, and many had watched their performances. They had a great many admirers.

Tonight they wore no heavy stage makeup, and no spotlight shone on them. Most pedestrians were looking at the stalls. Many women on the street wore kimonos too. In the dim, lanternlike light, few people paid the sisters close attention.

A passerby might notice a group of beautiful women and realize ten steps later that they looked familiar. Even so, the sisters kept to the less crowded parts of the street.

Walking behind Ethan, Miki watched the crowd and listened to the vendors calling out. It's been so long since we went out like this. I've missed it.

Me too, Kuni said. Since our shows became popular, we've barely had an evening just to wander.

Is it this lively every night? Ethan asked.

Not every night, Miki said. You came at a good time. Ecruteak is celebrating a traditional festival. There'll be a big fireworks display later.

Fireworks. Ethan filed that away, thinking of their plan for midnight.

Zuki gave him a sidelong look. We have someone to thank for these days off, don't we?

She meant him, of course. Ethan pinched her lightly as he passed, drawing an indignant look, then moved ahead laughing. He could hardly dispute that he was the reason their shows had been canceled.

At a mask stall, he bought one for each of the five sisters. Once they put them on, they no longer had to worry about being recognized.

The group continued along the street toward Bell Tower. Naoko and Sayo were especially delighted. They rarely had a chance to browse at leisure. Before long, their hands were full of trinkets and snacks, and they had tried games where visitors shot at balloons or tossed rings for prizes.

Everyone seemed to be enjoying themselves.

May and the two younger sisters stopped before a vendor selling Magikarp. They crouched to watch the Pokemon leap in a basin. Ethan watched for a moment too, then glanced around.

For an instant he thought he saw Ho-Oh. It was only a kite shaped like the Pokemon, wound with strings of little lights.

A neat-looking boy of seven or eight with a bowl haircut carried it through the crowd, heading alone toward Bell Tower. The kite was long and awkward for him. As he passed Ethan, one wing came loose and fell.

Ethan looked down. The wing had been fixed to the body with tape. Even if the kite managed to rise, it would probably come apart in the air.

He bent, picked up the wing, and handed it to the boy.

Oh, thank you. The child took it in a fluster and tried several times to put it back. It would not stay. Worry spread over his face.

Miki and the others had noticed and came over. With tonight's ceremony on her mind, Miki crouched beside him.

Why do you have a Ho-Oh kite, little one? Where are you taking it?

It was late for flying a kite, even during a festival. Lanterns would have been less surprising.

The boy looked nervous surrounded by the dressed-up women in Pokemon masks. Then he saw May's bright smile and blushed. He glanced at her once more before answering haltingly.

I'm taking it to Bell Tower. I want Grandpa to see Ho-Oh again.

Again? Kuni asked. Has your grandfather seen Ho-Oh before?

He has! The boy nodded. At home there's a photo of him when he was young, with a Rainbow Wing. He's looked for Ho-Oh for years, but he hasn't found it again. He's started to give up.

His voice grew quieter. It hurt him to see his grandfather lose hope in a lifelong dream.

I see, Kuni said. You hoped seeing a lit-up Ho-Oh kite would encourage him to keep looking?

Yes! If he sees Ho-Oh flying in the sky, he'll be like he used to be.

He looked at the broken kite and sighed. But it won't fly tonight.

I'm not sure a kite with lights could convince him, Ethan said. You'd at least need a Pokemon such as Fearow dressed up to look the part.

He turned toward Bell Tower, waving without looking back. Go home for now. Tonight, you and your grandfather will get your wish. Ho-Oh really will appear.

Chapter 885: Ho-Oh, We Meet Again!

They passed through the lively food street, left the city center, and followed Bellchime Trail through a wood filled with red and yellow maple leaves all year round. At last Ethan and the others reached Bell Tower.

Compared with the bustling center of Ecruteak, the place was remarkably quiet tonight. The occasional hoot of a bird Pokemon sounded from the trees. Otherwise there was an almost frightening silence, without so much as a light in sight.

However many years the tower had stood here, the locals seldom came out to it at night, even during a festival. By day, tourists visiting Ecruteak for the first time made their way to the famous landmark. After dark, the thought of the fire more than a century ago made the place feel rather eerie.

That suited Ethan and his companions.

He had been here once before, but he still took a moment to look over Bell Tower. It was a Japanese-style tower of nine stories, built within a fortified compound on a hill outside the city. From its top, a visitor could see all of Ecruteak. The city's distant festivities were still faintly audible.

With no one else around, the five sisters removed their masks. They switched on their flashlights and approached the compound's gate in the moonlight.

The compound resembled a castle. In former times, regional lords had surrounded their residences and keeps with walls to protect themselves and their families. The sisters' ancestors had not been such lords, but they had built similar defenses around the two towers.

The family had left the compound over a decade ago. Monks now cared for it and opened it to visitors during the day. Tonight the gates were shut.

Miki started toward the gate to knock, but Ethan stopped her. We're here to summon Ho-Oh. We should avoid drawing attention if we can.

That's true. Kuni looked at the closed gate above its dozen or so steps, then at the high stone walls. How do we get in?

With a Pokemon, of course! Ethan took out a Poke Ball and grinned. You've spent too long in polite society. Trainers don't always take the usual route.

The sisters exchanged glances. Entering without a word to the monks in the middle of the night felt improper. It also gave them a little thrill. Their lives were usually lived under spotlights and according to rules; they had rarely done anything so furtive.

A flash of blue light released Ethan's Gardevoir. With Teleport, it carried them silently past the walls and into the compound.

Inside, the silence was deeper still. They could no longer hear even the bird Pokemon. Miki and her sisters looked as though they expected to be caught at any moment, but Ethan caught the excitement in their eyes too. Amused, he said nothing and went with them into Bell Tower.

Moonlight lit the grounds outside. The tower's closed windows kept almost all of it from reaching the interior. Their flashlights revealed a broad, mostly empty space with a faint smell of aged wood.

The building was well cared for, yet its floorboards creaked under their feet. Every sound echoed through the hollow tower, adding to the unease.

Sayo was the sort of person who wanted company even on a nighttime trip to the bathroom. The tower sent a shiver through her, though having everyone close by kept her fear in check.

Ethan's flashlight swept across a wall and found a large wood carving of Ho-Oh. The Pokemon spread its wings before a rainbow and auspicious clouds, soaring toward the sun. It looked noble and imposing.

The likeness was good, he had to admit. Given his quarrel with Ho-Oh, he spared it only a glance.

A few minutes of climbing brought them to the ninth floor. Beyond it lay the roof. They emerged onto the outdoor platform, where cool night air immediately brushed their faces.

A huge brass-colored finial rose from the tower's summit. Its shape was peculiar, and Ethan could not tell what purpose it served. Perhaps centuries ago it had been part of Ho-Oh's dwelling.

They spent a while looking out over Ecruteak, then gathered together again. Zuki took the Clear Bell from the box she had carried with her.

Even up here, the strange transparent bell showed no change. She shook it hard, but it made no sound.

Just like before, Miki said. It still needs a catalyst. She turned to Ethan. Shall we begin?

Wait a little. He looked toward the sky above Ecruteak. When do the fireworks you mentioned start?

About now. Miki checked the time. They mark the end of the night market. Most people go home after the display.

As she spoke, streaks of color rose above the city and burst into brilliant flowers. Within moments, fireworks filled the sky, bathing Ecruteak in shifting colors. Their reports reached the tower despite the distance.

Ethan nodded to the sisters. Now.

They understood his timing. The fireworks would help conceal Ho-Oh's arrival from ordinary people, both in the sky and beneath the noise of the explosions. The display would not last long, so they set to work at once.

From their robes, the sisters brought out strands of fur from Raikou, Suicune, and Entei. The three legendary beasts did not have to stand here in person. Something from each of them, infused with their power, would serve as a catalyst for the Clear Bell, much as Ho-Oh's own Rainbow Wing could.

Holding the fur, the five sisters stood together in the middle of the platform and began to dance. Their steps matched precisely. In their splendid ceremonial dress, their graceful movement made a beautiful sight.

This was their family's ritual for calling Ho-Oh: a particular dance accompanied by the rhythmic shaking of the bell. As Zuki moved it gently, the Clear Bell finally gave a bright, clear chime. The fur of the three beasts glowed faintly in answer.

The fireworks thundered over Ecruteak, and the chime could be heard only nearby. Yet Ethan felt as if its sound had passed through earth and sky and was traveling ever farther away.

He had once asked Miki what would happen if Ho-Oh was too distant to hear it. Ho-Oh did not stay in one place for long; it might be in another region altogether.

Don't worry, she had told him with complete confidence. The Clear Bell has a special power. Ho-Oh gave it to our family as a token of its promise when it lived in Bell Tower. Its sound rings directly in Ho-Oh's heart. Wherever it is, once it hears the bell, it will come.

Her ancestors must have made that agreement with Ho-Oh centuries before the fire at Brass Tower and passed it down ever since.

Even if the bell failed, Ethan had another option. He could bring out all three beasts together and let their power call Ho-Oh. That was why he had dared promise the little boy on the food street that Ho-Oh would appear tonight.

The sisters continued their measured dance, their expressions intent and their gestures unhurried. Now and then a movement revealed a pale wrist beneath a sleeve.

Ethan took out his camera. Five sisters dancing atop a tower against a night sky full of fireworks were too lovely a sight to let pass without a photograph.

The shutter had barely clicked when something changed overhead. A golden shape broke through the clouds.

Even at night, its brilliant body shone like the sun. There was no mistaking it. Ho-Oh had come.

Rainbow light spilled from its feathers as it beat its wings and flew toward Bell Tower, a bright presence cutting through the dark.

Ethan's gaze sharpened. With a turn of his wrist, he brought three Great Balls into his hand.

The sisters stopped dancing as Ho-Oh descended. Zuki alone continued to shake the Clear Bell softly. All five looked up at the beautiful bird in awe.

To Ethan, Ho-Oh looked rather like a Fearow with finer feathers. He knew that judgment was colored by the dispute between them, but he could hardly view it impartially.

Ho-Oh came to a hover more than ten meters from the rooftop. It looked first at the Clear Bell, then at the sisters and the fur of the three beasts in their hands. Finally, its gaze settled on Ethan.

Ethan remembered Ho-Oh well, and Ho-Oh remembered him. Few humans in all its long years had made such an impression. This was the man whose attempt to catch the three beasts it had once stopped.

Now the sisters held the beasts' fur. Ho-Oh sensed the beasts' presence on them, along with traces of Ethan's. It understood that he had caught them after all.

It also remembered the bell. Though it had not heard that summons for a very long time, it had honored the old promise and come. It had not expected the people who once worshiped it to be standing with this man.

Ho-Oh gave a high cry and looked down at Ethan, studying him. Ethan met its gaze.

Surprised? You stopped me last time, but I caught them in the end. And now we meet again!

He threw the three Great Balls. Blue light flashed across the sky as Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres appeared around Ho-Oh. The three birds cried out and began circling it.

Ethan had told the sisters about these Pokemon while explaining his history with Ho-Oh. They knew he had them. Seeing all three legendary birds before their eyes still left them astonished and proud of him.

Ho-Oh felt the hostility in the birds' gazes at once. It ignored them for the moment and kept watching Ethan. A voice with a quiet authority, neither distinctly male nor female, sounded in his mind.

Human. Why have you summoned me?

Ethan hesitated. He could hardly say that he had called Ho-Oh here to fight it and settle his grievance from last time, even if that was what he intended.

I want to test myself against you, he said instead. As a Trainer, I want to keep growing stronger. You can see that I've gathered all three beasts. Now it's time for us to have a proper battle.

To his surprise, Ho-Oh took his challenge seriously.

You are indeed worthy of challenging me. I accept.

As its telepathic words faded, Ho-Oh's presence shifted. Light blazed from its body, and it readied itself to fight.

The sisters had not heard Ho-Oh's answer, but Ethan's words and the change in the air told them a battle was about to begin. They watched wide-eyed, eager to see how their man would face a Pokemon more legendary than legend itself. Zuki, especially, could not look away.

Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres cried out together. Their own fighting spirit surged, and all three turned in the air and charged straight at Ho-Oh.

Chapter 886: Birds, Birds, Birds!

Bang!

Fireworks burst over Ecruteak City, announcing the start of the battle.

Beneath their shifting colors, Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres closed in on Ho-Oh and attacked.

Ho-Oh, like Moltres, was Fire and Flying type. Of the three legendary birds, only Zapdos had a type advantage against it. Moltres and Ho-Oh would resist each other's Fire attacks, while Articuno was vulnerable to Ho-Oh's flames.

That was the theory. A real battle was rarely so simple.

After so much time training and fighting together, Ethan's three birds worked as a team. When he faced a powerful opponent, he sent them out together.

He could have challenged Ho-Oh with Deoxys, Rayquaza, or even his newly trained Charizard. But a fight with any one of them would cause an even greater disturbance. He was not trying to catch Ho-Oh, so there was no need to go all out.

Besides, these were the birds Ho-Oh had fought when it restored the three legendary beasts, ruining Ethan's attempt to catch them. The birds deserved a chance to settle that score themselves. That was why they had glared at Ho-Oh the moment they appeared.

Ethan was not the only one who resented that encounter. The three birds had their pride too. They were all great birds of the sky. Why should Ho-Oh stand so far above them? Tonight they meant to bring it down from its lofty perch.

Articuno fired an Ice Beam carrying a bitter chill. Moltres launched a blazing Flamethrower. Zapdos unleashed a powerful Thunderbolt. Three differently colored attacks streaked toward Ho-Oh from three directions.

Ho-Oh's strength lay beyond any one move. Its vast reserves of energy and the ways it could wield them set it apart. In a game, Pokemon might be measured by numbers. In the world before Ethan, a being like Ho-Oh could exercise powers ordinary Pokemon simply did not possess.

The three birds were formidable in their own right, but Ho-Oh still had an edge. An unseen force surged from its body and met all three attacks at once, stopping and canceling them.

Boom!

The explosion drowned out the fireworks. Its report carried all the way toward Ecruteak. People watching the display heard it and assumed an unusually large firework had gone off. They searched the sky, saw nothing to account for that particular sound, and soon returned their attention to the colors overhead.

Ho-Oh counterattacked at once. It climbed sharply, cried out, and poured Sacred Fire down across the sky. The flames spread wide enough to engulf all three birds.

The night turned red. From the roof of Bell Tower, the descending fire looked like an enormous net falling over the tower itself.

For the first time, Miki and her sisters saw the power of a legendary Pokemon at close range. They worried that the flames would reach everyone on the roof.

Each of the three birds used its own power to fend off the broad attack. None was hurt. But broken remnants of Sacred Fire kept falling toward Bell Tower.

Gardevoir raised both hands. An invisible barrier appeared above the tower and caught every remaining flame before it could reach them.

Fire spread across the barrier, briefly hiding the battle from view. When it cleared, four great bird Pokemon had closed in and were fighting at close quarters.

Ho-Oh was strong enough to hold back the three birds with raw power. At close range, however, the balance shifted. It was not poor at fighting up close; it simply had only two talons and one beak against three opponents.

It drove Moltres away, only for Articuno to rake its back. When it turned on Articuno, Zapdos darted in at high speed to harry it. By the time it shook Zapdos off, Moltres had returned.

The three birds had grown since Ethan first caught them. Now at the height of their strength, they pressed Ho-Oh so hard that it could scarcely fend them off.

Ho-Oh circled Bell Tower, struggling to draw them out and make space. Its powerful body let it break free at last. Having learned what the birds could do up close, it kept moving and fought them with attacks from a distance.

That made the battle far more conspicuous.

In truth, Ho-Oh's first wave of Sacred Fire had already caught Ecruteak's attention. The enormous blaze had lit much of the night sky and even outshone the fireworks. At first, people thought the city had arranged another spectacle for the festival. A sky full of flame at this hour was certainly impressive.

Then observant residents and Pokemon Trainers began to doubt it. The lights above Bell Tower looked less like a planned show than Pokemon battling.

Many residents were content to watch from where they stood. Trainers were different. Whether it was a battle or a rare Pokemon, they wanted a closer look. At least several dozen people hurried toward Bell Tower.

One Trainer rushed past a detached house. His pounding footsteps and the shouts of nearby residents disturbed a little boy inside. The boy opened his window and saw fire fading from the sky.

In the combined light of fireworks and flame, his face was clear. It was the boy Ethan had met on the food street with the Ho-Oh kite.

What's that...?

He peered toward Bell Tower. Several colorful, glowing shapes like birds seemed to be chasing and grappling with one another above it. Why were Pokemon flying there so late? They were distant and hard to make out, but one of them looked terribly like Ho-Oh.

He remembered the man at the night market and what he had said. The boy's expression changed.

Could he have been telling the truth? Had Ho-Oh really appeared? And what were those other bird Pokemon around it?

Grandpa!

He ran into the house. A moment later he returned, pulling a thin, silver-haired old man along with him.

Kuriu, what is it? Slow down, slow down! the man protested.

Kuriu paid little heed to his grandfather's aging legs. He pointed at the sky. Grandpa, look! It's Ho-Oh! The real Ho-Oh!

Ho-Oh? The old man shook his head with a weary smile. He knew his grandson too well. He had noticed the boy's efforts to cheer him up, including the Ho-Oh kite he had secretly made. The care behind them touched him deeply. But he was old now, and that impossible dream ought to be left behind...

His eyes turned toward Bell Tower. They widened at once.

It... it really is Ho-Oh?

...

Thoom!

Back over the tower, a blast of Ho-Oh's fire tore through Articuno's icy power and shot straight at it.

Articuno had traveled and fought beside Ethan for a long time. It had faced opponents of this caliber before. Rather than linger after its own attack, it beat its wings and rose, escaping the flames.

Zapdos and Moltres moved into the space it left and renewed the assault. The legendary Pokemon tangled together once more. This was no battle that would end in moments.

Then Ethan sensed something and looked toward Ecruteak. From the height of the tower, by the flashes of fireworks and the city's lights, he could see figures racing through the woods of Bellchime Trail toward them.

People had noticed the fight and come to investigate. Most were probably energetic fellow Trainers. With a battle of this scale, their arrival was inevitable. Ethan had prepared for it.

He calmly took an Ultra Ball from his belt and pressed its button. Deoxys appeared beside him.

The sisters instinctively stepped back. In the darkness, the unfamiliar Pokemon's red-and-blue face and expressionless stare were unsettling. Fear came easily when faced with something unknown.

They knew it belonged to Ethan, though, and it merely floated there without threatening them. Their alarm faded into curiosity, and they began to study it.

Ethan pointed toward the approaching Trainers. See those people coming from that direction? Stop them. Don't let them interrupt the birds' battle. Use the same trick your counterpart used in LaRousse City.

Deoxys made a string of sounds Ethan could not interpret and turned toward Ecruteak.

Copies began separating from its body. In moments, dozens surrounded it. Without any further visible command, they flew together toward the approaching Trainers. The original Deoxys remained beside Ethan. There was no need for it to deal with these people personally.

Barely a dozen seconds later, the Trainers met the copies. They had come to watch the spectacle and perhaps seize an opportunity. The strange figures startled them, and when the copies attacked without warning, they had to fight back.

These Trainers had noticed the battle quickly and made it this far; they were capable enough to destroy copy after copy. But the swarm seemed endless. One fallen copy was replaced by two. After they defeated those two, four more appeared.

The battle in the sky was tantalizingly close. No matter how hard they fought, the Trainers could not advance another step.

Ethan turned his attention back to Ho-Oh and the three birds. He had stopped the first visitors, but more would notice once the fireworks ended. The battle needed to finish soon.

He raised his voice toward the sky. Enough playing around! Use Tri-Bird Assault!

Chapter 887: Battling Ho-Oh

The Pokemon overhead were in the thick of battle, but Ethan's command reached his three birds. They had been listening for it even as they fought.

Without hesitation, Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres climbed higher together. They began to circle in a rising spiral, drawing the sky around them into motion with their power.

They had used Tri-Bird Assault during Ethan's previous confrontation with Ho-Oh, when he was trying to catch the three legendary beasts. But the attack had been aimed at the beasts. Ho-Oh had arrived only after the birds struck, so Ethan did not know whether it had seen their combined technique.

For now, he assumed it had. Ho-Oh had appeared almost as soon as he defeated the beasts. Perhaps it had been watching from somewhere nearby all along.

Ho-Oh watched energy pour from the three birds, a trace of gravity entering its gaze. It had indeed seen this attack. Although it had been far away and felt only the last of its power, the sight had left a deep impression.

Ordinarily, Ho-Oh would not stand still beneath such an obviously devastating move. But it had accepted Ethan's challenge. It would not evade so readily. This was a test of whether that human truly deserved to possess all three beasts, and a trial of whether Ho-Oh itself could withstand the birds' strength.

Heavy clouds blotted out the stars and swallowed the moon. In moments, a spiraling mass of dark cloud hung over Bell Tower. Lightning flickered and thunder rolled within it.

On the roof, Kuni hesitated. What are the three birds doing? she asked Ethan quietly, as if a louder voice might draw the lightning down.

Using a combined attack we developed together, he said. It's immensely powerful. It can seriously hurt even a Pokemon like Ho-Oh.

A combined attack? Kuni had never heard of such a thing. She was impressed, but she could not help asking, Doesn't that make it dangerous for us to stay here?

Miki, Zuki, Naoko, and Sayo all looked at Ethan. They were not merely close to the danger. They stood almost directly beneath the heart of that ominous cloud. Whatever came downlightning or something elsemight miss Ho-Oh, but Bell Tower would surely lie in its path. The surrounding compound and forest were at risk too.

Kuni wanted reassurance. Instead, she found Ethan wearing a knowing smile.

Hold on, Zuki said. You did remember that we're standing here when you gave that order, didn't you?

Of course I did. I'd never disregard your safety. Ethan spread his hands, perfectly confident. Then he gave a small snort. This is also a trap for Ho-Oh.

A trap? Zuki asked. What do you mean?

What is this tower to Ho-Oh? Ethan looked at them. It used to live here. If it doesn't want its former home to end up like the Burned Tower, it can't dodge Tri-Bird Assault. It has to stop it.

The sisters understood. It was another way for Ethan to repay Ho-Oh for the trouble it had caused him. If Ho-Oh took the full force of the attack, it would likely be hurt, and Ethan would have his satisfaction.

But did he truly intend to gamble with Bell Tower?

What if it doesn't stop the attack? Miki asked. It left this place more than a hundred years ago. It may have abandoned it long since. If that's the case...

She did not finish. Bell Tower was no empty patch of wilderness. It was a famous landmark, one of Ecruteak's symbols, and the only one of the two great towers still standing. If the sisters helped destroy it, the whole city would blame them.

Don't worry. Ethan shrugged. Then we use Plan B.

Plan B? The sisters exchanged looks. Since when did you have a Plan B? Why didn't you tell us?

Since just now. Plan B is this Pokemon right here. He patted Deoxys on the shoulder, looking every bit like a man with an ace in hand.

The sisters studied Deoxys's expressionless face again. Could this strange Pokemon really stop the attack? They had never even heard of its kind. They could not know that Ethan's Deoxys had once withstood Tri-Bird Assault itself.

Ethan had no time to explain. He looked up at Ho-Oh. First, I'll need to give it another push.

He called toward the sky. Ho-Oh! This is the three birds' strongest attack. If you can take it, I'll acknowledge you as the strongest bird Pokemon in the world. If you can't, you'll have to watch your old home be destroyed. Show me what you choose!

It was a ruthless thing to say. Ethan had deliberately laid the choice before Ho-Oh: face the attack and risk injury, or move aside and let Bell Tower share the fate of the tower that burned more than a century ago.

High above, Ho-Oh seemed not to hear him. In truth, it had already decided. Even without his provocation, it would not retreat.

When Ho-Oh remained in place, Ethan knew his gambit had worked. Still, he turned to the sisters. Ho-Oh, Deoxys, and Gardevoir give us three safeguards, but this is dangerous. You should leave before the attack reaches us.

Zuki shook her head at once. I'm staying. She narrowed her eyes at him. What kind of woman leaves her man here alone? If you won't go, neither will I.

That was Zuki all over. Miki spoke up too. She's right. If you're staying, so are we. I trust you to protect us.

You two... Their faith warmed Ethan even as it moved him. They were not being careless or failing to understand the danger. They were putting their trust in him. If they chose to remain, he would respect it.

He looked back up. Tri-Bird Assault had finished gathering power and was ready to fall. Over Ecruteak, the fireworks were slowing; the night market was almost over.

Then let this attack mark the night's end.

Ethan signaled to the birds. At the same moment, Gardevoir and Deoxys raised protective barriers around the top of Bell Tower.

Beneath the clouds, the three birds drove the last of their power into the attack. Looking somewhat drained, they flew aside and out of its path.

A luminous torrent poured from the cloud like a waterfall through the darkness, descending toward Ho-Oh. It shone so brightly that everyone still on Ecruteak's streets noticed. People turned toward Bell Tower, pointing and talking among themselves.

Those who had already ventured close to the tower were more than curious. They were horrified.

One of them was Ecruteak's foremost Trainer and Gym Leader, Morty.

A minute or two earlier, Morty had sensed the clash between Ho-Oh and the three birds almost as soon as it began. He had rushed toward the tower with several other Trainers.

Ethan had spotted them crossing the woods. Deoxys's copies intercepted them before they could reach the tower.

Morty was the strongest Trainer among them. Though the ambush had caught him off guard, his Pokemon dispersed one copy after another. His Ghost types handled the strange attackers especially well, and from their behavior he began to suspect they used Psychic power.

But the copies kept coming. No matter how many he defeated, he could not clear a path through the forest. Bell Tower was near, yet he had been unable to take another step toward it. He had never encountered anything quite like this.

Morty understood why they had been stopped. Someone did not want them interfering with the battle above Bell Tower.

From this close, he could identify the combatants. He had never seen them in person, but as a Gym Leader he knew them at a glance: Ho-Oh, Articuno, Moltres, and Zapdos.

Ho-Oh, above all, was unmistakable to anyone raised in Johto. The three birds' distinctive forms revealed them just as plainly.

Why were they fighting? Why here? Questions crowded Morty's mind. The mysterious copies raised another: who controlled the Pokemon that had sent them, and what connection did that person have to the legendary birds?

The copies were not individually overwhelming, nor did they show many different attacks, but their endless numbers made them maddening opponents. Morty considered several names. Could it be Lance, Bruno, Will, or Karen? Some hidden figure no one knew? Team Rocket? None of the possibilities satisfied him.

The other Trainers gradually gathered around him. They knew their local Gym Leader, and unlike him they were ordinary Trainers nearing the limits of what they could withstand.

Mr. Morty! a sweating man asked anxiously. What are these Pokemon? I've never seen one before. Why are they attacking us?

Morty had questions of his own. Does your Pokedex have no information on them?

Nothing, a woman answered. It just says Unknown.

That might mean their Pokedex data was incomplete, or that the Pokemon was not native to Johto. Either way, they knew almost nothing about it.

Morty was about to speak when he felt something above them. He raised his headand saw a sight he would remember for the rest of his life.

Chapter 888: Ho-Oh's Blessing

What had Morty seen?

High above him, a beautiful waterfall of raw energy was pouring down, filling the sky over the forest. What was itsome Pokemon's attack? An extreme kind of weather no one had seen before?

Its many colors shone against the night. For a moment, Morty was so struck by its breathtaking beauty that he nearly forgot where he stood.

A panicked voice beside him snapped him back. Damn it! What is that thing?

Morty turned. The man who had questioned him earlier was staring upward, mouth open in disbelief. Only then did Morty grasp the danger they were in.

Whatever that lovely torrent was, they were within its reach. In perhaps a dozen seconds it would fall over them. With that much power behind it, they would be obliterated.

Get out of here! he shouted.

The other Trainers were already moving. They might not have Morty's strength, but the first people to race toward a disturbance had quick minds. By the time he finished the word out, he was the only one still standing there.

They had run fast. Morty spared the thought only an instant before whistling for his Ghost-type Pokemon and retreating toward Ecruteak himself. He had arrived with confidence and was leaving in a scramble.

He did not like it, but no one knew how far the falling energy would spread. The only sensible choice was to put as much distance between themselves and Bell Tower as possible.

As if they needed more trouble, Deoxys's strange copies chased after them. The copies seemed unconcerned about the approaching attack or their own survival. They drove the fleeing Trainers on through the woods.

There they met a second group coming from Ecruteak. These Trainers had noticed the battle later and lacked suitable Pokemon to ride, so they had only just arrived. Before they could learn what was happening, they saw people running for their lives, pursued by unknown figures, beneath that descending torrent of energy. Bewildered, they turned and ran too.

It felt much longer, but barely a dozen seconds had passed since Morty first saw the attack. The Trainers had not even cleared the forest when Ho-Oh met Tri-Bird Assault above Bell Tower.

Golden light flared from Ho-Oh's body. It flew straight into the falling power without a hint of hesitation.

Night seemed to vanish. A dazzling radiance burst from the collision and spread across the sky, turning everything above Ecruteak and for kilometers around a brilliant gold. Then came a continuous, hissing roar as the two forces burned against one another.

Morty glanced back at the sudden daylight. A violent shock wave knocked him off his feet and sent him into a maple tree. Around him, the other Trainers were thrown apart as well. They struggled up from the ground, shaken but alive.

Morty looked toward Bell Tower again. The heart of the light was so bright that his eyes stung. However long he stared, he could make out nothing within it.

Across Ecruteak, people in the streets and in their homes turned toward the glow, stunned and unable to understand what had happened. Kuriu was especially shaken. Somehow, he felt certain that the man he had met at the night market was behind it all. He wanted desperately to know who that man was and what was happening at Bell Tower.

...

On the tower roof, Deoxys and Gardevoir's barriers had kept both Bell Tower and the compound below intact. Ethan, the sisters, and May, sheltered at the center of their protection, were unharmed.

They could see no more through the blinding light than Morty could. But apart from a fierce wind, nothing fell toward them. Ho-Oh must have stopped Tri-Bird Assault.

That was an astonishing feat, though Ethan was not surprised it had managed it. The question was what state Ho-Oh would be in when the light cleared. Untouched? Badly battered? Hurt somewhere in between?

For half a minute the brilliance held. Once the attack's energy was spent, it gradually faded.

The clouded sky had been swept clean, as clear as freshly polished glass. Moonlight and stars appeared again, brighter than ever. Beneath them, Ho-Oh hovered high above the tower, beating its wings slowly.

Its feathers were scorched and blackened. Gone was its earlier splendor, and its body showed the marks of the blow. Yet it still flew steadily. The damage, for all its ugly appearance, had not incapacitated it.

Ethan had to admire its strength. This was only the second time a Pokemon had endured Tri-Bird Assault head-on.

Then Ho-Oh cried out. Light flashed across its body. In the moonlight Ethan watched every injury vanish within seconds, as if it had never been struck at all.

Ho-Oh descended and came to a hover before him, looking just as it had before the battle. Had it used a move like Recover, or drawn upon its extraordinary ability to restore life? Ethan could not tell. After seeing it revive the three beasts before, and now heal itself, he knew how formidable that power was.

He shook his head, a little envious. Even Ho-Oh could hardly use such an ability without limit; it must place a great strain on its body. Still, it was an almost unfair advantage. No wonder so many legends surrounded it.

Articuno, Zapdos, and Moltres followed, breathing hard, and surrounded Ho-Oh again. Perhaps because it was so close to Ethan, or because they needed time to recover from Tri-Bird Assault, they watched without attacking.

The technique had consumed much of their strength, but less than it had on earlier occasions. They had practiced together and grown accustomed to using it. Ethan could see that they still had enough left to fight if they had to.

He waved them back. Their attack had hit Ho-Oh, and he had seen it wounded, if only briefly. That settled his grievance. There was no need to press the fight further. At his signal, the birds withdrew and landed one after another on Bell Tower's roof.

Impressive. Ethan applauded Ho-Oh. You're only the second Pokemon I've seen come through that attack intact.

While he spoke, Miki and the others studied Ho-Oh at close range. It was as beautiful, imposing, and noble as they had imagined. Even the three legendary birds seemed less commanding beside it. There was no denying that.

Ho-Oh glanced at Deoxys. It sensed considerable power in the Pokemon, but Deoxys did not move, so Ho-Oh looked back at Ethan. Its voice sounded in his mind.

Human, the fact that your three Pokemon can perform such an attack shows that you have raised them well. They are strong. You have proved yourself worthy of possessing fire, water, and thunder together.

Fire, water, and thunder? Ethan took a moment to realize Ho-Oh meant Entei, Suicune, and Raikou. People called them the three legendary beasts; Ho-Oh reduced them to the powers they embodied. It had the standing to do so, and Pokemon did not necessarily use the names people gave their group.

Still, whether Ho-Oh approved was beside the point. Ethan had already caught them. Was it going to demand that he let them go?

Your approval isn't what matters, he said evenly. I caught them, and they truly are my Pokemon now.

Ho-Oh turned toward Miki, Kuni, and Zuki. Then why have you entrusted them to these attendants? I can sense the beasts with these three women.

Attendants must have been how Ho-Oh thought of the sisters' family. They had once made offerings to it and had kept its covenant for more than a century.

For all its long life, Ho-Oh seemed not to grasp the human idea of a family, or of husbands and wives sharing responsibility for one another's Pokemon.

I left the beasts here to protect my women and keep them company, Ethan said. If I need them, they'll still come to me. And isn't this for the best? All three remain in Johto, where their legend can continue.

The sisters could not hear Ho-Oh's questions, but Ethan's answer told them roughly what the two were discussing. To be called his women in front of May and their two younger sisters made Miki, Kuni, and Zuki blush. It warmed them too. He had left such precious Pokemon with them because he cared.

Ho-Oh was pleased. Raikou, Suicune, and Entei belonged in Johto, the land where they had been born. Given that they had been caught, remaining here with the sisters was a good outcome.

I understand. Human, your actions have earned my respect, and you have passed my test. Now accept my blessing.

It gave Ethan no chance to refuse. Ho-Oh beat its wings, and a single feather detached and floated toward him.

A blessing? Ethan raised an eyebrow, unsure what Ho-Oh intended, but held out his hand and caught it.

The instant the feather touched his palm, it shone with a soft, intense light and melted into his body.

Ethan had not expected that. Heat flooded him. A vigorous energy surged through his body, and he staggered backward.

Gardevoir caught him with psychic power before he fell. The sisters had not even had time to cry out when Deoxys mistook Ho-Oh's gift for an attack. Its eyes flashed red, and it fired a bolt of energy at Ho-Oh. All three birds cried out and charged again.

Ho-Oh gave a light beat of its wings and climbed above the attacks. It kept rising until it vanished into the sky.

As it left, its voice sounded in Ethan's mind one last time.

This is the power of my life. Bear it, human, and come to understand it.

Chapter 889: Ho-Oh Is My Best Friend!

Ho-Oh flew away as suddenly as it had appeared. No one tried to follow. Gardevoir and the sisters crowded around Ethan, their faces anxious. Deoxys and the three birds returned to his side as soon as Ho-Oh was gone.

Are you all right?

What happened?

Everyone asked at once. Impatient Zuki had already reached out to feel his face. Ethan waved to show them he was all right, and she helped him stand steady.

His whole body felt unbearably hot, but he noticed no other immediate discomfort. The power that had entered him with Ho-Oh's feather seemed to be filling him with vigorous life. The weariness and strain of the past two days were already fading.

What did Ho-Oh do to you? Miki asked.

Ethan told them about his conversation with Ho-Oh and its supposed blessing. The sisters exchanged puzzled looks.

It sounds like a good thing, doesn't it? Kuni frowned. Then why did you nearly fall? Is there a side effect?

It feels as though a fire's burning inside me, Ethan said with a rueful smile. And I'm desperately thirsty.

Before they could question him further, he held up a hand. We shouldn't discuss it here. Let's go before a crowd traps us at the tower.

They had made enough noise and light to draw half of Ecruteak's attention. People would be arriving soon. The sisters put their masks back on, and Ethan recalled Deoxys and the three birds. Gardevoir used Teleport to bring them back to the spot where they had first entered the compound.

Monks had gathered beneath Bell Tower. They had not gone inside. Instead, they bowed repeatedly toward the tower and murmured prayers.

Ethan and the others shared a smile. The monks had come close enough to see what was happening, yet had not interrupted. They seemed to have taken the battle for a miracle of Ho-Oh.

Gardevoir was about to Teleport again when several figures and their Pokemon leaped over a wall on the other side of the compound.

The first Trainers to investigate had arrived. A moment later and they might have caught Ethan's group standing there.

The Trainers ran straight for Bell Tower, only to be stopped by the monks at its entrance. An argument quickly broke out. Ethan was too far away to hear the words, but the Trainers gestured urgently and several tried to push past. The monks stood firm and refused to let them through.

After a while, a few impatient Trainers mounted Flying-type Pokemon and rose along the outside of the tower toward its roof. Among them Ethan spotted a familiar face.

Miki followed his gaze. That person looks familiar, but it's too dark to see clearly.

Morty, the Ecruteak Gym Leader, Ethan said. I didn't expect him to get here so quickly.

He's a Gym Leader, Zuki said. Looking after the city is part of his job. She gave the group a quick glance, then urged, Come on. Let's leave before they notice us.

By the time they returned to the sisters' home, it was around one in the morning.

Everyone was hungry after the long night. Kuni and the others went to change, while Miki prepared a late meal. In the dining room, Ethan poured himself a glass of cool tea. He drank another, and then another. Nothing relieved his thirst. His skin still felt hot, and his cheeks had grown red.

So this was Ho-Oh's power. Like the phoenix he knew from stories, it seemed to carry an undying, blazing fire.

When Kuni and Zuki returned, his flushed face startled them. Ethan insisted several times that he felt no other ill effect, which eased their worry a little.

He ate a few hurried mouthfuls when the food arrived, then went to take a cold shower. The icy water cooled his skin. Before he had even dried himself, the heat returned. A restless fire remained inside him, accompanied by an unusually strong desire.

He went straight to Miki's room.

Miki was removing her makeup. As the eldest sister, she had seen to everyone else and cleaned the dining room before finally retiring. She had just placed her ornaments in their box when she heard the door open behind her.

She turned and saw Ethan, his eyes faintly red. Your eyes...

Before she could finish, he crossed the room, lifted her in his arms, and carried her toward the bed.

Miki was startled, but she felt his urgency. Blushing, she tucked her head against his chest and put her arms around his neck, listening to his heavy breathing and heartbeat. He laid her down and leaned over her.

...

Morning came. In the Japanese-style sitting room, the television carried a special report on Ho-Oh's battle with the three birds.

The footage did not clearly show any of the Pokemon. It showed only the fiery glow that had filled the sky when Ho-Oh collided with Tri-Bird Assault. A man and woman in the studio discussed it and offered their guesses.

Kuni, seated before the television, found their speculation amusing. They're not entirely clueless. At least they know Ho-Oh was involved.

People did see Ho-Oh, Miki said with a smile. She had been watching May, Naoko, and Sayo practice in the open space outside the room. There's no hiding that part. But they'll never guess why it was there, or why it fought the three birds.

Let them wonder. Kuni shook her head. It's been so long since Ho-Oh appeared before people. Perhaps this will remind them of its legend.

It will also bring countless Trainers to Ecruteak looking for traces of it.

That sounds good for our shows. Kuni stretched. We could fill the theater every day.

Miki glanced at the clock again. Kuni noticed. How long has Zuki been in there?

Nearly two hours, since breakfast.

That long? Kuni rose. She'll wear herself out. I'll take her place. You've had a rest, haven't you? You can relieve me later.

She left the sitting room and headed for Miki's bedroom. Soon Zuki came in, clothes and hair disheveled, face flushed and steps unsteady.

She sank down beside Miki and drank several gulps of water. Her throat was hoarse from calling out, and the water helped a little.

Honestly, he's like a bull, she complained. He never gets tired. If this goes on, he's going to get me pregnant.

Miki frowned. Weren't there condoms in the room?

Zuki set an empty box on the table and sighed. We used them all.

Then just now you... Miki gave a helpless smile. And Kuni has gone in there without any left.

I can't help that. She'll have to look after herself. Zuki turned to her sister. We've been together so often these past few days. You took your pill, didn't you?

Miki looked away.

You didn't? Zuki lowered her voice. What if you get pregnant? These aren't even your safe days.

Miki touched her abdomen. It's too late to take it now. And at my age, I do want a child.

You're the one who told us to be careful, Zuki said, rolling her eyes. And you had this in mind all along. But if you do get pregnant, your life will change for good.

I know. Miki smiled gently. I've chosen Ethan. Whatever happens, that won't change.

She added, The rest of you must be careful, though. Our theater is doing so well. If all three of us become pregnant together, what will we do?

It's not entirely in our hands, Zuki said. If it happens, Naoko and Sayo will have to keep the shows going.

They're not even adults yet! Miki laughed despite herself, then changed the subject. How is Ethan?

Didn't I just tell you? Zuki opened her collar to show the marks on her skin. Like a bull. He was awake all night and has kept all of us busy again and again. He's still full of energy. Ho-Oh's blessing is something else.

That's not what I meant. I meant how does he look?

Oh. Zuki understood. Much better. His skin isn't hot anymore, and his face isn't so red. I think he'll be back to normal when Kuni's done.

...

Ethan had been right. Rather than endure the heat alone, he had found relief in intimacy with the sisters.

From a little after one in the morning until well past eleven, they had taken turns keeping him company. The fire inside him was gone and his body felt normal. Even after a sleepless night, his mind remained clear and his muscles felt fresh. He thought he could keep going for hours.

Ho-Oh really had given him quite a blessing. Whatever else it might do, it had left him with a remarkable reserve of energy.

Kuni lay against his chest, eyes closed, too languid to move. Ethan stroked her back and was about to settle into the quiet warmth of the moment when Miki entered with a bowl of soup.

Seeing them lying together, she blushed faintly. They had lived together for only a few days, and she was still getting used to this. She knelt beside him and offered the bowl.

You look like yourself again. Drink this first.

The aroma made Ethan's stomach growl. He had eaten breakfast, yet now he was ravenous. Endless energy had to come from somewhere. Perhaps Ho-Oh's gift made him use up food, or the energy stored in his body, far more quickly. That might explain how he had stayed active all night without feeling tired.

At last he thought he understood what Ho-Oh had changed. What a gift for a man.

He really ought to thank Ho-Oh. This was the sort of ability many men would dream of. Ethan made up his mind on the spot: from now on, Ho-Oh was his best friend.

No one could tell him otherwise.

Chapter 890: Departure and the Grand Festival

Ethan and May stayed at the Kimono Sisters' home over the following days.

May practiced constantly. Apart from meals, sleep, and a few everyday chores, she spent every spare moment working with her Pokemon on the lawn. Miki, Kuni, and Zuki offered advice from their experience as stage performers whenever they had time. May took it seriously, and her performances improved rapidly.

As for Ethan, he did spend time training the Pokemon in his reserve team and the Snowman Snorlax he had recently caught. He also considered how the three legendary beasts might combine their powers in an attack. But more often, even during the day, he disappeared into Miki's, Kuni's, or Zuki's room for hours at a time.

He was like a tireless bee, always returning to the flowers for honey.

Naoko, Sayo, and May knew perfectly well what he was doing and pretended not to notice. What they could not miss was how the three older sisters glowed. Their skin and color improved day by day, and they looked as radiant as flowers at their height. Even the other women found themselves admiring their beauty.

Most of all, Miki, Kuni, and Zuki wore smiles that came from genuine happiness. The whole house felt lighter for it.

As the Grand Festival drew near, those days had to end. Brandon still had not contacted Ethan. Whatever the reason, he had rested long enough and it was time to leave.

Parting was painful, especially after the closeness they had shared. The sisters knew Ethan had ambitions that would not let him stay in one place until he had reached his goals. Understanding did little to ease the sadness.

They tried to keep their composure and helped pack everything he would need. Even Zuki stopped sparring with him. She stayed quietly at his side whenever she could, making the most of the time left.

On the night before his departure, Ethan and the three older sisters gathered in one room. No one said it aloud, but none of them wanted to surrender their last night together to another, not even a sister. They shared his company and finally fell asleep together beneath the covers.

Once again, Ethan had Ho-Oh, his new best friend, to thank. Its blessing had left him with plenty of stamina. If anyone spoke ill of Ho-Oh now, he would be the first to object.

...

After breakfast the next morning, Ethan and May stood outside the front gate with their backpacks, saying goodbye to the five sisters.

Miki straightened Ethan's collar and quietly repeated reminders he had heard many times already. He listened without complaint, then drew her into a long embrace.

I know. Take good care of yourselves too.

She nodded against him. After a moment she stepped back to make room for her sisters.

Kuni met him with a gentle smile. Be careful on the road. Call us often, and tell us about everything interesting you see.

I will. I'll send photos and videos too.

Kuni showed her love more quietly than Miki or Zuki. Ethan treasured the warmth in her gaze whenever she looked at him. He held her, breathed in the scent of her hair, and kissed her cheek.

She blushed. They were standing outside, where anyone might see them. She did not object to people knowing about their relationship, but choosing when to share it was different from becoming the subject of gossip by accident.

Fortunately it was early, and few people passed through this wealthy neighborhood of walled homes. No one witnessed the kiss.

Then Ethan turned to Zuki. Before he could open his arms, she hugged him and kissed him boldly. He tried to speak, but she deepened the kiss. Kuni, Naoko, and Sayo flushed at the sight.

When they finally parted, Zuki gave a small huff. You're my man now. You're traveling for me too, since I can't go myself. Catch more powerful Pokemon, and don't lose. Come back with honors I can be proud of.

She had placed her own wish to travel in his hands. Ethan smiled and nodded. I'm aiming for the very top. I'll give you every reason to be proud.

He looked toward Naoko and Sayo. They were the youngest sisters, and now they were family too; he had become their brother-in-law. He meant to say something fitting, but Naoko's expectant look drew him forward. Almost without thinking, he gave her a light hug.

Naoko blushed harder. Miki, Kuni, and Zuki traded meaningful glances. Ethan released her at once and hugged Sayo just as lightly, with the easy affection of family. The older sisters relaxed.

Focused on Ethan, they missed how quickly Naoko's and Sayo's hearts were beating.

May bowed to all five. Miss Miki, Miss Kuni, Miss Zuki, Miss Naoko, Miss Sayothank you for taking care of me!

Do your best at the Grand Festival, Miki said. We'll be watching you on television.

And make good use of all the work Naoko and Sayo put into your training, Kuni added.

The two younger sisters offered May their own heartfelt wishes. Moved, she embraced each of them.

It's getting late, Ethan said when they separated. We should go.

The five sisters placed their hands before them and bowed in a traditional farewell. May your journey be safe and your battles victorious.

Ethan waved. Go back inside. I'll return when I have the chance!

Holding back his reluctance to leave, he released Charizard. He and May climbed on, and at his quiet instruction Charizard spread its wings. It rose into the sky and carried them out of sight.

The sisters watched until Charizard was no more than a black speck. Miki was the first to gather herself. They're gone. Come on, let's get our minds back to what we have to do.

The others finally looked away. It feels strange already, Kuni said with a sigh. After living together all these days, the house will be so quiet without them.

It took only a few days for you to become this attached, Miki said fondly. Imagine if they had stayed longer. We've had a good rest, though. It's time to return to the stage.

That's right. Zuki straightened. Trainers have been arriving in Ecruteak to search for Ho-Oh. We can tell its legend to them through our performances.

...

Charizard flew throughout the day and landed near the Grand Festival venue at the Indigo Plateau around dusk. The competition would begin the day after next. Ethan had timed their arrival so May could rest and prepare tomorrow, become accustomed to the atmosphere, and enter the Festival the following day.

Charizard had barely touched down when a familiar voice called from beside the open ground. Over here!

Ash, Brock, and Max stood up from a rock and waved to Ethan and May. Smiling, the two of them climbed down and went to meet their friends.

The reunion eased the sadness Ethan had carried from Ecruteak. His mood had been heavy for much of the flight, but seeing them helped.

He had arranged this meeting with Ash by phone the day before. During their own travels, Ash had earned six Frontier Symbols and challenged Brandon. His first attempt had failed: Sceptile had fought with all it had, but lost to Brandon's Regirock.

Ash had wanted a rematch. Brandon, however, had an agreement with Ethan and was busy searching for Regice, the last of the three Regis he needed. He had postponed Ash's challenge.

With time on his hands and the Grand Festival approaching, Ash knew May would be competing. He had come to the Indigo Plateau with Brock and Max to meet her and Ethan. Yesterday's call had settled when and where they would gather.

The three boys looked much as they had before, though without May among them they gave the impression of a rather rough-and-ready traveling team.

They did notice something different about Ethan. None could say exactly what it was. He simply seemed to look a little better than beforeperhaps even handsomer.

You two are slow, Ash said, grinning. We've been waiting ages! His eyes moved to Ethan's Pokemon. Charizard? How is it here? Can it leave the Charicific Valley now?

Seeing Ethan's Charizard reminded Ash of his own. He knew the species well enough to see that Ethan's Pokemon was stronger than before, its gaze sharper and more aggressive. Even its presence was imposing. Ash did not like admitting it, but Ethan's Charizard seemed stronger than his.

Ethan laughed and told him how his Charizard had defeated the valley's strongest Charizard and reached the top there.

Ash could only envy him. His own Charizard still had a long way to go.

They headed into the town together. The Festival had not yet begun, but it was already crowded. Coordinators had arrived to compete, visitors to watch, vendors to serve them, and television reporters to cover the event.

Ethan and May had registered early and reserved a room at the Pokemon Center. Ash and the others had arrived in good time too, so no one had to worry about finding somewhere to stay.

As usual after meeting up, they went to a nearby restaurant for dinner. Over the meal, Ash, Brock, and Max asked how confident May felt about the Grand Festival.

She answered with a bright smile. Just wait and see! I've been through special training. I feel ready.

The three exchanged surprised looks. Max finally voiced what they were thinking.

May, don't forget that everyone here has earned five Contest Ribbons, just like you. They're strong. You shouldn't underestimate them.

I'm not underestimating anyone, May said, waving a hand. I just don't intend to lose!

Chapter 891: Umbreon

May was more modest now than she had been when she traveled with Ash. She had met stronger people and seen more of the world. When she had first arrived at this point in the anime, she had declared that she would win the Grand Festival and show everyone. After traveling with Ethan and improving so quickly, she sounded more measured instead. That was a good change.

The friends had plenty to talk about after so long apart. As the conversation went on, though, Ash noticed that Ethan seemed distracted.

Something wrong, Ethan? he asked. No appetite? Are you feeling sick?

Before Ethan could reply, May covered a laugh. I bet he's missing someone.

After spending day and night with Miki and the others, she assumed he was already saddened by leaving them.

Ethan shook his head. May, do you remember why we went to Ecruteak in the first place?

Of course. We went to decide what Eevee should evolve in She broke off. They had forgotten all about it.

We really did let that slip, she said with a rueful smile.

You and I both did. So did the sisters. Ethan sighed. He had let himself get too comfortable in their home, spending his days laughing with them and his nights even more pleasantly. Somehow the reason for the visit had fallen out of his mind.

Eevee had contributed to that. Back in the place it used to call home, it had roamed and played all day, often out of Ethan's sight. That made it easier to forget the unfinished decision. Ho-Oh's strange blessing had distracted everyone further.

The deeper problem was that no one had settled on an evolution. It seemed Ethan would have to make the final choiceor at least narrow it down for Eevee.

After dinner they returned to the Pokemon Center. Ethan released Eevee in their room. Ash and the others kept talking nearby, leaving him alone with his decision.

He considered every form Eevee could take. Jolteon was out first; he already had one. Vaporeon and Flareon were common, and he had no shortage of Water- or Fire-type Pokemon. That left Espeon, Umbreon, Leafeon, Glaceon, and Sylveon.

He ruled out Glaceon next. He had just caught the Ice-type Snowman Snorlax, and Ice types had their natural disadvantages. With Gardevoir, Metagross, and Deoxys on his team, he had little need for another Psychic type such as Espeon.

The choice was down to Sylveon, Umbreon, and Leafeon: Fairy, Dark, or Grass. Any of the three could strengthen his roster.

Sylveon was popular, and its airy, charming appearance made it a favorite with girls. But Eevee was male, and Ethan could not quite picture him battling in that soft pink form.
