Nor could he imagine giving commands to Sylveon in a tournament. It did not seem to fit the composed, exacting style he liked to bring to a fight.

So Umbreon or Leafeon. Erika had a Leafeon that had evolved with a stone Ethan gave her. Zuki had an Umbreon. Either choice would echo one of the women close to him.

No wonder they had talked it over so many times without finding an answer.

After thinking for a long while, Ethan still could not decide. He took Eevee outside for some air. Perhaps a walk would clear his head.

The moon hung high above the small town. Though it was eight or nine in the evening, the pedestrian street was still busy with tourists and Coordinators taking a break before the competition.

Ethan bought a snack for himself and one for Eevee, then left the crowd and walked along the lake in the competitors' village. A second moon shimmered on the water. They strolled side by side, trading bites of their snacks as they admired it.

Other Trainers and their Pokemon were walking by the lake too. To anyone watching, Ethan and Eevee looked like any ordinary, contented pair.

There Ethan put the remaining choice to his partner. Would you rather become Leafeon or Umbreon?

Two options were easier to face than eight. Eevee looked up at the moon and spoke softly. Ethan could not understand Pokemon speech, so he called on his usual interpreter.

Gengar.

Gengar rose from Ethan's shadow. As it reached his shoulder, it casually took the snack out of his hand and began eating.

Ethan glanced at his empty hand. You can eat in a moment. What did Eevee say?

Without turning around, Gengar answered, Ever since he was little, his favorite thing has been sitting on the roof to watch the moon. He thinks it's the most beautiful thing in the world.

Ethan looked up at the bright moon. Eevee's meaning was plain enough. He liked the moon and wanted to become Umbreon.

Are you sure? Ethan asked.

Eevee met his eyes and nodded earnestly.

Then Umbreon it is. Ethan would have respected either choice. Umbreon suited him too. Tyranitar, a Rock and Dark type, was his only Pokemon with the Dark type. A pure Dark-type Umbreon would fill a gap in the team.

With the choice made, Ethan began thinking about what they would need. If I remember right, Umbreon doesn't need an Evolution stone. It needs to be nighttime and for Eevee to have a strong bond with its Trainer. I wonder if you

He never finished. White light flared around Eevee and enveloped him.

Ethan understood. Eevee had been ready to evolve all along. He had held it back because he had not decided what he wanted to become.

You weren't any more decisive than I was, Ethan said, laughing and shaking his head. If I'd known you wanted Umbreon, we could have spared ourselves all that discussion.

Then again, without Eevee's patience, they might never have gone back to Ecruteak or experienced everything that followed. Ethan had reason to thank him.

The glow caught the attention of nearby Trainers. They could not see Ethan's face clearly in the dark, but a Pokemon evolving was always an exciting moment for its Trainer and an enviable one for onlookers.

When the light faded and revealed an Umbreon, the passersby looked away again. Umbreon was less common than Flareon, Vaporeon, Jolteon, or Espeon, but its evolution needed no stone. Trainers still encountered it often enough that it was no great surprise.

Ethan did not care what anyone else thought. His Pokemon had chosen a form he liked, and it suited the team. That was enough.

As Umbreon examined his new body, Ethan lifted him high with a delighted grin. This form really does suit you. Zuki will be happy when she hears you chose Umbreon too.

Back in their room, Ash, Brock, Max, and May noticed the change immediately.

Umbreon?

You chose Umbreon?

He evolved already?

They crowded around to look. They had all seen Umbreon before, but Ethan had gone out only to clear his head. Returning with an evolved Pokemon was unexpectedly quick.

Ash stared at Umbreon and thought of Gary, his first rival back in Pallet Town. Along with Blastoise, Umbreon was one of Gary's signature Pokemon. Seeing Ethan's brought Gary vividly to mind.

May was simply happy for Ethan. She knew how much discussion and trouble Eevee's evolution had prompted. Like Ethan, she also thought Zuki would be delighted by the choice.

After a few words with the others, Ethan moved to a corner with Umbreon and called Zuki on video. She answered almost at once.

To his surprise, she was dressed for the stage and sitting in a luxury car. The sisters had evidently finished a performance and were on their way home. Ethan could hear the others beside her, and Miki and Kuni leaned partly into view.

I thought you'd wait a few days before calling, Zuki said. You couldn't hold out even one night?

Ethan only smiled. Have you just finished a show?

Yes, and it was packed, Miki said. Your timing is good. A few minutes ago, we were wondering whether you and May had reached the venue.

May leaned into the camera to greet them.

Across the room, Brock heard several women's voices and turned at once. The glimpse of beautiful, brightly dressed sisters on Ethan's screen left him frozen in place.

With so many people listening, Ethan kept the conversation brief. Then he lifted Umbreon into view. Look who this is.

Surprised cries came from the car.

Eevee!

He chose Umbreon?

All five sisters were pleased that Eevee had finally made up his mind, and startled that Umbreon was his choice. Almost together, the other four turned toward Zuki.

The corner of her mouth lifted in a small, private smile. She had an Umbreon of her own. Now Ethan's Eevee had chosen the same form, and she could not help feeling as though her man had followed her lead.

Chapter 892: The Ungrateful Monkey

Perhaps Ho-Oh had changed Ethan's constitution. Although he had gone to bed late, he woke early the next morning. He had slept only a few hours, yet he felt full of energy, without a trace of fatigue from yesterday's long flight on Charizard.

He had said it many times already, but Ho-Oh's blessing really was powerful.

Eevee's evolution had settled another concern. With one day left before the Grand Festival began, Ethan could relax and look around the venue, remembering how it had felt when he competed in the Indigo League.

It was barely six in the morning. The others were still asleep, so he left them undisturbed and ate breakfast. As activity picked up outside, he took his newly evolved Umbreon for a walk beyond the Pokemon Center.

He had hardly stepped out when he saw an interview playing on a distant outdoor screen. The woman being filmed wore glasses and a disguise, but Ethan recognized Jessie at once. He knew her too well not to.

Team Rocket's disguises could be impressiveJames could even pass for a busty womanbut familiar details gave them away to Ethan. Ash and people who did not know the trio might remain fooled.

Still, seeing Jessie's face first thing in the morning put a dent in his mood. It was a beautiful day, and he had hoped for a pleasant surprise. Instead, the moment he stepped outside, he found Team Rocket.

He rounded the screen and spotted the trio filming in an open space nearby. Jessie had her hair in two long pigtails and wore large glasses, a short, ornate dress with a big red bow, knee-high white stockings, and orange shoes. She smiled professionally at the camera, trying very hard to look cute.

James, Meowth, and Wobbuffet were dressed as her camera operator and crew. Ethan moved closer through the onlookers to hear her report.

Hello, everyone! Jessie said in an affectedly sweet voice, holding a microphone. Tomorrow, the long-awaited Pokemon Grand Festival begins! I'm the adorable Jessadia, bringing you beautiful live reports from the scene!

She stretched her words and played up every cute gesture. Ethan could see how hard she was trying to win people over. To him, the costume and voice sat awkwardly on her. She had rather outgrown this sort of act.

Jessadia continued, Coordinators who earned five Ribbons across Kanto have been arriving at the Indigo Plateau! Excitement outside the venue has reached its peak. Everyone's busy checking their Pokemon's health before tomorrow's preliminary round!

James turned the camera to show the surrounding activity, which appeared on the big screen. Ethan stepped back into the crowd to stay out of the shot.

For all their failures at stealing Pokemon, the trio were good at this kind of work. When the short segment ended, Contest host Lilian walked up to Jessie.

Well done, Miss Jessadia! You volunteered for the job, and you're proving you have talent.

Thank you! Jessie bowed with a smile. I'll keep working hard!

Lilian had not recognized her. She had met Jessie many times and had even seen her posing as the Contest entrant Jessibella. Yet another name and a new outfit were enough to fool her. Perhaps she simply had no reason to expect Jessie to return as a reporter.

Then I'll leave it to you to keep the crowd excited, Lilian said. See you later! She waved and went on her way.

Ethan had no intention of exposing Team Rocket. If they did not cause trouble in front of him, he saw no reason to interfere. He shook his head and walked on with Umbreon.

After making a circuit of the venue, he put the encounter out of his mind. When he thought May and the others would have woken and eaten, he returned to the Pokemon Center. Team Rocket had never noticed him. If they had, their fine morning might have soured as quickly as his.

In the dining area, May was on a video call. As Ethan came closer, he saw her mother Caroline on the screen.

I'm sorry, May, Caroline was saying. I really can't get away. I can't come to Kanto to cheer for you in person.

Before May answered, Max let out a disappointed sound. Like his sister, he had hoped to see their mother after so long apart, rather than talk through a screen.

May shook her head understandingly. It's all right. You and Dad are busy.

Don't worry! Caroline said brightly. I'll send you all my cheering energy from Hoenn! She pushed both hands toward the camera as though sending a wave of power.

May and Max stared, their expressions flattening at their mother's playfulness. You don't need to do that. We know you're cheering for us...

Ethan stepped into view and greeted Caroline.

Oh, Ethan! Thank you for looking after May. She hasn't caused you trouble, has she?

Mom! May protested.

Not at all, Ethan said. May's helped me a great deal. Traveling with her has made things easier for me.

What a sweet thing to say! Caroline laughed. Her father and I can't be there, so please cheer for her in person.

Of course.

Ash leaned toward the screen and thumped his chest. Leave it to us, Aunt Caroline!

Thank you! Max, you cheer for your sister too. Bye, everyone!

The call had just ended, and May was about to speak when cries rose from the other end of the lobby.

An Aipom had appeared from somewhere and was snatching people's hats, stacking them on its head. When anyone tried to catch it, it darted through the crowd and stole still more hats. The commotion grew.

Is that...? Ash's eyebrows rose when he saw it.

Do you know that Aipom? May asked.

Ash gave an awkward smile. Brock explained. On their way here, after Ash lost to Brandon, they had come across a group of Aipom fleeing an angry farmer. One had taken Ash's hat. The effort to get it back had led to several more encounters with that particular Aipom.

Now it had followed them to the Indigo Plateau and was stealing hats again. May shook her head at their luck. Ethan, recognizing the Pokemon, smiled.

Anyone familiar with Ash's future team would know this Aipom. Ash would soon catch it and take it through Sinnoh on his Gym journey. Later he would trade it to Dawn, who would use it in Contests. Eventually it would leave them both to train with a Pokemon Ping-Pong player. Some fans would jokingly call it the ungrateful monkey.

It was capable in both battles and Contest performances. Its restless temperament and tendency toward jealousy, and the ease with which it later left its companions, made some viewers dislike it. Others jokingly called it a Pokemon of three masters.

Ethan was less bothered. Each departure had given Ash or Dawn a useful new partner, and Aipom had contributed plenty while traveling with them. They had parted amicably; it was the viewers who felt slighted.

Whether because Aipom was uncommon in Hoenn or because May found it cute, she raised her Pokedex. It supplied an entry.

Aipom, the Long Tail Pokemon. Normal type. Most of its body is purple, with cream-colored areas and a single tuft of hair on its head. Females have a longer tuft than males. It lives high in trees and can hang upside down from branches by its strong tail. Its tail also helps it balance as it leaps between branches. Aipom stays lively and energetic throughout the day.

By then Aipom had piled more than a dozen hats on its head. It came to a stop in front of Ash and wiggled about, plainly proud of itself. He had no doubt it was the same one.

Why are you stealing people's hats again? he asked helplessly.

To everyone nearby, that sounded as though Ash was its Trainer. Faces turned toward him.

Is that your Aipom?

Tell it to give our hats back!

Stop it from causing trouble!

With so many people speaking at once, Ash could hardly explain. He turned back to Aipom. Come on. Give everyone their hats back.

Perhaps Aipom listened. It twisted and sent the stack of hats flying off its head. Then it sprang forward, yanked Ash's cap away, and fled into the crowd without looking back.

That cap was one of Ash's most treasured possessions. He chased Aipom at once, but even he could not catch an agile monkey in such a crowded place. Pikachu joined in; its speed was little help against Aipom's leaps from one height to another.

Nurse Joy hurried over to investigate the noise. As Aipom passed her, it stole her cap too. That was enough to draw Brock into the chase on her behalf.

May stood holding her Pokedex, stunned. A moment ago everything had been peaceful. Now the lobby had turned into a contest of people and Pokemon chasing hats.

Then again, trouble seemed to follow Ash wherever he went. She almost felt nostalgic. She glanced at Ethan, about to ask whether they should intervene.

Before she could, Roselia sprang into the fray. Its Petal Dance formed a small whirlwind of petals around Aipom, trapping it. The crowd turned to see a green-haired boy in purple, hands tucked coolly in his pockets.

Drew? Ash and the others recognized him at once. None had expected to find him here, much less see him step in to stop the disturbance.

A woman's voice called from the crowd. Slowbro, use Psychic!

Psychic power wrapped around Aipom. It floated out of Roselia's swirling petals and drifted slowly back toward Ash.
